verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified line-by-line. Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589), started only on IsServer via StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") in Game.Start (:100069-100074), so a vanilla client never runs the pairer. Pass 1 predicate is exactly `zDO == null || tag mismatch || partner connection None` (:100600-100604) and pass 2 random-pairs via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679), gated by IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal (:100700). SetConnection (:100637-100651) is private and routes RPC_SetConnection to an online owner; the unconditional triad SetOwner/SetConnection/ForceSendZDO is the forceImmediateConnection path vanilla itself uses from ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698). ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73666). ZDOID renumbering on load confirmed (ZDO.Load :74552). Route-level control is genuinely server-owned: a vanilla client's TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the connection ZDOID live from the ZDO (:143539) and has no way to choose another target. Several factual corrections below; none defeat the option.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. Game.ConnectPortals is public (SERVER:100589), started only under IsServer from Game.Start (:100071-100074) via ConnectPortalsCoroutine (:100580-100587, 5 s). Pass 1 predicate is exactly `zDO == null || tag mismatch || partner connection None` (:100600-100604) with no reciprocity test; pass 2 re-pairs any unconnected, non-staged portal with a uniformly random same-tag partner (:100607-100622, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679). Staging guard is real: ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-writes both directions of last tick's pairs (:100689-100698), IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal excludes them (:100700-100710). SetConnection is private and routes through RPC_SetConnection to an online owner unless owner==0/dead/forced (:100637-100651); a mod must write the three-line triad itself. ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and SetDirtyPortals only on actual change (:73656-73666, ZDOExtraData.SetConnection :74951-74961). ZDOID renumbering on load is real (:74552). Also a second vanilla call site exists: ZDOMan.LoadChunks calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() at :76523. Route topology is genuinely server-owned, so server-enforced is honest for the ROUTE question — but it is server-asserted, not tamper-proof (see corrections c/d). Several stated details are wrong: the OnWorldReady hook timing, the load-time rationale, and the omission of vanilla client actions that silently overwrite managed links.

catalog.name: Phantom Anchor Fabrication
catalog.oneLine: Server-fabricated portal ZDOs at arbitrary coordinates, used as invisible destination endpoints so a hub can point anywhere without a player having built a portal there.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143517-143549) performs zero prefab validation on the destination: it resolves `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID)`, reads `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()`, and computes `pos = position + (rotation * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` (:143542-143545). Any ZDO with a position and rotation is therefore a legal arrival point for a 100% vanilla client.

Create one with `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` (:76674). CreateNewZDO does NOT set the prefab on the ZDO and does NOT set Persistent — replicate `ZNetView.Awake`'s fabrication block (:82613-82620): `zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);`. Pass a REAL portal prefab hash from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` to CreateNewZDO, because `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) fires on the hash argument, files the ZDO in `m_portalObjects`, removes it from the sector array, and sets `DirtyPortalObjects` — which is the only thing that causes the ChunkPortal save file to be written (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621-77635). A ZDO created with hash 0 and then `SetPrefab`ed to a portal hash is excluded from normal chunk saves by `AddObjectsPerChunk`'s filter (:77572) AND never entered the portal chunk — it exists in RAM and vanishes on restart with no error.

Two anchor flavours. A PORTAL-prefab anchor is always resident server-side, saved, and enumerated by GetPortalList — but it instantiates a visible portal mesh on any client who comes within ~96m (`ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea`, Chebyshev ≤ 1.5×64m, :82298-82319). Place these where players are meant to arrive. A NON-portal-prefab anchor (any harmless prefab hash) is invisible to vanilla's pairer entirely but must set `Persistent = true` explicitly or it is never saved, and must be resolvable by the traveller's client.

Delivery: the traveller's `TargetFound` (:143640-143656) requires the client to actually HOLD the target ZDO; if absent it fires `RequestZDO` and returns false with no message. The server answers via `RPC_RequestZDO` → `ForceSendZDO` (:77689-77692), so the second walk-through works. Pre-warm with `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId)` (:77714) when a player approaches.
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks into a hub portal and arrives standing one metre in front of an anchor, facing the direction the server chose. If the anchor uses a portal prefab they see a real portal there and can walk back through it. If it uses a non-portal prefab they arrive at what looks like empty ground — no structure at all, which reads as a genuine teleport-to-coordinates. The first attempt after a fresh server-side re-point to a never-visited region can silently do nothing: the player walks in, the screen does not fade, no message appears (gate 1 of Teleport returns without calling player.Message, :143519-143522). They step out, step back in, and it works.
failureModes: CreateNewZDO with the wrong prefab hash produces a ZDO that exists in RAM and is silently lost at world save
Anchor in an unvisited region: first transit is a completely silent no-op (no fade, no message) while RequestZDO round-trips — the single worst UX bug in this whole design space
Portal-prefab anchors are visible structures; players will try to demolish them, and WearNTear RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove are client-executed and unobservable to the server (:150332/:150419)
ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) only persists a connection when BOTH endpoints resolve in m_objectsByID — a deleted anchor silently loses the link across a restart

Never call zdo.SetPosition() on a portal-prefab anchor: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portals (:73752-73757) so it stays filed under its creation sector forever, and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) then looks it up by the new index and leaks it
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client cleanly handle a Portal connection pointing at a ZDO whose prefab it cannot instantiate? TargetFound only needs GetZDO != null and Teleport only reads pos/rot, but ZNetScene.CreateObject will still attempt an Instantiate when the client's active area covers it. Test both a valid harmless prefab and an unregistered hash.

Do fabricated portal-prefab anchors placed at arbitrary coordinates survive a full save/load round trip with their connection intact, given the disk format stores connections as matched int hashes rather than ZDOIDs (ZDO.Save :74315, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850)?
corrections: Portal-prefab anchors are destroyed by the vanilla owning client if not resting on a collider: WearNTear.UpdateWear (client :150402-150450) runs on the owner, and with m_noSupportWear (default true, :149945) an anchor whose OverlapBox finds no terrain/support (:150747-150790) takes 100 damage per wear tick until destroyed. The server cannot collider-test (reference position pinned at 1e6), so Y must come from pure WorldGenerator height and will be wrong wherever players have terraformed. This is the primary failure mode, not the RequestZDO round trip.

Unknown-prefab anchors (custom hash) are invisible but cause per-frame client log spam: ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted (client :82334-82370) retries every non-Created near ZDO each frame and CreateObject logs 'Missing prefab hash' each time (:82225-82236). Only the server destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs (`else if IsServer` branch :82361-82367), and the server only processes its own zone. Known-prefab anchors are instantiated (visible; a self-destroying effect prefab would destroy the ZDO). IsAreaReady (client :82293-82310) skips invalid-prefab ZDOs, so arrival completes.

Anchors placed beyond ±16384 m collapse to Sector 0 (SectorToIndex :115760-115773), the same bucket as the server's reference zone, and the server's own CreateDestroyObjects (:82268-82276) then processes them: known prefab -> server-side GameObject, unknown prefab -> 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' by the server. Keep anchors inside world bounds.

A portal-prefab anchor is a real, fully functional portal on the client: players can retag it (Interact -> RPC_SetTag on the owner clears both ends, :143587-143602) and walk into it. It is enumerated by GetPortalList and must be governed by the pairing takeover.

RequestZDO is only issued from TargetFound(), which UpdatePortal reaches via `flag2 && TargetFound()` (:143508) — short-circuited unless a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (5 m) — or from Teleport itself. So the 'first walk-through silently fails' only when the player enters the trigger before ~0.5 s poll + RTT has elapsed since coming within 5 m; standing at the portal for a second first avoids it. The claimed 'appears within ~96 m' is really sector-based (peer simulation distance in CreateSyncList :77211-77230), not PointInsideActiveArea.

Portal-prefab anchors are instantiated on any client within the active area with the full prefab, including WearNTear (m_noSupportWear = true, client :149945). Once ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands that client ownership (SERVER:76901-76924), WearNTear.UpdateWear applies 100 damage per wear tick when HaveSupport() is false (client :150402-150447, :150888-150891) and the collapse ends in RPC_DestroyZDO, which the server applies with no check (SERVER:76953-76961). Anchors must sit on real terrain support, not merely at WorldGenerator height; and any player can hammer/axe-remove them. Rain wear (m_noRoofWear) also degrades them to 50%.

Non-portal anchors: an unknown hash is not instantiated and does not block IsAreaReady (IsPrefabZDOValid, client :82215-82223) but CreateObject logs 'Missing prefab hash' on every creation attempt while a client is nearby (client :82225-82235). A known harmless prefab is instantiated (may collide/render). Prefab hash 0 is skipped silently but do NOT pass 0 to CreateNewZDO: ZDO.Reset does not clear m_prefab (SERVER:73536-73550), so a recycled pooled ZDO carries a stale prefab into `prefabHash = zDO.GetPrefab()` (:76686) and can accidentally trigger AddIfPortal.

'First attempt silently does nothing' is mostly mitigated by vanilla: UpdatePortal (0.5 s) evaluates `flag2 && TargetFound()` whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange = 5 m (:143491-143509), which issues RequestZDO before the player reaches the trigger. The silent failure hits only players already inside/adjacent when the re-point lands, or sprinting from >5 m into the trigger within one poll.

Arrival on the vanilla client: Player.UpdateTeleport (client :15331-15381) holds a distant teleport for at least 8 s, requires ZNetScene.IsAreaReady (zone loaded + every known-prefab ZDO in the 1-zone radius instantiated, client :82293-82311) then FindFloor; without floor for 15 s it drops the player to GetSolidHeight+0.5. Anchor Y must come from WorldGenerator math on the server. The 2 s m_teleportCooldown in Player.TeleportTo (client :15304-15329) applies on arrival.

Restart: the anchor's ZDOID is renumbered (:74552); a hub->anchor link survives via the hash slot but comes back RECIPROCAL (ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77893), so a portal-prefab anchor points back at the hub after every restart. Registry must re-find anchors by position.

Portal-prefab anchors are saved regardless of Persistent (GetSaveClonePerChunk clones all of m_portalObjects, :77624-77630), but set Persistent anyway: non-Persistent ZDOs are never handed to peers (:76910) and RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS (:77406-77418) would delete them if ownership ever left the server.
evidence: ZDOMan.RequestZDO -> server, RPC_RequestZDO, ForceSendZDO(peer,id) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77684-77692, 77714-77724; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(string) -> GetServerPeerID :83559-83562; Register RequestZDO :76156
AddObjectsPerChunk portal filter / GetSaveClonePerChunk portal chunk — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572, 77621-77635
Client ZDO eviction only on destroy — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:77129
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143517-143549) validates nothing about the destination ZDO beyond existence: GetZDO -> GetPosition/GetRotation -> pos = position + forward*m_exitDistance + up (:143539-143546); client copy is byte-identical to the server decompile (diffed). TargetFound (:143640-143656) requires the client to hold the ZDO and calls RequestZDO -> routed to server (InvokeRoutedRPC(string,...) targets GetServerPeerID, :83559-83562) -> RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692); server-side ForceSendZDO(peerID,id) exists (:77714-77724). CreateNewZDO(pos,hash) (:76674-76692) sets owner, calls AddIfPortal on the hash argument (:77732-77752), does NOT set m_prefab or Persistent; ZNetView.Awake's fabrication block (:82615-82619) is the right template. AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal-hash ZDOs (:77572) and only DirtyPortalObjects writes ChunkPortal (:77621-77631), so a hash-0-then-SetPrefab portal is indeed unsaveable. Client never evicts received ZDOs except on destroy (client m_objectsByID.Remove only at :77129) so a force-sent anchor persists on the traveller. Persistent must be set before SetPrefab/SetRotation or the chunk is never dirtied (IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector gated on Persistent, :73832-73840, :76695-76700). Mechanism holds; but the option understates what a vanilla client does to a fabricated anchor once it is instantiated.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Client TeleportWorld (client :144142, byte-identical to SERVER:143402-143662 by diff) validates nothing about the destination beyond `GetZDO(connection) != null`: Teleport reads position/rotation and calls TeleportTo (:143539-143547). TargetFound requires the client to HOLD the ZDO and otherwise fires RequestZDO and returns false silently (:143640-143656); RequestZDO is a routed RPC to the server (client :83788-83791, :76280) answered by RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692), and AddForceSendZdos inserts at index 0 subject only to ShouldSend revision checks, not area (:77263-77280, :76003-76013). CreateNewZDO indeed sets neither Persistent nor m_prefab and runs AddIfPortal on the hash ARGUMENT (:76674-76692, :77732-77752); AddIfPortal removes the ZDO from the sector array and sets DirtyPortalObjects; sector-chunk saving filters portal hashes (:77572) and the portal chunk is only written when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77635). So the 'hash 0 then SetPrefab' ZDO really is unsaveable. ZNetView.Awake fabrication block confirmed (:82613-82620). Unknown prefab hashes load with only a warning (FilterZDO :76346-76360). Mechanism confirmed; but the option under-states what a vanilla client does to a portal-prefab anchor and mis-describes the 'first walk silently fails' frequency.

catalog.name: Rotating Hub
catalog.oneLine: A hub portal whose Portal connection cycles through an ordered ring of destinations on a fixed schedule, rewritten server-side.
catalog.howItWorks:
A mod subsystem holds `{hubPositionKey, ZDOID[] destinations, int index, double nextRotateAt}`. On each `OnUpdate(dt)` tick (recommended 0.2s; cost is one dictionary lookup plus a comparison against `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds()` :81546) it checks whether `nextRotateAt` has passed. If so it resolves the hub ZDO fresh via `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(hubId)` — never a cached ZDO object, because ZDOPool recycles them (:78286-78311) — advances the index, and performs the write triad: `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destinations[index])`, `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(hubId)`.

Propagation is fast and deterministic. `ForceSendZDO(ZDOID)` adds the id to every `ZDOPeer.m_forceSend` (:77706-77712); `AddForceSendZdos` inserts it at index 0 of that peer's sync list (:77275), ahead of everything else; `SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per Update frame behind a 0.05s gate (:76837-76862). So the new connection reaches a standing player in roughly 50-100ms plus RTT, not seconds.

THE RACE, QUANTIFIED. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` at the instant of transit (:143539) — nothing is cached. So a player who enters the trigger during the propagation window (~50-200ms) goes to the OLD destination; a player who enters after it goes to the new one. There is no in-between state and no torn read: the connection is a single ZDOID field written atomically inside one `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` call (:74951-74961) and serialized as one byte + one ZDOID (`ZDO.Serialize` :74169-74173). The change IS atomic from the client's point of view.

What is NOT within that window: the 0.5s `UpdatePortal` poll (`InvokeRepeating("UpdatePortal", 0.5f, 0.5f)`, :143450) is purely cosmetic — it spawns the `m_connected` EffectList on the rising edge of `HaveTarget()` and drives `m_target_found.SetActive(...)` (:143491-143509). It does not gate teleporting. The 5s vanilla reconciler is irrelevant once pairing is taken over.

If the new destination ZDO is not held by the traveller's client, `TargetFound` returns false and the walk-through silently does nothing (:143646-143654). Pre-warm the whole ring with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)` for every peer within ~200m of the hub on rotation, or simply once per peer join.
catalog.playerExperience: A player standing at the hub sees the portal glowing and connected. At the rotation instant: within ~0.1s the destination has changed under them with no visual cue at all (the emission colour only changes when HaveTarget flips, and it never flipped). They walk in and arrive somewhere new. If the server blacked out the link first (see Blackout Swap), they instead see the glow die within 0.5s and the emission fade to m_colorUnconnected over ~1 second (Update lerps m_colorAlpha at 1.0/sec, :143513), hover text flips to "$piece_portal_unconnected", then the connected VFX/SFX puff fires when the new link lands. A player ALREADY STANDING inside the trigger volume when the swap lands does not re-trigger — OnTriggerEnter fires on ENTER only (:143673) — so they must step out and back in, which is an invisible, confusing dead portal until they move.
failureModes: Silent no-op on the first transit to a cold destination (TargetFound → RequestZDO → return false, no player.Message) — the player reports 'the portal is broken'
Player standing inside the trigger volume never re-triggers after a swap (OnTriggerEnter only, :143673)
Without Pairing Authority Takeover, Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 tears the link down within 5s because the destination's s_tag differs from the hub's (:100601)

A mid-transit rotation is harmless — Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos as a snapshot the moment TeleportTo is accepted (:15343) — but the traveller's arrival is the OLD target and the hub now points elsewhere, so their return walk lands somewhere else

Rotating faster than ~10s makes the hub effectively unusable: the ~8s hard floor on a distantTeleport (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349) means a player can depart and the hub has already moved on by the time they land
No delta encoding: ZDOMan.SendZDOs re-serializes the entire ZDO per peer per send (:77056-77064), ~80-120 bytes per rotation per in-range peer
prerequisites: Phantom Anchor Fabrication (only if destinations are not real player-built portals)
openQuestions: What is the actual collider geometry of TeleportWorldTrigger on the portal prefab? It determines how long a player can linger 'inside' a portal without re-triggering after a swap. Unity asset data — inspect the prefab hierarchy client-side.

Measured end-to-end propagation from server SetConnection to a standing client honouring the new target, on a real server with N peers. Predicted 50-200ms; log server write time and client arrival coordinate.
corrections: ZNet.GetTimeSeconds (:81546-81549) is world net-time, which EnvMan.UpdateTimeSkip (:96310-96323) advances at (delta/12 s) per second during a sleep skip. A rotation timer keyed on it compresses when everyone sleeps. Use Time.realtimeSinceStartup or DateTime.UtcNow for wall-clock rotation.

'Sees the portal glowing' needs qualification: m_target_found is only active when a teleportable player is within m_activationRange = 5 m (`flag2 && TargetFound()`, :143508). The far-visible cue is only the emission colour driven by m_hadTarget (HaveTarget, i.e. connection != None), which does not change on a swap between two non-None targets — so the 'no visual cue' claim is even stronger than stated.

Propagation latency has a backpressure floor: SendZDOs returns without sending when the peer's socket send queue exceeds 10240 bytes or has < 2048 bytes headroom (:77008-77019). Under heavy sync (a player just teleported into a dense base) the swap can lag well past 100 ms.

Ownership caveat inherited from the takeover: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76930) returns hub ownership to a peer within 5 m every 2 s; a simultaneous owner-side DataRevision bump can make that client drop the server's write (equal DataRevision -> ignored, RPC_ZDOData :77099-77108). Because SetConnection is idempotent, re-asserting the same value does not re-send; a genuine bump is required to repair.

UpdatePortal is not purely cosmetic: `m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound())` (:143508) calls TargetFound -> RequestZDO whenever a teleportable player is within 5 m, so vanilla pre-fetches the destination ZDO as a player approaches. Server-side ForceSend pre-warm is only needed for players already inside 5 m when the rotation lands, or when destinations rotate faster than the 0.5 s poll + RTT.

State `{ZDOID[] destinations, hubId}` does not survive a restart: ZDO.Load renumbers every ZDOID (:74552). Rebuild from a position/creator-keyed registry in a ZDOMan.LoadChunks postfix, not at OnWorldReady (ZNetScene.Awake fires before ZNet.Start loads the world, :79254-79277).

SetOwner(server) in the triad is undone within 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS when a player is near the hub (:76872-76924), costing an extra OwnerRevision bump and resend per rotation; harmless but not 'one write'.

Revision race with a client-owned hub: if the owner client bumps DataRevision in the same window, both copies reach d+1 and the client's RPC_ZDOData discards the server's data (client :77244-77252), leaving a stale connection on that client until the next server bump. Rare (client writes to portal ZDOs are only WearNTear support/health) — mitigate with a second revision bump or a periodic re-send.

Player-side timing not stated: Player.TeleportTo refuses within 2 s of the last teleport and a distant teleport holds the loading screen >= 8 s (client :15304-15381), so 'walk in and arrive somewhere new' is >= 8 s per hop regardless of server speed.

catalog.name: Blackout Swap Protocol
catalog.oneLine: A three-phase rotation (announce → disconnect → re-point) that turns an invisible destination change into a legible, signposted event on a vanilla client.
catalog.howItWorks:
A bare connection rewrite is atomic but INVISIBLE — the player has no way to know the destination changed. This protocol spends time to buy legibility, using the only three vanilla-client-visible portal channels the server controls: the tag string, the connected/unconnected state, and the connected EffectList.

Phase 1, T-30s (announce). Write `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, "Swamp 30s")` (:73721, key at :78617) then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — a tag-only write does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects and is silently lost at the next world save otherwise (only SetConnection/AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO set it, :73661/:77750/:76986). `GetHoverText` renders it live as `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"Swamp 30s"` every frame the player hovers (:143453-143463). There is NO server-side length cap — the 10-character limit lives only in the client's `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482). Rich text is stripped by `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), so no colour.

Phase 2, T-0 (blackout). `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` + ForceSendZDO. Within ~0.1s the client's next `UpdatePortal` (≤0.5s) sets `m_hadTarget=false`, `m_target_found` glow goes dark, and `Update` lerps the emission from `m_colorTargetfound` to `m_colorUnconnected` at 1.0/sec (:143513). Hover flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461). Crucially, a walk-through during blackout hits gate 1 of Teleport and returns silently with no message (:143519-143522) — the portal is safely inert, not mis-routed. Hold for a configured dwell (recommended 2-4s: long enough that the client's 0.5s poll definitely saw the flip and the colour visibly moved).

Phase 3 (re-point). Write the new connection + new tag. The client's next UpdatePortal sees `HaveTarget()` newly true and fires `m_connected.Create(transform.position, transform.rotation)` (:143499) — the vanilla portal-activation VFX and sound, at the portal, for free. Total legible swap: ~3-5s, of which ~2-4s is unusable.

Tick budget: one timer per hub, evaluated at 0.2s. Trivial.
catalog.playerExperience: A player hovering the hub reads `$piece_portal_tag:"Swamp 30s"`. Thirty seconds later the portal's blue glow visibly fades to its unlit colour over about a second and the hover line changes to "$piece_portal_unconnected". They walk through and nothing happens — no fade, no message — which reads as 'it's off right now' rather than 'it's broken'. Two seconds later the portal audibly and visually snaps back on (the same effect a portal plays when it first finds a partner), and hovering now reads `$piece_portal_tag:"Swamp"`. It reads like a scheduled train, not a glitch.
failureModes: A player who opens the tag dialog during announce sees the server's long tag pre-filled into a field whose characterLimit is 10 (TextInput.Show :61515-61522) and can save back a truncated string — keep announce tags ≤10 chars or accept the corruption
Tag writes are silently lost at the next world save unless ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called explicitly (:76702)
Under Pairing Authority Takeover this is safe; WITHOUT it, changing the tag instantly breaks the vanilla pair (tag equality at :100601) and pass 2 re-pairs the portal randomly
No colour or size markup is possible — RemoveRichTextTags (:143459) strips it from the hover string, and Chat.OnNewChatMessage replaces '<' and '>' with spaces on the other text channels
The blackout window is a real outage: a player who arrives mid-blackout and does not hover has no idea why walking in does nothing
openQuestions: Does GuiInputField clamp a programmatically assigned .text to characterLimit? TextInput.Show sets characterLimit = 10 then assigns m_inputField.text (:61519-61520). If it clamps, any server-written tag longer than 10 chars is destroyed the moment a player opens and confirms the dialog.
Does a client already standing at the portal pick up the tag change in hover text without a zone reload? GetTagInfo reads the ZDO directly every frame, so it should — confirm live.
corrections: On platforms where RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() is true (console/PlayFab), FilterUGC (client :94901-94920) runs on the tag; a server-written tag has an empty s_tagauthor (PlatformUserID.None), so display may be filtered/censored on those clients. PC/Steam is unaffected.

DirtyPortalObjects is one global flag for the whole portal chunk, so in practice any SetConnection anywhere between the tag write and the save also rescues the tag; calling SetDirtyPortals() is still correct and free.

Minor: 'within 0.5 s the glow dies' — the m_target_found glow is only ever lit when a teleportable player is within 5 m (:143508); for everyone else the only cue is the 1 s emission fade and the hover text.

m_target_found (the proximity glow) is only active when a teleportable player is within 5 m AND TargetFound (:143502-143508); the portal-wide cue during blackout is the emission colour lerp, not that glow.

Console/Xbox clients pass every tag through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC with PlatformUserID.None when s_tagauthor is empty (GetTagInfo :143557-143569; client FilterUGC :94901-94945, PlatformRequiresTextFiltering :88608). Server-authored tags may be word-censored or replaced by the blocked-UGC string on those platforms; Steam/PC returns the text unchanged.

The announce tag invites interaction: any player pressing E opens TextInput; submitting runs RPC_SetTag on the OWNER's client which writes UpdateConnection(None) and a new tag with no server veto (:143587-143602). The mod must re-assert tag + connection on a heartbeat and must expect its 'Swamp 30s' string to be overwritten.
DirtyPortalObjects is a single global flag; any managed SetConnection anywhere in the same save interval already covers the tag write. Calling SetDirtyPortals is still the correct explicit guard.

Restart/relog: the tag survives a save only if DirtyPortalObjects was set before the save; the announce/blackout phases themselves are transient and must be re-derived from the mod's schedule after LoadChunks, not from ZDO state.

Enforcement label 'client-honoured' is right for the signposting; the inert-during-blackout property is server-enforced as a route fact.

catalog.name: One-Way Ring Rotation
catalog.oneLine: Exploit vanilla's missing reciprocity check to build a stable A→B→C→A ring, then rotate the whole network by rewriting a single edge.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1's teardown predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(s_tag) != tag || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604). It never checks that the partner points BACK. So a ring, a chain, a fan-in hub and even a self-loop all survive vanilla's own reconciler indefinitely, provided every member shares one byte-identical tag string and no member's connection is None.

That makes a one-way ring the cheapest possible rotating network: N portals all tagged `"ring"`, with A→B, B→C, C→A. To "rotate", you do not rewrite N connections — you rewrite one edge and the topology shifts. To advance every member by one step you do rewrite N, but each write is the same three-line triad and the whole batch commits within one tick.

The killer caveat is persistence. The on-disk format collapses each ZDO to a single `ZDOConnectionHashData{type, int hash}` slot: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives the source `{Portal, h}` and the target `{Portal|Target, h}`. One slot per ZDO means the disk format can only express a pairwise perfect matching. Processing C overwrites A's source slot with a Target slot, so after a save/reload only one pair relinks and the rest are unconnected. Worse, `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (the load-time hash relinker, :77850-77893) writes RECIPROCAL connections on both ends — so a surviving one-way link comes back two-way. A self-loop A→A is erased outright (:75472-75475 writes then immediately overwrites the same key).

Mitigation is mandatory and simple: the mod re-asserts the entire ring from its own config in `OnWorldReady`, before any peer connects. At that moment `m_peers` is empty, `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner)` is always null, every write takes the immediate local path, and the server owns both ends of everything (ZDO.Load resets OwnerRevision/DataRevision to 0 and Owned to false, :74550-74556). That pre-peer window is the cheapest time in the whole server lifecycle to write a topology.

Also re-assert on a slow heartbeat (30-60s) because `ZDO.SetConnection` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on identical type+target, :74954-74957), so idempotent re-assertion costs zero DataRevision bumps and zero network traffic.
catalog.playerExperience: A player learns that the Meadows gate always leads to the Black Forest gate, which always leads to the Swamp gate, which leads back to Meadows — a genuine one-way circuit rather than a pair. Hover text on every gate reads `$piece_portal_connected` and they all share the tag "ring", so nothing looks unusual. After a rotation the same physical door now opens onto the next stop in the circuit, with the swap either invisible (~0.1s) or signposted via the Blackout Swap Protocol. Crucially, walking back through the arrival portal does NOT return them to where they came from — it advances them another step around the ring, which is the whole point and must be taught.
failureModes: Rings do not survive a save/load: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) has one hash slot per ZDO and can only express a pairwise matching — the mod MUST re-assert at OnWorldReady or the ring silently degrades to one pair plus orphans
One-way links come back BIDIRECTIONAL after a restart because ZDOMan.ConnectPortals writes both ends (:77879-77885)
Self-loops (A→A) are erased at save time — do not use one as a 'parked' state
If any single member's connection goes None, pass 1 tears down its neighbours' links too (the q.GetConnectionZDOID == None clause, :100601), cascading
Players find one-way navigation disorienting; without tag signposting they will report portals as 'randomly moving'
openQuestions: Confirm empirically that a 3-portal ring survives 60s of live vanilla ConnectPortals with pairing takeover DISABLED (the tag-cloaking cohabitation mode) — the decompile says it should, but it is the single most exploitable claim in this design and deserves a live test.
corrections: 'Re-assert in OnWorldReady' does not work with the Wonderland hook: OnWorldReady is a ZNetScene.Awake postfix (Plugin.cs:151-159) and ZNetScene.Awake (:81941) runs before ZNet.Start (:79254) loads the world via ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:76422). At that moment GetPortalList is empty. Hook a postfix on ZDOMan.LoadChunks / ZNet.LoadWorld (:80732) instead; the pre-peer window (m_peers empty, GetPeer(owner)==null, local write path) still holds there.

The load-time vanilla pass matters: LoadChunks calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (:76523) after the hash relink, so the collapsed ring's leftover unconnected 'ring' portals get randomly paired with each other before the mod re-asserts. Re-assertion must overwrite whatever that pass produced (direct SetConnection to the intended target, never via None).

The Pairing Authority Takeover prereq is only needed for the rotation writes and per-portal tags; the static ring itself is stable under the unmodified reconciler. Conversely, any player retag of a ring member (RPC_SetTag on the owning client, :143587-143602, clears its own connection via UpdateConnection and the target's via SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected — zero server hook) breaks the ring and vanilla then random-pairs the two None members within 5 s; the mod needs a reactive re-assert loop keyed on tag/connection drift, not only a 30-60 s heartbeat.
Citation fix: ZDOMan.LoadChunks spans :76422-76531, not :76474-76531.

'Re-assert in OnWorldReady before any peer connects' targets the wrong moment: OnWorldReady (ZNetScene.Awake postfix) runs before ZNet.Start -> ServerLoadWorld -> ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:79254-79277, :80768). Hook a postfix on ZDOMan.LoadChunks (or ZNet.LoadWorld); that is still pre-peer because peers are only accepted from ZNet.Update onward.

Before the mod re-asserts, LoadChunks itself calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (:76523). The orphaned ring member (connection None, tag 'ring') is eligible for random pairing with any same-tag unmanaged portal in that call. The Harmony prefix must therefore already be installed at plugin load, contradicting the parent option's 'not until OnWorldReady'.

Heartbeat is not zero-cost as written: SetConnection is idempotent but SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) is not — ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) hands ownership to a nearby peer within 2 s, so every 30-60 s triad steals it back, bumping OwnerRevision (:74627-74633) and forcing a resend. Compare GetConnectionZDOID first and only run the triad on mismatch.

Client retag is the real runtime threat, not vanilla's reconciler: RPC_SetTag on the owning client writes None + new tag (:143587-143602). With takeover active the cascade stops, but the retagged member stays dead (and its tag changed) until the heartbeat, and the mod must restore the tag string too.

Walking back through the arrival portal does advance a step, but not instantly: arrival lands 1 m in front of the next portal (:143542-143545) and Player.TeleportTo refuses for 2 s after a teleport (client :15304-15329), with an >= 8 s loading hold per distant hop (client :15353).
evidence: Wonderland OnWorldReady hook — SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:151-159
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Runtime stability verified: pass 1 (:100600-100604) never tests reciprocity, so A->B->C->A with one shared tag and no None member survives both passes indefinitely (pass 2 only touches portals whose connection IsNone, :100609). Disk collapse verified by walking RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478): for A->B, B->C, C->A the per-ZDO slot ends A={Portal|Target,h3}, B={Portal,h2}, C={Portal,h3}; load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) matches sources (type==Portal exactly, GetAllConnectionZDOIDs :75414-75425) against targets by hash and writes BOTH directions (:77878-77879), so only C<->A relinks (now bidirectional) and B comes back unconnected; a self-loop's source slot is overwritten by its own Target slot and is erased. Idempotent SetConnection (:74954-74957) and ZDO.Load resetting Owned/revisions (:74550-74556) confirmed. Persistence mitigation is sound in principle but the stated hook point is wrong.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Runtime stability under vanilla's reconciler confirmed: pass 1 tests only null/tag/None on the partner (:100600-100604), never that the partner points back; pass 2 skips anything with a non-None connection (:100609). Persistence collapse confirmed exactly as described: RegenerateConnectionHashData writes one ZDOConnectionHashData slot per ZDO, source {Portal,h} then target {Portal|Target,h}, later entries overwrite earlier ones (:75461-75478); PrepareSave snapshots it (:75480-75491); ZDO.Load restores only that single slot (:74592-74597); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals matches Portal slots to Portal|Target slots by hash and writes BOTH directions (:77850-77893). For A->B->C->A the surviving state after reload is one reciprocal pair plus one orphan; A->A is erased because the second write overwrites the same key. SetConnection idempotence confirmed (:74954-74957). ZDO.Load resets revisions/ownership (:74552-74556). The mitigation is sound in principle but its stated hook and the 'zero-cost heartbeat' claim are wrong.

catalog.name: Scheduled Routing (In-Game and Real-World Clocks)
catalog.oneLine: Destinations chosen by in-game day fraction, in-game day counter, or wall-clock time — including portals that only resolve during a window.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three independent clocks, all readable on a dedicated server.

(1) IN-GAME TIME OF DAY. `EnvMan.instance.GetDayFraction()` returns `m_smoothDayFraction` (:96290-96293), and the statics `EnvMan.IsDay()`, `IsNight()`, `IsAfternoon()` (:96363-96376) are recomputed in `EnvMan.FixedUpdate` (:95736-95743) from `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds()` (:95697) on EVERY machine including headless — only `UpdateTriggers` early-returns on a null local player (:95753). Proof that EnvMan.instance is live on a dedicated server: `Game.UpdateSleeping` sits behind `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return;` and then dereferences `EnvMan.instance.IsTimeSkipping()`, `EnvMan.IsAfternoon()`, `EnvMan.IsNight()` and `EnvMan.instance.SkipToMorning()` unguarded (:100714-100731). Night is `dayFraction <= 0.25 || >= 0.75` (:96457-96465).

(2) IN-GAME DAY COUNTER. `EnvMan.instance.GetDay()` = `(int)(ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() / m_dayLengthSec)` with `m_dayLengthSec = 1200` (:96295-96303, :95406). Lets a portal open on every 5th day, or change destination as the world ages.

(3) REAL-WORLD CLOCK. Plain `DateTime.UtcNow` in the mod. Independent of world time and immune to sleep-skipping.

Implementation: one subsystem evaluates a per-portal schedule expression at 1Hz (cheaper than the 0.2s hub tick — clock granularity does not need 5 ticks/sec). It computes the target destination index, compares to the last-written index, and only writes on change (`ZDO.SetConnection` is a no-op if unchanged, :74954-74957, so a blind re-write every tick is also safe but produces no traffic). Window portals write `ZDOID.None` outside the window — the portal then reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461), the glow dies within 0.5s, and a walk-through silently does nothing (:143519-143522), which is a legible 'closed' affordance for free.

THE SLEEP-SKIP GOTCHA: in-game time is not monotonic at a steady rate. `Game.UpdateSleeping` calls `EnvMan.SkipToMorning()` when every connected character has `ZDOVars.s_inBed` set (:100727-100729, `EverybodyIsTryingToSleep` :100735-100750), which ramps `ZNet.SetNetTime` forward over ~12 seconds (`UpdateTimeSkip`, :96310-96323; `m_timeSkipSpeed = delta / 12.0`, :96339). A schedule keyed on day fraction can jump an entire evening in 12 real seconds. Guard every transition with 'did the index change' rather than 'did we cross a boundary this tick', or an edge-triggered schedule silently skips.
catalog.playerExperience: The player learns a routine. The stone circle gate reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` and its runes are dark through the whole day; at dusk the glow comes up with the vanilla connect sound and the hover line flips to connected, and it now leads to the Swamp outpost. A hover-time tag reading "Dusk only" (written once, permanently) teaches this without any documentation. On a server running a real-world raid night, the raid gate is dead all week and lights up at 20:00 local. If someone sleeps through the night, the gate can flick closed and open again inside 12 real seconds — visible as the glow dying and coming straight back.
failureModes: Sleep-skip warps in-game time forward ~12 real seconds across a whole night (EnvMan.UpdateTimeSkip :96310-96323) — edge-triggered schedules skip their transition entirely; use level-triggered 'compute target, compare, write'
EnvMan.instance null on some headless configuration would NRE the scheduler; guard it even though vanilla's own server code does not
GetDayFraction is m_smoothDayFraction, which is LerpAngle-smoothed at 0.01 per FixedUpdate (:95704-95705) — it lags true fraction slightly and is not exactly 0 at midnight; do not test for equality
A window that closes while a player is mid-transit is harmless (the destination was snapshotted at TeleportTo, Player.UpdateTeleport :15343) but their return leg is now dead
Real-world schedules and in-game schedules on the same portal will contradict each other; pick one authority per portal
openQuestions: Confirm EnvMan.instance is non-null and GetDayFraction advances on a 1.0.7 headless dedicated server by logging it every 10s alongside ZNet.GetTimeSeconds(). Vanilla's Game.UpdateSleeping implies yes but this is the one assumption the whole scheduling family rests on.
Does EnvMan.FixedUpdate actually run on the server, or is the EnvMan GameObject disabled headless? Log s_isNight transitions over one full 1200s day.
corrections: GetDayFraction is not the raw fraction: it is RescaleDayFraction'd (:95650-95666, night compressed to raw 0.15-0.85 mapped onto 0.25-0.75) and then LerpAngle-smoothed at 0.01 per FixedUpdate (:95700-95702, ~2 s time constant), so it lags real net-time by a couple of seconds and lags further during a 12 s sleep skip. Schedules that need exact boundaries should derive the fraction directly from ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() % m_dayLengthSec (and apply RescaleDayFraction if 'night' semantics must match vanilla), and use GetDay() for day counts, which is exact.
m_dayLengthSec is a `long`, not an int (:95406) — cosmetic.

GetDayFraction() is not raw time: FixedUpdate first applies RescaleDayFraction (non-linear remap, :95650-95665) and then a LerpAngle smoothing at 0.01 per FixedUpdate (:95700-95705), so m_smoothDayFraction lags real time by seconds and moves non-uniformly; m_debugTimeOfDay can override it. For exact window boundaries compute `ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds() % m_dayLengthSec / m_dayLengthSec` directly (and apply RescaleDayFraction yourself if you want vanilla's dusk/dawn feel).
m_dayLengthSec is a public instance field (:95406) — other server mods can change it; read EnvMan.instance.m_dayLengthSec, do not hard-code 1200.

Window portals written to None are 'unconnected' portals with a tag; the mod's own unmanaged reconciler (from Pairing Authority Takeover) must exclude them or it will randomly pair them with any same-tag portal within 5 s. Also a player can retag/'repair' them via RPC_SetTag on the owner client; re-assert each evaluation tick, not only on index change.
Schedule state keyed on ZDOID must be rebuilt after ZDOMan.LoadChunks (ZDOID renumbering :74552); OnWorldReady (ZNetScene.Awake) is before world load.

Sleep-skip note is correct but incomplete: during the 12 s ramp the s_isNight/s_isAfternoon statics can flip several times; evaluate on the computed destination index (as the option says) and additionally suppress writes while EnvMan.instance.IsTimeSkipping() (:96325-96328) if flicker of the glow/VFX is undesirable.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] All three clocks verified as headless-safe. EnvMan.FixedUpdate (:95685-95744) has no local-player gate; it reads ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds (:95697), computes the rescaled smoothed day fraction, and recomputes the s_isDay/s_isAfternoon/s_isNight statics (:95737-95743); GetBiome() returns EmptyMeadows when there is no main camera (:96032-96037); only UpdateTriggers early-returns on null Player.m_localPlayer (:95753). Game.UpdateSleeping (:100712-100733) is IsServer-gated and dereferences EnvMan.instance.IsTimeSkipping()/IsAfternoon()/IsNight()/SkipToMorning() unguarded, proving EnvMan.instance is live on a dedicated server. GetDayFraction returns m_smoothDayFraction (:96290-96293); GetDay = (int)(time / m_dayLengthSec) with m_dayLengthSec = 1200L (:96295-96303, :95406); CalculateNight is `<= 0.25 || >= 0.75` (:96457-96465). Sleep skip: SkipToMorning sets m_timeSkipSpeed = delta/12 (:96329-96341) and UpdateTimeSkip advances SetNetTime each FixedUpdate on the server (:96310-96323). Window portals writing ZDOID.None produce the unconnected hover/glow/silent walk-through exactly as verified for Blackout. Route open/closed is a server-owned field: server-enforced.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] All three clocks verified on the dedicated server. EnvMan.FixedUpdate recomputes m_smoothDayFraction from ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds() and the s_isDay/s_isNight/s_isAfternoon statics every tick with no local-player gate (:95685-95744); only UpdateTriggers early-returns on null m_localPlayer (:95753). GetDayFraction/GetDay/statics at :96290-96303, :96363-96376; CalculateNight = fraction <= 0.25 || >= 0.75 (:96457-96465); m_dayLengthSec = 1200 (:95406). Server-liveness proof holds: Game.UpdateSleeping is IsServer-gated and dereferences EnvMan.instance unguarded (:100712-100733); EverybodyIsTryingToSleep reads s_inBed over GetAllCharacterZDOS (:100735-100750); SkipToMorning sets m_timeSkipSpeed = delta/12 and UpdateTimeSkip (IsServer-gated inside FixedUpdate) ramps SetNetTime (:96310-96341). ZNet.GetTimeSeconds returns m_netTime (:81546-81549). Window-closed behaviour (None -> unconnected hover, silent gate-1 return) verified (:143461, :143519-143522). The route-open question is server-owned, so server-enforced is honest. Two precision details are wrong.

catalog.name: Progression-Gated Sealed Gate
catalog.oneLine: A portal that resolves to nothing until the world has a given global key (boss defeated, quest flag), then permanently or conditionally opens.
catalog.howItWorks:
The gate condition is a world global key. Reading is a plain dictionary lookup: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_bonemass)` (:115948) or the string overload `GetGlobalKey("my_mod_flag")` (:115968) against `m_globalKeysEnums` / `m_globalKeysValues` (:113305-113309). Custom string keys are free — anything that does not parse as a `GlobalKeys` member is classified `NonServerOption` by `GetKeyValue` (:113560-113581) and persists in the world .db rather than the .fwl.

The subsystem evaluates each sealed gate at 1Hz: if the key is absent, hold `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`; if present, write the real destination. Because `ZDO.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74954-74957) the steady state costs literally zero — no DataRevision bump, no packet. That makes 'blindly re-assert every tick' the correct implementation, and it also means the gate self-heals against anyone who tampers with the connection: `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is an unauthenticated global routed RPC any client can invoke to rewire any portal, and a 1Hz re-assert reverts it within a second.

For an event-driven (rather than polled) version, postfix the private `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(string)` (:113483-113513), which is the single funnel for every key write. CRITICAL TRAP, already paid for by Wonderland's BossDefeatWatch: `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` re-adds EVERY persisted server-option key on every boot (:115904-115931), so a naive postfix re-fires the 'boss just died' handler for historical kills at every restart. Snapshot the existing key set in OnWorldReady and diff against it.

Hardening: `RPC_SetGlobalKey` and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` perform ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037) — any connected vanilla client can set or clear any key on the server. If a gate is meant to be earned, Harmony-prefix both RPCs to drop packets whose true sender (resolved by matching `p.m_rpc == rpc` over `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()`) is not an admin.
catalog.playerExperience: A player finds a large stone portal in a ruin. Its runes are dark; hovering reads `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"Sealed" [$piece_portal_unconnected]`. Walking into it does nothing at all — no message, no fade. Weeks later the server kills Bonemass; within one second the gate's runes light up with the vanilla portal-connect sound and hover now reads `$piece_portal_tag:"The Deep Road" [$piece_portal_connected]`. Everyone online near it sees it happen simultaneously. Walking in now takes them to the Mistlands outpost.
failureModes: Any client can set or clear the gating key: RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender check (:116022-116029). Without a prefix hardening it, a gate is one packet away from being opened

Server-option keys (ordinals 0-40) are mirrored into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys and baked into the .fwl permanently (GlobalKeyAdd :113511) — use a custom NonServerOption string key for mod gates so uninstalling the mod leaves nothing behind
A GlobalKeyAdd postfix re-fires for every historical key at every boot via SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115904-115931)
The 'sealed' state is indistinguishable from 'broken' to a player who does not hover — always carry an explanatory tag string

GlobalKeyAdd unconditionally dereferences Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() (:113506) and its UpdateWorldRates tail dereferences Minimap.instance (:101203); calling it too early in startup NREs before SendGlobalKeys
openQuestions: Is Minimap.instance genuinely non-null on a 1.0.7 headless server (Game.UpdateNoMap dereferences it on every key write, :101203)? Wonderland's WorldRatesEngine calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server, which is strong indirect evidence — but confirm with `setkey` on the server console and watch for an NRE.
corrections: Boot-replay attribution is wrong: SetStartingGlobalKeys :115904-115931 loops i<41 (= GlobalKeys.NonServerOption, enum :101270-101312) and only re-adds server-option keys from ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys. defeated_* keys are NonServerOption and are replayed by ZoneSystem.Load :113800-113806 (GlobalKeyAdd per saved key). The snapshot-and-diff advice still stands, but the postfix must ignore calls made during Load AND SetStartingGlobalKeys.

Citation fix: the idempotent early-return is ZDOExtraData.SetConnection :74951-74961; ZDO.SetConnection is :73656-73665 (it also calls ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals). ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) is :77706, not :77714 (that is the (long, ZDOID) overload).

'Hold None' is only safe from vanilla re-pairing if the sealed tag is unique or Pairing Authority Takeover is active: Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 :100607-100622 pairs any unconnected same-tag portal every 5 s. When opened, the gate->destination link survives pass 1 :100598-100605 only if the destination carries the same tag AND its own connection is non-None.

Do not route writes through Game.SetConnection :100640-100651 - it is private, calls portal.SetOwner (IncreaseOwnerRevision :74627-74634, a packet per tick if the owner differs) and, if the portal is owned by an online peer, delegates to that client via RPC_SetConnection. Write ZDO.SetConnection directly; the server's write propagates regardless of ownership (ShouldSend checks revisions only).

Tag rename 'Sealed' -> 'The Deep Road' is a ZDO.Set(s_tag) which does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects; the ChunkPortal is only rewritten when dirty (ZDOMan save path :77621-77634). Call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() :76702 after tag-only writes or the rename is lost at the next save.

Hardening claim is imprecise: RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string) receives m_senderPeerID deserialized from the packet (RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83488-83491) - a client-asserted long. A prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey cannot see the ZRpc. True-sender resolution (p.m_rpc == rpc, ZNetPeer.m_rpc :78780) requires prefixing ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) :83603-83614 and filtering by method hash. Vanilla clients send an honest sender, so the simple prefix works against vanilla only.

Server-side write of a custom key: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string) :115943-115946 routes 'SetGlobalKey' to the server peer ID, which on the server is handled locally (RPC_RoutedRPC :83607 targetPeerID == m_id). Wonderland's WorldRatesEngine.cs:55 instead calls the publicized GlobalKeyAdd directly; either works.

Hardening: do NOT drop non-admin SetGlobalKey packets globally. Character.OnDeath (:3153-3156), BaseAI.SetAlerted (:27256-27262), OfferingBowl (:135738), item use (:145637) all send SetGlobalKey from ordinary vanilla clients. Scope any veto to the mod's own custom key names.

Boot replay: defeated_* and custom keys are replayed by ZoneSystem.Load (:113855-113858); SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115904-115931) replays only server-option keys (enum < NonServerOption, loop removes indices 0..40). Snapshot-and-diff still correct.

Sender identity in a routed RPC handler is the packet's self-declared m_senderPeerID (RPC_RoutedRPC :83632-83643 does no socket cross-check). Resolve admin status via ZNet.instance.GetPeer(sender) + IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) (:81811-81814). 'p.m_rpc == rpc' only works in raw ZRpc handlers.

After writing s_tag on the gate, call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705); ZDO.Set alone marks only the sector chunk dirty and portal ZDOs are not in sectors (:77748-77751, :77621-77632).

Destination D must be a resident ZDO; if vanilla ConnectPortals is not fully suppressed, D.tag must equal the gate tag and D's own connection must be non-None or pass 1 clears the link (:100598-100605).

Self-heal caveat: Game.SetConnection routes through the owning ONLINE client unless forced (:100637-100651); the mod must use SetOwner(session)+ZDO.SetConnection+ForceSendZDO itself. A player already standing inside the trigger volume when the gate opens is not teleported (OnTriggerEnter only, :143671-143681).
evidence: ZDOMan portal save only when DirtyPortalObjects — :77621-77632
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. Global-key read is a plain dictionary lookup on the server (ZoneSystem.GetGlobalKey overloads :115948-115977, backed by m_globalKeysEnums/m_globalKeysValues :113307-113309); custom keys parse to GlobalKeys.NonServerOption via GetKeyValue :113560-113581 and ARE persisted in the .db (ZoneSystem.Save :113751-113759 strips only gk < NonServerOption; Load :113800-113806 replays the rest). The route side is server-owned: ZDO.SetConnection :73656-73665 calls ZDOExtraData.SetConnection :74951-74961 which returns false on an unchanged value, so no DataRevision bump and (via ZDOPeer.ShouldSend :76003-76013) no packet in steady state. Game.RPC_SetConnection :100653-100662 is registered unconditionally in Game.Start :100067 with no sender check, so the tamper vector is real and a 1 Hz re-assert does revert it. Client behaviour matches the described experience: TeleportWorld.Teleport :143517-143519 returns silently when TargetFound() is false; GetHoverText :143455-143465 prints $piece_portal_unconnected; UpdatePortal :143497-143511 plays m_connected when HaveTarget flips true (0.5 s InvokeRepeating :143451). Several factual errors need fixing (below), and one subtle self-heal gap: because the mod's re-assert early-returns on the SERVER's own value, a same-DataRevision divergence (owning client writes the portal in the same 50 ms window - RPC_ZDOData :77076-77128 drops the lower-or-equal revision on BOTH sides) is never repaired; the mod must periodically force a revision bump, not rely purely on idempotent writes.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. Route-form rule (connection field owned by server) so the server-enforced label is honest. Verified: GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) is a HashSet lookup on m_globalKeysEnums (:115948-115951); string overload hits m_globalKeysValues (:115974-115977); GetKeyValue classifies unparseable names as NonServerOption (:113560-113581); ZoneSystem.Save writes only gk >= NonServerOption keys into the .db (:113751-113760) while server-option keys live in World.m_startingGlobalKeys (.fwl). ZDOExtraData.SetConnection early-returns on unchanged value (:74951-74961) so ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73665) does not bump DataRevision at steady state. Game.RPC_SetConnection is registered unconditionally in Game.Start (:100067) and has no sender check (:100653-100662). RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey have no sender check (:116022-116036) and are registered only on the server (:113445-113448). Vanilla client UX matches: Teleport() returns silently when !TargetFound (:143517-143520); hover text uses $piece_portal_unconnected from HaveTarget (:143455-143463); the connect effect fires in UpdatePortal on the !m_hadTarget->HaveTarget transition (:143490-143500), and HaveTarget needs only a non-None connection, not a held ZDO (:143632-143639). Four factual defects: (1) the proposed admin-only prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey would break vanilla progression, because boss-defeat keys are sent by the boss-owning CLIENT (Character.OnDeath :3153-3156 -> ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey :115943-115946 -> routed RPC), as are activeBosses (:27259, :3164), OfferingBowl keys (:135738) and item-use keys (:145637); (2) the boot-replay attribution is wrong: defeated_*/custom keys replay through ZoneSystem.Load (:113855-113858), and SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115904-115931) replays only server-option keys (< NonServerOption); (3) the sender-resolution recipe 'p.m_rpc == rpc' does not apply to routed RPCs, which receive a long sender copied from the packet's self-declared m_senderPeerID (:83632-83643); (4) a mod tag write via ZDO.Set(s_tag) only dirties the sector chunk (IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector :73832-73838), but portals are removed from sectors (AddIfPortal :77748-77751) and saved only when DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632), so 'Sealed'/'The Deep Road' tags are lost at save unless SetDirtyPortals() is called.

catalog.name: Event-Driven Retarget
catalog.oneLine: Destinations that change in response to live world events — a raid starting, a boss being alerted, a global key write — rather than a clock.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three server-readable event sources, in descending order of reliability.

(1) GLOBAL KEY WRITES. Postfix `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(string)` (:113483) — the single funnel for every key mutation, including the server's own and any client's forged one. Diff against an OnWorldReady snapshot to suppress boot replay. This covers boss defeats (`defeated_*`), world modifiers, and any custom mod key. Latency: synchronous, zero.

(2) RANDOM EVENTS / RAIDS. `RandEventSystem` genuinely runs server-side: its update path is gated on `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (:106793-106798) and `UpdateRandomEvent(dt)` (:106838) selects events. The mod can read the private `m_randomEvent` (:106749) by reflection or publicizer for name/position/time, and `SetRandomEventByName(string name, Vector3 pos)` (:107067) is PUBLIC — so the mod can even force an event and retarget portals in the same tick. `SendCurrentRandomEvent` broadcasts `"SetEvent"` to all peers (:106952-106961), so client and server agree.

(3) BOSS ACTIVITY. `GlobalKeys.activeBosses` is a float key incremented by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` on whichever CLIENT owns the boss (:27258-27259) and decremented on death (:3163-3164). The server can read it with `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out float v)` (:115958). Use it to blackout a network during a boss fight, or to open a 'boss arena' gate.

Implementation: a 1Hz evaluator computes each managed portal's target from a small rule table `(condition → destination)` and writes on change. Rules are level-triggered, not edge-triggered, so a missed tick is self-correcting.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK SERVER-SIDE: `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106950) reads `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss()`, and EnemyHud's `m_huds` dictionary is filled in `LateUpdate` relative to `Player.m_localPlayer.transform.position` — permanently empty headless, so the server's own GetBossEvent always returns null. That matters because it is one half of the client-side `NoBossPortals` condition in `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143528): the client evaluates it locally and the server cannot predict the result. `activeBosses` is the only half the server can observe.

Also note `activeBosses` can leak above zero if the boss-owning client crashes mid-fight, permanently blocking every portal on the server if NoBossPortals is set; a server mod should watch for and zero it with `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f)` (:115933).
catalog.playerExperience: A raid siren goes up over the player's base. They run to their portal hall and find that every gate has gone dark except one, whose tag now reads "Muster" and which leads to the fortified keep — the server retargeted the whole network the instant the event fired. When the raid ends, the gates relight one by one on their normal destinations. Separately: the moment someone on the server drops Moder, a previously sealed mountain gate lights up for everyone simultaneously, with the vanilla connect sound playing at every instance of it.
failureModes: RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() always returns null server-side (EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss, :106941-106944) — the server cannot predict the client-side NoBossPortals gate
GlobalKeys.activeBosses is maintained by the boss-owning CLIENT (BaseAI.SetAlerted :27258) and leaks above zero if that client crashes mid-fight
Any client can forge a global key write (RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender validation, :116022), so an event-driven retarget is trivially triggerable by a hostile client unless the RPC is hardened
m_randomEvent is private — a publicizer or reflection dependency that can break across patches
A GlobalKeyAdd postfix fires during SetStartingGlobalKeys at boot for every historical key (:115904-115931)

Retargeting many portals at once floods every peer: ZDOMan.SendZDOs has no delta encoding (:77056-77064) and the send queue caps at 10240 bytes (:77011). Budget writes per sweep (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep uses 256)
openQuestions: Does a dedicated server ever instantiate a boss Character, and can it therefore ever move the activeBosses counter itself? Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465) which implies never — confirm by aggroing a boss with one client and watching `listkeys` on the server console.
Is EnemyHud.instance non-null but empty, or null outright, on a dedicated server? Determines whether GetBossEvent returns null or NREs.
corrections: No reflection needed: RandEventSystem.GetCurrentRandomEvent() :107373-107376 is PUBLIC and returns m_randomEvent (name via m_name, m_pos, m_time on RandomEvent). GetActiveEvent() :107378 is also public but is null on a server (SetActiveEvent depends on Player.m_localPlayer at :106806-106817).

activeBosses is NOT incremented 'on whichever CLIENT owns the boss': BaseAI.SetAlerted :27256-27260 has no IsOwner gate around the SetGlobalKey call (only the s_alert ZDO write at :27248 is owner-gated); the per-ZDO s_bossCount latch is set locally on every client that has the boss instantiated, so two clients can race and double-increment before the latch syncs. The leak-above-zero warning is therefore even more likely than stated; a server-side watchdog that zeroes it when no boss character ZDO exists is warranted.

SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f) :115933 formats 'activebosses 0' and RPC_SetGlobalKey :116024 only checks m_globalKeys.Contains(fullLine), so the reset goes through even though the key already exists with a different value (GlobalKeyAdd replaces the value :113489-113499).

catalog.name: Deterministic Assignment Replacement
catalog.oneLine: Replace vanilla's uniformly-random same-tag pairing with nearest / oldest / round-robin / least-recently-used selection, via a one-method Harmony postfix.
catalog.howItWorks:
The lowest-risk, highest-value intervention in the whole space. `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO> portals, ZDO skip, string tag)` (:100664-100679) is private, builds a candidate list filtered on reference inequality with `skip`, exact `s_tag` string equality, `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == None`, and `!IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal`, then returns `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` from the shared unseeded global RNG.

A Harmony POSTFIX on `AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")` that overwrites `__result` replaces the selection policy while leaving every other vanilla behaviour — the two-phase commit through `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`, the ownership handling in `SetConnection`, the logging — completely intact. The postfix receives the same candidate universe via `__args` and can rebuild the filtered list itself (the filter is four cheap predicates) then pick by policy:

• NEAREST: minimise `Vector3.Distance(skip.GetPosition(), c.GetPosition())`. Makes a large same-tag group behave like a sensible local network instead of a lottery.
• OLDEST / STABLE: sort candidates by `m_uid.UserID` then `m_uid.ID` and take the first. Deterministic across ticks; note it is NOT stable across restarts because ZDOIDs are renumbered (`ZDO.Load` :74552) — sort by rounded position for true restart stability.
• ROUND-ROBIN: a mod-side per-tag cursor advanced on each successful pair.
• LEAST-RECENTLY-USED: a mod-side per-portal 'last transit' timestamp fed by the position-straddle transit detector; pick the candidate with the oldest timestamp to spread traffic.
• LOAD-BALANCED: count how many portals currently point at each candidate and pick the minimum.

This also fixes vanilla's permanent-orphan behaviour. With N≥3 same-tag portals, the first iterated portal picks randomly from the rest, the second finds every remaining candidate excluded, and exactly one member is stranded forever (subsequent ticks re-confirm the surviving pair). Iteration order is `Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` bucket order — arbitrary and not stable across restarts — so which portal is orphaned changes on reboot. A deterministic replacement picker makes that predictable, and a mod-side detector can flag the orphan in a Heartbeat line or a Discord report.

Tick budget: runs only inside the existing 5s vanilla pass, over a candidate list that is almost always 1-3 entries. Free.
catalog.playerExperience: A player with five portals all tagged "home" stops seeing them shuffle partners at random every time one is rebuilt. The nearest-pairing policy means the two gates in the same building always link to each other, and the distant one links to its own neighbour. With LRU, a busy hub distributes arrivals across several outposts instead of hammering one. The permanently-stranded fifth portal, which vanilla leaves dead forever with no explanation, now either pairs predictably or shows up in a server report as 'orphaned: tag "home" has an odd member'.
failureModes: A private method target — AccessTools.Method by string name; a Valheim rename breaks it silently unless wrapped in SafePatch with a logged warning
Sorting by ZDOID is not stable across restarts (ZDO.Load renumbers, :74552); use rounded position for restart-stable ordering
Must not drop the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal filter (:100671) or portals owned by online peers double-pair within a tick
UnityEngine.Random.Range is the int overload and max-exclusive (:100678) — a replacement that uses the float overload off-by-ones the last candidate
Nearest-pairing over a very large same-tag group is O(n) per call inside an O(n) loop; cap candidate scanning or pre-bucket by tag
openQuestions: Does the postfix's __args expose the List<ZDO> and ZDO skip parameters reliably under HarmonyX 2.9.0 for a private instance method, or is an explicit typed signature required? Trivial to determine at build time.
corrections: 'Bucket order not stable across restarts' is overstated: portals are saved wholesale in m_portalObjects iteration order (ZDOMan save :77621-77630) and re-inserted via AddItemToList on load (:76480), and a .NET Dictionary preserves insertion order absent removals, so the order is usually reproduced across a clean restart; it is 'not guaranteed', not 'arbitrary'.

The pairing that the postfix selects is still committed through Game.SetConnection :100640-100651, which delegates to the owning ONLINE client via RPC_SetConnection when the portal is client-owned - the write round-trips through an untrusted vanilla client and lands one tick later (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-writes on the NEXT pass). Vanilla behaviour, unchanged, but 'server-enforced' here means server-selected; the commit path is shared with vanilla.
Composition warning: if 'Pairing Authority Takeover' (disabling ConnectPortals) ships alongside, this postfix never fires. The two are mutually exclusive designs for the same pass.
A prefix returning false with ref __result avoids the wasted vanilla list build and RNG call; the postfix approach works but recomputes the same filter.
Orphan claim: 'N>=3 leaves exactly one stranded' is wrong for even N; only odd same-tag groups leave one orphan (pass 2 :100607-100622 pairs staged-free candidates greedily, so 4 pair as 2+2).
NEAREST policy must be mutual-nearest or a global per-pass matching; naive nearest-from-skip is iteration-order dependent and can strand the adjacent gate.
IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal and m_currentlyConnectingPortals are private (:100700-100710); the postfix must reach them via AccessTools or re-derive staging from __result==null semantics.

GetPortalList order is Dictionary insertion order, which is reproduced from the ChunkPortal file on load (:76480, :76579, :76598); it is only perturbed by removals, so 'arbitrary across restarts' overstates — but do not rely on it.

Two errors in the analysis: (1) the permanent orphan occurs only for ODD same-tag group sizes — with N=4, A picks B, then C (not staged) finds D unstaged and pairs; (2) NEAREST-from-skip does not guarantee 'the two gates in the same building always link', because the first-iterated portal picks first: with A,B adjacent and C far, if C is iterated first it takes its nearest (A) and B is stranded. Mutual-nearest (return null unless skip is also the candidate's nearest) or a per-pass global matching is needed.
