catalog.name: Approach-Triggered Just-In-Time Routing
catalog.oneLine: Detect a player closing on a portal from their character ZDO position and write THEIR destination into the portal before they reach the trigger collider — the closest a shared portal can get to per-player routing.
catalog.howItWorks:
The transit decision is unhookable, but the APPROACH is fully observable. The owning client's `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zdo.SetPosition(GetPosition())` into the character ZDO every physics tick (:87527-87540), and client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent via `m_clientChangeQueue` drained by `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch (:77241-77258) on the same 0.05s round-robin (:76843-76852). So server-side character positions are fresh to roughly 50-150ms including RTT.

The loop: every 0.1s, for each `(ZNetPeer peer, ZDO characterZdo)` pair from `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` + `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)` (Wonderland's ConnectedCharacters wraps exactly this), compute distance to each managed JIT portal. On crossing an outer radius R_arm (recommend 12m), the mod: (a) looks up that player's selected destination from its own registry keyed on `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (:78539); (b) calls `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destinationId)` (:77714) to guarantee the client HOLDS the destination ZDO, because `TargetFound` requires it (:143646-143654); (c) writes the connection with the standard triad and `ForceSendZDO(portalId)`.

TIMING BUDGET. A sprinting player moves ~5-6 m/s. From 12m the lead time is ~2.0-2.4s. Detection costs up to 0.1s (poll) + ~0.15s (position staleness); the write reaches the client in ~0.05-0.2s. Total ~0.45s worst case, leaving ~1.5s of margin. At R_arm = 20m the margin doubles. The trigger collider itself is small (`m_activationRange = 5f` is only the glow radius, :143411; the collider is a separate child object of unknown size, :143664-143682).

CONTENTION is the fatal flaw and must be designed around explicitly. Two players inside R_arm at once share one ZDOID field. Policies: (1) FIRST-CLAIM LOCK — the first arriver locks the portal for T seconds; a second arriver gets a `PlayerNotify.Toast` ('gate busy') and the destination is not changed under the first. The second player can still physically walk in and be sent to the first player's destination — unavoidable. (2) BLACKOUT-ON-CONTENTION — write None while two claimants are present; both are safely blocked (silently, gate 1 at :143519) rather than mis-routed. (3) Accept it and use per-player terminals instead.

A second failure: a player who reverses direction after arming leaves the portal pointing at their destination for the lock duration. Disarm on leaving R_arm + hysteresis.
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks toward the hub gate. At about 12 metres out — before they can see any change, because the portal's glow does not encode the destination — the server has already pointed the gate at the outpost they selected earlier at the terminal. They walk straight in and arrive where they chose, with no pause, no menu, and no extra step. It genuinely feels like the portal knows who they are. Then a second player runs up behind them: that player gets a HUD toast reading 'Gate is claimed — wait 6s', and if they push through anyway they land at the first player's destination, which is the moment the illusion breaks.
failureModes: CONTENTION: two players inside the arming radius share one connection field. Someone will be mis-routed, or blocked, with no good third option
A player who arms and then turns away leaves the portal mis-set for the lock duration unless disarmed with hysteresis
Position staleness spikes on a laggy client: peer.m_refPos is only refreshed every 2s (ZNet.SendPeriodicData :80337) — you MUST use the character ZDO position, not peer.GetRefPos()
A dead or teleporting player's ZDO position is stale/garbage; skip on zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead) (:78403)
If the destination ZDO has not reached the client, the first walk-through is a silent no-op — the ForceSendZDO pre-warm is mandatory, not optional
A player arriving by portal lands at ~5m/s with no approach phase; the arming radius may never fire before they step back in
openQuestions: What is the TeleportWorldTrigger collider's actual size and shape on the portal prefab (Awake uses GetComponentInParent, :143670)? It sets the true 'point of no return' radius and therefore the real timing margin. Unity asset data — inspect the prefab hierarchy.

Measure real end-to-end latency: server logs the tick it detects a player crossing R_arm and the tick it writes; client logs arrival coordinate. Confirm the ~0.45s worst case on a live server with 10 peers.
corrections: Execution context: ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync and m_clientChangeQueue are CLIENT code paths (owner-gated / !IsServer branch); the option cites them from the server decompile, which is fine for text but should say they run on the owning client.

ForceSendZDO(peerId, destinationId) is necessary, not merely a guarantee: without it the first OnTriggerEnter (one-shot, :143673-143681) hits TargetFound()==false -> RequestZDO -> silent return, and the player is standing inside the trigger with no re-fire until they exit and re-enter. UpdatePortal :143497-143511 also requests it every 0.5 s while the player is within m_activationRange, so the visual glow self-corrects but the transit does not.
Simpler API: ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS() :81024 returns the character ZDOs directly (used by RandEventSystem.IsAnyPlayerInEventArea :107111).

Enforcement nuance: only 'route = X for T s' is server-enforced. 'Player P goes to P's destination' is a heuristic with no server hook; a modified client can also lie about its position (ZSyncTransform position is owner-written, never validated server-side beyond Wonderland-style PositionWatch heuristics).

Save boundary: JIT writes are transient and the write of a one-way link (portal -> destination whose connection points elsewhere) is subject to pass-1 clearing :100598-100605 unless Pairing Authority Takeover is active (already listed as prereq) - keep it so.

m_activationRange = 5f :143411 and m_exitDistance = 1f :143413 confirmed; note the exit position is destination + forward*1 + up (:143540-143543), so a 'destination' ZDO that is not a portal prefab still needs a sane rotation.

TargetFound self-requests a missing destination ZDO (:143651-143654 -> ZDOMan.RequestZDO :77684-77687 -> RPC_RequestZDO :77689-77692) and UpdatePortal polls at 0.5s; the mod's ForceSendZDO reduces latency but a trigger entry before arrival silently fails and the player must leave and re-enter the trigger (OnTriggerEnter only).

Add world-save/load handling: connections are saved as a single ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDO (:75461-75478); on load only reciprocal hash pairs reconnect (:77849-77890). A live JIT link at save time can hijack the destination portal's own link after restart. Re-assert all managed links from the mod registry after ZDOMan load, before the first vanilla pass.

Delivery is subject to SendZDOs' send-queue gate (:77010-77018); force-send is inserted at list head (:77263-77283) but still waits when the peer's queue is >8 KB (e.g. while the client is loading a zone).
Per-player exclusivity is not enforced by anything; only the route is. Keep the label but state that 'THEIR destination' is a heuristic, not a guarantee.

Rare revision-collision: server and owning client discard incoming ZDO data with DataRevision <= local (:77107-77115 server, symmetric on client). If the owner client writes the same revision number concurrently (e.g. WearNTear s_support :149675/150054/150096), the client keeps the stale connection and the server's idempotent SetConnection never re-sends. Bump a mod-private key to force a revision increment when re-asserting.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited primitive exists and runs where claimed. Client-side ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87527-87540 writes zdo.SetPosition when position changes (client execution, owner only); the client's ZDOMan.CreateSyncList non-server branch :77242-77258 drains m_clientChangeQueue to the server irrespective of distance, driven by SendZDOToPeers2 :76837-76862 (0.05 s). Server reads ZNet.GetPeers :81630-81633 / ZNetPeer.m_characterID :78794 / ZDO.GetPosition. ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) :77714-77723 is server-branch specific. TeleportWorld.TargetFound :143640-143656 does require the client to hold the destination ZDO and otherwise calls RequestZDO (server honours it: RPC_RequestZDO :77689-77692 -> peer.ForceSendZDO) and returns false; Teleport :143519 returns silently, and TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter :143673-143681 fires once per collider entry, so the pre-push of the destination ZDO is mandatory, not an optimisation (otherwise the first entry is a silent no-op and the player must step out and back in). The route write itself is server-enforced; the per-player guarantee is NOT enforced by anything - a second player is routed identically, exactly as the option admits. Server->client delivery is gated by the peer socket send queue (SendZDOs :77010-77018), so under zone-load traffic the write can lag. Save boundary not addressed: RegenerateConnectionHashData collapses each ZDO to one hash slot (:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals restores only reciprocal hash pairs (:77849-77890), so a JIT link that was live at save time comes back either as None or as a spurious bidirectional link that overwrites the destination portal's own connection; the mod must re-assert every managed link after world load. Enforcement: the route is server-owned, but per-player exclusivity is not enforceable (any player in the trigger goes where the field points) — the option says so.

catalog.name: Per-Player Private Portal Terminals
catalog.oneLine: Give every player their own physical portal; because only they ever use it, its pre-written destination IS a per-player destination. The honest answer to 'can routing be per-player'.
catalog.howItWorks:
Per-player routing is impossible at the protocol layer (see the ruled-out Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing option). The workaround is physical, not technical: one portal per player.

IDENTITY. A player-built portal already carries its builder: `Piece.SetCreator` writes `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) — the builder's PlayerProfile UID, identical to `ZDOVars.s_playerID` on their character ZDO (:78539, `Player.SetPlayerID` :10129-10136) — plus `s_creatorIndex` (:78395) indexing `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396), which the server persists in the .fwl from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs. So the mod can enumerate `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), read `s_creator`, and know whose terminal each portal is with zero extra bookkeeping. Note `SetCreator` only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417), so world-gen and pre-mod portals read 0.

SELECTION. The player chooses a destination by an observable gesture at their own terminal: an emote (`ZDOVars.s_emote` / `s_emoteID` polled at 0.25s, Wonderland's EmoteSignals), a map ping (`Chat.SendPing` broadcasts "ChatMessage" at targetPeerID 0 with the clicked world position — always reaches the server, :42058-42068), or an item placed on an adjacent ItemStand (`ZDOVars.s_item`, :78465). The mod stores `playerID → destinationId` in a position-keyed or playerID-keyed file — NEVER a ZDOID-keyed one (`ZDO.Load` renumbers, :74552).

WRITING. On selection change, the standard triad against that player's terminal only. No contention: only one player's selection ever touches that ZDO.

OUTBOUND IS FULLY SOLVED. INBOUND IS NOT, and this is the honest limit. A terminal T_p can point one-way at a shared public portal D_i (non-reciprocity is stable under vanilla's pass 1, :100598-100605 — but only if both carry the same tag, which pairing takeover makes free). The RETURN leg from D_i is shared: D_i has exactly one connection field, so it cannot send different players home. Three options: (a) one anchor per (player × destination) — N×M portal ZDOs, e.g. 20 players × 10 destinations = 200 extra ZDOs, which is fine for the server (portals are always resident and saved wholesale into ChunkPortal, :77621) but visually absurd unless the anchors use a non-portal prefab; (b) JIT approach-routing on the return portal, inheriting its contention; (c) a server-issued forced teleport home via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (:41957-41968) triggered by an emote at the arrival point — which bypasses the ore check and every global key.

ACCESS CONTROL IS NOT POSSIBLE. Wards do not gate walking through a portal, and `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547) iterates `m_allAreas`, permanently empty server-side, so it returns true vacuously. The only enforcement is architectural: put the terminal behind a door inside a warded base.

SCALE. 2 ZDOs per player minimum. `GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh List per call — cache it on a 1-5s tick; vanilla already allocates one every 5s.
catalog.playerExperience: Each player has a personal gate in their own base, distinguishable by a tag the server writes for them ("Rohan → Swamp"). They walk up to it, do the /point emote, and a HUD toast lists the next destination in their personal rotation; emoting again cycles it, and the gate's runes flicker off and back on as each new destination is written. When they walk through, they arrive exactly where their own gate said — every time, regardless of what anyone else is doing. The illusion is complete as long as nobody else walks into THEIR gate, at which point that person is sent to the owner's destination. Coming back is the rough edge: the public arrival portal leads to one fixed place, so the trip home either uses a second personal anchor they built at that destination, or a 'go home' emote that the server honours with a forced teleport.
failureModes: No access control exists: any player who reaches another player's terminal uses that player's destination. PrivateArea.CheckAccess returns true vacuously server-side (empty m_allAreas, :137173/:137547)
The return leg is fundamentally shared unless one anchor per (player × destination) is fabricated
ZDOVars.s_creator is 0 for any portal placed before the mod or by an admin (Piece.SetCreator only writes once when creator == 0, :136417)
A player who rebuilds their terminal gets a new ZDOID; the registry must key on s_creator + rounded position, not ZDOID
Player count scaling: every terminal is a persistent portal ZDO resident in RAM forever (portals are never unloaded, ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership :76872-76885)
Server-issued forced teleport as a return leg bypasses the ore/metal check entirely — Player inventories are never in any ZDO so the server cannot reproduce it (ZdoInventoryIO documents this)

A forced teleport silently no-ops if the target teleported in the last 2s (Player.TeleportTo :15309-15316) and latches forever on a dead player (UpdateTeleport runs only in the !IsDead branch, :10213/:10226)
openQuestions: Is ZDOVars.s_creator reliably populated on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7, and does it equal that player's s_playerID exactly? Place a portal on a vanilla client and compare both values server-side. The entire per-player identity model depends on it.
How many portal ZDOs can the server carry before GetPortalList allocation and the 5s sweep become measurable? Log Stopwatch timings at 200 / 500 / 1000 portals.
corrections: Identity is client-asserted, not socket-verified: s_creator and s_playerID are both written by the client from Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID() (Player.PlacePiece :12516; Player.SetPlayerID :10129-10136). Only PlatformUserID in m_playerHistory derives from the socket. A vanilla client is honest, so 'vanilla-respecting'; a modified client can forge either. If socket-bound identity matters, key the registry on the peer's PlatformUserID (ZNetPeer / ZNet.m_players userInfo) and map to the character ZDO via ZNetPeer.m_characterID :78794.
'pre-mod portals read 0' is wrong: vanilla has always written s_creator on player-placed pieces (Player.PlacePiece :12516). Only location/world-gen portals read 0.

One-way link stability condition is incomplete: pass 1 :100598-100605 clears a link when the target's tag differs OR the target's own connection is None. A terminal pointing at a public hub survives only if the hub has the same tag AND is itself connected to something.
Server-written personal tags ('Rohan -> Swamp') are ZDO.Set(s_tag) writes that do not dirty the portal chunk; call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() :76702 or they are lost at the next save.

The forced-teleport-home leg is client-honoured, not server-enforced: RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962-41968 runs on the receiving client and any routed RPC targeted at that peer is executed without sender validation (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :83618-83624); a vanilla client complies, a modified one can ignore it. Player.TeleportTo also silently returns false if m_teleportCooldown < 2f :15315.

Map-ping selection channel: Chat.SendPing :42058-42068 overwrites y with the local player's y and broadcasts 'ChatMessage' at targetPeerID 0; the server has no Chat instance, so the mod must register its own 'ChatMessage' handler (ZRoutedRpc.Register) or prefix RPC_RoutedRPC to see it. The sender long in the routed packet is client-asserted (RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83488-83491).
GetPortalList allocation note is accurate (:77648-77656); ZDOMan.GetPortals() :77643 returns the live dictionary for zero-alloc iteration.
'pre-mod portals read 0' is false: Player.PlacePiece (:12513-12517) has always called SetCreator, so all player-built portals carry s_creator. Only world-gen/console-spawned portals read 0.

s_creator / s_creatorIndex / s_playerID are client-written (:136415-136424, :10129-10136); m_playerHistory index is computed on the client against its synced copy (:81419-81433). Trustworthy only because clients are vanilla, not because of socket verification.

Save boundary: one-way and fan-in links are collapsed by RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) and restored only as reciprocal pairs by ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77849-77890). Rebuild every terminal link from the playerID-keyed registry after world load, before players connect.

Tags written for terminals ('Rohan -> Swamp') persist only if ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called after ZDO.Set(s_tag) (:73832-73838 dirties the sector chunk; portals are not in sectors :77748-77751).
Forced-teleport return via RPC_TeleportPlayer is subject to Player.TeleportTo's 2s cooldown and IsTeleporting guard (:15311-15318) and to UpdateTeleport's IsAreaReady wait (:15346-15349).
evidence: ZDOMan portal save / GetPortals / GetPortalList / SetDirtyPortals - assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77630, :77643-77656, :76702

(:12513-12517); Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator and s_creatorIndex only when owner and creator==0 (:136415-136424); Player.SetPlayerID writes s_playerID (:10129-10136); so s_creator == s_playerID on the character ZDO. m_playerHistory is synced to clients by HistoricalPlayerList (:81318-81341, :81419-81433) and the index is computed client-side. (3) The one-way T_p -> D_i topology does not survive a world save (single hash slot per ZDO :75461-75478; reciprocal-only restore :77849-77890) — fan-in to a shared D_i is collapsed to at most one bidirectional pair on reload, potentially overwriting D_i's own link; the mod must rebuild all terminal links from its registry after load. Effort 'large' plausible. Enforcement honest for the route; access control correctly stated as not enforceable.

catalog.name: Queue Dispatch
catalog.oneLine: "The next player to arrive gets the next target" — achievable only as arrival-detection plus a lock, not as a true queue, because the server cannot observe the moment of transit before it happens.
catalog.howItWorks:
Honest assessment first: a true queue is NOT observable. The only call site of `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter`, gated on `Player.m_localPlayer == component` (:143664-143682), so the server never learns that a transit is about to happen and never learns it happened as an event. There is no RPC, no ZDO write, no ownership handshake at the moment of transit.

What IS observable is (a) arrival near the portal, and (b) the transit AFTER the fact. (a) is the approach detector described in Approach-Triggered JIT Routing. (b) is Wonderland's `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit(fromPos, toPos, radius=40f)`, which walks `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (:77643, the live dictionary, zero-alloc) and flags a transit when both endpoints of a position sample sit within 40m of some portal, additionally following one endpoint's `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` to check the linked target is within 60m of the other endpoint. It was built to suppress a false positive — a 3s sample across a portal reads as ~110 m/s against a 40 m/s ceiling — and is already production-tested.

So the implementable feature is: maintain an ordered destination list and a per-portal cursor. When a player crosses the arming radius, atomically (a) claim the portal for that playerID, (b) write `destinations[cursor]`, (c) advance the cursor, (d) start a T-second lock. The NEXT player to arm after the lock expires gets the next destination. That satisfies the intent of 'next arrival gets the next target' with a visible, explainable rule.

Detection resolution: the position poll can run at 0.1s (far tighter than PositionWatch's 3s default) because character ZDO positions are fresh to ~50-150ms. Cost per tick is |peers| × |managed portals| squared-distance tests — trivial below a few thousand.

CONFIRMATION after the fact: to know a dispatch actually consumed, sample positions at 0.1s and detect a >40m jump whose origin is within ~8m of the portal and whose landing is within ~8m of the written destination. That is a strong, near-unambiguous signal. Suppress on `ZDOVars.s_dead` (respawn), on `Character.InInterior` boundary crossings and |Δy|>1000m (dungeon doors, interiors sit at locationY+5000, `Location.Awake` :133512, `InInterior` = y>3000 :4538-4541), and for admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811).
catalog.playerExperience: Three players queue at the dispatch gate. The first walks up, the gate's tag flicks to "→ Crypt 3" and they go. The tag then reads "LOCKED 4s" and walking in does nothing. Four seconds later the second player steps up, the tag becomes "→ Crypt 4", and they go. It reads as a working dispatcher — but only because the lock is enforcing turn-taking; a player who sprints in during someone else's window is silently blocked (if the mod blacks out on contention) or follows the previous player (if it does not). Nobody sees a queue UI, and the server only learns that anyone actually left ~0.1-3s after the fact.
failureModes: No pre-transit event exists anywhere: TeleportWorld.Teleport's only caller is the local-player-gated trigger (:143673-143681). A true queue cannot be built
A player who arms and walks away consumes a queue slot unless the lock is released on leaving the arming radius
Transit confirmation is a heuristic, not a signal — a 40m position straddle near two portals produces false positives for anyone sprinting past a portal pair
Dungeon doors (class Teleport) have NO ZDO at all (:143316-143390) and produce large position jumps that must be suppressed via the y>3000 interior test
Contention inside the lock window mis-routes or silently blocks; there is no third option
peer.m_refPos is 2s stale (:80337-80345) — using it instead of the character ZDO position blows the timing budget entirely
openQuestions: What is the real measured position-sample signature of a portal transit at a 0.1s poll rate — how many samples land inside the black screen, and does the character ZDO position update at all during Player.UpdateTeleport's 2s hold (transform.position is force-assigned every FixedUpdate from t>2s, :15343)? Determines whether a transit is one clean jump or a multi-sample smear.
corrections: Confirmation-after-the-fact signal is weaker than 'near-unambiguous' if the destination is not a portal: when the written destination is a non-portal anchor ZDO, PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit's extended check follows GetConnectionZDOID of the near-origin portal, which works, but its first check (both endpoints within 40 m of SOME portal) fails; use the mod's own managed-destination list, not ZDOMan.GetPortals, for the landing test.

Suppression list should also include RPC_TeleportPlayer-driven forced teleports issued by the mod itself and vanilla Player.TeleportTo from Bed respawn (s_dead covers death only); admins with debug fly are excluded via IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) as stated.

The lock must be enforced by the route field, not by a 'LOCKED 4s' tag: a tag write does not stop a vanilla client - only connection == None does (Teleport :143519 silent return). A tag rename also needs ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() :76702 to survive a save. The playerExperience text implies the tag alone blocks; it does not.

Detection latency: character ZDO position arrives via the client's 0.05 s SendZDOToPeers2 :76837-76862 and is dropped on the server when the client's send queue exceeds 10240 bytes (SendZDOs :77011-77015), so under load the 0.1-3 s figure can stretch; treat as best-effort.

Prereq chain (JIT routing -> Pairing Authority Takeover) is required for the same pass-1 reason as the other options: a dispatch target whose tag differs or whose own connection is None is cleared within 5 s by ConnectPortals :100598-100605.

Post-transit detection latency is >=2.0s + sync, not 0.1-3s: Player.UpdateTeleport only moves the transform after m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15337-15342); until then the character ZDO stays at the origin.

The in-flight player's destination is frozen at OnTriggerEnter (Teleport reads the target ZDO position into m_teleportTargetPos immediately, :143538-143546); rewriting the connection after entry cannot re-route them, so the lock only needs to span the approach window.

Per-second tag rewrites ('LOCKED 4s') must be followed by SetDirtyPortals() when restoring the base tag (:73832-73838 vs :77621-77632), and require vanilla pass 1 to be suppressed because a tag mismatch between linked portals clears the link (:100598-100605).
A player already inside the trigger volume when the lock expires and the next destination is written is not teleported (OnTriggerEnter only); they must step out and back in.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The honest framing is correct and every citation checks out. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter :143673-143681 is the sole caller of TeleportWorld.Teleport and is gated on Player.m_localPlayer == component; the whole Teleport body :143517-143545 does no RPC and writes no ZDO field other than the player's own TeleportTo, so the server has no transit event. ZDOMan.GetPortals :77643-77646 returns the live Dictionary. Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit exists at PositionWatch.cs:148 with the 40 m / 60 m logic as described. Character.InInterior :4538-4541 (y > 3000), Location.Awake interior at +5000 :133505-133515, ZDOVars.s_dead :78403, ZNet.IsAdmin(string) :81811-81814, class Teleport :143316 all verified. The lock is enforced on the route field (server-owned); the 'next player gets next target' promise is enforced only insofar as the second player physically waits - the option says so. Downgrade in enforcement is not warranted because the option already reduces the claim to route-timing; the corrections tighten what it must not promise.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The honesty framing is correct: OnTriggerEnter is the only Teleport caller and is m_localPlayer-gated (:143671-143681); nothing is written or sent at transit time. GetPortals returns the live dictionary (:77643-77646). Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit verified at PositionWatch.cs:148-200. Character.InInterior y>3000 (:4538-4541) and Location.Awake interior at y+5000 (:133505-133515) confirmed. ZNet.IsAdmin (:81811-81814) confirmed. One timing error: the after-the-fact jump is not visible '~0.1-3s' after the fact — Player.UpdateTeleport moves the transform only once m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15337-15342), so the character ZDO position jump reaches the server no earlier than ~2s after trigger entry plus sync latency. Conversely the destination is captured into m_teleportTargetPos at trigger entry (:143538-143546), so rewriting the connection during those 2s does not divert the in-flight player. The lock therefore must cover the approach window, and the 'consumed' confirmation arrives >=2s later. The countdown tag ('LOCKED 4s') rewritten each second is a data push to every peer holding the ZDO (cheap) but breaks vanilla pass 1 tag-equality if takeover is incomplete (:100598-100605) and requires SetDirtyPortals() to persist the restored base tag.

catalog.name: Self-Disconnecting Portals (One-Shot and Cooldown)
catalog.oneLine: A portal that severs its own link after a single use, or after any use for N seconds, driven by after-the-fact transit detection.
catalog.howItWorks:
Two variants on one mechanism.

COOLDOWN GATE. Cheapest and most reliable. On detecting a transit through portal P (position-straddle detector at 0.1s, see Queue Dispatch), write `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` + ForceSendZDO, record `reconnectAt = ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() + cooldown`, and restore the connection when the timer expires. The player who just left is unaffected — `Player.UpdateTeleport` snapshotted `m_teleportTargetPos` when TeleportTo was accepted (:15337-15348) and completes regardless. Anyone else arriving in the window finds the portal reading `$piece_portal_unconnected`, dark, and inert (gate 1 silent return, :143519-143522).

ONE-SHOT / CONSUMABLE. Same detection, but instead of restoring, the mod either leaves the connection None permanently, or destroys the portal ZDO outright: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` then `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929-76935, which is a silent no-op unless you own it) — `SendDestroyed` (:76937) then broadcasts the `DestroyZDO` routed RPC to every peer and the structure vanishes from every client's world. `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes it from `m_portalObjects` and sets `DirtyPortalObjects` (:76963-76999).

THE DETECTION LATENCY IS THE FEATURE'S WEAKNESS, and it is quantifiable. The detector needs two position samples: one near the portal, one near the destination. `Player.UpdateTeleport` does not move the transform until `m_teleportTimer > 2f` (:15337) and a distantTeleport (which portals always pass, :143546) does not COMPLETE until t>8s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:15349), with a 15s force-land fallback (:15360-15366). The character ZDO's position therefore changes ~2s after the transit and the player is locked in place until ~8s. So the earliest the server can confirm a transit is ~2.0-2.2s after the fact — during which a second player CAN walk through the still-live portal. The one-shot is therefore one-shot-per-2-seconds, not strictly one-shot.

MITIGATION: pair it with approach detection. Arm the portal when the first claimant enters the arming radius; the instant they cross an inner radius (~3m, i.e. committed), start a speculative cooldown and blacken the link. False positives (they turned away) cost a few seconds of outage; false negatives are eliminated. This converts a 2s hole into a <0.3s hole.
catalog.playerExperience: An adventurer finds a shimmering gate in a crypt tagged "One Way". They step through and arrive at the surface. Looking back, the gate they came from is dark — and if it was a consumable, the portal at the crypt end has simply vanished from the world with the standard destroy behaviour. Their companion, two seconds behind them, walks into the same gate and nothing happens: no fade, no message, just a dark frame. On a cooldown gate the tag reads "Recharging 18s" and the runes relight audibly when the timer expires.
failureModes: ~2.0-2.2s blind window between the transit and the earliest possible detection, because Player.UpdateTeleport does not move the transform until m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15337). A second player can slip through
Position-straddle detection is heuristic: a player sprinting past two nearby portals can false-positive and consume a one-shot nobody used
ZDOMan.DestroyZDO is a silent no-op unless the server owns the ZDO (:76929-76931) — SetOwner first or nothing happens at all
A destroyed portal's ZDOID enters m_deadZDOs (:76043/:76997) and any client replaying old ZDO data for it is force-destroyed; never recreate a portal under a reused ZDOID
The partner portal keeps a dangling connection until the next reconcile pass — under Pairing Authority Takeover the mod must clear it itself
Speculative blackout on inner-radius crossing produces visible flicker for players who walk near the portal without using it
openQuestions: Does the character ZDO position update at all during the 2s pre-move hold, or does it freeze at the origin? Poll a transiting player's ZDO at 0.1s across a real portal trip and record the exact sample at which position jumps.

Does destroying a portal ZDO while a client has it instantiated leave an orphaned local GameObject until the zone reloads, or does it disappear cleanly? Wonderland's SpawnGovernor does this for creatures; a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may differ.
corrections: Snapshot line ref is wrong: m_teleportTargetPos/Rot are assigned in Player.TeleportTo (:15300-15327, specifically :15324-15325), not :15337-15348; UpdateTeleport only reads them (:15342-15343).

No ownership claim is needed for the cooldown write itself: ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73665) + IncreaseDataRevision (:73832) propagate to the owning client through the normal near-sector sync (FindObjects :77376-77379 includes m_portalObjects; client RPC_ZDOData accepts higher DataRevision regardless of ownership). Only vanilla Game.SetConnection (:100629-100641) routes via RPC_SetConnection to the owner; a mod writing the ZDO directly bypasses that. ZDO.SetConnection also calls SetDirtyPortals itself (:73662-73664).

ONE-SHOT/DESTROY leaves the paired portal's connection pointing at a dead ZDOID. With the vanilla reconciler disabled (prereq), the mod must null the partner's connection, otherwise that client's TargetFound() calls ZDOMan.RequestZDO every 0.5 s forever (:143646-143654 via InvokeRepeating UpdatePortal :143447) and the server answers each with a ForceSendZDO of a ZDO it no longer has (AddForceSendZdos drops it, :77270-77277) — a harmless but permanent RPC spam.

DestroyZDO only queues; the actual removal happens at the next ZDOMan.Update via SendDestroyed → InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,"DestroyZDO") (:76950), which also self-dispatches on the server (InvokeRoutedRPC target 0 → HandleRoutedRPC, :83587-83590). The mod's own SetOwner must happen in the same frame as DestroyZDO, before ReleaseNearbyZDOS (2 s tick) can re-hand ownership.
Player.TeleportTo refuses while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15313-15316); this is per-player and does not help gate a second player.

Enforcement is split: the cooldown gate is route-form and server-enforced (with the quantified hole); 'one use only' is reactive-detection-only. Ship the cooldown, describe the one-shot as best-effort.

One-shot is not one-shot: the hole is ≥2.05 s plus RTT (transform pinned until m_teleportTimer > 2f, :15337; OwnerSync writes position only on transform change, :87526-87530; no earlier network signal exists). Document it as 'first-through plus anyone within ~2-3 s'.

The speculative-arming mitigation likely blocks the legitimate claimant: a None written at 3 m arrives (~1 send cycle, SendZDOToPeers2 :76838) before a running player reaches the trigger, and Teleport returns silently on !TargetFound (:143517-143521). Needs in-game tuning against the actual trigger collider size; do not ship as 'converts a 2 s hole into <0.3 s'.

Destroyed consumable portal does not get 'standard destroy behaviour' effects: HandleDestroyedZDO → ZNetScene simply destroys the GameObject; no WearNTear destruction VFX/SFX fires. It vanishes silently, and the builder's materials are lost.

After destroying P, the destination Q still holds a Portal connection to a dead ZDOID; every client near Q calls RequestZDO on each 0.5 s UpdatePortal (:143496, :143646-143650) until Q is nulled. The mod must also null Q's link (the vanilla pass-1 reconcile would do it within 5 s only if takeover leaves pass 1 running).

Cooldown countdown tags ('Recharging 18s') cost a full ZDO re-serialize to every nearby peer per write (SendZDOs :77056-77064); write at 1 Hz at most. Runes 'relight audibly' is real but only on the client's 0.5 s UpdatePortal sample (m_connected.Create on HaveTarget false→true, :143496-143500) and the emission lerp takes ~1 s (Update :143508-143512).

Vanilla pass 2 of Game.ConnectPortals (:100610-100622) re-pairs any None-connection portal with any other unconnected same-tag portal within 5 s; the cooldown only holds if Pairing Authority Takeover actually suppresses ConnectPortals, and ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) hands the portal back to a nearby peer within 2 s so server writes go through non-owner DataRevision races (RPC_ZDOData drops any revision ≤ local, :77113-77121).
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (no owner check) — SERVER :77076-77137; CLIENT assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:77217+
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified. Player.UpdateTeleport (SERVER :15329-15378) holds the transform for 2 s, then pins transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos every FixedUpdate, gates distant completion on t>8 s && ZNetScene.IsAreaReady, 15 s fallback — exactly as claimed, so the character ZDO position (written by ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync on the owning client) cannot move before ~2 s and the ~2 s detection hole is real. TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (:143518-143522) is a silent return when TargetFound() is false, and HaveTarget()/TargetFound() (:143632-143656) read the connection from the client's local ZDO copy, so a None connection pushed by the server does darken the frame (Update :143511-143515 lerps colour on m_hadTarget) and make Teleport a no-op. DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) is owner-gated, SendDestroyed (:76937-76951) broadcasts to peer 0, HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-76999) removes from m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects — all as cited. The one thing the option never establishes is how a server write reaches a portal ZDO that is owned by the nearby client (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926 hands it over). I checked: ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73665) writes ZDOExtraData unconditionally and calls IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73839, server path does not ClientChanged); portal ZDOs are included in the near-sector sync list via FindObjects (:77367-77382 adds m_portalObjects) and ShouldSend (:76003-76013) is pure revision compare; the CLIENT's RPC_ZDOData (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs :77217+, identical to SERVER :77076-77137) accepts any packet whose DataRevision exceeds its local copy with no ownership check. So the cooldown write propagates without an ownership claim, subject only to a revision race if the owning client wrote the same ZDO in the same window (portals have no ZSyncTransform, so rare). The strict 'one-shot' guarantee is not enforceable at the moment of transit — it is reactive detection followed by a route close; the cooldown variant is route-form and genuinely server-enforced with a ~2 s + one send-cycle hole.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The route-closure mechanism is real and vanilla-honoured: TeleportWorld.Teleport begins with `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (SERVER:143517-143521) and TargetFound/HaveTarget read only the client's local copy of the portal ZDO's Portal connection (:143632-143656), so a server-written `SetConnection(Portal, None)` (ZDO.SetConnection :73656-73664, bumps DataRevision + SetDirtyPortals) makes every vanilla client's trigger a silent no-op once the ZDOData packet lands. The departing player is unaffected: Player.TeleportTo snapshots m_teleportTargetPos/Rot (:15302-15326) and UpdateTeleport never re-reads the portal (:15329-15378). Destroy path verified: DestroyZDO is owner-gated and only enqueues (:76929-76935); SendDestroyed is flushed from ZDOMan.Update (:76820) as a routed RPC to peer 0 (:76950), which InvokeRoutedRPC also handles locally (:83585-83588), so the server's own HandleDestroyedZDO removes it from m_portalObjects, sets DirtyPortalObjects and records m_deadZDOs (:76963-76999). Detection latency confirmed: the transform is not moved until m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15337-15343); ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync only writes ZDO position when the transform changes (:87526-87530); nothing else (no ZDO var, no RPC — IncrementPlayerStat is local profile only :100569-100572) reveals the teleport earlier; client→server ZDO send cadence is ~20 Hz (SendZDOToPeers2 0.05 s :76838-76860). So the earliest server sighting is ~2.05 s + RTT, and a second vanilla player entering the trigger in that window passes. The 'approach detection' mitigation is worse than stated: a speculative None written when the claimant is ~3 m out reaches their client in one ZDO send (~50-150 ms) while a sprinting player covers 3 m in ~0.4 s, so the claimant themself frequently hits the trigger AFTER the None lands and is blocked (Teleport gate 1). Whether an inner radius can sit inside the trigger volume depends on the prefab's collider size, which the decompile does not expose. Enforcement: closing a route is server-authoritative and honoured; the 'exactly one use' property is only reactive.

catalog.name: Player-Requested Routing (Ping / Emote / Item Stand)
catalog.oneLine: The player names the destination through a vanilla input channel and the server pre-writes it — turning dynamic routing from a server decision into a player decision.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three vanilla client→server channels carry player intent with zero client install.

(1) MAP PING — the best one. `Chat.SendPing(Vector3 position)` invokes the routed RPC `"ChatMessage"` at `targetPeerID = 0` (ZRoutedRpc.Everybody) carrying the clicked world position, type 3 (Talker.Type.Ping), the sender's UserInfo and empty text (:42058-42068). Because it targets peer 0, `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` always calls `RouteRPC` (:83577-83595) and the dedicated server always receives it — with ONE player online, unlike chat text. A vanilla player triggers it by middle-clicking the large map, double-clicking with the Ping pin type selected, or gamepad JoyButtonX. The server captures it with a Harmony prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` matching `data.m_methodHash == "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()` (save and restore `m_parameters.GetPos()`), resolves the sender to a peer, finds the managed portal nearest that player, finds the destination nearest the pinged coordinate, and writes the connection. That is a complete destination picker on a stock client: open map, middle-click, walk through.

(2) EMOTE — 25 discrete values. `Player.StartEmote` writes `ZDOVars.s_emote` (string) and bumps `s_emoteID` (:15585-15598). Poll every connected character's `s_emoteID` at 0.25s (Wonderland's EmoteSignals does exactly this) and dispatch on the new `s_emote`. Ideal for 'cycle this gate' / 'confirm' / 'go home'.

(3) ITEM STAND — a physical radio button. `ZDOVars.s_item` on an ItemStand ZDO holds the mounted item's prefab stable hash (:78465). A row of stands beside a portal is a self-documenting, in-world destination menu the server reads with one ZDO poll.

FEEDBACK: `PlayerNotify.Toast` via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageType, text, 0)` (`Player.RPC_Message` :14820-14825) puts a HUD line in front of the player. `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered on every client at `Game.Start` :100068, handler :100823) drops a NAMED, SAVED map pin at the destination — but it is save:true with no removal RPC, so use it once per new destination, never as a live-synced pin set.

CHAT TEXT IS NOT A CHANNEL: `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each OTHER listed player individually (:41975-42043), so a solo player generates zero packets; slash commands run locally and print 'not a recognized command'.
catalog.playerExperience: The player opens their map, middle-clicks the Swamp outpost, and gets a HUD line: "Gate set → Bonemire (412m)". The ping marker everyone can see doubles as a public announcement of where they are about to go. They walk into the gate and arrive. Alternative flow: they stand at the gate and do /wave; a toast reads "1/4 Meadows", /wave again gives "2/4 Black Forest", and the portal's runes visibly blink off and back on with each cycle as the server rewrites the connection. Or they drop a Copper Ore on the stand labelled 'Mine' and the gate re-points within a second.
failureModes: Map pings are PUBLIC — broadcast to peer 0, so every online player sees the ping marker and its 5s map pin. A destination picker built on pings has no privacy and is trivially spammable; debounce hard
Registering a routed RPC name the server already has throws (ZRoutedRpc.Register uses Dictionary.Add) — probe m_functions or patch HandleRoutedRPC instead of registering
Chat text and slash commands are dead channels: SendText targets other players individually (:41996-42043) and unknown slash commands never leave the client
RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are save:true with no removal RPC — repeated pushes create duplicates unless name+type+position match within 1m (HaveSimilarPin)
EmoteSignals' 0.25s poll means a rapid double-emote can be coalesced; StopEmote bumps the counter with an empty name and must be ignored
The ping's y is forced to the pinging player's own y (:42058-42068), so the pinged coordinate is only meaningful in x/z
openQuestions: Is Chat.instance (and therefore the "ChatMessage" routed-RPC registration) present on a 1.0.7 dedicated server? If it is, ZRoutedRpc.Register will throw on a duplicate name and the mod must patch HandleRoutedRPC instead. Log the key set of ZRoutedRpc.instance's private m_functions at startup.

Is PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on a Steam client? If so, Chat.SendText collapses to a single broadcast at peer 0 (:42002-42005) and plain chat becomes a usable input channel even solo.
corrections: SendPing overwrites y with the local player's own transform.y (:42062-42063): treat the ping as an (x,z) only; never use its y for destination height.

'The sender's verified identity' is overstated: RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is read straight from the packet (Deserialize :83487-83495); the server never cross-checks it against the socket. Vanilla clients set it honestly, but for a verified identity prefix ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:83630) and map the ZRpc to its ZNetPeer.

Chat is a Terminal-derived HUD component (:41507); on a dedicated server it is almost certainly not instantiated, so "ChatMessage" is never in ZRoutedRpc.m_functions and HandleRoutedRPC silently drops it (:83645-83652). Either Harmony-prefix HandleRoutedRPC as the option says, or simply ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3,int,UserInfo,string>("ChatMessage", …) on the server — guard for a pre-existing key because Register uses Dictionary.Add (:83668+). Needs a one-line in-game confirmation that Chat.instance is null on the dedicated build.

Every vanilla ping is also the players' normal communication tool; an ungated 'nearest managed portal to the pinger' rule will re-route gates whenever anyone pings anything. Gate on the pinger standing within m_activationRange-ish (5 m, :143411) of a managed portal or on an armed state.

'Chat text is not a channel' holds only when PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider != null; if it is null the code broadcasts to peer 0 (:42002-42005) and chat text IS received by the server. The Steam platform implementation is not in the decompiles on disk — unverified.

Message RPC signature: Player registers "Message" as Register<int,string,int> (:10072) — matches the option's (type, text, 0) form; the RPC must be sent with the character ZDOID as targetZDO and the OWNER's peer uid, since RPC_Message checks m_nview.IsOwner() (:14822).
DiscoverLocation with showMap:true also opens the map and prints $msg_pin_added (client :58410-58417); use showMap:false for a quiet pin.
SendPing overwrites y with the local player's own y (:42062-42063); use only x/z of the pinged coordinate.

'Verified identity' is not free: RPC_RoutedRPC deserializes m_senderPeerID from the packet and never overwrites it with the socket's peer (:83629-83640). For vanilla clients it is accurate; if the design wants it verified, prefix ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) and map rpc→ZNet peer instead of trusting HandleRoutedRPC's sender.
Ping is unavailable on servers running the NoMap global key (client Minimap gating :39166, :101644) — the large map cannot open, so channel 1 vanishes; emotes remain.

StartEmote refuses while !CanMove(), InAttack, drawing a bow, attached (chairs/beds) or attached to a ship (:15587-15590); StopEmote also bumps s_emoteID with an empty s_emote (:15601-15608) — the poller must ignore empty names (EmoteSignals already does).

Item stand accepts only prefabs with an 'attach'/'attach_skin' child (ItemStand.GetAttachPrefab :131943-131955, gated in CanAttach :131963-131967) plus m_supportedTypes/m_supportedItems; 'drop a Copper Ore on the stand' needs an in-game check — raw ore prefabs generally lack an attach child. Use trophies/weapons as the radio-button tokens.

'Runes visibly blink off and back on with each cycle' is false for a direct A→B connection rewrite: the client's UpdatePortal only fires m_connected on a HaveTarget false→true edge sampled every 0.5 s (:143490-143500), and a None followed by the new target in the same server tick is serialized as one final state. To blink, hold None for ≥0.5-1 s before writing the new target; the emission lerp then takes ~1 s each way (:143508-143512).
RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse also forces the player's look direction toward the pin when the map is closed (:100826-100829) — a visible camera yank, not just a pin.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All three channels verified. Chat.SendPing (:42058-42069) calls ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,"ChatMessage", pos, 3, UserInfo, ""); InvokeRoutedRPC (:83577-83595) always RouteRPC()s when target != m_id, and the server's RPC_RoutedRPC (:83630-83641) calls HandleRoutedRPC locally for target 0 before re-routing — so the dedicated server receives every ping even with one player online. Player.StartEmote (:15585-15598) writes s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot on the owner client; ItemStand writes ZDOVars.s_item as an int prefab hash (:131845, read :131807/:132027, converted by ConvertPrefabs :78166). Player registers "Message" as <int,string,int> (:10072) and RPC_Message (:14820-14825) shows only when m_nview.IsOwner(), so the routed RPC must target the owning peer with the character ZDOID. RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse is registered unconditionally in Game.Start (:100068, handler :100823-100830); the client's Minimap.DiscoverLocation (client :58394-58419) AddPin(save:true), dedupes via HaveSimilarPin, and showMap=true forces the map open — no removal path, as claimed. The per-peer chat claim is verified in code (CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync :41996-42043, Talker.Say :18942-18950) but hinges on RelationsProvider != null. Routing decisions are route-form writes the server owns; enforcement is server-enforced.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Ping channel holds: client Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick / OnMapDblClick(PinType.Ping) / JoyButtonX all call Chat.SendPing (CLIENT:58580-58584, :58538-58548, :57060-57062); SendPing invokes routed 'ChatMessage' at targetPeerID 0 with (Vector3, 3, UserInfo, "") (SERVER:42058-42068); the server's RPC_RoutedRPC handles target-0 packets locally via HandleRoutedRPC before relaying (:83629-83640), and HandleRoutedRPC dispatches m_targetZDO==None packets through m_functions with the raw ZPackage (:83642-83650), so a Harmony prefix there sees the position regardless of whether a Chat instance exists on the server. Emote channel holds: Player.StartEmote writes s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot on the owner's character ZDO (:15585-15598) and the character ZDO syncs to the server unconditionally; 25 emotes (Chat.Awake loop :41634-41640). Item-stand channel holds: ItemStand.UpdateAttach writes ZDOVars.s_item = prefab stable hash (:131834-131845). Feedback holds: Player registers ZNetView RPC 'Message' (:10072) and RPC_Message shows it when the receiving client owns the character (:14820-14825), identical to Wonderland PlayerNotify; Game.Start registers RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse on every client (:100068) and its handler adds a pin and turns the player's look direction (:100823-100831). Chat-text negative holds (:41996-42043). Corrections concern the wire details and one player-experience claim.

catalog.name: Randomised Roguelike Re-Roll
catalog.oneLine: A portal whose destination is re-rolled to a fresh procedurally-validated world coordinate on an interval or after each use.
catalog.howItWorks:
Destination candidates must be validated without colliders, because every ZoneSystem raycast helper is dead on a dedicated server: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick in the SERVER build only (:100458-100466), so `GetGroundHeight`, `GetSolidHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `FindFloor` and `IsLava(Vector3)` all silently return their no-hit fallback rather than throwing.

Valid server-side validation stack, all pure math:
• `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x, z)` (:151944) — sea level is 30 (`ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel`, :113218). Reject `< 30 + margin`.
• `WorldGenerator.GetBiome(x, z)` (:151725) — biome filter.
• `WorldGenerator.GetNormal(point, radius)` (:151925) / `GetTerrainDelta(center, radius, out delta, out slopeDir)` (:152364) — slope/roughness; vanilla's own location placement accepts delta ≤ 2f.
• `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(pos, 0.6f)` (:115637) — STATIC, WorldGenerator-only, the only lava test that works headless.
• Reject `x*x + z*z > 110250000` (waterEdgeSqr, :151118-151122) and any y > 3000 (interiors, `Character.InInterior` :4538).
• Fast pre-filter: `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` (:92332/:92424) is an O(1) 12m-resolution cached grid; use it to reject candidates before spending a noise evaluation. `GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(biomeMask)` (:92683) hands you a pre-validated land point in one call.

The roll: pick a candidate, validate, then either move an existing anchor (DO NOT — see Roaming Portal) or destroy the old anchor and fabricate a fresh one at the new coordinate via Phantom Anchor Fabrication, then re-point the hub. Destroy requires `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` first (:76929-76931). Fabricate BEFORE destroying so the connection never dangles.

Re-roll cadence: per real interval (a 1Hz check against `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()`), per in-game day, or on transit-detected use (one-shot semantics). Pre-warm mandatory: a fresh far anchor is not held by any client, so the first walk-through is a silent no-op until `RequestZDO` round-trips (:143646-143654). Call `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId)` for every peer within ~200m of the hub immediately after the roll.

DANGER: `WorldGenerator` is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening (`ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations` re-resolves with a raycast and forces y=30 for m_snapToWater locations, :114957-114968). Treat heights as ±2m and always add clearance; `Player.UpdateTeleport`'s 15s fallback drops the player to `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` anyway (:15360-15366), and because portals pass distantTeleport:true the teleport can never fail outright.
catalog.playerExperience: A cracked obsidian gate in the hub hall is tagged "Unknown". Each dawn its runes flicker and the tag updates to "Unknown — Plains". A player steps through, takes the 8-second black screen, and lands on a random windswept ridge in the Plains they have never seen, next to nothing at all — no structure, no way back except the way they came, which is not there. Tomorrow it goes somewhere else. If the roll landed badly the player arrives a couple of metres above or below true ground and either drops a short distance or is force-landed on solid ground at the 15-second mark.
failureModes: Every ZoneSystem raycast helper silently returns its fallback on a dedicated server (reference position pinned to 1e6, :100463-100466) — a GetGroundHeight that returns p.y unchanged looks like a valid answer
WorldGenerator is blind to terraforming and location flattening; heights are ±2m
A fresh far anchor is never held by any client: first walk-through is a totally silent no-op
mask.a means lava only in the Ashlands (GetAshlandsHeight :152224); elsewhere the same channel carries an unrelated mask. Use IsLavaPreHeightmap, which biome-gates first
BiomeSector.Center is a perimeter centroid and can land outside its own biome; BiomeSector.MinZone/MaxZone are computed wrongly (:92577-92578) and must never be used
Churning anchors creates and destroys portal ZDOs repeatedly; each destroy enters m_deadZDOs (:76997) and each create dirties the portal chunk
One-way roguelike gates strand players with no return — either fabricate a return anchor at the destination or accept it as the design
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-generated zone within the 15s fallback on low-end hardware, and does it take fall damage? Player.UpdateTeleport resets m_maxAirAltitude every tick during teleport (:15345) which suggests no — verify with an 8km jump into unexplored Ashlands.

Are AllPoints / AllPointsAboveSeaLevel retained in memory after GenerateSectors, and at what RSS cost across 2048×2048 cells? Log Biomes[b].AllPoints.Count per biome at server start before leaning on GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.
corrections: GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel returns a BiomePointCoordinate in MAP space; convert with AltBiomeWorldData.MapSpaceToWorldSpace exactly as ZoneSystem does at :114681. With a multi-bit biome mask it first picks ONE biome uniformly (RandomBiomeFromBiomes :92709+) then a point — not area-weighted — and silently falls back to GetRandomPointByBiome (any point, possibly submerged) when AllPointsAboveSeaLevel is empty (:92688-92694).

Landing description needs precision: FindFloor (:115604-115612) raycasts from target+1 m straight down 1000 m with m_solidRayMask (includes 'terrain', :113424). A target ABOVE true ground therefore completes at t>8 s and the player simply falls; only a target whose +1 m origin is INSIDE the terrain collider fails FindFloor and reaches the 15 s GetSolidHeight+0.5 fallback (:15360-15366). Add clearance upward, never downward.

Re-roll on transit needs the same ~2 s detection latency as Self-Disconnecting (Player.UpdateTeleport :15337-15343); with per-use semantics a second player within that window lands at the OLD coordinate.

Pre-warm nuance: TargetFound re-issues RequestZDO every 0.5 s while the ZDO is missing (:143646-143654 from InvokeRepeating :143447), not once — so without pre-warm the first walk-through fails for one UpdatePortal tick, not indefinitely. ForceSendZDO(peerID,id) (:77714-77719) plus ShouldSend (:76003-76013) confirmed.

Save boundary: a portal→non-portal Portal connection is serialized by RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478), which stamps Portal|Target on the anchor; whether ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77850-77892) reattaches it or Game.ConnectPortals nulls it (predicate :100598-100605: anchor must carry the same s_tag AND a non-None Portal connection) is not exercised here — the mod must re-derive the pairing from its own state file on load, as the Seasonal option already recommends.

'The teleport can never fail outright' is only true once ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target) is true on the client: UpdateTeleport returns early while !IsAreaReady regardless of timer (:15349-15352), so the 15 s fallback (:15360-15366) is reached only after the destination zone has loaded client-side. Because the transform is pinned at the target from t>2 s and the client's ZoneSystem loads around the local player, this normally happens, but a target the client cannot load (outside world edge, or a zone that fails) leaves the player on a black screen indefinitely.

Usual completion is NOT the 15 s fallback: FindFloor raycasts down 1000 m on m_solidRayMask from target+1 m (CLIENT FindFloor) and the terrain collider almost always hits, ending the teleport at ~8 s with the player at the raw target y (:15354-15358). So a bad height means a drop from up to the height error, or — if the target is below terrain so the downward ray misses — the 15 s fallback to GetSolidHeight+0.5. Add ≥2 m clearance and never place below WorldGenerator.GetHeight.

'Runes flicker each dawn' requires a None hold ≥0.5 s before the new anchor is written (UpdatePortal edge detection :143490-143500); a same-tick fabricate+repoint produces no client-visible transition.

Once the traveller arrives, ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands them ownership of the persistent anchor (:76901-76927) and their ZNetScene tries to instantiate it every frame; an unknown prefab hash logs 'Missing prefab hash' per attempt (CLIENT CreateObject :82225-82236) — pick a real, benign, invisible-ish vanilla prefab for the anchor or accept warning spam on the arriving client. If the chosen prefab has a ZSyncTransform, the client owner will start writing position back.
The anchor must be Persistent and carry a valid prefab hash, otherwise it is dropped by the client's RemoveObjects (non-persistent + owner → DestroyZDO, CLIENT:82425-82455) or is unsaveable.

Destroying the old anchor from the server requires SetOwner(GetSessionID()) first (DestroyZDO owner gate :76929-76935); the DestroyZDO routed RPC is also handled locally (:83585-83588) so the server's own copy is removed and m_deadZDOs records it (:76995-76998).
evidence: AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateBiomePoints — :92429-92456; WorldSpaceToMapSpace — :92424-92427; GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel — :92683-92696; WorldGenerator.GetBiome IsReady check — :151797
Player.UpdateTeleport IsAreaReady gate / FindFloor / 15 s fallback — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15349-15366

ZNetScene.IsAreaReady / IsPrefabZDOValid / CreateObject / CreateObjectsSorted / RemoveObjects — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs (IsAreaReady, IsPrefabZDOValid, :82225-82236, :82334-82372, :82425-82455)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists with the claimed shape: Game.FixedUpdate pins ZNet.SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6) in the SERVER build (:100458-100466); WorldGenerator.GetHeight (:151944-151949), GetBiome (:151725), GetNormal (:151925), GetTerrainDelta (:152364-152390); ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap is static and WorldGenerator-only (:115637-115646); m_waterLevel=30 (:113218); waterEdgeSqr (:151121); Character.InInterior y>3000 (:4538-4541); AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace (:92424-92427) and GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel (:92683-92696); PointHeights is populated server-side (GenerateBiomePoints :92429-92456, and WorldGenerator.GetBiome itself consults m_biomeData.IsReady at :151797, so it exists on the dedicated server). ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations re-resolves with GetGroundData and forces y=30 for m_snapToWater (:114957-114966) — as claimed. FindFloor/GetSolidHeight are collider raycasts (:115604-115612, :115525-115536) and are indeed dead at the pinned position. The teleport-landing behaviour is correct in outcome. Route writes are server-owned; server-enforced. The load-bearing prereq (Phantom Anchor Fabrication) is outside this batch, but I checked the client never destroys unknown-prefab ZDOs (the destroy branch in ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted is `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`, client :82250-82258), so a bare coordinate ZDO survives on the client and TeleportWorld.Teleport only needs zDO.GetPosition()/GetRotation() (:143539-143545).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Server-side validation stack verified: Game.FixedUpdate (server build) pins the reference position every physics tick (:100458-100466); WorldGenerator.GetHeight/GetBiome/GetNormal/GetTerrainDelta exist at the cited lines (:151944, :151725, :151925, :152364); ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap is static and WorldGenerator-only (:115637-115646); m_waterLevel = 30 (:113218); waterEdgeSqr constant (:151122); Character.InInterior is y > 3000 (:4538-4541); AltBiomeWorldData.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel draws from a precomputed AllPointsAboveSeaLevel list (:92683-92697) and is what ZoneSystem itself uses for location placement (:114681). Vanilla client accepts a non-portal target: Teleport reads only GetPosition/GetRotation of whatever ZDO the connection names (:143539-143546) and an unknown prefab hash neither blocks IsAreaReady (IsPrefabZDOValid false → skipped, CLIENT IsAreaReady) nor gets destroyed on a client (CreateObjectsSorted only destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs when IsServer, CLIENT:82334-82372). Pre-warm claim holds: the client only receives sector-local ZDOs plus force-sends (CreateSyncList :77212-77240) and TargetFound re-requests a missing ZDO on every 0.5 s UpdatePortal until it arrives (:143646-143650). Arrival behaviour needs correction: the 15 s fallback is not unconditional.

catalog.name: Seasonal / Event Network Swap
catalog.oneLine: Swap an entire portal network's topology and naming at once — a Halloween layout, a raid-week layout, a wipe-eve layout — as a single batched, budgeted operation.
catalog.howItWorks:
A 'network' is a named config set of `{portalPositionKey → (tag, destinationPositionKey)}`. Swapping means, for every member: write `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617), write the Portal connection, ForceSendZDO, and call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` once at the end (a tag-only write does not set DirtyPortalObjects and is silently lost at the next world save — only SetConnection/AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO set it, :73661/:77750/:76986).

BATCHING IS MANDATORY. `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` performs no delta encoding — it re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO (every float/vec3/quat/int/long/string/byte[]) per peer per send (:77056-77064) — and `AddForceSendZdos` inserts each force-sent ZDO at index 0 of the sync list (:77275), so a hundred simultaneous force-sends monopolise every peer's next several send slots under the 10240-byte queue cap (:77011-77019). Wonderland's StructureUpkeep learned this the hard way and caps at 256 routed broadcasts per sweep. Apply the same discipline: rewrite at most K portals per tick (K=16 at a 0.2s tick gives ~80 portals/sec), and prefer ordering by distance from the nearest peer so visible portals change first.

CHEAPER PATH — do it at world load. `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76474-76531) loads the entire portal chunk into `m_portalObjects` before any peer connects, `ZDO.Load` leaves every ZDO unowned with revisions at 0 (:74550-74556), and `Game.ConnectPortals` runs synchronously from :76523 with `m_peers` empty so every write takes the immediate local path. A seasonal swap applied in an OnWorldReady hook costs zero network traffic and zero contention. Schedule swaps to coincide with a restart where possible.

REVERSION: keep the previous network in the mod's own state file so a swap is undoable. Do NOT rely on the world save to remember the old layout — rings, one-way links and self-loops do not survive `RegenerateConnectionHashData`'s single-hash-slot-per-ZDO format (:75461-75478).

ANNOUNCEMENT: the tag string is the free in-world signage channel (`GetHoverText` :143453-143463, no server-side length cap). For an out-of-world announcement, `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.Center, text)` (MessageHud registration :55808, handler :55848) puts a centre-screen line on every vanilla client, Localize'd client-side so `$token` strings resolve in each player's language.
catalog.playerExperience: On the night of the event, every player online gets a centre-screen line: "The ways have shifted." Over the next couple of seconds the portals nearest them visibly blink — runes dying and relighting with the vanilla connect sound — and their hover tags change from "Home"/"Mine"/"Swamp" to "Hollow I"/"Hollow II"/"Hollow III". The gate that led to their base yesterday now opens onto a crypt. When the event ends the whole thing reverts on the next restart, and their old tags come back exactly as they were.
failureModes: Un-budgeted mass force-sends monopolise every peer's sync queue (no delta encoding, :77056-77064; 10240-byte cap, :77011) and can visibly stall world streaming for everyone
Tag-only writes are silently lost at the next world save without ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702)
A player mid-transit when the swap lands arrives at the OLD destination (snapshotted at TeleportTo, :15343) and their return leg now goes somewhere else entirely
Players who opened the tag dialog before the swap can save back a stale 10-char-truncated tag afterwards (TextInput cap, :143482 / :61515-61522)
Reverting from the world save is impossible for non-pairwise topologies (RegenerateConnectionHashData, :75461) — the mod must keep its own before-state
With Pairing Authority Takeover disabled, every retag instantly re-pairs portals randomly within 5s (:100601)
openQuestions: Is MessageHud.instance present on a dedicated server, and is "ShowMessage" already registered in ZRoutedRpc.m_functions? Vanilla's ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll unguarded under IsDedicated() (:80258), implying yes — but the send side does not need it, only a duplicate Register would break.
corrections: LoadChunks ends with `DirtyChunks.Clear(); DirtyPortalObjects = false;` (:76526-76527) AFTER Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523). A swap performed inside the load path (e.g. a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals or ZDOMan.ConnectPortals) is un-dirtied and lost at the first save. Hook after LoadChunks/ZDOMan.Load returns and call SetDirtyPortals() last.

Game.Start starts ConnectPortalsCoroutine (:100074), whose first pass runs immediately: ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100691-100699) ForceSetConnection()s both directions of every pair that the load-time Game.ConnectPortals staged (AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100613), overwriting a load-time swap for those pairs; every 5 s thereafter pass 1 (:100598-100605) nulls any link whose target lacks the same s_tag or has a None connection. The Pairing Authority Takeover prereq must therefore either stop the coroutine before its first pass or clear the private m_currentlyConnectingPortals — merely 'running after load' is not enough.

'm_peers empty so every write takes the immediate local path' is correct (Game.SetConnection :100629-100641 takes the local branch when owner==0), but ForceSendZDO on an empty peer list is a no-op, so newly connecting peers receive the swapped ZDOs through the normal initial sync — fine, just not a 'force send'.

Hover-tag signage: the client's own tag dialog caps input at 10 chars (:143482) — display has no cap, so long event names show but cannot be re-entered by players; GetTagInfo runs CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC on the tag (:143566), which on PlayFab/console backends can mangle event names.

ShowMessage call shape: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.Center, text) — registered only in MessageHud.Awake on clients; the server has no MessageHud, so never target 0/self.

Portals 'visibly blink — runes dying and relighting with the vanilla connect sound' only if the swap writes None and leaves it for ≥0.5 s before writing the new target: the client's UpdatePortal samples HaveTarget every 0.5 s and fires m_connected only on a false→true edge (:143490-143500); a direct A→B rewrite (or None+target in the same tick, serialized as one state) produces no effect and the emission never changes. Budget a two-phase swap (all None, wait 1 s, all targets) if the blink is wanted.

The 'K=16 per 0.2 s tick' budget is a reasonable heuristic but the real cap is per-peer: each SendZDOs call sends until zPackage.Size() > (10240 - queue) and skips entirely if fewer than 2048 bytes are free (:77011-77019); force-sends therefore starve only the peers near the swapped portals, and only for the revisions that changed (ShouldSend :76003-76013). Ordering by distance from the nearest peer is correct.

Reverting 'exactly as they were' overwrites any player retags made during the event (RPC_SetTag writes tag+author on the owner client :143587-143600 and reaches the server via ordinary ZDOData); decide whether reversion is authoritative or merges.

Authorless server-written tags (empty s_tagauthor) go through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC with PlatformUserID.None (:143471-143478); on Steam PC with no platform text filtering this is a pass-through (CLIENT FilterUGC early return on !PlatformRequiresTextFiltering), but on filtered platforms authorless UGC may be censored — tag text should be plain ASCII and the option should not promise identical display on console clients.

Under a vanilla retag by any player, TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag first clears the connection (:143591-143596) — the seasonal topology for that portal is lost until the mod re-applies it; the mod must re-assert on tag change, which also means players cannot be allowed to 'rename' seasonal portals without the mod treating that as an event.

catalog.name: World-State Conditional Routing (Population, Load, Weather)
catalog.oneLine: Destinations that respond to ambient server state — how many players are online, which are where, and (with heavy caveats) the weather.
catalog.howItWorks:
POPULATION (fully feasible). `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` (:81630) returns the live peer list; `GetNrOfPlayers()` (:81516) and `GetConnectedPeers()` (:80516) give counts. Per-peer character ZDOs come from `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)` (:78794) and carry live position, `ZDOVars.s_dead` (:78403), `s_inBed` (:78457), health/stamina, and the full VisEquipment slot set as prefab hashes (:20569-20708). Rules that work: route the arrival gate to whichever outpost currently has the most players within 100m (a 'where is everyone' gate); open an overflow destination above N online; blackout a raid gate when fewer than 3 players are online; point a 'muster' portal at the centroid of the living player positions (fabricate/refresh an anchor there on a 5s tick).

DISTRIBUTION-AWARE LOAD BALANCING. Count players near each candidate destination and route new arrivals to the least crowded — the LRU/load-balanced policy of Deterministic Assignment Replacement, but driven by live occupancy rather than transit history.

WEATHER — LARGELY RULED OUT, and this is the important negative. `EnvMan.FixedUpdate` calls `UpdateEnvironment(num, GetBiome())` (:95719-95721), and `GetBiome()` on a dedicated server resolves against the pinned reference position at (1e6, 0, 1e6) (`Game.FixedUpdate` :100463-100466). The server's own `GetCurrentEnvironment()` therefore describes weather at a coordinate no player will ever stand on. Worse, weather is BIOME-LOCAL: each client computes its own current environment for its own biome, so there is no single 'server weather' to condition on even in principle. `EnvMan.IsWet()`/`IsCold()`/`IsFreezing()` (:96343-96356) read that same wrong environment. The only weather-adjacent state that IS globally coherent is the day fraction and the wind seed, both derived from `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()` and identical on every machine. So: time-of-day routing yes (see Scheduled Routing); weather-conditional routing no, unless the mod recomputes the environment itself from the destination's biome and the shared time seed, which duplicates `UpdateEnvironment`'s selection logic and is fragile.

Tick budget: 1Hz is ample for all of this. `GetPeers()` returns the LIVE list (do not mutate while iterating); a peer's `m_characterID` is `ZDOID.None` between connect and spawn and between death and respawn (`Game.SpawnPlayer` :100270, `Game._RequestRespawn` :100413) so guard every lookup.
catalog.playerExperience: A player logs in at 3am to a quiet server and finds the hub's 'Muster' gate dark and tagged "Too few awake". At peak hours the same gate lights up and leads to whichever outpost currently has the most people standing around it — hover reads "Muster → Bonemire (4)". A player who steps through the overflow gate during a busy evening is routed to the emptiest of three identical arrival pads rather than piling onto the first one. Weather never affects anything, and honestly telling players that up front is better than a feature that behaves differently on every client.
