The (1e6,0,1e6) pin (:100463-100466) is irrelevant to EnvMan.

Weather-conditional routing is feasible-with-caveats, not ruled out: recompute `period = (long)ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() / m_environmentDuration; Random.InitState((int)period); SelectWeightedEnvironment(GetAvailableEnvironments(WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiomeSector(destPos)))` with Random.state saved/restored, and honour m_forceEnv/GetEnvironmentOverride. Fragility is limited to matching two private members by reflection.

Positions: ZNet.UpdatePlayerList blanks m_position unless the peer opted into public position (:81284-81288), but that only affects the PlayerInfo list — the server always has peer.m_refPos and the character ZDO position; read those, never the PlayerInfo list.
GetPeers is the live list (mutating while iterating throws); GetConnectedPeers hands back a fresh List — use it for iteration.

'Muster' anchor at the player centroid depends on Phantom Anchor Fabrication and on the 8 s stale-snapshot behaviour (Player.UpdateTeleport :15337-15349): the arrival point is wherever the anchor ZDO's position was in the traveller's local copy when Teleport() ran, and that copy is only refreshed if the server ForceSendZDOs it (see Moving Destination Anchor). A 5 s refresh tick is fine for a centroid but the traveller may land up to 5 s + RTT stale.

Mechanism correction: EnvMan.GetBiome resolves via Utils.GetMainCamera(), not the pinned reference position; with no camera it returns EmptyMeadows (:96032-96040) and UpdateEnvironment exits before selecting anything (:95950-95955). The server-side IsWet/IsCold/IsFreezing statics are never written, not merely 'wrong'.

Weather-conditional routing is upgradable from 'ruled out' to feasible-with-caveats: recompute `period = ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()/m_environmentDuration`, `UnityEngine.Random.InitState((int)period)`, then SelectWeightedEnvironment(GetAvailableEnvironments(destBiomeSector)) (:95963-95980, :95871-95890) — a single Random.Range draw — plus GetEnvironmentOverride precedence (:95942-95949) and the Ashlands/DeepNorth override entries. It is deterministic across clients; the fragility is only that it copies private logic that may change between patches.

'Muster portal at the centroid of living player positions' must ground-snap the anchor with WorldGenerator.GetHeight and reject water/lava; a raw centroid is routinely mid-air, underground or at sea, and Player.UpdateTeleport only recovers via FindFloor (deck-height drop) or the 15 s fallback (:15354-15366). Refreshing an anchor's position from the server every 5 s also fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS ownership hand-off (:76901-76927) if any player is near the centroid — fabricate a new anchor rather than moving one (the catalog's own Roaming Portal warning).
Hover 'Muster → Bonemire (4)' updated per tick is a full ZDO re-serialize to every nearby peer per change (SendZDOs :77056-77064); throttle count updates to ≥1 s and only on change.

Population rules that gate a route (blackout under N online) are server-enforced; rules that read per-player VisEquipment/health to decide whether THIS player may pass are not — that is player-form and has no server hook (Teleport runs only on the local client :143664-143680).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Population half verified: ZNet.GetPeers returns the live m_peers list (:81630-81633), GetConnectedPeers copies it (:80516-80519), GetNrOfPlayers is m_players.Count (:81516-81519), ZNetPeer.m_characterID (:78794) is set from Game.SpawnPlayer via SetCharacterID (:100270) and cleared on respawn request (:100411-100413); peer.m_refPos is always known to the server even when m_publicRefPos hides it from other players (UpdatePlayerList :81245-81300). Routing on occupancy is route-form and the written connection is honoured by vanilla clients. However the recompute path the option calls 'fragile' is actually deterministic and cheap: weather is chosen per period `sec / m_environmentDuration` by `Random.InitState((int)period)` + SelectWeightedEnvironment over the biome's env table with one Random.Range call (:95963-95980, :95871-95890); every client computes the same pick for a given biome and period, and the EnvMan instance with its biome tables exists on the server (FixedUpdate runs :95700-95721). GetEnvironmentOverride (event/boss-forced env, :95942-95949) must also be replicated.

catalog.name: Moving Destination Anchor (Follow a Ship or Player)
catalog.oneLine: Keep the portal fixed but point it at a ZDO that itself moves — a ship, a player — so the arrival point tracks a target in real time.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads the destination ZDO's `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` at the instant of transit with no prefab validation (:143539-143545). So pointing a portal's `ConnectionType.Portal` at a Ship's ZDO, or at a player's character ZDO, genuinely resolves to that object's live coordinates on a vanilla client.

THREE HARD LIMITS, in ascending severity.

(1) Vanilla's reconciler kills it. `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 nulls the link within 5s unless the target ZDO carries the same `s_tag` AND a non-None Portal connection (:100598-100605). Fix: Pairing Authority Takeover. But note a ZDO holds exactly ONE connection (`s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` with a single readonly target, :74794/:75524-75534) — writing a Portal connection onto a player's ZDO would DESTROY their `SyncTransform` parentage (the ship-attachment record written by `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` :87542-87562). Ships never have a parent so they are safe; player ZDOs are not. Point at ships, not at players.

(2) Staleness. `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` requests a missing destination ZDO exactly ONCE via `RequestZDO` (:143646-143654), which `SendZDOs` consumes by removing it from `m_forceSend` after one send (:77051). After that the client never re-requests, so a distant moving target goes stale immediately. Keeping it fresh requires the server to call `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(shipUid)` every send cycle (~20Hz) for every peer — an expensive permanent broadcast, since SendZDOs re-serializes the whole ZDO each time (:77056-77064).

(3) THE KILLER. Arriving 'on' a moving ship is impossible in vanilla. `Player.UpdateTeleport` snapshots `m_teleportTargetPos` once and force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate from t>2s (:15343), and for `distantTeleport` — which portals always pass (:143546) — completion is blocked until t>8s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:15349). The traveller is nailed to an 8-second-old coordinate. Worse, `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` omits the 'vehicle' layer that `BaseAI` explicitly adds (:113424 vs :25909), so `FindFloor`/`GetSolidHeight` do not see a ship hull and the 15s fallback drops the player to seabed height (:15360-15366).

WHAT DOES WORK: pointing at a STATIONARY ship (a moored base-boat), or at a ship whose helmsman the server can identify via `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship ZDO (:78637, written by `ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl` :141326-141342) to blackout the portal while the ship is under way. That is a genuinely nice feature: 'the gate to the longship only opens while she's at anchor'.
catalog.playerExperience: The harbour gate is tagged "Sea Serpent — moored" and glows. A player steps through and lands on the longship's deck at the dock. Once the crew casts off, the gate goes dark within a second and the tag reads "Sea Serpent — under way"; walking in does nothing. If the server instead left it live, a player stepping through while the ship sails would spend 8 seconds on a black screen and splash into open water somewhere behind the wake, then be force-landed on the seabed at the 15-second mark.

catalog.id: dynamic-routing:Moving Destination Anchor (Follow a Ship or Player)
corrections: Limit (3), second paragraph, is wrong: Player.UpdateTeleport calls ZoneSystem.FindFloor (:115604-115612), which raycasts 1000 m down from target+1 m with ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask — and that mask DOES include 'terrain' (:113424); the seabed heightmap collider is hit, FindFloor returns true, and the teleport completes at t>8 s at the stale snapshot (:15351-15356). The player is released at sea level +1 m and falls into the water, swimming; the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15358-15366) is not reached. The missing 'vehicle' layer only affects the (unused) height value. Rewrite: 'lands in open water behind the wake', not 'force-landed on the seabed'.

Limit (2): TargetFound re-issues RequestZDO every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s, :143447) while the ZDO is absent (:143646-143654) — not exactly once; once the client holds the ZDO it never re-requests, which is the stale-copy problem. The refresh cost is not '20 Hz for every peer': ForceSendZDO goes through AddForceSendZdos → peer.ShouldSend (:77270-77273), so the ship is only re-sent when its DataRevision changed, i.e. the same cost as any nearby moving ship; the extra cost is only for peers outside the ship's sync range.

Limit (1): the vanilla reconciler can also be satisfied without full takeover by writing the same s_tag AND a non-None Portal connection onto the Ship ZDO (predicate :100598-100605 checks only those two things and pass 2 only iterates GetPortalList, :100607). Ship ZDOs carry no other connection (m_characterParentSync is character-only), so nothing is clobbered. Save-boundary behaviour of such a portal→ship link (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 stamps Portal|Target on the ship) is unverified — re-derive from mod state on load.

Better 'under way' signals than s_user: Ship writes ZDOVars.s_forward (speed enum) and s_rudder on the owner (:140867-140868), and ZSyncTransform writes s_velHash (:87538-87541); a ship can drift with no helmsman. Use s_forward != Stop || velocity > ε.

Enforcement note: blacking out the gate while under way is route-form and server-enforced, but the write reaches the traveller's client one send-cycle late (same propagation as the cooldown gate), so a player already inside the 5 m activation range when the ship casts off can still transit.

Limit (1) rewrite: the mod's own SetConnection never touches the target ZDO (:74951-74960). Player targets are unsafe because vanilla's retag path (RPC_SetTag → SetConnectedPortal → RPC_SetConnected → UpdateConnection(Portal, None) on the TARGET, :143591-143630, :74962-74975) overwrites the target's single connection slot — wiping a riding player's SyncTransform parentage — and because player ZDOs are non-persistent so the link is None after every restart. Ships are safe from the first only because they have no parent; both still need the takeover to stop Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 from nulling a tagless target (:100598-100605).

Limit (2) rewrite: TargetFound calls RequestZDO every 0.5 s until the ZDO arrives (:143496, :143646-143650), then never again. Freshness needs a periodic ForceSendZDO per peer, but AddForceSendZdos skips peers whose copy is current (ShouldSend :76003-76013, :77268-77276) and 1 Hz is sufficient; the '~20 Hz permanent broadcast' cost is overstated.

Limit (3) outcome: on a client FindFloor raycasts down 1000 m on m_solidRayMask (terrain included, CLIENT FindFloor) and hits the seabed, so the teleport completes at ~8 s with the player at the stale deck-height coordinate (:15354-15358) — they splash into open water and swim. The 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15360-15366) only fires if no terrain collider is under the point. Delete 'force-landed on the seabed'.

Stationary-ship arrival lands at ship.pos + forward×1 m + 1 m up (:143541-143545) — the ship ZDO position is the hull root near the waterline, so the exit point may be inside the hull mesh; needs an in-game check per ship prefab (Character colliders DO include the vehicle layer, so a clean deck spawn is plausible but unverified).

World-save: the hub→ship link is saved as a Portal hash on the hub and a Portal|Target hash on the ship (:75470-75475); on load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals writes ship.SetConnection(Portal, hub) as well (:77878-77883), giving the ship a Portal-type connection. Harmless for Ship code, but if a persistent ZDO also targeted the ship via SyncTransform at save time the ship's single hash slot may hold that instead and the link is dropped — the mod must re-assert from its own state file after load.

'Goes dark within a second' when the crew casts off: s_user is only set while someone holds the rudder (:141326-141342) and cleared on release (:141351); a drifting or towed ship has s_user == 0. Use ship ZDO position delta (or s_bodyVelHash written by OwnerSync :87584-87588) as the 'under way' test, not the helmsman alone.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds: Teleport reads the target ZDO's GetPosition/GetRotation with no prefab check (:143539-143546). Limit (1) is partially wrong: at runtime the mod's SetConnection writes only on the PORTAL's s_connections entry (ZDOExtraData.SetConnection keyed by the portal's zid :74951-74960); nothing is written to the target, so pointing at a player does not clobber their SyncTransform link by itself. The clobber is real but arrives through two other paths: (a) vanilla retag — TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag → SetConnectedPortal(target) → either SetConnection(Portal, None) on an unowned target or routed RPC_SetConnected → UpdateConnection(Portal, None) on the owner (:143591-143630), and UpdateConnection replaces whatever connection type the target had (:74962-74975), which for a player attached to a ship is the SyncTransform parent; (b) world load — ZDOMan.ConnectPortals writes a back-connection onto whichever ZDO carries the matching Portal|Target hash (:77850-77900), and RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps one slot per ZDOID so a ship that is simultaneously a SyncTransform target (rider aboard at save time) may lose the portal hash (:75461-75478). Limit (2) needs correction: TargetFound re-requests on every 0.5 s UpdatePortal call while the ZDO is missing (:143496, :143646-143650), not once; what is true is that once held, the client's copy is only refreshed by sector sync or force-send (CreateSyncList :77212-77240), and ZDOSectorInvalidated marks the ship invalid for peers outside its area (:76002-76010) without deleting the client copy. Force-send cost is bounded by ShouldSend (:76003-76013): only revisions that changed are sent, and a 1 Hz refresh (≤ ship speed × 1 s error) is plenty. Limit (3) is right that arrival on a moving ship is impossible (target snapshotted at TeleportTo :15302-15326, pinned from t>2 s :15337-15343, released at t>8 s :15349) but the outcome is misdescribed. Ship helmsman via s_user confirmed (RPC_RequestControl :141326-141342, cleared :141351).

catalog.name: Roaming Portal (Moving the Portal Itself)
catalog.oneLine: RULED OUT — a portal whose own position the server moves. Vanilla clients never re-read a portal's position, and the move permanently corrupts the portal registry.
catalog.howItWorks:
Four independent mechanisms each independently kill this.

(1) THE CLIENT NEVER MOVES THE MESH. `ZNetScene.CreateObject` applies `zdo.GetPosition()` only at the `Object.Instantiate` call (:82011-82013), and `ZNetView.Awake` never touches `transform.position` — it applies scale only, and only when `m_syncInitialScale` is set (:82566-82626). Unless the portal prefab carries a `ZSyncTransform` with `m_syncPosition` (Inspector data, almost certainly absent on a static building piece), the portal mesh AND its `TeleportWorldTrigger` collider stay frozen at the build site no matter what the server writes. It does not rubber-band and does not re-instantiate — it ignores the write entirely until the instance is destroyed and recreated by `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects`/`CreateObjects` (:82196-82226), at which point it POPS to the new coordinate.

(2) THE SECTOR KEY IS FROZEN. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73757). A portal ZDO stays filed in `m_portalObjects` under whatever sector index `AddIfPortal` gave it. `CreateSyncList` → `FindSectorObjects` → `FindObjects` (:77367-77382) therefore keeps delivering a moved portal to peers near its ORIGINAL location and never to peers at its new one. Only a permanent per-tick `ForceSendZDO` gets it anywhere.

(3) PERMANENT REGISTRY CORRUPTION. `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes a portal from `m_portalObjects` using `zDO.GetSectorIndex()` recomputed from the CURRENT position (:76976-76987), which no longer matches the dictionary key set at creation. A moved-then-destroyed portal leaks in `m_portalObjects` forever, and `GetPortalList()` / `Game.ConnectPortals()` keep processing a dead object. On the CLIENT side it is worse: every sector boundary crossing makes `AddIfPortal` append the ZDO under a second key without removing the old one (:77738), producing unbounded duplicate growth in each client's portal registry over a long session.

(4) IT IS NOT SAVED. `AddObjectsPerChunk` excludes portal prefabs from normal chunk files (:77572) and the ChunkPortal file is only written when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621-77635) — which `ZDO.InternalSetPosition`/`IncreaseDataRevision` never do (:73734-73745, :73832). Every relocation reverts on restart. And a position write on a ZDO the server does not own does not even bump DataRevision (`IsOwner()` gate at :73740), while `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` revokes server ownership of anything within ~96m of a player every 2 seconds (:76901-76927).

USE THIS INSTEAD: destroy the portal ZDO and fabricate a fresh one at the new coordinate (Phantom Anchor Fabrication). That is correct, saved, and delivered properly.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing. A player standing beside a 'roaming' portal sees it sit perfectly still while the server believes it has moved 500 metres. Walking into it still teleports them (the trigger is where the mesh is). Then they log out and back in, or walk 120m away and return, and the portal has silently teleported itself across the map with no animation — and everyone else in the old zone still sees it there until they too reload.
failureModes: Client never re-reads position: ZNetScene.CreateObject applies it only at Instantiate (:82011), ZNetView.Awake never does (:82566-82626)
Sector key frozen for portals (ZDO.SetSector early-return, :73752) — normal sector sync stops reaching the new location
HandleDestroyedZDO leaks the ZDO permanently if it was moved across a zone boundary (:76976-76987)
Clients accumulate duplicate m_portalObjects entries on every boundary crossing (AddIfPortal, :77738)
Position writes are not saved for portals (:77572 / :77621) and revert on restart
A position write on a non-owned ZDO does not bump DataRevision at all (:73740); ownership is revoked within 2s near any player (:76901)
openQuestions: Does the portal prefab carry a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition? This is the one thing that would change the verdict from 'ruled out' to 'possible but corrupting'. Test: with a player watching, run SetOwner + SetPosition(pos + up*3) + ForceSendZDO every tick for 3 seconds. If the mesh glides upward (a 20%/FixedUpdate lerp with a 5m snap, ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition :87700-87724) the component is present. Expect nothing to happen.
corrections: AddIfPortal is called on every received ZDOData (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77132, after InternalSetPosition :77129) and keys by current position (:77738-77748) — the portal sector key is frozen only for the writer's own local registry, not for any peer that subsequently receives the ZDO.

Mechanism (4) overstated: a client-echoed update re-keys the moved portal on the server, sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77751) and saves it once per key (:77621-77631); on reload each copy gets a fresh uid (ZDO.Load :74552) — relocation can persist as duplicate portal ZDOs, not revert.
Duplicate m_objectsByID.Add on ChunkPortal load (:76481) does not throw because uids are regenerated; remove the implied crash-free assumption either way — it is silently duplicated.
ZSyncTransform presence on the portal prefab is not verifiable from the decompile; state it as unverified Inspector data.
Cited range ':82011-82013' for CreateObject is off by two: position read is :82009, Instantiate :82013.

Mechanism (4) is wrong: the moved position IS persisted whenever DirtyPortalObjects is true — set by any Portal SetConnection/UpdateConnection (:73656-73678, i.e. every ConnectPortals pairing change), any portal destroy (:76986), or the public ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702). On reload ZDOMan re-files the portal under the saved position's sector (:76480), so restart HEALS the frozen-sector inconsistency rather than reverting the move.

Mechanism (2): 'permanent per-tick ForceSendZDO' overstates it. ForceSendZDO is one-shot and ShouldSend-gated (:77263-77277); after one delivery the receiving client files the ZDO under the new sector itself (:77132/:77738). The actual obligation is a force-send to every peer that subsequently approaches the new site or joins.

Mechanism (3) is more dangerous than described: the leaked m_portalObjects entry points at a ZDO handed back to ZDOPool (:76988). ZDOPool recycles it for an unrelated ZDO; GetPortalList()/ConnectPortals then iterate a non-portal and the next dirty portal save clones it into the ChunkPortal file; reload's m_objectsByID.Add (:76481) can throw on a duplicate key. 'Moved then destroyed' can corrupt the save, not just leak memory.

Add: moving a DESTINATION portal's ZDO position relocates the arrival point for vanilla clients immediately (TeleportWorld.Teleport reads target zDO.GetPosition() at :143540), even though the target's own mesh stays where it was built.

USE-INSTEAD advice must state the fabricated replacement needs Persistent=true, SetPrefab(hash) and ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (CreateNewZDO sets neither; AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal prefabs from normal chunks at :77572).
evidence: ZDOMan portal chunk load (re-file by saved sector) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76482
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The ruled-out verdict stands, but two of the four mechanisms are mis-described. Verified: ZNetScene.CreateObject applies zdo.GetPosition() only at Instantiate (:82009-82013); ZNetView.Awake only touches localScale under m_syncInitialScale (:82566-82626); ZDO.SetSector early-returns for PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757) so the SERVER's m_portalObjects key never follows the position; FindObjects merges m_portalObjects[sectorIndex] by that frozen key (:77367-77382); HandleDestroyedZDO removes with a freshly recomputed GetSectorIndex() (:76976-76987) so a moved-then-destroyed portal leaks; InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only under IsOwner() (:73734-73745); ReleaseNearbyZDOS runs every 2 s (:76871-76884, :76901-76927). Wrong/incomplete: (a) the claim that the sector key is frozen everywhere ignores ZDOMan.AddIfPortal, which is called on EVERY received ZDOData at :77132 right after InternalSetPosition(:77129) and keys by the CURRENT position (:77738-77748). A vanilla client that first receives the ZDO after the move (via ForceSendZDO/RequestZDO) files it under the NEW sector and will instantiate it at the new coordinate; a client that already had it gets a second entry under the new key (no cross-key dedupe, only per-list Contains :77740) while its instance stays put. (b) 'It is not saved' is only true while no client echoes the ZDO. If a client near the new position gains ownership (ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigns by GetPosition(), :76915-76925) and pushes any change, the server's RPC_ZDOData re-keys the portal via AddIfPortal under the new sector, sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77751), and GetSaveClonePerChunk then clones the ZDO once per key it appears under (:77621-77631). Because ZDO.Load regenerates uids (m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID), :74552) and the ChunkPortal loader does m_objectsByID.Add per entry (:76477-76482), the duplicate does not throw — it becomes a second, distinct, persistent portal ZDO with the same tag. So the failure mode is 'persists as ghost duplicates', not 'reverts on restart'. Whether the portal prefab carries a ZSyncTransform is Inspector data and cannot be settled from the decompile; the option's 'almost certainly absent' is an assumption. Also, the (1e6,0,1e6) pin means the server itself never instantiates any portal, so nothing here runs on a GameObject server-side — the whole option is pure ZDO plumbing, as claimed.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The RULED-OUT verdict holds, but two of the four stated kill-mechanisms are wrong or overstated and the corrective advice is under-specified. (1) Mesh freeze: confirmed — ZNetScene.CreateObject reads zdo.GetPosition() only at Instantiate (:82009-82013) and ZNetView.Awake touches only type/distant/scale (:82568-82611); nothing in TeleportWorld re-reads its own position. Whether the portal prefab carries ZSyncTransform is Inspector data and cannot be verified from the decompile. (2) Frozen sector key: confirmed — ZDO.SetSector early-returns for PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757); AddIfPortal files under GetSectorIndex() at insertion (:77738-77748); FindObjects merges m_portalObjects[sectorIndex] (:77376-77379) so peers near the NEW site never get it via the sector sweep. But 'only a permanent per-tick ForceSendZDO' is wrong: ForceSendZDO is one-shot and gated by ShouldSend (AddForceSendZdos :77263-77277), and once a client holds the updated ZDO its own AddIfPortal (:77132) files it under the new sector and ZNetScene will create it there. The real cost is a force-send to every peer that later approaches the new site / joins, not per-tick. (3) Destroy leak: confirmed and WORSE than stated — HandleDestroyedZDO removes from m_portalObjects using a sectorIndex recomputed from the CURRENT position (:76973, :76982), so the stale list entry survives, then ZDOPool.Release(zDO) resets and pools the object (:76988, ZDO.Reset :73530ff sets m_uid=None). The pooled instance can be recycled by ZDOPool.Create for an unrelated ZDO while m_portalObjects still references it: GetPortalList()/ConnectPortals then process a non-portal, and the next dirty portal save (:77621-77631) clones it into the ChunkPortal file; on reload :76476-76481 does m_objectsByID.Add(uid) and will throw on a duplicate key if that ZDO is also in its normal chunk. Client-side duplicate-key growth via AddIfPortal on every RPC_ZDOData is also confirmed (:77738 TryGetValue on new key → AddItemToList, no removal from old key). (4) 'IT IS NOT SAVED' is REFUTED: DirtyPortalObjects is set by ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for any Portal-type connection (:73656-73678, called by Game.SetConnection/RPC_SetConnection from the 5 s ConnectPortals pass whenever any pair changes), by HandleDestroyedZDO for any portal (:76986), and by the PUBLIC ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705). When the ChunkPortal file is written it clones every ZDO in m_portalObjects including m_position, and on load the portal is re-filed under GetSectorIndex() of the SAVED position (:76480). So a restart does not revert the move — it is the only thing that makes the registry consistent again. The ownership caveat is correct: InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only if IsOwner() (:73734-73745), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership to any peer in whose active area the portal sits (:76901-76926), so the mod must SetOwner(server) before writing. Note also that TeleportWorld.Teleport on the client reads the TARGET's zDO.GetPosition() at transit (:143540-143546), so moving a destination portal's ZDO does change where arrivals land even though its mesh stays put.

catalog.name: Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing
catalog.oneLine: RULED OUT — writing a different destination per player into the same portal. There is one ZDO object and the normal sync sweep reconverges every peer within ~50-100ms.
catalog.howItWorks:
The idea: write connection X, force-send only to peer A; write connection Y, force-send only to peer B; each holds their own destination. `ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)` (:77714) does exist and does target one peer.

It cannot work, for a structural reason. There is exactly ONE `ZDO` object per portal in `m_objectsByID`, holding one `ZDOConnection{m_type, m_target}` entry in the static `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` dictionary (:74794, :75524-75534). Per-peer state is only a REVISION CACHE: `ZDOPeer.m_zdos` maps ZDOID → `PeerZDOInfo(dataRevision, ownerRevision, syncTime)` (:75963-75981), and `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend(zdo)` returns true whenever `zdo.DataRevision > value.m_dataRevision` (:76003-76014).

So the second write (revision R2) makes `ShouldSend` true for peer A as well as B. `CreateSyncList` on the server gathers `FindSectorObjects(zone(peer.GetRefPos()), ...)` (:77212-77241), and `FindObjects` explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` back into the result (:77376-77379) — so any peer standing at the portal is, by definition, in the sector query and receives R2 on their next send slot. `SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per Update frame behind a 0.05s gate (:76837-76862), so reconvergence is ~50-100ms. The divergence window is shorter than a single human reaction, and the LAST write wins for everyone.

There is also no field-level merge on receive: `RPC_ZDOData` discards a packet whose DataRevision is ≤ the local one and otherwise calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` on the whole blob (:77103-77132). Nothing per-peer survives.

The only two things that genuinely differ per peer are (a) WHETHER a peer holds a ZDO at all — controllable via distance and `ForceSendZDO` — and (b) the revision cache. Neither carries divergent VALUES.

CONSEQUENCE: every 'per-player destination' feature must be physical (Per-Player Private Portal Terminals) or temporal (Approach-Triggered Just-In-Time Routing). There is no third route, and any design document claiming otherwise is wrong at the protocol level.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing coherent. Two players standing at the same portal would each briefly see a different destination for under a tenth of a second, then both converge on whichever the server wrote last, and both go to the same place. In practice it is indistinguishable from a portal that flickers between destinations at 20Hz.
failureModes: One ZDO object, one connection field — ZDOExtraData.s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection> with a single readonly target (:74794, :75524-75534)
ZDOPeer state is a revision cache only (:75963-75981); ShouldSend re-pushes the latest value to every peer whose sector query covers the portal (:76003-76014)
FindObjects merges m_portalObjects into every sector query (:77376-77379) so a peer at the portal always re-receives it
RPC_ZDOData replaces the whole blob with no field-level merge (:77103-77132)
Reconvergence is ~50-100ms (SendZDOToPeers2, :76837-76862) — far too fast to exploit
corrections: ZDO.Deserialize is an overlay (ZDOExtraData.Add per key; connection rewritten only when the Connections flag is set), not a whole-blob replace — :74206-74241.

Per-peer divergent VALUES are not protocol-impossible: ZDOMan.SendZDOs serializes each ZDO per peer (:77050-77066); a server-side patch on SendZDOs/ZDO.Serialize could emit per-peer blobs. Reword the conclusion to 'not achievable via ZDO writes + ForceSendZDO; a serialization-layer patch is an unverified alternative with owner-echo and revision caveats'.

The reconvergence estimate should note that only peers whose sector query contains the portal (or who are force-sent) receive R2 — peers far from the portal keep the stale value indefinitely, which is harmless for teleport since they cannot enter the trigger.
Retain 'ruled out' only for the naive ZDO-write + ForceSendZDO mechanism (ForceSendZDO is additionally ShouldSend-gated at :77263-77277, so a force-send with unchanged revision sends nothing at all).

Delete the corollary 'there is no third route / wrong at the protocol level'. ZDOMan.SendZDOs (:77008-77075) serializes each ZDO separately per peer; a serialization-time shim on SendZDOs/ZDO.Serialize that substitutes the connection per peer, plus a DataRevision bump so the vanilla client accepts it (:77110 revision guard), delivers genuinely divergent destinations that the client honours at TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143537). Needs in-game validation of ownership interactions (RPC_SetConnection to owner :100649, owner push-back, retag paths).
Effort for the shim route is medium, not small, and its enforcement is client-honoured (the client reads its own copy of the connection).
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData revision guard + whole-blob Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77110-77131 ; client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:77251
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists and does what is claimed for the vanilla ZDO-write path: one ZDOConnection per ZDOID in static ZDOExtraData.s_connections (:74794, :75524-75534); ZDOPeer.m_zdos is a revision cache only and ShouldSend is DataRevision/OwnerRevision comparison (:75961-76014); CreateSyncList uses FindSectorObjects around peer.GetRefPos() (:77212-77241) and FindObjects merges m_portalObjects (:77376-77379); SendZDOToPeers2 serves one peer per frame behind a 0.05 s gate (:76837-76862); ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) exists (:77714-77719); receiver discards packets with revision <= local (:77108-77118). So 'write X, force-send A, write Y, force-send B' reconverges on Y — correct. Two overstatements: (1) 'no field-level merge on receive / whole-blob replace' is wrong in detail — ZDO.Deserialize (:74206-74241) overlays keys via ZDOExtraData.Add and only rewrites the connection when the Connections flag is present; it never clears keys absent from the packet. Irrelevant to the conclusion but factually off. (2) 'There is no third route… wrong at the protocol level' is too strong. The wire protocol is per-peer: SendZDOs(ZDOPeer, bool) serializes each ZDO freshly per peer (item2.Serialize(zPackage2) inside the per-peer loop, :77050-77066) and records the revision it sent in peer.m_zdos. A Harmony patch on ZDOMan.SendZDOs/ZDO.Serialize can emit a different connection blob per peer with a per-peer-monotonic DataRevision; the client's TargetFound/Teleport read only its local copy (client :144380-144396, :143544). That is a real, untested route with heavy caveats (owner-client echo of its own copy back through RPC_ZDOData, revision bookkeeping, RequestZDO for the target ZDO, and the reconcile loop's Game.ConnectPortals rewriting the server truth). It is not achievable through ZDO writes + ForceSendZDO, which is what the option describes, so the option's conclusion for that mechanism holds; the categorical 'impossible at the protocol level' does not.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] Every factual claim about the NAIVE mechanism (write X, ForceSendZDO to A, write Y, ForceSendZDO to B) checks out and is in fact stronger than stated: ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) (:77714-77724) only adds to peer.m_forceSend, and AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77277) still requires peer.ShouldSend(zdo), which is purely revision-based (:76003-76014); the second write bumps DataRevision so A is resent on its next slot (SendZDOToPeers2 one peer per frame behind a 0.05 s gate, :76837-76862); RPC_ZDOData discards any packet with revision ≤ local and otherwise whole-blob Deserializes (:77110-77131, identical in the client build at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:77251). One ZDOConnection per ZDOID in the static s_connections dictionary (:74794, :75524-75534) is confirmed. BUT the conclusion 'no third route, wrong at the protocol level' is refuted. The protocol delivers a per-peer blob: ZDOMan.SendZDOs(ZDOPeer, bool) (:77008-77075) calls item2.Serialize(zPackage2) once PER PEER inside the per-peer loop and then stamps peer.m_zdos[uid] with the current revision. A Harmony prefix/finalizer on SendZDOs (or on ZDO.Serialize keyed by the peer currently being serviced) can swap ZDOExtraData.s_connections[uid] to a peer-specific target during serialization and restore it afterwards; nothing on the receiving vanilla client can tell the difference, and TeleportWorld.Teleport/TargetFound read the LOCAL connection (:143537, :143641). To push a new per-peer value the mod must raise DataRevision (public setter, :73494) so the client does not discard it, which triggers a resend to all holders — acceptable because the shim serves each their own value. It is not 'ruled out'; it is an ownership/interaction question that needs an in-game check: (a) if the owning client ever executes Game.RPC_SetConnection (the non-forced path in Game.SetConnection :100636-100651 routes to the ZDO owner) it overwrites its local view with server truth and pushes it back, wiping that peer's divergence until the next revision bump; (b) any push from the owning client after a local change re-sends the client's blob and the server must re-diverge; (c) the retag path RPC_SetTag/SetConnectedPortal (:143587-:143619) operates on each client's local view, so per-peer targets get 'disconnected' inconsistently. The stated player experience (20 Hz flicker) is correct for the naive mechanism only.

catalog.name: Transit-Instant Decision Hook
catalog.oneLine: RULED OUT — evaluating the destination at the moment a player steps in. Three independent gates make it unreachable on a dedicated server.
catalog.howItWorks:
This is the request every dynamic-routing feature actually wants, and it is impossible. Confirmed by direct inspection, not inference.

`TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly ONE call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider colliderIn)` (:143673-143681), which requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component`.

Gate 1 — no GameObject. The SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466); the CLIENT build's `Game.FixedUpdate` has no such line. `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` computes its zone from `GetReferencePosition()` (:82268-82276) and `CreateObjectsSorted` returns immediately unless `ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:82105-82112). No portal GameObject, no `TeleportWorld` component, no trigger collider ever exists server-side.

Gate 2 — no Player. `Player.Awake` is what adds a Player to `s_players` (:10032-10035); the list is permanently empty headless, so `Player.GetClosestPlayer` always returns null (:14840-14854) and no collider ever enters anything.

Gate 3 — `Player.m_localPlayer` is never populated on a dedicated server.

Corollaries. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `public` and appears in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable — it is not usefully callable: `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs `MessageHud.instance`, and `IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own throwaway profile. A Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `Teleport`, `UpdatePortal` or `TargetFound` compiles and applies on a dedicated server and never fires once. Even for a routed RPC that DID cross the wire, `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches ZDO-targeted RPCs through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` (:83646-83663, :82229), whose `m_instances` dictionary is permanently empty server-side — and a client that OWNS the ZDO never puts the RPC on the wire at all, because `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83588-83594).

The closest achievable substitutes, in descending fidelity: Approach-Triggered JIT Routing (~0.45s before the trigger), Per-Player Private Terminals (physical separation), and after-the-fact transit detection (~2.0-2.2s late, because the character ZDO position does not move until `m_teleportTimer > 2f`, :15337).
catalog.playerExperience: N/A — the mechanism does not exist. What a player experiences instead is whatever the server pre-wrote. The practical consequence is that no server-side feature can react to WHO is walking through at the moment they walk through, cannot reproduce vanilla's ore/metal check (inventories are never in any ZDO), and cannot refuse a specific player's transit.
failureModes: TeleportWorld.Teleport's only caller is the local-player-gated TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681)
No portal GameObject exists server-side: Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100463-100466)
Player.s_players is permanently empty (Player.Awake :10032), so GetClosestPlayer always returns null
ZNetScene.m_instances is empty, so ZDO-targeted routed RPCs are never dispatched server-side (:83656, :82229)
A ZDO-owning client's RPC never reaches the wire at all (InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch, :83588-83594)
Patches on TeleportWorld members apply cleanly and silently never fire — the most expensive possible failure mode, because it looks like it works
openQuestions: Confirm ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() (:82334) really is 0 on a running dedicated server with players online. It is the single empirical check that validates this entire ruled-out verdict.
corrections: Gate 1: replace 'CreateObjectsSorted returns immediately unless IsActiveAreaLoaded' with the sector-0 argument — ZoneSystem.Update creates local zones at the 1e6 reference position (:113930), and SectorToIndex clamps both the 1e6 zone and any out-of-bounds ZDO to Sector 0 (:115760-115773); portals at real coordinates are never in that bucket.
Player.Awake / s_players.Add citation should be :10035-10038, not :10032-10035.

Add corollary: Character.RPC_TeleportTo (client :886 register, :4128 handler, IsOwner-gated) lets the server order the owning client to relocate a player after the fact — reactive correction exists even though no pre-transit hook does.
Player.TeleportTo non-owner branch (server :15302-15307) shows the same RPC route from the server side; cite it rather than implying the server has no teleport lever at all.

Gate 1: replace 'CreateObjectsSorted returns immediately unless IsActiveAreaLoaded()' with the correct gate — the server does load local zones at the pinned position (:113930, :114023-114030), so IsActiveAreaLoaded can be true; no portal is instantiated because the pinned position's sector collapses to bucket 0 (:115759-115771) and no in-world portal lives there. Do not claim ZNetScene.m_instances is 'permanently empty' server-side (zone ctrl objects from PlaceZoneCtrl in Full mode carry ZNetViews).

Corollary: a ZDO placed beyond ±16.4 km lands in bucket 0 and would be instantiated server-side (the 'Sector Zero' mechanism); any statement that TeleportWorld patches 'never fire once' holds only for portals inside the world.

Player experience: the server can retroactively relocate a vanilla player with ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerId, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distant) (:41627, :41962-41968) — a reactive bounce, ~2 s after the transit registers, not a refusal.

catalog.name: Authentic Sender Context
catalog.oneLine: A thread-static ambient record of the socket-verified ZNetPeer for the duration of every routed-RPC and ZDOData dispatch — the prerequisite that turns every spoofable `sender`/`playerID`/`authorId` argument into something checkable.
catalog.howItWorks:
Two Harmony prefix/postfix pairs, both on methods that receive the real `ZRpc` and then discard it.

(1) `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632). The whole chain RPC_RoutedRPC → HandleRoutedRPC (:83646) → `m_functions[hash].Invoke(data.m_senderPeerID, data.m_parameters)` (:83652) is one synchronous call stack on the main thread. A prefix resolves `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (GetPeers is public, :81630; ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) is private) and assigns it to a `[ThreadStatic] static ZNetPeer s_current`; a `finally`-shaped postfix clears it. Every routed-RPC handler that runs during that window — including `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953), `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653), `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022), `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject` (:82355), `ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO` (:77689) — can now ask "who really sent this?" and get `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity on the box (Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth, ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79843-79870).

(2) `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:77076). Vanilla itself resolves the peer here (`FindPeer(rpc)`, :77078/:76800) and then throws the identity away before applying data. Same prefix/postfix pattern. Crucially, `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74206) is called *inside* this loop at :77131, so a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize` — the SpawnGovernor pattern (Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:58) — can read `s_current` and know exactly which authenticated account pushed that ZDO field set.

Derived helpers: `AuthPeer` (the ZNetPeer), `AuthUserId` (`peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`), `AuthIsAdmin` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)`, :81811 → `ListContainsId` :80159, which since 1.0.12 matches either ID form), and `AuthPlayerId` (`ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID)?.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` — still a client self-report, but now *bound* to a verified account so a mismatch is detectable).

Cost: two dictionary-free linear scans of `m_peers` per packet. Cache per-ZRpc in a small map keyed by reference to avoid the scan on hot paths.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing. This is pure plumbing — no player-visible behaviour changes. Its whole value is that every option below can say "and we know for certain that this packet came from Steam ID 76561198…" instead of "the packet claimed to be from peer 12345".
failureModes: `ZRpc` → peer resolution returns null during the handshake window (before `peer.m_uid` is assigned at ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79905) — treat null as untrusted and refuse, never as trusted.

A future Valheim build that dispatches routed RPCs asynchronously or off the main thread would silently break the ambient-context assumption with no error. Guard with a depth counter and assert single-entry.
It gives you identity, not authority: it does nothing about RPCs that never cross the wire (see Retag Interception at the Relay).
`ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` is private — bind with `AccessTools.Method(typeof(ZRoutedRpc), "RPC_RoutedRPC")` and wrap in SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch so a signature change degrades to a warning.
citations: ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.Deserialize (m_senderPeerID read straight off the wire) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83607-83615
openQuestions: Is there any path by which a routed RPC handler is invoked re-entrantly (a handler that itself calls InvokeRoutedRPC to Everybody, which self-dispatches at :83588)? IN-GAME CHECK: instrument the depth counter and log any depth > 1 over an hour of live play.
Does `peer.m_rpc` reference-compare reliably, or can a peer be re-created with a new ZRpc mid-session? IN-GAME CHECK: log identity-resolution failures per minute on a busy server.
corrections: RoutedRPCData.Deserialize is at :83487-83495 (class RoutedRPCData :83463); the cited :83607-83615 is inside ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC.
Drop 'since 1.0.12' — ListContainsId's dual-form match is present in this 1.0.7 decompile (:80159-80173); no version claim is supportable from the source.
Add: peer.m_uid is client-supplied (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79782, :79905) — cite this as the reason senderPeerID cannot be trusted.
Add: handlers also fire from server-originated InvokeRoutedRPC (target == m_id or 0, :83588-83591) with no ZRpc in hand — s_current == null must mean 'server', and every consumer must handle it.

Steam session-ticket check is at :79841-79851 and PlayFab auth callback at :79852-79866 (cited :79843-79870 roughly right; PlayFab check is asynchronous and only disconnects later, so for the first frames a PlayFab peer is not yet verified).
Use a Harmony Finalizer (or try/finally) rather than a plain Postfix to clear the ambient peer; a throwing handler would otherwise leak the previous peer into the next dispatch.
Drop the '(since 1.0.12)' qualifier: ListContainsId already matches both id forms in this 1.0.7 decompile (:80159-80173).

State explicitly that the context is only meaningful for peer-level (ZRoutedRpc.Register) handlers; ZDO-targeted RPCs (RPC_SetTag, RPC_SetConnected) are never dispatched on the server (FindInstance :83656-83662) and can only be inspected by a prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC itself.
evidence: ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo uid read/assign and ticket verification — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79782, :79841-79866, :79905
Handlers: RPC_DestroyZDO :76953, RPC_RequestZDO :77689, RPC_SpawnObject :82355, RPC_SetConnection :100653, RPC_SetGlobalKey :116022
ZNet.UpdatePlayerList id from socket host name — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81270-81278
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds. ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632-83644) deserializes the wire packet and, for target == m_id or 0, calls HandleRoutedRPC synchronously (:83646-83665), which invokes m_functions[hash](data.m_senderPeerID, params) — the sender id is read straight off the wire in RoutedRPCData.Deserialize (:83487-83495, NOT :83607-83615 as cited; that range is inside RouteRPC). ZNetPeer.m_uid itself is client-chosen (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo reads uid from the packet :79782 and assigns it :79905), which strengthens the premise that only m_socket.GetHostName() is trustworthy. ZNet.GetPeers is public (:81630); GetPeer(ZRpc) is private (:80504); ZNetPeer.m_rpc/m_socket are public (:78780-78782). ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData resolves the peer via FindPeer(rpc) (:77078, :76800-76810) and ZDO.Deserialize has a single caller at :77131, so a Deserialize postfix reading a thread-static set in an RPC_ZDOData prefix is attributable — the SpawnGovernor pattern (SpawnGovernor.cs:43-66) is exactly that. Identity verification: Steam VerifySessionTicket against the socket's peer id (:79841-79851) and PlayFab CheckIfUserAuthenticated (:79852-79866). IsAdmin → ListContainsId exists at the cited lines (:81811, :80159-80173) and already matches both ID forms in this 1.0.7 decompile — the 'since 1.0.12' attribution is unsupported and should be dropped. Handlers listed all exist at the cited lines (:76953, :100653, :116022, :82355, :77689). Caveats that must be stated: (1) HandleRoutedRPC also runs OUTSIDE the RPC_RoutedRPC window when the server itself calls InvokeRoutedRPC with target == m_id or 0 (:83588-83591), e.g. Game.SetConnection's local path — helpers must treat s_current == null as 'server-originated', not 'unauthenticated'. (2) On the server, RPC_RoutedRPC handles only target == m_id or 0; client-to-client ZDO-targeted RPCs are relayed without HandleRoutedRPC (:83636-83643), so the context is populated for relay-only packets only if the prefix is on RPC_RoutedRPC (as proposed), not on HandleRoutedRPC. (3) [ThreadStatic] is unnecessary — the whole chain is main-thread — harmless. (4) The 'AuthPlayerId' helper depends on peer.m_characterID (:78794) and ZDOVars.s_playerID (:78539), both client-written; the option already says so. This is admin-facing plumbing; 'server-enforced' is fair only in the sense that the identity it exposes is socket-verified — it enforces nothing by itself.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified. ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632-83643) deserializes RoutedRPCData — m_senderPeerID is read straight off the wire (RoutedRPCData.Deserialize, :83487-83490) and never overwritten by the server — then synchronously calls HandleRoutedRPC (:83646-83664), which invokes peer-level handlers from m_functions with data.m_senderPeerID; the server relays via RouteRPC (:83596-83629) without rewriting the sender. All handlers named are peer-level ZRoutedRpc.Register calls (DestroyZDO :76155, RequestZDO :76156, SpawnObject :81954, RPC_SetConnection :100067, SetGlobalKey :113447), so they do run server-side within the RPC_RoutedRPC stack; ZDO-targeted RPCs do not (FindInstance path :83656-83662), which the option does not claim. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData resolves FindPeer(rpc) by reference (:77078, :76800-76810) and calls zDO.Deserialize inside the loop (:77131), so a Deserialize postfix can read the ambient peer. ZNet.GetPeers() is public and returns m_peers directly (:81630-81633); ZNet.IsAdmin(string) → ListContainsId (:81811-81814, :80159-80173) matches both the raw Steam id and the PlatformUserID form in THIS 1.0.7 decompile — the '(since 1.0.12)' remark is unverifiable and irrelevant. Identity provenance is correct: peer.m_socket.GetHostName() is what UpdatePlayerList uses as the platform id (:81270-81278) and what RPC_PeerInfo verifies against the Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth (:79843-79870). Two engineering corrections: a Harmony Postfix does not run if the original throws — use a Finalizer (or try/finally transpiler) to guarantee the ambient slot is cleared, otherwise a handler exception leaves s_current pointing at the wrong peer for the next packet; [ThreadStatic] is unnecessary (all ZRpc dispatch is on the main thread) but harmless. AuthPlayerId caveat stands: ZNetPeer.m_characterID is a client self-report (RPC_CharacterID).

catalog.name: Retag Interception at the Relay
catalog.oneLine: Dropping `RPC_SetTag` packets at the server's `RouteRPC`/`RPC_RoutedRPC` chokepoint — RULED OUT as a general lock, because the most common case never puts a packet on the wire at all.
catalog.howItWorks:
The obvious design: prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632), deserialize a *copy* of the package, match `m_methodHash == "RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()`, resolve `m_targetZDO` via `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO()`, confirm it is a portal (`Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`, :100021), check the Authentic Sender Context against your ACL, and return false to drop both the local handling and the relay.

Why it fails. `TeleportWorld.SetText` calls `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", text, platformUserId)` (:143583), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, …)` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), m_zdo.m_uid, method, parameters)` (:82855-82858). `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` (:83577) then does:
```
if (targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0) HandleRoutedRPC(data);   // local
if (targetPeerID != m_id)                       RouteRPC(data);         // wire
```
In ordinary play the retagging player is standing next to the portal, so `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) has already handed that portal's ZDO to *that same client* within 2 seconds. `m_zdo.GetOwner() == m_id` for them, so the branch takes only the local path: the tag is written in-process, zero bytes are sent, the server's relay never sees it, and the change arrives at the server later, laundered, as an ordinary `RPC_ZDOData` field push with a bumped DataRevision (:77076-77132) that is indistinguishable from any other legitimate edit.

The complementary idea — Harmony-patching `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` itself (:143587) — is equally dead. `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC only through `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83659), and a dedicated server has no instances at all because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition((1e6,0,1e6))` every physics tick (:100458-100466), so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82268) never instantiates a world ZDO. The patch compiles, applies, and never fires once.

The relay hook is still worth building — as *telemetry*, not as a lock. It catches the minority of retags where a different client (or the server) owns the portal, which is exactly the case where a stranger is retagging a portal in someone else's base while its owner is offline. That is the grief case you most want logged.
catalog.playerExperience: If you shipped this as a lock: a player retagging their own portal while standing at it succeeds normally (packet never reached the server); a player retagging a portal whose owner is a different online player is silently refused with the text box appearing to accept the new name and the hover text never changing. Inconsistent and confusing — which is precisely why this cannot be the mechanism.
failureModes: The common case (owner retags own portal) is invisible to the server. Fatal for use as a lock.
`ZPackage` read position advances as you inspect it — a prefix must deserialize a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) or vanilla routing reads garbage.
Returning false from the prefix also suppresses the relay of a *legitimate* retag, producing a permanently desynced portal between two clients.
`m_senderPeerID` in the packet is self-reported (:83609) — useless without the Authentic Sender Context.
openQuestions: In steady state on a live server, what fraction of portals are owned by a nearby client versus by the server? That fraction is exactly the fraction of retags the relay hook can see. IN-GAME CHECK: log `zdo.GetOwner()` for every entry of `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` on a 10s timer, with players near and away from their bases.
corrections: Add: when the server owns the portal ZDO, vanilla's RPC_SetTag is dropped at ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC → ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83656-83664) — the relay prefix is then the only place the retag can be applied at all, not merely logged.

Add: RPC_SetTag also clears the Portal connection (ZDO.UpdateConnection(Portal, None), :143595-143597) before writing the tag, so a laundered retag arrives as connection=None + new tag in the same ZDOData packet — useful as a detection signature in the Deserialize postfix.
State the reactive ceiling explicitly: tag changes are detectable and revertable server-side via the ZDOData path (reactive-detection-only), which is the mechanism the 'lock' should be downgraded to.

Add the owner == 0 case: SetText on an unowned portal routes with targetPeerID 0, the packet DOES traverse the server relay (RouteRPC broadcast :83609-83618), but every recipient's RPC_SetTag no-ops on IsOwner() (:143589) — i.e. the retag silently fails in vanilla until ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigns an owner. Dropping it at the relay changes nothing.

Cross-reference: the only server-side seam that sees the common-case retag is ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData → ZDO.Deserialize (:77131); a lock built there is a reactive revert (server SetOwner + rewrite s_tag + revision bump), never a pre-write veto.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Verified end to end. TeleportWorld.SetText → m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", text, PlatformUserID) (:143579-143585); ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, …) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally when targetPeerID == m_id and only calls RouteRPC when targetPeerID != m_id (:83588-83594) — an owning client retags with zero packets on the wire. RPC_SetTag body is IsOwner-gated and writes s_tag/s_tagauthor plus clears the Portal connection via UpdateConnection (:143587-143602), all of which then reach the server as an ordinary ZDOData push (RPC_ZDOData :77076-77140). ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands nearby persistent ZDOs to the nearby peer every 2 s (:76871-76927). A server-side Harmony patch on TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag never fires because HandleRoutedRPC requires ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83656-83664) and the server instantiates nothing at real coordinates (Game.FixedUpdate pin :100458-100466). One additional vanilla fact worth adding: when the SERVER owns the portal (nobody nearby for >2 s, or the retagger acts within the first ownership window), the routed RPC targets the server, reaches HandleRoutedRPC, and is dropped at FindInstance — vanilla silently loses that retag. The relay hook therefore is not only telemetry for the other-client-owner case; a mod that wants server-owned portals to accept retags must reimplement RPC_SetTag's ZDO write itself. Enforcement classification 'not-enforceable' is right for the relay-drop design; the reactive alternative (ZDOData Deserialize postfix detects an s_tag change with the authenticated sender and reverts/overwrites) is the honest ceiling and belongs in the 'use instead' line.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every step verified. TeleportWorld.SetText → m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", text, platformUserId) (:143579-143585); ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,…) → ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …) (:82855-82858); InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally when targetPeerID == m_id and calls RouteRPC only when targetPeerID != m_id (:83588-83594). ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) gives any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer whenever it is unowned or its owner is not in range — and since the server's own 'active area' is around (1e6,0,1e6), server ownership of a real portal is always revoked in favour of the nearby player within 2 s. So the owner-retags-own-portal case produces zero routed packets; the change reaches the server only as an RPC_ZDOData blob (:77076-77131). RPC_SetTag itself is gated on m_nview.IsOwner() (:143589) and dispatched only via FindInstance (:83656-83662), which never resolves on the server; the Harmony-patch-never-fires claim holds. Two further cases the option omits, both consistent with its verdict: (a) owner == 0 → targetPeerID 0 → the client handles locally (no-op, not owner) AND broadcasts via RouteRPC; the server relays to everyone (:83609-83618) and every recipient's handler no-ops unless it owns the ZDO — so the retag of an unowned portal does cross the relay but also does not take effect in vanilla; (b) owner is another online peer → packet crosses the server relay and is droppable, exactly the telemetry case described. The true enforceable seam is not the relay but RPC_ZDOData/ZDO.Deserialize (detect a changed s_tag and revert with a server-owned write + revision bump), which is reactive, not a veto; that belongs to a different option but should be cross-referenced.

catalog.name: Creator Attestation
catalog.oneLine: Validate a newly-placed portal's `s_creator`/`s_creatorIndex` against the socket-verified account that actually sent the ZDO, at the instant of arrival — turning build ownership from a client self-report into a server-notarised fact.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Piece.SetCreator(long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID)` runs on the *placing client* and writes two fields into the piece's ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) = that client's local `PlayerProfile.m_playerID`, and `ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex` (:78395) = `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory.FindIndex(a => a.m_id == platformUserID)` (Piece.SetCreator :136415-136424). Both are client-authored and both are forgeable in isolation.

But `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` is a **server-maintained** table. `ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory` (:81436-81461) appends entries built by `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` (:81245-81299), which derives each `m_userInfo.m_id` from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` per backend (:81270-81281) — the platform-verified identity. The list is append-only (FindIndex-then-Add), persisted into the .fwl (`World.SaveWorldFWLData`, :112587-112591) and read back in order, so indices are stable across restarts. The server pushes its copy to clients via the `HistoricalPlayerList` RPC (:81317-81341), which is why the client's index is meaningful to the server at all.

The attestation, in the Deserialize postfix pair (SpawnGovernor pattern): a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) records the new ZDOID when `prefabHash == 0` (the network-receive path — the prefab is not known yet); a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74206) — reached at :77131, inside `RPC_ZDOData` — fires the moment the prefab IS known. There, for a ZDO in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`:
1. Read `idx = zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, -1)` and `claimed = zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0)`.
2. Resolve the Authentic Sender Context's `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` to a `PlatformUserID` and find its true index in `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory`.
3. If `idx` does not match, the claim is a forgery: overwrite both fields with the truth (`zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_creator, trueProfileId); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, trueIdx)`), `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706), and raise an audit flag.
4. If `idx == -1` (the placer had not yet entered the history when they placed — a real case, see failure modes), stamp the true index rather than trusting the zero.
5. Record the notarised `(position-key → PlatformUserID, profileId, firstSeenTicks)` into the Portal Record Store.

From that point on, every other option in this document can say "the owner of this portal is this Steam account" and mean it. Note the field is a per-piece stamp: the identity is captured at birth, when the server still has the sending socket in hand, and is never trusted again from the wire.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible when honest. A player places a portal and it is theirs; every later ownership decision (who may retag it, whose cap it counts against, whose network it joins) attributes correctly even after they log out, change display name, or the world restarts. A player running a modified client that forges `s_creator` to steal credit for someone else's structure gets their forgery silently corrected on arrival and an audit line appears in the server log and Discord.
failureModes: `Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `GetCreator() == 0L && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417). World-gen portals and anything placed before the field existed have `s_creator == 0` — treat 0 as "unowned", never as "owned by player 0".

`FindIndex` returns -1 if the placer is not yet in `m_playerHistory` when they place, which happens on a brand-new account's first minutes because the history is only refreshed by `SendPeriodicData` (~2s). The server must stamp the correct index rather than reject.
A client can forge `s_creator` (the profile-UID long) independently of `s_creatorIndex`; validating only the index leaves the long wrong. Overwrite both.
The attestation only fires on the *network-receive* path. A portal placed while the world is loading, or one the server itself fabricates, never passes through RPC_ZDOData — handle those separately.
If `m_playerHistory` ever gains a removal path in a future build, every stored index silently reattributes. Store the resolved `PlatformUserID` string in the mod's own record, not just the index.
citations: ZNet.UpdatePlayerList (id from socket host name) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81245-81299, esp. :81270-81281
openQuestions: Does a portal placed by a vanilla client reliably arrive with non-zero `s_creator` in 1.0.7? TortalPortal's PortalExport treats creator==0 as "admin-spawned or older", implying usually-but-not-always. IN-GAME CHECK: place a portal on a vanilla client, dump `s_creator` server-side in the Deserialize postfix, and confirm it equals that player's character-ZDO `ZDOVars.s_playerID`.

Does `s_creatorIndex` arrive in the *same* Deserialize call as `s_creator`, or can the piece ZDO arrive in two packets (position first, fields later)? IN-GAME CHECK: log both fields on every Deserialize of a portal-prefab ZDO for the first 5 seconds of its life.

Index mismatch is a normal transient on first join: the client computes FindIndex against a local copy that RPC_HistoricalPlayerList rebuilds then extends via UpdatePlayerHistory (:81419-81433, :81436-81461); the server pushes updates only when m_historicalPlayerListUpdated (:80349-80352). Stamp silently; do not audit-flag mismatches as forgery.

First-arrival validation does not make the field trustworthy afterwards: later ZDO owners can rewrite s_creator/s_creatorIndex via ordinary ZDOData; either re-assert on every Deserialize of a portal ZDO or have all consumers read the Portal Record Store, never the ZDO field.
Citation :81317-81341 for the HistoricalPlayerList RPC is the sender (SendHistoricalPlayerList :81318-81341); the client receiver is RPC_HistoricalPlayerList :81419-81433.
PlayFab authentication in RPC_PeerInfo is asynchronous (:79852-79866); a portal placed in the first frames after join could be attested against a peer not yet confirmed — negligible but nonzero.

Re-validate on every ZDO.Deserialize of a portal, not only at birth: any nearby client becomes owner via ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) and its ZDOData whole-blob replaces s_creator/s_creatorIndex (:77131). Delete 'never trusted again from the wire'.

'trueProfileId' is a client self-report (peer.m_characterID → s_playerID); only the PlatformUserID/index half is socket-notarised. s_creator is per character, not per account — the same account's second character has a different s_creator.

Effort: medium is plausible only if the Portal Record Store is keyed on something other than ZDOID (ZDOIDs are regenerated on load, :76528 m_nextUid = m_loadID + 1).

Only s_creatorIndex (→ PlatformUserID) can be notarised; s_creator can at best be bound-and-recorded. (2) The client's index is computed against its LOCAL m_playerHistory, which RPC_HistoricalPlayerList rebuilds and then extends with UpdatePlayerHistory() from its own m_players (:81430-81431) — a freshly joined player can hold an index the server has not yet assigned (server pushes only when m_historicalPlayerListUpdated, :80349-80352). Mismatch is therefore an expected transient for legitimate players, not proof of forgery; the option's 'idx == -1' case is the rare one and 'idx != trueIdx' the common one. The fix (stamp the server-computed index) is right; the 'raise an audit flag' step must not treat a first-join mismatch as a forgery. (3) 'Never trusted again from the wire' is not delivered by a first-arrival check: any later owner of the ZDO (ReleaseNearbyZDOS, :76901-76927) can Set s_creator/s_creatorIndex to anything and the postfix fires on that packet too; unless the mod re-asserts or consumers read only the Portal Record Store, the ZDO field is re-forgeable after birth. Also ZDOIDs regenerate on load (ZDO.Load :74552), so the record must be position-keyed as the option says. With those corrections the enforcement claim holds for the PlatformUserID binding: the server sees the socket of the packet that created the ZDO and can overwrite the index before any other peer receives it (ForceSendZDO :77706-77712).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core facts verified. Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) runs only when m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator()==0, writes s_creator = uid (Player.PlacePiece passes GetPlayerID(), :12516 — the per-CHARACTER profile id, not an account id) and s_creatorIndex = ZNet.World.m_playerHistory.FindIndex(id == platformUserID). It is called synchronously inside PlacePiece right after Instantiate, so the first ZDOData blob the server receives already carries both fields. Server-side m_playerHistory is built by UpdatePlayerList → UpdatePlayerHistory (:81244-81299, :81436-81461): ids come from peer.m_socket.GetHostName() per backend (:81270-81278), entries are FindIndex-then-Add (append-only; existing entries are updated in place, never reordered), and the list is written to the .fwl in order (:112587-112591) and read back in order (:113352). The server pushes it to clients by HistoricalPlayerList (:81318-81341), sent on join and whenever m_historicalPlayerListUpdated within the 2 s periodic tick (:80344-80352). The hook pair is sound: RPC_ZDOData calls the private CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3) with prefabHashIn defaulting to 0 (:76684-76692) and then zDO.Deserialize (:77131); ZDO.Set(int,long)/(int,int) have no IsOwner gate (:73648-73653, :73695-73700), so the server's corrective write bumps DataRevision and propagates even on a client-owned ZDO. Corrections: (1) An index mismatch is NOT proof of forgery. The client computes the index against ITS copy, which RPC_HistoricalPlayerList clears/refills and then the client's own UpdatePlayerHistory appends players from the last PlayerList packet (client :81604-81643); a client that receives PlayerList before the next HistoricalPlayerList can hold an extra trailing entry, and a freshly joined player may place before the first HistoricalPlayerList arrives (idx -1). Correct silently; only flag when idx resolves to a DIFFERENT known account than the sending socket. The attestation must re-check on EVERY Deserialize of a portal against the Portal Record Store and re-assert, not only at birth. Enforcement 'server-enforced' is fair for the server's own record; the ZDO field is client-honoured only in the sense that vanilla clients merely display/compare it.

catalog.name: Tag Author Rewrite
catalog.oneLine: Stop treating `s_tagauthor` as evidence and start treating it as a server-owned output field: overwrite it with the verified account of whoever actually caused the change.
catalog.howItWorks:
As shipped, `ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` (:78619) is worthless as identity. `TeleportWorld.SetText` fills it from `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString()` on the *client* (:143583), and `RPC_SetTag(long sender, string tag, string authorId)` writes `authorId` verbatim (:143599) without ever comparing it to `sender`, and `sender` itself is the self-reported `m_senderPeerID` off the wire (:83609). A modified client can name any account as the author of any tag. It is also cosmetic in vanilla: the only consumer is `TeleportWorld.GetTagSignature` (:143571) feeding `GetTagInfo`'s `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` call (:143566), and `FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591) and early-returns on non-PlayFab backends in the client build.

So the field is free real estate. The Tag Watchdog (below) already re-reads every portal's `s_tag`/`s_tagauthor` on its tick and holds the previous known-good snapshot. When it observes a tag change it must attribute it. Attribution sources, in descending confidence:
1. A relay-observed `RPC_SetTag` in the last tick with a matching target ZDOID, whose true sender came from the Authentic Sender Context. Certain, but only covers the minority of retags (see Retag Interception at the Relay).
2. The `RPC_ZDOData` packet that carried the change: a prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` stamps the current authenticated peer, and the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix fires per-ZDO inside that loop (:77131) — so for *every* laundered retag the server knows exactly which account's socket delivered it. This is the load-bearing path and it covers the common case the relay cannot.
3. Nothing else. Proximity heuristics ("who was standing nearest") are guesses and should never be logged as identity.

On attribution the mod writes the truth back: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, verifiedPlatformUserId)`, plus its own richer record in the Portal Record Store. Because the field is cosmetic and unfiltered on Steam, you can go further and make it human-readable — but note `ZDO.Set(string,…)` overloads exist (:73716) so mod-private keys such as `"tp_lastRetagBy"` / `"tp_lastRetagAt"` are cleaner than overloading a vanilla field, and `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` only *adds* the keys present in an incoming packet (:74718-74730) — it never clears — so a mod-private key the client does not know about survives a client's ZDO push intact.

This is reactive-detection-only for the *change*: the retag has already happened by the time you attribute it. It becomes enforcement only when paired with Tag Watchdog's revert.
catalog.playerExperience: A player retags a portal `MINE` and the hover text reads `MINE` as usual. Server-side, the admin's `/portals` report and the Discord audit line now say `"Elin's Gate" → "MINE" by Steam:76561198… (Elin) at 19:42`, which is true even if the player was running a client that claimed to be someone else. A player who forges the author field sees it corrected within one watchdog tick and appears in the audit trail as an attempted forgery.
failureModes: Reactive by construction: the tag was already wrong for up to one watchdog tick before you know who did it.

If a retag arrives inside a packet carrying many ZDOs, the per-ZDO Deserialize postfix still attributes correctly — but a *batched* packet from a proxying client would attribute all of them to that proxy. No such vanilla path exists; flag it if one appears.

Rewriting `s_tagauthor` bumps DataRevision and resends the ZDO to every peer (`ZDO.Set` → `IncreaseDataRevision` :73832; `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` :76003). Doing it on every tick for every portal is a broadcast storm — only write on actual change.

Vanilla's own `RPC_SetTag` rewrites the field on the next legitimate retag; your value is not sticky against an honest client. Keep the authoritative copy in the mod's record store and treat the ZDO field as a mirror.
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client's ZDO push of a portal it owns include *every* field it holds, or only changed ones? `ZDO.Serialize` (:74112) writes the whole field set, so it should be all — but confirm a mod-private key written by the server while the client owned the ZDO round-trips back unchanged. IN-GAME CHECK: write `tp_test` onto a client-owned portal ZDO, wait 30s, re-read it.
corrections: Client-side FilterUGC gate is `RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()` (CLIENT assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:88608-88618 — true on Xbox or console HardwareCategory), not 'non-PlayFab backend'. On console clients s_tagauthor is parsed and used (DetermineUGCFilteringMethod: BlockList/RelationsProvider lookups); keep it a syntactically valid PlatformUserID (Splatform format `{Platform}_{Id}`, e.g. `Steam_7656…`) and put human-readable data in mod-private `tp_` keys only.

Path 2 (ZDOData socket) attributes the PUSHER, which is the ZDO owner that executed RPC_SetTag (:143589 IsOwner gate), not the retagger. Order must be: match a relay-observed RPC_SetTag for that ZDOID first; fall back to the pusher only when none exists. A tag change arriving in a ZDOData push from a non-owner peer is a modified-client signal in its own right.
Line ref: the wire read of m_senderPeerID is RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83487-83495 (:83609 is RPC_RoutedRPC, which merely forwards the deserialized value).

RPC_SetTag applies when tag OR author differs (:143591), so a server-side author rewrite never triggers a client re-apply; a subsequent identical retag by the player will re-fire because the author now differs.

Attribution order must be exclusive, not merely ranked: if a relay-observed RPC_SetTag for the ZDOID exists in the window, the ZDOData socket is the OWNER who applied it, not the retagger — never fall through to source 2 in that case.

Relay observation must hook ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC or RouteRPC (:83633-83644, :83596-83620); a HandleRoutedRPC prefix (Wonderland's pattern) never sees owner-targeted RPC_SetTag because the server only calls HandleRoutedRPC for target == m_id or 0 (:83636-83639).

Do not write free-form text into s_tagauthor. On clients where RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() is true (client :88608, Xbox/console) GetTagInfo feeds `new PlatformUserID(authorString)` into DetermineUGCFilteringMethod; an invalid id takes the privilege branch and can replace the displayed tag with GetBlockedUGCString. Keep s_tagauthor a well-formed PlatformUserID string; put readable audit data in tp_ keys. PlatformUserID's string format lives in the non-decompiled Splatform assembly — copy an observed client value rather than inventing a format.

Rewriting the author field makes a later 'OK with no edits' by that player a real change under RPC_SetTag's `!(tagRaw == tag) || !(authorId2 == authorId)` test (:143591) → UpdateConnection(None) + SetConnectedPortal (:143593-143596) → link broken until the next ConnectPortals pass. Watchdog must ignore author-only diffs.
Citation fix: the wire-read of sender is RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83490, not :83609; ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC is :82838-82842.
evidence: Client FilterUGC / PlatformRequiresTextFiltering / DetermineUGCFilteringMethod — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs: FilterUGC body (early return on !PlatformRequiresTextFiltering), :88608, DetermineUGCFilteringMethod (invalid userId → privilege check → Censored/BlockedByPrivilege)
