Server-build CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591). The two attribution paths exist: a relay prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC sees owner-targeted RPC_SetTag only when retagger != owner (InvokeRoutedRPC :83576-83592 handles locally and sends nothing when targetPeerID == m_id); ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) resolves the peer via FindPeer(rpc) (:77076-77082) and calls zDO.Deserialize per ZDO at :77131, so a prefix/postfix pair can stamp the delivering socket. ZDODataHelper.ReadData adds per key without clearing (:74718-74730; ZDOExtraData.Add is `s_strings[zid][hash] = value` :74881-74884). Two claims are wrong: (1) the client FilterUGC is NOT gated on 'non-PlayFab backend' — it early-returns on `!RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()` (CLIENT :88608-88618: Xbox or console hardware), so on console clients s_tagauthor IS consumed: DetermineUGCFilteringMethod parses it as a PlatformUserID, consults BlockList and the platform RelationsProvider, and an invalid/blocked author makes the tag render as the blocked-UGC string. The field is not free real estate on crossplay servers. (2) Path 2 identifies the peer that PUSHED the ZDO, i.e. the owner that applied RPC_SetTag (IsOwner-gated :143589), not necessarily the actor; when retagger != owner the actor is visible only on the relay path. Still reactive-detection-only as claimed.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core facts hold: SetText sends the client's own PlatformUserID string (SERVER :143579-143585); RPC_SetTag writes authorId verbatim and never compares it to sender (:143587-143602); sender is read raw off the wire in RoutedRPCData.Deserialize (:83490) and passed through RPC_RoutedRPC (:83633-83644) and ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC (:82838-82842); the only readers are GetTagInfo/GetTagSignature (:143557-143577); server FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591); ZDO.Deserialize is called from exactly one place, ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77131, so a postfix attributes every laundered ZDO push to the delivering socket. Three things are wrong or under-specified. (1) Source 2 is not merely lower confidence than source 1 — it is WRONG in the relayed case: when the retagger is not the ZDO owner, RPC_SetTag is routed to the owning client (InvokeRPC targets m_zdo.GetOwner(), :82855-82858), the owner applies it (IsOwner gate :143589) and pushes ZDOData, so the ZDOData socket names the owner, not the retagger. Attribution must suppress source 2 whenever a relay-observed RPC_SetTag for that ZDOID landed in the window. And that relay observation cannot come from a HandleRoutedRPC hook: the server only calls HandleRoutedRPC when target == m_id or 0 (:83636-83639); an owner-targeted RPC goes only through RouteRPC (:83641-83644, :83596-83620). (2) Making s_tagauthor 'human-readable' is unsafe on console/crossplay clients: client FilterUGC early-returns only when !PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (client :88608, true on Xbox/console); otherwise GetTagInfo builds `new PlatformUserID(authorString)` and DetermineUGCFilteringMethod sends an invalid userId to the privilege path → Censored or BlockedByPrivilege → GetBlockedUGCString replaces the tag. Steam clients are unaffected. (3) Rewriting the author changes RPC_SetTag's no-op test `!(tagRaw == tag) || !(authorId2 == authorId)` (:143591): a player who later opens the box and presses OK without editing now triggers UpdateConnection(None) + SetConnectedPortal (:143593-143596), breaking the link until the next 5 s pass. The watchdog must treat author-only diffs as non-events, or write exactly the string that player's client will send back. Effort small-medium is plausible only after the Authentic Sender Context exists.

catalog.name: Ownership Pin
catalog.oneLine: Permanently hold managed portals' ZDO ownership on the server so `RPC_SetTag`, `RPC_Remove` and `RPC_Damage` all route to a machine with no component to receive them — the only genuinely unbypassable portal lock available server-side.
catalog.howItWorks:
Every mutating operation a client performs on a portal goes through `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, …)`, which targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858). If the owner is the dedicated server, the packet is sent to the server, `RPC_RoutedRPC` sees `m_targetPeerID == m_id` and calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83636-83639), which for a ZDO-targeted RPC requires `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83659) — permanently null on a dedicated server, because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick (:100465) and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` only instantiates around it (:82268-82276). The RPC is dropped on the floor. This is not a check that can be bypassed; it is an absence of the receiving code path.

What that kills, for a server-owned portal:
- **Retag.** `TeleportWorld.SetText` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", …)` (:143583) → dropped. The player types a name, confirms, and nothing changes anywhere. `RPC_SetTag` also no-ops on any other machine because it is gated on `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:143589).
- **Demolition.** The hammer's remove path calls `WearNTear.Remove()` for any WearNTear-bearing piece (Player.RemovePiece :12405-12408) → `InvokeRPC("RPC_Remove", blockDrop)` (:150411-150416) → dropped. Note the hammer only calls `ClaimOwnership()` on the *non*-WearNTear fallback branch (:12419), so it never tries to steal the portal first.
- **Damage destruction.** `WearNTear.Damage` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_Damage", hit)` (:150315-150320) → dropped. `RPC_Damage` is `IsOwner()`-gated anyway (:150332).
- **Client-side ZDO destruction.** `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(zdo)` is gated on `zdo.IsOwner()` (:76929-76935), so a non-owning client cannot even queue the destroy broadcast.

Holding the pin requires beating two independent ownership thieves:
(a) `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2s per peer and reassigns any persistent ZDO in that peer's active area whose owner is not itself in an active area — and the server never is, because of the 1e6 pin (`IsInPeerActiveArea` :76887-76892). Block with a Harmony **prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)`** (:74627) that returns false when the ZDO's prefab is in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, the portal is in the managed set, and `uid != 0L && uid != ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`. This is the Wonderland `ZdoSetOwnerPatch` pattern (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313). The predicate must fail fast on prefab hash — `SetOwner` is a global hot path.
(b) **The correction the existing research misses:** ownership also arrives over the wire *without* going through `SetOwner`. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` calls `zDO.SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal)` directly at :77114 and :77128, bypassing the public setter entirely — and the :77112-77117 branch applies an owner change even when the incoming DataRevision is *not* newer, as long as `OwnerRevision` is higher. A `SetOwner` prefix therefore does **not** stop a client from claiming a managed portal. You must also prefix the public `ZDO.SetOwnerInternal(long uid)` (:74636) with the same predicate, or re-assert ownership in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix on every arriving portal packet.

After claiming: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:77362 for the session id), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) so every peer learns the new owner immediately. A slow reconcile tick (2-5s) re-asserts the pin for anything that slipped through.

Scope this to *managed* portals only (admin networks, ward-protected gates, reserved-namespace hubs). Pinning every portal in the world would make the whole build system feel broken.
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks up to an admin hub portal tagged `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`, presses E, types a new name, presses OK — and the hover text still reads `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`. They try again. Nothing. They swing a hammer at it: the removal animation plays, resources are not refunded, the portal is still standing. They hit it with a maul: no damage number, no health loss. The portal is, from their side, part of the terrain. Pair it with a PlayerNotify toast (`"This gate is held by the server."`) triggered from the relay-observed RPC or the watchdog so the wall has an explanation rather than feeling like a bug.
failureModes: **The legitimate owner also cannot demolish or rename it.** This is total, not selective. Any managed portal needs a server-side unpin path (an emote command, an admin console command, or a ward/ACL check that releases the pin) or players will file bug reports.

`ZDO.SetOwner` is called constantly by `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` for every persistent ZDO near every peer. A slow predicate here is a server-wide framerate problem. Check `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` first and keep the managed set in a `HashSet<ZDOID>`.
Blocking `uid == 0L` would break `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`'s release path and vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651). Always let 0 and the session id through.

`ZDOID`s are regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552; `ZDOID.SetID` :75878) — the managed set must be rebuilt from the Portal Record Store by position on every boot, not persisted as ZDOIDs.

A pinned portal never receives a client's own connection writes, so `Game.SetConnection` (:100637) always takes the immediate local-write path for it — which is actually a benefit, but it means vanilla's deferred `RPC_SetConnection` path is never exercised for managed portals and will be untested code in your mod.

Does not stop `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953), which is a ZDO-*less* routed RPC that runs on the server and calls `HandleDestroyedZDO` with no ownership check at all. See Destroy Veto — the pin and the veto are both required.
citations: Player.RemovePiece calls WearNTear.Remove, ClaimOwnership only on the non-WNT branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12405-12423
ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies owner via SetOwnerInternal, bypassing SetOwner — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77112-77117, :77128

corrections: Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced: RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137) applies any peer's ZDO data with no ownership check, and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76955-76963) has no sender check. Against a modified client the pin degrades to packet-level detect-and-revert.

After a SetOwnerInternal prefix blocks a wire claim, RPC_ZDOData still assigns `zDO.OwnerRevision = num3` and updates `zDOPeer.m_zdos[id]` (:77112-77116, :77126-77130). ZDO.SetOwner is then a no-op (owner already the server, :74627-74634) and ForceSendZDO still runs through peer.ShouldSend (:77263-77276 → :76003-76013), so the corrective packet is never sent unless the mod bumps the public `OwnerRevision` setter (:73492) itself.

The server's own ReleaseNearbyZDOS pass never releases the pin: GetZone(1e6) clamps to sector 0 via SectorToIndex (:115760-115773) and FindObjects only visits that bucket (:77365-77380), so only the per-peer passes (:76880-76883 → :76901-76926) steal; the SetOwner prefix as described covers them.

Vanilla clients never self-claim a ZDO on instantiate (client ZNetView.Awake :82796-82860) — the only vanilla claim sites relevant to a portal are the server's ReleaseNearbyZDOS and TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal's owner==0 branch (:143607-143612), which a pinned (owner != 0) portal never hits.

Retagging an UNpinned portal paired to a pinned one leaves the pinned side pointing at a now-mismatched tag until Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100594-100606) clears it (≤5 s); the pinned side's SetConnection takes the local path because the owner is the server (:100628-100634).

Enforcement claim narrowed: server-enforced against VANILLA clients only. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies Deserialize for any ZDO from any peer without checking ownership (:77104-77132); a SetOwnerInternal prefix does not stop the tag/health/connection payload in the same packet. ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO has no sender check (:76950-76958). 'Only genuinely unbypassable' is false for modified clients — it is an absence of vanilla code paths, not an authority check.

Predicate must also block uid == 0 when arriving via RPC_ZDOData: a packet with owner 0 and OwnerRevision > current calls SetOwnerInternal(0) (:77112-77114, :77128), releasing the pin; SetConnectedPortal's `owner == 0L` branch (:143609-143613) then lets any client claim it.

After a vetoed SetOwnerInternal in the `num4 <= DataRevision` branch, OwnerRevision and the peer's PeerZDOInfo are still overwritten (:77112-77116); `zdo.SetOwner(server)` is then a no-op because ZDOExtraData already says server (:74627-74634) and no packet is generated. Re-asserts must call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid) (:77706) unconditionally.

Add as supporting fact: vanilla Game.SetConnection already server-owns every portal it writes (:100637), and the server's own session id is never in ZNet.m_peers so GetPeer(owner) is null → local write path (:100633-100639). Pinned portals therefore take the immediate write path in ConnectPortals with no RPC round trip.

Side effect to document: a server-owned portal never runs WearNTear owner logic on any client (UpdateWear/UpdateSupport/RPC_Damage all IsOwner-gated) — no weather wear, no support collapse, no repair. Acceptable for admin gates, wrong for player-owned ones.

catalog.name: Tag Watchdog (detect and revert)
catalog.oneLine: A slow server tick that snapshots every portal's `s_tag`, `s_tagauthor` and Portal connection, compares against the policy-approved state, and rewrites anything that drifted — the honest default mechanism for everything the Ownership Pin is too blunt for.
catalog.howItWorks:
This is **detect and revert**, not prevention. Say so plainly in the mod's own documentation: for a window of up to one tick, the griefer's tag is real and other players will see it.

Tick body, on a 1-2s timer from a subsystem's `OnUpdate` (the Wonderland Heartbeat/SubsystemRegistry shape):
1. `var portals = ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648) — a freshly flattened list of **every** portal in the world, always resident, no spatial query and no player needed, because portals live in `m_portalObjects` (:76039) and are never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883). Use the live `GetPortals()` dictionary (:77643) instead if you need zero allocation, but never mutate it.
2. For each portal: key it by rounded world position (`ZDO.GetPosition()`, :73822 → `(Mathf.RoundToInt(x), RoundToInt(y), RoundToInt(z))`) — **not** by ZDOID, which is regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552, `ZDOID.SetID` :75878). This is exactly the migration TortalPortal's Favorites.cs was forced to make (Favorites.cs:109-124).
3. Read `tag = zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (:73967 / :78617), `author = zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor)`, `conn = zdo.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal)` (:74002).
4. Diff against the Portal Record Store's approved state. On a mismatch, consult the policy chain: reserved namespace → ward gate → ACL → rate limit → claim registry (each is its own option below). The chain answers ALLOW (adopt the new value as the new approved state) or DENY.
5. On DENY: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, approvedTag)`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, approvedAuthor)`, `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — **mandatory**: a tag-only write does not dirty the portal chunk, and `GetSaveClonePerChunk` only writes the ChunkPortal file when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set, :77621-77635, so an un-dirtied revert is silently lost at the next world save), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706), then `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:100589) once at the end of the tick to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5s.
6. Attribute the change via the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix record (see Tag Author Rewrite) and emit an audit line.

Ordering matters. Vanilla's own `Game.ConnectPortals` runs every 5s (:100580-100587) and its phase-1 reconcile tears down any connection whose partner's `s_tag` differs (:100601). If your revert restores a tag but you do not also restore the connection, vanilla will have already broken the pair. Always revert tag and connection together, then call `ConnectPortals()`.

Budget the sweep. Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep because the first pass over a long-lived world produced thousands of dirty ZDOs in one frame; the same applies to a mass revert or a lockdown that nulls every connection.
catalog.playerExperience: A griefer walks into an unclaimed corner of your base, retags your `farm` portal to `farm ` (trailing space — a different network under vanilla's ordinal string comparison, :100601) and walks away. Within a second or two the tag snaps back to `farm`, the pair re-forms, and the griefer's own portal is left unconnected. Meanwhile the server log and the Discord channel carry `[SECURITY:PortalRetag] Steam:7656… (Bjorn) tried "farm" → "farm " at (412, 31, -1180); reverted.` A legitimate owner renaming their own portal sees the new name stick, because the policy chain said ALLOW and the store adopted it.
failureModes: **There is a real window.** Between the malicious write landing and the revert, up to one tick, the wrong tag is live and a fast attacker can walk through a mis-paired portal. Shortening the tick costs CPU and broadcast bandwidth linearly.

An attacker in a tight loop (a scripted client pushing `RPC_ZDOData` faster than your tick) makes the portal flap. Detect flapping (N reverts in M seconds on one portal) and escalate to the Ownership Pin for that portal plus a kick (`ZNet.instance.Kick`, :81658).
Forgetting `SetDirtyPortals()` makes every revert vanish at the next world save with no error anywhere — the single most likely shipped bug in this design.

`GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh `List<ZDO>` every call (:77648-77656). At 1s on a world with thousands of portals that is real GC churn; cache and refresh on a slower cadence, or iterate `GetPortals()`.

A moved portal appears twice in `GetPortalList()` because `AddIfPortal` keys on the *current* sector and never removes the old entry (:77732-77752), and `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portals (:73752). Deduplicate by ZDOID. Never move a portal ZDO.
Rewriting a tag on a portal a client owns loses a DataRevision race if the client re-pushes; pair the revert with a temporary Ownership Pin on that portal for a few seconds.

corrections: The connection is nulled by the retagger's own RPC_SetTag (:143594-143597: UpdateConnection(Portal, None) then SetConnectedPortal → partner's connection cleared), not by Game.ConnectPortals phase 1. If the record store holds the approved partner, write `SetConnection` on both ZDOs directly (:73656-73665, which also calls SetDirtyPortals) instead of relying on ConnectPortals, whose FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100677) is random when ≥3 portals share the tag.

`zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` before the revert is unnecessary for the data write (server ZDO.Set has no owner check :73648-73654; the vanilla client accepts any higher DataRevision, client RPC_ZDOData mirrors :77106-77131) and is undone within 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) whenever a player is nearby. Keep it only for the Ownership Pin case.
ZDO.SetConnection and UpdateConnection already call SetDirtyPortals (:73661-73664, :73673-73676); the explicit SetDirtyPortals is mandatory only for the tag/author writes.
Attribution via the ZDO.Deserialize postfix identifies the pushing peer (the owner that applied RPC_SetTag), not the actor — see Tag Author Rewrite correction.

Calling ConnectPortals() from the watchdog also executes ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals' force-writes for pairs staged on vanilla's previous tick (:100680-100689); harmless but it changes the two-tick commit cadence.

Restore the connection on BOTH ends: the vanilla retag cleared the partner too via SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected (:143594-143620). A one-sided restore is torn down by phase 1 (`target.connection == None`, :100601) and phase 2 re-pairs randomly (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100678) — original pairing not guaranteed when ≥3 portals share the tag.

ConnectPortals() only writes immediately for server-owned/unowned/dead-owner portals (SetConnection :100630-100642); for live-owner portals it is an RPC round trip force-committed next pass (:100685-100692). Claim ownership on both ZDOs before calling it, as step 5 does for one.
A client whose local DataRevision exceeds the server's discards the revert packet (:77110-77119) and re-pushes; only the periodic re-assert guarantees convergence.
Rounded-int position keys can collide for two portals placed within <1 m on both axes; add a tie-break.
Attribution caveat inherited from Tag Author Rewrite: the ZDOData socket is the owner, not necessarily the retagger.

Since the option already claims ownership first, this works — keep the ordering explicit. (3) Revision race: a client whose local DataRevision has run ahead of the server's ignores the revert packet (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision` → continue, :77110-77119) and re-pushes its value; the tick re-asserts and converges, but a single revert is not guaranteed to land. (4) Position key: Mathf.RoundToInt collides for two portals within <1 m on both axes; add a tie-break or use 0.5 m buckets. Effort medium is fair.

catalog.name: Portal Record Store
catalog.oneLine: Where per-portal ownership, ACLs, network membership and approved-tag state actually live: a position-keyed mod file as the authority, mirrored into mod-private ZDO keys for locality — with a precise account of what survives what.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three candidate stores, and only one combination works.

**(a) Vanilla ZDO fields.** `s_creator` (:78393) is the right *semantic* home for build ownership and, once notarised by Creator Attestation, is trustworthy. But it is a single long with no room for an ACL, a network name, a lock flag or a claim timestamp. `s_tagauthor` (:78619) is a free string but is overwritten by every legitimate `RPC_SetTag` (:143599).

**(b) Mod-private ZDO keys.** `ZDO.Set(string name, T value)` overloads exist for every type (:73559-73727) and hash the name internally, exactly as `PrivateArea` does with its runtime-concatenated `"pu_id"+i` / `"pu_name"+i` keys (:137338-137347). So `zdo.Set("tp_owner", platformUserIdString)`, `zdo.Set("tp_net", networkName)`, `zdo.Set("tp_lock", 1)`, `zdo.Set("tp_claimed", ticks)` all work and cost nothing.
  - They **persist**: portal ZDOs are saved wholesale into the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file (:113180) by `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77635) with no `Persistent` filter — but **only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set**, which a plain `ZDO.Set` does not do. Always follow with `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702).
  - They **survive a client's ZDO push**: `ZDO.Deserialize` → `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` (:74718-74730) calls `ZDOExtraData.Add` per key present in the packet and never clears the dictionaries, so a key the client's copy lacks is not removed. A client that *does* hold the key echoes it back verbatim from `ZDO.Serialize` (:74112). Either way the key survives an honest client. A *malicious* client can rewrite it (there is no ownership check on any ZDO setter — `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores its own parameter, :73648-73654), which is why this is a mirror, not the authority.
  - They must not collide with `ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly` (seeded from the 16 `ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes`, :74814-74825 / :78689-78693) or they are stripped from every save in the world. A `tp_` prefix is safe.
  - Keep the count small: `ZPackage.WriteNumItems` caps a per-type field count at 32767 (:83237-83246) and `ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk` warns above 100 (:74662-74675). Put anything list-shaped in one string or byte[].

**(c) A mod-side file.** `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath/TortalPortalLite.Portals.<worldName>.json`, written temp-then-move, the SupplySwitch pattern (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165). **Keyed by rounded world position, never by ZDOID** — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDOID on world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74552) and `ZDOID.SetID` forces `UserKey = UnknownFormerUserKey`, so a ZDOID-keyed file points at nothing after a restart. This is the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites hit and fixed (Favorites.cs:109-124) and the one Wonderland's SupplySwitch still masks by pruning dead ids on save.

**The working combination:** the file is the authority; the ZDO keys are a mirror the watchdog re-asserts. On boot, rebuild the in-memory `Dictionary<PosKey, PortalRecord>` from the file, then reconcile against `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`: portals in the world but not the file are new (attest and adopt); records in the file with no portal within ~0.5m are demolished (retain for a grace period, then prune). Because portals are all resident from world load (`ZDOMan.LoadChunks` :76474-76531, and the load-time `Game.ConnectPortals()` at :76523 runs before any peer connects), this reconcile can happen in the pre-peer window where every portal ZDO is server-owned and uncontested (`ZDO.Load` leaves `Owned = false`, :74550-74556) — the cheapest possible moment to claim and stamp.

A fourth store exists and should be used for *per-player* one-shot facts rather than per-portal ones: world global keys (`ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("tplite_...")`, :115943), which persist in the world save and travel with its backups — the FirstSpawnGrant pattern.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible directly. What players notice is that ownership, network membership and lock state survive server restarts, world backups being restored, and the portal being unloaded for months — and that an admin running `/portals` gets a report with real names attached to portals built by players who have not logged in since spring.
failureModes: Position keys break if a portal is ever moved. Never call `ZDO.SetPosition` on a portal: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752), so it stays filed under its old sector in `m_portalObjects` forever, `FindObjects` stops delivering it to the new zone (:77367-77381), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up under the *new* index and leaks it (:76976-76986).
Two portals stacked within the rounding tolerance collide in the key space. Use a 0.1m-resolution key or include the prefab hash.

A restored world backup and a current mod file disagree — the file will claim ownership of portals that no longer exist and miss ones that do. Reconcile at boot, log the delta, never auto-delete on the first pass.
The mirrored ZDO keys can be forged by a modified client; treat a mismatch between file and ZDO as an intrusion signal, and always resolve in favour of the file.
Forgetting `SetDirtyPortals()` after writing mod keys means they are never written to the ChunkPortal file and quietly vanish on restart.

How many mod-private keys can be added to a portal ZDO before the per-ZDO warning at :74670 fires in practice? IN-GAME CHECK: add 8 tp_ keys to one portal and watch for the WriteToDisk warning on save.
corrections: `enforcement: server-enforced` is a category label for infrastructure: the file is server-authoritative and unforgeable by clients, but the store enforces no player-facing rule; the enforcement level of anything built on it is that policy's own (mostly reactive-detection-only).

Global keys are not a private per-player store: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string) is a routed RPC to self (:115943-115946) handled by RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029), which has no sender check (any modified client can write or remove keys) and broadcasts the full key list to every client via SendGlobalKeys(0L). GlobalKeyAdd lowercases the key, replaces an existing value, bumps player stats and calls UpdateWorldRates on every write. Usable for coarse flags only; never for anything trust-sensitive.

Mod-private keys are subject to ZDO.Load stripping: longs whose hash is in ZDOHelper.s_stripOldLongData (:74355-74363) and empty strings (:74375-74378) are dropped on load; assert at boot that no `tp_*` hash collides with s_stripOldData / s_stripOldLongData (:75550-75617) and never rely on an empty-string sentinel.

Because LoadChunks clears DirtyPortalObjects after its own ConnectPortals (:76527), any pre-peer stamping done after world load still needs an explicit SetDirtyPortals or it is lost at the first save.

Minor: ZDOExtraData.Init line range is :74814-74825 as cited; ZDO.Deserialize also overwrites Persistent/Distant/Type/m_prefab from the packet (:74208-74212), so a malicious push can flip a portal's Persistent flag — another reason the file, not the ZDO, is the authority.

Global keys are not a safe per-player store: RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey have no sender or admin check (:116022-116035); any client can add or delete them. GlobalKeyAdd lowercases and splits on the first space, and every key is broadcast to all clients via SendGlobalKeys(0L). Use only for non-sensitive flags.
Add s_creatorIndex (:78395): Piece.SetCreator stores the index of the creator's PlatformUserID in ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:136415-136424) alongside s_creator — a second attestation input.

Enforcement label is nominal: the file is server-authoritative but the ZDO mirror is rewritable by any modified client because RPC_ZDOData applies any peer's payload without an ownership check (:77104-77132). Nothing in this option enforces a rule; it is a substrate.
evidence: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey / RPC_SetGlobalKey / GlobalKeyAdd — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115943-115946, :116022-116029, GlobalKeyAdd body following :116040
ZDOExtraData.Init session-only seeding / GetSaveData filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74814-74825, :75505-75513; ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes :78689-78693

ZPackage.WriteNumItems is a 15-bit encoding (:83237-83246); WriteToDisk warns above 100 (:74658-74675). catalog.name: Reserved Tag Namespace
catalog.oneLine: Declare a prefix (e.g. a leading `⌁` or `#`) that only the server and admins may write, and enforce it by reverting any player-written tag that uses it — plus the honest admission that vanilla's 10-character limit and rich-text stripping shape what is possible.
catalog.howItWorks:
A configured list of reserved prefixes and exact reserved names. The Tag Watchdog's policy chain rejects any tag change into the reserved space unless the attributed account is in `ZNet.instance.m_adminList` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)`, :81811) or the portal's Portal Record Store entry says it is server-managed.

The server side is unconstrained. `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` applies no length cap and no filter (:143587-143602), and `ZDO.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, …)` (:73721) writes any string. `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591), and on a Steam backend the client computes the censored flag in `GetTagInfo` (:143566-143569) and then discards it because `GetHoverText` only surfaces the warning when `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab` (:143462). So a server-written reserved tag can be as long and as decorated as you like — it will display in full on the hover label.

The **client** side is where the limits bite:
- The player-facing text box is hard-capped at 10 characters: `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` (:61515-61522). So a player *cannot type* a long reserved tag even if they wanted to — a long prefix is self-enforcing against honest clients, and the watchdog covers modified ones.
- Rich text is stripped from the displayed label: `GetHoverText` runs the tag through `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459 → assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703, `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")`). Do not plan on coloured reserved tags.
- `GetHoverName()` returns the hard-coded literal `"Teleport"` (:143466-143469), so the reserved marking can only appear in the hover *text*, never the hover *name*.
- Tag matching is bare C# `string !=` on `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with `""` default (Game.ConnectPortals :100601, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669) — **ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant**. `Hub` / `hub` / `Hub ` are three different networks. A reserved-namespace check must therefore be case- and whitespace-exact, and you should additionally normalise/reject trailing-whitespace tags as a griefing vector in their own right (see Anti-Grief Tag Integrity).

A reserved name is also a *lock*: combine with the Ownership Pin for reserved portals and the namespace becomes genuinely unwritable rather than merely reverted.
catalog.playerExperience: A player opens a portal's rename box and types `⌁HUB`. They get 10 characters to play with, hit OK, and within a second the name reverts to whatever it was, with a centre-screen toast: `Tags starting with ⌁ are reserved for server gates.` The admin hub network's portals all read `⌁HUB-CENTRAL`, `⌁HUB-SWAMP` — names no player can produce through the vanilla text box at all, because they are longer than 10 characters.
failureModes: Reactive unless combined with the Ownership Pin. A reserved tag written by a modified client is live until the next watchdog tick.
Unicode in a reserved prefix may render as a missing-glyph box in some clients' fonts. Test the exact glyph against the shipped UI font before committing to it.
A reserved tag written by the server *onto a portal a player owns* can be clobbered by that client's next ZDO push if you do not also pin ownership.
If the reserved prefix is short enough to type (≤10 chars total), an honest player can create a colliding tag by accident and be confusingly refused.
citations: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag: no length cap, no filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602
openQuestions: Does `GuiInputField` clamp a programmatically-assigned `.text` to `characterLimit`? `TextInput.Show` sets `characterLimit = 10` and then assigns the existing tag (:61519-61520). If it clamps, a player opening the rename dialog on a server-written 13-character reserved tag and pressing OK would save back a truncated version. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client, and re-read `s_tag`.
Which glyphs render correctly in the hover label's font? IN-GAME CHECK: server-write candidate reserved prefixes and screenshot the hover text on a vanilla client.
corrections: On Xbox/console clients FilterUGC is live (client :88608-88618) and a server-written tag with an empty or invalid s_tagauthor takes the 'userId invalid → privilege check → Censored' path in DetermineUGCFilteringMethod; the tag still displays but is profanity-filtered. Keep reserved tags clean and, if s_tagauthor is set, keep it a valid PlatformUserID string.

The glyph `⌁` (U+2381) is not verifiable from the decompile as present in the game's TMP font atlas; if missing it renders as a fallback box on vanilla clients. Prefer an ASCII sigil (`#`, `@`, `[`) or check in-game.

'Combine with the Ownership Pin and the namespace becomes genuinely unwritable' overstates: the pin is bypassable by a modified client's direct ZDOData push (see Ownership Pin verdict), so even the combined form is client-honoured plus detect-and-revert.
TextInput.OnEnter converts literal `\n`/`\t` to newline/tab after the 10-char limit (client :61557-61561); normalise/reject control characters, not just trailing spaces.
Client GetHoverText localizes the displayed tag (Localization.instance.Localize over the assembled string), so `$` tokens in a server-written reserved tag are substituted; avoid `$`.
Rename box pre-fills with the existing tag truncated to characterLimit 10 (client TextInput.Show :61515-61522); an unedited OK sends the truncated tag. Harmless under Pin/watchdog but document it.
The 10-char cap is enforced by GuiInputField.characterLimit, which is outside the decompiled set; verify paste behaviour in-game.
`⌁` glyph rendering in the game font is unverified; use `#` or another ASCII prefix unless checked in-game.

On Xbox/console clients (PlatformRequiresTextFiltering, client :88608) a server-written tag with an empty or malformed s_tagauthor can be censored/blocked by DetermineUGCFilteringMethod; write a valid PlatformUserID string when the server sets a tag.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Every cited fact holds. TeleportWorld.Interact requests text with charLimit 10 (:143470-143483) and TextInput.Show sets m_inputField.characterLimit (:61509-61522), so a vanilla client cannot submit >10 characters. RPC_SetTag applies no cap or filter (:143587-143602) and ZDO.Set(int,string) writes any string (:73719-73725). Server FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591). GetHoverText strips rich text via RemoveRichTextTags (:143459; utils_SERVER :6700-6703) and only shows the censored warning when the backend is PlayFab (:143461); GetHoverName is the literal 'Teleport' (:143466-143469). Tag matching is ordinal `!=` on GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) in ConnectPortals (:100601) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100669). ZNet.IsAdmin(hostName) exists (:81811-81814). The enforcement label is right: the length limit is client-honoured self-limiting, and the namespace itself is only reverted by the watchdog after the fact (reactive-detection-only); it becomes a lock only via the Ownership Pin, which is itself only client-honoured (see that verdict).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: Interact → RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) (:143482); TextInput.Show sets characterLimit and pre-fills m_inputField.text (:61515-61522); RPC_SetTag has no length cap or filter (:143587-143602); server FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591); GetHoverText strips rich text and shows the censored warning only on PlayFab (:143453-143464); GetHoverName is the literal "Teleport" (:143466-143469); tag comparison is ordinal `!=` on GetString(s_tag) (:100601, :100669); ZNet.IsAdmin(hostName) (:81811). Attacks that land: (1) TextInput.OnEnter replaces the two-character literals `\n` and `\t` with real newline/tab AFTER the 10-char cap (client :61557-61561), so a vanilla player can put control characters into a tag; whitespace normalisation must cover them. (2) The client's GetHoverText passes the tag through Localization.Localize (client GetHoverText body), so a server-written tag containing `$token` text is localized on display; avoid `$`. (3) Opening the rename box on a >10-char reserved tag pre-fills the InputField with the tag under characterLimit 10 — Unity InputField truncates on assignment — and an unedited OK sends the truncated tag; harmless (dropped by the Pin or reverted) but visible. (4) characterLimit enforcement lives in GuiInputField, which is not in the decompile set; the cap is Unity InputField behaviour and the paste path needs an in-game check. (5) Whether `⌁` (U+2301) renders in the game's TMP font is unverifiable from the decompile — prefer an ASCII prefix. (6) On console clients with text filtering the server-written tag goes through the tagauthor-driven UGC privilege path (see Tag Author Rewrite) — set a valid author id or accept possible blocking there. The 'combine with Ownership Pin to make it unwritable' claim holds for vanilla clients only.

catalog.name: Shadow Ward Index
catalog.oneLine: Rebuild PrivateArea coverage server-side purely from ZDO data, because `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` is a silent allow-all on a dedicated server — then gate retag and relink decisions on it.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.Interact` gates the rename dialog on `PrivateArea.CheckAccess(transform.position)` (:143471-143484) — entirely client-side, entirely unverified by the server, and the server cannot reuse the method: `CheckAccess` iterates the static `m_allAreas` list (:137547-137592, list declared :137173) which is appended to only in `PrivateArea.Awake` (:137197) on a live GameObject. A dedicated server instantiates nothing, so `m_allAreas` is permanently empty and `CheckAccess` **returns true for every point in the world — vacuously, not as a grant**. Calling it server-side is a bug that looks like working authorization.

Everything it needs, however, is in the ward's ZDO:
- `ZDOVars.s_enabled` (:78423) — bool, the active flag (`PrivateArea.IsEnabled` :137423).
- `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (:78529) — int count; then per-entry `"pu_id"+i` (long playerID) and `"pu_name"+i` (string), entries with id 0 skipped. Exactly reproduce `GetPermittedPlayers` (:137349-137363) with `zdo.GetLong("pu_id"+i, 0L)` / `zdo.GetString("pu_name"+i)`.
- `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) and `s_creatorName` (:78397) — the builder, written by `Piece.SetCreator` (:136415) and `PrivateArea.Setup` (:137446).
- `ZDO.GetPosition()` — the centre.

The missing piece is the radius. `PrivateArea.m_radius` (:137132) is a plain public compiled field with a class default of 10f, overridden per-prefab in the Unity Inspector, never written to any ZDO. There is no networked value. Options: (a) read it from the server's own prefab table at OnWorldReady — `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.GetComponent<PrivateArea>()?.m_radius` — which works if the server's prefab table is populated (Wonderland's ContainerRegistry and StructureUpkeep both enumerate `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` server-side and find real components, so this is very likely); (b) fall back to a per-prefab config value.

Building the index: wards are ordinary sector-filed ZDOs, so use `ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(prefabName, list, ref index)` (:77442) — a time-budgeted resumable scan (~400 non-empty sectors per call across a 262144-slot array) — or better, Wonderland's `PrefabSetSweeper` which walks `m_objectsBySector` once against a HashSet of prefab hashes with an explicit sector budget (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135-153), because the name-based scanner re-walks the whole array per prefab. Deduplicate: the iterative scanner re-scans `m_objectsBySector[0]` on its terminal call (:77445-77455), and sector 0 is both zone (-256,-256) and the out-of-range fallback bucket (`ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` :115755-115774). Keep the index as `List<(Vector3 centre, float radius, long creator, bool enabled, HashSet<long> permitted)>` and refresh it incrementally: a full resweep every few minutes, plus immediate updates from the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix whenever a ward-prefab ZDO arrives or changes.

Query: `WardCovers(portalPos, playerId)` → any indexed ward with `enabled && DistanceXZ(centre, portalPos) < radius` (mirroring `PrivateArea.IsInside`, :137707-137710) and `creator == playerId || permitted.Contains(playerId)`. Feed that into the Tag Watchdog's policy chain: a retag of a portal inside somebody's enabled ward, by an account whose notarised playerId is not the creator and not on the permitted list, is DENIED and reverted.

Be honest about the trust chain: the ward's permitted list is written by `RPC_TogglePermitted` (:137399-137412), which **ignores its routed-RPC `uid` entirely** and acts on the payload `playerID` — so any client can add any playerID to any un-enabled ward. And `RPC_ToggleEnabled` (:137414-137421) gates only on `m_piece.GetCreator() == playerID`, also from the payload. Hardening `m_senderPeerID` accomplishes nothing for these two. The ward list is therefore only as trustworthy as the Creator Attestation makes the underlying `s_creator`, plus whatever cross-check you add in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix when a ward's permitted list changes.
catalog.playerExperience: A stranger wanders into your walled compound, walks past the guard stone, and tries to rename your `mine` portal to `lol`. The tag flips for a heartbeat and snaps back; they get `This gate is inside a ward you are not permitted to use.` Your clanmate, whom you added to the guard stone last week, renames the same portal to `deepmine` and it sticks — because their playerID is in `pu_id3` on the ward's ZDO and the server read it. Outside any ward, the same stranger can rename the same portal freely, which is exactly vanilla's own rule, honestly reproduced.
failureModes: **`PrivateArea.CheckAccess` is an allow-all on a dedicated server** (m_allAreas empty, :137173/:137197/:137547). Any code that calls it as an authorization check silently permits everything. This is the single most dangerous trap in the whole access-control area.
`m_radius` is Inspector data (:137132). A wrong value under-covers or over-covers every ward on the server.

`RPC_TogglePermitted` ignores the sender and gates only on `!IsEnabled()` (:137399-137412) — the permitted list itself is attacker-writable on any disabled ward. The shadow index inherits that weakness.
A ward whose `m_ownerFaction != 0` is a different code path entirely (`PrivateArea.Interact` early-returns, :137376) and should be excluded from the index.

Ward ZDOs are ordinary sector ZDOs and are **not** resident world-wide the way portals are; the scan only finds ones currently in `m_objectsBySector`. A ward in a never-visited region may be missing from the index until a peer's ghost-zone generation creates it.

The index goes stale between resweeps — a ward destroyed or newly permitted mid-interval produces wrong decisions. Drive incremental updates off `ZDO.Deserialize` and `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` (:76033).
openQuestions: What is the shipped `m_radius` on the guard_stone prefab? Class default is 10f but the Inspector overrides it. IN-GAME CHECK: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("guard_stone").GetComponent<PrivateArea>().m_radius` on the dedicated server at OnWorldReady; if the prefab table is empty, binary-search the refusal distance in-game.

What is the exact guard_stone prefab name (and are there other PrivateArea-bearing prefabs)? IN-GAME CHECK: enumerate `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` server-side for anything with a PrivateArea component and log names plus radii.

Is `m_enabledByDefault` false on guard_stone (i.e. is a freshly placed ward inactive until the creator interacts)? That decides whether newly placed wards protect anything. IN-GAME CHECK: place one and read `s_enabled` server-side.
corrections: Reproduce vanilla's exact rule: CheckAccess (wardCheck=false, :137565-137580) is OR over covering wards — access is DENIED only when at least one enabled ward covers the point AND none of the covering wards grants (creator or permitted). Phrase the query as `covering = enabled && DistanceXZ < radius; denied = covering.Any() && !covering.Any(grants(playerId))`, not 'any ward denies'.

The identity to test is the profile playerID long (what Piece.SetCreator and pu_id store; readable from the peer's character ZDO via ZDOVars.s_playerID :78539), not the Steam hostname. Mapping peer → playerID is client-reported and belongs to Creator Attestation.

RPC_TogglePermitted is IsOwner-gated (:137401): on the wire it is only the ward-owning client that applies it, so 'any client can add any playerID' is true for a modified owner or a modified client pushing the ward ZDO directly (RPC_ZDOData has no ownership check, :77076-77137), not for an arbitrary vanilla sender.
Line refs: m_allAreas is declared at :137176 (not :137173); Awake registration at :137198.
GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative's terminal call also scans m_portalObjects (:77457-77469), irrelevant for wards but worth knowing when reusing it.

Mirror vanilla's any-ward-grants semantics (:137565-137579): DENY only when ≥1 enabled ward covers the portal AND none of the enabled covering wards has the player as creator or permitted. A stricter 'any covering ward denies' rule would reject renames vanilla allows.

Identity for the permitted/creator check is the profile playerID (Piece.IsCreator :136433-136437, HaveLocalAccess :137595-137606), not a platform id; the Creator Attestation must map account → playerID.

Reframe the player experience: vanilla clients already enforce this gate client-side in TeleportWorld.Interact (:143477-143481) with a populated m_allAreas, so for unmodified players the index changes nothing visible. The snap-back scenario only occurs against a modified client that skipped CheckAccess. Vanilla value = audit and cross-check of ward tampering.

m_radius must be read from the server's prefab (ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs is enumerable server-side per Wonderland ContainerRegistry.cs:35) or config; the class default 10f (:137132) is not the guard stone's shipped radius.
evidence: Wonderland PrefabSetSweeper / prefab-table reads — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135-160, Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:35-64, Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:53-59
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The vacuous-allow claim is confirmed: PrivateArea.CheckAccess (:137547-137592) iterates the static m_allAreas (:137176), populated only in Awake (:137198) on a live GameObject; with an empty list it sets flag=false, list stays empty, and `if (!flag && list.Count > 0)` fails, so it returns true. HaveLocalAccess depends on Player.m_localPlayer (:137595-137606). The ZDO layout is exactly as described: SetPermittedPlayers/GetPermittedPlayers use s_permitted plus `pu_id`+i / `pu_name`+i with id==0 skipped (:137338-137363); IsEnabled reads s_enabled (:137423-137430); Setup writes s_creatorName (:137446-137449); Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator IsOwner-gated and only when creator==0 (:136415-136420); m_radius is a plain compiled field defaulting to 10f (:137132); IsInside is DistanceXZ < m_radius + radius (:137707-137710). RPC_TogglePermitted ignores its `uid` and acts on the payload playerID, gated on IsOwner && !IsEnabled (:137399-137412); RPC_ToggleEnabled gates on payload playerID == creator (:137414-137421). GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative exists with the ~400-sector budget and the terminal-call rescan of m_objectsBySector[0] (:77442-77494, :77445-77455), and SectorToIndex clamps out-of-range to sector 0 (:115760-115773). Server prefab-table reads are precedented in Wonderland. One semantic correction on the access rule and one on identity.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: CheckAccess iterates static m_allAreas (:137173, :137547-137592), appended only in Awake (:137197), so on the dedicated server it returns true vacuously (flag=false, list empty → `!flag && list.Count > 0` false → return true). Ward state is fully in the ZDO: s_enabled (:78423, IsEnabled :137423), s_permitted + "pu_id"+i / "pu_name"+i (:78529, :137338-137362), s_creator/s_creatorName (:78393-78397, Piece.SetCreator :136415, Setup :137446). m_radius is a compiled field (:137132), never in the ZDO. IsInside is DistanceXZ < m_radius + radius (:137707-137710). RPC_TogglePermitted ignores uid, gated only on IsOwner && !IsEnabled (:137399-137412); RPC_ToggleEnabled gates on payload playerID == creator (:137414-137421). GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative rescans m_objectsBySector[0] on its terminal call (:77445-77455) and SectorToIndex clamps out-of-range to 0 (:115755-115774). Two corrections. (1) Rule fidelity: vanilla grants access if ANY enabled covering ward gives local access (flag=true wins over other covering wards that deny, :137565-137579). The option's WardCovers wording is ambiguous for overlapping wards; the server rule must be DENY iff at least one enabled ward covers the point AND no enabled covering ward lists the player as creator or permitted. Identity is the profile playerID (Piece.IsCreator compares s_creator to Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID(), :136433-136437), not a platform id. (2) Value against vanilla clients is audit only: TeleportWorld.Interact already refuses the rename dialog client-side when CheckAccess fails (:143477-143481), and on a real client m_allAreas contains every instantiated ward, which for any ward covering a loaded portal is always loaded (≤ ward radius away). The described player experience — a stranger's tag flipping then snapping back — happens only with a MODIFIED client; a vanilla stranger never sees the box. The index is therefore a modified-client countermeasure and an audit source, not a change to what vanilla players experience. Radius from the server prefab table is plausible (Wonderland enumerates ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs server-side, ContainerRegistry.cs:35) but the actual prefab value is Inspector data, not in the decompile; keep the config fallback.

catalog.name: Portal ACL
catalog.oneLine: An explicit per-portal and per-network permission list held in the Portal Record Store — owner, co-owners, network members, and a lock flag — decoupled from wards so it works anywhere.
catalog.howItWorks:
The Shadow Ward Index reuses vanilla's permission model and inherits its weaknesses; a first-class ACL is cleaner and fully server-authoritative in its *storage*, even though its *enforcement* is still revert-based unless paired with the Ownership Pin.

Record shape (Portal Record Store, one entry per rounded position):
```
{ owner: PlatformUserID, ownerProfileId: long,
  coOwners: [PlatformUserID], network: string, lock: none|retag|relink|full,
  approvedTag: string, approvedPartner: PosKey|null,
  claimedAt: ticks, lastRetagAt: ticks, retagCount: int }
```
Mirror the essentials into mod-private ZDO keys (`tp_owner`, `tp_net`, `tp_lock`) for locality, exactly as described in Portal Record Store, and treat the file as authoritative on any disagreement.

The policy chain the Tag Watchdog calls, in order, for a proposed tag or connection change on portal P by notarised account A:
1. `A` is in `ZNet.instance.m_adminList` → ALLOW (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811).
2. `P.lock == full`, or `lock == retag` for a tag change, or `lock == relink` for a connection change → DENY.
3. `A == P.owner` or `A ∈ P.coOwners` → ALLOW.
4. `P.network != null` and `A` is a member of that network's roster → ALLOW (see Team/Guild Networks).
5. Shadow Ward Index says a ward covering P permits A → ALLOW.
6. `P.owner == null` (never claimed) → ALLOW and claim for A.
7. Otherwise DENY and revert.

Player-facing mutation of the ACL has exactly one reliable channel on a vanilla client: emotes. `ZDOVars.s_emote` / `s_emoteID` / `s_emoteOneshot` are written into the character's own ZDO by `Player.StartEmote` (:15585-15598) and polled server-side at 0.25s by Wonderland's EmoteSignals (EmoteSignals.cs:46), which is the CacheClaimControl pattern (CacheClaimControl.cs:16). Chat is **not** a channel: `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each *other* listed player individually (:41975-42043), so a solo player generates zero packets, and `Chat.InputText` runs unknown slash commands locally with `silentFail` (:41947-41955). Map pings are a second channel and carry a world coordinate: `Chat.SendPing` broadcasts `"ChatMessage"` at `targetPeerID = 0` (:42058-42068) with no permission gate and no player-count dependency, so the server always receives them — usable for "lock the portal nearest where I pinged".

So: stand at your portal, `/point` to claim it, `/wave` to toggle its lock, `/challenge` while another player stands within N metres to add them as a co-owner. Feedback via `PlayerNotify.Toast` (PlayerNotify.cs:15 → the routed `"Message"` RPC on the player's own character ZDO, registered in `Player.Start` :10072, handled at :14820-14825).
catalog.playerExperience: You build a portal, stand in front of it, and `/point`. A toast reads `Gate claimed — Bjorn's Gate. Only you can rename it.` A friend stands next to you; you `/challenge` and get `Added Elin as co-owner of this gate.` A stranger later tries to rename it: the name flickers and reverts, and they get `That gate belongs to Bjorn.` You `/wave` and get `Gate unlocked — anyone may rename it.` None of this needs a client mod; the whole interface is the vanilla emote wheel plus the vanilla toast HUD.
failureModes: Revert-based, not preventive, unless the locked portal is also Ownership-Pinned. With the pin, `lock == full` becomes genuinely unbypassable; without it, there is always a one-tick window.

Emote commands are a coarse interface: 25 vanilla emotes (Emotes enum :6216-6246), no arguments, and any of them might be used innocently. Require proximity to a portal plus a confirmation emote for destructive actions.

The claimed account is the notarised one only if Creator Attestation ran; for pre-existing portals the owner must be inferred from `s_creator`, which may be 0 for anything world-generated or admin-spawned (`Piece.IsPlacedByPlayer` :136443).
A player who never claims their portal leaves it open under rule 6 — decide deliberately whether unclaimed means open or owner-by-`s_creator`.
Emote polling at 0.25s across all connected characters is cheap, but `ConnectedCharacters.All()` allocates a fresh list per call; reuse a buffer.
openQuestions: Are all 25 emotes reachable from the vanilla emote wheel on both mouse and gamepad, or is the wheel a subset with the rest only typeable? IN-GAME CHECK: open the wheel on a vanilla client and count entries against the enum at :6216-6246.

Does a map ping's reported y-coordinate (forced to the pinger's own y, :42058-42068) cause mis-selection when picking the nearest portal? IN-GAME CHECK: ping from a mountain above a valley portal and log the resolved nearest portal.
corrections: Revert must also restore the pairing: RPC_SetTag clears the retagged portal's connection (:143590) and its partner's via RPC_SetConnected (:143612-143633); a tag-only revert leaves both unconnected until vanilla re-pairs randomly on its 5s tick. Pair with the Managed Network Governor's approvedPartner re-assert or accept a re-roll.

There is a leak window of up to one vanilla ConnectPortals tick (5s) plus watchdog latency during which the victim portal can be paired into the stranger's tag group; state this in playerExperience instead of 'the name flickers and reverts'.

'Zero packets for solo chat' depends on PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider != null (:42002-42006); when it is null the message is sent to 0L (broadcast) and DOES reach the server. Verify per platform; not provable from these assemblies.

Server-session ownership of a portal silently drops every vanilla RPC_SetTag (no ZNetView instance server-side, HandleRoutedRPC :83656-83663) — a free hard lock, but ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) re-assigns it within 2s of any player entering the active area unless ZDO.SetOwner is guarded (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern).
s_tagauthor is client-written and untrusted; derive the actor from the ZDO owner uid at the time the change arrived, mapped to the peer socket host name for IsAdmin.

StartEmote refuses while !CanMove, InAttack, IsDrawingBow, IsAttached or IsAttachedToShip (:15587) — emote commands are unavailable while sitting on a chair/ship or mid-swing; two emotes inside one 0.25s poll window collapse to the last one (only s_emoteID/s_emote values are observed).
"Message" RPC is registered in Player.Awake (method starts :10032, registration :10072), not Player.Start.

Chat.InputText (:41947-41955) calls TryRunCommand(text, this) at :41953; the only overload is TryRunCommand(string text, bool silentFail = false, bool skipAllowedCheck = false) (:45734) — silentFail is true only because UnityEngine.Object's implicit bool conversion of `this` is used. The conclusion (unknown slash commands fail silently) holds, but the mechanism is that decompiler quirk.

Map pings reach ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC on the server (:83647-83655, ZDO-less branch), but a dedicated server registers no "ChatMessage" handler — Chat.Awake (:41626) only runs where a Chat component exists. The mod must ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3,int,UserInfo,string>("ChatMessage", …) itself or prefix HandleRoutedRPC. Also note HandleRoutedRPC passes the payload m_senderPeerID (spoofable, :83651); attribution must come from the ZRpc in RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632).
ZNet.m_adminList is a private SyncedList (:79101); use the public ZNet.IsAdmin(string hostName) (:81811) rather than reading the list.

With ≥2 players online, chat packets DO transit the server (RPC_RoutedRPC → RouteRPC :83636-83644) and could be sniffed by a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC; the 'not a reliable channel' verdict stands only because solo players emit nothing.

Reverts are a race, not a block: RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137) applies any client write with a higher DataRevision (including tag and tagauthor via Deserialize :74206-74240), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, portals included via FindObjects :77376) re-hands server-claimed ownership to a nearby peer within 2 s. State this explicitly instead of 'fully server-authoritative in its storage'.

The design is correctly labelled reactive: the server cannot block a write, only revert it. Both are inherent to the reactive model and do not change the enforcement label. Minor cite errors noted below.

catalog.name: Managed Network Governor
catalog.oneLine: Replace vanilla's random same-tag pairing with a server-authored topology that is re-asserted every tick — the only real defence against a stranger linking into your private network, and the only way to build rings, hubs and one-way routes.
catalog.howItWorks:
Vanilla's pairing is an open lottery. `Game.ConnectPortals()` (:100589-100627), run every 5s from `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` (:100580) started only under `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (:100073-100074), does two passes over a fresh `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` snapshot: phase 1 breaks any connection whose partner is missing, whose `s_tag` differs, or whose own connection is None (:100596-100605); phase 2 pairs each still-unconnected portal with a **uniformly random** same-tag partner via `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679, `UnityEngine.Random.Range` at :100678). Anyone who learns your tag string and plants a portal with it becomes a candidate for your network on the next tick.

The governor takes the decision away. Two levels:

**(a) Minimal — postfix `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal`.** Bind with `AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")` and overwrite `__result` with a deterministic, policy-approved choice (nearest same-network partner; the Portal Record Store's `approvedPartner`; null to refuse pairing outright for an unauthorised portal). Lowest risk: vanilla's two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging all stay intact.

**(b) Full — prefix `Game.ConnectPortals` returning false, and run your own pass.** Then you own the whole topology. Reimplement faithfully or you will introduce bugs vanilla already avoids: the `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` two-phase commit (added at :100681-100688, force-committed at the top of the next call by `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` :100690-100698) exists because a connection write delegated to an owning client leaves the server's own copy reading None, which would otherwise let the same portal be paired twice in one pass (`IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guards at :100609 and :100671).

Write primitive, copying `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651) exactly: if the portal is unowned, or its owner is not a connected peer, or you want force — `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);`. Otherwise route the vanilla `RPC_SetConnection` (registered on every peer at :100066, handler :100653) to the owner. For managed portals, prefer the Ownership Pin so the immediate local path is always taken.

What topologies are actually stable, and what is not:
- **Non-reciprocal links survive at runtime.** Phase 1 never checks that the partner points back (:100600-100604). Rings (A→B→C→A), one-way chains, hub fan-in and even self-loops (A→A) are indefinitely stable *provided every member shares one byte-identical tag string and no member's connection is None*.
- **None of them survive a save/reload.** The disk format collapses each ZDO to a single `ZDOConnectionHashData{type, int hash}` slot: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75460-75478, called from `PrepareSave` :75480-75491) gives the source `{Portal, h}` and the target `{Portal|Target, h}`, so a ring >2 loses a link, a one-way link comes back **bidirectional** via `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals`'s hash-matching relink (:77850-77893, which writes reciprocal connections at :77879-77885), and a self-loop is **erased** because the same key is written twice (:75471-75475). Every managed topology must be re-asserted by the mod after every world load. The load-time window is ideal: `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76474-76531) puts every portal in memory before any peer connects, `ZDO.Load` leaves every ZDO unowned (:74550-74556), and the load-time `Game.ConnectPortals()` at :76523 runs with `m_peers` empty so every write takes the immediate local path.
- A ZDO holds **exactly one** connection (`ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` with a single readonly target, :74797, :75524-75534). A simultaneous multi-destination hub is structurally impossible; only time-sliced rotation works.
- Never write `Portal|Target` (0x10|0x01) onto a live portal — `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` requires exact type equality (:75094-75102) and vanilla would read it as unconnected and re-pair it.

The governor is the piece that makes `network` membership in the Portal ACL mean something: an unauthorised portal carrying your tag is simply never given a partner, and is optionally re-tagged to `""` by the watchdog.
catalog.playerExperience: Your clan's four portals all read `⌁VALHALLA`. A stranger builds a fifth portal, somehow learns the tag, and sets it. Under vanilla he would have a 1-in-4 chance of being wired into your base on the next 5-second tick. Under the governor his portal simply never connects — the hover text reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` forever — while your four stay wired in exactly the ring you configured: front gate → mine → swamp outpost → mountain camp → front gate. After a server restart the ring is still a ring, because the mod rebuilt it from its own records before the first player logged in.
failureModes: A prefix returning false on `Game.ConnectPortals` disables vanilla pairing for **every** portal on the server, including unmanaged player ones. Either reimplement pairing for them faithfully or scope the override with the postfix-on-FindRandomUnconnectedPortal approach.

Dangling connections are dropped at save time independently of the runtime reconcile: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` only persists a connection when both endpoint ZDOs resolve in `m_objectsByID` (:75461-75478). A managed link to a destroyed portal silently disappears across a restart.

Vanilla caches raw `ZDO` object references in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` for a full 5s, and `ZDOPool.Release` recycles ZDO objects on destruction (:76990, :78286-78311, `ZDO.Reset` sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` at :73536-73545). **Hard rule for your own code: cache ZDOIDs, never ZDO objects, across ticks.**

3+ portals on one tag permanently strand exactly one member under vanilla, and which one is arbitrary (dictionary bucket order, unstable across restarts). If you leave vanilla pairing in place for unmanaged portals, you inherit this.

`ZDO.SetConnection` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns, :74951-74961), so re-asserting a correct topology every tick is free — but a 'touch to force clients to re-read' idiom needs `ForceSendZDO`, not a re-Set.

`TargetFound()` requires the client to actually hold the destination ZDO, not just its id (:143640-143655); after a server-side re-pair to a distant portal the first walk-through fails **silently** (gate 1 returns with no message) while `RequestZDO` fetches it. Plan for a one-transit warm-up, or pre-push with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, targetId)` (:77714).
openQuestions: Does `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` actually stop it? `StartCoroutine` was called with the string overload (:100074) so Unity semantics say yes, but that is not a decompile fact. IN-GAME CHECK: call it, place two same-tag portals, and watch for the absence of `[ Connected N portals ]` log lines.

Does a client cleanly handle a portal whose connection target is a ZDO it cannot instantiate (a pure destination anchor)? `TargetFound` needs only a non-null ZDO and `Teleport` reads only position/rotation (:143539-143548), but `ZNetScene` will still try to create an object for it. IN-GAME CHECK: point a portal at an anchor ZDO with an existing harmless prefab hash and with an unregistered hash, and watch the client log.

Is `WaitForSeconds(5f)` affected by any server-side time-scale manipulation during the sleep/time-skip path (`Game.UpdateSleeping` :100712)? IN-GAME CHECK: trigger a sleep skip and measure the interval between `[ Connected N portals ]` lines.
corrections: Enforcement: server-enforced against vanilla clients only. Against a modified client the connection field is writable ZDO data (ZDO.Deserialize :74219-74224; RPC_ZDOData :77076-77140 has no owner/socket check) and its local TeleportWorld honours its own copy — the governor is reactive there.

Ownership Pin needs a Harmony guard on ZDO.SetOwner (or a prefix on ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS); otherwise server ownership is lost within 2s of any peer entering the active area (:76874, :76901-76926) and SetConnection takes the delegated RPC path.

Level (a) (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix) cannot produce rings, chains or one-way links — phase 2 writes and force-commits both directions (:100614-100615, :100692-100694) — and cannot break an already-connected unauthorised pair. Non-pairwise topologies require level (b) or an override pass after vanilla's.

Load-time order: ZDOMan.LoadChunks calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() at :76523 after the hash relink; ring members that lost their link on save are randomly re-paired there (immediate path, no peers). Re-assert in a postfix on LoadChunks (or later in ZNet world load), not before it.
Save collapse also affects the mod's own record store only if keyed by ZDOID — ZDO.Load regenerates every ZDOID (:74511 m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)); key records by rounded position.

Approach (a) (postfix FindRandomUnconnectedPortal) cannot build rings, one-way routes or hubs: phase 2 always writes both directions (SetConnection(item2, zDO2) and SetConnection(zDO2, item2), :100615-100616). Every non-reciprocal topology requires approach (b). State this explicitly.

Approach (a) also never inspects already-connected portals. A protocol-level client can write A→X and X→A directly through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137; connections applied by ZDO.Deserialize :74228-74233, no owner/prefab check) — such a link passes phase 1 (same tag, non-None target) and is never re-examined. Only approach (b) with an every-tick re-assertion against the record store catches it, and there is still up to one tick (5 s) of exposure. Against a vanilla client the governor is airtight; against a forged client it is 're-asserted every 5 s', not 'never connects'.

RPC_SetConnection registration is at :100067 (block :100062-100069), not :100066. On a dedicated server the handler is only ever reached by an inbound client packet: the server's own InvokeRoutedRPC to an owner peer never self-dispatches (:83576-83583), so any inbound RPC_SetConnection is illegitimate — see Ungated RPC Hardening.

Ring save collapse is worse than 'loses a link': with the dictionary iteration A→B, B→C, C→A the hash data ends A={Portal|Target,h3}, B={Portal,h2}, C={Portal,h3}; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks only C↔A, so a 3-ring reloads as one mutual pair plus an orphan. Rings of any size collapse to a partial perfect matching.

'Ownership Pin' cannot be assumed: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925) iterates FindObjects, which includes m_portalObjects (:77376), and IsInPeerActiveArea(point, m_sessionID) tests against the 1e6 reference position (:76887-76890) — server ownership of any real-world portal is re-handed to a nearby peer within 2 s. Writes still land without a pin (SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision :74627-74633; the ex-owner client stops writing once it sees the new owner), so the pin is only needed to make RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove undeliverable, and needs its own patch.

A vanilla client retagging any ring member calls UpdateConnection(Portal, None) on its own portal (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :143583-143597); phase 1 then unwinds the ring one link per tick (each member whose target reads None is cleared). The mod's re-assert must run on the same tick (e.g. in the ConnectPortals prefix) to avoid transient dead gates.
