Non-reciprocal runtime stability holds because phase 1 never looks back. The server-enforced label is right in the route sense: a vanilla client can only teleport when its own ZDO copy carries a server-written connection (TeleportWorld.TargetFound :143640-143655, Teleport :143517-143543). Corrections: approach (a) cannot produce the advertised topologies and neither approach withstands a protocol-level client without periodic full re-assertion.

catalog.name: Anti-Grief Tag Integrity
catalog.oneLine: First-claim registry, whitespace/homoglyph normalisation, and orphan-starvation detection — the three concrete defences against tag squatting, stranger-linking and the 3-portals-one-tag denial attack.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three distinct griefing vectors, each with its own mechanism.

**(1) Tag squatting.** Tag comparison is bare `string !=` on `ZDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with `""` default — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, no trimming (`Game.ConnectPortals` :100601, `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` :100669). So `farm`, `Farm`, `farm ` and `fаrm` (Cyrillic а) are four different networks, and a griefer can register a visually identical tag to confuse, or occupy your tag to steal a pairing slot. Defence: a **first-claim registry** in the Portal Record Store mapping `normalisedTag → { firstClaimant: PlatformUserID, claimedAt: ticks, memberPositions: [...] }`. Normalisation for *collision detection only* (never for the stored value, which must stay byte-exact or vanilla will unpair it): trim, casefold with `ToLowerInvariant`, strip zero-width characters, map a configured homoglyph table. When the Tag Watchdog sees a tag change into a normalised bucket already claimed by a different account, and the ACL chain does not otherwise ALLOW, revert and audit. Also reject outright, by policy, any tag with leading/trailing whitespace or a zero-width character — there is no legitimate use and it is the cheapest confusion attack available.

**(2) Stranger linking into a private network.** Fully solved only by the Managed Network Governor, which refuses to give an unauthorised same-tag portal any partner at all. The registry above is the data it consults. Note that without the governor, a faster mod timer does **not** reliably win the race — vanilla's tick is 5s and its phase-2 pairing is one atomic pass; you must either own the pairing decision or accept intermittent leakage.

**(3) The 3-portals-one-tag orphan attack.** This is a real, cheap denial-of-service and it deserves naming. With N portals sharing one tag and all unconnected, vanilla pairs greedily in dictionary-bucket order: the first-iterated portal picks uniformly at random from the others; the next unpaired portal finds its remaining candidates already excluded (either non-None or in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`) and is **permanently orphaned** — subsequent ticks re-confirm the surviving pair, so the orphan never rotates in. `N` odd ⇒ `floor(N/2)` pairs and exactly one permanent orphan. So an attacker who plants a single portal with your tag has a coin-flip chance of stranding one of your gates forever, and the strand is sticky. Worse, which member is orphaned depends on `Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` enumeration order and is **not stable across restarts** (`ZDOMan.GetPortalList` :77648-77656; `ZoneSystem.SectorIndex.GetHashCode` returns the raw sector, :113114-113117), so the victim changes after every reboot.
  Detection is free and needs no new bookkeeping: on each watchdog tick, group `GetPortalList()` by exact `s_tag`, and flag any group with an odd count, or any group containing a portal with `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` while ≥2 others in the group are paired. Report it in the Heartbeat line (`"47 portals, 3 orphaned tags, 2 managed rings intact"`) and in the admin report. Remediation is the governor: an explicit topology has no orphans by construction, and an intruding portal is excluded from the group rather than competing for a slot.

A fourth, related vector worth covering: the **empty tag**. `ZDO.GetString` defaults to `""` and never null (`ZDOExtraData.GetString` :75079-75082), so every untagged portal in the world is one giant tag group and a freshly placed untagged portal auto-pairs with a random untagged portal anywhere on the map. That is vanilla behaviour, not an attack, but it produces exactly the same "why is my new portal connected to a stranger's basement" reports, and the governor should treat `""` as a special group that is never auto-paired.
catalog.playerExperience: You notice your `mine` portal has gone dark. The admin report says `TAG GROUP "mine": 3 portals, 1 orphaned — intruder at (1204, 8, -3312) placed by Steam:7656… 14 minutes ago`. With the governor enabled it never happens in the first place: the intruder's portal reads `unconnected` permanently and your pair is untouched. A player who tries to claim `farm ` (trailing space) while you own `farm` gets `That name is too close to an existing network.` and the tag reverts.
failureModes: Normalisation is for *detection only*. Writing a normalised value back into `s_tag` changes the network identity under vanilla's ordinal comparison and will unpair legitimately-connected portals.
Homoglyph tables are never complete. Treat the registry as reducing, not eliminating, confusion attacks.
Orphan detection by odd-count produces false positives for a solo portal a player has simply not built the partner for yet. Require ≥3 in the group before flagging.
Which member is orphaned changes across restarts (bucket order), so an admin comparing two reports will see the "victim" move. State this in the report text or it reads as a bug in the mod.
Reverting a squatted tag on a portal the squatter owns loses a DataRevision race unless you also pin ownership briefly.
Without the Managed Network Governor, none of this stops the actual linking — it only reports it.
citations: Game.ConnectPortals ordinal tag comparison and teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100606 (:100601)
Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal candidate filter and random pick — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 (:100671, :100678)
Wonderland Heartbeat summary shape — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Heartbeat.cs:21
openQuestions: Does the hover label render zero-width and RTL-override characters, or does `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459) already strip some of them? IN-GAME CHECK: server-write tags containing U+200B, U+202E and a Cyrillic homoglyph and screenshot the hover text on a vanilla client.

With 3 same-tag portals, is the orphan genuinely permanent across many ticks, or does any path re-shuffle it? IN-GAME CHECK: place 3 same-tag portals, leave the server running an hour, and log the connection state every minute.
corrections: The 3-portals-one-tag attack cannot break an already-connected pair: phase 1 (:100596-100605) preserves it and the intruder orphans itself. Reword to: the intruder wins a slot only at a re-pairing moment (victim retag, destroy/rebuild, or a connection written after the last save and lost), where it has a chance proportional to enumeration order/random pick.

The orphan does NOT rotate across restarts for connected pairs — ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) relinks saved pairs by hash before Game.ConnectPortals (:76523). Remove the 'victim changes after every reboot' claim.
Attribute enumeration order to Dictionary insertion order (chunk/sector load order), not SectorIndex.GetHashCode (:113114-113117); the hash only affects bucketing, not enumeration.
Drop the 'odd count ⇒ flag' rule (false positive for every lone portal); keep 'None member while ≥2 same-tag members are paired'.

Vanilla client tag entry is capped at 10 characters (TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10), :143480); a modified client can exceed it — reject over-length tags in the same policy check.

Vector (3) cannot break an existing pair. Phase 1 (:100596-100605) never tears down a same-tag pair whose target has a non-None connection, and phase 2 (:100607-100622) only considers portals whose own connection is None. An intruder placed against an already-connected pair orphans only itself. The DoS bites only when the victim's portals are unconnected at the same time as the intruder's (victim retags, rebuilds, or adds a third gate): then the first-iterated portal picks uniformly among the rest, so P(a victim gate is orphaned) ≈ 2/3 (intruder iterated first → 100 %, victim first → 50 %), not a 'coin flip' against an established network.

'Not stable across restarts / the victim changes after every reboot' is wrong. Mutual pairs survive the save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 leaves the pair as {Portal,h}/{Portal|Target,h} with equal h) and are relinked by ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) at :76515, before Game.instance.ConnectPortals runs at :76523 — so the previously-paired portals come back paired and the orphan stays the orphan. Dictionary enumeration order only decides which portal is iterated first in a fresh lottery.

Vanilla tags are capped at 10 characters by TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) in TeleportWorld.Interact (:143481) — client-side only; server-side nothing bounds tag length, so normalisation must also handle arbitrarily long strings from forged clients.
Detection line cites are fine; ZoneSystem.SectorIndex.GetHashCode returning the raw sector is at :113114-113117 as claimed, but it is irrelevant to orphan choice for the reason above.
Reverts share the ACL's race: RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137) accepts any higher-revision client write and ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925) hands ownership back within 2 s; a revert loop, not a block.
evidence: Game.ConnectPortals phase-1 predicate and phase-2 pairing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100596-100622
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] (1) Ordinal, untrimmed tag comparison verified: `zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string` (:100601) and `!(portal.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != tag)` (:100669); ZDOExtraData.GetString defaults to "" (:75079-75082). Normalisation-for-detection with byte-exact storage is sound. (2) Correct: the governor is the only real fix. (4) Empty-tag group verified: ConnectPortals never special-cases "", so untagged portals pair with each other. (3) The orphan-attack narrative is overstated. Phase 1 (:100596-100605) keeps any pair whose partner exists, has the same tag and a non-None connection; a newly planted same-tag portal therefore NEVER displaces an existing connected pair — it finds zero candidates in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100669-100671, both members non-None) and orphans itself. The 'coin-flip' only exists at a re-pairing moment: when a victim retags (RPC_SetTag clears its own and its partner's connection, :143590-143597, :143612-143633), rebuilds, or the pair failed to reach disk. 'Not stable across restarts' is also wrong for connected pairs: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks saved pairs by hash at load (:77850-77893) before Game.ConnectPortals runs (:76515-76523), so the same orphan stays orphaned after a reboot. Dictionary enumeration order in .NET follows entry insertion order (not GetHashCode), so the 'bucket order' explanation is wrong even though the conclusion (order-dependent) holds. Detection heuristic: 'any group with an odd count' is a false positive for every solo portal legitimately waiting for its partner; the second predicate (a None member while ≥2 others are paired) is the useful one. Enforcement label is honest.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Tag comparison is bare ordinal string inequality on ZDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) with "" default — confirmed at Game.ConnectPortals :100601 and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669, ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082. Empty-tag portals form one global group with no exclusion anywhere in phase 2 — confirmed. Odd-count orphan is real: phase 2 pairs greedily and phase 1 only breaks pairs on missing/mismatched/None targets, so an orphan never rotates in. Detection by grouping GetPortalList (:77648-77656) is sound. But the threat model for vector (3) is overstated: an intruder cannot displace an existing valid pair, and the orphan is stable across restarts, so the 'coin-flip against your gates' and 'victim changes every reboot' claims are refuted while the mechanism itself is confirmed.

catalog.name: Destroy Veto
catalog.oneLine: A prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` that refuses to delete a protected portal — a genuine, unbypassable server-side veto, because unlike every other portal RPC this one actually executes on the dedicated server.
catalog.howItWorks:
`ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage pkg)` (:76953-76961, registered in the ZDOMan constructor at :76155) is a **ZDO-less** routed RPC. Its `m_targetZDO` is `ZDOID.None`, so `HandleRoutedRPC` takes the `m_functions` branch at :83648-83654 rather than the `FindInstance` branch — meaning it runs on the dedicated server for real. It reads a count and that many ZDOIDs and calls `HandleDestroyedZDO(uid)` on each, with **no sender check, no ownership check and no prefab check** (:76963-76999). Any client speaking the vanilla protocol can broadcast a forged DestroyZDO and permanently delete any portal in the world. This is a pre-existing hole, and it is also the cleanest enforcement point in the whole design.

The veto: a Harmony **prefix** on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`. Because the package is consumed by reading, work on a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`), enumerate the ZDOIDs, and for each resolve `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` and test `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` (:100021). If none of them is a protected portal, return true and let vanilla run. If any is, you must not simply return false (that would drop legitimate destructions batched in the same packet) — instead return false and re-dispatch the permitted subset yourself by calling `HandleDestroyedZDO` (private, `AccessTools.Method`) for each allowed id. Consult the Portal ACL chain with the Authentic Sender Context: an admin, the owner, or a ward-permitted account may destroy; anyone else is refused, audited, and toasted.

Second layer, non-Harmony: `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` is a **public `Action<ZDO>` field** (:76033) invoked from `HandleDestroyedZDO` at :76975-76978, *before* the ZDO is removed from `m_objectsByID`, so the ZDO is still fully readable in the callback. `ZNetScene.Awake` already combines onto it (:81953). Subscribe to it for audit and for record-store pruning even when you allow the destroy.

Third layer, for the gap the veto does **not** cover: destruction by damage. `WearNTear.Damage` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_Damage", hit)` routes to the ZDO owner (:150315-150321), and `RPC_Damage`/`RPC_Remove` are `IsOwner()`-gated (:150332, :150419-150425). A dedicated server has no instance, so it can neither observe nor veto a damage-driven destruction on a client-owned portal — it only sees the resulting health write in `RPC_ZDOData` and, eventually, the DestroyZDO broadcast (which the veto *does* catch, since the destroying client must route it through the server). The Ownership Pin closes this gap completely by making both RPCs undeliverable.

Recovery, if a protected portal is destroyed anyway: the Portal Record Store holds its position, rotation, tag and owner, so the mod can recreate it — `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` (:76674-76692) followed by the five lines `ZNetView.Awake` normally supplies (`zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ObjectType.Default; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);`, mirroring :82613-82620). Pass the real portal hash to `CreateNewZDO` or `AddIfPortal` never runs and the ZDO is never written to the ChunkPortal file. Use a **fresh** ZDOID — `m_deadZDOs` (:76043) makes the server immediately re-destroy any ZDO recreated under a previously-destroyed id (:77133-77137).
catalog.playerExperience: A raider walks into an undefended outpost and swings a hammer at the clan's portal. Under the Ownership Pin, nothing happens — no damage numbers, no removal. Without the pin but with the veto, he chops it down and the ZDO delete reaches the server, which refuses: the portal stays in the world and reappears on his screen the next time the zone reloads, while the clan's Discord gets `[SECURITY:PortalDestroy] Steam:7656… (Raider) tried to destroy "⌁VALHALLA-OUTPOST" at (2104, 41, 880); refused.` An admin or the owner demolishing the same portal succeeds normally and the record is pruned.
failureModes: Does not cover damage-driven destruction on a client-owned portal — the server has no `RPC_Damage` hook (no instance). Only the Ownership Pin closes that.
A blanket `return false` drops legitimate destructions batched into the same packet. You must re-dispatch the allowed subset through the private `HandleDestroyedZDO`.

The destroying client has already destroyed its **local** GameObject. Refusing the ZDO delete leaves that client seeing a hole until the zone reloads — a visible desync that will be reported as a bug. Force-push the ZDO (`ForceSendZDO`) and consider a toast explaining it.
`sender` in the handler signature is spoofable (:83609); without the Authentic Sender Context the veto cannot tell who asked.
Recreating a destroyed portal under its old ZDOID is silently undone by `m_deadZDOs` (:76043, enforced :77133-77137). Always mint a fresh id.
`ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` is private — bind by name and wrap in SafePatch.
citations: ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed public Action<ZDO> — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033, invoked :76975-76978; ZNetScene subscription :81953
openQuestions: When the server refuses a destroy, how does the destroying client behave — does the portal reappear on its own, or does the client hold a ghost hole until it leaves and returns? IN-GAME CHECK: veto a destroy with a player standing there and describe what they see over the next 60 seconds.

Are build resources refunded to the demolisher before the ZDO delete is sent? `WearNTear.Destroy` runs on the owner (:150427); if so a vetoed destroy is a free-material exploit. IN-GAME CHECK: veto a destroy and inspect the demolisher's inventory.
corrections: The prefix does not stop propagation: the sender already deleted locally (:83586-83592) and the server forwards 'DestroyZDO' to all other peers after handling (:83641-83646). Repair requires SetOwner(sessionID) (OwnerRevision++, :74627-74633) plus ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(id) to all peers so ShouldSend (:76003-76012) passes; otherwise the portal stays invisible until the peer's sector record is invalidated.

WearNTear.Destroy already wrote s_health=0 and s_support=0 and dropped resources before the RPC (:150434-150440). A vetoed portal returns at 0 health (immune per :150334 but visually broken) and every attempt dupes greydwarf eyes/fine wood/surtling cores. Reset s_health/s_support in the veto and clear the dropped ItemDrop ZDOs or accept the dupe.
Without a SetOwner guard the Ownership Pin does not hold (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926, 2s timer :76874); the 'no damage numbers' experience needs that patch.
Recovery via CreateNewZDO produces a ZDO with no s_creator/s_health/s_support keys; that is fine (defaults) but the piece will not be ward-attributed to the original builder.

The packet is forwarded regardless of the veto: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632-83645) calls HandleRoutedRPC and then RouteRPC independently, and RouteRPC broadcasts a targetPeerID==0 packet to every other ready peer (:83636-83644 / :83605-83612). Every other vanilla client still runs its own RPC_DestroyZDO and deletes the object locally. To stop propagation the filter must live in a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (or RouteRPC), matching m_methodHash == "DestroyZDO".GetStableHashCode(), not only on the handler.

'Reappears on his screen the next time the zone reloads' is false. ZDOPeer.m_zdos (:75981) records the revision each peer already has and is pruned only by HandleDestroyedZDO (:76992) and sector invalidation (:75989-75995) — never by leaving the zone. ShouldSend (:76003-76013) then suppresses re-sends, and ForceSendZDO is itself gated by ShouldSend in AddForceSendZdos (:77270-77275). After a veto the mod must bump the revision (zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) → OwnerRevision++ :74627-74633, or write a key) and ForceSendZDO to all peers, or reflectively remove the uid from each peer's m_zdos.

The vetoed ZDO's server-side owner record still names the destroying client (which no longer holds the ZDO); reclaim ownership as part of the veto or the ZDO sits owned-by-nobody-in-practice until ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns it.

Scope is deletion only. A forged client can still zero s_health, move, or retag the portal through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137, no owner/prefab check); the vanilla damage→Destroy path simply re-issues DestroyZDO each time, so the veto is exercised repeatedly, not once.

'The Ownership Pin closes this gap completely' assumes the pin holds. ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925) iterates FindObjects, which includes m_portalObjects (:77376), and IsInPeerActiveArea for the server uid tests the 1e6 reference position (:76887-76890) — server ownership is handed to a nearby peer within 2 s. The pin needs its own patch (e.g. prefix ReleaseNearbyZDOS / IsInPeerActiveArea) before RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove become undeliverable.
Recovery block is correct; note CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) (:76674-76692) calls AddIfPortal with the passed hash, and ZNetView.Awake's fabrication lines are :82613-82619.
evidence: ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed public field — :76033; m_deadZDOs — :76043; re-destroy on re-create — :77133-77137
ZDOPeer.m_zdos / ZDOSectorInvalidated / ShouldSend — :75981-76013; peer.m_zdos.Remove in HandleDestroyedZDO — :76992
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The enforcement point is real: 'DestroyZDO' is registered ZDO-less in the ZDOMan ctor (:76155), so HandleRoutedRPC takes the m_functions branch (:83648-83654) and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953-76961) → HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-76999) executes on the dedicated server with no sender/owner/prefab check. m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> (:76033) invoked before removal (:76975-76978); ZNetScene.Awake combines onto it (:81953). m_deadZDOs re-destroy path verified (:76997, :77133-77137). CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) sets only owner and portal bookkeeping; ZNetView.Awake fabrication block (:82613-82620) is what must be mirrored. WearNTear RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove owner-gated (:150332-150334, :150419-150425) so damage is unobservable server-side. Attacks that land: (1) Refusing the RPC does not undo what already happened on the wire: the sender executed HandleRoutedRPC locally before routing (:83586-83592), and ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC forwards the packet to every other peer unconditionally AFTER the server's handler returns (:83641-83646) — the prefix cannot stop the forward. Every client in the zone deletes the portal locally; the server's per-peer record (peer.m_zdos) still holds the old revision, so ShouldSend (:76003-76012) is false and the portal is NOT resent until sector invalidation (:75989-75996). 'Reappears the next time the zone reloads' is not guaranteed; the veto must bump the ZDO (SetOwner(session) increments OwnerRevision, :74627-74633) and ForceSendZDO to all peers, after which clients CreateNewZDO on receipt and reinstantiate. (2) WearNTear.Destroy (:150427-150465) ran on the owning client BEFORE the DestroyZDO packet: it wrote s_health=0 and s_support=0 (:150434-150435) and DropResources (:150440) spawned the portal's build materials as real ItemDrop ZDOs. A vetoed portal comes back with 0 health — immune to further hits (RPC_Damage early return :150334; ApplyDamage :150389-150393) but rendered broken, and each repeated hammer swing dupes the materials. The veto must reset s_health/s_support and should delete the fresh drops; the option's playerExperience omits this. (3) The playerExperience line about 'no damage numbers under the Ownership Pin' is only true if ownership actually sticks (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926 reassigns within 2s without a SetOwner guard). With those fixes the veto is a genuine server-side refusal of the authoritative delete; server-enforced stands.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953-76961) is registered as a ZDO-less routed RPC in the ZDOMan ctor (:76155); ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC dispatches ZDO-less RPCs through m_functions (:83647-83655), so it executes on the dedicated server. It reads a count and ZDOIDs and calls HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-76999) with no sender, owner or prefab check. m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> (:76033) invoked at :76975-76978 before RemoveFromSector and m_objectsByID.Remove; ZNetScene combines onto it at :81953. Game.PortalPrefabHash is a public getter (:100021). m_deadZDOs (:76043) re-destroys a re-created ZDO under an old id in RPC_ZDOData (:77133-77137). WearNTear.Damage/RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove routing and IsOwner gates confirmed (:150315-150321, :150332, :150411-150425). A Harmony prefix on RPC_DestroyZDO therefore does block the server-side deletion — server-enforced for the delete operation. However the option's picture of what the clients see afterwards is wrong, and the pin it leans on is not free.

catalog.name: Ungated RPC Hardening
catalog.oneLine: Sender checks on the four unauthenticated global routed RPCs a client can use to defeat any portal policy — `SetGlobalKey`, `RemoveGlobalKey`, `RPC_SetConnection` and `RequestZDO`.
catalog.howItWorks:
Four handlers that run on the dedicated server (all ZDO-less routed RPCs, so `HandleRoutedRPC` takes the `m_functions` branch at :83648-83654) and validate nothing.

**(1) `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string name)` (:116022-116029) and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116031-116037).** Registered only on the server (:113444-113455) and neither inspects `sender`: `if (!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)) { GlobalKeyAdd(name); SendGlobalKeys(0L); }`. Any connected client can set or clear `noportals`, `nobossportals`, `teleportall` and `dungeonbuild` at will. Any policy built on those keys (see Progression Gate) is one packet from being lifted. Harmony **prefix** both: allow through only when the Authentic Sender Context resolves to the server's own id or to an account in `m_adminList` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811); otherwise return false, audit, and toast. Note `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors every key with ordinal < `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (41) into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113483-113513, list write :113511) which is written to the .fwl on every autosave — so an unhardened server that gets griefed once has `noportals` baked into the world file permanently.

**(2) `Game.RPC_SetConnection(long sender, ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)` (:100653-100662).** Registered on **every** peer, outside the `IsServer()` block (:100066-100070). No sender check, no ownership check, no prefab check: it takes ownership of the named ZDO, writes an arbitrary Portal connection, and ForceSendZDOs it. This is a complete portal-hijack primitive — and it also means a "lockdown" implemented by forcing every connection to `ZDOID.None` can be undone instantly by one malicious client. Prefix it with the same admin/server check. Keep in mind you must still let the *legitimate* vanilla path through: `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651) routes this RPC to an owning client, and the sender in that case is the server itself.

**(3) `ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO(long sender, ZDOID id)` (:77689-77692).** `GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO(id)` — using the *spoofable payload* `sender`. A client can force the server to push any ZDO it names to any other peer: a reconnaissance and amplification primitive (enumerate the whole world's portal set, or flood another player's connection). Prefix it to replace the payload `sender` with the authenticated peer's uid, which both closes the amplification and makes the legitimate `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` → `RequestZDO` path (:143650) work exactly as before.

**(4) `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject(long spawner, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)` (:82355-82366, registered :81954).** The one exception to "a dedicated server instantiates nothing" — it does a bare `Instantiate` of any prefab in `m_namedPrefabs`. Not portal-specific, but it is free unauthenticated server-side instantiation and belongs on the same hardening list.

All four prefixes are one shape: resolve the authentic peer from the ambient context, check admin, return false with an audit line if not. Each is a handful of lines and each closes a hole that would otherwise make several other options in this document decorative.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing changes for honest players. A player with a cheat client who tries `SetGlobalKey teleportall` to carry iron through portals finds the key never applies, gets a console-visible refusal (`ZNet.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, …)`, :81635), and appears in the admin audit. The server operator's `noportals` maintenance lockdown can no longer be cancelled by a player.
failureModes: `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies PascalCase (`"NoPortals"`, :115938-115941) while the store holds only lowercase, so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` dedupe (:116024) never trips and every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the entire key list. Your own server-side calls must use lowercase literals or pre-check with `GetGlobalKey`, or you create a broadcast storm.

Hardening `RPC_SetGlobalKey` also blocks any *other* mod or vanilla client path that legitimately sets a key (e.g. the `setkey` console command issued by an admin client, which arrives via `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand`, :81879-81889 — that one is already admin-gated, so allow it).
`RPC_RequestZDO`'s spoofable sender is also how a *legitimate* client asks for a portal's destination ZDO. Replacing rather than rejecting is essential or you break `TargetFound` for everyone.
`RPC_SetConnection` is vanilla's own cross-machine write protocol; a prefix that is too strict breaks `Game.SetConnection`'s deferred path and portals stop pairing near online players.

`ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd` dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` (:113506-113508) and its `UpdateWorldRates` tail dereferences `Minimap.instance` (:101203) with no null guards; these survive headless only because the dedicated build instantiates the GUI scene. Do not call them before Game/Minimap exist.
citations: Game.RPC_SetConnection (registered on every peer, no checks) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100066-100070, :100653-100662
openQuestions: Does any vanilla client path legitimately invoke `SetGlobalKey` from a non-admin client in normal play (e.g. a boss defeat writing `defeated_*`, or `BaseAI.SetAlerted` writing `activeBosses` at :27258)? Those are written by whichever client owns the boss — blocking them would break progression. IN-GAME CHECK: log every `RPC_SetGlobalKey` with its authenticated sender over a boss fight and a full progression run before enabling the block; almost certainly you must allow the ordinal ≥ NonServerOption keys through and restrict only 0..40.
corrections: Do NOT gate RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey to admin/server only: boss-defeat keys, activeBosses and other progression keys are sent by non-admin clients through this RPC (Character.OnDeath :3153-3164, BaseAI.SetAlerted :27256-27260, BossStone :120184-120188, OfferingBowl :135738, ItemDrop :145637, :148013). Gate by key class: refuse gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (ordinals 0-40, via GetKeyValue :113560-113581) from non-admins; allow NonServerOption keys from any authenticated peer.

RPC_SetConnection on a dedicated server only ever runs for client-originated packets (Game.SetConnection targets the owning client peer, :100648, never self); refuse every non-admin invocation — there is no legitimate server-to-self path to preserve.

The payload sender is never rewritten server-side (RPC_RoutedRPC :83634-83637 deserialises m_senderPeerID from the packet); the Authentic Sender Context must be a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC mapping the ZRpc to ZNet peer uid and stashing it for the handler prefixes.
ZNet.RemotePrint delivers to the client's console window (:81644 rpc.Invoke("RemotePrint")), not the HUD; use the Player 'Message' RPC for a visible toast.
'SpawnObject' is dead vanilla API (no callers of ZNetScene.SpawnObject); it is also broadcast to 0L so each receiving client instantiates its own copy — refuse it entirely.

Admin-only gating of RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey breaks vanilla. Ordinary non-admin clients legitimately send these: Character.OnDeath sets m_defeatSetGlobalKey (client decompile :3155-3158, i.e. defeated_*); BaseAI.SetAlerted sets activeBosses (:27256-27262 server copy, executed on the boss-owning client); pieces/items set and remove world keys (client :120924-120928, :136478, :146377, :148753); Ship sets AshlandsOcean (client :141499). The gate must be key-scoped: refuse from non-admins only keys with gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers) plus the mod's own private key names; pass everything GetKeyValue (:113560-113581) classifies as NonServerOption. Consequence: vanilla progression keys stay spoofable by any client.

GlobalKeys.NonServerOption is ordinal 43 in this build (enum :101270-101326: NoMap=33, NoPortals=34, NoBossPortals=35, DungeonBuild=36, TeleportAll=37, NoHeavySnow=40, AllHeavySnow=41, Preset=42, NonServerOption=43), not 41.

The four routed RPCs are not the only — or largest — unauthenticated write path. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137) accepts, from any peer, data for any ZDOID with a higher DataRevision, including the owner field and the Portal connection (ZDO.Deserialize :74228-74233), with no owner/prefab/sender check; it is the same channel vanilla owners use, so it cannot be blanket-refused. Hardening RPC_SetConnection therefore does not close the hijack primitive; connection re-assertion (Managed Network Governor) remains necessary.

RPC_SetConnection needs no 'let the legitimate path through' carve-out. The server's own SetConnection delegation (:100649) targets the owner peer ≠ m_id, which InvokeRoutedRPC never self-dispatches (:83576-83583); no vanilla client code invokes RPC_SetConnection. Every inbound RPC_SetConnection at a dedicated server is illegitimate and can be rejected unconditionally. Registration line is :100067.

RPC_RequestZDO amplification is bounded: the forced send still passes ZDOPeer.ShouldSend in AddForceSendZdos (:77270-77275), so a victim only receives ZDOs it does not already hold at the current revision. The reconnaissance use (enumerate by ZDOID against the attacker's own peer id) stands.
RPC name is "SpawnObject" (registration :81954), handler RPC_SpawnObject; RemotePrint is console-only on the client (client RPC_RemotePrint :81879-81884 → Console.instance.Print), not HUD.
evidence: Character.OnDeath sets defeat key on owning client — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:3153-3164
ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (.fwl mirror gated on gk < NonServerOption) — :113483-113513; GetKeyValue — :113560-113581
ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch rule — :83576-83592; HandleRoutedRPC payload sender — :83647-83655
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] All four holes verified. RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (:116022-116037) registered server-only (:113445-113449) and ignore sender; GlobalKeyAdd mirrors gk < NonServerOption into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113487, :113511) which SaveWorldFWLData writes (:112581-112584, called from the save thread :80632). Game.RPC_SetConnection registered on every peer (:100066) with no checks (:100653-100662). RPC_RequestZDO uses payload sender (:77689-77692); RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID comes straight off the wire in RPC_RoutedRPC (:83634-83637) — nothing on the server rewrites it, so 'Authentic Sender Context' (prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC capturing the ZRpc) is a genuine prerequisite. ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' registered in Awake with no IsServer gate (:81954), handler does bare Instantiate (:82355-82366); vanilla never calls ZNetScene.SpawnObject (only definition at :82339-82343, zero callers), so blocking it breaks nothing. The critical error: a blanket admin/server-only prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey breaks vanilla progression. Boss defeat keys are set by the boss's OWNING CLIENT — Character.OnDeath → SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey) (:3153-3155) and the activeBosses decrement (:3162-3164); BaseAI.SetAlerted writes activeBosses (:27256-27260); OfferingBowl (:135738), ItemDrop use (:145637), BossStone set AND remove (:120184-120188), plus :148013 — all client-side, all non-admin, all via this same RPC. The prefix must be key-class-aware: refuse ordinals < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers, classified by GetKeyValue :113560-113581) from non-admins and pass NonServerOption keys (defeated_*, activeBosses, custom) from any authenticated peer; same for RemoveGlobalKey. RPC_SetConnection is simpler than stated: Game.SetConnection routes it to a client owner (:100648), so on a dedicated server the local handler runs only for client-originated packets — refuse all non-admin invocations outright, no 'let the legitimate path through' carve-out needed. RemotePrint (:81635-81644) prints to the F5 console, not the HUD.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All four handlers exist as described and validate nothing: ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (:116022-116037) registered server-only in ZoneSystem.Start (:113446-113450); Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662) registered on every peer at :100067; ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) uses the payload sender; ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject (:82355-82366) does a bare Instantiate, registered as "SpawnObject" at :81954. GlobalKeyAdd mirrors keys with gk < NonServerOption into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113483-113513). HandleRoutedRPC passes the spoofable payload m_senderPeerID (:83651) — confirmed. Prefixes on these do execute on the dedicated server, so the enforcement label is right for these four RPCs. Two corrections are load-bearing: the proposed admin-only gate on the global-key RPCs breaks vanilla progression, and the four RPCs are not the biggest hole — RPC_ZDOData is.

catalog.name: Progression Gate
catalog.oneLine: Require a world global key before a network is wired at all — server-ENFORCED at the connection layer, which is strictly stronger than the client-honoured `NoPortals` key everyone reaches for first.
catalog.howItWorks:
There are two completely different ways to gate portals on progression and they sit on opposite sides of the enforcement line.

**Client-honoured (weak).** Set `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` (ordinal 32) or `NoBossPortals` (33). `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946), which on the server self-dispatches synchronously to `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022) and then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` (:113466-113471) broadcasts the full key list; each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and rebuilds its set (:113473-113481). `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads both keys **live at the moment of transit** (:143523, :143528) and refuses with `$msg_blocked` / `$msg_blockedbyboss`. This is genuinely vanilla-respecting — an unmodified client honours it exactly as it honours vanilla's own boss gating — and it reaches already-connected players within one network frame with no relog. But it is client-executed, so a modified client ignores it entirely, and it is world-wide, not per-network. It also gives **no visual warning**: `GetHoverText` still reports `$piece_portal_connected` and `UpdatePortal` still lights the target-found effect (:143453-143508), so a blocked portal looks completely normal until you walk in.

**Server-enforced (strong).** Gate the *connection* instead of the transit. The Managed Network Governor simply refuses to write a Portal connection for any portal whose network's required key is not present: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_bonemass)` (:115948) is a plain dictionary lookup on the server. An unconnected portal cannot teleport anyone — `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s gate 1 is `!TargetFound()` → silent return (:143519), and `TargetFound` requires a non-None connection (:143640-143655). A modified client cannot fake a connection into existence, because the destination comes from the ZDO the server owns and re-asserts. When the key appears, the governor wires the network on its next tick and the gates come alive.

Useful keys and their persistence, which differ sharply by ordinal (`GlobalKeys` enum :101270-101325): ordinals **0-40** are world-modifier keys — `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) which is persisted to the **.fwl** and stripped from the .db by `ZoneSystem.Save` (:113742-113760), and `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (:115904-115931) wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load and re-adds only what the .fwl held — so a mod-owned world-modifier key must be reapplied in a **postfix** on `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (the Wonderland WorldRatesPatches pattern, WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-15), never a prefix, because a `preset` key (ordinal 40) causes `ServerOptionsGUI.SetPreset` to reapply a whole key set at :115920-115926. Ordinals **≥41** (`defeated_eikthyr` 42 … `defeated_bonemass` 46, plus any arbitrary custom string, which `GetKeyValue` classifies as `NonServerOption` at :113560-113581) go the other way: .db only, never .fwl. Progression keys are therefore in the .db and survive normally.

Custom keys work fine as gate conditions: any unrecognised string becomes a NonServerOption key persisted in the .db, which is how a mod records "this clan has unlocked the swamp network" (the FirstSpawnGrant `wonderland_starter_<id>` pattern). Set them with the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` if you want session-only semantics.
catalog.playerExperience: Your server's `⌁HUB-SWAMP` gate stands finished in the hub from day one, glowing dead and reading `unconnected`. The hover text never changes and walking into it does nothing at all. The night the server kills Bonemass, the key lands, and within five seconds every swamp gate on the network snaps live simultaneously — the connected effect fires at each one and the hover reads `$piece_portal_connected`. No client mod, no relog, and no amount of client-side cheating opens it early, because there was never a destination to teleport to.
failureModes: Unhardened, any client can set or clear the key (`RPC_SetGlobalKey` has no sender check, :116022). Requires Ungated RPC Hardening or the gate is decorative.

`NoBossPortals` is a **world-wide blackout**, not a per-fight lock: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` checks `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528). One player aggroing Eikthyr blocks every portal for every player. Worse, `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded (`BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27258-27259), so a mid-fight client crash can leave it stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked — a server mod should watch for and zero it.

`NoPortals` does **not** close dungeon/crypt doors: `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads it and never calls `IsTeleportable`. Advertise it as "disables all constructed portals", never "disables all teleporting".

Setting a world-modifier key at runtime permanently edits the world's .fwl modifier list (:113511) — remove the mod later and `noportals` stays baked in. Use `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` for session-only.
`GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` does not allow everything: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` rejects any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` **before** consulting the key (:68860-68880).

The Steam/PlayFab browser modifiers badge is snapshotted in `ZNet.OpenServer` (:79454-79480) and refreshed only on the registration-retry path, so a live toggle leaves the public listing stale. Cosmetic.
citations: TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / UpdatePortal give no blocked affordance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143508
openQuestions: Is `Minimap.instance` genuinely non-null on a headless 1.0.7 server? `GlobalKeyAdd` → `UpdateWorldRates` → `UpdateNoMap` dereferences it unguarded (:101199-101204). Wonderland calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server, which is strong indirect evidence. IN-GAME CHECK: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm no NullReferenceException.

Does `activeBosses` reliably return to 0 after a boss dies and after a client force-quits mid-fight? IN-GAME CHECK: `setkey nobossportals`, aggro a boss, alt-F4 the fighting client, then `listkeys` on the server console.
corrections: Enforcement scope: the connection gate is server-enforced against vanilla clients; against a modified client the Portal connection is plain ZDO data writable by the ZDO owner over RPC_ZDOData (ZDO.Deserialize :74219-74224; :77076-77140 has no owner check) and the local TeleportWorld honours the local copy — reactive-revert only there. Replace 'no amount of client-side cheating opens it early'.

'Session-only semantics' claim is wrong for custom/NonServerOption keys: ZoneSystem.Save strips only gk < NonServerOption (:113749-113753), so a custom key always persists in the .db regardless of canSaveToServerOptionKeys. Session-only behaviour is only available for ordinals 0-40 (wiped by SetStartingGlobalKeys :115906-115910).
Teleport.Interact (dungeon doors) ignores NoPortals but does honour NoBossPortals inside an active boss dungeon (:143354-143358).
Removing a required key later does not un-wire an existing network: vanilla phase 1 keeps connected same-tag pairs; the governor must actively write None when the key disappears.

The prereq chain is heavier than 'small-medium': it inherits the Managed Network Governor (medium-large) and Ungated RPC Hardening; the standalone effort figure only covers the client-honoured key path.

Ordinals are off by two throughout: GlobalKeys enum (:101270-101326) has NoMap=33, NoPortals=34, NoBossPortals=35, DungeonBuild=36, TeleportAll=37, NoPseudoDrops=38, NoBuildingFall=39, NoHeavySnow=40, AllHeavySnow=41, Preset=42, NonServerOption=43, defeated_eikthyr=44, defeated_dragon=45, defeated_goblinking=46, defeated_gdking=47, defeated_bonemass=48. The .fwl mirror (GlobalKeyAdd :113487) and the .db strip (ZoneSystem.Save :113749-113753) use gk < NonServerOption, i.e. ordinals 0..42; the SetStartingGlobalKeys wipe loop is the literal `for (int i = 0; i < 41; i++)` (:115906), i.e. 0..40 — AllHeavySnow and Preset are mirrored to the .fwl but not wiped. Preset detection (:115915-115918, SetPreset :115923) is by enum value, not ordinal 40.

'No amount of client-side cheating opens it early' is false. ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029) accepts any string from any peer, and progression keys (defeated_*) cannot be admin-locked without breaking vanilla (Character.OnDeath sets them from the boss-owning client, client decompile :3155-3158). A protocol-level client sends SetGlobalKey defeated_bonemass and the governor wires the network on its next tick. Mitigation: gate on a mod-private key name that the hardening refuses from non-admins and that the server writes itself; note the server still has no first-hand boss-kill signal (it observes the client-reported key or the boss ZDO's client-reported death), so the gate is strong against vanilla and local-toggle cheats only.

'Session-only semantics' via GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false) is wrong: that flag only skips the .fwl mirror (:113487, :113509-113511). A NonServerOption key still enters m_globalKeys and is written to the .db by ZoneSystem.Save, whose RemoveWhere strips only gk < NonServerOption (:113749-113753). There is no session-only global key.

The strong tier's prereq chain is self-inconsistent as written: if Ungated RPC Hardening is applied admin-only, defeated_bonemass never lands and the gate never opens. The hardening must be key-scoped (see that verdict).

SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) stringifies PascalCase (:115938-115941) while GlobalKeyAdd lowercases (:113487 keyStr.ToLower()); RPC_SetGlobalKey's m_globalKeys.Contains(name) pre-check (:116024) therefore misses for PascalCase input and re-runs GlobalKeyAdd (idempotent) — harmless, but do not rely on the Contains short-circuit.
Line cites: Teleport gate order is :143517-143543 (TargetFound :143519, NoPortals :143521, NoBossPortals :143526, IsTeleportable :143531).
evidence: Client Character.OnDeath sets defeat key — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:3155-3158
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Client-honoured half verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport gate order is TargetFound → NoPortals → NoBossPortals(with boss event / activeBosses>0) → IsTeleportable (:143517-143537); GetHoverText only reports connected/unconnected (:143453-143463) and UpdatePortal's target_found effect ignores the keys (:143489-143506), so a blocked portal looks live. SetGlobalKey → routed RPC → server-local RPC_SetGlobalKey → SendGlobalKeys(0L) broadcast → client RPC_GlobalKeys rebuild (:115943-115946, :116022-116029, :113466-113481). Persistence split verified: GlobalKeyAdd mirrors gk<NonServerOption into m_startingGlobalKeys (:113487, :113511); ZoneSystem.Save strips gk<NonServerOption from the .db (:113749-113753); SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes ordinals 0..40 then re-adds the .fwl list and applies a preset via ServerOptionsGUI (:115904-115931), called from ZNet.WorldSetup (:80851-80854); ordinals: NoPortals 32 (:101304), NoBossPortals 33, NonServerOption 41 (:101313), defeated_bonemass 46 (:101318). Server-enforced half: an unconnected portal cannot teleport (TargetFound :143640-143655 requires non-None connection and a resolvable target ZDO) and no vanilla client path ever writes a Portal connection except to None (RPC_SetTag :143590, SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected :143612-143633), so withholding the connection is server-enforced AGAINST VANILLA CLIENTS. Against a modified client the claim 'no amount of client-side cheating opens it early' is false even with Ungated RPC Hardening: the connection is ZDO data accepted from the wire by ZDO.Deserialize (:74219-74224) via RPC_ZDOData with no owner/socket check (:77076-77140); a cheating owner writes A↔B into its own ZDO copies and its local TeleportWorld teleports at once — the governor reverts only on its next tick. Also: 'session-only semantics' via GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false) is wrong for custom keys — any NonServerOption key is always written to the .db (Save only strips <41); canSaveToServerOptionKeys only matters for ordinals 0-40. Note Teleport.Interact DOES read NoBossPortals inside an active boss dungeon (:143354-143358); only NoPortals is ignored there.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The two-tier picture is right. Client-honoured tier: TeleportWorld.Teleport reads NoPortals and NoBossPortals live at transit (:143521-143530) after the TargetFound gate (:143519), and neither GetHoverText (:143453-143464) nor UpdatePortal (:143489-143510) consults them, so a blocked portal looks connected. ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey → InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey") self-dispatches on the server (:115943-115946 → :83562-83566, :83584-83587) and SendGlobalKeys(0L)/RPC_GlobalKeys rebuild every client's set (:113466-113481). Server-enforced tier: an unconnected portal cannot teleport a vanilla client because Teleport's first gate is TargetFound (:143519, :143640-143655) and the connection is a server-written ZDO field — with the governor withholding the connection this is genuine route-level enforcement for vanilla clients. GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) is a HashSet lookup (:115948-115951). Persistence split (.fwl for gk < NonServerOption via GlobalKeyAdd :113483-113513, .db strip in ZoneSystem.Save :113749-113753, wipe-and-reapply in SetStartingGlobalKeys :115904-115931) confirmed in shape, but every ordinal quoted is wrong, the 'session-only' claim is wrong, and the 'no amount of client-side cheating' claim is refuted by the RPC_SetGlobalKey hole the option's own prereq cannot close for progression keys.

catalog.name: Key-Item Requirement
catalog.oneLine: A network that only wires while a specified item sits in a designated container beside the gate — server-enforced, because the server can read container inventories even though it can never read a player's.
catalog.howItWorks:
The server cannot see a traveller's inventory. `Player.Save` serialises inventory, skills, recipes and uniques into a `ZPackage` that `PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData` stores in `m_playerData` and writes only to that client's own `.fch` (:14091-14170, :105706-105711); `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. An exhaustive scan of the Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO writes yields only vitals, identity, pose and equipment — never `s_items`. `ZDOVars.s_items` is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save()` (:122294-122300). So "must be carrying X" is impossible; "must have deposited X" is easy.

Design: each managed portal may declare a *key container* — the nearest container ZDO within a configured radius, found with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, radius, buffer)` (Wonderland ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25) filtered by `ContainerRegistry.IsContainer` (ContainerRegistry.cs:58), and recorded by rounded position in the Portal Record Store. On each governor tick, for each such portal: read the container's inventory with `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` over the `s_items` byte blob, skipping any container with `ZDOVars.s_inUse` set (a player has the UI open — `Container.UpdateUseVisual` :121990-122000, `ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy`); count the required item; if the requirement is met, write the Portal connection, otherwise write `ZDOID.None`. A consumed-toll variant additionally removes the item (`ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem` with add-then-remove ordering) and journals it through the ItemLedger (ItemLedger.cs:43/:51) — never remove items without an audit trail.

This is genuinely server-enforced: an unconnected portal cannot teleport anyone, because `TeleportWorld.Teleport` returns silently at gate 1 when `!TargetFound()` (:143519, :143640-143655) and the destination is re-read from the live ZDO at the instant of transit (:143539-143543). A modified client cannot conjure a connection the server did not write, and the Managed Network Governor re-asserts the correct state every tick.

Equipment is a partial exception worth naming: `VisEquipment` mirrors the *visible equipped* items into the character's own ZDO as prefab stable hashes — `s_rightItem`, `s_leftItem`, `s_helmetItem`, `s_chestItem`, `s_legItem`, `s_shoulderItem`, `s_utilityItem`, `s_trinketItem`, the back slots (:20569-20708). So "must be **wielding** the Swamp Key" is server-readable in real time, unlike "must be carrying it". But it cannot gate a transit per-player (see Per-Player Transit Gate) — only whether the network is wired at all, which makes it a poor fit for a key-item mechanic with multiple users.
catalog.playerExperience: The `⌁DEEPMINE` gate has a stone chest beside it with a plaque-sign reading `FEED ME IRON`. While the chest is empty the gate reads `unconnected` and walking into it does nothing. Drop a single iron bar in and within a couple of seconds the gate hums to life and connects to the mine. Take the bar back out and it goes dark again. In toll mode the bar disappears when the first traveller comes through, and the clan's Discord logs `⌁DEEPMINE toll: 1x Iron consumed (Bjorn).`
failureModes: **All-or-nothing per network, never per player.** The connection is global; once the toll is paid the gate is open to everyone until it lapses. There is no way to charge each traveller.

Container ownership races: the container's owning client rewrites `s_items` on every inventory change (`Container.Save` :122294-122300 runs from `OnContainerChanged` when IsOwner). A server write must claim ownership at the moment of commit and respect `s_inUse`, or it will silently lose the race or duplicate items. Use Wonderland's ZdoInventoryIO which already implements this discipline.
The container can be moved, destroyed or replaced; the position-keyed binding must be re-validated each tick and the portal fails closed when the container is missing.

`TargetFound` requires the client to actually hold the destination ZDO (:143646-143654); the first walk-through after a newly-written connection to a distant partner fails **silently** with no message at all. Pre-push with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, targetId)` (:77714) when the connection is made.

A toll that consumes items is a duplication/loss risk under any ZDO race. Journal every transfer and every rejection (ItemLedger pattern) and prefer a non-consuming "presence" requirement for anything valuable.
Container ZDOs are ordinary sector ZDOs, not world-resident like portals — a container in an unloaded region may be absent from `FindNear`. Cache the last known contents and fail closed, not open.
citations: VisEquipment mirrors equipped items into the character ZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:20569-20708
openQuestions: How quickly does a container's `s_items` blob reach the server after a player drops an item in? `Container.Save` runs on the owner's OnContainerChanged and the ZDO syncs on the ~0.05s `ZDOMan` cadence, but the perceived latency matters for the UX. catalog.name: Team / Guild Networks
catalog.oneLine: A server-side roster keyed on platform-verified accounts, mapping players to named networks, with membership changes driven by emotes and enforced by the governor's refusal to wire non-members.
catalog.howItWorks:
Valheim has no faction, guild or team concept for players. `PrivateArea.m_ownerFaction` exists but any non-zero value makes `PrivateArea.Interact` early-return (:137376) and routes damage handling down an entirely different path — it is for creature-faction structures, not player groups. There is no PvP team field on the character ZDO beyond `s_pvp` (a plain bool). So the roster has to be the mod's own.

Roster storage, two options with different properties:
- **World global keys.** `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("tplite_net_<network>_<platformUserId>")` — an arbitrary string is classified as `NonServerOption` by `GetKeyValue` (:113560-113581) and therefore persisted in the **.db** and never in the .fwl. On the server `SetGlobalKey` self-dispatches synchronously (:115943-115946 → :116022), so the key is readable the instant it is set, and it travels with the world and its backups. This is the FirstSpawnGrant pattern (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:91, :185). Downside: the key set is broadcast in full to every client on every change (`SendGlobalKeys(0L)` :113466), so a large roster is real per-change bandwidth and every player can read every membership.
- **A mod file** alongside the Portal Record Store. Private, arbitrary structure, no broadcast cost. Preferred for anything beyond a handful of members; use global keys only for the small once-only facts.

Key on `PlatformUserID` (from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity), not on `s_playerID` — `s_playerID` is a per-character-file value the client writes into its own ZDO (`Player.SetPlayerID` :10129-10136) and a player with several characters has several of them. Keep a secondary `playerID → PlatformUserID` map, learned each session while both halves are in hand (the Authentic Sender Context), so that ward permitted lists and `s_creator` values — which are playerID-shaped — can be resolved to accounts. `ZNetPeer.m_playerID` is useless: the server registers the `"PlayerID"` RPC (:79916, handler :80919-80927) but no vanilla client ever invokes it, so the field is permanently 0.

Enforcement is the Managed Network Governor plus the Portal ACL. A network name maps to a roster; a portal in that network is wired only to other portals in the same network; a portal carrying the network's tag whose owner is not on the roster is refused a partner and optionally re-tagged. Membership changes through emote commands with proximity (the CacheClaimControl shape): leader stands next to a candidate, `/challenge` to invite, candidate `/point` to accept, both get `PlayerNotify` toasts. Leadership and invite rights live in the roster record.

Cross-session identity resolution for *offline* members is why the roster must be account-keyed: `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396, persisted :112587-112591) gives you display names for every account that has ever played, and `s_creatorIndex` on any piece resolves into it — so an admin report can say "this portal was built by an account that last played in March and belongs to network VALHALLA" without that player ever logging in again.
catalog.playerExperience: Your clan leader stands beside you and does the `/challenge` emote; you get a toast `Bjorn invites you to network VALHALLA — /point to accept.` You `/point` and get `You joined VALHALLA.` Every portal your clan tags `⌁VALHALLA` wires into the clan ring. A stranger who builds a portal and somehow sets the same tag gets nothing — his gate reads `unconnected` forever and he never learns why, because nothing in vanilla tells him. Months later, after you have all stopped playing, an admin's report still reads `⌁VALHALLA: 6 gates, network owner Bjorn (Steam:7656…), last active 2026-03-14`.
failureModes: The whole roster is mod-side state with no vanilla backing. A corrupted or deleted file orphans every network; back it up alongside the world save and reconcile on boot.
Emote-driven invites are ambiguous when several players stand close together. Require the nearest candidate within a tight radius and confirm by name in the toast.
`s_playerID` is per-character, so a player switching characters appears as a new identity to anything keyed on it. Always resolve through the account map.
`ZNetPeer.m_playerID` is always 0 (the `"PlayerID"` RPC is registered at :79916 but never invoked by any vanilla client). Reading it looks correct and yields nothing.

Global-key rosters are world-readable by every client and re-broadcast on every change (`SendGlobalKeys(0L)` clears and rebuilds the client's set, :113473-113481). Not suitable for anything private or large.
Players cannot see their own network membership except through toasts you send them. There is no vanilla UI to hook.

catalog.name: Retag Rate Limit
catalog.oneLine: A per-account token bucket on tag and connection changes, enforced by reverting everything over budget and escalating to an ownership pin or a kick — the defence against flap attacks and scripted tag churn.
catalog.howItWorks:
The Tag Watchdog is a revert loop, and a revert loop can be attacked by out-writing it. A scripted client pushing `RPC_ZDOData` with a bumped DataRevision every frame will make a contested portal flap between the attacker's tag and yours at whatever rate your tick runs, generating a `ForceSendZDO` broadcast to every peer on each revert (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serialises the **entire** ZDO with no delta encoding, :77053-77062) — so the attacker turns your defence into an amplifier against your own bandwidth.

The rate limit sits in the watchdog's policy chain, before the ALLOW/DENY decision:
- Per account (keyed on the notarised `PlatformUserID`), a token bucket: N tag changes per window, refilling at R per minute, configurable, with a separate and smaller budget for connection changes.
- Per portal, a cooldown: after a successful retag, further retags of the same portal are refused for T seconds regardless of who asks. This is also the anti-squatting cooldown — it stops a griefer cycling a contested tag faster than the legitimate owner can respond.
- Exhausting the bucket escalates in stages: (1) revert and toast; (2) apply a temporary Ownership Pin to the contested portal, which makes further retags physically impossible because `RPC_SetTag` now routes to a server with no instance (:82855-82858, :83656-83664) — this is the stage that actually stops the attack rather than absorbing it; (3) `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` (:81658) or `Ban` (:81744), both public and server-side, resolving by PlatformUserID exactly as vanilla's adminlist does.
- Suppress the broadcast half of the revert while flapping: `ZDO.Set` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345, so `IncreaseDataRevision` is skipped), so re-asserting an already-correct tag is genuinely free — but the first revert after each attacker write is not. Cap reverts-with-broadcast per sweep the way Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps health broadcasts at 256 (StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40), and prefer stage (2) over grinding.

All counters live in the Portal Record Store (`lastRetagAt`, `retagCount`) and a per-account in-memory bucket rebuilt on boot; nothing needs to persist beyond a rolling window except the abuse tally you want in the audit trail.

Be honest about the classification: this is reactive-detection-only in stages 1, and becomes server-enforced only at stage 2. A rate limit alone never prevents the first offence.
catalog.playerExperience: An honest player renaming their portal a few times while deciding on a name notices nothing. A player who renames the same portal fifteen times in a minute gets `Slow down — that gate was just renamed.` and the change is refused for thirty seconds. A scripted attacker hammering a contested portal sees the tag lock solid after a few seconds — the gate becomes server-held and stops responding to them entirely — and an admin gets a Discord alert naming their Steam ID and the portal's coordinates.
failureModes: Stage 1 absorbs the attack rather than stopping it, and each revert costs a full-ZDO broadcast to every peer (no delta encoding, :77053-77062). Escalate to the pin quickly.

Attribution depends on the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix catching the packet; a change whose sender cannot be resolved must be charged to nobody, which means an unattributable attacker is only rate-limited per-portal, not per-account. Rely on the per-portal cooldown for that case.
A per-portal cooldown can be weaponised: a griefer retags your portal once, and your own corrective retag is refused for T seconds. Exempt the record's owner and admins from the per-portal cooldown.
Kicking on a false positive (a laggy client re-pushing a stale ZDO repeatedly) is a bad outcome. Require sustained abuse over a long window and log heavily before ever enabling stage 3.
`ZNet.Kick`/`Ban` resolve by PlatformUserID or player name via `InternalKick` (:81689); player names are not unique, so always pass the host name.
