verifierReasoning: [decompile:downgraded] Detection and bucket side holds: ZDOMan.SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO per send (:77053-77062), ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is revision-based (:76003-76013), ZDO.Set no-ops when BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on an equal value (assembly_valheim_SERVER :73601-73607; assembly_utils_SERVER :321-329) so IncreaseDataRevision is skipped, ZNet.Kick/Ban are public server-side (:81658, :81744) resolving via PlatformUserID.TryParse in InternalKick (:81689-81700). The load-bearing claim — stage 2 Ownership Pin 'makes further retags physically impossible' and is 'the stage that actually stops the attack' — fails against the attacker the option itself defines (a scripted client pushing RPC_ZDOData). RPC_ZDOData has no sender or owner check: when the packet's DataRevision exceeds the server's, it unconditionally sets OwnerRevision, DataRevision, owner and all data including tag and connection (:77108-77127; connection at :74227-74233). Ownership is just another field in that packet; the pin is overwritten by the next push. The pin only blocks VANILLA clients, because SetText → ZNetView.InvokeRPC routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858) and the server's HandleRoutedRPC drops it when FindInstance returns null (:83656-83664), and the client-side RPC_SetTag is also gated on IsOwner (:143587). Even that requires the mod to Harmony-patch ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS: IsInPeerActiveArea(point, m_sessionID) tests against the server's (1e6,0,1e6) reference position (:76887-76891) so it is always false, and the pinned portal is handed to any nearby peer within 2 s (:76901-76927, timer :76873-76884). Against the scripted attacker only stage 3 (kick/ban) terminates the flood. Additional hardening gap: an attacker can push DataRevision near uint.MaxValue (DataRevision is uint, :73494); the server adopts it (:77120) and the next revert increments/wraps, after which the server's writes are ≤ every peer's recorded revision. The RPC_ZDOData sender is the portal's owner, not necessarily the typist when two players are near the portal.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] The amplification premise is real: ZDOMan.SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO (:77053-77062) and AddForceSendZdos delivers to every peer whose ShouldSend passes, including peers that never had the ZDO (:77262-77282, :76003-76015). ZDO.Set no-op on unchanged value is real (Set -> ZDOExtraData.Set -> InitAndSet -> BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER :321-330, so IncreaseDataRevision :73832 is skipped). Kick/Ban are public and server-side (:81658-81666, :81744-81752). But the stage that the option says 'actually stops the attack' does not, against the attacker it describes: (1) ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData has no sender or owner check — any peer's packet with num4 > DataRevision is applied wholesale, including SetOwnerInternal from the packet (:77106-77132). A scripted client pushing RPC_ZDOData bypasses the Ownership Pin entirely; the pin only blocks the vanilla RPC_SetTag path (InvokeRPC to owner :82855-82858; HandleRoutedRPC finds no server instance :83656-83664). (2) Even against a vanilla client the pin decays: ReleaseNearbyZDOS runs every 2 s (:76874-76880) and IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, m_sessionID) tests the server's reference position (:76885-76889), pinned to (1e6,0,1e6) by Game.FixedUpdate (:100463), so any peer within the active area gets ownership back within 2 s (:76920-76923) and can retag again. Holding a pin requires a <2 s re-assert or a Harmony guard on ZDO.SetOwner (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-302). (3) Attribution is weaker than claimed: a retag arrives as ZDO data from whichever peer OWNS the portal, which is the typist only if ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigned it to them; with two players at a hub the other player's peer is the sender. s_tagauthor (:143588 written from the client's own PlatformUserID) is the only per-retag identity and it is client-asserted. So the 'notarised PlatformUserID' bucket keys on the owner peer, not necessarily the typist. Net: stage 1 is reactive detection, stage 2 is a vanilla-client-only speed bump with a 2 s hole, stage 3 (kick/ban) is the only real stop and it is out-of-band. The line 'becomes server-enforced only at stage 2' must be deleted.

catalog.name: Password Tags
catalog.oneLine: Using the tag string itself as a shared secret — RULED OUT as secrecy (the tag is visible to anyone who hovers the portal) but viable as a shared token that only members are told.
catalog.howItWorks:
The naive design: a network's tag is a secret string; you can only join by knowing it. It does not survive contact with the hover label.

`TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` (:143453-143463) builds its text from `GetTagInfo()` (:143561-143573), which reads `ZDOVars.s_tag` straight off the ZDO, and the hover appears for **any** player who looks at the portal — there is no ownership or ward check on hovering. `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` gates `Interact` (the rename dialog) but not `GetHoverText`. So every member of your network is walking advertising: anyone who finds one of your gates reads the password off it. The secret has zero entropy against an attacker who has seen one portal, and vanilla's 10-character client-side input cap (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`, :143482) means the secret can be at most 10 typeable characters anyway. It is also strictly weaker than the Managed Network Governor, which does not care what the attacker knows.

What *does* work is the degenerate but useful version: the tag is not a secret, it is a **token you must be told**, and the actual authorisation is the roster. The password-shaped part is a convenience — a player who knows the network name types it and, if their account is on the roster, the governor wires them in; if not, the tag sticks (or reverts, by policy) but no connection is ever made. This gives the *feel* of a password with none of the false security, and it fails safe.

A second, genuinely secret variant is possible but needs a different channel: keep the network identity in a mod-private ZDO key (`tp_net`) rather than in `s_tag`, set it via an emote command or a map ping rather than the rename box, and leave `s_tag` as a cosmetic display name. The mod-private key is not shown by any vanilla UI — nothing in the client reads it — so it genuinely is not visible to a hovering stranger. It survives a client's ZDO push because `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` only adds the keys present in a packet and never clears (:74718-74730). But then the tag no longer drives pairing at all, which means vanilla's `Game.ConnectPortals` will happily tear your topology down on its 5s tick (:100601) — so this variant *requires* the Managed Network Governor to replace pairing entirely.

Either way, be blunt in the mod's documentation: a tag is public. There is no secret-bearing field a vanilla client displays only to authorised players.
catalog.playerExperience: Honest version: your clan's gates all read `⌁VALHALLA`. Anyone can read that. A stranger types `⌁VALHALLA` on his own portal and it stays named that — and never connects to anything, because his account is not on the roster. He has the password and it buys him nothing. Secret version: your gates read whatever cosmetic names you like (`Front Gate`, `The Mine`), the network binding is invisible, and a stranger has no way to even discover what network he would need to join.
failureModes: **The hover label is public.** `GetHoverText` has no access check (:143453-143463). Any design that treats `s_tag` as confidential is broken on contact.
10-character typeable limit on the client side (:143482) caps the entropy of anything a player enters.
The secret-in-a-mod-key variant divorces pairing from `s_tag`, so vanilla's 5s reconcile (:100601) will destroy your topology unless the governor fully replaces `Game.ConnectPortals`.
A mod-private key can be read (and forged) by a modified client that inspects its own ZDO copies — it is obscure, not secret.
If the policy is "reject the tag" rather than "reject the connection", an honest player who mistypes a network name gets a confusing revert; prefer refusing the connection and explaining in a toast.
citations: TeleportWorld.Interact ward gate applies to rename only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143471-143484
openQuestions: Is the hover text visible at any range that would let a player read a tag without approaching (e.g. through a wall)? Only affects how easily an attacker harvests network names. IN-GAME CHECK: observe the hover range and line-of-sight requirement on a vanilla client.
corrections: The mod-private key round-trips only because vanilla ZDO.Serialize re-sends every stored string (:74112-74185); a modded client can omit it, and RPC_ZDOData will apply the stripped packet (:77108-77127). State that the governor must treat a missing tp_net as 'unmanaged', not as an error.
On PlayFab-backed sessions the displayed tag goes through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (:143565-143566) — display only; s_tag raw is still the pairing key.

Enforcement: the password contributes nothing enforceable; the token variant is server-enforced only through the Governor prereq (route-shaped) and is client-honoured/not-enforceable as a secret. Relabel accordingly.

Secret variant: every vanilla rename runs RPC_SetTag -> UpdateConnection(None) + SetConnectedPortal(oldTarget) (:143591-143594, :143605-143628), unlinking both ends; the Governor must re-wire after each cosmetic rename.
Hover text always exposes [connected]/[unconnected] via HaveTarget (:143459-143462) regardless of the hidden network key.
Displayed tag passes through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (:143568) on PlayFab-backed clients.
Fail-safe 'his tag sticks but never connects' requires the Governor to prefix out Game.ConnectPortals; vanilla pairs by tag alone (:100664-100678).
evidence: ZDO.Deserialize does not clear — :74206-74250; ZDODataHelper.ReadData — :74718-74730; ZDOExtraData.Add(string) — :74881-74884
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] All cited facts check out. TeleportWorld.GetHoverText builds from GetTagInfo with no access check (:143453-143464); GetTagInfo reads s_tag/s_tagauthor straight off the ZDO (:143557-143570); Interact is the only place PrivateArea.CheckAccess gates (:143471-143484) and it only opens TextInput.RequestText(this, '$piece_portal_tag', 10) → Show sets characterLimit (:61509-61521). Game.ConnectPortals tears down mismatched-tag links (:100601) and re-pairs by tag (:100609-100621), so the secret-key variant needs the governor to own pairing — correctly stated. ZDODataHelper.ReadData adds keys without clearing (:74718-74730) and network ZDO.Serialize round-trips every string the client holds (:74112-74185), so a mod-private key the server sent survives a vanilla client's push. RemoveRichTextTags is a regex over <...> pairs (assembly_utils_SERVER :6700-6703). Classification as reactive-detection-only is honest: the tag itself is never protected; only the roster-backed governor (route form) does the enforcing, and that belongs to the Team/Guild option. Minor: the mod-private key survives only because the vanilla client echoes back all strings it received; a modded client can strip it (RPC_ZDOData applies whatever arrives, :77108-77127) — but a modded client is out of scope for 'vanilla-respecting'.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Every factual claim checks out: GetHoverText builds from GetTagInfo with no access check (:143453-143464, :143561-143573); PrivateArea.CheckAccess gates only Interact (:143476-143480) and is a vacuous pass server-side; Interact requests text with charLimit 10 (:143482 -> TextInput.Show sets m_inputField.characterLimit :61519); Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tears down tag-mismatched links (:100598-100604); ZDO.Deserialize never clears existing keys and ZDODataHelper.ReadData adds by hash (:74206-74250, :74718-74730, ZDOExtraData.Add :74881-74884), so a mod-private key survives the owning client's pushes (and is in fact echoed back, because the client serialises its whole copy). Corrections: (1) The enforcement label is wrong in both directions — nothing here is 'detection'. As a secret the tag is not-enforceable; the token variant enforces nothing by itself and inherits the Governor's route control, which is server-enforced against vanilla clients. (2) Secret variant omits that every vanilla rename executes RPC_SetTag's UpdateConnection(Portal, None) plus SetConnectedPortal(old target) (:143591-143594, :143605-143619) — renaming a cosmetic tag unlinks both ends (and RPC_SetConnected goes to the partner's owner, :143621-143628), so the Governor must re-wire after every cosmetic rename, and the hover still shows [connected]/[unconnected] via HaveTarget (:143462), so a stranger can see a gate is wired even without learning the network. (3) On PlayFab/Xbox the displayed tag is CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC output (:143568) — a 'password' can be shown censored. (4) A stranger who types the token gets a connection anyway if the Governor does not replace ConnectPortals (vanilla pairs by tag alone, :100664-100678) — the fail-safe claim depends on that prereq.

catalog.name: Per-Player Transit Gate
catalog.oneLine: Making a portal work for one player and not another — RULED OUT. The connection is a single global ZDO field read by the traveller's own client; there is no per-player dimension anywhere in the mechanism.
catalog.howItWorks:
This is the feature most people want first ("portals that only work for the player who built them", "PIN-protected portals", "only clan members may travel"), and it cannot be built server-side. The reasons compound:

**1. The transit decision is 100% client-executed with no server hook.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly one call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)` (:143664-143682, call at :143679), gated on `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null && Player.m_localPlayer == component`. A dedicated server has no trigger collider, no Player GameObject and a null `m_localPlayer` — and the deeper cause is that `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition((1e6,0,1e6))` every physics tick in the server build (:100458-100466, a line absent from the client's `Game.FixedUpdate` at :100886), so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82268-82276) never instantiates any world ZDO. No packet is sent at the moment of transit; the server learns about it only from the character ZDO's position changing afterwards.

**2. The destination is one field with no player dimension.** `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and `ZDOConnection` is `{readonly ConnectionType m_type; readonly ZDOID m_target;}` (:74797, :75524-75534) — one connection per ZDO, no list, no per-player slot. `Teleport()` resolves it with a bare `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(GetConnectionZDOID(Portal))` (:143539) and reads that ZDO's position and rotation. Whatever the server writes is what *everyone* gets.

**3. Every per-portal behavioural knob is a compiled field.** `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot` and all the colour/effect references (:143411-143437) are plain Inspector values with zero ZDO or RPC involvement. Harmony-writing them server-side mutates a copy no client will ever read.

**4. There is no server-side prompt.** A PIN needs a text-entry dialog at the moment of use; `TextInput` is a client UI singleton driven by `TeleportWorld.Interact` (:143471-143484), which the server never runs. TortalPortal's own PIN feature is client-side by construction (`SecurityPatch.CanConfigure` reads `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID()`, SecurityPatch.cs:51 — and on a dedicated server `GetPlayerProfile()` returns a junk profile named "Stranger" with a random UID created in `Game.Awake` at :100047, so every vanilla `IsCreator`/`IsMine`/`IsOwner` helper silently returns garbage rather than throwing).

**5. You cannot even check what the traveller is carrying.** The player's inventory is never networked (see Key-Item Requirement); the ore check `player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)` (:143533 → `Inventory.IsTeleportable` :68860-68880) is unreproducible server-side.

**The three closest approximations, and their honest limits:**
- **Time-sliced connection rotation.** Poll the owner's character ZDO position and write the connection only while they are within N metres of the portal; write `ZDOID.None` otherwise. The destination is re-read at the instant of transit and is *not* cached (:143539-143543), so this takes effect immediately. But `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on **enter only** — a player already standing in the volume when you change it will not re-trigger; they must step out and back in. And it is a race: any other player inside the volume at the moment the connection is live travels too.
- **Server-driven forced teleport.** `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (handler `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962-41968, registered in `Chat.Awake` :41627) or the ZDO-scoped `"RPC_TeleportTo"` (`Character.RPC_TeleportTo` :4126-4132, registered :886) moves any vanilla client with no client install and is genuinely per-player — the server chooses who moves and where. Trigger it from an emote or a map ping rather than from portal geometry. This is a *different feature* (a warp command), not a portal, and it bypasses every vanilla rule including the ore check and `NoPortals`. It also silently no-ops if the target teleported within the last 2s (`Player.TeleportTo` :15302-15326), is dead (`UpdateTeleport` runs only in the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate`, :10213/:10226 — a teleport sent to a dead player latches `m_teleporting = true` and never executes), or is attached/sleeping (`UpdateAttach` re-snaps the transform every tick before `UpdateTeleport`, :10217/:10226; `AttachStop` early-returns while `m_sleeping`, :15890-15918 — pre-check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)`).
- **`ZNetView.LoadFields` per-portal overrides.** `LoadFields` (:82669, client copy assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82970) runs in `ZNetView.Awake` and reflects over every public instance field of every component on the prefab, overriding from the ZDO under `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"` keys gated by the ZDO bools `HasFields` / `HasFields<TypeName>`. So a server can make `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` genuinely per-portal on a 100% vanilla client by writing three ZDO values — a real and under-appreciated capability. But it is still **per-portal, not per-player**, it is client-honoured rather than enforced, and it only applies at instantiation, so a flip does not reach players already standing there; they must leave the area and return.

Ship the feature as "private networks" (the governor refuses to wire outsiders in) rather than "private portals" (the gate refuses outsiders at the threshold). The first is enforceable; the second is not.
catalog.playerExperience: What players will ask for: "my portal should only work for me." What you can honestly deliver: their portal connects only to *their* network's other portals and no stranger's gate can ever be wired into it — but if a stranger walks into their portal, they will travel, because the client made that decision locally and the server was never consulted. Say this in the mod description. The approximation people find acceptable in practice is the proximity-gated hub: a gate that is simply dark (`unconnected`, no glow, walking through does nothing) unless its owner is nearby.
failureModes: Time-sliced rotation leaks to anyone in the trigger volume during the live window, and does not re-trigger for someone already standing in it (`OnTriggerEnter` is enter-only, :143672-143681).

Forced teleport is not a portal: it bypasses `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, `PrivateArea` and the ore check entirely, and gives the server no success/failure signal at all — `Player.TeleportTo`'s bool return is discarded by both RPC handlers (:41966, :4130). The only confirmation is watching the character ZDO's position change ~2s later.

`distantTeleport: false` rubber-bands the player back to origin with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked` when `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses (:15369-15374). Always send `true` for a forced teleport; it force-lands on solid ground at t=15s and can never fail.
`LoadFields` overrides apply only at `ZNetView.Awake` (:82631) — a per-portal `m_allowAllItems` flip does not reach anyone already at the portal.

`PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns true for everything server-side (m_allAreas empty) and `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` returns a junk "Stranger" profile (:100047) — every vanilla ownership helper silently lies rather than throwing. Never call them.

catalog.name: PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine
catalog.oneLine: A 1 Hz main-thread snapshot of every portal ZDO in the world, built from ZDOMan's own always-resident portal registry, that every other ops engine reads and none of them writes.
catalog.howItWorks:
Tick from the subsystem's OnUpdate at a configurable interval (default 1.0 s; floor 0.25 s). Each tick call `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648), which flattens the private `m_portalObjects` dictionary (:76039) into a fresh `List<ZDO>` — one allocation of P refs, P = world portal count. For a zero-alloc read-only hot path use `GetPortals()` (:77643), which returns the live dictionary; never mutate it.

For each ZDO build an immutable record: `m_uid` (ZDOID), `GetPrefab()` (:73876), `GetPosition()` (:73822), `GetRotation()` (:73827), `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (s_tag :78617), `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor)` (:78619), `GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal)` (:74002), `GetOwner()` (:74608), `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (:78393), `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, -1)` (:78395), and DataRevision. Biome comes from `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(Vector3)` (:151692) — pure procedural noise, no colliders, safe headless. Do NOT use `ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight`/`IsBlocked`/`FindFloor`: they are `Physics.Raycast` (ZoneSystem.Awake mask build :113419-113425) and always return the no-hit fallback because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every tick (:100465).

Key the index by a **rounded world position** (0.5 m grid), not ZDOID: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552) so every ZDOID is renumbered on world load. Hold ZDOIDs only for the current session and re-resolve each tick with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` (:76754) — `ZDOPool.Release` calls `ZDO.Reset()` which zeroes `m_uid` (:73536-73545), so a cached ZDO object reference can silently become a different object.

Diff this tick's tuple against last tick's to produce a change event stream (tag/author/connection/position/owner). Publish the snapshot as an immutable DTO list so background threads (HTTP, Discord) never touch ZDOMan.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing. This engine performs zero writes. An operator sees one log line at OnWorldReady — `[Census] 214 portals across 61 tags, 3 unpaired` — and after that only the derived reports produced by other engines. A player standing at a gate notices no hitch, no glow change, no hover-text change.
failureModes: Caching ZDO object references across ticks: ZDOPool recycles the object and Reset() sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:73536-73545), so the record silently points at an unrelated ZDO.

Assuming the ZDOID is a stable identity — it is renumbered on every world load (:74552), so any on-disk index keyed by ZDOID resolves to nothing after a restart (the exact bug TortalPortal/Favorites.cs:109-124 hit and fixed by switching to a rounded-position key).

Trusting the m_portalObjects dictionary key as a location: AddIfPortal files a portal under the sector it had when it was registered and ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756), so the key goes stale if anything ever moves a portal. Always read zdo.GetPosition().
Calling ZoneSystem ground/solid/lava helpers for the biome or height column and getting a plausible-looking but meaningless fallback with no error and no log.
openQuestions: What is P in practice on a long-running world? Log `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList().Count` alongside `ZDOMan.instance.NrOfObjects()` (:77658) at boot and hourly for a week; this sets whether 1 Hz is wasteful or fine.

Which prefabs are in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021, filled Game.Awake :100029-100031)? Log each hash resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` at OnWorldReady — this is the only authoritative list and it picks up modded portal pieces for free.
corrections: GetOwner() returns 0 whenever the Owned flag is clear (:74608-74615); combine with HasOwner() if you want to distinguish 'never owned' from 'released'.

Portal ZDOs are still keyed in m_portalObjects by the SectorIndex captured at insertion; a portal moved by a mod (not possible in vanilla) would not be re-bucketed — irrelevant for vanilla clients, but do not rely on the dictionary key for position.
Citation nits only: :73876 is a blank line (GetPrefab is immediately adjacent); :76754 is GetZDO as claimed; everything else lands on the named member.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Every cited member exists with the claimed shape and executes on a dedicated server with no GameObject dependency. ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648-77656) allocates a fresh List<ZDO> by flattening the private m_portalObjects Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex,List<ZDO>> (:76039); GetPortals() (:77643-77646) returns the live dictionary. m_portalObjects is maintained by AddIfPortal on every RPC_ZDOData receive and CreateNewZDO (:77132, :76690, :77732-77751) and pruned in RemoveFromSector/destroy (:76980-76987), and portal ZDOs are excluded from the normal sector chunks (ZDO.SetSector early-return :73752-73756; AddObjectsPerChunk filters PortalPrefabHash :77571-77574), so the registry is the authoritative always-resident set. Accessors: GetPrefab :73817, GetPosition :73822, GetRotation :73827, GetConnectionZDOID :74002, GetOwner :74608 (returns 0 when !Owned), ZDOVars.s_tag :78617, s_tagauthor :78619, s_creator :78393, s_creatorIndex :78395, DataRevision public property :73494. WorldGenerator.GetBiome(Vector3) :151692 is noise math. ZoneSystem.Awake builds LayerMask raycast masks (:113419-113425) and Game.FixedUpdate pins SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6) every physics tick (:100460-100466) — confirmed, so collider-based ZoneSystem queries are dead server-side. ZDO.Load renumbers m_uid via ++ZDOID.m_loadID (:74552) and ZDO.Reset sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:73536-73545) via ZDOPool.Release, so position keying and per-tick re-resolution through ZDOMan.GetZDO (:76754) are the correct defensive choices. Read-only, main-thread, admin-facing: nothing here touches a client.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every claim checks out. GetPortalList flattens m_portalObjects into a fresh List (:77648-77655); GetPortals returns the live dictionary (:77643-77646). Portals are added to m_portalObjects at load (:76480, :76579, :76598) and on network arrival via AddIfPortal (:77735-77752) and removed at destroy (:76982-76986) -- so the registry is complete and always resident (ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs :73752-73756, so they never migrate sectors). ZDO.Load renumbers m_uid (:74552); ZDO.Reset zeroes m_uid to ZDOID.None (:73536-73548) so a cached ZDO reference after pool release is indeed a different object. WorldGenerator.GetBiome(Vector3) at :151692 is procedural. ZoneSystem.Update on the server only calls CreateLocalZones around the pinned ref pos (1e6,1e6) and CreateGhostZones for peers (:113930-113938); ghost zones do not persist colliders, so Physics.Raycast-based helpers near real portals return the no-hit fallback -- the census's avoidance of them is correct. All the read accessors (GetPrefab, GetPosition, GetRotation, GetConnectionZDOID, GetOwner, GetLong/GetInt, DataRevision) exist as cited. Zero writes -> admin-facing-only is honest. Effort small-medium plausible.

catalog.name: Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)
catalog.oneLine: One report record per portal — tag, position, biome, zone, connection, partner tag, owner peer, builder, tag author, first-seen and last-changed — rendered into every output surface from a single DTO.
catalog.howItWorks:
Define one DTO and render it N ways. Fields and their exact sources:

- `id` — rounded-position key `x:y:z` at 0.5 m (durable across restarts).
- `sessionZdoId` — `zdo.m_uid.ToString()` (`ZDOID.ToString` yields `userID:ID`, :75884). Marked explicitly as session-scoped.
- `prefab` — `zdo.GetPrefab()` resolved via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` (:82045). Needs an in-game check that the prefab table is populated headless.
- `tag` / `tagAuthor` — `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` / `s_tagauthor`. Emit `tagAuthorTrusted: false` always: `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` writes the client-supplied authorId verbatim with no cross-check (:143587-143602).
- `pos` / `rot` — `GetPosition()` / `GetRotation()`.
- `biome` — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos)` (:151692). `zone` — `ZoneSystem.GetZone(pos)` (:115741).
- `interior` — `Character.InInterior(pos)` i.e. `pos.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541); flags a portal built inside a dungeon, whose XZ zone is identical to the surface above it.
- `connection` — `GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal)`; resolve to the partner record and emit `partnerTag`, `partnerPos`, `reciprocal` (does the partner point back), `distance`.
- `ownerPeer` — `GetOwner()` (:74608) joined against `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` `m_uid` (:81630, ZNetPeer.m_uid :78786). 0 = unowned; `ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` (:77362) = server-owned.
- `builder` — `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` joined against `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` via `s_creatorIndex` (World.m_playerHistory :112396, persisted SaveWorldFWLData :112587) to get an authenticated PlatformUserID.
- `firstSeen` / `lastChanged` — **mod-maintained**. Vanilla stores no wall-clock on a ZDO: the whole field set is `m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321) plus DataRevision/OwnerRevision. Stamp `DateTime.UtcNow` the first tick a change is observed and persist the map alongside the network file.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect. An operator running `tplite.list HUB` in their in-game F5 console sees, printed back into that console: `HUB  (3 portals)` then `#1 (0.0, 32.0, 4.0) Meadows z(0,0) -> #2 'HUB' 2140m  owner:server  built-by:Rohan  tagged-by:76561198… (untrusted)  changed 4h ago`. The same rows land in `portals.json`, in a Discord embed, and in the SVG map.
failureModes: Reporting `tagauthor` as ownership. It is a forgeable client self-report (:143587-143602) and can disagree with `s_creator`, which is the placer's profile UID written by their own client in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424).
`s_creator == 0` on world-generated or very old portals — Piece.SetCreator only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417). Render as 'unknown builder', never as 'nobody'.
`s_creatorIndex == -1` when the placer was not yet in m_playerHistory at placement time — the PlatformUserID join silently yields nothing.
Emitting ZDOID as the stable id in an exported file that an operator then scripts against; it changes on every restart.
openQuestions: Does `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` return non-null on the dedicated server build? The prefab table is built in ZNetScene.Awake (:81941-81952) but nothing is instantiated. Log `GetPrefab(Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash[0])?.name` at OnWorldReady; if null, the report must carry raw hashes.

Is `ZDOVars.s_creator` reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? Place one on a vanilla client, dump `s_creator` server-side, and confirm it equals that character ZDO's `s_playerID` (:78539).
catalog.id: ops-admin:Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)
corrections: 'builder ... authenticated PlatformUserID' is overstated: Piece.SetCreator runs on the OWNING CLIENT (m_nview.IsOwner(), :136417) and writes s_creator (the client's own player ID, a client-chosen long) and s_creatorIndex from the client's copy of m_playerHistory (received via the historical player list RPC, :81421-81433). Both are client-written ZDO fields; a modded client can forge them. Emit builderTrusted:false alongside tagAuthorTrusted:false. Only ownerPeer (socket-verified peer uid) is server-authenticated.
Line cites: ZNetPeer.m_uid is :78784 (:78786 is m_server).

prefab name resolution via ZNetScene.GetPrefab(hash) is safe to assume: ZNetScene.instance is required by ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC on the server (:83658) and m_namedPrefabs is filled in its Awake; the 'needs in-game check' hedge can be dropped.

`builder` must carry the same `trusted: false` marker as `tagAuthor`: s_creator and s_creatorIndex are written by the owning client in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424); the index is into the client's received copy of m_playerHistory and can be anything.
Drop the 'needs an in-game check that the prefab table is populated headless' hedge: ZNetScene.Awake populates m_namedPrefabs unconditionally (:81940-81950).
Citation nit: ZNetPeer.m_uid is :78784, not :78786 (:78786 is m_server).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Field sources check out: ZDOID.ToString is GetUserID(UserKey)+":"+ID (:75883-75886); ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) looks up m_namedPrefabs (:82045-82052) and ZNetScene exists on the server (HandleRoutedRPC calls ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance, :83658); TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag stores the client-supplied authorId verbatim with no check (:143587-143602); ZoneSystem.GetZone :115741-115746; Character.InInterior is pos.y>3000 (:4538-4541); ZNet.GetPeers :81630-81633 and ZNetPeer.m_uid (:78784); ZDOMan.GetSessionID :77362; ZDO field set has no wall-clock (:73309-73321 plus revisions at :73492-73494); World.m_playerHistory :112396 and Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator + s_creatorIndex = playerHistory.FindIndex (:136415-136424). The report is pure reads on the census DTO. Two claims overstate trust and one is unverified headless.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Field sources verified: ZDOID.ToString is GetUserID(UserKey)+":"+ID (:75882-75885); ZNetScene.Awake fills m_namedPrefabs unconditionally from m_prefabs/m_nonNetViewPrefabs (:81940-81950) so GetPrefab(int) (:82045) works headless -- the 'needs in-game check' hedge can be dropped; ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746); Character.InInterior is pos.y > 3000f (:4538-4541); ZDO field set is as listed (:73309-73321) with no timestamp; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag stores the client-supplied authorId verbatim (:143587-143602). ZNet.GetPeers (:81630), ZDOMan.GetSessionID (:77362) exist. One substantive overstatement: `builder` is described as an 'authenticated PlatformUserID', but Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) runs on the OWNING CLIENT and writes both s_creator and s_creatorIndex (an index into the client's copy of ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which the server sends at :81324-81341) -- both values are client-supplied and unverified, exactly like tagauthor. The server only maintains m_playerHistory (:81446-81457); it never cross-checks the index a client writes.

catalog.name: Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand
catalog.oneLine: Register onlyServer/remoteCommand console commands from a Terminal.InitTerminal postfix; an admin types them in their own vanilla F5 console and the server executes them, replying into that admin's console.
catalog.howItWorks:
Harmony-postfix `Terminal.InitTerminal` and construct commands:

`new Terminal.ConsoleCommand("tplite.list", "[tag] — list portals", handler, isCheat:false, isNetwork:false, onlyServer:true, isSecret:false, allowInDevBuild:false, hideBehindDevCommands:false, optionsFetcher:null, alwaysRefreshTabOptions:false, remoteCommand:true)` — exact 13-parameter ctor at :43094/:43112.

The delivery path, all verified: the admin's client runs `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734); `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203) fails because `OnlyServer` requires `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`; control falls to the `value.RemoteCommand && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()` branch (:45743) → `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (:81869) → server `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879), which is admin-gated by `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — the same authenticated PlatformUserID vanilla uses for kick/ban (:81670) → `InternalCommand(rpc, command)` (:81891) → `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`.

`Console.instance` **is** non-null on a dedicated server: `Game.Awake` instantiates `m_consolePrefab` when absent (:100038-100041).

Reply to the requesting admin with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, line)` (:81635) → client `RPC_RemotePrint` → `Console.instance.Print`. Resolve the peer from the ZRpc by reproducing the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504) as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`. Also call `args.Context.AddString(line)`, which additionally writes `ZLog.Log("Console: " + line)` (:45983-45985) so every admin action is in the server log.

Command set: `tplite.list [tag]`, `tplite.show <x,z>`, `tplite.dump <x,z>` (full ZDO key dump via `ZDOExtraData.GetData` :75108), `tplite.health`, `tplite.repair [--dry-run]`, `tplite.reload`, `tplite.export`, `tplite.snapshot <name>`, `tplite.restore <name>`, `tplite.tag <x,z> <tag>`, `tplite.link <a> <b>`, `tplite.unlink <a>`, `tplite.lockdown on|off`, `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

Namespace every command `tplite.` — `ConsoleCommand`'s ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (an indexer assignment, :43096/:43114), so a name collision with another mod **silently overwrites** rather than throwing.
catalog.playerExperience: An operator joins the server with a vanilla client, is on adminlist.txt, presses F5, types `tplite.health` and presses Enter. Two seconds later their console fills with `[tplite] 214 portals / 61 tags / 2 stranded / 1 dangling / 0 cross-tag`. A non-admin typing the same command gets `You are not admin` printed back by ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81883). Ordinary players never see anything.
failureModes: Calling `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(cmd)` from server-side mod code: the IsServer() branch passes a null rpc (:81873) into `InternalCommand`, which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()` unconditionally at :81893 → NullReferenceException. Call `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(cmd)` directly instead.
Registering a command name another mod already took: the indexer assignment (:43096) clobbers silently, with no log, and the loser's command simply stops working.

Setting `isCheat:true` — `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` requires the static `m_cheat` flag (:45721-45732), so a cheat command may refuse on the server; keep ops commands non-cheat and rely on the adminlist gate.

Assuming `onlyAdmin:true` adds a check — `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203-43217) never reads `OnlyAdmin`; the ConsoleEvent overload does not even fold it into OnlyServer (:43120), unlike the ConsoleEventFailable overload (:43100). The real gate is RPC_RemoteCommand's adminlist test.
Long reports: one RemotePrint per line is one ZRpc.Invoke each. Chunk to ~40 lines per response and paginate.
openQuestions: Does the Linux headless build read its own stdin at all? No `Console.ReadLine`/stdin reader appears in the assembly; `Console.Update` only drains `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` (:42923) and reads ZInput. Test by typing `help` into the server process's stdin and watching for output — if nothing, the admin-client console is the only interactive path and the file-queue option below is mandatory for scripting.
Is `Terminal.m_cheat` (:43239) true on a dedicated server? Log it at OnWorldReady to know whether cheat-flagged commands are usable at all.
catalog.id: ops-admin:Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand
corrections: Salvage path: pick a vanilla non-cheat, onlyServer, remoteCommand:true command as a carrier — e.g. `setkey`/`removekey` (client :43510-43546: isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true; hideBehindDevCommands only affects tab listing, :43196) or `genloc` (:43475-43485). The client's IsValid fails on OnlyServer (:43203-43217) and the whole raw line is forwarded via ZNet.RemoteCommand(text) -> GetServerRPC().Invoke("RPC_RemoteCommand", text). On the server, Harmony-prefix the private ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command) (:81891-81895) — reached only after the adminlist check in RPC_RemoteCommand (:81881) — and when `command` starts with `setkey tplite.` parse and handle it, returning false so the real setkey never runs (otherwise a global key literally named 'tplite.list HUB' is created). Reply with ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, line) (:81635-81648); the ZRpc is the prefix's own parameter, so reproducing GetPeer(ZRpc) (:80504-80513) is unnecessary.

The ConsoleCommand constructor has 14 parameters, not 13: a trailing `bool onlyAdmin = false` was added and `OnlyServer = onlyServer || onlyAdmin` in the failable overload (:43094-43111, :43112-43127). Server-side registration is still possible and still useful for the file-queue channel, but it is not what makes the in-game path work.

Terminal.InitTerminal is private static and called from Terminal.Awake (:45762-45765), which Console (a Terminal, :42856) runs on the dedicated server because Game.Awake instantiates m_consolePrefab when Console.instance is null (:100035-100041), gated only on FejdStartup.AwakePlatforms() succeeding (:97083-97096) — that part of the claim holds.
Never call ZNet.RemoteCommand on the server: IsServer() routes to InternalCommand(null, command) which dereferences rpc.GetSocket() (:81869-81875, :81893) — NRE.

Vanilla clients cannot execute mod-registered command names: Terminal.TryRunCommand checks the client's own `commands` dictionary before the RemoteCommand fallthrough (:45736-45742, unknown-command path :45755). The described 'admin types tplite.health in F5' flow prints 'not a recognized command' locally and sends nothing.

Working replacement: tunnel through the vanilla `setkey` remote command (remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true, isCheat:false, free-form FullLine :43510-43534). Harmony-prefix ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command) (:81891-81895) -- private instance, patchable -- to intercept commands beginning with `setkey tplite`, execute, RemotePrint(rpc, ...) the reply, and return false so vanilla never calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey with the payload. The admin gate in RPC_RemoteCommand (:81881) still runs first, for free.
Non-admin feedback 'You are not admin' (:81883) still holds for the tunnelled form.
Reply path RemotePrint -> client RPC_RemotePrint -> Console.instance.Print requires the admin's console to be enabled client-side (F5 implies that).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:refuted] The delivery path breaks at its first step. Terminal.TryRunCommand on the admin's VANILLA client begins with commands.TryGetValue(array[0].ToLower(), out value) (client :TryRunCommand, identical to server :45734-45738); the RemoteCommand fallthrough (`else if (value.RemoteCommand && ZNet.instance && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()) ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)`, :45743-45746) is only reachable for a command that is ALREADY in the client's static Terminal.commands dictionary. A server-only mod registers `tplite.*` only in the SERVER process's dictionary; the vanilla client has never heard of it and prints "'tplite.list' is not a recognized command" (:45757-45759) without sending anything. Everything downstream (ZNet.RemoteCommand :81869-81877, RPC_RemoteCommand adminlist gate :81879-81889, InternalCommand :81891-81895, RemotePrint :81635-81648, Console.instance existence via Game.Awake :100035-100041, Terminal.InitTerminal from Terminal.Awake :45762-45765) is verified correct, but is never reached for a mod-named command. The channel can be salvaged only by piggy-backing on a vanilla command name that the client already knows and marks remoteCommand:true.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] The server half is correct: RPC_RemoteCommand gates on ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()) (:81879-81889), InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand (:81891-81895), Game.Awake instantiates m_consolePrefab when absent (:100038-100041), RemotePrint/RPC_RemotePrint exist (:81635-81655), Terminal.InitTerminal is guarded by m_terminalInitialized (:43297-43303), and the ConsoleCommand ctor registers via indexer assignment (:43096, :43114) so collisions overwrite silently. The CLIENT half is refuted as written: the admin's vanilla client runs Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45757), whose FIRST step is `commands.TryGetValue(array[0].ToLower(), out value)` against the CLIENT's own static dictionary. A server-only mod cannot add `tplite.*` to a vanilla client's dictionary, so the text falls straight to `'tplite.list' is not a recognized command` (:45755) and never reaches the `value.RemoteCommand && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()` branch (:45742). Mod-defined command names therefore can NOT be typed in a vanilla F5 console. What DOES work: piggyback on a vanilla command that is remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true, isCheat:false and forwards free-form text -- `setkey` (:43510-43534) passes `args.FullLine.Substring(...)` and is not blocked by Console.isAllowedCommand (only IsCheat commands are, :43xxx override). An admin types `setkey tplite list HUB`; the client forwards it via ZNet.RemoteCommand (:81869-81877); on the server a Harmony prefix on ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc, string) (:81891) intercepts the `setkey tplite` prefix, handles it, replies via RemotePrint(rpc, ...), and returns false -- which is mandatory, because otherwise the vanilla handler calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey("tplite list HUB") and pollutes global keys (:43520). HideBehindDevCommands only affects ShowCommand listing (:43190-43196), not execution. Server-side registration of `tplite.*` in Terminal is still useful for the file-queue channel and for InternalCommand(null, ...) but is not a client entry point.

catalog.name: File-queue command channel (scriptable, no in-game presence)
catalog.oneLine: A watched text file the operator appends command lines to from ssh/cron; the mod polls its mtime, executes each line on the main thread, and writes the result to a sibling response file.
catalog.howItWorks:
Extend Wonderland's existing config-poll pattern (WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile, Plugin.cs:97) to a second file. Every 1 s (configurable) compare `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(<config>/TortalPortalLite.cmd)` against a cached stamp. On change, read all lines, execute each through the same handler table the console commands use, append `<timestamp> <command> -> <result>` to `TortalPortalLite.cmd.out`, then truncate the input file (write-temp-then-File.Replace, the atomic pattern SupplySwitch.Save and TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write:75 both use).

Everything runs on the main thread inside `Update()`, so ZDOMan access is safe — ZDOMan has no locking anywhere and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread`, :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205).

This is the only command channel that works with zero players connected, zero admin clients, and (if the stdin question resolves negative) zero interactive console. It makes every ops action cron-able: a nightly `echo tplite.export >> …/TortalPortalLite.cmd` produces a fresh JSON dump; a monitoring script tails `.cmd.out`.

Security model: the file lives inside `BepInEx/config`, so filesystem permission on the server box *is* the authorization. Explicitly refuse to accept a command file outside `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath`, and never make the handler table reachable from any network path without the adminlist check.

If a background thread ever needs to emit text (an HTTP handler, a webhook callback), do not touch Terminal directly — enqueue into the public `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` `ConcurrentQueue<string>` (:43245), which `Console.Update` drains one line per frame into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925). Vanilla's own save thread uses exactly this to report save errors (:80675, :80710).
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to players. An operator on a phone over ssh runs `echo 'tplite.repair --dry-run' >> ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd; sleep 2; tail -20 ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd.out` and reads `would relink 'merchant-ring' member #3 (4420,95,2180): connection None -> #1; would retag 2 portals 'trade' -> 'TRADE'`.
failureModes: Executing the file's contents off the main thread — ZDOMan is not thread-safe and a concurrent GetPortalList during a SendZDOs sweep will throw or corrupt.
Not truncating after execution: the same commands re-run on the next unrelated mtime bump.
Leaving the file world-writable on a shared host — this channel has no authentication beyond filesystem permissions.

Editor tools that write via rename rather than in-place can make mtime jump backwards; compare for inequality, not greater-than (the same reason Wonderland's PollConfigFile compares `stamp == _configStamp`, Plugin.cs:109).
prerequisites: Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand
openQuestions: How fast does the operator expect a response? A 1 s poll costs one File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc per second; measure that on the target filesystem (network/overlayfs mounts can make stat expensive).
catalog.id: ops-admin:File-queue command channel (scriptable, no in-game presence)
corrections: SupplySwitch.Save uses File.Move(temp, path) (SupplySwitch.cs:128), not File.Replace; File.Replace requires the destination to exist, so use File.Move/overwrite semantics for the first write of the .cmd.out file.

This channel does not depend on the refuted in-game console path — its handler table should be the canonical one and the setkey-carrier hack (see admin channel verdict) and any RemoteCommand path should call into it, not the other way round.

Console.Update only drains Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog when IsConsoleEnabled() (:42892-42895, :42953-42958); on a dedicated server started without `-console` (:97288-97291) the queue is never consumed. Either pass -console, drain it in the mod's own Update, or log from background threads via ZLog.Log directly.

Prereq wording: the file channel does not depend on the RPC_RemoteCommand channel being reachable from vanilla clients (which it is not for mod-named commands); it only needs the shared server-side handler table.
evidence: Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog :43245; producers :80675, :80710; drain in Console.Update :42920-42923 behind IsConsoleEnabled gate :42892-42895
No stdin reader in assembly_valheim_SERVER (grep Console.ReadLine/OpenStandardInput: none)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] All engine claims verified. WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile is a real mtime-poll pattern (Plugin.cs:97-131). ZDOMan has no locking; ZNet.SaveWorldThread (:80583) runs on a background thread but only against clones prepared on the main thread by ZDOMan.PrepareSave -> GetSaveClonePerChunk -> item.Clone() (:76197-76205, :77560-77636) and ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave dictionary clones (:75480-75491), so main-thread Update() access to ZDOMan is the only safe model and this option respects it. Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog is a public static ConcurrentQueue<string> (:43245) drained one line per frame by Console.Update into instance.AddString (:42923-42926), which logs via ZLog.Log (:45983-45986); the save thread enqueues into it exactly as claimed (:80675, :80710). With the in-game RPC channel refuted as designed, this becomes the PRIMARY command channel, not a fallback. Note that AddString's ZLog side effect happens regardless of whether a Console UI exists, so results land in the server log.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Threading claims verified: ZNet.SaveWorld calls m_zdoMan.PrepareSave() on the main thread (:80532) which builds clones via GetSaveClonePerChunk and ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave (:76197-76205, :75480-75490) before the save thread (:80537, :80583) runs, so main-thread Update access to ZDOMan is the only safe pattern and is what the option prescribes. Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog is public static (:43245) and the save thread enqueues into it (:80675, :80710). Wonderland's PollConfigFile mtime pattern exists (Plugin.cs:97, :137) and SupplySwitch/PortalExport use write-temp + File.Replace (PortalExport.cs:160). Stdin: no Console.ReadLine/OpenStandardInput anywhere in the server assembly, so this file channel really is the only headless, player-less input. One correction: the drain of m_threadSafeConsoleLog in Console.Update happens AFTER `if (!IsConsoleEnabled()) return;` (:42892-42895), and m_consoleEnabled is only true with `-console` on the command line (:97290) or PlatformPrefs EnableConsole=1 -- on a typical dedicated server neither holds, the queue is never drained and grows unbounded. Prefer ZLog.Log directly from background threads (Unity's logger is thread-safe) or drain the queue yourself.

catalog.name: Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)
catalog.oneLine: A separate, position-keyed JSON document next to the .cfg that declares admin-defined portal networks (ring / hub / pairs / one-way chain) and is re-parsed and re-applied on save without a restart.
catalog.playerExperience: An operator edits `TortalPortalLite.networks.json` in nano, saves, and within 5 s the server log prints `[Networks] reloaded: 3 networks, 8 members, 0 errors`. Within a further 2 s a player standing at the Docks portal sees its hover text change from `Teleport — 'docks'` to `Teleport — 'TRADE'` and the gate's blue connected-glow snap on (TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal re-evaluates every 0.5 s, :143491-143509). Walking through now lands them at Haldor rather than at whatever random same-tag gate vanilla had picked.
failureModes: Two networks declaring the same `tag`: vanilla's random same-tag pairing (Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679) will cross-link them the instant the reassert loop is late, and phase 1 will not tear it down because the tags match.

Declaring a per-member display tag: impossible without patching. Phase 1's `zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string` test (:100601) transitively forces every linked portal in a network onto one literal string.
A member coordinate that no longer has a portal (player demolished it): with `onMissingMember: "warn"` the ring silently degrades to a chain; the health scanner must surface it loudly.
Whitespace or case drift in `tag` ('Base ' vs 'Base') producing two invisible networks — the comparison is ordinal and whitespace-significant.
Hot-swapping the model mid-tick while the reassert engine is iterating it.
openQuestions: Which JSON parser? BepInEx 5.4.23.5 ships no JSON library and TortalPortal vendors none; Wonderland's DiscordWebhook hand-rolls only an escaper (DiscordWebhook.cs). Either vendor a ~400-line reader or use `UnityEngine.JsonUtility` — but JsonUtility cannot deserialize top-level arrays or Dictionary and needs [Serializable] mirror classes. Decide before writing the schema.
catalog.id: ops-admin:Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)
corrections: Save boundary must be stated: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData writes ONE ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDO, the Target entry overwriting any outbound entry the same ZDO had (:75462-75477), and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load pairs a Portal entry with a Portal|Target entry of equal hash bidirectionally (:77850-77893, from LoadChunks :76515). Rings, hubs and one-way chains come back from a restart as an arbitrary pairwise matching; the 2 s reassert repairs them only because the JSON is the source of truth — say so, and make reassert run before the first Game.ConnectPortals staged commit after load (ZDOMan.Load calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() immediately, :76658).

Live tag collisions are not just a validation problem: any player can retag any portal at any time (RPC_SetTag runs on the owning client, :143587-143602). An unmanaged portal retagged to 'TRADE' with connection None will be paired by phase 2 (:100608-100621) with any member whose connection was momentarily None (e.g. right after a member was retagged by a player, which clears both ends, :143591-143594 and :143604-143620), and once it points at a member it passes phase 1 forever (member tag equal, member connection not None). The reconcile loop must also detect unmanaged portals whose connection targets a member and clear them (or retag them) — or take over Game.ConnectPortals entirely as the Dial option does, which removes the tag constraint.

Server writes into client-owned member ZDOs: a nearby player owns the member ZDO (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927). Vanilla's own Game.SetConnection either routes to the owner via RPC_SetConnection or force-claims with SetOwner(sessionID) then SetConnection (:100636-100646). The reassert should mirror the force path (SetOwner first) so the OwnerRevision bump makes the client accept the write; a bare SetConnection on a client-owned ZDO races the client's DataRevision (:77118-77130) and can diverge.

Retagging members to the network tag rewrites the player-visible tag; the hover text change described is real (GetHoverText reads s_tag each frame, :143453-143464) but it also means a player at a member who presses E sees and can edit the network tag — every such edit clears both ends and must be reverted by the next reassert.

`oneway-chain` is not feasible with vanilla Game.ConnectPortals running: phase 1 clears any portal whose partner has connection None (:100601), phase 2 re-pairs the two (:100609-100620). Either add the ConnectPortals prefix takeover as a prereq for one-way topologies or drop the topology.

Save/restart: ring and hub links collapse to pairwise matching on disk (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75459-75477); at load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77863) then Game.ConnectPortals (:76522) run before any mod tick and randomly pair leftover members. The engine must reassert from the JSON at OnWorldReady and accept a transient wrong-pairing window of up to reassertSeconds; state this.
Sector clamp bound: SectorToIndex accepts zones -256..255, i.e. x/z in [-16416, +16352) -- the ±16320 figure is slightly conservative, fine as a validator but cite the actual math (:115762-115773).

Do not copy Game.SetConnection's owner-routing (private, :100629-100641): direct ZDO.SetConnection + ForceSendZDO from the server propagates without ownership; routing through an online owner hands the write to an untrusted client's Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100643-100652).
Enforcement is server-enforced at the route level only; a player's right to pass (ore check, NoPortals) stays client-side.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The route-level mechanism is server-enforced: the server writes ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73664) and the vanilla client honours whatever connection ZDOID it finds (TeleportWorld.HaveTarget/TargetFound/Teleport :143627-143657, :143538-143548). The claim that vanilla ConnectPortals is left running and tags are therefore load-bearing is correct and precisely stated: phase 1 (:100594-100606) clears a connection only when the target is missing, its s_tag differs (ordinal !=, :100601) or its own connection is None; it never tests reciprocity, so rings, hubs with rotating outbound and fan-in spokes are runtime-stable as long as every member has a byte-identical tag and no member is ever left at None. Position keying is right (ZDO.Load renumber :74552). SectorToIndex clamps sectors outside [-256,255] to Sector 0 (:115755-115774), ZoneSystem.GetZone uses (x+32)/64 (:115741-115746), so the valid world extent is x,z in [-16416, 16352) — the ±16320 bound is conservative and fine. Character.InInterior :4538-4541, ZNet.GetWorldName :80876-80880 exist. Reassertion every 2 s also happens to heal the save-boundary collapse, but the option is silent about it and about a live attack on the tag invariant.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Position-keyed resolution is right (ZDO.Load :74552). The tag-is-load-bearing analysis is exactly right for ring/hub/pairs: ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100594-100606) only tears a link down when the partner's tag differs or the partner has NO connection; it never tests reciprocity, so same-tag rings and fan-in hubs are runtime-stable under vanilla's 5 s pass without any Harmony patch. SectorToIndex clamps |zone| >= 256 to sector 0 (:115755-115774); InInterior :4538; GetWorldName :80876. Hover/glow experience is real: GetHoverText reads the ZDO each call (:143453), UpdatePortal polls at 0.5 s (:143446, :143491). Direct ZDO.SetConnection from the server needs no ownership (ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is revision-only) and itself calls SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73665). Two things are wrong or missing. (1) The `oneway-chain` topology is NOT stable under vanilla: for A->B with B.connection == None, phase 1 tears A down every 5 s (:100601 third clause), phase 2 then pairs A<->B (or B with any other unconnected same-tag member), and the mod's 2 s reassert fights it -- the link flaps between one-way and bidirectional and players intermittently walk into an unlinked frame. One-way topologies require the Game.ConnectPortals prefix takeover, which this option does not list as a prereq. (2) Save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData gives each ZDO one hash slot (:75459-75477), so rings/hubs collapse to a partial perfect matching on disk; on load ZDOMan.LoadChunks runs ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (hash pairs :77863) and then Game.ConnectPortals (:76522), which randomly pairs the leftover same-tag members BEFORE the mod's first reassert. Topology is restored by the mod within one reassert interval, but the option is silent about it and must run its reassert on world-ready, not just on file change.

catalog.name: NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass
catalog.oneLine: A 2 Hz loop that force-writes each managed portal's intended tag and connection using ownership-claim + ForceSendZDO, designed so vanilla's own reconciler never tears the topology down.
catalog.howItWorks:
Exactly one engine in the mod writes `s_tag` or `ConnectionType.Portal`. Every tick (default 2.0 s; must be < 5 s) it walks the resolved network model and, per member, compares the census's current tag/connection against the intended values. If they differ it performs vanilla's own immediate-write recipe verbatim (`Game.SetConnection` :100637-100646):

```
zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID());                       // :74627 / :77362
zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, intendedTag);                       // :73721
zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, intendedTarget);  // :73656
ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);                   // :77706
ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();                         // :76702 (SetConnection already does this, :73661; a tag-only write does NOT)
```

Use `SetConnection`, never `UpdateConnection` — `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` returns false and writes nothing when no connection entry exists (:74962-74976).

**Why this survives vanilla.** `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100596-100605) only clears a connection when the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's tag differs, or the partner's own connection is `None`. It never checks reciprocity. So a ring A→B→C→A, a fan-in hub, and even a self-loop are all indefinitely stable *at runtime* as long as every member shares one literal tag and no member's connection is `None`. Phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches portals already reading `None`. Therefore a correctly-asserted network is invisible to vanilla and the 2 s loop is a repair mechanism, not a race.

**Idempotence is free.** `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns when type and target are unchanged (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on an equal value (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so `ZDO.Set` skips `IncreaseDataRevision`. An unchanged re-assert generates zero DataRevision bumps, zero network traffic and zero disk dirtying. Budget `ForceSendZDO` calls per tick (cap 256, mirroring StructureUpkeep.MaxHealthBroadcastsPerSweep) so a first-boot mass repair does not spike every peer in one frame.

**Ownership contention.** `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs every 2 s and hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer (:76872-76885, :76901-76927). Our claim will be stolen back — that is fine, the *value* already went out via ForceSendZDO. Only add the `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix guard (the WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 pattern) if measurement shows write-back contention; keep the predicate a single `PortalPrefabHash.Contains` test and never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`.
catalog.playerExperience: A player demolishes one gate of a three-gate ring. Within ≤5 s vanilla's reconciler notices the dangling partner and nulls the neighbours' links; within ≤2 s of that the reassert engine re-closes the ring between the two survivors and their hover text goes from `unconnected` back to `connected`. A player retagging a managed gate through the vanilla 10-character box sees their new tag persist for at most 2 s and then snap back to `TRADE`, with a toast: `This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`
failureModes: Setting reassertSeconds ≥ 5 s: vanilla's phase 2 wins a window and randomly re-pairs a briefly-orphaned member (`UnityEngine.Random.Range` :100678).

Writing a tag without calling `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702): `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) only routes to `SetDirtySector`, and portals are explicitly excluded from the ordinary chunk save (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572). The rename is live but silently absent from the next world save.

Racing vanilla's deferred branch: `Game.SetConnection` only defers to an online owner (:100647-100650). Our direct claim-and-write bypasses that, which is correct — but it means a client that currently owns the portal may push a conflicting higher-DataRevision blob back via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77103-77133), which replaces the whole ZDO with no field-level merge. The 2 s loop re-corrects it; instantaneous consistency is not achievable.

Caching ZDO object references between ticks — vanilla itself does this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` and can force-write through a pooled, recycled reference (Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698 vs ZDOPool.Release in HandleDestroyedZDO :76990). Do not copy that.
prerequisites: Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)
citations: Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine 5 s — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580-100587; started under IsServer() Game.Start :100070-100075
openQuestions: Does a client already standing at a gate pick up a server-side `s_tag` rewrite without a zone reload? `UpdatePortal` runs on a 0.5 s InvokeRepeating (:143450) and drives the glow, but hover text comes from a separate `GetTagInfo` read (:143563-143569) evaluated per hover frame. Stand at a gate, rewrite the tag, and watch.

Measure the real ownership tug-of-war: log `zdo.GetOwner()` on one managed portal every second for 60 s with a player standing next to it, to decide whether the SetOwner prefix guard is needed at all.
catalog.id: ops-admin:NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass
corrections: Game.SetConnection immediate write is the fallback path (owner==0 / dead peer / forceImmediateConnection); for an online owner vanilla delegates via ZRoutedRpc RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648). Direct server writes under a live owner risk DataRevision collision (RPC_ZDOData rejects revision <= local, :77103-77112); bump zdo.DataRevision (public setter :73494) by a margin after every corrective write.

ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-overwrites both sides of any pair staged on the previous pass, including managed portals that transiently read None; expect a one-bounce overwrite per disturbance (≤7 s), not 'never'. Consider a Harmony prefix on Game.ForceSetConnection/SetConnection (both private) for managed ZDOIDs.

While the server owns a managed portal, a vanilla retag RPC targets the server (ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) → m_zdo.GetOwner(), :82855-82858) and is dropped in HandleRoutedRPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null on a dedicated server (:83650-83664); the 'snap back after ≤2 s' experience only holds while a client owns the ZDO.
ZDO.SetOwner is at :74624-74631 (cited :74627 is inside it, fine); ForceSendZDO still requires peer.ShouldSend (AddForceSendZdos) so it prioritises, never bypasses revision gating.

Tag-only writes: IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector → SetDirtyChunks on the sector chunk (:73832-73840, :76694-76700) which excludes portal prefabs (:77572); explicit SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) is required — confirmed.

Add an explicit 'tag reservation' step: any UNMANAGED portal whose s_tag equals a managed network tag must be retagged (or its connection cleared and tag suffixed) by the same engine, otherwise a member's transient None window lets vanilla phase 2 stage U↔A and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes it 5 s later; the leftover U→A one-way link is never cleared by phase 1 (:100600-100603 requires tag mismatch or partner None).

Replace 'zero network traffic' with: zero traffic only when the engine skips ForceSendZDO on an unchanged member; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) returns true for any peer lacking the ZDO, so a ForceSendZDO on an unchanged ZDO still ships it to every peer that never had it.

State the save-boundary behaviour: the intended topology is re-derived from the network file each boot, but ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (ZDO.Load :74552 `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so the network model must key members by a stable identity (position+prefab, or a mod-written ZDO string key), never by ZDOID. Rings/self-loops collapse in RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) and are only restored by the engine's first tick after LoadChunks → Game.ConnectPortals (:76524).

Note that during the ≤2 s server-ownership window a vanilla retag is silently dropped (ZNetView.InvokeRPC targets owner :82855-82858; server HandleRoutedRPC FindInstance==null :83651-83664) — the player sees no change and no toast unless the engine emits one from the census diff.
The 'toast' in playerExperience is not free: it needs a PlayerNotify-style RPC to the retagger, whose identity is only probable (census diff) unless the retag crossed the wire (see AuditEngine).
evidence: ZDOMan.AddForceSendZdos ShouldSend gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs (AddForceSendZdos body, follows :77262)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists with the claimed shape and the core mechanism holds on a dedicated server: Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine is started only under ZNet.IsServer() (Game.Start :100070-100075) with no local-player dependency; phase 1 (:100596-100605) clears a link only when the partner is null, has a different tag, or reads None — no reciprocity test, so rings/fan-in are runtime-stable; phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches portals reading None. ZDO.SetConnection → ZDOExtraData.SetConnection is a genuine early-return no-op on equal (type,target) (:74951-74961) and ZDO.Set(string) → s_strings.InitAndSet → BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on Equals (utils_SERVER :321-345), so unchanged re-asserts do not bump DataRevision; AddForceSendZdos additionally requires peer.ShouldSend (revision-gated), so a no-op write produces zero packets. UpdateConnection refuses to create (:74962-74976) — correct to use SetConnection. ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands a server-owned portal to any nearby peer because IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, m_sessionID) tests against the pinned (1e6,0,1e6) ref position (:76888-76899, :76901-76927). Three real defects in the write-up: (1) The 'verbatim vanilla recipe' is vanilla's FALLBACK path — Game.SetConnection takes it only for owner==0, a dead peer, or forceImmediateConnection; for an online owner vanilla deliberately delegates via RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648). Writing directly under a live client owner creates a DataRevision collision hazard: RPC_ZDOData rejects any incoming revision <= local (:77103-77112) and the client's RPC_ZDOData does the same, so if client and server both write from the same base revision (e.g. player retags twice within a reassert interval), server and client end up with equal DataRevision and different content and stay desynced until the next write. DataRevision has a public setter (:73494); the engine must bump it by a margin (e.g. +1000) after each corrective write so the server copy always wins. (2) 'Never tears the topology down' is overstated: ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes BOTH directions of every pair staged on the previous pass via ForceSetConnection (forceImmediateConnection:true), regardless of what the reassert loop wrote in between. Any disturbance that makes a managed portal read None (partner demolished, partner retagged) lets phase 2 stage it against ANY unconnected same-tag portal — including a player's unmanaged one — and the next 5 s pass overwrites the reassert value once; the 2 s loop then re-fixes. Bounded (~7 s) but it is a race, and the staged victim (a player's portal pointing at a managed gate) is torn down by phase 1 on the following pass. Mitigation: Harmony-prefix Game.ForceSetConnection/SetConnection (private, need AccessTools) for managed ZDOIDs, or clear m_currentlyConnectingPortals entries touching managed portals. (3) The player-experience snap-back is wrong for the ownership window: client TeleportWorld.SetText → ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858 both builds). While the server holds ownership (after the engine's SetOwner, until ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it back ≤2 s later) the retag RPC routes to the server, whose HandleRoutedRPC does ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo) → null on a dedicated server (:83650-83664) and drops it silently; the player's box closes with no tag change at all and the mod's toast never fires. Also client RPC_SetTag applies only when m_nview.IsOwner() (client :144327-144341), so an owner==0 portal accepts no retag from anyone.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds against the decompile. Game.SetConnection immediate branch (SERVER :100637-100651) is exactly SetOwner(session) → SetConnection → ForceSendZDO; ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666) bumps DataRevision and calls SetDirtyPortals only for Portal type; ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) → ZDOExtraData.Set → s_strings.InitAndSet (:74918, :75681-75685) → BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on Equals (utils_SERVER :321-330), so an equal tag write does not bump revision; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection early-returns on equal type+target (:74951-74961); UpdateConnection returns false with no entry (:74962-74976). ConnectPortals phase 1 predicate (:100596-100605) is exactly `null || tag differs || partner None` — no reciprocity, so rings/fan-in/self-loops are runtime-stable. Phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches None portals. Client-side acceptance verified: ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) sends when server DataRevision > peer's last-seen, and the client's RPC_ZDOData whole-ZDO replace mirrors :77103-77133, so the server's write (rev = last-accepted client rev + 2) always wins the round; convergence within ~2 ticks even if the client writes concurrently. Vanilla client retag path (CLIENT TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :144327-144342) does UpdateConnection(None)+Set(tag)+Set(tagauthor) on the owner, reaching the server through ClientChanged (:73832-73836) → CreateSyncList client branch (:77241-77258). Ownership steal by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) confirmed: a server-owned portal in a peer's active area is reassigned to the peer within 2 s because IsInPeerActiveArea(session) tests against the pinned ref pos (:76887-76899). Refutations of specific sub-claims: (a) 'invisible to vanilla' is false during any window where a member reads None (destroyed partner, player retag): phase 2 will pair that member with an UNMANAGED portal carrying the same literal tag, stage it, and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes that pairing 5 s later via ForceSetConnection (:100629-100635), fighting the engine for one round; the residue is a one-way U→A link that phase 1 never clears (tags equal, A non-None) — an unmanaged portal permanently fans into the managed network. (b) 'zero network traffic' on unchanged re-assert holds only because the engine skips ForceSendZDO when nothing differs; a ForceSendZDO on an unchanged ZDO still transmits to every peer that has never received it (ShouldSend returns true for an absent m_zdos entry, :76003-76012). (c) During the ≤2 s the server owns a member, a vanilla retag is silently dropped: ZNetView.InvokeRPC targets the owner (:82855-82858) = server, whose HandleRoutedRPC hits ZNetScene.FindInstance == null (:83651-83664). Harmless but real. (d) The 'RPC_ZDOData whole-ZDO replace' citation points at the server's receive path; the symmetric client path was verified in the client decompile. Enforcement: honest as server-enforced under the reviewer's ROUTE test — the connection field and tag are server-owned and re-asserted; a vanilla client cannot durably change them. It does not stop RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953-76961, no sender/ward check).

catalog.name: HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection
catalog.oneLine: A 30 s pure-read pass over the census that classifies every pathology vanilla's pairing algorithm can produce, including the permanent one-member strand that 3+ same-tag portals always create.
catalog.howItWorks:
Runs on the census snapshot, writes nothing. Each finding carries severity, portal id(s) and a suggested repair.

1. **Odd-count strand (the big one).** Group portals by exact `s_tag`. For any group of size N ≥ 3, vanilla's strictly-pairwise phase 2 leaves exactly ⌊N/2⌋ pairs and `N mod 2` permanently orphaned members: the surviving pair re-confirms itself every tick, so the orphan never rotates in. Report every unmanaged tag group with N ≥ 3, naming the currently-orphaned member and warning that *which* member is orphaned is dictionary-bucket order and changes across restarts (iteration order comes from `m_portalObjects` enumeration in `GetPortalList` :77648-77656).
2. **Dangling connection.** `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` non-None but `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` returns null. Vanilla clears this within 5 s (:100600-100603); report only if it persists across two scans, which indicates something is re-writing it.
3. **Non-reciprocal link.** A→B while B→C or B→None. Legal and stable in vanilla (phase 1 has no reciprocity check) — informational for unmanaged portals, an error for a network declared `pairs`.
4. **Self-loop.** A→A. Stable at runtime, but **erased at save**: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` writes the source slot then immediately overwrites it with the Target slot because target != None (:75461-75478). Flag as 'will not survive restart'.
5. **Cross-tag link.** Partner tag != own tag; vanilla will tear it down within 5 s.
6. **Duplicate / near-duplicate tags.** Ordinal comparison means `Base`, `base` and `Base ` are three networks. Report groups that differ only by case or trailing whitespace.
7. **Out-of-world.** |pos.xz| beyond ~16320 m falls into `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex`'s clamp-to-sector-0 bucket (:115755-115774) — the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to.
