8. **Interior portal.** `pos.y > 3000f` (:4538) — built inside a dungeon; shares the surface XZ zone, worth flagging for operators who forbid it.
9. **Unknown prefab.** `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())` null — a portal from an uninstalled mod.
10. **Sector duplication.** The same ZDOID appearing twice in `GetPortalList()` — `AddIfPortal` adds under the current sector without removing the old entry (:77732-77752), so any repositioned portal duplicates and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) can only clean one bucket, leaking the other permanently.

Note there is **no** 'portal in an unloaded zone' pathology: portals live in `m_portalObjects`, are loaded wholesale from the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file at world load (:76474-76482), are never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76885), and `FlushClientObjects` is client-only (:76180-76183). The census is always complete.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect. The operator's 30 s log line reads `[Health] OK` most of the time, and on a problem: `[Health] tag 'home' has 5 portals — 2 pairs + 1 permanently stranded at (410,33,-88); tag 'Base ' (trailing space) is a separate 1-portal network, probably a typo for 'Base'`. A player who tagged three gates `home` and wondered why one never connects finally gets an answer an admin can give them.
failureModes: Reporting a dangling connection during the normal 5 s window after someone demolishes a gate — require two consecutive scans before flagging.

Reporting every untagged portal as one giant broken group: `ZDO.GetString` defaults to `""` (ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082), so every untagged portal in the world is a single tag group and freshly placed untagged gates genuinely do auto-pair at random. Treat tag `""` as a special case with its own message.
Treating the orphan as a stable identity — it is bucket-order-dependent and can differ after a restart.
Missing a duplicated portal because the diff is keyed by rounded position, which collapses the two entries; key the duplicate check on ZDOID reference count within the raw list.
openQuestions: Confirm in-game that a 3-portal same-tag group really does permanently strand one member rather than rotating: place three, watch `[ Connected N portals ]` log lines (:100625) for 5 minutes, and confirm the orphan never changes.
catalog.id: ops-admin:HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection
corrections: Orphan choice: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal uses UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100677); m_portalObjects enumeration order only decides which member searches first.

Orphan identity is stable across restarts when the pairing was saved — ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load restores pairs from ZDOConnectionHashData (:77850-77891). It re-randomises only when a pair breaks.
Out-of-world threshold is x >= 16352 or x < -16416 (and same for z) per GetSectorIndex/SectorToIndex (:115742-115768).

Item 9 only applies to ZDOs persisted in ChunkPortal while a mod had registered its prefab in Game.PortalPrefabHash (:100029-100031); those also leak from m_portalObjects on destroy because HandleDestroyedZDO gates removal on PortalPrefabHash.Contains (:76980).
Item 10 sector duplication is mod-induced only (vanilla never repositions a portal ZDO).

Item 1: the orphan is selected by UnityEngine.Random.Range over the candidate list (:100678), not dictionary-bucket order; and the orphan identity is preserved across restarts because the paired members are saved as a hash pair (:75461-75478) and restored by ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) before Game.ConnectPortals runs at :76524. It only changes if the save missed the pairing or a member was destroyed.

Item 10: sector duplication requires a portal ZDO's position to cross a sector boundary; vanilla never repositions a portal (no ZSyncTransform on the prefab, TeleportWorld never writes position). Classify as mod/admin-induced. The stale bucket entry points at a ZDOPool-released object (:76988), so GetPortalList consumers must filter with IsValid().

Item 2: Game.SetConnection defers the clear to the online owner via RPC_SetConnection (:100647-100651); if that owner has the portal outside its instantiated area the clear is dropped until ownership migrates, so a dangling link can outlive two scans without any re-writer. Report as 'stale, owner-side clear pending' rather than 'being re-written'.
Item 7: state the clamp per axis (SectorToIndex :115762-115774): sectorX or sectorY outside [-256,255]; in metres x/z ≥ 16320 or < -16416.
Cross-restart identity: findings that name a portal by ZDOID are meaningless after a restart (ZDO.Load :74552 regenerates IDs); name by position/prefab.
evidence: ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal branch and Game.ConnectPortals call — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76482, :76524-76527
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Pure-read, runs on the server's own ZDO tables, no GameObject or local-player dependency anywhere — execution context is correct. Verified: odd-group strand follows from phase 2 pairing strictly two at a time and phase 1 never breaking a confirmed pair (:100596-100622); self-loop erasure is real — RegenerateConnectionHashData writes s_connectionsHashData[key]=(Portal,hash) then overwrites the same key with (Portal|Target,hash) when target==key (:75461-75478), and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load only pairs a Portal-typed source with a distinct Target-typed entry (:77850-77891); AddIfPortal duplicates when the sector changed because ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so RPC_ZDOData's InternalSetPosition never moves the bucket and AddIfPortal appends under the new sector (:77732-77752), while HandleDestroyedZDO removes only from the current sector (:76980-76986); portal chunk loaded wholesale (:76474-76482), ReleaseZDOS only touches ownership (:76872-76885), FlushClientObjects only under !IsServer in ShutDown (:76180-76183); GetString default "" (:75079-75082); SectorToIndex clamps to 0 (:115755-115768). Corrections: (1) Orphan selection is not 'dictionary-bucket order' alone — FindRandomUnconnectedPortal picks via UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100677); iteration order only decides who searches first. (2) 'Changes across restarts' is wrong when the pairing was persisted: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals restores saved pairs from ZDOConnectionHashData at load (:77850-77891), so the orphan identity is stable across restarts as long as the portal chunk was saved with the pair; it re-randomises only when a pair is broken. (3) Out-of-world threshold: sectorX = floor((x+32)/64) clamps at sectorX >= 256 or < -256, i.e. x >= 16352 or x < -16416 (:115742-115768), not '~16320'. (4) Item 9 'unknown prefab' only fires for ZDOs that were saved into ChunkPortal while a mod had added its hash to Game.PortalPrefabHash (populated solely from Game.m_portalPrefabs, :100029-100031); a modded portal never registered there is not in m_portalObjects at all. Such leftovers also leak: HandleDestroyedZDO's PortalPrefabHash.Contains gate (:76980) skips removing them from m_portalObjects. (5) Item 10 sector duplication requires a position change across a 64 m sector boundary, which vanilla never does to a portal — mod-induced only. (6) Item 2: vanilla's clearing goes through Game.SetConnection which may delegate to an online owner via RPC (:100637-100648), so 'within 5 s' can extend by a round-trip; the two-scan persistence rule is sound.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Pure-read classification over GetPortalList (:77648-77656) is sound and every cited mechanism exists. Odd-count strand confirmed: phase 2 (:100607-100622) pairs strictly pairwise, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) only returns None-connection candidates, and phase 1 keeps a pair alive forever, so the Nth member never rotates in. Two claims in item 1 are wrong: (a) the orphan is chosen by UnityEngine.Random.Range over candidates (:100678), seeded by GetPortalList iteration order — not 'dictionary-bucket order'; (b) it does NOT change across restarts in the normal case: the surviving pair is saved as a matching hash pair by RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478, SetConnection already set DirtyPortals :73661-73664) and restored verbatim by ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77850-77893) before Game.ConnectPortals (:76524) runs, so the same member stays orphaned. Self-loop erasure confirmed: source slot written then overwritten with Portal|Target for the same key (:75471-75475); on load GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal) requires exact type equality (:75414-75424) so the entry is excluded and the connection vanishes. Sector duplication confirmed in code (ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs :73752-73756; GetSectorIndex derives from m_position :73776-73779; AddIfPortal keys on current sector without removing old :77732-77752; HandleDestroyedZDO removes only from the current sector :76980-76986) but it only fires if a portal ZDO's position changes across a 64 m sector boundary, which nothing in vanilla does (portals have no ZSyncTransform; TeleportWorld never writes position) — it is a mod/admin-induced pathology, and the stale entry then references a pooled ZDO (ZDOPool.Release :76988), so the census must IsValid()-filter. Out-of-world clamp confirmed (:115762-115774; x or z ≥ 16320 or < -16416 per axis → Sector 0). Interior y>3000 confirmed (:4538-4541). 'No unloaded-zone pathology' confirmed: LoadChunks loads the whole ChunkPortal file (:76474-76482), ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership (:76872-76885). Item 2 caveat: vanilla clears a dangling link by Game.SetConnection which routes through RPC_SetConnection to an online owner (:100647-100651) — that client-side hop can legitimately delay clearing beyond one 5 s tick if the owner has the object unloaded, so the 'persists across two scans ⇒ something is re-writing it' inference has a benign false positive.

catalog.name: Automatic repair pass (with dry-run and blast-radius cap)
catalog.oneLine: Turn each health finding into a bounded, logged, reversible corrective ZDO write — normalising tags, splitting odd groups, clearing dangling links — gated behind an explicit config opt-in and a --dry-run default.
catalog.howItWorks:
A repair is a (finding → action) table executed on demand (`tplite.repair`) or on a slow timer if `AutoRepair` is enabled. Default is **dry-run**: compute and print every action, write nothing.

Actions, each using the reassert engine's write primitive (claim owner → write → ForceSendZDO → SetDirtyPortals):
- **Tag normalisation.** Trim trailing/leading whitespace and optionally case-fold, when and only when it merges a 1-member group into an existing group. Writing `s_tag` alone requires `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` explicitly (:76702) — `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) routes to `SetDirtySector`, which the portal chunk ignores (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572).
- **Odd-group resolution.** For an N≥3 unmanaged group, either (a) suffix the orphan's tag (`home` → `home-2`) so it stops competing, or (b) promote the whole group into a managed ring in the network file. Never silently retag a player's gate without `AllowTagRewrite=true` and an audit entry naming the original tag.
- **Dangling clear.** `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` — identical to what vanilla does 5 s later, useful only when combined with an immediate `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` call (public, :100589) to re-pair in the same frame instead of waiting.
- **Self-loop removal.** Break it before the next save silently does.
- **Duplicate-bucket cleanup.** Not repairable through any public API: the duplicate lives inside the private `m_portalObjects` dictionary. `GetPortals()` (:77643) returns the live dictionary and *can* be mutated to remove the stale entry — powerful and dangerous; gate behind a separate `AllowRegistrySurgery` flag and log loudly.

Every repair emits an audit line and is preceded by an automatic state snapshot (see the snapshot/rollback option), so `tplite.restore pre-repair` undoes the whole batch.

Cap actions per invocation (default 64) and per tick (default 16). Vanilla's own cost model makes this cheap — idempotent re-writes are free — but a first repair on a neglected 400-portal world can otherwise issue hundreds of `ForceSendZDO` calls in one frame, each of which re-serialises the entire ZDO to every peer with no delta encoding (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` :77053-77062).
catalog.playerExperience: An operator types `tplite.repair` and gets a printed plan: `DRY RUN — 4 actions: retag (410,33,-88) 'home' -> 'home-2' [orphan of 5]; trim 'Base ' -> 'Base' at (12,30,80); clear dangling link at (2600,41,-700); break self-loop at (0,32,4). Re-run with --apply.` They run `tplite.repair --apply`; the log shows `[Repair] applied 4/4, snapshot 'pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z' saved`. A player who had two gates tagged `Base ` and `Base` walks into one and now arrives at the other for the first time.
failureModes: Auto-repair on by default: silently retagging player-built gates is the single fastest way to make an operator uninstall the mod. Default off, default dry-run.
Repairing during the 5 s window in which vanilla is itself mid-repair — the two writes fight and produce audit noise. Skip any portal whose connection changed within the last 6 s.

Mutating the live `m_portalObjects` dictionary returned by `GetPortals()` (:77643) while `Game.ConnectPortals` is iterating a `GetPortalList()` snapshot of it — the snapshot is a copy so it will not throw, but `AddIfPortal`/`HandleDestroyedZDO` bookkeeping desynchronises.
Assuming a repair persists: without `SetDirtyPortals()` a tag-only repair is live in memory and absent from the world file.
prerequisites: HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection
NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass
Network state snapshot, rollback and migration
openQuestions: Does removing an entry from the live `m_portalObjects` dictionary cause any vanilla path to throw? `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77632), `FindObjects` (:77367-77381) and `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77457-77469) all enumerate it. Test on a scratch world before enabling registry surgery.
catalog.id: ops-admin:Automatic repair pass (with dry-run and blast-radius cap)
corrections: `tplite.repair` cannot be typed from a vanilla client console: client Terminal.TryRunCommand forwards only commands present in the client's own table with RemoteCommand=true (client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45734-45760); the server's RPC_RemoteCommand (:79921, body via Console.instance.TryRunCommand) never sees mod-only names. Vanilla dedicated server has no stdin command reader (no ReadLine/OpenStandardInput in assembly_valheim_SERVER). Provide a mod-owned trigger.
Apply the DataRevision-margin rule from the reassert engine on every repair write under a live client owner (RPC_ZDOData revision gate :77103-77112).
Registry surgery on the live m_portalObjects dictionary must call SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) afterwards and must delete the entry under the stale sector, not the current one.
Vanilla's 'dangling clear' may route through the owner via RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648); the mod's write is the forceImmediateConnection path.

Tag normalisation must check the target group's parity: merging a 1-member group into an existing EVEN group (a paired pair) produces N=3 and strands the merged portal permanently (phase 2 :100607-100622 never repairs a live pair). Merge only into a size-1 group or an odd group with a stranded member.

Enforcement is admin-facing-only, not server-enforced: for unmanaged portals each action is a single write with no re-assertion; a vanilla owner client can retag it back at any time (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag client :144327-144342) and vanilla's 5 s pass keeps operating on the result. Continuing enforcement exists only for portals then adopted by the reassert engine.

Registry surgery on GetPortals(): the leaked entry is a ZDOPool-released object (HandleDestroyedZDO :76988), so identify it by m_uid == ZDOID.None / !IsValid(), never by position; and set DirtyPortalObjects (SetDirtyPortals :76702) afterwards so the corrected list is what gets saved.

Soften the ForceSendZDO spike claim: SendZDOs is budgeted per peer per frame (10240 bytes, :77007-77046) with overflow left in m_forceSend (:77260-77280); the mod cap avoids queue growth, not a single-frame burst.
Snapshot/rollback prereq must not key on ZDOID (ZDO.Load :74552 regenerates IDs); restoring a 'pre-repair' snapshot after a restart requires stable keys.
evidence: ZNet RPC_RemoteCommand register / body — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79921; RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand bodies (grep 'private void RPC_RemoteCommand')
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All write primitives are real and server-executable: Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589) and callable on demand; GetPortals returns the live Dictionary (:77643-77646) so registry surgery is possible; SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO per peer with no delta (:77045-77062); tag-only writes need SetDirtyPortals because IncreaseDataRevision only dirties the sector chunk (:73832-73840, :76694-76700) from which portal prefabs are excluded (:77572). Corrections: (1) The `tplite.repair` console trigger is not reachable from a vanilla client: client Terminal.TryRunCommand only forwards to ZNet.RemoteCommand when the command exists in the CLIENT's own dictionary with RemoteCommand=true (client :45734-45760); an unknown `tplite.*` command prints 'not a recognized command' and never leaves the client. RPC_RemoteCommand on the server (:79921 register; body admin-gated by adminlist hostname → Console.instance.TryRunCommand) therefore only ever carries vanilla remote commands. Terminal.UpdateInput is GUI/input-focus driven (:45775-), and the dedicated server has no stdin reader in vanilla (no Console.ReadLine/OpenStandardInput anywhere in the server assembly). Invocation must come from the mod's own channel (config flag/timer, a watched file, a stdin thread the mod owns, or a piggy-backed vanilla remote command). (2) Inherits the reassert engine's DataRevision-collision caveat: repairs under a live client owner must bump DataRevision by a margin. (3) 'Dangling clear identical to vanilla' — vanilla's path delegates to an online owner via RPC (:100637-100648); the mod's direct write is vanilla's force path. (4) A tag suffix like `home-2` is fine, but any mod-written tag longer than the client's 10-char input limit cannot be re-entered by a player. (5) Registry surgery on m_portalObjects must also set DirtyPortalObjects (SetDirtyPortals) or the corrected bucket state is not written at the next save; and removing the stale duplicate must remove the entry whose sector != zdo.GetSectorIndex(), otherwise HandleDestroyedZDO later fails to find the live one.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Write primitives are real: Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589) and callable on demand (it first runs ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, committing any staged pair early — harmless); ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is required for a tag-only write because IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector (:73832-73839, :76695-76700) only marks a normal chunk and AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal prefabs (:77572) while the ChunkPortal file is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77631); GetPortals returns the live m_portalObjects (:77643-77646). Two design errors: (1) 'Tag normalisation ... when and only when it merges a 1-member group into an existing group' recreates the odd-count strand whenever the target group is already an even pair — merging 'Base ' into a 2-member 'Base' yields N=3 and the merged portal becomes the permanent orphan (phase 2 :100607-100622 only pairs None portals). The merge must be gated on target-group parity (size 1, or odd with a stranded member). (2) The enforcement label is wrong: for unmanaged portals every repair is a one-shot write; nothing stops a vanilla client from retagging 'home-2' back to 'home' the next second (client RPC_SetTag :144327-144342 needs only ownership, which ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927 grants within 2 s), and vanilla's reconciler keeps acting on the result. Only portals subsequently handed to the reassert engine are enforced. Registry surgery caveat verified: the stale duplicate entry references a ZDOPool-released object (:76988), so mutation must compare by m_uid/IsValid, not object identity alone. The ForceSendZDO fan-out concern is overstated: SendZDOs (:77007-77062) already caps each peer's packet at the 10240-byte send budget and breaks (:77043-77046), leaving the rest queued in m_forceSend (:77260-77280) — the per-tick cap is still good practice, but vanilla does not spike 'every peer in one frame'.

catalog.name: AuditEngine — attributed change log for every tag and link write
catalog.oneLine: Census-diff as the complete channel, an RPC_RoutedRPC prefix for authenticated attribution, and m_onZDODestroyed for deletions — with 'probable' vs 'confirmed' actor never conflated.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three complementary sources, only one of which is complete:

**(1) Census diff — the only complete source.** Every tick, diff (tag, tagauthor, connection, position, owner) per portal. This catches changes that never touch the wire: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,…)` targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858), so a client that already owns a portal retags it in-process with zero packets. The resulting ZDO change still reaches the server, because `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` queues `ZDOMan.ClientChanged` on a client (:73832-73849, :77727-77730) and `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains that queue to the server peer regardless of distance (:77241-77258). Detection latency = the census tick.

**(2) `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` Harmony prefix — authenticated attribution when available.** `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632) is the one and only place where the authentic socket and the payload coexist; `m_senderPeerID` is deserialised straight off the wire (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495) and is a client self-report everywhere downstream. In the prefix: save `pkg.GetPos()`, deserialise a **copy** (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`), match `m_methodHash` against `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()`, resolve the true sender as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`, and take `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — the PlatformUserID the Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth actually verified at connect (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79843-79870; the same identity vanilla's own admin check uses, ZNet.RPC_Kick :81670). Restore `pkg.SetPos()` and return true.

**(3) `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033, invoked :76975) — a public `Action<ZDO>` field fired before removal, so the portal is still readable. Filter with `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`. **Combine, never assign**: `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953).

Record shape: `{utc, portalId, field, from, to, actor, actorConfidence}`. `actorConfidence` is `confirmed` only for source (2); for a census-detected change with no matching RPC it is `probable`, resolved to the nearest connected character within 40 m at detection time (`ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS` :81024-81044), or `unknown`. Follow `AuditLog.Flag`'s discipline of writing `Unknown` rather than guessing (AuditLog.cs:15). Suppress the mod's own writes by having the reassert engine register each intended change in an 'expected' set the audit subtracts.

Store as a bounded ring buffer (2000 entries, the `ItemLedger` pattern) plus an append-only `portal-audit.log`.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect unless the operator enables the optional toast. The log reads `[AUDIT] tag (1240,31,-3310) 'trade' -> 'TRADE' by 76561198…/Rohan (confirmed) at 14:02:11Z` for a retag that crossed the wire, and `[AUDIT] link (0,32,4) #A -> #B by (probable) Rohan @ 6m` for one that did not. A player who demolishes someone else's gate shows up as `[AUDIT] destroyed (410,33,-88) tag 'home' builder Sigrid`.
failureModes: Reading the live `ZPackage` in the RPC prefix without saving/restoring `GetPos()` — the real handler then reads garbage and every routed RPC on the server breaks.
Assigning to `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` instead of `Delegate.Combine` — this wipes ZNetScene's own handler (:81953) and breaks client-side object destruction for the whole server.
Trusting `m_senderPeerID` or `s_tagauthor`: both are unverified client input (:83489, :143587-143602).
Presenting a 'probable' actor as fact in a Discord channel where players read it — this is how a mod gets someone falsely accused of griefing.
Missing changes made while the mod was down: the audit is a live diff, not a reconstruction. Snapshot at shutdown and diff at boot to catch the gap.
openQuestions: In steady state, who owns a portal ZDO — the nearest client or the server? This decides what fraction of retags are 'confirmed' vs 'probable'. Log `zdo.GetOwner()` for every entry of `GetPortalList()` on a 10 s timer with players near and away.
catalog.id: ops-admin:AuditEngine — attributed change log for every tag and link write
corrections: RPC_SetTag observed at RPC_RoutedRPC can be a dropped attempt (server/owner-less target → HandleRoutedRPC FindInstance null, :83650-83664); log as 'attempted' and confirm the change only via census diff.

Deletions are authenticatable: prefix-match "DestroyZDO" (registered :76155, routed with targetPeerID 0 at :76950) in the same RPC_RoutedRPC prefix; payload is a ZPackage of ZDOIDs. Upgrade destroyed-portal actor to 'confirmed' when matched.
s_tagauthor is client self-reported (client TeleportWorld.SetText :144323) — never a confirmed actor.
RPC_PeerInfo spans :79774-; Steam ticket check :79842-79852; PlayFab check is async and non-blocking (:79854-79868).

Source (2) attribution is an attempt record, not proof of effect: the RPC only takes effect if the owner client has the portal instantiated and passes IsOwner (client RPC_SetTag :144329); when owner is 0 or the server, HandleRoutedRPC drops it server-side (:83651-83664) and no client applies it. Mark actorConfidence 'confirmed' only when the census diff shows the corresponding tag change within one tick of the RPC; otherwise log 'attempted'.

Owner-local retags (zero packets) are the COMMON case, not the exception: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) hands any nearby portal to the nearby peer within 2 s, so the player standing at a portal is almost always its owner. Expect most entries to be 'probable', and set expectations in the playerExperience text accordingly.
s_creator is a long player ID; 'builder Sigrid' requires a persisted ID→name map (ZNetPeer.m_playerName is client-supplied and only available while online).

Census-diff latency and the 'expected' suppression set both depend on the census tick; document that a client change that is overwritten by the reassert engine within the same tick is invisible to the diff (only the RPC prefix, if the retag crossed the wire, sees it).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All three sources verified. (1) Owner-local retag never hits the wire: InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id (:83577-83595); ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858). The resulting ZDO edit still reaches the server: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision calls ZDOMan.ClientChanged when !IsServer (:73832-73840, :77727-77730) and the client branch of CreateSyncList drains m_clientChangeQueue gated only by peer.ShouldSend (revision), not distance (:77241-77258). (2) RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) is private and is the only point where the authentic ZRpc and the payload coexist (:83632-83643); m_senderPeerID is read off the wire in RoutedRPCData.Deserialize (:83487-83495); ZNet.GetPeers returns the live m_peers list (:81630-81633), ZNetPeer.m_rpc/m_socket exist (:78780/:78782), ZPackage.GetArray/SetPos/GetPos exist (:83418-83432); RPC_Kick uses rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName() against the adminlist (:81668-81676); Steam ticket verification in RPC_PeerInfo (:79842-79852). (3) m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> (:76033) invoked before removal (:76975-76978); ZNetScene.Awake combines onto it (:81953). Corrections: (a) The RPC_SetTag prefix also sees retags that were never applied: when the server (or nobody) owns the portal the routed RPC goes to the server, where HandleRoutedRPC's ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null and drops it (:83650-83664) — record these as 'attempted', not as changes; only the census diff proves a change. (b) Deletions can be 'confirmed', not just 'probable': client destruction arrives as the routed RPC "DestroyZDO" (registered :76155, sent :76950 with targetPeerID 0) whose ZPackage lists the ZDOIDs; the same RPC_RoutedRPC prefix matching "DestroyZDO".GetStableHashCode() yields the authenticated socket. RPC_DestroyZDO itself only gets the self-reported long sender (:76953-76961). (c) s_tagauthor is a client self-reported PlatformUserID string (client SetText :144323); treat it as a hint, never as the confirmed actor. (d) RPC_PeerInfo begins at :79774, ticket verification at :79842-79852; the PlayFab branch authenticates asynchronously and disconnects on failure rather than blocking (:79854-79868), so a PlayFab peer's identity is briefly unverified at connect. (e) The 'probable' resolver must also handle the server's own character slot: GetAllCharacterZDOS includes m_characterID which is None on a dedicated server (:81024-81044), harmless but should be skipped.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] All three sources verified. (1) Owner-local retag never touches the wire: ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858); InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id (:83577-83595). The ZDO change still reaches the server via IncreaseDataRevision → ClientChanged (:73832-73836, :77727-77730) and the client CreateSyncList branch (:77241-77258), gated only by ShouldSend revision comparison, not distance. (2) RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632-83643) is the only place the socket and payload coexist; m_senderPeerID is read straight off the wire (:83487-83495); ZNet.GetPeers() is public (:81630) and ZNetPeer.m_rpc is public (:78780), so matching the ZRpc works (ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) itself is private, :80505-80514). GetHostName is the Steam-ticket-verified identity (RPC_PeerInfo :79841-79852) and what RPC_Kick's admin check uses (:81670-81673). (3) m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> (:76033) invoked before RemoveFromSector/pool release (:76975-76978), and ZNetScene.Awake Delegate.Combines its own handler (:81953). Two corrections. First, source (2) records an ATTEMPT, not a confirmed change: a routed RPC_SetTag reaching the server is only applied if the owner client instantiates the object and passes IsOwner (client :144329); if the target owner is 0 or the server session, HandleRoutedRPC finds no ZNetView server-side (:83651-83664) and no client applies it — the prefix would log a 'confirmed' retag that never happened. Confidence must be 'confirmed' only when the census diff observes the matching change within a tick of the RPC. Second, since ZNetPeer.m_uid is also client-reported at PeerInfo, the hostname is the only verified identity — the option gets this right but should state that mapping hostname → player name uses peer.m_playerName, itself client-supplied. Also the 'builder Sigrid' example requires resolving s_creator (a long player ID) through a name map that only exists for currently or previously seen peers.

catalog.name: MetricsEngine — portal counts, transit counts and most-used routes
catalog.oneLine: Inventory metrics for free from the census; transit metrics only from Wonderland's position-straddle heuristic, because vanilla's own PortalsUsed stat never leaves the client.
catalog.howItWorks:
**Free, exact metrics** (census-derived, zero extra cost): total portals; portals per tag; per biome (`WorldGenerator.GetBiome` :151692); per builder (`s_creator`); connected vs unconnected; managed vs unmanaged; new/destroyed per hour (from the audit stream). Plus server-wide context vanilla already exposes: `ZDOMan.instance.NrOfObjects()` (:77658), `GetSentZDOs()`/`GetRecvZDOs()` (:77663-:77671), `ZDOPool.GetPoolActive/Size/Total` (used by vanilla at :42773) — all public and all useful for the 'is my ZDO count exploding' question that portal mods get blamed for.

**Transit counts are heuristic only.** Vanilla increments `PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed` (ordinal 15, :106516) via `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` → `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` (:100569-100572, :106287-106300), which writes an in-memory dictionary saved only into that client's own `.fch`. `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own file and returns nothing. So the server can never read it.

The usable signal is the straddle test Wonderland already ships and has already tuned against a live false-positive: `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit(fromPos, toPos, radius=40f)` (PositionWatch.cs:148) walks `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (zero-alloc, :77643) and fires when both ends of a position sample sit within 40 m of some portal, with a secondary check that one end's `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` target is within 60 m of the other end. Sample every 3 s from `ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024). Invert its sense (count the transit instead of suppressing the speed alarm) and additionally record the two nearest portal ids → a (from,to) route counter, which yields 'most-used routes'.

Exclusions, all cheap and exact: skip when `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (respawn); skip when `Character.InInterior(pos)` (:4538) changes across the sample or |Δy| > 1000 (a dungeon door — `class Teleport` has no ZDO at all, :143316-143390, so it must never be counted as a portal transit); skip admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())` :81811) whose `tplite` teleports would otherwise inflate the numbers.

Aggregate on a 60 s timer into a rolling window; emit into the heartbeat line, the JSON export and Discord.
catalog.playerExperience: Players see nothing. The operator's heartbeat line becomes `[Heartbeat] 'Wubarrk' up 3h12m | 4 online: Rohan, Sigrid, … | 214 portals / 61 tags | 37 transits/hr | top route Spawn->Swamp (11)`. A community Discord gets a weekly `#portal-report` embed showing the busiest gates.
failureModes: Presenting heuristic transits as exact. A 3 s sample can miss a player who walks through and back, and two portals within 40 m of each other produce false positives.
Counting dungeon-door transits as portal transits — `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never touches `NoPortals` and has no ZDO, but produces a huge position jump.
Counting server-issued teleports (RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41957-41968) as portal use.
Trying to read `PortalsUsed` from anywhere server-side — it is not networked at all.
Sampling faster than 3 s on a large server: the cost is O(players) ZDO reads plus a `GetPortals()` walk per player per sample.
openQuestions: What is the real false-positive/false-negative rate of the 40 m straddle on a dense base with many gates close together? Instrument both the heuristic and a manual tally over a play session.

Does a portal transit reliably produce two samples on opposite sides at a 3 s interval, or does the ≥8 s distantTeleport black screen (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349) mean the arrival sample lands mid-teleport at the frozen origin? Log raw samples around a known transit.
catalog.id: ops-admin:MetricsEngine — portal counts, transit counts and most-used routes
corrections: PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit is private static (PositionWatch.cs:148) — copy it; and its nearFrom/nearTo are first-match, not nearest.

For route counting make the partner test mandatory: fromPortal.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) resolved via ZDOMan.GetZDO must lie within radius of toPos; the primary 'both ends near some portal' test alone counts hub walk-throughs as transits.

Admin teleports via Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer execute on the client (gated on Player.m_localPlayer, :41962-41968); the admin-skip is correct but should key on the mod's own teleport log rather than admin status, or admins' real portal use is also dropped.

IsPortalTransit as shipped is a suppression filter reached only after speed > ceiling (PositionWatch.cs:66-76, :140); used standalone it fires when both ends are within 40 m of any portal, including the same one. The counter must require displacement (e.g. distance > 2×radius or speed > ceiling) and nearFrom != nearTo.

The helper returns the first matching portal in m_portalObjects iteration order (PositionWatch.cs:160-176), not the nearest; for route attribution rewrite it to select the nearest portal at each end and to prefer the pair where nearFrom's ConnectionZDOID == nearTo (the extended check at :183-207 already encodes this).
Respawn skip via s_dead is redundant: the respawned player is a new ZDO (new ZDOID, new peer.m_characterID), so a ZDOID-keyed sampler never compares across death. Keep it only as belt-and-braces.
Route keys must be stable across restarts (position or mod key), since ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (ZDO.Load :74552); a rolling window that spans a restart otherwise fragments.
State explicitly that transit counts are a lower-bound heuristic: a transit and return within one 3 s sample window, or a transit between two portals < 80 m apart, is missed or double-counted.
evidence: Player.UpdateTeleport 2 s single-step jump (client) — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs (UpdateTeleport body)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Inventory side is exact and server-resident: GetPortalList/GetPortals (:77643-77656), NrOfObjects/GetSentZDOs/GetRecvZDOs public (:77658-77671), ZDOPool.GetPoolActive/Size/Total public (:78312-78325, used at :42773), WorldGenerator.GetBiome(Vector3) is an instance method (:151692) and WorldGenerator.instance exists on the server. Transit side: PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed is ordinal 15 (enum start +15), Game.IncrementPlayerStat → PlayerProfile.IncrementStat writes m_playerStats in memory only (:100569-100572, :106287-106300); SaveOtherPlayerProfiles just invokes "SavePlayerProfile" on each peer and returns void (:79653-79670); nothing ever ships the stat to the server — confirmed, the server cannot read it. PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit exists at PositionWatch.cs:148 and walks ZDOMan.GetPortals() with the 40 m / 60 m logic described; GetAllCharacterZDOS (:81024-81044) and IsAdmin(string) (:81811) exist; Character.InInterior is y>3000 (:4538-4541); Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer runs only where m_localPlayer exists (:41962-41968) — client-side, as claimed for admin teleports. Corrections: (a) IsPortalTransit is `private static` in Wonderland — it must be copied, not called. (b) The existing code records the FIRST portal within radius (nearFrom/nearTo are first-match), not the nearest; 'record the two nearest' is new work and matters in hubs where several portals sit inside 40 m. (c) False positives: any two samples both within 40 m of any portal count — a player walking across a portal hub without teleporting satisfies the primary test; the extended 60 m partner check is only applied when the primary test fails, so the counter needs the partner check made mandatory (from-portal's GetConnectionZDOID must be within radius of toPos) to be a route counter at all. (d) Sample rate is bounded by the owning client's ZDO position pushes, not by the server's timer; a 3 s server sample is fine but the position is whatever the client last synced.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Inventory metrics: all cited accessors exist and are public (NrOfObjects :77658, GetSentZDOs/GetRecvZDOs :77663-77671, ZDOPool.GetPoolActive/Size/Total :78312-78322, WorldGenerator.GetBiome(Vector3) :151692). PortalsUsed never reaches the server: TeleportWorld.Teleport (client :144287) calls Game.IncrementPlayerStat → PlayerProfile.IncrementStat (:106287-106300) into m_playerStats in memory; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles (:79654-79670) only invokes 'SavePlayerProfile' on each peer and reads nothing back. Confirmed. Transit heuristic: PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit exists at PositionWatch.cs:148 and walks GetPortals() (:77643-77646); the position jump is visible server-side because the owning client's ZDO position write bumps DataRevision (InternalSetPosition :73734-73745) and ClientChanged forwards it; the client teleports in one step after a 2 s delay (Player.UpdateTeleport client :m_teleportTimer > 2f then transform.position = target). Critical flaw in the 'invert its sense' plan: in Wonderland IsPortalTransit is only reached AFTER the speed gate (speed > 40 m/s, PositionWatch.cs:66-76 → IsLegitimateTransit :119 → :140). Called standalone it returns true whenever BOTH sample ends are within 40 m of ANY portal — including the same portal — so a player idling beside a gate would register a 'transit' every 3 s. The counter needs the displacement/speed gate and nearFrom != nearTo. Route attribution: the helper returns the FIRST portal within radius in dictionary iteration order (:160-176), not the nearest; in a hub with several gates within 40 m the (from,to) route is misattributed unless the helper is rewritten to pick the nearest and prefer the connection-target match. Respawn exclusion via s_dead is unnecessary but harmless (respawn creates a new character ZDO, so the per-ZDOID sample map never straddles it). Admin exclusion undercounts admins' legitimate portal use.

catalog.name: Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export
catalog.oneLine: A periodic and on-demand write of the full census, health findings and metrics to a JSON (and CSV) file under BepInEx/config, written temp-then-replace so a reader never sees a torn file.
catalog.howItWorks:
Serialise the immutable census DTO plus the current health findings and the metrics window. Write to `<name>.tmp`, then `File.Replace`/`File.Move` — the exact atomic pattern `TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write` (PortalExport.cs:75) and Wonderland's `SupplySwitch.Save` (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165) already use, so an external tool tailing the file never reads a half-written document.

Cadence: on a timer (default 300 s), on every network-file reload, on `tplite.export`, and once from the `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` hook (`public static Action`, :78989, invoked at :80524 on the main thread before `PrepareSave`) so the export is always consistent with the world file on disk.

Two files: `portals.json` (full, nested, machine-readable) and `portals.csv` (flat, one row per portal, for spreadsheets and `awk`). CSV columns: `id,tag,x,y,z,biome,zone,prefab,connected,partnerId,partnerTag,distance,reciprocal,network,ownerPeer,builder,tagAuthor,firstSeen,lastChanged`.

Prior art is already server-side and directly liftable: `PortalExport` is an `IsServer()`-gated coroutine that waits for ZDOMan/Game, counts portals per `s_creator` from `PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals()` (which wraps `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` with a prefab-iterative fallback, PlacementPatch.cs:195) and joins names from `PlayerNames` — the only two files of full TortalPortal that already run exclusively on the server.

Build the DTO on the main thread; serialisation itself can be done on a thread-pool task from the already-copied DTO, never from live ZDOs.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to players. A community website cron-rsyncs `portals.json` every 5 minutes and renders a public gate directory. An operator runs `jq '.portals[] | select(.connected==false) | .tag' portals.json | sort | uniq -c` to find every broken network in one line.
failureModes: Writing directly over the live file — a reader mid-read gets a truncated document. Always temp-then-replace.
Serialising live ZDO objects from a background thread; they are pooled and can be recycled mid-serialise (ZDOPool.Release → ZDO.Reset :73536-73545).
Exporting `sessionZdoId` as the primary key and letting an external tool build state on it — it changes every restart.
Exporting on a very short timer with a large world: JSON for 1000 portals is ~400 KB and rewriting it every 10 s is pointless disk churn.
prerequisites: Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)
catalog.id: ops-admin:Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export
corrections: SupplySwitch.Save (SupplySwitch.cs:117-128) is delete-then-move, not atomic — cite PortalExport.Save's File.Replace (PortalExport.cs:149-161) as the pattern; File.Move(src,dst,bool) does not exist on net472/net48.

`tplite.export` cannot be invoked from a vanilla client console (client Terminal.TryRunCommand remote-forward rule, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45734-45760); rely on timer / WorldSaveStarted / file-reload triggers or a mod-owned input channel.
Newtonsoft.Json is available on the dedicated server (referenced by assembly_valheim_SERVER :31-32, :118542-118591) — no extra dependency needed.

Drop SupplySwitch.Save as prior art for atomic writes: it deletes the target before moving the temp file (SupplySwitch.cs:124-128), leaving a window with no file. PortalExport.Write (PortalExport.cs:154-161, File.Replace when the target exists) is the correct citation.

Add a stable portal key column (e.g. `key` = prefabHash+rounded position, or a mod-written `tplite.key` string on the ZDO) because `id`/`partnerId` are ZDOIDs regenerated on every load (ZDO.Load :74552 `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`) and `ownerPeer` is a per-session UID; `firstSeen`/`lastChanged` must be tracked against the stable key.
Document that `builder` (s_creator, long) and `tagAuthor` (PlatformUserID string) are IDs; names come from a separate persisted map and may be absent.

The WorldSaveStarted export should be synchronous or at least snapshot the DTO before returning: SaveWorld proceeds straight into PrepareSave/Clone on the same frame (:80522-80535), which is fine for a main-thread DTO copy but means a deferred serialisation task must own its own copy, as the option already says.
evidence: PortalExport.OnZNetStart IsServer gate / Save File.Replace — TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32-37, :149-161
Wonderland.csproj net472 / TortalPortal.csproj net48 — TargetFramework lines
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Server-side and hook-correct: ZNet.WorldSaveStarted is a public static Action (:78989) invoked on the main thread at the top of SaveWorld before m_zdoMan.PrepareSave (:80524-80531), so a DTO built in that callback matches the world file. ZDOMan.GetPortalList allocates a fresh list (:77648-77656) — safe to snapshot. Newtonsoft.Json is referenced by the server assembly itself (using directives :31-32, JsonConvert use :118542-118591), so a JSON serialiser is present on a dedicated server without shipping one. TortalPortal.PortalExport.OnZNetStart is IsServer-gated (PortalExport.cs:32-37) and its Save uses File.Replace / File.Move (PortalExport.cs:149-161) — that one is atomic-on-rename. Corrections: (a) Wonderland's SupplySwitch.Save is NOT the atomic pattern: it does File.Delete(path) then File.Move(temp, path) (SupplySwitch.cs:117-128), leaving a window in which the file does not exist; a reader sees 'missing', not torn, but the option's 'exact atomic pattern ... already use' is wrong for that citation. Use File.Replace (or rename-over) as PortalExport does; File.Move(src,dst,overwrite) is not available on net472/net48. (b) `tplite.export` as a console command is not reachable from a vanilla client (client Terminal.TryRunCommand forwards only commands in its own table with RemoteCommand=true, client :45734-45760) and the dedicated server has no vanilla stdin reader; timer, save-hook and network-file-reload triggers are the real invocation paths. (c) PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals wraps GetPortalList with a prefab-scan fallback (PlacementPatch.cs:195-215) — confirmed, but on the server the fallback is dead code since m_portalObjects is always populated from ChunkPortal (:76474-76482).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanically sound and the cheapest option in the batch. ZNet.WorldSaveStarted is a public static Action (:78989) invoked synchronously on the main thread at the top of SaveWorld (:80520-80522) before ZDOMan.PrepareSave (:80529), so a DTO built in that callback matches the save clone exactly. GetPortalList (:77648-77656) is a fresh flattened list. PortalExport.Write really does temp-then-File.Replace/File.Move (PortalExport.cs:154-161) and PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals wraps GetPortalList with IsValid filtering (PlacementPatch.cs:195-215). Two citation/design errors: (1) SupplySwitch.Save is NOT the atomic pattern — it does File.WriteAllLines(temp), File.Delete(path), File.Move(temp,path) (SupplySwitch.cs:117-128); a reader between Delete and Move sees no file. Cite PortalExport only. (2) The CSV/JSON `id` and `partnerId` columns are ZDOIDs, which are regenerated sequentially on every world load (ZDO.Load :74552) and are also the on-disk key SupplySwitch persists — so any external tool correlating exports across a restart, or `firstSeen`/`lastChanged` history keyed on id, silently breaks. `ownerPeer` is likewise a per-session UID. The export needs a stable key (position+prefab hash, or a mod-written string ZDO key) alongside the transient ZDOID. Minor: `builder`/`tagAuthor` are a long player ID and a PlatformUserID string respectively; name resolution requires the PlayerNames map, which only knows peers it has seen.

catalog.name: Output surface: Discord webhook reporting
catalog.oneLine: Fire-and-forget posts of health findings, audit events and a periodic portal summary through Wonderland's already-shipped DiscordWebhook helper.
catalog.howItWorks:
Lift `DiscordWebhook` verbatim (DiscordWebhook.cs): one shared static `HttpClient` with a 10 s timeout, `Send()` fire-and-forget, `SendBlocking(msg, timeoutMs)` for the shutdown message only — the process can exit before a fire-and-forget task runs — and a hand-rolled JSON escaper so no JSON library is needed. It requires a `System.Net.Http` reference resolved from the net472 reference assemblies (Wonderland.csproj:72).

Event classes, each independently toggleable in config:
- **Health digest** (default: only when findings change) — 'tag `home` now has 5 portals; one is permanently stranded'.
- **Audit stream** (default off, high volume) — retags and relinks with attribution and a confidence marker.
- **Destruction notices** — from `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` (:76033), filtered to `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021).
- **Network reload** — 'networks.json reloaded: 3 networks, 0 errors' / the full error list on a failed parse.
- **Periodic summary** — shares the Heartbeat timer rather than running a second one, exactly as Wonderland's `Heartbeat.OnUpdate` shares between the log and Discord heartbeats (Heartbeat.cs:21-56).
- **Server lifecycle** — 'portal engine online / offline', the offline one via `SendBlocking` from `OnDestroy`.

Rate-limit and coalesce in the mod, not in Discord: batch findings into one message per interval, and hard-cap messages per minute. Delivery is best-effort by design — a failed post is logged and dropped, never retried, because nothing else depends on it landing.

Everything posted is derived from the main-thread DTO; the HTTP call itself happens on a thread-pool task and must never touch ZDOMan.
catalog.playerExperience: Players see nothing in-game. The server's Discord gets, in `#server-ops`: `🌀 **Portal health** — 214 portals / 61 tags. ⚠️ tag `home` (5 portals) permanently strands one gate at (410, 33, -88). ⚠️ tag `Base ` looks like a typo for `Base`.` Community members who built the gates learn why one never connects, without an admin having to log in.
failureModes: Posting the audit stream by default: a busy server generates dozens of retag events an hour and the channel becomes unreadable.
Posting 'probable' attribution to a channel players read — a false griefing accusation.
Using `Send()` from `OnDestroy` — the process exits first and the offline message never arrives; that is exactly why `SendBlocking` exists.
Creating a new HttpClient per post: socket exhaustion under Mono.
Leaking the webhook URL into the exported JSON or a log line.
prerequisites: HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection
corrections: Subscribe with `+=` / `Delegate.Combine`, never assignment: vanilla `ZNetScene.Awake` already chains its own `OnZDODestroyed` onto the same field (:81953) and the server does run ZNetScene. Subscribe only after `ZDOMan.instance` exists (e.g. Harmony postfix on `ZNetScene.Awake` or `ZNet.Awake`), not from the plugin's own Awake.

The destruction callback carries no sender identity. If the audit stream wants 'destroyed by <player>', take it from a Harmony prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage pkg)` (:76950) where the routed sender is available; the callback alone can only say 'destroyed'.

Audit 'attribution' for retags is inherently partial: an owning client retags with no routed RPC on the wire (prior review), so the only evidence is the ZDO data change plus owner id; the 'confidence marker' must reflect that, and it depends on the audit/health engines that are prerequisites, not on anything in this option.

Note for the Health digest example: an odd-sized tag group strands one gate because `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679) pairs randomly with no tie-break, so the stranded gate changes identity across reconnects; the digest should say 'one of N is stranded' rather than naming a permanent loser unless the health engine has pinned it.

`m_onZDODestroyed` is a public multicast field that `ZNetScene.Awake` populates with `Delegate.Combine` (:81953). The mod must `+=` (Combine), never assign `=`; assigning after ZNetScene.Awake silently removes ZNetScene's own `OnZDODestroyed` handler.
The destroy callback carries no sender. Destruction attribution (who deleted the gate) needs a Harmony prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage)` — the callback alone cannot say who.

`Heartbeat.OnUpdate` (Heartbeat.cs:21-56) is Wonderland-specific code driven from WonderlandPlugin.Update and reads WonderlandConfig; 'sharing the timer' means copying the pattern into TortalPortal Lite, not calling Wonderland.

`SendBlocking` from `OnDestroy` only fires if the plugin MonoBehaviour is destroyed during an orderly `Application.Quit`; a SIGKILL/container stop skips it. Fine as best-effort, but do not promise the offline post.

catalog.name: Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint
catalog.oneLine: An HttpListener on a configurable loopback port serving the census/health/metrics snapshot as JSON and Prometheus text, answered entirely from a main-thread-built immutable DTO.
catalog.howItWorks:
`System.Net.HttpListener` lives in `System.dll` and the dedicated server ships a full Mono runtime, so no new dependency beyond what the csproj already resolves for `System.Net.Http`.

Architecture is forced by thread-safety: ZDOMan has no locking anywhere, and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread` :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205). So the listener thread must **never** touch ZDOMan, ZNet, ZoneSystem or WorldGenerator. Instead: the census engine publishes `volatile Snapshot _latest` (fully immutable, pre-serialised to a `byte[]` on a thread-pool task) each tick; the listener thread only hands out `_latest`.

Routes: `GET /portals.json`, `GET /portals.csv`, `GET /health` (200 with `{ok:true}` or 503 with findings — directly usable as a container health probe), `GET /metrics` (Prometheus text: `tplite_portals_total`, `tplite_portals_unconnected`, `tplite_tag_groups`, `tplite_transits_total`, `tplite_repairs_total`, plus `valheim_zdos_total` from `ZDOMan.NrOfObjects()` :77658 sampled on the main thread).

Security: bind `127.0.0.1` by default and require an explicit `Bind` config change plus a bearer token to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Refuse to start without a token when bound non-loopback. No write routes at all in v1 — writes go through the file-queue or the admin console, both of which already have an authorization story.

Any text the listener thread wants in the server log must go through `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog.Enqueue(...)` (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245), drained one line per frame by `Console.Update` into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925) — vanilla's own save thread reports errors exactly this way (:80675, :80710).
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible in-game. An operator points Grafana at `http://server:9101/metrics` and gets a graph of portal count and transits per hour; their Docker healthcheck hits `/health` and restarts the container if the portal engine stops ticking.
failureModes: Touching any Valheim singleton from the listener thread — ZDOMan, ZNetScene and ZDOExtraData are all unsynchronised static state; this will produce intermittent, unreproducible crashes.
HttpListener requiring elevated privileges or an http.sys URL ACL on Windows hosts — Linux/Mono is fine, Windows dedicated servers may need `netsh http add urlacl`.
Binding 0.0.0.0 with no token and exposing the full builder/PlatformUserID list to the internet.
Not disposing the listener in `Shutdown()`/`OnDestroy` — the port stays bound across a BepInEx hot reload.
Serialising on the listener thread from live objects instead of from the pre-built byte[].

Does BepInEx's Mono resolve `System.dll` for the plugin without an explicit reference? Confirm at build and at load.
corrections: WRONG: 'Any text the listener thread wants in the server log must go through Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog'. That queue (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245) is drained only inside `Console.Update` (:42922-42925), which early-returns at :42892-42895 unless `IsConsoleEnabled()`; on a dedicated server that is true only with `-console` on the command line (`FejdStartup.ParseArguments` :97288-97290) or the `EnableConsole` PlatformPref (:42880). Without it the queue is never dequeued and grows without bound. Vanilla's own save thread logs directly with `ZLog.Log(" ### Save World Thread Started! ### ")` (:80597) — `ZLog.Log` is a bare `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` wrapper (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13049-13054) and Unity's Debug.Log is thread-safe. Use `ZLog`/`Debug.Log` or BepInEx's ManualLogSource from the listener thread; do not use the Terminal queue.

WRONG: 'vanilla's only background thread (ZNet.SaveWorldThread)'. The server assembly also spawns `ZNtp.NtpThread` (:82916), `PlayFabZLibWorkQueue.WorkerMain` (:89324), `ZPlayFabMatchmaking.BackgroundLookupPublicIP` (:90716), `HeightmapBuilder.BuildThread` (:129677) and `LiquidVolume.UpdateThread` (:132692). The conclusion (never touch ZDOMan off-thread) is unchanged.

`tplite_transits_total` cannot be a server-observed count: there is no server-side hook on teleport (see central constraint); it must be labelled as the PositionWatch `IsPortalTransit` heuristic (Wonderland/Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs), i.e. reactive-detection-only.
`Console.Update`'s `AddString` path is `ZLog.Log("Console: " + text)` plus a chat-buffer write (:45983-46002), so even when drained it adds nothing a direct `ZLog.Log` would not.

Mono `HttpListener` caveats to state explicitly: prefixes must end in '/', `GetContext`/`BeginGetContext` callbacks run on thread-pool threads (never call Unity APIs there), and the listener must be stopped in `OnDestroy` or the port stays bound until process exit.

Do NOT route listener-thread log lines through `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog`: `Console.Update` drains it only when `IsConsoleEnabled()` (:42890-42893, :42923), which on a dedicated server requires `-console` (:97288-97291) or the EnableConsole pref (:42880). Log directly with `ZLog.Log`/`UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13051) or the BepInEx logger — both thread-safe; vanilla's save thread does exactly that at :80673.

'vanilla's only background thread' is false: `ZNtp.NtpThread` (:82916), `PlayFabZLibWorkQueue.WorkerMain` (:89324), `ZPlayFabMatchmaking.BackgroundLookupPublicIP` (:90716), `HeightmapBuilder.BuildThread` (:129677), `LiquidVolume.UpdateThread` (:132692), plus `Task.Run` in ZNet's public-IP lookup (:79415). The conclusion (ZDOMan has no locking; touch it only on the main thread) still stands.

`tplite_transits_total` cannot be a real counter: no server-side hook observes a teleport. It is a heuristic from player position jumps near two portals (Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit, PositionWatch.cs:148) and must be labelled as such in /metrics.

Loopback-by-default contradicts the stated Grafana experience: `http://server:9101/metrics` from another host needs the non-loopback bind + bearer token path. Inside Docker, a 127.0.0.1 bind serves the container's own healthcheck but nothing outside.
'pre-serialised each tick' is wasteful and unnecessary; serialise on change (the census ticks on a multi-second cadence anyway).

Two factual claims are wrong, one of them dangerous if followed: the logging advice would silently leak memory on a default dedicated server.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Architecture (never touch ZDOMan off-thread; serve an immutable DTO) is right: `ZNet.SaveWorldThread` (:80583) works only on clones built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205) and `ZDOMan.NrOfObjects()` is `m_objectsByID.Count` (:77658-77661), all correctly cited. `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` is a `public static ConcurrentQueue<string>` (:43245) and the vanilla producers at :80675/:80710 are real. But the logging claim is wrong in a way that would bite: the drain at :42923 sits inside `Console.Update` AFTER `if (!IsConsoleEnabled()) return;` (:42890-42893), and `IsConsoleEnabled()` is `m_consoleEnabled` (:42952-42959), set only by `-console` (`FejdStartup.ParseArguments` :97288-97291) or PlatformPrefs 'EnableConsole'==1 (:42880). A typical dedicated server passes neither, so every enqueued line is never drained (unbounded queue growth) — vanilla's own save-thread messages at :80675/:80710 are already dead there, which is why it also calls `ZLog.LogError` directly from the thread (:80673). `ZLog.Log` is a straight `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13051-13054) and is thread-safe; BepInEx's ManualLogSource is too. The 'vanilla's only background thread' premise is also false. HttpListener itself is standard System.dll and Mono ships a managed implementation, but binding on the game's Mono runtime has not been exercised in this codebase — leave it needs-a-check on the listener start, which is cheap to verify.

catalog.name: Output surface: generated realm map (SVG first, PNG as a stretch)
catalog.oneLine: A server-rendered top-down map of every portal, coloured by biome and linked by its connection, emitted as plain-text SVG — with a hand-rolled PNG encoder only if a raster is truly required.
catalog.howItWorks:
**SVG (recommended, feasible today).** Pure string building, zero image libraries, zero graphics device. World XZ maps to SVG coordinates with `sx = (x + 10500) * scale`, `sy = (10500 - z) * scale` (world radius constants: `WorldGenerator.worldSize = 10000f`, `waterEdge = 10500f`, :151118-151122). Draw, in order: a background disc for the ocean; optional biome tinting by sampling `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(x, z)` (:151725) on a coarse grid (a 256×256 sample grid = 65 536 closed-form noise evaluations — run it once at OnWorldReady on a time-sliced coroutine, never per export, and cache); a `<line>` per portal connection; a `<circle>` per portal coloured by network; a `<text>` label per tag. Output ~50–200 KB, opens in any browser, zooms losslessly, and is trivially diffable in git.

For an even cheaper variant, use `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92332) — a precomputed 2048×2048 grid at 12 m/cell with `PointBiomes[x,y]` and `PointHeights[x,y]`, populated by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` before any peer connects (:79273-79285), indexed via `AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float)` (:92424). That is an O(1) lookup per cell with no noise evaluation at all.

**PNG (stretch, needs an in-game check).** `Texture2D` + `EncodeToPNG` requires the ImageConversion module and a graphics device; a dedicated server reports `SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == GraphicsDeviceType.Null` (vanilla itself branches on exactly that in `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` :81245-81299). `System.Drawing` is unreliable under Mono without libgdiplus. The safe route is a ~120-line hand-rolled PNG writer (IHDR + zlib *stored* blocks + Adler-32 + CRC-32 + IEND) over a raw RGB byte buffer — no compression, larger files, but no dependency and no GPU.

Either renderer runs off the main thread from the census DTO, writing temp-then-replace.
catalog.playerExperience: No in-game effect. The operator opens `portals.svg` in a browser and sees the whole realm: 214 dots on a biome-tinted disc, coloured lines showing every link, the `TRADE` ring drawn as a closed triangle, and three grey dots with no line at all — the stranded gates. They post it in Discord and players immediately understand the network layout without any client mod.
failureModes: Calling `Texture2D`/`EncodeToPNG` headless and getting a null graphics device exception at runtime, or worse a silently black image.
Sampling `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` per export instead of once — 65 536 noise evaluations on every 5-minute export is pure waste.
Using any `ZoneSystem` raycast helper for terrain shading; they all return the no-hit fallback server-side (Game.FixedUpdate reference pin :100465).
Labelling every portal at full zoom — 200 overlapping `<text>` nodes is unreadable; label per tag group, not per portal.
Drawing interior portals (y > 3000, :4538) at their XZ position on top of the surface gate above them without a distinct marker.

corrections: File misattribution: `AltBiomeWorldData` is in assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92332 (WorldSpaceToMapSpace :92424, MapSpaceToWorldSpace :92414), NOT assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs (that file is only 15,120 lines).

`System.IO.Compression.dll` is also present in Managed, so a hand-rolled PNG writer can emit a real zlib stream via `DeflateStream` (2-byte zlib header + deflate + Adler-32) instead of stored blocks; stored blocks remain the zero-risk fallback.

`PointBiomes` is `Heightmap.BiomeIndex[,]`, not `Heightmap.Biome`; convert with the `ToBiome()` extension (:129582). Index order is `[x, y]` (`GenerateBiomePoints` writes `PointBiomes[j, i]` with j from world x, :92439-92449). Outside `waterEdgeSqr` it is pre-filled Ocean with height -1000 (:92442-92446).

Treat EncodeToPNG as needs-ingame-check (one call), with the hand-rolled writer as fallback. Texture2D is main-thread-only, so the PNG variant cannot 'run off the main thread'.

Prefer the `m_biomeData` grid to re-sampling `GetBiome` on a coroutine: the grid is already computed at load (:79281) and read-only afterwards, safe to read from the render thread; a 256×256 downsample of it is 65k array reads, not 65k noise evaluations.

catalog.name: Network state snapshot, rollback and migration
catalog.oneLine: Capture the live portal topology (positions, tags, links) to a versioned file that can be diffed, restored onto a running server, or replayed onto a different world.
catalog.howItWorks:
A snapshot is the census DTO plus a schema version and a world fingerprint (`ZNet.instance.GetWorldName()` :80876, `GetWorldUID()` :80871, `ZNet.World.m_seedName` :112376). Written temp-then-replace to `<config>/snapshots/<name>.json`. Taken automatically before every `--apply` repair, on every network-file reload, and on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` (:78989/:80524) so the newest snapshot always matches the world file on disk.

**Restore** re-resolves every snapshot entry by rounded position (never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers, :74552), then issues the reassert engine's write primitive for each tag and connection that differs. Portals present in the snapshot but absent from the world are reported, not recreated, unless `--recreate` is passed; recreation uses `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` (:76674-76692) followed by the mandatory five lines `ZNetView.Awake` normally performs (:82613-82620): `Persistent = true; Type = ObjectType.Default; Distant = false; SetPrefab(hash); SetRotation(rot);` — `CreateNewZDO` sets none of them, and a prefab-less ZDO will not survive a save. Pass the real portal hash to `CreateNewZDO` so `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) files it in `m_portalObjects` and sets `DirtyPortalObjects`; setting the prefab afterwards on a hash-0 ZDO leaves it in the sector array, where `AddObjectsPerChunk` (:77572) then skips it as a portal and it is written to no chunk file at all.

**Migration to another world** rewrites the network file's `at` coordinates but cannot move the portals themselves — never call `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so the `m_portalObjects` key goes stale, clients in the new zone never receive it through sector sync, and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) later fails to remove it, leaking the entry permanently. Destroy and recreate instead: claim ownership (`DestroyZDO` is a silent no-op unless `IsOwner()`, :76929-76935) then `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. Note the recreated portal must use a **fresh** ZDOID — `m_deadZDOs` (:76043) causes the server to immediately re-destroy any ZDO recreated under a previously-destroyed id (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133-77137).

Complement this with vanilla's own safety net: `ConsiderAutoBackup` runs inside `SaveWorldThread` (:80601-80604), so a bad mass repair is also recoverable from the world backup.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect during a snapshot. During a restore, players near affected gates see hover text change and the connected-glow flicker once as links are rewritten. The operator types `tplite.restore pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z` and gets `restored 4 portals, 0 missing, 0 recreated`.
failureModes: Restoring a snapshot taken on a different world — the position keys resolve to unrelated portals. Refuse on a world-UID mismatch unless `--force`.
Recreating a portal without the five ZNetView.Awake lines: the ZDO is non-persistent and prefab-less, vanishes at the next save, and clients log a CreateObject failure.
Recreating under an old ZDOID: `m_deadZDOs` makes the server destroy it again immediately.
Repositioning a portal instead of destroy-and-recreate: permanent `m_portalObjects` corruption.

Snapshotting during a save: take it from `WorldSaveStarted` (before `PrepareSave`), never from `WorldSaveFinished`, which is reached through `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581) — a method that dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded at :80574/:80578.
prerequisites: Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)
NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass
openQuestions: Does `WorldSaveFinished` actually fire on a dedicated server, or does `PrintWorldSaveMessage` NRE on `MessageHud.instance` first (:80574)? Probe by subscribing and logging; if it never fires, the post-save hook is unavailable and only `WorldSaveStarted` can be used.
catalog.id: ops-admin:Network state snapshot, rollback and migration
corrections: The `m_deadZDOs` warning is misplaced: `CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int)` cannot reuse a dead id (fresh `m_sessionID` per process, monotonically increasing `m_nextUid`, :76674-76682). The re-destroy at `RPC_ZDOData` :77133-77137 applies only to ZDOs newly created from a PEER packet (`flag == true`); it protects against a client re-sending a destroyed ZDO, not against server-side recreation. Keep the note but reattribute it.

Restore's write primitive must claim ownership first: `ZDO.SetConnection` from the server on a client-owned portal bumps DataRevision and pushes to peers, but the owning client's own subsequent writes (and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` handing ownership to a nearby peer) can overwrite it; vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` delegates via `RPC_SetConnection` to an online owner (prior review). The 'restored 4 portals' report must be verified on the next reconcile tick, not assumed at write time.

Durability caveat must be explicit: the on-disk format holds one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot per ZDO (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478), so a restored ring/fan-in/one-way/self-loop topology lives only until the next world load; the snapshot file plus a boot-time reapply is the ONLY durable record. Restore-then-restart without the mod re-applying at boot silently degrades to pairs.

Recreation: also set `zdo.SetRotation`/`Persistent = true` BEFORE the next save and call `SetDirtyPortals()` is already implied by AddIfPortal; but the tag write (`Set(ZDOVars.s_tag)`) does NOT dirty the portal chunk (see footprint verdict) — since AddIfPortal already dirtied it in the same tick this is fine only if tag and creation happen before the next save; otherwise call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes.

Minor: `ZNet.PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581) is cited but unused; `WorldSaveFinished` fires from it on the main thread after the save thread completes, which is the correct hook for a post-save snapshot verification if wanted.

`ConsiderAutoBackup` is not a per-save safety net: it backs up only when `m_backupCount != 1` and only at `m_backupShort` (7200 s) / `m_backupLong` (43200 s) intervals (:80718-80732, :79053-79057, `-backupshort/-backuplong/-backups` :97463-97473). A bad `--apply` followed by the next autosave is recoverable from vanilla only if a backup happened to be due at that save; the mod's own pre-apply snapshot is the real rollback path.

Restore writes go through `Game.SetConnection`, which is private and routes to the owning online client via `RPC_SetConnection` unless owner==0/dead peer/force; and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2 s and reassigns ownership of Persistent ZDOs in a peer's active area to that peer. Restore of gates with a player nearby must claim ownership per write and accept a round-trip; the 'flicker once' experience is real only when the write lands directly.

`WorldSaveStarted` fires on the main thread inside `SaveWorld` (:80524) before `PrepareSave` — snapshot there is consistent with the clone — but for non-pairwise topologies the on-disk file does NOT match the snapshot (the file collapses rings/one-way links); say 'the snapshot matches the live state at save time', not 'the world file'.

Snapshot position keys must be rounded coarsely enough to survive a client repositioning nothing (portals do not move) but not so coarse that two adjacent gates collide; also `m_seedName` is the user-typed seed string while `m_seed` is the int — fingerprint on `m_uid` + `m_seed`.
