catalog.name: World-save footprint of mod-created ZDOs, and how to clean them up
catalog.oneLine: Quantify exactly what the mod adds to the world file — one portal chunk rewrite plus per-portal key bytes — and ship an explicit garbage-collection command for mod-created anchors and keys.
catalog.howItWorks:
**Where portals live on disk.** Every portal in the world is written to one dedicated chunk, `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180). `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones *every* entry of `m_portalObjects` into it (:77621-77632, via `ZDO.Clone` :73552) — but only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621). There is no `Persistent` filter on that path, unlike ordinary chunks (:77572). Consequences:
- Adding a mod key to every portal grows exactly one file. At ~16 bytes per int key, 500 portals × 3 keys ≈ 24 KB. Negligible.
- Any single portal change dirties the flag and rewrites the **whole** portal file at the next autosave (default `Game.m_saveInterval = 1800f`, :99914; overridable by `-savinterval`, :97477).
- Idempotent re-assertion costs nothing: `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on equality (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so no DataRevision bump, no dirty flag, no rewrite.
- After a world load `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76474-76531), so a freshly loaded world will not rewrite the portal file until something actually changes.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** (used for computed-coordinate destinations) go into ordinary chunks and are only written when `Persistent == true` (:77572). `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does **not** set Persistent (:76674-76692).

**Cleanup.** Tag every mod-created ZDO with a mod-private int key (e.g. `"tplite_owned"` = a schema version). GC pass: enumerate `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, hash)` (:75390-75407 — Float/Long/Int/String only; an unindexed nested scan, so one-shot at boot, never per tick), and for each result not referenced by the current network model, claim ownership and `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929). For keys written onto *player-built* portals (which must survive), remove the key instead with the public statics `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveString/RemoveFloat` (:75122+) and then `SetDirtyPortals()`.

Expose the footprint in the report: mod-created portal count, mod-created anchor count, total mod keys, and the estimated added bytes.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect. The operator runs `tplite.footprint` and sees `mod-created portals: 4 (hub anchors); mod-created anchors: 2; mod keys on 214 portals: 642; est. added save bytes: ~11 KB; portal chunk rewritten on 3 of the last 10 autosaves`. On uninstall they run `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys --destroy-anchors` and the footprint drops to zero.
failureModes: Creating an anchor without `Persistent = true` — it vanishes on the next restart with no error and the portal it served becomes permanently dangling.

Creating an anchor with a fabricated prefab hash: `FilterZDO` only drops prefabs in `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut` (two entries, :76109/:76350); an unknown hash merely logs a warning and the ZDO is **kept forever** (:76346-76361), so every boot prints 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients attempt to create an object for it. Always use a real, harmless prefab hash.

Running `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` or `GetAllZDOsWithHash` on a tick — the former walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array ~400 non-empty sectors per call (:77442-77494), the latter is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary (:75390-75407).
Calling `DestroyZDO` without claiming ownership: it is a silent no-op (:76929-76935).
Assuming a tag write persists without `SetDirtyPortals()`.
openQuestions: Measure the real portal chunk file size on a mature world before and after enabling the mod, to replace the byte estimate with a number.
catalog.id: ops-admin:World-save footprint of mod-created ZDOs, and how to clean them up
corrections: WRONG: 'Any single portal change dirties the flag and rewrites the whole portal file'. `DirtyPortalObjects` is set ONLY by `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` with `ConnectionType.Portal` (:73657-73677), `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` (:77751), `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76986), legacy `ZDOMan.Load` (:76539) and explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702-76705). A tag or mod-key write goes `ZDO.Set` -> `IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832-73840) -> `SetDirtySector` -> `SetDirtyChunks` (:76696-76722), which dirties the ORDINARY chunk hierarchy for that sector — a file the portal is not in (AddIfPortal removed it from `m_objectsBySector`) — and leaves the portal chunk clean. Net effect: every mod key write on a portal triggers a wasted rewrite of up to four ordinary chunk files and is silently dropped at the next save unless the mod also calls `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Even a client's own retag arriving through `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74206-74241) dirties nothing; vanilla only persists it because the resulting `Game.ConnectPortals` disconnect calls SetConnection.

Consequence for the GC/`--clean-keys` command: `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt` etc. are raw table edits with no DataRevision bump and no dirty flag; the option's 'then SetDirtyPortals()' is mandatory, and the removal is also never pushed to connected clients (use the instance methods `zdo.RemoveInt/RemoveString` :74060-74075 style if propagation matters; they still do not dirty the portal chunk).
Byte estimate: an int key on disk is 4-byte hash + 4-byte value (~8 bytes) plus a per-type count byte, not ~16; the conclusion (negligible) stands.
Flag spelling: the server argument is `-saveinterval` (`FejdStartup.ParseServerArguments` :97475-97478, `Mathf.Max(5, result4)`), not `-savinterval`.
`GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` with an unsupported type calls `UnityEngine.Debug.Break()` after LogError (:75403-75405) — harmless in a player build but never pass Vec3/Quat/ByteArray.

Enforcement label: this is an operator report plus a mod-scoped GC; nothing player-facing is enforced. The destroy/remove writes are server-authoritative only after an ownership claim (`DestroyZDO` :76929-76935).

'Any single portal change dirties the flag' is false for key/tag writes. Only `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` (Portal type) call `ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()` (:73656-73676; sole callers :73663, :73675). `ZDO.Set(int,int)`/`Set(int,string)` → `IncreaseDataRevision` → `SetDirtySector` → `SetDirtyChunks(sector)` (:76694-76700) marks the ORDINARY chunk of the portal's sector — which does not contain the portal — so the mod key is not saved and an unrelated chunk file is rewritten. Every mod key write onto a portal ZDO must be followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`; this is also why tag writes are silently lost.

Side effect to add to the footprint report: each mod key write on a portal dirties that sector's ordinary chunk hierarchy (3 sizes, `SetDirtyChunks` :76706+), so 'grows exactly one file' is wrong on the first write pass — it also rewrites up to one ordinary chunk per portal sector touched. Subsequent idempotent writes cost nothing.

`ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt`/`ZDO.RemoveInt` (:75126-75129, :74027-74030) do not bump DataRevision: the removal never replicates to connected clients and does not persist unless `SetDirtyPortals()` (portals) / `SetDirtySector` (anchors) is called. Worse, `ZDO.Deserialize` merges with `ZDOExtraData.Add` (:73xxx Deserialize, ReadData → Add), so a client that still holds the key and later becomes owner (`ReleaseNearbyZDOS` :76901-76926) re-adds it on its next push. Run `--clean-keys` on an empty server (or at boot before peers connect), then save.

Anchor GC by `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, hash)` is fine, but note `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` is a no-op unless `IsOwner()` (:76929-76935) — claim ownership with `SetOwner(sessionID)` first; and a destroyed ZDOID lands in `m_deadZDOs` (:76993-76995) so never reuse ids.

`FilterZDO`'s unknown-prefab warning (:76346-76361) only runs when `newVersion` (chunk saved under a different world version) — it is not a per-boot log spam source; the real cost of an unknown-prefab anchor is a ZDO that no client can instantiate.

BUT the option's central dirty-tracking claim is wrong and, if believed, loses data: mod key writes on portals do NOT dirty the portal chunk.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Disk model is right: `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180); `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones every `m_portalObjects` entry into that chunk with no Persistent filter, gated on `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77621-77632), while ordinary chunks filter `Persistent && !portal` (:77572); `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76527); `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on equality (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on `Equals` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345) so idempotent re-assertion bumps nothing. `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` supports Float/Long/Int/String only (:75390-75407); `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveFloat` are public statics (:75121-75129) and `ZDO.RemoveInt` wraps them (:74027-74030); `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` covers `m_portalObjects` (:77457-77459). The important thing the option gets WRONG is the dirtying model: only `ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection` call `SetDirtyPortals()` (:73656-73676; the only callers of `SetDirtyPortals` are :73663 and :73675). A plain `Set(int/string)` goes `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ZDOMan.SetDirtySector` → `SetDirtyChunks(zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (:73605, IncreaseDataRevision body, :76694-76700), which dirties the ORDINARY chunk for that sector — one the portal is not in — and never the portal file. So writing `tplite_owned` onto 500 portals rewrites up to N unrelated ordinary chunk files at the next save and does not persist the keys at all unless the mod calls `SetDirtyPortals()`. `RemoveInt` bumps nothing (:74027-74030) so removals neither replicate nor persist without the same call. Net: feasible, but the footprint arithmetic and the 'any single portal change dirties the flag' sentence need rewriting. Enforcement relabelled: this is admin tooling that enforces no player-facing rule.

catalog.name: What happens when the mod is removed (graceful-uninstall design)
catalog.oneLine: Nothing corrupts and no phantom portals appear — but managed topologies degrade to random same-tag pairs after one restart, so ship an explicit uninstall command that lands the world in a clean, vanilla-stable state.
catalog.howItWorks:
Traced end to end through the decompile:

**Mod-created portal-prefab ZDOs survive and behave like normal portals.** They are written into the portal chunk unconditionally when dirty (:77621-77632) and `LoadChunks`'s portal branch loads them straight into `m_portalObjects` and `m_objectsByID` with **no** `FilterZDO` call at all (:76474-76482). Vanilla then pairs them by tag like any other gate. No phantoms, no orphan files.

**Mod keys on portal ZDOs become dead bytes.** Nothing reads them; they cost a few bytes each in the portal chunk forever. Harmless, but removable — hence `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** persist if `Persistent` was set and the prefab is real. With an unknown prefab hash they are *kept* and merely warned about (:76346-76361) — a permanent log-spam legacy. Destroy them on uninstall.

**Topologies unravel, in two stages.** At runtime, a ring A→B→C→A survives indefinitely because `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100600-100604). At the **next world load**, it does not: the on-disk format gives each ZDO exactly one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478 writes the source slot then overwrites it with the Target slot), which can only express a pairwise perfect matching. So `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850-77893) restores at most one pair per ring and vanilla randomly re-pairs the leftovers. One-way links come back **bidirectional** (ConnectPortals writes both sides, :77879-77885). Self-loops are erased entirely.

**Therefore the honest answer is: no corruption, but any non-pairwise topology is lost at the first restart after removal, silently and without warning.**

`tplite.uninstall` should: (1) snapshot; (2) collapse every managed network into plain vanilla pairs, or split tags so that each group has an even count (eliminating the permanent strand); (3) remove mod keys; (4) destroy mod anchors; (5) write a final report naming every gate whose tag was changed so the operator can tell players. Also expose `tplite.export --for-uninstall` producing a human-readable 'here is what your networks were' document.
catalog.playerExperience: If the operator just deletes the DLL: for the rest of that session every gate keeps working exactly as it did. After the next server restart, players find the three-gate `TRADE` ring has become one working pair plus one gate that says `unconnected` forever, and nobody can tell them why. If the operator runs `tplite.uninstall` first, every network has already been split into clean pairs with distinct tags (`TRADE-1`, `TRADE-2`) and a Discord post lists the new tag for each gate, so nothing changes at the restart.
failureModes: Removing the mod without running uninstall and only discovering the topology loss days later, after a restart.
Leaving anchors with unknown prefab hashes behind — every boot logs 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients fail to create the object.
Leaving an odd-sized managed tag group behind: vanilla permanently strands one member (Game.ConnectPortals phase 2, :100607-100622).

Assuming `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (load-time, hash-based, :77850) is the same thing as `Game.ConnectPortals` (runtime, tag-based, :100589) — patching or reasoning about the wrong one gives the wrong uninstall model.
prerequisites: Network state snapshot, rollback and migration
openQuestions: Confirm the ring-collapse empirically: build a 3-gate ring, restart the server twice, and record the resulting topology each time.
catalog.id: ops-admin:What happens when the mod is removed (graceful-uninstall design)
corrections: 'At most one pair per ring' is only guaranteed for a 3-ring. For rings of n>=4 the surviving pairs depend on `s_connections` Dictionary iteration order: pair X->Y survives iff X's Portal slot and Y's Target slot are both the last writes to those keys, so a 4-ring can come back as two pairs (order B,D,A,C) or one. State it as 'a subset of a pairwise matching, order-dependent, at most floor(n/2)'; the 3-gate TRADE example is correct as written.

'A permanent log-spam legacy' for unknown-prefab anchors is wrong server-side: `FilterZDO` only classifies when `newVersion` (`bool newVersion = world != version`, :76476; guard at :76348), i.e. only on the first load after a game-version change; on same-version loads unknown prefabs load silently. The real spam is client-side: `ZNetScene.CreateObject` logs `"Missing prefab hash: ..."` (client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82225-82236) on every create pass while a player is in that sector. Still destroy them on uninstall — the reason is client log noise and a phantom ZDO in sector sync, not server logs.

Uninstall step (2) must claim ownership before every tag/connection write and call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes: `ZDO.Set(s_tag)` does not dirty the portal chunk (see footprint verdict), so a split-tag uninstall followed by a save without any connection change would lose the new tags. In practice the split changes connections too (phase-1 tag mismatch -> SetConnection(None) dirties), but do not rely on it.

'Mod keys become dead bytes ... forever' is true only for keys that reached disk, which requires a portal-chunk-dirtying event between the write and a save; keys written without `SetDirtyPortals()` may never have been saved at all.

Also note the degradation is not specific to uninstall: any non-pairwise topology is lost on EVERY restart; the mod itself must re-apply from its network file at boot. Uninstall merely removes the re-applier. The design should say so, since it defines what the 'reassert at boot' engine must do.

'With an unknown prefab hash they are kept and merely warned about — a permanent log-spam legacy' is wrong: `FilterZDO` (:76346-76361) only evaluates `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut`/`HasPrefab` when `newVersion` is true (chunk saved under a different world version than current, :76472). Unknown-prefab anchors are kept silently on normal boots; the warning appears once per version transition. They should still be destroyed on uninstall — clients can never instantiate them.

'split tags so that each group has an even count (eliminating the permanent strand)' is arithmetically impossible for an odd group: pairing leaves one gate over regardless of tags. The uninstall command can only make the strand explicit (name the gate, or retag it to a solo tag) — it cannot eliminate it. State this instead of promising even counts.

Mod-created portal ZDOs survive only if the mod set `Persistent = true` and the real portal prefab hash at creation (`CreateNewZDO` sets neither, :76674-76692; `ZNetView.Awake` :82613-82620). They are then written unconditionally because the portal chunk path has no Persistent filter (:77621-77632) — but a portal created with hash 0 then `SetPrefab` stays in the sector array and is dropped by `AddObjectsPerChunk` (:77572), i.e. it vanishes at the first save, not 'survives'.

The uninstall command's own tag/connection rewrites must call `SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes (only `SetConnection` does it automatically, :73656-73676) and route through ownership (`Game.SetConnection` delegates to an online owner) — otherwise the 'clean pairs' state is not what the world file contains at the next save.

catalog.name: Version migration — mod schema, world version and Valheim build fingerprinting
catalog.oneLine: Version every persisted artifact, fingerprint the game build at boot, and refuse to run destructive passes when the fingerprint is unrecognised.
catalog.howItWorks:
Three independent versions, all recorded in every persisted file and in the boot log:

1. **Mod schema version** — an int in `networks.json`, every snapshot and the audit file. Migrations are forward-only, run on load, write the upgraded file back after taking a `.bak`, and log every field they changed. Refuse to load a schema newer than the running mod.
2. **Valheim build** — `Version.GetVersionString()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112112) plus the network version literal (40u as seen at :42875/:97033) logged at Awake. Keep a config'd allowlist of verified builds; outside it, run in read-only mode (census/health/export still work, reassert and repair refuse) until the operator sets `AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true`. Precedent: TortalPortal's MIGRATE-1.0.md re-verified the mod unmodified against 1.0.12 (build 25253764, network version 40) with 37 types / 55 method bodies changed and all 48 Harmony targets still resolving — so the 1.0.7 decompile is a valid authority through at least 1.0.12 for everything this mod touches.
3. **World version** — `ZNet.World.m_worldVersion`/the `Version.World` enum used by `ZDOMan.LoadChunks(…, Version.World version)` (:76486). Record it so a snapshot taken on an older save format is flagged on restore.

Structural self-checks at Awake, all cheap and all failing *soft*: confirm `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` is non-empty (:100021); confirm `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` returns without throwing; confirm the Harmony targets resolve via `AccessTools.Method` before patching and wrap each patch set in `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` (SubsystemRegistry.cs:99), which degrades a signature change to a logged warning rather than killing Awake.

Honour the Mono JIT rule GameShape.cs encodes: a compile-time binding to a member the loaded assembly lacks throws at JIT of the *calling* method, so an internal try/catch does not save it. Any version-sensitive call must live in its own method reached only after a reflection-based probe confirms the shape (GameShape.Detect, Core/Compat/GameShape.cs:72). Never use the single-result `Type.GetMethod` overload — a compatibility patcher can inject a same-name/same-parameter overload and make it throw `AmbiguousMatchException` (GameShape.cs:155 comment, learned live).
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing player-facing. On a game update the operator sees `[tplite] Valheim 1.0.14 is not in the verified list (last verified 1.0.12). Running READ-ONLY: census/health/export active, reassert and repair disabled. Set AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true to override.` Their gates keep working exactly as vanilla does; the mod simply stops writing until a human says it is safe.
failureModes: Silently continuing to write ZDOs after a game update that changed a signature — the worst possible failure for a mod that rewrites persistent world data.
Binding at compile time to a member that may not exist and taking down the whole Awake at JIT time.
Migrating a file in place without a `.bak` — a bad migration is unrecoverable.
Using the game version string as a Harmony-target guarantee; verify the targets directly with AccessTools.

catalog.name: Compatibility with other server mods that touch ZDOs
catalog.oneLine: Enumerate the exact shared mutable surfaces — m_onZDODestroyed, ZDO.SetOwner prefixes, Game.ConnectPortals patches, Terminal.commands, ZRoutedRpc.Register — and adopt a defensive convention for each.
catalog.howItWorks:
Each contention point, with the safe convention:

1. **`ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033) is a single public `Action<ZDO>` field, and `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953). Always `Delegate.Combine`; never assign. An assignment silently disables ZNetScene's destruction handling for the entire server.
2. **`ZDO.SetOwner` prefixes.** Wonderland's `WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch` (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) already prefixes this global hot path (`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` calls it for every peer every 2 s, :76901-76927). Two mods both vetoing is a real hazard. Convention: only add the guard if measured contention demands it; fail fast on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` as the very first test; never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`; log once per minute when a veto fires so contention is visible.
3. **`Game.ConnectPortals` patches.** A prefix returning false disables *all* vanilla pairing, including for portals we do not manage. Do not do it. If our cooperative model is being defeated because another mod prefixed it, detect that (managed links stop being torn down when we deliberately mistag a probe portal) and log a compatibility warning rather than fighting.
4. **`Terminal.commands`.** The ConsoleCommand ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (:43096/:43114) — an indexer assignment, so a duplicate name silently clobbers with no exception and no log. Namespace every command `tplite.` and, at registration, check whether the key already exists and log if so.
5. **`ZRoutedRpc.Register`.** Per the digest it uses `Dictionary.Add`, so re-registering an existing name throws `ArgumentException`. Never register a vanilla name (`ChatMessage`, `ShowMessage`, `RPC_SetConnection`); for a mod-private RPC use a GUID-prefixed name and probe the private `m_functions` dictionary via `AccessTools` before registering.
6. **Sender identity.** `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is registered on every peer with **no** sender check and will rewire any ZDO's Portal connection to any target. Any mod (or malicious client) can undo our topology instantly. Our reassert loop restores it within 2 s; do not claim 'unbypassable'. The same applies to `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116022-116037), which also have no sender validation.
7. **Other mods writing `s_tag`.** Detect: if the census sees a managed portal's tag change to a value we did not write, and no `RPC_SetTag` crossed the wire, log a 'foreign writer' warning naming the portal rather than silently fighting forever.

Ship a `tplite.compat` command that lists every Harmony patch currently applied to the methods we care about, via `Harmony.GetPatchInfo(MethodBase)` — this turns a support ticket into one line of output.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect. The operator running two ZDO-touching mods sees `[tplite] compat: ZDO.SetOwner has 2 prefixes (wubarrk.wonderland, wubarrk.tortalportal-lite) — ownership guards may interact; Game.ConnectPortals has 1 prefix (other.mod) — cooperative pairing may be disabled` instead of a mysterious, intermittent 'my portals keep unpairing'.

corrections: Point 7 heuristic is void. TeleportWorld.SetText → m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", …) (:143583) routes to the ZDO OWNER; when the caller owns the portal the RPC executes locally with no packet. When the SERVER owns the portal, the server receives the routed packet but ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC (:82778-82795) resolves target-ZDO RPCs via ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo), which is null on a headless server (no ZNetView instances), so the RPC is dropped — and vanilla RPC_SetTag itself is gated on m_nview.IsOwner() (:143589). Net: from the server's viewpoint 'no RPC_SetTag on the wire' is ALWAYS true; the only observable is the s_tag value change arriving via ZDOData sync. A mod write and a vanilla owner retag are indistinguishable by this test. (Side effect worth logging: a vanilla client retagging a server-owned portal is silently dropped until ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership back.)

`tplite.compat` and every namespaced `tplite.*` ConsoleCommand is unreachable from a vanilla client. Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45747) only forwards to ZNet.RemoteCommand when the name exists in the CLIENT's own `commands` dictionary AND has RemoteCommand=true; an unknown name prints "'tplite.compat' is not a recognized command" locally and sends nothing. The dedicated server reads no stdin (no Console.ReadLine/KeyAvailable anywhere in assembly_valheim_SERVER). So registration in Terminal.commands only matters as a dispatch target for the mod's own file queue / HTTP, for another server mod, or via piggybacking: `setkey` (:43510-43534) and `removekey` (:43535) are vanilla remoteCommand:true/onlyServer:true commands a vanilla client forwards verbatim, so a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879-81889, runs after the built-in adminlist check) can intercept `setkey tplite.<verb> …` text before InternalCommand (:81891-81895).
Point 6 line range: RPC_SetConnection body is :100656-100664 (cited :100653-100662 is off by three lines, includes the tail of Game.SetConnection).

Point 2: the SetOwner prefix will fire for portals — confirmed, because FindObjects (:77376-77379) appends m_portalObjects entries to the sector result that ReleaseNearbyZDOS iterates; the PortalPrefabHash fast-fail is the right first test (PortalPrefabHash is a List<int>, :100021 — Contains is O(number of portal prefabs), fine).

Item 7: 'no RPC_SetTag crossed the wire' is the normal vanilla retag path (owner-client handles RPC_SetTag locally, InvokeRoutedRPC :83577-83595 skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id; tag arrives via RPC_ZDOData :77076). Detect foreign writers via s_tagauthor (written with s_tag in RPC_SetTag :143594-143598) instead.

Item 2: a Harmony prefix on ZDO.SetOwner cannot veto ownership asserted by clients — RPC_ZDOData writes ownership through SetOwnerInternal (:77127), which SetOwner (:74627) merely wraps. The guard only affects server-local SetOwner callers.

Item 4/`tplite.compat`: server-only ConsoleCommands cannot be typed by any vanilla client (Terminal.TryRunCommand :45733-45757 checks the client's own dictionary; RPC_RemoteCommand :81879 relays only client-known RemoteCommand names). Expose compat output through the file queue / HTTP / log instead.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Every game-side contention point cited exists and behaves as described: `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` is a public `Action<ZDO>` (:76033) and ZNetScene.Awake Delegate.Combines onto it (:81954); `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` calls `SetOwner` for every peer on a 2 s timer (:76872-76885 → :76901-76927); `ConsoleCommand` ctors do `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (:43096, :43114) — silent clobber confirmed; `ZRoutedRpc.Register` overloads all do `m_functions.Add(name.GetStableHashCode(), …)` (:83667-83700) on a `private readonly Dictionary<int,RoutedMethodBase>` (:83510) — duplicate throws; `Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered in `Game.Start` for all peers with no IsServer gate (:100066) and its body (:100653-100662) rewrites any ZDO's Portal connection with no sender check; `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116022-116037) likewise. Wonderland's ZdoSetOwnerPatch is at WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313. Two items are wrong. (1) Item 7's foreign-writer heuristic misfires on ordinary players: `TeleportWorld.SetText` → `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", …)` (:143579-143585) → `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` (:83577-83595), which handles locally when `targetPeerID == m_id` and only calls RouteRPC when `targetPeerID != m_id`. A client that owns the portal (the normal case after ReleaseNearbyZDOS) retags with zero RPC_SetTag packets — the new tag reaches the server only as ZDO data (RPC_ZDOData :77076). So 'no RPC_SetTag crossed the wire' is the vanilla norm, not a foreign-mod signal. The usable signal is `s_tagauthor`, which RPC_SetTag writes alongside `s_tag` (:143594-143598): a tag change whose author is unchanged / not a connected peer's platform id is the anomaly. (2) Item 2 overstates what a `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix can veto: `RPC_ZDOData` applies client-asserted ownership via `SetOwnerInternal` (:77127), and `SetOwner` (:74627-74634) is only a wrapper that calls SetOwnerInternal + IncreaseOwnerRevision. A prefix intercepts server-local calls (ReleaseNearbyZDOS, Game.SetConnection, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals) but never a client's own ownership claim arriving in a ZDO packet. Also: a `tplite.compat` ConsoleCommand is unreachable from a vanilla client — client `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45733-45757) resolves its own `commands` dictionary first and prints 'not a recognized command'; `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81888) only ever carries strings the client already knows as RemoteCommand — so the command is only invokable via the mod's own file/HTTP dispatcher.

catalog.name: Performance budget and cache-invalidation policy
catalog.oneLine: Portal ops cost is independent of world ZDO count because portals live in their own always-resident dictionary — everything expensive is a non-portal query, and this option defines the budgets for each.
catalog.howItWorks:
**The headline fact:** portals are not in `m_objectsBySector` at all. `AddIfPortal` files them in `m_portalObjects` and explicitly calls `RemoveFromSector` (:77732-77752); they are loaded wholesale from the dedicated portal chunk at world load (:76474-76482) and never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership :76872-76885; `FlushClientObjects` is client-only :76180-76183). So `GetPortalList()`/`GetPortals()` is O(P) in portal count and completely independent of whether the world holds 10 000 or 300 000 ZDOs.

**Budgets:**
- `GetPortalList()` — one `List<ZDO>` alloc of P refs (:77648-77656). At P = 500 and 1 Hz that is ~4 KB/s of gen-0 garbage. Acceptable. `GetPortals()` (:77643) is zero-alloc for read-only walks; `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` already uses it.
- Census tick 1.0 s; health 30 s; reassert 2.0 s; metrics sample 3.0 s; metrics aggregate 60 s; export 300 s; file-queue poll 1.0 s; config poll 5.0 s; heartbeat 15 min.
- **Non-portal queries are the expensive ones.** `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77442-77494) walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array (`new ZDOMan(512)` :79163, `ResetSectorArray` :76163) at ~400 *non-empty* sectors per call, re-hashing the prefab name each call — one full pass is ⌈nonEmpty/400⌉+1 calls. `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` (:75390-75407) is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary. Both are one-shot/boot-only. Use Wonderland's `PrefabSetSweeper` with an explicit `sectorBudget` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135, :153) when several prefab families are needed in one walk; its header records the name-based scanner taking *hours* for ~800 prefabs.
- Spatial 'nearest altar/bed/ship' lookups use `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25) over `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` (:77142) — note that method reuses a shared `m_visitedSectorIndices` HashSet and is **not reentrant**.
- Broadcast budget: cap `ForceSendZDO` at 256 per sweep (StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40 precedent); `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serialises the entire ZDO with no delta encoding (:77053-77062) and a 10 240-byte per-peer send-queue cap (:77010-77016).

**Cache policy:** cache the biome grid (immutable for the life of the world), the prefab-hash→name map (immutable after OnWorldReady), and the `s_creator`→name map (append-only). Invalidate the census every tick — there is no dirty flag to key off, and `GetPortalList` has no cache of its own. Never cache ZDO object references across ticks (ZDOPool recycling, :73536-73545). Cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible effect, which is the point: the operator's `ServerLog` line (vanilla's own 10-minute `InvokeRepeating("ServerLog", 600f, 600f)`, :100048/:100089-100096) showing `Connections N ZDOS:M sent:X recv:Y` should be indistinguishable with and without the mod. `tplite.perf` prints each engine's last and 95th-percentile tick cost in microseconds so a regression is visible immediately.
failureModes: Running any prefab-iterative or hash scan on a tick instead of at boot.
Calling `FindSectorObjects` from inside a loop already iterating its results — the shared visited-set makes it non-reentrant.
Mass `ForceSendZDO` in one frame on first boot after enabling networks.
Assuming `GetPortalList()` is cached and calling it several times per tick from different engines instead of once into a shared snapshot.
Scaling worry to world ZDO count — the relevant number is portal count, and it is the one to alarm on.
openQuestions: What is P on the target server today and after a year? Log `GetPortalList().Count` next to `NrOfObjects()` hourly. If P ever exceeds a few thousand, drop the census to 2–5 s and make the health scan incremental.

catalog.name: Subsystem architecture — registry, engines, tick rates, data ownership, config surface
catalog.oneLine: One BepInEx plugin, one ops subsystem, nine engines with disjoint write ownership and a fixed intra-tick ordering, mirroring Wonderland's registry/heartbeat shape so the two mods are maintainable side by side.
catalog.howItWorks:
**Plugin shell** (copy `WonderlandPlugin`, Plugin.cs:35-143 and `SubsystemRegistry`, SubsystemRegistry.cs, renamed). `Awake()`: init logger → `GameShape.Detect()` (only if `FindNear` is used) → build `ConfigSync` → `TpLiteConfig.Bind` → `RegisterSubsystems()` → `Subsystems.InitializeAll(Config, ConfigSync, harmony)` → `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch(harmony, typeof(WorldReadyHook))`. `WorldReadyHook` is a postfix on `ZNetScene.Awake` — the first point prefab lists are populated. `Update()`: `PollConfigFile()` (5 s) → `PollNetworkFile()` (5 s) → `PollCommandFile()` (1 s) → `Heartbeat.OnUpdate(dt)` → `Subsystems.OnUpdate()`. `OnDestroy()`: `Subsystems.ShutdownAll()` → `_harmony.UnpatchSelf()` → `DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking("portal engine offline")`.

**One subsystem, `PortalOpsSubsystem`**, owning nine engines. Fixed intra-tick order, because ordering is semantics not taste:

1. `PortalCensus` — 1.0 s. **Owns** the snapshot + the change stream. Writes nothing.
2. `NetworkModel` — event-driven on file change. **Owns** the parsed networks and their position→ZDOID resolution.
3. `AuditEngine` — consumes the change stream *before* any write this tick, subtracting the reassert engine's declared 'expected changes' set. **Owns** the ring buffer and `portal-audit.log`.
4. `NetworkReassertEngine` — 2.0 s. **The only writer of `s_tag` and `ConnectionType.Portal`.** Declares its intended writes to the audit engine before issuing them.
5. `HealthScanEngine` — 30 s. **Owns** findings. Pure read.
6. `RepairEngine` — on demand / slow timer, opt-in, dry-run by default. Writes only through the reassert engine's primitive; never writes directly.
7. `MetricsEngine` — 3 s sample, 60 s aggregate. **Owns** counters + route table.
8. `ExportEngine` — 300 s + on-change + on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted`. Pure read; serialises off-thread from the DTO. **Owns** `portals.json`, `portals.csv`, `portals.svg`.
9. `CommandEngine` — registers ConsoleCommands from a `Terminal.InitTerminal` postfix; drives the file queue; dispatches to the others. **Owns** nothing.

Plus a mod-wide `Heartbeat` ticked directly from `Update()` (not through the registry), exactly as Wonderland does (Heartbeat.cs:21) — it is a mod-wide concern, not any one engine's.

**Ownership rule, enforced by convention and by code review:** exactly one engine may write any given ZDO field, and the census may never write at all. Everything else reads the census snapshot, never live ZDOs.

**Config surface** (BepInEx `.cfg`, scalars only; topology lives in `networks.json`): `[General]` Enabled, VerboseLogging, AcceptUnverifiedBuild. `[Census]` IntervalSeconds. `[Networks]` File, ReassertSeconds, AllowTagRewrite, MaxWritesPerTick. `[Health]` IntervalSeconds, ReportUnmanagedOddGroups, ReportInteriorPortals. `[Repair]` AutoRepair (default false), DryRunDefault (true), MaxActionsPerRun. `[Audit]` Enabled, LogFile, RingSize, ToastOnBlockedRetag. `[Metrics]` TransitDetection, SampleSeconds, StraddleRadius. `[Export]` Json, Csv, Svg, IntervalSeconds, Directory. `[Discord]` WebhookUrl, Health, Audit, Destructions, Heartbeat. `[Http]` Enabled, Bind, Port, Token. `[Commands]` FileQueueEnabled, ConsolePrefix.

Every scalar is bound through the `BindSynced*` helpers (WonderlandConfig.cs:406-442) and registered with `ConfigSync` — pointless for a zero-client mod but free, and it gains the locking/version behaviour if a companion client ever appears.
catalog.playerExperience: Ordinary players experience the mod only as: gates that stay correctly connected, occasionally a tag that snaps back to the network's tag with a toast (`This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`), and nothing else. The operator experiences it as one `.cfg` of scalars, one `networks.json` of topology, a set of `tplite.*` console commands, a JSON/CSV/SVG export directory, a Discord channel and a heartbeat line every 15 minutes.
failureModes: Two engines writing the same ZDO field — the classic way a self-healing mod oscillates forever.
Running the audit after the reassert without an 'expected changes' set, so the mod attributes its own writes to players.
Putting topology in the BepInEx `.cfg` — flat key=value cannot express nested lists, and the resulting stringly-typed format is unvalidatable.

Doing ObjectDB/ZNetScene prefab reads in `Initialize()` instead of `OnWorldReady()`; worse, assuming `ObjectDB.instance` is non-null even at `OnWorldReady` — it frequently is not (BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96 retries once per tick until it resolves).
Letting an engine throw and take down the whole plugin — every call must go through the registry's try/catch (SubsystemRegistry.cs:29-79) and every patch through `SafePatch` (:99).
citations: Heartbeat ticked from Update — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Heartbeat.cs:21
Wonderland.csproj (net472, server assemblies, publicizer) — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:1-31, :19-27
openQuestions: Should this be a separate plugin or a Wonderland subsystem? A separate plugin duplicates ~600 lines of shell (Plugin/Registry/Heartbeat/Config/AuditLog/DiscordWebhook/ZdoSpatialQuery/ConnectedCharacters/PlayerNotify) but keeps the portal problem out of a general-purpose mod, which is the reason TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md was split out in the first place. Decide before writing the shell.

corrections: CommandEngine: a `tplite.*` ConsoleCommand registered on the server is unreachable from any vanilla client — Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45747) forwards via ZNet.RemoteCommand only for names present in the CLIENT's dictionary with RemoteCommand=true, and the headless server reads no stdin. State explicitly that console registration serves (a) the file queue, (b) HTTP, (c) other server mods, and optionally (d) a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879-81889) intercepting `setkey tplite.<verb> …` — `setkey` is vanilla remoteCommand:true (:43510-43534), the client forwards its raw text, and the adminlist check (:81881) has already run. Update the operator playerExperience line accordingly: admins do not get `tplite.*` in their in-game console.

[Http] HttpListener: not verifiable from the decompile (the game assemblies never reference it). Precedent in this workspace: Wonderland ships System.Net.Http.HttpClient on the server (DiscordWebhook.cs:18) and TheRavensCall/Companion.cs:27-80 constructs an HttpListener in a Valheim mod — same Unity Mono System.dll — but neither is a verified Linux-headless run of HttpListener. Mark the HTTP engine needs-ingame-check (bind ACL, System.dll presence in the server's Managed/ folder) and keep it optional/off by default.

'Registered with ConfigSync — free': ServerSync sends its config package to every peer via a routed RPC on connect; vanilla clients drop it silently (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :82778-82786, unknown m_methodHash → no-op) but it is not zero bytes. Acceptable, just not 'free'.

Plugin.OnDestroy is at Plugin.cs:76-80 (cited :78) and does not call DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking — that is an addition, and SendBlocking (DiscordWebhook.cs:42, 3000 ms default timeout) exists to support it.

Structural probes (PortalPrefabHash, GetPortalList) referenced by the sibling version option belong in OnWorldReady, not Awake — Game.instance/ZDOMan.instance are null at plugin Awake (:100026, :79163).

CommandEngine: server-only ConsoleCommands are unreachable from vanilla clients (Terminal.TryRunCommand :45733-45757 checks the client's own dictionary; RPC_RemoteCommand :81879-81888 relays only client-known RemoteCommand names) and the dedicated server reads no stdin. Treat the file queue / HTTP as the only real command surfaces; console registration is only for other mods or the mod's own dispatcher via Console.instance.TryRunCommand.

Do not route server-side dispatch through ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand — its IsServer branch calls InternalCommand(null, cmd) which dereferences rpc.GetSocket() (:81869-81901) and throws NRE. Call Console.instance.TryRunCommand directly.

Terminal.InitTerminal is private static (:43297) called from Terminal.Awake (:45762-45765); a postfix fires at first Terminal Awake, before ZNet exists — acceptable because ConsoleCommand.IsValid (:43203-43217) checks OnlyServer/ZNet at run time.

The 'single writer of s_tag / Portal connection' rule is an intra-mod convention only; vanilla Game.ConnectPortals (:100589), Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653) and client RPC_SetTag/ZDO sync also write those fields.
[Http] HttpListener availability under the game's Mono runtime remains unverified.

So the console registration is dead surface unless another mod or the mod's own file-queue/HTTP dispatcher calls `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` — which exists on the dedicated server because vanilla's own RPC_RemoteCommand depends on it (:81896-81900). The 'only writer' ownership rule is intra-mod only: vanilla `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) and `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) also write the Portal connection and any client's RPC_SetTag/ZDO sync writes s_tag. `[Http]` under Mono was not verified here (no game-side evidence either way). The player-facing toast is a ShowMessage routed RPC — client-honoured display, not enforcement. ConfigSync registration is, as the option says, inert for zero-client.

catalog.name: RULED OUT — vanilla PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut as server metrics
catalog.oneLine: Portal usage counters exist in vanilla but are written to each player's local character file and never networked to the server in any form.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.Teleport` ends with `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat(PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed)` (:143548), and `Teleport.Interact` (dungeon doors) increments `PortalDungeonIn`/`PortalDungeonOut` (:143362). `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` delegates to `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` (:100569-100572), which writes an in-memory `Dictionary<PlayerStatType,float>` inside `PlayerProfile.m_playerStats` (:106287-106300) and feeds `Achievements`. That dictionary is serialised only into that client's own `.fch` via `PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData`/`SavePlayerToDisk` (:105706-105711, :105760+).

There is no path off the client. `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) sounds like a collector and does the opposite: it invokes the `SavePlayerProfile` RPC on each peer, whose handler calls `Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile` on that client (:79672-79675, :100204-100240) — writing that client's own local file and returning nothing.

The only client→server per-player dictionary is `ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData` (:79051), serialised in `SendServerSyncPlayerData` (:80365-80377) and received in `RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` (:80395-80410) — and vanilla populates it with exactly three unrelated keys (`platformDisplayName`, `baseValue`, `possibleEvents`, written at :79212, :11400, :11095). A server-only mod cannot add a key to it because that would require client code.

Also note the counters would be wrong even if readable: the stat is incremented on `TeleportTo`'s *acceptance*, before `UpdateTeleport` moves anything, so a teleport that later fails and restores position (`Player.UpdateTeleport` :15359-15376) still counted.
catalog.playerExperience: A player's own in-game stats screen shows their true portal count. The server, and therefore any leaderboard, Discord report or admin query, can never see that number. An operator asking 'who uses portals most' gets the heuristic answer or none.
failureModes: Building a leaderboard on a number that is silently always zero server-side.
Assuming `SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` gathers data.

catalog.name: RULED OUT — a vanilla per-portal 'last changed' timestamp, and offline link reconstruction by ZDOID
catalog.oneLine: No ZDO carries a wall clock, and the on-disk connection is a random int hash pair rather than a ZDOID — so both 'when did this change' and 'read the links out of the world file' must be mod-maintained.
catalog.howItWorks:
**No timestamp.** `ZDO`'s complete field set is `m_uid`, `m_rotation`, `m_position`, `m_tempSortValue`, `m_prefab`, `m_dataFlags`, `m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321), plus the revision counters. `DataRevision`/`OwnerRevision` are monotonic `uint`s with no time base, and `IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832-73840) bumps them for *any* field change, so they cannot even distinguish a tag edit from a position sync. The only clock anywhere near a ZDO is `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks` in `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76993-76998) — a destruction time, for destroyed ZDOs only, in a private dictionary. Conclusion: `lastChanged` must be stamped by the mod's own census diff and persisted alongside the network file, and is therefore blind to anything that happened while the mod was not running.

**No ZDOID on disk.** `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` plus `connectionData.m_hash` (:74315-74317) — an int generated by `ZDOExtraData.GetUniqueHash` seeded from the session id (:75440-75459) — not the target ZDOID. `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives the source side `ConnectionType.Portal` (1) and the target side `Portal|Target` (0x11) with the same hash, and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850-77893) re-pairs by matching those hashes at load. So offline tooling reading a `.chunk` file cannot resolve a portal's destination by id; it must replicate the hash-matching pass. Worse, `ZDO.Load` renumbers every `m_uid` (:74552), so the ids in the file bear no relation to the ids in the previous session.

**Implication for ops:** the durable identity for any portal record is its rounded world position, and the durable representation of a link for export/backup purposes is a *pair of positions*, never a pair of ZDOIDs.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing player-facing. The operator sees `changed ~4h ago (observed)` rather than an authoritative timestamp, and `tplite.export` emits position pairs rather than id pairs, with a note that ids are session-scoped.
failureModes: Exporting ZDOID-keyed links and building external tooling on them.
Using `DataRevision` as a change clock — it advances for position syncs too, so on a portal a player is standing next to it can advance constantly.
Writing an offline world-file reader that expects ZDOIDs in the connection field.
catalog.id: ops-admin:RULED OUT — a vanilla per-portal 'last changed' timestamp, and offline link reconstruction by ZDOID
evidence: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision — :73832-73840; InternalSetPosition owner-gated bump (15 call sites of IncreaseDataRevision())
ZDOMan.ConnectPortals hash matching, SetOwner(GetSessionID()) both sides — :77850-77893
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Read every cited site. ZDO's instance fields are exactly m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark (:73309-73321) plus the OwnerRevision/DataRevision properties — no clock. IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) is a bare DataRevision++ plus ClientChanged/SetDirtySector, invoked from 15 setters including InternalSetPosition (owner only), so it is a 'something changed' counter, not a field-level or time-based one. The only timestamp is the private m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks in HandleDestroyedZDO, server-only branch (:76993-76998). ZDO.Save writes (byte)m_type + m_hash for the single connection slot (:74315-74317); GetUniqueHash is seeded from ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode() + a counter (:75440-75454); RegenerateConnectionHashData assigns the source ConnectionType.Portal and the target Portal|Target with the same hash (:75461-75478); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (private, :77850-77893) re-pairs by hash equality and force-owns both sides; ZDO.Load renumbers m_uid via ++ZDOID.m_loadID (:74552). All claims hold; the implication that durable identity must be position-based is correct.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every claim verified against the source. ZDO instance fields are exactly `m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321) plus revision counters; `IncreaseDataRevision` just does `DataRevision++`, notifies ClientChanged on clients, and `SetDirtySector` (:73832-73840) — no time and no field discrimination. The only clock near a ZDO is `m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks` in `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76995-76999), server-only, for destroyed ZDOs; and `ZNet.GetTime()` (:81535-81539) is derived from `m_netTime` (game net time), not wall clock — so even that is not a real-world timestamp. On disk `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` + `connectionData.m_hash` (:74313-74317); `GetUniqueHash` seeds from `ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode()` (:75445-75459); `RegenerateConnectionHashData` assigns the same hash to source (type) and target (type|Target) (:75461-75478); `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` re-pairs by hash equality at load (:77850-77893), taking the first match and breaking; `ZDO.Load` renumbers with `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552-74555; SetID :75877-75881 also resets UserKey). Attack from the save boundary strengthens rather than weakens it: because the file holds one hash slot per ZDO and pairing is first-match, any non-pairwise topology collapses on reload, so a position-pair export is the only durable representation. Minor nuance, not a correction: ZDO extra-data string/long keys could in principle hold a mod-written net-time stamp, but vanilla writes none on TeleportWorld (its RPC_SetTag writes only s_tag/s_tagauthor :143594-143598), and any such key is invisible to offline tooling anyway. Position-as-identity is sound for portals (static pieces, position written once at placement).

catalog.name: RULED OUT — the vanilla noportals command, and any in-game admin GUI
catalog.oneLine: The stock noportals command is inert on a dedicated server and cannot even be fired remotely; and any panel, list or picker rendered in-game is inherently client work.
catalog.howItWorks:
**`noportals`.** Its entire body is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (:45284-45298), which is never true on a dedicated server — `Player.m_localPlayer` is populated only by `Player.SetLocalPlayer` (:10110) and no Player GameObject is ever instantiated, because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick (:100465) and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` only builds objects around that reference position (:82268-82276). It is also registered `remoteCommand:false` (:45298), so an admin cannot fire it from a client console either. Note the correction to the existing spec: the neighbouring `nomap` command is **equally** dead — its `IsServer()` branch is nested *inside* the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283), not an alternative to it. Use `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("noportals")` (:115943) or the `setkey` console command (`onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true`, :43510-43534).

**In-game GUI.** Every rendering surface is client-side: `Minimap`, `InventoryGui`, `MessageHud`, `TextInput` and IMGUI all require a local player and a graphics device. The server's only channels to a vanilla client are (a) `PlayerNotify.Toast` via the per-character `"Message"` routed RPC (Player.Start registration :10072, RPC_Message :14820-14825), (b) the global `"ShowMessage"` RPC (MessageHud.Start :55808, RPC_ShowMessage :55848-55851), (c) a saved map pin via `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered for every peer, Game.Start :100068; handler :100823-100829), (d) floating world text via `"RPC_DamageText"` (DamageText.Awake :46352-46356), (e) a one-shot VFX/SFX via `"SpawnObject"` (ZNetScene.Awake :81954; RPC_SpawnObject :82355-82366), and (f) the portal's own hover text through `s_tag`. None of those is a panel, a list, or a picker.

The admin's interface is therefore the F5 console, the config files, the export files, the HTTP endpoint and Discord — not anything drawn in the game world.
catalog.playerExperience: An operator who expects to open an admin panel in-game does not get one. What they get instead: press F5, type `tplite.list TRADE`, read the reply in the console. A player who expects a gate directory in-game gets, at most, a server-pushed map pin per gate and the tag on the gate's hover text — never a browsable list. This is precisely the gap full client-side TortalPortal exists to fill.
failureModes: Planning an admin UX around an in-game panel and discovering at implementation time that no rendering surface exists.
Using the vanilla `noportals` command in operator documentation and having it silently do nothing.
Citing `nomap` as the correct counter-example — it is equally dead.
openQuestions: Are `MessageHud.instance`, `Minimap.instance` and `DamageText.instance` actually non-null on a 1.0.7 dedicated server? `Console.instance` provably is (Game.Awake :100038-100041); the others matter only for the send side, which does not need them, but `ZNet.PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80574) dereferencing MessageHud unguarded suggests the GUI scene does load headless. Log all five at OnWorldReady.
catalog.id: ops-admin:RULED OUT — the vanilla noportals command, and any in-game admin GUI
corrections: `Player.SetLocalPlayer` is declared at :10103; :10110 is inside its body.

Add channel (g): `ZNet.RemotePrint(ZRpc, string)` (:81635-81647) prints arbitrary text into a vanilla client's F5 console (`RPC_RemotePrint` -> `Console.instance.Print`). The 'RemotePrint' ZRpc is registered on every peer at :79912. This makes a server-pushed TEXT list feasible; only panels/pickers are ruled out.

An adminlisted vanilla client can already fire `setkey noportals` / `removekey noportals` from F5: client `TryRunCommand` -> `ZNet.RemoteCommand` (client :82098-82105) -> server `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889, `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())`) -> `InternalCommand` -> `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` (:81891-81895). The 'cannot be fired remotely' statement is true only of the `noportals` command itself, not of the NoPortals key.

The playerExperience story 'press F5, type tplite.list TRADE' does not work on a vanilla client as written: the client's `Terminal.commands` (:43230) has no such entry and prints 'not a recognized command' (:45752-45755). A mod-defined command is only reachable from the dedicated server's own stdin console, or by smuggling it behind a vanilla `remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true` token (e.g. `setkey tplite.list TRADE`) and intercepting it in a Harmony prefix on `ZNet.InternalCommand` (:81891) BEFORE `TryRunCommand` — otherwise unpatched `setkey` would write the junk string as a global key (:43520).

`setkey noportals` is subject to `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat` (:43515, :59610ff) which depends on the modifier prefab's key lists (`KeyToggle.m_enabledKey` / `KeySlider.m_settings[].m_keys`); whether 'noportals' is in that list is prefab data, not verifiable from the decompile.

Replace 'cannot even be fired remotely' with: it cannot be forwarded through RPC_RemoteCommand, but every vanilla client (admin or not — OnlyAdmin is a dead field) can execute it locally and the resulting SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey routed RPC is accepted by the server with no sender check. The vanilla command is the reason 'Global-Key RPC Hardening' is needed.

Remove the 'press F5, type tplite.list TRADE' experience: unknown command names are rejected client-side (Terminal.TryRunCommand :45737) and never sent. A mod-registered ConsoleCommand on the server is unreachable from a vanilla client.
The dedicated server has no interactive console in vanilla (no stdin reader in the server assembly); server-side command entry is RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879) or mod/BepInEx-provided.

Add the one viable in-console admin path: carrier commands. A vanilla client forwards any command whose ConsoleCommand has RemoteCommand=true and is not valid locally (setkey/removekey/resetkeys/save/kick/ban…) via ZNet.RemoteCommand (:81869-81877); the server checks m_adminList by socket host name (:81881) and runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand (:81894). A prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand (server) can intercept e.g. 'setkey tplite list TRADE' and answer with ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, …) (:81635) which lands in the admin's console (:81650). This is admin-authenticated, unlike the key RPCs.
Note nomap correction stands (:45261-45283 nested inside the same m_localPlayer guard).

Wonderland EmoteSignals.cs:8-16 (vanilla client never sends unknown console commands)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core claims hold. `noportals` body is entirely inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (:45284-45298) and is registered `remoteCommand:false, onlyAdmin:true` (:45298); `onlyAdmin` forces `OnlyServer=true` (ConsoleCommand ctor :43101), so on a client `IsValid` fails (:43203-43217) and `TryRunCommand` (:45734-45757) falls to 'not valid in the current context' because `RemoteCommand` is false — it cannot be fired remotely. `nomap`'s `IsServer()` branch is nested inside the same local-player guard (:45261-45283) — the correction to the spec is right. `Game.FixedUpdate` on the server build is nothing but the reference-position pin (:100456-100466) and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` builds only around that position (:82268-82276), so no Player object exists. `setkey` IS usable on a dedicated server: `Console.instance` and `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance` are instantiated in `Game.Awake` (:100038-100045) / `FejdStartup` (:97485-97488), so `SetKeyAndValueIsCheat` (:59610ff, iterates static `m_modifiers` set in `ServerOptionsGUI.Awake` :59597-59602) does not NRE. All six server->client channel citations verified at the cited lines. What the option misses: the vanilla remote-console path. `setkey`/`removekey` are `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` (:43530-43534, :43546); on a vanilla client `TryRunCommand` routes them via `ZNet.RemoteCommand` (client :82098-82105) to the server's `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889, admin-list check on `rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()`), which runs `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` (:81891-81895) and replies through `ZNet.RemotePrint` (:81635-81647) into the client's `Console.instance.Print` (client `RPC_RemotePrint`). So an adminlisted vanilla client CAN toggle NoPortals from its own F5 console today, and the server has a text channel into the vanilla console — a plain text LIST is pushable, even if a panel/picker is not.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The core ruling stands: `noportals` is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (Terminal :45284-45298) and `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the server reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick (:100465), so on the dedicated server the body never runs; it is `remoteCommand:false` so `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734-45746) never forwards it via `ZNet.RemoteCommand`. All six server->client channels cited (Player "Message" :10072/:14820, MessageHud "ShowMessage" :55808/:55848, RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse :100066/:100823, RPC_DamageText :46352, SpawnObject :81954/:82355, s_tag hover) verified. BUT two load-bearing statements are wrong. (1) The vanilla command is NOT inert in practice: `ConsoleCommand.OnlyAdmin` is assigned (:43082,:43109,:43127) and never read anywhere in either assembly (client grep: only the same three lines), `isCheat:false`, `onlyServer:false`; `Chat.isAllowedCommand` (:41938) only rejects cheats. So ANY vanilla player typing `noportals` in F5 or `/noportals` in chat runs it locally with a live `m_localPlayer`, which calls `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` -> `InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey")` to the server (:115943) -> `RPC_SetGlobalKey` with no sender check (:116022). The stock command is the live, unauthenticated, world-wide toggle for this exact feature; 'cannot be fired remotely' is true only of the RPC_RemoteCommand path. (2) The promised operator experience ('press F5, type tplite.list TRADE') is impossible with a vanilla client: `TryRunCommand` looks the name up in the client's own `commands` dictionary first (:45737) and prints 'not a recognized command' for anything the client does not know; it never reaches the wire (Wonderland EmoteSignals.cs:10-12 already documents this). The dedicated server itself has no stdin/console reader in vanilla (no `Console.In`/`ReadLine`/`KeyAvailable` anywhere in the server assembly) — server-side command entry exists only through `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889, admin-list gated by `rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()`) which calls `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` on the server (:81891-81895). The only in-console admin channel therefore is hijacking a vanilla `remoteCommand:true` command as a carrier (e.g. `setkey tplite ...`, `removekey ...`, :43510-43534/:43535-43546) with a server-side prefix on `Terminal.TryRunCommand` or `ZNet.InternalCommand`, replying through `ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, text)` (:81635-81647) which prints in the admin's client console (:81650-81656). That is admin-authenticated by socket identity, unlike the global-key RPCs.

catalog.name: The Routing Kernel
catalog.oneLine: Take ownership of portal pairing from vanilla so that "which routes exist right now" becomes a pure server decision, and the tag string is freed up as a display channel.
catalog.howItWorks:
Everything else in this domain is a child of this option. Vanilla's authority lives in `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589), driven by `Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine` (:100580) which `Game.Start` launches only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` (:100074) and which fires immediately then every 5.0s forever. Its two passes are: (1) teardown — for each portal in `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), clear the connection if the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's `ZDOVars.s_tag` string differs, or the partner's own connection is `ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604); (2) pairing — for each still-unconnected portal, pick a uniformly random same-tag unconnected partner via `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664, `UnityEngine.Random.Range` at :100678) and write both directions through `Game.SetConnection` (:100637).

Three escalating levels of takeover:

**L1 — selection override.** Harmony postfix on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO skip, string tag)`, overwriting `__result` with your own choice (nearest, oldest, admin-designated, or `null` to refuse). Lowest risk: vanilla keeps teardown, ownership handling, the two-phase commit through `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` / `Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690), and its own `ZLog` audit lines (:100619).

**L2 — full replacement.** Harmony prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` returning `false`, then run your own topology pass in the same frame. You must reproduce the `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard (:100609/:100671) or you will double-pair portals owned by online players, whose connection writes are deferred over `RPC_SetConnection` (:100649) and therefore still read `None` in the server's own copy that tick.

**L3 — coroutine stop.** `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` (started by the string overload at :100074, so the string form is valid) and drive your own timer.

Write primitive, copied verbatim from `Game.SetConnection` (:100643-100645): `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);`. `ZDO.SetConnection` (:73656) is idempotent — `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` (:74954-74957) returns false on an unchanged type+target, so no DataRevision bump and no packet. Re-asserting the whole topology every tick is therefore free. It also calls `ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()` for you, which is what actually gets the portal chunk written at save (`ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621).

The decisive consequence: once you own pairing, `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) stops being the routing key and becomes a free 80-column display string on every vanilla client's hover text (`TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` :143453). That is what makes "MINE 43/50c" or "LEASED til d.412" possible at all.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible when idle: gates pair the way they always did, except deterministically (the nearest same-tag partner rather than a coin flip), so the third portal on a shared tag stops being randomly orphaned. What players notice is that the tag text starts carrying information the game never put there — walking up to a gate reads `Teleport tag:"MINE 43/50c" [Connected]` instead of `tag:"mine"`. Renaming still works: the player presses E, the 10-character vanilla text box opens pre-filled, and whatever they type becomes their *label*; the server re-decorates it on the next tick and the route they belong to is unchanged, because routing is now a server-side table keyed on position, not on the string.
failureModes: L2/L3 inherit a latent vanilla bug: `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` caches raw `ZDO` object references for a full 5s, and `ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76990) releases destroyed ZDOs back to `ZDOPool`, whose `ZDO.Reset()` (:73536) sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None`. Never cache `ZDO` objects across ticks — cache `ZDOID` and re-resolve with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)`.

`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs every 2s per peer and reassigns portal ownership to any player within ~96-112m (`ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea` :82297). Your `SetOwner` claim evaporates; the connection VALUE survives because it was already `ForceSendZDO`'d, but the next write must re-claim. Guard with the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix pattern from Wonderland `Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301` if you need a persistent claim.

Non-pairwise topologies (rings, one-way, self-loops) survive at runtime but are mangled at save: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives each ZDO exactly one hash slot, so a 3-ring loses a link and a self-loop is erased. The kernel must re-assert its whole topology in an `OnWorldReady` pass after every load.
If another mod also patches `Game.ConnectPortals`, an L2 prefix returning false silently disables theirs. Use `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` (Wonderland `Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:99`) and log loudly.

Two classes are named `ConnectPortals`. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850) is private, runs only at world load, and matches save-file hashes with no tag involvement. Patching it achieves nothing at runtime.
openQuestions: Does `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` actually stop it? The string StartCoroutine overload at :100074 makes it valid per Unity's API, but that is a Unity claim, not a decompile claim. Check: call it, place two same-tag portals, and watch for the absence of `[ Connected N portals ]` in the server log.

Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828)? Inspector data. Log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` at first heartbeat; this also tells you whether modded portal pieces join the registry for free.

Does a client already standing at a gate pick up a server-side `s_tag` rewrite without a zone reload? `TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal` runs on a 0.5s InvokeRepeating (:143450) but the hover text goes through a separate `GetTagInfo` read (:143561). Check by standing at a gate while the server renames it.
corrections: 'Tag becomes a free display string' holds only at L2/L3. At L1 vanilla pass 1 still runs and nulls any link whose two ends carry different s_tag strings (`zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string`, :100601). Decorated text must be byte-identical on both ends of every route, or the mod must replace ConnectPortals entirely.

'Re-asserting the whole topology every tick is free' is false for the primitive as quoted. ZDO.SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision whenever the current owner differs (SetOwner body, ZDOExtraData.GetOwner != uid), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands every portal in a player's active area back to that player every 2 s (:76870-76884, :76901-76926), so an unconditional SetOwner each tick flaps ownership, emits a packet per portal per tick, and — because the server owning a portal makes HandleRoutedRPC drop RPC_SetTag (:83656) — silently breaks vanilla renaming for everyone near a portal. Guard like vanilla's ForceSetConnection (:100630-100636): compare GetConnectionZDOID first and only claim ownership when a write is actually needed.

Renaming tears the route: the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag calls UpdateConnection(Portal, None) on itself and SetConnectedPortal on the old partner (:143594-143597, :143604-143618) before writing the new tag, so every rename produces an [Unconnected] flicker until the kernel re-asserts on its next tick. The RPC_SetConnected path to the partner's owner (:143615) also fires on the wire.

TextInput prefill is capped: RequestText sets characterLimit = 10 before assigning the current tag (:61509-61522), so a decorated tag longer than 10 characters pre-fills truncated and pressing Enter submits the truncated string. Label parsing must treat 'first 10 chars of the decorated tag' as no-change.

Restart: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks purely from saved hash data (:77850-77890) and Game.ConnectPortals is invoked inside LoadChunks (:76524) — both before any per-tick kernel pass. Because RegenerateConnectionHashData persists only one slot per ZDO (:75461-75477), any non-pairwise topology (fan-in, ring, one-way) comes back as a pairwise matching or not at all; the kernel must persist its own table (keyed on position, not ZDOID — ZDOIDs are regenerated at load) and re-assert after ZNet finishes loading.

Modded clients: a client that owns a portal can write any connection via its ZDOData (Deserialize -> ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, :74224-74232; accepted at :77107-77118 when DataRevision is higher); the kernel re-asserts within one tick. Enforcement is over the route field, not over the traveller — movement remains client-authoritative.

L1 does NOT free the tag: Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (:100601) clears any link whose partner tag differs, so the tag is still the routing key at L1. Tag-as-display requires L2 or L3 (or identical decoration on both ends of every pair).

Write primitive must be gated on GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != target (vanilla ForceSetConnection :100628-100634). Unconditional per-tick SetOwner (ZDO.SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision on any owner change) fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) every 2s and emits a packet per portal per tick; only ZDO.SetConnection is idempotent.

After any client-side drift, force a DataRevision bump: server and client writes at the same revision are mutually rejected (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118 and client twin), and ShouldSend does not re-send an unchanged revision.

Renaming: the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag nulls both ends (:143587-143629); the kernel must capture the player's raw text from the incoming ZDO update before re-decorating, and the route is down for up to one kernel tick.

L2 prefix also blocks the load-time Game.instance.ConnectPortals() call in ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:76523); run the kernel pass there too. ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77891) restores only a pairwise matching from saved hash data and ZDOIDs regenerate per load, so the position-keyed table must be re-applied after LoadChunks.
TextInput charLimit is 10 (:61515-61522; RequestText :143486) - decorated tags longer than 10 chars are truncated in the rename prefill.
