verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The vanilla authority chain is exactly as described: Game.Start starts 'ConnectPortalsCoroutine' by string under IsServer (:100072-100075); the coroutine fires immediately then every 5 s (:100580-100587); ConnectPortals is public and runs teardown then pairing in one call (:100589-100625); FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is private, filters skip/tag/unconnected/staged and uses UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100664-100680); SetConnection defers to RPC_SetConnection when an online peer owns the portal (:100637-100650); ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false on an unchanged type+target (:74951-74960) so ZDO.SetConnection neither bumps DataRevision nor dirties portals when unchanged (:73656-73665); DirtyPortalObjects gates the ChunkPortal write (:77621-77636). The takeover is real and the route field is server-owned. Three claims are wrong as stated: the tag is NOT freed at L1, the verbatim write primitive is NOT free to re-assert every tick, and the player-rename story omits that vanilla's RPC_SetTag tears the route down on every rename.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Anchors verified: Game.Start registers RPC_SetConnection and, under ZNet.instance.IsServer(), StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") by string (:100062-100075), so StopCoroutine(string) is valid (L3). ConnectPortalsCoroutine (:100580-100587) fires immediately then every 5s. ConnectPortals is public (:100589); pass 1 teardown predicate :100601; pass 2 :100607-100621 with IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal guard (:100609, :100671) and UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100678). FindRandomUnconnectedPortal, SetConnection, RPC_SetConnection, ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals are all private - Harmony can reach them. ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666) calls ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (:74951-74960) which returns false on unchanged type+target, so no revision bump and SetDirtyPortals only on change. GetSaveClonePerChunk gates the portal chunk on DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77636). TeleportWorld.GetHoverText (:143453-143463) renders the raw tag (after CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC keyed on s_tagauthor). Corrections: (1) 'tag freed as display channel' is FALSE at L1 - pass 1 (:100601) tears down any link whose partner tag differs, so under L1 the tag remains the routing key; the decoupling only holds at L2/L3, or if both ends of every pair carry byte-identical decoration. (2) The write primitive is not free as written: ZDO.SetOwner (:73893-73900 region) bumps OwnerRevision whenever the owner differs, which is every tick for any portal a player stands near, because ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) hands ownership back to the peer within 2s; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend returns true on a higher OwnerRevision, so a naive per-tick SetOwner+SetConnection generates a packet per portal per tick and an ownership ping-pong. Gate the write on GetConnectionZDOID != target exactly as vanilla ForceSetConnection does (:100628-100634). (3) Revision tie: a server write and a client-owner write that both reach N+1 are mutually rejected (server :77108-77118; client symmetric), and the idempotent no-bump re-assertion never pushes the server's value across; after any observed client drift the server must force a DataRevision bump. (4) Player rename does not leave 'the route unchanged': the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag (:143587-143602) nulls its own connection with UpdateConnection and nulls the partner via SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected (:143604-143629); the route is down until the kernel's next tick, and the kernel must read the player's raw text out of the incoming ZDO update before re-decorating, or the label is lost. (5) L2 prefix on Game.ConnectPortals also suppresses the load-time call at ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76523; the mod must run its own pass there. (6) ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77850-77891) rebuilds pairs from ZDOConnectionHashData as a pairwise matching (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75477 keeps one slot per ZDO), so any kernel topology that is not a perfect matching must be re-derived from the position-keyed table after every load; keying on ZDOID does not survive a restart. (7) TextInput.Show applies characterLimit 10 (:61515-61522, RequestText call :143486), so decorated tags longer than 10 chars display fine but the E-prefill is truncated.

catalog.name: Park and Release
catalog.oneLine: The atomic enforcement primitive: hold a named route closed until a condition is met, and open it the instant it is — three techniques with different visibility, cost and failure characteristics.
catalog.howItWorks:
A parked portal has `GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None`. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` then returns at its very first gate — `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519) — with no message, no effect and no way for a modified client to route around it, because the destination simply is not in the ZDO the client holds. This is the only one of `Teleport`'s four gates that is genuinely server-ENFORCED rather than client-honoured (the other three read global keys or the local inventory, :143523/:143528/:143533).

Naively writing `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` loses: vanilla's pass 1 and pass 2 run in the *same* `Game.ConnectPortals()` call (:100594 then :100607), so a nulled portal is re-paired ≤5s later, often within the same frame. Three ways to actually hold it:

**A — Tag mutation (no Harmony).** Rewrite `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) to a value no other portal shares, e.g. `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, label + " #" + token)`. Pass 1 clears the existing link on tag mismatch (:100601); `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100669) finds no same-tag candidate and returns null forever. Follow with `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — a tag-only write does NOT set `DirtyPortalObjects` (only `ZDO.SetConnection` :73661, `AddIfPortal` :77750 and `HandleDestroyedZDO` :76986 do) so it is silently lost at the next world save. Cheapest, zero patches, but the tag is the routing key AND the display, so parking mangles the label.

**B — Pairing veto (recommended).** Postfix `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` and return `null` when `skip` is in your parked set; separately force `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on parked portals each tick (idempotent, so free after the first write). Tag stays pristine and available for status text. Requires the Routing Kernel at L1.

**C — Decoy sink.** See the Customs House option.

Release is the inverse: drop the park flag, restore the tag (A) or clear the veto (B), and call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` directly for instant re-pairing rather than waiting up to 5s.

Timing caveat for both: pass 1's clear is NOT forced (`SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` at :100603 with `forceImmediateConnection` defaulting false), so when an online player owns the portal ZDO the clear is deferred over `RPC_SetConnection` to that client and the server's own copy still reads the old value that tick. Re-pairing after a release near a standing player takes 2+ ticks. Write with force semantics yourself (`SetOwner` then `SetConnection` then `ForceSendZDO`) to make park and release single-tick.
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks up to a gate they have used for weeks and the frame reads `[Unconnected]` instead of `[Connected]`, and the runic ring has gone dark (`TeleportWorld.Update` lerps `m_colorAlpha` toward 0 when `m_hadTarget` is false, :143511). Walking into it does absolutely nothing — no message, no shove, no error — which is exactly how vanilla behaves for a portal with no partner, so it reads as a game state rather than a mod refusal. Because that silence is confusing, pair every park with a reason in the tag (`"BRIDGE closed"`, `"MINE 43/50c"`) and a one-line toast to anyone standing within 20m at the moment of parking, via `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Wonderland `Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15`). The release is dramatic in a good way: the ring lights, `m_connected` EffectList fires on the 0.5s `UpdatePortal` poll (:143496), and the player can step through on the next stride.
failureModes: First transit after a release to a distant partner silently fails: `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` (:143640) requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO, and calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO` and returns false when it does not. The player walks through, nothing happens, they walk through again and it works. Mitigate by `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destinationId)` (:77714) to every peer within 40m of the released gate at the moment of release.

Technique A mangles the label, and `TeleportWorld.Interact` opens the vanilla text box capped at 10 characters (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` :143482, cap applied at `TextInput.Show` :61519) pre-filled with the current tag — a player who opens and confirms the dialog on a long server-written tag may save back a truncated version, permanently corrupting your routing key.
A parked portal whose tag still matches another parked portal will pair them to each other under technique A if your token is not unique. Derive the token from the ZDO position, not a counter.

`Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) is a global routed RPC registered on every peer with NO sender check and NO ownership check. A malicious client can rewire any portal to any ZDOID at will, undoing a park in one packet. Harden with a prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) dropping that method hash from non-server senders — that hook has the authentic `ZRpc` socket in scope and nothing downstream does.
Parking a gate a player is currently standing inside does not eject them, and `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only (:143672) — they must step out and back in after a release.
openQuestions: Does `GuiInputField` clamp a programmatically assigned `.text` to `characterLimit`? `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.text` AFTER setting `characterLimit = 10` (:61519-61520). If it clamps, every long server-written tag is one player interaction away from truncation. Check: server-write a 24-char tag, open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client, re-read `s_tag`.

Confirm a parked portal's dark/unconnected state actually propagates to a client standing next to it without a zone reload, and stays dark for 60s (i.e. the owning client does not clobber the write). Check with a player parked at the gate while the server nulls the connection every 2s.
corrections: Technique B's postfix must veto `__result` as well as `skip`. FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's candidate filter (:100667-100673) excludes only skip, tag-mismatch, already-connected and staged portals, so when another same-tag unconnected portal is the `skip`, the parked portal is a legal candidate and pass 2 writes SetConnection on BOTH (:100614-100615). The mod's per-tick null on the parked side then leaves the partner holding a live one-way door into the parked location (partner's TargetFound is true, :143640-143655) until pass 1 clears it up to 5 s later (:100601-100604). Return null when either `skip` or `__result` is parked, or prefix-filter the candidate list.

'No way for a modified client to route around it' is false: Player.TeleportTo is entirely client-local (:15302-15327) and a modded client can teleport to any coordinate without a connection, or write a connection into its own ZDO copy if it owns the portal (ReleaseNearbyZDOS grants ownership to nearby peers every 2 s, :76901-76926). Parking is server-enforced against VANILLA clients only.

Technique A side effect: pass 1 also nulls the former partner (its target's tag now differs), and the partner is immediately re-paired with any other same-tag unconnected portal in the same call (:100607-100621) — parking one gate of a three-gate tag reshuffles the other two.

SetDirtyPortals: when the parked portal was connected, pass 1's SetConnection(None) already dirties the portal chunk (:73661-73664); the silent loss occurs only for tag writes on an already-unconnected portal. Still call it unconditionally.

The recommended force primitive (SetOwner -> SetConnection -> ForceSendZDO) claims server ownership; until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns it (≤2 s), vanilla RPC_SetTag on that portal is dropped at HandleRoutedRPC (:83645-83663). Guard with a compare-before-write so ownership is claimed only when the value actually changes.

Release via Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (public, :100589) is valid; note it also runs ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) early, which is harmless, but with an online owner the fresh pairing writes are still deferred over RPC_SetConnection and finalized by ForceSetConnection on the next call — so 'instant' re-pairing near a standing player needs the force primitive, as the option already says.

Player-experience timing: m_hadTarget is refreshed by UpdatePortal every 0.5 s (:143496-143507) and m_colorAlpha lerps at 1/s (:143511-143513), so the ring takes ~0.5-1.5 s to go dark after the park lands on the client.

Technique A is trivially undone by a vanilla rename (RPC_SetTag :143587-143602 -> RPC_ZDOData -> pass 2 re-pair within 5s); it only holds when re-asserted every tick, and even then the mangled tag is visible for a tick.

State the modified-client boundary: a client can write any Portal connection into its own ZDO copy (ZDO.Deserialize :74219-74233 accepts any target) and TargetFound (:143640-143654) checks only the local copy. The park is fully enforced for vanilla clients and enforced with a one-tick window for modified clients, provided the server forces a DataRevision bump on drift (revision tie is mutually rejected, ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118).

Gate the forced null on GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != None before SetOwner (vanilla ForceSetConnection :100628-100634); unconditional per-tick SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision and ping-pongs with ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926).
Key the parked set by portal position, not ZDOID (ZDOIDs are regenerated at world load; ZDOMan.Load :76532-76537 sets a new session ID).
Line ref: m_connected.Create is :143499 inside UpdatePortal (:143491-143507); Teleport gate 1 is :143519-143521.
evidence: Game.ConnectPortals :100589-100626 (pass1 :100594-100606, non-forced null :100603; pass2 :100607-100621); FindRandomUnconnectedPortal tag filter :100669; ForceSetConnection :100628-100634; SetConnection :100637-100650

verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The core mechanism is verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport returns at `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143517-143520) and TargetFound is false when the connection is None (:143640-143655); the other three gates read global keys or the local inventory (:143521-143535). Pass 1 and pass 2 run in the same ConnectPortals call (:100594-100621), so a naive null is re-paired within 5 s. Technique A (unique tag) works because pass 1 nulls on tag mismatch (:100601) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal finds no same-tag candidate (:100669). Tag-only writes do not set DirtyPortalObjects (ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision only, :73650-73654 vs SetConnection :73656-73665). The deferred-clear caveat is real (:100639-100650). The emission lerp and m_connected effect are real (:143496-143515). Technique B as written is incomplete, and the 'modified client' claim is false.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Gate 1 verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport :143517-143521 returns on !TargetFound(); TargetFound (:143640-143654) requires a non-None Portal connection in the client's own copy of the ZDO and a resolvable target (else RequestZDO). The other three gates (:143523, :143528, :143533) read global keys or local inventory - client-honoured. Pass 1 then pass 2 in the same ConnectPortals call (:100594-100621) - confirmed, so a bare null is re-paired within the same call. Technique A: pass 1 nulls on tag mismatch (:100601); FindRandomUnconnectedPortal filters on exact tag (:100669); ZDO.Set(int,string) -> IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840) marks the sector chunk, but portals are excluded from sector-chunk saves (:77572) and only saved through the portal chunk when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77636), which a tag-only write never sets - confirmed lost at save without SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705). Technique B correct: Harmony postfix on the private FindRandomUnconnectedPortal with __result=null prevents pass 2 from ever choosing a partner; vanilla clients never create Portal links themselves (RPC_SetTag only nulls, :143587-143602; Game.RPC_SetConnection only executes what the server sends), so a veto plus a periodic forced null holds against all vanilla clients. Timing caveat confirmed: pass 1 SetConnection(item, None) at :100603 is non-forced, so an online owner receives RPC_SetConnection (:100647). Game.instance.ConnectPortals() is public (:100589) so calling it on release is valid. Emission lerp at :143511-143515 and m_connected.Create in UpdatePortal (:143491-143507, effect at :143499) as described. Corrections: (1) Technique A is defeated by a vanilla E-press: the owning client's RPC_SetTag rewrites s_tag to the player's text, the update lands on the server via RPC_ZDOData, and pass 2 re-pairs on the next 5s tick - A holds only if re-asserted every tick and is visibly mangled. (2) Modified clients: the park is enforced against vanilla clients, but a modified client can write a Portal connection into its own copy (Deserialize path :74219-74233 accepts any target) and pass TargetFound immediately; the server's re-null lands only on its next write AND only if its DataRevision exceeds the client's (tie is mutually rejected, :77108-77118) - so parking is server-enforced with a one-tick window against modified clients and needs a forced revision bump on observed drift. (3) The forced write primitive (SetOwner each tick) fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926); gate it on GetConnectionZDOID != None as vanilla's ForceSetConnection does (:100628-100634). (4) Parked-set keying: ZDOIDs regenerate per world load, key the parked set by position. (5) 'Toast to anyone within 20m' via PlayerNotify.Toast (Wonderland PlayerNotify.cs:15-30) is a routed 'Message' RPC to the player's own ZDO - exists as cited.

catalog.name: The Customs House
catalog.oneLine: Instead of disconnecting a gate, route it to a server-fabricated dead-end anchor — the portal reads Connected and glows, but walking through drops you in a holding area two metres away or at a toll booth.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.Teleport` performs NO prefab validation on its destination — it resolves `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(GetConnectionZDOID(Portal))` and reads only `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` off it (:143539-143543), then computes `pos + (rot * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` and calls `player.TeleportTo(..., distantTeleport: true)`. Any ZDO with a position is therefore a legal destination.

Fabricate the anchor: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(anchorPos, anchorPrefabHash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetPrefab(anchorPrefabHash); z.Distant = false; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.SetRotation(rot);` — `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` (:76674) sets neither prefab nor persistence; those five lines mirror `ZNetView.Awake` (:82613-82620) and omitting them yields a ZDO that vanishes at world save.

Two anchor flavours:

**Portal-prefab anchor.** Pass a hash from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021). `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` (:77732) files it in `m_portalObjects`, so it is always resident, saved wholesale in the `ChunkPortal` file (:77621), and `ForceSendZDO`-able. But it now participates in vanilla pairing, so give it the sink's tag and manage it through the Routing Kernel.

**Non-portal anchor.** Any other persistent prefab hash. Vanilla's pairer never iterates it (it only walks `GetPortalList()`), so it is invisible to teardown — but `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 inspects the *partner*, so the anchor MUST carry the same `s_tag` string as the gate and a non-`None` Portal connection back, or the gate's link is torn down within 5s (:100601).

Sink geometry decides the experience. Set the anchor 2m in front of the gate facing back at it and a transit is a ~10s black screen that returns you where you started — an honest "you may not pass" with vanilla's own visual grammar. Set it inside a built customs hall with a payment chest and an exit gate and the closed route becomes a place. Note `Player.UpdateTeleport` (:15337-15352) pins the player at the frozen target for ≥8s under `distantTeleport: true` regardless of distance, so even a 2m hop costs the full loading screen.

Persistence: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) persists a connection only when BOTH endpoints resolve in `m_objectsByID`, and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850) relinks by hash at load and writes BOTH directions — so a gate↔anchor pair survives a restart, but a deliberately one-way gate→anchor link comes back two-way.
catalog.playerExperience: The gate looks perfectly healthy — ring lit, hover text `[Connected]`, tag reads `"CUSTOMS"`. You walk in, the screen goes black with the familiar teleport swirl, eight seconds pass, and you are standing in a small stone room with a chest labelled by a sign, a second portal on the far wall, and no way back except the gate you came from. Drop 50 coins in the chest, walk to the far gate, and it is lit; walk to it without paying and it is dark. The mod never told you "no" — it moved the refusal into level design. The cheap variant is more brutal and also fine: you walk in, black screen, and you are standing two metres from where you started facing the gate. Repeat it and you learn.
failureModes: A vanilla client near an anchor with a prefab hash it cannot instantiate logs `Missing prefab hash:` from `ZNetScene.CreateObject` (:82003) and does nothing further — harmless, but the SERVER's own `CreateObjectsSorted` would destroy such a ZDO (:82137). In practice the server never sees it because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465), but a mod that ever moves that reference position would silently delete every anchor.

`ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal-prefab ZDOs (:73752), so a portal-flavoured anchor stays filed under its creation sector in `m_portalObjects` forever. Never reposition an anchor — destroy it (claim ownership first: `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` is gated on `zdo.IsOwner()` at :76929) and create a new one.
The 8s `distantTeleport` floor makes a 2m bounce feel like a bug to a first-time player. Pair it with a `PlayerNotify.Toast` fired on arrival so the black screen resolves into an explanation.
`ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs` (:76043) makes the server destroy any ZDO re-created under a previously-destroyed ZDOID (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133). Always mint a fresh id via `CreateNewZDO`.
Anchors accumulate. Every parked gate that uses a sink adds a persistent ZDO; without a reaper keyed on "no portal points at me" they leak into the save forever.
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client cleanly handle a portal connected to a ZDO carrying a harmless real prefab (a marker piece) versus an unregistered hash? Check: build both, stand near each with a vanilla client, and watch the client log for CreateObject failures and whether `TargetFound` returns true.

What is the portal prefab's ZNetView `m_persistent` / `m_type` / `m_distant`? A portal-flavoured anchor should match exactly or the first owning client rewrites Type/Distant in `ZNetView.Awake` (:82632-82640). Check on a client: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood").GetComponent<ZNetView>()`.
Does a two-metre `distantTeleport` actually complete at the 8s mark, or does `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:82064) pass instantly and the 8s timer dominate? Measure the black screen length in game.
corrections: The cited server-side 'destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs' path (CreateObjectsSorted :82137-82148, CreateDistantObjects) only runs for ZDOs the server's CreateDestroyObjects visits — the Sector-0 bucket around the pinned reference position (:82268-82276, SectorToIndex clamp :115763-115768). An anchor at a real coordinate is never visited, so a bogus prefab hash is NOT cleaned up server-side; instead every vanilla client whose active area contains it calls CreateObject at 30 Hz and logs 'Missing prefab hash' each time (:81996-82006; the client branch has no destroy). The anchor MUST be a real prefab hash.

A real-prefab anchor is instantiated as a GameObject on nearby vanilla clients (it sits in m_objectsBySector, not the portal list) and, being Persistent, is handed to the nearest player by ReleaseNearbyZDOS every 2 s (:76901-76926). That client's components then run against it — WearNTear can be damaged/deconstructed, ItemDrop despawns, Piece can be hammer-removed — and the client's own ZNetScene.Destroy -> DestroyZDO (:82023-82036) or RPC_DestroyZDO (no sender check) erases it, tearing down the route within 5 s. Choose an inert, invisible, non-interactable prefab, and have the vault re-create it on I1 failure. IsAreaReady (:82062-82078) additionally requires the anchor instantiated on the arriving client before the black screen ends.

Per-player gating is not available: the exit gate's park/release state is a single server-owned field, so once any player pays, the exit gate is open for everyone in the hall until re-parked. The 'walk to it without paying and it is dark' line is only true while nobody else has paid recently.

Portal-prefab anchor variant: with a real portal prefab it is rendered as a visible portal on clients and its ownership migrates to nearby players like any portal; with SetPrefab omitted it is unsaveable (m_prefab unset) — the option's warning is correct, and additionally GetPrefab() of an unset ZDO is not the passed hash, so HandleDestroyedZDO's PortalPrefabHash check (:76980) would then fail to remove it from m_portalObjects (leak, see harness V5).

Dead-end geometry: the traveller lands at anchor + forward*1 + up (:143541-143543) and SetLookDir points them along the anchor's forward (:15340); with the anchor 2 m in front of the gate facing it, the player materialises 1 m from the gate facing it, and stepping forward re-triggers after the 2 s cooldown (:15313). Fine as designed, but describe it as 1 m, not 2 m.

One-way gate->anchor links do not survive even at runtime (pass 1 nulls a link whose partner's connection is None, :100601-100604) — the restart behaviour is moot; the anchor must always carry the reciprocal Portal connection and identical s_tag.
ZDO.SetSector portal exemption (:73752-73756) is cited but irrelevant to a non-portal anchor; it matters only for the portal-prefab flavour, where it is the V5 hazard if the anchor is ever moved.

ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects (:82137, :82166-82172) only destroy invalid-prefab ZDOs the SERVER tries to instantiate, which is the Sector 0 clamp bucket around the (1e6,0,1e6) pin; an anchor at a normal position is never touched by the server. The vanilla client near the sink DOES instantiate the anchor prefab (CreateObject :81995-82012): it is a visible, interactable object, and an unknown hash logs 'Missing prefab hash' every CreateDestroyObjects pass on the client.

Portal-prefab anchor participates in pass 2 (AddIfPortal :77732-77752 -> GetPortalList): it must carry a tag no gate uses and be vetoed in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal, or vanilla will pair it with a same-tag gate.

Customs-hall geometry: the traveller arrives at the anchor, not at the origin gate, so the hall must contain its own exit portal; 'no way back except the gate you came from' is only true for the 2m-sink variant.

Save persistence requires Persistent=true BEFORE the first Set/SetRotation/SetConnection (IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector :73832-73840 is gated on Persistent); the order given in the option is correct, keep it.
ZDOIDs regenerate at load; any gate->anchor registry must be re-derived from the saved mutual pair (ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77891) or from positions, not from stored ZDOIDs.
evidence: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision :73832-73840; ZDOMan.SetDirtySector :76694-76699; sector chunk save excludes portals :77572; portal chunk :77621-77636; AddIfPortal :77732-77752
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport reads only GetPosition/GetRotation off whatever ZDO the connection names (:143537-143546) and TargetFound only needs the client to hold that ZDO, requesting it otherwise (:143648-143652); RPC_RequestZDO force-sends any ZDO by id with no filter (:77684-77692, AddForceSendZdos :77263-77285), so a non-portal anchor is reachable. CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) files the ZDO by the passed hash in m_portalObjects but never calls SetPrefab or sets Persistent (:76674-76690); the five follow-up lines mirror ZNetView.Awake (:82613-82620). Pass 1 requires the partner's tag to match and its connection to be non-None (:100601), so the anchor must link back. RegenerateConnectionHashData needs both endpoints (:75468) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks both directions from hash data (:77850-77890), so a mutual gate<->anchor pair survives restart and a one-way link returns two-way. Player.UpdateTeleport holds the traveller ≥8 s under distantTeleport (:15329-15346) with a 2 s cooldown (:15313). The design works for vanilla clients; the caveats are about what the anchor prefab does on clients and a mis-cited server destroy path.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Destination read verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport :143540-143548 does ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection) and reads only GetPosition()/GetRotation(), computes pos + rot*forward*m_exitDistance + up, calls player.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport:true). No prefab check anywhere; TargetFound (:143640-143654) only needs the ZDO to resolve on the client, requesting it via RequestZDO -> RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO (:77684-77693) which works for any ZDO regardless of prefab. ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) (:76674-76691) creates via ZDOPool.Create (AddToSector :73496-73504), sets owner, calls AddIfPortal, and sets neither Persistent nor prefab - the five follow-up lines mirror ZNetView.Awake :82611-82618 exactly. Persistence chain: IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840) only if Persistent, so setting Persistent before SetPrefab/SetRotation/SetConnection is what dirties the chunk; regular chunks save non-portal persistent ZDOs (:77572), portal-prefab anchors go to the portal chunk via AddIfPortal (:77732-77752, :77621-77636). Pass-1 partner test confirmed (:100601): a non-portal anchor must carry the same s_tag and a non-None Portal connection back. Player.UpdateTeleport (:15329-15350) holds distantTeleport for >8s regardless of distance and Player.TeleportTo rejects when m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15302-15320). Save/load: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) writes hash data for both endpoints when both resolve (last-processed entry wins, hashes stay consistent for a mutual pair); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77850-77891) matches Portal-typed against Portal|Target-typed hash data with no prefab check and writes both directions - a mutual gate<->anchor pair survives, a one-way link comes back two-way, exactly as claimed. Owner-gated DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) as cited. Corrections: (1) ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects 'server destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs' (:82137, :82166-82172) applies only to ZDOs the server tries to instantiate, i.e. those in the Sector 0 clamp bucket around the (1e6,0,1e6) pin; an anchor at a normal position is never touched by that path, but a vanilla CLIENT near the anchor will instantiate the prefab (CreateObject :81995-82012), so the anchor prefab is a real, visible, interactable object at the sink - pick it deliberately, and an unknown hash spams 'Missing prefab hash' on the client at 30Hz because Created never becomes true. (2) Portal-prefab anchor: AddIfPortal puts it in GetPortalList, so pass 2 will pair it with any other portal sharing its tag unless the kernel vetoes; give it a tag no gate shares and veto it explicitly. (3) 'no way back except the gate you came from' is wrong for the customs-hall geometry - the arrival point is the anchor, not the origin gate; a hall needs its own exit portal or the player is trapped. (4) The 2m-sink 'returns you where you started' places the player 1m in front of the origin gate (anchor pos + 1m forward + up), i.e. the same spot a normal arrival puts them; verify in-game that this does not sit inside the TeleportWorldTrigger collider (vanilla's own 1m exit implies it does not).

catalog.name: Prepaid Toll Escrow
catalog.oneLine: A gate that is connected only while a bound chest holds at least N of an item — the flagship genuinely-enforced economy mechanic, because the check happens before anyone travels, not to anyone travelling.
catalog.howItWorks:
Bind one Container ZDO to each tolled portal: the nearest ZDO within `BindRadius` (4m default) found with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 4f, buf)` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25`) whose prefab classifies as a container via `ContainerRegistry.IsContainer` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:58`). Persist the binding keyed on the rounded portal POSITION, never on a ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552) so every id is renumbered at world load.

Read the balance: skip if `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_inUse) == 1` (a player has the UI open — `Container.UpdateUseVisual` :121996), then `ZdoInventoryIO.Load(zdo, w, h)` deserialises `ZDOVars.s_items` into a scratch `Inventory` and you count matching stacks. Cost warning: `Inventory.Load` (:68543) routes through `AddItem(int prefabHash, ...)` (:68726) which does `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(itemPrefab)` + `Destroy` for every stack, resolving through `ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab`. That is real GC churn. Gate every read on a cheap `zdo.DataRevision` change filter — exactly the trick `Container.Load` itself uses (:122305) — and poll at 1 Hz, only for portals in a state where the answer matters.

**The enforcement design is a standing-balance requirement, not a debit.** Each tick: `open = (balance >= price)`. Park on false, release on true. No item is moved, so there is no race with the owning client, no clawback problem, and no way to travel-then-refuse. A player who empties the chest closes their own gate within one tick.

Layer a meter on top if you want consumption: debit `perTransit` on each detected transit (see Reactive Transit Toll) or `perHour` on a timer, via `ZdoInventoryIO.Save` → `zdo.SetOwner(ZNet.GetUID()); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())`. The owning client's `Container.CheckForChanges` (`InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f)`, :121920) picks the change up within 1s. Critically, the debit does not need to be reliable: if it races and loses, the standing-balance check on the next tick still closes the gate once the balance actually drops. The system is self-correcting because enforcement and accounting are decoupled.

Status in the tag, refreshed on change only: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, label + "  " + balance + "/" + price + "c")` plus `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Requires the Routing Kernel so the tag is not the routing key.
catalog.playerExperience: Your long-haul mine gate reads `Teleport tag:"MINE 0/50c" [Unconnected]` and its ring is dark. You open the small chest bolted to the frame, drop 50 coins in, close it, and within about a second the hover text flips to `"MINE 50/50c" [Connected]` and the ring lights. You step through. Every trip the counter ticks down — `48/50`, `46/50` — and at `48/50` the gate is still lit because the threshold is 50 for *opening* and the meter only bills for use; when it falls below the reopen threshold the ring goes dark mid-session and you have to walk home the old-fashioned way or top it up from the other end. Two players who share a base share one meter, which makes the chest a social object: somebody has to keep it fed, and whoever raids it for coins turns the lights off for everyone.
failureModes: A player holding the chest's UI open sets `s_inUse = 1` and you must skip it entirely; a player who parks the UI open indefinitely freezes the meter. Treat `s_inUse` held for > 5 minutes as stale and read anyway (accepting a clobber risk), or just let the gate hold its last state.

Conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field: `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77107-77132) discards an incoming packet only when its DataRevision is not higher, otherwise it replaces the entire blob. A server debit can be reverted wholesale by the owning client's next `Container.Save`. Standing-balance enforcement survives this; a debit-only design does not.

Reading a 4x4 chest full of distinct stacks instantiates and destroys ~16 GameObjects per read. Ten tolled gates polled at 1 Hz with no revision filter is 160 Instantiate/Destroy pairs a second on the server.

`ObjectDB.instance` is frequently still null at the `ZNetScene.Awake` postfix commonly treated as world-ready (Wonderland `Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:83`). Retry the item-prefab resolution each tick until it succeeds or the first balance read silently returns zero and parks every gate on the server.
Griefing: an unwarded toll chest is a free coin dispenser AND an off switch. The chest must be inside a ward or the toll is theatre. See Ward Tariff Classes.
A chest destroyed (`WearNTear`) orphans the binding. Detect with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(boundId) == null` and fall back to re-discovery by position, then park with a `"NO METER"` tag.
openQuestions: What is the coin item's prefab name? No portal- or coin-related item string appears anywhere in the decompiles (item names are AssetBundle data). Read it at runtime: enumerate `ObjectDB.instance.m_items` and log names, or resolve `ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab("Coins")` and check for null.

Is `ObjectDB.instance` non-null and fully populated on a 1.0.7 dedicated server, and how long after `ZNetScene.Awake` does it take? Log `ObjectDB.instance?.m_items?.Count` every tick from world-ready until non-zero.

What `m_width`/`m_height` should the scratch Inventory use? `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` takes them as parameters; wrong dimensions can drop items at the grid edges on save-back. Read them off the real prefab: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponent<Container>()` server-side.
corrections: Cost warning is overstated. Instantiate/Destroy only happens if you load through the scratch `Inventory(string,Sprite,int,int)` ctor as Wonderland does. Counting needs no Inventory: Inventory.Save (:68510) writes int version (109), ushort count, then per-item `ItemData.Save`; `ItemDrop.ItemData.Load(ZPackage, Version.Item)` is public static (:69398) and returns (prefabHash, itemData) with m_stack, with zero ObjectDB/Instantiate. Alternatively `new Inventory(true)` (:67710) routes AddItem through AddTempItem (:68696), which only does an ObjectDB lookup. Writing back via ItemData.Save needs m_dropPrefab set (:69345/69382), so a hand-rolled writer must set it from ObjectDB.GetItemPrefab(hash) — a lookup, not an Instantiate.

Gate only the DEBIT write on s_inUse, not the read. s_items is updated live during use because the owner's OnContainerChanged -> Save() fires on every change (:122284-122301); and s_inUse can stick at 1 if the owning client disconnects with the chest open (nothing writes 0), which would stall a read-gated gate indefinitely.

Server ownership claim is transient: ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS runs every 2 s (:76872-76885); IsInPeerActiveArea for the server session tests InActiveArea(point, refPos=(1e6,0,1e6)) (:76890-76894) which is false for any real coordinate, so any server-owned ZDO near a player is handed to that peer within <=2 s. During that window Container.Interact's `InvokeRPC("RPC_RequestOpen")` is routed to the owner (ZNetView.InvokeRPC -> owner) and ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC drops it because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null on the server — the player's E press does nothing until ownership reverts.

Revision race is symmetric: both server and client drop incoming data with DataRevision <= local (:77099-77108 server; same code client-side), so a server debit and a concurrent client write from the same base revision diverge until the next client write. Consistent with the option's 'debit need not be reliable' stance, but say it.

Enforcement latency: park is visible to the client only after poll period (1 Hz) + ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2 0.05 s timer (:76837-76850) + RTT; a transit initiated in that ~1-1.5 s after the chest is emptied still succeeds.
ContainerRegistry.IsContainer is at Wonderland Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:45 (takes a GameObject prefab); :58 is ResolveTemplate.

Park must defeat Game.ConnectPortals (:100592) — with vanilla tag routing an unconnected portal whose tag matches its partner is re-paired within two 5 s passes. The Routing Kernel prerequisite is load-bearing, not optional; and every s_tag rewrite for the balance display changes the vanilla pairing key.

Replace the Instantiate/Destroy cost warning: count stacks with `ItemDrop.ItemData.Load(pkg, version)` (public static, :69398) after reading the version int and ushort count exactly as Inventory.Load does (:68543-68556); no ObjectDB, no Instantiate. Handle the pre-`Version.Item.Smaller` LoadOld layout (:68565) for chests untouched since the format change. Use Inventory.Load only for write-back.
Add explicit hysteresis: openThreshold (e.g. 50) and closeThreshold (e.g. 0) — the current text has open = balance >= price and a gate that stays lit at 48/50, which is contradictory.

Parked connections do not survive a world save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461 emits no hash for a None target); at startup vanilla re-pairs at ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76523 and every 5 s. The state must be re-derived from the chest each tick and the Routing Kernel must replace Game.ConnectPortals entirely (its tag-mismatch loop :100595-100599 would disconnect status-suffixed pairs).

Ownership claim is optional and hazardous: ZDO.Set(int,byte[]) has no owner check; while the server session owns the chest every client RPC to it (RPC_RequestOpen) is silently dropped (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :83650-83660, no server ZNetView). If you claim, immediately SetOwner back to the nearest peer's uid.

s_inUse skip is only needed before a WRITE (Container.Load returns false while m_inUse :122307, so the client would later overwrite the server's blob); balance READS while the UI is open are fine because Container.Save fires on every item move (:122282-122298).
Citation fix: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData revision compare is at :77109 (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision`); the client accepts any higher DataRevision regardless of ownership.
evidence: ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (no owner filter) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76003-76013; CreateSyncList server branch — :~76950
ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC (drops ZDO-targeted RPC with no instance) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs (HandleRoutedRPC body)
Client TeleportWorld.Teleport/TargetFound — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs (class TeleportWorld, Teleport uses GetConnectionZDOID only)
ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC drops ZDO-targeted RPC with no instance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83650-83660
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The core rule is route-shaped ("is this route open?") and the server owns the connection field: ZDO.SetConnection (server :73656) bumps DataRevision, Serialize always emits the Connections flag for a Portal-typed entry even with target None (:74113-74118), ZDOMan.SendZDOs/ShouldSend (:76003) pushes any higher-revision ZDO in the peer's sector regardless of owner, and the vanilla client's TeleportWorld.Teleport/TargetFound reads only its local ZDO connection (client TeleportWorld, HaveTarget/TargetFound). So park/release is honoured by an unmodified client. Container internals verified: Container.Save/Load :122294/:122303 (DataRevision filter, m_inUse skip), CheckForChanges InvokeRepeating 1 s (:121920), UpdateUseVisual writes s_inUse on owner (:121990-122000), OnContainerChanged -> Save on every inventory change (:122284-122289), s_items/s_inUse :78475/:78673, RPC_ZDOData drops incoming DataRevision <= local (:77076-77120). Several claims need fixing (below), but none breaks the mechanic.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Route-level gating holds: the client's TeleportWorld.Teleport() re-checks TargetFound() at trigger time (SERVER :143497-143500, identical client code), and a parked (Portal, None) connection DOES propagate — ZDO.Serialize sets the Connections flag whenever m_type != 0 (:74117), so (Portal, ZDOID.None) is wired to the client and its UpdatePortal (0.5 s) darkens the ring. Chest reads are legitimate: Container.Save writes s_items on every owner-side change (:122294), Load() gates on DataRevision (:122303), s_inUse is written by the owner in UpdateUseVisual (:121990). Server writes to a non-owned ZDO are accepted by the client via the DataRevision compare in RPC_ZDOData (:77109) and the concurrent-write race is symmetric (both sides drop the other's equal-revision packet) and self-corrects on the next client write — so the option's claim that the debit need not be reliable is true. Problems: (1) The cost warning is overstated — ItemDrop.ItemData.Load(pkg, version) is public static (:69398) and returns the prefab hash + stack without ObjectDB or Instantiate, and `new Inventory(true)` (:67710) takes the AddTempItem path (:68696) with no Instantiate; only a write-back needs the full path. (2) playerExperience contradicts howItWorks: with open = balance >= price the gate is dark at 48/50; an explicit hysteresis (openAt/closeAt) is required. (3) Parked state is not persisted: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461) writes no hash for a None target, so on reload the portal is unconnected and vanilla's Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs it at LoadChunks (:76523) and every 5 s (:100580) unless the Routing Kernel replaces it — state must be re-derived from the chest at startup. (4) Ownership-claim hazard: while the server holds ownership after ZdoInventoryIO.Save, any client RPC to that ZDO (RPC_RequestOpen) is dropped because HandleRoutedRPC needs a ZNetScene instance (:83650-83660); ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership within 2 s (:76901). ZDO.Set has no owner check, so the claim is optional; if used, hand ownership back to the nearest peer immediately. (5) Status-in-tag makes the two ends' tags differ, which vanilla's first ConnectPortals loop treats as a mismatch and disconnects (:100595-100599) — the Routing Kernel must fully replace ConnectPortals, not just add to it. (6) SetDirtyPortals is harmless but DirtyPortalObjects is only ever cleared after load (:76527), never after save.

catalog.name: The Token Turnstile
catalog.oneLine: An item stand beside the gate is the payment slot — a single readable int on its ZDO decides whether the route is open, with no inventory deserialisation anywhere.
catalog.howItWorks:
`ItemStand` stores what is mounted on it as `ZDOVars.s_item` (:78465), an int holding `m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode()`, written by `ItemStand.UpdateAttach` (:131845) on the owning client, with the full `ItemData` additionally serialised through `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO` (:70653) and orientation/variant/quality in sibling fields. Removing the item writes `Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0)` (:131795/:131824).

Server side this is a one-line read: `int mounted = standZdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item);`. No `ObjectDB`, no `Inventory`, no `Instantiate`, no `s_inUse` race, no byte blob. Compare against a per-route allowed set of prefab hashes and park/release accordingly. Poll cost is negligible — you can run this at 4 Hz across hundreds of gates.

Binding: find the nearest item-stand-prefab ZDO within 4m of the portal via `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear`, classified by `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())?.GetComponent<ItemStand>() != null` (the prefab table IS populated server-side, `ZNetScene.Awake` :81941). Persist by rounded position.

Consuming the token is also a single write: `standZdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); standZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0);`. Every client with the stand loaded re-reads the ZDO on `InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f)` (:131573), so the item visibly disappears within 4 seconds. That gives you a true turnstile: mount a token, the gate lights, walk through, the server detects the transit and eats the token, the gate goes dark behind you.

This composes into the whole progression economy: the token IS the key. A `TrophyEikthyr` on the stand opens the Black Forest route; a `DragonEgg` opens the mountain trunk; a crafted `PortalShard` item opens anything. Because the check is "what object is physically sitting here", it is legible without any UI, it is transferable, it is stealable if unwarded, and it is exactly as forgeable as the item itself.

Multi-slot variant: bind N stands to one gate and require a specific combination (three trophies) — still N integer reads.
catalog.playerExperience: Beside the mountain gate stands a stone item stand, empty, and the gate is dark. You place a Wolf Trophy on it. Within a second the gate lights and the tag flips from `"SUMMIT locked"` to `"SUMMIT open"`. You step through; four seconds later the trophy is gone from the stand and the gate behind you is dark again — one trophy, one trip. The stand is a physical, readable, stealable object: it says what the toll is without a single line of UI, and a rival who breaks your ward can lift your trophy off it. For a permanent key instead of a fare, the server simply never consumes it: the trophy sits there forever and the route stays lit, which turns a gate into a trophy room that happens to be load-bearing.
failureModes: Anyone who can reach the stand can take the token off it — `ItemStand.Interact` gates only on `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, which is meaningful only client-side. An unwarded turnstile is a theft target and an off switch.
A stand holding a stack-of-one only: `UpdateAttach` forces `itemData.m_stack = 1` (:131843), so there is no "50 coins" on a stand. Fares are one-token-per-trip or nothing.
The prefab hash on `s_item` is the DROP prefab name hash, not the item's display name — you must build your allowed set from `ObjectDB`/`ZNetScene` prefab names at runtime, not hard-code strings.

Server-clearing `s_item` leaves the `s_itemData` blob written by `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO` behind on the ZDO. `ItemStand.DropItem` reads `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item)` first (:131807) so a zeroed item is treated as absent, but the stale blob wastes save space; clear it too.
Visual lag: the item vanishes from the stand up to 4 seconds after the server consumes it (`UpdateVisual` interval, :131573). A fast player sees a ghost trophy they can no longer interact with.
openQuestions: Which item-stand prefabs exist (wall, floor, armour stand, guardian stone) and do they all carry an `ItemStand` on the ZNetView root rather than a child? `m_netViewOverride` at `ItemStand.Awake` (:131559) suggests some use an override root, which would put `s_item` on a different ZDO than the one you find by position.

Does clearing `s_item` server-side while a client has the stand loaded reliably remove the visual, or does the client's `m_visualItemDrop` persist until a scene reload? Check by mounting a trophy, clearing it from the server, and watching for 10s.
Is the guardian-stone `ItemStand` variant (`m_guardianPower` at :131597) safe to use as a turnstile, or does mounting a trophy there trigger the power grant path?
corrections: Token set is bounded by ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131981): the item prefab must have an `attach` or `attach_skin` child (GetAttachPrefab) AND be in m_supportedItems/m_supportedTypes and not in m_unsupportedItems. Trophies, weapons, shields, tools, armor pieces qualify; Coins, DragonEgg and generic materials are not stand-mountable — drop the DragonEgg example, or mark needs-ingame-check per item. A 'crafted PortalShard item' requires a client-side prefab and is impossible in a server-only mod — strike it.

The consume step is reactive-detection-only: it depends on the position-jump detector. A missed detection leaves the trophy in place and the route open indefinitely; the option should not present 'one trophy, one trip' as enforced.

SetOwner(server) before the clear opens a <=2 s window (ReleaseZDOS :76872-76885, IsInPeerActiveArea :76890) in which the client's `InvokeRPC("RPC_RequestOwn")` from UseItem (:~131875) is dropped by ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC; UseItem's `InvokeRepeating("UpdateAttach", 0f, 0.1f)` keeps polling IsOwner so it self-heals once ownership reverts — mention the delay.

The clear leaves ItemDrop.SaveToZDO's sibling keys (durability, quality, variant, crafter) stale on the stand ZDO; harmless because HaveAttachment only tests s_item, but DropItem's LoadFromExternalZDO would read them if s_item were ever repopulated externally.
Line cites: ItemStand.Awake begins :131558 (cited :131557 is blank); RPC_DestroyAttachment :131789; DropItem :131800.
Remove `PortalShard`: no custom item can exist on a vanilla client. Tokens must be vanilla prefabs present in the client ObjectDB.

Token eligibility is constrained client-side by ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131980): the item prefab needs an `attach` child (GetAttachPrefab) and must pass m_supportedTypes/m_supportedItems/m_unsupportedItems. Trophies qualify; DragonEgg and other Misc items need an in-game check per stand prefab (itemstand vs itemstandh).
'One trophy, one trip' has a ~2 s multi-rider window: the token is consumed only after transit detection; anyone entering the still-open portal before that rides free.

After `standZdo.SetOwner(session); standZdo.Set(s_item, 0)`, hand ownership straight back (SetOwner(nearestPeerUid)) — otherwise the next player's RPC_RequestOwn is silently dropped for up to 2 s (HandleRoutedRPC :83650-83660, ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901).

Optional instant visual: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ZRoutedRpc.Everybody, standZdo.m_uid, "SetVisualItem", 0, 0, 0, 0)` mirrors vanilla :131797 so the trophy vanishes immediately instead of on the 4 s poll.
Citation precision: UpdateAttach s_item write is at :131842-131846; UpdateVisual body :131857-131867.
evidence: Prefab dump: itemstand/itemstandh carry ItemStand; DragonEgg is an ItemDrop — libs-Tools/WubarrksEye_Dumps/2026-09-08_10-37-33-.../Prefabs_Dump.json
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: ItemStand.UpdateAttach (:131834-131853) writes `s_item = m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode()` on the owner plus ItemDrop.SaveToZDO; RPC_DestroyAttachment (:131789-131797) and DropItem (:131800-131825) clear it to 0; HaveAttachment is `GetInt(s_item) != 0`; Awake registers RPC_RequestOwn and `InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f)` (:131558-131575); UpdateVisual re-reads s_item/s_variant/s_quality and calls SetVisualItem, so a server clear is visually applied within 4 s. ZNetScene.Awake populates m_namedPrefabs from m_prefabs on the server (:81941-81952) and GetPrefab(int) (:82045) works. A single int read for the gate decision is accurate. The gate-open leg is a route-shaped rule and therefore server-enforced; the 'eat the token after transit' leg is reactive detection.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The single-int read is real: ItemStand.UpdateAttach writes s_item = prefab name hash (:131842-131846), RPC_DestroyAttachment/DropItem clear it to 0 (:131795, :131824), UpdateVisual re-reads s_item on InvokeRepeating(1f,4f) (:131573, :131857-131867). Server prefab table exists (ZNetScene.Awake :81941-81951; GetPrefab(int) :82045). Route-level park/release is enforced on the client via TargetFound (see Escrow). Refuted parts: (1) `PortalShard` — a server-only mod cannot add an item to a vanilla client's ObjectDB; ItemStand.UpdateAttach runs on the client and DropItem resolves via ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab (:131808); only vanilla prefabs can be tokens. (2) Not every item can be mounted: ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963) requires GetAttachPrefab(item.m_dropPrefab) != null (an `attach` child on the item prefab) and a supported type/explicit support list; trophies are fine, DragonEgg needs an in-game check. (3) One token can admit several people: detection lands ~2 s after transit while the gate stays open, so a second player entering inside that window rides free; the option's 'one trophy, one trip' is approximate. (4) While the server session owns the stand after clearing s_item, the client's RPC_RequestOwn (:131851) is dropped by ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC (:83650-83660) until ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership back (≤2 s). (5) Clearing only s_item leaves the ItemDrop.SaveToZDO sibling fields — same as vanilla RPC_DestroyAttachment, harmless. Enhancement: the server can also route `SetVisualItem(0,0,0,0)` to ZNetView.Everybody on the stand's ZDOID for instant visual removal, exactly as vanilla does at :131797.

catalog.name: Reactive Transit Toll
catalog.oneLine: Detect that a transit happened and bill afterwards — genuinely useful for metering and auditing, but structurally incapable of preventing anything, and the detector has a real false-positive tail.
catalog.howItWorks:
There is no server hook on the moment of transit. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` has exactly one call site — `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` (:143672) — gated on `Player.m_localPlayer == component`, and a dedicated server instantiates no portal GameObject because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick (:100465), so `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105) only ever builds objects in a sector 1e6 m from the world. The server can only infer transits from the character ZDO's position.

Detector, sharpened from Wonderland's `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` (`Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:148`): every 0.25s, for each `ConnectedCharacters.All()` entry, sample `zdo.GetPosition()`. Keep the previous sample. On a jump exceeding `MaxLegitimateSpeed * dt`, test whether the FROM sample lies within `R` (use 8m, not Wonderland's 40m) of some portal P and the TO sample within `R` of a portal Q, AND `P.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == Q.m_uid`. That link check is what collapses the false-positive rate: a coincidental near-two-portals jump that is not along a live edge is rejected. Portals come free from `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (:77643, the live dictionary, zero-alloc).

Latency: `Player.UpdateTeleport` does nothing until `m_teleportTimer > 2f`, then force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate (:15337-15343). `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` pushes that into the ZDO (:87527) and the client's ZDO change queue drains to the server on a 0.05s timer (`ZDOMan.Update` :76843). So the server learns ~2.0-2.3s after the player stepped in — which is inside the ≥8s black screen, but long after the decision was irrevocable.

Billing: on a confirmed transit, resolve the payer as `ConnectedCharacter.PlayerId` (`ZDOVars.s_playerID`, :78539) and debit the route's escrow chest, or increment a debt counter stored as a world global key `mod_debt_<playerID>` via `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(key, value)` (:115933) — keys at or above `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (ordinal 41, :101313) persist in the world .db (`ZoneSystem.Save` strips only ordinals < 41, :113749).

What to do about non-payment is the whole point: you cannot stop the trip that already happened. You CAN park the route, park every gate the debtor built, or escalate — see Debtor's Lien.
catalog.playerExperience: The player notices nothing at the moment of travel. Two seconds after they arrive, a toast appears in the top-left: `Bridge toll: 5 coins (chest 45/50)`. If the chest cannot cover it, the toast instead reads `Bridge toll unpaid — 5 owed` and the gate they just came through goes dark behind them, stranding them on the far side until somebody funds it. That is the honest shape of the mechanic: it never stops the first free ride, it makes the second one impossible. Over a week of play the ledger is visible in the tag (`"BRIDGE 45/50c"`) and in a Discord feed, so the social pressure does the enforcement the code cannot.
failureModes: Fundamentally unenforceable as prevention. By the time the server sees the position change the player has already moved, has already been invulnerable for 2s (`Character.RPC_Damage` is suppressed while `IsTeleporting()`, :2425/:2429/:2582), and cannot be refused.

False positives: an admin using `goto`/`recall` (`Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962 — registered on every client with no sender check), a dungeon entry (interiors sit at y+5000, `Location.Awake` :133512), a `Ladder.Interact` instant snap (:132064, no cooldown and no checks at all), a respawn, and `Player.EdgeOfWorldKill`'s inward shove (:11132). Suppress on `ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())` (:81811), on `Character.InInterior` boundary crossings (:4538), and on `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)`.

False negatives: two portals of the same pair within 16m of each other make FROM and TO indistinguishable; a player who logs out mid-teleport never produces a TO sample; a 0.25s poll can miss a transit followed immediately by another move.

A player can farm free trips by disconnecting before the debit lands — the character ZDO is non-persistent and destroyed by `ZDOMan.RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS` (:77406) on disconnect. Debt must be keyed on `s_playerID` and persisted outside the character ZDO.

`ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE dictionary; iterating it while your own code mutates portal ZDOs in the same pass will throw. Snapshot with `GetPortalList()` (:77648) if you write during the sweep.
prerequisites: Prepaid Toll Escrow (for a payment target)
openQuestions: Measured false-positive rate at R=8m with the link-match requirement, over a week on a populated server. Instrument it: log every candidate jump with its FROM/TO portals and whether the link matched, and hand-classify.
Exact end-to-end latency from trigger-enter to the server seeing the moved ZDO position. Poll a test character at 20 Hz and timestamp the first sample past 100m.

Does `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` actually run during the teleport window, or is the position push suppressed until the teleport completes? `Player.FixedUpdate` gates on `IsOwner` and `!IsDead()` (:10204/:10213); confirm the ZDO position really moves at t≈2s and not at t≈8s.
corrections: `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(key, value)` at :115933 is `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key, float value)` — an enum overload. For `mod_debt_<playerID> <amount>` use `SetGlobalKey(string name)` (:115943), which routes RPC "SetGlobalKey" to the server peer (self-delivered on the server via InvokeRoutedRPC targetPeerID == m_id) -> RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022) -> GlobalKeyAdd. GlobalKeyAdd lower-cases the key and every add/remove calls SendGlobalKeys(0L) — each debt key is broadcast to and stored on every connected client (visible via the client `listkeys` console). Wonderland calls GlobalKeyAdd directly via reflection/publicizer (WorldRatesEngine.cs:55,:94) rather than SetGlobalKey.
ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync begins at :87472, not :87527 (that line is a closing brace).
The 0.05 s per-peer send timer lives in ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2 (:76837-76850), not `ZDOMan.Update`.

peer.m_refPos is client-reported (RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData reads it straight from the packet) — fine for gating idle burn, but not a verified position; the character ZDO position is the better source and is also client-written.
Toast/tag side effects are fine, but note the tag rewrite for `"BRIDGE 45/50c"` changes the vanilla pairing key (Routing Kernel dependency, same as Escrow).

`ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(key, value)` with a string key does not exist. Use `SetGlobalKey("mod_debt_<id> <amount>")` (:115944, routed through RPC_SetGlobalKey :116022) or call the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(string, bool)` (:113483) + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` (:113466) as Wonderland's WorldRatesEngine does. Keys are lowercased and the full list is broadcast to all clients on every change (visible via `listkeys`).

Update semantics: RPC_SetGlobalKey only skips when the exact 'key value' string is already present (:116024); GlobalKeyAdd removes the previous value for the same key (:113488-113496), so rewriting a debt amount works.

Detector timing: the client's ZDO position jumps at t≈2 s of the ≥8 s distant-teleport black screen; a route parked in reaction cannot affect the in-flight traveller (UpdateTeleport never re-reads the portal) — correct as stated, but it also means anyone who enters within the ~2 s before detection travels for free.

Debt keyed on s_playerID is client-asserted (PlayerProfile.m_playerID written by Player.SetPlayerID :10129); for a vanilla client it is stable per character but it is not the socket-verified identity — use peer.m_socket.GetHostName() for anything ban-grade.
evidence: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey overloads — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115933, :115938, :115943; RPC_SetGlobalKey — :116022; GlobalKeyAdd — :113483-113512; GetKeyValue — :113560; Save strip — :113750-113754
ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-delivery (targetPeerID == m_id) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs (InvokeRoutedRPC(long, ZDOID, string, params) body)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Central constraint confirmed: TeleportWorld.Teleport's sole call site is TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter gated on `Player.m_localPlayer != component` (server :143664-143681, identical on client), and Game.FixedUpdate pins the server reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every physics tick (:100458-100466), so no portal GameObject exists server-side. Player.UpdateTeleport assigns transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos only after m_teleportTimer > 2f (:15329-15343). ZDOMan.GetPortals (:77643) returns the live dictionary. Peer refPos refresh via RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData (:80395-80401) is correct. Global-key persistence path verified: GlobalKeyAdd (:113483) stores any non-enum key as NonServerOption and ZoneSystem.Save strips only gk < NonServerOption (:113750-113754). The enforcement label 'reactive-detection-only' is honest and correct.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Every structural claim checks out. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter is the only caller of Teleport and is gated on Player.m_localPlayer (:143672-143680); the server's Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465); Player.UpdateTeleport assigns transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos every FixedUpdate once m_teleportTimer > 2 s (:15337-15343) and never re-validates the portal — so parking the route behind a mid-flight traveller cannot strand them in limbo, and a distant teleport never reverts to the origin (:15353-15360).
