[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every load-bearing claim checks out against the decompile. (1) Game.FixedUpdate in the server assembly unconditionally pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100458-100466); the string '1000000f' appears in the client assembly only in unrelated UI/physics fields (client :33266, :54275, :54318), so the pin is server-only. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter is the sole caller of TeleportWorld.Teleport and is gated on Player.m_localPlayer (:143664-143682, client :144412-144420). (2) ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC dispatches ZDO-targeted RPCs only via ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance (:83646-83663); InvokeRoutedRPC skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id (:83577-83595), so an owning client's RPC_SetTag never hits the wire. (3) Player-class ZDO writes (scan of :9414-16500) are vitals/identity/pose/emote only (s_adrenaline, s_baseValue, s_cheated, s_crowned, s_dead, s_dodgeinv, s_eitr, s_emote*, s_inBed, s_playerID, s_playerName, s_pvp, s_stamina, s_stealth, s_wakeup, s_weaponLoaded); s_items has exactly one live writer, Container.Save (:122299). ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles only invokes 'SavePlayerProfile' on each peer (:79653-79668). (4) Player.TeleportTo enforces a 2 s cooldown and returns false silently (:15302-15315). PlayerStatType indices verified: PortalsUsed=15, PortalDungeonIn=83, PortalDungeonOut=84 (:106499+). Dungeon Teleport has a compiled m_targetPoint reference and no ZNetView (:143316-143322). One nuance worth recording, which does not weaken the ruling: a reactive UNDO primitive exists — Character.RPC_TeleportTo is owner-gated with no sender check (client :4128-4134), so the server can bounce a player back after detecting a transit, but only after the 2 s teleport cooldown has elapsed and only as a visible after-the-fact correction, never a refusal.

catalog.name: NoPortals Global Key
catalog.oneLine: Flip vanilla's own world-modifier key so every unmodified client refuses portal transit with the stock $msg_blocked message.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("noportals")` is a one-line call whose entire body is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946). The 1-arg InvokeRoutedRPC targets `GetServerPeerID()`, which on the server is its own id, so `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` dispatches synchronously through `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83588) and the key is readable before the call returns. `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022-116029) checks `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)`, calls `GlobalKeyAdd`, then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`. `SendGlobalKeys` (:113466-113471) invokes the `GlobalKeys` routed RPC at peer 0 with `new List<string>(m_globalKeys)`; each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` (:113473-113481) does `ClearGlobalKeys()` then re-adds every entry. Propagation is one routed-RPC hop inside the same call stack — `RouteRPC` (:83597-83629) calls `peer.m_rpc.Invoke` immediately, with no accumulation buffer. There is no polling interval and no relog requirement. Late joiners are covered by `ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer` (:113607-113616), hooked onto `ZRoutedRpc.m_onNewPeer` in `ZoneSystem.Start` (:113444), which calls `SendGlobalKeys(peerID)` for every peer that becomes ready. On the client, `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads it live at :143523 and returns after `player.Message(Center, "$msg_blocked")`. CRITICAL CALLING DETAIL: use the lowercase string literal `"noportals"`, not `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)`. The enum overload stringifies PascalCase (:115938-115941) and the store only ever holds lowercase (normalised in `GlobalKeyAdd` :113487), so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` dedupe guard at :116024 never trips and every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the entire key list to every peer. In a polling loop that is a broadcast storm. Pre-check with `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` (:115948, a `m_globalKeysEnums.Contains` lookup) and only write on an actual transition.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing visible changes until the player walks into a portal. The portal still glows, `GetHoverText` still reads `$piece_portal_connected` (:143461) because `HaveTarget()` only inspects the connection, and `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s poll still lights `m_target_found` (:143507) — none of that reads the key. The player steps through the ring, nothing happens, and a centre-screen `$msg_blocked` appears. Every portal on the server behaves identically and instantly, including for players who were already standing next to one. Dungeon and crypt doors keep working normally, ore and all. When the key is cleared the very next step through the ring teleports — no relog, no zone reload.
failureModes: 100% client-honoured. A modified client that deletes the `if` at :143523 teleports normally and the server observes nothing — not the attempt, not the transit.

`RPC_SetGlobalKey` has zero sender validation (:116022-116029). Any connected vanilla client can clear `noportals` at will by invoking the routed RPC. Unusable as a lockdown without the hardening option.

Setting the key at runtime permanently edits the world: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors any key with ordinal < 41 into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511), written to the .fwl at the next autosave. Uninstalling the mod leaves `noportals` baked into the world forever.
Zero player-facing warning before the block. The portal looks and sounds fully functional right up to the moment of refusal, which reads as a bug to players.
Does not touch dungeon/crypt doors at all — `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads NoPortals. Advertising this as 'disable all teleportation' is factually wrong.

`GlobalKeyAdd` unconditionally dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` at :113506-113508 and its `UpdateWorldRates` tail reaches `Minimap.instance` via `Game.UpdateNoMap`. Calling it before those objects exist turns a key write into an NRE that aborts before `SendGlobalKeys`.
openQuestions: Is `Minimap.instance` genuinely non-null on a 1.0.7 headless dedicated server? `Game.UpdateNoMap` (:101199-101204) dereferences it unguarded on every key write. Strong indirect evidence yes (Wonderland's WorldRatesEngine calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server), but not provable from the decompile. IN-GAME CHECK: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm no NullReferenceException in the log and that connected clients immediately get `$msg_blocked`.

Which `WorldModifierOption` values the vanilla Portals slider maps to which key strings — the mapping lives in `KeySlider.m_settings[].m_keys` Inspector data. IN-GAME CHECK: `setworldmodifier Portals <each option>` then `listkeys` and read the 'Server Option Keys' block.
corrections: The TeleportWorld citations point at the server decompile for code that only ever executes on the client; the executing copy is assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144257-144267 (identical body).

State explicitly that the key is revocable by any unmodified client: every vanilla player can type `noportals` (runs locally, OnlyAdmin never checked) and the server's RPC_RemoveGlobalKey/RPC_SetGlobalKey accept it with no sender check (:116022-116037). Global-Key RPC Hardening is a hard dependency for any lockdown that must hold.

State that the plain `SetGlobalKey` write persists: GlobalKeyAdd's default canSaveToServerOptionKeys=true adds 'noportals' to ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113488, :113511), which SaveWorldFWLData writes to the .fwl (:112581-112585). Use Session-Only Key Writes if the lockdown is temporary.
'No accumulation buffer' is true for ZRoutedRpc; the packet still sits in the ZRpc/socket send queue until the socket flushes — same frame, not same call stack, on the wire side.

Pre-check must use `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` (:115948, m_globalKeysEnums) exactly as written; `m_globalKeys.Contains("noportals")` would also work because the stored form is the lowercase trimmed string.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Every cited member exists at the cited line with the claimed behaviour. `SetGlobalKey(string)` is one `InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946); the 1-arg overload targets `GetServerPeerID()` which returns `m_id` when `m_server` (:83565-83576); `InvokeRoutedRPC` dispatches to `HandleRoutedRPC` synchronously when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595). `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022-116029) guards with `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` then `GlobalKeyAdd` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`; `SendGlobalKeys` (:113466-113471) routes `GlobalKeys` to 0 and `RouteRPC` (:83597-83629) calls `peer.m_rpc.Invoke` immediately for every ready peer. `OnNewPeer` (:113607-113616) is hooked at :113444 and fired from `ZRoutedRpc.AddPeer` (:83527-83535). The dedupe/broadcast-storm warning is correct: `m_globalKeys` is a case-sensitive `HashSet<string>` (:113305), `GlobalKeyAdd` stores `GetKeyValue(keyStr.ToLower())` output (:113483-113500, lowercase via :113560-113579), the enum overload passes `key.ToString()` = 'NoPortals' (:115938-115941), so `Contains('NoPortals')` is always false. Notably `RemoveGlobalKey(GlobalKeys)` DOES lowercase (:115984-115987) — the asymmetry is real. `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` is ordinal 32, `NonServerOption` 41 (enum at :101272ff). Client-side gate confirmed in the client decompile: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` checks `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144263 (server copy :143523-143527). `UpdatePortal`/`GetHoverText`/`HaveTarget` do not read the key (:143495-143508, :143461, :143631-143638). Client-honoured is the right label: the check runs in client code only.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited line verified. `SetGlobalKey(string)` is one routed RPC (:115943-115946); `InvokeRoutedRPC(methodName, params)` targets `GetServerPeerID()` which is `m_id` on the server (:83560-83572), and `InvokeRoutedRPC` dispatches synchronously via `HandleRoutedRPC` when target == m_id (:83577-83595). `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022-116029) -> `GlobalKeyAdd` (:113483-113513, lowercases via GetKeyValue :113560-113579) -> `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` (:113466-113471) -> every client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and re-adds (:113473-113481). `OnNewPeer` (:113607-113615) covers late joiners, hooked in Start (:113444). `RouteRPC` (:83597-83629) calls `peer.m_rpc.Invoke` per peer immediately (delivery is then subject to the socket send queue, not a routed-RPC buffer). Client `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (client :144268-144272) returns `$msg_blocked` after `TargetFound()`; `UpdatePortal` (client :144222-144240), `HaveTarget`, `Update` colour lerp and `GetHoverText` never read the key, so glow/hover are unchanged — playerExperience is accurate. Dungeon `Teleport` reads only NoBossPortals (:143355), not NoPortals. The PascalCase dedupe bug is real: enum overload sends "NoPortals" (:115938-115941), store holds lowercase (:113511/:113498), so `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` at :116024 never trips and every call rebroadcasts. Server-side GlobalKeyAdd touches `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` (:113503-113505) — safe, the dedicated server constructs a PlayerProfile at :100047. The systemic hole the option under-states: ANY vanilla client can lift (or set) this key at will — the stock `noportals` command runs client-side for every player (OnlyAdmin is never evaluated, see the ops-admin verdict) and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116031-116037) has no sender check. So 'client-honoured' is right, but it is also 'any-player-revocable' until Global-Key RPC Hardening is in place. Also, because the default `canSaveToServerOptionKeys=true` path adds the key to `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511), the plain write is written into the .fwl on next save (World.SaveWorldFWLData :112581-112585) — a permanent modifier, which is what the Session-Only option exists to avoid; the option should say so rather than leaving persistence implicit.

catalog.name: Global-Key RPC Hardening
catalog.oneLine: Prefix RPC_SetGlobalKey and RPC_RemoveGlobalKey to drop any packet that did not originate from the server itself, closing the hole that lets any client lift a key lockdown.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.Start` registers `SetGlobalKey` and `RemoveGlobalKey` on `ZRoutedRpc.instance` only when `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (:113445-113449), so both handlers genuinely execute on the dedicated server and are real Harmony targets (unlike ZDO-targeted handlers). Neither body inspects `sender` (:116022-116037). The mod adds `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(ZoneSystem), "RPC_SetGlobalKey")] static bool Prefix(long sender, string name)` and the matching one for `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`, returning false unless `sender == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` (:77362, the server's own id, which is what `ZRoutedRpc`'s self-dispatch path stamps into `m_senderPeerID` at :83580) OR the mod is itself the caller (set a `[ThreadStatic] bool s_selfWrite` flag around its own `SetGlobalKey` calls, which is more robust than an id compare because the id path depends on `GetServerPeerID`). Scope the veto to a configured allowlist of key NAMES — resolve with the public static `ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue(name, out value, out gk)` (:113560-113579) and veto only when `gk` is one of NoPortals/NoBossPortals/TeleportAll/DungeonBuild, so legitimate client-originated key traffic (boss `defeated_*` keys written by `Character.OnDeath` :3153-3156, `activeBosses` written by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27258-27259) still passes. A vetoed packet should be routed to `AuditLog.Flag("GlobalKeyTamper", playerName, key)`. Resolve the offending peer for the log by matching `sender` against `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` `m_uid` — but note `m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495) and is a client self-report, so for a *forensic* identity you must patch `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632) instead, where the authentic socket is in scope, and map `rpc` to a peer via `GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`. There the true identity is `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the same string vanilla's own `ZNet.RPC_Kick` uses against `m_adminList` (:81670).
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to honest players. A cheating client that fires `RemoveGlobalKey noportals` sees absolutely nothing happen — no error, no key change, no broadcast — because the veto drops the packet before `GlobalKeyRemove` runs, and the client's own key set is a read-only mirror that the next `SendGlobalKeys` overwrites anyway. The server log gets one `[SECURITY:GlobalKeyTamper]` line naming the SteamID64 that tried it.
failureModes: Does nothing for the far larger hole: `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) applies any incoming ZDO wholesale when the incoming DataRevision exceeds the local one, with no ownership, prefab or field validation. Global keys are not ZDO data so they are safe here, but a client can still rewrite portal tags and connections directly.

Vetoing too broadly breaks vanilla progression: `Character.OnDeath` writes `m_defeatSetGlobalKey` from the client that killed the boss (:3153-3156), and `BaseAI.SetAlerted` writes `activeBosses` from whichever client owns the boss (:27258-27259). An allowlist keyed on `GetKeyValue`'s parsed `GlobalKeys` enum is mandatory.

`m_senderPeerID` is spoofable, so an id-based allow test can be forged by a client claiming the server's own id. The `[ThreadStatic]` self-write flag plus a socket-derived check in `RPC_RoutedRPC` is the only sound version.

A prefix on `RPC_SetGlobalKey` that returns false also suppresses `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`, so if the mod ever vetoes its own write by accident the key silently never propagates and the lockdown appears to work server-side while every client is unlocked. Always read back with `GetGlobalKey` after writing.
openQuestions: Does any vanilla client path legitimately invoke `SetGlobalKey` for a world-modifier-ordinal key? `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys` → `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` (:59630-59680) runs in the main menu on the host, which on a dedicated server is the server itself — but a connected admin client using the modifier GUI would be a client-origin write. IN-GAME CHECK: with the veto active, have an admin client attempt `setworldmodifier Portals <opt>` and confirm whether it is dropped, then decide whether to allowlist admin sockets.
corrections: Remove `sender == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` as an accept condition: the server uid is public to clients (`ZNet.SendPeerInfo` writes `GetUID()` :79739) and `m_senderPeerID` is client-controlled (:83487-83495). Use provenance instead: the server's own key writes never traverse `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632-83643); a flag set for the duration of that method (prefix + finalizer) identifies every wire-originated call, including one with a forged sender id.
`ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` and `HandleRoutedRPC` are `private`; patch by string name or publicize (Wonderland already patches `HandleRoutedRPC` by name at WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:315).
Forensic identity: `ZNet.GetPeers()` is public (:81630) and `ZNetPeer.m_rpc` matches the `ZRpc` argument; `ZNet.IsAdmin(hostName)` (:81811-81814) is the same check `RPC_Kick` uses (:81668-81676).

Replace the allow rule. Do not allow on `sender == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` — m_senderPeerID is deserialized from the wire (:83487-83495) and forgeable. Do not rely on a self-write flag alone — it blocks vanilla server-local writers (setkey/removekey/resetkeys via RPC_RemoteCommand :81879-81895; startup -setkey/-modifier via SetStartingGlobalKeys :80853). Instead prefix ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632) to (i) drop packets whose m_senderPeerID != ZNet.GetPeer(rpc).m_uid (:80504) and (ii) flag 'wire-originated' around HandleRoutedRPC; veto allow-listed keys only when wire-originated.

Document the operational consequence: vanilla `noportals` typed in a client console becomes a vetoed write for admins too. The authenticated admin route is `setkey`/`removekey noportals` forwarded via RPC_RemoteCommand (admin list checked at :81881); verify in-game that ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat('noportals') returns false (:43515) or setkey will refuse it.

Route AuditLog attribution through the RPC_RoutedRPC prefix where the ZRpc is in scope (peer.m_socket.GetHostName(), same identity ZNet.RPC_Kick uses at :81670) — as the option's forensic paragraph already says; make that the primary mechanism rather than an addendum.
evidence: ZDOMan.GetSessionID / ZNet sets routed UID from it — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77362-77365, :79204
ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.Deserialize — :83487-83495; InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch stamping m_senderPeerID=m_id — :83577-83595; RPC_RoutedRPC — :83632-83643; HandleRoutedRPC — :83646-83665
Terminal setkey/removekey/resetkeys — :43510-43549; ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat — :59860-59870; ServerOptionsGUI instantiated on dedicated server — :97485-97488, :100042-100045
Character.OnDeath defeat key — :3153-3156; BaseAI.SetAlerted activeBosses — :27256-27261; GetKeyValue — :113560-113579
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds: `SetGlobalKey`/`RemoveGlobalKey` handlers are registered only under `IsServer()` (:113445-113449), neither reads `sender` (:116022-116037), and they are ordinary instance methods reachable by Harmony. `ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue` is `public static` (:113560). Boss keys are written client-side via `Character.OnDeath` (:3153-3156) and `BaseAI.SetAlerted` (:27256-27259), so an allowlist scope is necessary. `RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` reads `m_senderPeerID` off the wire (:83487-83495) and `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage)` (:83632-83643) has the authentic socket. Ownership of the rule is server-side (key state), so server-enforced is right. The defect: the proposed allow condition `sender == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` is trivially spoofable. The server's uid is handed to every client in `SendPeerInfo` (`pkg.Write(GetUID())` :79739), and a client stamps any `m_senderPeerID` it likes. The option itself notes the field is a self-report but still offers the id compare as a valid branch. The only sound discriminator is provenance: the server's own `SetGlobalKey` calls go `InvokeRoutedRPC` -> `HandleRoutedRPC` directly (:83577-83595) and never pass through `RPC_RoutedRPC`, whereas every client packet does (:83632-83643). So veto whenever the handler is executing inside `RPC_RoutedRPC` (set a flag in a prefix/finalizer on it) — equivalently the ThreadStatic self-write flag — and drop the id compare entirely.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Registration is server-only (:113445-113449) so both handlers are real server-executed Harmony targets; neither inspects `sender` (:116022-116037). `RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` reads `m_senderPeerID` straight off the wire (:83487-83495) and `RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632-83643) forwards it to `HandleRoutedRPC` unverified, so a sender-id compare is forgeable — the option's own forensic paragraph already concedes this. The proposed allow rule ('sender == GetSessionID() OR s_selfWrite flag') is therefore unsound in both directions: (a) a client stamping m_senderPeerID = server id passes the id half; (b) a flag-only rule breaks vanilla's legitimate server-local writers that the mod does not wrap — `setkey`/`removekey`/`resetkeys` executed on the server via `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` from an admin-list-authenticated client (:81879-81895 -> Terminal :43510-43549 -> SetGlobalKey self-dispatch), and startup `-setkey`/`-modifier`/`-preset` args (FejdStartup :97498-97536, which write m_startingGlobalKeys and flow through SetStartingGlobalKeys at :80853/:115904). Correct design: mark packets that arrive over the wire — prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage)` and either reject any packet whose deserialized m_senderPeerID != `ZNet.GetPeer(rpc).m_uid` (private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` :80504) or set a static 'in-wire-dispatch' flag around `HandleRoutedRPC`; then veto SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey for the allow-listed enum values only when the write came from the wire. Everything self-dispatched (mod, setkey via RPC_RemoteCommand, startup args) then passes without an id compare, and the id is trustworthy for logging. Allow-list by `GetKeyValue`'s `gk` is sound: `Character.OnDeath` (:3153-3156) and `BaseAI.SetAlerted` (:27256-27261) run on the creature's owning client and arrive over the wire as defeated_*/activeBosses — they must pass. Consequence the option omits: hardening kills the vanilla admin workflow of typing `noportals` in a client console (that IS a wire-originated client write). The admin fallback is `setkey noportals` / `removekey noportals` which the client forwards through RPC_RemoteCommand (admin-gated by socket host name) and the server executes locally — but note `setkey` first runs `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat` (:43515, :59860-59870) against the modifier GUI's key list (ServerOptionsGUI is instantiated on the dedicated server, :97485-97488 / :100042-100045); whether 'noportals' is in that list is prefab data (KeyToggle.m_enabledKey :53265) not visible in the decompile — verify in-game. Enforcement 'server-enforced' is honest: this is a routing rule on data the server owns. [ThreadStatic] is unnecessary (Unity main thread) but harmless.

catalog.name: Session-Only Key Writes
catalog.oneLine: Write NoPortals/TeleportAll through the publicized GlobalKeyAdd with canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false so a temporary lockdown never gets baked into the world's .fwl modifier list.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` routes through the RPC and always ends in `GlobalKeyAdd(name)` with the default `canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true`, whose only effect is the `flag` computed at :113488 (`canSaveToServerOptionKeys && ZNet.World != null && gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption`) which drives `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys.Add(keyStr.ToLower())` at :113511. Bypassing that is a direct call to the private `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` followed by an explicit `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` — both require `<Publicize>true</Publicize>` on assembly_valheim, which the sibling Wonderland csproj already sets. The full session-only write is: `ZoneSystem.instance.GlobalKeyAdd("noportals", false); ZoneSystem.instance.SendGlobalKeys(0L);` and the matching clear is `ZoneSystem.instance.GlobalKeyRemove("noportals", false); ZoneSystem.instance.SendGlobalKeys(0L);` (:113516-113539). Because the key is absent from `m_startingGlobalKeys` it is also absent from the .fwl (`World.SaveWorldFWLData` :112581-112585) and absent from the .db (`ZoneSystem.Save` strips ordinals < 41 at :113751-113755), so a restart returns the world to whatever `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (:115904-115931) finds in the .fwl — i.e. the pre-mod state. The mod's own intent is then persisted in its own config/state file and re-applied after boot. Re-application must be a POSTFIX on `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys`, never a prefix, because a `preset` key in the world causes `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.SetPreset(ZNet.World, text)` to reapply an entire slider key set at :115920-115926 and would clobber a prefix-applied key. Note the asymmetry in `GlobalKeyAdd`: the removal of a prior value at :113492-113496 uses the trimmed `keyValue + " " + value2` form while the add at :113511 uses the raw `keyStr.ToLower()`, so always pass the same canonical lowercase literal for both add and remove or the .fwl entry can be orphaned.
catalog.playerExperience: Identical in-game to the plain key write — `$msg_blocked` on transit while engaged. The difference is invisible to players and entirely visible to the operator: after a restart the world is clean, the server-browser modifier badge does not permanently claim 'Portals: off', and removing the mod does not leave a locked world behind.
failureModes: Requires the assembly publicizer for `GlobalKeyAdd`, `GlobalKeyRemove` and `SendGlobalKeys` (all private). A signature change in a future patch breaks it silently unless wrapped in Wonderland's `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` / a reflection probe.

A session-only key vanishes on an unplanned restart. If the intent was a multi-day lockdown the mod must re-apply from its own state file at boot, and there is a window between `ZNet.WorldSetup` → `SetStartingGlobalKeys` and the mod's postfix where the key is absent — harmless because no peer is connected yet, but it must be verified the postfix runs before `ZNet.OpenServer`.

`GlobalKeyAdd` with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false` still fires `Achievements.MarkAchievementDifficultyDirty()` (:113505) and `UpdateWorldRates()` (:113513) — the achievement-integrity side effects are unchanged.
Does not solve tamper: a client can still `SetGlobalKey`/`RemoveGlobalKey` freely. Needs the hardening option.
openQuestions: Does the mod's `SetStartingGlobalKeys` postfix reliably run before `ZNet.OpenServer` snapshots `m_startingGlobalKeys` for the server-browser badge (:79457 region)? Ordering matters only for badge accuracy, not gameplay. IN-GAME CHECK: boot with a session-only key applied and inspect the public listing's modifier badge from a second machine.
corrections: The add/remove 'asymmetry' warning is moot for this option: with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false` neither path touches `m_startingGlobalKeys`, and for a valueless key like `noportals` the two forms (`keyValue + " " + value` trimmed vs `keyStr.ToLower()`) are byte-identical anyway. It only matters for keys carrying values with irregular whitespace.

`SetStartingGlobalKeys(send:true)` broadcasts before any postfix runs; the postfix must call `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` itself after re-adding (harmless at boot since `m_peers` is empty and `OnNewPeer` :113607-113616 resends to each joiner).

Prefix-vs-postfix rationale: the decisive reason is the unconditional GlobalKeyRemove loop over ordinals 0..40 at the start of SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115906-115910), not the preset re-application. Keep the postfix.

Add Global-Key RPC Hardening as a prerequisite: without it any vanilla client's `noportals` toggle re-adds the key via RPC_SetGlobalKey's default canSave=true path (:116026) and bakes it into the .fwl, defeating session-only semantics.
Note that `resetkeys` (:43547-43552) re-triggers the postfix; the mod's own state file is the only way to end the lockdown.
Enforcement remains client-honoured and any-player-revocable until hardening is present; the .fwl hygiene is operator-facing only.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] All cited behaviour verified. `GlobalKeyAdd(string, bool canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true)` computes `flag = canSaveToServerOptionKeys && ZNet.World != null && gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (:113488) and only under `flag` touches `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113492-113496 remove, :113511 add). `GlobalKeyRemove(string, bool)` mirrors it (:113516-113539). Both are `private`; Wonderland's csproj sets `<Publicize>true</Publicize>` for assembly_valheim. `SendGlobalKeys` is private (:113466). `ZoneSystem.Save` strips every key with `gk < NonServerOption` from the .db (:113751-113755), and `World.SaveWorldFWLData` writes only `m_startingGlobalKeys` (:112579-112583), so a `canSave:false` key survives neither file. On boot `ZNet.WorldSetup` (:80851-80855) calls `SetStartingGlobalKeys()` (:115904-115931), which wipes ordinals 0..40 via `GlobalKeyRemove(..., false)`, re-adds the .fwl list, and applies `SetPreset` when a preset key exists (:115920-115926) — so the postfix (not prefix) requirement is correct; `ResetGlobalKeys` (:115889-115894, the `resetkeys` command) takes the same path so the postfix also covers that. `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance` is non-null on a dedicated server (Game.Awake :100042-100045) so `SetPreset` does not NRE. The Wonderland postfix pattern exists at WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-25. Client-honoured is right — the key's effect is still `TeleportWorld.Teleport` on the client.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified line-for-line. `GlobalKeyAdd(keyStr, canSaveToServerOptionKeys)` computes `flag = canSave && ZNet.World != null && gk < NonServerOption` (:113488) and only under that flag touches `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113495, :113511); `GlobalKeyRemove` mirrors it (:113516-113539). `ZoneSystem.Save` strips every key with gk < NonServerOption from the .db clone (:113751-113755); `World.SaveWorldFWLData` writes only m_startingGlobalKeys (:112581-112585); NoPortals is ordinal 32, NonServerOption 41 (:101271-101313). On boot `ZNet.LoadWorld` -> `LoadChunks` -> `WorldSetup()` -> `SetStartingGlobalKeys()` (:80764-80769, :80851-80855) which first REMOVES ordinals 0..40 (:115906-115910) and then re-adds the .fwl list — so the pre-mod state is restored; a postfix on SetStartingGlobalKeys is the right re-apply point (Wonderland WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-15 does exactly this). Server-browser modifiers are taken from m_startingGlobalKeys at registration (:79232/:79457), so the badge stays clean. Both GlobalKeyAdd/Remove/SendGlobalKeys are private -> publicizer or reflection needed, as stated. Corrections: (1) the stated reason a PREFIX fails is wrong-ordered — the primary reason is the unconditional wipe of ordinals 0..40 at the top of SetStartingGlobalKeys (:115906-115910), which erases any prefix-applied key regardless of whether a preset exists; SetPreset (:115920-115926 -> :59695-59730) is a secondary clobber. (2) Session-only is NOT guaranteed without the hardening option: any vanilla client can send `SetGlobalKey "NoPortals"` (the stock `noportals` command) which the server applies through the DEFAULT canSave=true path (:116026 -> :113483), baking 'noportals' into m_startingGlobalKeys and hence the .fwl. A vanilla player who toggles the key off then on has permanently written the modifier. Prereqs must include Global-Key RPC Hardening. (3) `resetkeys` (:43547-43552 -> ResetGlobalKeys :115888-115893) also calls SetStartingGlobalKeys(send:false) then SendGlobalKeys — the postfix fires there too, which is correct behaviour but means an admin cannot use resetkeys to clear the mod's key; the mod's own state file is the only off switch. (4) The 'asymmetry' note is harmless: the removal path uses `(keyValue + " " + value2).TrimEnd()` which for a valueless key equals the lowercase key, identical to what :113511 added; passing the lowercase literal is still the right practice.

catalog.name: Force-Disconnect Lockdown
catalog.oneLine: Null every portal's Portal connection server-side and suppress vanilla's 5s re-pairing, leaving even a fully hacked client with no destination coordinate to travel to.
catalog.howItWorks: Enumerate with `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648-77656, a freshly flattened list of every portal ZDO in the world, always resident because portals live in `m_portalObjects` and are never unloaded). For each portal: record `(rounded position, s_tag, current connection's rounded position)` into the Connection Vault, then `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627 / :77362), `zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, ZDOID.None)` (:73656-73666 — bumps DataRevision and calls `SetDirtyPortals`), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) to push it to every peer immediately rather than waiting for the ordinary sync sweep. This is exactly the shape of vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` immediate-write branch (:100641-100646), so it is a supported access pattern, not a hack. THREE DEFENCES ARE MANDATORY OR THE LOCK UNDOES ITSELF. (1) Vanilla re-pairing: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 2 (:100607-100622) pairs every `ZDOID.None` portal with a random same-tag partner within 5s (`ConnectPortalsCoroutine` :100580-100586). Add `[HarmonyPrefix]` on the public `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) returning false while locked. Note it must be a full suppression, not just phase 2, because phase 0's `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698) force-commits the previous tick's proposals with `forceImmediateConnection: true` regardless of ownership. (2) Ownership theft: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2s from `ReleaseZDOS` (:76872-76883) and hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer; the server always fails `IsInPeerActiveArea` for real coordinates because its reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465). Guard with a `[HarmonyPrefix]` on `ZDO.SetOwner` returning false for portal-prefab ZDOs while locked, allowing through only `uid == 0` and `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` — the exact `ZdoSetOwnerPatch` shape in Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313. Fail fast on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` because SetOwner is a global hot path. (3) Client write-back: `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is a global routed RPC registered on every peer at `Game.Start` :100066 with zero sender validation — prefix it to drop any call whose portal ZDO is under lockdown. And `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77107-77132) replaces the whole ZDO blob on a higher DataRevision, so also run a 1s re-assert tick that re-nulls any locked portal whose connection has become non-None, bumping `DataRevision += 4096` to win the race (Wonderland's proven counter-measure).
catalog.playerExperience: A player walking up to a locked portal sees it visibly dead: `HaveTarget()` returns false (:143631-143638) so `GetHoverText` reads `$piece_portal_unconnected` (:143461), `Update()` lerps `m_colorAlpha` toward 0 and the emission material fades from `m_colorTargetfound` to `m_colorUnconnected` (:143511-143515), and `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s poll leaves `m_target_found` off (:143507). Walking through the ring does absolutely nothing — no message at all, because `Teleport()` returns at gate 1 (`if (!TargetFound()) return;` :143519-143522) before any `player.Message` call. That silence is a UX problem in its own right and is why the graceful-lockdown option pairs an explicit announcement with the disconnect. A hacked client that strips all four gates still cannot move: :143539 resolves the connection to `ZDOID.None`, `ZDOMan.GetZDO` returns null for None (:76756-76759), and the whole teleport body is inside `if (zDO != null)` at :143540. When lockdown lifts and the vault restores the wiring, the first walk-through may still fail silently once — `TargetFound()` requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO and fires `RequestZDO` and returns false when it does not (:143646-143655) — so plan a one-transit warm-up, or pre-push destinations with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)`.
failureModes: THE BIG ONE: `ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...)` sets `DirtyPortalObjects` (:73661-73664), and that flag is the sole trigger for writing the portal chunk (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621-77632). An autosave during lockdown persists every connection as None; on reload `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:76523) and phase 2 randomly re-pairs same-tag portals (:100678). The original network is not merely still-locked, it is SCRAMBLED. Mandatory mitigation: the Save-Boundary Transparency option, or the Connection Vault with load-time restore, or both.

Suppressing `Game.ConnectPortals` wholesale also suppresses its self-heal pass (:100594-100606), so dangling connections to destroyed portals accumulate for the duration of the lockdown. A portal demolished mid-lockdown leaves its partner holding a dead ZDOID that is only cleaned when suppression lifts.

Eventually consistent with a ~50-100ms tail. `ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2` services one peer per 0.05s (:76837-76861). A player who steps into a trigger in that window uses their client's stale connection and teleports. `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only (:143673), so a player already standing inside the volume never re-triggers either way.

Cannot recall an in-flight traveller. Once `Player.TeleportTo` returns true the destination is snapshotted into `m_teleportTargetPos` (:15324) and `UpdateTeleport` force-assigns it every tick (:15343); a counter-teleport is refused because `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15313) and is zeroed every tick while teleporting (:15336).
A fully hacked client can call `Player.TeleportTo` locally with no portal at all. 'Unbypassable' means no portal-mediated travel, never no travel.
Mass `ForceSendZDO` on hundreds of portals floods every peer's sync queue against the 10240-byte cap (:77010-77016) — see the spike-control option.
The `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix is on a global hot path touched by `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` for every peer every 2s. A slow or throwing predicate degrades the whole server.
openQuestions: Does a client already standing next to a portal reliably re-render it as disconnected when the server nulls the connection, or does the visual state stick until the zone reloads? `UpdatePortal` re-reads `HaveTarget()` every 0.5s (:143491-143508) so it should, but `GetHoverText` is a separate read path. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a portal, null its connection server-side, and confirm both the hover text and the emission colour change within ~1s without walking away.
Does the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix measurably cost anything at scale? IN-GAME CHECK: profile `ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS` frame time with 10 peers and ~500 portals, with and without the prefix.
corrections: Defence (2) `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix only intercepts local `SetOwner` callers (`ReleaseNearbyZDOS` :76924, `Game.SetConnection` :100642). `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` writes ownership through `SetOwnerInternal` (:77114, :77127), bypassing the prefix; a client `ClaimOwnership` therefore always lands and must be undone by the re-assert tick (defence 3). State the prefix as latency reduction, not a guarantee.

Boot ordering: `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` at :76523 inside `ZNet.Start` -> `ServerLoadWorld` -> `LoadWorld` (:79254-79277, :80768). A world saved mid-lockdown carries no `ZDOConnectionHashData` for None targets (:75461-75477), so vanilla random-pairs every portal at that call. The lock prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` must be active from plugin Awake using persisted lock state, otherwise the lock silently lifts and wiring is scrambled before any of the mod's load hooks run.

During lockdown vanilla clients cannot change portal tags: `RPC_SetTag` (:143587-143602) requires `m_nview.IsOwner()` and is routed to the owner ZDO; the server has no instantiated `TeleportWorld`, so `HandleRoutedRPC` finds no `ZNetView` (:83648-83652) and drops it. Document as intended behaviour or exempt tag-only ownership hand-offs.
`Game.PortalPrefabHash` is `List<int>` (:100021), not a HashSet; `Contains` is linear but the list holds one or two hashes (:100031), so the fail-fast is still cheap.

Add: pinned server ownership silently disables retag (RPC_SetTag), hammer-remove (WearNTear.RPC_Remove) and damage/repair (WearNTear.RPC_Damage) on every locked portal — these are owner-routed ZNetView RPCs (:82855-82858) that the server drops because it has no ZNetView for the ZDO (HandleRoutedRPC :83656-83664). State this as intended lockdown behaviour or design a narrower ownership window.

Correct the warm-up claim: UpdatePortal (0.5 s) calls TargetFound() -> RequestZDO whenever a teleportable player is within 5 m (client :144222-144240, :144386-144399), so the destination is usually already held before the trigger fires; the silent first-transit failure is an edge case, not the norm.

Make explicit that RPC_ZDOData writes ownership via SetOwnerInternal (:77121, :77127), not SetOwner, so the SetOwner prefix does not cover hostile ZDOData; the 1 s re-assert tick (and an OwnerRevision bump alongside DataRevision) is mandatory for the 'fully hacked client' claim.
Game.SetConnection/RPC_SetConnection/ForceSetConnection are private; reproduce the three-call shape (SetOwner, SetConnection, ForceSendZDO) directly rather than calling them.

When ownership pinning is unacceptable, the fallback is vanilla-honoured only: send RPC_SetConnection(portal, None) to the client owner (client registers it too, :100066) — an unmodified client executes it, a hacked one need not.
evidence: Game.ConnectPortals / ForceSetConnection / SetConnection / RPC_SetConnection / FindRandomUnconnectedPortal / ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580-100698; Game.Start registrations — :100060-100075

(3) `RPC_SetConnection` is registered on every peer at Game.Start (:100066) with no sender check (:100653-100662); `RPC_ZDOData` replaces the ZDO on higher DataRevision and writes ownership through `SetOwnerInternal`, bypassing the SetOwner prefix (:77107-77132) — the re-assert tick is therefore necessary, not optional, against a hacked client. `GetPortalList` (:77648-77656), `ZDO.SetConnection` + SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73666), `ForceSendZDO` -> per-peer m_forceSend -> `AddForceSendZdos` inserts at list head regardless of distance (:77706-77711, :75998-76001, :77263-77284) all verified. Lesser correction: the 'one-transit warm-up' on restore is overstated — `UpdatePortal` polls every 0.5 s and evaluates `TargetFound()` (which fires `RequestZDO`) whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange=5 m (client :144222-144240, :144386-144399), so the destination ZDO is normally requested during the approach, before the trigger volume; a failed first transit needs the player to reach the ring within 0.5 s of entering the 5 m radius. Pre-pushing with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId)` (:77713-77720) is still a sound belt-and-braces. Effort medium-large is plausible.

catalog.name: Connection Vault and Crash Recovery
catalog.oneLine: A position-keyed side-file recording the true wiring of every portal before any lockdown touches it, restored at world load so a crash mid-lockdown never scrambles the network.
catalog.howItWorks: A JSON or line-delimited file under `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath`, named per world UID, written atomically (write `.tmp`, then `File.Replace` / temp-then-move — the SupplySwitch pattern). Each record is `{ tagBefore, posA (x,y,z rounded to 0.1), posB (x,y,z rounded to 0.1), lockedAtUtc, reason }`. KEYED BY ROUNDED WORLD POSITION, NEVER BY ZDOID: `ZDO.Load` renumbers every ZDO on every world load (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so a ZDOID-keyed vault silently points at nothing after a restart — this is the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit and documented before switching to a position key. Position is safe for portals specifically because `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73756), meaning portals are never repositioned by any vanilla path and a mod must never reposition one either. WRITE ORDER on engage: snapshot the whole vault and fsync it FIRST, then begin nulling connections. Never interleave. RESTORE runs at world load, which is the cheapest possible window: at `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` every ZDO comes back with `Owned=false, OwnerRevision=0, DataRevision=0`, `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection`'s `owner == 0L` branch (:100641) always takes the immediate local write, and no client can contend. Hook a postfix on `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (or `Game.Start` before the `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` StartCoroutine at :100074) and for each vault record: find the live portal ZDO nearest `posA` within a 1.0m tolerance in `GetPortalList()`, find the one nearest `posB`, verify both still carry `tagBefore` (or at least both carry the same tag as each other), then `SetOwner(sessionID)` + `SetConnection(Portal, otherUid)` on both ends + `ForceSendZDO`. Discard any record whose endpoints no longer resolve — that portal was demolished while locked. Then delete the vault. EXPECTATION MANAGEMENT: exact restoration is only meaningful for tag groups of exactly 2. `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679) picks uniformly at random among same-tag unconnected portals, and for a group of 3+ vanilla itself strands exactly one member arbitrarily, with the stranded member determined by `m_portalObjects` dictionary bucket order which is not stable across restarts. For groups of 3+ the vault restores *a* valid pairing identical to the one that was live, which is strictly better than a random re-shuffle but is not a promise vanilla ever made.
catalog.playerExperience: Operator-facing. After an unplanned restart during a lockdown the server log prints `[TortalPortal] Restored 47/49 portal links from vault (2 endpoints missing — portals demolished during lockdown)`, and players find their base-to-mine and base-to-swamp portals connected to exactly the same partners as before the crash, rather than discovering their swamp portal now leads to someone else's identically-tagged outpost.
failureModes: Only protects what it recorded. A portal built during the lockdown has no vault entry and will be randomly paired by vanilla on restore — correct behaviour, but it must be logged rather than silently absorbed.

A world rollback to an older backup makes the vault describe portals that no longer exist, or exist at those positions with different tags. Every record must be validated against live state before restore, and a record whose endpoints resolve but whose tags disagree must be discarded, not forced.
Two portals within the 1.0m position tolerance (stacked or clipped builds) make the nearest-match ambiguous. Tie-break on tag, then refuse and log rather than guess.
Restoring a 3+ member tag group reproduces the previous pairing, not a canonically 'correct' one — there is no canonical one. Do not advertise it as such.

If the mod is uninstalled while a lockdown is active, the vault is never replayed and the world keeps nulled connections until vanilla re-pairs them randomly. The uninstall path must be documented: lift the lockdown before removing the plugin.
Vault writes are disk I/O on the main thread. Batch them; a per-portal fsync on a 500-portal world will stall a frame.
citations: Wonderland SupplySwitch atomic state file — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/SupplySwitch.cs:100-165
openQuestions: What position tolerance is actually safe? Portal positions are written once at placement and never move, so exact float equality may work — but a world rollback plus float round-tripping through the save format could perturb them. IN-GAME CHECK: place a portal, save, restart, and compare `zdo.GetPosition()` bit-for-bit against the pre-restart value.

Is there a reliable hook that fires after `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` but before `Game.ConnectPortals` runs at :76523? If not, the restore must instead run as a postfix on the first `Game.ConnectPortals` call and repair whatever vanilla just randomised. IN-GAME CHECK: log the call order of LoadChunks / ConnectPortals / Game.Start on a cold boot.
corrections: Restore must run BEFORE or INSTEAD OF the load-time `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` at ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76523. Correct shapes: (a) a Harmony prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` (public, :100589) that performs the vault restore on its first invocation and then lets vanilla run (vanilla leaves already-connected same-tag pairs alone, :100594-100606); or (b) keep the lock prefix (returning false) armed through boot from plugin Awake, restore in a `LoadChunks` postfix, then release. A plain `LoadChunks` postfix without either is clobbered by `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698) on the next 5 s tick unless it also clears the private `Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals` (:99903).

Drop the 'Game.Start before StartCoroutine :100074' alternative: `ZNet.Start` -> `ServerLoadWorld` -> `LoadWorld` -> `LoadChunks` (:79254-79277, :80768) already invoked `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` at :76523; `Game.Start` timing relative to it is not guaranteed and does not gate that call.

`ZDO.SetSector` early-return for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) does not make portal positions immutable: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition` (:73734-73744) still writes `m_position` (SetSector merely no-ops), and `RPC_ZDOData` applies wire positions (:77128). The position key is safe only because no vanilla path moves a placed portal, not because of that check.

Odd-sized tag groups strand exactly one portal; even-sized groups (4, 6, ...) pair fully. The stranded/partner choice is `UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)` (:100678); `m_portalObjects` order only fixes which portal is `item2` first.

Tolerance note: `ZDO.Load` with `SmallPosition` flag (:74562ff) quantises position on disk; a 1.0 m nearest-match is adequate but the vault should round to the same precision the save uses rather than assuming 0.1 m fidelity round-trips.

Move the restore hook: ZDOMan.LoadChunks calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() synchronously at :76523, and ZNet.LoadWorld (:80762-80769) runs before Game.Start, so a LoadChunks postfix or Game.Start hook is too late — vanilla has already randomly paired every None portal with an immediate owner==0 write. Use a postfix on private ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850, runs between the hash restore and :76523) or a first-run-gated prefix on Game.ConnectPortals.

During restore, set connection=None on every portal that is not an endpoint of a vault record before letting vanilla run; otherwise portals vanilla paired before the restore keep pointing at now-reassigned partners and the reconcile predicate (:100596-100604, no reciprocity check) leaves them as permanent fan-ins.

Drop the SetSector justification: :73752-73756 skips sector bucketing for portals (they live in m_portalObjects), it says nothing about position. Position keys are safe because no vanilla path moves placed pieces.

Under Force-Disconnect's ownership pin, vanilla clients cannot demolish locked portals (WearNTear.RPC_Remove owner-gated, dropped by HandleRoutedRPC :83656-83664); the 'demolished during lockdown' branch only covers hacked-client RPC_DestroyZDO or post-unlock demolition.

The SupplySwitch file pattern (Wonderland SupplySwitch.cs:108-135) is not fsync'd, not atomic (Delete then Move), and ZDOID-keyed — do not cite it as the model. Write via FileStream with Flush(true), then rename over the old file.
Game.SetConnection/ForceSetConnection are private; do SetOwner(sessionID) + SetConnection(Portal, uid) + ForceSendZDO directly (:100641-100646 shape).
Relabel enforcement: admin-facing-only (operator crash hygiene), not server-enforced.
evidence: ZDOMan.LoadChunks (portal chunk, ConnectPortals at :76512, Game.instance.ConnectPortals() at :76523) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531
Game.ConnectPortals reconcile predicate (no reciprocity) — :100596-100604; SetConnection owner==0 path — :100637-100651; FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — :100664-100679
ZDO.SetSector portal early-return — :73752-73756; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal — :77732-77745; HandleDestroyedZDO portal removal — :76963-77000
ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC drops owner RPCs without a ZNetView — :83646-83665; WearNTear.RPC_Remove owner gate (client) — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:151155-151162
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The need is real and the position key is right: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` and resets `OwnerRevision/DataRevision/Owned` (:74549-74556), `ZDOID.m_loadID` is zeroed in `ZNet.Awake` (:79159), and the Favorites.cs post-mortem exists (:109-111). `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` picks with `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100664-100679). `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes portals from `m_portalObjects` (:76963-77000). SupplySwitch's temp-then-`File.Move` pattern exists (SupplySwitch.cs:117-128). At load `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection`'s `owner == 0L || !flag` branch writes locally (:100637-100646). But the restore hook as specified is broken. `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` itself calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` at :76523 — before any LoadChunks postfix. A world saved mid-lockdown has no on-disk pairing (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75477 drops None targets), so that call randomly pairs every same-tag portal AND stages each pair in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` (:100683). If the vault then rewrites connections in a postfix, the next `ConnectPortals` tick (5 s, :100580-100586) opens with `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698), whose `ForceSetConnection` sees `current != staged` (:100631) and force-writes the random pairs back — the restore is clobbered. The 'Game.Start before StartCoroutine' alternative does not help: :76523 fires regardless, and `Game.Start` vs `ZNet.Start` (:79254-79277) ordering is Unity script-order dependent. Two secondary factual errors in the reasoning: the `SetSector` early-return (:73752-73756) does not prevent repositioning — `InternalSetPosition` still updates `m_position` (:73734-73744) and `RPC_ZDOData` writes position from the wire (:77128); it only pins the sector bucket. And the 3+ group claim is imprecise: only odd-sized groups strand a member, and the choice is `Random.Range` (:100678), not dictionary order (iteration order only decides which portal asks first).

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] The need is real and the ZDOID-instability premise is verified: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552), `m_loadID` reset at :75842/:79159, so ZDOIDs are regenerated every load; TortalPortal Favorites.cs:111 documents the same lesson. Vanilla persists pairings via `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` at PrepareSave (:75461-75483) and restores them in private `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` during LoadChunks (:77850-77891, called at :76512), so the vault only matters if a world save (autosave/shutdown) captured the nulled state — which is the likely case in any lockdown longer than the save interval. `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` random pick (:100664-100679) and 3+ group stranding are correctly described. But the restore hook as specified is wrong and would silently produce the very scramble it is meant to prevent: `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` itself calls `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` synchronously at :76523 before returning, and ZNet.LoadWorld runs from ZNet.Awake before Game.Start, so a postfix on LoadChunks or a hook in Game.Start (:100074) runs AFTER vanilla has already randomly re-paired every None portal (owner==0 at load -> immediate write, :100639-100646). Restoring the vault on top of that leaves the displaced partners pointing at portals that no longer point back, and the reconcile predicate (:100601) never tests reciprocity, so those become permanent fan-ins. Correct window: a postfix on private `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850) — after the hash-based restore, before :76523 — or a first-run-gated prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals`, and the restore must also null every portal NOT covered by a vault record so vanilla re-strands cleanly. Second premise error: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returning for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) concerns sector bucketing (portals live in m_portalObjects, :77732-77745), not position immutability; position stability holds simply because nothing in vanilla moves placed pieces. Third: with Force-Disconnect's ownership pin, vanilla clients cannot demolish a locked portal at all (WearNTear.RPC_Remove is owner-gated and dropped on the server), so 'endpoints missing — demolished during lockdown' can arise only from a hacked client's RPC_DestroyZDO or after unlock. Fourth: 'fsync it FIRST' — the cited SupplySwitch pattern (Wonderland SupplySwitch.cs:108-135) is WriteAllLines + Delete + Move, neither fsync'd nor atomic (a crash between Delete and Move loses the file), and it is ZDOID-keyed, the exact bug this option warns about; use FileStream.Flush(true) then File.Replace/rename-over. Fifth: `Game.SetConnection` is private — reproduce SetOwner+SetConnection+ForceSendZDO directly. Enforcement: this mechanism enforces nothing on players; it is operator-facing crash hygiene, so 'server-enforced' is the wrong label — admin-facing-only. Feasible with those corrections; downgraded because the design as written does not achieve its stated outcome.

catalog.name: Save-Boundary Transparency
catalog.oneLine: Sandwich the world-save snapshot between a restore and a re-lock so that a lockdown is never written to disk at all, making crash recovery a non-event.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZNet.SaveWorld` (:80521-80546) runs entirely on the main thread up to the point it spawns the writer thread: it fires `WorldSaveStarted?.Invoke()` at :80524, then `m_zdoMan.PrepareSave()` at :80532, then `ZoneSystem/RandEventSystem/PersistentEventSystem.PrepareSave()`, then starts `m_saveThread`. `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205) is public and does `m_saveData.m_objectsByChunk = GetSaveClonePerChunk()` — which deep-clones every portal ZDO into the ChunkPortal bucket when `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77621-77632) — followed by `ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave()` (:75480-75491) which calls `RegenerateConnectionHashData()` (:75461-75477) to turn live `s_connections` into the saveable `s_connectionsHashData`. Everything the writer thread later serialises is captured in those two calls. So: `[HarmonyPrefix]` on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` writes the TRUE connections back from the vault into `s_connections` via `zdo.SetConnection(Portal, trueTarget)`; `[HarmonyPostfix]` on the same method immediately re-nulls them. Both halves run in the same frame with no `ZDOMan.Update` between them (the send sweep is gated on a 0.05s timer at :76843-76861 and is driven from Update, not from the save path), so no peer ever receives the unlocked state. Use `ZDO.SetConnection` rather than poking `ZDOExtraData` directly so `DirtyPortalObjects` stays set and the chunk is actually written. DO NOT close the sandwich with `ZNet.WorldSaveFinished` (:78991): it is invoked from `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80580), ~0.5s after the thread ends via `UpdateSave` (:80548-80564), and that method dereferences `MessageHud.instance.MessageAll` unguarded at :80574 and :80578 — if that singleton is ever null on a headless build the event never fires and the world is left unlocked in memory. `WorldSaveStarted` is a safe *notification* hook (public static Action, :78989) for logging and for forcing a vault flush, but the actual sandwich must be the PrepareSave prefix/postfix pair because only that is guaranteed to bracket the snapshot. Additionally guard against re-entrancy: `SaveWorld` joins a still-running previous save thread at :80525-80530, and a synchronous shutdown save (`ZNet.Shutdown(save:true)` → `Save(sync:true)` :79466-79472) goes through the same path — the sandwich covers both.
catalog.playerExperience: Entirely invisible. The only observable difference is that a `kill -9` during a two-hour maintenance lockdown produces a world that comes back with every portal wired exactly as it was, with no vault replay needed and no log noise.
failureModes: Relies on a Harmony patch on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` running atomically around the snapshot. If another mod also patches it and returns false from a prefix, the postfix may not run and the world is left restored-and-unlocked in memory until the next re-assert tick catches it. Make the re-assert tick authoritative rather than trusting the postfix alone.

`ZoneSystem.SkipSaving()` (:115874-115881) and `DungeonDB.SkipSaving()` can make `ZNet.Save` bail at :80183 BEFORE `SaveWorld` is ever called, so the sandwich never runs — harmless (nothing is written either) but the mod must not assume a paired prefix/postfix for every `Save()` call.

If the mod's own re-assert tick fires between prefix and postfix (it cannot, same frame, but a coroutine or thread could), the lock state becomes indeterminate. Keep all lockdown mutation single-threaded on the main thread.

`ConsiderAutoBackup` runs INSIDE `SaveWorldThread` at :80601, after the snapshot — so a backup taken during lockdown contains the sandwiched (restored) state, which is correct. But a manual file-level backup taken by an external cron while the server is running copies whatever is already on disk, which is also the restored state. Both are fine; a backup taken by copying live memory is not possible, so there is no third case.

Doubles the number of `SetConnection` calls per save on a locked world — 2N revision bumps per save cycle. On a 500-portal world that is 1000 dictionary writes plus 1000 `IncreaseDataRevision` calls inside the save freeze. Measurable but small; still worth a budget.

catalog.name: Scheduled Blackout Windows
catalog.oneLine: A cron-style schedule that engages and lifts portal restrictions at fixed real-world or in-game times, with announcements and an idempotent reconciler rather than edge-triggered toggles.
catalog.howItWorks: A config list of windows, each `{ days, startLocal, endLocal, mode }` where mode is one of `KeyOnly` (NoPortals), `Disconnect` (force-disconnect), or `TagQuarantine`. The engine ticks from the subsystem `OnUpdate(dt)` at 1Hz and computes the DESIRED state from wall-clock time, then reconciles: if desired != actual, apply the transition. Level-triggered, never edge-triggered — this is the single most important design choice, because an edge-triggered scheduler that misses its tick (server restart across the boundary, a long save freeze, a clock change) leaves the world in the wrong state forever. On every tick the reconciler also verifies the invariant (all locked portals still have `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone()`) and repairs drift, which doubles as the anti-tamper re-assert. In-game-time scheduling is also available and is often what operators actually want ('portals closed at night'): the server's day fraction comes from `EnvMan` / `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds`, and `Game.m_dayTimeSpeed`-scaled day length means a real-time schedule and an in-game schedule drift apart — pick one per window and label it in the config. State (which windows are currently engaged, and the vault) persists to the mod's own file so a restart inside a window resumes correctly rather than re-announcing. Announcements fire at T-10min, T-5min, T-60s and at engage, through the channels in the graceful-lockdown option; each announcement is rate-limited per player so a reconciler that runs at 1Hz does not spam. Hot-reload of the schedule without a restart comes free from the Wonderland `PollConfigFile` pattern (5s mtime poll, `SaveOnConfigSet` parked false during `Config.Reload()` so re-applied values do not bump mtime and cause a reload loop).
catalog.playerExperience: At 21:50 server time every online player gets a top-left message: 'Portal network closes in 10 minutes (nightly maintenance window).' At 21:55 and 21:59 the warning repeats, the last one centre-screen. At 22:00 every portal in the world visibly goes dark — hover text flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected`, the ring's emission fades — and walking through does nothing. At 06:00 the reconciler restores every link from the vault and a message reads 'Portal network is open.' A player who logs in at 03:00 sees dark portals and, on their first `OnNewPeer`, a toast explaining the window and when it ends. A player mid-transit at exactly 22:00:00 still arrives — `Player.UpdateTeleport` cannot be interrupted (:15343-15349).
failureModes: Wall-clock schedules across a daylight-saving transition either fire twice or not at all. Compute in UTC and convert for display only.

`WaitForSeconds` and `Time` are scaled; `Game.UpdateSleeping`'s time-skip path can advance in-game time in a jump, so an in-game-time window can be skipped entirely by a sleep. The level-triggered reconciler absorbs this correctly; an edge-triggered one does not.

A restart inside a window must not re-run the engage transition (re-announcing, re-vaulting over an already-vaulted state). Persist 'currently engaged' and treat a matching persisted state as already-applied.
Two overlapping windows with different modes need a defined precedence or they will fight each other on every tick. Define strictest-wins and log the resolution.

A window that engages within the 30s pre-save warning (`Game.UpdateSaving` :100474 fires `$msg_worldsavewarning 30s`) piles two disruptive announcements on top of each other and puts the lock right next to a snapshot. Refuse to engage within 60s of `m_saveInterval` (default 1800f, :99914) elapsing, or force a clean save first.

Disconnect mode requires the vanilla 5s Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100628, coroutine :100580) to be suppressed for the window; a 1Hz re-null alone yields a portal that re-pairs and flickers every 5-10s.

KeyOnly mode is client-honoured (gate in client TeleportWorld.Teleport :144263) and NoPortals is persisted to the .fwl world-modifier list by GlobalKeyAdd (:113483-113517) — it survives a crash and mod removal; only Disconnect mode is server-enforced.

Enforcement is mode-dependent. `Disconnect` (connection field) is route-form server-enforced. `KeyOnly` (NoPortals) is CLIENT-HONOURED: the only reader is TeleportWorld.Teleport :143523-143527 which runs on the client. `TagQuarantine` is route-form but the s_tag field is freely rewritten by the owning vanilla client via RPC_SetTag :143583-143600 with no server hook; it is only as strong as the reconciler's re-assert cadence.

`Game.m_dayTimeSpeed` does not exist (grep: no match). Day length is EnvMan.m_dayLengthSec = 1200L :95406; the authoritative clock is ZNet.GetTimeSeconds() :81546; day fraction is computed in EnvMan.FixedUpdate :95697-95703 from that clock (runs on the dedicated server, no local-player gate) and exposed as EnvMan.GetDayFraction() :96290 (note it is a smoothed/lerped value; compute your own fraction from GetTimeSeconds % m_dayLengthSec for exact boundaries).

Persisted state 'which windows are engaged, and the vault' keyed on ZDOID does not survive a restart: ZDO.Load :74551 assigns m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) on every world load. Key the vault by (position, tag) or rely on Save-Boundary Transparency so disk already holds true wiring; and note ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76523 runs ConnectPortals on load, so a restart inside a window comes up UNLOCKED until the reconciler's first tick re-engages.

The anti-tamper invariant check only detects the connection field. A vanilla client cannot create a connection on its own (only Game.RPC_SetConnection :100651-100660 sent by the server, and TeleportWorld.RPC_SetConnected :143630-143636 which only sets None), so drift is limited to the server's own ConnectPortals coroutine :100580-100587, which the Force-Disconnect prereq must suppress.

catalog.name: Graceful Lockdown and Announcement
catalog.oneLine: Warn, give a grace period, then disconnect — with a multi-channel server-to-vanilla-client announcement stack, because a silently dead portal reads as a mod bug.
catalog.howItWorks: Force-disconnect is silent by construction: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` returns at gate 1 (`if (!TargetFound()) return;` :143519-143522) WITHOUT any `player.Message` call, unlike gates 2/3/4 which each emit `$msg_blocked`, `$msg_blockedbyboss` or `$msg_noteleport`. So the mod must supply the words. Five channels exist to a 100% vanilla client, in descending order of appropriateness. (1) Per-character toast: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.Center, text, 0)` — registered on the owning client only in `Player.Start` :10072, handler `Player.RPC_Message` :14820-14825, re-checks `IsOwner`. This is Wonderland's `PlayerNotify.Toast` verbatim and is the safest because it cannot be delivered to the wrong player. (2) Broadcast HUD text: the global routed RPC `"ShowMessage"` (int type, string text), registered in `MessageHud.Start` :55799-55809, handler :55848-55851, `MessageType.TopLeft=1 / Center=2`. (3) Fabricated chat: `"ChatMessage"` (Vector3 pos, int type, UserInfo user, string text), registered in `Chat.Awake` :41626 — a Shout (type 2) produces a chat line, yellow uppercase in-world text, AND a 5s labelled map pin, with the speaker name fully server-chosen. Note `<` and `>` are replaced with spaces in `Chat.OnNewChatMessage` so no rich text. (4) Floating world text near the portal: `"RPC_DamageText"` with a ZPackage of `{int TextType, Vector3 pos, string text, bool mySelf}`, culled at 30m (`DamageText.m_maxTextDistance`). (5) Admin console: `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, text)` :81635. All text is run through `Localization.Localize` on the client, so `$token` strings render in the player's own language. THE SEQUENCE: T-300s broadcast ShowMessage TopLeft; T-60s ShowMessage Center; T-10s per-player Center toast, but ONLY to players whose character ZDO position is within ~40m of any portal (walk `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` — the live zero-alloc dictionary — exactly as Wonderland's `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` does, and compare against `ConnectedCharacters.All()` positions); at T-0 engage the disconnect and send one final Center message plus a `RPC_DamageText` at each portal within 30m of a player reading 'PORTAL CLOSED'. After engage, re-send the explanation on each `OnNewPeer` for the duration, and on any detected transit attempt — detectable because a player standing inside a trigger volume produces no server-side signal at all, so instead detect proximity-dwell: a character ZDO within ~3m of a locked portal for >2 consecutive samples.
catalog.playerExperience: Five minutes before a scheduled maintenance the top-left corner reads 'Portal network closes in 5 minutes.' At one minute it moves to the centre of the screen. At ten seconds, a player standing at their base portal specifically gets 'This portal closes in 10 seconds — step through now or walk.' At zero the ring goes dark and 'PORTAL CLOSED' floats above it in orange. Walking into it produces the same 'Portal network is closed until 06:00' centre message rather than the vanilla silence, because the mod detects the dwell and answers it. A player who logs in during the window is told once, on connect, rather than discovering it by walking into a dead ring.
failureModes: The dwell-based transit detector is a heuristic with a sampling floor. `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` refreshes the character ZDO position every physics tick so the data is fresh to ~50-100ms, but polling every character against every portal at that rate is wasteful; a 0.5-1s poll misses a player who sprints through and leaves.

`Chat.instance` and `MessageHud.instance` may or may not exist on a headless build. The SEND side never needs them (`ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC` is enough) but registering a handler name the server already has would throw from `ZRoutedRpc.Register`'s `Dictionary.Add`. Never call Register for `ChatMessage`/`ShowMessage`; only invoke.

`RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` map pins are added with `save:true` and there is NO removal RPC — do not use pins for transient lockdown state or every maintenance window permanently litters every player's map.
A broadcast at `targetPeerID 0` also makes the server attempt a local dispatch (:83588), which silently misses; harmless but prefer per-peer targeting.

Announcement spam: a 1Hz reconciler that re-announces on every tick is worse than silence. Rate-limit per player per message-class with a cooldown table keyed on `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (not `peer.m_uid`, which is regenerated every reconnect).

Players in flight at T-0 arrive regardless and receive a 'closed' message on arrival, which is confusing. Suppress the message for any player whose character ZDO position changed by a portal-transit-sized delta in the last sample.

At ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer time the peer has no character ZDO yet, so channel (1) cannot be used there; per-peer delivery must be `InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "ShowMessage", type, text)` (global routed RPC, no ZDO target). Even that can arrive before the client's MessageHud.Start has run its Register; safer to defer the connect-time explanation until the peer's character ZDO first appears (ConnectedCharacters), then use the per-character Message RPC.

A made-up UserInfo may be denied on console/PlayFab relation backends — needs in-game check per platform before relying on it. Channel (5) RemotePrint only writes to the client's F5 console (client ZNet :80104 registers it per-connection) — not a player-facing announcement channel; drop it from the stack or label it admin-only.

Dwell detection is reactive-detection-only and bounded by the character ZDO position sync cadence; it is a UX reply, not a gate. The option correctly says the lock itself is the prereq's; this option's own enforcement contribution is delivery only.
