(c) The on-connect notice cannot use the character-ZDO 'Message' RPC at m_onNewPeer time (no character ZDO yet) — send a peer-targeted 'ShowMessage' or defer until the character ZDO appears. (d) The dwell detector is reactive-detection-only: it observes the character ZDO position the owning client chose to send and cannot stop or reverse a transit; label it as such. The enforcement label is inherited from Force-Disconnect (route closed server-side); this option's own contribution is client-rendered UI plus a reactive heuristic. The 'ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer' citation is a private handler; the hook is ZRoutedRpc.instance.m_onNewPeer.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited channel exists with the claimed signature and registration context: Player.Start registers "Message" only inside `if (m_nview.IsOwner())` :10070-10072 and RPC_Message :14820-14826 re-checks IsOwner and MessageHud.instance; MessageHud.Start registers global routed "ShowMessage"<int,string> :55808 with handler :55848-55851 (MessageType TopLeft=1, Center=2 at :55765); Chat.Awake registers "ChatMessage"<Vector3,int,UserInfo,string> :41626; DamageText.Awake registers "RPC_DamageText"<ZPackage> :46352-46356 with handler :46494-46510 reading {int,Vector3,string,bool} and culling at m_maxTextDistance (30f, client :46371); ZNet.RemotePrint :81635-81648. TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 :143519-143522 returns with no Message call — confirmed silent. ZDOMan.GetPortals :77643-77646 returns the live dictionary. ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer :113607-113616 exists. Wonderland PlayerNotify.Toast (PlayerNotify.cs:15-30) and PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit (:148) match. Several delivery details need correction.

catalog.name: Boss Auto-Lockdown with activeBosses Watchdog
catalog.oneLine: Set NoBossPortals for boss fights and ship the watchdog that unsticks vanilla's leaky activeBosses counter, which otherwise jams every portal shut indefinitely.
catalog.howItWorks: Two mechanisms read `NoBossPortals` and they are NOT the same condition. (A) World portals: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` :143528 blocks when `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out value) && value > 0f))`. That is a WORLD-WIDE blackout — one player aggroing Eikthyr closes every portal for everyone. `GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106950) requires `EnemyHud.instance` and reads the *viewing client's* own boss HUD, so in practice the `activeBosses` disjunct is what fires for remote players. (B) Dungeon/crypt doors: `Teleport.Interact` :143355 blocks only when `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos)`. `Character.InInterior(Vector3)` is `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541), so it can only ever be true for a player ALREADY inside an interior — it blocks the OUTBOUND leg only, never entry. And `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631-133645) dereferences `EnemyHud.instance`, returns false if null, and otherwise requires `ZoneSystem.GetZone(point) == ZoneSystem.GetZone(activeBoss.transform.position)` with the boss having a non-empty `m_bossEvent`. It is client-HUD-dependent, XZ-zone-based (64m column, y ignored), and effectively means 'you are in an interior above the same 64m column as a boss your HUD is currently showing'. THE WATCHDOG IS THE REAL WORK. `BaseAI.SetAlerted` (:27256-27261) increments `activeBosses` once per boss and sets the ZDO bool `s_bossCount` to `true` on that same first call unconditionally, so the intended `-1` on de-alert can never execute. The only decrement is `Character.OnDeath` at :3161-3165, guarded on `s_bossCount`. A boss that is alerted and then unloaded (its owning client logs out, the zone drops) leaves the counter permanently above zero and every portal in the world permanently blocked. The watchdog runs on a 30s tick: read `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out float v)` (:115958-115966); if `v > 0f`, verify at least one live boss ZDO actually exists by walking connected players' regions or by maintaining a boss-ZDO registry; if none, write `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f)` (:115933-115936, formats as `"activebosses 0"` with InvariantCulture) and log it. Because `activeBosses` has ordinal 47 (≥ NonServerOption) it is a .db key, not a .fwl key, so resetting it is not a world-modifier edit.
catalog.playerExperience: A player fighting Bonemass finds every portal on the server refuses with a centre-screen `$msg_blockedbyboss` — including players on the other side of the map who have nothing to do with the fight. Crypt doors keep working for anyone entering a crypt; only a player standing inside an interior directly above an active boss is refused on the way out. When the boss dies, portals work again on the next attempt. Without the watchdog, one crashed client mid-Moder-fight leaves the whole server portal-locked with `$msg_blockedbyboss` until an admin intervenes — and the message blames a boss that is not there.
failureModes: Client-honoured only. Both gates are in client-executed code.

The blast radius is the whole world, not the fight. Operators expecting 'portals disabled during YOUR boss fight' will be surprised; there is no per-player or per-region variant available through this key.
`activeBosses` leaks by design (`s_bossCount` set unconditionally at :27260). Without the watchdog a server WILL eventually lock itself out. This is not a hypothetical.

`GetBossEvent()` returns null when `EnemyHud.instance` is null, so on any client without the HUD (or with it hidden) the first disjunct never fires and only the counter matters — meaning the gate's behaviour differs between players in the same fight.
Blocking dungeon doors at all is impossible beyond this key: `Teleport` has no ZDO, no RPC and no server-side presence whatsoever (:143316-143390).
Resetting `activeBosses` to 0 while a boss genuinely IS alive but unowned re-opens portals mid-fight. The watchdog must require a sustained 'no live boss' observation, not a single sample.

`SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f)` goes through the RPC and `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` guard (:116024) compares the exact `"activebosses 0"` string — if the key is already exactly that, the write is a silent no-op, which is the desired idempotence but must not be mistaken for failure.
openQuestions: Does a dedicated server ever instantiate a boss Character (and therefore ever move `activeBosses` itself)? `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position at :100465 so it should never, but `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` still runs. IN-GAME CHECK: `setkey nobossportals`, aggro a boss with one client, read `listkeys` on the server console and watch `activeBosses` appear, decrement on death, and confirm whether it returns to 0 after a client force-quits mid-fight.

How does the watchdog cheaply prove 'no live boss exists'? Boss ZDOs are ordinary creature ZDOs with no dedicated registry. Options are a `ZDOVars.s_bossCount` int-field index via `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, ZDOVars.s_bossCount)` (:75390-75407, a full unindexed scan — startup/occasional only) or tracking alerted bosses by observing `activeBosses` transitions. IN-GAME CHECK: confirm `s_bossCount` is queryable that way and measure the scan cost.
corrections: The leak is not crash-specific: SetAlerted (:27242-27267) latches s_bossCount on first alert, so activeBosses stays >0 for the whole remaining life of any once-alerted boss, including a de-aggroed one standing at its altar.

The watchdog test 'no live boss ZDO exists' will not fire in the common case because bosses are persistent ZDOs; use 'no s_bossCount boss ZDO is s_alert==true AND inside any connected peer's active area' (s_alert written at :27249-27251; area test per IsInPeerActiveArea :76887-76898).

When resetting activeBosses also write s_bossCount=false on the stale boss ZDOs; otherwise the reset is a one-way ratchet and that boss never re-closes portals (the increment branch is gated on !s_bossCount).
Boss detection server-side requires a hard-coded boss prefab-hash list; Character.IsBoss() is a prefab field, not a ZDO key.
Enabling NoBossPortals via SetGlobalKey is a .fwl world-modifier write (GlobalKeyAdd :113483-113517, gk < NonServerOption) that persists after mod removal.

Only call SetGlobalKey(activeBosses,0) when v>0 — RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116028) re-broadcasts all keys on every call because its Contains check compares un-lowered input against the lower-cased store.

SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,float) formats `$"{key} {value}"` = "activeBosses 0" (enum name case preserved); lowercasing happens in GlobalKeyAdd via GetKeyValue(keyStr.ToLower()). RPC_SetGlobalKey's `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` guard compares the raw string, so a re-send with the same value is a no-op only if case matches the stored lowercase form — always call GlobalKeyAdd's path once and do not assume idempotence of the raw string.

'Permanently above zero' is overstated: the alerted boss ZDO is Persistent and keeps s_bossCount=true, so Character.OnDeath :3161 still decrements when that boss is eventually killed by anyone. The practical effect (world-wide portal lock until someone goes back and kills it) is real; true irrecoverable leaks are boss ZDOs destroyed without OnDeath (e.g. ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO, which has no sender check) or a lost s_bossCount ZDO write after the SetGlobalKey RPC already landed.

The watchdog invariant should be `activeBosses <= count(boss ZDOs with GetBool(ZDOVars.s_bossCount))`, enumerated with the PUBLIC `ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO>, ref int index)` :77442 over the known boss prefab names — not 'walking connected players' regions'. Clamp DOWN only: vanilla undercounts under concurrent alerts (two owners both read 0 and both write 1, then Max(0, v-1) on each death), so raising the value to the ZDO count would create a lock vanilla never had.

SetAlerted is effectively owner-only: BaseAI.Alert :27236-27239 is IsOwner-gated, the OnDamaged callers run on the owner (Character.RPC_Damage is owner-only), and non-owners mirror `m_alerted = zdo.GetBool(s_alert)` :26001 without calling SetAlerted — so the increment really is once-per-boss-per-owner, which supports the option's analysis.

SetGlobalKey goes out as `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` :115945 to Everybody; RPC_SetGlobalKey (ZoneSystem, registered :113447) has no sender/admin check, so any client can also set or clear activeBosses — the watchdog is also the defence against that.

NoBossPortals (33) < NonServerOption (41): enabling it via SetGlobalKey writes ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (.fwl) through GlobalKeyAdd's `flag` path — it IS a world-modifier edit, unlike activeBosses. Belongs to the NoPortals prereq but the option's contrast should say so.
evidence: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,float) :115933-115936; SetGlobalKey(string) :115943-115946; GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,out float) :115958-115966; GlobalKeyAdd (NonServerOption gate); RPC_SetGlobalKey registration :113447
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The two gates and the leak are real, but the proposed watchdog condition is wrong and would almost never fire. Gate A: client TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143528 server copy / client :144268) blocks on NoBossPortals && (GetBossEvent()!=null || activeBosses>0); GetBossEvent (:106939-106950) reads EnemyHud.instance — client-local. Gate B: Teleport.Interact (:143355) requires InInterior (y>3000, :4538-4541) && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon (:133631-133645, EnemyHud + XZ zone equality). Both are client-executed → client-honoured is correct. The leak: BaseAI.SetAlerted (:27242-27267) increments activeBosses and latches s_bossCount=true on the FIRST alert; the -1 branch is unreachable thereafter; the only other decrement is Character.OnDeath (:3161-3165). Non-owner clients never call SetAlerted (UpdateAI :25993-26004 just copies s_alert), so the increment is once per boss per lifetime. Consequence the option misses: the counter stays >0 for the ENTIRE remaining life of any boss that has ever been alerted, not only after a crash — a summoned-but-unkilled Eikthyr that de-aggroed keeps every portal in the world shut until it dies. Because bosses are persistent ZDOs that stay in the world when unloaded, the watchdog's test 'does any live boss ZDO exist' will find that boss and refuse to reset, so it does not fix the common case. A workable condition: reset when no boss-prefab ZDO with s_bossCount==true is both s_alert==true (owner-written, :27249-27251) AND inside any connected peer's active area (ZNetScene.InActiveArea vs peer.GetRefPos, cf. IsInPeerActiveArea :76887-76898); and when resetting also clear s_bossCount on those boss ZDOs, otherwise the latch makes the reset a one-way ratchet and that boss can never re-close portals when re-engaged. Server-side boss identification needs a hard-coded boss prefab-hash list (Character.m_boss is a prefab field, not a ZDO key). Also: NoBossPortals is ordinal < NonServerOption, so ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey → RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022) → GlobalKeyAdd (:113483-113517) writes it into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys — a .fwl world-modifier edit that survives mod removal; the claim that activeBosses (> NonServerOption) is .db-only is correct. SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,float) (:115933-115936) formats with InvariantCulture as claimed; RPC_SetGlobalKey's Contains check is case-mismatched against the lower-cased store so every call re-broadcasts keys — only write when v>0.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All citations verified. TeleportWorld.Teleport :143528-143532 blocks on NoBossPortals && (GetBossEvent()!=null || activeBosses>0) — client-only code. Teleport.Interact :143355 blocks on NoBossPortals && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos); Character.InInterior(Vector3) is y>3000 :4538-4541; Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon :133631-133645 needs EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss() with non-empty m_bossEvent and same XZ zone. RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent :106939-106950 reads EnemyHud. Character.OnDeath :3161-3165 is the only decrement, guarded on s_bossCount. ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,float) :115933-115936, GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys,out float) :115958-115966. Enforcement client-honoured is correct.

catalog.name: Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction
catalog.oneLine: Use the server-authoritative RandEventSystem raid state to lock only the portals inside the active event radius, so a base under attack cannot be escaped or reinforced through its own gate.
catalog.howItWorks: Raid state is genuinely server-side, unlike the boss gate. `RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent` runs under `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return;` (:106838-106843) and `FixedUpdate` evaluates `IsAnyPlayerInEventArea(m_randomEvent)` (:106797) which itself iterates `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:107111-107121) — so the server already reasons about raid geometry using character ZDOs, exactly the data a server-only mod has. `RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent()` is public (:107373-107376) and returns the live `RandomEvent` carrying `m_name`, `m_pos`, `m_time`, `m_duration` (default 60f) and `m_eventRange` (default 96f, :107451). `IsInsideRandomEventArea` is `position.y <= 3000f && Utils.DistanceXZ(position, re.m_pos) < re.m_eventRange` (:106829-106836) — trivially reimplementable. The engine ticks at 1Hz: read the current event; if non-null and its name matches a configured raid allowlist (or any event with a non-empty `m_spawn` list), compute the set of portal ZDOs from `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` whose `GetPosition()` falls inside `m_eventRange` of `m_pos`; force-disconnect exactly those, vaulting their wiring; when the event ends (`GetCurrentRandomEvent()` returns null, or `SetRandomEvent(null,...)` at :106800) restore them. Because the lock is a strict subset of portals it is far cheaper than a global lockdown and produces no world-wide save churn — though note `DirtyPortalObjects` has no per-portal granularity, so ANY portal write still rewrites the whole portal chunk at the next save. Optionally pair with a `RPC_DamageText` at each affected portal reading 'SEALED — RAID' so the reason is legible. A stricter variant locks the whole tag GROUP any affected portal belongs to, so the defenders cannot simply walk 100m to a second gate on the same network.
catalog.playerExperience: A 'The ground is shaking' troll raid starts on a player's base. Every portal within 96m of the raid centre visibly goes dark — hover flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected`, the ring stops glowing, orange text floats above it reading 'SEALED — RAID'. The player cannot bail out through the portal and cannot summon a friend in through it; they fight or they run on foot. Portals elsewhere in the world are entirely unaffected. Sixty seconds later the raid ends and the same portals light back up with their original partners, which is the vault doing its job. A player mid-transit when the raid started still arrives — nothing can interrupt `UpdateTeleport`.
failureModes: `m_eventRange` and `m_duration` are Inspector values per event; the 96f/60f in the class are defaults and the shipped raids may differ. Read them off the live `RandomEvent` rather than hard-coding.

Locking on raid start and unlocking on raid end means a raid that is cancelled by `SetRandomEvent(null, ...)` for any reason (a `SetEvent` RPC from a client, an admin command, `m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea` logic) fires the unlock path — which is correct, but the reconciler must be level-triggered off `GetCurrentRandomEvent()` rather than edge-triggered off an event-start hook.

`RPC_SetEvent` is a routed RPC (:106781) and on a non-server it sets the local event; the server's own `RandEventSystem` is authoritative and `SendCurrentRandomEvent` broadcasts it (:106952-106962). A client cannot forge a raid on the server, but do not read raid state from anything a client could influence.

Portals just outside the radius become the obvious escape hatch, which may be the intended tactical texture or may be seen as a loophole. The tag-group variant closes it at the cost of surprising players whose unaffected remote portal also goes dark.
Frequent short raids mean frequent portal-chunk dirtying and therefore a full portal-chunk rewrite on every save. On a large world that is the dominant cost of this feature.
Does not and cannot stop a raided player from logging out, which is the actual escape most players use.
openQuestions: Do the shipped raid events actually use the class-default `m_eventRange = 96f`? Inspector data. IN-GAME CHECK: log `RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent()`'s `m_name`, `m_pos`, `m_eventRange` and `m_duration` during a live raid on the dedicated server.

Is `RandEventSystem.instance` reliably non-null on a headless server at the time the subsystem's first tick runs? `Start` registers the `SetEvent` RPC at :106781. IN-GAME CHECK: null-guard and log on the first 60 ticks.
corrections: Subset locking interacts with vanilla Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100628): the out-of-radius partner is torn down by phase 1 (:100601) and both are re-paired by phase 2 within 5-10s; ConnectPortals must be skipped or FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100663-100677) filtered, and the vault must hold both ends.

Raid end is not time-bounded: RandomEvent.Update (:107521-107530) pauses m_time while no player is in the area (m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea default true); a raid everyone leaves keeps its portals sealed until someone returns. m_duration/m_eventRange are per-event data, not fixed 60s/96m.
Also read RandEventSystem.GetActiveEvent (:107378) for admin-forced events (m_forcedEvent :106753); GetCurrentRandomEvent returns only random events.
DamageText 'SEALED — RAID' persists at most 3s (TextType.Bonus :46439-46441); re-send while a player is within 30m.
Effort should be medium-large given ConnectPortals suppression/filtering and two-ended vaulting.

`m_eventRange = 96f` and `m_duration = 60f` are C# field initialisers (:107451, :107445), not the values raids actually use — per-event values come from the RandEventSystem asset, which is not in the decompile. Always read `re.m_eventRange` / `re.m_duration` from the live RandomEvent; the 'sixty seconds later' player-experience line is a default, not a guarantee.

`m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea = true` (:107449): RandomEvent.Update :107521-107537 does not advance m_time while no character ZDO is inside the area, so a raid (and therefore the lock) persists indefinitely if all defenders leave the area. Document it or add a wall-clock cap on the lock.
`m_forcedEvent` (boss-fight music events) is set client-locally from EnemyHud and never reaches the server — only m_randomEvent is usable.

Ownership: the server's connection write propagates without an ownership claim (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77076-77140 applies purely on DataRevision, no owner check), and any server-held ownership of a portal inside a peer's active area is handed to that peer within 2s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76925 (portals are in FindObjects results :77376). Do not rely on SetOwner sticking; rely on revision and re-assert.
`Game.ConnectPortals` tears down and re-pairs by tag every 5s :100589-100626; without the prereq suppressing phase 2 for vaulted portals the raid lock is undone within 5s.
evidence: RandomEvent fields :107441-107500 (m_duration :107445, m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea :107449, m_eventRange :107451, m_spawn :107498); RandomEvent.Update :107521-107537
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Raid state is genuinely server-authoritative: UpdateRandomEvent early-outs on !IsServer (:106838-106843); FixedUpdate evaluates IsAnyPlayerInEventArea (:106797) over ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS (:107111-107121); IsInsideRandomEventArea is the stated y<=3000 && DistanceXZ<m_eventRange test (:106829-106836); GetCurrentRandomEvent is public (:107373-107376) and RandomEvent.m_pos/m_time/m_name/m_eventRange/m_duration/m_spawn are public fields (:107437-107508). The route-lock is server-owned and a vanilla client honours it (client TeleportWorld.TargetFound :144380 reads the ZDO connection). What the option gets wrong: (1) Vanilla Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100628) is not a passive bystander for a SUBSET lock. Nulling only the in-radius portal makes phase 1 tear down the out-of-radius partner (predicate `target.connection == None` at :100601) and phase 2 then re-pairs both (same tag, both None) within 5-10s. Unless ConnectPortals is Harmony-skipped for the duration or FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100663-100677) is filtered to exclude locked portals, the lock lasts seconds. The vault must record both ends, and the design must state which suppression it uses (global skip = no new pairings anywhere while any raid runs). (2) Event lifetime is not 'sixty seconds': RandomEvent.Update (:107521-107530) only advances m_time while a player is in the area (m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea=true default), so if every player leaves the radius the raid — and the seal — persists indefinitely until someone returns; m_duration/m_eventRange are per-event prefab data, 60f/96f are only class defaults. (3) Admin-forced events (m_forcedEvent, :106753, set via the console 'event' command) are not returned by GetCurrentRandomEvent; on a dedicated server GetActiveEvent (:107378) returns only the forced event (the m_localPlayer branch at :106812 is dead). Read both. (4) 'SEALED — RAID' floating text lives 3s max (DamageText TextType.Bonus :46439-46441) and must be re-sent. (5) Mid-transit arrival claim is correct (Player.UpdateTeleport :15329-15378 has no abort). Effort 'medium' is optimistic once the ConnectPortals interaction and both-end vaulting are included.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Raid state is genuinely server-authoritative: RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent :106838-106843 early-returns unless IsServer; FixedUpdate :106793-106802 evaluates IsAnyPlayerInEventArea(m_randomEvent) which iterates ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS() (ZNet :81024; RandEventSystem :107111-107121); IsInsideRandomEventArea :106829-106836 is y<=3000 && DistanceXZ < m_eventRange; GetCurrentRandomEvent :107373-107376 is public and returns m_randomEvent; SetRandomEvent :107083-107109 and SendCurrentRandomEvent :106952-106962 match; RPC_SetEvent :106964-106977 is ignored on the server so clients cannot spoof raid state. ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648 and the no-per-portal-granularity claim (GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77632 clones every portal when DirtyPortalObjects) are correct. The lock is route-form (connection field), so server-enforced holds, subject to the Force-Disconnect prereq suppressing Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine :100580-100587.

catalog.name: Biome and Region Restricted Networks
catalog.oneLine: Enforce that a portal may only pair with a partner in an allowed biome or region, implemented as a server-side tag-namespace rewrite so vanilla's own pairing does the enforcing.
catalog.howItWorks: Do not fight `Game.ConnectPortals` — recruit it. Its phase 1 tears down any link whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601) and phase 2 only pairs portals whose tags are byte-identical (`FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` :100669, ordinal `string !=`, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant). So enforcing a region rule reduces to: rewrite `s_tag` so that portals in different allowed-regions can never share a tag string. On a slow tick (30s) walk `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`, and for each portal derive its region key purely from procedural world data — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos.x, pos.z)` (:151725) for biome, or a configured named rectangle/circle list for hand-drawn regions. Collider-based classification is impossible server-side (the reference position is pinned at 1e6, so `ZoneSystem.GetGroundData`/`IsBlocked` always return their no-hit fallbacks), and `WorldGenerator` is the only viable terrain oracle. Then compute the desired tag as `userTag` (unchanged) if the portal's region is in the same allowed-group as its current partner, or `userTag + regionSuffix` when the rule requires namespacing. Write with `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, newTag)` (:73721 / :78617 — no length cap, no validation at this layer), then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` EXPLICITLY, because a tag-only write does NOT set that flag (only `SetConnection`, `AddIfPortal` and `HandleDestroyedZDO` do) and the rename is otherwise silently lost at the next world save. Finally call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` once to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5s. Record the original user tag in the vault so the rule can be lifted. THE SUFFIX MUST KEEP THE TOTAL AT OR BELOW 10 CHARACTERS or a player who opens the rename dialog will truncate it — `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) sets `m_inputField.characterLimit` and the field is pre-filled with the existing tag. A single-character suffix (`Base~M` for Meadows) is the safe shape. An alternative that avoids tag mutation entirely is to leave tags alone and instead patch `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` with a postfix that overwrites `__result` with null when the proposed partner's region is disallowed — a much smaller, lower-risk change that leaves all user-visible state untouched, at the cost of leaving one portal permanently unpaired with no explanation visible to the player.
catalog.playerExperience: A player builds a portal in the Mistlands tagged 'ore' and another in the Meadows also tagged 'ore'. Under a 'no cross-biome-tier travel' rule the two never connect: both hover as `$piece_portal_unconnected` and stay dark. If the tag-suffix variant is used, the player sees their tags have become 'ore~M' and 'ore~m' and can work out why; if the FindRandomUnconnectedPortal variant is used they see nothing at all and will file a bug. A second Mistlands portal tagged 'ore' pairs with the first immediately. An admin-run `listregions` style report shows which portals are in which region group and which are orphaned by the rule.
failureModes: `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening, and biome boundaries are fractal — a portal built exactly on a Meadows/BlackForest seam can flip region between ticks and thrash its tag. Hysteresis (require N consecutive samples of the new region) and a snap-to-first-observed-region cache are mandatory.
Tag rewriting is visible, surprising, and collides with the 10-char client cap. A player re-saving a truncated tag corrupts the namespacing and silently re-enables a forbidden pairing.

`Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 will tear down an existing cross-region link the moment the tags diverge, stranding a player who was relying on it, with no warning. Announce before applying a new region rule.

The `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` postfix variant is a private-method patch (`AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")`) and will silently stop applying if the signature changes; wrap in SafePatch.
Rich-text or unusual characters in the suffix are stripped from the hover label by `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459), so the suffix must be plain.
A tag-only write that forgets `SetDirtyPortals()` looks correct in memory and in the live game and vanishes at the next world save — a classic silent data-loss bug.
citations: ZDO.SetConnection is the only auto-dirty path — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656-73666
openQuestions: Does `GuiInputField` clamp a programmatically assigned `.text` to `characterLimit`? `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.text = existingTag` AFTER setting `characterLimit = 10` (:61515-61522). If it clamps, any server-written tag longer than 10 chars is truncated the instant a player opens the dialog. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client, re-read `s_tag`.

How stable is `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` at a fixed coordinate across server restarts? It is pure and seed-driven so it should be bit-identical, but confirm before keying persistent state on it. IN-GAME CHECK: log the biome for 100 portal positions before and after a restart and diff.
corrections: Normalise tags in a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) rather than a 30s tick; otherwise a fresh rename can be cross-region paired for 5-10s and used.

The FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix-null variant is nondeterministic and over-blocks (random single pick at :100677); replace with a prefix that filters the candidate list by region and keeps the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal exclusion.
Suffixing must strip its own prior suffix before re-deriving (rename dialog is pre-filled with the suffixed tag, client :144223); user tags of 9-10 characters cannot be suffixed without truncation.
Rewritten tags are saved to disk and persist after mod removal; the vault must replay at least once to lift the rule.
Portals in interiors (y>3000) are not classifiable by WorldGenerator.GetBiome; assign an explicit region.
Server tag writes can revision-collide with a concurrent client RPC_SetTag (client RPC_ZDOData :77217); rare.

Enforcement gap: a 30s rewrite tick vs the 5s ConnectPortalsCoroutine :100580-100587 means an owner-side rename (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :143583-143600 — no server hook, arrives only as ZDO sync) can get a cross-region pair connected for up to ~35s. To be server-enforced the backstop must live at pairing time: a Harmony PREFIX on private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664 that removes disallowed candidates (or a prefix on ConnectPortals that runs the rewrite first). The described POSTFIX that nulls __result is wrong: the method picks `list[Random.Range(0,list.Count)]` :100679, so a postfix would non-deterministically block or allow depending on which candidate the RNG chose that tick.

`zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` is neither needed nor durable: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77076-77140 applies incoming ZDO data purely on DataRevision with no owner check (on both client and server), so the server's Set propagates regardless; and ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76925 hands server-owned portals inside a peer's active area to that peer within 2s. While the server transiently owns a portal, a player's rename (ZNetView.InvokeRPC routed to the owner) lands on a server with no ZNetView instance and is silently dropped.

Revision race: if the client renames in the same window as the server rewrite, both bump from the same DataRevision and each side ignores the other's update (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision` :77110); the next server rewrite (higher revision) wins. The 30s tick must be treated as the convergence bound, not 'immediate'.
Blank tags: two empty-tag portals pair in vanilla (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal matches "" == ""); a suffix turns "" into "~M", which is visible and may surprise players.
`Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal`, `SetConnection`, `RPC_SetConnection` are all private on Game (:100636-100660, :100664) — Harmony can patch them, but there is no public API; say so.

Nothing here survives a world save unless SetDirtyPortals is called, as the option says — confirmed by reading the dirty-flag setters; note vanilla itself has the same gap for client-originated renames (RPC_ZDOData -> AddIfPortal :77732-77752 does not dirty an already-registered portal), which is why ConnectPortals' forced second-tick commit (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals -> ForceSetConnection -> local SetConnection) is what normally saves pairings.

catalog.name: Per-Network Quarantine-Tag Lockdown
catalog.oneLine: Lock a single named portal network by rewriting its members' tags to per-portal-unique quarantine strings, so vanilla's own reconciler tears the links down and can never rebuild them.
catalog.howItWorks: This is the self-reinforcing alternative to nulling connections, and it needs no `Game.ConnectPortals` suppression at all. To lock the network named `mine`: for every portal in `GetPortalList()` whose `s_tag` equals `mine`, vault `(position, "mine")`, then `SetOwner(sessionID)` and `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, uniquePerPortalString)` where the string is distinct for every member (e.g. `"!lk" + shortHash(position)` kept at or under 10 characters), then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` and `ForceSendZDO`. Vanilla then does the enforcement for free: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 sees each portal's partner carrying a different `s_tag` and calls `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` at :100603 within 5s, and phase 2 can never re-pair them because `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100669) requires exact tag equality and no two quarantine strings match. The lock is therefore stable under vanilla's own 5s reconciler with zero Harmony patches on `Game.ConnectPortals`, which is a major robustness and compatibility win over the force-disconnect approach. Unlocking is the reverse tag write plus one `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` call; because every member returns to the shared tag simultaneously, phase 2 re-pairs them — RANDOMLY, so the original partner assignment is not preserved unless the vault also re-asserts connections explicitly after the tag restore. Note phase 1's `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` is NOT forced (:100603, no `forceImmediateConnection`), so for a portal owned by an online peer the clear is routed as `RPC_SetConnection` to that client and the server's own copy still reads the old value for at least one more tick — meaning the teardown takes 2+ ticks (up to ~10s) near a player rather than 5s. If the lock must be instant, do the tag write AND an explicit forced `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` with `SetOwner` in the same pass.
catalog.playerExperience: An admin runs the network-lock command for `mine`. Within about five seconds (or ten if a player is standing next to one) every portal on that network goes dark and its hover text changes from `$piece_portal_tag:"mine" [$piece_portal_connected]` to `$piece_portal_tag:"!lk3f2a" [$piece_portal_unconnected]` — visibly and legibly quarantined, unlike a silent connection null. Other networks are completely untouched and keep working. On unlock the tags revert to `mine` and the portals re-pair, though a player may find their mine portal now leads to a different one of the three mine portals than before unless the vault re-asserted the exact pairing.
failureModes: MUTATES USER-VISIBLE STATE. If the server crashes while quarantined and the vault is lost or not replayed, players are left with portals permanently named `!lk3f2a`. Strictly worse failure surface than connection-nulling, which at least leaves tags intact.

The 10-char truncation hazard is acute here: a confused player will absolutely open the rename dialog on a `!lk3f2a` portal. Keep quarantine tags ≤10 chars and expect some to be manually renamed by players mid-lock, which silently removes that portal from the vault's ability to restore it.

Unlock re-pairs randomly via `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100678) unless connections are explicitly re-asserted from the vault after the tag restore. A 2-member network is unaffected; a 4-member one can come back completely rewired.
A 3+ member network unlocked back to a shared tag strands exactly one member (vanilla behaviour, :100607-100622), and which one is arbitrary and unstable across restarts.
Tag writes do not set `DirtyPortalObjects` automatically — forgetting the explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` loses both the lock AND the restore across a save.

A player can defeat the lock on a portal they own by simply renaming it back to `mine` through the vanilla dialog; the mod must re-assert on a tick, and that re-assert is a tag write that dirties the portal chunk every time.
openQuestions: How quickly does a client already standing at a portal pick up a server-side `s_tag` change in its hover text? `GetTagInfo` is read fresh in `GetHoverText` every frame the player hovers (:143455), so it should be immediate once the ZDO arrives. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and time the hover-text change and the connected/unconnected flip.
corrections: Not self-reinforcing against players: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, every 2 s) transfers server-owned portals to any nearby peer, after which vanilla RPC_SetTag (:143571-143585) can restore 'mine' or set any tag with no server hook; add a re-assert loop keyed on the vault and expect up to ~5-10 s transient reconnection windows.
'zero Harmony patches on Game.ConnectPortals' is true only for the reconciler interaction; enforcement still requires the mod's own periodic tag/ownership re-assert (not free of a runtime loop).

ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals is mandatory for tag persistence: IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) -> SetDirtySector (:76694-76699) only dirties the spatial chunk, and GetSaveClonePerChunk rewrites the ChunkPortal file only when DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632).
The 10-char TextInput cap (:143482) is client-UI only and does not constrain mod-written tags; keep quarantine strings short purely for hover-text legibility.
Unlock re-pairing is random (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100677) — the vault must explicitly ForceSetConnection both directions to restore original partners.

Quarantine strings must be >10 characters (e.g. 12-16), not <=10: vanilla clients cannot type tags longer than the TextInput charLimit of 10 (:143482; client :61572-61583), which is what stops a player retagging a spare portal to the displayed quarantine string and pairing into the locked network.

The lock is not self-sustaining against vanilla clients: nearby peers receive ownership every 2 s (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926, portals included via FindObjects :77376-77381) and RPC_SetTag runs locally on the owner (:143587-143602) with no packets; a periodic tag reassert (level-triggered) is required, plus tolerance for RPC_ZDOData revision races (:77112-77135) that can briefly overwrite the server's tag.

Because the mod SetOwner(sessionID)s before the tag write, phase-1 SetConnection takes the local branch (ZNet.GetPeer(sessionID) == null at :100639-100641), so teardown is normally immediate at the next 5 s pass; the routed 2-tick path only occurs when ReleaseNearbyZDOS handed ownership to a nearby player within the prior 2 s.

Hover text format is '$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"<tag>" [<state>]' and the tag passes through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC before display (:143453-143463, :143563-143576); pick quarantine strings that cannot trip the word filter.

Unlock must re-assert the vaulted pairs via zdo.SetOwner(sessionID)+zdo.SetConnection (public ZDO API) or the original partner assignment is lost to Random.Range in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100678).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified line-by-line. Game.ConnectPortals (SERVER :100589-100626) phase 1 nulls a portal whose partner's s_tag differs (:100600-100603, unforced SetConnection) and phase 2 pairs only exact-tag-equal unconnected portals via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679); the coroutine is started under ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:100071-100074) with no local-player dependency. ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) bumps DataRevision; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is required because IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) only dirties the spatial chunk and the ChunkPortal file is only rewritten when DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632). SetConnection's deferred branch (:100637-100651): after the mod's SetOwner(sessionID), GetPeer(sessionID) is null so the local path is taken. GetHoverText (:143452-143462) does show the tag through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC, so the quarantine string is visible. THE CLAIM 'can never rebuild them' with 'zero patches' is FALSE against players, not just the reconciler: (a) ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925), invoked every 2 s for every peer (:76880-76883), hands a server-owned portal to any peer whose active area contains it, because IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, serverSessionID) (:76887-76891) tests against the pinned (1e6,0,1e6) reference and returns false; (b) once a client owns it, vanilla TeleportWorld.Interact (:143470-143483, ward-gated only by PrivateArea.CheckAccess client-side) -> SetText (:143560-143566) -> RPC_SetTag (:143571-143585) rewrites s_tag locally with zero validation and zero packets to the server beyond the ZDO sync; (c) two quarantined portals retagged to the same string re-pair on the next 5 s phase-2 pass. While the SERVER owns the portal a client retag is a ZDO-targeted routed RPC that ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC drops for lack of a ZNetScene instance (FindInstance null), but ownership is lost within 2 s of a player standing near it. The lock therefore needs a level-triggered re-assert loop (compare s_tag to vault, rewrite + SetOwner) and must accept reconnection windows of up to one reconciler period (~5-10 s) between a player retag and the re-assert. Also: DataRevision ties (client wrote its own revision while the server wrote) make RPC_ZDOData (:77104-77112) silently ignore the other side's copy — ForceSendZDO does not bypass the revision gate — so the re-assert loop is not optional.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified: Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100594-100606) nulls a connection when the partner's s_tag differs, and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) requires exact tag equality, so per-portal-unique tags are never re-paired. Tag persistence across save/restart holds: DirtyPortalObjects forces a clone of every portal (:77621-77632) and load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) only rebuilds from hash slots, which are empty for unconnected portals. Route-form rule, so 'server-enforced' is honest. Three real defects: (1) the recommended quarantine string length is exactly backwards - the string is displayed in hover text (:143453-143463) and a vanilla client can type any tag up to 10 chars (TextInput.RequestText(...,10) at :143482; client sets m_inputField.characterLimit at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:61582), so a player with a spare portal can retag it to the displayed quarantine string and phase 2 pairs them; strings LONGER than 10 chars are untypeable by vanilla and ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73717) has no cap. (2) It is not a one-shot: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) runs every 2 s and hands ownership of portal ZDOs (portals are returned by FindObjects :77376-77381) to any peer in the active area, after which Interact->RPC_SetTag (:143587-143602) runs locally on the owner and rewrites s_tag with zero packets; and RPC_ZDOData (:77112-77135) accepts any client copy whose DataRevision exceeds the server's, so a concurrent client write can overwrite the quarantine tag. A level-triggered reassert loop is mandatory; 'zero Harmony patches' still holds. (3) The 2-tick/10 s teardown caveat is overstated for the described flow: since the mod calls SetOwner(sessionID) first, SetConnection's GetPeer(owner) returns null for the server's own id (:100637-100651) and the phase-1 clear takes the immediate local path; the routed path only applies if ReleaseNearbyZDOS re-assigned ownership to a nearby peer in the intervening <=2 s. Unlock re-pairing is random (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal uses Random.Range) - confirmed.

catalog.name: TeleportAll and DungeonBuild Policy Levers
catalog.oneLine: The two remaining portal-adjacent world-modifier keys — cargo policy and dungeon building — with their exact, commonly-misstated semantics.
catalog.howItWorks: Both are plain global-key writes with the same propagation path as NoPortals (`SetGlobalKey` → `RPC_SetGlobalKey` → `GlobalKeyAdd` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` → every client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clear-and-rebuild). TELEPORTALL (ordinal 35, :101307): read by `Inventory.IsTeleportable(bool allowAllItems)` (:68860-68880) which is reached from `Humanoid.IsTeleportable` (:8791-8794) and thence `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 4 (:143533). THE CRITICAL SEMANTIC: the method first rejects outright if ANY item has `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (:68862-68868) and only THEN honours `allowAllItems || GetGlobalKey(TeleportAll)` at :68869. So `teleportall` is emphatically NOT 'allow all cargo' — a hard-coded tier-1000 item class remains non-teleportable regardless of the key and regardless of any per-portal flag. Any feature description must carry that caveat. The key also drives visible client UI with no extra work: `InventoryGui` sets `element.m_noteleport.enabled = !item.m_shared.m_teleportable && !GetGlobalKey(TeleportAll)` (:49462) and the item tooltip appends `$item_noteleport` under the same condition (:69755), both per-refresh reads — so toggling the key live updates every vanilla client's inventory icons and tooltips instantly, which is a free and honest UX signal. DUNGEONBUILD (ordinal 34, :101306): read in the client's piece-placement validation as `!component.m_allowedInDungeons && InInterior() && !EnvMan.instance.CheckInteriorBuildingOverride() && !GetGlobalKey(DungeonBuild)` (:13353) — setting it lets vanilla clients place any piece, portals included, inside dungeons. Purely client-honoured; the server never validates placement and there is no server-side placement veto short of the SpawnGovernor-style destroy-on-arrival hook (`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` postfix + `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix). Both keys are below `NonServerOption` so both persist into the .fwl unless written with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false`, and both appear in the server-browser modifier badge on the next registration.
catalog.playerExperience: With `teleportall` set, a player opens their inventory and the little 'no teleport' badge disappears from their iron bars and tin ore in real time, with no relog — and they can carry them through a portal. With it cleared the badges reappear instantly and the next transit gives `$msg_noteleport`. Flametal-class tier-1000 items keep the badge and keep being refused either way, which will generate bug reports unless documented. With `dungeonbuild` set, a player standing in a burial chamber can place a portal inside it and it pairs normally with a surface portal on the same tag — dungeon interiors sit at the same XZ sector as the surface above (`ZoneSystem.GetZone` ignores y) so nothing about sync or pairing is special-cased.
failureModes: `TeleportAll` does not override the `m_toolTier >= 1000` rejection (:68862-68868). Advertising 'carry anything' is wrong.

Both keys are client-honoured. A modified client ignores the cargo restriction whether the key is set or not, and the server cannot detect it — player inventories are never mirrored into any ZDO, so there is no server-side audit of what was carried.
Both keys are world-modifier ordinals and therefore permanently edit `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` and the public modifier badge unless the session-only write is used.
`dungeonbuild` is global — it enables dungeon building for every piece and every player, not just portals. There is no portal-specific variant.

A portal built inside a dungeon is an ordinary portal in every respect, including being randomly paired by `Game.ConnectPortals` with any same-tag surface portal — which is usually the point, but it also means a dungeon portal participates in every lockdown and every network rule identically.
openQuestions: Which shipped items actually carry `m_toolTier >= 1000`? Inspector/ObjectDB data. IN-GAME CHECK: enumerate `ObjectDB.instance.m_items` and log every `m_itemData.m_shared.m_name` with `m_toolTier >= 1000`, so the caveat can name them.

Does the portal piece itself have `m_allowedInDungeons` set on any prefab variant? Inspector data — if true for some variant, `dungeonbuild` is unnecessary for that piece. IN-GAME CHECK: read `GetComponent<Piece>().m_allowedInDungeons` on each portal prefab.
corrections: `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false` is a parameter of the PRIVATE ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (:113480); no public SetGlobalKey overload (:115933-115946) exposes it — the RPC path always passes the default true. Session-only writes need reflection/Harmony on GlobalKeyAdd + private SendGlobalKeys(0L).
Which items carry m_toolTier >= 1000 is prefab data and cannot be confirmed from the decompile; state the code rule (:68862-68868) and verify the item list in-game.
Player placement check (:13353) sits in Player code that only runs on a client; the server assembly merely contains it.
Location.Awake places the interior at base.transform.position.y + 5000f (:133510), not zoneCenter.y + 5000.

The public ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string) routes through RPC_SetGlobalKey which calls GlobalKeyAdd(name) with canSaveToServerOptionKeys defaulted to true (:116022-116029); a session-only write requires reflection into the private GlobalKeyAdd(string,bool) followed by the private SendGlobalKeys(0L) - there is no public parameter to pass.

Which items carry m_toolTier>=1000 is prefab data not present in the decompile; state the rule ('any item with toolTier>=1000 is never teleportable') rather than naming Flametal unless verified in-game.

RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender/admin check (:116022-116029), so the same key is also writable by any client; the server-side reconciler should re-assert the intended value rather than assume it is stable.

catalog.name: Ironman and Hardcore Rulesets
catalog.oneLine: Named composite presets that combine the key levers, the disconnect lockdown and the region rules into one-line server personalities, with a single authoritative reconciler.
catalog.howItWorks: A ruleset is a named record that expands to a desired-state description, and one level-triggered reconciler drives the world toward it. Useful shapes, each expressible purely in the primitives already established: (1) NO PORTALS AT ALL — `noportals` session-only key plus a permanent force-disconnect of every portal plus a `Game.ConnectPortals` prefix returning false, so even a hacked client has no destination; optionally combined with a destroy-on-arrival cap of zero via the SpawnGovernor hook pair (`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int)` postfix to remember the id, `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` postfix to read the now-known prefab and, if it is in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, `zdo.SetOwner(sessionID)` + `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` plus a toast) so portals cannot even be built. (2) ONE-WAY OUTBOUND ONLY — every portal keeps a connection but the return leg is nulled; note this is runtime-only because `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` at load writes BOTH directions from the matched hash pair (:77879-77885), so the one-way state must be re-asserted after every world load. (3) TIERED TRAVEL — the biome-region rule with allowed-group sets keyed to boss progression, read from the `defeated_*` global keys which are genuine .db-persisted world state (`Character.OnDeath` writes `m_defeatSetGlobalKey` at :3153-3156). (4) NIGHT CURFEW — the scheduled-window engine on in-game time. (5) RAID SEAL + BOSS BLACKOUT — the raid geofence plus `nobossportals` with the watchdog. (6) CARGO IRONMAN — `teleportall` cleared and documented with the tier-1000 caveat. The reconciler must be single: every rule contributes a desired per-portal state (`Locked | Free | RegionTag(x)`), the reconciler resolves conflicts by a declared precedence (locked beats tagged beats free), and applies the minimum diff. Never let two subsystems write the same portal independently — that is how a portal ends up flapping between states at 1Hz, dirtying the portal chunk on every save.
catalog.playerExperience: An operator sets `Ruleset = Ironman` in the config and the file hot-reloads within five seconds. Every online player gets one centre-screen message: 'Server ruleset changed: Ironman — portals are disabled.' Every portal in the world goes dark and stays dark; attempting to place a new portal consumes nothing and produces a toast 'Portals are disabled on this server.' The `noportals` key also means an unmodified client that somehow reaches a connected portal still gets `$msg_blocked`. Crypt doors keep working, which the ruleset description states explicitly. Under `Tiered`, a player who has not killed Bonemass finds their Swamp portal refuses to pair with their Meadows one and the tags show a tier suffix; after the server-wide Bonemass kill the suffixes merge and the link forms on the next 5s pass.
failureModes: Composite rules multiply the conflict surface. Without a single reconciler and a declared precedence, two rules will fight over one portal every tick, producing endless `DirtyPortalObjects` churn and a full portal-chunk rewrite on every save.

The destroy-on-arrival portal cap destroys a ZDO the placing client already has a live GameObject for; whether that desyncs cleanly, leaves a ghost until the zone reloads, or refunds materials is untested for a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object.

One-way topologies are silently converted back to two-way by `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` on every world load (:77879-77885) and rings lose a link entirely because `RegenerateConnectionHashData` gives each ZDO one slot and overwrites source with target at :75474. Any non-pairwise ruleset is runtime-only and MUST be re-asserted post-load.

Tiered rules keyed on `defeated_*` keys inherit `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys`' boot-time replay: those keys are ≥ NonServerOption so they live in the .db and are restored by `ZoneSystem.Load` → `GlobalKeyAdd` (:113804-113805), which means any naive 'on key added' hook re-fires for every historical boss kill at every boot. Pre-seed an already-seen set from `OnWorldReady`, exactly as Wonderland's BossDefeatWatch does.
A ruleset change is a large, sudden, world-wide state change. Applying one without the graceful announcement sequence will strand players far from home with no warning.

Uninstalling the mod while a restrictive ruleset is engaged leaves the world in whatever state it was in — nulled connections, quarantine tags, and possibly a `noportals` key baked into the .fwl. The uninstall path must be a documented 'set Ruleset = None, wait for the reconciler, then remove'.
citations: Wonderland SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize hook pair — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70
openQuestions: Can the server destroy a client-created portal ZDO inside the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix without desyncing the placing client, which already has a live GameObject? SpawnGovernor does exactly this for creatures and ships it, but a Piece/WearNTear object may differ. IN-GAME CHECK: set a cap of 0, place a portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost disappears cleanly, persists until the zone reloads, or consumes/refunds materials.

Any per-player ruleset depends on it. IN-GAME CHECK: place a portal and confirm `s_creator` equals that player's character-ZDO `s_playerID`.
corrections: Placement is NOT free under destroy-on-arrival: Player consumes resources client-side right after TryPlacePiece (:10801-10807); the server-side destroy leaves the player minus materials. Either document the loss, or spawn refund ItemDrop ZDOs at the player's position.

Replace 'even a hacked client has no destination' with 'vanilla reconciler is suppressed; the mod's reconciler must re-null connections a modified client writes, because RPC_ZDOData (:77104-77129) accepts any higher-revision ZDO write from any peer'.
Tiered travel keys on defeated_* are world-global; rewrite playerExperience as server-wide progression, not per-player.
Session-only `noportals` requires reflection into private ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(name, false) + private SendGlobalKeys(0L) (:113480, :113463); public SetGlobalKey always persists to .fwl.

Every SetConnection in the reconciler also dirties the portal's spatial chunk via IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76699); see Mass-Rewrite verdict for the save-cost consequence.

Remove 'consumes nothing': Player consumes piece resources client-side right after TryPlacePiece (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:10801-10810) before the server sees the ZDO; a destroy-on-arrival hook cannot prevent the cost. Either document material loss, refund via server-spawned ItemDrop ZDOs, or set the piece-specific free-build key.

State enforcement per component: force-disconnect + ConnectPortals prefix + destroy-on-arrival = server-enforced (route/existence form); noportals/nobossportals/teleportall messages and inventory badges = client-honoured; tier-suffix tags = server-written but retaggable by a nearby owning vanilla client (see Quarantine-Tag verdict), so the reconciler must reassert them.

Destroy-on-arrival must evaluate in the ZDO.Deserialize postfix, not the CreateNewZDO postfix: RPC_ZDOData creates with prefab 0 and only Deserialize supplies the prefab hash (:77120-77132); AddIfPortal runs after Deserialize, so the doomed ZDO is briefly enumerated by GetPortalList until HandleDestroyedZDO removes it (:76963-76985).
Effort: large, not medium - single desired-state reconciler over lockdown, vault, region tags, schedules, raid geofence, plus config hot-reload and crash recovery.

Enforcement is also mixed, not uniformly server-enforced: the connection-level components (force-disconnect, ConnectPortals prefix, destroy-on-arrival) are route-form and server-enforced; the key-level components (noportals $msg_blocked, teleportall, tier suffixes visible in hover text) are client-honoured, and tier-suffixed tags are subject to the same nearby-owner retag hole as option 1. Effort 'medium' is optimistic for a hot-reloading single reconciler spanning five subsystems plus the vault; realistically large. Hence downgraded rather than refuted.

catalog.name: Modifier Badge Honesty
catalog.oneLine: Reconcile the fact that the public server-browser 'modifiers' badge is a boot-time snapshot that a runtime lockdown never updates, so the listing lies about the rules.
catalog.howItWorks: The badge payload is `string[] modifiers = m_world.m_startingGlobalKeys.ToArray()` passed to `ZSteamMatchmaking.instance.RegisterServer(...)`, snapshotted at registration time and re-snapshotted only on the registration-retry coroutine (visible at :79457 inside `DelayThenRegisterCoroutine`). Clients render it via `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary(m_serverListEntry.m_modifiers, ...)` (:64826-64827). Three distinct dishonesty modes follow. (A) A runtime `SetGlobalKey("noportals")` with the default `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:true` DOES add to `m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) but the badge is not re-registered, so the listing keeps saying portals are on for the rest of the session and then permanently says they are off after the next restart — including for scheduled windows that are currently open. (B) A session-only write (`canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false`) never touches `m_startingGlobalKeys`, so the badge never reflects the lockdown at all, ever. (C) A force-disconnect lockdown is not a global key in any form, so the badge can never represent it regardless. There is no supported API to re-register with fresh modifiers at runtime. The honest options are therefore all out-of-band: (1) rewrite `ZNet.instance.m_ServerName` to carry the state — but that is also snapshotted at RegisterServer, so it has the same staleness; (2) push the truth through channels that ARE live — a `ShowMessage` on `OnNewPeer`, a Discord webhook status message (Wonderland's `DiscordWebhook.Send`, fire-and-forget with a shared static HttpClient), a status file/endpoint, and the `Heartbeat` log line; (3) document in the server description that portal rules are dynamic and where to check; (4) if the operator insists the badge be truthful for a long-lived ruleset, set the key persistently and restart once so the boot-time snapshot is correct, and accept that transient windows are never represented. Additionally: `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary` returns the literal string `"Error!"` when its `m_presets` is null, so any server-side use of it for a status report must be guarded.
catalog.playerExperience: A player browsing the server list sees 'Portals: on' and joins expecting to portal home, then discovers the nightly maintenance window has every portal dark. With the mitigation, the moment they connect they get a top-left message: 'Portal network is currently CLOSED (nightly window, reopens 06:00).' The Discord channel carries the same state, and `/status` on the operator's side prints the authoritative rule set. The badge itself still says what it said at boot and is documented as doing so.
failureModes: There is genuinely no runtime re-registration API. Anything short of a restart leaves the badge stale; this is a limitation to be communicated, not engineered around.

Setting the key persistently to make the badge honest means permanently editing the world's `m_startingGlobalKeys`, which survives uninstalling the mod — trading one honesty problem for a world-integrity problem.
`GetWorldModifierSummary` returns `"Error!"` if `m_presets` is null (prefab not initialised), so a naive status report can publish that string.

The `OnNewPeer` announcement is the only channel guaranteed to reach a joining player, and it competes with every other join-time message; a player who dismisses it has no way to re-query state from a vanilla client except by walking to a portal.
A force-disconnect lockdown is invisible to every metadata channel by construction. Operators will forget it is on.

catalog.name: Destination Safety Validator
catalog.oneLine: A purely procedural server-side check that refuses to wire a portal to an unsafe coordinate — underwater, in lava, underground, inside a dungeon interior, or off the map edge.
catalog.howItWorks: Every collider-based helper is dead server-side (the reference position is pinned to (1e6,0,1e6) at :100465 so no Heightmap collider exists near real coordinates; `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` :115604 raycasts against `m_solidRayMask` and silently returns `height = 0f, false`; `GetSolidHeight`, `GetGroundHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `GetGroundData` and the instance `IsLava(Vector3)` :115647 all return their no-hit fallbacks WITHOUT throwing or logging). The validator must therefore be pure `WorldGenerator` math plus the one static lava test. The checks, in order of cheapness: (1) OFF-MAP — reject when `x*x + z*z > 110250000f` (`WorldGenerator.waterEdgeSqr`); `GetBiomeHeight` returns `-2f * GetHeightMultiplier()` = -400 beyond 10500m. (2) INTERIOR — reject when `pos.y > 3000f`, which is vanilla's own test (`Character.InInterior(Vector3)` :4538-4541); dungeon interiors are instantiated at `zoneCenter + 5000y` by `Location.Awake` (:133505-133515). (3) UNDERWATER — reject when `WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) < 30f` (sea level is `ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel = 30f`). (4) LAVA — reject when `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(pos, 0.6f)` (:115637-115645), which is static, biome-gates to Ashlands first and then tests `mask.a > lavaValue` from `GetBiomeHeight`; NEVER use `ZoneSystem.instance.IsLava` because it goes through the dead raycast path and returns `defaultTrue` on a miss. (5) UNDERGROUND — reject when `pos.y < WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) - tolerance`; note this is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening so a ±2m tolerance is mandatory. (6) SLOPE — reject when `WorldGenerator.instance.GetNormal(new Vector2(x,z), r).y` is below a threshold, or use `GetTerrainDelta(center, radius, out delta, out slopeDir)` (:152364-152390), which is the exact roughness test vanilla uses for location siting. A fast pre-filter for (3) is the `AltBiomeWorldData` grid: `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` is an O(1) 12m-resolution cached height. Crucially, the validator governs what the mod WIRES, not what the client does on arrival. What the client does is fixed: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` computes `pos = targetPos + (targetRot * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` (:143542-143545) and passes `distantTeleport: true` (:143546). With `distantTeleport:true` the teleport can never strand — `Player.UpdateTeleport` force-lands at `ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(target) + 0.5f` at t=15s (:15360-15366). With `distantTeleport:false` (which vanilla portals never use, but a mod-issued forced teleport might) a floor-find failure instead rubber-bands the player to `m_teleportFromPos` with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked` (:15368-15374). So: always use `distantTeleport:true` for any mod-issued teleport, and use the validator to avoid wiring somewhere the player would merely be *unhappy* to arrive, since arrival itself is guaranteed.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible in the normal case. Where it bites: an admin tries to wire a hub to a coordinate the validator rejects and gets a console line 'Refused: destination at (1234, 18.2, -5610) is below sea level (terrain height 18.2, water 30)'. A server-fabricated anchor portal is never placed in an Ashlands lava field or 40m inside a mountain. A player pointed at a far unvisited region still experiences the standard vanilla behaviour: black screen, at least 8 seconds, then arrival — and if the zone is slow to generate, a hard landing on solid ground at 15 seconds rather than a fall or a stranding.
failureModes: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGroundHeight/GetSolidHeight/FindFloor/IsBlocked/IsLava(Vector3)` all COMPILE and RUN on a dedicated server and silently return their no-hit fallback. A `GetGroundHeight` that hands back `p.y` unchanged looks like a valid answer and is the single easiest way to ship a broken validator.

`WorldGenerator` is blind to player terraforming and to location flattening, so a portal on a levelled building platform can be misjudged as underground and a portal in a dug-out pit as above ground. Tolerances must be generous and the validator must be advisory for existing portals, blocking only for mod-fabricated destinations.

`mask.a` from `GetHeight(x, z, out Color mask)` means lava ONLY in the Ashlands; in Mistlands and Deep North that channel carries an unrelated value. Always go through `IsLavaPreHeightmap`, which biome-gates first.
`GetTerrainDelta` uses `UnityEngine.Random` for its 10 samples (:152364-152390) and is therefore non-deterministic between calls — do not use it for a stable accept/reject boundary without averaging.

The exit offset uses the DESTINATION portal's own `m_exitDistance` (a compiled Inspector field, :143413) and `+Vector3.up` — the mod cannot tune it, so a destination validated as safe at the ZDO position can still put the player 1m forward into a wall. Validate the exit point, not just the anchor.

`ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` (:113424) omits the 'vehicle' layer that `BaseAI` explicitly adds (:25909), so even client-side `FindFloor` cannot see a ship hull — landing a traveller on a deck is not something vanilla's teleport can do at all.
citations: Player.UpdateTeleport 8s gate, FindFloor, 15s force-land, non-distant rubber-band — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15378
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client reliably complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-visited, ungenerated zone within the 15s fallback on low-end hardware? The 8s/IsAreaReady gate and the 15s force-land are clear in code but terrain-generation latency is empirical. IN-GAME CHECK: wire a portal 8km into unexplored Ashlands, time the black screen, and confirm no fall damage and no `$msg_portal_blocked`.

How large is the practical error between `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` and the actual placed terrain height at a built-up base? IN-GAME CHECK: sample 50 existing portal positions and compare `zdo.GetPosition().y` against `GetHeight(x,z)`.
corrections: 'With distantTeleport:true the teleport can never strand' is overstated: UpdateTeleport (:15351-15354) waits for ZNetScene.IsAreaReady without any timeout, and the 15 s force-land (:15360-15366) is reached only after the area is ready and FindFloor fails. Underground/off-map destinations can still leave a player black-screened; treat the validator as arrival-critical.

Player.TeleportTo requires m_nview.IsOwner() (:15302-15306) — a mod-issued teleport must go through the routed RPC path (RPC_TeleportPlayer / 'RPC_TeleportTo'), not a direct call; the 2 s cooldown gate (:15311-15314) also applies.

AltBiomeWorldData off-map cells store -1000f (:92444), and the grid is [x,z] indexed (:92450); treat < 30f uniformly as water/off-map.

Enforcement: admin-facing-only, not server-enforced - the validator constrains mod-issued wiring only; vanilla pairings and player-chosen destinations are untouched unless the reconciler also tears down pairs that fail validation.

WorldGenerator.GetTerrainDelta (:152364-152390) uses UnityEngine.Random.insideUnitCircle for 10 samples - nondeterministic; seed or replace with a fixed sample pattern if results must be reproducible. Do not confuse with the private ZoneSystem.GetTerrainDelta at :115469.

With distantTeleport:true the 15 s force-land uses GetSolidHeight, so an underwater destination puts the player on the seabed, not stranded but submerged; the validator's sea-level check is therefore about comfort, as stated.
Character.InInterior(Vector3) is static (:4538); call it without an instance.
