catalog.name: Mass-Rewrite Spike Control and Save-Bloat Budget
catalog.oneLine: Bound the per-tick portal writes and the resulting network and save cost, because a naive world-wide lockdown floods every peer's sync queue and forces a full portal-chunk rewrite.
catalog.howItWorks: THE NETWORK COST. `ZDO.SetConnection` bumps DataRevision (:73660), which makes `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` (:76003-76015) true for that ZDO for every peer. `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` performs NO delta encoding — it writes uid + OwnerRevision + DataRevision + owner + position (38 bytes) followed by a full `ZDO.Serialize` of every field, per peer, per send (:77053-77062) — and `SendZDOToPeers2` services ONE peer per `ZDOMan.Update` behind a 0.05s timer (:76837-76861) against a 10240-byte send-queue cap (:77010-77016). A portal ZDO carries prefab, position, rotation, connection, `s_tag` and `s_tagauthor`, so roughly 80-120 bytes. Nulling 500 portals is ~50KB per peer, i.e. ~5 full sweeps, i.e. ~0.25s per peer serialised round-robin — and `ForceSendZDO` pushes all of them to the HEAD of every peer's queue, displacing legitimate traffic for that whole period. MITIGATION: process at most N portals per tick (Wonderland's `StructureUpkeep` caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep after a first pass over a long-running world turned up thousands of dirty ZDOs at once); use `ForceSendZDO` only for portals within a peer's likely interest radius and let the rest ride the normal sweep; and exploit idempotence — `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` returns false and writes nothing when type AND target are both unchanged (:74951-74960), so `ZDO.SetConnection` neither bumps the revision nor generates traffic, making a high-frequency re-assert loop genuinely free as long as nothing has drifted. THE SAVE COST. `DirtyPortalObjects` has NO per-portal granularity: one `SetConnection(Portal, ...)` anywhere sets the flag (:73661-73664) and `GetSaveClonePerChunk` then deep-clones EVERY portal in the world into the ChunkPortal bucket (:77621-77632), with no `Persistent` filter, on the main thread inside the save freeze. So the marginal save cost of locking one portal equals the cost of locking all of them; there is no incentive to batch for save reasons, only for network reasons. Budget accordingly: measure `m_portalObjects` total count at `OnWorldReady` and surface it in the Heartbeat line, because clone cost scales with it. THE CPU COST per write is negligible — `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so no re-bucketing happens, and `IncreaseDataRevision` → `SetDirtySector` is skipped for the portal path. The real per-write tail is that `SetDirtyChunks` inserts up to 4 ChunkIndex entries per dirty persistent ZDO, which portals avoid.
catalog.playerExperience: Operator-facing. Without the budget, engaging a world-wide lockdown on a 500-portal server produces a visible multi-second hitch for every connected player — position updates stall, creatures freeze, and the server log shows the send queue saturated. With the budget, the lockdown rolls out over ~10 seconds portal by portal (which is fine, because the announcement already gave a grace period) and nobody notices anything except the portals going dark in waves.
failureModes: A rolling lockdown means a window during which some portals are locked and some are not — a player can beat the rollout by sprinting to a not-yet-locked gate. If atomicity matters, set the `noportals` key FIRST (one small broadcast, instant, covers all vanilla clients) and then roll out the disconnect behind it.

`ForceSendZDO(ZDOID)` pushes to every peer; the single-peer overload `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)` (:77714) is the targeted form and is internally server-guarded. Using the broadcast form for hundreds of portals is the main amplifier.

Idempotent re-asserts are free ONLY when nothing changed. A tamper loop where a client keeps writing the connection back turns the re-assert into a real write every tick, with full serialisation cost per peer. Rate-limit the response and escalate to a kick rather than a write war.

There is no way to save a subset of portals. Any portal mutation costs a full portal-chunk clone at the next save. On a very large world that clone happens inside the synchronous `PrepareSave` and is directly additive to the save freeze.

Measuring the wrong thing: `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh `List<ZDO>` on every call (:77648-77656). Calling it per tick to check the budget is itself a cost; use the live `GetPortals()` dictionary (:77643-77646) for hot paths as `PositionWatch` does.
citations: ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portals from normal chunks — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572
openQuestions: How many portals does a real long-running server actually have, and what does the ChunkPortal clone cost inside PrepareSave at that scale? IN-GAME CHECK: log `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList().Count` and Stopwatch `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` with and without `DirtyPortalObjects` set.

What is the real serialized size of one portal ZDO on the wire? IN-GAME CHECK: instrument `ZDO.Serialize` for a portal and log the package size, to replace the 80-120 byte estimate with a measurement.
catalog.id: lockdown-safety:Mass-Rewrite Spike Control and Save-Bloat Budget
corrections: Portal writes do NOT avoid SetDirtyChunks: IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) -> ZDOMan.SetDirtySector (:76694-76699) -> SetDirtyChunks(GetSectorIndex()) for every Persistent ZDO; only ZDO.SetSector (:73752-73756) has the portal early-return. Each portal write dirties its spatial chunk, and AddObjectsPerChunk re-clones every persistent ZDO in every dirty chunk (:77556-77578). Save cost scales with distinct chunks touched per save interval — batching DOES matter for save reasons.
'Marginal save cost of locking one portal equals locking all' holds only for the ChunkPortal file; the spatial-chunk clone cost is per touched chunk.

The idempotent re-assert loop is free only if SetOwner is not re-issued each tick; ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s) flips ownership near players and OwnerRevision bumps (:73842-) re-trigger ShouldSend.
ForceSendZDO reaches peers that have never received the portal (ShouldSend true on miss, :76003-76015) — the flood is world-wide per peer, confirming the need for interest-radius filtering.

ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) always calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector -> SetDirtyChunks for Persistent ZDOs (:76694-76722); portals are NOT exempt. Each portal write dirties the portal's regular chunk (4 ChunkIndex sizes), and AddObjectsPerChunk re-clones and re-saves any chunk in m_dirtyChunks[0] (:77553-77556). Save cost of a world-wide lockdown = ChunkPortal clone + one full chunk rewrite per distinct portal sector touched.

Consequently there IS a save-cost reason to minimise writes: rely on ZDOExtraData.SetConnection's no-op return (:74951-74960) so only portals whose connection actually changes get a revision bump, and never 'refresh' tags/connections that already match. Pacing alone does not reduce the dirty-chunk union.

SendZDOToPeers2 cadence: one peer per ZDOMan.Update call, 0.05 s wait between rounds (:76837-76861); per-peer throughput is bounded by the 10240-byte send-queue cap per SendZDOs call, not by a per-peer timer.

ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) (:77706-77712) queues to every peer irrespective of distance and AddForceSendZdos prepends them (:77263-77285); the per-peer overload ForceSendZDO(long,ZDOID) (:77714-77724) is the tool for the 'interest radius only' mitigation.
evidence: ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk dirty filter + portal exclusion — :77544-77580; GetSaveClonePerChunk — :77583-77641
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Network-cost claims verified: ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:73656-73666); ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is a pure revision gate and returns true for a ZDO the peer has never received (:76003-76015); SendZDOs writes uid/OwnerRevision/DataRevision/owner/position then a full ZDO.Serialize per ZDO with no delta (:77053-77062) under the 10240-byte / 2048-byte-minimum queue cap (:77010-77016); SendZDOToPeers2 services one peer per Update after a 0.05 s inter-round wait (:76837-76861); AddForceSendZdos inserts force-sent ZDOs at index 0 for every peer regardless of distance (:77263-77285), and portals are only otherwise synced through FindObjects for a peer's near sectors (:77367-77382). ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false on unchanged type+target (:74951-74960). Save-cost claims: GetSaveClonePerChunk clones every portal into ChunkPortal when DirtyPortalObjects is set, no Persistent filter (:77621-77632); AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portals from spatial chunks (:77572) and only clones chunks in m_dirtyChunks (:77556-77559). REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector is skipped for the portal path... SetDirtyChunks ... which portals avoid' is wrong. ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) unconditionally calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector(this), which for any Persistent ZDO calls SetDirtyChunks(zdo.GetSectorIndex()) (:76694-76699, :76709-76722) — GetSectorIndex is computed from position (:73776-73779) and the portal-prefab early return is in SetSector (:73752-73756), a different method. So every portal connection/tag write also marks the portal's SPATIAL chunk (up to 4 ChunkIndex sizes) dirty, and the next save re-clones and rewrites every persistent non-portal ZDO in each such chunk. A world-wide lockdown over 500 portals in ~500 distinct zones therefore dirties a large fraction of the world's chunk files, not just ChunkPortal — the save cost DOES scale with the number of distinct chunks touched, which reverses the option's 'no incentive to batch for save reasons' conclusion (spreading writes across save intervals bounds the per-save clone set). Additionally, the 'free re-assert loop' is only free if it does not also call SetOwner each tick: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925) reassigns ownership every 2 s near players, and SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision -> ShouldSend true, so an ownership-flapping loop generates traffic.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Network analysis verified: ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is a pure revision compare (:76003-76015); SendZDOs writes uid+OwnerRevision+DataRevision+owner+position then a full ZDO.Serialize per ZDO, no delta (:77043-77062), behind a 10240-byte queue cap with a 2048 minimum (:77018-77026); AddForceSendZdos inserts forced ZDOs at index 0 for every peer that has them queued (:77263-77285) and ForceSendZDO(id) adds to every peer regardless of distance (:77706-77712); ZDOExtraData.SetConnection is a no-op on unchanged type+target (:74951-74960) so ZDO.SetConnection neither bumps revision nor sets DirtyPortalObjects (:73656-73666); GetSaveClonePerChunk clones every portal when DirtyPortalObjects is set, no Persistent filter (:77621-77632); ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756). One claim is false and it flips the save-cost conclusion: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) unconditionally calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector, which for any Persistent ZDO - portals included - calls SetDirtyChunks and inserts up to 4 ChunkIndex entries (:76694-76722). AddObjectsPerChunk only clones chunks present in m_dirtyChunks[0] (:77553-77556), so every portal touched additionally forces a full re-clone and rewrite of that portal's regular terrain chunk (all non-portal persistent ZDOs in it) at the next save. A world-wide lockdown across N distinct sectors therefore dirties up to N regular chunks - potentially most of the world's chunk files - not just the ChunkPortal bucket. The 'no incentive to batch for save reasons' conclusion is wrong in direction: pacing does not shrink the dirty-chunk union, but minimising the number of portals actually written (idempotent no-op writes, touching only portals whose state differs) matters for save cost as much as for network cost. Cadence nit: SendZDOToPeers2 services one peer per Update call with a 0.05 s pause between full rounds (:76837-76861), not 0.05 s per peer.

catalog.name: Invariant Assertion Harness and Panic Restore
catalog.oneLine: A runtime self-check that verifies a fixed list of never-violate invariants every tick and, on a violation it cannot repair, restores the vault and disables itself loudly rather than continuing to corrupt the world.
catalog.howItWorks: The harness runs from the subsystem `OnUpdate` at 1Hz using the live `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` dictionary (zero-alloc) and a full `GetPortalList()` pass at a slower 30s cadence. THE INVARIANTS, each with its assertion and its repair. (I1) NO ORPHANED VAULT — every vault record's two endpoints resolve to a live portal within tolerance; on failure, drop the record and log (a portal was demolished). (I2) LOCK COMPLETENESS — while a lockdown is engaged, every portal in its scope has `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone()`; repair by re-nulling with SetOwner + SetConnection + DataRevision bump, and count the repair as a tamper event. (I3) NO SELF-LOOP — no portal's connection equals its own `m_uid`; vanilla's reconciler tolerates self-loops indefinitely (phase 1 never checks reciprocity, :100601) but `RegenerateConnectionHashData` erases them at save (:75472-75475), so a self-loop is a silent data-loss bug. Repair by nulling. (I4) NO DANGLING TARGET — every non-None connection resolves via `ZDOMan.GetZDO` to a live ZDO; `RegenerateConnectionHashData` drops unresolvable connections at save (:75468), so a dangling link is lost at restart anyway. Repair by nulling and letting the vault or vanilla re-pair. (V5) NO DUPLICATE PORTAL ENTRY — `GetPortalList().Count` equals the count of distinct `m_uid` values; a mismatch means a portal was repositioned across a 64m sector boundary, because `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) adds to the bucket for the CURRENT sector without removing the old one while `ZDO.SetSector` is a no-op for portals (:73752-73756), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76976-76986) then looks it up by the recomputed sector and permanently leaks the other entry. THERE IS NO REPAIR — this is unrecoverable corruption of the portal registry. The only correct response is to assert loudly and to enforce the hard rule: NEVER call `SetPosition` on a portal ZDO; destroy and recreate instead. (I6) NO STALE ZDO REFERENCES — the mod caches ZDOID values only, never `ZDO` object references, across ticks, because `ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO` calls `ZDOPool.Release(zdo)` → `Reset()` which sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` and the pooled object can be handed out for an unrelated new ZDO; vanilla itself violates this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` (:100681-100698). Assert by re-resolving every cached id through `GetZDO` before use. (I7) DIRTY-FLAG DISCIPLINE — every tag write is followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`; assert by checking a write-counter against a dirty-call counter in debug builds. (I8) NO TARGET BIT ON LIVE PORTALS — no live portal carries `ConnectionType.Portal | Target` (0x11), because `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` requires exact type equality (:75094-75102) and would report such a portal as unconnected, causing vanilla to re-pair it. (I9) SINGLE WRITER — exactly one subsystem writes any given portal per tick; assert with a per-tick written-set and log a hard error on a second write. (I10) NO PORTAL AT AN OUT-OF-RANGE COORDINATE — `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps any zone beyond ~±16320m to Sector 0, the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to; assert no portal position exceeds that. PANIC RESTORE: on any repeated unrepairable violation, or on an unhandled exception inside the lockdown engine, the harness restores every vault record, clears the lockdown state, sets a `Disabled` flag that all subsystems check, logs `[TortalPortal] PANIC: <invariant> violated N times, lockdown disabled and wiring restored`, and posts to Discord. Failing open (portals work) is always the right failure direction for a portal mod; failing closed strands players.
catalog.playerExperience: Operator-facing and, when it works, invisible. A cheating client that keeps writing a connection back to a locked portal produces `[SECURITY:LockTamper] <SteamID64> - portal (1204,-88) relinked 12 times in 60s`, and after a threshold either the player is kicked via `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` or the mod stops fighting and logs that the lock is contested. If the mod itself malfunctions, players find their portals working normally and the operator finds one loud PANIC line explaining exactly which invariant broke — rather than a silently half-locked world that scrambles itself at the next save.
failureModes: I5 has no repair. Once a portal is duplicated in `m_portalObjects` the registry is permanently corrupt for that ZDO and `Game.ConnectPortals` will keep processing a dead entry after it is destroyed. The harness can only detect and refuse to make it worse.
A 1Hz full-list assertion on a very large world is itself a cost; tier the checks (cheap invariants at 1Hz over the live dictionary, expensive ones at 30s over an allocated list).

Panic-restoring the vault while a legitimate scheduled lockdown is mid-rollout will unlock everything and the scheduler's reconciler will immediately re-lock it, producing a flap. The panic flag must be sticky until an operator clears it.

Kicking on tamper escalates a cheating problem into a moderation problem and can false-positive on a legitimate `Game.RPC_SetConnection` from a client racing vanilla's own pairing. Require a sustained pattern, and prefer logging over kicking by default.

Asserting I6 by re-resolving every cached id every tick costs a dictionary lookup per portal per tick — acceptable, but it must not be done inside the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix, which is a global hot path.

The harness cannot assert anything about client state. A client that has stale ZDO data believes a portal is still connected and the server has no way to know or to force a refresh short of `ForceSendZDO`.
citations: Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 does not check reciprocity — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606 (:100601)
openQuestions: Which ZDO actually owns a portal in steady state on a live server — the nearest client, or the server after `Game.SetConnection` claims it? This determines how often the re-assert path has to fight for ownership and how often a client's `RPC_SetTag` is purely local and therefore invisible. IN-GAME CHECK: log `zdo.GetOwner()` for every entry of `GetPortalList()` on a 10s timer with players nearby and away.

Is `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` a viable non-Harmony hook for detecting a portal demolished during lockdown? It is a public `Action<ZDO>` invoked before the ZDO leaves `m_objectsByID` (:76975), so the ZDO is still readable in the callback. IN-GAME CHECK: subscribe, demolish a portal, and confirm the callback fires with a readable prefab hash.
catalog.id: lockdown-safety:Invariant Assertion Harness and Panic Restore
corrections: V5 assertion form is wrong: after HandleDestroyedZDO leaks a bucket entry, the leaked object has m_uid = ZDOID.None (ZDO.Reset :73540) and, once the pool re-issues it (ZDOPool.Get :78297-78310), carries the uid of an unrelated new ZDO — the distinct-uid count then still matches. Assert instead `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(entry.m_uid) == entry && Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(entry.GetPrefab())` for every entry of GetPortalList().

V5 root cause: the duplicate is created by ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData, which calls InternalSetPosition then AddIfPortal (:77128-77132) on every client update; a server-side SetPosition (:73729-73735) never calls AddIfPortal, so it does not duplicate immediately — it misfiles the entry, HandleDestroyedZDO then fails to remove it, and the next client ZDOData for that portal creates the duplicate. The 'never SetPosition a portal' rule stands, with that mechanism.

I2 tamper attribution cannot come from a 1 Hz poll: only ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:77076) knows which peer wrote the connection (ZDO.Deserialize writes connections straight into ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, bypassing ZDO.SetConnection and SetDirtyPortals, :74206-74232). A Harmony prefix/postfix on RPC_ZDOData is required before any SteamID can be logged or kicked. Without the pairing veto from Park-and-Release technique B, vanilla's own pass 2 (:100607-100621) re-pairs a nulled portal every 5 s and would be counted as a 'tamper event' and, past the threshold, kick an innocent owner.
I4 duplicates vanilla: pass 1 already nulls any connection whose target ZDO is missing within 5 s (:100598-100604). Keep it as a consistency check but it is not a mod-only concern.

I8 is purely defensive: vanilla never writes a Target-flagged type into runtime s_connections (Target appears only in s_connectionsHashData, :75472-75475, and RPC_SetTag/ConnectPortals write plain Portal). It can only catch the mod's own bugs.

I7: in the common case a tag mutation on a connected portal is followed within 5 s by pass 1's SetConnection(None) (:100603) which already calls SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73665); the loss only occurs for an already-unconnected portal. Still call SetDirtyPortals — the point stands.

I10's consequence is not registry corruption: an out-of-range portal lands in the Sector-0 bucket that the server's own ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects visits (:82268-82276 -> FindObjects :77367-77382 includes m_portalObjects[Sector 0]) and, once IsActiveAreaLoaded is true at the pinned ref pos (:114054-114069), it is instantiated headless (TeleportWorld.Awake registers RPCs and InvokeRepeating UpdatePortal). Assert it, but describe the effect correctly.

Kick path: ZNet.Kick(string) -> InternalKick parses a PlatformUserID and looks up the peer by host name (:81658-81667 and InternalKick body); pass the peer's host name, not the player name. The kick/threshold half of this option is reactive detection, not enforcement.

Enforcement honesty: the repairs (re-nulling) are server writes to a server-owned field and are enforced against vanilla clients; a modded client that owns the ZDO can re-write the connection in its ZDOData (accepted when its DataRevision is higher, :77107-77118) and can teleport itself regardless, so the harness only narrows the window.

V5: a server-side ZDO.SetPosition on a portal does not duplicate the entry by itself (SetSector :73752-73756 is a no-op so AddIfPortal is never re-run); it mis-files the entry, and the duplicate appears when AddIfPortal runs again on the next RPC_ZDOData for that ZDO (:77132). The leaked entry after HandleDestroyedZDO is a pooled ZDO with m_uid==None (Reset :73536-73549 clears m_uid/Valid but not m_prefab) that GetPortalList keeps returning - add asserts 'entry.Valid', 'entry.m_uid != None', 'ZDOMan.GetZDO(entry.m_uid) == entry' and 'PortalPrefabHash.Contains(entry.GetPrefab())' to the distinct-uid count.

V5: repair IS possible - remove the stale entry from the private readonly Dictionary m_portalObjects (:76039) by reflection (the dictionary object is mutable). The 'never SetPosition a portal' rule remains good policy; if a move is unavoidable, reflection-move the bucket entry in the same call.

I2: do not count every relink as a client tamper. Vanilla's own pass 2 (:100607-100621) and the staged force-write in ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) relink nulled portals every 5s, and for client-owned portals that write arrives through Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100649-100659) executed by the vanilla client. Tamper attribution is only valid once pairing is vetoed (Routing Kernel L1/L2) and should attribute via the RPC_ZDOData sender socket (:77080-77140 region), not the ZDO owner field.

I2/I4 repairs: a no-bump idempotent re-null does not converge a client whose DataRevision tied with the server's (server :77108-77118 rejects num4<=DataRevision; client symmetric; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend only re-sends when the server's revision exceeds the peer record). Force a real DataRevision bump (e.g. Set a scratch int) whenever a client-side drift is observed.
I4 is redundant with vanilla: pass 1 already nulls a connection whose target is null (:100598-100604) every 5s; keep the assert, drop the repair or make it force-immediate.
Line refs: AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals is :100681-100688 and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698; SectorToIndex(int,int) body is :115762-115775.

Several assertions, however, are mis-specified or attribute vanilla behaviour to attackers, and the tamper/kick path is reactive detection that requires a hook the option does not name.

ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) skips connections whose target does not resolve (:75468) and, for a self-loop, overwrites the ZDO's own slot with Portal|Target at :75474 so at load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77891) never lists it among Portal-typed entries; the self-loop is gone after a restart (I3/I4 correct). ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID (:75094-75102) requires exact type equality, and ZDO.Deserialize (:74219-74233) writes whatever ConnectionType byte a peer sends via ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, so a live Portal|Target entry is injectable by a modified client and vanilla would treat that portal as unconnected (I8 correct). ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666) sets DirtyPortalObjects only on change; a tag-only Set never does, and GetSaveClonePerChunk saves the portal chunk only if DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77636) (I7 correct). ZDOMan.GetPortals (:77643-77646) returns the live dictionary (zero-alloc claim correct). V5 is real but its mechanism is misdescribed: ZDO.SetPosition -> InternalSetPosition -> SetSector (:73729-73762) is a no-op for portal prefabs, so a server-side SetPosition alone produces a MIS-FILED entry (still in the old bucket), not a duplicate; the duplicate appears only when AddIfPortal is invoked again for that ZDO, which happens on every RPC_ZDOData receipt (:77132) and in CreateNewZDO (:76689) - AddIfPortal only checks the CURRENT-sector bucket for Contains (:77738-77744). Then HandleDestroyedZDO removes from the recomputed sector only (:76982), and the stale entry is a pooled/reset ZDO that GetPortalList keeps returning (m_uid None, m_prefab NOT reset by Reset) and that ConnectPortals will feed into FindRandomUnconnectedPortal with tag "". Also 'THERE IS NO REPAIR' is wrong: m_portalObjects is a private readonly Dictionary (:76039) whose contents are mutable via reflection. I2's tamper attribution is wrong as stated: a relink of a nulled portal is produced by vanilla itself (pass 2 at :100607-100621 and the staged force-write in ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, delivered to client-owned portals through Game.RPC_SetConnection which vanilla clients execute) unless the lockdown also vetoes pairing; counting those as SteamID tamper events would kick innocent players. Revision tie split-brain: server write N+1 and client-owner write N+1 are mutually rejected (server ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118 num4<=DataRevision; client copy identical), and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:75990-76000 region) re-sends only when the server's revision exceeds the peer record, so an idempotent no-bump re-assertion leaves the client holding its own value; a repair must force a DataRevision bump past the client's. Enforcement is honest: every invariant is of the form 'is this ROUTE field in the state the server wants', which the server owns.

catalog.name: RULED OUT — Moment-of-Transit Veto and Per-Portal Item Policy
catalog.oneLine: There is no server-side hook on the act of teleporting and no networked per-portal setting of any kind, so per-transit approval, per-portal ore rules and PIN gates are all impossible without a client mod.
catalog.howItWorks: THE TRANSIT VETO. `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly ONE call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)` at :143679, which requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component` (:143673-143681). Three independent conditions make it unreachable server-side: no portal GameObject is ever instantiated (the SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick at :100465, a line absent from the client's `Game.FixedUpdate`, so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` :82268 only ever builds objects in an empty sector 1e6m out), no Player GameObject is ever instantiated (`Player.Awake` is what fills `s_players`, :10032-10035), and `Player.m_localPlayer` is null. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `public` and appears in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable — it is not usefully callable: `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs `MessageHud.instance`, and `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own throwaway profile. The server sees no packet either: the whole decision and the whole move happen inside the traveller's own process. PER-PORTAL ITEM POLICY. Every public field of `TeleportWorld` is a plain Inspector-compiled value with zero ZDO backing and zero RPC: `m_activationRange` (:143411), `m_exitDistance` (:143413), `m_proximityRoot` (:143415), the two colours (:143418, :143421), `m_target_found` (:143423), `m_model` (:143425), `m_connected` (:143427), `m_allowAllItems` (:143429), `m_hoverOffset` (:143431). A Harmony write to `m_allowAllItems` on the server mutates a copy no client will ever read. The only ZDO-backed fields the class touches are `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) and `s_tagauthor` (:78619), plus the `ConnectionType.Portal` connection. PIN GATES. A PIN requires prompting the player at the moment of transit and refusing the move — both halves are inside the client-only path above. TortalPortal's own PIN implementation is entirely client-side: `SecurityPatch.CanConfigure` reads `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID()` (a local profile that on a dedicated server is a throwaway `new PlayerProfile()` named 'Stranger' created in `Game.Awake` :100047), and `TeleportWorld_SetText_Prefix` writes the PIN key from the client. THE CARGO AUDIT. Even observing what a traveller carried is impossible: no character ZDO carries item data. `ZDOVars.s_items` is written by exactly one live code path, `Container.Save()` (:122294-122300); `Player.Save(ZPackage)` serialises inventory, skills and recipes into `PlayerProfile.m_playerData` which goes only to that client's own .fch (:14091-14170, :105706-105711); and `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles()` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. THE ONLY THING THAT IS SERVER-ENFORCEABLE at transit granularity is the destination's existence — nulling the connection, covered by the Force-Disconnect option. THE ONLY PARTIAL WORKAROUND for per-portal settings is `ZNetView.LoadFields()` (:82669, client copy assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898), which is vanilla on both builds and reflects over every public instance field of every component on the instantiated prefab, overriding from the ZDO under keys `"HasFields"`, `"HasFields<TypeName>"` and `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"`. Writing three ints to a portal ZDO would in principle give per-portal `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` on a 100% vanilla client — but it is client-honoured, it only applies at instantiation (`ZNetView.Awake` :82631, so a player standing at the portal is unaffected until they leave and return), and it is UNVERIFIED in-game. It is listed here as a lead, not as a shipped capability.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing. These features cannot be built, and the honest documentation line is: 'TortalPortal Lite cannot approve or refuse an individual teleport, cannot set per-portal item rules, and cannot ask for a PIN. It can make a portal have nowhere to go, which stops the teleport entirely — including for modified clients.'
failureModes: Attempting a Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.Teleport` or `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` on a dedicated server compiles cleanly, applies cleanly, and never fires once. This is the single most common wasted effort in this problem space.

Attempting to patch `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is equally dead: it is registered on the portal's ZNetView in `Awake` (:143448), the server never instantiates one, and `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` drops ZDO-targeted RPCs because `ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo)` is always null (:83646-83663, :82229).
Setting `m_allowAllItems` server-side via reflection appears to succeed and changes nothing observable, which reads as a subtle bug rather than an impossibility.
Any 'portal toll' or 'cargo check' feature must be redesigned around an adjacent Container ZDO (`s_items`, readable and writable) rather than the traveller's inventory.
The PIN concept can only degrade to an all-or-nothing per-portal lock (connection nulled / restored), which is a different product and must be named differently.

This is the single highest-value experiment available and would partially un-rule-out per-portal item policy (as a client-honoured setting). catalog.id: lockdown-safety:RULED OUT — Moment-of-Transit Veto and Per-Portal Item Policy
corrections: 'It can make a portal have nowhere to go, which stops the teleport entirely — including for modified clients' is false. Movement is client-authoritative: Player.TeleportTo runs entirely in the owning client (:15302-15327) and a modded client can call it, or write any position into its own character ZDO, without any portal connection at all. Nulling the connection stops VANILLA clients only.

The server is not entirely without a lever after the fact: the vanilla client registers Chat 'RPC_TeleportPlayer' on ZRoutedRpc (:41627) and the handler (:41962-41968) is gated only on `Player.m_localPlayer != null` with no sender check, so a server-only mod can relocate a vanilla player after detecting a transit (Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit heuristic). That is a reactive bounce, not a veto, and belongs in a separate option — it does not change this ruling.

LoadFields detail: `m_allowAllItems` is a bool and LoadFields has a `typeof(bool) && zDO.GetBool(text, out …)` branch (:82701); the three keys ('HasFields', 'HasFieldsTeleportWorld', 'TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems') are bools at the API level (stored as ints by ZDO.Set(string,bool)). The lead is correctly labelled unverified and client-honoured; it also only takes effect on ZNetView.Awake (:82631), i.e. after the portal is re-instantiated on that client.

Minor: the RPC 'RPC_TeleportTo' is also registered per-character on ZNetView (:886) and its handler (:4126-4132) requires m_nview.IsOwner(), so it cannot be used from the server; only the Chat-level RPC_TeleportPlayer can.

Replace 'only ever builds objects in an empty sector 1e6m out' with: the pinned reference position clamps to Sector 0 (ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex :115762-115775), the shared bucket for every out-of-range position and real sector (-256,-256); ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects (:82268-82276) therefore instantiates whatever ZDOs sit in that bucket. No Player exists in it, so Teleport is still unreachable.
Qualify 'no character ZDO carries item data': equipped-item prefab hashes are in the player ZDO via VisEquipment (s_rightItem :20590, s_chestItem :20632); inventory contents, including ore, are not.

LoadFields lead: note that vanilla's Console spawn command (client :44430-44450) already uses the same 'HasFields' key convention on arbitrary prefabs, and that the keys are read only in ZNetView.Awake (:82631) and LocationProxy.SpawnLocation (:103150), never on later ZDO updates.

'The server sees no packet' is true for the decision, but the resulting position jump is visible in the player's ZDO sync (basis of Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit) - reactive detection of transits is possible, vetoing is not.

Only re-run on Awake or LocationProxy (:103150) - never on later ZDO changes. Two factual corrections: (1) 'only ever builds objects in an empty sector 1e6m out' is mechanically wrong - ZoneSystem.GetZone((1e6,0,1e6)) gives zone (15625,15625) and every zone FindSectorObjects (:77295-77340) visits around it clamps through SectorToIndex (:115762-115775) to Sector 0, which is the shared bucket for all out-of-range positions plus real sector (-256,-256); the server does instantiate whatever sits in m_objectsBySector[0] and m_portalObjects[Sector 0] (FindObjects :77367-77380). In practice nothing legitimate sits there, and even a portal placed there would only get TeleportWorld.Awake/UpdatePortal running with s_players empty - Teleport still never fires - so the conclusion stands. (2) 'no character ZDO carries item data' overstates: VisEquipment writes equipped-item hashes to the player ZDO (s_rightItem :20590, s_chestItem :20632, read :20860-20861); non-teleportable ore is never equippable, so cargo audit remains impossible for the items that matter.

catalog.name: RULED OUT — Blocking Dungeon Doors and Vetoing Retags at the RPC Layer
catalog.oneLine: Crypt and dungeon teleports have no networked state at all, and portal retags issued by the ZDO's owner never reach the wire — so neither can be blocked, observed, or audited server-side.
catalog.howItWorks: DUNGEON DOORS. `class Teleport` (:143316-143390) is a 75-line MonoBehaviour with exactly four fields — `m_hoverText`, `m_enterText`, `public Teleport m_targetPoint`, `m_hoverOffset` — and NO ZNetView field, NO Awake, NO m_nview, NO ZDO access and NO RPC registration anywhere in the class body. Its destination is a plain Inspector object reference resolved by Transform math (`GetTeleportPoint()` returns `transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`, :143372-143375, and is private and called on the *other* instance so it is not even overridable through a public surface). It is therefore invisible to `ZDOMan`, absent from `m_portalObjects`, untouched by `Game.ConnectPortals`, and has no save-file representation. There is nothing for a server-only mod to read, write, redirect, log, or veto. Its only shared lever is `GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals`, and even that is a narrower and stranger check than the world-portal one: `Teleport.Interact` blocks only when `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos)` (:143355), where `InInterior()` is `y > 3000f` so it gates the OUTBOUND leg only, and `IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631-133645) returns false whenever `EnemyHud.instance` is null and otherwise depends on which boss health bar that specific client currently has on screen. Note also what `Teleport.Interact` does NOT do: it never reads `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and never calls `Player.IsTeleportable`. So a full `noportals` lockdown leaves every crypt door working, ore and all — and vanilla never restricted ore through them in the first place. Worth cataloguing alongside it: `Ladder.Interact` (:132064-132079) performs an instant `character.transform.position = m_targetPos.position` with no `TeleportTo`, no 2s cooldown, no fade, no key check and no item check, gated only on interaction range — a third Transform-based relocation component, equally invisible to the server, which any 'all teleport paths' audit must list and which any server-side transit detector will misattribute. RETAG VETO. `TeleportWorld.SetText` invokes `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId)` (:143579-143585), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, ...)` routes to `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858). `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` then handles the call LOCALLY and skips `RouteRPC` entirely whenever `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595, branch at :83588-83594). A client that owns the portal ZDO — which, because `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands ownership to any peer in whose active area the portal sits every 2s (:76901-76926), is the normal case for any portal near a player — therefore retags it entirely in-process with ZERO packets on the wire. The server cannot see it, cannot log it, and cannot drop it. And in the opposite case, if the SERVER owns the portal ZDO, the RPC is routed to the server and then dropped on the floor, because `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83656) which is always null headless — so server ownership of a portal silently BREAKS vanilla retagging for players. Separately, `authorId` is a raw client self-report never cross-checked against the sending peer (:143587-143602), so `s_tagauthor` is not an audit trail. THE ONLY WORKING APPROACH is detect-and-revert on the ZDO: poll `s_tag` on `GetPortalList()` against a desired-state map and rewrite on drift, accepting a poll-interval-sized window during which the player's tag stood.
catalog.playerExperience: For dungeons: a player with `noportals` set server-wide walks into a burial chamber and out again completely normally, carrying iron. Operators who announced 'all teleportation disabled' will be contradicted. For retags: a player renames their own portal and it just works, with no server record of who renamed what or when — and if a mod has claimed server ownership of that portal, the rename appears to succeed client-side (the text dialog closes) and then silently does nothing, which is a far worse experience than a refusal.
failureModes: A Harmony patch on `Teleport.Interact` compiles and applies on a dedicated server and never fires, because `ZoneSystem.CreateLocationProxy` passes `spawnNow = (mode == SpawnMode.Full)` so the visual location prefab never expands server-side and no `Teleport` component is ever instantiated.

A Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` likewise never fires. A prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` or `HandleRoutedRPC` keyed on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` catches only the minority of retags that actually cross the wire.
Claiming server ownership of portal ZDOs to 'control' them silently disables player retagging with no error on either side — a severe, hard-to-diagnose regression.

Detect-and-revert on `s_tag` fights `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`'s whole-ZDO clobber (:77107-77132): the owning client's next higher-DataRevision push restores its value. Winning requires bumping DataRevision aggressively and re-asserting on a tick.

Any per-player audit keyed on `s_tagauthor` is spoofable (:143587-143602, `sender` never validated against `authorId`). Use `Piece` `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) for ownership instead, and cross-check identity against `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`.
`Ladder.Interact` bypasses even the 2s `TeleportTo` cooldown, so it is the cheapest vanilla-legitimate teleport in the game and will confuse any position-delta-based detector.

openQuestions: Which ZDO owns a typical portal in steady state — the nearest client or the server? This determines what fraction of retags are invisible (owner-local) versus observable (routed). IN-GAME CHECK: log `zdo.GetOwner()` for every portal on a 10s timer with players nearby and away, and correlate against retag events.

Does the `Teleport` component share a GameObject with a ZNetView on the shipped dungeon-entrance prefabs? It would not change the conclusion (the location prefab never expands server-side) but would settle whether a `Teleport` ever exists for a single frame during ghost world-gen. IN-GAME CHECK: patch `Teleport.OnTriggerEnter` on the dedicated server, log, and confirm zero hits across a full world-gen pass.
catalog.id: lockdown-safety:RULED OUT — Blocking Dungeon Doors and Vetoing Retags at the RPC Layer
corrections: 'Never reach the wire … cannot see it, cannot log it' applies to the RPC only. The owning client's RPC_SetTag writes s_tag, s_tagauthor and UpdateConnection(None) into its ZDO copy (:143594-143600), IncreaseDataRevision on a client queues the ZDO via ClientChanged (:73832-73839, :77728-77731), and the server receives it in ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77076) with the sending peer's identity available from `rpc`. Detection, attribution and revert are therefore possible after the fact (reactive-detection-only), which is what the option's own last paragraph describes. The claim line should say 'cannot be vetoed', not 'cannot be observed or audited'.

Add the systemic consequence for the sibling options: any mod write that uses `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (the Game.SetConnection primitive, :100643) makes the server the owner until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns it (≤2 s, :76870-76884), and during that window every vanilla rename of that portal is silently dropped at HandleRoutedRPC (:83656). Mods that re-claim ownership every tick will break vanilla retagging continuously.

Dungeon-door detection is likewise reactive: a client's character ZDO position crossing y = 3000 (InInterior threshold :4538-4541) is visible to the server, so entries/exits can be logged and bounced (Chat RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41627/:41962), but not prevented.
TeleportHome (:143392-143400) is a fourth Transform-based relocation component (calls Game.RequestRespawn on trigger) worth adding to the 'all teleport paths' list alongside Teleport and Ladder.

Retag CAN be observed and attributed server-side: the client-owner's tag write arrives via ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77080-77140); the ZRpc parameter identifies the sending peer. Replace 'cannot see it, cannot log it' with 'cannot veto it before it lands; can detect it event-driven with sender attribution and revert'.

'THE ONLY WORKING APPROACH is poll' is wrong - a Harmony hook on RPC_ZDOData (or a prefix that declines to Deserialize the package) is event-driven and poll-free. Reverting still requires bumping the server's DataRevision above the client's (revision tie is mutually rejected, :77108-77118).

The server-owned case is not merely 'broken': a mod that pins portal ownership to the server (patch ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926 / IsInPeerActiveArea :76887-76898 for PortalPrefabHash) and intercepts 'RPC_SetTag' in ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632-83643) gets a real pre-write veto on retags from vanilla clients, with the caveat that all other owner-routed RPCs on the portal (WearNTear damage/repair/remove) must then also be serviced by the mod. Modified clients can still write the tag directly via ZDO sync.
RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is read from the client's packet (:83634-83636) and never overwritten from the socket - do not use it as an audit identity.
verifierReasoning: [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Dungeon half verifies exactly: class Teleport (:143316-143390) has four fields, no ZNetView, no ZDO access, no RPC registration; Interact checks only NoBossPortals && InInterior (y > 3000, :4538-4541) && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon (EnemyHud-dependent, :133631-133645) and never NoPortals or IsTeleportable (:143345-143370); GetTeleportPoint is private Transform math (:143372-143375). Ladder.Interact is an instant transform write with no key or item check (:132064-132079). Retag-veto half verifies: SetText -> ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:143579-143585, :82855-82858); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id (:83577-83595); HandleRoutedRPC on the server drops any ZDO-targeted RPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null headless (:83645-83663, :82229-82236); ReleaseNearbyZDOS runs every 2 s (:76870-76884) and hands Persistent ZDOs — including portals, which FindObjects pulls from m_portalObjects (:77376-77379) — to any peer whose active area contains them (:76901-76926); authorId is a raw self-report (:143587-143602). The one overreach is the claim that an owner retag 'cannot be observed or audited': the resulting s_tag/connection change does hit the wire in the client's next ZDOData packet.

[decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Dungeon half fully confirmed: class Teleport (:143316-143390) has four fields, no ZNetView, no Awake, no RPC; GetTeleportPoint is private Transform math (:143372-143375); Interact (:143344-143370) checks only NoBossPortals && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon, never NoPortals, never IsTeleportable; InInterior is y>3000 (:4538-4541); IsInsideActiveBossDungeon depends on EnemyHud.instance (:133631-133646). Ladder.Interact (:132064-132079) is an instant transform set gated only on InUseDistance. Retag half: the wire claim is correct - TeleportWorld.SetText (:143579-143585) -> ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC (:83577-83595) handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID==m_id; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) transfers a server-owned ZDO to any peer whose active area contains it because IsInPeerActiveArea for the server session tests against the (1e6,0,1e6) pin (:76887-76898); and HandleRoutedRPC (:83645-83663) drops ZDO-targeted RPCs without a ZNetScene instance (:82229-82236). RPC_SetTag uses authorId verbatim (:143587-143602). BUT the headline 'cannot be observed or audited server-side' is refuted: the resulting tag write reaches the server as an ordinary ZDO update through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77080-77140), whose ZRpc argument identifies the sending socket - a Harmony hook there gives event-driven, sender-attributed detection of every tag change (and every connection change) with no polling, and a prefix can even refuse to apply the package (the client's copy keeps its value until the server bumps DataRevision past it). Also, the 'server ownership silently breaks retagging' observation cuts the other way for a mod: a server that keeps portal ownership (patching ReleaseNearbyZDOS/IsInPeerActiveArea for portal prefabs) receives every vanilla retag as a routed RPC with a socket-identifiable sender and can accept, log or refuse it by handling 'RPC_SetTag' in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC/HandleRoutedRPC patch - at the cost of also having to service every other owner-routed RPC on that object (WearNTear damage/repair/remove). Note m_senderPeerID in RoutedRPCData is deserialised from the client packet (:83632-83636) and is spoofable; attribute via the ZRpc socket, not the field. So: veto-at-RPC-layer for client-owned portals is impossible (confirmed); observe/audit is reactive-detection-only, not 'impossible'.

catalog.name: The Void Anchor
catalog.oneLine: A destination ZDO whose prefab hash is literally 0 — invisible, never instantiated, never logged, ignored by IsAreaReady — turning any world coordinate into a valid portal exit.
catalog.howItWorks:
TeleportWorld.Teleport (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539-143546) resolves its destination with a bare ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) and then reads only GetPosition() and GetRotation(). It never checks the target's prefab, tag, type, persistence or ownership. TargetFound (:143640-143656) requires only that the client holds the ZDO. So the destination does not have to be a portal — it does not have to be anything.

The cleanest anchor is a ZDO with prefab hash exactly 0. ZNetScene.CreateObject (:81996-82002) opens with `if (prefab == 0) return null;` BEFORE the GetPrefab lookup, so no GameObject is made and, uniquely, NO 'Missing prefab hash' warning is logged (contrast :82004-82008 for an unknown non-zero hash). ZNetScene.IsPrefabZDOValid (:81986-81993) also returns false for hash 0, so IsAreaReady (:82064-82082) skips it entirely and the arriving player's teleport is never blocked waiting for it.

Recipe, server-side: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, 0); z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(0); z.SetRotation(rot);` Note CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) leaves m_prefab at its pooled default of -1 (ZDO field decl :73317, `c_PrefabInvalid = -1`), and -1 DOES log a warning, so SetPrefab(0) is mandatory, not optional. Then on the player-facing portal: `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, z.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.m_uid);` (mirrors Game.SetConnection :100643-100645).

Delivery: the anchor is not in the traveller's sector, so it arrives only via TeleportWorld.TargetFound calling ZDOMan.RequestZDO (:143653), which routes to the server's RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) and force-sends it. First walk-through therefore fails silently; the second succeeds. Pre-warm with ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId) on peer join to remove the warm-up.

Persistence: prefab 0 is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash, so ZDO.SetSector (:73752) does NOT early-return and the anchor files normally in m_objectsBySector; AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) saves it because Persistent is true and the prefab is not a portal hash. FilterZDO (:76346-76361) only warns on unknown prefabs when the world version changed, and never removes them.
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks into a portal tagged 'Sanctum'. The far end is not a portal — it is nothing at all. They arrive standing on a mountain ledge, or in the middle of a stone circle, or on a specific dock plank, facing a direction the server chose, with no return gate visible. The only way back is the way the server decided. Because the anchor is invisible, an admin destination cannot be griefed, deconstructed, or found by exploring — there is no object there to hit with a hammer. On the very first use after the link is created the player walks through and nothing happens, no message, no effect; they step out and back in and it works.
failureModes: First transit after linking silently no-ops while RequestZDO fetches the anchor — TeleportWorld.Teleport returns at gate 1 (:143519) without any player.Message, so it reads as a bug

Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100601) nulls the portal's connection within 5s unless the anchor ZDO also carries the identical ZDOVars.s_tag string AND a non-None Portal connection of its own (a self-loop anchor.SetConnection(Portal, anchor.m_uid) satisfies the second clause)

A self-loop on the anchor is erased at world save by ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75472-75475), which overwrites the source slot with the Target slot — so the link must be re-asserted after every world load

An anchor placed beyond roughly +/-16384 m lands in ZoneSystem SectorToIndex bucket 0 (:115760-115773), the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to, and the server will then reap it via ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted's IsServer() destroy branch (:82137-82143)
Anchor ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load sets m_uid via ZDOID.SetID), so mod state must key anchors by rounded position or a custom ZDO field, never by ZDOID
prerequisites: A Game.ConnectPortals reconciliation strategy (either matching tag + self-loop on the anchor, or a Harmony prefix suppressing phase 1 for managed portals)
citations: TeleportWorld.Teleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143549 (destination read at :143539-143545, no prefab check)
ZNetScene.CreateObject — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81996-82022 (silent null return on prefab 0 at :81999-82002)
openQuestions: Does a vanilla 1.0.7 client tolerate a prefab-0 ZDO sitting in its own loaded sector indefinitely with zero log output? IN-GAME: create a prefab-0 anchor 10 m from a player, stand there 5 minutes, grep the client log for any ZDO-related line.

Does ZDO.Save/Load round-trip prefab hash 0 without tripping any load-time guard? IN-GAME: create the anchor, force a world save, restart the server, and confirm ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO resolves it and the teleport still lands.
corrections: 'First walk-through fails silently; the second succeeds' is overstated. UpdatePortal (:143489-143505) evaluates `flag2 && TargetFound()` every 0.5 s as soon as a teleportable player is within m_activationRange=5 m, so RequestZDO fires ~1 s before a walking player reaches the trigger and the force-send normally lands first; only a sprint straight into the arch races it. Pre-warm on peer join is still the robust fix.

'never logged' is false at boot: the chunked loader calls FilterZDO(newVersion: true) (:76583, :76602) and !ZNetScene.HasPrefab(0) (:82040) puts the anchor in warningZDOs → every server start logs 'Found N ZDOs with unknown prefabs. Will load anyway.' and 'Hash 0 appeared N times.' (:76371-76386). It IS loaded; only the log claim is wrong.

m_prefab default: ZDO.Reset (:73536-73549) does NOT clear m_prefab, so a recycled pooled ZDO carries its previous occupant's hash — possibly a real prefab, which every client would then instantiate at the anchor. SetPrefab(0) is mandatory for that reason, not merely to avoid the -1 warning; do it before anything else.

Save boundary — the suggested 'self-loop on the anchor' is order-dependently lossy: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) writes the anchor's single slot twice for Z→Z ((Portal,h) then (Portal|Target,h)) and again for P→Z; depending on s_connections iteration order the final pair of hashes may not match and load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77854-77891) drops the portal's link, after which vanilla Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs the portal by tag elsewhere. Use a mutual back-link (anchor→portal) instead: it is a proper pairwise matching and is restored on load regardless of order (ConnectPortals pairs any ZDO with a matching hash, not only portal prefabs).

Dedicated-only: on a player-hosted world (IsServer() with a local player) CreateObjectsSorted destroys the anchor the moment the host comes within the active area (:82140-82146). Also do not place anchors outside ±16.4 km — those land in Sector 0, which IS the dedicated server's own near set (SectorToIndex :115760-115774, Game.FixedUpdate :100465) and would be destroyed the same way.

Dirty-chunk ordering: Initialize→AddToSector runs with Persistent=false so no chunk is dirtied (:76723-76729); set Persistent=true BEFORE the first Set/SetPrefab so IncreaseDataRevision→SetDirtySector (:73833-73840, :76694-76700) marks the chunk; the back-link SetConnection does this anyway.
Ownership: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76900-76927) will hand the anchor to whichever client stands near it; harmless (no instance, no writes) but expect GetOwner() != 0.

Line nit: ZDO.Deserialize sets m_prefab from the wire (:74212) — a prefab-0 ZDO round-trips to clients unchanged; CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash) public overload is at :76674 and requires the int argument (not optional).

Creation recipe: use ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, <non-zero non-portal hash>) then z.SetPrefab(0). With prefabHash 0, CreateNewZDO uses the pooled ZDO's stale m_prefab for AddIfPortal (:76684-76688); ZDO.Reset/Init never clear m_prefab (:73496-73550) and ZDOPool is LIFO (:78269-78300), so an anchor allocated right after a portal destroy is misregistered as a portal (in m_portalObjects, removed from m_objectsBySector, enumerated by GetPortalList and reconciled by Game.ConnectPortals).

Replace the 'self-loop' prerequisite with a reciprocal link anchor->portal (ConnectionType.Portal). RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) keeps one hash slot per ZDO overwritten in dictionary order, so a self-loop can clobber the slot the portal link needs and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77852-77890) drops the pair at reload; a reciprocal pair survives for either ordering and still passes Game.ConnectPortals (:100600-100604) because the anchor's connection is non-None.

'First walk-through fails silently' is a race, not a rule: TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal calls TargetFound() (which issues RequestZDO) every 0.5 s while a teleportable player is within 5 m (client :144231-144247), so the anchor usually arrives during the approach. Pre-warming with ForceSendZDO(peer, id) on spawn removes the residual race.

'Never logged': ZDOMan.FilterZDO is always called with newVersion:true (:76573, :76591) so each world load logs a warning line for hash 0 ZDOs (WarnAndRemoveBrokenZDOs :76368-76385). Harmless, but not silent.

Bounds: anchor position must stay within ±16,384 m; ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex sends out-of-range sectors to index 0 (:115758-115772), the bucket the dedicated server's pinned reference position also resolves to, where server-side CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects destroy invalid-prefab ZDOs (:82105+, client mirror :82361-82372).

ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted IsServer destroy branch — server :82140-82146, client :82365-82372; CreateDistantObjects — client :82405-82411; RemoveObjects — client :82425-82449

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The primitive holds. TeleportWorld.Teleport reads only GetPosition/GetRotation of ZDOMan.GetZDO(connection) with no prefab/tag/type check (:143539-143546); TargetFound only needs the client to hold the ZDO and calls RequestZDO on a miss (:143640-143656); RPC_RequestZDO force-sends to the requester (:77689-77692). Client TeleportWorld is identical to the server copy (diff verified). ZNetScene.CreateObject returns null silently for prefab 0 before the GetPrefab lookup (server :81996-82002, client :82226-82231) and IsPrefabZDOValid returns false for 0 (server :81986-81993, client :82215-82222), so IsAreaReady (:82064-82082) ignores it and the arriving player's UpdateTeleport proceeds. No client path destroys it: CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects only destroy invalid ZDOs under ZNet.instance.IsServer() (client :82365-82372, :82405-82411), RemoveObjects only touches instances (client :82425-82449), RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS spares Persistent (client :77547-77558). ZDO.SetSector's early-return is portal-hash only (:73752-73757) so the anchor files in m_objectsBySector via Initialize→AddToSector (:73496-73503) and is saved by AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572). Several details in the option are wrong or overstated — none fatal.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The client side is exactly as claimed: ZNetScene.CreateObject returns null silently for prefab 0 before the GetPrefab lookup (client :82225-82231) while a non-zero unknown hash logs 'Missing prefab hash' (:82232-82236); IsPrefabZDOValid is false for 0 (:82215-82223); IsAreaReady skips invalid-prefab ZDOs (:82293-82310); CreateObjectsSorted retries every frame but only destroys when IsServer() (:82334-82372); client RPC_ZDOData accepts any prefab (client CreateNewZDO(zDOID, vector) + Deserialize) and clients never evict ZDOs (client ZDOMan.Update :872-882 only releases on server). TeleportWorld.Teleport reads only GetPosition/GetRotation of the target (client :144290-144297); TargetFound only needs the ZDO held and RequestZDO's on miss (:144380-144396); RPC_RequestZDO force-sends (:77689-77692). Player.UpdateTeleport waits for IsAreaReady then FindFloor, falling back to GetSolidHeight after 15 s (client :15331-15380), so an arbitrary coordinate always resolves. Server persistence: SetSector only early-returns for portal hashes (:73752-73757), AddObjectsPerChunk saves Persistent non-portal ZDOs (:77572), unknown-prefab ZDOs load with a warning (:76346-76361, :76364-76372). Three corrections. (1) Pool hazard: ZDO.Reset()/Init() never clear m_prefab (:73496-73550) and ZDOPool is a LIFO stack of released ZDOs (:78269-78300); CreateNewZDO(pos, 0) computes prefabHash = zDO.GetPrefab() when prefabHashIn==0 (:76684-76688) — a ZDO recycled from a just-destroyed portal carries the portal hash, so AddIfPortal files the anchor in m_portalObjects and removes it from the sector list (:77732-77752). Will load anyway. / Hash 0 appeared N times' — 'never logged' is false at load. Keep anchors within ±16,384 m: SectorToIndex maps anything outside to bucket 0 (:115758-115772), which is the server's own near set at the (1e6,0,1e6) pin and CreateObjectsSorted destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs there when IsServer().

catalog.name: Skyfall, Seabed and Underworld Exits
catalog.oneLine: Exact arrival behaviour for destinations at impossible altitudes, derived from the 8s/15s/FindFloor/GetSolidHeight ladder in Player.UpdateTeleport.
catalog.howItWorks:
Player.UpdateTeleport (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15379) is a four-stage ladder and each stage has a hard number.

Stage 1, t <= 2s: nothing happens; the player is frozen at origin with a black screen.

Stage 2, t > 2s: transform.position is force-assigned to m_teleportTargetPos EVERY FixedUpdate (:15343), linearVelocity is zeroed (:15345), and m_maxAirAltitude is reset to the target's y (:15346). This means no fall accumulates DURING the hold.

Stage 3, the exit gate (:15349): for distantTeleport (which TeleportWorld always passes, :143546) completion requires t > 8s AND ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target).

Stage 4, the floor test (:15354): ZoneSystem.FindFloor raycasts DOWN from target + Vector3.up * 1f for exactly 1000 m against m_solidRayMask (:115604-115613). If it hits, the teleport ends cleanly at t >= 8s. If it misses, at t > 15s the player is force-placed at ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(target) + 0.5f, where GetSolidHeight raycasts from target.y + 1000f down 2000 m and returns target.y unchanged on a miss (:115525-115534).

Concrete consequences for an anchor at height H above terrain:
- H <= 1000: FindFloor hits, teleport completes at t = 8s, m_maxAirAltitude is released at the target y, and the player falls H metres taking full fall damage on landing.
- H > 1000 but H <= 2000: FindFloor misses, 15s hold, GetSolidHeight hits (its ray spans target.y+1000 down to target.y-1000), player is placed 0.5 m above the ground directly below — a soft landing after a 15-second black screen.
- H > 2000: both miss, player is left at H + 0.5 and falls the full distance.

Below ground: Character.UnderWorldCheck (:1055-1075) runs EVERY frame for players (`m_underWorldCheckTimer > 5f || IsPlayer()`), raycasts ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, and if position.y < groundHeight - 1 snaps the player to groundHeight + 0.5 with zeroed velocity. A buried destination therefore always pops the player to the surface directly above.

Underwater: sea level is 30 (ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel). The seabed is terrain and inside FindFloor's 1000 m reach, so an ocean-floor anchor completes at t = 8s and the player surfaces swimming with no damage.

World edge: Player.EdgeOfWorldKill (:11132-11152) pushes the player inward past 10420 m XZ while swimming or below y=30, and applies 99999 HitType.EdgeOfWorld damage past 10420 m when y < -10.
catalog.playerExperience: Three distinct arrivals, each a deliberate design choice. 'The Drop': the screen clears at 8 seconds and the player is suddenly 300 m above the Black Forest canopy in freefall, with a few seconds to deploy nothing at all before they die — a one-way punishment gate, or a feather-fall gimmick if the server also grants a status effect on arrival. 'The Long Fall': a 1500 m anchor gives a 15-second black screen (noticeably longer than any normal portal, which is itself a tell) and then the player simply appears standing on the ground, no fall, no damage — a stealth long-hop. 'The Well': a destination buried 40 m underground means the player materialises, the screen clears, and in the same frame they are snapped up to the surface — visually indistinguishable from a normal arrival, which makes it a free 'land exactly on top of whatever terrain is here' primitive with no height calculation needed at all.
failureModes: A destination above roughly 1000 m of clear air imposes a 15-second black screen, which players will report as a freeze or a crash
Fall damage after a Stage-3 completion is entirely real and can kill; there is no server-side way to see it happened except the character ZDO s_dead flag
A destination in a never-visited region may fail IsAreaReady past 8s; the 15s fallback then fires regardless, so worst case is always 15 seconds not infinity
EdgeOfWorldKill kills outright at >10420 m XZ and y < -10 with a HitType the player sees as an unexplained death

UnderWorldCheck uses ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, a raycast — inside a dungeon interior (y > 3000) the dungeon floor mesh is what it hits, which is correct, but over a hollow cave with no collider below it can pop a player through geometry
citations: Player.UpdateTeleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15379 (2s gate :15338, position pin :15343, maxAirAltitude reset :15346, 8s+IsAreaReady gate :15349, FindFloor :15354, 15s fallback :15360-15367)
openQuestions: Exact fall-damage curve versus drop height for a 1.0.7 player with mid-game armour — Character fall damage is computed from m_maxAirAltitude minus landing y. IN-GAME: drop a test character from 50/100/200/400 m via a Void Anchor and record HP loss.

Does IsAreaReady ever succeed for a point 1500 m above terrain? It queries the XZ zone only (:82066), so it should, but the sector's ZDOs must all be instanced. IN-GAME: time the black screen for a high anchor over a dense base versus open wilderness.
corrections: Delete the 'H > 1000 but H <= 2000' tier. GetSolidHeight(Vector3) :115525-115534 spans target.y+1000 → target.y-1000, the same ~1000 m downward reach as FindFloor (:115604-115613). For H > ~1000 both rays miss; the player is placed at target.y+0.5 after 15 s and falls the whole H. 'The Long Fall' stealth soft-landing does not exist. GetSolidHeight can only change the outcome by hitting something in the +1000 m ABOVE the target (e.g. a dungeon interior floor), which places the player higher, not lower.

Fall damage is capped at 100 (Character.UpdateGroundContact :2949-2958: `Clamp01((num-4)/16)*100`, then m_seman.ModifyFallDamage). 'The Drop' from any height ≥20 m deals 100 damage; a player above 100 HP survives.

'The Well': FindFloor from a buried point never hits the terrain above its origin, so the arrival is the 15 s branch (GetSolidHeight from y+1000 finds the surface). Buried anchors give a 15-second hold, not an 8-second one, and the surface placement comes from GetSolidHeight/UpdateTeleport, with UnderWorldCheck (:1064-1073) only as a same-frame backstop afterwards.

All of this runs only on the local owning client (Player.FixedUpdate :10204-10212 gates on m_nview.IsOwner() && m_localPlayer==this); the SERVER decompile citations are correct as code but the execution context is the client.

REFUTE 'H > 1000 but H <= 2000 soft landing': GetSolidHeight(Vector3) at :115525-115534 starts at p.y+1000 and casts 2000 m, reaching p.y-1000 — the same reach as FindFloor (:115604-115613, p.y+1 minus 1000). For H > 1000 both miss, GetSolidHeight returns p.y, player is placed at target.y+0.5 after 15 s and falls the full height. Only three bands exist: H <= ~1000 (8 s, full fall) and H > ~1000 (15 s, full fall).

'The Well' takes the 15 s path, not 8 s: FindFloor is cast from m_teleportTargetPos (inside the terrain mesh, no backface hit) so it fails; the surface placement comes from the t>15 GetSolidHeight branch (:15360-15367), not from UnderWorldCheck. UnderWorldCheck (:1055-1075) runs before UpdateTeleport each FixedUpdate and is overwritten by the position pin.

Fall damage is capped at 100 (Clamp01((num-4)/16)*100 at :2966-2968) and passes through m_seman.ModifyFallDamage; 'The Drop' is lethal only for players at <=100 HP. Water landings deal zero fall damage (:1644-1651).
Anchors at y > 3000 make Character.InInterior true (:4538-4541); note this for very high anchors.
Citation: the linearVelocity zero is at :15344 and m_maxAirAltitude reset at :15345 (option is off by one line); the 8 s gate is :15348.
evidence: Character.UnderWorldCheck — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:1055-1075; call order Character.CustomFixedUpdate :1011 before Player.FixedUpdate :10226
Client build identical: assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs UpdateTeleport/FindFloor/GetSolidHeight (verified by grep)
