catalog.name: Crypt Ingress — Portals Into Dungeon Interiors
catalog.oneLine: Dungeon interiors sit at zone-centre XZ with y + 5000, which is the same 64 m sector as the surface, so a portal can drop a player directly into a specific crypt room.
catalog.howItWorks:
Location.Awake (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133505-133515) instantiates a location's interior at `new Vector3(zoneCenter.x, transform.position.y + 5000f, zoneCenter.z)`. Character.InInterior(Vector3) is literally `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541). Zones and sectors are XZ-only — ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746) and GetSectorIndex (:115748-115753) ignore y entirely. So a dungeon interior occupies the SAME sector as the surface above it, and any ZDO placed at (zoneCentreX, ~5030, zoneCentreZ) syncs, saves and pairs exactly like a surface ZDO with no special handling anywhere.

Finding a specific room: DungeonGenerator.Save (:152970-152999) serialises every placed room into the generator's own ZDO as the byte array ZDOVars.s_roomData (:78573) with the layout `int count; { int roomHash; Vector3 worldPos; Quaternion worldRot; } * count`, read back verbatim by Load (:153002-153033). A server mod can BinaryReader that blob and get real, exact interior room coordinates. Resolving the room hash to a name needs DungeonDB.GetRoom (:152489), which is asset data.

Locating the DungeonGenerator ZDO itself is the hard part: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (:75390-75407) refuses ByteArray, so you cannot index on s_roomData. Two workable routes: (a) query Type.Int on ZDOVars.s_location (:78501) to enumerate every LocationProxy ZDO in the world with its location hash and position, then spatially query that zone's sector for a ZDO whose prefab carries a DungeonGenerator; or (b) simply place the anchor at the location's own zone centre + 5000 y and accept landing in whatever room the generator put there.

Critically, the dungeon room ZDOs only exist once that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer (ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115162, CreateGhostZones :113934-113938). On a fresh server the ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances entry exists from world creation but the s_roomData blob does not. So the mod must either wait for generation or fall back to the LocationInstance surface position.

Departure is free: the crypt door (class Teleport, :143316-143390) is untouched and still works normally. Note that building a portal inside a dungeon requires the client-honoured GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild key (read at Player piece validation :13353) — but a SERVER-created portal ZDO needs no such permission, because nothing validates placement server-side.
catalog.playerExperience: A dungeon-delve server where clearing a crypt permanently unlocks a shortcut back into its deepest room. The player finishes a Sunken Crypt, and a stone portal appears at the surface entrance tagged 'Crypt VII - Deep'. Walking in gives the normal 8-second portal fade, and they materialise in the same torch-lit chamber they fought the boss in, with the crypt door behind them for the walk out. To a vanilla client this is completely ordinary — the interior geometry loads exactly as it does when you walk in through the front door, because the sector is the same one. The server-authored portal inside the crypt cannot be built by hand without the DungeonBuild key, which means it reads unmistakably as a reward rather than something anyone could place.
failureModes: The dungeon interior is a Location prefab instantiated by the client's LocationProxy; if that expansion has not happened when the teleport completes, IsAreaReady (:82076) fails and the player waits out the full 15 s, then lands at GetSolidHeight — which may be the SURFACE terrain 5000 m below, dropping them outside the crypt entirely
s_roomData only exists after that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer, so on a fresh world the room list is empty and the mod has nothing to aim at
A portal ZDO physically inside dungeon geometry may intersect a wall; the TeleportWorldTrigger collider still fires but the model clips
Character.InInterior gates several unrelated client behaviours (crypt door NoBossPortals at :143355, building rules); a player standing at y>3000 is 'in an interior' to all of them
Interior room positions are stored in the generator ZDO, which is owned by whichever client generated it — reading it is safe, but it can be rewritten under you
prerequisites: The Void Anchor (or a real portal ZDO placed at the interior coordinate)
openQuestions: Does a distantTeleport into a dungeon interior actually satisfy IsAreaReady, or does the Location proxy expansion race it? IN-GAME: link a portal to a crypt room and time the black screen from a cold zone versus a warm one.

What is the prefab name of the DungeonGenerator component's host object, so it can be found by GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative? IN-GAME: dump prefab names of all ZDOs in a crypt's sector and look for the one carrying s_roomData.
catalog.id: wildcard:Crypt Ingress — Portals Into Dungeon Interiors
corrections: Route (a) (enumerate ZDOVars.s_location Int keys) depends on the LocationProxy ZDO, which is created by ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation during ghost generation (:115162+, :102657) — it does not exist any earlier than s_roomData does. Only m_locationInstances (:113295) is available pre-generation.

Handle the legacy room format: DungeonGenerator.Load falls back to `rooms` + `room{i}`/`_pos`/`_rot`/`_seed` keys (:153034+) and Save removes them on rewrite (:152987-152998). A world last saved before the byte-array format has no s_roomData until the dungeon is next loaded and saved.

Departure via the crypt door is gated: Teleport.Interact (:143360-143364) blocks with $msg_blockedbyboss when GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals is set and Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos). Not 'untouched' under that key.

DungeonDB.GetRoom needs DungeonDB.instance and its hash table (:152489-152496, GenerateHashList :152498); on a dedicated server verify DungeonDB is initialised before relying on room-name resolution — it is asset data, not ZDO data.
s_roomData write is at :152984, not :152986 (minor).

The dungeon start room / generator is at the entrance's prefab-local offset (+~5000 y), not at zone centre; m_zoneCenter (:152742-152745) is only the generation Bounds. Dropping a portal at zoneCentre+5000 blindly is likely to land in empty interior air (FindFloor miss → 15 s → GetSolidHeight also misses inside the 500 m-tall EnvZone unless a room is below). Always derive the target from s_roomData positions or from the DungeonGenerator ZDO's own GetPosition() (start room).

Simpler discovery: DungeonGenerator is its own networked object (ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115243-115252) whose ZDO prefab hash is the generator prefab's name; enumerate with ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab (:77447-77470) instead of the LocationProxy + sector scan. s_roomData is read via zdo.GetByteArray(ZDOVars.s_roomData).

Add: vanilla already guards the arrival race — DungeonGenerator.LoadRoomPrefabsAsync calls ZoneSystem.SetLoadingInZone (:152786-152787), IsZoneLoaded returns false while rooms load (:114045-114051), so IsAreaReady blocks UpdateTeleport until geometry exists. No timeout: a failed room load hangs the teleport on the black screen.
GetAllZDOIDsWithHash's default branch (:75403-75406) also calls UnityEngine.Debug.Break() — never pass Type.ByteArray.
portal_wood.m_allowedInDungeons is asset data; the DungeonBuild claim (:13353) is plausible but unverified from the decompile.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core geometry holds. Location.Awake (:133505-133515) instantiates m_interiorPrefab at (zoneCenter.x, transform.y+5000, zoneCenter.z) with scale (64,500,64). Character.InInterior(Vector3) is `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541). ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746) and GetSectorIndex (:115748-115753) use only x and z, so an interior ZDO shares the surface sector; ZNetScene.IsAreaReady (:82064-82081) is also zone-XZ only, so a vanilla client's UpdateTeleport will complete at an interior target once the zone's ZDOs are instantiated. DungeonGenerator.Save (:152970-152999) writes `count {roomHash, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot}` to ZDOVars.s_roomData (:78573, write at :152984) and Load (:153002-153033) reads it back through DungeonDB.instance.GetRoom(hash) (:152489-152496). ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (:75390-75407) supports only Float/Long/Int/String — ByteArray hits the default branch (LogError + Debug.Break). LocationProxy writes ZDOVars.s_location as an Int (:102657), so route (a) is valid. SpawnLocation (:115162+) instantiates the DungeonGenerator ZNetView and calls Generate(mode) (:115247-115255); CreateGhostZones runs on the server around every peer refpos (:113934-113938), so s_roomData exists only after some peer has been near. Corrections: LocationProxy ZDOs are themselves only created by SpawnLocation, so route (a) has exactly the same generation dependency as s_roomData — only ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances (:113295) exists pre-generation. Older worlds may still carry the legacy `rooms`/`roomN_pos` Int/Vec3 keys (Save cleans them at :152987-152998; Load's else-branch at :153034+ reads them), so a parser must handle both formats. The crypt door's Teleport.Interact is NOT unconditional: it refuses with $msg_blockedbyboss when NoBossPortals is set and the character is inside an active boss dungeon (:143360-143364). The DungeonBuild key check (:13353) is read correctly.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. Location.Awake instantiates the interior EnvZone at (zoneCenter.x, y+5000, zoneCenter.z) (:133505-133515); InInterior is position.y > 3000 (:4538-4541); GetZone/GetSectorIndex ignore y (:115741-115753); ZDOMan.FindObjects is purely sector-keyed (:77374-77387) so interior ZDOs sync like surface ZDOs; GetPortalList has no y filter so an interior portal pairs normally. DungeonGenerator.Save/Load format (int count; {int hash; Vector3 pos; Quaternion rot}) is exact (:152970-153033) and DungeonDB.instance.GetRoom exists in the server assembly (:152489). The DungeonGenerator is instantiated by ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation as its own networked object with its own ZDO (:115243-115252, `component2.Generate(mode)`), and in Ghost mode on the dedicated server (ZoneSystem.Update → CreateGhostZones per peer, :113930-113938) Generate() calls Save() — so s_roomData exists once any peer has ghost-generated the zone, as the option says. Two things the option gets wrong or misses. (a) The generator itself is NOT at zone centre: Generate sets m_zoneCenter = GetZonePos(zone) with y = transform.y - m_originalPosition.y (:152742-152743) only as a bounds box; the generator/start room sits at the entrance's local offset (+5000 y) unless m_useCustomInteriorTransform. Route (b) 'place at zone centre + 5000 and accept whatever room is there' can therefore land in empty air inside the 64x500x64 EnvZone with no room under it — FindFloor then misses and the player is dropped at target after 15 s, falling to whatever the interior has below (possibly nothing until GetSolidHeight fails too). Use roomData positions (or the generator ZDO's own position = start room) instead. (b) A cheaper locator than the LocationProxy spatial query: the generator ZDO's prefab hash is the generator prefab name, obtainable server-side from ZoneSystem.m_locations[i].m_prefab.Asset.GetComponent<Location>().m_generator.name; ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab (:77447-77470) then enumerates them directly. Also, the arrival race is handled by vanilla: DungeonGenerator.LoadRoomPrefabsAsync registers ZoneSystem.SetLoadingInZone (:152786-152787, :115817), which makes IsZoneLoaded false (:114045-114051) and therefore IsAreaReady false, so Player.UpdateTeleport waits for room geometry before FindFloor. Caveat: there is no timeout on that wait. GetAllZDOIDsWithHash's unsupported-type branch also calls UnityEngine.Debug.Break() (:75404) — harmless in a player build but do not call it with ByteArray. Whether portal_wood.m_allowedInDungeons is false (so hand-building is DungeonBuild-gated, :13353) is asset data not visible in the decompile; the server-side placement claim (no validation) is correct because piece placement is a client-authored ZDO. Enforcement: the portal's existence and pairing are server-authored ZDO state, but transit is client-executed; client-honoured is the honest label.

catalog.name: Ephemeral Event Gates
catalog.oneLine: Portals the server conjures for the duration of an event and destroys afterwards, with no player ever placing a piece.
catalog.howItWorks:
Creation (the full five-line recipe, because ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO does not do it for you): `int h = <portal prefab hash>; var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, h); z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(h); z.SetRotation(rot); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag);` CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) pools a ZDO, sets owner to the server session, and calls AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash) — which, because the hash is in Game.PortalPrefabHash, files it in m_portalObjects, removes it from the sector array, and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77732-77752). It does NOT write the prefab onto the ZDO body and does NOT set Persistent; ZNetView.Awake (:82612-82620) is where vanilla does those, and a hand-built ZDO missing SetPrefab has m_prefab = -1 and will spam 'Missing prefab hash' on every client every frame (:82004-82008).

Portal ZDOs are saved by a special path: GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621-77632) dumps the WHOLE of m_portalObjects into the ChunkPortal file whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set, with no Persistent filter at all — so a mod-created portal survives restart even if you forgot Persistent. Conversely, AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) explicitly excludes portal-hash ZDOs from normal chunks.

Deletion: ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) is a silent no-op unless zdo.IsOwner(), so always `z.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` first. It queues into m_destroySendList and SendDestroyed broadcasts the routed DestroyZDO RPC to every peer; each client's HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) removes it from m_portalObjects, sets DirtyPortalObjects, and ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the GameObject in front of the player. The ZDOID goes into m_deadZDOs (:76997) so it can never be resurrected by a replayed packet.

Lifecycle: trigger on anything the server can see — a boss key appearing (Harmony postfix on ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd, the BossDefeatWatch pattern), a RandEventSystem event starting, a clock, an admin command on the dedicated server's stdin. Pair the gate with Game.instance.ConnectPortals() called directly (:100589) instead of waiting up to 5 s.

To hide a temporary gate from vanilla's pairer entirely, ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643) returns the LIVE m_portalObjects dictionary — removing an entry makes Game.ConnectPortals blind to it while the ZDO stays fully alive for clients. That lets a server hold a hand-wired one-way link with no reconciliation race at all.
catalog.playerExperience: Eikthyr dies. Within a second, a stone portal fades into existence in the middle of the sacrificial circle, already glowing 'connected', tagged 'Stag Road - 20m'. Everyone present sees it appear from nothing — no build effects, no materials, no one placed it. It links to a fixed hub the admins maintain. Twenty minutes later it winks out mid-conversation and the ground is empty again. Nobody can deconstruct it for materials while it exists, nobody can retag it into their own network, and it leaves no trace in the world save once the timer runs out.
failureModes: Omitting SetPrefab leaves m_prefab at -1 and every client logs 'Missing prefab hash: -1' 30 times per second while standing near it
Forgetting SetOwner before DestroyZDO makes the delete a completely silent no-op — the portal stays forever

Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903) caches raw ZDO object references across a full 5 s tick; if an ephemeral gate is destroyed inside that window, ZDOPool.Release recycles the object and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes a connection through a stale reference
If the gate shares a tag with player portals, Game.ConnectPortals will happily pair a player's portal to it and then strand that player when it vanishes

Creating a portal ZDO with a hash that is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash skips AddIfPortal entirely, so it lands in m_objectsBySector, is excluded from the chunk save by the portal filter (:77572), and disappears on restart with no error
prerequisites: Runtime discovery of Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash / m_portalPrefabs (never hard-code portal_wood)
openQuestions: Which prefabs are in Game.m_portalPrefabs (:99828)? Inspector data. IN-GAME: log Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs names and Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash at first Heartbeat on the dedicated server.

Does removing an entry from ZDOMan.GetPortals() desynchronise HandleDestroyedZDO's later removal attempt? IN-GAME: hide a portal from the dictionary, destroy it, and check for a leaked m_objectsByID entry.
corrections: Drop the 'remove from ZDOMan.GetPortals()' hiding trick. Portal ZDOs are not in m_objectsBySector (AddIfPortal → RemoveFromSector :77749), so FindObjects (:77376-77379) is the only route to peers and GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77624) the only route to disk; an unlisted portal is invisible to new peers, receives no revision sync, and is not saved. To keep a hand-wired link from being reconciled, either Harmony-prefix Game.ConnectPortals on the server (this is a server-side mod; Harmony is available) or exploit the reconcile predicate (:100600-100604): a link A→B survives phase 1 whenever B exists, B.tag == A.tag and B has ANY non-None connection — reciprocity is never tested.

'Nobody can deconstruct it / nobody can retag it' is not true of a bare server-created portal. Player.RemovePiece → WearNTear.RPC_Remove (:150411-150425) and TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) succeed for whichever client ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership to. Those guarantees come only from the Adamant Gate (m_canBeRemoved via LoadFields) plus a tag/connection re-assert loop.

Calling Game.instance.ConnectPortals() once stages the pair (AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100681, SetConnection immediate for server-owned ZDOs :100636-100648); the ForceSetConnection re-write happens on the NEXT call (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698). For a gate to a fixed hub, write both ZDO.SetConnection directions yourself instead of relying on the pairer.
HandleDestroyedZDO starts at :76962 and ZNetView.Awake fabrication at :82613 (minor line drift).

Do NOT remove the gate from ZDOMan.GetPortals(): m_portalObjects is also the sync index (ZDOMan.FindObjects :77380-77383) and the save index (:77621-77632); a removed portal is never delivered to peers who lack it and is never saved. Hide from the pairer with a Harmony postfix on the public ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648-77656), which allocates a new list per call and is only used by Game.ConnectPortals and ConvertPortals.

Refute 'nobody can deconstruct it': Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12420) allows any vanilla client to remove a creator-less piece; DropResources yields Max(1, n/3) materials for !IsPlacedByPlayer (:136343-136346). Needs the Piece.m_canBeRemoved LoadFields override to hold.

Refute 'nobody can retag it': TeleportWorld.Interact/RPC_SetTag (:143470-143480, :143587-143600) is client-side and ward-gated only; an unwarded conjured gate can be retagged (and thereby disconnected) by anyone. Server can only re-assert reactively.

'No trace in the save' holds only if the timer completes before a save: the portal chunk ignores Persistent, so a live gate at save time persists across restart. Mark gates with a mod key and sweep on ZDOMan.Load/Game start.

Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589), not private as the prior notes implied; SetConnection/ForceSetConnection/RPC_SetConnection are private. A server-owned gate takes the immediate SetConnection path because ZNet.GetPeer(serverSessionId) is null (:100637-100641).
Player.RemovePiece also emits no message on the m_canBeRemoved refusal, consistent with the Adamant option.
evidence: ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632; AddObjectsPerChunk exclusion :77572; load :76475-76482
ZDOMan.FindObjects uses m_portalObjects for sync — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77381; CreateSyncList :77212-77238
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Creation recipe verified. ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) (:76674-76692) → ZDOPool.Create → ZDO.Initialize (AddToSector) → SetOwnerInternal(m_sessionID) → AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash) (:77732-77752), which files it in m_portalObjects, RemoveFromSector, DirtyPortalObjects=true, and never writes m_prefab (default -1, :73317) or Persistent. ZNetView.Awake's fabrication block (:82613-82619) is where Persistent/Type/Distant/SetPrefab/SetRotation are set; a ZDO left at m_prefab=-1 makes ZNetScene.CreateObject log 'Missing prefab hash' (:82005-82007) on each CreateObjects pass (only prefab==0 is skipped silently, :81986-81993). Save: GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621-77632) clones every m_portalObjects entry into ChunkPortal with no Persistent test; AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal hashes (:77572); the load path re-files ChunkPortal entries unconditionally (:76475-76482). DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) is a no-op unless IsOwner; SendDestroyed routes 'DestroyZDO' to 0L (:76937-76950); HandleDestroyedZDO (:76962-77000) removes from m_portalObjects, sets DirtyPortalObjects, releases, and on the server records m_deadZDOs (:76995-76998), which RPC_ZDOData uses to re-destroy resurrected IDs (:77133-77137). ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the client GameObject. Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589) and Game.SetConnection takes the immediate path for server-owned ZDOs (:100636-100648). REFUTED sub-claim: 'remove the entry from the live GetPortals() dictionary to hide it from the pairer while the ZDO stays fully alive for clients'. AddIfPortal removed the ZDO from m_objectsBySector, so m_portalObjects is the ONLY container the sync path enumerates: FindObjects (:77367-77381) reads m_objectsBySector then m_portalObjects; CreateSyncList (:77212-77238) → FindSectorObjects → FindObjects. Removing the entry means peers entering the sector never receive the ZDO, existing peers never receive further revisions, and the save path (:77624) drops it. The trick kills the portal. Also the 'nobody can deconstruct / retag it' experience text is false for a bare server-spawned portal: a vanilla client's Player.RemovePiece → WearNTear.Remove → RPC_Remove (:150411-150425) and TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) both work once ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands the client ownership; those protections require the Adamant Gate / tag re-assert options.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Creation, save and deletion mechanics are verified line-for-line: CreateNewZDO pools via ZDOPool.Create (whose Initialize adds to m_objectsBySector, :78269-78275), sets owner to the server session, and AddIfPortal moves it into m_portalObjects and out of the sector array (:77732-77752); it sets neither Persistent nor m_prefab (ZNetView.Awake does that, :82612-82620). GetSaveClonePerChunk dumps all of m_portalObjects when DirtyPortalObjects with no Persistent filter (:77621-77632); AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal hashes (:77572). DestroyZDO is a silent no-op unless IsOwner (:76929-76935); SendDestroyed broadcasts to 0L; HandleDestroyedZDO has no owner/sender check, prunes m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:76963-77000); ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed destroys the GameObject (:82186-82194). Game.ConnectPortals is PUBLIC (:100589) and can be called directly; because a server-created ZDO's owner is the server session, ZNet.GetPeer(owner) is null and SetConnection takes the immediate local path (:100637-100651), so one call pairs it. Three claims fail. (1) 'Remove the entry from GetPortals() to hide it from the pairer': ZDOMan.FindObjects (:77374-77387) is the ONLY way sector sync discovers ZDOs and it reads m_objectsBySector (which AddIfPortal removed the portal from) plus m_portalObjects. Removing the portal from m_portalObjects makes it invisible to every peer who has not already received it (new joiners, players entering the sector), to ReleaseNearbyZDOS, and to the save. The clean hiding primitive is a Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.GetPortalList (public, returns a fresh list, only callers are Game.ConnectPortals :100592 and ConvertPortals :77815) that filters out mod-flagged ZDOs. (2) 'Nobody can deconstruct it for materials': Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12420) gates only on m_canBeRemoved, no-build locations, ward access and CheckCanRemovePiece; a creator-less piece is removable by any vanilla hammer. Piece.DropResources drops Max(1, amount/3) when !IsPlacedByPlayer (:136325-136355, :136443) — reduced, not zero. Immunity requires the Adamant Gate/LoadFields option. (3) 'Nobody can retag it': TeleportWorld.Interact → RequestText → RPC_SetTag runs on the owning client with only a client-side PrivateArea.CheckAccess (:143470-143480, :143587-143600); with no ward anyone retags it, which also clears its connection. The server can only reactively re-assert. (4) 'Leaves no trace in the save': only if the timer fires before shutdown. Because the portal save path ignores Persistent, a gate alive at save time is written to ChunkPortal and comes back after restart with no timer — the mod must mark gates (e.g. a string key) and sweep them on load. Minor: m_deadZDOs is written only under ZNet.IsServer (:76994-76998), which is fine here. Enforcement 'server-enforced' is correct for existence/lifecycle/pairing (route-form), not for the immunity claims.

catalog.name: The Decoy Gate
catalog.oneLine: A portal that reports itself connected and glows, but silently refuses to teleport forever, built by pointing its connection at a ZDOID that does not exist.
catalog.howItWorks:
The client evaluates 'connected' and 'usable' with two DIFFERENT functions and only one of them is on the hover path.

TeleportWorld.HaveTarget (:143631-143638) returns `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` — a pure field test, no lookup. GetHoverText (:143461) picks between $piece_portal_connected and $piece_portal_unconnected from HaveTarget alone, and UpdatePortal (:143496-143501) fires the m_connected EffectList and drives m_hadTarget from it, which Update (:143511-143515) lerps into the model's _EmissionColor toward m_colorTargetfound.

TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143640-143656) additionally requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) != null`, and when the ZDO is absent it calls ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO and returns false. Teleport() gate 1 (:143519-143522) is `if (!TargetFound()) return;` — a bare return with NO player.Message.

So: write `portal.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, new ZDOID(someSessionId, someNeverAllocatedId))`. HaveTarget is true (hover says connected, portal glows blue), TargetFound is permanently false (the ZDO never resolves), and walking through does absolutely nothing with zero feedback. The client's RequestZDO goes to the server's RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692), which calls peer.ForceSendZDO(id); AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77281) then finds GetZDO(id) == null and prunes the entry silently. No log, no packet, no cost.

Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100600-100604) WILL tear this down within 5 s because `zDO == null`. Two ways to keep it: (a) re-assert the fake ZDOID every 2 s with SetOwner + SetConnection + ForceSendZDO, which costs one DataRevision bump per rewrite because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (:74951-74960) no-ops on an unchanged value and phase 1 always changes it back; or (b) cleanly, remove the decoy from the live ZDOMan.GetPortals() dictionary (:77643) so vanilla's pairer never iterates it at all.

A softer decoy variant: point it at a real Void Anchor that the server deliberately never force-sends and that sits in a sector no peer visits. The link is then legitimate and survives reconciliation (given a matching tag and a self-loop), but every client's TargetFound fails until the server chooses to deliver the anchor — a switchable gate with no visible state change.
catalog.playerExperience: A grand stone portal stands at the top of a ruined tower, humming and glowing exactly like a working one, hover text reading 'Portal, tag: THE DEEP ROAD [connected]'. Players walk in. Nothing. No message, no black screen, no bounce-back — they simply walk out the other side of the frame. They try again. They check their inventory for ore. They ask in chat. The portal is, as far as any vanilla client can tell, perfectly healthy and connected to something. Used deliberately this is the best puzzle primitive in the whole toolkit: the gate is 'sealed' in a way that gives the player no error to Google, and the server can make it real later by simply delivering the anchor — at which point the very same portal, unchanged, suddenly works.
failureModes: Game.ConnectPortals nulls a dangling connection every 5 s (:100601, zDO == null branch), so the decoy needs either a re-assert loop or removal from the live portal dictionary
A re-assert loop that fights vanilla generates a DataRevision bump and a ForceSendZDO per cycle to every peer — budget it like Wonderland's StructureUpkeep 256-broadcast cap
The complete absence of feedback is genuinely indistinguishable from a mod bug; pair every decoy with a PlayerNotify toast or a DamageText Bonus string, or players will file it as broken

A fabricated ZDOID could theoretically collide with a real future ZDOID from the same session; mint decoy targets from a real ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO that is then destroyed, so the id lands in m_deadZDOs (:76997) and can never be reused
ZDOID.UserID values are renumbered on world load, so a hand-built fake id must be re-derived after every restart
openQuestions: How often does a vanilla client actually fire RequestZDO for an unresolvable target — every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s) or only on transit? UpdatePortal calls TargetFound at :143507, so likely 2/s per nearby player. IN-GAME: count RequestZDO packets server-side with a player idling next to a decoy for 60 s.
corrections: There IS a visible tell: TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal :143505 `m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound())` — the proximity activation effect never turns on for a decoy when a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (5 m). Real portals do. 'Perfectly healthy as far as any vanilla client can tell' is overstated; the hover text and idle glow match, the approach effect does not.

Remove fix (b). Deleting the decoy from ZDOMan.GetPortals() also deletes it from the only sync path (FindObjects :77376-77379, CreateSyncList :77212-77238) and the save path (:77624). Replace with a server-side Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals that skips mod-flagged ZDOs, or accept the 2 s re-assert cost.

The 'softer decoy' (undelivered Void Anchor) does not work unmodified: RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) force-sends any existing ZDO to the requesting client on demand. It needs a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO (or ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO) to withhold the anchor.

Not save-stable: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) requires GetZDO(target) != null, so the fake-ZDOID connection is dropped at world save and the decoy reloads as 'unconnected' until the mod re-writes it on startup.
A vanilla client that receives ownership (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS) can retag the decoy via RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600), which clears the connection; the mod must re-assert.

Visible tell: UpdatePortal sets m_target_found active only when `closestPlayer.IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` (:143502-143506); a decoy never shows the in-frame effect when approached — identical to the 'unteleportable items' look, not 'perfectly healthy'.
'No packet' is wrong: TargetFound calls ZDOMan.RequestZDO (:143653) on every 0.5 s UpdatePortal with a teleportable player within 5 m and on every trigger enter — one routed RPC each.

Keep-alive (a) rewrite-every-2s produces a visible flicker every reconcile (HaveTarget false→true fires m_connected.Create at :143498-143501 and toggles hover/emission). Keep-alive (b) removing from m_portalObjects breaks sync and save (FindObjects :77380-77383, GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77632). Use a Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.GetPortalList (public, :77648-77656) or on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) to skip/re-assert decoys within the same tick.
Save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75475) requires the target ZDO to exist, so a fake-ZDOID connection is dropped at save; re-assert decoys on load.

Softer variant: the server cannot passively 'never deliver' an existing anchor — RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) force-sends it on the first client request. Withholding needs a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO filtering that ZDOID.
Use a fake ZDOID whose UserID is not the server session (or any peer) so m_nextUid growth can never allocate it.
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO / AddForceSendZdos / ZDOPeer.ShouldSend — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77689-77692, 77263-77281, ShouldSend in ZDOPeer
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The two-function split is real. TeleportWorld.HaveTarget (:143631-143638) is `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`; TargetFound (:143640-143656) additionally requires ZDOMan.GetZDO(id) != null and calls RequestZDO on miss. GetHoverText (:143453-143464) picks $piece_portal_connected from HaveTarget; UpdatePortal (:143491-143507) fires m_connected on the HaveTarget transition and Update (:143509-143513) lerps emission toward m_colorTargetfound from m_hadTarget. Teleport() gate 1 (:143519-143522) is a bare return. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) has no feedback either. RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) → ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO adds to m_forceSend; AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77284) prunes IDs with GetZDO==null silently. So the fake-ZDOID decoy is real. Three refutations of detail: (1) 'no visible state change' is wrong — UpdatePortal line :143505 `m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound())` drives the proximity 'target found' effect object from TargetFound, so a decoy never shows the activation effect when a teleportable player stands within m_activationRange (5 m) — a visible tell versus a real portal. (2) The 'remove from ZDOMan.GetPortals() dictionary' fix is broken: portals live only in m_portalObjects (AddIfPortal RemoveFromSector :77749) and FindObjects (:77376-77379) is the sync path, so an unlisted decoy is never sent to new peers, gets no revision updates and is dropped from the save (:77624). Use a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals instead. (3) The 'softer' variant ('a real Void Anchor the server deliberately never force-sends') fails in vanilla: the client's TargetFound → RequestZDO → server RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) → ForceSendZDO → AddForceSendZdos delivers any existing ZDO to the requesting peer regardless of sector (ShouldSend only compares revisions). Withholding the anchor requires a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO / ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO. Save boundary: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) only emits hash data when GetZDO(target) != null, so a fake-ZDOID connection is discarded at save; after restart the decoy loads unconnected (grey, 'unconnected') until re-asserted. Retag: a vanilla owner retag (RPC_SetTag :143587-143600) clears the connection, so the decoy must be held/re-asserted like any server-authored link. Enforcement stays server-enforced because this is a 'route open?' decision the server owns.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The split between HaveTarget (pure ZDOID != None, :143631-143638) and TargetFound (requires ZDOMan.GetZDO != null, else RequestZDO + false, :143640-143656) is exactly as claimed; GetHoverText uses HaveTarget (:143459-143463); Teleport gate 1 is a bare `if (!TargetFound()) return;` with no message (:143519-143522); Update lerps emission from m_hadTarget which UpdatePortal sets from HaveTarget (:143491-143515). Server RPC_RequestZDO → peer.ForceSendZDO → AddForceSendZdos prunes when GetZDO is null (:77689-77692, :77263-77281). Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 clears it within 5 s (:100594-100606). Four corrections. (1) There IS a visible tell: UpdatePortal drives m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound()) (:143506) — the in-frame portal effect that vanilla shows when a teleportable player stands within 5 m never appears on a decoy. It looks exactly like the 'carrying ore' state, not like a healthy portal. (2) 'No packet, no cost' is false: every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s) with a teleportable player within m_activationRange, plus every trigger enter, sends a routed RequestZDO RPC client→server (:143653). Cheap, but not zero. (3) Keep-alive option (a) 'rewrite every 2 s' is a bad design: between the 5 s teardown and the rewrite the client sees HaveTarget flip false→true, which fires m_connected.Create (:143498-143501), swaps hover to $piece_portal_unconnected and starts the emission lerp — a flicker every 5 s. Option (b) 'remove from GetPortals()' breaks sync and save (ZDOMan.FindObjects :77380-77383 and GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77632 both read m_portalObjects). The clean primitive is a Harmony postfix on the public ZDOMan.GetPortalList (:77648) filtering decoys, or a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) that re-asserts in the same frame (ForceSendZDO only queues, so peers see the final state). (4) Save boundary: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75475) drops any connection whose target ZDO does not exist (`GetZDO(m_target) != null` required), so a fake-ZDOID decoy reloads as unconnected; the mod must re-assert on world load. The 'softer variant' has a further hole: the server does not choose whether to deliver the anchor — the vanilla RPC_RequestZDO handler force-sends any existing ZDO on client request (:77689-77692, AddForceSendZdos :77273-77276 sends whenever peer.ShouldSend), so 'never force-sends' requires a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO (or ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO) filtering the anchor's ZDOID. Also pick the fake ZDOID with a userID no session will ever use; a fake (serverSessionId, highId) can become a real object once m_nextUid reaches it. Enforcement server-enforced is fair: the sealed state is a server-owned connection field the client cannot make usable.

catalog.name: The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface
catalog.oneLine: ZDOVars.s_tag is an uncapped, unfiltered, server-writable string that a vanilla client renders live through Localization.Localize — the only in-world text channel a server-only portal mod has.
catalog.howItWorks:
The write side has no limits whatsoever. ZDO.Set(int, string) performs no ownership check and no validation (:73721). The 10-character cap lives only in TeleportWorld.Interact's call to TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, '$piece_portal_tag', 10) (:143482), which sets m_inputField.characterLimit on the CLIENT UI. CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC in the SERVER build is the single statement `return text;` (:94588-94591), and in the CLIENT build (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) it early-returns unless ugcType is ServerName or RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() — false on Steam. The censored flag from CensorShittyWords.Filter is computed in GetTagInfo (:143568) and then only surfaced when ZNet.m_onlineBackend == PlayFab (:143462). On a Steam dedicated server the raw string is what every player reads.

The render path is the interesting part. GetHoverText (:143453-143463) builds `Localization.instance.Localize('$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"' + text + '" [' + text2 + ']' + newline + text3 + ...)` — the tag is CONCATENATED INTO the string BEFORE Localize runs. Three exploitable consequences:
(1) A tag containing a localization token such as $piece_portal_connected or $KEY_Use is resolved by the client in the player's own language and their own keybinds.
(2) A newline character in the tag produces a genuine multi-line hover panel. The tag is a small text box, not a single line.
(3) Rich text: `text.RemoveRichTextTags()` is applied at :143459, and StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703) is `Regex.Replace(text, '<[/a-zA-Z0-9= "''#;:()$_-]*?>', '')`. The character class EXCLUDES the less-than sign. Regex.Replace makes a single forward pass and does not re-scan its own output. Therefore the input `<<color=red>color=red>` has no match starting at index 0 (the lazy class cannot consume the second less-than), matches `<color=red>` starting at index 1, and the surviving output is exactly `<color=red>` — which TextMeshPro then renders as real markup. Nested-tag smuggling gives coloured, sized and sprite-tagged portal hover text from a pure ZDO write.

Persistence trap: a tag-only write does NOT dirty the portal chunk. DirtyPortalObjects is set by ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for ConnectionType.Portal (:73661-73676), by AddIfPortal (:77750) and by HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986) — and by nothing else. ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision goes to SetDirtySector (:73839), and SetDirtyChunks marks a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). So every server-side tag rewrite MUST be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) or it silently vanishes at the next world save.
catalog.playerExperience: Portals stop being labels and become signage. A hub gate reads, on hover, a three-line panel: 'THE CROSSROADS' in gold, then 'Next rotation in 04:12', then 'Currently open to: Ashlands Foothold'. A quest gate's tag counts down live as the server rewrites it. A contested gate turns red when another faction holds it. During a server event every portal in the world briefly reads the same line. And because the tag is also the pairing key for Game.ConnectPortals, the mod has to be careful: the visible text and the routing key are the same field, so a 'display' tag must either be shared byte-for-byte across a whole network or the mod must own pairing outright.
failureModes: s_tag is BOTH the display string and Game.ConnectPortals's equality key (:100601, :100669) — any per-portal display text inside one network is torn down every 5 s unless the mod owns pairing
A tag-only write is lost at the next save unless ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called explicitly

If a player opens the vanilla tag dialog on a server-written long tag, TextInput.Show assigns the existing text after setting characterLimit = 10 (:61515-61522) — a vanilla client may clamp and save back a truncated tag, destroying the display AND the routing key
RemoveRichTextTags strips plain markup; only the nested-smuggle form survives, and TMP's tolerance for it is unverified
A very long tag is re-serialized in full on every ZDO send (ZDOMan.SendZDOs :77062 has no delta encoding), so a 500-character tag on 200 portals is real per-peer bandwidth

Rewriting a distant portal's tag as a message does not reach a player until they are in that portal's sector (CreateSyncList :77212-77227) unless the mod calls ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, id)
prerequisites: Ownership of Game.ConnectPortals pairing if per-portal display text is wanted
citations: CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591; client version assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947
openQuestions: Does TextMeshPro actually honour the smuggled <color=...> that survives RemoveRichTextTags, or does the hover label use a non-rich-text component? IN-GAME: set a tag to the doubled form and hover it on a vanilla client.

Does GuiInputField clamp a programmatically assigned .text to characterLimit? TextInput.Show sets the limit then the text (:61519-61520). IN-GAME: server-write a 40-character tag, open and confirm the vanilla dialog, re-read s_tag.

Does Localization.Localize resolve tokens embedded mid-string, and does it handle an unknown $token gracefully? Localization lives outside this decompile set. IN-GAME: set a tag to $KEY_Use and hover.
catalog.id: wildcard:The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface
corrections: Raw-string rendering depends on the reading CLIENT's platform, not on the server's backend: client CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) filters when RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (:88608-88620: Xbox or HardwareCategory.Console) is true, returning censored text or the $ugc_* placeholder. Crossplay console players will not see rich/long tags as intended.

AddIfPortal sets DirtyPortalObjects only on first insertion (:77740-77743 early-returns when already listed), so a routine RPC_ZDOData re-application of a tagged portal does NOT dirty the portal chunk either — the SetDirtyPortals() requirement after every server tag write stands and is stricter than stated.

A vanilla client that holds ownership (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS) can replace the tag via RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) with no server-side veto; the display tag needs a re-assert loop and, because the tag is the pairing key, the mod must own pairing (Harmony on Game.ConnectPortals) for any per-portal display text.
Hover-panel layout/overflow for multi-line or very long tags is UI behaviour not present in the decompile — needs an in-game check before relying on 3-line signage.

Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced: any vanilla client can overwrite the tag through TeleportWorld.Interact → RPC_SetTag (:143470-143480, :143587-143600) with only a client-side ward check; the server can only reactively re-write. Display fidelity is honoured by the client; the text is not protected.

Hover text is rendered only while the crosshair is on the portal within interact range; the 'signage' is on-demand, not ambient. No other vanilla surface renders the tag (map pins for portals are not vanilla).
Every server tag rewrite on a paired portal must update both ends in the same tick; Game.ConnectPortals (:100600-100604) disconnects on any tag mismatch at its next 5 s pass.
Clear or set ZDOVars.s_tagauthor alongside the tag when rewriting; RPC_SetTag compares both (:143590-143592).
Localize caches each distinct input (assembly_guiutils.decompiled.cs:863); rapidly changing tags produce unbounded distinct strings — verify cache bound before per-second countdowns on many portals.
evidence: StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703; assembly_utils.decompiled.cs:6714-6717 (regex executed locally to confirm smuggling)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists and does what is claimed. ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) has no ownership test. The 10-char cap is only TextInput.Show's `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` (:61515-61521) via TeleportWorld.Interact (:143482); RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) does not validate length. Server CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591). GetTagInfo (:143556-143570) computes censored at :143568 and GetHoverText only surfaces it when ZNet.m_onlineBackend == PlayFab (:143462). GetHoverText (:143453-143464) applies RemoveRichTextTags at :143459 then concatenates the tag INTO the string before Localization.Localize (:143463), so $tokens (including $KEY_*) resolve client-side and an embedded newline yields a multi-line panel. StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags is `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")` in both assembly_utils_SERVER (:6700-6703) and the client assembly_utils (:6714-6717); the class excludes '<', Regex.Replace is single-pass, so `<<color=red>color=red>` → no match at index 0, `<color=red>` removed at index 1, output `<color=red>` — the smuggling analysis is correct. Persistence trap confirmed: ZDO.Set → IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) → SetDirtySector (:76694-76700) → SetDirtyChunks on a regular chunk that excludes portal hashes (:77572); DirtyPortalObjects is set only by ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for Portal (:73661-73676), AddIfPortal (:77750, and only on first insertion — :77740-77743 returns early if already listed) and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986); SetDirtyPortals is :76702-76705. Correction: the raw-string claim is per-CLIENT platform, not per-server backend. Client FilterUGC (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) returns raw text only when `ugcType != ServerName && !RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()`; PlatformRequiresTextFiltering (:88608-88620) is true on Xbox and any HardwareCategory.Console. Crossplay console players on the same Steam dedicated server get the Censored or BlockedByPrivilege ($ugc_* placeholder) path. Also, LoadFields-style rendering limits (TMP overflow, hover panel sizing) are UI-side and unverifiable from the decompile; treat very long tags as untested. Enforcement: the string is server-written and a vanilla client honours it, but any owning vanilla client can overwrite it through RPC_SetTag with no server veto (owner-side execution, no routed packet when the owner is local per handoff), so 'server-enforced' means 'server-writable and re-assertable', not tamper-proof.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Write side verified: ZDO.Set(int,string) has no ownership check (:73722-73727); the 10-char cap is only TextInput.m_inputField.characterLimit set from TeleportWorld.Interact's RequestText(this,'$piece_portal_tag',10) (:143482, :61509-61521); server CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` (:94588-94591); client FilterUGC early-returns unless ServerName or PlatformRequiresTextFiltering (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94910); censored flag only surfaces on PlayFab (:143462). Render path verified: GetHoverText concatenates the tag into the string BEFORE Localization.Localize (:143463), and Localize (assembly_guiutils.decompiled.cs:838-866) does $-token substitution over the whole string, so tokens and keybind names in the tag resolve client-side; '\n' in the tag survives. RemoveRichTextTags regex is `<[\/a-zA-Z0-9= "\"''#;:()$_-]*?>` on both builds (utils SERVER :6700-6703, client :6714-6717); the class excludes '<', and I confirmed by running the pattern: '<<color=red>color=red>' → '<color=red>', '<<size=40>size=40>BIG<</size>/size>' → '<size=40>BIG</size>'. Nested-tag smuggling is real. Persistence trap verified: DirtyPortalObjects is only set in ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection (:73656-73676), AddIfPortal (:77750) and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986); IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector → SetDirtyChunks marks a normal chunk that excludes portal hashes (:73832-73840, :76694-76700, :77572). Corrections: (1) 'server-enforced' is not honest for this option — the field is server-writable but any vanilla client that owns or can reach an unwarded portal overwrites it via RPC_SetTag with zero server-side veto (:143587-143600), and that overwrite also clears the connection. The server can only re-assert reactively. The display itself is client-honoured. (2) Hover text is only rendered while the player's crosshair is on the portal within interact range, so 'signage'/'live countdown' is visible only to a player actively looking at it, not ambiently. (3) The vanilla owning client's RPC_SetTag also writes s_tagauthor; a server rewrite that leaves a stale author is harmless on Steam but the mod should clear it. (4) Live per-second rewrites on a paired portal must hit both ends before the next ConnectPortals pass or the `tag != tag` predicate (:100600-100604) disconnects the route — the option already notes this; add that even a one-tick mismatch is enough because the pass runs every 5 s and writes are immediate. (5) Localization caches every distinct input string (m_cache.Put, :863), so per-second unique hover strings churn that cache; low impact but non-zero.

catalog.name: The Adamant Gate — Server-Enforced Indestructible Portals
catalog.oneLine: Writing a huge ZDOVars.s_health onto a portal makes it survive any vanilla-client damage, and Repair can never undo it.
catalog.howItWorks:
WearNTear.ApplyDamage (:150387-150409) reads the CURRENT health straight from the ZDO every hit: `float f = m_nview.GetZDO().GetFloat(ZDOVars.s_health, m_health); if (f <= 0) return false; f -= damage; m_nview.GetZDO().Set(ZDOVars.s_health, f); if (f <= 0) Destroy(hitData);` The prefab field m_health (:149248) is only the DEFAULT when the ZDO key is absent. So a single server-side `portalZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_health, 1e9f)` means a player must land a billion points of damage to break the portal.

The repair path cannot undo it. WearNTear.Repair (:149522-149539) returns false immediately when `GetFloat(s_health, m_health) >= m_health` — an inflated value always satisfies that, so RPC_Repair (:149541-149548), which would reset s_health to m_health, is never invoked. Cosmetics are also safe: WearNTear.Awake computes `m_healthPercentage = Mathf.Clamp01(num / m_health)` (:149439), which clamps to 1, so the piece renders as pristine rather than glitching.

ZDO.Set performs no ownership check at any type (the okForNotOwner parameter at :73648-73654 is accepted and ignored), so the write lands immediately and propagates by DataRevision. A nearby owning client can clobber it with a higher-revision push (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132 replaces the whole blob), so re-assert on a slow tick — the write is idempotent and free when unchanged, because BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on an equal value and ZDO.Set then skips IncreaseDataRevision.

The complementary half is deconstruction, which ignores health entirely. Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12378) refuses outright when `!piece.m_canBeRemoved`, silently returning false with no message. m_canBeRemoved is a `public bool` on Piece (:136171) — exactly the shape ZNetView.LoadFields can override (see 'Field Injection'). Writing `HasFields`, `HasFieldsPiece` and `Piece.m_canBeRemoved = false` onto the portal ZDO means a vanilla client's hammer refuses to remove it.

Both halves together give a portal that cannot be smashed and cannot be deconstructed by an unmodified client, with no client install. It is still NOT tamper-proof against a modified client — a hostile client can write s_health directly through RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139, zero validation) or broadcast a forged DestroyZDO (RPC_DestroyZDO :76953, ungated on receive). That is the honest ceiling: this stops griefing, not cheating.
catalog.playerExperience: The public hub portals at spawn are simply unbreakable. A new player swings a hammer at one out of curiosity and the deconstruct prompt does nothing at all — no 'private zone' message, no refusal text, the hammer just declines. A raider who decides to cut the network drops a boulder on the gate and it takes a hit sound and a chip of effect and nothing else. Admins can still remove it with the mod's own command. Critically the portal still looks and behaves completely normally — full health bar, normal wear model, normal glow — so it reads as 'this is a server fixture', not as a bug.
failureModes: A modded client can write s_health or forge a DestroyZDO packet; RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77132) and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953) validate nothing
LoadFields only runs inside ZNetView.Awake (:82631), so a m_canBeRemoved change reaches a player only after that portal is next created in their scene — they must leave and return to the area
The field-injection half depends on the portal prefab actually carrying a Piece component; that is asset data
Terrain destruction, fire spread and a fully destroyed supporting structure can still orphan a portal even if the portal itself is immortal

A per-hit re-assert loop would fight the owning client's revision; use a slow idempotent re-assert (the write is free when unchanged, BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue at assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321)
WearNTear.Destroy (:150427-150477) writes s_health = 0 directly, so an already-destroyed portal cannot be revived by re-inflating health

corrections: ZNetView.LoadFields runs only from ZNetView.Awake (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82860, method :82898-82960). Writing HasFields/HasFieldsPiece/Piece.m_canBeRemoved onto a portal already instantiated on a client does nothing until that client re-instantiates it (leaves and re-enters the sector, or relogs). Set the keys at portal creation or accept the delay.

The health write is subject to a symmetric revision rule, not a one-way clobber: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77116) ignores any incoming blob whose DataRevision is not strictly greater than the local copy, on server and client alike. If the owning client has bumped its copy (any hit) before the server's write arrives, the write is dropped client-side and the client's next push wins on the server. Re-assert by comparing the server-visible s_health to the target and re-writing until it holds; do not assume 'idempotent and free'.

float ulp at 1e9 is 64: any single hit under 64 damage leaves s_health bit-identical, so ApplyDamage's Set is a no-op and no revision bump occurs on the client — which is actually favourable, but means the server cannot detect hits by watching s_health.

Structural collapse and rain wear are also absorbed (UpdateWear :149662-149713 routes both through ApplyDamage as 100 / 5 damage), so the portal survives support loss too — a correction in the option's favour.
RPC_DestroyZDO is at :76952-76960 (minor line drift).

ZNetView.LoadFields is called once, at the end of ZNetView.Awake (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82860, body :82898-82960). Field overrides written after a client has already instantiated the portal do not apply until that client re-instantiates it (sector unload/reload or relog). Write the keys before first sync for new portals; for existing ones expect a delay.

The s_health write is subject to the symmetric revision race in ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77107-77117): concurrent server and owner-client writes from the same base revision are mutually discarded. Re-assert on a periodic tick unconditionally; do not rely on 'idempotent when unchanged' since the server copy may have been replaced.
Damage below ~32 against a 1e9 float is lost to rounding (ulp 64); harmless, but the hit effect still plays via RPC_HealthChanged (:150404-150406).
Support failure is not a bypass: !HaveSupport sets 100% wear (:149708-149710) which becomes ApplyDamage(m_health) per tick (:149822-149827), still routed through s_health.

catalog.name: Field Injection Through ZNetView.LoadFields
catalog.oneLine: Vanilla reflects every public field of every component on an instantiated prefab out of the ZDO — which makes per-portal m_allowAllItems, m_exitDistance and m_activationRange genuinely achievable on a 100 percent vanilla client.
catalog.howItWorks:
ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739, byte-identical in the client at :82898) is called as the last step of ZNetView.Awake (:82631), immediately before AddInstance. It is a reflection override mechanism baked into vanilla for the modding-adjacent 'spawn a variant' use case, and it is entirely ZDO-driven:

1. `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields')) return;` — one gate key on the whole object.
2. `gameObject.GetComponentsInChildren(m_tempComponents)` over List<MonoBehaviour> (so self plus active children).
3. Per component, `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields' + typeName)) continue;`
4. For each `BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Public` field, look up the ZDO key `typeName + '.' + fieldName` and, if present, SetValue. Supported types are exactly int, float, bool, Vector3, string, GameObject (resolved by prefab name) and ItemDrop (resolved by prefab name). Color, enum and arrays are NOT supported.

Applied to a portal, the reachable knobs are: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems (bool, :143429) — a genuine PER-PORTAL ore policy, read by Teleport at :143533 and by UpdatePortal's glow at :143505; TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance (float, :143413) — per-portal arrival offset, used at :143545; TeleportWorld.m_activationRange (float, :143411); TeleportWorld.m_hoverOffset (float, :143431); Piece.m_canBeRemoved (bool, :136171); Piece.m_comfort (int, :136120 region); Piece.m_allowedInDungeons (bool); WearNTear.m_health (float, :149248); WearNTear.m_burnable, m_ashDamageImmune, m_noRoofWear, m_noSupportWear, m_supports, m_triggerPrivateArea (bools, :149201-149258 region).

Server-side write for an ore-permissive gate: `z.Set('HasFields'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('HasFieldsTeleportWorld'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems'.GetStableHashCode(), true); ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();` Booleans are stored as ints by ZDO.GetBool/Set (:73937-73940), which is what GetBool reads back, so this is a plain ZDO int write.

This directly REFUTES the common 'there are no per-portal knobs server-side' conclusion. The correct statement is: the fields are not RPC'd or ZDO-backed by TeleportWorld itself, but ZNetView has a generic override channel underneath them and the server owns the ZDO. It is client-honoured (a modified client can ignore it), on exactly the same footing as vanilla's own boss gating.

The one hard limitation is timing: LoadFields runs only at instantiation. Flipping the field on a portal a player is already standing next to does nothing until that object is destroyed and recreated in their scene — i.e. they walk about 100 m away (ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea, :82298-82320) and come back, or relog. Note also that TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems cannot lift the Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier >= 1000 gate, which is checked BEFORE allowAllItems (:68862-68872).
catalog.playerExperience: Two portals side by side at the mining outpost, both stone, both tagged. One is labelled 'ORE ROAD - heavy cargo' and the other 'PASSENGER'. A player loaded with iron walks into the ore gate and it works; the same player walking into the passenger gate gets the normal '$msg_noteleport'. Nothing about the ore gate looks unusual — its ready-glow correctly lights up for a player carrying metal, because UpdatePortal reads the same injected field. The catch a server operator has to explain: after an admin flips a gate's policy, players standing beside it will not see the change until they wander away and come back. In practice the mod flips policy on portals nobody is near, or accepts one relog of latency.
failureModes: LoadFields fires only in ZNetView.Awake (:82631) — a live change never reaches an already-instantiated portal until the client destroys and recreates it (~100 m away and back, or a relog)
Client-honoured only: a modified client simply does not apply the override
Color fields (m_colorUnconnected, m_colorTargetfound) are NOT supported by LoadFields (:82693-82736) — per-portal colour is ruled out through this route
GlobalKeys.TeleportAll and m_allowAllItems both sit AFTER the m_toolTier >= 1000 rejection in Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68862-68868); some items can never be carried through
A wrong key spelling silently does nothing — there is no error path in LoadFields
HasFields keys are plain ZDO ints and count against the per-ZDO per-type item budget; ZPackage.WriteNumItems corrupts above 32767 (:83237-83246) and ZDODataHelper warns above 100 (:74662-74676)
A stale HasFieldsTeleportWorld key applies to every TeleportWorld component found in children if a modded prefab has more than one
openQuestions: THE single highest-value experiment in this whole report: does LoadFields actually apply a server-authored TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems on a live 1.0.7 vanilla client? IN-GAME: write the three ints server-side, have a player carrying iron leave the area and return, then walk through.

Is TeleportWorld on the portal prefab root or a child, and are all target components active (LoadFields uses the List overload of GetComponentsInChildren, which excludes inactive by default)? IN-GAME: dump the portal prefab hierarchy and component list.
Does the portal prefab carry Piece and WearNTear, giving the exact type names for the HasFields keys? IN-GAME: log GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names.
corrections: Write-path race, not ownership: ZDO.Set has no owner check, but ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData on the RECEIVER drops any update whose DataRevision <= its local copy (:77108-77118). Server and owning client each bump the same counter independently (:73832-73840), so a server write to a client-owned portal can be silently discarded if the client wrote in the same window (rare for portals, but it is why Game.SetConnection routes to the owner :100637-100651). Do SetOwner(session)+Set+ForceSendZDO, or write while owner==0.

Awake-order caveat for fields read inside a component's Awake: WearNTear.Awake reads m_health at :149428-149440 (GetFloat(s_health, m_health), world-level scaling). That only sees the override if ZNetView.Awake ran first, which depends on prefab component order (unverifiable from decompile). TeleportWorld itself is safe — every listed field is read at runtime, not in Awake.

'Runs at instantiation' includes the PLACING client: Player.PlacePiece → ZNetView.Awake else-branch (:82613-82630) → LoadFields with no HasFields yet, so the builder sees defaults until their scene recreates the object.
Line-number nit: the option's ':82298-82320 ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea' is correct; ':143429/143413' etc. verified exact.

Another vanilla caller exists: LocationProxy.SpawnLocation calls m_nview.LoadFields() at :102689 after spawning a proxy location — irrelevant to portals but confirms the mechanism is used by shipped content, not a dead path.

m_exitDistance is read from the portal being ENTERED and applied at the partner's position (Teleport: pos = target.GetPosition() + target.forward * m_exitDistance + up, :143539-143546). It is a per-SOURCE arrival offset at the destination, not a per-destination arrival offset.

m_activationRange only feeds Player.GetClosestPlayer for the ready-glow in UpdatePortal (:143497-143507). The actual transit trigger is the child Collider handled by TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143664-143681); Colliders are not MonoBehaviours, so GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour> cannot resize the trigger. Do not describe m_activationRange as changing the transit zone.

Add the DataRevision race: ZDO.Set on a client-owned portal races the owner's own writes; a same-window collision drops one side's packet (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77117). Write while owner==0, after SetOwner(session), or re-send after the owner's next revision; verify presence before relying on it for the next instantiation.

Keys persist in the portal save chunk only if ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called after the write (plain Set dirties the normal chunk via SetDirtySector :73839 -> :76694, from which portals are excluded at :77572).
Injected keys outlive the mod: a vanilla server/client keeps applying them. Reverting a policy requires deleting the 'HasFields*' / 'TeleportWorld.*' keys, not just uninstalling.
Evidence that arbitrary prefabs work without Inspector support: the vanilla client `spawn` command path writes the identical key set and calls LoadFields on any spawned prefab (client :44423-44450).

Inventory.IsTeleportable tests m_toolTier>=1000 before allowAllItems (:68860-68881) as claimed. Keys are ordinary ints: they replicate (ZDO.Serialize) and save; ZDO.Deserialize merges via ZDOExtraData.Add without clearing (:74232-74238, :74896), so a peer's later sends never strip them. Save persistence requires SetDirtyPortals (only ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection Portal, AddIfPortal, HandleDestroyedZDO and Load set DirtyPortalObjects: :73656-73677, :77751, :76986, :76539). Instantiation-only timing is correct: RemoveObjects destroys the instance when the ZDO leaves the near set (:82196-82225); portals are only ever in the near set because FindDistantObjects reads m_objectsBySector only (:77384-77398), so ~1.5 zones / 112 m radius (PointInsideActiveArea :82298-82320). Enforcement is honestly client-honoured. Two real caveats the option omits: (1) non-owner write revision race — the server's Set bumps DataRevision (:73832-73840); if the owning client also writes in the same send window, each side drops the other's packet (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision` :77108-77117) and the client never sees the key until the server writes again; claim ownership (SetOwner) or write while owner==0 / a player is not nearby (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924 re-assigns ownership every 2 s). (2) The mechanism survives mod uninstall — vanilla keeps honouring the keys — so reverting requires actively removing them.

catalog.name: Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport
catalog.oneLine: Abandon the connection field entirely: poll character ZDO positions near a portal and force-teleport with RPC_TeleportPlayer — which breaks the one-destination-per-ZDO ceiling and gives true multi-destination hubs.
catalog.howItWorks:
A ZDO holds at most ONE connection — ZDOExtraData.s_connections is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and ZDOConnection carries one readonly type and one readonly target (:74794, :75524-75534). Simultaneous multi-destination hubs are therefore structurally impossible through the vanilla mechanism. This option sidesteps it completely.

Leave the portal's Portal connection at ZDOID.None (or pointed anywhere). The portal never teleports anyone — TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 returns silently (:143519). Instead, the server polls: `foreach (peer in ZNet.instance.GetPeers()) { var z = ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID); ... }` at 0.2-0.4 s, comparing z.GetPosition() against every entry of ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals() (:77643, the live zero-alloc dictionary) within about 3-4 m. Position freshness is good: the owning client's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zdo.SetPosition every physics tick (:87527-87540) and ZDOMan services one peer per Update on a 0.05 s timer (:76843-76861), so character positions are 50-100 ms stale regardless of distance.

On a hit, send `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, rot, true)`. The handler is registered on every vanilla client in Chat.Awake (:41627) and its entire body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender check, no admin check, no key check, no item check (:41962-41968). A second, ZDO-scoped path exists: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, 'RPC_TeleportTo', pos, rot, true)`, handled by Character.RPC_TeleportTo (:4126-4132), registered for every Character in Character.Awake (:886) and owner-gated so it cannot be misdirected.

What this buys: the DESTINATION is chosen by the server at the moment of transit, per player, per condition. A hub can route by player identity (character ZDO ZDOVars.s_playerID), by the emote they last performed (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID), by a map ping they sent (Chat.SendPing broadcasts 'ChatMessage' to peer 0 with the clicked world Vector3), by time of day, by a rotation counter, or round-robin. It also bypasses vanilla's ore check entirely, which is a design decision the operator must make consciously.

Mandatory pre-checks, all readable from the character ZDO: skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead) (Player.UpdateTeleport runs only inside the !IsDead() branch of FixedUpdate at :10213/:10226, so a teleport sent to a dead player latches m_teleporting true and never executes); skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed) (Player.UpdateAttach at :10217 runs BEFORE UpdateTeleport at :10226 and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and AttachStop early-returns while sleeping at :15892). And rate-limit per player to at least 12 s: Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting() or while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15309-15316), and m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick of a teleport (:15336), so the dead window is the whole 8+ s teleport plus 2 s.
catalog.playerExperience: A single great archway at spawn labelled 'THE WAYGATE'. Walking into it does not take you to a fixed partner. Before stepping through you open your map and middle-click a location you have discovered; that ping goes to the server. You walk into the arch, and after the usual black screen you are standing at the spot you marked. If you did not ping anything, it takes you to the destination you used last. One archway, unlimited destinations, on a completely unmodified client, with the standard portal fade and no visual tell that anything unusual happened. The failure mode players will notice: if you step in twice within about twelve seconds, the second attempt does nothing at all and gives no message.
failureModes: Every failure is silent and one-directional: TeleportTo returns false (:15309, :15313), both RPC handlers discard the return (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent — the server's only confirmation is watching the character ZDO position change roughly 2 s later

The real cooldown is not 2 s after the RPC; m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick WHILE teleporting (:15336), so the refusal window spans the entire teleport plus 2 s, at least 10-12 s for distantTeleport
A dead player latches: the teleport is accepted, m_teleporting goes true, and UpdateTeleport never runs (:10213/:10226). Check ZDOVars.s_dead first
An attached or sleeping player ping-pongs between the attach point and the target every tick because UpdateAttach runs first (:10217, :15818-15836); check ZDOVars.s_inBed first
Position polling at 0.2-0.4 s can miss a fast player; a 4 m radius at 5 m/s and 0.5 s sampling is about the floor
This bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, PrivateArea and the ore check completely — every rule the operator wants must be re-implemented in the mod

RPC_TeleportPlayer is not a privileged channel: vanilla's own client-side `recall` command sends it peer-to-peer (:44548-44556) and RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is a self-report (:83487-83495), so shipping this feature obliges the mod to also harden ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC

With distantTeleport true the player is invulnerable and input-locked for ~8 s (Player.CanMove at :14423-14428, damage suppression at :2425/:2429/:2582) — abusable as a stun if triggered by another player
prerequisites: A per-player destination selector (emote signal, map ping, item stand, or chest content)
openQuestions: What poll interval and radius reliably catch a sprinting player through a portal frame without false positives from someone standing nearby? IN-GAME: log character ZDO positions at 0.1 s while a player runs laps through a portal and measure the dwell time inside 4 m.

What is the real per-peer cadence at which the server receives character position updates on a loaded server? CreateSyncList is per-peer round-robin on a 0.05 s timer (:76843), so it degrades with player count. IN-GAME: log position-change timestamps for one player with 1, 5 and 20 peers online.
catalog.id: wildcard:Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport
corrections: Enforcement: client-honoured. RPC_TeleportPlayer is a request the vanilla client obeys; position authority and the teleport state machine live on the client.

No 'ChatMessage' handler exists on a dedicated server: it is registered in Chat.Awake (:41626), a UI MonoBehaviour that is not instantiated headless. The mod must ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3,int,UserInfo,string>("ChatMessage", ...) itself (HandleRoutedRPC :83630-83640 dispatches by hash from m_functions). Also RPC_RoutedRPC (:83617-83628) does NOT validate m_senderPeerID against the socket — the 'verified identity' of a ping is the client-supplied field in the routed packet; verify against ZNet.GetPeer(rpc) if identity matters.

With the hub's Portal connection left at None, Game.ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100608-100622) will pair it with any other unconnected portal carrying the same tag every 5 s; the hub needs a unique tag or the mod must own ConnectPortals. It also renders as 'unconnected' (no glow, HaveTarget false :143630-143637) on every vanilla client — there is a visual tell.

Position freshness is bounded by the CLIENT→server send cadence (client ZDOMan.Update timer 0.05 s + frame, queue cap 10240 bytes :77008-77016), not only the server→peer scheduler cited at :76843-76861.

Trigger geometry: the server only has the portal ZDO position (base of the arch) and the character ZDO position; a 3-4 m radius also catches players editing the tag or standing beside it. Needs an entry-edge/dwell rule, not a radius test.

Player experience: an unlinked portal is visibly unconnected (no glow, '[unconnected]' hover, m_target_found off). Either accept that tell or accept that vanilla's own trigger wins if the portal is linked to anything resolvable.

Do not point the portal 'anywhere': a resolvable Portal connection lets TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter -> Teleport -> TeleportTo run first on the client and the server's later RPC is refused at IsTeleporting (:15311). The only compatible state is connection == None.

Replace the '3-4 m sphere' with an edge-triggered, rotation-aware crossing test on consecutive samples plus re-arm-on-exit; a static sphere yanks players who merely stand beside the portal and ping-pongs at any portal-shaped destination (arrival is exitDistance 1 m in front).

Ping destinations carry the SENDER's current y (Chat.SendPing :42061). Compute y server-side from WorldGenerator (colliders unavailable), else the client sits on the black screen until the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15364-15371) and may arrive inside terrain/buildings.
Enforcement wording: the destination is server-chosen, but the teleport act is a client-honoured RPC; a modified client can ignore it (it cannot, however, use this portal to go anywhere else).
Effort: large, not medium-large — the trigger-geometry/edge logic, y-resolution, and per-player state machine are the bulk of the work; the RPC itself is trivial.
