verifierReasoning: [decompile:downgraded] Every cited API exists with the claimed shape: Chat.Awake registers RPC_TeleportPlayer<Vector3,Quaternion,bool> at :41627; the handler body (:41962-41968) is exactly `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) TeleportTo(...)` with no sender/admin/key/item check. Character.Awake registers RPC_TeleportTo at :886 (inside `if (m_nview.GetZDO() != null)` :868); Character.RPC_TeleportTo (:4126-4132) is owner-gated; Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15327) refuses while IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown<2f and zeroes the cooldown; UpdateTeleport (:15329-15378) waits >2 s, then for distantTeleport >8 s and IsAreaReady, then FindFloor, giving up at 15 s. Player.FixedUpdate ordering (:10213-10226) — !IsDead gate, UpdateAttach at :10217 before UpdateTeleport :10226 — verified. AttachStop early-return on m_sleeping :15892. ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zdo.SetPosition each tick (:87527-87532). ZDOMan.GetPortals returns the live dictionary (:77643-77646). Chat.SendPing routes 'ChatMessage' to peer 0 (:42058-42068). ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC/RouteRPC (:83554-83610) deliver a server-originated RPC to a specific ready peer. The single-connection ceiling (s_connections :74794, ZDOConnection :75524-75534, GetConnectionZDOID exact-type :75094-75102) is real. So the design works on a vanilla client. But the enforcement label is wrong under the ground rules: the act of teleporting is executed by the client (owner of its character ZDO), the trigger is inferred from a client-authored position, and nothing stops a modded client that owns the portal ZDO (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924 hands it over within 2 s) from writing its own Portal connection and using vanilla transit. The server chooses a destination and asks; the client honours. That is client-honoured, not server-enforced.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] The transport primitive is real: Chat.Awake registers 'RPC_TeleportPlayer' on every vanilla client (:41627) and the handler is unconditionally `Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (:41962-41968); Character.Awake registers the owner-gated 'RPC_TeleportTo' (:886, :4128-4134); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC routes to a peer id with no permission check (:83554-83596). Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting or m_teleportCooldown<2 (:15304-15316) and UpdateTeleport zeroes the cooldown every tick (:15331-15340); single-slot ZDOConnection is confirmed (:74794, :75524-75534). Position freshness claim holds (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87527-87540; ZDOMan send timer :76843-76861). But the claimed player experience is wrong and the trigger design is under-specified. (a) 'No visual tell' is false: with the connection at None, HaveTarget() is false, so the portal's emission stays m_colorUnconnected, m_target_found never activates, and the hover text reads '$piece_portal_unconnected' (client :144193-144205, :144217-144225). (b) 'Or pointed anywhere' is worse: any resolvable target makes vanilla's TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter fire Teleport() on the client instantly, TeleportTo latches m_teleporting, and the server's RPC — which arrives 50-100 ms of ZDO lag plus a 200-400 ms poll later — is refused at IsTeleporting (:15311). Vanilla's destination wins every race. (c) A 3-4 m sphere around the portal ZDO position is not a trigger volume: players standing beside the portal to read/retag it are inside it and get yanked; and any destination that is itself a portal puts the arrival 1 m in front of it, so after the 2 s cooldown the poll fires again — ping-pong unless the mod implements enter-edge/re-arm-on-exit semantics equivalent to OnTriggerEnter. (d) Chat.SendPing sets vector.y = the sender's CURRENT y (:42058-42063), so a pinged destination has the wrong altitude; ZoneSystem height queries are collider-dead on the server, so the mod must use WorldGenerator math; a wrong y is only self-corrected by the client at m_teleportTimer>15 s via GetSolidHeight (:15364-15371) — a 15 s black screen instead of 8. (e) Dead-player latch is harmless (the Player object is destroyed on respawn) but skipping is still right. Enforcement: the route decision is server-owned and the portal itself cannot take a vanilla client anywhere, but delivery is a client-executed RPC the client merely honours.

catalog.name: Portals As A Data Store
catalog.oneLine: Portal ZDOs are the only always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent ZDO collection in the game — and they take arbitrary mod-private keys for free.
catalog.howItWorks:
Portals have four properties no other ZDO family has. (1) They live in their own dictionary ZDOMan.m_portalObjects (:76039) and are removed from the sector array by AddIfPortal (:77750), so they are never unloaded and never released — ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership (:76872-76924) and FlushClientObjects is client-only. (2) They are enumerable world-wide for free with ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648) with zero bookkeeping and no prefab-name guess. (3) They save to a dedicated ChunkPortal file (ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal, :113180), written wholesale with NO Persistent filter whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632). (4) They are loaded straight into m_portalObjects at world load, bypassing FilterZDO entirely (:76474-76483).

A ZDO's extra data is seven independent int-keyed dictionaries — float, Vector3, Quaternion, int, long, string, byte[] (ZDOExtraData s_floats ... s_byteArrays, :74757-74771). Keys are arbitrary ints; vanilla just uses name.GetStableHashCode(). So a mod can hang whatever it likes on a portal: a network id, a rotation index, a cooldown timestamp, an owning faction, a toll price, a puzzle state, an ordered route list serialized into one byte array. It round-trips through both the network (ZDO.Serialize :74112-74174) and the save with no work.

The correct write discipline: ZDO.Set has no ownership check on any overload (:73601-73727), so write freely; but ALWAYS follow with ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702), because only ConnectionType.Portal SetConnection, AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO set DirtyPortalObjects — a plain field write goes through IncreaseDataRevision to SetDirtySector (:73839), which dirties a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). Without SetDirtyPortals the whole portal file is skipped and every portal reverts to its last-dirtied state.

Two hard budgets. ZPackage.WriteNumItems (:83237-83246) encodes a per-ZDO per-type item count in one byte below 128 and two bytes up to 32767 — above that the stream corrupts; ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk logs a warning above 100 items of a single type (:74662-74676). And ZDOMan.SendZDOs (:77053-77062) re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO on every send with no delta encoding, under a 10240-byte per-peer queue cap (:77010-77016). So: a handful of scalar keys plus one byte array, never two hundred int keys.

One global landmine: ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly is a GLOBAL hash set (:74776) seeded from the 16 entries of ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693) and from anything ever passed to AddSessionHash. Any key in it is stripped from the save for EVERY ZDO in the world. Never reuse s_support, s_inUse, s_alert, s_velHash and friends for portal metadata.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to players — this is infrastructure. What they see downstream is that the network remembers: the hub they set to 'Ashlands' is still pointed at Ashlands after a server restart, a gate they unlocked stays unlocked, a toll they paid stays paid, and the rotation schedule picks up exactly where it left off rather than resetting. Nothing in the world save is a separate mod file that can drift out of sync with the world; the state travels with the portals, which means it also travels with world backups and world copies.
failureModes: A field write without ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is silently lost at the next world save — the single most likely bug in the whole mod
ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load sets m_uid via ZDOID.SetID), so a portal's identity must be derived from position, tag, or a mod-written key — never from its ZDOID
Reusing any of the 16 ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes strips that key from the save for every ZDO in the world, not just portals
More than 100 keys of one type on one ZDO logs a warning; more than 32767 corrupts the wire stream
Every extra byte is re-sent in full on every ZDO sync to every nearby peer (no delta encoding), so a large byte array on a hub portal is real recurring bandwidth
A nearby owning client can clobber the whole ZDO with a higher-revision push (RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132) — conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field
citations: ZDOMan.SendZDOs full re-serialize and queue cap — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77008-77074
openQuestions: Does a portal ZDO carrying mod-private keys round-trip cleanly through the ChunkPortal save, including a byte array? IN-GAME: write a 512-byte array plus five ints to a portal, force a save, restart, and read them back.

Does ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (Type.Int/Long/String, :75390-75407) usefully index mod keys on portals, given portals live outside m_objectsBySector? It scans the field dictionaries directly so it should. IN-GAME: write a marker int to three portals and query it.
corrections: 'Only always-resident, distance-independent ZDO collection' is an overclaim. On a dedicated server EVERY ZDO is resident in m_objectsByID for the whole session (nothing on the server path unloads ZDOs; FlushClientObjects is client-only). What is unique to portals is the cheap enumeration, the exclusion from sector churn, and the no-Persistent-filter save. Network delivery is NOT distance-independent: CreateSyncList → FindSectorObjects → FindObjects (:77212-77240, :77368-77381) only includes m_portalObjects entries whose sector is inside the peer's scanned area; remote portal ZDOs reach a client only via ForceSendZDO (Game.SetConnection :100643) or the client's own RequestZDO (:77684-77692, no prefab check).

'Write freely' needs the revision caveat: the receiver drops updates with DataRevision <= its local copy (RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118), and portals near a player are owned by that player within 2 s (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924). A concurrent client write can silently discard the server's key write. Use the Game.SetConnection pattern (SetOwner(session) then Set then ForceSendZDO :100637-100651) or write when owner==0.

Key naming: also avoid every hash in ZDOHelper.s_stripOldData/s_stripOldFloats/s_stripOldVecs/s_stripOldQuats/s_stripOldStringData/s_stripOldLongData/s_stripOldUnknownLongData (:75550-75618) — ZDOMan strips those from every ZDO at load (:78213-78223). s_stripOldUnknownLongData is 39 raw uint hashes, so a mod long key has a tiny but nonzero collision risk; prefer int/string/byte[] keys.

ZDOIDs are reassigned at load (m_nextUid = ZDOID.m_loadID + 1 :76525), so a route list serialized as ZDOIDs into a byte array does not survive a restart; store a stable identity (tag+position or a mod-assigned id key) instead.
GetSectorIndex is computed from m_position (:73776-73779), so m_portalObjects keys are position-derived — never move a portal ZDO's position after it is filed.

'Only always-resident, distance-independent ZDO collection' is overstated for a dedicated server: the server never runs ZNetScene.RemoveObjects, so every persistent ZDO is always resident there; the genuinely unique properties are (a) free enumeration with no prefab scan, (b) the ChunkPortal save path with no Persistent filter and no FilterZDO. Portals are still sector-bucketed and replicated to clients by sector via FindObjects (:77367-77381) — replication is not distance-independent.

Never store a ZDOID inside a mod key (byte array, long pair, 'ordered route list'): ZDO.Load re-issues every id (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74549-74552). Only the connection slot (via hash data) and vanilla's s_zdoidUser conversion survive a reload. Reference other portals by tag/position or by a mod-assigned stable id key on the target.

Non-owner write race: the server's Set bumps DataRevision; if the owning client writes in the same send window, ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData drops whichever packet is not strictly newer (:77108-77117) — the client's copy can miss the key (irrelevant for a server-private store; relevant when a client must see the key, e.g. LoadFields). The server's own copy is what gets saved.
ZDO.Set still dirties a normal chunk uselessly (SetDirtySector on a Persistent ZDO) — harmless but means each portal write also forces a normal chunk rewrite.

Portal chunk is written in full whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632) — a high-frequency counter (per-transit writes) makes every autosave rewrite all portals; batch counters on a slow tick.

GetPortalList (:77648-77656) is a free world-wide enumeration. GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621-77632) writes ALL of m_portalObjects into ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal (:113180) with no Persistent filter, only when DirtyPortalObjects; AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) excludes portal prefabs from normal chunks; LoadChunks (:76474-76483) loads ChunkPortal straight into m_portalObjects/m_objectsByID without FilterZDO. Seven typed dictionaries at :74757-74771. SetDirtySector (:76694-76699) only dirties a normal chunk; SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is the only public way to dirty the portal file, and DirtyPortalObjects is otherwise set only by AddIfPortal (:77751), HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986), ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for Portal (:73656-73678) and legacy Load (:76539); it is reset to false after LoadChunks (:76527). [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core claims hold. m_portalObjects is a private Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> (:76039); AddIfPortal files any ZDO whose prefab is in Game.PortalPrefabHash there, calls RemoveFromSector, and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77732-77752); GetPortalList/GetPortals are free world-wide enumerations (:77643-77656). GetSaveClonePerChunk clones EVERY portal ZDO into ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal with no Persistent test whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632; ZDO.Clone :73552), and LoadChunks loads that chunk straight into m_portalObjects/m_objectsByID without FilterZDO (:76474-76483). DirtyPortalObjects is set only by Load (:76539), SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705), HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986), AddIfPortal (:77751) and ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for ConnectionType.Portal (:73656-73677); a plain ZDO.Set goes through IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76700) which dirties a normal chunk from which portals are excluded (:77572) — so the SetDirtyPortals discipline is exactly right. ZDO.Set has no owner check (:73600-73727). Seven typed dictionaries (:74757-74771); s_sessionOnly global set seeded from the 16-entry ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes plus AddSessionHash (:74814-74830, :78689-78693) and applied to every ZDO at save (:75507-75509). WriteNumItems format (:83237-83246) and WriteToDisk >100 warning (:74655-74677) confirmed; SendZDOs re-serializes whole ZDOs under the 10240-byte queue cap (:77008-77016, :77053-77062). Corrections concern over-claimed uniqueness, an omitted ZDOID-regeneration trap, and the non-owner revision race.

catalog.name: Non-Portals As Portals — Extending Game.PortalPrefabHash At Runtime
catalog.oneLine: PortalPrefabHash is a mutable List<int> behind a private setter, so an arbitrary prefab can be enrolled into the portal registry, the portal save chunk and vanilla's own pairing.
catalog.howItWorks:
Game.PortalPrefabHash is declared `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` (:100021) and populated in Game.Awake from the Inspector list m_portalPrefabs (:100027-100032). The SETTER is private but the LIST OBJECT is not — `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add(someHash)` is a legal, no-reflection mutation of live game state.

Everything portal-specific keys off membership in that list, in four places: ZDOMan.AddIfPortal (:77734) decides whether a new ZDO is filed in m_portalObjects and removed from the sector array; ZDO.SetSector (:73754) early-returns, freezing the sector key; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) excludes it from normal chunk saves; and GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621) includes it in ChunkPortal.

Adding a hash makes any FUTURE ZDO of that prefab a portal for all four purposes, and makes it appear in ZDOMan.GetPortalList() and therefore in Game.ConnectPortals's tag-pairing loop (:100592-100622). It does NOT retroactively re-file existing ZDOs — AddIfPortal only runs from CreateNewZDO (:76689) and from the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77132), so already-loaded instances of that prefab stay in the sector array until they are destroyed and recreated. Conversely, `.Remove(hash)` does not un-register already-tracked ZDOs from m_portalObjects.

The DANGEROUS half is the mirror image: removing a portal hash, or adding a hash for a prefab that already has thousands of instances in the world, changes where those ZDOs are saved. Adding a common prefab hash means every new instance goes into the single global ChunkPortal file, which is written in full whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set — a pathological save-size and save-time regression.

The genuinely useful applications are narrow and deliberate: (a) enrolling a modded portal piece from another server mod so vanilla's own pairing handles it for free; (b) enrolling a rare marker prefab so that mod-created network anchors get the always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent treatment portals get; (c) in reverse, NOT enrolling an anchor so it is invisible to vanilla's pairer while still being a legal teleport destination (see The Void Anchor).

The converse question — can a portal be made into a non-portal — is effectively no: removing the hash after ZDOs exist leaves them stranded in m_portalObjects with a frozen sector key and no path back into the sector array, because ZDO.SetSector for a ZDO whose current prefab is no longer in the list would then try to AddToSector but the ZDO was already RemoveFromSector'd, and nothing re-triggers it.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing directly visible. What players notice is that a modded portal piece from a different mod suddenly behaves exactly like a vanilla one — it pairs by tag, it survives restarts, it shows up in the server's portal census and its Discord reports — with no per-mod integration code. And, in the other direction, that admin waypoints the server maintains never show up in anyone's portal list and cannot be accidentally paired to by a player who happens to pick the same tag.
failureModes: Adding a hash does not retroactively move existing ZDOs into m_portalObjects — only ZDOs created or received afterwards (AddIfPortal call sites :76689 and :77132)
Removing a hash strands already-tracked ZDOs in m_portalObjects permanently and they are never reachable from the sector array again
Enrolling a common prefab dumps every new instance into the one global ChunkPortal file, which is rewritten in full on every dirty save — a real save-size and save-time regression
Portal-hash ZDOs are exempt from ZDO.SetSector (:73752), so an enrolled prefab that MOVES (anything with a Rigidbody) silently stops syncing to clients at its new location
Load order matters: PortalPrefabHash is filled in Game.Awake (:100027), so the mutation must happen after that and before any relevant ZDO is created or received
Another mod doing the same thing will collide; the list has no ownership model
citations: Game.PortalPrefabHash property — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021; populated in Game.Awake :100027-100032; m_portalPrefabs field :99828
openQuestions: Does Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add actually take effect for ZDOs received over RPC_ZDOData after the mutation? The AddIfPortal call at :77132 happens per received ZDO, so it should. IN-GAME: enrol a marker prefab, have a client place one, and check GetPortalList().

What happens on world load if the saved ChunkPortal file contains a prefab hash that is no longer in PortalPrefabHash at boot? LoadChunks puts it straight into m_portalObjects regardless (:76480). IN-GAME: enrol, save, remove the enrolment, restart, and observe.
catalog.id: wildcard:Non-Portals As Portals — Extending Game.PortalPrefabHash At Runtime
corrections: Enrolling a prefab with existing instances causes SILENT DATA LOSS, not just a size regression. The chunked load path (LoadChunks :76484-76490) sends every non-ChunkPortal ZDO through FilterZDO → InitialAddToSector (:76505-76510) with NO PortalPrefabHash check; only the legacy monolithic ZDOMan.Load (:76576, :76595) files by hash. Those pre-existing instances therefore sit in the sector array, where AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) now EXCLUDES them, while the ChunkPortal writer (:77621-77632) only iterates m_portalObjects. The next dirty save of their chunk writes them nowhere. Enrolling before world load does not help (same chunk path). A mod that enrols a prefab must re-file its existing instances itself (the private AddIfPortal via reflection, or destroy/recreate) before any save.

ZDO.SetSector for an enrolled prefab returns early (:73752-73757) but the instance stays in m_objectsBySector at its load-time sector — RemoveFromSector is only done by AddIfPortal — so until re-filed it is neither properly a portal nor properly a sector object.

The vanilla CLIENT's PortalPrefabHash is unchanged. Client-side AddIfPortal/SetSector treat the prefab as a normal piece; this is harmless for data but means client-side ZNetScene distance handling for it is ordinary.

The reverse (Remove) analysis needs one more consequence: ZDOs already in m_portalObjects are still written to ChunkPortal (no hash check in :77624-77630) and reloaded into m_portalObjects (:76474-76483), so they persist as portals forever; additionally, with the hash gone ZDO.SetSector no longer early-returns and a position change would AddToSector them, double-listing them. 'Effectively no' stands.
Feasibility for use (a)/(b) is fine; effort should include the re-filing pass and a guard that refuses to enrol a hash that already has instances outside m_portalObjects.

Enrolling a prefab hash that has existing ZDO instances silently deletes those instances at the next save: they remain in m_objectsBySector but are excluded from normal chunks (:77572) and are not in m_portalObjects (:77624). Only enroll prefabs with zero existing instances, or re-file existing ones via reflection into m_portalObjects before the next save.

Never Remove a hash while instances exist: HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980-76987) skips the m_portalObjects removal when the hash is absent, then releases the ZDO to the pool — leaving a dangling pooled ZDO in m_portalObjects that GetPortalList/ConnectPortals iterate.

Enrolled non-portal prefabs are tag-paired by Game.ConnectPortals like any portal; an empty-tag anchor pairs with any empty-tag player portal. Give anchors a reserved tag no player can type (portal tags are capped at 10 chars by TextInput; use a longer/control-character tag).

Clients never see the enrollment (vanilla PortalPrefabHash); the enrolled prefab works only as a DESTINATION (position/rotation read from its ZDO), never as a source — it has no TeleportWorld/TeleportWorldTrigger.
Application (a) — enrolling another mod's portal piece — requires that piece to actually carry a TeleportWorld component on the client for transit; enrollment alone only gets it pairing/persistence.

ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal chunk :76474-76483; legacy Load hash test :76575-76600; InitialAddToSector for normal chunks :76507-76510
ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO hash-gated portal removal then ZDOPool.Release — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76970-76990

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Game.PortalPrefabHash is `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; } = new List<int>()` (:100021), populated in Game.Awake (:100027-100032) from m_portalPrefabs (:99828); Add() on the list is a legal mutation. The list is consulted in exactly six places: ZDO.SetSector (:73754), legacy ZDOMan.Load (:76576, :76595), HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980), AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) and AddIfPortal (:77734). AddIfPortal is called only from CreateNewZDO (:76689) and RPC_ZDOData (:77132), so enrolment affects only future/network-received ZDOs, as claimed; a client-placed instance of a modded prefab arrives via RPC_ZDOData and is filed. Game.ConnectPortals iterates GetPortalList (:100592) so enrolled prefabs are tag-paired. However the option misjudges the danger of enrolling a prefab that already has instances, and the 'save-size regression' framing understates it.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The mutability claim is literal: `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; } = new List<int>();` (:100021), populated in Game.Awake from m_portalPrefabs (:99828, :100027-100032); the list instance is public and Add/Remove are ordinary calls. All four membership tests are as claimed: AddIfPortal (:77734), ZDO.SetSector early-return (:73752-73757), AddObjectsPerChunk exclusion (:77572), and the save/load portal chunk (:77621-77632, legacy load :76575-76600). AddIfPortal runs from CreateNewZDO (:76685-76691) and the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77128), so enrollment is prospective only. Game.ConnectPortals iterates GetPortalList (:100589-100627) so enrolled ZDOs are tag-paired by vanilla. But the option under-states the hazards. (1) Enrolling a hash that already has instances is data loss, not just 'they stay in the sector array': at the next save AddObjectsPerChunk skips them (hash now in the list, :77572) and GetSaveClonePerChunk only writes m_portalObjects (:77624) — those ZDOs are written to NO chunk and vanish on the next load. Re-filing them needs reflection into the private m_portalObjects. (2) Removing a hash is worse than 'stranded': HandleDestroyedZDO only removes from m_portalObjects when the hash is present (:76980-76987) and then ZDOPool.Release()s the ZDO — a portal destroyed after its hash was removed leaves a released, recyclable ZDO object inside m_portalObjects, and GetPortalList/ConnectPortals will iterate it. (3) The mod runs only on the server: clients keep the vanilla list, so client-side AddIfPortal/SetSector treat the enrolled prefab as a normal object — harmless, but the enrolled prefab has no TeleportWorld component, so it can only ever be a destination (client Teleport uses ZDOMan.GetZDO(target) position/rotation, :144250-144257, and TargetFound RequestZDOs it, :144386-144395; RPC_RequestZDO honours any id, :77689-77692). (4) Tag pairing applies to enrolled ZDOs: an anchor with an empty tag matches every blank-tag player portal in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679); enrolled anchors need a unique, unguessable tag or vanilla will randomly route players into them.

catalog.name: The Connection Field Beyond Portals
catalog.oneLine: An honest map of the other ConnectionType values, what abusing them buys and costs, including the one-connection-per-ZDO ceiling and a latent creature-spawner suppression trick.
catalog.howItWorks:
ConnectionType is a [Flags] byte enum with None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 (:74747-74754). Note Portal, SyncTransform and Spawned are NOT independent bits — 1, 2 and 3 overlap, so Spawned is bitwise Portal|SyncTransform. Only Target is a real flag. ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID (:75094-75102) requires EXACT type equality, which is what keeps these from cross-matching.

A ZDO holds exactly one connection (s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>, one readonly type and one readonly target, :74794, :75524-75534). Consequences:
- Writing Portal onto a player's character ZDO destroys their SyncTransform ship-parent link (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync at :87548 writes it).
- Writing Portal onto a CreatureSpawner's ZDO destroys its Spawned link.
- A portal can never simultaneously be a Portal endpoint and a SyncTransform child, so a portal physically parented to a moving ship is structurally impossible.
- Writing Portal|Target (0x10 | 1 = 0x11) onto a live portal makes GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) return None, so vanilla treats it as unconnected and re-pairs it. The Target bit belongs only to the save-hash representation.

SyncTransform (:87542-87571) is written by the RIDER's client when standing on a Rigidbody with a ZNetView, alongside ZDOVars.s_relPosHash, s_relRotHash and s_attachJointHash. It is a latch, written only when the parent changes (:87546). Reading it server-side is the documented way to know a player is on a ship — though ShipAttachment's ZDOVars.s_user read on the Ship's own ZDO (written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl :141332) is stronger because it has no Inspector dependency. There is also a genuine vanilla bug worth not building on: OwnerSync writes relative velocity to ZDOVars.s_velHash while SyncPosition reads s_velRelHash (:87561 vs :87647), so velRel is never written by anything.

Spawned (:5649-5656, :5820) is CreatureSpawner's link to the creature it made. `SpawnedCreatureStillExists(connectionZDOID)` plus `m_respawnTimeMinuts <= 0f` means a spawner whose Spawned connection points at ANY still-resident ZDO never spawns again. Writing `spawnerZdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Spawned, somePermanentPortalZdoId)` therefore permanently silences a fixed creature spawner from the server — an off-label but real world-governance primitive, and a reason a portal mod must be careful never to write a Portal connection onto a non-portal ZDO it did not create.

The save-time collapse is the hard ceiling on all of it: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) gives the source ZDO {type, h} and then OVERWRITES the target's slot with {type|Target, h}. With one slot per ZDO, the disk format can express only a pairwise perfect matching. Rings lose links, one-way links come back bidirectional via ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77879-77885), and self-loops are erased outright (:75472-75475, target != None so the source slot is immediately overwritten).
catalog.playerExperience: Indirectly visible as topology that vanilla could not produce: a one-way drop gate that only works in one direction, a ring of six portals where each leads to the next rather than to a random partner, a fan-in where four remote outposts all exit at one hub. All of it holds at runtime because Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601 tests only that the partner resolves, shares the tag, and is itself non-None). All of it quietly degenerates after a server restart into ordinary random pairs unless the mod re-asserts it on world load — which players experience as 'the network scrambled overnight' if the mod forgets.
failureModes: Non-pairwise topologies are runtime-only. Rings above 2, one-way links and self-loops do not survive RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) — they must be re-asserted after every world load
Writing any connection type onto a ZDO that already has one destroys the old one silently; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection just replaces (:74951-74960)

ZDO.UpdateConnection (:74962-74976) writes nothing at all when no entry exists — it can never CREATE a link, only overwrite one. TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag uses it (:143595), which is why retagging a never-connected portal is a no-op on the connection field
Writing Portal|Target onto a live portal makes vanilla read it as unconnected and re-pair it
Suppressing a CreatureSpawner via a Spawned connection is off-label and will confuse any other world-governance mod inspecting spawner state

GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType) (:75414-75427) reads s_connectionsHashData — the SAVE-time table — not the live s_connections, so it is empty at steady state. Use the parameterless overload (:75409) or iterate GetPortalList()
prerequisites: Ownership of Game.ConnectPortals, or a world-load re-assert pass
citations: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals load-time hash relink makes links reciprocal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850-77893 (:77879-77885)
ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync SyncTransform write — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87542-87571; velHash/velRelHash mismatch :87561 vs :87647
Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 does not check reciprocity — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100600-100604
openQuestions: Does SpawnedCreatureStillExists actually accept an arbitrary non-creature ZDO as 'still alive'? It takes a ZDOID and the guard at :5651 short-circuits on m_respawnTimeMinuts. IN-GAME: write a Spawned connection to a portal ZDO on a fixed draugr spawner and watch for 30 minutes.
Does the portal prefab carry a ZSyncTransform at all (which would make SyncTransform parenting of a portal meaningful)? IN-GAME: dump the prefab components.
corrections: Do NOT point Spawned at a portal ZDO. At save, RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75470-75476) overwrites the TARGET's single ZDOConnectionHashData slot with {Spawned|Target,h}. Depending on s_connections iteration order this either clobbers the portal's own saved {Portal,h'} pairing (portal comes back unpaired → Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs it randomly) or is itself clobbered (spawner's hash finds no target at load → ConnectSpawners sets it to Spawned→None :77939-77943). Either way the trick corrupts portal pairing. For one-shot spawners (m_respawnTimeMinuts<=0, :5649-5653) a Spawned→ZDOID.None 'done' marker is sufficient and is saved as-is (RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps Spawned regardless of target :75469). For respawning spawners the target must be a persistent non-portal ZDO that has no connection of its own.
The spawner write must land on the OWNING client's copy: UpdateSpawner is owner-gated (:5633-5637) and CreatureSpawner runs client-side; the same RPC_ZDOData revision race (:77108-77118) applies.

One-way gate A→B is only runtime-stable if B itself holds a non-None Portal connection (phase-1 predicate :100601 resets A when target.connection==None). A B with connection None gets A reset within 5 s and both re-paired by phase 2. B→B (self-loop) or B→C are the stable sink forms; the self-loop is erased at save (:75472-75475) so it must be re-asserted on load.

Do not write Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal to 'unpair' it: RegenerateConnectionHashData saves it as a real type 0x11 with a fresh hash and its target gets 0x11|0x10=0x11 too, which pollutes the Portal|Target list ZDOMan.ConnectPortals scans at load. Use UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) (:73668-73678), which also sets DirtyPortals.

Ring collapse is worse than 'loses a link': for A→B→C→A the per-ZDO slot overwrite leaves one pair (e.g. B↔C) plus a stranded member, and which pair survives depends on s_connections dictionary order.

Spawner suppression is not permanent: at save, RegenerateConnectionHashData gives the target ZDO the {Spawned|Target,h} slot (:75473-75476). If the target is a PORTAL, that write collides with the portal's own {Portal,h'} / {Portal|Target,h'} slot in dictionary-iteration order — one of the two links is lost on disk: either the portal comes back unpaired or the spawner comes back unsuppressed (ConnectSpawners :77926-77960 only relinks matching hashes). Point suppression at a dedicated non-portal, otherwise-unconnected persistent ZDO, and re-assert after every world load.

Ring collapse: for an N-ring the hash-data pass leaves each ZDO with a single slot that later iterations overwrite; a 3-ring A->B->C->A comes back as one bidirectional pair plus one orphan (which vanilla then cannot pair, since the pair re-confirms itself). General statement: after a save/load any topology degrades to a dictionary-order-dependent pairwise matching of at most floor(N/2) pairs — not 'rings lose a link'.

One-way links are only runtime-stable when the TARGET's own Portal connection is non-None and its tag matches: Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 resets a source whose target has connection None (:100601-100604). A->B with B unconnected is torn down within 5 s.

Writing Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal is self-defeating beyond the 5 s pass: phase 2 sees None and re-pairs it with SetConnection(Portal, ...) which overwrites the slot; it is a way to force a re-pair, not a state.

Enforcement nuance: the CreatureSpawner reads the server-written connection but the spawn decision runs only on the ZDO owner's client (UpdateSpawner `if (!m_nview.IsOwner()) return;` :5639); the data is server-owned, the effect is client-honoured like all portal routing.

Game.ConnectPortals start-of-pass ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-writes both directions of pairs staged on the previous pass (:100690-100698) — any mod topology written between the staging pass and the next pass is overwritten once.

CreatureSpawner: UpdateSpawner returns early when `m_respawnTimeMinuts <= 0 && connection.type == Spawned`, and otherwise when SpawnedCreatureStillExists(connectionZDOID) — which is true for ANY resident ZDO id and also refreshes s_aliveTime (:5648-5660, :5703-5711); Spawn writes the Spawned connection (:5820). Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tests only target-resolves / same tag / target non-None, never reciprocity (:100596-100606). Corrections: the spawner trick is not 'permanent' and can corrupt a portal's saved pairing; ring collapse is worse than 'lose a link'; one-way links need a non-None target; and the spawner decision is executed on the owning client, i.e. server-owned data but client-honoured behaviour.

catalog.name: Self-Organising Networks From Player Behaviour
catalog.oneLine: Rewire the world's portal topology from what players actually do — transit counts, dwell time, build ownership — using data the server can already see for free.
catalog.howItWorks:
Every input this needs is already server-readable with no client install.

Usage: PositionWatch-style sampling of character ZDO positions (Wonderland Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31, IsPortalTransit at :148) already detects a portal transit by checking whether two consecutive position samples both sit within about 40 m of some entry in ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals(), and additionally follows one endpoint's GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) to see whether its partner is near the other endpoint. It was built in Wonderland v0.6.4 precisely because portal transits were tripping a speed check at roughly 110 m/s over a 3 s window. Invert its sense and it is a transit counter.

Ownership: every player-placed piece carries ZDOVars.s_creator (:78393), a PlayerProfile UID written by Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12514-12517), plus s_creatorIndex indexing ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396), which the server persists in the .fwl and maintains from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs (ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461). So 'who built this portal' is durable, offline-readable and account-level.

Dwell and adjacency: ConnectedCharacters.All() gives (peer, character ZDO) pairs; character positions are refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (:87527-87540). Count time spent within a radius of each portal.

The rewiring step is then the standard write triad, applied on a slow tick (30-120 s, not per transit): `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — literally what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645. Because TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads GetConnectionZDOID at the instant of transit (:143539) and never caches, a rewire takes effect on the very next walk-through with no client refresh.

The cleanest way to own the decision without owning the whole algorithm is a Harmony POSTFIX on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` (:100664-100679) that overwrites __result — swapping UnityEngine.Random.Range for nearest / most-used / least-used / admin-designated, while leaving vanilla's two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging completely intact. For full control, prefix Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) and return false.

Three structural facts shape what topologies are worth aiming for. Phase 1 never checks reciprocity, so rings and fan-in are stable at runtime. Three or more portals on one tag PERMANENTLY strand exactly one member (the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself), which is a free 'broken network' detector for an admin report. And which member gets stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and is not stable across restarts, so no admin-facing feature may assume a stable orphan identity.
catalog.playerExperience: The network learns. A player builds a portal at a new outpost and tags it with the same name as their base gate — and instead of the usual coin-flip about which of their three same-named portals it links to, it links to the one they actually use most. Over a week the hub at spawn rotates its outbound link toward whichever frontier the server's population is currently pushing into, and the hover text says so: 'THE CROSSROADS - currently: Mistlands Camp (41 crossings this week)'. A long-abandoned outpost quietly falls out of the rotation. Nobody configured any of it, and nobody installed anything.
failureModes: Transit detection is sampled, not eventful — a 3 s sample can miss a transit and a 0.25 s sample costs a per-player allocation and a full portal-dictionary walk each tick
Three or more same-tag portals permanently strand one member and the victim changes across restarts (dictionary bucket order, ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648)

A rewire on a portal an online player currently owns is deferred by Game.SetConnection over RPC_SetConnection (:100649) and the server's local copy still reads the old value that tick — phase 2 then skips it, so a retag near a player takes 2+ ticks

ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) hands portal ownership to any peer within roughly 96-112 m every 2 s, so the mod's ownership claim is transient; guard with a ZDO.SetOwner Harmony prefix (the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern)
Never cache ZDO object references across ticks — ZDOPool.Release recycles them and Game's own m_currentlyConnectingPortals violates this; cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve
A mass rewrite spikes every peer; budget routed broadcasts per sweep (Wonderland StructureUpkeep uses 256)
Rewiring under a player standing inside a portal's trigger volume does not re-trigger — TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673) fires on ENTER only; they must step out and back in
prerequisites: Portals As A Data Store (to persist usage counters)
The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface (to surface the result)
citations: TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads the connection at transit — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539
openQuestions: Is ZDOVars.s_creator reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator()==0 and IsOwner (:136417). IN-GAME: place a portal on a vanilla client and compare s_creator against that character ZDO's s_playerID.
How expensive is a 0.25 s tick that walks GetPortals() for every connected player on a world with several hundred portals and 20 peers? IN-GAME: Stopwatch the loop at scale.
corrections: 'Three or more portals on one tag permanently strand exactly one member' is wrong for even counts: N same-tag portals pair off in phase 2 until none are unconnected, stranding one only when N is odd (and nobody retags). The stranded member is chosen by Random.Range among the unpaired at pairing time (:100678), not by 'dictionary bucket order'.

'Not stable across restarts' is wrong when the world was saved: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) writes each pair as {Portal,h}/{Portal|Target,h} and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals restores them at load (:77850-77893) before Game.ConnectPortals runs (:76513-76521). The saved pair, and therefore the orphan identity, survives a restart. It is only unstable if the portal file was not dirtied (see SetDirtyPortals) or the pair is manually reset.

Creator data is client-written, not server-verified: s_creator is the placing client's own PlayerProfile id (GetPlayerID :12516) and s_creatorIndex is an index the client computed against its copy of m_playerHistory, both written owner-gated on that client (:136417-136423). The history list itself is socket-derived and server-persisted; the per-piece link to it is client-honoured.

A postfix that returns an already-connected portal (e.g. 'most used' that is currently paired) makes ConnectPortals overwrite that portal's connection (:100616-100617) and silently orphan its previous partner into a fan-in; the selector must filter to unconnected candidates unless fan-in is intended.

Server writes to a portal owned by a nearby client hit the RPC_ZDOData revision gate (:77108-77118); ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) re-assigns ownership every 2 s, so the triad must run immediately before ForceSendZDO and tolerate an occasional dropped write (the 30-120 s tick will re-assert).

PositionWatch's 40/60 m two-sample heuristic (PositionWatch.cs:148-200) is a speed-check exemption, not a transit counter: it also fires for a player walking between two portals 40 m apart. A transit counter needs a large positional jump (>>60 m) between consecutive samples plus both endpoints matching a connected pair, and it still counts the 2 s pre-jump window from Player.UpdateTeleport (:15338-15345).

The player-facing example is self-defeating: the tag IS the pairing key. Writing 'THE CROSSROADS - currently: Mistlands Camp (41 crossings this week)' into s_tag makes phase 1 (`zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string`, :100601) tear the pair down within 5 s unless the partner carries the identical string. Tag-as-display requires either mirroring the exact string onto the partner or replacing Game.ConnectPortals entirely (prefix returning false) and pairing on a mod-private key.

Usage/transit counting is reactive detection only: Wonderland's IsPortalTransit (PositionWatch.cs:148-185) classifies a 3 s position jump by 40 m / 60 m proximity to any portal; it cannot distinguish a portal transit from a nearby death/respawn or a server-initiated teleport, and misses back-to-back transits within one sample. No server-visible vanilla event marks a portal use (Game.IncrementPlayerStat(PortalsUsed) is client-local).

A Harmony postfix on FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only influences portals whose connection is currently None; steering an established pair toward 'most used' requires the mod to first write None on both ends (or let it strand), after which the staged two-tick commit (AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals -> ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals on the NEXT pass, :100680-100698) delays the new pair by up to 5 s and force-overwrites any mod write made in between.

Fan-in and one-way shapes are runtime-stable only while every target holds a non-None Portal connection with a matching tag (phase 1 resets a source whose target is None, :100601-100604); they collapse to a pairwise matching at the next save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478), so a world-load re-assert pass is mandatory, and it must be keyed on tag/position, not ZDOID (ZDO.Load re-issues ids, :74549-74552).

'Takes effect on the very next walk-through' needs a qualifier: the client's TargetFound() requires the new target ZDO to be present locally; if not, it calls RequestZDO and Teleport() returns silently (client :144386-144395, :144229-144232), and the ready-glow drops until the ZDO arrives — one server round-trip, typically well under a second, but a walk-through in that window is a silent no-op.

s_creator is the per-character PlayerProfile id, not an account id; account-level attribution comes only via s_creatorIndex -> m_playerHistory, which is written by the placing client (SetCreator :136421) and is absent on pieces placed before that field existed or by clients whose history copy was stale at placement.

ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) re-assigns portal ownership to a nearby peer every 2 s, so the mod's SetOwner(session) is transient; that is fine for the connection write (Game.SetConnection does the same) but a mod must not assume it retains ownership between ticks.
evidence: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — :75461-75478; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals load relink — :77850-77893; LoadChunks call order — :76513-76521
ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory — :81436-81461; m_players ids from socket host name — :81273-81276; World.m_playerHistory — :112396

TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads connection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539; client TargetFound RequestZDO — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144386-144395; Teleport early return :144229-144232

ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461; SendHistoricalPlayerList :81318-81341; RPC_HistoricalPlayerList :81419-81434; broadcast trigger :80349-80353; World.m_playerHistory :112396, save/load :112587-112590, :112709-112712
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The rewiring half is solid: Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100627) is started from Game.Awake only when ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:100071-100075) and runs every 5 s (:100580-100587) with no local-player dependency; FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is `private ZDO FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` (:100664-100679) and its result feeds AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals + SetConnection both ways, so a Harmony postfix on __result does swap the selector while keeping the two-tick commit (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal :100700-100709). The write triad is exactly Game.SetConnection's local path (:100641-100645). TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads GetConnectionZDOID at transit (:143539). TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) is client-only and enter-only. Phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601), so fan-in/rings are runtime-stable. Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator/s_creatorIndex (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12516); ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory (:81436-81461) maintains World.m_playerHistory (:112396) from m_players whose ids come from socket host names (:81273-81276). Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit exists at PositionWatch.cs:148 as described. Two factual claims about stranding are wrong and the input-trust framing needs tightening.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Inputs verified. Piece.SetCreator writes ZDOVars.s_creator (PlayerProfile id) and s_creatorIndex = index into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, owner-side, only when creator==0 (:136415-136424; s_creator :78393); the server maintains m_playerHistory from its own m_players list (UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461), persists it in the world (:112396, :112587-112590, :112709-112712), and broadcasts the full list to clients via 'HistoricalPlayerList' whenever it changes (:80349-80353, :81318-81341; client replaces its copy :81419-81434), so indices written by clients resolve against the server's list. Character positions: ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync every physics tick (:87527-87540). Rewrite triad is what Game.SetConnection does on its immediate path (:100637-100651); TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads GetConnectionZDOID at transit (:143539) with no cache. Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is private and returns list[Random.Range] (:100664-100679) — a Harmony postfix overwriting __result is valid. Three-on-a-tag stranding and phase-1 non-reciprocity confirmed (:100596-100627). Corrections: the transit signal is heuristic (Wonderland IsPortalTransit :148-185 is a 40 m/60 m proximity guess over a 3 s sample, not a transit event; PortalsUsed is a client-local stat); the hover-text example breaks pairing; one-way/fan-in shapes have the phase-1 None constraint and the save collapse; the FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix cannot rotate an existing pair; and a fresh rewire needs one RequestZDO round-trip on the client before TargetFound is true.

catalog.name: Portal-Driven Map Surfaces
catalog.oneLine: Honest inventory of what a server can put on a vanilla client's map because of a portal — three real channels, none of them portal-specific, and one hard limitation.
catalog.howItWorks:
Vanilla shows portal tags NOWHERE on the map; TeleportWorld exposes them only through GetHoverText (:143453-143463). So there is no portal pin to influence. What exists are three general server-to-client map channels, all usable in reaction to portal events.

(1) A NAMED, SAVED pin: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse', pinName, (int)Minimap.PinType, pos, showMap)`. Game.Start registers this handler on EVERY peer, outside the IsServer block (:100068), and the client body (:100823-100831) calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation, which AddPin(..., save: true) and shows a '$msg_pin_added' toast, optionally centring the map. This is Wonderland's FirstSpawnGrant pattern (Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263). The hard catch: save:true means the pin lands PERMANENTLY in that player's own profile and there is NO removal RPC. Re-pushing after a rename creates a second pin; HaveSimilarPin only suppresses an identical name+type within 1 m. So this is a one-shot discovery push, not a live-synced pin set.

(2) An ICON-ONLY overlay the server fully owns: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons (:113581-113593) packs a (Vector3, string) list into a ZPackage and sends the 'LocationIcons' routed RPC; the client's RPC_LocationIcons (:113595-113607) CLEARS and replaces its whole m_locationIcons dictionary, and Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds pins from it every 5 s. The server therefore controls the entire location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, and can add or remove entries at will. Limits: no label text at all, and only names that resolve to a sprite in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons render — an invented name is silently dropped. Also note this same channel is the authority for where a vanilla client respawns, via the Game.m_StartLocation ('StartTemple') entry read by Game.FindSpawnPoint.

(3) A TEMPORARY labelled pin plus in-world text plus a chat line, from one RPC: a fabricated 'ChatMessage' (Chat.Awake registration :41626; Chat.RPC_ChatMessage :41970-41973; OnNewChatMessage :41775-41816). Type 2 (Shout) renders a chat line, yellow uppercase floating world text, and an animated map pin labelled '<UserInfo.Name>: <TEXT>' for m_worldTextTTL = 5 s. Type 3 (Ping) gives no chat line and forces the world text to 'PING'. UserInfo.Name is entirely server-chosen, so 'The Waygate' can be the speaker. Less-than and greater-than are replaced with spaces in OnNewChatMessage (:41795-41796), so no markup.

Combined, a portal event can: permanently pin a newly discovered destination (once), keep a live icon-only overlay of every active gate, and flash a 5-second labelled pin plus a floating caption at the moment a hub rotates.
catalog.playerExperience: A player uses a hub gate for the first time this week. As the black screen clears, a toast reads 'Pin added: Ashlands Foothold' and a marker is now permanently on their map at the place they just arrived. Meanwhile a set of small icons has appeared across the map wherever the server currently maintains an open public gate — no names, just markers, updating every five seconds as gates open and close. And at the moment the hub rotates, everyone within range sees 'THE WAYGATE: NOW OPEN TO MISTLANDS CAMP' briefly appear in chat, in the air above the arch, and as a labelled pin on the map for five seconds. None of it required a client install; all of it is vanilla's own discovery and shout machinery.
failureModes: RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are save:true and there is NO removal RPC — a demolished portal's pin stays on the player's map forever
A renamed destination produces a SECOND permanent pin; HaveSimilarPin matches on name AND type AND within 1 m
LocationIcons pins carry no name and render only for names present in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list — invented names are dropped with no error
LocationIcons is a full replace, not a delta, and it is also what tells a vanilla client where StartTemple is (Game.FindSpawnPoint) — overwriting the set carelessly can move where players respawn

A fabricated Shout or Ping renders its map pin only if Chat.AddInworldText runs, which is skipped when Minimap.m_mode is None AND the position is beyond m_nomapPingDistance (50 m) — i.e. in nomap worlds or with the HUD hidden
Minimap.AddPin forces any PinType outside the visible range to Icon3, so exotic types silently collapse
Map pings are public: Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 (:42058-42068), so a ping-driven feature is a visible, shared, spammable gesture
prerequisites: Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport (for arrival-time pin pushes)
citations: TeleportWorld.GetHoverText is the only tag surface — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464
openQuestions: Which names exist in the shipped client's Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list? That bounds the LocationIcons overlay entirely. IN-GAME: on a client, enumerate Minimap.instance.m_locationIcons and log every m_name.

Does RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse render identically on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client? Wonderland ships it but has no dated live-test note. IN-GAME: push a pin to a crossplay client, relog, and confirm persistence.

Does overwriting the LocationIcons set actually move a vanilla client's respawn point (Game.FindSpawnPoint reads GetLocationIcon(StartTemple))? IN-GAME: omit StartTemple from a push and have a test character die.
corrections: Channel (2): ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons is private and builds only from m_locationInstances (server-side GetLocationIcons branch, CLIENT :116093-116103); a mod must craft its own ZPackage and call ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, 'LocationIcons', pkg) directly. Vanilla re-sends the pure vanilla set on every new peer (ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer, SERVER :113609-113616) and whenever any m_iconPlaced location is placed (SERVER :114998-115001), silently wiping the mod overlay; the mod must include vanilla's entries (public ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons(dict)) in every push and re-push after those events (Harmony postfix on SendLocationIcons).

Channel (2) is load-bearing for respawn: the client's Game.FindSpawnPoint resolves m_StartLocation ('StartTemple') via ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(name, out pos), which on a client iterates m_locationIcons (CLIENT :100796-100800, :116062-116088). A mod push that omits the StartTemple entry makes bed-less respawn return false forever; a push that adds a second 'StartTemple' entry can redirect it (dictionary iteration order, first match). Also the dictionary is keyed by exact Vector3, so two overlay icons at the same position collapse to one.
Channel (2): the set of renderable names is asset data (Minimap.m_locationIcons, CLIENT :56373) not present in the decompile; which names exist must be checked in-game.

Channel (3): Chat.OnNewChatMessage calls RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync(sender.UserId, CommunicateWithUsingText, ...) for any senderID that is not the local player (SERVER :41780-41786). CheckPermissionAsync returns Error (message dropped) when !user.IsValid, and when PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider != null it calls RelationsProvider.GetUserProfileAsync(user, ...) on the fabricated id (CLIENT :88643-88700). UserInfo deserialises UserId via new PlatformUserID(pkg.ReadString()) (CLIENT :72903-72907). So the server-chosen speaker must carry a syntactically valid platform id string, and the Steam/PlayFab profile-lookup outcome for a fake id is unverifiable here (Splatform assembly not decompiled) — needs an in-game check. The displayed name is also passed through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC(Name, CharacterName, UserId) (CLIENT :72915-72918).

Channel (3): the world text and pin are skipped when the receiver is InIntro, and the in-world text is skipped when the large map is open and the receiver is farther than Minimap.m_nomapPingDistance (SERVER :41797, :41808).
Channel (1): the toast icon and the pin sprite come from Minimap.GetSprite((PinType)pinType); the pin is persisted only when that client next saves its profile.

Chat-line speaker cannot be server-chosen: Chat.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) SERVER :45950-45955 looks the UserId up in ZNet.m_players (TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID :81477-81493); unknown id => 'Failed to get player info' LogError and no chat line; known id => attributed to that player's character name. Only AddInworldText/world text and the shout map pin use UserInfo.Name (WorldTextInstance.m_name => m_userInfo.GetDisplayName() :41531).

Robust send pattern: per-peer InvokeRoutedRPC with UserInfo.UserId = that recipient's own PlatformUserID. CheckPermissionAsync short-circuits to Granted for the local user (CLIENT RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync, 'user == LocalUser.PlatformUserID' branch) so no platform lookup, the chat line is attributed to the recipient's own character, and the world text/pin still reads 'The Waygate: ...'. Any other UserId is subject to RelationsManager (mute list, platform profile lookup) and can be silently dropped.

All server-fabricated messages share one WorldTextInstance slot keyed by senderID (FindExistingWorldText :41927-41936 uses the routed m_senderPeerID, i.e. the server id) — a second message within 5 s replaces the first instead of stacking.
RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse has a side effect: if the map is not open the client rotates the player toward the pin for 3.5 s (Player.SetLookDir, SERVER :100826-100829).
'Permanent' pin = until the player deletes it manually on the map; there is no server-side removal, but the player can.

LocationIcons overlay is overwritten by vanilla: ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation calls SendLocationIcons(0L) whenever an m_iconPlaced location is placed (SERVER :114999-115001), wiping the mod's list on every client; the mod must re-send after that (Harmony postfix on SendLocationIcons or periodic rebroadcast). The mod's list must also MERGE vanilla's entries (server GetLocationIcons builds from m_locationInstances m_iconAlways/m_iconPlaced, :116089-116105) — omitting 'StartTemple' makes the client's Game.FindSpawnPoint (CLIENT :100796-100804) fall to Vector3.zero for characters with no bed.
SendLocationIcons is private; the mod should build the ZPackage (count, then Vector3+string pairs) and call ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, 'LocationIcons', pkg) directly.

Citation fixes: Game.Start registration is :100067 not :100068; Minimap.DiscoverLocation CLIENT :58394-58421, HaveSimilarPin :58423-58432, AddPin :58434+ (the listed 58375-58406 / 58363-58374 ranges are off).
evidence: Game.Start RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse registration on all peers — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100062-100073
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All three channels exist in the decompile with the claimed shapes. (1) Game.Start registers RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse on every peer outside the IsServer block (SERVER :100068); the client body calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation (SERVER :100823-100831), which does AddPin(pos, type, name, save:true, isChecked:false, 0L) and a '$msg_pin_added' toast (CLIENT :58394-58421); HaveSimilarPin requires equal name+type+save and DistanceXZ < 1 m (CLIENT :58423-58433). No removal RPC exists; the only removal path is Minimap.RemovePin on the local client (CLIENT :58380-58385). (2) ZoneSystem.RPC_LocationIcons clears and rebuilds m_locationIcons from the package (SERVER :113595-113607); Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds every 5 s and only adds a pin when GetLocationIcon(name) resolves a sprite in the compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons list (CLIENT :57551-57603); RPC 'LocationIcons' is registered on the client only in the non-server branch (SERVER :113453). (3) Chat.Awake registers 'ChatMessage' (SERVER :41626); RPC_ChatMessage -> OnNewChatMessage (SERVER :41970-41973); Shout uppercases and colours yellow, Ping forces 'PING' (SERVER :41895-41907); Minimap.UpdateShoutPins builds an animated pin named m_name + ': ' + m_text for Shout-type world texts only (CLIENT :57684-57713, GetShoutWorldTexts :42073-42081); TTL m_worldTextTTL = 5f (CLIENT :41589). Corrections below are real gaps, not refutations: the location-icon channel is clobbered by vanilla re-sends, must preserve the StartTemple entry, and the fabricated-UserInfo chat path passes through RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync, which drops the message on an invalid PlatformUserID and, on platforms with a RelationsProvider, does a profile lookup on the fake id (Splatform is not in the decompile set, so this needs an in-game check).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Channels (1) and (2) hold exactly as read. RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse is registered in Game.Start on every instance outside the IsServer block (SERVER :100067) and the client body calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation (:100823-100831) which does HaveSimilarPin(save:true) then AddPin(save:true) and a '$msg_pin_added' TopLeft toast (CLIENT :58394-58421); no pin-removal RPC exists. RPC_LocationIcons clears and rebuilds m_locationIcons wholesale (SERVER :113595-113607) and the client's Minimap.UpdateLocationPins polls it every 5 s, removing pins absent from the dictionary and adding PinType.None double-size pins only when GetLocationIcon resolves a sprite (CLIENT :57551-57590); UpdatePins has no explored-area gate (CLIENT UpdatePins IsPointVisible check only). Channel (3) is HALF wrong: the chat LINE goes through Chat.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) (:45933-45955) which resolves the speaker via ZNet.TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID (:81477-81493) against the live player list and LogErrors + returns when the UserId is not a connected player; the display name is that player's character name, NOT UserInfo.Name. Only the floating world text and the 5 s shout map pin use m_userInfo.GetDisplayName() (:41531, UpdateWorldTextField :41915-41924, CLIENT UpdateShoutPins :57684-57700), so 'The Waygate' can speak in the world/map but never in the chat log. Additionally OnNewChatMessage (:41777-41783) runs RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync(sender.UserId) unless senderID equals the recipient's own peer id; an invalid PlatformUserID yields Error and the message is dropped (CLIENT :88604+ CheckPermissionAsync 'UserID was invalid'), and on a platform with a RelationsProvider an arbitrary valid-format id triggers a platform profile lookup with unverifiable outcome. Effort 'medium' is fair; enforcement client-honoured is honest.

catalog.name: The Tag Is Also The Lock — Puzzle And Progression Gates
catalog.oneLine: A composite: use the tag, the connection, global keys and the Void Anchor together to build gates that open and close on server-side conditions with no client install.
catalog.howItWorks:
Four independent levers compose into real puzzle mechanics.

HARD LOCK (server-enforced): null the connection. `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (:143519) is the ONLY genuinely server-enforced gate of the four, because it reads the ZDO connection the server owns. Vanilla's pairer will re-pair it within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists, so a locked gate must either be alone on its tag or the mod must own pairing.

SOFT LOCK (silent): the Decoy Gate — connection pointed at an unresolvable ZDOID. Hover still reads connected, glow still lights, transit silently does nothing. This is the better puzzle primitive because it gives the player no error to search for.

GLOBAL LOCK (client-honoured, world-wide): `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey('noportals')` reaches every connected vanilla client within one network frame — SetGlobalKey (:115943-115946) routes to the server's own handler synchronously, RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029) adds and then SendGlobalKeys(0L) (:113466-113471) broadcasts the whole key list, and each client's RPC_GlobalKeys clears and rebuilds. TeleportWorld.Teleport reads it live at gate 2 (:143523) and shows '$msg_blocked'. Two operational cautions: this is world-wide, not per-portal; and GlobalKeyAdd mirrors any key below GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (41) into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113511), permanently baking it into the .fwl — use the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` plus SendGlobalKeys(0L) for a session-only lock.

STATE: per-portal puzzle state lives in mod-private ZDO keys on the portal itself (see Portals As A Data Store), plus per-player once-only flags as world global keys following the Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant convention `<mod>_<feature>_<playerID>` — persisted in the .db, readable synchronously after SetGlobalKey returns.

INPUT: the only reliable vanilla-client-to-server channels are emotes (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID polled on the character ZDO at 0.25 s, the Wonderland EmoteSignals pattern), map pings (Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 with a world Vector3), equipped item hashes on the character ZDO (VisEquipment writes s_rightItem etc.), item stands (ZDOVars.s_item is the mounted prefab hash), signs (ZDOVars.s_text, written directly by the client with no RPC), and chest contents (ZDOVars.s_items). Chat text is NOT usable — a solo player's chat produces zero packets.

FEEDBACK: PlayerNotify toasts via the character-ZDO 'Message' RPC, DamageText.TextType.Bonus floating text within 30 m, a granted status effect, a vanilla vfx/sfx through the 'SpawnObject' routed RPC, and the portal's own tag rewritten live.
catalog.playerExperience: A ring of five ancient portals in a stone circle, all tagged with runes, all glowing 'connected', none of them working. Beside each is an item stand. Mount the right offering on the right stand — the server reads ZDOVars.s_item on each stand's ZDO — and when the combination is correct, all five tags change in the same instant from runes to 'THE ROAD OPENS', a vfx flares at each one, everyone present gets a centre-screen toast, and the ring becomes a real fan-in network to a sixth, hidden gate. The puzzle state persists across server restarts because it lives on the portal ZDOs themselves. A player who solves it gets a permanent map pin to the destination. Nobody installed anything; every element is either vanilla's own hover text, vanilla's own effects, or vanilla's own map.
failureModes: Nulling a connection is undone by Game.ConnectPortals within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists (:100607-100621)
GlobalKeys.NoPortals is world-wide and client-honoured, and RPC_SetGlobalKey has ZERO sender validation (:116022-116029) — any client can lift it unless the mod Harmony-prefixes that RPC
Setting a portal key at runtime permanently edits the world's .fwl modifier list via GlobalKeyAdd (:113511) unless canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false is passed

ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes enum ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115904-115931) and re-adds only what is in the .fwl — mod-owned world-modifier keys must be re-applied in a POSTFIX on it
Emote polling has a 0.25 s resolution and a first-sighting seed; a player can emote faster than the poll
Map pings are broadcast to every player, so a ping-based puzzle input is public
All puzzle logic runs server-side against sampled state; there is no atomic transaction and two players can race a combination
