catalog.id: wildcard:The Tag Is Also The Lock — Puzzle And Progression Gates
corrections: SOFT LOCK (Decoy Gate) is reverted by vanilla: Game.ConnectPortals first loop calls SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None) when ZDOMan.GetZDO(connection) == null, when the target's s_tag differs, or when the target's own connection is None (SERVER :100594-100606). A dangling ZDOID is therefore cleared within 5 s unless the mod prefixes Game.ConnectPortals (private) to skip locked portals. If instead the target IS a server-held ZDO, the client resolves it via TargetFound -> ZDOMan.RequestZDO -> server RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO, which AddForceSendZdos sends irrespective of the peer's area (SERVER :77684-77692, :77263-77285), and the vanilla client then teleports to zdo.GetPosition() (SERVER :143538-143547). There is no configuration in which hover shows 'connected' indefinitely while transit silently does nothing without patching ConnectPortals.

HARD LOCK re-pairing is faster than stated and symmetrical: nulling portal A leaves its former partner B pointing at A; on the next pass loop 1 nulls B (its target's connection is None, :100600) and loop 2 re-pairs A<->B via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100608-100620, :100662-100676). The only vanilla-stable states are: unique tag, tag rewritten to a mod-private value, or ConnectPortals suppressed. Ownership is not required for the server's connection write to replicate (ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision has no owner gate on the server build, :73832-73840), but a portal owned by an online peer is normally written via RPC_SetConnection round-trip inside Game.SetConnection (:100637-100650) — the mod should write the ZDO directly and call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO.

GLOBAL LOCK persistence: GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false) only prevents the .fwl mirror (:113489, :113510-113511). m_globalKeys itself is always cloned into the .db save (ZoneSystem.PrepareSave :113734-113740), so a 'session-only' NoPortals still persists across a restart unless removed (GlobalKeyRemove / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey :113517, :116031-116037) before the save. GlobalKeyAdd and SendGlobalKeys are both private.

STATE: mod-private keys on a portal ZDO are only written to disk when the portal chunk is dirty; DirtyPortalObjects is double-buffered and reset per save (:76139-76149, :76221-76230), and a plain zdo.Set(...) does not set it. The mod must call the public ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705) after each puzzle-state write or the state is lost at the next save.

Per-player once-only flags as global keys are broadcast to every client in the full key list and stamped into every client's PlayerProfile m_knownWorldKeys stats on receipt (:113505-113509) — functional, but noisy and visible to any client that inspects its stats.
Citation fix: ItemStand s_item mount write is at SERVER :131845 (stableHashCode); :131795 is RPC_DestroyAttachment writing 0.
Enforcement label applies only to the connection-null hard lock; the global lock and all feedback/input channels are client-honoured.

Owning pairing is mandatory, not optional: Game.ConnectPortals second loop (:100606-100618) re-pairs any two same-tag unconnected portals every 5 s, and 'alone on its tag' is not a lock (no route existed). Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (or a filtered ZDOMan.GetPortalList) is required for BOTH hard and soft locks.

Decoy Gate is wiped by vanilla within 5 s: ConnectPortals first loop (:100598-100603) nulls any connection whose target ZDO resolves to null. Also, while it stands, m_target_found is NOT active (UpdatePortal :143507 gates on TargetFound) — only the emission lerp lights (Update :143512-143516) — and each client with the instance sends a 'RequestZDO' routed RPC every 0.5 s (:143650-143652, :77684-77687).

Puzzle state on portal ZDOs is lost at the next save unless the mod calls ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() after each write: ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76699) only dirties normal chunks, which exclude portals (:77572); ChunkPortal is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77632).

Fan-in network does not survive save/reload: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) stores one ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDO (H's Target entry is overwritten by each spoke, then replaced by H's own Portal entry), and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77855-77887) rebuilds pairwise only. After restart the ring is one pair plus unconnected portals which vanilla re-pairs among themselves within 5 s; the mod must rebuild the fan-in at startup from its own persisted state.

'SpawnObject' routed RPC is safe only for prefabs without ZNetView: RPC_SpawnObject (:82355-82366) calls Object.Instantiate on every receiving client; a ZNetView prefab would spawn a new ZDO per client (ZNetView.Awake m_initZDO==null path :82615-82626).

Chat text IS partially usable: with 2+ players Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync sends the shout per recipient uid (CLIENT :42008-42034) and each copy passes through the server's ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC/RouteRPC (CLIENT :83861-83873, :83826-83859) where a Harmony patch can read it; only the solo-with-RelationsProvider case (self-send only, :42007) produces zero packets, and with no RelationsProvider it is sent to Everybody (:42004) and the server handles it.

Per-player once-only global keys are unknown strings (gk = NonServerOption) so they ARE saved in the .db (:113751-113755 keeps them) and the entire key list is rebroadcast to every client on every change (RPC_SetGlobalKey -> SendGlobalKeys(0L)); each also increments every client's m_knownWorldKeys stats (:113505-113507).

Per-player route gating is impossible: the connection is one value per portal ZDO read by every client; a route is open for everyone or nobody. The composite is server-enforced ONLY for the hard route lock; NoPortals, the ore check and the offering-detection feedback are client-honoured.
evidence: ZDO.SetConnection / IncreaseDataRevision (no owner gate) / InternalSetPosition (owner gate) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656-73665, 73832-73840, 73734-73745
TeleportWorld.Teleport gates / HaveTarget / TargetFound / UpdatePortal / Update — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143490-143546, 143512-143516, 143631-143655
ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portals; GetSaveClonePerChunk ChunkPortal only when DirtyPortalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572, 77621-77632
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The hard lock is real and route-form: TeleportWorld.Teleport returns before any player check when TargetFound() is false (SERVER :143517-143521), TargetFound is false when the ZDO connection is ZDOID.None (SERVER :143643-143656), and on the server build ZDO.SetConnection -> IncreaseDataRevision has no owner check (SERVER :73656-73665, :73832-73840; contrast InternalSetPosition :73734-73745), so a server write replicates. The global lock path is exactly as cited: SetGlobalKey -> InvokeRoutedRPC(GetServerPeerID()) dispatches synchronously to the local handler when m_server (SERVER :115943-115946, :83559-83593), RPC_SetGlobalKey -> GlobalKeyAdd + SendGlobalKeys(0L) (SERVER :116022-116029, :113466-113471), client RPC_GlobalKeys clears and rebuilds (SERVER :113473-113481), and Teleport reads GlobalKeys.NoPortals live at gate 2 (SERVER :143522-143526); NoPortals sits below NonServerOption in the enum (SERVER :101304, :101313) so GlobalKeyAdd mirrors it into m_startingGlobalKeys when flag is true (SERVER :113483-113511). Input channels check out: Player.StartEmote writes s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot (SERVER :15585-15598), Sign.SetText claims ownership and writes s_text directly (SERVER :141915-141928), ItemStand stores the prefab hash as an int in s_item (SERVER :131845, read :132027), Chat.SendPing broadcasts to 0L (SERVER :42058-42068); shouts on a platform with a RelationsProvider are sent per-target and a solo player's shout is handled locally with no RouteRPC (SERVER :41983-42004, :83583-83593). Feedback: Character 'Message' RPC (SERVER :10072), DamageText.m_maxTextDistance = 30f (SERVER :46338), ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' (SERVER :81954, :82355-82366). But the SOFT LOCK / Decoy Gate as described does not survive vanilla: Game.ConnectPortals nulls any portal whose connection target GetZDO() returns null, or whose target has a different tag or a None connection, on every 5 s pass (SERVER :100594-100606); and if the target does exist server-side, a vanilla client's TargetFound calls RequestZDO, the server's RPC_RequestZDO force-sends it regardless of area (SERVER :77689-77692, :77263-77285), TargetFound becomes true, and Teleport moves the player to that ZDO's position (SERVER :143538-143547). So a decoy is only silent if ConnectPortals is Harmony-suppressed for that portal AND the ZDOID never resolves server-side. The composite's 'server-enforced' label is honest only for the connection-null hard lock; every other lever is client-honoured.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The four levers exist, but two of the four descriptions are wrong about vanilla's reconciliation, and the persistence story is wrong twice. HARD LOCK: TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143640-143655) does gate on the ZDO connection, so nulling it is a genuine route-form server lock — but Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100620) re-pairs any two same-tag unconnected portals in its second loop within 5 s, and a portal 'alone on its tag' never had a route to lock, so the mod MUST own pairing (Harmony on Game.ConnectPortals or on ZDOMan.GetPortalList, the only two callers being :77815 load-time and :100592). SOFT LOCK: a decoy ZDOID is wiped by the FIRST loop (:100598-100603, `zDO == null` => SetConnection(None)) within 5 s, so the decoy is also impossible without owning pairing; while it stands, HaveTarget lights the emission (:143512-143516) but m_target_found stays off (:143507 requires TargetFound) and every client that has the portal instantiated fires RequestZDO every 0.5 s (:143650-143652 -> :77684-77692). GLOBAL LOCK: SetGlobalKey -> RPC_SetGlobalKey -> GlobalKeyAdd -> SendGlobalKeys(0L) confirmed (:115943-115946, :116022-116029, :113483-113513, :113466-113471); NoPortals enum ordinal 34 < NonServerOption 43 so it is mirrored into m_startingGlobalKeys with the default flag (:113487, :113511), and ZoneSystem.Save strips keys < NonServerOption from the .db (:113751-113755) so GlobalKeyAdd(key,false)+SendGlobalKeys(0L) is indeed session-only. STATE: mod-private keys on portal ZDOs are NOT saved by default — ZDO.Set->IncreaseDataRevision->SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76699) dirties normal chunks which exclude portals (:77572); the ChunkPortal file is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77632), so SetDirtyPortals() is mandatory after every write. The fan-in topology in the player experience does not survive a save: RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps one hash slot per ZDO and overwrites H's entry for each incoming link (:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load pairs strictly pairwise (:77855-77887). INPUT list is accurate (StartEmote :15585-15598, Sign.SetText :141916-141928, ItemStand s_item :131795) except the chat claim, which is only true for a solo player when a RelationsProvider exists (CLIENT :42003-42007). FEEDBACK: 'Message' RPC on the character ZDO exists (:10072, :14816); 'SpawnObject' exists (:81954, :82355-82366) but instantiates on every receiving client, so only ZNetView-less vfx/sfx prefabs are safe.

catalog.name: Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World, And Server-Side Instantiation
catalog.oneLine: Any ZDO beyond roughly plus or minus 16.4 km clamps into the same sector bucket the dedicated server's own pinned reference position maps to, which makes the server instantiate it.
catalog.howItWorks:
This is the mechanism nobody documents and it cuts both ways.

ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex (:115760-115773) computes `uint num = (uint)(sectorX + 256)` and clamps ANY sector outside 0..511 to `result.Sector = 0`. Zones are 64 m, so the legal range is roughly x/z in [-16416, +16352]; a normal world is plus or minus 10500, comfortably inside. Sector 0 is therefore shared by zone (-256,-256) and by EVERY out-of-range coordinate.

Game.FixedUpdate in the SERVER build pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466) — a line that exists in no form in the client build. Zone (15625, 15625) maps through SectorToIndex to Sector 0.

Crucially, the server does NOT simply idle there. ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone (:114021-114037) chooses `SpawnMode.Full` when `ZNet.instance.IsServer() && !IsZoneGenerated(zoneID)`, and SpawnZone (:114071-114107) succeeds and registers the zone in m_zones. So the server's own local zones around (1e6, 0, 1e6) ARE created, and ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:114054-114069) becomes true for them. ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects runs every 1/30 s (:82257-82276) and calls FindSectorObjects for zone (15625,15625) — which, via the clamp, returns m_objectsBySector[0] plus m_portalObjects[SectorIndex 0].

Two real consequences:
(a) A ZDO created at an out-of-range coordinate WILL be instantiated as a real GameObject on the dedicated server. For a portal that means a live TeleportWorld with a ZNetView, a running InvokeRepeating('UpdatePortal', 0.5f, 0.5f), and a TeleportWorldTrigger collider — harmless only because Player.m_localPlayer is null and Player.s_players is empty, so OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) can never fire. It is still a per-tick cost and a surprise in any object dump.
(b) The invalid-prefab reaper is SERVER-ONLY: CreateObjectsSorted's `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` branch (:82137-82143) takes ownership and destroys any ZDO whose CreateObject returns null. That branch is the ONLY thing in the game that reaps prefab-less ZDOs — and it only ever sees bucket 0. This is exactly why a Void Anchor placed at normal world coordinates survives indefinitely, and exactly why one placed out of bounds is deleted within a frame.

Practical rules: never create a portal or an anchor beyond about plus or minus 16000 m; if a mod wants a 'nowhere' anchor, put it at a legal but unvisited coordinate (deep ocean, or high above terrain) rather than out of bounds. And if any mod ever moved the server's reference position into the real world, the server would start instantiating real portal GameObjects with real colliders everywhere.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing intentional — this is a trap to be avoided rather than a feature to sell. The player-visible symptom of getting it wrong is an admin waypoint or an event gate that works for exactly one frame and then vanishes with a 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' line in the server log, or a portal placed 'off the map' that quietly consumes server CPU forever while being reachable by nobody. The one legitimate use is diagnostic: a mod can deliberately park a marker ZDO in bucket 0 to confirm from the log whether the server's active area is loaded on a given build.
failureModes: A Void Anchor placed out of bounds is destroyed by the server's own invalid-prefab reaper within a frame (:82137-82143)
A valid portal prefab placed out of bounds is instantiated server-side as a live MonoBehaviour with a repeating invoke, permanently
WorldGenerator.GetBiomeHeight returns -400 beyond 10500 m (:151978-151981), so out-of-bounds coordinates have no meaningful terrain at all
Bucket 0 also holds legitimate zone (-256,-256) content, so anything a mod does there is mixed with real world data
The whole behaviour hinges on IsActiveAreaLoaded being true for the pinned zone, which depends on HeightmapBuilder succeeding at (1e6, 0, 1e6) — plausible but unverified
citations: Game.FixedUpdate pins reference position (SERVER build only) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466
ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone uses SpawnMode.Full on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:114021-114037
ZDOMan.FindObjects merges m_portalObjects for the clamped sector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77382
openQuestions: Does ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() actually return true on a running 1.0.7 dedicated server at (1e6,0,1e6)? IN-GAME: log IsActiveAreaLoaded(), m_zones.Count and ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() every 10 s.

Does the server genuinely instantiate a portal ZDO parked in bucket 0? IN-GAME: create a portal ZDO at (20000, 0, 20000) and log ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() and Heightmap.GetAllHeightmaps() positions before and after.
catalog.id: wildcard:Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World, And Server-Side Instantiation
corrections: The invalid-prefab reaper is not unique to CreateObjectsSorted: ZNetScene.CreateDistantObjects has the same server-only SetOwner + DestroyZDO branch for Distant ZDOs ('Destroyed invalid predab ZDO', SERVER :82156-82181). Both run only over the server's reference-zone neighbourhood, so the conclusion (only bucket 0 is ever reaped) is unchanged.

Whether the server's active area ever loads (and therefore whether bucket-0 objects are instantiated at all) depends on HeightmapBuilder producing terrain for zones around (15625,15625) — IsTerrainReady queues an HMBuildData and returns false until the builder thread finishes (SERVER :129879-129899). The code has no coordinate guard and WorldGenerator returns a constant ocean-floor height beyond 10500 m, so it should succeed, but this is runtime behaviour that must be confirmed from a server log or object dump before any design relies on 'instantiated on the server'.

Side effect not mentioned: SpawnZone in SpawnMode.Full calls SetZoneGenerated for the far zones (SERVER :114105), so the server's phantom zones are recorded in m_generatedZones and persisted in the .db.

A Void Anchor at legal coordinates is never reaped server-side, but a vanilla client inside its area will retry CreateObject every 1/30 s and log 'Missing prefab hash' each time (SERVER :82000-82008, no client-side reaper branch) — a client log-spam cost this option's 'survives indefinitely' framing omits.
Enforcement label: this is a server-internal lifecycle behaviour, not a rule applied to players; 'server-enforced' is a category error. It is relevant only to mod authors and admins.

Server-side instantiation is conditional on ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() (CreateObjectsSorted :82107-82110), i.e. SpawnZone succeeding at zone (15625,15625) via HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady (:114073-114078). The code path has no gate, but whether the heightmap builds at 1e6 needs an in-game log check ('Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' after parking a hash-less ZDO out of bounds is the probe).

Client side of the reaper claim: a vanilla client never reaps, but for a ZDO whose prefab hash is non-zero and unknown, CreateObject logs 'Missing prefab hash' (:82004) on every 30 Hz CreateDestroyObjects pass for as long as it is in the active area, because the ZDO never becomes Created (:82115). Only prefab hash 0 is silent (:81999). A Void Anchor at legal coordinates must therefore use hash 0 or a real harmless prefab, not an invented hash.

SpawnMode.Full at the pinned zone also runs PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation/PlaceZoneCtrl for zone (15625,15625) (:114093-114095) and adds it to m_generatedZones (SetZoneGenerated :114106, saved by ZoneSystem.Save :113745-113749) — harmless but visible in the .db.

Precise legal range: sector index x,y in [-256,255] => world x/z in [-16416, 16352) (GetSectorIndex FloorToInt((p+32)/64) :115747-115752). A portal's m_portalObjects key is fixed at AddIfPortal time (CreateNewZDO :76683, RPC_ZDOData) and SetSector is a no-op for portals (:73752-73757), so a portal created in-range and later moved out of range stays in its original bucket, not bucket 0.
evidence: Game.FixedUpdate reference-position pin (server build) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466; no equivalent in assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs (grep 1000000f: only :33266, :54275, :54318 UI/m_maxYPos)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The sector math is exactly as claimed: ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex computes (uint)(sector+256) and sets Sector = 0 for anything outside 0..511 (SERVER :115760-115773), and ZDO.GetSectorIndex routes through ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex(m_position) (SERVER :73776-73779). Game.FixedUpdate in the SERVER build pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every physics tick (SERVER :100458-100466); the client build has no such line (grep of 1000000f in the client shows only unrelated UI/physics constants). Zone(1e6) = floor((1e6+32)/64) = 15625, which SectorToIndex clamps to 0. ZoneSystem.Update calls CreateLocalZones(ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition()) every 0.1 s once connected and locations are generated (SERVER :113905-113938); PokeLocalZone chooses SpawnMode.Full on the server for an ungenerated zone (SERVER :114021-114037); SpawnZone instantiates the zone prefab once HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady is true (SERVER :114071-114107), and WorldGenerator returns a flat -2*multiplier height beyond 10500 m (SERVER :151978-151981), so nothing in the code prevents the far zones from building. ZNetScene.Update -> CreateDestroyObjects every 1/30 s uses the reference zone, FindSectorObjects visits bucket 0 (deduped by m_visitedSectorIndices) and FindObjects merges m_objectsBySector[0] and m_portalObjects[SectorIndex 0] (SERVER :82257-82276, :77142-77185, :77367-77382). CreateObjectsSorted requires IsActiveAreaLoaded (SERVER :82105-82109) and its else-if IsServer branch claims ownership and destroys any ZDO whose CreateObject returns null (SERVER :82137-82143); IsZoneReadyForType only consults m_loadingObjectsInZones, not m_zones, so it does not block bucket-0 objects (SERVER :115797-115813). AddIfPortal keys portals by GetSectorIndex at first sight (SERVER :77732-77752), so an out-of-range portal lands in m_portalObjects[0]. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter requires Player.m_localPlayer == component (SERVER :143673-143681). The chain holds on paper; what cannot be confirmed from the decompile is that the HeightmapBuilder thread and Heightmap component actually complete at coordinate 1e6 on a headless server so that IsActiveAreaLoaded ever turns true — that is the single in-game check the option depends on.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The sector math holds exactly as claimed: SectorToIndex clamps any sectorX/Y+256 outside 0..511 to Sector 0 (:115760-115773); Game.FixedUpdate in the SERVER build pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every physics tick (:100458-100466) and no 1000000f reference-position write exists in the client build (only unrelated UI/m_maxYPos uses); zone (15625,15625) clamps to Sector 0. ZoneSystem.Update calls CreateLocalZones(GetReferencePosition()) every 0.1 s with no dedicated-server gate (:113901-113933); PokeLocalZone picks SpawnMode.Full on the server (:114021-114035); SpawnZone registers the zone if HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady succeeds (:114071-114107); IsActiveAreaLoaded then returns true (:114054-114069). ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects runs at 30 Hz (:82257-82276), FindSectorObjects->FindObjects merges m_objectsBySector[0] and m_portalObjects[Sector 0] with visited-set dedup (:77367-77382), RemoveObjects is earmark-based not distance-based (:82196-82227) so bucket-0 instances persist, and the invalid-prefab reaper is inside `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` in CreateObjectsSorted (:82137-82143) with no other caller — so the reaper sees only bucket 0. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter requires Player.m_localPlayer (:143673-143681) so an instantiated server-side portal cannot teleport anyone. What the decompile cannot prove is that SpawnZone actually succeeds at (1e6,0,1e6): it depends on HeightmapBuilder producing terrain there (WorldGenerator returns beyond-edge ocean, but the builder is threaded and not readable here). Effort 'small' is fine because this is a rule to obey, not a feature to build.

catalog.name: Cross-Server And Multi-World Travel
catalog.oneLine: RULED OUT for a zero-client-install mod — no vanilla server-to-client redirect mechanism exists anywhere in the protocol.
catalog.howItWorks:
I searched the client assembly for every connection-control surface and there is nothing to hook.

ZNet registers exactly three handshake RPCs on a peer: 'Disconnect', 'ServerHandshake' and 'ClientHandshake' (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:79819-79831). ZNet.RPC_Disconnect (:80165-80177) takes no parameters at all — it resolves the peer, sets m_connectionStatus to ErrorDisconnected if the peer was the server, and calls Disconnect. There is no destination, no address, no redirect payload.

The only ways a client ever points itself at a server are ZNet.SetServerHost(string remotePlayerId) / (ulong serverID) / (string host, int port, OnlineBackendType) (:81288-81302) and ZNet.SetServer (:81249). Every call site is in FejdStartup — the main menu — driven by the server list UI (ServerListEntryData, m_startup.SetServerToJoin at :65795, :65812, :66100) or by command-line parsing (:97925). None of them is reachable from any RPC, any ZDO, any global key, or any routed message. A dedicated server cannot make a connected vanilla client change which server it is talking to, full stop.

The character-data half is equally closed. Player.Save (:14091-14170) serialises inventory, recipes, uniques, trophies, foods, skills and customData into a package that PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData (:105706-105711) writes only to that client's own .fch file. ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles (:79653-79670) sounds like it collects profiles and does the exact opposite: it invokes the 'SavePlayerProfile' RPC so each client saves its OWN local file, and returns nothing. No player inventory, skill or recipe state ever crosses the wire in either direction. So even a scheme that somehow moved the client would have nothing to hand the destination server.

What IS possible, and is the honest ceiling: a multi-server OPERATOR-side illusion. Two servers sharing one Discord webhook and one exported state file can present a coherent 'network' — server A's portal tagged 'TO THE NORTHLANDS' is a Decoy Gate that, on transit detection, toasts the player the second server's join address (PlayerNotify, or ZNet.RemotePrint into an admin's console) and optionally kicks them with ZNet.instance.Kick. They then rejoin manually with the same character. That is a social mechanic with a portal-shaped skin, not travel.

A second honest variant: a single server hosting a second WORLD is impossible (ZNet holds one ZNet.World, ZoneSystem holds one m_locationInstances, WorldGenerator is a singleton seeded once in ZNet.ServerLoadWorld at :79273-79285). 'Another world' can only be faked by carving a far region of the same world and gating it, which is a Void Anchor plus a lock, not multi-world.
catalog.playerExperience: The best that can honestly be delivered: a player walks into the gate marked 'TO THE NORTHLANDS', gets a black screen, and arrives standing in front of a rune stone with a centre-screen message reading 'The Northlands lie beyond this world. Rejoin at northlands.example.com:2456 with this character.' Their map may also gain a permanent pin naming it. Then they alt-tab, open the server browser, and connect by hand. Anything smoother requires a client mod.
failureModes: There is no redirect RPC — this cannot be made to work without a client install, at any effort level
Character data never crosses the wire in either direction, so even with a redirect the destination server would receive a fresh character unless both servers share a save directory
ZNet.Kick / Ban are the only server-initiated disconnects and they carry no destination
Presenting an address in a toast invites phishing-shaped confusion if any third party can trigger it
A 'second world' on one server process is structurally impossible: one ZNet.World, one WorldGenerator, one ZoneSystem
citations: ZNet peer RPC registrations (Disconnect / ServerHandshake / ClientHandshake only) — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:79819-79831
ZNet.SetServerHost overloads, called only from FejdStartup — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:81288-81302, 81249; call sites :65795, :65812, :66100, :97925
Player.Save writes to the local profile only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14091-14170
ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles tells clients to save locally and returns nothing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79675
openQuestions: None that would change the verdict. The only thing worth confirming is that no platform-layer assembly (Splatform / PlayFab) exposes a server-initiated join redirect — those assemblies are outside this decompile set. IN-GAME: grep the shipped Splatform and PlayFab DLLs for any join or redirect entry point reachable from a server.
corrections: ZNet registers more than 'exactly three' peer RPCs: PeerInfo, Disconnect, SavePlayerProfile, RPC_RequestValidSimulationDistance, RPC_ValidatedSimulationDistance on every peer, plus Kicked, Error(int) and ClientHandshake on the client and ServerHandshake on the server (CLIENT :79815-79831), and PeerInfo then adds ServerSyncedPlayerData/PlayerList/HistoricalPlayerList/AdminList/RemotePrint (CLIENT :80100-80104). None carries a redirect payload, so the conclusion is unchanged.

catalog.name: Relocating The Base Instead Of The Player
catalog.oneLine: RULED OUT as a general mechanism — ZDO position writes are ownership-gated, portals are sector-frozen, and vanilla clients never re-apply a changed position to an existing instance.
catalog.howItWorks:
The idea is appealing and it fails at three independent layers.

Layer 1, the write. ZDO.InternalSetPosition (:73734-73745) updates m_position and calls SetSector, but only calls IncreaseDataRevision() `if (IsOwner())`. A position write on a ZDO the server does not own mutates the local copy and never goes on the wire. The server can claim ownership with SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()), but ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) runs every 2 s for every peer and hands ownership of any Persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area back to that peer. A base is by definition where players are. So the claim must be defended with a Harmony prefix on ZDO.SetOwner (the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern at Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313), on a global hot path, for every piece of a structure.

Layer 2, the client. This is the killer. ZNetScene.CreateObject (:81996-82022) applies zdo.GetPosition() ONLY at the Object.Instantiate call. ZNetView.Awake (:82567-82633) never touches transform.position afterwards — it applies scale only, and only when m_syncInitialScale is set. Unless a prefab carries a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition (buildings do not), a vanilla client simply ignores the new position. The mesh and the colliders stay exactly where they were created. The object only appears at its new coordinate after RemoveObjects destroys the instance (when it leaves the roughly 96-112 m active area, ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea :82298-82320) and CreateObjects re-instantiates it — at which point it POPS rather than moves.

Layer 3, portals specifically. ZDO.SetSector early-returns for any prefab in Game.PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757), so a portal's m_portalObjects key stays whatever it was when AddIfPortal last ran. Move a portal and ZDOMan.FindObjects (:77367-77382) keeps delivering it to peers near its OLD location and never to peers at its new one. Worse, ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO (:76976-76986) removes it using the RECOMPUTED current sector index, which no longer matches the dictionary key, so a later destruction leaks the dead ZDO in m_portalObjects forever and Game.ConnectPortals keeps processing a corpse. And AddIfPortal on the receiving CLIENT adds the ZDO under the NEW key without removing the old one (:77738-77748), duplicating it in every client's registry on every sector crossing.

Layer 4, persistence. A moved portal's new position is never saved: portals are excluded from normal chunks (:77572) and the ChunkPortal file is only written when DirtyPortalObjects is set, which a position write never does.

What remains genuinely possible is far narrower: destroy-and-recreate. Read a small structure's piece ZDOs, record prefab hash, local offset, rotation and the handful of ZDO fields that matter, destroy each (SetOwner then DestroyZDO), and CreateNewZDO the set at the new location. That works, but it loses WearNTear support relationships, terrain modifications, container contents unless explicitly copied, and creator attribution unless re-written — and it is a different feature from 'moving a base'.
catalog.playerExperience: Attempted naively, a player watches their portal apparently not move at all, then walks away and back and finds it has teleported across the valley with no animation, and their friend standing 200 m away still sees it in the old spot. That is the honest outcome and it is why this is ruled out rather than shipped with caveats.

corrections: Layer 4 overstates: a moved portal's new position is saved as soon as DirtyPortalObjects is set by any other event — every ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection on any portal (SERVER :73656-73676), every AddIfPortal (:77751), every portal destruction (:76986) — because the portal chunk writes a Clone() of every m_portalObjects entry with its live position (:77621-77631). The corrupted m_portalObjects keying is therefore repaired at the next reload, not permanent.

Layer 2 nuance: the pop happens only when the ZDO leaves the client's current sector list; a position change that stays inside the client's active area leaves the stale instance in place indefinitely (RemoveObjects earmarks by presence in the current lists, SERVER :82196-82227), and a portal never changes sector list at all (m_portalObjects key frozen), so a moved portal never pops on a client that stays in range.

Destroy-and-recreate caveat to add: ZDOMan.DestroyZDO of a client-owned piece requires the server to claim ownership first (same ReleaseNearbyZDOS race), and Piece creator/PlatformUserID attribution plus WearNTear support state must be re-written explicitly.

Layer 1 is bypassable but irrelevant: any subsequent zdo.Set(...) calls IncreaseDataRevision unconditionally (:73648-73653 pattern, :73832), so a non-owning server CAN put a new position on the wire after a data write; Layer 2 still makes the client ignore it, so the verdict stands.

Layer 3 is worse than a 'corpse': HandleDestroyedZDO calls ZDOPool.Release(zDO) (:76988) while the stale m_portalObjects entry keeps the reference; the pooled object can be re-Initialize()d as a different ZDO and Game.ConnectPortals will then treat that unrelated ZDO as a portal.

So a moved portal's position IS saved at the next save following any portal churn, and reload re-keys it correctly (AddIfPortal at load). [vanilla-reality:confirmed] All four layers verify. Layer 2: ZNetScene.CreateObject passes zdo.GetPosition() only to Object.Instantiate (:82013-82016); ZNetView.Awake (:82567-82633) touches only Type/Distant/scale/body; the client's ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (CLIENT :77217-77280) calls InternalSetPosition and Deserialize on an existing ZDO and nothing re-applies it to the instance; RemoveObjects/CreateObjects is the only path that moves a piece, as a destroy-and-recreate pop. Layer 3: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757); HandleDestroyedZDO removes by the recomputed GetSectorIndex() (:76974-76986); AddIfPortal on the client is invoked on every ZDO update (CLIENT :77273) and adds under the new key without removing the old (:77732-77752). Layer 4: portals excluded from normal chunks (:77572), ChunkPortal only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621), and a position write never sets it. Two additions strengthen the ruling-out rather than weaken it.

catalog.name: Portal Scaling Through s_scaleHash
catalog.oneLine: ZNetView applies a ZDO-stored localScale at instantiation when m_syncInitialScale is set — which would give server-set giant or tiny portals with proportionally scaled trigger volumes.
catalog.howItWorks:
ZNetView.Awake, in the branch taken when a client instantiates from a received ZDO (m_initZDO != null), contains this block at :82591-82606: `if (m_syncInitialScale) { Vector3 vec = m_zdo.GetVec3(ZDOVars.s_scaleHash, Vector3.zero); if (vec != Vector3.zero) transform.localScale = vec; else { float f = m_zdo.GetFloat(ZDOVars.s_scaleScalarHash, transform.localScale.x); if (!transform.localScale.x.Equals(f)) transform.localScale = new Vector3(f, f, f); } }`

ZDOVars.s_scaleHash is 'scale' (:78581) and s_scaleScalarHash is 'scaleScalar' (:78583). Both are plain ZDO writes with no ownership requirement.

If the portal prefab's ZNetView has m_syncInitialScale ticked, then `portalZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_scaleHash, new Vector3(3f, 3f, 3f))` produces a portal three times normal size on every vanilla client that instantiates it afterwards. Because Unity scales the whole transform hierarchy, the TeleportWorldTrigger child collider scales with it — so a giant portal genuinely has a larger walk-in volume, which is a real gameplay change and not just cosmetic. A 0.3 scale gives a portal you have to aim at.

The critical unknown is whether m_syncInitialScale is set on the portal prefab. It is a public bool on ZNetView (:82543), so LoadFields could in principle set it — but LoadFields runs at :82631, AFTER the scale block at :82591, and Unity's Instantiate copies the PREFAB's serialized value each time, not the previous instance's. So the ZDO cannot bootstrap this: either the prefab already has it or the mechanism is dead for portals. Almost certainly it is off for building pieces; it exists for things like trees and rocks that vary in size.

If it turns out to be off, there is no ZDO-only substitute. ZSyncTransform also reads s_scaleHash (:87814-87820) but that requires a ZSyncTransform on the prefab, which a building piece does not have.

Like LoadFields, this applies only at instantiation — a scale change reaches a player only after the portal is next created in their scene.
catalog.playerExperience: If it works: the spawn hub is a colossal arch you can ride a boat through, while a secret gate hidden in a cave is a knee-high shimmer you have to crouch to notice. Because the collider scales too, the big arch genuinely catches anyone who walks near it and the small one genuinely takes care to enter. Nobody can build one of these — the size is unmistakably an admin fixture. If it does not work, absolutely nothing happens and no error is logged, which is exactly why this needs an in-game check before any design leans on it.

A scaled portal's TeleportWorldTrigger volume scales too, which can make a large portal catch players who did not intend to travel

catalog.name: The Portal Census — Free World-Wide Reporting
catalog.oneLine: ZDOMan.GetPortalList is a complete, always-resident, zero-bookkeeping enumeration of every portal in the world, and vanilla already logs a parseable pairing audit trail.
catalog.howItWorks:
Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times. ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648-77656) flattens m_portalObjects into a fresh List<ZDO> covering the ENTIRE world regardless of player proximity — the server never unloads them (ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883; FlushClientObjects is client-only). ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643) returns the live dictionary for a zero-alloc hot path.

From each ZDO, readable with no ownership and no client: position (:73822), rotation (:73827), prefab hash (:73817), owner (:74608), ZDOVars.s_tag and s_tagauthor (:78617, :78619), GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) (:74002), ZDOVars.s_creator and s_creatorIndex (:78393, :78395), and ZDOVars.s_health (:78443). s_creatorIndex resolves through ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396) to a socket-verified PlatformUserID, and the same value appears as s_playerID on that player's live character ZDO — so the census is joinable to accounts, offline, across restarts.

Derived reports that need no extra bookkeeping at all:
- Orphan detection. Game.ConnectPortals permanently strands exactly one member of any tag group of odd size, because the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself (:100607-100621 plus FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679). A census flags every tag with an odd count.
- Dangling links: connection non-None but GetZDO(target) null.
- Near-miss tags: tag comparison is bare C# string inequality (:100601, :100669) — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, with an empty-string default. 'Base', 'base' and 'Base ' are three separate networks, and every untagged portal in the world is one giant group. Flagging tags that differ only by case or trailing whitespace catches a real, common, invisible griefing and confusion vector.
- Per-player counts by s_creator, which is exactly what a server-enforced cap needs (see the SpawnGovernor hook pattern).
- Density and reach: portals per biome via WorldGenerator.GetBiome (:151725), and distance to the nearest icon-flagged location via ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons (:115450-115467).

Vanilla already writes a parseable audit trail with zero patching: ZLog.Log('Connected portals ' + a + ' <-> ' + b) per pair and ZLog.Log('[ Connected N portals ]') per tick (:100619, :100625), plus 'ConnectPortals => Connected N portals.' at load (:77891). ZDO.ToString returns m_uid.ToString() in userID:ID form.

Delivery: TortalPortal's PortalExport (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32-75) is already a pure server-side, IsServer-gated coroutine that counts portals per s_creator and writes an atomic JSON file; Wonderland's DiscordWebhook (Subsystems/DiscordNotify/DiscordWebhook.cs:27) and Heartbeat (Core/Heartbeat.cs:21) are the other two halves. All three are lift-and-rename.
catalog.playerExperience: Admin-facing, but it surfaces to players as competence. The Discord channel gets a nightly line: '412 portals, 6 orphaned tags, 3 near-duplicate tags (Base / base / Base ), 14 dangling links repaired'. When a player complains their gate leads somewhere random, the admin can answer in ten seconds with the actual tag group and the actual orphan. And a web dashboard can show every public gate on a map without any client ever sending anything.

catalog.id: wildcard:The Portal Census — Free World-Wide Reporting
corrections: Framing 'Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times' is wrong: a dedicated server holds EVERY ZDO in m_objectsByID for the whole session (no eviction path exists server-side). Portals are only special in being indexed separately — AddIfPortal calls RemoveFromSector (:77750) so they live in m_portalObjects instead of the sector arrays.

s_creator and s_creatorIndex are CLIENT-written: Piece.SetCreator(long, PlatformUserID) (:136415-136424) writes GetPlayerID() (the client's own character profile ID, not socket-verified) and a FindIndex computed against the client's mirrored copy of m_playerHistory (-1 if not found). The list contents are server-generated, but the index into it is client-asserted; 'socket-verified' holds only for honest vanilla clients. Same for s_tagauthor, which is LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString() sent by the client (:143582).
Piece.SetCreator has a two-argument signature (long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID), not one.
Reconcile predicate line is :100600, not :100601 (off by one; immaterial).

Log lines go through ZLog.Log → UnityEngine.Debug.Log; on a dedicated server they land in the console/log file — parseable but unstructured; the load-time ConvertPortals/ConnectPortals lines use UnityEngine.Debug.Log directly (:77814, :77890).

'Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times' is false. ZDOMan.LoadChunks loads EVERY chunk file into m_objectsByID (:76454-76511) and the server never unloads any ZDO; portals are merely indexed separately (m_portalObjects) and saved in ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal. The census is free because the whole world is resident, not because portals are special.

s_creatorIndex is not server-derived or socket-verified. It is written by the placing CLIENT in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424, gated on m_nview.IsOwner(), called from Player.PlacePiece :12516) as FindIndex into the client's mirror of m_playerHistory (refilled by RPC_HistoricalPlayerList :81419-81433) using the client's self-reported LocalUser.PlatformUserID. It is -1 when unresolved. A vanilla client writes it faithfully; a modded client can write any index. The server list itself is authoritative and persisted, so the join is stable across restarts for vanilla-written values only.

s_creator is the character's profile m_playerID (Player.GetPlayerID → s_playerID :10133/:10144), i.e. per-CHARACTER, not per-account. Per-player counts keyed on s_creator are bypassed by rolling a new character; per-account needs s_creatorIndex with the caveat above.

The load-time 'ConnectPortals => Connected N portals.' line (:77891) is UnityEngine.Debug.Log from ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (hash-based reconnect of saved ZDOConnectionHashData, :77850-77894), not Game.ConnectPortals. Game.ConnectPortals is additionally invoked once at the end of LoadChunks (:76518).

GetPortalList entries can include ZDOs whose destroy is queued but not yet applied (DestroyZDO only appends to m_destroySendList :76929-76935; removal happens in HandleDestroyedZDO on the next ZDOMan.Update SendDestroyed :76820). Filter with IsValid as PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals does.

Tag changes are not observable as events server-side: RPC_SetTag is ZDO-targeted and the dedicated server's HandleRoutedRPC needs ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83645-83660), which is null for portals; and an owning client sends no packet at all (InvokeRoutedRPC :83583-83594). The census must be polled ZDO state, which is what the option describes — but 'audit trail' covers pairing only, not retags.
evidence: ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal chunk + all chunks resident — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76454-76518
Piece.SetCreator client-side index write — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136415-136424; Player.PlacePiece call :12516

ZDOMan.GetPortals()/GetPortalList() (:77643-77656) flatten m_portalObjects (:76039), which AddIfPortal (:77732-77752) populates on load (:76480, :76579, :76598) and on every RPC_ZDOData arrival (:77132), and HandleDestroyedZDO prunes (:76980-76987). Nothing on the server ever evicts ZDOs: ReleaseZDOS/ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76872-76924) only call SetOwner, and FlushClientObjects (:76864) is gated on !IsServer() in ShutDown (:76180-76183). Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100629) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) use bare C# string != on GetString(s_tag) (:100600, :100669) — ordinal, case- and whitespace-sensitive, default "" — and TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143587-143598) stores the tag verbatim with no trim, so near-miss tags are real. GetLocationIcons (:115450) and WorldGenerator.GetBiome (:151725) are pure server-side math. PortalExport.cs:32-75 is a real IsServer-gated coroutine.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The mechanism holds: ZDOMan.GetPortals()/GetPortalList() (:77643-77656) flatten m_portalObjects, which is populated from the ChunkPortal save file at LoadChunks (:76476-76481), from network arrival in RPC_ZDOData via AddIfPortal after every Deserialize (:77131-77132, :77732-77752), and pruned only in HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980-76987). ReleaseZDOS/ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76872-76924) only call SetOwner; nothing on the server path ever removes a ZDO for distance. Game.ConnectPortals logs exactly as claimed (:100619, :100625), tag comparison is bare string != (:100601, :100669), FindRandomUnconnectedPortal picks randomly among same-tag unconnected portals (:100664-100679) so an odd tag group leaves one member unpaired while the pair keeps re-confirming (:100597-100606 only clears when target null/tag mismatch/target None). ZDO.ToString → m_uid.ToString() (:72467) → 'userID:ID' (:75883). GetLocationIcons has an IsServer branch reading m_locationInstances directly (:115450-115461). m_playerHistory is persisted in world meta (:112587-112590, :112709). PortalExport.cs is IsServer-gated (line 36) and reads GetPortalList via PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals (PlacementPatch.cs:203). Several framing claims are wrong or overstated, listed under corrections. The identity-joining claim in particular is weaker than stated because s_creatorIndex is client-written.

catalog.name: Server-Enforced Portal Caps Via The ZDO Arrival Hook
catalog.oneLine: The only server-side hook that sees a client-placed object appear is the ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO plus ZDO.Deserialize pair — which makes a genuinely unbypassable per-player portal cap possible for the first time.
catalog.howItWorks:
Placement itself is unreachable server-side: Player.PlacePiece and TryPlacePiece need a Player instance the server never has, and ZNetScene.Instantiate never runs for a client-placed piece because the CLIENT instantiates and only the ZDO crosses the wire. PortalLock (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114) patched exactly those and combined them with an `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return true;` guard, which means it could never fire once. That is the canonical failure and it is why this option exists.

The working hook is Wonderland's SpawnGovernor pair (Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58, :70), verified against the decompile:

(1) A postfix on the PRIVATE `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684-76692). On the network-receive path the caller is the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77132) and prefabHashIn is 0, so `zDO.GetPrefab()` is consulted — which for a freshly pooled ZDO is -1. The postfix therefore can only REMEMBER the ZDOID; it cannot yet classify anything. SpawnGovernor's own header records that a CreateNewZDO-only postfix was a shipped bug for exactly this reason.

(2) A postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` — the first moment the real prefab hash exists. Here: if the ZDOID is in the remembered set and `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`, read `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L)`, count that player's existing portals by walking `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` and comparing s_creator, and if the count exceeds the configured cap do `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` plus a PlayerNotify toast naming the cap.

DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) queues into m_destroySendList and SendDestroyed broadcasts the routed DestroyZDO RPC to every peer; the placing client's ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the GameObject in front of them. The ZDOID also enters m_deadZDOs (:76997), so a replayed packet cannot resurrect it (:77133-77137).

This is STRICTLY STRONGER than the full client-side TortalPortal mod, whose cap lives in a prefix on Player.TryPlacePiece (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:89) and is therefore trivially bypassed by an unmodded client — its own LogRefusal comment records the effective cap 'wandered between values nobody had deliberately set' before a locking config entry existed. It is the one place the server-only mod beats the full one outright.

Admin bypass is ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) (:81811) — NOT Player.IsAdmin, which needs a Player instance.
catalog.playerExperience: A player with six portals already tries to place a seventh. It goes down normally — build effects, materials consumed — and then, within a fraction of a second, it vanishes. A centre-screen message reads 'Portal limit reached (6 of 6). Remove one first.' Because the server destroyed the ZDO rather than blocking the placement, the client-side illusion is a brief flicker rather than a clean refusal, which is the visible cost of the mechanism. Unlike every client-side cap, there is no config file a player can edit and no build of the game that ignores it.
failureModes: The placing client already instantiated the piece and consumed materials; the server-side destroy is a flicker, and whether materials are refunded is an in-game unknown
A postfix on CreateNewZDO ALONE always sees GetPrefab() == 0 or -1 and can never classify — both hooks are mandatory
ZDO.Deserialize is a global hot path; the check must fail fast on the remembered-ZDOID set before touching anything else
s_creator is 0 for anything placed before the field existed or by an admin spawn — treat 0 as uncapped or as a separate bucket deliberately
Counting by walking GetPortalList() on every arrival is O(all portals); cache a per-player tally and invalidate on ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (:76033)
A Piece/WearNTear-bearing object destroyed mid-arrival may behave differently from the creatures SpawnGovernor was built for; SpawnGovernor has no portal-specific live test
A modded client can still spam RPC_ZDOData to recreate; the cap is enforced on arrival, so it holds, but it becomes a packet-rate problem
prerequisites: The Portal Census (for the per-player tally)
openQuestions: Does destroying a client-created portal ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix desync the placing client, and are the build materials refunded, consumed, or duplicated? IN-GAME: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe the ghost, the inventory, and the client log.
Is the CreateNewZDO overload signature stable enough for AccessTools to bind across 1.0.7 to 1.0.12? MIGRATE-1.0.md reports no signature changes. IN-GAME: verify the patch applies on 1.0.12.
catalog.id: wildcard:Server-Enforced Portal Caps Via The ZDO Arrival Hook
corrections: Ordering detail: the ZDO.Deserialize postfix runs BEFORE AddIfPortal (:77131 vs :77132), so the new portal is NOT yet in GetPortalList() when counted. The test must be existingCount >= cap, not > cap.

The cap key s_creator is a client-written long (Piece.SetCreator writes GetPlayerID(), the client's profile ID). Unbypassable for vanilla clients; a modified client can write any creator value. A stronger key is the arriving packet's owner (ownerInternal = the peer's session UID, matched via ZNet.instance.GetPeer(long) :80492) — the server already has it in scope in RPC_ZDOData and it is the identity the socket authenticated.

Admin bypass needs a peer lookup: the Deserialize postfix has no ZRpc; resolve ZNet.instance.GetPeer(zdo.GetOwner()) then IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) (:81811-81814). Owner at that moment is the placing client's UID because RPC_ZDOData just called SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal) (:77127).

Player-visible cost is slightly larger than a 'flicker': the client's WearNTear/Piece placement effects and material consumption have already happened, and the TeleportWorld component ran InvokeRepeating before destruction; no refund is possible from the server side.
Piece.SetCreator signature is (long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID); citation :136415-136424 is otherwise correct.

Ordering: the ZDO.Deserialize postfix runs BEFORE RPC_ZDOData's AddIfPortal (:77132), so the arriving portal is not yet in GetPortalList when counted — the test must be 'existing >= cap', not '> cap'. After the postfix returns, AddIfPortal files it in m_portalObjects until the next ZDOMan.Update applies the destroy; if Game.ConnectPortals's 5 s tick lands in that window the portal can be staged for pairing, and the partner's dangling link is cleared on the following tick (:100597-100606). Cosmetic, but real.
A simpler single hook exists: a postfix on the private ZDOMan.AddIfPortal(ZDO,int) (:77732) fires for every portal arrival with the prefab known; the remembered-set approach is still valid.

The cap keys on s_creator = character profile ID (Player.GetPlayerID → s_playerID :10133/:10144). A vanilla player bypasses it by creating a new character. Per-account needs s_creatorIndex → ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which is client-written (Piece.SetCreator :136415-136424) and spoofable by a modded client; for the admin-bypass and for a trustworthy identity, resolve the sender from the RPC_ZDOData ZRpc (FindPeer :76800-76810) rather than the packet's owner field (:77128, untrusted).

Materials are consumed client-side in Player.PlacePiece with no refund path: every capped attempt costs the player the portal's materials. The option mentions the flicker but should state the material loss as the enforcement cost.
Within one ZDOMan.Update, SendZDOToPeers2 runs before SendDestroyed (:76818-76820), so the rejected ZDO can be relayed once to other nearby peers before the DestroyZDO RPC follows. Cosmetic.

Owner of a rejected ZDO must also not be a server-side ZNetScene instance concern: the dedicated server's ZNetScene subscribes to m_onZDODestroyed (:81953) but holds no portal instance, so OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) is a no-op server-side; the client-side counterpart destroys the GameObject.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Read the whole path. RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77139): unknown ZDOID → CreateNewZDO(zDOID, vector) with prefabHashIn defaulting to 0 (:76684) → zDO.GetPrefab() is -1 because ZDOPool.Release→ZDO.Reset sets Valid=false whose setter writes m_prefab=-1 (:73476, :73536-73549) — so the CreateNewZDO postfix indeed cannot classify. Then SetOwnerInternal(client), InternalSetPosition, zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) which reads m_prefab (:74212) and all keys, then AddIfPortal (:77132). Vanilla itself uses exactly the proposed destroy idiom two lines later for dead ZDOs: zDO.SetOwner(m_sessionID); DestroyZDO(zDO) (:77133-77137). DestroyZDO requires IsOwner (:76929-76935); SendDestroyed broadcasts routed 'DestroyZDO' to target 0 (:76937-76951), which the server also handles locally; HandleDestroyedZDO fires m_onZDODestroyed, removes from m_portalObjects and m_objectsByID, and records m_deadZDOs on the server (:76963-77000) — m_deadZDOs is never pruned (only Clear on load :76524/:76659), so a late client update for that ZDOID is re-destroyed (:77133-77137). Client side, ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed destroys the GameObject (:82186-82194). s_creator is present in the FIRST packet: client PlacePiece calls SetCreator synchronously right after Instantiate (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:12518) inside one Update call, before any ZDOMan send. This is a 'should this OBJECT exist' rule, which the server owns — server-enforced is the correct mark. SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70 implements precisely this pair.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The hook chain is real and the enforcement claim is honest, because the rule is about world state ('may this ZDO exist'), not about a player's act. RPC_ZDOData for an unknown ZDOID calls the private CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int) with prefabHashIn defaulted to 0 (:77121, :76684-76692); ZDOPool.Release→Reset sets Valid=false → m_prefab=-1 (:73536-73550, :73468-73478), so GetPrefab() is -1 at that point and AddIfPortal does nothing; m_prefab is only assigned in ZDO.Deserialize (:74206-74212). RPC_ZDOData then SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal) from the packet, Deserialize, then AddIfPortal (:77128-77132). SetOwner(sessionID)+DestroyZDO works because DestroyZDO only checks IsOwner (:76929-76935); SendDestroyed runs every ZDOMan.Update (:76820) and InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,...) dispatches HandleRoutedRPC locally before RouteRPC (:83583-83594), so the server's own HandleDestroyedZDO removes it and records it in m_deadZDOs (:76995-76998). m_deadZDOs is never pruned (only cleared at load :76524, :76659), and any re-arrival of that ZDOID is auto-destroyed (:77133-77137), so even a modded client that ignores the DestroyZDO RPC cannot make the server keep it. s_creator is written synchronously in Player.PlacePiece (:12516 → Piece.SetCreator :136415-136424) before the first ZDO send, so it is present at first Deserialize. Wonderland SpawnGovernor implements exactly this two-hook shape (SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70) and its header documents the CreateNewZDO-only bug. TortalPortal's cap is a Player.TryPlacePiece prefix (PlacementPatch.cs:89) — client-only. PortalLock's PlacementPatches guard is at line 22. ZNet.IsAdmin(string) exists (:81811). Effort medium is plausible.

catalog.name: Cross-Mod Integration Surface
catalog.oneLine: The exact contention points a portal mod shares with other server-only mods, and the hooks it should expose so they can cooperate.
catalog.howItWorks:
Five shared surfaces, each a real collision risk.

(1) ZDO.SetOwner prefixes. Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine already installs an unconditional prefix on ZDO.SetOwner to block passive ownership handover (Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313). A portal mod that does the same is stacking prefixes on a global hot path touched by ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS for every peer every 2 s. Rule: fail fast on prefab hash first, and never block uid == 0 or uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID() — those are release and claim.

(2) Game.ConnectPortals. It is public (:100589), it runs every 5 s from an IsServer-gated coroutine (:100074, :100580), and any mod that prefixes it to return false disables pairing for everyone. The politer target is a postfix on the private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) overwriting __result, which leaves vanilla's two-phase commit and logging intact and composes far better with a second mod.

(3) Game.PortalPrefabHash. It is a mutable List<int> behind a private setter (:100021) with no ownership model; two mods adding and removing entries will corrupt each other's assumptions about where ZDOs are filed and saved.

(4) ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC / RouteRPC / RPC_RoutedRPC. These are the universal server-side observation and veto points (:83597, :83632, :83645). Everything wanting to see client traffic patches them. A portal mod watching for the RPC_SetTag hash must save and restore the ZPackage read position (pkg.GetPos / SetPos) or it breaks vanilla routing and every other mod's read.

(5) ZDO key namespace. Mod-private keys are plain int hashes of arbitrary strings, so prefix everything ('tpl_route', 'tpl_lock') and never reuse anything in ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693) — that set is global and strips the key from the save for every ZDO in the world.

What to EXPOSE. The cheapest useful integration is a public static registry: a delegate other mods can register to veto or redirect a pairing decision, a delegate fired on detected transit, and a read-only accessor for the mod's managed-network view. A non-Harmony observation hook already exists for the destruction side: ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> field (:76033) invoked from HandleDestroyedZDO (:76975-76978) before the ZDO leaves m_objectsByID, so the ZDO is still readable in the callback — combine onto it rather than patching.

On the output side, the mod should also be a good citizen of the ecosystem's existing channels: PlayerNotify toasts, DiscordWebhook, AuditLog.Flag, and the portals.json export shape TortalPortal already writes.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible. What operators experience is that installing a portal mod alongside a world-governance mod, a storage mod and a security mod does not silently break any of them — portal transits stop tripping the speed-cheat detector, ownership tug-of-war between two mods does not strand ZDOs, and the Discord channel carries one coherent stream rather than four competing ones.
failureModes: Two unconditional ZDO.SetOwner prefixes on a global hot path compound into a measurable per-tick cost with tens of peers
A Game.ConnectPortals prefix returning false silently disables pairing for every other mod and for vanilla
Two mods mutating Game.PortalPrefabHash corrupt each other's filing and save assumptions with no error
A RPC_RoutedRPC prefix that consumes the ZPackage without restoring GetPos breaks every downstream reader including vanilla
Reusing a ZDOVars session hash strips that key from the save for every ZDO in the world

PositionWatch-style security mods will flag portal transits at roughly 110 m/s over a 3 s sample unless the portal mod's detection is shared or the security mod's IsPortalTransit suppression is present
openQuestions: What is the measured per-tick cost of two stacked ZDO.SetOwner prefixes with 20 peers and a large world? IN-GAME: profile ZDOMan.Update with and without.
Does HarmonyX ordering between two Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfixes behave predictably without explicit priority? IN-GAME: install two test postfixes and observe.
corrections: (1) A ZDO.SetOwner prefix does NOT cover the client-asserted ownership path: RPC_ZDOData applies incoming owners via SetOwnerInternal (:77116, :77127), which bypasses SetOwner entirely. Such a prefix only blocks server-local calls (ReleaseNearbyZDOS, Game.SetConnection/RPC_SetConnection, ConvertPortals). Say so, or a second mod will assume it is a full ownership fence.

(2) Redirecting via a FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix only composes when the substituted target shares the tag: the reconcile pass on the next tick tears down any pair whose target tag differs (:100600), so cross-tag redirects last at most one 5 s cycle after the ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-write. A cross-tag redirect needs the reconcile predicate patched too.

(4) On a dedicated server a ZDO-targeted routed RPC (RPC_SetTag) is dropped at HandleRoutedRPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null with no GameObject (:83656-83664); observation must be a prefix on HandleRoutedRPC or RPC_RoutedRPC, and it never sees a retag issued by the ZDO owner (no packet on the wire, per InvokeRoutedRPC's local short-circuit :83586-83591).
(5) ZDOExtraData.AddSessionHash(int) is public (:74827-74830) — a mod could ALSO add session-only keys; the warning should cover both the static list and that API.

The RPC_SetTag observation channel is narrower than stated. On a dedicated server HandleRoutedRPC never dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null for portals (:83645-83660), and RPC_RoutedRPC only calls HandleRoutedRPC when target == server or 0 (:83632-83643) — RPC_SetTag targets the portal owner. The only server-side sighting is a prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC/RouteRPC on the relay path, and it sees nothing when the retagging client owns the portal (InvokeRoutedRPC :83583-83594 skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id). Wonderland's HandleRoutedRPC prefix works only because RPC_RequestOwn targets a server-owned ZDO.

ZPackage read-position: RouteRPC relays via RoutedRPCData.Serialize → ZPackage.Write(ZPackage) which uses GetArray() (whole buffer, :83087-83092, :83418-83423) and is immune to read position. Position restore matters only for local dispatch (HandleRoutedRPC → RoutedMethod.Invoke reads m_parameters from its current pos). The advice stands; the stated reason ('breaks vanilla routing') is only true for the local-dispatch half.
Add ZDOHelper.s_stripOldData to the key blacklist: ZDOExtraData.Init also strips 256 'room{i}_seed' hashes on load (:74817-74820).

Mutating PortalPrefabHash after LoadChunks does not re-file existing ZDOs: LoadChunks files portals from the ChunkPortal file and everything else via InitialAddToSector (:76476-76481, :76505-76508); a hash added at runtime leaves already-loaded ZDOs of that prefab out of m_portalObjects until they are re-received. This strengthens the option's warning.
evidence: ZDO.SetOwner vs SetOwnerInternal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74627-74640; RPC_ZDOData uses SetOwnerInternal :77116, :77127

Wonderland's patches are at the cited lines (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-327, PositionWatch.cs:148). Two mechanics are misdescribed, corrected below.

catalog.name: The Ashlands Stone Portal
catalog.oneLine: There is no code difference between portal variants anywhere in the assembly — every behavioural difference is Inspector data on the prefab, and none of it is network-reachable.
catalog.howItWorks:
I searched both assemblies. There is exactly ONE TeleportWorld class and it is byte-identical between the server and client decompiles (server :143402-143682 versus client :144142-144422; a diff of the two regions is empty). There is no subclass, no variant branch, no prefab-name test, no per-prefab code path of any kind. No portal prefab name string (portal_wood, portal_stone, portal_blackmarble) appears anywhere in either decompile — the only portal literals are localization keys ($piece_portal, $piece_portal_tag, $piece_portal_connected, $piece_portal_unconnected, $piece_portal_censored_warning, $piece_portal_settag, $msg_portal_blocked).

Everything that could distinguish an Ashlands stone portal from a wood one lives in serialized Inspector fields: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems (:143429), m_exitDistance (:143413), m_activationRange (:143411), m_hoverOffset (:143431), the two Colors (:143418, :143421), the EffectFade and EffectList references (:143423, :143427), plus whatever WearNTear.m_health, WearNTear.m_ashDamageImmune and Piece values the prefab carries.

The widely believed 'the Ashlands stone portal allows all items' would, if true, be m_allowAllItems = true on that prefab. Nothing in code confirms or denies it and nothing in code can change it over the wire — the field is never read from or written to a ZDO by TeleportWorld and never appears in any RPC. A Harmony write to it on the server mutates a prefab copy no client will ever read, because the server never instantiates a portal.

The ONE route that does exist is ZNetView.LoadFields (see Field Injection), which is a generic ZNetView mechanism and completely indifferent to which portal prefab it is applied to. So the honest statement is: a server-only mod cannot make portal_stone behave differently from portal_wood by virtue of it being portal_stone, but it CAN give any individual portal ZDO of either prefab an overridden m_allowAllItems.

The only correct handling of prefab variety is to never hard-code the list: read Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:100021) and Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs (:99828) at runtime, which also picks up modded portal pieces for free. TortalPortal hard-codes portal_wood, portal_stone and portal_blackmarble (PlacementPatch.cs:217-219, ScatterCommand.cs:158) purely as a fallback.
catalog.playerExperience: No player-visible feature. The practical consequence is a documentation one: an operator who expects the mod to 'turn on ore transport for stone portals only' must be told that the mod can turn it on for INDIVIDUAL portals (via field injection) or for the whole world (via GlobalKeys.TeleportAll), but never for a prefab class — and that GlobalKeys.TeleportAll does not mean everything either, because Inventory.IsTeleportable rejects any item with m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000 BEFORE it ever consults the key.
failureModes: All per-prefab differences are Inspector data with zero network reachability
Harmony-writing m_allowAllItems on the server mutates a prefab copy that no client ever reads, because the server instantiates no portals
Hard-coding prefab names misses modded portal pieces and breaks on a game update
GlobalKeys.TeleportAll cannot lift the m_toolTier >= 1000 rejection (Inventory.IsTeleportable :68862-68868)

IN-GAME: on a client, read ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(name).GetComponent<TeleportWorld>().m_allowAllItems for each entry of Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs.

catalog.name: The Minimal Optional Client Mod — Where The Ceiling Actually Sits
catalog.oneLine: A few hundred lines of optional client code removes almost every Ruled Out item at once, and the single cheapest thing it can buy is a moment-of-transit hook.
catalog.howItWorks:
Every hard ceiling in this report traces to one of four root causes, and a small optional client plugin dissolves three of them.

ROOT 1 — no moment-of-transit hook. TeleportWorld.Teleport has exactly one caller, TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681), gated on Player.m_localPlayer. A client-side Harmony PREFIX on TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player) is about 15 lines and is the single highest-leverage thing an optional client mod can add: it fires exactly once, at the exact instant, with the portal instance and the Player in scope. From there the client can InvokeRoutedRPC a request to the server and return false to suspend the transit while the server decides. That one hook alone buys: per-transit server authorization, a real destination-picker UI, per-player routing, tolls charged at the moment of use, and accurate transit logging — replacing the 0.2-0.4 s position-polling approximation entirely.

ROOT 2 — the server cannot see inventory. Player.Save writes only to the local .fch (:14091-14170) and ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles collects nothing (:79653-79675). A client plugin can serialise an inventory summary into ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData (the arbitrary string dictionary in RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData, :80395-80410) or send it in the transit-request RPC. That buys server-side ore enforcement, tolls, and 'you may not carry this here' rules.

ROOT 3 — no UI. All of TortalPortal's PortalUIManager, LivePreview, PortalMapPins and Favorites are structurally unreachable server-side. A client plugin re-enables them, and ServerSync's CustomSyncedValue<T> (already vendored identically in both Wonderland/Shared/ServerSync.cs:91 and TortalPortal/ServerSync.cs) is the ready-made delivery channel for the server's portal index over the login handshake — a channel a vanilla client has no handler for and will never receive.

ROOT 4 — no cross-server redirect. A client plugin CAN call ZNet.SetServerHost and reconnect (:81288-81302), which is the only way multi-server travel is ever happening. Character data still does not transfer; that requires the two servers to share a save directory or an out-of-band profile sync.

Design shape for 'optional': the server ships a ServerSync VersionCheck that does NOT enforce (Wonderland/Shared/ServerSync.cs:1117), and gates the enhanced path on whether the peer announced the plugin. Vanilla clients keep the degraded ZDO-only experience described in every other option here; modded clients get the full one. TortalPortal's SectorSubscription (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/SectorSubscription.cs:106) is worth remembering as the other half — a postfix on the private ZDOMan.CreateSyncList appends arbitrary sectors to a specific peer's sync packet, which is the only way to put portal data in front of a client who is not standing next to a portal.

Cost estimate: the transit prefix plus a request/response RPC pair plus a version handshake is roughly 200-300 lines. Everything beyond that is UI polish.
catalog.playerExperience: A vanilla player sees the full server-only feature set: managed networks, indestructible admin gates, rotating hubs, tag signage, event portals, map pins. A player who installs the optional 200-line plugin additionally gets: a destination list when they walk into a hub instead of a coin-flip; a message that actually explains why a gate refused them; a toll prompt; and their ore checked against server rules rather than client ones. Crucially the two can stand at the same portal at the same time and both have a working, coherent experience — the modded one is just better informed.
failureModes: A client prefix on TeleportWorld.Teleport that suspends the transit must handle the server never replying, or the player is stuck at a dead gate
Any inventory data the client reports is client-authored and therefore spoofable by a hostile client — it buys convenience and honesty, not security
Once a feature depends on the client plugin, version skew becomes a real support burden; use ServerSync VersionCheck in non-enforcing mode
CustomSyncedValue delivery happens at the login handshake, so a plugin installed mid-session sees nothing until relog
Cross-server travel via SetServerHost still cannot move character data; the two servers must share a save directory or an external profile sync
A ZDOMan.CreateSyncList postfix that streams extra sectors competes with the peer's own negotiated simulation distance and the 10240-byte send queue cap (:77010-77016)

corrections: ROOT 2 cadence: the client pushes m_serverSyncedPlayerData only every 2 s (m_periodicSendTimer >= 2f, :80340-80356), so an inventory summary carried there is up to 2 s stale at the moment of transit; the transit-request RPC path is the one that gives an exact snapshot.

ROOT 1 mechanics: OnTriggerEnter fires once per entry; a prefix that returns false to 'suspend' must later resume by calling player.TeleportTo / TeleportWorld.Teleport itself — the trigger will not re-fire until the player leaves and re-enters the collider.

ROOT 4 overstates: SetServerHost only writes static fields (m_serverHost/m_serverSteamID/m_onlineBackend, :81288-81308); an actual redirect additionally needs Game.instance.Logout and the FejdStartup join/connect flow (:98979-99019 call sites), i.e. a full disconnect/reconnect cycle through the menu, not an in-session hop.

Player.Save citation :14091-14170 is Player.Save(ZPackage) (character serialization into the profile package); the .fch write itself is PlayerProfile.Save. The conclusion (server never receives inventory) is unaffected — inventory is not in the player ZDO.

Returning false from a Teleport prefix does not 'suspend' the transit — OnTriggerEnter fires once per trigger entry (:143673-143681). After the server replies, the client plugin must itself resume the transit (re-invoke Teleport or call Player.TeleportTo :143543-143547), otherwise the player must step out of the 5 m trigger and back in.
If the plugin resumes via player.TeleportTo directly instead of re-entering Teleport, it must replicate the NoPortals / NoBossPortals / IsTeleportable checks (:143523-143536) itself.

ZNet.SetServerHost is not a live reconnect: it only sets static join parameters consumed by FejdStartup's join flow (client :98979-98984). Cross-server travel requires a Game logout back to the main menu and a fresh JoinServer, i.e. a full loading screen, not a seamless hop.

Inventory via m_serverSyncedPlayerData is a periodic whole-dictionary snapshot (RPC clears and refills it each time, :80402-80408) and so is stale by up to one peer-info interval; ore enforcement must ride the transit-request RPC, which the option also proposes — prefer that channel exclusively for the decision.
