catalog.name: The Dial — portal tag as a command line
catalog.oneLine: The player retags a portal with a 10-char opcode string (`>Haldor`, `#Base`, `?`); the server reads it out of the ZDO, rewrites the connection, and echoes a canonical answer back into the same tag in ~250 ms.
catalog.howItWorks:
OBSERVATION — do NOT hook RPC_SetTag. `TeleportWorld.SetText` calls `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId)` (:143583) = `InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …)` (ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855). `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) gives every persistent ZDO in a peer's ~96 m active area to that peer within 2 s, so the retagging player owns the portal, `targetPeerID == m_id`, and `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and SKIPS `RouteRPC` (:83587-83594). Zero packets — an RPC prefix sees nothing. The change instead arrives as ordinary ZDO data: client `ZDO.Set(s_tag,…)` bumps DataRevision, `ZDOMan.ClientChanged` queues it (:77727), flush every 0.05 s (:76843), server `RPC_ZDOData` → `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74225). HOOK = Harmony postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)`, filter `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(GetPrefab())` (:100021), diff `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (:78617). Backstop: poll `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648) at 0.25 s — world-global, always resident.

GRAMMAR, char 0 = opcode, chars 1-9 = operand: `>NAME`/`>7` dial · `#NAME` name this portal · `-` unlink · `?` help+directory · `*NAME` join public network · `@spawn`/`@haldor` world target · `!` lock. ASCII only; `>` is safe because `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459) only strips a `<…>` pair.

ACTION: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627/:77362) → `zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destId)` (:73656) → `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, echo)` → `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702, mandatory — a tag-only write never dirties the portal chunk and is lost at save) → `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) → PRE-WARM `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId)` (:77714) so `TargetFound()` (:143640) succeeds on the first walk-through instead of silently failing while `RequestZDO` round-trips.

PAIRING: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears down any link whose two ends' `s_tag` differ (:100601) every 5 s, so per-portal display tags require prefixing it out and re-implementing both passes for unmanaged portals.

LATENCY: 0.05 s client flush + ½RTT → Deserialize postfix (synchronous) → write + ForceSendZDO → 0.05 s server flush + ½RTT → `GetHoverText` (:143453) reads the ZDO live every frame. ≈1 RTT + ≤100 ms; ~160 ms on a 60 ms server.
catalog.playerExperience:
You walk to a portal. Hover reads `Teleport Portal tag:"?help" [unconnected]`. You press E — the stock vanilla rename box, topic `Portal tag`. Type `?`, Enter. Within a quarter second six toasts stack in the corner: `>name dial`, `#name name this portal`, `- unlink · ! lock · @ world`.

Press E again, type `#Base`, Enter. The hover instantly reads `"#Base"`; toast: `Named: Base. 4 portals on this server.` You run 600 m to your mine, press E there, type `>Base`, Enter. Before you let go of the key the hover flips to `">Base"`, the blue connect effect fires (`UpdatePortal` :143499), and a toast reads `Dialed → Base (Meadows, 612m)`. You step through — it works first try, no dead transit, because the destination ZDO was force-sent in the same breath.

Mistype `>Bsae`: 200 ms later the hover reads `"?Bsae"` and a toast says `No portal named Bsae. Did you mean: Base, Bog?` The old link is untouched. Locked portal: hover flicks to `"!Vault"`, toast `Vault is locked by Bjorn.`

Total human time per command: press E, type ≤10 characters, Enter, read. About four seconds.
failureModes: The echo MUST be ≤10 chars. `TextInput.Show` sets `characterLimit = 10` then assigns `m_inputField.text` (:61515-61521); Unity's InputField text setter clamps, so a longer server tag is truncated in the dialog and a reflexive Enter submits the truncation as a new command.
The parser must treat re-submission of its own canonical echo as a no-op, or every dialog open+OK re-fires the last command.
Two players retagging the same portal inside one 0.05 s flush: last DataRevision wins, the loser's command is never observed and never reported.
`TextInput.OnEnter` does `.Replace("\\n","\n")` (:61496) — typing backslash-n injects a literal newline into `s_tag`, breaking the quoted hover string. Sanitize on read.
Vanilla `Game.ConnectPortals` destroys any managed link within 5 s unless prefixed out (:100601).
Without `SetDirtyPortals()` every rename silently reverts at the next world save (:77621, :76702).
An address book keyed by ZDOID is empty after a restart — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every uid (:74552). Key by rounded world position.
prerequisites: Prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (or full pairing takeover)
Position-keyed portal address book persisted to a mod file
Per-character Message RPC for the error channel
openQuestions: Does Valheim's GuiInputField override UnityEngine.UI.InputField's clamping text setter? The class body is in none of the four decompiles (grep for `class GuiInputField` returns nothing). IN-GAME: server-write a 20-char tag, open the rename dialog on a vanilla client, read the box.
Does the TMP font atlas render `>`,`#`,`?`,`*`,`@`,`!`,`-` in hover text, or do some show as missing-glyph boxes? IN-GAME: one tag per sigil, hover each.
Does `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` work (started by the string overload at :100074)? Cleaner than a returning-false prefix.

corrections: Remove zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) from the action sequence: the server's ZDO.Set/SetConnection do not require ownership, and while the server owns the portal (≤2 s until ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927 returns it) a vanilla rename is silently dropped — SetText routes to the owner (:82855-82858), the server has no instance (:83656-83664), and client RPC_SetTag is IsOwner-gated (:143587).

Client RPC_SetTag clears this portal's connection and RPC_SetConnected clears the previous partner's (:143590-143593, :143605-143625); the governor must rewrite both ends when the topology is bidirectional.

Attribution: the RPC_ZDOData sender is the portal's current owner (FindPeer(rpc) :77078), which with two nearby players may not be the typist; s_tagauthor (:143597) is client-supplied and spoofable. Treat lock ownership as vanilla-honest only.
The client's push always carries connection=None (ZDO.Serialize includes the connection, :74170-74175); the postfix must re-assert the managed connection even when the tag string is unchanged.
ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage) begins at :74206, not :74225.

Remove zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) from the ACTION or document a <=2 s window in which the next vanilla RPC_SetTag is routed to the server and dropped (HandleRoutedRPC :83656-83664; ReleaseNearbyZDOS cadence :76874-76880). Server-side ZDO.Set/SetConnection do not check ownership (:73648-73666); clients accept any higher DataRevision (:77106-77120).

Every vanilla retag also executes UpdateConnection(Portal, None) and SetConnectedPortal(oldTarget) on the client (:143591-143594, :143605-143628); the ACTION must rewrite both ends of the new link and clean the old partner each command.

Sender identity: the ZDOData packet comes from the portal's owner peer, which is the typist only when ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigned it to them; key '!' lock ownership on s_tagauthor (:143584, client-asserted), not the RPC sender.

Prewarm ForceSendZDO(peer, destId) shaves at most one 0.5 s UpdatePortal poll; TargetFound already self-heals via RequestZDO (:143652-143654, :77689-77692) and the trigger fires on entry, so 'dead transit' is not a real failure mode.
Displayed tag is CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC output on PlayFab backends (:143568); keep opcodes to plain ASCII punctuation.
Effort: medium-large (full pairing takeover + Deserialize postfix on all incoming ZDOs + address book).

(:82855-82858); when targetPeerID == m_id the client handles locally and skips RouteRPC (:83587-83594). The 'press E again' UX would intermittently no-op. (2) Client RPC_SetTag clears this portal's connection and sends RPC_SetConnected to the OLD partner's owner, which clears the partner's link (:143590-143593, :143605-143625), so each dial also breaks the previous partner's outbound link — the governor must rewrite both ends for bidirectional pairs. (3) With two players near the portal the ZDO owner (and therefore the RPC_ZDOData sender) may be the other player, so attribution for '!' lock must not use the ZDOData peer; s_tagauthor (:143597) is client-supplied. (4) Every retag's push carries connection=None (network Serialize includes the connection :74170-74175), so a Deserialize postfix that only writes the connection when the tag changed will leave a re-sent identical tag with a torn-down link; always re-assert the connection for managed portals in the postfix.

(:82855-82858); when targetPeerID == m_id the RPC is handled locally and RouteRPC is skipped (:83587-83594). ReleaseNearbyZDOS iterates FindSectorObjects which includes m_portalObjects (FindObjects :77367-77382) and assigns unowned/out-of-area ZDOs to the peer (:76920-76923), so the typist normally owns the portal and no RPC crosses the wire. The change reaches the server as ZDO data: client RPC_SetTag -> zDO.Set(s_tag) -> IncreaseDataRevision -> ClientChanged (:73832-73838) -> server RPC_ZDOData -> ZDO.Deserialize (:77076-77139, :74206-74250) -> AddIfPortal. A Harmony postfix on ZDO.Deserialize filtered by Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:100021) is a valid hook; GetPortalList (:77648-77655) is world-global and resident from load (:76574-76597). SetDirtyPortals is genuinely mandatory: a tag-only write dirties the sector chunk (:73838 -> SetDirtySector) but portals are excluded from chunk files (:77572) and the portal chunk is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77631), which a server-side Deserialize never sets. ForceSendZDO(peer, id) is real (:77714-77724) and AddForceSendZdos inserts at the head (:77262-77282). Client hover reads the ZDO each frame (:143453-143464); RemoveRichTextTags only strips <...> (assembly_utils_SERVER :6700-6703). Corrections: (1) zdo.SetOwner(GetSessionID()) in the ACTION creates a <=2 s dead window: while the server owns the portal, the next vanilla RPC_SetTag routes to the server, HandleRoutedRPC finds no ZNetView instance and drops it silently (:83656-83664); ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership only on its 2 s cadence (:76874-76880). A quick second command ('Press E again, type #Base') is lost. Server ZDO.Set/SetConnection need no ownership (no owner check :73648-73666) and the client accepts any higher revision (:77106-77120), so drop the SetOwner or accept the dead window. (2) The client's RPC_SetTag also runs UpdateConnection(None) and SetConnectedPortal(oldTarget) (:143591-143594, :143605-143619), unlinking both ends and routing RPC_SetConnected to the old partner's owner — after every command the mod must rewrite both ends, and vanilla ConnectPortals must be fully prefixed (already listed). (3) When another nearby peer owns the portal, the ZDOData sender is that peer, not the typist; '!' lock and any permission must key on s_tagauthor (client-asserted, :143584) not the packet sender. (4) The prewarm is a minor optimisation, not a dead-transit fix: UpdatePortal's 0.5 s poll already calls TargetFound -> RequestZDO -> RPC_RequestZDO -> ForceSendZDO (:143652-143654, :77689-77692), and OnTriggerEnter fires on entry, so by the time the player walks in the ZDO is resident. (5) PlayFab-backed clients display FilterUGC output (:143568); censored opcodes would show as filtered text. (6) Effort 'medium' understates a full pairing takeover plus a Deserialize postfix on every incoming ZDO; medium-large is more honest.

catalog.name: Raising the 10-character tag cap
catalog.oneLine: Server-side widening of the portal rename box past 10 characters.
catalog.howItWorks:
The cap is a literal argument in client-only code with no ZDO, RPC, config or global-key backing: `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and `TextInput.Show` assigns it to `m_inputField.characterLimit` (:61519). `Interact` is reached only from `Player.Update` → `Interact(m_hovering,…)` gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`, and no `TeleportWorld` MonoBehaviour ever exists on a dedicated server: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6)` every physics tick (:100465) so `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` never instantiates a portal (:82105). Nothing server-side to patch, nothing on the wire to intercept.

The WRITE side is uncapped — `ZDO.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, string)` (:73721) has no length check, `RPC_SetTag` performs none (:143587-143602), and `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the server build (:94588). So the server CAN store a 200-char tag and vanilla clients render it after `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459). But it is a trap: the moment any player presses E on that portal, `TextInput.Show` clamps the pre-filled text to 10 and Enter submits the truncation as the portal's new tag AND as a command. A long display tag is a live footgun on every player-reachable portal.

A stateful multi-submission concatenation (`>Halr` then `>dor`, joined per (playerId, portalPos, 30 s)) technically extends the budget but is worse than 10-char discipline and confuses everyone. Put the long text on a Sign (50 chars) or in a HUD toast (unlimited) instead.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing changes. The rename box stops accepting input at exactly 10 characters on every vanilla client, forever. If the server wrote a longer tag, the box shows only the first 10 and the player has no way to know the rest existed.
failureModes: Storing >10-char tags on player-reachable portals turns every accidental Enter into a silent destructive truncation.
corrections: The claim that TextInput.Show clamps pre-filled text to 10 and Enter submits a truncated tag is not supported by the decompile: GuiInputField (gui_framework.dll, not decompiled) is a TMP_InputField, whose SetText does not truncate to characterLimit; long server-written tags are most likely round-tripped intact and RPC_SetTag no-ops on equality (:143591). Mark this sub-claim needs-ingame-check.

Add: RPC_SetTag runs only on the portal ZDO owner (:143589); with server-claimed ownership, vanilla renames are routed to the server and dropped in ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC because FindInstance is null (:83657-83662).

`GuiInputField` (SERVER:61436) is not in any decompile on disk; the prefill-truncation claim rests on TMP_InputField's documented `characterLimit`-on-assignment behaviour, not on read source. If a build ever ships a GuiInputField that does not clip on assignment, Enter would resubmit the full long tag and `RPC_SetTag`'s equality check (SERVER:143591) would make it a no-op — i.e. the trap would vanish, but the cap would still be un-raisable.
Add: Escape in `TextInput.Update` hides without submitting (SERVER:61468-61471), so a player who opens the box and backs out does not truncate.
evidence: gui_framework.dll string table: TMP_InputField, GuiInputField, get_characterLimit (strings, client/gui_framework.dll)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Ruled-out verdict holds. `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (SERVER :143482) — a literal in client-only code; `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` (:61519). No ZDO key, RPC, config or global key carries the limit, and `TeleportWorld` is only instantiated where `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` runs against a real reference position; `Game.FixedUpdate` pins it to (1e6,0,1e6) on the server (:100465), so there is nothing server-side to patch. Write side is genuinely uncapped: `ZDO.Set(int, string)` (:73721-73726) has no length check, `RPC_SetTag` only compares tag/author and writes (:143587-143602), server `FilterUGC` is `return text;` (:94588-94591). Corrections: (1) the 'footgun' mechanism is NOT verifiable from the Valheim decompile. `m_inputField` is `GuiInputField` (:61438), defined in gui_framework.dll (not decompiled), whose string table shows it derives from TMP_InputField. TMP_InputField.SetText does not apply `characterLimit` to programmatic assignment (the limit only blocks appended keystrokes), so a 200-char server tag pre-filled in the box is most likely shown in full and re-submitted unchanged on Enter — `RPC_SetTag` then sees `tagRaw == tag` and writes nothing (:143591-143592). The truncation-on-Enter trap is probably false; treat as needs-ingame-check, but it does not rescue the option. (2) The option's line range :143587-143602 for RPC_SetTag is right; note `RPC_SetTag` executes only on the ZDO OWNER (`m_nview.IsOwner()`, :143589) via `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string)` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …)` (:82855-82858) — if the mod claims portal ownership server-side, every vanilla rename is routed to the server, hits `ZNetScene.FindInstance == null` in `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83657-83662) and is silently dropped. Not this option's problem but a hazard for any design relying on '>tag' commands.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Holds up. Server build `TeleportWorld.Interact` is `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (SERVER:143482) and the client build has the identical literal (CLIENT:144222). `TextInput.Show` does `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit; m_inputField.text = text` (SERVER:61519-61521) — `m_inputField` is a `GuiInputField` (SERVER:61436), whose source is not on disk; on the standard TMP_InputField base `SetText` applies `characterLimit` on assignment, so the prefill is clipped to 10. `TextInput.OnEnter`/`OnInput` submit `m_inputField.text` unconditionally (SERVER:61486-61497) → `TeleportWorld.SetText` → `InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag")` (CLIENT:144319-144325) → `RPC_SetTag` compares `tagRaw == tag` and, on mismatch, clears the connection and writes the truncated tag (SERVER:143587-143602). So the footgun is real: any E+Enter on a long-tagged portal silently truncates it and breaks its link. Escape cancels without submitting (SERVER:61468-61471), which is the only escape hatch. Write side is uncapped as claimed: `ZDO.Set(int,string)` has no length check (SERVER:73721-73727); server `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` (SERVER:94588-94591); hover renders the full stored string through `RemoveRichTextTags` only (SERVER:143459). No `TeleportWorld` exists server-side: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick (SERVER:100458-100466) and `CreateObjectsSorted` builds only near that position (SERVER:82105-82112). Nothing to patch, nothing on the wire carrying the limit. `ruled-out` / `not-enforceable` is the correct label.

catalog.name: The Ledger — signs as a server-written live directory
catalog.oneLine: Any Sign within 8 m of a managed portal is adopted by the server, which rewrites `ZDOVars.s_text` so the sign shows a live paged portal directory; the player reads it with zero mod.
catalog.howItWorks:
DISCOVERY: every 10 s, for each portal from `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), run `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 8f)` (Wonderland Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25 → `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` :77142) and keep ZDOs whose prefab resolves via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` to a GameObject carrying `Sign`. Sort by (y desc, then bearing around the portal) so a stacked wall reads top-to-bottom. Each sign is one line.

WRITE: `Sign.Awake` runs `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (:141779) and `UpdateText` early-returns when `m_lastRevision == zdo.DataRevision` (:141837-141843). A server write to `s_text` (:78629) bumps DataRevision and every client in range repaints within 2 s with no further work. Write `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, line)` AND `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_author, "")`. Never write `"host"`: `UpdateText` maps it to `m_author = null`, and `UpdateViewPermission` calls `OnCheckPermissionCompleted(Denied)` then FALLS THROUGH with no `return` to `if (m_author.Value.IsValid)` (:141867-141876) — `Nullable.Value` on a null throws every 2 s on every viewer. Empty author → `PlatformUserID.None`, HasValue true, Granted path. Claim ownership then `ForceSendZDO` so distant boards can be pushed.

BUDGET: `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141756) is the client input widget only; the server write is uncapped, but the same truncation trap applies, so stay ≤50 per sign. `GetHoverText` strips rich text (:141785) but `m_textWidget.text` is set RAW (:141891/:141895) — so TMP markup (`<color=#ffcc00>`) DOES render on the physical sign face while being stripped from the hover tooltip. Colour-coded directories are real.

PAGING with a 6-sign wall: line 0 header + page N/M, lines 1-4 entries `7  Base  612m  OK`, line 5 footer. Page turn driven by any other channel (crouch, a jump, a `>p2` tag).
catalog.playerExperience:
You build four ordinary wooden signs in a column beside your portal and walk away. Ten seconds later they read, in Valheim's own sign lettering:

`— PORTAL DIRECTORY 1/3 —`
`1 Base      0m    HOME`
`2 Haldor    1.2k  open`
`3 BlackFors 840m  open`

A fifth sign reads `type >1 on the portal`. You press E on the portal, type `>2`, Enter. A quarter second later the portal glows; two seconds later the board repaints and line 2 reads `2 Haldor 1.2k ▸YOU` in yellow. When your friend dials line 3 from her outpost your board updates for you too — same server state.

Entries you cannot use render grey. A destroyed portal shows `4 Mine2 --- GONE` until the server prunes it.

Cost: four signs of wood and thirty seconds of building. No typing, no learning — signs are the most legible object in Valheim and every player already knows they display text.
failureModes: Writing `s_author = "host"` throws inside `Sign.UpdateViewPermission` on every viewing client every 2 s (:141869-141876). Write an empty string.

A player pressing E on a managed sign sees the text clamped to 50 and can overwrite the server's line; the server rewrites within a tick, so the net effect is a flicker plus the player's text silently lost.
Sign text only updates for clients holding the sign's ZDO. A distant board is stale unless the server calls `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, signZdoId)` per peer.
`m_characterLimit` is an Inspector field; 50 is the class default and hanging/large sign variants may differ.
Rich text renders on the face but not in hover, so the two surfaces disagree for a player who reads by hovering.
openQuestions: Is `PlatformUserID.None.IsValid` false? It lives in the Splatform assembly, absent here. Either branch appears safe (`RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync` is a Granted-returning stub at :88350) but confirm no exception path. IN-GAME: server-write a sign with an empty author and watch a client's log for 2 s-cadence exceptions.

Does `RelationsManager.UpdateAuthorIfHost(resolvedAuthor, ref resolvedAuthor)` (:141848, runs when the viewer owns the sign) rewrite an empty author to `"host"` and walk into the NRE? IN-GAME: stand at a server-written sign for 60 s.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:The Ledger — signs as a server-written live directory
corrections: Exception on author "host" is InvalidOperationException from Nullable<PlatformUserID>.Value (:141872), swallowed by Unity's InvokeRepeating; effect is 2 s log spam and the runic hidden text, not a crash.

Ownership claim is unnecessary: ZDO.Set (:73721) and ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) (:77714) have no owner check; server→peer sync is sector+revision only (:77212-77238, :76003-76013). Remove 'claim ownership'.

Add revision-collision caveat: a client write issued before the server's reply arrives produces equal DataRevisions and both sides drop each other's packet (:77105-77110); rely on the periodic rewrite to reconverge.

Rich-text rendering on the sign face depends on the prefab's TMP richText flag (not in the decompile); vanilla sign colour tags are common knowledge, but mark needs-ingame-check for markup beyond <color>.
Enforcement: server-written but overwritable by any player who can Interact (client-side ward check only, :141917); re-assert on timer.

Enforcement: not `server-enforced`. It is a server-AUTHORED, client-RENDERED display; any vanilla client can overwrite or destroy the sign between passes (`Sign.SetText` SERVER:141915-141929; `RPC_DestroyZDO` has no sender check). Label as client-honoured output.

`RPC_ZDOData` discards client updates whose DataRevision <= the server copy's (SERVER:77104-77114). Server rewrites bump the revision; a player editing an adopted sign in the delivery window loses the edit silently. Only rewrite when the text actually changes.
Drop `ClaimOwnership`: `ForceSendZDO` requires no ownership (SERVER:77706) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` reassigns server-owned persistent ZDOs near a player every 2 s (SERVER:76874-76925).
Non-ASCII glyphs (▸ — ·) and space-aligned columns are unverified against the sign font atlas — needs-ingame-check for the rendered layout, not for the mechanism.
`s_text` is saved to disk: directory text persists across restart and after mod removal as stale plain text.
evidence: Sign.UpdateViewPermission (fall-through on null author) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141867-141881; client identical assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:142604-142616
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. `Sign.Awake` → `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (:141779); `UpdateText` gates on `m_lastRevision == zdo.DataRevision` (:141837-141842), reads `s_text` (:141844), and ends in `OnCheckPermissionCompleted` which assigns `m_textWidget.text = m_currentText` raw (:141895). Server `ZDO.Set(int,string)` bumps DataRevision with no owner check (:73721-73726, :73832-73840); server→client sync is sector-based and ownership-agnostic — `CreateSyncList` on the server collects `FindSectorObjects` results filtered only by `peer.ShouldSend` (revision compare, :76003-76013; :77212-77238); the client's `RPC_ZDOData` applies any packet with `num4 > zDO.DataRevision` regardless of who owns it (:77105-77127). `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID)` is public (:77714). The 'host' hazard is real and present in the client build too: `resolvedAuthor == "host"` → `m_author = null` (:141857-141859), `UpdateViewPermission` calls Denied then falls through to `m_author.Value.IsValid` (:141867-141876; client :142607-142613). Rich text: `GetHoverText` strips tags (:141785), widget receives raw string (:141895) — vanilla players already use colour tags on signs, so rendering is a safe assumption though the TMP `richText` flag is prefab data not in the decompile. Corrections: (1) the thrown exception is `InvalidOperationException` (Nullable.Value), not an NRE, and it is caught by Unity's InvokeRepeating dispatcher — log spam plus the runic Denied text, not a client crash. Vanilla itself writes "host" when `!IsSignedIn` (:141922) and only the OWNER remaps it via `UpdateAuthorIfHost` (:141848, :88385) — so avoid "host" as stated. (2) 'Claim ownership then ForceSendZDO' — ownership is unnecessary for the write or the push; `ZDO.Set` and `ForceSendZDO` have no owner requirement, and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` would hand it back anyway. Drop the claim. (3) Revision race: after a server write the server copy is at rev N+1; if the owning client writes the sign again before the push lands, its rev also becomes N+1 and BOTH directions are discarded by the `<=` guard (:77108, server side symmetric) — the sign silently diverges until the next write. Harmless for an output-only board but must be re-asserted on a timer (the 10 s rewrite already does this). (4) 8 m adoption will overwrite any pre-existing player sign (chest labels) near a portal — needs an opt-in marker or ignore-signs-with-existing-non-directory-text rule. (5) Enforcement label: the server authors the text but any player outside a ward can retype it (`Sign.SetText` checks only client-side `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, :141917); it is server-written output, not protected state.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. `Sign.Awake` runs `UpdateText()` then `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (SERVER:141772-141780); `UpdateText` early-returns on `m_lastRevision == DataRevision` (SERVER:141837-141842) and otherwise reads `s_text`/`s_authorDisplayName`/`s_author` (SERVER:141844-141847). Server-side `ZDO.Set` has no ownership check and bumps `DataRevision` (SERVER:73648-73654, 73832-73840); the server's sync list is sector-based per peer and `ShouldSend` compares `DataRevision` (SERVER:77212-77238, 76003-76013), so any viewer in range receives the new text and repaints within 2 s. Client `RPC_ZDOData` applies incoming data whenever `num4 > zDO.DataRevision` regardless of ownership (same code, SERVER:77104-77128). The `"host"` trap is real and identical in the client build: `resolvedAuthor == "host"` → `m_author = null` (SERVER:141855-141858) → `UpdateViewPermission` calls Denied then falls through to `m_author.Value.IsValid` (CLIENT:142604-142616) → `InvalidOperationException` every 2 s. Empty author → `PlatformUserID.None` → `IsValid` false → Granted (SERVER:141851-141853, 141871-141879). Raw `m_textWidget.text = m_currentText` (SERVER:141895) and hover via `RemoveRichTextTags` (SERVER:141785) both confirmed. `m_characterLimit = 50` is only the `Interact` widget cap (SERVER:141756, 141831). Attacks that land: (1) The enforcement label is a category error — this is an OUTPUT surface; nothing is enforced, and any vanilla client can overwrite the text (`Sign.SetText` is a plain owned write, SERVER:141915-141929) or delete the sign (`RPC_DestroyZDO`, no sender check) until the next 10 s pass. (2) DataRevision race: `RPC_ZDOData` DROPS any client ZDO update whose revision is not strictly greater than the server's copy (SERVER:77104-77114). Every server rewrite bumps the server revision; a player who presses E on an adopted sign between the server's write and its delivery (~50 ms + ½ RTT) has their edit silently discarded. Small but real, and it means the mod must never rewrite unchanged text (harmless: `ZDOExtraData.Set` returns false on equal value so no bump). (3) `ClaimOwnership` + `ForceSendZDO` is unnecessary — `ForceSendZDO` needs no ownership (SERVER:77706-77712) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands ownership to any nearby peer every 2 s anyway (SERVER:76874-76879, 76901-76925). (4) Glyphs: `▸`, `—`, `·` are not guaranteed to exist in the sign's TMP font atlas; missing glyphs render as boxes/blank. Columns aligned with spaces will not line up in a proportional font. Needs an in-game check. (5) Save/restart: `s_text` is persistent (not a session hash), so directory text survives restarts and mod removal as frozen text — cosmetic, but the option should say so. (6) The paging channel and toast are prereqs (Ledger alone has no input).

catalog.name: Signs as INPUT — the 50-character command line
catalog.oneLine: Instead of the 10-char portal box, the player writes a full sentence on an ordinary sign beside the portal; the server reads `s_text` and treats it as the routing order.
catalog.howItWorks:
The biggest usable-bandwidth win available to a zero-client mod, and absent from the research digest. `Sign.SetText` runs entirely on the writing client: `m_nview.ClaimOwnership(); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, text); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_author, …)` (:141915-141929) — no RPC, a pure ZDO write. It reaches the server as `RPC_ZDOData` → `ZDO.Deserialize` (:77124-77132) within one 0.05 s client flush plus ½ RTT. The input widget is `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141831, :141756) — five times the portal tag's budget, on a UI the player already knows, with the text left permanently visible in the world rather than hidden behind a hover.

HOOK: the same `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` postfix; filter to prefabs whose GameObject carries a `Sign` (resolve once at world-ready via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponent<Sign>()`, cache the hash set). On a text change, find the nearest managed portal with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(signPos, 8f)` filtered by `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021). The control sign is by convention the lowest-y adopted sign, or any whose text starts with a verb.

GRAMMAR AT 50 CHARS is a real command line: `dial Haldor` · `dial Base and lock` · `route Mine2 -> Base one-way` · `name this portal Northgate` · `allow Bjorn, Astrid` · `list plains`. One-way links, aliases, permission lists, multi-token commands and human-readable errors all become expressible.

PAIR WITH THE LEDGER: one column of server-owned output signs plus one designated input sign at the bottom that the player types into and the server replaces with the reply. That is a terminal — prompt line and scrollback — built from vanilla wood.

OWNERSHIP: `SetText` calls `ClaimOwnership()` so the writer owns the sign afterwards; the server's reply still lands because `ZDO.Set` has no ownership check (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter, :73648) and the server's DataRevision is higher.
catalog.playerExperience:
You place one sign under your portal, press E — the ordinary sign box, 50 characters, the one you've used to label chests a hundred times — and type `dial Haldor and lock`, Enter.

The sign shows your text for about a second, then repaints to `→ HALDOR  1.2km  LOCKED to you` in yellow, and a toast reads `Portal locked. Only you and Bjorn may re-dial.` The portal beside it lights up; its hover tag reads `">Haldor"`.

You type `list plains` on the same sign. It repaints to `plains: Fuling1 2.1k · Tarpit 3.4k · Bog 4k` — three destinations, full names, distances, readable from five metres without hovering anything.

Mistype `dial Halodr`: the sign repaints to `? no portal "Halodr" — try Haldor, Home` and stays that way until you fix it. The portal keeps its old link throughout.

Genuinely close to a real console. The only jank is that you are typing into a wooden plank.
failureModes: The server's reply overwrites the player's typed text; if a reply exceeds 50 chars, a later E+Enter submits the clamp as a command. Keep replies ≤50 and make the parser idempotent on its own replies.
Two signs near one portal are ambiguous without an explicit convention plus a toast saying which sign was used.

A sign inside a ward the player cannot access silently refuses `SetText` client-side (`PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, :141917) with no message — the box just does nothing on Enter, and the server sees no ZDO change and cannot distinguish that from the player not typing.
Sign text is public: anyone can read another player's routing commands and, unless gated on `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) or ward permission, retype the sign and re-dial someone else's portal.
The visible reply lags the toast by up to 2 s (`UpdateText` cadence), which reads as the sign thinking — arguably good feedback.
openQuestions: Do all sign prefabs share `m_characterLimit = 50` or do some override it? IN-GAME: press E on each variant and count accepted characters.

Does `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` inside `Sign.SetText` swallow the write with genuinely no player-visible message? Reading :141917 there is no `Message` call. IN-GAME: build a sign in someone else's ward and try to write.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Signs as INPUT — the 50-character command line
corrections: Game.PortalPrefabHash is `List<int>` (:100021-100032); use Contains(zdo.GetPrefab()), not equality.
Revision collision: a second player write within the server-reply RTT is silently dropped on both sides (RPC_ZDOData `num4 <= DataRevision` guard, :77105-77110); re-assert the reply on a timer.
ZDO.Deserialize postfix fires for every client ZDO update including character ZDOs at 20 Hz; gate on cached Sign prefab-hash set before touching ZDOExtraData.
The okForNotOwner dead parameter exists only on Set(int,int,bool) (:73648); Set(int,string) (:73721) has no owner parameter at all — same conclusion, cite correctly.

Hook `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:77076), not `ZDO.Deserialize`: Deserialize has no sender parameter and no old-text view. Identity from the `ZRpc` peer (private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` SERVER:80504) or `zdo.GetOwner()` after `ClaimOwnership`.

Commands are silently dropped if the client's ZDO copy is stale: `RPC_ZDOData` requires `dataRevision > server DataRevision` (SERVER:77104-77114). Never rewrite the input sign on a timer; only in direct reply.
Server reply must set `s_author` to `""`, never leave `"host"` (SERVER:141925 → NRE at 141867-141876 on every viewer).
`LOCKED` / `allow Bjorn` semantics are reactive-detection-only: an owning client retags with zero packets (SERVER:83587-83594); the server can only revert after the fact.
Route writes must be reconciled with `Game.ConnectPortals`' tag-equality predicate (SERVER:100596-100605) or they are undone within 5 s — dependency on the address-book prereq, not free.
Effort: small-medium is optimistic once identity resolution, change detection, replay-guard after world load, and the 5 s reconcile interplay are included; medium.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified end to end. `Sign.Interact` → `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141831, :141756). `Sign.SetText` is a pure owner-side ZDO write: client-side `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, `ClaimOwnership()`, `Set(s_text)`, `Set(s_author)`, optional `Set(s_authorDisplayName)` (:141915-141929) — no RPC. `ZDO.Set(int,string)` → `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ClientChanged(m_uid)` on non-servers (:73832-73840); the client flush timer is 0.05 s (`SendZDOToPeers2`, :76837-76862) and the server's `RPC_ZDOData` calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` (:77128) — `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` is public at :74206, so a Harmony postfix is available. `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` exists but is a `List<int>` property (:100021), not a single hash — filter with `.Contains`. `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores the flag (:73648-73654); the string overload has no such parameter at all (:73721). Server reply lands because the server's rev is client-rev+1 and the client applies any higher rev (:77105-77127). Corrections/caveats: (1) same revision-collision hazard as the Ledger — if the player re-submits within the RTT of the server's reply, both packets are dropped and the sign diverges; the command parser should also key on the s_author/text pair and re-assert. (2) `ZDO.Deserialize` on the server is called for EVERY ZDO update from every client (character ZDOs every 50 ms); a postfix must early-exit on prefab hash before any string read. World load uses a different path, so the hook does not fire during load. (3) The reply overwrites the prompt, so the next E pre-fills the server's reply text; whether TMP's focus-select-all makes this painless is a UI detail not in the decompile. (4) `Sign.SetText` writes `s_author` as the writer's PlatformUserID (or "host" when not signed in, :141922) — the server can use `s_author` to attribute the command to a platform identity, and should map "host" per `UpdateAuthorIfHost` semantics rather than trusting it.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds. `Sign.SetText` is `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` → `ClaimOwnership` → `zdo.Set(s_text)` → `zdo.Set(s_author, PlatformUserID or "host")` → optional `s_authorDisplayName` → `UpdateText()` (SERVER:141915-141929); no RPC. The owning client queues it via `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ClientChanged` (SERVER:73832-73840) and the client `ZDOMan.Update` flushes every 0.05 s (SERVER:76843-76860); server `RPC_ZDOData` applies it via `ZDO.Deserialize` (SERVER:77104-77132), which merges keys with `ZDOExtraData.Add` (SERVER:74206-74241). `Sign.Interact` calls `RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with the default 50 (SERVER:141831, 141756). `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is a `List<int>` populated in `Game.Awake` (SERVER:100021, 100027-100032). `ZDO.Set` ignores ownership (SERVER:73648) so the server reply lands. Refutations/corrections: (1) `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` has NO sender context — a postfix there cannot tell who wrote the sign. Hook `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` instead (SERVER:77076) and resolve the peer from `rpc` (`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` is private, SERVER:80504); or trust `zdo.GetOwner()` (set to the writer by `ClaimOwnership`) / `s_author` (client-supplied, vanilla-honest, spoofable). A Deserialize postfix also cannot see the OLD text — keep a per-sign text cache to detect changes. (2) Silent-drop hazard: `RPC_ZDOData` skips any update with `dataRevision <= server DataRevision` (SERVER:77104-77114). The server reply bumps the revision; if the player submits before the reply has been delivered (~50-150 ms) the command is discarded with no error. Typing takes seconds so this is rare, but the mod must not rewrite the input sign on a timer. (3) The `"host"` author: a non-signed-in writer stores `"host"` (SERVER:141925), which is the NRE path in every viewer's `UpdateViewPermission` (SERVER:141867-141876) until the owner's `UpdateAuthorIfHost` (CLIENT:88762-88780) rewrites it — the server reply should always overwrite `s_author` with `""`. (4) Enforcement: the ROUTE write is server-side and honest; but the playerExperience's `LOCKED to you — only you and Bjorn may re-dial` is not enforceable at the act: `RPC_SetTag` runs on the owning client and when the sender owns the portal no packet is routed (`InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally when `targetPeerID == m_id`, SERVER:83587-83594). A lock can only be REVERTED reactively when the server sees the tag change in `RPC_ZDOData`. (5) The written route must survive `Game.ConnectPortals`, whose predicate tears down any connection whose target tag differs (SERVER:100596-100605) — the address-book prereq must equalize tags or the link dies within 5 s. (6) The `s_text` write persists to disk, so a stale command survives restart — replay-guard by (zdoid, text) after load.

catalog.name: Map ping as a freehand destination picker
catalog.oneLine: The player middle-clicks the map; the server receives the exact world coordinate and routes their portal there — the only vanilla input that carries an arbitrary Vector3.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Chat.SendPing(Vector3)` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")`, with `vector.y` forced to the player's own y and x/z from the map click (:42058-42071). `targetPeerID == 0` makes `InvokeRoutedRPC` run `HandleRoutedRPC` locally AND `RouteRPC` (:83587-83594), so the packet ALWAYS reaches the dedicated server regardless of player count — unlike chat text, which is addressed per-listed-player and produces zero packets for a solo player. Three vanilla gestures fire it: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick`, `Minimap.OnMapDblClick` with the Ping pin selected, and gamepad JoyButtonX on the large map. Mouse and controller both covered, no keybind config.

HOOK: prefer a Harmony prefix on the private `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData)` (:83646) over `ZRoutedRpc.Register`, because `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (:83672) and throws if a `Chat` MonoBehaviour already claimed the name headless. Match `data.m_methodHash == "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()`, snapshot `data.m_parameters.GetPos()`, deserialize `Vector3,int,UserInfo,string`, restore the position, return true. Filter `type == 3`.

BINDING: the ping carries no portal reference. Bind it to the player's LAST TOUCHED PORTAL — `Dictionary<long playerId,(ZDOID portal,float time)>` refreshed whenever that player's character ZDO (`ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` :81024) is within 6 m of a portal from `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643), 5-minute TTL. On a ping, resolve the nearest managed portal within 64 m of the ping x/z and route the remembered portal to it. If nothing is in range, either reject with a toast or fabricate an anchor: `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` + `SetPrefab` + `Persistent = true` + `SetRotation` (:76674, :73808, :73323, :73781), height from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x,z)` (:151944) + 1 m, validated against `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` (:115637) and sea level 30.

DEBOUNCE: pings are public and cheap. Rate-limit to one acted-on ping per player per 3 s and require the ARM step so casual pings during a hunt do not re-route a base portal.
catalog.playerExperience:
You stand at your portal, press M, scroll to the Black Forest, put the cursor on your friend's outpost and middle-click. The normal vanilla ping marker appears — everyone online sees and hears it.

You close the map. Within about 200 ms a toast reads `Dialed → Northgate (Black Forest, 1,140m)`. The portal you were standing at is already glowing, and the destination ZDO has been pushed to you so the first step through works.

Middle-click empty ocean: `Nothing within 64m of that ping.` Middle-click 30 m from an unmanaged portal: `Nearest is "Bog" (unmanaged). Name it with #Bog first.`

Because it is public, a group sees where you just sent yourself — either party coordination or a privacy leak. The mod should never echo the destination NAME to anyone but you.

Cost: open map, one click. The fastest input in the inventory and the only one where the player expresses an arbitrary PLACE rather than picking from a list.
failureModes: Pings broadcast to every connected player — the gesture is inherently public and spammable.

`data.m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire and never cross-checked against the ZRpc connection (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495, `RPC_RoutedRPC` :83632). A modified client can ping 'as' someone else.

`SendPing` overwrites y with the PLAYER's y, not terrain height (:42063-42064). Re-derive height with `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` — never `ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight`, a collider raycast that silently returns `p.y` server-side because no terrain collider exists near real coordinates (:115502, :100465).
Ping precision is bounded by map zoom; at full zoom-out a click spans tens of metres. Snap to the nearest managed portal rather than using the raw coordinate.
If a `Chat` MonoBehaviour exists headless, `ZRoutedRpc.Register("ChatMessage",…)` throws ArgumentException at Awake and takes the plugin down.
A prefix that reads `data.m_parameters` without restoring `GetPos()` corrupts vanilla's own dispatch of the same packet.
prerequisites: An arming gesture to prevent accidental re-routes
openQuestions: Is `Chat.instance` non-null on a 1.0.7 dedicated server (is `"ChatMessage"` already in `ZRoutedRpc.m_functions`)? `Game.Awake` instantiates only the console and ServerOptionsGUI prefabs (:100034-100045), but `ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer` dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded under IsDedicated (:80258). IN-GAME: dump `m_functions` keys at server start.
Does the gamepad JoyButtonX path ping the map VIEW CENTRE rather than a cursor (`Minimap.UpdateMap` :57058)? That changes precision for controller players.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Map ping as a freehand destination picker
corrections: Sender identity is NOT verified at HandleRoutedRPC: m_senderPeerID comes from the client's packet (:83487-83495, :83651). Hook RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632) and map the ZRpc to a peer via ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) (private, :80504) for a socket-verified identity.

CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int) registers the ZDO as a portal via AddIfPortal but does not set m_prefab (:76684-76690); SetPrefab must still be called (:73808). The result is a real, visible, reconciled portal piece, not an invisible anchor.
Ping Vector3.y is the sender's own y (:42063); derive target height from WorldGenerator.GetHeight only.
Dictionary.Add collision on Register is irrelevant server-side (no Chat MonoBehaviour); keep the prefix approach for the identity fix, not for this reason.

Identity: `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is packet-supplied (SERVER:83487-83495), not verified. Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:83632) and map `rpc` → peer via the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (SERVER:80504). `HandleRoutedRPC` also fires for the server's own local invocations.
Route survives only if both portals carry equal `s_tag` — `ConnectPortals` clears mismatched links every 5 s (SERVER:100596-100605). Hard dependency on the address-book prereq.

Fabricated anchors are physical portals: `CreateNewZDO` registers in `m_portalObjects` (SERVER:76684-76692) but leaves `m_prefab`=0 and `Persistent`=false unless set; vanilla `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` pairs untagged portals with each other (SERVER:100664-100680), so an untagged anchor is immediately eligible for vanilla pairing.
Vanilla already fetches the target ZDO via `TargetFound → RequestZDO` (CLIENT:144380-144396); no server push needed for the first step.
Feasibility: feasible-with-caveats — the anchor branch and the reconcile interplay are the risk, not the ping channel.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified. `Chat.SendPing` sets `vector.y = localPlayer.transform.position.y` and calls `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")` (:42058-42071); 3 == `Talker.Type.Ping`. `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally when `targetPeerID == 0` and always calls `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID != m_id` (:83577-83595); client-side `RouteRPC` sends to every peer, i.e. the server (:83621-83627). Server `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `HandleRoutedRPC` (target 0) and relays to all other ready peers except the sender (:83632-83644, :83603-83619). `HandleRoutedRPC` with `m_targetZDO.IsNone()` looks up `m_functions` and silently drops on miss (:83646-83654); `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (:83667-83679). Shout chat, by contrast, is addressed per player through `CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` (self + each listed player, :41983-42040), so a solo shout never leaves the client when a RelationsProvider exists — the contrast claim holds (it goes to 0L only when `RelationsProvider == null`, :41999-42002). Ping call sites confirmed: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick` (:58516-58524), `OnMapDblClick` with `m_selectedType == PinType.Ping` (:58478-58489), large-map `JoyButtonX` (:56999-57002). Anchor-creation cites are correct: `CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int)` (:76674-76682) already calls `AddIfPortal` with the passed hash (:76686-76688) but does NOT call `SetPrefab` — that must follow (:73808-73815); `Persistent` is a public settable flag (:73323-73338); `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` (:151944); `IsLavaPreHeightmap` (:115637-115645); `GetAllCharacterZDOS` (:81024-81044); `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` (:78794). CORRECTIONS: (1) 'sender's verified identity' is wrong at the HandleRoutedRPC layer: `m_senderPeerID` is read verbatim from the packet (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize`, :83487-83495) and passed to handlers unchanged (:83651); a modded client can forge it. Prefix `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` instead and resolve identity from the socket via the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504). (2) A fabricated 'anchor' created with a portal prefab hash is a full vanilla portal: clients in range instantiate the piece, it enters `m_portalObjects` and `Game.ConnectPortals` reconciliation, and it is visible/interactable. It is not a hidden anchor. (3) Ping y is the SENDER's altitude, not terrain at the target; never use it. (4) The server-side `Register` collision concern is moot on a dedicated server (no Chat/Hud instance), but the HandleRoutedRPC/RPC_RoutedRPC prefix is still the right choice for the identity reason above.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Channel verified end to end. `Chat.SendPing` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")` with `vector.y` = local player y (CLIENT:42058-42071). Call sites: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick` (CLIENT:58581-58585), `OnMapDblClick` with Ping pin (CLIENT:58546-58549), gamepad `JoyButtonX` on large map (CLIENT:57060-57063). `InvokeRoutedRPC` with `targetPeerID == 0` handles locally AND `RouteRPC`s (SERVER:83587-83594) so the server always receives it. Server `RPC_RoutedRPC` handles target-0 locally (no `Chat` handler → `m_functions.TryGetValue` miss → silently dropped) then relays to all other ready peers (SERVER:83632-83644, 83646-83665). `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (SERVER:83668-83670) so a duplicate name throws — prefix advice is sound. `UserInfo` is `ISerializableParameter` with `Name` + `UserId` (SERVER:72774-72800). Client `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` calls `ZDOMan.RequestZDO` itself when the target ZDO is missing (CLIENT:144380-144396), so no push is needed. Corrections: (1) 'sender's verified identity' is FALSE at the `HandleRoutedRPC` level: `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is read straight from the packet (SERVER:83487-83495) and never overwritten by `RPC_RoutedRPC`. Vanilla clients are honest, but the honest hook is a prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (SERVER:83632) resolving the peer from `rpc` (`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)`, private, SERVER:80504) — also the only place the mod can distinguish the server's own local `HandleRoutedRPC` calls from network ones. (2) The route write is undone by `Game.ConnectPortals` within 5 s unless the two portals' `s_tag` values are equal (SERVER:100596-100605) — the option leans entirely on the address-book prereq for that. (3) The 'fabricated anchor' is a REAL portal ZDO: `CreateNewZDO(pos, hash)` registers it in `m_portalObjects` via `AddIfPortal` (SERVER:76684-76692) but does not set `m_prefab` or `Persistent` (caller must `SetPrefab`+`Persistent=true`); every vanilla client in range instantiates a visible `portal_wood` at that spot; it participates in `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (SERVER:100664-100680) — note vanilla does NOT skip empty tags, so an untagged anchor pairs with any other untagged portal. (4) Height from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` ignores player terraforming and buildings; the spawned portal can clip into a base. (5) Server-only `nomap`/NoMap worlds have no map to ping. Enforcement claim is honest for the route write itself.

catalog.name: Animator SetTrigger as a real-time gesture channel (jump, dodge, forsaken power)
catalog.oneLine: Every jump, dodge-roll and forsaken-power activation is broadcast as a routed RPC that passes through the dedicated server carrying the player's character ZDOID — a zero-latency, zero-polling gesture input absent from the research digest.
catalog.howItWorks:
NEW FINDING, verified. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger(string name)` is `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (:87260-87263). `ZNetView.Everybody` is 0, and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…)` becomes `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, m_zdo.m_uid, "SetTrigger", name)` (:82850). `targetPeerID == 0` → the client handles locally AND calls `RouteRPC`, sending it to the server; the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) sees `m_targetPeerID == 0`, calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (dropped — `ZNetScene.FindInstance` is null server-side, :83659) and relays to every other peer. A Harmony PREFIX on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage)` therefore sees every animation trigger from every player, one hop, no polling.

Payload: `(ZDOID m_targetZDO = the character's ZDO, string name)`. Map ZDOID → player via `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` → `peer.m_characterID`, then `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (:78539) for stable identity and `GetPosition()` for where.

VERIFIED VOCABULARY: `"jump"` (`Character.ForceJump` :3483, every spacebar press) · `"dodge"` (Player roll :15196) · `"gpower"` (forsaken power :15717, cooldown-limited, unmistakable as a commit) · `"eat"` (:7705/:7766) · `"interact"` (:7659) · `"equip_hip"` (:8749/:8777) · `"attach"`/`"detach"`/`"attack_abort"`/`"stagger"`.

GRAMMAR: per-playerId ring of (trigger, time, position). JUMP×3 within 4 s while within 6 m of a portal and having moved <2 m between jumps = advance; JUMP×2 = back; `gpower` = commit. Combine with the crouch bit for a 2×N modal menu.

WHY IT BEATS EMOTES: `Player.StartEmote` requires `CanMove() && !InAttack() && !IsDrawingBow() && !IsAttached() && !IsAttachedToShip()` (:15585-15590) and is observed only by POLLING `s_emoteID` (:78419). `SetTrigger` is pushed, arrives in one hop, needs no emote wheel, and works while moving.
catalog.playerExperience:
You stand in front of your portal, tag `"Base"`. You jump — nothing. You jump twice more inside four seconds and a toast appears: `Base → next: Haldor (2/5)`. Three more jumps: `Base → next: Mine2 (3/5)`. You crouch to confirm and a toast reads `Locked in: Mine2`; the tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows.

About eight seconds of hopping in place, which looks exactly like a player being impatient. No UI opened, no typing, works with a full load of ore, works on a controller.

The forsaken-power variant is one gesture: stand at the portal, hit your power key, toast reads `Committed → Mine2`. Unmistakable, un-accidental, naturally rate-limited — but it burns your Eikthyr/Elder power, which most players will resent.

Honest assessment: jumping-as-a-menu is the most embarrassing-looking mechanic in this document. It works, it is fast, it needs nothing — and a new player watching a veteran hop three times and vanish will have no idea what happened. Power-user shortcut layered over a legible primary input, never the primary.
failureModes: Every jump on the server becomes a mod event; a player bunny-hopping near a portal trips the window constantly. Require proximity <6 m AND near-stationarity between jumps AND an armed state.
Triggers fire on the OWNING client only; a dead, teleporting or attached player produces none (`Player.CanMove()` is false while `m_teleporting`, :14423).
`"jump"` also fires from knockback and the grappling hook via `ForceJump`, so it is not purely voluntary.
The prefix must not consume the ZPackage read position — deserialize a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) or vanilla's relay of the same packet reads garbage.
`m_senderPeerID` is spoofable; resolve identity from `m_targetZDO` (the real character ZDOID) instead.
This prefix runs on EVERY routed RPC on a busy server. Compare the int method hash first and return immediately.
openQuestions: Does the dedicated server ever hold a ZNetView for a character ZDO such that `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches rather than dropping? It should not (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). IN-GAME: log `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()` (:82334) on a live server.
How many `SetTrigger` packets per second does a busy 10-player server carry? Determines whether the hot-path hash compare is acceptable. IN-GAME: count for 60 s.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Animator SetTrigger as a real-time gesture channel (jump, dodge, forsaken power)
corrections: Jump and dodge are blocked when encumbered (Character.Jump :3406-3410; Player.UpdateDodge :15186) — 'works with a full load of ore' holds only below the weight limit.
ForceJump clears the crouch toggle (SetCrouch(false), :3487); any crouch+jump grammar must latch the armed state on the crouch edge server-side.
"gpower" requires m_guardianSE != null and cooldown == 0 (:15702-15716); unavailable to players without a forsaken power.
Sender/target identity in the routed packet is client-supplied (:83487-83495); verify by hooking RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) and matching ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc).m_characterID to data.m_targetZDO.
ZSyncAnimation.Awake registration line is :87157-87158 (Register<string>("SetTrigger")); fine as cited.

Crouch cannot be held across jumps: `ForceJump` → `SetCrouch(false)` (SERVER:3486) → `UpdateCrouch` writes `crouching=0` (SERVER:15669-15672). The '2×N modal menu with the crouch bit' must be redesigned as a latched arm state; drop the concurrent-modifier framing.

Hook `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:83632), not `HandleRoutedRPC`, and take identity from the `ZRpc` peer; verify `m_targetZDO == peer.m_characterID` — both `m_senderPeerID` and `m_targetZDO` are packet fields (SERVER:83487-83495).
Filter on character ZDOIDs before deserializing: all creature ZSyncAnimation triggers from all clients traverse the same RPC (SERVER:87157 registers `SetTrigger` on every ZSyncAnimation).
`"jump"` also fires on out-of-stamina and swimming jumps (SERVER:3412-3457); the '<2 m between jumps' rule must allow the forward impulse of `m_jumpForceForward` (SERVER:3450).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger(string)` is exactly `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (:87260-87263); `ZNetView.Everybody = 0L` (:82535); `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long, …)` → `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetID, m_zdo.m_uid, …)` (:82850-82853). With target 0 the client handles locally and calls `RouteRPC` (:83587-83594), which on a client sends to all peers = the server (:83621-83627). Server `RPC_RoutedRPC` calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (target 0) then relays to every other ready peer (:83632-83644, :83610-83619). `HandleRoutedRPC` resolves the ZDO and `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83656-83663), which is a `m_instances.TryGetValue` (:82229-82236) and is null server-side, so the trigger is dropped there but a prefix on `RPC_RoutedRPC` or `HandleRoutedRPC` sees it. Vocabulary confirmed as `m_zanim.SetTrigger` (networked) calls: "jump" (`Character.ForceJump`, :3483), "dodge" (`Player.UpdateDodge`, :15196), "gpower" (`Player.StartGuardianPower`, :15717), "eat" (:7705, :7766), "interact" (:7659), "equip_hip" (:8749, :8777), "stagger" (:2851), "attack_abort"/"detach" (:23006, :23010), "attach" (:24045), plus attack animation names. Emotes do NOT use this channel: `StartEmote` writes `s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot` to the ZDO (:15591-15594) and `UpdateEmote` fires the trigger on the LOCAL `m_animator`, not `m_zanim` (:15611-15636) — so the 'beats emotes' argument is correct. `StartEmote` preconditions confirmed (:15585-15588). `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` (:78794), `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (:78539) exist. CORRECTIONS: (1) 'works with a full load of ore' is wrong when encumbered: `Character.Jump` returns immediately on `IsEncumbered()` (:3406-3410) and `UpdateDodge` also requires `!IsEncumbered()` (:15186) — an over-weight-limit player cannot emit jump or dodge at all. (2) `ForceJump` calls `SetCrouch(false)` (:3487) — any grammar combining jump with the crouch bit must latch the crouch server-side; it cannot be a held modifier. (3) "gpower" requires an equipped forsaken power (`m_guardianSE == null` → return, :15704-15707) and off-cooldown (:15712-15716); pre-Eikthyr players have no commit gesture. (4) Identity: `m_senderPeerID` and `m_targetZDO` are packet-supplied and unverified at HandleRoutedRPC (:83487-83495); use the `ZRpc` from `RPC_RoutedRPC` and `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504) then check `peer.m_characterID == data.m_targetZDO`. (5) Volume: the prefix sees every networked trigger for every client-owned character including monster attack animations; filter on character ZDOIDs first. (6) Non-player `Character.Jump` (AI) also emits "jump" — the ZDOID filter handles it.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Channel verified. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger(name)` = `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (SERVER:87260-87263); `Everybody = 0L` (SERVER:83498); `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…)` = `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetID, m_zdo.m_uid, method, parameters)` (SERVER:82850-82853). `InvokeRoutedRPC` with target 0 handles locally and `RouteRPC`s to the client's only peer, the server (SERVER:83587-83594); server `RPC_RoutedRPC` calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (drops: `ZNetScene.FindInstance` null server-side, SERVER:83656-83663) then relays (SERVER:83632-83644). Vocabulary confirmed: `"jump"` in `Character.ForceJump` reached from `Character.Jump` (SERVER:3406-3490); `"dodge"` in `Player.UpdateDodge` (SERVER:15183-15200); `"gpower"` in `StartGuardianPower` only after the cooldown/precondition checks (SERVER:15702-15717); the others at the cited lines. `StartEmote` gates and `s_emoteID` polling confirmed (SERVER:15585-15599). `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` (SERVER:78794), `GetAllCharacterZDOS` (SERVER:81024-81044), `s_playerID` (SERVER:78539) all exist. Corrections: (1) 'Combine with the crouch bit for a 2×N modal menu' is impossible as a held modifier: `ForceJump` calls `SetCrouch(crouch: false)` (SERVER:3486) and `UpdateCrouch` then writes `crouching=false` (SERVER:15669-15672); `StartEmote` also clears crouch (SERVER:15591). Crouch can only be a one-shot latch, not a concurrent modifier. (2) Identity: `m_senderPeerID` and `m_targetZDO` are packet-supplied (SERVER:83487-83495); hook `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:83632), resolve the peer from `rpc`, and require `data.m_targetZDO == peer.m_characterID` — otherwise a routed trigger targeting some other creature's ZDO is attributed to a player. (3) Volume: every creature owned by every client routes its triggers through the same path (stagger, attack_abort, eat…); the prefix must filter by character ZDOID before deserializing parameters. (4) `"jump"` fires on failed-stamina jumps too (`ForceJump` runs with reduced force, SERVER:3451-3457) and while swimming (SERVER:3412) — fine for a gesture, but 'having moved <2 m' must tolerate the forward jump impulse. (5) Enforcement label is a category confusion — this is an input; the resulting route write is server-side. Keep server-enforced only in that sense.

catalog.name: Posture bits — crouch and block as a silent modifier key
catalog.oneLine: Crouching and raising a shield are each mirrored into the character ZDO as a live boolean the server can poll — a hands-free arming gate that costs one keypress.
catalog.howItWorks:
NEW FINDING, verified. `Player.UpdateCrouch` calls `m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching, …)` where `s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (:9984, :15667, :15671). `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool(int hash, bool)` does, when `m_nview.IsOwner()`, `zdo.AddSessionHash(438569 + hash); zdo.Set(438569 + hash, value ? 1 : 0)` (:87270-87281); the salt is the literal `c_ZDOSalt = 438569` (:87144). Server read:

  int key = 438569 + UnityEngine.Animator.StringToHash("crouching");
  bool crouching = characterZdo.GetInt(key) != 0;

`Animator.StringToHash` is a pure static in UnityEngine.AnimationModule, callable headless. The key is registered as a SESSION hash so `ZDOExtraData.GetSaveData` strips it from disk (:75507), but session hashes are NOT filtered from `ZDO.Serialize` — the value is live on the wire every tick.

Second bit, already a named constant: `ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash` = `"IsBlocking"` (:78463), written on the character ZDO at :8690/:8708. Third, analogue: `ZDOVars.s_stealth` (:78613) written at :16372.

USE: poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.2 s. Crouch alone as the ARMING gate for the ping and jump channels solves their biggest problem — accidental activation — at essentially zero cost. Crouch is a TOGGLE in Valheim (`m_crouchToggled`, `SetCrouch` :15675) so the armed state can be held indefinitely with no input strain; block is momentary (held mouse button) so it suits a transient 'show me detail' mode.

IMPORTANT: `UpdateCrouch` calls `SetCrouch(false)` when `IsBlocking()` (:15662), so the crouch+block combination is UNREACHABLE. Three modes exist, not four.
catalog.playerExperience:
You walk to your portal. Nothing happens — you are standing normally and the server is ignoring you. You press crouch (default Ctrl) and a toast appears instantly: `Portal armed — jump to cycle, crouch again to commit.` Your character is visibly crouching, which IS the feedback: anyone watching can see you are 'in the menu'.

You jump. `1/5 Base`. Jump. `2/5 Haldor`. You raise your shield and the toast expands to `2/5 Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest · open`. You lower it, press crouch again, and the toast reads `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows.

Six seconds, no menu, no typing, one hand.

The honest problems: crouching is something players do constantly for sneaking, so ARMED fires whenever anyone sneaks past a portal — it needs a proximity gate and a 15 s auto-disarm. And crouch-as-a-modifier is invisible to a new player; nothing in the game hints that crouching near a portal means anything. This is a shortcut for people who already know.
failureModes: Crouch is a common movement action; without tight proximity gating and auto-disarm, arming fires constantly.
`IsBlocking()` forces crouch off (:15662) — crouch+block is unreachable, so only three of four states exist.

`UpdateCrouch` also clears crouch on `!HaveStamina() || IsSwimming() || InBed() || InPlaceMode() || m_run || IsFlying()` (:15662), so the armed state silently drops when the player sprints or runs out of stamina.

The write depends on `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool` running, which it does whenever the owner's `UpdateCrouch` runs — but never hard-code the resulting integer key; `Animator.StringToHash` is Unity-internal and only stable within one build.
Session hashes are stripped from the save, so the armed state does not survive a relog — correct behaviour, but no persistent flag is possible here.
openQuestions: Is `"crouching"` in the Player prefab's `ZSyncAnimation.m_syncBools` list? Irrelevant to the server READ (SetBool writes whenever owner) but determines whether other players see the animation. IN-GAME: log `characterZdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching"))` while a player toggles crouch.
What is the full contents of the Player prefab's m_syncBools/m_syncFloats/m_syncInts? Each entry is another free server-readable player-state bit. IN-GAME: dump from a client at world-ready.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Posture bits — crouch and block as a silent modifier key
corrections: Crouch cannot be a HELD modifier across jumps or blocks: ForceJump → SetCrouch(false) (:3487) and UpdateCrouch → SetCrouch(false) when IsBlocking() (:15662). Latch ARMED on the crouch rising edge with a TTL; the described crouch→jump→block→crouch sequence only works with latching.

Crouch toggle is additionally cleared on !HaveStamina(), IsSwimming(), InBed(), InPlaceMode(), m_run, IsFlying() (:15660); the anim bool reads 0 during attacks/bow-draw even while toggled (:15665-15667).
IsBlocking ZDO bit requires an equipped item that can block; the write is inside the current-blocker branch (:8686-8710).

Crouch cannot coexist with the jump channel: `ForceJump` → `SetCrouch(false)` (SERVER:3486) and `UpdateCrouch` immediately writes `crouching=0` (SERVER:15669-15672). Replace 'live crouch = armed' with a server-side latch set on the crouch rising edge, TTL-expired; the playerExperience sequence as written reads a bit that is already 0 by the second step.
Crouch is also force-cleared by run, no stamina, swim, block, fly, place mode (SERVER:15660-15663) and emotes (SERVER:15591); 'held indefinitely' only while idle.
'Crouch again to commit' after a jump is a rising edge identical to arming — needs an explicit state machine, not edge detection alone.
Block bit requires an equipped blocker and is suppressed during attack/dodge/place-mode/encumbrance/minor actions (SERVER:8673-8681).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Data path verified. `Player.s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (:9984) where `GetHash` is `Animator.StringToHash` (:87196-87199). `Player.UpdateCrouch` calls `m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching, …)` (:15667, :15671) and forces `SetCrouch(false)` when `IsBlocking()` among other conditions (:15662). `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool(int,bool)` writes only on animator-state change and only when `IsOwner()`: `AddSessionHash(438569 + hash); Set(438569 + hash, value ? 1 : 0)` (:87270-87281); `c_ZDOSalt = 438569` (:87144). `ZDO.Serialize` reads via `ZDOExtraData.GetData` with no session filter (:74112-74140) while `GetSaveData` uses `GetValuesOrEmptyFilterSession` (:75505-75512) — session keys are on the wire, not on disk, as claimed. The character ZDO is already flushed at 0.05 s by the owner because of position updates, so latency is ~50 ms + RTT. `IsBlocking` ZDO write confirmed: `Set(ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash, true/false)` (:8690, :8708) via `Set(int,bool)` → int (:73685-73688); `s_isBlockingHash = "IsBlocking"` (:78463). `s_stealth` float write confirmed (:16372, :78613). `GetAllCharacterZDOS` (:81024-81044). CORRECTIONS: (1) The playerExperience script is contradicted by the decompile: `Character.ForceJump` calls `SetCrouch(false)` (:3487) and `UpdateCrouch` drops the toggle on `IsBlocking()` (:15662). So 'crouch to arm, jump to cycle, raise shield for detail, crouch again to commit' cannot use crouch as a held modifier — the first jump or block un-crouches and the bit goes to 0 on the next tick. Design must latch ARMED on the crouch rising edge with a TTL (the option's own 15 s auto-disarm) and treat the second crouch edge as commit. (2) Crouch toggle is also dropped on `!HaveStamina() || IsSwimming() || InBed() || InPlaceMode() || m_run || IsFlying()` (:15660), and the anim bool reads false during `InAttack() || IsDrawingBow()` even while toggled (:15665-15667). (3) Blocking requires an equipped blocker; the write happens inside the block-update branch guarded by a current blocker (:8686-8692). (4) `UpdateCrouch` runs only on the owning client's Player, so the bit reflects the owner's local state — which is the intended source; no server-side Animator is required since the read is a raw `zdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching"))`, and UnityEngine.AnimationModule.dll ships in the server lib set.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Bits verified. `Player.s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (SERVER:9984); `UpdateCrouch` calls `m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching, …)` every frame (SERVER:15658-15673); `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool(int,bool)` writes `AddSessionHash(438569+hash)` + `zdo.Set(438569+hash, 0/1)` when the animator value changes and `IsOwner()` (SERVER:87270-87281); `c_ZDOSalt = 438569` (SERVER:87144); `GetHash` is `Animator.StringToHash` (SERVER:87194-87197). Session hashes are filtered only in `GetSaveData` (SERVER:75505-75512) while `ZDO.Serialize` uses unfiltered `GetData` (SERVER:74112-74114) — so the bit is on the wire and off the disk, as claimed. Block: `Humanoid.UpdateBlock` writes `s_isBlockingHash` on state change (SERVER:8685-8709); non-owner `IsBlocking()` reads the same key (SERVER:8667-8672). `s_stealth` written from the stealth update (SERVER:16372). `UpdateCrouch` drops crouch when `IsBlocking()` (SERVER:15662) — three modes, not four, confirmed. Client flush cadence 0.05 s (SERVER:76843-76860) so ~50 ms + ½ RTT to the server. Refutation of the grammar: the described flow 'crouch → armed, jump → cycle, crouch again → commit' cannot be read as live posture. `Character.ForceJump` calls `SetCrouch(crouch: false)` (SERVER:3486), so the first jump clears `m_crouchToggled` and the ZDO bit flips to 0 within a frame (SERVER:15669-15672). Crouch is ALSO dropped by running, no stamina, swimming, blocking, flying, place mode (SERVER:15660-15663) and by any emote (SERVER:15591). 'Held indefinitely with no input strain' is only true while standing still doing nothing. The ARM state must therefore be a server-side latch set on a crouch rising edge with a TTL — which the option's own 15 s auto-disarm already implies but its prose contradicts. Also: after a jump the player is standing, so 'crouch again to commit' is a fresh toggle-on rising edge, indistinguishable from re-arming — the grammar needs a state machine, not two edges of one bit. Block requires an equipped blocker (`GetCurrentBlocker`, SERVER:8681) and `IsBlocking()` is false during attack/dodge/place-mode/encumbered/minor action (SERVER:8673-8676). Effort 'small' is fair for the read; the state machine is the real cost.

catalog.name: Emote signalling near a portal
catalog.oneLine: The player uses a vanilla emote while standing at a portal; the server polls the character ZDO's emote counter and treats each of 24 emotes as a command token.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Player.StartEmote(string emote, bool oneshot)` writes three fields on the player's own character ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_emoteID` incremented (:78419), `ZDOVars.s_emote` = the lowercased enum name (:78417), `ZDOVars.s_emoteOneshot` (:78421) — see :15585-15599. `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty name (:15601-15609). No RPC; the change reaches the server as ZDO data within one 0.05 s client flush.

SERVER LOOP: reuse Wonderland's `EmoteSignals` verbatim (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:38/:46/:125) — every 0.25 s, for each `ConnectedCharacters.All()` entry read `s_emoteID`; if it differs from cache, read `s_emote` and dispatch. Seed the counter on first sighting so a pre-existing emote does not fire a phantom command. Ignore empty names.

VOCABULARY: 24 usable emotes (`enum Emotes` :6216-6246). A sane portal mapping: Point → next destination · ThumbsUp → confirm · NoNoNo → cancel · Wave → list destinations as toasts · Challenge → lock/unlock · Shrug → status. Bind to the nearest managed portal within 6 m via `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643) and the character ZDO position.

WHY SECOND-CHOICE: `StartEmote` refuses when `!CanMove() || InAttack() || IsDrawingBow() || IsAttached() || IsAttachedToShip()` (:15587) — no emoting while seated, on a boat, mid-swing or mid-teleport. The emote wheel is a real UI the player must open; typing `/point` is faster but requires knowing the names, and an unknown name is silently swallowed by the client's own `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:41947-41955). The 0.25 s poll adds a perceptible beat, and 24 tokens is far more than anyone will memorise — realistically 4-6 are usable.

It is nevertheless completely reliable, independent of player count, and the one channel Wonderland has already shipped and live-tested in production (`CacheClaimControl.cs`, `SupplySwitch.cs`).
catalog.playerExperience:
You stand at your portal, hold the emote key, and pick Wave. Your character waves. About a third of a second later five toasts stack up:

`1 Base      612m`
`2 Haldor  1,140m`
`3 Mine2     840m`
`4 Bog      3,010m`
`Point to cycle · ThumbsUp to confirm`

You emote Point: `▸ 1 Base (612m)`. Point again: `▸ 2 Haldor (1,140m)`. On the one you want you emote ThumbsUp: `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows, the tag flips to `>Haldor`.

Twelve to fifteen seconds, because opening the wheel and picking takes two to three seconds each time and every emote plays a full animation. Visibly slower than typing into the portal.

The upside: entirely mouse-driven, works on a controller, and your character is visibly doing something — a bystander sees you pointing at a portal and can guess what is happening, which is more than the jump or crouch channels offer.
failureModes: `StartEmote` returns false and writes nothing while attached, on a ship, attacking, drawing a bow, or unable to move (:15587). The player gets no feedback that the command was swallowed.
0.25 s polling collapses two emotes in one tick into one observed event. Read the `s_emoteID` DELTA — a jump of 2 means a step was missed, and the mod should say so rather than silently mis-advance.
Emotes are social: waving hello beside a portal fires a directory dump. Proximity gating plus an armed state is mandatory.
`Sit`, `Rest`, `Relax`, `Vibe` are non-oneshot (`[Emote(OneShot=false)]`, :6219) and latch; the following `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty string that must be ignored.
24 tokens is beyond memorisation; only 4-6 are practical.
Two players emoting at the same portal inside one tick are indistinguishable in ordering.
openQuestions: Does the emote WHEEL expose all 24 enum entries or a subset, with the rest reachable only by typing `/<emote>`? This decides the practical vocabulary size. IN-GAME: open the wheel and count.
