corrections: Vocabulary is 25 emotes, not 24: enum Emotes (:6216-6246) has Wave..LoveYou = 25 named members before Count, and the client registers exactly 25 console commands (`for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++)` at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45370).

'an unknown name is silently swallowed by Terminal.TryRunCommand (:41947-41955)' is wrong twice: :41947-41955 is Chat.InputText, and the client's Terminal.TryRunCommand (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45734-45759) prints "'x' is not a recognized command. Type 'help'..." locally (:45758) unless silentFail — it is not silent, just never networked.

StartEmote calls SetCrouch(crouch:false) before writing (:15590): any arming scheme built on the crouch bit is cancelled by the emote itself; sequence the arming gesture so crouch is not required to persist through the emote.
Every emote produces two counter bumps (StartEmote then StopEmote with empty name); the mod must ignore empty s_emote exactly as EmoteSignals does or every command double-fires.
Vocabulary is 25 emotes, not 24: enum Emotes (:6216-6246) lists Wave..LoveYou = 25 entries before Count, and the console-command loop is `for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++)` (:45370). LoveYou was omitted.

An unknown /command is NOT silently swallowed: Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45757) prints "'x' is not a recognized command. Type 'help'..." into the player's own chat window (silentFail defaults false). Harmless but visible.

Player.StartEmote calls SetCrouch(crouch: false) (:15591) before writing the ZDO. Any design that uses crouch as the 'arming gesture' (a prereq of the sibling equipped-item and positional options) is cancelled by the very emote meant to confirm; ThumbsUp-to-confirm and crouch-to-arm cannot coexist in one flow.

Poll aliasing: s_emoteID is a counter; two emotes inside one 0.25 s window (possible via two chat commands, since InEmote() is not in StartEmote's refuse list :15587) arrive as a counter jump of 2 with only the LAST name readable. Wonderland's poller (EmoteSignals.cs:72-84) treats any delta as one event, so the first command is dropped. Acceptable, but document it; lowering the poll to 0.1 s does not fully close it.

Only Sit is non-oneshot ([Emote(OneShot=false)] :6219); it writes s_emoteOneshot=false and is ended by StopEmote bumping the counter with '' (:15603-15608), which the poller must ignore (it does). Sit is therefore a poor command token because standing up produces a second counter change.

Toast delivery relies on Player's routed "Message" RPC (registered :10072, handler RPC_Message :14820) — exists and is targeted at the player's own character ZDO; Wonderland PlayerNotify.cs:24 uses it. Fine, but that is a separate prereq that the option folds in silently.
evidence: Client emote console commands loop — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45370-45377; emote wheel Emote.DoEmote — :166405
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified in the server decompile. Player.StartEmote (:15585-15599) gates on !CanMove()||InAttack()||IsDrawingBow()||IsAttached()||IsAttachedToShip(), calls SetCrouch(false), then writes s_emoteID (+1), s_emote (string), s_emoteOneshot into the player's own character ZDO via m_nview.GetZDO().Set — no RPC. StopEmote (:15601-15609) bumps s_emoteID again with s_emote="". ZDO.Set → IncreaseDataRevision → ZDOMan.ClientChanged on non-server, so the change is queued to the server regardless of distance (:77727, :77241-77258). Emote.DoEmote (:6207-6214) writes emote.ToString().ToLower(). Both client input paths exist: console commands registered in a `for (i < 25)` loop (client :45370-45377) and the emote wheel (client :166405). Wonderland EmoteSignals.cs (:38 Register, :46 OnUpdate, :125 Is) does exactly the 0.25 s counter-diff poll with first-sighting seed and empty-name skip, consumed by CacheClaimControl.cs:18 and SupplySwitch.cs:40. Execution context is correct: the server only reads ZDO ints/strings on ZDOs it already holds for every connected peer (ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS :81024-81044). Enforcement: the emote is a client-originated signal, but the resulting dial (tag/connection write on the portal ZDO) is a server write — 'should this ROUTE be open' form — so server-enforced for the dial holds; the transit itself stays client-executed as for every option. Errors found: emote count and the unknown-command claim.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds end to end. Player.StartEmote (SERVER:15585-15599) writes s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot on the owning client's character ZDO; ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision -> ZDOMan.ClientChanged (:73720-73727, :77727) queues it for the 0.05 s client flush (:76843), distance-independent. Emote.DoEmote (:6207-6214) is reached from the radial wheel (RadialMenu.EmoteElement :165660-165676) and from 25 chat console commands registered in a loop `for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++)` (:45370-45376) that Chat.isAllowedCommand permits (:41938-41945, only cheats rejected). Wonderland EmoteSignals (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:31-100) implements exactly the seed-then-diff poll and ignores empty names from StopEmote (:15601-15609). The dial action is a route-form write (server owns the connection field), so 'server-enforced' is honest. Attacks that failed: nothing in the vanilla 5 s reconcile, zone loading, or ownership migration touches character ZDOs (players are always self-owned); emote keys are session-irrelevant because character ZDOs are non-persistent, so no save/reload concern. Attacks that landed are corrections only: vocabulary count wrong, 'silently swallowed' wrong, StartEmote un-crouches the player, and poll aliasing.

catalog.name: Equipped item as a destination selector
catalog.oneLine: Hold a specific item while touching the portal; its prefab hash is already in your character ZDO, so the server reads which one and dials the matching destination.
catalog.howItWorks:
`VisEquipment` mirrors every VISIBLE equipped item into the character's own ZDO as a prefab stable hash: `s_rightItem` (+variant/quality), `s_leftItem`, `s_helmetItem`, `s_chestItem`, `s_legItem`, `s_shoulderItem`, `s_utilityItem`, `s_trinketItem`, `s_leftBackItem`, `s_rightBackItem` — written at :20569-20708 by the owning client. Server reads `characterZdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_rightItem)` and resolves via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` (:82045).

SCHEME: a binding table `itemPrefabHash → destination` (server config or per-player). Torch = home, Cultivator = farm, a boss trophy = that boss's altar (resolvable server-side from `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` :113295 via `FindClosestLocation` :115707). Poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.25 s; when an ARMED player within 6 m of a managed portal changes `s_rightItem`, dial.

WHY IT IS INTERESTING: it is the only channel that is simultaneously zero extra actions (players swap items constantly), physically legible (everyone can SEE what you hold), and thematically native (hold the key to the door). A row of stone portals where you show a Fine Wood for the Meadows and a Black Metal for the Plains reads as a game mechanic rather than a mod UI. The back slots (`s_leftBackItem`/`s_rightBackItem`) are also visible, doubling the vocabulary without the player holding anything awkward.

CRITICAL LIMIT: this reads EQUIPPED items only. A living player's inventory is never mirrored into any ZDO — `ZDOVars.s_items` (:78475) is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save` (:122293-122300), and an exhaustive scan of Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO writes yields only vitals, identity, pose and equipment visuals. So 'carry a key item' cannot be a requirement, only 'hold' one, and nothing can be charged.
catalog.playerExperience:
You are at your base portal holding a Bronze Axe and you want the mine. You open your inventory, right-click your Antler Pickaxe to equip it, close the inventory, and step toward the portal.

As the pickaxe goes into your hand a toast reads `Pickaxe → Mine2 (840m). Step through.` The tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows. You walk through.

At the mine you swap back to the axe and the return portal reads `Axe → Base`. You never opened a menu, never typed, and the thing in your hand is the thing that tells you where you are going. A friend watching sees you draw a pickaxe and walk into a portal, and understands the rule the first time they see it.

The failure is equally concrete: you arrive at the portal holding a Draugr Fang because you were fighting on the way, and the portal silently re-dials itself. Hence the arming gate — crouch, swap, un-crouch — or bind only to items nobody carries by accident.

Jank rating: low-to-medium. It feels like a game mechanic rather than a workaround, which is rare in this list.
failureModes: Equipping happens constantly in normal play; without an arming gate a player re-dials portals by fighting near them.
Only VISIBLE slots are in the ZDO — backpack contents are invisible, so no 'must be carrying X' requirement and no fee.
`VisEquipment`'s read-back branches on `m_isPlayer` (:20857-20885), an Inspector bool; some slots may not be written for a Player specifically.
The binding table has to be taught — nothing in the game indicates a Cultivator means anything to a portal.
Two portals within 6 m are ambiguous; bind to the nearest and name it in the toast.
Requires `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` to be non-null on a dedicated server.
openQuestions: Is `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood")` (and item prefabs generally) non-null on a 1.0.7 dedicated server? IN-GAME: log it at the ZNetScene.Awake postfix.
Are the shoulder/trinket/back slots actually written for a Player, or gated by `m_isPlayer` paths a real Player never takes? IN-GAME: equip each slot and dump the character ZDO's int fields.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Equipped item as a destination selector
corrections: Only VISIBLE equipment is mirrored, and visibility is state-dependent: sheathing (hide hands) moves the item hash from s_rightItem/s_leftItem (set to 0) to s_rightBackItem/s_leftBackItem, and setters only fire on change (`m_leftItem != itemHash` guard). The mod should treat hand+back slots as one 'carried visible' set or the selector flips when the player sheathes on approach.

Citation nit: :20590-20591 is SetRightItemVisual (a visual-only setter), not SetRightItem proper; the equivalent in-hand write for the right item is the s_rightItem/s_rightItemQuality Set pair inside SetRightItem a few lines above it. Same effect, different method.

Materials and trophies cannot be held: ItemDrop.ItemData.IsEquipable (:69450-69457) admits only Tool, One/TwoHandedWeapon(Left), Bow, Shield, Helmet, Chest, Legs, Shoulder, Ammo, Torch, Utility, Trinket. 'Show a Fine Wood for the Meadows', 'a Black Metal for the Plains' and 'a boss trophy = that boss's altar' are impossible on this channel. Vocabulary = tools, weapons, shields, torches, armour pieces, utility (belts/wishbone), trinkets. Ammo is equippable but is NOT mirrored by SetupVisEquipment (:8192-8215), so it is invisible to the server.
Torch = home reads the wrong key: torches are left-hand items (Humanoid.SetupAnimationState :8238-8246 treats Torch as m_leftItem); the server must read s_leftItem, not s_rightItem. Read both hands.

Sheathed weapons vanish from the hand keys: SetupVisEquipment writes m_hiddenLeftItem/m_hiddenRightItem into s_leftBackItem/s_rightBackItem (:8199-8200) and the hand keys become 0. A player who arrives with weapons put away (R) presents the item on their back, not in hand — the binding table must treat 'in hand OR on back' as the same token or the mechanic silently fails after the player sheathes to sprint.
ZNetScene.GetPrefab returns the PREFAB name (e.g. 'AxeBronze'), not the localized item name; the binding table must be keyed on prefab names.

Prereq 'Arming gesture' = crouch is readable server-side (Player writes m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching) :15667-15671 -> ZSyncAnimation.SetBool stores int at key 438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching") :87271-87281, marked session-only via AddSessionHash), but note Player.StartEmote force-uncrouches (:15591), so crouch-arm and emote-confirm cannot be combined.

The 'friend sees you draw a pickaxe' claim is true only when the item is drawn (in-hand slot); equipping a tool via right-click does put it in hand (Humanoid.EquipItem -> SetupEquipment :8217), so the flow described works.
evidence: VisEquipment.SetLeftItem — :20560-20573; SetRightItemVisual — :20586-20593; SetChestItem — :20628-20634; SetUtilityItem — :20704-20710; SetTrinketItem — :20713-20722; s_leftBackItem/s_rightBackItem writes — :20604, :20619

catalog.name: Item stand token board
catalog.oneLine: A row of vanilla item stands beside a portal; mounting an item on a stand selects that stand's destination, read from `ZDOVars.s_item` on the stand's own ZDO.
catalog.howItWorks:
`ItemStand.UpdateAttach` (on the stand's owning client) does `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_item, m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode())` plus `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO(itemData, zdo)` and `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetVisualItem", …)` (:131834-131854). Detach writes `Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0)` (:131824). `HaveAttachment()` is `GetInt(s_item) != 0` (:132018).

SERVER: discover stands like signs — `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 8f)` filtered to prefabs carrying `ItemStand`. Order deterministically by bearing around the portal then y. Poll `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item)` (:78465) at 0.5 s, or better catch it in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix. Stand index N occupied → destination N.

TWO ENCODINGS: (a) POSITIONAL — the stand index is the address, item identity irrelevant; simple, teachable, and a sign under each stand becomes its label. (b) SEMANTIC — the item's prefab hash is the address; one stand, N destinations.

PUSH NOTIFICATION FOR FREE: `"SetVisualItem"` is `InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, …)` (:131849), targetPeerID 0, so it also passes through the server as a relayed routed RPC carrying `(itemHash, variant, quality, orientation)` and the stand's ZDOID — catchable with the same `RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix as the animation triggers, matching `"SetVisualItem".GetStableHashCode()`. No polling needed.

HARD LIMIT — NO STACK COUNT. The 'stack count = index' idea does not work here: `UpdateAttach` sets `itemData.m_stack = 1` unconditionally (:131843) and mounts exactly one item. Stack encoding requires a Container.

SERVER WRITE-BACK: the mod can clear a stand (`SetOwner(GetSessionID())`, `Set(s_item,0)`, `Set(s_type,0)`, `ForceSendZDO`) — but the item is then GONE, because spawning the drop needs a live GameObject (`DropItem` at :131820). Never auto-clear a player's item; that is item destruction.
catalog.playerExperience:
Beside your hub you have five item stands in a row, each with a sign under it: `1 Base`, `2 Haldor`, `3 Mine2`, `4 Bog`, `5 Swamp`. You are holding a Torch.

You walk to stand 3, press E, and the torch mounts with the usual vanilla animation. Within half a second a toast reads `Dialed → Mine2 (840m)` and the portal lights up. You step through.

The torch is still sitting on stand 3 across the map — so your base portal is still pointed at Mine2, which is what you want. The board is a physical, persistent, at-a-glance record of where every portal in your hub currently points. Anyone walking into your base reads the routing state off the wall without hovering anything or knowing any commands.

To re-route you take the torch off stand 3 (`Mine2 released`) and put it on stand 2 (`Dialed → Haldor`).

The most physically satisfying scheme in this list and arguably better than a UI — it is a patch panel. Its costs are build effort (five stands plus five signs is a real project) and that it scales only as far as you are willing to build.
failureModes: An item on a stand is a persistent world object anyone can take; removing your torch silently un-dials your portal.
`m_stack = 1` is forced (:131843) — no stack-count encoding.
The server cannot return a mounted item; clearing `s_item` destroys it.
Stand ordering must derive from world position (bearing around the portal), never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers uids (:74552).
Stands inside a ward the player cannot access refuse the interaction client-side with no server-visible signal.
Two occupied stands need an explicit precedence rule (last-changed wins, via the Deserialize hook ordering).
openQuestions: Which item-stand prefabs exist and do they all carry the same ItemStand component (wall-mount vs floor vs armour stand)? IN-GAME: enumerate `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` for GameObjects with an ItemStand.
corrections: Vocabulary for the SEMANTIC encoding is far smaller than 'the item's prefab hash': ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131981) requires GetAttachPrefab(item.m_dropPrefab) != null (the item prefab must carry an 'attach' child) AND the type to be in m_supportedTypes / m_supportedItems. Raw materials (Coal, Wood, ore, Amber…) cannot be mounted; only weapons, tools, shields, torches, trophies and a few misc items can. The Torch example works; a 'Coal token' does not.

The SetVisualItem RPC is also fired on DETACH (DropItem :131825, RPC_DestroyAttachment) with all-zero args, so the RPC catcher receives clear events too — treat hash==0 as release, do not dispatch it as a selection.

Server write-back caveat should be stated in ownership terms: after a mod SetOwner(sessionID) on a stand, RPC_RequestOwn from a player is dropped on the server (no ZNetView) until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership within ≤2 s; a player pressing E in that window gets nothing and must retry.

Server write-back makes the stand dead for up to 2 s: ItemStand.UseItem (:131757-131775) sends RPC_RequestOwn to m_zdo.GetOwner() (ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) :82856-82858); if the mod has set owner = server session ID, the RPC lands on the server where HandleRoutedRPC finds no instance (:83646-83661) and is dropped, and UpdateAttach spins on IsOwner() (:131836) until ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s cadence :76870-76885) reassigns the stand to the nearby peer. Same handback applies to any 'proactive' server claim — the server cannot hold a stand near a player.

Client visual refresh after a server-side s_item write is slow: the client's ItemStand only re-reads the ZDO in InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f) (:131573), so a server-cleared stand keeps showing the item for up to 4 s unless the mod also sends the SetVisualItem routed RPC itself (ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0, standZdoId, "SetVisualItem", 0,0,0,0)). Since the option already says never auto-clear, this is informational.

SetVisualItem carries (hash, variant, quality, orientation) but NOT the stand index — the prefix must map RoutedRPCData.m_targetZDO back to the board slot; and the RPC is only fired by the attaching client, so a stand loaded from disk already populated produces no RPC — the 0.5 s poll (or a ZDO.Deserialize postfix) is still required for startup/relog state, the RPC is only an accelerator.

ZDOVars.s_item = "item" is at :78465 as cited; s_items = "items" (:78475) is the Container key — do not conflate; a stand ZDO also carries ItemDrop.SaveToZDO fields (durability, quality, variant, crafterID...) written at :131844.
evidence: ZNetView.InvokeRPC — :82850; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC — :83577-83594; ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC + HandleRoutedRPC (FindInstance null on server)
ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — :76874-76883 (2 s timer), :76901-76925 (body); IsInPeerActiveArea (uid==m_sessionID → server ref pos)

HaveAttachment is GetInt(s_item)!=0 (:132018); GetAttachedItem (:132027). ZDOVars.s_item="item" (:78465). [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited line holds. ItemStand.UpdateAttach (:131834-131854) writes s_item = prefab-name hash, forces m_stack = 1 (:131842), and fires InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetVisualItem", hash, variant, quality, orientation) (:131847). The only weak spots are the write-back caveat and the ownership dance, both of which the option under-describes.

catalog.name: Chest tokens — item type as destination, stack count as index
catalog.oneLine: Drop a specific item into a chest beside the portal; the server parses the chest's serialized inventory blob and reads item type AND stack size as a two-field command — the only channel that can also charge a fee.
catalog.howItWorks:
A Container's whole inventory is one serialized byte blob on its ZDO: `Container.Save` does `m_inventory.Save(pkg); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())` on every `OnContainerChanged` (:122286-122300); `ZDOVars.s_items` = `"items"` (:78475). Decode server-side with Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs), which builds a scratch `Inventory` over the blob — already shipped and tested.

Unlike an ItemStand, a Container DOES carry stack counts, so 'item type = destination, stack count = index' is available here and nowhere else: one Coal = network 'Mine', three Coal = slot 3 within it.

TIMING AND THE IN-USE GATE: `Container` runs `InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f)` (:121922) and `Load()` early-returns while `m_inUse` (:122305). `UpdateUseVisual` writes `ZDOVars.s_inUse` (`"InUse"`, :78673) into the ZDO when the client owns it (:121990-122001), so the server can SEE that the chest is open and must not write `s_items` during that window (Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy`). The player's deposit reaches the server as soon as their `Save()` fires and the ZDO flushes (≤0.05 s + ½ RTT), but the server's REPLY does not repaint on their screen until they close the chest.

TOLL VARIANT: because the server can also WRITE `s_items`, this is the only channel that can charge for a teleport — consume 1 Coal per long-range dial via `ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem`. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit can take an item from a player.

WRITE PROCEDURE: `if (zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_inUse) == 1) defer;` then `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, mutate the scratch inventory, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, newBlob)`, `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)`.
catalog.playerExperience:
There is a chest under your portal with a sign on it reading `DROP A TOKEN`. You open it — ordinary vanilla chest UI — drag two Coal in, and close it.

About a second later a toast reads `Coal x2 → Haldor (1,140m). Fee paid.` The portal glows. You look back at the chest: empty, the coal spent on the trip.

Drop in something unrecognised and the toast reads `Flint is not a token. Valid: Coal, Amber, Ruby.` and the flint is still there when you reopen. Drop Coal x7 with only five destinations: `Only 5 destinations. Coal x1-x5.` and the coal stays.

The unavoidable weirdness: if you keep the chest OPEN, nothing visibly changes inside it no matter what the server does, because vanilla refuses to reload a container's contents while its UI is up. You must close it to see the result. The toast fires immediately, so you are told what happened — you just cannot watch it happen.

Cost: open inventory, open chest, drag, close. Six or seven seconds, and it costs an item. High jank as routine navigation; excellent as an economy layer under a different primary input.
failureModes: `Container.Load` refuses while `m_inUse` (:122305), so the server's reply is invisible until the player closes the chest.
Writing `s_items` while the player has the chest open races their client's own Save and can destroy items. Always check `ZDOVars.s_inUse` first.
Chests are public containers; anyone can drop a token into someone else's control chest unless the mod gates on ward permission or `s_creator`.
The 1 s `CheckForChanges` cadence plus the flush means the observed deposit can lag a deposit-then-immediately-withdraw by enough to misread the state.
Charging a fee is a destructive operation on player property — it must be opt-in, clearly signed, and never silent.
openQuestions: Does a fresh chest write `s_items` promptly, or only after the owning client's first `OnContainerChanged` tick? Matters for a newly-built control chest. IN-GAME: build a chest, drop one item, and time how long until the server reads a non-null blob.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Chest tokens — item type as destination, stack count as index
corrections: Act on CLOSE, not on deposit: Save() fires on every inventory change while the chest is open, so a read-on-change design sees intermediate states (drag 1 Coal → 'Base', drag second → 'Haldor'). Trigger only on the s_inUse 1→0 transition (or require IsBusy()==false at read time as ZdoInventoryIO.Load already enforces) — the howItWorks text implies acting as soon as Save() fires.

Ownership window: after the mod's SetOwner(sessionID) write, a player's RPC_RequestOpen targets the server, which has no Container GameObject and drops it (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC → FindInstance null). ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership within ≤2 s; a player who presses E in that window gets no OpenResponse and must retry. Same behaviour Wonderland already tolerates; document it.

Race at open: s_inUse=1 is written only after RPC_OpenResponse → InventoryGui.Show → SetInUse(true) (client :122850-122866), so there is an RTT-sized window where the server sees s_inUse==0 but the chest is about to be owned+opened. A server write landing there is overwritten by the opener's next Save(). Mitigate by re-checking s_inUse and DataRevision immediately before commit and never writing to a chest whose owner changed in the last tick.

The prescribed SetOwner(sessionID) makes the chest unopenable for up to 2 s: Container.Interact (:122042-122068) sends RPC_RequestOpen to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82856-82858); on the server there is no Container instance so HandleRoutedRPC drops it (:83646-83661) and the player gets no RPC_OpenResponse at all (not even '$msg_inuse'). Ownership returns only via ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s timer :76870-76885). Wonderland's ZdoInventoryIO.Save (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:52-58) claims only at commit for this reason; the design must say 'E does nothing for ~2 s after a fee is charged'.

Revision race can void the fee: RPC_ZDOData rejects a packet whose DataRevision is <= the local one (:77108-77118). If the client bumps its revision (any Save) between the server's read and the client receiving the server's write, both copies sit at the same revision with different contents and neither side ever reconciles. The s_inUse gate closes most of it, but a re-open in the ~RTT window after the server's write opens the UI on the stale local m_inventory; because the incoming packet has already flipped the owner to the server, OnContainerChanged skips Save (IsOwner() false :122288) and the player can take the 'spent' coal into their own (client-authoritative) inventory. Mitigation: debit only after s_inUse == 0 has been observed on two consecutive polls AND the depositor's character ZDO is > ~3 m from the chest.

byte[] ZDO writes ALWAYS increment DataRevision: BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue compares with Equals (utils_SERVER:321-333), which is reference equality for arrays, so even an identical blob is a 'change'. Harmless for the toll, but a server loop that re-Saves an unchanged inventory every tick would flood every nearby peer with the full blob — write only on actual mutation.

Inventory.Load on the server resolves items through ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab; that works on a dedicated server (Wonderland ships it) but any modded/unknown prefab in the blob is dropped by Inventory.Load and would be silently destroyed on the server's Save — token chests should be rejected/ignored if any item fails to resolve rather than re-saved.

'Stack all' cannot deposit by accident from a distance: Container.StackAll (:122174-122215) and InventoryGui.OnStackAll (:50610-50615) act only on the currently OPEN container; there is no 'stack to nearby chests' in 1.0.7. Accidental deposits require opening the token chest.

The toast while the chest is open is achievable (Player "Message" RPC :10072/:14820 renders through MessageHud independent of InventoryGui), but the DEBIT must wait for s_inUse == 0, so 'Fee paid' should be shown only when the debit actually committed, i.e. after close.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified. Container.OnContainerChanged (:122288-122292) → Save() (:122294-122301) writes m_inventory.Save(pkg) bytes to s_items on every change while owner; Load() (:122303-122322) early-returns on DataRevision==m_lastRevision and on m_inUse; InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f) at :121922; UpdateUseVisual (:121990-122001) writes s_inUse ("InUse", :78673) only when owner. s_items="items" (:78475). Client Container.Interact (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:122782-122806) always goes through m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_RequestOpen") to the owner; RPC_RequestOpen (:122874-122897) transfers ownership to the requester via ForceSendZDO+SetOwner, so the opener is the owner while the UI is up and s_inUse is authoritative. Server write-back: ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) exists (:77706) and ZDO.SetOwner is public; Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO.Save (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:52-58) claims ownership at commit only, and ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76874-76925) hands it back to a nearby peer within 2 s so the next RequestOpen finds a live owner. Stack counts are real Inventory data (Inventory.Save/Load), so the two-field encoding holds. Toll: MoveMatchingItem exists (ZdoInventoryIO.cs:68). The 'no repaint while open' claim is correct (Load returns false while m_inUse). Route dial is a server write.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified: Container.OnContainerChanged (:122286-122291) -> Save (:122293-122300) writes the whole Inventory blob to s_items on every change while the opening client owns it; Load (:122302-122322) is polled from CheckForChanges every 1 s (:121922) and refuses while m_inUse without advancing m_lastRevision, so the server's write is applied on close — the 'must close to see it' UX claim is exactly right. UpdateUseVisual (:121990-122001) publishes s_inUse from the owner. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77135) accepts any incoming ZDO whose DataRevision is strictly higher regardless of ownership, and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76002-76013) has no ownership exclusion, so a server-written blob does reach and overwrite the owning client's copy. Stack counts do live in the blob (Inventory.Save), so the two-field encoding and the toll are real; nothing else in the batch can take an item. The option's own caveat rating is fair. What it omits: the ≤2 s 'chest will not open' window caused by its own SetOwner step, a narrow revision race that can void the fee, and that byte[] writes always bump revision.

catalog.name: Debiting a living player's own inventory
catalog.oneLine: Taking an item directly from the player (rather than from a chest), or checking what they are carrying — the obvious design that is structurally impossible.
catalog.howItWorks:
`ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles()` does NOT collect anything — it invokes a `"SavePlayerProfile"` RPC on each peer whose handler calls `Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile` on that client, writing that client's own local `.fch` file; nothing returns to the server (:79653-79675). `Player.Save(ZPackage)` serialises inventory, known recipes, skills and uniques into `PlayerProfile.m_playerData`, stored only on that client's disk (:14091-14170, :105706-105711). An exhaustive read of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` call inside Character (:178-6796), Humanoid (:6796-9414) and Player (:9414-16500) finds only vitals, identity, pose, emote and equipment-visual fields — never items.

The single exception is a DEAD player: `Player.CreateTombStone` moves the whole inventory into a tombstone Container whose ZDO carries `s_items` plus `s_owner`/`s_ownerName`/`s_timeOfDeath`/`s_spawnPoint` (:12702-12714, :19845-19853, :19732-19740). So the server can read and debit a corpse, and nothing else.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PORTAL UX: the server can never reproduce vanilla's ore/metal restriction for a server-issued teleport, because `Inventory.IsTeleportable` (:68860-68880) runs entirely client-side against data the server does not hold. Any forced-teleport feature silently allows ore through. Design around it — advertise it honestly, or never use forced teleport as the primary movement and let the vanilla portal (which DOES check) do the work.
catalog.playerExperience: Not applicable — nothing can be built, so the player experiences nothing. Any documentation promising 'the server checks what you are carrying' or 'the portal charges you a coin' without a chest is a promise that cannot be kept.
failureModes: Any design stating 'the server checks the player is carrying X' or 'the server takes X from the player' is impossible without a client mod.
A server-issued teleport always bypasses the ore/metal restriction, which will be perceived as a cheat vector if not stated plainly.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Debiting a living player's own inventory
corrections: Add the nuance: the server can see EQUIPPED items (VisEquipment mirrors hand/back/armour/utility/trinket prefab hashes into the character ZDO, Humanoid.SetupVisEquipment :8192-8215), so a 'wear the key' or 'hold the key' check is possible; only the bag contents and stack counts are invisible, and nothing can be charged from a living player.
evidence: Set(ZDOVars.s_*) grep over :178-16500 (class headers :178, :6796, :9414) — no item keys
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Ruled-out verdict holds. ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles (:79654-79670) only does peer.m_rpc.Invoke("SavePlayerProfile") per peer; RPC_SavePlayerProfile (:79672-79675) calls Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile(setLogoutPoint:true, isFromRpc:true) on the receiving client — nothing is returned. Player.Save(ZPackage) (:14091 ff.) serialises into a package consumed by PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData (:105706-105711) → m_playerData byte[] on the client. Exhaustive grep of Set(ZDOVars.s_*) over :178-16500 (Character :178, Humanoid :6796, Player :9414) yields only tiltrot, modifiers, isBlocking, inBed, emote*, dead, cheated, aliveTime, weaponLoaded, wakeup, timeOfDeath, tamed, stealth, stamina, seed, pvp, playerName, playerID, noise, maxHealth, lookTarget, level, health, growStart, eitr, dodgeinv, crowned, bodyVelocity, baseValue, attackers, adrenaline — no item keys. s_items writers are Container.Save (:122299) and a ZDOMan legacy conversion (:78075-78094) only. Tombstone exception verified: Player.CreateTombStone (:12700-12714) Instantiates m_tombstone, MoveInventoryToGrave, TombStone.Setup writes s_ownerName/s_owner (:19845-19853), TombStone.Awake writes s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint when owner (:19732-19740). Equipment hashes (VisEquipment) are the one partial exception and are correctly covered by the sibling option.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Tried to refute and could not. ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles (:79654-79669) only invokes the client-side "SavePlayerProfile" RPC; RPC_SavePlayerProfile (:79671-79674) calls Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile locally and nothing returns. Player.Save (:14091ff) feeds PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData (:105706-105711) into m_playerData on the client's disk only. ZDOVars.s_items has exactly two writers in the whole server assembly: Container.Save (:122299) and a one-time legacy string->bytes migration (:78075-78094); no Character/Humanoid/Player code path writes it. The tombstone exception is correct: Player.CreateTombStone (:12708-12712) moves the inventory into a tombstone Container and TombStone.Setup (:19845-19853) / Awake (:19735-19739) stamp owner, name, time of death and spawn point. The consequence claim is also correct and now verified on the CLIENT assembly: Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer (client :41962-41968) calls Player.TeleportTo (client :15304-15329), which checks only IsTeleporting and m_teleportCooldown — Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68860-68880) is consulted solely by TeleportWorld.Teleport (client :144270), so a server-issued teleport carries ore. Ruled-out stands. One nuance the option should carry: equipped items ARE visible (VisEquipment, :8192-8215, :20560-20711), so 'is the player wearing/holding X' is answerable even though 'is X in the bag' is not.

catalog.name: Positional input — plates, walk-sequences, approach vector
catalog.oneLine: The server polls every connected character's ZDO position and treats named spots, dwell times, ordered sequences and the compass bearing of approach as commands.
catalog.howItWorks:
POSITION IS THE CHEAPEST AND FRESHEST SIGNAL THE SERVER HAS. `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every FixedUpdate on the owning client (:87527-87534), and client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent (`ZDOMan.ClientChanged` :77727 → `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains `m_clientChangeQueue` wholesale :77241-77258, flushed every 0.05 s :76843). So `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetPosition()` is fresh to ~50-100 ms regardless of how far the player is from the server's pinned reference position (1e6,0,1e6, :100465).

PRIMITIVES:
(1) PLATE — a mod-side `(worldPos, radius, action)`. A player whose horizontal distance drops below radius and stays for a dwell time (default 1.5 s) triggers. Accumulate `dwell[playerId] += dt` while inside, reset on exit. Ignore y so a raised platform still counts.
(2) SEQUENCE — an ordered list of plates entered within a window. `A→B→A` inside 20 s is deliberate and essentially unspoofable. Bounded per-player ring of (plateId, time).
(3) APPROACH VECTOR — the bearing from which the player entered the portal's 6 m radius, quantised to 8 sectors. Walk in from the north for destination 1, from the east for 3. Zero construction, zero UI, the most invisible input available.
(4) LOOK DIRECTION — `CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation` writes `ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = eyePos + lookDir * 100f` into the character ZDO, at most every 0.2 s and only on change (:5041-5081). Disambiguates which of several adjacent portals/signs/stands the player means.

MARKING: the plates are ordinary player-built decoration (a stone tile, a rug, a torch ring); the mod needs only a coordinate list.

SAMPLING: 0.1-0.2 s is comfortable — a player at ~5 m/s covers 0.5-1 m per sample, so a 3 m plate is never missed. Far tighter than Wonderland's `PositionWatch` 3 s security sampling (Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31), costing one `GetAllCharacterZDOS()` allocation plus N distance checks per tick.
catalog.playerExperience:
In front of your portal you have laid three stone tiles in a row, each with a torch, and a sign above reading `STAND TO CHOOSE`. The tiles are pure decoration you built with the hammer.

You walk onto the left tile and stop. About a second and a half later a toast reads `▸ Base (612m). Walk into the portal.` and the tag flips to `>Base`. You step off; nothing changes — the dial is set.

You walk onto the middle tile, wait, `▸ Haldor (1,140m)`. You step into the portal and you are in Haldor's meadow.

The approach-vector variant is quieter still: there are no tiles. You walk into the portal from the north and come out at your mine; from the east and you come out at the swamp. After the third time you stop thinking about it. A guest walks straight in from whichever side, gets destination 1, and is confused about nothing because they never knew there was a choice.

Cost: walking. Literally zero extra actions — that is its whole appeal. The problem is that it is undiscoverable and accident-prone; you will re-dial your hub by pathing across a tile on the way to a workbench.
failureModes: Players path across their own base constantly; without an armed state and generous dwell times this fires by accident all day.
Undiscoverable — nothing in the game hints that a floor tile means anything. Requires player-built visible marking plus a sign written by the server.
Approach-vector input is invisible even after you know about it: a guest cannot tell there was a choice, and a player who circles a portal while fighting gets a random destination.
Position is owner-authoritative; a player being knocked back or teleported crosses plates involuntarily.
Dwell timers must be reset on death/respawn (`ZDOVars.s_dead`, :78403) and on large position jumps (dungeon transits cross y=3000, `Character.InInterior` :4538) or the tracker desyncs.
openQuestions: Does the Player prefab have `CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation` enabled and `m_head` assigned? Both are Inspector fields gating the `s_lookTarget` write (:5043). IN-GAME: poll `s_lookTarget` for 10 s while a player spins in place; a changing non-zero Vector3 confirms the channel.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Positional input — plates, walk-sequences, approach vector
corrections: Freshness is bounded by socket back-pressure, not just the 0.05 s timer: ZDOMan.SendZDOs skips the tick when the peer socket's send queue exceeds 10240 bytes or has <2048 bytes free (SendZDOs head), so under congestion position updates batch and the ~50-100 ms figure degrades. Dwell timers (1.5 s) absorb this; the approach-vector variant, which relies on the first sample inside the 6 m ring, should use two consecutive samples or a minimum inbound displacement to avoid mis-quantised bearings when a burst arrives.

s_lookTarget is written only when the value CHANGES at a 0.2 s check (:5065-5071); a perfectly still player emits nothing, so the mod must keep the last value rather than expect a heartbeat, and the initial value for a freshly connected character may be Vector3.zero until the first head move.

Approach vector has a hard timing budget: from the 6 m ring to the trigger collider at sprint (~7 m/s) is ≈0.6 s. The dial must traverse server poll (0.1-0.2 s) + ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666, bumps revision + SetDirtyPortals) + 0.05 s flush + RTT, AND the client must already hold the destination ZDO: client TeleportWorld.TargetFound (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144383-144399) returns false and calls ZDOMan.RequestZDO when it does not, and Teleport() then returns SILENTLY (:144259-144262) — no message. Because TeleportWorldTrigger fires only on OnTriggerEnter (:144413-144421), the player must step out and back in. Fix: detect at 10-12 m and pre-push every managed destination ZDO to the peer via ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) (:77714) when the player enters the outer ring.

The 'portal glows' feedback in the player experience lags: client UpdatePortal polls HaveTarget/TargetFound every 0.5 s (:144231-144248) and the emission colour lerps over ~1 s (:144251-144255), so a plate dial is visible on the portal 0.5-1.5 s after the toast, not with it.
Look-direction as a disambiguator is 0.2 s stale and quantised by the 'only on change' guard (:5066-5071); it is fine for 'which of three stands' but not for sub-second gestures.

Dwell plates are exposed to Character.InInterior (:4538-4541): a player inside a crypt has y > 3000, so a horizontal-only distance check would match plates whose x/z lie under the dungeon; include a |Δy| < ~10 m guard rather than ignoring y outright.

The prereq 'Arming gesture' (crouch) is a real server-readable bit — Player.UpdateCrouch -> m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching) (:15667-15671) stores int at key 438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching") (ZSyncAnimation.SetBool :87271-87281, session-hash, never saved) — but Player.StartEmote force-uncrouches (:15591), so an emote confirm cancels the arm; and IsCrouching on the server cannot use GetCurrentAnimHash (no Animator), only that ZDO int.
evidence: ZDOMan.Update send cadence — :76843-76852; ZDOMan.SendZDOs queue-size throttle (10240 / 2048)
ZDOMan.ClientChanged / CreateSyncList client branch / 0.05 s timer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77727-77730, :77241-77258, :76838-76856
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified. ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (:87472 ff., position write at :87528-87533) writes zDO.SetPosition when changed, invoked from the fixed-update path (:87839, :87847). ZDO.InternalSetPosition → SetSector + IncreaseDataRevision when owner; IncreaseDataRevision calls ZDOMan.instance.ClientChanged(m_uid) on non-server (:77727-77730). CreateSyncList's non-server branch (:77241-77258) drains m_clientChangeQueue subject only to peer.ShouldSend (revision comparison, no distance term), and ZDOMan.Update's 0.05 s send cadence (:76843-76852) applies. Server-side the character ZDO is fetched via peer.m_characterID (GetAllCharacterZDOS :81024-81044) and GetPosition is plain data — no GameObject, no local player. s_lookTarget: CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (:5041-5081) writes lookFromPos + GetLookDir()*100f at most every 0.2 s and only on change, owner-only — correct. Reference-position pin (:100465) and Character.InInterior (:4538-4541) exist as cited. PositionWatch.cs:31 confirms the 3 s default. Enforcement: the dial is a server write on the portal ZDO; the position itself is client-authored and trivially spoofable by a modified client, but that is true of every input channel here and irrelevant for a vanilla-client threat model.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Freshness claim verified: ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zDO.SetPosition on every FixedUpdate when the cached position changed (:87528-87533); ZDO.InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision when owner (:73734-73744) -> ClientChanged (:77727); the client's CreateSyncList drains m_clientChangeQueue wholesale (:77241-77258) on the 0.05 s timer (:76843), independent of the server's pinned reference position (Game.FixedUpdate :100465). CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (:5041-5075) writes s_lookTarget = lookFrom + lookDir*100 at ≤0.2 s only on change, owner-side, gated on m_headRotation && m_head (:5043) which the player prefab has. Plates, dwell, sequences and look-direction are pure server-side reads on data the client already sends — 'server-enforced' is honest because the resulting action is a route write. No vanilla subsystem interferes: character ZDOs never change owner, are non-persistent, and are unaffected by the 5 s portal reconcile. The approach-vector variant, however, has a timing hole the option does not mention, and the 'silently re-dials' failure mode is worse than described because the client's portal trigger fires exactly once.

catalog.name: Build-shape input — placing a piece as a latching switch
catalog.oneLine: Placing (or removing) a specific build piece in a specific socket near a portal is detected the moment the ZDO arrives and acts as a permanent, visible switch.
catalog.howItWorks:
THE HOOK IS THE NON-OBVIOUS PART. A dedicated server never sees `Player.PlacePiece` (no Player instance) and never runs `ZNetScene.Instantiate` for a client-placed piece (the client instantiates locally and only the ZDO arrives). The PAUSED PortalLock project patched exactly those and could never fire once (`PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114`).

The correct hook is Wonderland's SpawnGovernor pair (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58`): a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) that only REMEMBERS the ZDOID — on the network-receive path `prefabHash` is 0 and `GetPrefab()` returns 0, so nothing can be decided — plus a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225), the first moment the prefab hash is known. There, read `GetPrefab()`, `GetPosition()` and `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (:78393 — the placer's stable PlayerProfile UID, written by `Piece.SetCreator` :136415-136424, the same value as that player's `ZDOVars.s_playerID`).

SWITCH DESIGN: per portal, a set of SOCKETS `(relativeOffset, acceptedPrefabSet, action)`. A Wood Beam in socket 1 → dial destination 1. A blue-burning torch in the lock socket → lock the portal. Because the ZDO persists, the switch is latching, survives restarts, and a visitor reads the routing state off the architecture.

DESTRUCTION is the other half: subscribe to the public `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` `Action<ZDO>` field (:76033), invoked from `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76975) BEFORE the ZDO leaves `m_objectsByID`, so it is still readable inside the callback. No Harmony needed.

SAME HOOK = THE SERVER-ENFORCED PORTAL CAP: on a new portal-prefab ZDO, read `s_creator`, count that player's portals in `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), and if over the limit `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` (:76929 — owner-gated on send, so the SetOwner is mandatory) plus a toast. Strictly stronger than TortalPortal's client-side `Player.TryPlacePiece` cap, which any client can ignore.
catalog.playerExperience:
Your portal sits in a stone frame. On the left there are three empty 1×1 sockets where a wood beam obviously goes — you built the frame that way because the server-written sign beside it reads `PLUG A BEAM: 1 Base · 2 Haldor · 3 Mine`.

You take out your hammer, select Wood Beam, and place one in socket 2. It snaps in with the normal building sound. Within about a quarter second a toast reads `Haldor plugged. Portal → Haldor (1,140m).` The portal glows. The beam stays there forever.

A week later you come back and need to remember nothing: there is a beam in socket 2, so the portal goes to Haldor. Anyone standing in your base can read it. To change it you remove the beam (`Haldor unplugged`) and place one in socket 3.

Cost: equip hammer, select piece, place — about five seconds and one piece of wood. Slower than typing but permanent, visible, and it turns routing state into architecture, which is a genuinely Valheim-native idea.

Jank rating: medium. The mechanism is elegant; discoverability depends entirely on the server writing a sign that explains the sockets and on the sockets being visually obvious, which is on the player's building skill.
failureModes: A `CreateNewZDO`-only postfix always sees `GetPrefab() == 0` on the network path and can never act — SpawnGovernor's header records this as a shipped bug in its own first version.
Patching `Player.PlacePiece` / `Player.TryPlacePiece` / `ZNetScene.Instantiate` produces code that can never execute on a dedicated server (PortalLock's precedent).

Socket matching must tolerate snap-grid offsets and rotation; a hard equality on position will miss almost every placement. Use a radius of ~0.75 m around the expected offset, in the portal's local frame.

`Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0` (:136417), so world-gen structures and some pieces have `s_creator == 0`. Do not treat a missing creator as 'unowned' without checking.
Destroying a client-created ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix may leave an orphaned local instance on the placing client until the zone reloads; the build materials may or may not be refunded.
Players rebuild and remodel constantly — a socket that overlaps a common building position will fire spuriously.
openQuestions: Can the server destroy a client-created portal/piece ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix without a visible desync on the placing client? SpawnGovernor does this for creatures and is shipped, but a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may differ. IN-GAME: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost disappears cleanly and whether materials are refunded.

Is `ZDOVars.s_creator` reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? TortalPortal's export treats 0 as 'admin-spawned or older'. IN-GAME: place a portal and confirm `s_creator` equals that player's `s_playerID`.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Build-shape input — placing a piece as a latching switch
corrections: ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage) begins at assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74206, not :74225 (the cited range is mid-body).

The Deserialize postfix fires on EVERY ZDO update, not only creation; the pending-ZDOID set from the CreateNewZDO postfix (SpawnGovernor.cs:34-66) is mandatory to distinguish new arrivals, and must only record when prefabHash==0 (network path). World-load never passes through CreateNewZDO/Deserialize (ZDOMan.Load uses ZDOPool.Create() at :76478/:76488 and ZDO.Load), so loaded sockets must be indexed separately at startup by scanning m_objectsByID/GetPortalList.

Inside the Deserialize postfix the new portal is NOT yet in GetPortalList() — AddIfPortal runs after Deserialize (:77132) — so the count is of pre-existing portals only (correct for a cap, but do not expect the new one to be present).
Destroying a client-placed piece from the server gives no resource refund on the client (it is a DestroyZDO, not a WearNTear.Remove); the toast should say so.

The capped portal's materials are already gone: the client runs ConsumeResources right after TryPlacePiece succeeds (client Player.Update :10803-10809), before the ZDO ever reaches the server. A server-side destroy therefore eats the piece cost unless the mod spawns refund ItemDrop ZDOs itself. State this in howItWorks.

The Deserialize hook fires only on the network-receive path. ZDOs loaded from disk at boot go through ZDOMan.Load, never CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int) with hash 0, so socket state does NOT come back from the hook after a restart; the mod must rebuild it with a spatial scan of m_objectsByID / sector lists at load. 'Survives restarts' is true of the ZDO, not of the derived switch state.

Per-creator portal count via GetPortalList() (:77648) relies on s_creator on every existing portal; portals placed by a build-plan/copy tool or pre-existing world portals may carry creator 0 and are uncountable — treat 0 as 'unowned' explicitly.

m_onZDODestroyed also fires for the server's own DestroyZDO calls (RPC to 0L is handled locally in InvokeRoutedRPC :83587-83590), so the destroy callback must ignore ZDOs the mod itself is destroying to avoid re-entrancy/double toasts.
The 'quarter second' toast latency is plausible but unmeasured: it is client SendZDOs cadence + server Update + routed 'Message' RPC; mark as needs in-game timing.
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77140 (CreateNewZDO(zDOID, vector) at :77123, Deserialize at :77131, AddIfPortal at :77132, SetOwner+DestroyZDO dead-ZDO pattern at :77133-77138)

ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77140 (CreateNewZDO(zDOID, vector) at :77123, Deserialize at :77131, dead-ZDO SetOwner+DestroyZDO at :77132-77136)
Client Player.PlacePiece SetCreator after Instantiate — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:12504-12518; ConsumeResources after TryPlacePiece — :10803-10809
Client ZDOMan.CreateSyncList sends m_clientChangeQueue to server — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs (CreateSyncList, non-server branch)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Hook pair verified against the server decompile. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77140) creates an unknown ZDO via the private CreateNewZDO(uid, pos) with prefabHashIn defaulting to 0 (:77123, :76684-76692) — at that moment GetPrefab() is 0 so nothing can be classified — then calls zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) (:77131) and only afterwards AddIfPortal (:77132). ZDO.Deserialize (method starts :74206, not :74225) fills the prefab hash and every string/long including s_creator. Client Player.PlacePiece (client :12505-12518) Instantiates the prefab (ZNetView.Awake creates the ZDO) and calls Piece.SetCreator(GetPlayerID(), ...) in the same frame, and SetCreator (:136415-136424) writes ZDOVars.s_creator = the placer's s_playerID (client GetPlayerID :10140-10147 reads ZDOVars.s_playerID) while the placer still owns the fresh ZDO — so the first packet the server sees already carries the creator. Portal cap: DestroyZDO is gated on zdo.IsOwner() (:76929-76935) and vanilla itself does exactly 'SetOwner(m_sessionID); DestroyZDO(zdo)' for dead-ZDO resurrection at :77133-77138, so the pattern is native.
