[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Hook pair verified. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77140) calls the private CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3) with prefabHash defaulted to 0 (:77123, :76684), then SetOwnerInternal(client), InternalSetPosition, and only then zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) (:77131) where the prefab hash and all keys land — so a CreateNewZDO postfix sees GetPrefab()==0 and a Deserialize postfix keyed on the remembered ZDOID is the first usable moment, exactly as Wonderland SpawnGovernor does (SpawnGovernor.cs:43-67). s_creator is written client-side by Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) immediately after Instantiate in Player.PlacePiece (client :12504-12518), i.e. before the client's ZDOMan.Update ships the new ZDO, so the first packet carries the creator. Destruction: HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-76999) invokes m_onZDODestroyed before m_objectsByID.Remove; ZNetScene subscribes with Delegate.Combine (:81953) so a mod += is safe. Portal cap: the SetOwner(sessionID)+DestroyZDO idiom is vanilla's own dead-ZDO branch in the same method (:77132-77136); DestroyZDO is owner-gated (:76929-76935); SendDestroyed broadcasts to 0L (:76950) and the client's HandleDestroyedZDO removes the instance. Enforcement is honestly server-side: the server owns whether the ZDO exists. Corrections needed on player cost, boot rescan, and toast timing.

catalog.name: Chat commands (`/portal home`)
catalog.oneLine: Typing a command in chat — the obvious design, dead on a dedicated server for three independent reasons.
catalog.howItWorks:
(1) SLASH COMMANDS NEVER LEAVE THE CLIENT. `Chat.InputText` does `text = ((text[0] != '/') ? ("say " + text) : text.Substring(1)); TryRunCommand(text, this);` (:41947-41955). `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734-45758) looks the name up in the CLIENT's own compiled dictionary; `/portal` is not in it and the call uses silentFail, so the client does nothing and prints nothing. There is no network path for an unrecognised slash command.

(2) PLAIN CHAT IS INVISIBLE TO A SOLO PLAYER. Plain text becomes `say <text>` → `Chat.SendText`. Shout goes through `CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` (:41996-42042), which — when a RelationsProvider exists, i.e. on Steam — sends one RPC to `ZNet.instance.LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID` (the sender's OWN peer id) plus one per OTHER listed player's `m_characterID.UserID`. `InvokeRoutedRPC` calls `RouteRPC` only `if (targetPeerID != m_id)` (:83591). For a lone player every target IS their own id, so ZERO packets go on the wire. Normal/Whisper take `Talker.Say` → `m_nview.InvokeRPC(user, "Say", …)` (:18942-18950), same addressing, same result.

(3) WITH 2+ PLAYERS IT IS RELAY-ONLY. The packets pass through the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `RouteRPC` (:83632-83643) but are never addressed to the server, so no registered handler fires. A prefix CAN sniff them — but a channel that works only when a second player is online is not a channel.

THE ADMIN EXCEPTION: `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889) is gated on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` and runs the string through the SERVER's `Console.instance.TryRunCommand`; replies return via `ZNet.RemotePrint` → the client's console (:81635-81656). A mod-registered server-side `Terminal.ConsoleCommand` with `onlyServer: true, remoteCommand: true` gives ADMINS a genuine text console — invisible to ordinary players and landing in a window most people never open.
catalog.playerExperience: The player types `/portal home` and presses Enter. Absolutely nothing happens — no error, no message, no log line on their machine or the server's. The chat box closes. They try `/tp home`, `!home`, `portal home`. The last one appears in chat as a shout nobody but they can see if they are alone. They conclude the mod is broken and file a bug.
failureModes: Silent failure is the worst possible outcome for a discovery path — the player tries the obvious thing and gets zero signal.
Any documentation saying 'type /portal …' generates support tickets forever.
Sniffing shouts via a RouteRPC prefix works only with 2+ players online: untestable solo and unreliable in production.
openQuestions: Is `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider` null on a Steam client? If yes, `SendText` shout collapses to a `targetPeerID 0` broadcast (:42002-42005) and shout-as-command becomes fully viable even solo — a total reversal of this ruling and by far the highest-value single test in this document, because it would give the mod a free-text command channel and make most of the janky schemes unnecessary. IN-GAME: prefix `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` on the server, have a SOLO player type a plain sentence and a `/s` shout, and see whether `"ChatMessage"` arrives.
corrections: Reason (2) depends on Splatform.Steam's DistributionPlatform exposing a non-null RelationsProvider; that assembly is absent from /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/libs-Tools/1.0/client and cannot be verified from the decompile. If RelationsProvider is null on Steam, Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:42002-42005) calls the handler with 0L and a solo player's shout IS a routed broadcast reaching a server-registered 'ChatMessage' handler. Needs a one-line in-game test (register 'ChatMessage' on ZRoutedRpc server-side, shout while alone).

The admin exception cannot use a mod-registered command: Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45746) only calls ZNet.RemoteCommand for names present in the vanilla client's compiled table with RemoteCommand=true. The only admin text channel is to hijack an existing remote-flagged, non-cheat vanilla command whose full line is forwarded verbatim — e.g. 'setkey' (client :43510-43534: isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true), 'removekey', 'setworldmodifier', 'genloc' — and intercept the line server-side with a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (:81879-81894) before Console.instance.TryRunCommand runs it. Still admin-list gated (:81881).
Slash-command verdict (ruled-out) stands on reason (1) alone regardless of the RelationsProvider question.

Replace the ADMIN EXCEPTION: registering a new server-side Terminal.ConsoleCommand does NOT create a remote text channel for vanilla-client admins — Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45758) requires the name to exist in the CLIENT's dictionary before it will call ZNet.RemoteCommand. The only working admin text channel is piggybacking a vanilla remoteCommand:true / onlyServer:true command that carries free text — 'setkey <text>' (:43510-43534) or 'removekey <text>' (:43535) — and intercepting it server-side with a prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (:81879-81895) before Console.instance.TryRunCommand runs the real setkey. Note IsValid failing for ANY reason (onlyServer, cheat flag) still falls through to the RemoteCommand branch, so cheats need not be enabled client-side.

The RelationsProvider != null claim for Steam cannot be verified from these decompiles (the provider lives in the Splatform assembly, not on disk). If RelationsProvider were null the shout/say path broadcasts to 0L (:42002-42005) and a server prefix on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC could sniff even a solo player's chat; behaviour on Steam PC should be confirmed in-game rather than asserted.
'No log line on their machine' is slightly overstated for plain text: Talker.Say logs 'Saying <type> <text>' to the client Player.log (:18944). For '/portal' the statement is exact.
evidence: Splatform.dll strings show only the IRelationsProvider interface; no Steam implementation on disk (libs-Tools/1.0/client)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Reason (1) holds exactly: Chat.InputText (:41947-41955) strips '/' and calls TryRunCommand(text, this) where 'this' coerces to silentFail=true; Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45758) looks the name up in the client's static commands dictionary and, for an unknown name with silentFail, does nothing — ZNet.RemoteCommand is reached ONLY for a name that exists in the client table AND has RemoteCommand=true AND fails IsValid (:45743-45746). Reason (3) holds: server RPC_RoutedRPC handles locally only when m_targetPeerID == m_id or 0 and otherwise relays (:83632-83643). Reason (2) is CONTINGENT, not proven: CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42042) sends to the sender's own UserID (handled locally, never routed: InvokeRoutedRPC :83577-83595 routes only when targetPeerID != m_id) plus other players ONLY IF PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider != null; if it is null the handler is invoked with 0L and the shout/say becomes a BROADCAST that the dedicated server's HandleRoutedRPC dispatches to any function a mod registered under 'ChatMessage' (or sniffs for 'Say' on a ZDO target). The Steam platform implementation (Splatform.Steam) is NOT in the decompile set on disk (libs-Tools/1.0/client contains only Splatform.dll core with the IRelationsProvider interface), so 'i.e. on Steam' is unverified. The ADMIN EXCEPTION is wrong as written: a mod-registered server ConsoleCommand name is unknown to the vanilla client's table, so the client prints 'not a recognized command' and never forwards it.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Ruled-out verdict for player-facing chat commands holds. Chat.InputText (:41947-41955) turns '/x' into TryRunCommand('x', this) — `this` converts to bool via UnityEngine.Object so silentFail=true; Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45758) looks the name up in the client's own compiled dictionary and, on miss with silentFail, does nothing. Plain text → 'say' → Chat.SendText (:41975-41994): Shout uses CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42042) which, when a RelationsProvider exists, targets the sender's own LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID first and then each other player's m_characterID.UserID; Normal/Whisper go through Talker.Say → m_nview.InvokeRPC(user, 'Say') (:18942-18950) with the same addressing. ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC only calls RouteRPC when targetPeerID != m_id (:83587-83594), so a lone player emits zero packets; with peers, the server's RPC_RoutedRPC only HandleRoutedRPC's when target == m_id or 0 (:83632-83643) — relay only, and Chat/Talker have no server instance anyway. The ADMIN EXCEPTION paragraph is wrong as written: a vanilla client only forwards commands that are IN ITS OWN dictionary and marked RemoteCommand (the `else if (value.RemoteCommand && !IsServer()) ZNet.RemoteCommand(text)` branch at :45743-45746 is reached only after a successful commands.TryGetValue). A mod-registered server-side ConsoleCommand is unknown to the vanilla client, which prints 'not a recognized command' in F5 and sends nothing.

catalog.name: Ward toggle as a switch (and ward data as the permission source)
catalog.oneLine: Using a guard stone's Enable/Permit buttons as a portal command — dead as an RPC intercept, fine as a ZDO poll, and far more valuable as the source of portal permissions.
catalog.howItWorks:
RPC PATH (ruled out): `PrivateArea` registers `"ToggleEnabled"` and `"TogglePermitted"` on its own ZNetView in `Awake` (:137200-137201); `Interact` sends them with `m_nview.InvokeRPC(...)` (:137370-137392), targeting the ward ZDO's OWNER — normally the interacting player, so the RPC is handled locally and never hits the wire (:83587-83594). Even when it crosses, the server's `HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` non-null (:83659) and it never is (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). A patch on `RPC_ToggleEnabled`/`RPC_TogglePermitted` compiles and never fires. Worse, both handlers IGNORE the routed `uid` and act on the payload `playerID` (:137399-137421), so sender hardening buys nothing.

ZDO PATH (works): every field is plain ZDO data. `ZDOVars.s_enabled` (:78423) — the on/off state. `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (:78529) — the permitted COUNT; entries are raw runtime-concatenated string keys `"pu_id" + i` (long) and `"pu_name" + i` (string), with id==0 skipped on read (`SetPermittedPlayers` :137338-137347, `GetPermittedPlayers` :137349-137363). These have NO ZDOVars constant — hash the concatenated string. `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) and `s_creatorName` (:78397) give the builder.

SO: poll `s_enabled` at 0.5 s and treat a double-toggle within 5 s as a command — or, far more usefully, build the SERVER-SIDE WARD MODEL portal permissions actually need: 'may this player re-dial this portal?' answered from `s_creator` plus the pu_id list, entirely from ZDO reads with no `PrivateArea` instance.

NEVER call `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547-137593): it iterates the static `m_allAreas` list populated only in `Awake` (:137197), which is permanently EMPTY on a dedicated server, so it returns true for every point — a silent allow-all that looks like a working permission check.

RADIUS is the missing piece: `PrivateArea.m_radius` is a compiled Inspector field with a class default of 10f (:137132) and no ZDO backing.
catalog.playerExperience:
You press E on your guard stone to switch it off, then E again to switch it back on within a couple of seconds. A toast reads `Portal network unlocked for 60s.` You walk to any portal inside the ward and re-dial freely. After a minute it relocks: `Relocked.`

More useful and entirely invisible: you add your friend Bjorn to the ward's permitted list the normal vanilla way (he presses E while the stone is off). From then on, when Bjorn types `>Vault` on your portal it just works, and when a stranger types it they get `Vault is warded. Ask Bjorn or Astrid.` The server derived all of that from the ward's own list without anyone configuring anything mod-specific.

That second use — ward-derived permissions — is far more valuable than ward-as-a-button. The toggle gesture is clumsy, since it disables your base's protection to press a button, and should never be a routine input.
failureModes: `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns TRUE for everything server-side because `m_allAreas` is always empty (:137173, :137197, :137547) — a silent allow-all masquerading as a permission check.
`m_radius` is Inspector data (class default 10f, :137132); hardcoding 10 will mis-cover every real ward.
Toggling a ward off to issue a command disables base protection for the duration — a bad trade.

Any client can add itself to an un-enabled ward's permitted list, because `RPC_TogglePermitted` gates only on `m_nview.IsOwner() && !IsEnabled()` and trusts the payload playerID (:137399-137412). Ward-derived permissions inherit that vanilla weakness.
`pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>` have no ZDOVars constant; writing `s_permitted` without the matching indexed keys produces phantom entries.
prerequisites: Ward ZDO index (spatial scan for guard_stone prefabs)
openQuestions: What is the guard_stone prefab's actual `m_radius`? IN-GAME: place one and binary-search the distance at which another player's build is refused; or dump the prefab.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Ward toggle as a switch (and ward data as the permission source)
corrections: PrivateArea.Interact has an additional early-out 'if (m_ownerFaction != 0) return false' (:137375-137378) before the creator check — irrelevant for player-built wards but present.
Ward pu_id values are the same s_playerID namespace as Piece s_creator, so the permission model needs no name matching; pu_name is display-only.

The toggle RPC targets the ward ZDO's OWNER, which after ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) can be any nearby peer, not necessarily the interacting player; and if the server session momentarily owns the ward ZDO the toggle is silently dropped by the FindInstance gate (:83659). The ZDO-poll design is unaffected but the write may originate from a different client than the presser.

m_radius: the class default 10f (:137132) is NOT the guard_stone prefab value (Inspector-serialized, 32 m in vanilla). The server cannot read the prefab; the mod must hardcode 32 m for guard_stone and treat it as an in-game-verified constant, not derive it from the decompile.

The 'double-toggle within 5 s' input is creator-only (Interact requires m_piece.IsCreator() to send ToggleEnabled, :137380) and each toggle also fires FlashShield to everyone; document that only the ward's creator can use the gesture.
Enforcement should read: server-enforced for the permission decision (route form), client-honoured for the toggle detection (the server merely observes a ZDO field the owning client writes).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] All cited members exist with the claimed semantics. PrivateArea.Awake registers 'ToggleEnabled'(long) and 'TogglePermitted'(long,string) on its ZNetView (:137200-137201); Interact sends them with m_nview.InvokeRPC(method, ...) (:137378-137392), and ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, params) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858) — the interacting player normally owns the ward, so InvokeRoutedRPC handles it locally and routes nothing (:83587-83593). Even a routed copy dies at HandleRoutedRPC's ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo) null check (:83657-83664) since no ward GameObject exists server-side. RPC_ToggleEnabled/RPC_TogglePermitted ignore the routed uid and act on the payload playerID (:137399-137421). IsEnabled/SetEnabled are plain ZDOVars.s_enabled bool reads/writes (:137423-137436); SetPermittedPlayers/GetPermittedPlayers use ZDOVars.s_permitted count plus runtime-concatenated 'pu_id'+i (long) / 'pu_name'+i (string) keys via ZDO.Set(string,long)/Set(string,string) which hash with GetStableHashCode (:73690, :73717), skipping id==0 on read (:137338-137363). ZDOVars.s_enabled :78423, s_permitted :78529, s_creator :78393, s_creatorName :78397 confirmed. CheckAccess (:137547-137593) iterates the static m_allAreas populated only in Awake (:137197); with the list empty the non-wardCheck branch sets flag=false, list stays empty, and the final 'if (!flag && list.Count > 0)' is false → returns true: allow-all confirmed. m_radius is a public Inspector float defaulting to 10f (:137132) with no ZDO key. The permission model answers 'may this route be opened' from ZDO data alone, so it is server-enforced in the route sense; the clumsy double-toggle input is a plain ZDO poll.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] RPC path ruled out correctly: PrivateArea.Awake registers ToggleEnabled/TogglePermitted on its ZNetView (:137200-137201); Interact sends via m_nview.InvokeRPC (:137380-137390) which targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855-82858); server-side HandleRoutedRPC needs ZNetScene.FindInstance non-null (:83659-83662), never true on a dedicated server. RPC handlers act on the payload playerID and require IsOwner locally (:137399-137421). ZDO path verified: SetPermittedPlayers/GetPermittedPlayers use s_permitted count plus string keys 'pu_id'+i / 'pu_name'+i with id==0 skipped (:137338-137363); ZDOVars.s_enabled :78423, s_permitted :78529. CheckAccess (:137547-137593) iterates static m_allAreas populated only in Awake (:137197) — with wardCheck=false and an empty list it returns true (allow-all), confirmed. Enforcement label survives only for the permission-source use (the server decides whether to honour a re-dial by reverting the tag / refusing to write the connection); the toggle-as-button is an input channel, not an enforcement.

catalog.name: Feedback: the tag echo (primary confirmation surface)
catalog.oneLine: The server rewrites the portal's own `s_tag` and the vanilla client redraws the hover text from the live ZDO every frame — the fastest, most in-context confirmation available.
catalog.howItWorks:
`TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` (:143453-143464) calls `GetTagInfo()`, which reads `zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` FRESH on every call — no cache, no timer, no DataRevision gate. The hover UI calls it each frame the player looks at the portal, so the instant a server-written ZDO update lands the text under the crosshair changes. Sub-frame repaint, no polling on either side.

The write: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, reply)` + `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702, mandatory or the change is lost at save) + `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706). No ownership claim is strictly required — no ZDO setter checks ownership (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter, :73648) and `IncreaseDataRevision` fires regardless — but claiming (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, :74627/:77362) guarantees the server wins a revision race with the nearby owning client. `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands ownership back within 2 s, which is fine and keeps vanilla retagging working.

HARD CONSTRAINTS ON THE ECHO:
• ≤10 characters, always (the `TextInput.Show` clamp, :61515-61521).
• No rich text — `GetHoverText` runs `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), regex `<[\/a-zA-Z0-9= "\"''#;:()$_-]*?>` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703). Colour is impossible here; it IS possible on a Sign face.
• ASCII only pending a glyph test.
• Both ends of a vanilla-paired link must carry BYTE-IDENTICAL tags or `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears the pair down within 5 s (:100601).
• Censoring is not a concern: `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` server-side (:94588-94591) and the censored flag is surfaced only on PlayFab (:143462).

ECHO ALPHABET (char 0 = state glyph): `>NAME` dialed · `#NAME` this portal's own name · `?NAME` unknown/ambiguous · `!NAME` denied/locked · `-` unlinked · `.NAME` pending.
catalog.playerExperience:
You are hovering the portal; the text under your crosshair reads `Teleport  Portal tag:"#Base" [Connected]`. You press E, type `>Haldor`, hit Enter. The dialog closes, you are looking at the portal again — and the text now reads `Teleport  Portal tag:">Haldor" [Connected]`. It changed while you were watching it, with no perceptible gap.

A bad name reads `"?Haldr"` instead, and the `?` tells you at a glance something is wrong before you read the toast in the corner. A portal locked against you reads `"!Vault"`.

This is the single best feedback surface available: instant, exactly where the player is already looking, and persistent — you can walk away, come back tomorrow, hover the portal, and it still tells you where it points. A toast cannot do that.
failureModes: An echo longer than 10 characters is truncated in the rename dialog and the truncation is submitted as a command on the player's next Enter.
Rich text is stripped, so the echo cannot use colour to distinguish states — the leading glyph is the only channel.
Distinct per-portal echoes are incompatible with vanilla pairing (`Game.ConnectPortals` tag-equality teardown, :100601) without prefixing it out.
Without `SetDirtyPortals()` the echo is lost at the next world save.
A player who opens the dialog and presses OK re-submits the echo as a command unless the parser is idempotent on its own canonical strings.
openQuestions: Does a client already standing at a portal pick up the tag change without a zone reload? `GetHoverText` reads live so it should be immediate, but confirm the ZDO update actually reaches a client that currently OWNS the portal. IN-GAME: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and watch the hover.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Feedback: the tag echo (primary confirmation surface)
corrections: '≤10 characters, always' is a dialog constraint, not a display one: GetHoverText renders a tag of any length; 10 is the characterLimit passed by TeleportWorld.Interact → TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) (:143482) and applied to m_inputField.characterLimit in Show (:61515-61521). The real hazard is that opening the dialog on a longer echo pre-fills a truncated string the player may re-submit; keep echoes ≤10 for that reason and verify GuiInputField's truncation on set in-game.

Ownership does not make the server 'win a revision race'. Client RPC_ZDOData applies incoming data purely on DataRevision (skips when incoming ≤ local, :77107-77116 server mirror), and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) is also revision-only. Claiming ownership stops the client's RPC_SetTag handler from writing (it is IsOwner-gated, :143587-143589) but a concurrent local Set on the client still bumps its revision and can beat the server's. Use ForceSendZDO plus a re-check on the next poll rather than relying on ownership.

Vanilla ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100608-100620) pairs ANY two unconnected portals with equal tags — two portals echoing '>Haldor' would be vanilla-paired to each other. The 'Pairing takeover' prereq is therefore hard, not optional.

Client-side GetTagInfo runs CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC which is a no-op only when !RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (client FilterUGC body); Steam PC is unfiltered, console/PlayFab clients may censor server-written echoes.
Line reference: ZDO.Deserialize-independent; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag body starts :143587 as the brief says.

Censoring: the server stub (:94588-94591) is irrelevant — hover text is rendered on the CLIENT, whose CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is real (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94940). It passes text through when !RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (Steam PC), but on console/crossplay clients a server-authored tag with an empty or stale s_tagauthor can resolve to BlockedByPrivilege and render as the '$ugc_text' placeholder. State 'Steam PC unaffected; console clients need an in-game check'.

'Claiming ownership guarantees the server wins the race' is wrong on both counts. (a) Race: if server and owning client each Set from revision N, both produce N+1 and each side's RPC_ZDOData discards the other's packet (`num4 <= DataRevision` → continue, :77109-77118) — split-brain, not a server win; ForceSendZDO does not bypass ShouldSend. (b) Side effect: while the server holds ownership, a vanilla retag is routed to owner=server and dropped by the FindInstance gate (:83659), so vanilla retagging is dead for up to the 2 s ReleaseZDOS cadence (:76870-76884). Recommend no ownership claim for pure tag echoes; rely on the fact the client only writes s_tag inside RPC_SetTag.
The `-` unlinked glyph must coincide with an actual ZDOID.None connection, otherwise the vanilla suffix reads '[Connected]' (HaveTarget = connection != None, :143632-143638) beside an 'unlinked' tag.

The echo alphabet (`>NAME` on the dialing portal, `#NAME` on the target) is by construction incompatible with vanilla pairing (tags must be byte-identical, :100601-100606); it works ONLY with the 'Pairing takeover' prereq that suppresses Game.ConnectPortals, and that takeover must also re-apply the connection after every client RPC_SetTag, which clears it (UpdateConnection(Portal, None) :143594-143596). Make the dependency explicit rather than listing it as a soft prereq.

ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals :76702-76705 ; ForceSendZDO :77706-77712 ; SetOwner :74627-74634 ; GetSessionID :77362 ; ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927 ; FindObjects merges m_portalObjects

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] TeleportWorld.GetHoverText (:143453-143464) calls GetTagInfo() (:143556-143570) which does zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) with no cache; the client Hud.UpdateCrosshair calls hoverable.GetHoverText() every frame (client decompile, UpdateCrosshair body). ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner) never reads okForNotOwner (:73648-73654) and Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) has no owner check; IncreaseDataRevision always fires. Server FilterUGC is 'return text' (:94588-94591). Two claims are over-stated: the 10-char limit is not a display constraint, and ownership does not decide a revision race.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. TeleportWorld.GetHoverText (:143453-143464) calls GetTagInfo() (:143556-143570) which reads zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) fresh each call; no cache. ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73726) has no ownership check and calls IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector (:73580-73588). SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is genuinely mandatory: portal ZDOs are pulled out of sector lists (AddIfPortal :77732-77751) and the portal chunk is written only `if (DirtyPortalObjects)` (:77621-77636); a bare tag Set only dirties the sector chunk, and DirtyPortalObjects is otherwise raised only by SetConnection/UpdateConnection (:73656-73678), new-portal add, destroy and load. ForceSendZDO (:77706-77712) only prioritizes; AddForceSendZdos still gates on ZDOPeer.ShouldSend revision compare (:77263-77275, :76003-76013). The 10-char limit is TextInput.Show characterLimit (:61519) from RequestText(this,'$piece_portal_tag',10) (:143482). RemoveRichTextTags regex confirmed (assembly_utils_SERVER :6700-6703). ConnectPortals phase-1 tag-mismatch teardown confirmed (:100592-100606). Corrections concern the client-side censor, the ownership-claim side effect, and the revision race.

catalog.name: Feedback: MessageHud toasts (the detail channel)
catalog.oneLine: Server-pushed top-left or centre-screen HUD messages, addressed to one player, localized client-side, with no length limit and no truncation trap.
catalog.howItWorks:
TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS, both proven in Wonderland.

(A) PER-CHARACTER, safer. `Player.Start` registers the routed RPC `"Message"(int type, string msg, int amount)` on the player's own ZNetView and ONLY when `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:10072); `Player.RPC_Message` re-checks IsOwner before calling `MessageHud.ShowMessage` (:14820-14825). Server: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.TopLeft, text, 0)`. Because it is registered only on the owning client it can never be delivered to the wrong player. Wonderland ships this as `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15).

(B) GLOBAL. `MessageHud.Start` registers `"ShowMessage"(int type, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:55799-55809) and `RPC_ShowMessage` calls `ShowMessage` unconditionally (:55848-55851). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)type, text)`, or `0L` to broadcast. No ZDOID needed, so it works in the window before `peer.m_characterID` is populated.

`MessageHud.MessageType` is `TopLeft = 1, Center = 2` (:55705-55709). TopLeft stacks and persists briefly; Center is the big single-line banner vanilla uses for `$msg_blocked`. Text is run through `Localization.Localize` on the RECEIVING client, so sending `"$piece_portal"` renders in that player's own language — a free i18n path for any string with a vanilla token.

NO LENGTH LIMIT and no truncation trap, because this is one-way output that never becomes input. Use it for everything the 10 characters cannot hold: distances, biome names, error explanations, directory listings, permission reasons. Sending 5 toasts in one frame produces 5 stacked TopLeft lines — that is how a directory is delivered. Keep it to ~6 lines before they scroll off.
catalog.playerExperience:
You type `>Haldor` on the portal. As the hover flips to `">Haldor"`, a line appears in the top-left: `Dialed → Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest`. It fades after a few seconds.

You type `?`. Six lines stack up:

`— PORTALS —`
`1 Base      612m   yours`
`2 Haldor  1,140m   public`
`3 Mine2     840m   yours`
`4 Vault   2,300m   LOCKED`
`type >1 .. >4 or >name`

You try a locked one and get a Center banner across the middle of your screen, the same one vanilla uses when a portal is blocked: `Vault is locked by Bjorn.`

This is the workhorse. It carries everything the tag cannot, needs no construction, no proximity and no learning, and it looks identical to vanilla's own messages — a player will not perceive it as 'a mod talking to me'.
failureModes: More than ~6 stacked TopLeft lines scroll off before they can be read.
Center messages are intrusive; overusing them for routine confirmations trains players to ignore the banner that also carries vanilla's real warnings.

Path (A) requires `peer.m_characterID` to be populated — it is `ZDOID.None` between connect and `Game.SpawnPlayer` and again between death and respawn (:100270, :100413). Guard with `!peer.m_characterID.IsNone()` and fall back to path (B).
Path (B) depends on a `MessageHud` existing on the RECEIVING client (it always does) but the registration is global, so another mod registering `"ShowMessage"` server-side would collide.
Toasts are transient — a player who alt-tabs misses the only record of what happened. Pair with the persistent tag echo.
openQuestions: Is `MessageHud.instance` non-null on a dedicated server (which would mean `"ShowMessage"` is already registered in `ZRoutedRpc.m_functions` and a mod re-registering it would throw)? `ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer` dereferences it unguarded under IsDedicated (:80258) while `Game.UpdateSaving` guards it (:100474). IN-GAME: dump `m_functions` keys at server start.
corrections: TopLeft does NOT stack. MessageHud queues TopLeft messages and shows one per second in a single text field (:55864-55869, :55910-55953); five toasts in one frame = five sequential 1-second replacements. Identical text repeated within 4 s is merged with an ' xN' suffix (:55916-55925).

A directory listing must be delivered as ONE message containing embedded '\n' (ZPackage strings carry newlines); whether m_messageText (TMP_Text) wraps/overflows multiple lines is an in-game check, not established by the decompile.
ShowMessage is suppressed entirely while Hud.IsUserHidden() unless showDespiteHiddenHUD, which the RPC path never sets (:55855-55858, :14824).
Every TopLeft/Center message is also appended to MessageHud.m_messageLog (:56056-56062), bounded by m_maxLogMessages.

Rewrite the multi-line claim: TopLeft is a one-slot queue drained at 1 message/second with a 4 s fade (MessageHud.UpdateMessage :55910-55950). N messages sent in one frame display sequentially over N seconds, one at a time. There is no stacking.

Possible workaround for a directory: send ONE TopLeft/Center message containing embedded '\n' — m_messageText is a TMP_Text and will render multiple lines unless the prefab clips/overflows; this is unverified and needs an in-game check (layout, wrapping, vertical growth).

All toasts are also appended to the Logs list capped at m_maxLogMessages and readable in Inventory → Texts → Logs (:61904-61908); that is the only place a full listing persists client-side, and it is the honest 'directory' surface.
Enforcement label: nothing is enforced; the client renders (and drops when HUD is hidden). Mark client-honoured.

Path A vs B: RPC_ShowMessage ignores the sender entirely, so any client can spam any other client's HUD via 'ShowMessage' — irrelevant to the mod but worth noting when choosing path A for per-player addressing.
evidence: MessageHud.ShowMessage (Localize, HUD-hidden drop, single queue, Center single field) — :55853-55897
MessageHud.UpdateMessage one-per-second dequeue and 4 s fade — :55899-55950
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Both paths verified. Player.Start registers 'Message'(int,string,int) on the player's ZNetView only inside if (m_nview.IsOwner()) (:10070-10072); RPC_Message re-checks IsOwner before MessageHud.instance.ShowMessage (:14820-14825); Wonderland PlayerNotify.Toast (PlayerNotify.cs:15-29) sends InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, zdo.m_uid, 'Message', type, text, 0) exactly as claimed. MessageHud.Start registers 'ShowMessage'(int,string) on ZRoutedRpc (:55808) and RPC_ShowMessage calls ShowMessage unconditionally (:55848-55851). MessageType is TopLeft=1, Center=2 (:55705-55709). ShowMessage runs Localization.instance.Localize(text) on the receiver (:55859). However the stacking claim is false: TopLeft messages are Enqueued into m_msgQeue (:55864-55869) and UpdateMessage dequeues ONE per second (m_msgQueueTimer >= 1f, :55910-55919) into the single m_messageText, with an identical consecutive text within 4 s collapsed into an 'xN' counter (:55916-55925). Center replaces a single line and fades over 4 s (:55876-55890). A six-line directory sent as six toasts appears one line at a time over six seconds, not stacked.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] Both delivery paths verified: Player.Start registers 'Message' only when m_nview.IsOwner() (:10070-10072) and RPC_Message re-checks IsOwner (:14820-14825); MessageHud.Start registers routed 'ShowMessage' (:55808) and RPC_ShowMessage calls ShowMessage unconditionally (:55848-55851); MessageType TopLeft=1, Center=2 (:55705-55709); ShowMessage runs Localization.Localize on the receiving client (:55859). But the headline UX claim — 'Sending 5 toasts in one frame produces 5 stacked TopLeft lines — that is how a directory is delivered' — is refuted by the decompile. TopLeft messages go into a single Queue<MsgData> (:55869) and UpdateMessage dequeues at most one message per second (`m_msgQueueTimer >= 1f`, :55917) into the single m_messageText field, replacing the previous text and fading it over 4 s (:55919-55937); identical consecutive text merges into 'x2'. The message log (AddLog :56056-56062) is only rendered in the inventory TextsDialog 'Logs' tab (:61904-61908). A 6-line directory therefore arrives as six one-second slides, each overwriting the last, not a stacked list. Center is likewise one field replaced immediately. The channel is real and useful for single-line toasts; the directory-listing use is not as described. Also ShowMessage drops everything when Hud.IsUserHidden() (:55855-55858).

catalog.name: Feedback: server-pushed map pin
catalog.oneLine: `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` puts a named, permanently-saved pin on a vanilla client's map plus an iconed HUD toast — with no way ever to remove it again.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Game.Start` registers `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"(string pinName, int pinType, Vector3 pos, bool showMap)` on EVERY peer, outside any IsServer branch (:100068). The handler calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation(pos, (PinType)pinType, pinName, showMap)` and, if map mode is None, also `Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f)` — physically turning the player's head toward the target (:100823-100830).

`Minimap.DiscoverLocation` (:58334-58361): if `HaveSimilarPin(pos, type, name, save:true)` it bails (showing `$msg_pin_exist` only when showMap); otherwise `AddPin(pos, type, name, save: true, isChecked: false, 0L)`. In BOTH branches it calls `Player.m_localPlayer.Message(MessageType.TopLeft, "$msg_pin_added: " + name, 0, sprite)` — so every pin push also yields an iconed HUD toast for free.

`HaveSimilarPin` matches name AND type AND save AND `Utils.DistanceXZ < 1f` (:58363-58373), so re-pushing the identical pin with showMap:false is idempotent and silent. `AddPin` clamps an out-of-range PinType to `Icon3` and force-enables that icon's filter if the player had turned it off (:58375-58405) — the server's pins cannot be filtered away.

`Minimap.PinType` verified: Icon0=0, Icon1, Icon2, Icon3, Death=4, Bed=5, Icon4=6, Shout=7, None=8, Boss=9, Player=10, RandomEvent=11, Ping=12, EventArea=13, Hildir1-3, Memorial=17 (:56079-56099).

THE FATAL CAVEAT: `save: true` is hard-coded. The pin goes permanently into that player's own PlayerProfile map data on their disk. There is NO removal RPC anywhere in the assembly. A demolished or renamed portal leaves its pin stuck on every player's map forever, and a re-push under a new name creates a SECOND pin. This is a one-shot discovery gift, NOT a live-synced set — TortalPortal's client-side PortalMapPins rebuilds every 2 s precisely because it can add AND remove.

SANE USE: push exactly once per (player, portal) when that player first NAMES a portal, storing the pairs in mod state so a restart does not re-push.

SECOND, NON-SAVING CHANNEL: `ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons` / the `"LocationIcons"` routed RPC (:113581-113607) replaces the client's whole `m_locationIcons` dictionary, which `Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` rebuilds from every 5 s as `save:false` pins — fully server-controlled and removable, but ICON-ONLY with no name, and rendering only for names present in the client's compiled sprite list.
catalog.playerExperience:
You name your first portal: press E, type `#Base`, Enter. The hover flips to `"#Base"` and simultaneously a toast with a small map-pin icon appears: `Pin added: Base`. You open your map and there it is, a named marker at your base, exactly like one you placed yourself — because it IS a pin you now own, saved into your character file, surviving logout.

Each new portal you name drops another pin. After a week your map has every portal labelled and you never placed a pin by hand.

The ugly part arrives when you tear down the mine portal. The `Mine2` pin stays on your map forever. You can delete it manually the vanilla way but the server cannot do it for you and will never try. Rename `Mine2` to `DeepMine` and you now have two pins a metre apart.

So the mod must be conservative: one pin per portal per player, pushed once at naming time, with a toast reading `Pin added: Base (delete it yourself if you move it)`. Anything more aggressive turns the player's map into litter.
failureModes: `save: true` is hard-coded and there is no removal RPC — every pushed pin is permanent on that player's disk.
Renaming a portal and re-pushing creates a duplicate pin one metre from the old one, because `HaveSimilarPin` matches on name.
`RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation` unguarded (:100825); harmless on a client but it means the RPC must never be sent to the server's own peer id.
`AddPin` force-enables the icon filter (:58400-58403), overriding a player's deliberate choice to hide that pin category.
Repeated pushes with showMap:true spam `$msg_pin_exist` and re-centre the player's map, which is intensely annoying. Always send showMap:false for routine pushes.
prerequisites: Per-(player, portal) pushed-pin ledger persisted in mod state
openQuestions: Does `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` render identically on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client? Wonderland ships it behind StarterBoatMapPin but carries no dated live-test note for it. IN-GAME: push a pin, confirm it appears, log out and back in to confirm save:true persisted, then re-send the identical payload and confirm HaveSimilarPin suppresses the duplicate.
Which names does the client's compiled `Minimap.m_locationIcons` sprite list contain? That bounds what the non-saving LocationIcons overlay can render. IN-GAME: enumerate it on a client.
corrections: The LocationIcons secondary channel is overwritten by vanilla: the server re-sends the real location list on every new peer (ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer :113615) and broadcasts SendLocationIcons(0L) whenever a location with m_iconPlaced is spawned (:114998-115001). A mod using this channel must postfix SendLocationIcons (private) or re-send after those events.

RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse also physically turns the player's view toward the pin for 3.5 s when the map is closed (:100826-100829); push pins while the player is already looking at the portal or accept the head turn.
Add: PinType.Icon4 (=6) is the vanilla portal icon, so a pushed portal pin can use the same glyph players place by hand — cite :56085.

Add: the SetLookDir head-yank (:100826-100829) happens on EVERY push while the map is closed, including idempotent re-pushes that show no toast; a passive re-sync at login would still turn the player's head. Reinforces 'push once'.

Add for the LocationIcons channel: replacing the dictionary drops vanilla's real location icons (Haldor, Hildir, bosses, start temple) unless the mod re-includes them from ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons (:113627-113640); portal markers must borrow an existing sprite name from Minimap.m_locationIcons and render double-size with no name (:58690-58696). SendLocationIcons is private; the mod invokes the routed RPC directly.
evidence: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons / RPC_LocationIcons — :113581-113607 ; callers :113615, :115000 ; GetLocationIcons server branch
Minimap.UpdateLocationPins (5 s rebuild, save:false, sprite-gated) — UpdateLocationPins body
ZoneSystem 'LocationIcons' client registration — :113448-113454; SendLocationIcons / RPC_LocationIcons — :113581-113607; GetLocationIcons — :113627-113640
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed] Game.Start registers 'RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse'(string,int,Vector3,bool) on ZRoutedRpc outside the IsServer branch (:100067, branch begins :100069). RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (:100823-100830) calls Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation and, when map mode is None, Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f). Minimap.DiscoverLocation (:58334-58361): HaveSimilarPin(pos,type,name,save:true) → bail (Center '$msg_pin_exist' only if showMap); else AddPin(pos,type,name,save:true,isChecked:false,0L) and a TopLeft '$msg_pin_added: name' with the type sprite in both showMap branches. HaveSimilarPin (:58363-58373) matches name && type && save && DistanceXZ < 1f, so identical re-push with showMap:false is silent. AddPin (:58375-58406) clamps out-of-range types to Icon3 and calls ToggleIconFilter if that icon was hidden. PinType enum order confirmed Icon0..Memorial=17 (:56079-56099). No routed RPC anywhere removes a pin (RemovePin is only called locally at :44133, :45472, :57056). ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons/RPC_LocationIcons (:113581-113607) replaces m_locationIcons wholesale and Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds save:false PinType.None pins from it every 5 s, dropping any not in the dictionary and adding only names with a sprite in m_locationIcons (UpdateLocationPins body). Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263 uses the pin RPC as described.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every cited mechanism holds. Game.Start registers 'RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse'(string,int,Vector3,bool) outside the IsServer branch (:100068); the handler calls Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation and, when m_mode==None, SetLookDir toward pos (:100823-100830). Minimap.DiscoverLocation (:58334-58361): HaveSimilarPin(save:true) bail (Center '$msg_pin_exist' only if showMap), else AddPin(save:true) and a TopLeft '$msg_pin_added: name' toast with the pin sprite in both showMap branches. HaveSimilarPin requires name+type+save+DistanceXZ<1 (:58363-58373). AddPin clamps invalid types to Icon3 and force-enables the icon filter (:58375-58405). PinType enum order verified Icon0..Memorial=17 (:56079-56099). No routed RPC for pin removal exists (grep of ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register hits only RPC_Ping and LocationIcons among pin/map-related names). LocationIcons: client registers 'LocationIcons' in the non-server branch (:113453); RPC_LocationIcons replaces m_locationIcons wholesale (:113597-113607); Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds save:false, name-empty pins every 5 s only for names GetLocationIcon can resolve (:58660-58700). Caveats stated in the option are accurate.

catalog.name: Feedback: the server as a speaking voice (fabricated ChatMessage)
catalog.oneLine: One forged `"ChatMessage"` RPC yields a chat line, floating world text and a labelled animated map pin from an arbitrary named speaker.
catalog.howItWorks:
`Chat.Awake` registers `"ChatMessage"(Vector3 pos, int type, UserInfo user, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:41626); `Chat.RPC_ChatMessage` hands it to `OnNewChatMessage` (:41970-41973). The server forges one: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ChatMessage", worldPos, (int)Talker.Type.Shout, userInfo, text)` with `userInfo.Name` set to anything — `"Portal Network"`, `"The Gate"`.

WHAT ONE PACKET PRODUCES (`OnNewChatMessage` :41775-41816): `type != Ping` → `AddString(sender.UserId, text, type)`, a real persistent scrollable chat line; `AddInworldText(go, senderID, pos, type, sender, text)`, floating text at `pos` with TTL `m_worldTextTTL` = 5 s, Shout uppercased and yellow; and `Minimap.UpdateShoutPins`/`UpdatePingPins` render a large animated map pin labelled `"<Name>: <TEXT>"` for Shout or `"<Name>: PING"` for Ping (:57591-57650).

GATE: `AddInworldText` is skipped only when `Minimap.instance.m_mode == MapMode.None` AND the position is farther than `m_nomapPingDistance` (50 m) (:41808). Normal play has the small minimap up, so it always runs.

PERMISSIONS: `OnNewChatMessage` routes through `RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync` unless the sender id equals the local character — and that is a one-line stub returning Granted synchronously in 1.0.7 (:88350-88353). No mute filter to defeat, no async delay.

SANITISATION: `text.Replace('<',' ').Replace('>',' ')` (:41795-41796). No rich text — and note this mangles a `>` sigil, so strip sigils before speaking a tag string.

PING TYPE (3) is the interesting one for portals: NO chat line, world text forced to the literal `"PING"`, and a labelled map pin at the given position. So the server can drop a transient, self-expiring beacon at a portal's DESTINATION — a 'this is where you are about to go' preview that costs nothing and leaves nothing behind, unlike the permanently-saved `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` pin.
catalog.playerExperience:
You dial your portal to Haldor. Along with the tag flip and the toast, a line appears in your chat log:

`Portal Network: → HALDOR, 1,140M NNE, BLACK FOREST`

and for five seconds a yellow shout-text hangs above the portal frame saying the same thing, and a labelled marker pulses on your minimap at Haldor's position so you can see where you are about to end up. Because it went into the chat log you can scroll back ten minutes later and find out where you sent yourself.

The beacon variant: you type `>Haldor` and a Ping-type message drops a pulsing marker at the destination with no chat spam at all. You check your map, see where it is, and decide whether to step through.

The risk is tone. A server that 'speaks' in the chat log reads as a bot, and if it speaks too often players tune it out. Reserve it for consequential events: a dial confirmed, a lock changed, a portal destroyed.
failureModes: `<` and `>` are replaced with spaces (:41795-41796), mangling any echoed sigil and ruling out rich text.
Shout-type messages clutter the chat log; over-use trains players to ignore the channel.
The forged speaker name is arbitrary, which is also an impersonation vector if the mod ever lets player-supplied text set it.
Ping type suppresses the chat line entirely and forces the world text to `"PING"` — you cannot say anything with it, only point.
`AddInworldText` is skipped in nomap worlds beyond 50 m (:41808), so the world-text half silently vanishes on those servers.
openQuestions: Does a forged ChatMessage with an arbitrary `UserInfo` render its speaker name without a platform lookup on a Steam client? `UserInfo.GetLocalUser()` is the only construction vanilla uses. IN-GAME: send one with a fabricated name and read the chat line.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Feedback: the server as a speaking voice (fabricated ChatMessage)
corrections: REFUTED: 'Portal Network: ...' chat-log line. Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) (:45933-45959) ignores UserInfo.Name, looks the sender up in ZNet.m_players via TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID (:81477-81493) and returns without adding a line when not found. A headless server is never in that list (UpdatePlayerList :81248). Chat line only achievable by sending a real listed player's PlatformUserID, and it is then attributed to that player's name.
The arbitrary speaker name is real only for the floating world text and the map pin (WorldTextInstance.m_name :41531 -> FilterUGC identity :94588-94591; pins :57604, :57633).

Single slot per sender: FindExistingWorldText(senderID) (:41925-41935) makes all server-originated messages share ONE WorldTextInstance per client (server sender id = ZRoutedRpc.m_id, :83565). A second message replaces the first; a Shout and a Ping cannot coexist; 'one label per portal' is impossible via ChatMessage (use RPC_DamageText for that).
Ping/Shout world text is never distance-culled: off-screen texts are clamped to the screen edge (:41843-41858). A beacon at a distant destination is also a 5 s HUD-edge label.
Shout/Normal messages force the chat window open (m_hideTimer = 0, :41799).
m_worldTextTTL is at :41589, not :41594.
Enforcement: client-honoured (client-rendered feedback), not server-enforced.

Chat-log line requires UserId to match an entry in the client's ZNet.m_players (Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID) :45950-45954, ZNet.TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID client :81668); otherwise the message is dropped with a LogError and no line appears.

The chat-log speaker name is playerInfo.m_name from the player list, never UserInfo.Name — 'Portal Network' cannot be the chat-log speaker; only floating text and the map pin honour the forged Name (WorldTextInstance.m_name :41531).

All server messages share one world-text/pin slot because FindExistingWorldText keys on senderID = server's ZRoutedRpc.m_id (:41919-41928, :83581); successive messages overwrite each other rather than stacking.
Ping beacon label is '<Name>: PING' with the text field ignored (:41898-41901, :57603) — encode the destination in Name.
PlatformUserID(string) parsing is in the Splatform assembly (not decompiled); use a real online player's m_userInfo.m_id.ToString() rather than an invented id string.
Enforcement is client-honoured (server sends, vanilla client renders); the RPC has no sender validation so any client can forge it equally.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:downgraded] The RPC, its registration, the sanitisation, the permission stub, the Ping/Shout world text and the animated map pins all check out at the cited lines. The headline claim does NOT: a chat-log line 'from an arbitrary named speaker' is impossible against a vanilla client. Chat.OnNewChatMessage (:41775-41816) calls AddString(sender.UserId, text, type) — the PlatformUserID overload, Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) at :45933-45959 — which never reads UserInfo.Name. It resolves the display name via ZNet.TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID (:45950 -> :81477-81493) from the client's m_players list (populated by RPC_PlayerList :81397-81416 from the server's UpdatePlayerList :81245-81300). If the forged UserId matches no listed player it logs 'Failed to get player info...' and RETURNS: no chat line at all. A headless dedicated server never lists itself (UpdatePlayerList skips the self-entry when SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == Null, :81248), so there is no 'server' identity to borrow. The only way to get a chat line is to send a real player's PlatformUserID (e.g. the recipient's own, from ZNet.m_players[i].m_userInfo.m_id), and the line is then attributed to THAT player's name, not 'Portal Network'. The arbitrary name DOES work for the floating world text and the map pin: WorldTextInstance.m_name => m_userInfo.GetDisplayName() (:41531) = CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC which is an identity function (:94588-94591), and the Shout/Ping pins label with tempShout.m_name (:57604, :57633). Second unlisted constraint: Chat.AddInworldText (:41873-41876) reuses the WorldTextInstance found by FindExistingWorldText(senderID) (:41925-41935); every server-originated message carries the same m_senderPeerID = the server's ZRoutedRpc.m_id (:83565), so a client can hold exactly ONE server world text/pin at a time — a new message overwrites the previous one's position, type, text and timer. Fan-out ('one per portal') and a simultaneous Shout line + Ping beacon are impossible on this channel. Third: world text is not distance-culled; UpdateWorldTexts (:41843-41858) clamps off-screen texts to the screen edge, so a Ping beacon 1 km away also renders as an edge-clamped '<Name>: PING' HUD label for 5 s, not only a map pin. Fourth: AddString is only skipped for type Ping; for Shout it also sets m_hideTimer = 0 (:41799), popping the chat window open on every server message. Delivery path holds: InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid,...) with targetPeerID != m_id never runs a local handler and RouteRPC unicasts to that peer (:83557-83583), so no Chat.instance is needed on the server. Enforcement relabelled: this is a client-rendered feedback channel, not a rule.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] The world-text and map-pin halves hold; the chat-LOG half with an arbitrary speaker name is refuted by the source. Chat.OnNewChatMessage (SERVER :41775-41816, identical in client :41806) calls `AddString(sender.UserId, text, type)` — the Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) overload (:45933-45958, client :45933-45990). That overload does `if (!ZNet.TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID(user, out playerInfo)) { LogError(...); return; }` (client :81668-81684 iterates ZNet.m_players comparing m_userInfo.m_id). A forged UserId that is not in the client's player list produces NO chat line at all. When it IS a real online player's id, the displayed speaker is `playerInfo.m_name` from the player list, NOT the forged UserInfo.Name. So 'Portal Network: → HALDOR' can never appear in the chat log; the best achievable is '<some online character name>: → HALDOR' (e.g. the recipient's own name). By contrast AddInworldText (:41873-41917) and the shout/ping pins (Minimap.UpdateShoutPins/UpdatePingPins :57592-57650) use WorldTextInstance.m_name => m_userInfo.GetDisplayName() (:41531) = CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC(Name) which returns Name unchanged (:94588-94591) — so the floating text and the map-pin label DO carry the arbitrary name. Further corrections: (1) AddInworldText keys world texts by senderID via FindExistingWorldText (:41919-41928); every server-originated message has senderID = server ZRoutedRpc m_id (:83581), so the server owns exactly ONE world-text/pin slot — a second message (or a Ping beacon after a Shout) overwrites the first rather than stacking; two 'speakers' from the server share the slot too. (2) Ping-type world text is forced to the literal 'PING' and the pin label is `Name + ': PING'` (:41898-41901, :57603) — the destination can only be conveyed through the Name field. (3) Permission stub confirmed: RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync returns Granted synchronously (:88350-88353); the `senderID == LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID` short-circuit (:41777) never fires for a server sender. (4) UserInfo.Deserialize does `new PlatformUserID(pkg.ReadString())` (:72788-72792) — PlatformUserID lives in the Splatform assembly which is not in the decompile set; parse behaviour on a non-'Platform_id' string is unverified, so pass a real online player's `m_userInfo.m_id.ToString()` from the server's ZNet.m_players rather than a made-up string. (5) Sanitisation confirmed (:41795-41796); `<`/`>` become spaces. (6) Gate confirmed: `Minimap.m_mode != 0 || dist <= m_nomapPingDistance(50f, :56396)` (:41808). TTL 5 s confirmed (:41589). Enforcement is not 'server-enforced' — the server sends a packet and an unmodified client renders it; nothing is enforced. Note the same RPC has no sender check: any connected client can forge ChatMessage from any online player's id just as the server can.

catalog.name: Feedback: floating world text over a portal (RPC_DamageText)
catalog.oneLine: Arbitrary text hovering in 3D above any object within 30 m of the viewer, addressed to one player — the only surface that says WHICH portal changed.
catalog.playerExperience:
You walk into your portal hall — six portals in a row in a stone building. You crouch (the arming gesture). For three seconds a line of orange text pops above each frame:

`→ BASE`   `→ HALDOR`   `→ MINE2`   `→ BOG`   `— UNLINKED —`   `LOCKED: VAULT`

Then it fades. You know instantly which door goes where without hovering six objects one at a time. You walk into the third one.

When you dial a portal, a green `→ HALDOR` floats up out of its frame — the same visual language as a heal number, which every player already reads as 'good thing happened here'.

The best surface in this list for disambiguating which object a command applied to, and it costs one small RPC.
failureModes: 30 m culling (`m_maxTextDistance`, :46338) means nothing renders for a distant portal — useless for remote feedback.
`TextType.TooHard` overwrites the string with `$msg_toohard` and `Blocked` prefixes `$msg_blocked:` — both mangle the payload.
Text is localized on the client, so a raw string containing a `$` prefix that happens to match a token is substituted unexpectedly.
Broadcasting instead of per-peer spams everyone standing at a hub.
The payload is hand-packed into a ZPackage; a field-order mistake produces garbage with no error.
openQuestions: Does `Bonus` text render legibly against a lit portal at 2.2 m above the frame, or does it clip into the portal's own emissive glow? Purely visual. IN-GAME: push one and look.

catalog.name: Feedback: status effect as a persistent state indicator
catalog.oneLine: The server grants a vanilla status effect so the player carries a buff icon representing portal state — the only indicator that survives walking away from the portal.
catalog.howItWorks:
`SEMan` registers `"RPC_AddStatusEffect"(int nameHash, bool resetTime, int itemLevel, float skillLevel, int variant)` on the character's own ZNetView (SEMan shares `Character.m_nview`) (:28724-28729). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "RPC_AddStatusEffect", nameHash, true, 0, 0f, -1)`. `Internal_AddStatusEffect` (:28831-28850) resolves the hash purely against the RECEIVING client's own `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects`, so only effects every vanilla client already ships can be granted. Wonderland ships this as `StatusEffectRpc.Grant` (Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs:27) with a `StatusEffectRegistry` keyed on `effect.name` (not `m_name`).

WHAT IT BUYS: a persistent, always-visible UI element where the player is already trained to look — the buff bar — with an icon and a countdown, that survives walking away. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit gives persistent per-player UI state.

THE HARD LIMIT: there is NO RemoveStatusEffect RPC anywhere in the assembly. A granted effect can only be allowed to expire. So the vocabulary is restricted to short, self-expiring effects, and 'armed' must be a re-pinged short buff rather than a toggle. `BuffRosterEngine` is the reference re-ping loop: `RepingInterval = clamp(ttl*0.4, 0.2, ttl-0.2)`, decremented by real frame dt (Wonderland Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:121).

The semantics are borrowed, not authored: granting `Rested` to mean 'armed' is a lie the game acts on (it actually gives regen). Pick effects whose mechanical side-effect is harmless or thematically apt — an asset question, not a code one.
catalog.playerExperience:
You crouch near a portal. A new icon appears in your buff bar with a short timer. You now know, without looking at the portal or reading anything, that the server is listening — and the timer tells you how long before it stops.

You pick a destination and stand up; the icon fades. You walk through the portal. On arrival a different icon appears for ten seconds — the server's way of saying 'this trip was logged'.

Honestly the weakest feedback channel here. The icon has a vanilla meaning players already know, and using `Rested` to mean 'portal armed' confuses people who then wonder why they are getting regen. Its one real strength is persistence — the only indicator that stays on screen after you stop looking at the portal — so it is worth exactly one slot, for the armed state, and nothing else.
failureModes: No RemoveStatusEffect RPC exists — an effect can only expire, so every state must be modelled as a re-pinged short buff.
Effect semantics are borrowed: any effect chosen carries its real gameplay side-effect (regen, resistance, movement) which the player will notice and misattribute.
Only effects present in the client's `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects` can be granted; no novel icon or name is possible.
`ObjectDB.instance` is frequently still null at the ZNetScene.Awake 'world ready' hook (live-confirmed in Wonderland 2026-09-11) — any registry build must retry per tick until it resolves.
A re-ping loop that stalls leaves the icon showing a stale state for up to the effect's full TTL.
openQuestions: Is there a vanilla status effect with a near-zero mechanical side-effect and a neutral icon, suitable as a pure indicator? This is asset data. IN-GAME: enumerate `ObjectDB.instance.m_StatusEffects` and inspect each one's tooltip and modifiers.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Feedback: status effect as a persistent state indicator
corrections: Restrict to effects with m_ttl > 0: StatusEffect.IsDone() only expires when m_ttl > 0 (see IsDone), so a ttl-0 effect granted via RPC can never be removed by the server — a permanent, irreversible footgun. BuffRosterEngine's 120 s re-ping for ttl<=0 effects (:112) is not a mitigation for this.
SEMan.AddStatusEffect(StatusEffect,...) runs statusEffect.CanAdd(m_character) (:28866) — virtual, subclass overrides may reject silently; the server gets no result back.
Only effects with a non-null m_icon render in the buff bar; verify the asset, not just the name.
Enforcement: client-honoured (owner-side IsOwner/CanAdd gate, client-rendered), not server-enforced.
Effect duration is the asset's m_ttl; the server cannot set or shorten it. The buff-bar countdown reflects m_ttl, not the mod's arming window, unless the two are deliberately matched.
The icon does not fade when the player stands up; it persists until m_ttl elapses after the last re-ping (no removal RPC exists — verified by grep of all Register calls).
resetTime:true on an already-active vanilla effect (e.g. Rested) resets its timer and extends the real buff (Internal_AddStatusEffect :28833-28840).
Every fresh grant fires the effect's m_startMessage and start effects (StatusEffect.Setup :31079-31086).
Only effects with m_ttl > 0 self-expire (IsDone :31173-31179); an m_ttl == 0 effect granted by mistake is permanent until relog.
Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Wire path verified: SEMan ctor registers `RPC_AddStatusEffect`(int,bool,int,float,int) on the Character's ZNetView (:28724-28729); RPC_AddStatusEffect gates on m_nview.IsOwner() (:28823-28829) which is true for the recipient's own Player; Internal_AddStatusEffect resolves via ObjectDB.instance.GetStatusEffect(nameHash) on the receiving client (:28831-28850) and, if already present with resetTime, calls ResetTime() (m_time = 0, :31182-31185). AddStatusEffect(StatusEffect,...) clones, calls CanAdd (virtual, default true :31074-31077) and Setup (:31079-31086), which fires m_startMessage via Character.Message and TriggerStartEffects. A grep of every Register call finds no removal RPC — only `RPC_AddStatusEffect` (:28728) and Character's `RPC_UpdateEffects` (:139442, unrelated) — so the 'no RemoveStatusEffect RPC' claim is confirmed. IsDone = `m_ttl > 0 && m_time > m_ttl` (:31173-31179). Corrections to the player experience: (1) duration is owned by the asset's m_ttl, not the server — the icon countdown shows the effect's own TTL, so 'the timer tells you how long before it stops [listening]' is only true if the mod's arming window is set equal to the chosen effect's m_ttl; (2) 'You pick a destination and stand up; the icon fades' is false — the server cannot remove it, so it persists for the full m_ttl after the last re-ping; (3) resetTime:true on an effect the player ALREADY has (e.g. Rested from a bed) resets its timer to zero each ping and thereby EXTENDS the real buff (:28833-28840), a mechanical side-effect beyond the icon; (4) every first grant fires the effect's m_startMessage and start effects (:31081-31085), so each arming pings a vanilla message like the effect's own toast; (5) the mod must ship a vetted list of vanilla effects with short m_ttl > 0, an icon, and harmless m_attributes/SE_Stats — effects with m_ttl == 0 never expire client-side (IsDone :31174) and would become permanent until relog. The RPC routes to a ZDO (HandleRoutedRPC → ZNetScene.FindInstance → ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC :83645-83664), which always succeeds for the player's own character. Enforcement: client-honoured (the client applies the effect from its own ObjectDB; nothing is enforced; any client can send the same RPC to any character ZDO — no sender check).

catalog.name: Feedback: forced teleport as the delivery mechanism
catalog.oneLine: Skip the portal entirely — the server moves the player with a routed RPC, visually indistinguishable from a portal transit, but bypassing every vanilla rule.
catalog.howItWorks:
TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS against a 100% vanilla client.
(A) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` — `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` with no sender, admin, key or item check (:41962-41968), registered in `Chat.Awake` on every client (:41627). The server needs no `Chat.instance`: `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is a one-line wrapper (:41957-41960) and `InvokeRoutedRPC` with `targetPeerID != m_id` never touches a local handler.
(B) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)` — `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is registered on every Character in `Character.Awake` (:886) and gates on `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:4126-4132), so it can only move that character on its own owner.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A PORTAL: `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` picks the teleport swirl purely from `ShowTeleportAnimation()` = `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` (:47872, :15386), and `TeleportWorld.Teleport` passes `distantTeleport: true` (:143546). A forced teleport with `true` is byte-for-byte the same experience — same black screen, same swirl, same ~8 s duration. Nothing to add, nothing missing.

ALWAYS PASS TRUE. With `false`, if `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses at the destination the client rubber-bands the player back to the origin and shows `$msg_portal_blocked` (:15369-15374) — a lie that will be reported as a mod bug. With `true` it cannot fail: the 15 s fallback force-lands on `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` (:15360-15366).

MANDATORY SERVER PRE-CHECKS, all off the character ZDO: `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (:78403) — `UpdateTeleport` runs only inside the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate` (:10213, :10226), so a teleport to a dead player latches `m_teleporting` and never executes. `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` (:78457) — `UpdateAttach` (:10217) runs BEFORE `UpdateTeleport` (:10226) and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and `AttachStop` early-returns while `m_sleeping` (:15892), so a sleeping player is stuck outright. And your own cooldown table: `Player.TeleportTo` returns false with NO message if `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15309-15316), and the cooldown is zeroed every tick while teleporting (:15331-15336), so the real dead window is the whole ~8 s trip plus 2 s. `m_teleporting` is a private compiled bool never written to any ZDO (:9901) — the server can NEVER see it. Space forced teleports ≥12 s.
catalog.playerExperience:
You crouch at the portal, pick Haldor, and instead of walking through the frame the screen goes black with the same swirling teleport animation you have seen a thousand times. Eight seconds later you are standing outside Haldor's tent. If you did not know a mod was involved you would assume you had walked into a portal.

The difference you might notice: you did it carrying a full stack of iron and nothing stopped you.

Try again immediately and nothing at all happens — no message, no error, no swirl. That is vanilla's 2-second cooldown silently eating the request, and the server has no way to know. A good mod tracks its own send times and says `Wait 9s` instead of leaving you confused.

Best used NOT as the primary movement — walking into a portal is more satisfying and free — but as the escape hatch: 'send me home', the admin rescue, the 'you fell out of the world' recovery.
failureModes: Bypasses `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, ward checks and `Inventory.IsTeleportable` entirely; every rule must be re-implemented, and the ore check CANNOT be because the server never holds the player's inventory.

Silent failure in both directions: `TeleportTo` returns false, both handlers discard it (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent. The only after-the-fact signal is the character ZDO position changing ~2 s later.
The cooldown window is the whole teleport plus 2 s (≥10 s), not 2 s after the RPC — anything retrying faster burns every retry.
A dead player latches `m_teleporting` true and never advances; check `ZDOVars.s_dead` first.
An attached player ping-pongs between attach point and target every tick; a sleeping one is stuck outright. Check `ZDOVars.s_inBed`.
`distantTeleport: false` rubber-bands the player back with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked`.
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-visited, ungenerated zone within the 15 s fallback on low-end hardware? The gates are clear in code but terrain-generation latency is empirical. IN-GAME: force-teleport a test player 8 km into unexplored Ashlands and time the black screen; confirm no fall damage and no '$msg_portal_blocked'.
catalog.id: player-ux-no-client:Feedback: forced teleport as the delivery mechanism

Forced teleport does not increment PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed (only TeleportWorld.Teleport does, :143547) — cosmetic.
A sleeping player is deferred, not stuck: Game.SleepStop → SetSleeping(false) + AttachStop (:100761-100767) lets the latched teleport complete on waking.

s_inBed only covers beds (AttachStart sets s_inBed = isBed :15799); chair/throne attachment also blocks the teleport via UpdateAttach re-snapping (:15820-15837) and prevents IsAreaReady from ever passing. Distant teleport duration is >= 8 s AND gated on ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target) (:15348, :82064-82080); it can exceed 8 s and can hang indefinitely if the target area never becomes ready.
The player transform is moved at t = 2 s (:15342-15347), not at the end of the swirl; a server-side position watcher must whitelist the jump.
Minimum safe spacing is 8 s + 2 s cooldown = 10 s; 12 s is a margin, not a derived constant.

Enforcement is client-honoured: the client decides whether to execute (cooldown, IsTeleporting, dead, attached) and can silently drop the request; the RPC also has no sender check so any client can teleport any other player.
