verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified end to end. TeleportWorld.Teleport does a bare ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection) and reads only GetPosition/GetRotation (:143539-143546); TargetFound requires only that the client's ZDOMan holds the ZDO (:143640-143655). CreateNewZDO(pos, 0): ZDOPool.Get→Init sets Valid=true which sets m_prefab=0 (:73513-73517, :73470-73478), so prefabHash resolves to 0 and AddIfPortal returns early (:77734-77737); ZDO.Initialize files it in m_objectsBySector (:73496-73502). Client: RPC_ZDOData accepts any prefab (client :77217-77290, no validity test), the client never removes ZDOs except on destroy (client m_objectsByID.Remove only at :77129), CreateObject returns null silently for prefab 0 and LogWarning for unknown hash (client :82225-82237), and CreateObjectsSorted destroys null-instantiations only under ZNet.instance.IsServer() (client :82363-82369). IsAreaReady skips prefab-0/unknown ZDOs via IsPrefabZDOValid (client :82215-82223, :82305), so the arriving player's loading gate is not blocked. Save: AddObjectsPerChunk includes every Persistent non-portal ZDO (:77572); FilterZDO puts unknown prefabs into warningZDOs and WarnAndRemoveBrokenZDOs logs 'Will load anyway' (:76346-76375) — note FilterZDO only warns when newVersion is true, otherwise loads silently. Reciprocal source↔anchor survives RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) regardless of iteration order, and load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals enumerates s_connectionsHashData for all ZDOs, not m_portalObjects (:77850-77893, GetAllConnectionZDOIDs :75414-75424). Moving: SetSector takes the normal re-file path for prefab 0 (:73752-73768) and InternalSetPosition bumps revision only when IsOwner (:73734-73745), so SetOwner first is required, as stated. Server-side destruction of the anchor is impossible via ZNetScene because the server's reference zone maps to sector 0 (:100465, SectorToIndex :115760-115772) and an in-world anchor is never there. Corrections: (a) the uninstall sentence contradicts itself — after uninstall the link survives while the anchor exists (pass 1 sees target non-null, tag equal, connection non-None) and is cleared only once the anchor is purged; write it that way; (b) arrival offset comes from the SOURCE portal's m_exitDistance (:143545), not a fixed 1 m unless the source is stock; (c) the anchor is a bare ZDO nobody owns after ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it to nearby peers (:76901-76924) — harmless, but a vanilla client's RPC_DestroyZDO has no sender check (:76950-76960) so hostile clients can delete it like any ZDO; re-assert tick must re-mint; (d) the '1/30 s re-attempt' is correct (CreateDestroyObjects timer client :82262-82266, Created never set) and for a custom hash the LogWarning fires on every one of those passes — prefer prefab 0 as stated.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified end to end. TeleportWorld.Teleport performs a bare ZDOMan.GetZDO(connectionId) and uses only GetPosition/GetRotation (:143539-143548); TargetFound only needs GetZDO non-null, else RequestZDO (:143640-143655) → server RPC_RequestZDO → peer.ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692, :75998-76001) whose AddForceSendZdos path sends regardless of area (ShouldSend returns true for a ZDO the peer has never seen, :76127-76139). CreateNewZDO(pos, 0) skips AddIfPortal (0 ∉ PortalPrefabHash, :76684-76692, :77732-77736) and Initialize files it in m_objectsBySector (:73496-73502); prefab 0 is a valid ZDO (IsValid = m_prefab != -1, :73513-73516). Runtime reconciliation: GetPortalList iterates only m_portalObjects (:77648-77656) so the anchor is never a pass-2 candidate; pass 1 on the source requires the anchor's tag to match and its connection to be non-None (:100600-100604), satisfied by the reciprocal write. Client: CreateObject returns null silently for prefab 0 and logs 'Missing prefab hash' for unknown hashes (client :82225-82237); only `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` destroys uncreatable ZDOs (client :82361-82367), and the dedicated server never sees the anchor in its near set because its reference zone clamps to sector 0 (:100465, :115760-115774) — PROVIDED the anchor lies inside the ±256-zone grid. Save: Persistent non-portal ZDOs go to normal chunks (:77572), FilterZDO puts unknown/zero prefabs in warningZDOs and loads them (:76346-76375), RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps the pair because both endpoints resolve (:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks from hash data (:77850-77893). Moving: InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only when IsOwner (:73734-73745) and SetSector re-files non-portal ZDOs (:73752-73768). Arrival robustness: Player.UpdateTeleport calls ZoneSystem.FindFloor / GetSolidHeight on the client after the 8 s minimum (:15334-15375), so a slightly wrong y is corrected client-side. Corrections: (1) moving the anchor calls ZDOSectorInvalidated (:73764-73767) → each peer that holds the anchor outside its active area gets it removed from peer.m_zdos and an invalidate notice (:75988-75996, client :77230-77233 InvalidateSector) — the client's copy keeps the OLD position and GetZDO still succeeds, so a distant traveller whose client cached the anchor teleports to the stale coordinate; follow every move with ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(anchor) (the peer entry was removed, so ShouldSend is true). (2) The anchor must stay within |x|,|z| < ~16352 m; outside, SectorToIndex returns sector 0 (:115760-115774), which is exactly the bucket the dedicated server's CreateDestroyObjects scans (:82268-82276), and the server would then hit the IsServer 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' branch (:82141-82147). (3) The uninstall-residue sentence is self-contradictory; the actual behaviour is: the anchor persists ('Will load anyway'), pass 1 keeps the source linked to it because tag matches and its connection is non-None, so the source stays a one-way door to an invisible spot until purged. (4) Client-side cost: for prefab 0 the not-Created anchor is re-sorted and re-attempted every CreateDestroyObjects pass (1/30 s, client :82489-82493) while in the near set — silent but nonzero; custom hash adds a LogWarning per pass.

catalog.name: Admin Coordinates
catalog.oneLine: An operator names an X/Z (and optional Y/rotation) in the config or server console; the mod validates it against procedural terrain and drops a phantom there.
catalog.howItWorks: Input: a hot-reloaded config entry (Wonderland PollConfigFile pattern) or a Terminal.ConsoleCommand registered `onlyServer:true` (usable from the dedicated server stdin and by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand, which gates on the adminlist). Validation must be pure math because every ZoneSystem raycast helper (GetGroundHeight, GetSolidHeight, FindFloor, IsBlocked, GetGroundData) silently returns its fallback on a dedicated server (Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position at 1e6 so no terrain collider exists near real coordinates). Use: `float h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)`; reject if `x*x+z*z > 110250000` (beyond waterEdge, height is −400); reject if `h < 30` unless the operator flagged 'allow water'; reject if `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(new Vector3(x,h,z))`; reject if `WorldGenerator.instance.GetNormal(new Vector2(x,z), 1f).y < 0.7` (steep); reject if y > 3000 (interior space). Optional structure check: `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(pos, 3f)` and reject if any ZDO whose prefab has a Piece component is within 1.5 m (approximate — no colliders). For a fast pre-filter use `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` (12 m grid, O(1)). Then create the phantom (Option 1) at (x, h + 0.2, z) with rotation from the config yaw, tag = the operator's label, and pair it to the operator-named source (identified by position or existing tag, since ZDOIDs change per load). Arrival correctness on the client: Player.UpdateTeleport calls ZoneSystem.FindFloor(target) (raycast down 1000 m from target+1 m) which hits the terrain the client generated locally; if the pre-flattening WorldGenerator height is a metre off, the 8 s/IsAreaReady gate plus the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback still lands the player on the actual surface. Tick cost: creation is one-shot; validation is ~10 noise evaluations; the maintenance re-assert loop is shared with all managed pairs.
catalog.playerExperience: The admin runs `tpl_target "Ashlands Camp" 1234 -5678 yaw=90 source="hub3"`; within one tick the hub portal's hover text changes to `Portal tag:"Ashlands Camp" [connected]` for anyone standing there (UpdatePortal re-reads HaveTarget every 0.5 s; hover text re-reads the tag every frame). A player walks in, gets the 8 s swirl, and steps out of a real portal at the coordinate facing the configured yaw. The destination portal shows the same tag. If the coordinate was underwater/lava/off-map the command prints the rejection reason to the admin's console via ZNet.RemotePrint and nothing changes.
failureModes: WorldGenerator is blind to player terraforming and location flattening: an arrival point may be up to a few metres off or inside a raised earth wall; the client fallback still lands on solid ground but possibly on top of it.
Coordinates inside a player base can drop travellers inside walls; only approximate piece-ZDO proximity checks are possible.
Console commands from a vanilla player's own console never reach the server unless the player is an admin and the command is RemoteCommand-flagged.
prerequisites: Wonderland-style config polling or a server ConsoleCommand
openQuestions: How far off is WorldGenerator.GetHeight from the real placed surface at typical location sites (needs a sampled comparison against a client-side raycast)?
corrections: Dedicated server has no stdin command reader in vanilla: Console.Update polls ZInput only (SERVER :42883-42900); no Console.In/ReadLine in the assembly. 'usable from the dedicated server stdin' requires a mod-added stdin thread.

'usable by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand' is false for a mod-specific command: vanilla client Terminal.TryRunCommand rejects unknown command names before the RemoteCommand branch (:45734-45758). Only vanilla commands flagged remoteCommand:true are forwarded; a mod would have to intercept one of those (e.g. `setkey <payload>`, :43529-43534) on the server, or use chat.
ZNet.RemotePrint feedback only exists for the RPC path (needs the ZRpc); config-file input can only report via log.

Terminal.ConsoleCommand ctor signature confirmed: (command, description, action, isCheat, isNetwork, onlyServer, isSecret, allowInDevBuild, hideBehindDevCommands, optionsFetcher, alwaysRefreshTabOptions, remoteCommand, onlyAdmin) at :43094; Terminal.commands is protected static (:43241) so a server-side mod can register into it, but registration on the server does not make the client aware of it.

PointHeights pre-filter: array is indexed [mapX, mapY] where mapX derives from world x and mapY from world z (GenerateBiomePoints :92440-92450); values are GetBiomeHeight (pre-flattening), -1000 outside waterEdge.
Remove 'usable from the dedicated server stdin' — the vanilla dedicated server has no stdin command reader; the mod must add its own thread (grep: no ReadLine/Console.In in assembly_valheim_SERVER).

Remove 'by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand' for a mod-registered command: the vanilla client's Terminal.TryRunCommand (SERVER:45734-45760, same on client) only forwards commands it has itself registered with RemoteCommand=true; an unknown name prints 'not a recognized command' locally and nothing is sent.

Replace the input channel with: (a) map ping (Chat.SendPing CLIENT:42058-42066 → routed RPC 'ChatMessage' type 3 to peer 0, no permission check) for X/Z, with adminlist check server-side; and/or (b) a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (SERVER:81879-81894) intercepting a vanilla remoteCommand-flagged command carrying free text, e.g. `setkey tpl:...` (SERVER:43546) — adminlist gate at 81881 is vanilla.
Chat keywords are unreliable: chat text is sent per-OTHER-player (CLIENT:41996-42040); a lone admin emits nothing.

Phantom y must sit within ~0.15 m of the client's real terrain or the owning vanilla client's WearNTear destroys it ~30 s after instantiation (CLIENT:150361-150389 bounds margin, 150781-150838 terrain support, 150445-150450 + 150561-150567 damage). Set `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` through LoadFields keys (HasFields, HasFieldsWearNTear, 'WearNTear.m_noSupportWear') on every phantom; Piece.m_canBeRemoved does not help (Piece.CanBeRemoved CLIENT:137050-137062 ignores it).
Effort: medium (input channel + validation + LoadFields keys), not small-medium.

GetHoverText format is `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"<tag>" [$piece_portal_connected]` (SERVER:143453-143463); `[connected]` reflects HaveTarget (connection ID != None) while the glow needs TargetFound, which triggers ZDOMan.RequestZDO → server ForceSendZDO with no distance filter (SERVER:143643-143657, 77689-77692, 77263-77285).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The validation math and arrival path hold up against the decompile: WorldGenerator.GetHeight -> GetBiomeHeight edge guard returns -2*GetHeightMultiplier() = -400 beyond 10500 m (SERVER :151978-151981, :152396); GetNormal is pure height sampling (:151925-151932); IsLavaPreHeightmap is pure WorldGenerator mask math (:115637-115646); FindFloor/GetGroundHeight are Physics.Raycast (:115604-115612, :115502-115510) and Game.FixedUpdate pins the server reference position at 1e6 (:100458-100466). Client arrival: TeleportWorld.Teleport passes distantTeleport:true (:143546) so Player.UpdateTeleport applies the 8 s/IsAreaReady gate and the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15349-15378; GetSolidHeight raycasts from p.y+1000 and returns p.y on miss). The phantom position/rotation come from the destination ZDO on the client (:143541-143545), so the route is server-authoritative. The INPUT CHANNEL claims are wrong, though. (1) The vanilla dedicated server reads no stdin at all: Console.Update only polls ZInput (:42883-42900) and there is no Console.In/ReadLine anywhere in the server assembly - a 'server console' command needs the mod's own stdin thread or the config file. (2) Admins on vanilla clients cannot reach a mod-registered command through RPC_RemoteCommand: Terminal.TryRunCommand looks the command name up in the client's static `commands` table first (:45734-45737) and prints 'not a recognized command' for unknown names (:45757); the RemoteCommand forwarding branch (:45743-45745) is only reached for commands the vanilla client already has. The adminlist gate itself is real (:81879-81889). So enforcement of the DESTINATION is server-side; the operator input surface is config/own-stdin only unless the mod hijacks a vanilla remoteCommand-flagged command (setkey/removekey/listkeys/players/genloc/sleep/setworldmodifier, e.g. :43529-43546) or chat.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The core mechanism (pure WorldGenerator validation + phantom at the coordinate) holds: WorldGenerator.GetHeight/GetNormal/waterEdge guard and ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap are pure math (SERVER:151944-151949, 151978-151981, 151122, 151925-151932, 115637-115645); Game.FixedUpdate pins the ref pos at 1e6 (SERVER:100458-100466) and ghost zones destroy their root immediately after PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation (ZoneSystem.SpawnZone SERVER:114085-114104), so GetGroundHeight/FindFloor raycasts (SERVER:115502-115511, 115604-115613) are dead at real coordinates. The client arrival path is as described (Player.UpdateTeleport CLIENT:15331-15380: 8 s distant gate, FindFloor from target+1 m, 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback). BOTH claimed input channels are wrong for a vanilla client, though. (1) No stdin reader exists in the dedicated server assembly (no Console.ReadLine/Console.In anywhere in assembly_valheim_SERVER); the mod would have to run its own stdin thread. (2) RPC_RemoteCommand is only reached from a client whose own Terminal already has the command registered with RemoteCommand=true: Terminal.TryRunCommand (SERVER:45734-45760, identical on the client) does commands.TryGetValue(name) first and prints 'not a recognized command' for anything a mod registered server-side only; the forward `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` is in the else-branch of that lookup. A vanilla admin therefore cannot type `tpl_target ...` anywhere that reaches the server. Chat is also not a reliable channel: Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync sends one routed RPC per OTHER player (CLIENT:41996-42040), so a lone admin generates no packet. Real vanilla-client admin channels are: the map ping (Chat.SendPing CLIENT:42058-42066, routed to peer 0 = server, carries a free world X/Z), and hijacking a vanilla remoteCommand:true command that accepts free text such as `setkey <arg>` (SERVER:43546, onlyServer+remoteCommand, isCheat:false) by Harmony-prefixing ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (SERVER:81879-81894, adminlist-gated at 81881) — the vanilla client forwards it unmodified because IsValid fails on OnlyServer (SERVER:43203-43218). ZNet.RemotePrint (SERVER:81635-81647) works for feedback given the admin's ZRpc from ZNet.GetPeer(uid).m_rpc. A second systemic problem shared by every option in this batch: y = WorldGenerator height + 0.2 is the PRE-modifier height; the client's actual terrain includes TerrainComp/location edits. The vanilla client's WearNTear support check overlaps the piece colliders expanded by only 0.15 m per side (SetupColliders CLIENT:150361-150389); if no terrain-layer collider is inside that box (CLIENT:150781-150784, 150830-150838) m_support drops to 0, and with m_noSupportWear (public, CLIENT:149945) the owner applies 100 % damage after the 30 s ShouldUpdate grace (CLIENT:150392-150399, 150445-150450, 150561-150567). Piece.CanBeRemoved() does not consult m_canBeRemoved (CLIENT:137050-137062) so that override does not save it. Mitigation is real and vanilla-honoured: write HasFields/HasFieldsWearNTear/`WearNTear.m_noSupportWear`=false via ZNetView.LoadFields (CLIENT:82898-82960), or accept the GlobalKeys.NoBuildingFall side effect. Effort is medium, not small-medium, once the input channel is built.

catalog.name: World Spawn / Start Temple
catalog.oneLine: Portal to the exact spot vanilla respawns new characters, read from the server's own LocationIcons source.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out Vector3 pos)` — the server branch scans m_locationInstances for the first entry whose ZoneLocation is icon-flagged and whose `m_prefab.Name == "StartTemple"`; this is the very value the server ships to clients in the LocationIcons RPC and the one Game.FindSpawnPoint uses for a fresh spawn (`pos + Vector3.up * 2f`). m_locationInstances is populated by ZNet.ServerLoadWorld→GenerateLocationsIfNeeded before any peer connects, so this works at OnWorldReady with zero players. Place the phantom (Option 1) ~6–8 m from the temple centre on the side away from the stones: sample four candidate offsets, keep the one with the lowest `|WorldGenerator.GetHeight − pos.y|` and best GetNormal.y, orient the phantom's forward toward the temple. Because the start temple has m_clearArea the placed terrain may differ from the stored pre-flattening height by a metre or two — set phantom y = max(stored, GetHeight) + 0.2 and rely on the client's FindFloor/15 s fallback. Persistence: the temple never moves, so this is a create-once pair; the maintenance tick only re-asserts. Multiple hubs can each get their own phantom near the temple (spread them around the ring so exit points do not overlap). Tick cost: one dictionary scan at creation, nothing afterwards.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:"Spawn" [connected]`. Walk in → 8 s swirl → step out of a real portal a few metres from the Sacrificial Stones, facing them, with the temple's own map icon already on their map (vanilla LocationIcons). Walking back into that portal returns to the source hub.
failureModes: Two mods or a heavily modified world could register additional StartTemple instances; GetLocationIcon returns the first dictionary match, not the closest — acceptable since vanilla uses the same call.
If the temple's location flags (m_iconAlways) were altered by a location mod, GetLocationIcon returns false; fall back to FindClosestLocation("StartTemple", Vector3.zero).
openQuestions: Exact placed height delta at the temple after m_clearArea flattening (sample once in-game and bake an offset).
corrections: Define 'OnWorldReady' as ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsCompleted (public event :113396-113405; fires immediately if LocationsGenerated is already true). On a fresh world GenerateLocationsIfNeeded only STARTS a coroutine (:114456); ZNet.OpenServer is deferred until completion (:79216-79220) so zero-player timing still holds.

GetLocationIcon returns the first matching instance only if the location is m_iconAlways or (m_iconPlaced && m_placed) (:115427); StartTemple's iconAlways flag is asset data - safe by construction because vanilla spawning itself depends on it (client :100796).

PlaceLocations never writes the re-resolved height back into m_position (:114957-114990 mutate local `p` only), so stored y stays the pre-flattening value - the option's max(stored, GetHeight)+0.2 approach is consistent with that.

Gate creation on ZoneSystem.instance.LocationsGenerated / the GenerateLocationsCompleted event (SERVER:113396); on a new world location generation is a time-sliced coroutine (SERVER:114447-114523) and m_locationInstances is incomplete at OnWorldReady.

Phantom must be kept within ~0.15 m of the client-side terrain or set `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` via LoadFields; the temple's terrain edits make WorldGenerator height unreliable there (WearNTear CLIENT:150361-150389, 150781-150838, 150445-150450).
Stone-ring/altar overlap cannot be validated server-side (no colliders, prefab geometry is asset data); exact offsets are an in-game tuning task, not derivable from the decompile.
LocationInstance.m_position is the pre-placement WorldGenerator height; PlaceLocations (SERVER:114957-114990) never writes the resolved p back into the instance.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(name, out pos) on the server scans m_locationInstances for an instance whose location is m_iconAlways (or iconPlaced&&placed) and whose m_prefab.Name matches (SERVER :115422-115447). Game.m_StartLocation = "StartTemple" (:99845). Game.FindSpawnPoint uses exactly this call and adds Vector3.up*2 (client :100796-100800; same code in server :100368-100372). m_locationInstances is loaded from the world save (ZoneSystem.Load :113870-113892, all instances including unplaced ones are saved :113738-113763) or generated by GenerateLocationsIfNeeded from ZNet.ServerLoadWorld (:79273-79285). The temple is a single, persisted instance, so create-once is right. One timing correction: GenerateLocations runs as a time-sliced coroutine (:114456, :114460-114530) and ZNet only opens the server after ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsCompleted fires (:79216-79220, :79285) - so 'before any peer connects' holds, but a mod hook that runs synchronously right after world load on a FRESH world may see an incomplete m_locationInstances; subscribe to the public GenerateLocationsCompleted event (:113396-113405, which invokes immediately if already generated). Height caveats are accurate: LocationInstance.m_position.y is the WorldGenerator height assigned at generation (:114735) and PlaceLocations re-resolves via GetGroundData on a local copy only (:114957-114968).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon (SERVER:115422-115447) server branch scans m_locationInstances for icon-flagged instances with m_prefab.Name == name, exactly as claimed, and Game.m_StartLocation = "StartTemple" (SERVER:99845); the client's FindSpawnPoint uses the same call + up*2 (CLIENT:100796-100801). LocationInstance.m_position carries the WorldGenerator height assigned at generation (SERVER:114735) and is never updated by PlaceLocations (SERVER:114957-114990 only flips m_placed). Two corrections. (1) 'populated before any peer connects at OnWorldReady' is only true for a world that already has locations saved; on a fresh world ZNet.ServerLoadWorld → GenerateLocationsIfNeeded (SERVER:79273-79287, 113458-113464) starts a time-sliced COROUTINE (GenerateLocations SERVER:114447-114457, GenerateLocationsTimeSliced 114459-114523 sets LocationsGenerated only at the end), so the mod must gate on ZoneSystem.LocationsGenerated or subscribe to the public event GenerateLocationsCompleted (SERVER:113396). (2) Placement near the temple is blind: no colliders exist server-side, the temple ring stones/altar are asset geometry the server cannot see, and the temple area's terrain edits mean WorldGenerator height can be off by the amount the catalog admits — which, per the WearNTear analysis (client bounds margin 0.15 m, CLIENT:150361-150389; terrain support 150781-150838; collapse 150445-150450/150561-150567 after the 30 s grace at 150392-150399), destroys a floating phantom unless WearNTear.m_noSupportWear is forced false via LoadFields. The 'faces the stones' and 'a few metres from the Sacrificial Stones without overlapping them' promises need an in-game check. Save/relog/restart: a two-node pair is a perfect matching and survives the ZDOConnectionHashData save format; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals rebinds by hash at load (SERVER:77854-77891).

catalog.name: Boss Altars (per boss / nearest / next-undefeated)
catalog.oneLine: Portal to any boss altar, the nearest altar of a given boss, or the altar of the next boss not yet marked defeated in the server's global keys.
catalog.howItWorks: Discovery: altars are world-gen Locations, present in `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationInstances` from world load regardless of whether any player has visited. Per boss: `ZoneSystem.instance.FindLocations(altarName, ref list)` for all instances, or `FindClosestLocation(altarName, refPoint, out inst)` for nearest to the source portal (both are O(all location instances) linear scans — cache a name→List index at OnWorldReady). Altar location prefab names are Unity asset data, not in the decompile: build the map at boot by dumping `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` and matching `m_iconAlways==true && m_quantity small` plus name heuristics, then confirm in-game (open question). Next-undefeated: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_eikthyr)` … `defeated_goblinking` (enum ordinals 42–46; later bosses use string keys, enumerate GetGlobalKeys()) in canonical order; pick the first false and resolve that altar. Position: `inst.m_position` already carries a WorldGenerator ground height (sea level 30); place the phantom (Option 1) at `inst.m_position + dir * (inst.m_location.m_exteriorRadius + 4)` where dir is the flattest of 8 compass samples by GetNormal.y and not lava (IsLavaPreHeightmap — Fader's altar is in Ashlands), forward facing the altar. Do NOT try to reach the OfferingBowl object: OfferingBowl is a MonoBehaviour with no ZDO of its own (GetComponentInParent<ZNetView> in Start) and its parent piece ZDO only exists after a peer's ghost-generation of that zone; the LocationInstance is always available. 'Next-undefeated' re-evaluates on a slow tick (30 s) or from a postfix on ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (BossDefeatWatch pattern, pre-seeding at boot to avoid the SetStartingGlobalKeys replay) and re-targets the phantom by destroy-and-recreate (never SetPosition on a portal prefab). NoBossPortals interaction: when the key is set and a boss is alerted (activeBosses > 0), the client refuses transit with `$msg_blockedbyboss` — the mod cannot override that per-portal.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:">Bonemass" [connected]` (or `>Next Boss` for the auto mode). 8 s swirl, arrive on flat ground ~4 m outside the altar's footprint facing the altar; the altar's vanilla map icon is already visible. For 'next boss', after Bonemass is killed anywhere on the server, within ~30 s the hub portal's tag flips to `>Moder` and the old phantom vanishes from the Bonemass swamp (it simply ceases to exist on the next zone load for anyone there). If a boss is currently alerted and NoBossPortals is on, walking in shows the vanilla `Portals are blocked by a boss` message.
failureModes: Altar location prefab names unknown until an in-game dump; a wrong name yields FindLocations empty and the option silently disables.
m_position is the pre-placement height; altars with m_clearArea may sit a metre lower/higher — client fallback handles it but the phantom mesh can float/sink visually.
Boss fights: a phantom 4 m outside the altar is inside the arena; consider 15–20 m offsets so it is not destroyed by the boss (WearNTear damage → Destroy → resources drop).
Deep North / Ashlands: IsLavaPreHeightmap only means lava inside Ashlands; sample multiple offsets.
prerequisites: In-game dump of ZoneSystem.m_locations names and flags
openQuestions: Exact vanilla altar location prefab names (Eikthyr, gd_king, Bonemass, Dragonqueen, GoblinKing, Mistlands queen, Fader) — dump m_locations on the server.
Are later-boss defeat keys enum members or free-form strings in 1.0.7 (check GetGlobalKeys() after a Queen/Fader kill)?
corrections: Altar map pins are NOT shown by vanilla until a Vegvisir is read (Vegvisir.Interact :139329 -> Game.DiscoverClosestLocation :100793 -> server RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation :100799-100821 -> client RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse :100823-100830). The mod must push the pin itself via InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", name, (int)Minimap.PinType.Boss, pos, false) if it wants one.

Boot heuristic must not rely on m_iconAlways==true (that selects StartTemple-class locations); filter by prefab name (m_prefabName :112892 is populated in SetupLocations :113672) confirmed in-game, or by m_group/m_biome.
NoBossPortals block condition is `GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528) - a boss random event also blocks.

Canonical boss order differs from enum order (enum: eikthyr=42, dragon=43, goblinking=44, gdking=45, bonemass=46; activeBosses=47). Queen/Fader keys are not enum members - only GetGlobalKey(string) (:115968) / GetGlobalKeys() (:115994) can read them.
Public name-indexed caches already exist: m_locationIDCache (AssetID -> List<LocationInstance>) and m_locationGroupCache (:113297-113299); RemoveNonPlaced keeps them in sync (:114387-114400).

Positions of unplaced altars can move only after a location-version bump or `genloc` (regeneration path :114474 ClearNonPlacedLocations); re-resolve at every boot rather than caching positions on disk.

GlobalKeys defeated_* enum order (SERVER:101314-101318) is eikthyr, dragon, goblinking, gdking, bonemass — not canonical; supply an explicit progression list; defeated_queen/defeated_fader are asset strings (Character.m_defeatSetGlobalKey SERVER:275, set via SetGlobalKey at 3153-3155) and must be read through GetGlobalKey(string)/GetGlobalKeys().

Boss altars have no always-on map icon in vanilla; icons are Vegvisir-driven per-player pins (Vegvisir SERVER:147959+, Game.RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation/RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse SERVER:100804-100831). Push the pin explicitly if the experience requires it.
ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd is private (SERVER:113483); the BossDefeatWatch pattern patches it via Harmony — fine, but say so.

Destroy-and-recreate must claim ownership before ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (SERVER:76927-76933) and rewrite hub tag+connection atomically within the 5 s reconcile window (Game.ConnectPortals SERVER:100592-100626) or the hub is nulled and can be randomly re-paired.

Apply the LoadFields `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` override; altar terrain is uneven and the client collapses a phantom floating >0.15 m (WearNTear CLIENT:150361-150389, 150781-150838, 150445-150450).
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Discovery primitives are real and server-side: m_locationInstances (SERVER :113295), LocationInstance{m_location,m_position,m_placed} (:113001-113008), bool FindLocations(string, ref List<LocationInstance>) (:115728-115738), FindClosestLocation (:115707-115726), both linear over all instances. Unplaced instances persist in the save (Save :113738-113763, Load :113870-113892) and are regenerated only when LocationsGenerated is false or m_locationVersion changed (:113894-113897, ClearNonPlacedLocations :114474), so altar positions are stable across restarts. defeated_eikthyr..defeated_bonemass are enum ordinals 42-46 (enum at :101270; order eikthyr, dragon, goblinking, gdking, bonemass), GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) :115948 and GetGlobalKey(string) :115968 exist; GlobalKeyAdd is private (:113483) but postfix-able. OfferingBowl.Start uses GetComponentInParent<ZNetView> (:135652-135661) - no own ZDO. TeleportWorld.Teleport NoBossPortals gate confirmed (:143528). Two substantive errors: (1) 'the altar's vanilla map icon is already visible' is wrong - vanilla altar pins are produced only by Vegvisir.Interact -> Game.DiscoverClosestLocation -> RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation -> RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (:139329, :100793-100816, :100823-100830); GetLocationIcons only ships m_iconAlways / (iconPlaced&&placed) locations (:115450-115460). The existence of the Vegvisir path is the reason altars are not iconAlways, so the proposed boot heuristic 'm_iconAlways==true && m_quantity small' would select the StartTemple, not altars. (2) The NoBossPortals gate also fires while RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null, not only on activeBosses>0 (:143528).

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Discovery via m_locationInstances / FindLocations / FindClosestLocation is correct (SERVER:115707-115726, 115728-115739; both linear scans on m_prefab.Name). ZoneLocation exposes m_name, m_prefabName, m_prefab.Name (Hash uses m_prefab.Name SERVER:112979), m_iconAlways, m_iconPlaced, m_unique, m_exteriorRadius, m_snapToWater at runtime (SERVER:112885-112990) so the boot dump is real. OfferingBowl.Start uses GetComponentInParent<ZNetView> (SERVER:135652-135661) — correct that it has no ZDO of its own. NoBossPortals gate in TeleportWorld.Teleport is client-executed (SERVER:143520-143524 body, identical on the client). Corrections: (1) the GlobalKeys enum order is eikthyr, dragon, goblinking, gdking, bonemass (SERVER:101314-101318) — NOT progression order; the mod must hard-code eikthyr→gdking→bonemass→dragon→goblinking→queen→fader, and queen/fader are string keys set from Character.m_defeatSetGlobalKey (SERVER:275, 3153-3155) not present in the enum. (2) 'the altar's vanilla map icon is already visible' is unsupported: altar icons in vanilla come from Vegvisir → Game.DiscoverClosestLocation → RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (SERVER:147959+, 100804-100831), i.e. per-player saved pins, not iconAlways location icons; a fresh player at the phantom sees no icon unless the mod pushes RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse itself (which also swings the player's look direction, SERVER:100826-100829). (3) GlobalKeyAdd is private (SERVER:113483) — patchable, but must be a Harmony patch on a private member; SetStartingGlobalKeys (SERVER:115904) replays existing keys at load as the catalog says. (4) Re-targeting by destroy-and-recreate requires the mod to own the ZDO first (ZDOMan.DestroyZDO only queues if IsOwner, SERVER:76927-76933) and to rewrite BOTH tags and BOTH connections before the next 5 s Game.ConnectPortals pass, which otherwise nulls the hub (target==null predicate, SERVER:100600-100606) and may randomly re-pair it with any other portal carrying the same tag (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal SERVER:100663-100677). (5) Same WearNTear floating-collapse caveat as the other options: altar surroundings are often uneven and m_position is the pre-placement height (SERVER:114735), so use LoadFields WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false. Enforcement is server-enforced for the route only; the boss/ore/NoPortals transit gates remain client-executed.

catalog.name: Traders (Haldor, Hildir, Bog Witch)
catalog.oneLine: Portal to any trader camp, resolved from the location registry; traders are placed-on-discovery icons so gating on m_placed is the difference between 'exists' and 'has been generated'.
catalog.howItWorks: Trader camps are Locations (prefab names live in asset data — dump `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` at boot and pick entries whose `m_iconPlaced==true` and `m_unique==true`, which in vanilla is the trader set; confirm names in-game). `FindLocations(name, ref list)` gives every instance with `m_position` and `m_placed`. Vanilla shows the trader map icon only once `m_placed` is true (GetLocationIcons: `m_iconAlways || (m_iconPlaced && m_placed)`), i.e. once some peer's reference position has ghost-generated the zone. The mod can choose either: (a) 'discovered only' — offer the trader as a destination only when `m_placed`, matching vanilla's reveal rules; or (b) 'always' — target the instance position regardless, which lets a hub portal lead players to an undiscovered trader (a design choice, not a technical limit). Place the phantom (Option 1) at `m_position + dir * (m_exteriorRadius + 3)` on the flattest compass sample, forward toward the camp. Trader camps are unique and static, so this is create-once; the phantom should carry `Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false` via LoadFields because trader camps are heavily visited. A 'nearest trader' mode picks min Vector3.Distance over all three (or N) instances relative to the source portal. Optionally push a saved map pin to travellers on first use with `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", "Haldor", (int)Minimap.PinType.Icon3, pos, false)` — redundant once m_placed because vanilla's own icon appears, but useful for mode (b).
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:">Haldor" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive a few metres outside the camp facing it. If mode (a) and the trader has never been generated, the hub's tag reads `>Haldor (unfound)` and the portal is deliberately left unconnected (hover shows `[unconnected]`, no glow) until someone discovers the camp on foot, at which point the maintenance tick creates the phantom and the tag flips within one tick.
failureModes: Trader location names unverified until an in-game dump.

Camp ZDOs (the trader NPC itself) do not exist until the zone is ghost-generated; arriving via portal in mode (b) triggers generation on the arriving client's own CreateGhostZones — expect a longer black screen on first arrival.
m_exteriorRadius is Inspector data per location; if 0 the offset math needs a default (12 m).
citations: ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations re-send of LocationIcons when placed assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115000-115003
openQuestions: Exact trader location prefab names and their m_exteriorRadius values.
Does arriving by portal into a never-generated zone complete within the 15 s teleport ceiling on a slow client?
corrections: Unique locations have multiple candidate instances until one is placed (GenerateLocationsTimeSliced :114662-114669); RemoveUnplacedLocations (:114994-114996, :115005-115020) deletes the others after placement. Mode (b) must (1) pick one candidate, (2) on every maintenance tick verify the targeted instance still exists in m_locationInstances (key = zone id, :113295) and re-resolve to the placed one if it vanished.
'Create-once' is only true after m_placed; before that the destination is provisional.
'Nearest trader' must run FindLocations per trader prefab name and take the min over the union; there is no cross-type query.
Piece.m_canBeRemoved via LoadFields is an unverified primitive (see prior notes) - do not present it as settled.

Sea-level/height: LocationInstance.m_position.y is the pre-flattening WorldGenerator height (:114735); PlaceLocations' GetGroundData/snapToWater adjustments apply to a local copy only (:114957-114966).

Unique locations have multiple pre-placement candidate instances; RemoveUnplacedLocations (SERVER:115006-115030, called from PlaceLocations 114990-114993) deletes the losers when one is placed. Mode (b) must pick one candidate deliberately, rebuild the phantom if its candidate disappears, and accept that the first ghost-generated candidate wins — including one triggered by the arriving traveller (CreateGhostZones per peer ref pos SERVER:113971-113990).
'create-once' holds only after m_placed; before that the maintenance tick must re-validate the instance still exists.

Piece.m_canBeRemoved via LoadFields is client-honoured hammer-only protection (CLIENT:12377, 136911); it does not prevent damage/collapse (Piece.CanBeRemoved CLIENT:137050-137062) or RPC_DestroyZDO. Add WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false to prevent floating collapse (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150445-150450, 150781-150838).

Pushed pins via RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse are permanent on the client and also swing the player's camera toward the target (SERVER:100826-100829); vanilla will additionally add its own trader icon once m_placed, so mode (b) travellers end up with two markers.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] GetLocationIcons rule `m_iconAlways || (m_iconPlaced && m_placed)` confirmed (SERVER :115450-115460); PlaceLocations sets m_placed and re-sends icons when m_iconPlaced (:114990-115002); CreateGhostZones runs per peer ref pos on the server (:113934-113938); RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse registered at :100068 with handler :100823-100830; Minimap.PinType.Icon3 exists (:56079). The unique-location mechanics were not understood, though: for a m_unique location the generator still creates up to m_quantity CANDIDATE instances while none is placed (`if (!location.m_unique || placed <= 0)` :114662; loop `placed < m_quantity` :114669), and only when one is placed does RemoveUnplacedLocations delete the rest (:114994-114996, :115005-115020). So before discovery FindLocations("Vendor_...") returns several candidates, all of which are 'the trader' - mode (b) is self-fulfilling if the traveller's ghost zone places the targeted candidate first, but if another candidate is placed first (a player walking there), the targeted instance is deleted and the phantom points at nothing. 'Nearest trader over all three (or N) instances' also conflates trader TYPES with candidate instances; FindLocations is per prefab name.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The icon rule is exactly `m_iconAlways || (m_iconPlaced && m_placed)` (ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons SERVER:115449-115466) and PlaceLocations re-sends LocationIcons when an m_iconPlaced location is placed (SERVER:114999-115002); FindLocations returns m_position+m_placed (SERVER:115728-115739). The RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse signature (string,int,Vector3,bool) matches its registration (SERVER:100068) and the client's Minimap.DiscoverLocation adds a saved pin (CLIENT:58394-58420). The load-bearing error is 'trader camps are unique and static, so this is create-once': for m_unique locations the generator seeds MULTIPLE candidate instances and PlaceLocations → RemoveUnplacedLocations deletes every other unplaced candidate the moment one is placed (SERVER:114990-114993, 115006-115030). So before discovery FindLocations(name) returns N candidates, not one; mode (b) 'always' must choose among them, and a phantom placed at candidate A is self-fulfilling only if a player arrives there first (their ref pos triggers CreateGhostZones → SpawnZone → PlaceLocations for that zone, SERVER:113971-113990, 114085-114104) — if anyone ghost-generates candidate B first, A is removed and the phantom points at empty terrain. Mode (a) 'discovered only' is unaffected. Secondary: `Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false via LoadFields` is real (public field CLIENT:136911, LoadFields CLIENT:82898-82960, Player.RemovePiece check CLIENT:12377) but is client-honoured only and blocks nothing except the hammer — it does not stop WearNTear damage/collapse (Piece.CanBeRemoved ignores it, CLIENT:137050-137062) or RPC_DestroyZDO; add `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` for the floating-collapse problem. Trader camps carry a no-build radius (Location.IsInsideNoBuildLocation CLIENT:12381) which already blocks hammer removal inside it; the phantom at exteriorRadius+3 is likely outside it. RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse also forces the recipient's look direction toward the pin (SERVER:100826-100829).

catalog.name: Dungeon / Crypt Entrances (interior ruled out)
catalog.oneLine: Portal to the surface entrance of a crypt/dungeon location; targeting the interior itself is possible geometrically but pairs a portal with a space the client only builds on demand, and crypt doors are invisible to the server.
catalog.howItWorks: Entrances are Locations (Crypt2/3/4, SunkenCrypt4, MountainCave02, GoblinCamp is not a dungeon, etc. — names from a boot dump of m_locations filtered on `m_hasInterior`-bearing prefabs, an Inspector flag readable only after the prefab loads; the mod can instead filter by name pattern confirmed in-game). Nearest-of-type: `FindClosestLocation(name, sourcePos, out inst)`; place the phantom (Option 1) `m_exteriorRadius + 3` m from `inst.m_position`. Many crypt entrances are on slopes (Black Forest burial chambers are half-buried, sunken crypts sit in swamp water at y≈30): validate with GetNormal.y and reject h<31 for swamp crypts or accept and set y=30.5. Interior: `Location.Awake` instantiates the interior at `(zoneCenter.x, surfaceY + 5000, zoneCenter.z)` and `Character.InInterior` is `y > 3000`, so the interior origin is derivable server-side and a phantom COULD be placed at (zoneCenter.x, surfaceY+5000+k, zoneCenter.z). RULED OUT in practice: the interior geometry is generated client-side from DungeonGenerator room data (`ZDOVars.s_roomData` byte blob on the DungeonGenerator ZDO, readable but unsearchable via GetAllZDOIDsWithHash), the safe floor of any room is unknown without colliders, the client's FindFloor over a 5000 m-high interior raycasts 1000 m down and would hit interior geometry only if the arrival point is above a room floor — otherwise the 15 s fallback uses GetSolidHeight from y+1000 (hits the dungeon roof mesh or nothing → keeps y). And building portals inside interiors is normally blocked (m_allowedInDungeons) unless GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild is set — a phantom bypasses that, which is a gameplay-policy concern. The crypt doors themselves (`class Teleport`) have no ZDO, no RPC, and a compiled `m_targetPoint` reference: a server-only mod cannot re-route, pair, or even enumerate them.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:">Crypt" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive outside the burial chamber entrance facing its door; the player walks through the vanilla crypt door (which ignores NoPortals and the ore check). Return by walking out and into the phantom. No map pin unless pushed.
failureModes: Entrance locations are numerous (dozens per type); 'nearest' relative to the source is the only sane picker.
Sunken crypts: arrival on swamp water at y≈30; phantom exit +1 m puts the player in knee-deep water — acceptable but wet.
Interior targeting: unknown floor height, possible arrival inside a wall, and DungeonBuild policy bypass — do not ship.
openQuestions: Which location names correspond to each dungeon type in 1.0.7 (dump m_locations).
Does a phantom placed at a derived interior coordinate ever land a player on a room floor (interior test with a client, purely for the record)?
corrections: Teleport.Interact honours NoBossPortals when leaving an active boss dungeon (:143354-143358); it does ignore NoPortals and the ore check (no IsTeleportable call, :143344-143370).
LocationInstance.m_position.y for m_snapToWater locations is NOT 30 - PlaceLocations writes 30 into a local `p` only (:114960-114966). Use 30 explicitly for sunken crypts.
Dungeon entrance locations are non-unique; unplaced instances persist in the save (:113738-113763) so nearest-of-type is stable across restarts unless locations are regenerated.
m_hasInterior lives on the Location MonoBehaviour (:133474), not ZoneLocation - filtering requires loading the location prefab (SoftReference) or name matching, as the option already concedes.
Teleport.Interact honours NoBossPortals for a character inside an active boss dungeon interior (SERVER:143347-143351); only NoPortals and the ore check are skipped.

Interior room world positions/rotations ARE recoverable server-side from DungeonGenerator's s_roomData blob (SERVER:152970-152985); the interior is ruled out because room floor geometry is asset data, not because positions are unsearchable.

Add the LoadFields `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` override; crypt entrances are on slopes and the vanilla owner collapses a phantom floating >0.15 m (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150445-150450, 150781-150838).
Expect the GetNormal.y<0.7 slope filter to reject many burial-chamber sites; fall back to a wider search radius around inst.m_position.
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited anchor checks out: Location.Awake instantiates the interior at (zoneCenter.x, y+5000, zoneCenter.z) when m_hasInterior (SERVER :133505-133515; m_hasInterior :133474 is on the Location component, so it needs the prefab loaded); Character.InInterior is y>3000 (:4538-4541); ZDOVars.s_roomData :78573 and DungeonGenerator.Load reads it via GetByteArray (:153012); ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash supports only Float/Long/Int/String (:75390-75407); dungeon `Teleport` has no ZNetView, only a compiled m_targetPoint reference and GetTeleportPoint (:143322, :143372-143375); build-in-dungeon gate uses GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild (:13353); m_snapToWater sets y=30 in PlaceLocations (:114964-114966); UpdateTeleport 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15360-15366; GetSolidHeight returns p.y on miss). Surface-entrance targeting via FindClosestLocation is server-side and the interior ruling-out is sound. Corrections: the crypt door does NOT ignore all portal gating - it refuses when NoBossPortals is set and the character is inside an active boss dungeon (:143354-143358); and for snapToWater locations the stored m_position.y is still the WorldGenerator height because PlaceLocations only modifies its local copy (:114960-114966), so the mod must apply y=30 itself.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: Location.Awake instantiates the interior at (zoneCenter.x, y+5000, zoneCenter.z) scaled 64x500x64 (SERVER:133505-133515); Character.InInterior is y>3000 (SERVER:4538-4541); class Teleport has no ZDO/RPC and a compiled m_targetPoint (SERVER:143316-143379); its OnTriggerEnter is Player.m_localPlayer-gated (143333-143340); Player build check for m_allowedInDungeons/DungeonBuild (SERVER:13353); PlaceLocations m_snapToWater y=30 (SERVER:114963-114966); ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash supports only Float/Long/Int/String (SERVER:75390-75407). FindClosestLocation is the correct nearest-of-type call (SERVER:115707-115726). Corrections: (1) 'the vanilla crypt door ignores NoPortals and the ore check' is true, but Teleport.Interact DOES honour NoBossPortals when the character is in an interior inside an active boss dungeon (SERVER:143347-143351) — the return trip out of an active boss dungeon can be blocked. (2) The interior is not as opaque as claimed: DungeonGenerator.Save writes each placed room's hash, world position and rotation into s_roomData (SERVER:152970-152985), so room origins are derivable server-side from the DungeonGenerator ZDO (found by prefab hash of the dungeon root, not by GetAllZDOIDsWithHash); what remains unknown is the room prefab's floor geometry — the ruling-out stands, just for a narrower reason. (3) m_hasInterior lives on the Location component (SERVER:133474) and is only readable after the prefab is loaded, as stated; the name-pattern fallback is asset-dependent and needs the in-game dump. (4) Half-buried Black Forest crypt entrances sit on slopes: the GetNormal.y check will reject many of them, and the same WearNTear floating-collapse caveat applies (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150781-150838, 150445-150450) — use the LoadFields WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false override. (5) Sunken crypt phantom at y=30.5 in swamp water: TeleportWorld has no water check, but the exit point is portal+forward*1+up*1 in water; cosmetic only.

catalog.name: Biome Targets (nearest edge, centroid, nearest N, random-in-biome)
catalog.oneLine: Portal into a biome using the server's precomputed 12 m biome/height grid and flood-filled biome sectors — no player, no ZDO scan.
catalog.howItWorks: `AltBiomeWorldData d = ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (populated in ZNet.ServerLoadWorld via VerifyBiomeData, disk-cached as biomedatacache.bin). Grid: 2048×2048 cells, 12 m each; `PointBiomes[x,y]`, `PointHeights[x,y]`, `PointSectors[x,y]`; convert with `WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float)` and `MapSpaceToWorldSpace(Vector2i)` (= (map−1024)*12+6). Nearest edge of biome B from the source: spiral outward in map space from the source cell until `PointBiomes==B && PointHeights>=31`; cost is O(cells searched), cache per (source, biome). Centroid: `d.Biomes[B].Sectors` gives every contiguous region as a BiomeSector with world-space `Center`, `Min`, `Max`, `HeightMin/Max/Avg`, `EdgeCount` (size proxy) and `DistanceFromCenter`; pick the largest by EdgeCount or nearest by `Vector2.Distance(Center, sourceXZ)`. Never use `BiomeSector.MinZone/MaxZone` (both computed from Min with z=0 — garbage). `Center` is a perimeter centroid and can fall outside a crescent-shaped region, so re-validate `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(x,z)==B` and walk toward the region's Min/Max interior if not. Nearest N: sort Sectors by distance, take N, emit N phantoms with tags `>Plains 1..N`. Random: `d.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(B)` (UnityEngine.Random; seed if reproducibility matters). Final point: `h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x,z)` (exact, not the 12 m sample), reject lava (IsLavaPreHeightmap) and slopes (GetNormal.y<0.7), then Option 1 phantom at (x, h+0.2, z). Ashlands: `WorldGenerator.IsAshlands` and ashlandsMinDistance=12000 mark the boundary; Deep North via IsDeepnorth. Tick cost: all queries are array reads; centroid enumeration is O(sectors per biome), done once.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:">Plains (nearest)" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive on open ground just inside the biome edge, a real portal behind them for the return trip. For 'nearest N' the hub shows several portals side by side tagged `>Plains 1`, `>Plains 2`, each leading to a different region. Random mode re-rolls on a configurable timer; players see the tag change to `>Mistlands (random)` and the destination silently differ next transit.
failureModes: Perimeter-centroid bug: without re-validation a 'Meadows centroid' can be in the Ocean.
A biome edge cell adjacent to Ocean may be a beach at y≈31 — fine — or a cliff; the slope test rejects but the spiral must continue rather than stop.

Random mode + phantom re-target requires destroy-and-recreate (portal prefab cannot be moved); do it only when nobody is within 100 m of the old phantom to avoid a visible pop (check ConnectedCharacters positions).
openQuestions: Memory footprint of BiomeTypeInfo.AllPoints lists on a dedicated server (log counts per biome at boot).
Does m_biomeData.IsReady ever lag OnWorldReady (cache miss forces regeneration)?
catalog.id: targeted-portals:Biome Targets (nearest edge, centroid, nearest N, random-in-biome)
corrections: PointBiomes[x,y] is Heightmap.BiomeIndex (:92360); compare against `B.ToBiomeIndex()` (:129559) or convert with `.ToBiome()`.

AshLands, DeepNorth, Ocean are single global sectors created up-front (:92481-92486) and filled in the first pass (:92487-92500); Biomes[AshLands].Sectors has one entry whose Center is the perimeter centroid of the whole ring - do not use centroid/nearest-N modes for those three biomes; use the spiral edge search or GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.
BiomeSector.HeightMin/HeightMax are computed only over edge cells (:92520-92556) and HeightAvg = (HeightMin+HeightMax)/2 (:92578) - they are not interior statistics.
GetRandomPointByBiomeAboveSeaLevel falls back to any point (including underwater) when AllPointsAboveSeaLevel is empty (:92690-92693); always re-check GetHeight >= 30.
IsAshlands boundary is DUtils.Length(x, y-4000) > 12000 + noise (:151697-151700), i.e. the Ashlands circle is centred at z=+4000; a plain 'distance from origin' test is wrong.
Sector flood fill uses 4-neighbour adjacency on BiomeIndex equality (:92460-92470) - biome mask combinations (RandomBiomeFromBiomes) are only handled by the random helpers, not by Sectors.

BiomeSector.Min is always (-12282,-12282) world: the field defaults to zero (SERVER:93906) and GenerateSectors only lowers it (92539-92550); do not use Min (or MinZone/MaxZone/ZoneCount). Max, Center, EdgeCount, HeightMin/Max are valid.
AshLands, DeepNorth, Ocean each have exactly one pre-seeded sector (SERVER:92481-92503); centroid/nearest-N modes degenerate for them — use nearest-edge spiral or GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.
PointBiomes holds Heightmap.BiomeIndex (SERVER:92357); convert with ToBiomeIndex()/ToBiome() before comparing.
Filter sectors by EdgeCount (single-cell sectors exist) and treat HeightAvg as (min+max)/2 of perimeter cells only (SERVER:92579).

Apply the LoadFields `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` override on phantoms; biome-edge terrain is steep and the owning vanilla client collapses a phantom floating >0.15 m (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150445-150450, 150781-150838).
Random re-roll = destroy (needs ownership, ZDOMan.DestroyZDO SERVER:76927-76933) + recreate + rewrite hub connection before the next 5 s Game.ConnectPortals pass (SERVER:100592-100626).
evidence: AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92476-92616 (global sectors :92481-92500; edge stats :92520-92556; Center :92573; MinZone/MaxZone :92576-92577; HeightAvg :92578)

AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92476-92616 (pre-seeded sectors 92481-92503; Min/Max update 92539-92550; Center 92571-92573; MinZone/MaxZone 92577-92578; HeightAvg 92579)
verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] AltBiomeWorldData is real and server-populated: ZNet.ServerLoadWorld calls AltBiomeWorldData.VerifyBiomeData(m_world) (SERVER :79281; :92395-92403 loads biomedatacache.bin or regenerates, then GenerateSectors). Fields PointHeights (float[,]), PointBiomes, PointSectors, Biomes dictionary and c_pixelSize=12/c_halfWidth=1024 exist (:92342-92360). MapSpaceToWorldSpace = (x-1024)*12+6 and WorldSpaceToMapSpace = (int)((x-6)/12+1024) (:92419-92427). Arrays are indexed [mapX(world x), mapY(world z)] (:92440-92450). BiomeSector carries EdgeCount, Center, Min, Max, MinZone/MaxZone, HeightMin/Max/Avg, DistanceFromCenter, Neighbors (:93884-93905); the constructor registers itself into Biomes[biome].Sectors (:93930-93935). MinZone/MaxZone both computed from Min (:92576-92577) - bug confirmed. Center is a perimeter centroid (:92531-92533, normalised :92573). GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel uses UnityEngine.Random (:92694). Corrections: PointBiomes is Heightmap.BiomeIndex[,] (:92360), so compare with B.ToBiomeIndex() (:129559); AshLands, DeepNorth and Ocean are each ONE pre-created global sector, not per-contiguous-region (:92481-92500), so 'centroid' and 'nearest N regions' are meaningless for Ashlands/Deep North; HeightMin/Max accumulate only over EDGE cells and HeightAvg is (min+max)/2 (:92520-92556, :92578); the random helper silently falls back to below-sea-level points when a biome has none above sea level (:92690-92693). IsAshlands uses an offset centre (y+ashlandsYOffset=-4000) with ashlandsMinDistance 12000 (:151697-151700), not a plain radius.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] AltBiomeWorldData is populated unconditionally in ZNet.ServerLoadWorld via VerifyBiomeData (SERVER:79283, 92403-92411; cache 'biomedatacache.bin' 92340); grid 2048x12 m with the stated conversions (SERVER:92342-92346, 92414-92427); GenerateBiomePoints stores GetBiomeHeight per cell and -1000 beyond waterEdge (92429-92460); GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel exists (92683). Sector Center is the perimeter centroid (92531-92535, 92571-92573) and MinZone/MaxZone are both computed from Min (92577-92578) — both confirmed. Corrections: (1) BiomeSector.Min is ALSO garbage: Min/Max are plain Vector2 fields defaulting to (0,0) (SERVER:93906-93908) and the edge loop only lowers Min with `<` over j,i >= 1 (92539-92550), so Min stays (0,0) in map space = (-12282,-12282) world for every sector; only Max, Center, EdgeCount, HeightMin/HeightMax (edge cells only) are usable. The 'walk toward Min/Max interior' fallback must use Max/Center or a re-flood of PointSectors. (2) AshLands, DeepNorth and Ocean are pre-seeded as ONE sector each and skipped by the flood fill (92481-92503), so 'nearest N' and 'centroid' modes are meaningless for Ashlands/Deep North (single sector whose perimeter centroid lies in the ocean ring); use the spiral/nearest-edge or random-point modes there. (3) PointBiomes is Heightmap.BiomeIndex[,], not Biome (92357) — compare with B.ToBiomeIndex(). (4) Sectors include one-cell slivers; filter by EdgeCount before ranking. (5) HeightAvg is (HeightMin+HeightMax)/2 over edge cells (92579), not a real average. Arrival-side: same floating-collapse caveat — biome edges are often steep and WorldGenerator height ignores player terrain edits; apply the LoadFields WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false override (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150781-150838, 150445-150450). Random-mode re-roll must destroy-and-recreate with ownership claim and rewrite the hub connection inside the 5 s reconcile window (Game.ConnectPortals SERVER:100592-100626).

catalog.name: Named World-Gen Locations (generic) and LocationProxy ZDOs
catalog.oneLine: Any location type by name — runestone camps, villages, tar pits, shipwrecks — from the registry; plus the ZDO-level LocationProxy index for 'only locations that physically exist'.
catalog.howItWorks: Registry route: `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` (List<ZoneLocation>) is the vocabulary (m_prefabName, m_biome, m_quantity, m_iconAlways/m_iconPlaced, m_exteriorRadius) and `GetLocationList()` / `FindLocations(name)` / `FindClosestLocation(name, point)` give instances. This is exactly what vanilla's `find` console command does. Build a name→List<LocationInstance> index once at OnWorldReady (thousands of entries; O(n) per query otherwise). Place the phantom (Option 1) outside m_exteriorRadius on the flattest sample. Materialised-only route: `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(ZDOExtraData.Type.Int, ZDOVars.s_location)` enumerates every LocationProxy ZDO in the world (one per placed location, written by LocationProxy.SetLocation with the location hash as an Int) — an unindexed full scan of every ZDO's int fields, so run it once and cache; each proxy ZDO's GetPosition() is the actual placed origin and its s_location int identifies the type. Use this when the design wants 'only places someone has already discovered/generated'. Config exposes a list of (label, locationName, mode=nearest|random|index) per hub; the maintenance tick creates missing phantoms and reaps ones whose config entry was removed. Locations never move, so no moving-target logic is needed; 'random' mode re-rolls on a timer with destroy-and-recreate.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover: `Portal tag:">Tar Pit" [connected]`. Standard swirl, arrival outside the location's footprint facing it. For icon-flagged locations the vanilla map icon is already present; for others the mod can push a saved pin via RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse with the location's display name.
failureModes: `SoftReference<GameObject>.Name` (used by FindClosestLocation) is in an assembly not in the decompile set; if it forces an asset load, index by ZoneLocation.m_prefabName (plain string) instead.
GetAllZDOIDsWithHash default branch calls Debug.Break() for unsupported types — only pass Int here.
Locations flagged m_snapToWater sit at y=30 regardless of m_position.y.
openQuestions: Cost of one full GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Int, s_location) pass on a mature world (Stopwatch it at boot).
Is SoftReference.Name a cheap string property?
catalog.id: targeted-portals:Named World-Gen Locations (generic) and LocationProxy ZDOs
corrections: The 'find' Terminal helper (SERVER:45602-45631) is a static local function that also calls UnityEngine.Object.FindObjectsOfType and GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative; it is not a server-side template. Drop the 'exactly what vanilla's find does' framing - only the m_locationInstances loop is relevant.

Registry position vs. placed position differ: PlaceLocations snaps p via GetGroundData (collider raycast) and forces p.y=30 for m_snapToWater (SERVER:114961-114968) before creating the proxy ZDO, while LocationInstance.m_position.y is WorldGenerator height (SERVER:114737). Compute phantom y from WorldGenerator, never from the registry y, and treat the proxy ZDO position as the true origin when available.

m_placed is only ever set on the server's own copy (SERVER:114985-114991) because only the server spawns in Full/Ghost mode (SERVER:114028, 114086) - it is authoritative on the dedicated server, which strengthens the 'materialised-only' route; the Int scan is not needed just to learn 'placed', only to get the snapped origin.

Hash->ZoneLocation mapping: ZoneSystem.m_locationsByHash (SERVER:113250) is private; either publicize it or rebuild the map from m_locations using m_prefab.Name.GetStableHashCode() (as SetLocation does at SERVER:102655).
Enforcement is server-enforced only in the 'route' sense; the ore/NoPortals/boss checks in TeleportWorld.Teleport (SERVER:143520-143533) run on the client.

Replace the GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Int, s_location) full scan with LocationInstance.m_placed (S:113001-113008, persisted via ZoneSystem.Load S:113813-113817) and ZoneSystem.m_locationIDCache (S:113297); the ZDO scan adds nothing and is O(all ZDO int fields).

Random-mode re-roll MUST destroy-and-recreate the phantom rather than SetPosition it: portal ZDOs never re-bucket (ZDO.SetSector returns early for PortalPrefabHash; portals live in m_portalObjects keyed by creation sector, S:77738-77752, and are excluded from m_objectsBySector so Wonderland's sector sweepers never see them).
RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse side effect: Player.SetLookDir toward the pin for 3.5 s when the map is closed (S:100825-100830); pin is saved and cannot be removed remotely.

For m_snapToWater locations (shipwrecks) the phantom must be placed on land found by WorldGenerator height >= 30 or the traveller exits into water; FindFloor (C:116244) hits seabed terrain so the teleport still completes, they just swim.
Location terrain is levelled inside the location radius by TerrainModifiers that pure WorldGenerator math does not see; keep the phantom outside m_exteriorRadius as written.

catalog.name: Player's Bed
catalog.oneLine: Portal to a bed a player has claimed, found by scanning bed ZDOs for ZDOVars.s_owner == the player's stable profile ID.
catalog.howItWorks: Identity: the player's stable ID is `characterZdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (ConnectedCharacters.PlayerId); never peer.m_uid (session) and never peer.m_playerID (always 0 — the PlayerID RPC is never invoked by a vanilla client). Bed ownership: Bed.RPC_SetOwner writes `s_owner` (long = profile UID) and `s_ownerName` into the bed's own ZDO, persistent and offline-readable. Discovery: bed prefab names are asset data; enumerate `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` at OnWorldReady and keep hashes of prefabs with a Bed component (Wonderland ContainerRegistry pattern), then run ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper over those hashes with a sector budget to build a map playerId→List<(ZDOID, pos)>; incrementally maintain it with the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfix pair (new bed ZDOs) and ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (removed beds); watch s_owner on a slow tick because claiming happens later than placement. Ambiguity: vanilla lets a player own unlimited beds and never clears s_owner — 'the player's bed' must be chosen by rule: (a) the bed nearest the player's last known position, (b) the most recently claimed (mod records the tick it first saw s_owner set), (c) the one the player was last seen sleeping in — infer from `characterZdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` and match the character position to the nearest bed ZDO within 2 m (Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep reads the same field server-side). Placement: the bed's spawn offset (Bed.m_spawnPoint child Transform) is not in the ZDO; place the phantom (Option 1) 3–4 m from the bed ZDO position along the flattest compass sample with a piece-proximity check (FindNear 2 m) to avoid dropping the phantom inside the player's own walls — imperfect without colliders. Because a bed is inside a base, the arrival exit may hit a wall; the client's FindFloor still lands them on the floor piece (piece layer is in m_solidRayMask). Per-player hub: a single 'Home' hub portal cannot be per-player (one connection per ZDO); implement as one phantom per player, re-targeted when the requesting player emotes (EmoteSignals) — or use the two-hop relay (Option 20).
catalog.playerExperience: The player stands at the 'Home' hub, performs the configured emote (e.g. /wave); within 0.25 s the server writes the hub's tag to `>Home: Rohan` and links it to a phantom beside Rohan's bed; a toast says `Home portal set to your bed`. They walk in, 8 s swirl, step out next to their bed inside their base. The phantom stays there (they can return through it). Another player emoting at the hub re-targets it for themselves; hover text changes for everyone nearby.
failureModes: Beds inside cramped houses: arrival point may be inside a wall or on a roof; the mod can only approximate structure clearance from piece ZDO positions.
A player with no claimed bed: fall back to StartTemple with a toast.
Shared hub re-targeting is a race between players; a per-player phantom per hub or the relay option removes it.
Bed destroyed: bed ZDO vanishes → phantom orphaned; maintenance tick reaps it and toasts the owner.

corrections: Ownership churn on the phantom: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands every PERSISTENT ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer whenever the current owner is not in its own active area, and the server's session is never 'in area' because its ref pos is (1e6,0,1e6) (IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280; ReleaseNearbyZDOS SERVER:77282-77306). A phantom parked beside a bed inside a base will therefore be client-owned whenever anyone is home. ZDO.Set(...) still propagates (IncreaseDataRevision unconditional, SERVER:73600-73607) but ZDO.SetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner (SERVER:73734-73745) - so any re-positioning must SetOwner(session) first, or use a non-persistent phantom (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS keeps m_sessionID-owned ZDOs: IsPeerConnected SERVER:77423-77435).

'the player's bed' identity gating is NOT enforced: the server sets the route, but any vanilla client near the hub can walk through after the retarget (TeleportWorld.Teleport SERVER:143516-143548 has no identity check). State this explicitly in the option.

Bed index keyed by ZDOID must be rebuilt on every boot (ZDOIDs are session-scoped; prior-session note) - the PrefabSetSweeper pass is the boot path, the SpawnGovernor postfix pair only covers incremental arrivals.

The client-side FindFloor claim is right about the mask but note FindFloor raycasts 1000 m down (SERVER:  ZoneSystem.FindFloor), so it returns true even when the frozen target is above a roof; arrival inside a multi-storey base can land on the roof/upper floor, not necessarily beside the bed.

Sleeping requires the bed to be the CURRENT custom spawn point (Bed.Interact: IsMine() && IsCurrent() before AttachStart, S:119691-119714; IsCurrent S:119790-119793). s_inBed + nearest bed ZDO therefore identifies the active spawn bed exactly — make rule (c) the primary rule, (a)/(b) fallbacks only.

Return trip is single-slot: once any other player emotes at the hub, the previous phantom is disconnected by Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (S:100597-100604) and cannot be re-paired. Say so in playerExperience; reap stale phantoms.

FindFloor (C:116244) does not relocate the player; UpdateTeleport pins them at phantom pos + forward*1 + up*1 (C:15347-15370). Wall-adjacent placement leaves them inside geometry. Piece layer being in the mask only affects when the swirl ends.
Phantom is a genuine portal_wood ZDO: retaggable via RPC_SetTag on the owner client (S:143583-143600) and deletable via the ungated DestroyZDO path (S:76953-76960). The mod must re-assert.

Server writes to hub/phantom must SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) first and ForceSendZDO; ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76901-76926) returns ownership to a nearby peer within 2 s; tag-only writes need ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (S:76702) or are lost at save.

Wonderland PrefabSetSweeper walks m_objectsBySector only (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:153-176) — fine for beds, but it will never enumerate portal ZDOs (AddIfPortal removes them from the sector map, S:77738-77752).

catalog.name: Player's Custom Spawn Point (direct read ruled out; inference feasible)
catalog.oneLine: The active spawn point lives only in the client's .fch profile and is never networked; the server can infer it from peer.m_refPos while the player is dead and from sleep events.
catalog.howItWorks: RULED OUT as a direct read: `PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_spawnPoint/m_haveCustomSpawnPoint` are written by Bed.Interact's non-claim branch via `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(...)` with no RPC and no ZDO write, and ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles only tells clients to save their own files. No packet ever carries it. INFERENCE 1 (respawn leak): Game.UpdateRespawn on the client calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(customSpawnPoint)` (or the logout point on login, or the StartTemple icon) while the character is dead; the client's periodic ServerSyncedPlayerData (every 2 s) then delivers that reference position into `peer.m_refPos`. Server logic: on `characterZdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)==true` (or peer.m_characterID.IsNone() after RPC_CharacterID(None) in _RequestRespawn), sample peer.m_refPos over the next few seconds; the stable value before the new character ZDO appears is the spawn point. Persist it in a mod file keyed by playerID. INFERENCE 2 (sleep): `s_inBed==true` on the character ZDO plus nearest bed ZDO within 2 m → that bed is at least a candidate; vanilla only lets you sleep in a bed you own, and most players sleep in their spawn bed. INFERENCE 3 (login leak): on first RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData after PeerInfo, m_refPos equals the logout point (Game.UpdateRespawn uses HaveLogoutPoint first), a good proxy for 'home'. Combine: spawn-point candidate = INFERENCE 1 if ever observed, else INFERENCE 2, else INFERENCE 3, else bed rule from Option 10. Then Option 1 phantom near that point, or Option 20 relay. The mod cannot SET a player's spawn point either (Bed.Interact is local).
catalog.playerExperience: Identical to Option 10 from the player's side (`>Home` hub, emote to claim, arrive beside their bed). Difference: the destination matches where they actually respawn, but only after the mod has observed at least one death/respawn or login of that player on this server; before that, a toast explains `No home known yet — using your nearest bed`.
failureModes: Never-died, never-relogged players have no INFERENCE 1 sample; fall back to bed/login heuristics.
peer.m_refPos is also written during ordinary play (position lagging ≤2 s); the sampling window must be strictly gated on s_dead / characterID None.
A player who changes spawn bed after the last observation is targeted at the stale point until they die or relog.
Cross-world profiles: WorldPlayerData is per world UID, so a stale spawn point from another world is never leaked — only this world's.
prerequisites: Phantom Destination Portal (Option 1) or Two-hop Relay (Option 20)
Per-player mod-side persistence keyed by s_playerID
openQuestions: Exact timing: how many ServerSyncedPlayerData packets arrive between death and the new character ZDO (determines how reliable the refPos sample is).

catalog.id: targeted-portals:Player's Custom Spawn Point (direct read ruled out; inference feasible)
corrections: Trigger on peer.m_characterID.IsNone(), NOT on s_dead: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead then calls Game.RequestRespawn(10f, afterDeath:true) (SERVER:12847); for those 10 s the local Player still exists and Player.Update keeps ref pos at the corpse (SERVER:11070-11074). Only after _RequestRespawn destroys the player and sends CharacterID(None) does FindSpawnPoint (called from UpdateRespawn while m_requestRespawn, CLIENT:100937-100941) drive the ref pos. The window is at least m_respawnLoadDuration = 8 s (SERVER:100295), i.e. >=3 periodic sends.

If the player has no custom spawn point (or its bed is gone: ClearCustomSpawnPoint at SERVER:100357 then falls through next tick), the leaked ref pos is the StartTemple icon + 2 up (SERVER:100365-100369). The mod must compare the sample against ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(StartTemple) and discard it, or it will record the spawn temple as 'home'.

The leaked value is the bed's m_spawnPoint.position captured at claim time (SERVER:119689/119724, GetSpawnPoint SERVER:119796-119799), not the bed ZDO position; FindBedNearby tolerates 5 m (SERVER:100350). Match beds within ~5 m, not 2 m.

peer.m_refPos is never blanked by the privacy flag (SERVER:80399-80400 unconditional); only the player-list position is (UpdatePlayerList). The option's login inference therefore works for privacy-off players too.
The SetReferencePosition calls live in Game.FindSpawnPoint (SERVER:100313-100375), not in UpdateRespawn itself; UpdateRespawn only calls it (CLIENT:100939).

Sleep observation (s_inBed on the character ZDO while within ~1 m of a bed ZDO) proves the bed is the CURRENT custom spawn point, because Bed.Interact requires IsMine() && IsCurrent() before AttachStart (S:119691-119714, IsCurrent S:119790-119793). Promote INFERENCE 2 above INFERENCE 3.

Respawn leak has a second, exact channel: the new character ZDO's initial position after a death equals bed.GetSpawnPoint() (Game.FindSpawnPoint C:100784-100791 -> UpdateRespawn/SpawnPlayer C:100937-100947) or StartTemple pos + 2 m if no custom point.

INFERENCE 3 is wrong as 'home': on login the logout point branch is taken first (C:100746-100774) and the custom-spawn branch never runs; peer.m_refPos on login is the quit position, which is at best 'last seen', not home.

Window sizing: m_respawnLoadDuration = 8 s (C:100295) and periodic send cadence 2 s (C:80532) → ≥3 refPos samples of the spawn point per death; s_dead is visible on the old character ZDO for ~10 s before it is destroyed (C:12849, C:100831-100845).

Observed spawn points can go stale: FindSpawnPoint calls ClearCustomSpawnPoint when no Bed is within 5 m (C:100793-100801); a destroyed bed silently reverts the player to StartTemple with no signal to the server other than the next respawn refPos.

The respawn leak is real: Game.FindSpawnPoint calls ZNet.SetReferencePosition(logoutPoint | customSpawnPoint | StartTemple pos) (SERVER:100317, 100346, 100367) and the client's SendServerSyncPlayerData writes m_referencePosition unconditionally every 2 s (CLIENT SendPeriodicData/SendServerSyncPlayerData; server RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData writes peer.m_refPos SERVER:80395-80410, cadence SERVER:80337-80345).
