[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Direct-read ruling confirmed: Bed.Interact's non-claim branch calls Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(GetSpawnPoint()) with no RPC/ZDO write (S:119719-119731); nothing networks WorldPlayerData. Respawn leak confirmed and STRONGER than described: client Game.FindSpawnPoint (C:100741-100813) calls ZNet.SetReferencePosition(customSpawnPoint) every frame while m_requestRespawn, waits m_respawnWait > m_respawnLoadDuration (8 s, C:100295) plus IsAreaReady, and the client's SendPeriodicData pushes m_referencePosition to the server every 2 s regardless of the privacy flag (C:80529-80568; server RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData writes peer.m_refPos S:80395-80404) — so at least 3-4 samples equal the custom spawn point exactly. Then SpawnPlayer places the new character at bed.GetSpawnPoint() (C:100786-100791), so the first position of the new character ZDO after a death is itself the spawn point. Death timeline: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead (C:12736) and RequestRespawn(10f, afterDeath:true) (C:12849); _RequestRespawn destroys the character and sends CharacterID(None) (C:100831-100845, C:81080). Sleep inference is also stronger: Bed.Interact only allows sleeping when IsCurrent() (S:119691-119714), so s_inBed ⇒ that bed IS the active spawn point at that moment. Correction to INFERENCE 3: on login (m_respawnAfterDeath false) FindSpawnPoint uses the LOGOUT point, which is wherever the player quit — not a 'home' proxy — and the logout branch runs before the custom-spawn branch, so login never leaks the spawn point. Also: if no bed exists within 5 m of the custom point at respawn, ClearCustomSpawnPoint runs and the player falls back to StartTemple (C:100793-100801), so an observed refPos may be a spawn point the client has since cleared. Enforcement 'reactive-detection-only' is honest.

catalog.name: Player's Death Spot / Tombstone
catalog.oneLine: Portal to a player's most recent tombstone, read straight off the TombStone container ZDO (owner, time of death, death position, and even the items).
catalog.howItWorks: Player.CreateTombStone (client) instantiates the tombstone prefab and TombStone.Setup writes `ZDOVars.s_ownerName` (string) and `ZDOVars.s_owner` (long = profile UID); TombStone.Awake on the owner writes `s_timeOfDeath` (ZNet time ticks) and `s_spawnPoint` (the death position) once. The tombstone is a real persistent ZDO in the sector map. Detection: the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO(prefab 0)+ZDO.Deserialize postfix pair sees every client-created ZDO the instant it arrives; filter on the tombstone prefab hash (asset name unknown in the decompile — discover at boot by scanning ZNetScene.m_prefabs for a TombStone component, or match the first ZDO carrying both s_ownerName and s_timeOfDeath) and index playerId→(ZDOID, pos, ticks). Alternatively bootstrap with `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, ZDOVars.s_timeOfDeath)` once at boot (s_timeOfDeath is written only by TombStone). Filter by prefab because `s_owner` is also used by Bed (profile UID) and GrapplingPoint (a ZDOID.ID). Target: the newest tombstone for the requesting player (max s_timeOfDeath); place the phantom (Option 1) 3 m from `zdo.GetPosition()` on the flattest sample (deaths are often on slopes, in water, or in lava — validate with GetHeight/IsLavaPreHeightmap and if the death spot is underwater, walk toward the nearest cell with PointHeights≥31). Lifecycle: the tombstone despawns when emptied (TombStone.UpdateDespawn) and the ZDO is destroyed → ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed fires → reap the phantom and clear the hub link, toast the player `Your grave has been recovered`. Optional flourish: read the tombstone's `s_items` blob via ZdoInventoryIO.Load to toast `12 items waiting`, and push a saved map pin via RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (PinType.Death) — vanilla already adds a death pin client-side, so only useful as a named marker.
catalog.playerExperience: Player dies in the Plains, respawns at their bed, walks to the `>Grave` hub portal and performs the claim emote; toast `Grave portal set: 2 min ago, 14 items`; hover reads `Portal tag:">Grave: Rohan" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive 3 m from their skull marker with a portal behind them for the return trip. Once they loot the grave it despawns; the phantom is removed on the next tick (visibly vanishing if they are still standing there) and the hub tag reverts to `>Grave (none)` / unconnected.
failureModes: Death in deep water/lava: the phantom must be displaced to the nearest land; the arrival is then a swim/run away.
Death near a boss/mob camp: arrival drops the player straight back into danger — a 'safe radius' from the death spot (10–20 m) is advisable.
The tombstone's s_items blob only lands once the owning client's Container ticks after MoveInventoryToGrave; item count may read 0 for a second.
Tombstone prefab name unverified (assumed Player_tombstone).
prerequisites: SpawnGovernor-style ZDO arrival hooks or a boot-time GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Long, s_timeOfDeath) scan
openQuestions: Tombstone prefab name/hash (kill a test character and log the new ZDO's prefab).
Does s_spawnPoint on the tombstone differ from GetPosition() once the ragdoll body settles (m_body velocity in Setup)?
corrections: 's_timeOfDeath is written only by TombStone' is FALSE: Corpse.Awake (class SERVER:5444, write SERVER:5460-5463) writes the same key for creature corpses. The Long-scan bootstrap must additionally require s_owner != 0 / s_ownerName present (Corpse writes neither) or filter by prefab hash.

Do not use s_spawnPoint as a discriminator or as the death position: it is also written by BaseAI (SERVER:25933-25936), Fish (SERVER:126104-126107), RandomFlyingBird (SERVER:137940-137943) and the legacy ZDO loader (SERVER:74399). Use zdo.GetPosition() - the tombstone has a Rigidbody + Floating (SERVER:19730-19733) and can drift/float to the surface.
A tombstone only exists when the inventory was non-empty and DeathKeepInventory is unset (SERVER:12694-12695); the '(none)' state is the common case for empty-handed deaths.

Despawn runs only on the ZDO-owning CLIENT (SERVER:19883 `if (m_nview.IsOwner())`); the server never runs UpdateDespawn. An emptied grave whose area nobody is loading stays as a ZDO until a client instantiates it - the phantom reap will lag until then.
Index keyed by ZDOID must be rebuilt each boot (ZDOIDs are session-scoped); the boot scan is mandatory, not optional.

s_timeOfDeath is ALSO written by Corpse.Awake (S:5460-5462) — bootstrap scans on (Type.Long, s_timeOfDeath) must additionally require s_ownerName (string) or match the tombstone prefab hash discovered from ZNetScene.m_prefabs.
No tombstone is created when the inventory is empty or GlobalKeys.DeathKeepInventory is set (Player.CreateTombStone C:12696); the feature has nothing to target for such deaths — toast accordingly.
Return-trip portal beside the grave is single-slot: re-targeting the hub for another player disconnects it (Game.ConnectPortals S:100597-100604).
Tombstone ZDO position moves (Floater/Rigidbody, TombStone.PositionCheck/UpdateFloater S:19882-19886); keep using zdo.GetPosition() and re-place the phantom if it drifts >N m.
Server-created phantom writes need SetOwner(session) + ForceSendZDO and SetDirtyPortals for tag writes (S:76702); ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76901-76926) reassigns persistent ZDOs near players every 2 s.

catalog.name: Player's Ship (moving vehicle)
catalog.oneLine: Portal toward a ship a player is steering or riding; the destination can be the Ship ZDO itself (live position) but vanilla's 8-second frozen-snapshot teleport guarantees the traveller lands in the water behind a moving boat.
catalog.howItWorks: Which ship: (a) confirmed signal — `shipZdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_user)` equals the helmsman's stable playerID (written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl on the ship's own ZDO, zeroed on release) — Wonderland ShipAttachment.IsSteeringShip already implements a 40 m scan; (b) passenger signal — `characterZdo.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.SyncTransform)` gives the Rigidbody+ZNetView parent the rider stands on, written by ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync only if the Player prefab's `m_characterParentSync` Inspector bool is on (unverified); prefab-check the target for a Ship component before trusting it, cross-check `shipPos + shipRot*GetVec3(s_relPosHash) ≈ playerPos` to reject stale latches. Destination choice 1 — point the source portal DIRECTLY at the Ship ZDO: `src.SetConnection(Portal, shipZdo.m_uid)`; TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the ship ZDO's live position/rotation at the instant of transit with no prefab check. But Game.ConnectPortals nulls it within 5 s unless the ship ZDO carries the same s_tag AND a reciprocal Portal connection — writing `shipZdo.Set(s_tag, tag)` and `shipZdo.SetConnection(Portal, src.m_uid)` is safe (ships never hold a SyncTransform parent of their own, and a ZDO has exactly one connection slot), but it means the ship's ZDO now carries a Portal link that must be scrubbed when the feature ends. Also the client fetches the ship ZDO once (TargetFound→RequestZDO) and never re-requests, so the server must `ForceSendZDO(peer, shipUid)` on a tick for peers standing at the source to keep the position fresh. Destination choice 2 — a moving Invisible Anchor (Option 2) re-positioned every tick to `shipPos + shipRot*(-forward*6)` (behind the stern) with `a.SetOwner(session); a.SetPosition(...)`: no writes on the ship, but the same ForceSendZDO requirement. Arrival physics: Player.UpdateTeleport snapshots m_teleportTargetPos once, pins the player there from t>2 s, and for distantTeleport waits until t>8 s AND IsAreaReady; FindFloor's mask omits the vehicle layer so the deck never counts as floor — the traveller lands at sea level behind wherever the ship was 8 s ago. Recommended product: 'portal to the ship' only for anchored/moored ships (velocity ≈0 from position deltas), arriving in the water 5 m astern; for moving ships use the Two-hop Relay (Option 20) which re-teleports to the live position.
catalog.playerExperience: At the `>Ship` hub the player emotes; toast `Linked to Rohan's longship (moored)`; hover `Portal tag:">Ship: Rohan" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, splash into the water a few metres behind the boat, swim to the ladder. If the ship was sailing, they surface 50–100 m behind it in open sea with no portal to return through. If the helmsman lets go of the tiller (s_user→0) the mod keeps the last ship for a grace period then unlinks with a toast.
failureModes: 8 s frozen snapshot: landing on a moving deck is impossible in vanilla; open-sea arrival with no return portal.
m_characterParentSync unverified → passenger detection may not exist; helmsman-only (s_user) is the safe subset.

Writing tag/connection onto a Ship ZDO is invasive; if the mod is removed the ship keeps a Portal connection (vanilla ignores it because the ship is not in the portal list, but the source portal stays linked until reconciled).
Continuous ForceSendZDO of a ship ZDO to every peer near the source costs ~100 bytes/peer/cycle.
Ship destroyed/despawned: GetZDO null → reconcile clears the link within 5 s.
prerequisites: Invisible Anchor (Option 2) or direct ship link

corrections: Server writes on the client-owned ship ZDO propagate because ZDO.Set/SetConnection bump DataRevision unconditionally (SERVER:73600-73607, 73656-73665), and the owner's subsequent higher-revision update is accepted by RPC_ZDOData whose Deserialize is ADDITIVE (ZDOExtraData.Add; the connection is only replaced if the packet carries one, SERVER ZDO.Deserialize) - so tag+connection survive on the server copy. But the OWNER client never receives them (ShouldSend false after its own update, SERVER:76003-76013) and exactly one owner position update is dropped by the `num4 <= DataRevision` check in RPC_ZDOData. Harmless, but 'safe' needs this reasoning, not 'ships have no connection'.

Save boundary: a ship<->hub Portal link is serialised by RegenerateConnectionHashData as a (Portal,hash)/(Portal|Target,hash) pair on BOTH ZDOs regardless of prefab (SERVER:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals re-links them at load and SetOwner(session) on both (SERVER:77850-77889). The ship keeps the s_tag string and Portal connection across restarts unless the mod scrubs at boot as well as at feature end.

s_user goes stale: only the ship-owner client clears it via RPC_ReleaseControl (SERVER:141344-141350); a helmsman who disconnects mid-sail leaves s_user set forever. Cross-check the playerID against ConnectedCharacters before trusting it (the option's grace period should be a hard timeout).

Direct ship link arrival point is shipPos + shipRot*forward*1 + up (SERVER:143541-143546) - 1 m ahead of the ship pivot, i.e. inside the hull; FindFloor raycasts 1000 m down through 'terrain' (seabed) so it returns true over open water and ends the teleport at that frozen point. Use the anchor variant only.

Anchor ownership: a PERSISTENT server-owned anchor is handed to the nearest peer every 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (Persistent-only loop, SERVER:77282-77306; the server session is never 'in area', IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280), after which SetPosition no longer bumps DataRevision (SERVER:73734-73745) and updates stop. Either make the anchor non-persistent (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS keeps m_sessionID-owned ZDOs: IsPeerConnected SERVER:77423-77435) or accept per-tick SetOwner (OwnerRevision churn).

TargetFound re-issues RequestZDO every 0.5 s (UpdatePortal InvokeRepeating) until the ZDO exists locally, then never again - 'single RequestZDO' is right in effect but the per-tick ForceSendZDO(peer, uid) is only useful if the ship's DataRevision keeps rising (it does while moving; a moored ship with no changes will not resend, which is fine).
Player.TeleportTo refuses when m_teleportCooldown < 2 s (SERVER:15310-15313) - relevant to any relay chaining.

Moving anchor ownership: ZDO.InternalSetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner() (S:73734-73744), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns every PERSISTENT ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer every 2 s (S:76901-76926). Create the anchor NON-persistent (server-owned non-persistent ZDOs survive RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS because IsPeerConnected(sessionID) is true, S:77406-77419) or re-SetOwner(session) each tick (extra OwnerRevision churn).

Arrival geometry: the traveller is pinned at targetPos + targetForward*1 + up*1 (S:143542-143545, C:15347-15352); FindFloor (C:116244) only decides when the swirl ends and succeeds on seabed terrain. Direct ship link ⇒ arrival ~1 m ahead of the ship ORIGIN (inside/over the hull for a moored ship), not astern; astern requires choice 2's offset anchor.

Direct link persists across save/reload: RegenerateConnectionHashData (S:75461-75477) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (S:77850-77889) rebuild any mutual Portal pair with no prefab filter — scrub s_tag and the ship's Portal connection on feature end or the ship remains a portal endpoint after restart.
RPC_SetTag on the source by any nearby player triggers SetConnectedPortal → RPC_SetConnected on the ship owner, clearing the ship's Portal connection (S:143583-143622); the mod must re-assert.

TargetFound/RequestZDO only runs while a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (5 m) of the source (C:144231-144247); a sprinter can trigger before the ship ZDO arrives → Teleport() silently does nothing (S:143539-143548, zDO == null branch).
m_characterParentSync on the Player prefab remains unverified (Inspector bool, S:87361); passenger detection via SyncTransform connection must be treated as probable, not proven.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core claims verified: ShipControlls.m_nview is the SHIP's ZNetView and RPC_RequestControl writes s_user = playerID on the owner (S:141258-141261, S:141326-141339); ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes SetConnection(SyncTransform, parent) only under m_characterParentSync (S:87542-87562), Character/Player.GetRelativePosition supply the parent from m_lastGroundBody/m_attachPoint (S:4423-4444, S:16551-16576); TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the connection target's live position/rotation with no prefab check (S:143539-143548); TargetFound calls RequestZDO only when the client lacks the ZDO (S:143640-143658), invoked from UpdatePortal every 0.5 s only while a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (C:144231-144247); server RPC_RequestZDO → peer.ForceSendZDO (S:77689-77692), per-peer ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) exists (S:77714-77724), force-send entries are cleared after each send (S:77048), and the client's RPC_ZDOData accepts updates for any known ZDO whose DataRevision rose (C:77217-77270). Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls the source unless the ship carries the same s_tag AND a non-None Portal connection (S:100597-100604); the ship is never in GetPortalList (prefab-keyed m_portalObjects, S:77648) so it is never re-paired. Single connection slot per ZDO confirmed (Dictionary<ZDOID,ZDOConnection> S:74797). Player.UpdateTeleport snapshot/8 s/IsAreaReady gate confirmed (C:15331-15370). Corrections: (1) ZDO.InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only when IsOwner() (S:73734-73744) and ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands every PERSISTENT ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer within 2 s (S:76901-76926) — a moving anchor must be created non-persistent (then RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS leaves it alone because IsPeerConnected(sessionID) is true, S:77406-77419, C:77562-77565) or the tick must re-SetOwner(session) before every SetPosition. (2) 'FindFloor omits vehicle so they land at sea level' misdescribes the physics: FindFloor only ends the teleport (it hits seabed terrain at sea, C:116244), the player is pinned at shipZdoPos + shipForward*1 + up*1 (S:143542-143545) — for a moored ship that is inside the hull near the ship origin, not '5 m astern'; astern placement only comes from choice 2's anchor offset. (3) Direct link survives a world save: RegenerateConnectionHashData/ZDOMan.ConnectPortals reconnect any mutual Portal pair regardless of prefab (S:75461-75477, S:77850-77889), so the ship keeps its Portal slot across restarts until scrubbed. (4) A player retagging the source via RPC_SetTag calls SetConnectedPortal → RPC_SetConnected on the ship's owner, which clears the ship's Portal connection client-side (S:143583-143622). (5) Anchor ZDOs with prefab 0 are silently skipped by the client (CreateObject returns null C:82225-82230, IsPrefabZDOValid false C:82293-82305) and only a server would destroy them (C:82357-82363) — safe. Verdict: mechanism real, product recommendation (moored only / relay for moving) sound.

catalog.name: Nearest Player (player-to-player portal)
catalog.oneLine: Portal to the nearest online player, or a named player, using the live character ZDO position; the character ZDO can be the destination directly but is non-persistent and must never receive a Portal connection.
catalog.howItWorks: Positions: ConnectedCharacters.All() → `zdo.GetPosition()` refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform (distance-independent client→server delivery), far fresher than peer.m_refPos (2 s, and blank in GetPlayerList for privacy-off players). Nearest: min distance from the source portal over all connected characters excluding the traveller. Destination mechanism A — direct: `src.SetConnection(Portal, characterZdo.m_uid)`; TeleportWorld.Teleport would read the character's live position. But Game.ConnectPortals will null it within 5 s (the character ZDO has no matching tag and no Portal connection back) and you MUST NOT write a Portal connection onto a player ZDO (it would overwrite their SyncTransform parent slot). So A requires a prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (or a 1 s re-assert that always loses the race half the time) — a Harmony prefix that skips reconcile for TPL-managed sources is clean (SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch). Character ZDOs are also destroyed on disconnect (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS) and s_dead players sit at their corpse. Mechanism B — an Invisible Anchor (Option 2) re-positioned to `targetPos + 2 m` behind the target each 0.5–1 s with SetOwner+SetPosition, plus `ForceSendZDO(peer, anchorUid)` to peers near the source so their copy is fresh. Arrival lands where the target was ~8 s earlier (frozen snapshot); fine for a standing player, off by up to 60 m for a runner. Safety: skip targets with `s_dead`, `s_inBed`, InInterior (y>3000 — the anchor would need to be at interior coordinates, which works geometrically but the client must have that interior loaded, i.e. be there already), or in water (GetHeight<30 at their XZ). Tag: `>Nearest: <s_playerName>`. Selection input: emote at the hub cycles through candidates (toast the name each press) — EmoteSignals.
catalog.playerExperience: At the `>Player` hub the traveller presses the cycle emote; toasts show `Target: Erik (412 m)`, `Target: Anna (2.1 km)`; hover updates to `Portal tag:">Erik" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive ~2 m behind where Erik stood 8 s ago. No portal at the far end (anchor is invisible); return via another portal or the relay. If Erik logs out mid-transit the anchor is reaped and the traveller still arrives at the last position.
failureModes: Direct-link variant fights vanilla's reconciler; without a ConnectPortals prefix it is unreliable.
Never write Portal connections onto character ZDOs (single connection slot; destroys ship/mount parenting).

Target in a dungeon interior: anchor at y>3000 — the traveller's client only completes if it has that interior instanced (it will not), leading to the 15 s fallback and a drop at GetSolidHeight (surface) — block interior targets.
Griefing vector: portal-stalking a player; gate with a consent emote on the target side or restrict to group/ward-permitted players (ward permitted lists are ZDO-readable).
prerequisites: Optional Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals for direct links
openQuestions: Does the vanilla client accept a destination ZDO that moves between TargetFound() and Teleport() without issue (it reads once at transit — expected fine)?
corrections: Mechanism A does NOT give 'live position': the traveller's client only holds the target character ZDO if it is in its sector sync range or force-sent. After TargetFound's RequestZDO (one ForceSendZDO, SERVER:77689-77692, consumed at SERVER:77048) the copy is frozen. ForceSendZDO(peer, uid) per tick (SERVER:77714) is required for A exactly as for B; ShouldSend passes because the target's DataRevision rises every tick it moves (SERVER:76003-76013).

Server-side src.SetConnection on a client-owned hub works without Game.SetConnection's owner routing because ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision unconditionally (SERVER:73656-73665) and portals never self-update; but note every such write calls SetDirtyPortals and marks the ZDO for the next save, and the reconcile prefix must also cover the load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (SERVER:77850-77889), which would otherwise pair the hub with whatever (Portal|Target,hash) entry was saved.

Anchor (mechanism B) ownership churn: a PERSISTENT server-owned anchor 2 m behind a player is inside that player's active area and ReleaseNearbyZDOS transfers it to them every 2 s (Persistent-only loop SERVER:77282-77306; server session never in-area via IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280); after that ZDO.SetPosition no longer bumps DataRevision (SERVER:73734-73745) and the client copies stop updating. Make the anchor NON-persistent (kept alive because IsPeerConnected(m_sessionID) is true, SERVER:77423-77435) rather than re-SetOwner every tick.

Interior caveat is overstated: ZoneSystem.GetZone uses x/z only (SERVER:115740-115745) and ZNetScene.IsAreaReady only requires the target's zone loaded and its sector ZDOs instantiated (SERVER:82064-82081); after the 2 s snap the traveller's own Player.Update sets the ref pos to the target (SERVER:11070-11074) so that zone (including interior ZDOs at y~5000 in the same sector) loads. Whether the dungeon interior spawns correctly for a player who arrives by teleport without entering through the Teleport door has not been checked in game - mark that sub-case needs-ingame-check rather than 'must already be there'.

When the target disconnects, the hub's dangling connection is nulled by the reconcile `zDO == null` branch within <=5 s (SERVER:100598-100601) if the prefix does not intercept it; the traveller who is mid-transit still lands at the frozen snapshot (client already holds m_teleportTargetPos, SERVER:15324).
Identity/ore/boss gating remains client-side (TeleportWorld.Teleport SERVER:143516-143533); 'server-enforced' applies only to which route is open.

Mechanism A (direct character-ZDO link) needs the same per-tick ForceSendZDO(peer, characterUid) to peers near the source as mechanism B; RequestZDO yields a single send (force-send entries removed after send, S:77048) and nothing else pushes a far-away character ZDO to that client.

Anchor must be created NON-persistent: ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns persistent ZDOs in the target player's active area to that player within 2 s (S:76901-76926) and ZDO.InternalSetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner() (S:73734-73744). Server-owned non-persistent ZDOs are not orphan-collected (IsPeerConnected(sessionID) true, C:77562-77565).
Anchor needs s_tag == source tag AND a Portal connection back to the source or Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls the source within 5 s (S:100597-100604); tag-only is not enough.

s_dead window is ~10 s: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead (C:12736) and RequestRespawn(10f) destroys the character (C:12849, C:100831-100845); afterwards the peer has no character ZDO until respawn (peer.m_characterID = None via C:81080).
Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals must skip only pass 1 for TPL-managed sources; pass 2 already ignores them because their connection is non-None (S:100609-100611).
'Off by up to 60 m for a runner' is a lower bound: the 8 s gate is a minimum and IsAreaReady (C:82293-82310) can extend it while the destination zone streams in.

Game.ConnectPortals nulls a hub whose target has a different tag or no connection (SERVER:100597-100604) so mechanism A needs a prefix; a Portal connection on the character ZDO would overwrite the single SyncTransform slot (SERVER:74797, 75524-75534) - correct. Character ZDOs are non-persistent and destroyed by RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS when the owner is gone (SERVER:77406-77419). Player.UpdateTeleport freezes m_teleportTargetPos (SERVER:15330-15352). PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers keys are as cited (SERVER:137349-137363). Mechanism holds with corrections.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Position source verified: the owning client's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zdo.SetPosition every FixedUpdate (S:87527-87534); IncreaseDataRevision on a client queues ClientChanged (S:73832-73840) and the client branch of CreateSyncList sends every queued owned ZDO to the server irrespective of distance (S:77241-77258), so the server's copy of every character ZDO is fresh. peer.m_refPos is always populated server-side (S:80395-80404); privacy only blanks the player LIST (S:81280-81285). Direct-link analysis holds: Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls the source because the character ZDO has neither the tag nor a Portal connection back (S:100597-100604); a single connection slot per ZDO (S:74797) means writing Portal onto a player ZDO would clobber the SyncTransform parent ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync maintains (S:87542-87562); Game.ConnectPortals is public (S:100589) so a Harmony prefix is possible. Non-persistent character ZDOs are destroyed on disconnect (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS S:77406-77419). TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the target ZDO's live position with no prefab check (S:143539-143548); the traveller's client obtains the target via TargetFound→RequestZDO (S:143640-143658) → server per-peer force-send (S:77689-77692, S:77714-77724). Client-side an unknown/zero-prefab anchor is skipped harmlessly (CreateObject null C:82225-82230, only servers destroy C:82357-82363, IsPrefabZDOValid excludes it from IsAreaReady C:82293-82305). Corrections: (1) mechanism A ALSO needs the per-tick ForceSendZDO to source-side peers, otherwise the traveller's copy of the character ZDO is the one-shot snapshot from RequestZDO (m_forceSend entries are consumed after one send, S:77048) and the arrival is stale by far more than 8 s. (2) Anchor persistence/ownership: an anchor 2 m behind the target sits in the target's active area; if persistent, ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it to the target within 2 s (S:76901-76926) and server SetPosition then stops bumping DataRevision (S:73734-73744) — create it non-persistent (safe under RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS because IsPeerConnected(sessionID) is true, S:77406-77419, C:77562-77565). (3) The anchor must itself carry the source's s_tag and a Portal connection back or ConnectPortals nulls the route every 5 s (S:100597-100604). (4) s_dead players do not 'sit at their corpse' for long: OnDeath sets s_dead then RequestRespawn(10f) destroys the character ZDO (C:12736, C:12849, C:100831-100845). (5) Save boundary for mechanism A is benign: the source gets a Portal hash whose Portal|Target lands on a non-persistent ZDO, so the link is simply absent after reload (S:75461-75477) and must be re-asserted. Enforcement is 'server-authored route'.

catalog.name: Player-Placed Anchor (sign / item stand / ward / chest token / tagged portal)
catalog.oneLine: Let players designate destinations with things the server can read from ZDOs: a sign's text, an item on an item stand, a ward's permitted list, a token item in a chest, or a portal tagged with a reserved prefix.
catalog.howItWorks: All five are ZDO fields written by the placing client and delivered to the server distance-independently. (1) Sign: Sign.SetText claims ownership and writes `ZDOVars.s_text` (≤50 chars via the client widget) plus s_author; no RPC exists — poll signs. Recognise `#tpl <name>`; the sign ZDO position is the anchor. (2) Item stand: `ZDOVars.s_item` is the mounted item's prefab hash — a physical radio button; e.g. a Surtling core on the stand next to a hub means 'link here'. (3) Ward: PrivateArea ZDO carries s_creator, s_enabled, s_permitted + `pu_id{i}`/`pu_name{i}`; a ward tagged via an adjacent sign or simply 'the ward the player owns' becomes the anchor, and its permitted list doubles as the access list for who may target it. (4) Chest token: Container.Save writes the whole inventory into `ZDOVars.s_items`; ZdoInventoryIO.Load (skip if s_inUse) lets the server detect a specific token item (e.g. a Ymir flesh) in a chest within 3 m of a portal — and can consume it as a toll. (5) Tagged portal: a player portal whose s_tag starts with a reserved prefix (`@` + name) registers itself as a named destination; the hub's tag `>@name` links to it directly — no phantom needed at all, and the reconciler is satisfied by rewriting BOTH tags to one identical literal while linked (the mod stores the player's original tag in a mod-private key and restores it on unlink). Discovery of new anchors: SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfixes see every new ZDO with s_creator; classify by prefab hash sets built from ZNetScene.m_prefabs components (Sign, ItemStand, PrivateArea, Container). Registry keyed by rounded position. Arrival: a phantom (Option 1) 2–3 m from the anchor, or for (5) the player's real portal. Ownership check for who may register: s_creator on the anchor piece (profile UID) vs the emoting player's s_playerID; s_creatorIndex→ZNet.World.m_playerHistory gives the socket-verified PlatformUserID for stronger checks. Tick: poll sign/stand/container ZDOs in the registry every 2–5 s (cheap reads).
catalog.playerExperience: A player builds a sign at their outpost and writes `#tpl Mine`. Within 5 s a toast says `Destination 'Mine' registered`. At any hub portal they emote to cycle destinations; the hub's hover becomes `Portal tag:">Mine" [connected]`; walking in lands them 2 m from their sign, with a real portal standing there for the return trip. For the tagged-portal variant, the player's own portal at the mine shows `Portal tag:"@Mine"` and is simply connected to the hub — no extra objects appear. Placing a specific item on an item stand beside the hub switches the hub's destination instantly (toast confirms).
failureModes: Sign text is 50 chars and player-editable by anyone not ward-blocked; griefers can retarget by editing the sign — require s_author/s_creator to match the registrant.

Tagged-portal variant: the hub's tag and the player's tag must be byte-identical while linked, so the player's chosen name is temporarily overwritten; a third portal with the same literal tag can be orphaned/re-paired by vanilla — reserve the prefix.
Chest token consumption races the owning client (whole-ZDO revision clobber) — claim ownership at commit and skip when s_inUse.
Phantom placed 2 m from a sign inside a hut may be inside geometry.
prerequisites: SpawnGovernor hooks, ZdoInventoryIO, ContainerRegistry-style prefab classification
openQuestions: Does a client standing at a portal whose s_tag the server rewrote see the new hover text and connected state without a zone reload (expected yes: hover re-reads every frame, UpdatePortal every 0.5 s)?
Does a player's TextInput (pre-filled with the server-written tag) clamp and save back a truncated tag on cancel/confirm?
catalog.id: targeted-portals:Player-Placed Anchor (sign / item stand / ward / chest token / tagged portal)
corrections: ItemStand citation: the s_item attach write is ItemStand.UpdateAttach SERVER:131845 (also ItemDrop.SaveToZDO on the same ZDO); :131795 is RPC_DestroyAttachment writing 0.

s_creatorIndex is NOT a stronger/socket-verified check: Piece.SetCreator computes it on the placing CLIENT via ZNet.World.m_playerHistory.FindIndex (:136421) and writes it as a plain int; s_creator and the character's s_playerID are likewise client-written. The only socket-verified identity is the ZNetPeer itself (ZNet.GetPeer(long) :80492 / GetPeer(ZRpc) :80504). Drop the 'stronger checks' claim.

Ward permitted list as 'access list for who may target it' is enforceable only as 'who may RETARGET the hub' (a server-side decision at emote/selection time). Once the hub's connection points at the ward anchor, every vanilla client walking in goes there — there is no per-player transit gate (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143512-143540 checks only global keys and the local IsTeleportable).

Tagged-portal variant: both ends must carry the byte-identical s_tag (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100647 and the teardown predicate :100601 compare the raw string). The playerExperience text showing hub '>@Mine' and the mine portal '@Mine' simultaneously is impossible; pick one literal for both.

Tag writes from the server do not mark portals dirty for save: ZDO.Set(int,string) -> IncreaseDataRevision only calls SetDirtySector (:73721-73726, :73832-73840), and portals are only written to disk when DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77631). Mod tag writes must be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705) or they are lost at the next save.

Server writes to a ZDO owned by an online client (retagging a player's portal, consuming a chest token) race with that client: ZDO.Set bumps DataRevision without an owner check, but the receiving side discards any packet whose revision is <= its own (RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118) and only updates ownership when OwnerRevision is newer — a concurrent client write with the same revision number loses one side's data silently. Claim ownership first (ZDO.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) as Game.SetConnection does :100617-100621, or WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch), and expect ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76898-76924) to hand it back within 2 s while a player is nearby.
The 50-char sign limit is a client UI limit only (Sign.m_characterLimit :141756 passed to TextInput :141831); a modified client can write any length, so bound the parser.

Chest-token toll: Container.Load on the owning client re-reads only when DataRevision changed (:122304); if the chest is open (s_inUse) the owner's next Save overwrites the server's edit — 'skip if s_inUse' is necessary but the ownership race above still applies.

Every server-side portal tag write (variant 5 rewrite and hub retag) must be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals(): ZDO.Set(s_tag) only calls SetDirtySector for the regular chunk (S:73832-73840), while portal ZDOs are saved from the separate ChunkPortal list only when DirtyPortalObjects is true (S:77621-77635). Without it the tag reverts at the next save.

The ward permitted list can only gate RETARGETING (who may point a hub at this anchor). Passage is not per-player enforceable: TeleportWorld.Teleport (client C:144264-144296) checks only TargetFound/NoPortals/IsTeleportable; anyone at the linked hub travels. State this as client-open once linked.

Variant (5) tag literal: the client tag widget is capped at 10 chars (TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) C:144222), so the player-side reserved prefix must fit in 10 (e.g. '@'+9). Server-written literals are not length-capped and display fine on PC. On console/crossplay clients CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (C: FilterUGC) applies UGC gating when PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() is true; a server-written tag with an empty s_tagauthor may render as the '$ugc_text' placeholder there.

Variant (5): the player's portal is client-owned; the mod must SetOwner(sessionID) before SetConnection or the write path in Game.SetConnection round-trips through RPC_SetConnection on the owning client (S:100632-100655). ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76897-76924) will hand ownership back within 2 s; that is harmless because the connection data persists, but do not assume the server keeps ownership.

When the player later re-tags their portal, the owning client's RPC_SetTag clears its own connection and calls SetConnectedPortal on the hub; if the hub is server-owned that is an RPC to an owner with no ZNetView instance and is dropped in HandleRoutedRPC (S:83650-83668), so the hub keeps a stale connection until the 5 s pass tears it down (target tag mismatch). Mod must re-detect and re-link; expect up to ~10 s of '[unconnected]' on the hub.

Chest-token consumption: a server write to s_items bumps DataRevision without ownership (ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision S:73832); the owning client's next write carries an equal revision and is silently dropped in RPC_ZDOData (num4 <= DataRevision, S:77110-77118) until it receives the server copy. Only consume while s_inUse == 0 and expect a brief desync window if the chest is opened in the same second.

s_creatorIndex is written by the placing client from ITS copy of ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (S:136420); it is not socket-verified. The only socket-verified identity is the ZNetPeer of the emoting/placing connection (ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) S:80504); use s_creator (long) plus peer.m_playerID for ownership checks, and treat the index as a display-name hint only.

Sign/stand/chest detection is poll-only for content (s_text/s_item/s_items are set after the ZDO first arrives), so the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO/Deserialize postfix only discovers the piece; a 2-5 s poll is required for the payload as stated.
evidence: ZDO.Set(int,string) :73721-73726; IncreaseDataRevision :73832-73840; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals :76702-76705; portal save gate :77621-77631

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All five anchor sources are real server-readable ZDO fields written by the placing client: Sign.SetText claims ownership and writes s_text/s_author/s_authorDisplayName with no RPC (SERVER:141915-141928; Sign.Awake registers nothing, :141772-141781); ItemStand.UpdateAttach writes s_item = prefab-name hash (:131845, NOT :131795 which is RPC_DestroyAttachment writing 0); PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers/GetPermittedPlayers use s_permitted + "pu_id"+i / "pu_name"+i (:137338-137363); Container.Save writes s_items (:122294-122300) and UpdateUseVisual writes s_inUse (:121990-122000); Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator + s_creatorIndex on the owner (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12514-12517). Tagged-portal variant is consistent with Game.ConnectPortals: the pair is stable as long as both tags are equal and both connections non-None (:100601-100603). Route selection is server-owned so the enforcement label holds for 'which destination the hub points at'. But several sub-claims are wrong or overstated: identity verification, the access-list semantics, tag persistence, and write races on client-owned ZDOs.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] All five ZDO channels check out against the server decompile: Sign.SetText (client) does PrivateArea.CheckAccess, ClaimOwnership, then Set(s_text)/Set(s_author) with no RPC registered in Sign.Awake, so polling is the only way (S:141772-141781, S:141913-141928). ItemStand writes s_item = m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode() on attach and 0 on removal (S:ItemStand +370-371, S:131795). PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers/GetPermittedPlayers use s_permitted + pu_id{i}/pu_name{i} (S:137338-137363). Container.Save writes s_items bytes on the owner (S:122294-122300) and Container.Load skips while m_inUse (S:122302-122310). Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator/s_creatorIndex on the placing client (S:136415-136424, called from Player.PlacePiece S:12514-12517). Client-modified ZDOs reach the server distance-independently through m_clientChangeQueue in CreateSyncList (S:77212-77260). The reconciler predicate (S:100601) is target null / tag mismatch / target connection None with no reciprocity test, so variant (5) with identical literal tags on hub and player portal is literally a vanilla pair and is the only variant that needs no phantom and survives save/reload (RegenerateConnectionHashData + ZDOMan.ConnectPortals S:75461-75478, S:77850-77891). Enforcement is genuinely server-side for the ROUTE (the mod writes the connection field). What is NOT enforced: once a hub is linked to an anchor, every vanilla player at the hub can walk through; the ward permitted list only gates who may retarget the hub, not who may pass. Several details in howItWorks need fixing (below).

catalog.name: Map Ping → Destination, and Map-Pin Feedback
catalog.oneLine: The vanilla middle-click map ping is a free coordinate-bearing player→server channel: 'ping a spot, get a portal there', with saved map pins pushed back for every managed destination.
catalog.howItWorks: Input: Chat.SendPing invokes routed RPC "ChatMessage" to targetPeerID 0 with (Vector3 pos, int type=3 Ping, UserInfo, ""), always on the wire regardless of player count. Capture server-side with a Harmony prefix on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC comparing `data.m_methodHash == "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()`, snapshot `data.m_parameters.GetPos()`, read Vector3/int/UserInfo/string, restore the position (do not Register the name — Chat may already own it on a headless build). Map `data.m_senderPeerID` → ZNetPeer via ZNet.GetPeer (cross-check against the socket-derived peer for anti-spoof). Semantics: the ping's Y is the pinger's own Y, so recompute `h = WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x,z)`; validate (water/lava/slope/off-map); then either re-target the hub the pinger last stood near (within 10 m of a managed source, from ConnectedCharacters positions) or, if the player is standing inside a portal's activation range, that portal. Create/replace the phantom (Option 1; destroy-and-recreate on retarget) and tag `>Ping: <name>`. Debounce per player (one accepted ping per 10 s) and rate-limit, since pings are public and spammable. Feedback pins: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", label, (int)Minimap.PinType.Icon3, pos, showMap:false)` adds a SAVED, named pin on that vanilla client (dedup within 1 m of same name+type; no removal RPC exists). For the shared map, an ephemeral labelled marker for all players: fabricate a Shout ChatMessage with UserInfo.Name="Portal" and text=label at the destination (5 s animated pin + chat line). Also `Vegvisir`-style discovery: reuse RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse for each managed destination on login (PeerJoinLeaveHook). Tick cost: zero polling; one RPC prefix compare per routed packet.
catalog.playerExperience: The player opens the map and middle-clicks a spot on the Plains coast; every player sees the vanilla ping. Within a second a toast reads `Hub 'Harbour' now points to your ping (1.9 km)`; the hub portal's hover shows `Portal tag:">Ping: Rohan" [connected]`; a saved pin named `Portal: Ping` appears on their map at the spot. They walk in, 8 s swirl, and step out of a real portal at the pinged coordinate. On login, players receive saved pins for every fixed destination (`Portal: Spawn`, `Portal: Haldor`) with the `$msg_pin_added` toast for each.
failureModes: Pings are public: every player sees the gesture and can spam; without debounce the hub thrashes.
Pinged spot underwater/off-map: rejected with a toast; the player must ping again.
Saved pins cannot be removed by the server; a renamed destination leaves the old pin behind — keep pin names stable (`Portal: Harbour`) and change only the tag.
Registering "ChatMessage" via ZRoutedRpc.Register throws if Chat exists headless — use the HandleRoutedRPC prefix.
openQuestions: Is Chat.instance non-null on the dedicated server (decides Register vs prefix)?
Does RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse render identically on PlayFab/crossplay clients?
catalog.id: targeted-portals:Map Ping → Destination, and Map-Pin Feedback
corrections: Anti-spoof cross-check cannot be done in a HandleRoutedRPC prefix: that method receives only RoutedRPCData (:83645) and has no socket in scope. Cross-check m_senderPeerID against the actual connection in a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:83632) using ZNet's private GetPeer(ZRpc) (:80504); vanilla never validates m_senderPeerID anywhere on that path.

RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse has a side effect the option omits: when the map is closed it calls Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f) (:100826-100829), forcibly turning the player's view toward the pin. Pushing N pins on login yanks the camera N times; batch them or push while the map is likely open.

Fabricated Shout: OnNewChatMessage first runs RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync(sender.UserId, Permission.CommunicateWithUsingText, ...) (:41783) unless senderID == the local character's UserID; a made-up UserInfo.UserId's result on Steam/PlayFab backends is unverified from the decompile. Also world texts are keyed by senderID (FindExistingWorldText :41926-41936), so every server-fabricated message with the server's m_senderPeerID overwrites the previous one — at most one live server marker per fake sender id. Text has '<' and '>' replaced with spaces (:41796-41797) and Shout text is upper-cased (:41893-41894).
Ping pins are labelled 'Name: PING' by the client (AddInworldText :41898-41900; Minimap.UpdatePingPins CLIENT:57652-57668) — the ping itself cannot carry a custom label; only the Shout variant can.
Minor: the ping is also visible to every other player and there is no client-side rate limit; the server-side debounce is mandatory, not optional.

Anti-spoof: HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData) has no socket; m_senderPeerID is a packet field written by the sender. Hook RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (S:83632-83643) instead and resolve the true peer with ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) (private, S:80504); or hook HandleRoutedRPC only for the payload and accept that identity is the unverified m_senderPeerID. Also skip data.m_senderPeerID == server m_id to ignore the mod's own broadcasts.

Fabricated Shout: Chat.OnNewChatMessage on a vanilla client runs RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync(sender.UserId, ...) for any senderID != its own LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID (C:41775-41816). CheckPermissionAsync returns Error when !user.IsValid (C:88643-88650) and the message is discarded (result not granted). UserInfo.Name="Portal" with a default/empty UserId will never render. Fix: send per peer with UserInfo.UserId = that recipient's own PlatformUserID (short-circuits to Granted at C:88651-88655), or craft the RoutedRPCData with m_senderPeerID = the recipient's own peer uid so the senderID == LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID branch grants immediately. On PlayFab/console clients a fake ID goes to RelationsProvider.GetUserProfileAsync and fails.

Shout rendering details: text is upper-cased and the pin/world text reads 'Name: TEXT' (C:41892-41895, C:41916-41924); '<' and '>' are stripped (C:41798-41799); the shout also lands in the chat log (AddString). WorldTextInstance is keyed by senderID (FindExistingWorldText C:41926-41935), so consecutive server shouts from the same senderID replace each other rather than stack; pin lifetime is m_worldTextTTL = 5 s (C:41589).

Login pin push: Minimap.DiscoverLocation returns false silently when Player.m_localPlayer == null (C:58396-58399). PeerJoinLeaveHook fires before the character exists; delay the RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse burst until the peer's character ZDO is present (ConnectedCharacters). Pins the player deletes are re-added on every login (no removal RPC; dedup only against existing pins).
The ping Vector3 arrives with y = pinger's own y (S:42062-42063), as stated; recompute with WorldGenerator.GetHeight — do not use any ZoneSystem collider query on the server.
Phantom retag after ping: portal tag writes must call ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() or the tag is lost at the next save (S:77621-77635).

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The input channel is exactly as described: Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick -> Chat.instance.SendPing (CLIENT:58580-58584, also OnMapDblClick :58538-58548) -> InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", pos(y=player y), 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "") (SERVER:42058-42068). targetPeerID 0 makes the server both HandleRoutedRPC it and RouteRPC it to everyone (ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC :83632-83643); HandleRoutedRPC :83645-83663 dispatches on m_methodHash with m_parameters as a ZPackage, so a prefix can peek and rewind. Feedback: Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse is registered unconditionally (:100068) and calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation(pos,type,name,showMap) which AddPin(save:true) unless HaveSimilarPin (same name+type+save, <1 m XZ) (CLIENT:58394-58432); no network path calls Minimap.RemovePin (all callers are local console/UI). Shout fabrication renders via OnNewChatMessage -> AddInworldText -> Minimap.UpdateShoutPins as a 5 s animated pin (m_worldTextTTL :41589). Route retargeting is a server-owned connection write, so the enforcement label holds. Corrections concern the anti-spoof hook location, an unmentioned camera side-effect, and the fabricated-shout path.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Input side holds: Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick -> Chat.SendPing (C:58580-58584) -> InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", pos(y = pinger y), 3 /*Talker.Type.Ping*/, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "") (S:42058-42068, Talker.Type enum S: Whisper/Normal/Shout/Ping). On the server ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC calls HandleRoutedRPC for targetPeerID 0 regardless of whether 'ChatMessage' is registered, then RouteRPC forwards to all other peers (S:83632-83668, S:83597-83625), so a Harmony prefix on HandleRoutedRPC sees every ping and the vanilla broadcast is unaffected. Feedback side holds: Game.Start registers RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse on both sides (S:100067) and the client handler calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation(pos, type, name, showMap) which adds a SAVED pin with a '$msg_pin_added' toast and dedups by name+type+save within 1 m XZ (C:58394-58432); PinType.Icon3 is valid (C:56139). Wonderland already ships this exact push (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263). ZRoutedRpc.Register uses Dictionary.Add, so re-registering 'ChatMessage' would throw if Chat exists (S:83680-83716) — the prefix approach is correct. Route retargeting is server-owned, so server-enforced holds. Three claims are wrong or incomplete: the anti-spoof cross-check cannot be done at HandleRoutedRPC, the fabricated Shout will be DROPPED by vanilla clients unless its UserInfo carries a valid PlatformUserID that passes RelationsManager, and the login pin push has a timing hazard.

catalog.name: Last Place the Portal's Builder Stood
catalog.oneLine: A 'retreat' portal that follows its builder's last known position (or last position before logout), tracked live from the character ZDO and keyed by the portal's s_creator.
catalog.howItWorks: Builder identity: every player-placed portal carries `ZDOVars.s_creator` (long profile UID, written by Piece.SetCreator on the placing client) — read `portalZdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)`. Position tracking: on a 1–3 s tick (PositionWatch already samples this) record `playerId → (pos, time)` from ConnectedCharacters; on disconnect (PeerJoinLeaveHook prefix on ZNet.Disconnect) the last sample IS the logout point (the real logout point is client-only, but the last server sample is within 2 s of it). Persist to the position-keyed mod file so it survives restarts. Variants: (a) live — the destination anchor (Option 2, invisible, movable) is re-positioned to the builder's last-sampled position every tick while they are online and frozen at logout; (b) 'last stood before building' — capture the builder's position at the moment the portal ZDO arrives (SpawnGovernor Deserialize postfix: s_creator known → look up that player's current character position) and pin the phantom there forever — a 'way back' portal to wherever you were when you built this. Safety: reject samples with s_dead, InInterior, water (GetHeight<30), or while s_inBed. Tag: `>Back to Rohan`. Because Option 2 anchors can be moved with SetPosition (non-portal prefab), variant (a) costs one SetPosition + ForceSendZDO per tick per portal only while the builder actually moves (skip if delta <1 m).
catalog.playerExperience: Rohan builds a portal at the swamp edge; its hover immediately reads `Portal tag:">Back to Rohan" [connected]` and glows. Anyone walking in lands 2 m behind wherever Rohan currently is (or where he was standing when he logged out) — with nothing there to walk back into. In variant (b) it lands at the meadow where Rohan stood when he placed the portal, permanently.
failureModes: Anchor is invisible: one-way trip unless paired with a return mechanism.
8 s snapshot: a running builder is up to ~60 m from the arrival point.
Builder never seen online since the mod was installed: no sample → portal left unconnected with tag `>Back (unknown)`.
s_creator==0 on pre-mod or admin-spawned portals (Piece.SetCreator only writes when creator was 0 and owner) — skip those.
openQuestions: Reliability of s_creator population on player-placed portals in 1.0.7 (dump s_creator on a freshly placed portal).
catalog.id: targeted-portals:Last Place the Portal's Builder Stood
corrections: PlayerProfile citation range is wrong: SetLogoutPoint is :106173, HaveLogoutPoint :106204, GetLogoutPoint :106209 (106180-106253 spans SetDeathPoint/SetMapData etc.).
s_creator is client-written and unverifiable server-side (a modified client can place with any UID); acceptable for a convenience feature but do not describe it as a trust anchor.

Variant (a) is a moving destination and needs the full Moving-Target discipline: re-claim ownership before every SetPosition (InternalSetPosition skips the revision bump when not owner :73739-73742, and AddForceSendZdos drops force-sends that fail ShouldSend :77263-77275), ForceSendZDO to peers near the SOURCE portal, and the anchor must be a non-portal prefab (ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs :73752-73756).

'Hover immediately reads connected' only once the server has written the source's connection and the client has received that ZDO update (TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal polls HaveTarget every 0.5 s :143489-143507); 5 s worst case, not immediate.
The arrival is 'position + rot*forward*1 + up' of the anchor (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143533-143537); '2 m behind' requires the mod to set the anchor rotation/offset itself.

Variant (a) needs the full Moving-Target engine: each tick `a.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); a.SetPosition(p); a.SetRotation(r);` (SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision S:74627-74634; SetRotation bumps DataRevision unconditionally S:73782-73787) and `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, a.m_uid)` for every peer within activation range of the SOURCE portal, because TeleportWorld.TargetFound requests the target ZDO only while it is missing (C:144380-144396) and a distant anchor is never in that peer's sector sync list (CreateSyncList S:77212-77240).

Variant (b) is degenerate: the placing player is within m_maxPlaceDistance = 5 m of the portal when Piece.SetCreator runs, so the captured position is beside the new portal. Drop it or redefine it as 'position N seconds before placement' from the sampler history.

Logout point: the server never sees PlayerProfile.GetLogoutPoint (client-only, S:106180-106253); the last PositionWatch sample (<=3 s old) is the only data. State it as an approximation and reject samples flagged s_dead/s_inBed (S:78403, S:78457) as written.
Tag `>Back to Rohan` (14 chars) is a server write; call ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() after writing s_tag on the source portal or the tag is lost at the next save (S:77621-77635).

Anchor rotation drives the exit vector (Teleport: pos + rot*forward*m_exitDistance + up, C:144287-144292); set the anchor rotation to the builder's facing or the traveller may exit into whatever the builder is facing.

Position source: the character ZDO behind ZNetPeer.m_characterID (Wonderland ConnectedCharacters.cs:57-79) is kept fresh by the owning client's ZSyncTransform, which keeps writing even during teleport (OwnerSync has no IsTeleporting gate, :87352ff). Logout point is profile-local (PlayerProfile.SetLogoutPoint/GetLogoutPoint :106173/:106209, used only by Game :100317-100319) so the last server sample is the only server-side approximation; a ZNet.Disconnect prefix (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:48-57) runs before ZDOMan.RemovePeer -> RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS destroys the character ZDO (:76775-76783, :77406-77418), so the ZDO is still readable there. Moving the anchor via ZDO.SetPosition bumps DataRevision only when IsOwner() (:73734-73745) and ForceSendZDO(long,ZDOID) exists (:77714). Variant (b) is sound: the portal ZDO arrives at the server with s_creator already set (CreateNewZDO+Deserialize in RPC_ZDOData :77120-77128) while the builder's character ZDO is at the build spot. Destination is a server-owned connection, so the label holds; variant (a) inherits every Moving-Target caveat.

[vanilla-reality:downgraded] Builder identity is real: Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator on the placing client and it reaches the server (S:136415-136424, S:12514-12517). ZNet.Disconnect is patchable (S:80015). Character ZDO positions are visible server-side. The route is server-owned so enforcement is honest. But the option's own tracking mechanics are wrong for variant (a) and variant (b) is pointless: (a) says 'one SetPosition + ForceSendZDO per tick'. The anchor sits AT the builder, so ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76897-76924, every 2 s) hands its ownership to the builder's client (server-owned ZDOs fail IsInPeerActiveArea because the server refPos is never near anyone); ZDO.InternalSetPosition then does not bump DataRevision (S:73734-73745), AddForceSendZdos drops the ZDO when ShouldSend is false (S:77262-77283, S:76003-76015), and the traveller's client keeps a stale copy. The option must adopt the Moving-Target engine rules verbatim (SetOwner each tick or a SetOwner prefix; per-peer ForceSendZDO to peers near the SOURCE hub). (b) 'where the builder stood when placing' is always within Player.m_maxPlaceDistance = 5 m of the portal itself (C:9574), so the 'way back' lands next to the portal that was just built — not a meaningful destination. Feasibility downgraded to feasible-with-caveats.

catalog.name: Geometric Centre of a Base
catalog.oneLine: Portal to the centroid of a player's build cluster, computed from the s_creator field on every piece ZDO and snapped to the nearest bed/floor.
catalog.howItWorks: Data: every player-placed piece ZDO carries `ZDOVars.s_creator` (profile UID). Enumeration: there is no per-player index, so run a whole-map sweep — ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper over the hash set of all prefabs with a Piece component (built once from ZNetScene.m_prefabs), or cheaper, `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, ZDOVars.s_creator)` once at boot (full scan of all long fields; cache the result) and then maintain incrementally via SpawnGovernor's CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfixes and ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed. Clustering: bucket each player's pieces by 64 m zone (ZoneSystem.GetZone(pos)); flood-fill adjacent zones into clusters; the 'base' is the cluster with the most pieces (or the one containing their claimed bed from Option 10, or their most recently placed piece). Centre: mean XZ of the cluster's piece positions; height from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` is wrong inside a raised base — instead take the median y of floor-ish pieces (prefabs whose name contains 'floor' or the bed) within 5 m of the centroid, +0.3. Structure clearance: without colliders, pick the candidate cell (2 m grid over the cluster bbox) with the fewest piece ZDOs within 1.5 m in XZ and the smallest |y − medianFloorY| — heuristic, but the client's FindFloor (piece layer included) will land the player on whatever floor is under the arrival point, and the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback guarantees a landing. Phantom (Option 1) at that cell, tag `>Base: Rohan`. Recompute on a slow schedule (every 5 min or on N new pieces) and re-target with destroy-and-recreate only when the centre moves >8 m and no player is within 100 m of the old phantom (avoids pops).
catalog.playerExperience: At the `>Base` hub the player emotes; toast `Base found: 312 pieces near (−1240, 860)`; hover `Portal tag:">Base: Rohan" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrival inside the base compound, hopefully in the courtyard, with a real portal now standing there. If the arrival cell was inside a wall, the player pops onto the roof or floor per the client's floor search and the phantom mesh may clip a wall — the mod offers a 'nudge' emote that re-samples another cell.
failureModes: Piece-density heuristics cannot see walls/roofs; expect occasional arrivals on rooftops or in closets.
GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Long, s_creator) on a big world is a heavy one-shot scan (seconds) — do it once, off the hot path.
Pieces with s_creator==0 (older than the field or admin-built) are invisible to clustering.
Placing a phantom portal inside a ward zone: the ward blocks players from hammer-removing it, which is good, but it also lets the ward owner's permitted list decide who can retag it (client-side).
prerequisites: PrefabSetSweeper or GetAllZDOIDsWithHash boot index + SpawnGovernor incremental hooks
openQuestions: Wall-clock cost of a full s_creator scan on a mature world.
Which piece prefab names reliably denote floors (for the median-floor height heuristic)?
corrections: Remove 'the client's FindFloor ... will land the player on whatever floor is under the arrival point': FindFloor does not move the player (UpdateTeleport :15342-15359 sets position = m_teleportTargetPos and only ends the teleport when FindFloor returns true).

Remove 'the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback guarantees a landing': GetSolidHeight raycasts from p.y+1000 downward (body after :15367) and would return the top of the base, and it is reached only when FindFloor found nothing within 1000 m below — practically never over land because terrain is in m_solidRayMask (:113424).

Height selection must be done entirely server-side from ZDO positions (floor/bed piece y + ~0.3, plus the +1 m the client adds in TeleportWorld.Teleport :143536). Treat as a heuristic that needs in-game verification, and provide the 'nudge' re-sample as a first-class feature, not an afterthought.

ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, s_creator) also returns non-Piece ZDOs if any other component writes 'creator'; filter by prefab hash set from ZNetScene.m_prefabs as the option already suggests for the sweeper.

Arrival height: the client lands at EXACTLY m_teleportTargetPos.y; FindFloor only gates completion (S:15353-15359 vs C: FindFloor returns hit height that UpdateTeleport ignores). Pick y from an actual floor-ish piece's ZDO position (+0.3) directly under the chosen cell, never from a median across the cluster, or the player arrives inside/under geometry. The 15 s fallback uses GetSolidHeight from +1000 m and therefore lands on the roof of a covered base.

Phantom survival: portal prefabs carry WearNTear with m_noSupportWear = true; an unsupported (floating or overlapping nothing supporting) phantom takes 100 damage per wear tick on the nearest client and is destroyed. Place the phantom so its collider bounds overlap terrain or a supporting piece (put it on a floor piece's exact y), or use the Invisible Anchor (non-piece prefab) for the arrival point and keep the return portal elsewhere.

Structure clearance heuristic cannot see colliders; expect the phantom mesh to clip walls as the option admits. The 'nudge' emote should re-sample AND re-create (destroy-and-recreate, since portal-prefab ZDOs cannot be moved: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for PortalPrefabHash S:73752-73756).
Any hub retag (`>Base: Rohan`) requires ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() to persist (S:77621-77635).

Incremental index: ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed fires from HandleDestroyedZDO (S:76963-76975) for every destroyed ZDO including non-pieces; filter by presence in the creator index rather than by prefab to keep it cheap.

verifierReasoning: [decompile:downgraded] Enumeration and clustering are sound: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, hash) is public and does a full scan of s_longs (SERVER:75390-75407, :75707-75722), ZoneSystem.GetZone is pure math (:115741-115746), ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed exists (:76033), and PrefabSetSweeper walks m_objectsBySector (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135-160). The load-bearing arrival claim is wrong, though: Player.UpdateTeleport places the player at exactly m_teleportTargetPos every frame after 2 s (:15342-15343) and uses ZoneSystem.FindFloor only as the 'done' predicate — FindFloor raycasts 1000 m straight down from p+1 on m_solidRayMask which includes 'terrain' (:113424; FindFloor body), so it succeeds essentially anywhere over land and never adjusts the player's y. The 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (raycast from +1000 m down, i.e. it returns the ROOF height of a base) only fires if nothing at all is below the point. A wrong y therefore lands the traveller inside or under geometry with no client-side correction; the phantom/anchor y must be right server-side, and the server has no colliders to compute it (reviewer note: collider-based ZoneSystem is dead server-side). The median-floor-y heuristic is unverified and the option's own text admits arrival 'hopefully in the courtyard'. Route targeting remains server-owned.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Data path is sound: s_creator is a long on every player-placed piece (S:136415-136424); ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, hash) is a full linear scan over s_longs (S:75390-75407, S:75707-75722) — acceptable once at boot; ZoneSystem.GetZone is pure math (S:115741-115746); ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed exists (S:76033). Route selection is server-owned. The client landing claims are wrong, though: Player.UpdateTeleport (S:15337-15378) sets transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos at t>2 s and, when ZoneSystem.FindFloor succeeds (any collider on m_solidRayMask within 1000 m below p+1, C: FindFloor), simply ends the teleport WITHOUT using the returned height — the player stays at exactly the target y. Only the 15 s fallback re-heights, and GetSolidHeight casts from +1000 m so it returns the topmost surface (a roof). So a wrong median-floor y puts the player under the floor/in the crawlspace, not 'on whatever floor is under the arrival point'. Additionally the phantom is a real portal piece with WearNTear.m_noSupportWear = true (C:149945): if the server places it floating (courtyard height estimate off, or over a floor piece it does not overlap), the nearest client's WearNTear.UpdateWear applies 100 damage per wear tick until it is destroyed (C:150445-150451, support = OverlapBox against terrain/supporting pieces C:150742-150800). Feasible-with-caveats stands; corrections required.

catalog.name: Moving Target Updated on a Tick (general engine)
catalog.oneLine: A destination that tracks a moving thing every tick: only non-portal anchor ZDOs can be moved; phantom portals must be destroyed and recreated; and every moving destination needs per-cycle ForceSendZDO to stay fresh on clients.
catalog.howItWorks: Rules from the ZDO layer: (1) `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in Game.PortalPrefabHash, so a phantom portal that is SetPosition'ed stays filed under its creation sector in m_portalObjects — normal sector sync stops reaching its new location and HandleDestroyedZDO leaks the entry; on the client, AddIfPortal re-adds it under the new sector without removing the old one (unbounded duplicate growth). Therefore a moving destination must be an Invisible Anchor (Option 2, non-portal prefab) — SetPosition on it goes through SetSector normally. (2) `ZDO.InternalSetPosition` bumps DataRevision only when `IsOwner()`, and ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS re-assigns ownership of persistent ZDOs inside any peer's active area every 2 s; so each tick: `a.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); a.SetPosition(p); a.SetRotation(r);` (or hold ownership with a ZDO.SetOwner prefix keyed on the TPL_anchor int, WaterBuoyancyEngine pattern). (3) Clients fetch a distant destination ZDO once (TargetFound→RequestZDO) and never re-request; ShouldSend is revision-gated but only for ZDOs in the peer's sync list (sector-based) — so for every peer within ~20 m of the SOURCE portal call `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, a.m_uid)` on each tick the anchor moved (skip when delta <0.5 m). (4) SendZDOs has no delta encoding: each push is ~80–120 bytes; at 2 Hz for 5 peers and 3 moving anchors ≈ 3 KB/s total — trivial. (5) Tick rate: 0.5–2 s is plenty because the arrival is an 8-second-old snapshot anyway. Sources of motion: ship ZDO position (Option 13), character ZDO position (Options 14/17), a Vagon, a tamed creature's ZDO (Tameable s_tamedName, s_follow), a Leviathan (unstable, self-destructs), or a scripted patrol path from config. Reconciler: the anchor is not in GetPortalList so vanilla never touches it; the source's link survives as long as the anchor exists, its s_tag matches, and its reciprocal Portal connection stays non-None (write it once at creation). Persistence: anchor position at save time is whatever it was; at load, the maintenance tick resumes tracking. If the tracked thing disappears, freeze the anchor at its last position and retag `>… (lost)`, or reap it.
catalog.playerExperience: Hover shows e.g. `Portal tag:">Longship" [connected]` and the glow stays on. Walking in gives the 8 s swirl and drops the traveller where the tracked object was ~8 s before transit — beside a slow cart, or in the wake of a sailing ship. Nothing visible exists at the arrival point; there is no way back through it. If the object was destroyed while they were mid-swirl, they still arrive at its last coordinate.
failureModes: 8-second stale snapshot is intrinsic to Player.UpdateTeleport; fast targets are always missed.
Forgetting per-tick SetOwner makes every SetPosition a silent no-op on the wire.
Forgetting per-peer ForceSendZDO leaves the traveller's client holding the position from their first approach.
Using a portal prefab for the moving end corrupts the portal registry on both server and clients.

catalog.id: targeted-portals:Moving Target Updated on a Tick (general engine)
corrections: Force-send is revision-gated too: AddForceSendZdos only keeps ids where peer.ShouldSend(zdo) is true (:77263-77285; ShouldSend :76003-76015). So the per-tick SetOwner(GetSessionID()) is mandatory, not an optimisation — a SetPosition on a client-owned anchor bumps nothing and the ForceSendZDO is silently discarded.

Sector crossings have a side effect: server-side SetSector calls ZDOMan.ZDOSectorInvalidated (:73763-73766) which, for every peer that holds the ZDO but is not in its new active area, queues an invalidate and removes it from peer.m_zdos (:75989-75995, sent in SendZDOs :77028-77036). The client then parks it in sector zero (client ZDO.InvalidateSector) but keeps it, so TargetFound still succeeds; the next force-send re-sends it in full because the peer entry is gone. Harmless but it means the anchor is re-sent whole on every 64 m boundary crossing.

A NON-persistent anchor is exempt from ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76910-76913) and would keep server ownership, but RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS (:77406-77418) only spares it while its owner is a connected peer or the server session; it is never saved, so the source's connection dangles after a restart until the mod recreates it. State explicitly which choice is made.

The anchor prefab must not carry ZSyncTransform/Rigidbody: while a nearby client owns it (2 s windows between reclaims) that client's ZNetScene instantiates it and would write its own position back (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87352ff). This is Option 2's prefab choice, but it is load-bearing here.

Save-time hash pairing requires both ZDOs to exist and the target's connection to point back (RegenerateConnectionHashData null checks :75468); a one-way anchor (connection None or to itself) is not restored as the source's target after load.

ZDO.SetRotation bumps DataRevision unconditionally (S:73782-73787), so a tick that changes rotation will pass ShouldSend even without ownership; ownership is still required because the position write itself is owner-gated and because the owning client would otherwise win any write race. Keep SetOwner each tick as written.

Each SetOwner increments OwnerRevision and the anchor ping-pongs between server and the nearest peer every ~2 s (ReleaseNearbyZDOS); this is benign but adds an OwnerRevision-only resend to every peer that holds the ZDO. The SetOwner-prefix variant avoids the churn.
Client-side duplicate growth in m_portalObjects for a MOVED portal-prefab is one stale entry per distinct sector visited, not per update — still a reason never to move phantoms.

Save survival requires the anchor to be Persistent AND carry a prefab hash the save path accepts (CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) sets neither Persistent nor validates the hash, S:76674-76694); the option's 'Persistence' sentence should say this explicitly.

On the traveller's client the moved anchor is only as fresh as the last force-send it received; TargetFound never re-requests once the copy exists, so a peer that entered the source's activation range between ticks may hold a copy older than one tick — send a force-send on first sight of a new nearby peer, not only when delta >0.5 m.
