verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every ZDO-layer rule checks out. (1) ZDO.SetSector returns early for any prefab in Game.PortalPrefabHash (SERVER:73752-73756); portals are filed only in m_portalObjects keyed by sector (AddIfPortal :77732-77751 even removes them from m_objectsBySector), GetSectorIndex is computed from m_position (:73776-73779), so after a SetPosition the server's bucket is stale, FindObjects for the new sector misses it (:77367-77381), HandleDestroyedZDO's TryGetValue(new sector) fails and leaks the entry (:76980-76986), and on a client RPC_ZDOData->AddIfPortal adds a second entry under the new sector without removing the old (:77128, :77738-77749). (2) InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only when IsOwner() (:73734-73745); ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns any Persistent ZDO in a peer's active area away from an owner that is not itself in that area — the server's ref pos never is (:76898-76924, :76884-76896). (3) TeleportWorld.TargetFound calls RequestZDO only when GetZDO is null (:143640-143658); RPC_RequestZDO is a one-shot ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692); CreateSyncList is sector-based + force list (:77212-77240). (4) SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO each time (:77053-77062). Persistence as a reciprocal pair survives save/load: RegenerateConnectionHashData writes one hash slot per ZDO (:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals re-pairs Portal with Portal|Target by hash (:77856-77887) — works for any prefab, not only portals. Two omissions need adding.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every rule in the option checks out. (1) ZDO.SetSector returns immediately for Game.PortalPrefabHash prefabs (S:73752-73756) while ZDO.GetSectorIndex is computed from m_position (S:73776-73779), so a moved portal-prefab ZDO stays filed under its creation key in m_portalObjects; FindObjects reads m_portalObjects by the peer's sector (S:77367-77381) so sync stops reaching the new location; HandleDestroyedZDO looks the entry up by the CURRENT position-derived index (S:76974-76986) and leaks the old bucket; client RPC_ZDOData -> AddIfPortal adds under the new index without removing the old (S:77126, S:77732-77750). (2) InternalSetPosition bumps DataRevision only when IsOwner (S:73734-73745); ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns persistent ZDOs in any peer's active area every 2 s (S:76872-76924) and the server never counts as 'in area' (refPos far away), so per-tick SetOwner (bumps OwnerRevision S:74627-74634) is required; WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch exists as the prefix pattern (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313). (3) TeleportWorld.TargetFound calls RequestZDO only while the target is missing (C:144380-144396); RPC_RequestZDO just does GetPeer(sender).ForceSendZDO(id) (S:77689-77692); CreateSyncList is sector-based plus m_forceSend (S:77212-77240, S:77262-77283); ShouldSend is revision-gated but also returns true when the peer's m_zdos has no entry (S:76003-76015), and ZDOSectorInvalidated removes the entry for peers outside the new sector (S:75990-75997), so the per-peer ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) (S:77714-77725) does deliver. (4) SendZDOs writes uid/revisions/owner/position + full Serialize with no delta (S:77053-77068). (5) Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos at TeleportTo time (S:15302-15327) and Teleport() reads the client's copy of the target ZDO (C:144287-144292), so arrival is the last-received snapshot. Reconciler: the anchor is never in GetPortalList (only PortalPrefabHash enters m_portalObjects S:77732-77750); the source's predicate (S:100601) only needs the anchor's tag equal and its Portal connection non-None. Save/reload: RegenerateConnectionHashData assigns hashes per connection without any prefab check (S:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load restores by hash (S:77850-77891), so a pairwise hub<->anchor link survives a save provided the anchor is Persistent with a saveable prefab hash. Minor precision notes only.

catalog.name: Two-Hop Relay: Phantom Landing Pad + RPC_TeleportPlayer
catalog.oneLine: The portal leads to a fixed phantom 'lobby'; on arrival the server force-teleports the player to the real target via RPC_TeleportPlayer — enabling per-player destinations from one portal, live-position targets, and rule enforcement the ZDO layer cannot express.
catalog.howItWorks: Stage 1: source portal ↔ one phantom (Option 1) placed somewhere harmless (e.g. 30 m from the hub, or an isolated 'transit island' the mod picks with WorldGenerator on a small islet), tag `>Anywhere`. Stage 2: the server detects arrival — PositionWatch already samples every character at 3 s; tighten to 0.5 s for players within 15 m of any managed phantom, and treat `distance(characterPos, phantomPos) < 3 m && previous sample > 40 m away` as an arrival (or simpler: any character within 3 m of a pad). Resolve that player's selected destination (set earlier via emote/ping/sign; keyed by s_playerID), validate it (Option 3 rules, plus `!s_dead`, `!s_inBed`), then `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (or the ZDO-scoped `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)`). Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer runs `Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo` with no checks — but Player.TeleportTo returns false (silently) if `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, and the cooldown only accrues while NOT teleporting: the player just finished an 8 s portal transit, so the mod must wait ≥2 s after the arrival sample before sending (poll their ZDO position: it changes at t≈2 s of the first teleport; arrival completes at t≥8 s). Confirmation is a position poll ~2 s after the RPC (no ack exists). distantTeleport:true guarantees a landing (15 s fallback to GetSolidHeight+0.5); it also gives the portal swirl. For live targets (moving ship, another player) recompute pos at send time — the traveller lands where the target was ~2–8 s before completion, far better than the ZDO route's 8 s + stale copy. Rules: this is where the mod can enforce anything it likes (tolls via chest tokens, group/ward permission, cooldowns, biome locks) because the second hop is fully server-initiated; the vanilla ore/metal check is NOT applied on hop 2 (server cannot see inventory) — hop 1 through the real portal already applied it, so cargo rules still hold. Return trip: a second phantom pad at the destination is optional; without it the return is a chat-less emote command or a normal portal.
catalog.playerExperience: The player picks a destination at the hub with an emote (toasts cycle `Destination: Haldor`), walks in, sees the 8 s swirl and appears on a small transit island next to a portal. About 2–3 s later — before they can do more than look around — a second swirl starts unprompted and after ~8 s they are standing outside Haldor's camp. Total ~20 s of black screen across two hops. A toast at the pad says `Relaying to Haldor…`. If they had no destination selected, the pad simply is the destination and a toast says `Choose a destination with /wave`.
failureModes: Two black screens (~18–20 s) instead of one.
If the second RPC is sent inside the cooldown window it is silently dropped; the player is stranded on the pad until the mod retries (must retry at 1 s intervals until the position moves).
A dead/sleeping/attached player at the pad cannot be teleported (UpdateTeleport skipped for dead; UpdateAttach fights it) — check s_dead/s_inBed first.
RPC_TeleportPlayer is unauthenticated: any client can already use it; the mod should drop client-originated RPC_TeleportPlayer packets in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix so only the server relays.
Detection is a heuristic on 0.5 s samples; a player who walks 3 m away from the pad within half a second could be missed — use 'within 3 m at any sample after being >40 m away'.
prerequisites: Optional RPC_RoutedRPC prefix to veto client-originated RPC_TeleportPlayer

catalog.id: targeted-portals:Two-Hop Relay: Phantom Landing Pad + RPC_TeleportPlayer
corrections: Timing: the character ZDO position snaps to the pad at t≈2 s of hop 1 (UpdateTeleport :15336-15343; ZSyncTransform keeps syncing during teleport), but m_teleporting stays true until t≥8 s for distantTeleport (:15352) and up to 15 s (:15359), and m_teleportCooldown only starts accruing after that (:15329-15334). Earliest hop-2 RPC that will not be silently refused is therefore ≥8 s after the observed position snap (≥15 s worst case), not '≥2 s after the arrival sample'. m_teleporting is a private, unsynced field, so the server must send-and-verify: send at ~8 s, poll the character ZDO, resend at intervals until the position leaves the pad.

The 'PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit' heuristic (Wonderland PositionWatch.cs:148) matches on GetPortals() buckets, which are stale for any portal moved via SetPosition (ZDO.SetSector early return :73752-73756) — keep pads stationary or key detection on the mod's own pad registry.

Chat is not instantiated on the dedicated server, so ZRoutedRpc has no local "RPC_TeleportPlayer" handler there; that is fine for invoking, but a RPC_RoutedRPC veto prefix must key on the method hash, not on m_functions.

PlayerExperience: the 'second swirl' is the client's IsTeleporting loading screen (ZNetScene.InLoadingScreen :82084-82090); total black-screen time is ≥16 s plus the ≥8 s wait, i.e. closer to 25-30 s than 20 s.

Timing: the character ZDO position jumps to the pad at t~2 s of hop 1 (UpdateTeleport sets transform at m_teleportTimer > 2, S:15342-15346), but hop 1 stays in IsTeleporting until t >= 8 s (distant) or up to 15 s, and TeleportTo then needs m_teleportCooldown >= 2 s of NON-teleporting time. An RPC sent 2 s after the arrival sample is dropped silently. Send no earlier than ~10 s after the position jump, and retry every 2 s until the position leaves the pad (there is no ack). Realistic experience: ~8 s hop 1, 2-3 s standing on the pad, ~8 s hop 2; the 'second swirl starts 2-3 s after arrival' wording is right only with the corrected wait.

Arrival heuristic: 'any character within 3 m of a pad' relays anyone who WALKS or sails to the pad, bypassing the client-side ore check that only ran in TeleportWorld.Teleport (C:144264-144296). A pad 30 m from the hub is trivially walkable. Require the transit signature (previous sample > 40 m away and delta consistent with a portal jump, PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit-style) and/or an isolated islet, and treat a within-3-m-without-jump as 'no relay'.

Multiple hubs sharing one pad is fan-in: runtime-stable (no reciprocity check S:100601) but the on-disk format keeps one connection slot per ZDO (RegenerateConnectionHashData S:75461-75478), so after a save/reload only one hub stays paired with the pad. Use one pad per hub or re-link at boot.

RPC_TeleportPlayer is accepted from ANY peer by every vanilla client (no sender check in Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer); the optional RPC_RoutedRPC prefix veto (S:83632-83643) should be treated as required if the mod advertises the relay, since the same channel lets any client yank any other player.

The pad phantom must be a persistent portal-prefab ZDO connected pairwise to its hub for the vanilla return trip to work (client TargetFound/Teleport only need the connection field and a fetched target ZDO); retag writes need ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (S:77621-77635).

verifierReasoning: [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The relay primitive is real and unguarded: Chat.Awake registers ZRoutedRpc "RPC_TeleportPlayer"<Vector3,Quaternion,bool> (SERVER:41626-41627, runs on clients where Chat exists) and the handler is Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos,rot,distant) with no sender or permission check (:41962-41968); Chat.TeleportPlayer is the vanilla wrapper (:41957-41960) and the admin 'recall' console command already drives it (:44548-44556). Character registers the ZDO-scoped "RPC_TeleportTo" (:886, :4126-4132) which is owner-gated — satisfied by targeting peer.m_characterID. A dedicated server needs no registration to invoke either (InvokeRoutedRPC :83577-83595 routes by hash). Player.TeleportTo silently returns false when IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown < 2 (:15302-15327); the cooldown accrues only while not teleporting (:15329-15334). The pad gate is genuinely server-side: a vanilla client parked on the pad has no way onward except the server's RPC. Client-originated RPC_TeleportPlayer can be vetoed in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix because the server is the only router (:83632-83643). The timing claim is wrong, though, and is the part that would make a naive implementation fail silently.

[vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The second hop is real: Chat.Awake registers 'RPC_TeleportPlayer' as a routed RPC (S:41627) and the handler calls Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport) with no checks (S:41962-41968); the vanilla 'recall' admin command uses exactly this path (S:44548-44556). Character.RPC_TeleportTo (ZDO-scoped, S:4126-4132, registered S:886) is an equivalent owner-gated route. Player.TeleportTo silently returns false when IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown < 2 (S:15302-15327), and the cooldown accrues only while not teleporting (S:15329-15335). A distant teleport cannot complete before m_teleportTimer > 8 s and needs IsAreaReady + FindFloor, else up to 15 s (S:15353-15378). The server decides whether to send the RPC, so the destination is unreachable without server consent — server-enforced in the route sense, with execution client-honoured. Two howItWorks statements are wrong: the timing ('wait >=2 s after the arrival sample') and the simpler arrival heuristic ('any character within 3 m of a pad'), which is an ore-rule bypass.

catalog.name: RemoteCommand Piggyback — the vanilla F5/chat admin channel
catalog.oneLine: A vanilla admin types `removekey tpl <verb> …` in their own console or chat window; the stock client forwards it as RPC_RemoteCommand, a server-side prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand executes the mod verb and answers into the admin's console — zero client install.
catalog.howItWorks:
Transport (client side, unmodified): `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (server :45734-45758, client :45734, byte-identical) looks the first word up in the static `commands` dictionary; if `IsValid` fails AND `value.RemoteCommand && ZNet.instance && !IsServer()` it calls `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (:81869-81877) → `GetServerRPC().Invoke("RPC_RemoteCommand", command)`. `IsValid` (:43203-43218) fails on every client for any `onlyServer:true` command (:43207-43213), so `removekey` (isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true, :43535-43546) is forwarded verbatim, full line included. Two vanilla entry points reach TryRunCommand: the F5 console, and the CHAT window — `Chat.InputText` (:41947-41955) strips a leading `/` and calls `TryRunCommand(text, silentFail:true)`, and `Chat.isAllowedCommand` (:41938-41945) only rejects IsCheat commands, so `/removekey tpl list` typed in ordinary chat is forwarded too; no `-console` launch flag needed.

Server side: `RPC_RemoteCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command)` (:81879-81889) is registered only when `m_isServer` (:79921), gates on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` (socket-verified identity, the same check as RPC_Kick), then `InternalCommand` → `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)` (:81891-81895). `Console.instance` exists headless: `Game.Awake` instantiates `m_consolePrefab` (:100038-100041) and `FejdStartup` does the same on the server path (:97043-97045).

Mod: `[HarmonyPrefix] ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command)`. If `command` does not start with the reserved carrier (`removekey tpl ` or `removekey tpl:`), return true (vanilla continues). Otherwise: (1) re-check `ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` (public, :81811-81814) — the prefix runs BEFORE vanilla's check; (2) resolve the peer with `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`; (3) dispatch the verb on the main thread (RPC handlers already run there); (4) reply with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, line)` (:81635-81648 → client `RPC_RemotePrint` → `Console.instance.Print`, registered on both sides at :79912); (5) return false so the carrier never reaches Terminal, never reaches `RemoveGlobalKey`, and never writes the misleading `Remote admin … executed command` log line (:81893). Because replies land in the F5 console buffer (`Console.Print` → `AddString`), also mirror each reply line to the admin as a `PlayerNotify.Toast` or a fabricated `ChatMessage` (Whisper type, targeted to `peer.m_uid`; `Chat.OnNewChatMessage` :41775-41816 has no distance gate for the chat line) when the request arrived via the chat path — detectable only heuristically, so make it a config switch (`ReplyToChat=true`).
catalog.playerExperience: An admin (adminlist.txt) presses Enter, types `/removekey tpl list` (or F5 and `removekey tpl list` with -console). Nothing visible happens in chat except their own line disappearing. Within one frame a toast appears top-left: `tpl: 47 portals, 3 stranded, 1 orphan link` (and the full multi-line report is in the F5 console). A non-admin typing the same gets vanilla's `You are not admin` in their F5 console (:81883) and nothing else — the mod never sees the packet's payload because vanilla's check runs after the prefix returns true. A non-admin who has -console and looks at `help` never sees `removekey` listed (hideBehindDevCommands:true) but can still type it; it is refused server-side.
failureModes: Server-side `ZNet.RemoteCommand(cmd)` (stdin/mod-driven) calls `InternalCommand(null, cmd)` (:81873) which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket()` at :81893 → NRE. Never call RemoteCommand on the server; the dispatcher must be callable directly, and a prefix on RPC_RemoteCommand is not reached by that path anyway.

If the mod is absent/broken, `removekey tpl …` falls through to `RemoveGlobalKey("tpl …")` → `GlobalKeyRemove` → `GetKeyValue` splits on the first space, key `tpl` is not present → returns false, no broadcast, no persistence (:113516-113539). Safe. (`setkey tpl …` would instead hit `SetKeyAndValueIsCheat` (:59860-59870) and be refused with a cheat warning unless the server's junk profile is cheat-flagged — also safe, but noisier; and a cheat-flagged profile would let `setkey` persist a junk NonServerOption key into the .db.)
Replies via RemotePrint are invisible to an admin who has no `-console` (Console.IsConsoleEnabled :42952 gates only the window, not the buffer). Mitigation: mirrored toast/whisper.

`Terminal.commands` is a static dictionary written by indexer (:43096, :43114); a later plugin registering `removekey` clobbers vanilla silently — but this design never touches Terminal registration, so only the fallback (mod absent) behaviour changes.

Another server mod that also prefixes ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand and returns false first would swallow the carrier. Use a distinctive carrier prefix and Harmony priority; log at Initialize if another patch is present on the method (Harmony.GetPatchInfo).
Admin list is host-name based; a PlayFab/crossplay admin id must be in adminlist.txt in the platform-prefixed form ListContainsId accepts (:80159-80173).

catalog.name: tpl: command grammar, dispatcher and the catalog correction
catalog.oneLine: Resolve the catalog's self-contradiction: a mod-named command (`tplite.*`) is indeed dead, but a reserved namespace riding a vanilla remote-flagged command is live — plus the finding that a vanilla dedicated server has NO stdin console at all, so RPC_RemoteCommand is the ONLY console channel it has ever had.
catalog.howItWorks:
Why `tplite.*` is dead: the vanilla client's `TryRunCommand` (:45736-45737) forwards nothing unless `commands.TryGetValue(array[0].ToLower())` succeeds — an unknown first word prints `not a recognized command` (:45756) and never reaches ZNet. Why the piggyback is live: the six non-cheat remote-flagged commands a client will forward are `genloc`, `setkey`, `removekey`, `resetworldkeys`, `setworldpreset`, `setworldmodifier` (all isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true — :43475, :43510, :43535, :43553, :43558, :43570). `restartparty` (:44586) is onlyServer:false so IsValid succeeds client-side and it runs locally. The other seven remote commands (`confirmcheats`, `players`, `resetkeys`, `listkeys` — note listkeys IS isCheat:true at :43640, contrary to the gap text — `sleep`, `skiptime`) are cheat-flagged: the client still forwards them (IsValid fails on `!IsCheat || IsCheatsEnabled()` since client IsCheatsEnabled :45721-45732 requires IsServer), but the server's own Terminal refuses them unless a remote `devcommands` (:43341-43355, which calls RemoteCommand itself) has flipped the static `Terminal.m_cheat`.

Carrier choice: `removekey` — its mod-absent fallout is a provable no-op (see previous option). Grammar: `removekey tpl <verb> [args…]`; the dispatcher tokenises `command.Split(' ')`, drops the two carrier tokens, and routes on verb. Verb table (each returns List<string> lines): `ping` (liveness + build fingerprint), `list [tag|near <r>|mine]`, `show <tag|x,z>`, `health`, `repair --dry-run|--apply`, `net list|apply|revert`, `lock <tag>` / `unlock <tag>`, `pin <tag>` (push RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse to self), `export`, `probe` (dump CapabilityProbe), `help`. Every verb is a pure function over the PortalCensus DTO plus the engines' public API; the dispatcher never touches Terminal.

Two interception points, pick one: (A, recommended) prefix on `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` — sees the authentic `ZRpc`, runs before vanilla's admin check (so re-check with `ZNet.IsAdmin`), never lets the carrier reach Terminal. (B) prefix on `Terminal.TryRunCommand(string text, bool, bool)` keyed on `text.StartsWith("removekey tpl")` — also catches mod-driven local `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` calls, but has no `ZRpc` for the reply unless a companion prefix on RPC_RemoteCommand stashes `rpc` in a static for the duration of `InternalCommand`. (B) is only worth it if another mod already supplies a server stdin reader.

The stdin finding: grepping all four server decompiles for `Console.ReadLine`/`Console.In`/`StandardInput` yields zero hits (the three ReadLine hits are StringReader/StreamReader file parsers: assembly_guiutils_SERVER:977/1068/1107, assembly_utils_SERVER:7202). A vanilla 1.0.7 dedicated server does not read stdin. Every earlier brief line of the form 'from the dedicated server's stdin console run setkey/listkeys' describes a channel that does not exist; the only way those onlyServer commands have ever been run on a dedicated server is exactly this RPC_RemoteCommand path from an admin client (or a third-party stdin mod).
catalog.playerExperience: Admin: `/removekey tpl health` → toast `tpl: 2 findings` and F5 console lines `STRAND tag=Base members=3 orphan=(x,z)` … `/removekey tpl repair --apply` → `applied 2/2 (dry-run off)`. `/removekey tpl help` lists verbs. Anything malformed replies `tpl: unknown verb 'foo' — try help`. Non-admins never get a mod reply.
failureModes: Typo in the carrier (`removekeys tpl …`) → client prints `not a recognized command` locally and nothing is sent.

An admin who has run remote `devcommands` and then a cheat command has set the server's junk profile `m_usedCheats` (RunAction :43180-43183) — irrelevant to this channel but it changes the mod-absent fallout of `setkey` carriers; another reason to use `removekey`.

Arguments containing spaces are split by `text.Split(' ')` on the client before forwarding? No — the whole `text` string is forwarded intact (:45743); splitting happens server-side in the dispatcher, so quoted args must be handled by the dispatcher.

Terminal.commands is process-static; a ConsoleCommand named `removekey` registered by another plugin on the SERVER changes the fallback only; on the CLIENT it could change whether the command is forwarded at all (a client mod is out of scope).
Replies over ~4 KB per RemotePrint line are fine (ZRpc string), but 300-line reports scroll off the 300-entry console buffer (:45989); paginate `list` at 40 lines.

catalog.name: Portal Dirty-Flag Guardian — persisting CLIENT-originated renames
catalog.oneLine: Vanilla loses a vanilla player's portal rename at the next world save whenever no connection write follows it, because RPC_ZDOData never dirties the portal chunk; the mod watches for observed changes and calls ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() on every one, and HealthScan reports 'renamed-but-not-dirty'.
catalog.howItWorks:
The hole, traced: a vanilla client's `RPC_SetTag` runs on the owning client and writes `s_tag`/`s_tagauthor` into its own ZDO copy; the change reaches the server via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139), which on a higher DataRevision calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` (:77129) and then `AddIfPortal(zDO, zDO.GetPrefab())` (:77130). `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74205-74240) writes the connection with raw `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` (:74951-74961 — no ZDOMan call) and every field with `ZDOExtraData.Add` (:74881 — dictionary assignment only). `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) early-returns at :77739-77742 (`if (value.Contains(zdo)) return;`) for a portal already in its bucket, BEFORE `DirtyPortalObjects = true` at :77751. The portal chunk (`ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal`) is written only `if (DirtyPortalObjects)` (:77621-77632), and a successful save resets the flag (`UpdateSaveState` :76221-76222). Portals are excluded from every normal chunk (:77572). So the rename survives only if something else dirties the flag before the next save: `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` of type Portal on the SERVER (:73661-73675), a NEW portal's AddIfPortal, `HandleDestroyedZDO` of a portal (:76986), or the public `SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702-76705).

When vanilla is rescued: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears down the OLD partner (`SetConnection(item, None)` :100603) — but only via a local write when the partner is unowned or its owner offline (`Game.SetConnection` :100637-100651); if a player is near the partner it is deferred over RPC_SetConnection and the partner's None arrives back through RPC_ZDOData — again no dirty. Phase 2 dirties only if a same-tag partner exists. Net: a rename of an unconnected portal, or of a connected portal whose old partner is player-owned and whose new tag has no partner, is silently reverted on restart — and blamed on the mod.

Mod: the PortalCensus already snapshots (tag, tagauthor, connection) per ZDOID at 1 Hz. On any diff not attributed to the mod's own writer, call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` and record `dirtiedAt`. Cost: one bool; the next save writes the whole portal chunk (every portal cloned, :77623-77629) which vanilla does anyway on any connection change. HealthScan reads the private `m_dirtyPortalObjects[(int)m_currentSaveState]` via AccessTools (or the publicized property) and reports `portal chunk dirty: yes/no` plus every portal whose observed tag differs from the tag at last save (`lastSavedTag`, captured from a postfix on `ZDOMan.PrepareSave`/`ZNet.SaveWorldThread`).

Corollary for reverts: `ZDO.Deserialize` only Adds; `ZDO.RemoveString` (:74072) mutates the local dictionary without a revision bump, and `Serialize` writes only present keys, so a removed key is never removed on any peer — the owning client's next push re-adds it to the server. Reverts of mod keys must overwrite with a sentinel ("" / 0), never Remove.
catalog.playerExperience: A vanilla player renames an unconnected portal `Ore1` on a quiet server, logs off; the server autosaves 20 minutes later and restarts overnight. With the mod: the portal still reads `Ore1`. Without: it has reverted to its previous tag and the player files a bug. Admins see `[tpl] portal 12:3456 renamed 'Ore1' by <playerID> — portal chunk marked dirty` in the log and, via `tpl health`, `dirty-since-save: 3 portals`.
failureModes: A rename that lands between `GetSaveClonePerChunk` and `UpdateSaveState` is written to `m_dirtyPortalObjects[1]` (CurrentlySaving state, :76139-76150) and merged back at :76221/:76228 — handled by vanilla; the mod's SetDirtyPortals is state-aware because it goes through the same property.

Mod writes and client writes are indistinguishable in the census diff unless the NetworkReassertEngine stamps its own writes (it must — otherwise every reassert looks like a client change; harmless but noisy).
`m_dirtyPortalObjects` is private; reading it needs the publicizer or AccessTools.Field — reporting only, never write it directly (use SetDirtyPortals()).

The whole portal chunk is rewritten on every dirty save; on a world with thousands of portals this is one extra file of N×~100 B per save — negligible, but the ZLog `Number of dirty chunks to save` count will show +1.

catalog.name: OnJoin Briefing & login-time state push
catalog.oneLine: Use the peer-join lifecycle (ZRoutedRpc.m_onNewPeer / RPC_PeerInfo postfix) plus the first appearance of the character ZDO with s_playerID as the one event that seeds per-player ledgers, force-sends managed anchors, re-pushes idempotent map pins, and toasts a portal briefing (admins get a health summary).
catalog.howItWorks:
Three join stages, each a distinct hook: (1) Peer ready — `ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo` assigns `peer.m_uid/m_playerName` (:79905-79906) and ends with `m_routedRpc.AddPeer(peer)` (:79943), which fires the PUBLIC field `ZRoutedRpc.m_onNewPeer(long uid)` (:83500, :83531-83533) — the same hook ZoneSystem uses to push global keys and location icons to a new peer (:113444, :113609-113617). No Harmony needed; Wonderland's `PeerJoinLeaveHook` postfix on RPC_PeerInfo is the equivalent. At this stage the socket host name (`peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, platform-verified) and character name are known; the character ZDO is not. Seed here: `lastSeen[PlatformUserID] = now` in a mod file (m_playerHistory carries no timestamp — `CrossNetworkUserInfo` is {m_id, m_displayName, m_serverAssignedDisplayName, m_playfabId} :78868-78885). Force-send here: for every managed anchor / managed portal ZDO call `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, id)` (:77714-77719); `AddForceSendZdos` is gated on `peer.ShouldSend` (:77273) but a fresh `ZDOPeer` has an empty `m_zdos` (:76767-76773) so ShouldSend returns true (:76003-76015) — the join is the one moment a force-send is guaranteed to transmit. This eliminates the 'first transit fails while RequestZDO fetches the destination' warm-up. (2) Character known — `RPC_CharacterID` sets `peer.m_characterID` (:80899-80909). (3) Identity known — poll `ConnectedCharacters.All()` until `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID) != 0`; then key the per-character ledger by s_playerID and join it to the PlatformUserID from stage 1.

Briefing (stage 3, after a configurable settle delay, default 8 s, and only while `!zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)`): from the PortalCensus compute the player's own portals (`s_creator == s_playerID`, or `s_tagauthor == hostName`), stranded/orphaned ones among them, and toast via `PlayerNotify.Toast` ("Message" RPC on the character ZDO). Re-push pins: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", tag, (int)PinType.Icon3, pos, false)` per own portal; the client's `HaveSimilarPin` dedups by name+type+<1 m so repeats are no-ops. Admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)`): additionally `RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, …)` the HealthScan summary lines. Leave: prefix on `ZNet.Disconnect(ZNetPeer)` (:80015) writes `lastSeen` and clears the stage-3 pending state.
catalog.playerExperience: Player logs in, loading screen ends, ~8 s later a top-left toast: `Portals: you own 4 (1 has no partner: 'Ore1')`, and 4 pins named after their tags appear on the map (already-present pins are not duplicated). If the mod manages a hub route, the destination is already resident so the first walk-through works immediately. An admin additionally sees, in the F5 console, `tpl health: 47 portals, 2 stranded, 0 dangling, chunk dirty: no`.
failureModes: Toast sent before `Player.Start` registers the "Message" RPC (:10072) is dropped with a client-side 'Failed to find rpc method' warning; the settle delay covers this, and the RPC is only registered on the owning client anyway.
A toast during the post-spawn black screen may expire unseen (TopLeft messages time out); hence the delay and `s_dead` check — the exact safe delay is an in-game measurement.

Pins are `save:true` and permanent; a renamed portal produces a second pin next join. Only push pins for tags unchanged since last push (census `lastPinnedTag` per player), and never for portals the player did not build.
Force-sending hundreds of anchors at join inflates the first sync batch; cap per-peer force-sends per join (StructureUpkeep's 256-per-sweep pattern) and prefer anchors of managed routes only.
`m_onNewPeer` is a plain delegate field: Delegate.Combine, never assign; another mod assigning it would drop the hook (log a warning at OnWorldReady if the invocation list lacks the mod's handler).
prerequisites: Managed-anchor registry from NetworkReassertEngine for the force-send list.

catalog.name: CapabilityProbe — boot-time Inspector-data and singleton census
catalog.oneLine: A one-shot engine at OnWorldReady (with retries for late singletons) that logs every Inspector/runtime fact the decompile cannot answer and publishes a Capabilities record every other engine reads to self-disable with a logged reason.
catalog.howItWorks:
Runs from the ZNetScene.Awake-driven OnWorldReady, re-tried once per Heartbeat tick until every probe has either resolved or hit its retry cap (ObjectDB/EnvMan can be null at first call — Wonderland's BuffRosterEngine precedent). Probes, each wrapped in its own try/catch and its own METHOD (mono JITs the calling method; a missing member throws at JIT of the caller — GameShape.cs rule):

Portals: `Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs` names (:99828) and `PortalPrefabHash` (:100021); for each prefab via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` (:82045): `GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>()` type names (these ARE the `HasFields<TypeName>` keys LoadFields uses), `ZNetView.m_persistent/m_distant/m_type/m_syncInitialScale` (:82537-82543), presence of `ZSyncTransform` and its `m_syncPosition`/`m_characterParentSync` (:87354, :87362), `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems/m_exitDistance/m_activationRange` (:143429/:143413/:143411), `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear/m_health`, `Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea`. Wards: `GetPrefab("guard_stone")?.GetComponent<PrivateArea>().m_radius` (:137132), `m_enabledByDefault`, `m_ownerFaction`. Player prefab: `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync`, `CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation` (:4652), `ZNetView.m_persistent`. Singletons: null-ness of `Chat.instance` (:41611), `MessageHud.instance` (:55787), `Minimap.instance` (:56461), `DamageText.instance` (:46350), `Console.instance` (:42866), `EnvMan.instance` (:95571), `ObjectDB.instance`. Routed RPC table: `AccessTools.Field(typeof(ZRoutedRpc),"m_functions")` (:83510) keys vs the stable hashes of `ChatMessage`, `ShowMessage`, `RPC_TeleportPlayer`, `RPC_DamageText`, `SpawnObject` — decides Register-vs-Harmony for the ping hook (Register throws on a duplicate). Scene: `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()` (:82334), `ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition()` (:81019), `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:114054-114069), `m_zones.Count` (private :113274, AccessTools), and whether `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` has a Sector-0 bucket. Time: `EnvMan.instance.GetDayFraction()` sampled at t0 and t0+60 s (FixedUpdate :95685-95705 derives it from ZNet time with no local-player gate, so it should advance headless), `GetCurrentEnvironment().m_name`. Save: postfix on `ZNet.SaveWorldThread`/`ZDOMan.PrepareSave` to timestamp last save.

Output: `[tpl-probe] key=value` lines plus `BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.probe.json` (atomic write). A static `Capabilities` object with typed nullable fields; each engine's Initialize reads it: e.g. FieldInjection requires `PortalPrefabComponents.Contains("TeleportWorld")`; MovingDestination requires `PortalHasZSyncTransform`; ShadowWardIndex requires `GuardStoneRadius.HasValue`; PingInput chooses Register vs HandleRoutedRPC prefix from `RoutedRpcHasChatMessage`; every engine logs `disabled: precondition X unresolved` instead of silently no-oping.
catalog.playerExperience: Players see nothing. The operator sees a ~40-line block in the server log ten seconds after world load, e.g. `portalPrefabs=portal_wood,portal_stone,portal_blackmarble`, `portal_wood.ZSyncTransform=false`, `guard_stone.PrivateArea.m_radius=32`, `Chat.instance=null`, `routedRpc.ChatMessage=absent`, `envDayFraction 0.412→0.427 (+60s)`, and `tpl probe` (admin command) reprints it on demand.
failureModes: Probing a prefab that lacks a component returns null — every probe must null-guard and report `n/a`, never assume.
`GetComponentsInChildren` on a prefab ASSET (not an instance) works in Unity but disabled children are skipped unless `includeInactive:true` — pass true.
A probe that dereferences a singleton set by a client-only prefab (Hud) is fine (null → reported) but a probe that instantiates anything is not — the probe must be read-only.
Reading `m_functions` via reflection couples to a private field name; guard with null and report `unknown` so nothing else breaks.
The `m_zones` count at (1e6,0,1e6) may grow per player (CreateGhostZones runs per peer :113930-113939) — report both the count and whether the reference-position zone itself is loaded.
prerequisites: Heartbeat/registry lifecycle (Wonderland Plugin shape) for the retry loop.
GameShape.cs reflection discipline for version-sensitive members.

EnvMan.FixedUpdate day-fraction derivation (no local-player gate) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:95685-95710; GetDayFraction :96290-96293

First run on the testbed decides: portal prefab list, ZSyncTransform presence, guard_stone radius, Player m_characterParentSync, singleton null-ness, ChatMessage registration, EnvMan advancing, IsActiveAreaLoaded at the pinned position.

catalog.name: In-process HTTP endpoint — downgraded to needs-ingame-check, with probe and fallback
catalog.oneLine: HttpListener is a System.dll facility the decompile cannot vouch for; vanilla proves outbound HttpClient works headless (ZNet.GetPublicIP) but nothing proves inbound listening does, so ship it behind a boot probe with the atomic JSON export as the guaranteed fallback.
catalog.howItWorks:
Evidence available: the dedicated server's Managed folder ships `System.dll` (2.6 MB, REFERENCE-DLL-PROVENANCE.md:322) and `System.Net.Http`; vanilla's own `ZNet.GetPublicIP` (:79390-79420, called from :79324 and by PlayFab matchmaking :90726) constructs a `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` and runs `Task.Run(async …).Result` against public HTTPS endpoints on the server — proof the runtime's sockets, TLS and thread pool work headless. Zero `HttpListener` references exist in any game assembly (grep of all four decompiles), so inbound listening on Unity's Mono is unverified: known Mono quirks are prefix handling (`http://+:port/` vs `http://127.0.0.1:port/`), no HTTPS without an external cert store, and abrupt shutdown throwing ObjectDisposed/ThreadAbort into a blocked `GetContext`.

Probe (part of CapabilityProbe or a standalone `tpl httpprobe` verb): in Initialize, `new HttpListener()`, `Prefixes.Add("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/")`, `Start()`, then `BeginGetContext` loop; the mod immediately self-tests with an outbound `HttpClient.GetAsync("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health")` on a thread-pool task and logs `httpListener=ok` on a 200, else the exception. Operator cross-check: `curl -s 127.0.0.1:port/health` from the host shell; on shutdown (`Plugin.OnDestroy`) call `listener.Close()` and confirm the log shows no ThreadAbortException/unhandled ObjectDisposedException.

Threading contract (unchanged from the ops notes): the main thread builds an immutable snapshot DTO (census + health + metrics) once per tick and swaps a `volatile` reference; the listener callback serialises THAT object only (Newtonsoft.Json.dll is present in Managed as of 1.0 — provenance :157 — or a hand-rolled writer as DiscordWebhook does) and never touches ZDOMan/ZNet/Unity APIs. Endpoints: `/health`, `/portals.json`, `/metrics` (Prometheus text). Bind loopback only by default; anything else is the operator's reverse proxy.

Fallback: if the probe fails, the engine logs `http: disabled (…)` and the atomic JSON/CSV export (already in the catalog) remains the machine-readable surface; an external script polls the file. Nothing else in the mod depends on HTTP.
catalog.playerExperience: Players: nothing. Operator: `curl 127.0.0.1:7770/portals.json` returns the census; Grafana scrapes `/metrics`. If the runtime refuses to listen, the log says so at boot and the operator reads `BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.portals.json` instead — same schema.
failureModes: `HttpListener.Start()` throws HttpListenerException on Mono if the prefix host form is unsupported — try `127.0.0.1` first, then `localhost`, then `+`, and report which worked.
Blocking `GetContext()` on a foreground thread keeps the process alive after Unity quits; use `BeginGetContext` or `IsBackground=true`.
Serialising on the listener thread while the main thread mutates the DTO — avoided only by the immutable-snapshot swap; never expose live lists.

BepInEx/Unity may run without `System.Net.Http` loaded until first use; reference resolution failures show up at JIT of the calling method — isolate all HTTP code in its own class so a missing assembly disables only this engine.
Port already bound (a second server instance) — treat as probe failure, do not retry-storm.

catalog.name: Terminal Architecture (LocationProxy shell / Ghost-mode SpawnLocation / RegisterLocation)
catalog.oneLine: Build the place around a managed portal with vanilla world-gen: a server-authored LocationProxy ZDO makes every vanilla client raise a location's static geometry, colliders and no-build ring at the hub; Ghost-mode SpawnLocation adds the location's real persistent piece ZDOs (walls, altar bowls, dungeon rooms) server-side; RegisterLocation makes it a first-class map/registry location.
catalog.howItWorks: Three primitives, all server-only, composable. (a) PROXY SHELL: mint `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, proxyHash)` where `proxyHash = ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationProxyPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode()` (:113216; read the prefab's ZNetView m_persistent/m_type at runtime and mirror them), then `zdo.SetPrefab(proxyHash); zdo.Persistent=true; zdo.SetRotation(rot); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_location, location.m_prefab.Name.GetStableHashCode()); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_seed, seed)`. On every vanilla client the proxy instantiates, `LocationProxy.Awake → SpawnLocation` (client :103092-103158) resolves the hash via `GetLocation(int)` (server :114352, `m_locationsByHash` filled at :113674-113676), waits for the async prefab load (`ShouldDelayProxyLocationSpawning` :115139, marking the zone loading so `IsAreaReady` waits), then `SpawnProxyLocation → SpawnLocation(SpawnMode.Client)` (:115150-115159; Client branch :115294-115341) which SetActive(false)s every ZNetView child before `Utils.Instantiate` — so ONLY non-ZNetView content appears: static meshes, colliders, EnvZone, EffectArea, the `Location` component. Then `m_nview.LoadFields()` runs on the proxy AFTER the instance is parented under it (client :103149-103150), and LoadFields walks `GetComponentsInChildren` (client :82905), so ZDO keys `HasFields`, `HasFieldsLocation`, `Location.m_noBuild` (bool), `Location.m_noBuildRadiusOverride` (float), `Location.m_exteriorRadius` (float) override the spawned Location. `Location.IsInsideNoBuildLocation` reads those fields live (:133619-133629, `IsInside(buildCheck:true)` :133560-133564) and is consulted by piece placement (:13484-13487) and hoe/cultivator/pickaxe TerrainOps (:24126-24141) — a client-honoured no-build/no-terraform ring with zero pieces. (b) REAL PIECES: `ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation(location, seed, pos, rot, SpawnMode.Ghost, list)` (private :115162; publicized) instantiates every enabled ZNetView child under `ZNetView.StartGhostInit` (:115239-115243), runs `DungeonGenerator.Generate(mode)` (:115252), stamps `s_preSnow`, creates the proxy with spawnNow=false (:115347-115362), then `SnapToGround.SnappAll()` (:115343). The caller must `Object.Destroy` every entry of the returned list (SpawnZone does this at :114096-114102). Because `SnappAll`/`GetGroundData` need a terrain collider, wrap the call as SpawnZone does: wait until `HeightmapBuilder.instance.IsTerrainReady(zonePos, hm.m_width, hm.m_scale, hm.IsDistantLod, WorldGenerator.instance)` (:114075; it queues a build and returns false the first time, :129879-129899), `Instantiate(m_zonePrefab, zonePos)` for the frame, resolve y with `GetGroundData` (:114963), honour `m_snapToWater` (:114966), then destroy the root. (c) REGISTRY: `RegisterLocation(location, pos, generated:true)` (private :115364-115382) adds a LocationInstance so `GetLocationIcons`/`FindClosestLocation` and the LocationIcons RPC see it; refuses if the zone already holds a location (:115372-115377). Do NOT use `TestSpawnLocation` (:115033-115077): it dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded (:115071), sets `m_didZoneTest` which makes `SkipSaving()` return true (:115072, :115875-115881), and stamps `s_cheated` (:115075, :115258-115261). `SpawnLocationMidGame` (:115079-115106) only registers with `placed:false` and `pos.y = GetGroundHeight(pos)` (a dead raycast, :115102) — it is placed later by `PlaceLocations` only if the zone is still ungenerated (:114086, :114960); in a generated zone it is never placed.
catalog.playerExperience: The player steps out of a managed portal into a stone circle, a ruined fort, or an altar plaza instead of bare grass. Walls and braziers are real pieces (from the Ghost pass) they can lean on, damage or repair; the plaza's static statue/floor is the proxy shell. Trying to place a workbench or dig with the hoe inside the ring shows the vanilla 'NoBuildZone' placement status and refuses, exactly like building next to a boss altar. If the shell is a crypt entrance, the vanilla door works (it is prefab-internal) and the rooms exist because the Ghost pass generated `s_roomData`. Nothing looks modded; the location is on their map if the mod registered it and the location type has `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced`.
failureModes: Which geometry is static vs ZNetView is per-location Inspector composition; a proxy-only shell of a location whose walls are all pieces shows only the floor. Needs a per-location in-game survey.

Location.Awake on the client instantiates the interior at y+5000 when m_hasInterior (:133509-133515); a proxy of a dungeon location without the Ghost pass yields an interior with NO rooms (DungeonGenerator is a ZNetView child, disabled in Client mode).
Ghost SpawnLocation called without a zone root: SnapToGround/GetGroundData raycast against nothing, pieces float or sink. Always instantiate m_zonePrefab for the frame and gate on IsTerrainReady.
RegisterLocation throws no error but silently refuses when the zone already has a location (:115372-115377); the mod must check ZoneHasLocation first and pick another zone.
Spawned pieces are ordinary WearNTear ZDOs: players can demolish the shell unless the mod re-asserts it or wraps it in a Shadow Ward policy.

The ClearArea from m_clearArea is only added inside PlaceLocations for world-gen instances; a mid-game Ghost drop into an ungenerated zone gets vegetation grown through it unless Destination Zone Governor's ClearArea injection is also used.
`Location.m_clearArea`/`m_exteriorRadius` LoadFields overrides only affect the client-side Location component; they do not retroactively clear vegetation.

catalog.name: Destination Zone Governor (pre-generate, clear-area inject, barren pad)
catalog.oneLine: Control what the world-gen pipeline does to every managed destination zone: ghost-generate it at route-write time so arrival never pays for generation, inject a ClearArea so vegetation never grows through a phantom portal, and optionally mark a zone generated-without-generating to produce a spawn-free barren clearing.
catalog.howItWorks: Facts: zones are generated ONLY by the server. `ZoneSystem.Update` (:113924-113941) calls `CreateLocalZones(GetReferencePosition())` then, on the server and only when that did nothing, `CreateGhostZones` for its own pinned refpos and for every `peer.GetRefPos()` (:113932-113938). `CreateGhostZones` (:113971-113991) spawns at most ONE ungenerated zone per 0.1 s tick within `TotalSimulationDistance`. Clients call `PokeLocalZone`, which picks `SpawnMode.Client` for any non-server (:114028), so a client never places vegetation/locations. `SpawnZone` (:114071-114107) gates on `HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady` (:114075) and on the zone's location prefab being loaded (:114080), then for Ghost/Full on an ungenerated zone runs `PlaceLocations`, `PlaceVegetation`, `PlaceZoneCtrl` (:114091-114093), destroys everything in Ghost mode (:114094-114103), and `SetZoneGenerated` (:114104, private, adds to the private `m_generatedZones` HashSet :113276, saved/loaded at :113736/:113798). Three mod actions: (1) PRE-GENERATE: when a route is written, for the destination zone and its ring (radius = `m_simulationDistance.NearSimulationDistance`), if `!IsZoneGenerated(z)` call publicized `SpawnZone(z, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _)` — one zone per Update tick, retrying while it returns false (terrain not built yet: IsTerrainReady queues a build and returns false, :129879-129899). This is exactly what vanilla does when a peer approaches, moved forward in time. (2) CLEAR-AREA INJECTION: `PlaceVegetation` tests `InsideClearArea(clearAreas, p)` (:114134 signature, box test :114340-114350) and the list is the private `m_tempClearAreas` filled only by PlaceLocations (:114968-114972). A Harmony prefix on `ZoneSystem.PlaceVegetation` appends `new ZoneSystem.ClearArea(portalPos, radius)` (private nested class :112757-112768, publicized) for every managed destination in `zoneID`. Vegetation's only other exclusion is `veg.m_blockCheck && IsBlocked(p)` — a raycast against Default/static_solid/Default_small/piece (:113423, :115496-115500) that never sees a phantom ZDO because it has no server GameObject. (3) BARREN PAD: `m_generatedZones.Add(zone)` WITHOUT calling SpawnZone marks it generated; PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation/PlaceZoneCtrl are then skipped forever (:114086). No `_ZoneCtrl` ZDO means no `SpawnSystem` for that zone: `SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning` needs its own ZNetView owner and a local player (SpawnSystem :110642, Awake/UpdateSpawning gating `!m_nview.IsValid() || !m_nview.IsOwner() || Player.m_localPlayer == null`), so ambient creature spawns never occur there (CreatureSpawners inside locations and RandEventSystem still can). The inverse — `m_generatedZones.Remove(zone)` — re-runs generation on top of whatever exists (double vegetation, a second location attempt) and must only be used on a zone the mod itself marked barren. Persist the mod's own per-zone state (pre-generated / barren / cleared) in a position-keyed file because `m_generatedZones` carries no provenance. Budget: one SpawnZone per tick, and skip zones beyond ±16 320 m (SectorToIndex clamp :115760-115773).
catalog.playerExperience: A traveller arrives at a phantom destination and the zone is already there: no 15 s fallback landing on seabed height, no trees sprouting through the portal frame when the zone finally generates, no boar pack spawning on the pad. On a barren pad the clearing is grass-only terrain with no rocks, trees or roaming creatures within the 64 m zone — a visibly 'kept' hub area. Nothing is visibly modded; it looks like a naturally empty zone.
failureModes: Marking a zone barren before any player visits also suppresses its world-gen LOCATION (PlaceLocations is skipped); check ZoneHasLocation first or you erase a runestone/crypt that the registry still lists as unplaced.

Ghost SpawnZone instantiates the zone prefab plus every vegetation/location ZNetView child on the main thread and destroys them the same frame — a full zone can cost tens of ms; do one per tick and never in a burst at route-write.
SpawnZone returns false while the location prefab for that zone is async-loading (:114080); the mod must retry, not treat false as done.

ClearArea injection only affects zones generated AFTER the prefix is installed; already-generated zones need the mod to destroy offending vegetation ZDOs itself (SetOwner + DestroyZDO inside the radius).
Removing a zone from m_generatedZones to 'regenerate' duplicates vegetation ZDOs and may place a second location; only use on mod-marked barren zones.
IsTerrainReady at the server never fails for coordinates inside the world, but zones beyond the SectorToIndex clamp collide with sector 0; refuse those.
prerequisites: Publicized assembly_valheim (SpawnZone, SetZoneGenerated, m_generatedZones, PlaceVegetation, ClearArea are private)
Position-keyed per-zone state file (Wonderland SupplySwitch pattern, keyed by zone not ZDOID)

catalog.name: Target Materialiser (ghost-generate the destination so altars, traders and crypt rooms always exist)
catalog.oneLine: Before routing to a boss altar, trader or dungeon, force-ghost-generate the target zone and its neighbours server-side so the OfferingBowl parent, Trader, LocationProxy and DungeonGenerator (s_roomData) ZDOs exist — turning 'portal to X' from 'if someone has been there' into 'always', and letting the safety validator inspect real placed objects.
catalog.howItWorks: Vanilla generates a zone only when `CreateGhostZones(peer.GetRefPos())` (:113935-113938) brings it inside a peer's `TotalSimulationDistance`, so an unvisited altar has a `LocationInstance` (m_placed=false) but no ZDOs. The mod calls the same private `SpawnZone(zone, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _)` (:114071) itself. Sequence per target: (1) resolve the LocationInstance via `FindClosestLocation`/`FindLocations` (:115707-115740) and its zone `GetZone(m_position)`; (2) if `IsZoneGenerated(zone)` (:115869) the objects already exist — done; (3) otherwise call `SpawnZone(zone, Ghost, out _)`. It returns false twice legitimately: terrain not built (`HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady` :114075 queues the build) and location prefab not yet loaded (`PokeCanSpawnLocation(isFirstSpawn:true)` :114080 starts an async `LocationPrefabLoadData` load with a lifetime refreshed each call, :115108-115129) — retry every tick until true. On success `PlaceLocations` (:114957-115003) resolves y with the now-live terrain collider (`GetGroundData` :114963), applies `m_snapToWater` (:114966), slope/random rotation (:114974-114987), calls `SpawnLocation(..., Ghost, ...)` which ghost-instantiates every ZNetView child (real persistent ZDOs: altar pieces, chests, Trader, runestones, CreatureSpawners) and runs `DungeonGenerator.Generate(Ghost)` (:115252, rooms persisted in `s_roomData`), creates the proxy ZDO (:115292), sets `m_placed=true` (:114990), prunes duplicates for unique locations (:114994-114997), and — the free win — `SendLocationIcons(0L)` for `m_iconPlaced` locations (:114998-115001), so traders that never appeared on any map now do. Also generate the 8 neighbours (or the NearSimulationDistance ring) so the traveller's `IsAreaReady` (:82064-82082, requires `IsZoneLoaded` for the target zone only) and view distance are covered. The validator then reads real object positions (e.g. the OfferingBowl parent piece's ZDO, found by `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` at the altar position) instead of pre-flattening heights, and the phantom can be dropped at a validated stand-off from real pieces. Note `PlaceLocations` runs only on the first generation of a zone (:114086), so this is a one-time cost per target and is persisted by ZoneSystem.Save via m_generatedZones (:113736). Interacts with the sector-0 clamp: never request zones beyond ±16 320 m (:115760-115773). Works with zero peers online (it only needs ZNet/ZoneSystem/HeightmapBuilder, all live headless because vanilla's own ghost generation uses them).
catalog.playerExperience: The 'Eikthyr' or 'Haldor' portal option is available the moment the world boots, not after some player has sailed there. Walking through lands the player beside a fully placed altar/camp with the trader standing there, and the trader/altar pin is already on the map for everyone (LocationIcons). For a crypt target the entrance ruin and its rooms are exactly as vanilla would have generated them (same seed :114988), so nothing looks different from an organically discovered location.
failureModes: Each forced zone is a main-thread instantiate+destroy of the whole zone's vegetation and location; a boss altar in Mistlands can be heavy. One zone per tick, never all targets at boot in one frame.

A unique location that was already placed elsewhere has had its other instances removed (:114994-114997); FindClosestLocation may return an instance that no longer exists in m_locationInstances — re-check membership after generation.

Generating a zone also spawns its CreatureSpawners/RandomSpawn content as real ZDOs; the traveller may arrive into a fully populated fuling camp. That is vanilla behaviour, but the mod chose the moment.
If `SpawnZone` keeps returning false because the location's SoftReference prefab fails to load (m_prefab invalid), the loop must time out and fall back to the LocationInstance position.
Sector-0 clamp: coordinates beyond ±16 320 m map to the server's own sector bucket; refuse them.

catalog.name: Corpse-Run Gate (auto death → ephemeral portal to the tombstone)
catalog.oneLine: On a player's death the server raises a private, ephemeral portal pair: a phantom at their claimed bed (or the hub) paired to a phantom/anchor 2 m from the tombstone, tagged with a per-player reserved tag so vanilla's pairer keeps them together; both are torn down when the tombstone despawns or a TTL expires.
catalog.howItWorks: DETECT DEATH: the tombstone is a client-instantiated prefab (`Player.CreateTombStone` :12702-12714, `Instantiate(m_tombstone)` :12708) whose ZDO arrives over the wire. Use the SpawnGovernor pair — postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int)` (:76684) to remember the id, postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74205-74240) to read the prefab — and match the tombstone prefab hash (resolve at OnWorldReady by scanning `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` for the one carrying a `TombStone` component; the name is Inspector data). `TombStone.Setup` writes `s_ownerName` + `s_owner` (profile UID) (:19845-19853); `TombStone.Awake` on the owner writes `s_timeOfDeath` and `s_spawnPoint` (:19732-19740). Because Setup/Awake run on the owning client, the first Deserialize may lack `s_owner`; queue the ZDOID and poll `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_owner)` until non-zero (dead player's `s_dead` on the character ZDO, :78403, is a corroborating signal). ORIGIN: bed = scan Bed-prefab ZDOs (`GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative`) for `s_owner == uid`; several beds may match (Bed.Interact never clears :119670-119725) — pick nearest to `peer.m_refPos`, which during respawn IS the custom spawn point (`Game.UpdateRespawn` :100349 → `RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` :80395-80408). Fallback: the hub. BUILD: mint origin phantom (portal hash from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`) 3 m from the bed, and destination = Void Anchor or phantom 2 m from `tombZdo.GetPosition()` at `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` +0.2 with rotation facing the grave; give both `s_tag = "​cr:"+uid` (zero-width prefix keeps players from typing it; no length cap, :143587-143602) and reciprocal `SetConnection(Portal, …)` after `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, then `ForceSendZDO` both (recipe of `Game.SetConnection` :100637-100651). Same literal tag + non-None both sides means `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100594-100606) never tears it down; since the pair count is exactly 2, phase 2 never re-pairs it. Push a map pin via `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` (:100068, :100823-100831) named 'Corpse gate' at the origin and `PlayerNotify.Toast` on respawn (character ZDO reappears with a new `m_characterID`, :80899-80909). CLEANUP: `TombStone.UpdateDespawn` runs on the owning client and calls `m_nview.Destroy()` when empty (:19871-19890) — the server sees it in `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` (:76033, invoked :76975-76978) → destroy both gate ZDOs (`SetOwner(session)` then `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` :76929-76935). Also a TTL (default 30 min) and a 'player used it' signal (character ZDO within 10 m of the tombstone) — first pickup of any item does NOT destroy the tombstone, so use proximity + TTL, not despawn alone. Mark the gate ZDOs in a position-keyed mod file so a restart mid-run can reconcile (ZDOIDs renumber on load, :74552).
catalog.playerExperience: The player dies in the Plains, respawns at their bed. A toast reads 'A corpse gate has opened beside your bed' and a saved map pin marks it. Next to the bed stands an ordinary-looking portal glowing as connected. They walk through, the normal 8 s portal transit plays, and they arrive two metres from their tombstone facing it. They loot, and can walk back through the same gate to the bed. When the tombstone empties and vanishes (or after 30 min), both portals silently disappear. Vanilla ore rules still apply on the way back: if they picked up ore the return trip is refused with '$msg_noteleport' exactly as at any portal — unless the mod also field-injects `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` on the return gate (unproven LoadFields test).
failureModes: Tombstone ZDO arrives before the owning client writes s_owner; without the poll the mod attributes it to nobody.
Player has several claimed beds; the bed chosen may not be the active spawn point when they died at a spot far from where m_refPos pointed. Fall back to the hub and say so in the toast.

Portal frames left floating when the tombstone is in water or on a cliff: destination phantom must be validated (Destination Safety Validator) and the anchor placed on the nearest land within 20 m, not at the grave.

Unsupported phantom on a slope loses WearNTear support and is demolished by the owning client (UpdateWear :149705-149711, m_noSupportWear default true :149205) — place at terrain height, not floating.
If the player dies again before cleanup, two gates share the bed; key the tag by uid+death tick and cap at one active gate per player.
Another player can use the gate (it is a normal portal); the tag prefix hides it from typing but not from walking through. Acceptable for co-op; use the Two-Hop Relay if strict privacy is required.
First transit may fail silently if the client has not yet received the destination ZDO (TargetFound → RequestZDO :143640-143655); ForceSendZDO to the peer on gate creation mitigates.
prerequisites: Invisible Anchor ZDO or a second phantom for the grave side

catalog.name: Two-Hop Relay: Cooldown-Correct Timing Spec
catalog.oneLine: The relay's second hop only works if the server waits out vanilla's teleport state machine: hop 1 (portal, distant) holds m_teleporting for ≥8 s and zeroes the cooldown the whole time, so the earliest accepted hop 2 is ≥10 s after the portal accepted — the honest transit is ~20 s and must be designed as a lobby moment, not discovered in testing.
catalog.howItWorks: State machine (all on the traveller's client, `Player`): `TeleportTo` refuses while `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, then sets `m_teleporting=true`, `m_teleportTimer=0`, `m_teleportCooldown=0` (:15302-15326). `UpdateTeleport` holds `m_teleportCooldown=0` every tick while teleporting and only accrues it once `m_teleporting` is false (:15329-15335); it pins the transform to the target from t>2 s (:15340-15346); for `distantTeleport` (what TeleportWorld always passes, :143546) completion needs t>8 s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target)` (:15349), then `FindFloor` (:15354); if no floor, distant lands at `GetSolidHeight+0.5` at t>15 s (:15359-15366). TIMELINE: T0 portal accepts hop 1. T0+2 s the client transform snaps to the lobby and `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` pushes it; the server observes the character ZDO inside the lobby radius ≈T0+2.1 s — that is the ONLY signal it gets (both RPC handlers discard TeleportTo's bool, :41966, :4130). Hop 1 ends at T0+8 s (lobby zone is pre-generated and tiny so IsAreaReady is immediate). Cooldown reaches 2 f at T0+10 s. Any hop 2 sent before then is silently dropped. RULE: schedule hop 2 at (lobby-arrival-observed + 8.5 s) ≈ T0+10.6 s, i.e. a fixed ≥8.5 s hold after the position appears, never earlier; add +1 s if the lobby is not pre-generated. PRE-CHECKS before sending hop 2: `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (dead player latches m_teleporting and never advances, UpdateTeleport only runs in the !IsDead branch :10213-10226), `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` (:78457; attach ping-pong :10217/:15818-15840), and that the character ZDO is still inside the lobby (player may have walked out). SEND hop 2 as `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, false)` (:886, :4126-4132) with `distantTeleport:false`: no 8 s floor, completes at the first tick after t>2 s where `IsAreaReady` and `FindFloor` pass (:15349-15357). Hazard: with distant=false a FindFloor miss at t>2 s immediately rubber-bands the player back to the lobby with '$msg_portal_blocked' (:15367-15374) — so the final target must be validated ground (WorldGenerator height + Destination Safety Validator), and the target zone should be pre-generated (Target Materialiser) so IsAreaReady does not stall the black screen. UX: total black screen ≈8 s (hop 1 swirl) + ~2.5 s standing in the lobby + ~2 s (hop 2, plain black without the swirl since `ShowTeleportAnimation = m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` :15386-15393; Hud :47872-47877) ≈ 12.5 s of screen time, ~20 s wall clock from portal entry. The lobby moment is unavoidable — dress it (Terminal Architecture shell, a toast 'Routing to <dest>…' via PlayerNotify, a SpawnObject VFX). Retry policy: if the ZDO position has not left the lobby 4 s after hop 2, resend once (the first may have hit the cooldown window by a few ms); then give up and toast. Rate-limit per player ≥12 s.
catalog.playerExperience: Enter the hub portal → normal 8 s portal swirl → appear on a small stone landing pad with a toast 'Routing you to Haldor…' for about two seconds (they can look around, cannot leave in time) → screen goes black (no swirl) for ~2 s → they stand at the trader. If the mod picked a bad floor they instead pop back onto the landing pad with the vanilla 'portal blocked' message and the toast explains. A dead or sleeping player is never relayed; they are left in the lobby with an explanation.
failureModes: Hop 2 sent even 100 ms early is silently eaten; there is no ack. Under-estimating the 8 s floor (e.g. assuming cooldown starts at RPC send) makes every relay fail.
distant=false + FindFloor miss = rubber-band to lobby with a misleading vanilla message; always validate ground and pre-generate the target zone.
A player who walks off the pad during the 2.5 s window is teleported from wherever they are; check position before sending.
Client hitching/loading extends hop 1 beyond 8 s (IsAreaReady false for the lobby); the fixed hold must key off observed lobby arrival plus margin, and the retry covers the rest.
Two players relayed simultaneously share the lobby; per-player hold timers and per-player destinations are required (keyed on s_playerID, not m_uid).
prerequisites: Two-Hop Relay: Phantom Landing Pad + RPC_TeleportPlayer (the option this specifies)
Destination Zone Governor / Target Materialiser (pre-generate lobby and target zones)
Destination Safety Validator (validated ground for hop 2)

verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Every numeric threshold in the timing spec is verified exactly against Player.TeleportTo/UpdateTeleport. TeleportTo confirmed at exactly :15302-15326: rejects while IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown<2f (exact line :15313), then zeroes cooldown/timer and sets m_teleporting=true. UpdateTeleport confirmed at exactly :15329-15378: cooldown only accrues while !m_teleporting (held at 0 the entire time hop 1 is in flight, exactly as claimed); transform pin to target happens unconditionally once m_teleportTimer>2f (exact line :15338, executes every tick thereafter); the distant-teleport gate (!(m_teleportTimer>8f) && m_distantTeleport) || !IsAreaReady(...) is confirmed verbatim at exactly :15349, so a distant hop cannot complete before t=8s regardless of area readiness; the 15s hard-fallback vs immediate-rubber-band-if-not-distant branch is confirmed verbatim at :15360-15378. Since cooldown only starts accruing once m_teleporting flips false (earliest ~t=8s for a successful distant hop) and TeleportTo requires cooldown≥2f, the derived 'earliest accepted hop 2 is ≥10s after hop 1 accepted' is arithmetically correct from the verified code, not an invented number.
