catalog.name: Owner-Delegated Retag
catalog.oneLine: Send vanilla's own `RPC_SetTag` / `RPC_SetConnected` from the server TO the owning client so the owner executes the rename and pushes it back as ZDOData — the race-free write primitive for every revert on a client-owned portal.
catalog.howItWorks: `TeleportWorld.Awake` registers `RPC_SetTag(long,string,string)` and `RPC_SetConnected(long,ZDOID)` on every client-side portal ZNetView (:143448-143449); both gate only on `m_nview.IsOwner()` / `zDO.IsOwner()` (:143589, :143625) and ignore `sender`. The server therefore calls `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ownerPeerUid, portalZdo.m_uid, "RPC_SetTag", approvedTag, verifiedPlatformUserId)` (:83577) — `targetPeerID != m_id` so the server never dispatches locally (:83587-83594), `RouteRPC` delivers to that one peer (:83603-83610), the client's `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `HandleRoutedRPC` → `ZNetScene.FindInstance` → `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83656-83663, :82838-82843) runs the handler. The handler compares against `GetTagSignature` and no-ops if tag+author already match (:143591-143592), else `UpdateConnection(Portal, None)` (only if an entry exists — `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` :74962), then `SetConnectedPortal` on the now-None id (vanilla bug — the partner is never told, :143595-143597), then `Set(s_tag)`/`Set(s_tagauthor)` (:143598-143599). Those `ZDO.Set` calls bump DataRevision and `ClientChanged` (:73832-73838), so the client's next `CreateSyncList` (client branch :77242-77258) ships the ZDO to the server within ~50 ms, where `RPC_ZDOData` applies it because the revision is higher (:77110-77131). No DataRevision race: the owner authored the write. Ownership is identified by `portal.GetOwner()` compared against `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` — exactly `Game.SetConnection`'s deferral test (:100639-100641); when the owner is 0 or offline the mod writes locally instead (SetOwner(session) + Set + ForceSendZDO). Follow-up on the server: (a) `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` — the returning ZDOData hits `AddIfPortal`, which early-returns for an already-registered portal without dirtying (:77738-77742), so the rename would be lost at save; (b) if the write was a REVERT to the partner's tag, phase 1 of the next `Game.ConnectPortals` still clears the partner (its target's connection is None, :100601) and phase 2 re-rolls the pair randomly (:100607-100622) — to preserve the pairing, immediately re-link both ends via `RPC_SetConnection` to the owner (:100649, handler :100653-100662) or the local write path. `RPC_SetConnected` is the same trick for clearing a client-owned partner's connection (:143622-143629).
catalog.playerExperience: The player who renamed a locked portal sees the tag flip back on the next hover (GetHoverText reads the ZDO live, :143453-143463) within a network round-trip, with no black screen, no ownership flicker and no zone reload; the mod can pair it with a PlayerNotify toast explaining the revert. If the mod also re-links, the portal never shows '[unconnected]'. Other players near the portal see the same tag via the normal ZDOData fan-out.
failureModes: The owning client must currently have the portal INSTANTIATED — `HandleRoutedRPC` drops the RPC silently when `FindInstance` returns null (:83659-83663). A peer that just became owner via `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76922-76925) but whose `CreateObjectsSorted` pass has not run yet loses the message; retry on the next tick if the tag has not changed.
`authorId` is written verbatim (:143599) — pass the socket-verified PlatformUserID or empty string, never the client-supplied value.
On an unconnected portal `UpdateConnection` is a no-op (:74962-74975), so the connection field is untouched; on a connected one it is cleared and the partner is orphaned until re-linked.
A hostile modified client can simply not execute the handler; the server observes no change in `s_tag` within N ticks and escalates to the Ownership Pin.
If the vanilla client build ever changes the handler signature the routed call is dropped with 'Failed to find rpc method' on the client (:82846) — invisible to the server.
prerequisites: Tag Watchdog (detect and revert) as the caller
Real Ownership Pin as the escalation
Authentic Sender Context for the verified authorId
openQuestions: IN-GAME: stand next to a portal you own, have the server send RPC_SetTag with a different tag, confirm hover text changes without leaving the area and that the server-side s_tag updates within 100 ms.
IN-GAME: confirm the peer-targeted ZDO RPC is delivered when the target client has the object instantiated but the server's copy shows owner==that peer only since the last 2 s ReleaseZDOS pass.
corrections: Relabel enforcement from server-enforced to client-honoured: the write is applied by the owning client's vanilla RPC_SetTag/RPC_SetConnected handler, not independently by the server. The server can direct the write and detect its absence, but cannot force it through if the target peer never processes the RPC (disconnect, packet loss); Real Ownership Pin is the only path in this catalog that is genuinely server-enforced for this data.
evidence: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long,ZDOID,string,params) — :83577-83595 (verified exact, local dispatch skipped when targetPeerID != m_id)
ZDOMan.AddIfPortal early return — :77732-77751 (verified exact, confirms dirty-loss bug)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:downgraded] Every cited API and line matches the decompile exactly: TeleportWorld.Awake registers RPC_SetTag/RPC_SetConnected (143448-143449), both handlers gate only on IsOwner()/zDO.IsOwner() and ignore sender (143587-143629), ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long,ZDOID,string,params) skips local dispatch and routes to one peer when targetPeerID != m_id (83577-83610), ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC is the real handoff (82838-82848 per anchors; class at 82531), IncreaseDataRevision bumps DataRevision and triggers ClientChanged only on non-server (73832-73840), AddIfPortal genuinely early-returns without dirtying for an already-sectored portal (77732-77751, confirmed by direct read), Game.SetConnection's owner/online-peer deferral test is exact (100637-100651), ConnectPortals is a verified two-phase pass with no reciprocity check (100589-100622). The mechanism is real. But the enforcement label is wrong by the ground rules' own test: the actual WRITE only happens if the owning CLIENT executes RPC_SetTag/RPC_SetConnected -- the server only directs a routed RPC to that peer and never applies the change itself. This is 'should this player's client honor an instruction' (client-honoured), not a server-owned field write the server can force through regardless of the other side. The option's own prereq list ('Real Ownership Pin as the escalation') implicitly concedes this by naming the actually-enforceable fallback. Under the stated project assumption that every client is 100% vanilla, an unmodified client will always execute the handler, so the mechanism is reliable in practice -- but it is a vanilla-respecting write, not a server-enforced one, and should be labeled that way per the ground rules ('Say so explicitly when a mechanism is client-honored rather than server-enforced').

catalog.name: Extended RPC Veto Table
catalog.oneLine: Add PersistentEventSystem's RequestStartEvent/RequestStopEvent/UpdateClientEventsList and Ship's Forward/Backward/Stop/Rudder to the `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix veto list — three more unauthenticated levers a stock-protocol client can pull against any portal policy.
catalog.howItWorks: All three families pass through `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632-83644), the only place the authentic socket is in scope; a prefix deserialises a COPY of the package, reads `m_methodHash`/`m_targetZDO`, resolves the true sender via `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`, and returns false to drop. (1) `PersistentEventSystem.Start` registers `RequestStartEvent`/`RequestStopEvent`/`UpdateClientEventsList`/`RequestActiveEventsList` as global routed RPCs (:105284-105287, names :105093-105099). `RPC_RequestStartEvent` runs on the server (:105343) with NO sender or admin check: it indexes `m_possibleEvents[sourceEventId]` unchecked (:105347 — an out-of-range int throws inside the RPC dispatch), generates a location, calls `ZoneSystem.SpawnLocationMidGame` and `ObjectSpawnSettings.Create`, which does `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate` server-side (:105033) and adds a persistent event that `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)` broadcasts (:105377). `RPC_RequestStopEvent` does `FindIndex` then `RemoveAt(index)` with no -1 guard (:105385-105386) — a bogus id throws ArgumentOutOfRange in the server's RPC handler. `RPC_UpdateClientEventsList` is applied by every NON-server recipient (:105412-105418) and the server relays a client broadcast at targetPeerID 0 to all other peers (:83612-83619), so a client can forge the whole active-event list (positions, radii, weather overrides) on everyone else's screen. Policy: allow RequestStart/Stop only from admin sockets (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(host)` :81811) and drop UpdateClientEventsList from any non-server sender outright. (2) `Ship.Start` registers `Stop`/`Forward`/`Backward`/`Rudder` on the ship's ZNetView (:140482-140485) and the handlers set `m_speed`/`m_rudderValue` unconditionally (:140538-140575) with no owner/sender gate; `Ship.Forward/Backward/Stop` send to the ZDO OWNER (:140530, :140545 via `InvokeRPC(string)` :82855) but a modified client can address any peer with `InvokeRPC(long,...)`. Policy: for a `m_targetZDO` whose prefab has a Ship component, require the true sender's character ZDO to be within N metres of the ship ZDO position, or to equal `ZDOVars.s_user` (the helmsman, :141332). Also note: `Register` for these names would throw on the server if PersistentEventSystem lives there (Dictionary.Add), so patch, do not register.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to honest players: their own event participation is server-initiated and their own helm input reaches the ship owner unchanged. A griefer spamming forged events, remote-steering someone's longship into a portal dock, or crashing the server's RPC dispatch with an out-of-range event id gets a dropped packet and an AuditLog line; admins can still trigger events from the console.
failureModes: Distance-gating ship RPCs relies on the sender's character ZDO position, which is client-reported (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync) — a hacked client can fake proximity; the veto still removes the remote-steering case.

Whether an exception thrown inside `RPC_RequestStartEvent` kills the whole `ZRpc` dispatch loop for that peer or is caught is not visible in the decompile — treat the index guard as a hard requirement either way.
If `PersistentEventSystem` is not instantiated on the dedicated server the start/stop handlers are unregistered and the attack surface collapses to the relay case only.
openQuestions: IN-GAME: confirm `PersistentEventSystem` exists on the dedicated server (log `PersistentEventSystem` instance null-ness at world ready) — it decides whether RequestStart/Stop are live server handlers.
IN-GAME: does a thrown exception in a routed RPC handler disconnect the peer, log and continue, or take down `ZNet.Update`?
evidence: RPC_RequestStartEvent unchecked indexer, no sender check — :105341-105379 (verified exact)
RPC_UpdateClientEventsList applied by any non-server recipient — :105412-105418 (verified exact)
ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) targets owner; InvokeRPC(long,...) targets any peer — :82850-82857 (verified exact)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] All three RPC families check out precisely. PersistentEventSystem.Start registers RequestStartEvent/RequestStopEvent/UpdateClientEventsList (105284-105287); RPC_RequestStartEvent indexes m_possibleEvents[sourceEventId] with zero bounds checking and no sender/admin gate (105341-105379, confirmed by direct read -- an invalid id throws inside the dispatch); RPC_RequestStopEvent does FindIndex then RemoveAt(index) with no -1 guard (105381-105389, confirmed exact); RPC_UpdateClientEventsList is applied unconditionally by every non-server recipient with zero validation (105412-105418, confirmed exact -- 'if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) JsonUtility.FromJsonOverwrite(...)'). Ship.Start registers Stop/Forward/Backward/Rudder (140482-140485, confirmed) and all four handlers mutate m_speed/m_rudderValue unconditionally with no owner/sender check (140538-140580, confirmed exact). ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) sends to m_zdo.GetOwner() while InvokeRPC(long,...) can target any peer -- confirmed exact at 82850-82857, validating the claim that a modified client could address a ship RPC at an arbitrary peer instead of the owner. The veto point (RPC_RoutedRPC prefix, before any handler dispatch) is genuinely server-side and independent of client cooperation, so server-enforced is the correct label.

catalog.name: Per-Peer ZDO Withholding
catalog.oneLine: Filter portal ZDOs out of a non-member's sync list so the vanilla client never receives them — no mesh, no trigger, and a withheld DESTINATION makes `TargetFound` false forever, the first genuinely server-enforced per-player transit gate.
catalog.howItWorks: A client obtains a ZDO from the server only through `ZDOMan.CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer peer, List<ZDO> toSync)` (:77212-77241): sector objects near `peer.m_peer.GetRefPos()` filtered by `peer.ShouldSend` (:77221-77237), then `AddForceSendZdos` (:77239, :77263-77286) which drains `peer.m_forceSend` (fed by `ForceSendZDO` and `RPC_RequestZDO` :77689-77692). `SendZDOs` serialises exactly that list and records `peer.m_zdos[uid]` only for what it sent (:77045-77067). Clients never exchange ZDOs with each other — `RouteRPC` forwards routed RPCs only (:83597-83629) and ZDOData is a direct ZRpc to the server. So a Harmony postfix on the private `CreateSyncList` (nested private `ZDOPeer` type reached via `AccessTools.TypeByName("ZDOMan+ZDOPeer")`, `m_peer` field → `ZNetPeer` → `m_socket.GetHostName()`) that removes every ZDO the account is not permitted to hold — the portal, its partner, and any anchor — is complete: the client never has the object. Remove the id from `peer.m_forceSend` in the same postfix or `AddForceSendZdos` re-inserts it every cycle. Effects on the vanilla client: at the withheld portal's site nothing is instantiated (no `TeleportWorld`, no `TeleportWorldTrigger`); at a permitted SOURCE whose destination is withheld, `HaveTarget()` is true (the connection id is in the source ZDO, :143631-143637) so hover reads `$piece_portal_connected`, but `TargetFound()` finds `GetZDO(target)==null`, calls `RequestZDO` and returns false (:143646-143655); `Teleport` gate 1 returns silently (:143519) and the ready-glow stays off (`UpdatePortal` :143507). The `RequestZDO` is vetoed in the `RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix by hash + true socket (or simply stripped by the same postfix since it lands in `m_forceSend`). Ownership hazard: `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` assigns ownership to any peer in whose active area the ZDO sits without consulting `m_zdos` (:76901-76926), so a withheld portal near a non-member becomes owned by a client holding no copy; `Game.SetConnection` then defers `RPC_SetConnection` to it (:100647-100649), which no-ops on `GetZDO==null` (:100655), and a member's `RPC_SetTag` routes to it and is dropped. Withheld portals must therefore be held by the Real Ownership Pin. Persistence: nothing is written; the policy is a pure send-side filter keyed on the socket-verified account.
catalog.playerExperience: A non-member walks up to a private hub and sees empty ground — no portal, no hover, nothing to interact with. Standing at a public portal whose destination is private, they see '[Connected]' on hover but the portal never lights up and stepping in does nothing (no message at all — gate 1 is silent). A member standing beside them sees the portal glow and transits normally. Nothing distinguishes 'server withheld it' from 'not loaded yet' on the vanilla client.
failureModes: Silent failure for the non-member: gate 1 has no `player.Message`, so the mod should pair a withheld destination with a PlayerNotify toast when the player enters the source's 5 m activation range (position poll).

`CreateSyncList` is private and takes a private nested type — the postfix signature must use `object`/`__0` and reflection; a game update renaming `ZDOPeer.m_peer` breaks it silently (wrap in SafePatch and verify at world ready).
Any ZDO the non-member already holds before the policy applies (or before revocation) stays until Withholding Revocation runs.
Late-joining members are fine (`ShouldSend` true on first sight, :76013); a member downgraded to non-member mid-session needs revocation.
Per-peer filtering runs inside the 0.05 s per-peer send path (:76843-76861) — keep the lookup an O(1) HashSet<ZDOID> per account, rebuilt only when policy changes.
prerequisites: Real Ownership Pin (mandatory for withheld portals)
Withholding Revocation & Re-grant for mid-session changes
openQuestions: IN-GAME (decisive): withhold one portal from peer B; confirm B sees nothing at the site, B's partner-side hover reads connected but never glows/teleports, and A transits normally.
IN-GAME: measure the added cost of the postfix on a world with thousands of sector ZDOs per peer per 0.05 s.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] CreateSyncList (77212-77241, confirmed exact body read), ShouldSend (76003-76014, confirmed exact), AddForceSendZdos (77263-77286, confirmed exact) all check out precisely -- a client only ever obtains a ZDO through this path, so a postfix that strips entries is a genuine, independent-of-client-behavior withholding mechanism: server-enforced in the strictest sense of the ranked-priority test (it decides whether the ROUTE/OBJECT is delivered at all, not whether a player 'may pass'). TeleportWorld.HaveTarget/TargetFound and the RequestZDO fallback (143631-143657) confirmed exact, matching the claimed silent-failure behavior at a withheld destination. ReleaseNearbyZDOS (76901-76926) confirmed to check only position/active-area, not peer.m_zdos or sync state -- so it can indeed hand a withheld portal's ownership to a non-member client that never received a copy, exactly the hazard claimed, correctly flagged as requiring Real Ownership Pin.

catalog.name: Withholding Revocation & Re-grant
catalog.oneLine: Pull an already-delivered portal back out of one client with a peer-targeted `DestroyZDO` routed RPC, clear the server's per-peer cache, and later re-deliver it — the mid-session half of per-peer withholding.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZDOMan`'s constructor registers the global routed RPC `DestroyZDO` on every peer (:76155) and `RPC_DestroyZDO` reads a count plus ZDOIDs and calls `HandleDestroyedZDO` on each (:76953-76961). The server invokes `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "DestroyZDO", pkg)` targeted at ONE peer (:83603-83610) — the server's own copy is untouched because `targetPeerID != m_id` skips local dispatch (:83587). On the client, `HandleDestroyedZDO` fires `m_onZDODestroyed` → `ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed` destroys the GameObject and drops the instance (:82186-82194), removes the ZDO from `m_objectsByID` and pools it (:76988-76989); the `m_deadZDOs` resurrection block is `IsServer()`-only (:76994-76998), so a later re-delivery via ZDOData creates a fresh client ZDO (:77121-77125). Server side, `ShouldSend` would still return false for that peer because `peer.m_zdos[uid]` holds the last-sent revisions (:76005-76011) — the mod must remove the id from that private dictionary by reflection (the same `ZDOPeer` handle used by the withholding postfix). Re-grant is then just removing the id from the withhold set: the next `CreateSyncList` sends it. For the partner side: if the revoked ZDO was a DESTINATION the client's `TargetFound` flips false on its next `UpdatePortal` (0.5 s); if it was the SOURCE the trigger collider disappears with the GameObject. If the revoked client was the ZDO's server-recorded owner, nothing breaks further than the withholding case already requires (pin it).
catalog.playerExperience: The non-member watching a portal they were just removed from sees it vanish in place (same pop as a zone unload); if they were mid-walk-in, the trigger is gone before `OnTriggerEnter`. If they are already teleporting the client finishes the vanilla teleport (destination position was snapshotted at :15324) — see Arrival Bouncer. When re-granted, the portal pops back in on the next sync.
failureModes: Client-side `HandleDestroyedZDO` for a Player-adjacent ZDO owned by that client: the client never re-sends it, but the server's copy still lists that client as owner — pin ownership first.
If the id is not purged from `peer.m_zdos`, re-grant silently never sends (ShouldSend false) until the ZDO's DataRevision moves.
A client that received the ZDO via a member's shared `RPC_SetConnection`-driven ForceSend before policy changed is covered only if revocation runs on every policy change, not just on join.
Whether the vanilla client's `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects`/creation loop tolerates a ZDO being destroyed while its `TeleportWorldTrigger` is mid-`OnTriggerEnter` is untested.
citations: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC targeted skip of local dispatch — :83587-83594
openQuestions: IN-GAME (decisive): send a peer-targeted DestroyZDO for a portal the client has instantiated; confirm the GameObject disappears, no error is logged on the client, and re-delivery after purging m_zdos recreates it cleanly.
IN-GAME: confirm the client does not itself broadcast a DestroyZDO back (it should not — `DestroyZDO` only queues when IsOwner and HandleDestroyedZDO never calls it).
corrections: Worth stating explicitly: the 'stop re-sending' half of this mechanism (removing from peer.m_zdos) is server-enforced regardless of client behavior, but the 'pop out immediately' half depends on the target client actually processing the routed DestroyZDO RPC (client-honoured) -- a mixed guarantee the option does not separate out.
evidence: Local-dispatch skip for non-server/non-zero target — :83577-83595 (verified exact)
ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO / HandleDestroyedZDO, no sender check, per-peer m_zdos cleanup — :76953-76999 (verified exact, confirms cleanup only runs on the machine dispatching locally)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] InvokeRoutedRPC(long,string,params) resolves to the ZDOID.None overload and, for a specific non-server, non-zero peer id, skips local HandleRoutedRPC dispatch and routes only to that peer (83554-83594, confirmed exact) -- the server's own copy is genuinely untouched. RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO (76953-76999, confirmed exact) show no sender check whatsoever, and critically HandleDestroyedZDO removes the id from EVERY peer's m_zdos -- but only on whichever machine actually runs HandleRoutedRPC locally. Because a single-peer-targeted DestroyZDO never triggers local dispatch on the server (targetPeerID is neither m_id nor 0), the server's own ZDOPeer.m_zdos entry for that one peer is NOT auto-cleaned, confirming the option's claim that manual reflection removal is required. m_deadZDOs resurrection block is IsServer()-only, confirmed at RPC_ZDOData's create path (77133). This is a genuinely subtle and correctly-reasoned mechanism.

catalog.name: Destination Pre-Delivery
catalog.oneLine: Drive the `CreateSyncList` postfix from server policy to push a managed portal's DESTINATION ZDO to members before they step in — killing the silent first-transit failure — with no client request RPC at all.
catalog.howItWorks: The codebase brief dismissed TortalPortal's `SectorSubscription` postfix on `ZDOMan.CreateSyncList` as useless without a client because it waits for a client RPC; the postfix itself needs no request. `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` returns false and fires `RequestZDO` when the client lacks the destination (:143651-143654), and `UpdatePortal` only evaluates it when a teleportable player is inside `m_activationRange` (:143503-143507), so vanilla's own warm-up starts only when the player is already at the portal — the first walk-through fails at gate 1 (:143519) with no message. Server-side: on each `CreateSyncList` call for a peer (:77212-77241), for every managed portal within R metres of `peer.m_peer.GetRefPos()` (iterate `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` :77643, cheap), resolve `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` and, if `peer.ShouldSend(target)` (:76003-76014), append the target ZDO to `toSync`. `SendZDOs` then serialises it like any other entry and records it in `peer.m_zdos` (:77056-77064), so it is sent once and only again when its revision moves. This is exactly the delivery `Game.SetConnection` performs with `ForceSendZDO` at pairing time (:100645) but re-applied for any peer approaching the source later — including peers who joined after the pairing and never received the force-send. Combine with Per-Peer Withholding: the same postfix both strips withheld ids and injects permitted destinations, so one hook implements the whole per-account view.
catalog.playerExperience: A member walking up to a managed hub finds it already glowing 'ready' the moment they enter the 5 m activation range, and the first step through works. Without this, the first attempt at any portal whose destination is in an unvisited region does nothing and the second attempt works — a known vanilla annoyance that server-side re-pairing makes worse.
failureModes: `ShouldSend` is true for a never-seen ZDO but false once cached (:76013); a destination that MOVES (a ship anchor) is not re-sent until its DataRevision changes — that is inherent, not a bug here.
Injecting many distant ZDOs per peer per 0.05 s cycle competes for the 10240-byte send budget (:77010-77018); cap injections per cycle.

The injected ZDO lands in the client's `m_objectsByID` but not in its sector view; the client's own `RemoveObjects` never instantiates it (it is outside the active area) — which is exactly what TargetFound needs (a ZDO, not an instance).
prerequisites: Managed Network Governor or any managed-portal list
Optional: Per-Peer ZDO Withholding (shares the hook)
openQuestions: IN-GAME: pair two portals 5 km apart server-side, have a fresh client approach the source without ever visiting the destination, and confirm the first walk-through succeeds with the injection enabled and fails without it.
evidence: ZDOMan.GetPortals() Dictionary-returning method — :77643-77646 (verified exact, distinct from GetPortalList at :77648)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] CreateSyncList (77212-77241) and GetPortals() -> Dictionary<SectorIndex,List<ZDO>> (77643-77646, confirmed the method genuinely exists and returns that type, contra the anchor list's GetPortalList which is a different, separately-existing method at 77648) are both real. TargetFound/RequestZDO (143640-143657) and Teleport gate 1 (143519) confirmed exact, validating the claimed first-transit failure mode. This is a pure send-side injection under full server control -- server-enforced is the correct label since it needs no client cooperation to work (the client simply receives data it would have requested anyway, sooner).

catalog.name: Untagged Auto-Pair Suppression
catalog.oneLine: Stop freshly placed, never-named portals from linking to a random stranger's untagged portal within 5 s — a one-line prefix on `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` for the empty tag, with a unique-tag fallback.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZDO.GetString(s_tag)` defaults to "" (`ZDOExtraData.GetString` :75079-75082), so every never-named portal shares one tag group and `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 2 (:100607-100622) pairs each with `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(portalList, item2, "")` (:100612, :100664-100679) — a random untagged portal anywhere in the world. Primary mechanism (server-enforced, no ZDO write): a Harmony prefix on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` that sets `__result = null` and returns false when the tag is empty or whitespace-only; phase 2 then skips the portal (`if (zDO2 != null)` :100613). Because the runtime pairer is the ONLY tag-based pairer — `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` at load (:76515) re-links by saved hash pairs, not tags — this fully prevents new ""↔"" links. Existing ""↔"" pairs survive phase 1 (tags equal, both non-None, :100601), so a one-time sweep after `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (postfix after `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` at :76523) nulls both ends of any pair whose tag is "" via the local write path (SetOwner(session); SetConnection(Portal, None); ForceSendZDO — :100643-100645). A hostile client can still force a pairing through `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) — covered by Ungated RPC Hardening. Fallback (if patching Game is undesirable): at the arrival hook (SpawnGovernor's `CreateNewZDO`+`Deserialize` postfix pair, /Wonderland/.../SpawnGovernor.cs:43-68) write a unique tag `"<" + 8-char position hash + ">"` (10 chars, within the client's `characterLimit` :61519) which `RemoveRichTextTags` strips from hover (regex :6700-6703 admits `<[a-zA-Z0-9…]*?>`), plus `SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702); the watchdog re-applies it on any later clear to "". Load-time: iterate the ChunkPortal-loaded list (:76474-76482) before the synchronous `Game.ConnectPortals` at :76523. The primary mechanism is preferred because the fallback leaks the odd tag into the rename dialog (`TextInput.Show` pre-fills `sign.GetText()` :61512, :61520).
catalog.playerExperience: A player places a portal and, until they name it, hover shows '[unconnected]' and it never glows — exactly the behaviour most players already expect. The moment they type a tag it pairs with the matching portal on the next 5 s tick. With the fallback the dialog opens pre-filled with something like `<3f9a1c07>`, which they overwrite.
failureModes: Whitespace-only and homoglyph tags are a separate group problem — normalise in Anti-Grief Tag Integrity, not here.
An admin who deliberately uses the empty tag as a 'public network' loses it; expose a config toggle.
The load-time sweep of existing ""↔"" pairs breaks links players may have been relying on unknowingly — log each one to AuditLog and Discord.
Fallback only: a player who opens the rename dialog and saves it unchanged commits the invisible tag as a real name; harmless but confusing in exports.
prerequisites: Ungated RPC Hardening (RPC_SetConnection veto) for the hostile case
Tag Watchdog only for the fallback path
citations: ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal load and Game.ConnectPortals call — :76474-76482, :76515, :76523
openQuestions: IN-GAME: place two untagged portals 1 km apart on a vanilla client with the prefix active and confirm neither ever shows connected; then name both identically and confirm pairing within 5 s.
evidence: Game.ConnectPortals full body, phase1 no-reciprocity / phase2 tag pairing — :100589-100622 (verified exact)
TeleportWorld.Interact RequestText charLimit 10 — :143482 (verified exact, matches fallback tag length design)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Every load-bearing claim verified directly. ZDOExtraData.GetString defaults to '' (confirmed exact signature and default at ~75079). Game.ConnectPortals phase 2 pairs by exact tag string including '' via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal, and phase 1's predicate never checks reciprocity (100589-100679, full body read and confirmed). Game.SetConnection's local-write path (owner==0/offline/force) and RPC_SetConnection handler match exactly (100637-100662). TextInput.instance.RequestText(this,"$piece_portal_tag",10) is called with charLimit exactly 10 from TeleportWorld.Interact (confirmed exact at 143482), which precisely matches the fallback tag design '<' + 8-char hash + '>' = 10 characters. StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags' regex admits alphanumeric tag bodies and would strip the fallback tag from hover text (confirmed exact in assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703). The primary mechanism (prefix on FindRandomUnconnectedPortal, no ZDO write) is genuinely server-enforced and does not depend on any client behavior.

catalog.name: Creator Reassignment
catalog.oneLine: Rewrite `s_creator`/`s_creatorIndex` on a portal ZDO to transfer, adopt or reclaim it — the writable lever every vanilla client honours for 'built by', scoped to portal prefabs.
catalog.howItWorks: `Piece.Awake` reads `m_creator = zdo.GetLong(s_creator, 0)` and `m_creatorPlatformUserIDIndex = zdo.GetInt(s_creatorIndex, -1)` at instantiation (:136246-136250); `Piece.SetCreator` writes only when `IsOwner() && GetCreator()==0` (:136417), so nothing in vanilla ever overwrites a non-zero creator. `ZDO.Set` performs no ownership check (:73648-73654) and `ZDO.Deserialize` is additive (:74205-74240), so a server write is authoritative once delivered. Procedure: claim (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`), `Set(ZDOVars.s_creator, newPlayerId)` (the target's stable `ZDOVars.s_playerID` from their character ZDO, :10129-10136), `Set(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, ZNet.World.m_playerHistory.FindIndex(a => a.m_id == newPlatformUserId))` (mirror of :136421; `m_playerHistory` is server-maintained from socket-verified ids :81436-81461), `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — portals are excluded from normal chunk saves :77572 and the ChunkPortal file writes only when dirty :77621), then `ForceSendZDO`. Uses: 'transfer this gate to player X' (admin emote/console), 'adopt creator==0 portals to a maintenance account' (admin-spawned via Instantiate never run `SetCreator` because `PlacePiece` is the only caller :12514-12517), 'reassign a departed player's portals to a guild' (join on Team/Guild roster). Because `m_creator` is cached in the component at Awake, already-instantiated copies on nearby clients keep the OLD value until that object is recreated — ward `HaveLocalAccess` → `m_piece.IsCreator()` (:137595-137606, :136436-136441) and hover 'built by' text lag until the player leaves and returns. Scope strictly to `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021); applied to a guard stone it silently flips ward creatorship.
catalog.playerExperience: After an admin transfers a gate, the new owner sees 'built by <their name>' on hover once they re-enter the zone (or immediately if they were not nearby), can rename it under ward rules, and the export/Discord listing attributes it to them. The old owner loses nothing visible except attribution. Adopted admin portals stop showing an empty creator in reports.
failureModes: Stale cached `m_creator` on already-loaded clients — the transfer is not visible to a player standing at the portal until re-instantiation; a PlayerNotify toast bridges the gap.
`s_creatorName` (used by PrivateArea :137446-137449) is a separate string on wards, not on portals — do not expect a name field on the portal ZDO.
`s_creatorIndex` is -1 if the new owner has never connected (not in `m_playerHistory`); write -1 rather than a wrong index.
A hostile client can rewrite `s_creator` back through `RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) — the Tag Watchdog should include creator in its snapshot for managed portals.
prerequisites: Real Ownership Pin optional for contested gates
openQuestions: IN-GAME: transfer a portal while its builder stands beside it; confirm the hover still shows the old builder until they leave and return, and the new builder afterwards.
IN-GAME: confirm `s_creator` on a vanilla-placed portal equals the placer's character `s_playerID` (needed so transfers match `ConnectedCharacters.PlayerId`).
corrections: Minor clarification, not a defect: Piece.IsCreator() is defined entirely in terms of the calling client's own local PlayerProfile, reinforcing that only the WRITE (the ZDO field) is server-enforced -- any consumption of that field (ward access text, hover 'built by') is inherently client-local and vanilla-respecting rather than server-verified.
evidence: ZDO.Set(int,long) / Set(int,int,bool) no ownership check — :73648-73654, :73695-73701 (verified exact)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Piece.Awake reads m_creator/m_creatorPlatformUserIDIndex from ZDO at instantiation (confirmed exact, lines ~136246-136249); Piece.SetCreator only writes when IsOwner() && GetCreator()==0 (confirmed exact at 136415-136423), so nothing in vanilla overwrites a non-zero creator. ZDO.Set(int,long) and ZDO.Set(int,int,bool) both perform NO ownership check whatsoever regardless of the (unused) okForNotOwner flag (confirmed exact at 73643-73702) -- a claimed-ownership server write is genuinely authoritative. Player.SetPlayerID (10129-10136) and ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory (81436-81461) confirmed exact, validating that m_playerHistory is server-maintained from socket-verified connected players. Player.PlacePiece's SetCreator call (12514-12515) confirmed exact -- admin-instantiated pieces via bare Object.Instantiate indeed skip this, supporting the 'adopt creator==0 portals' use case. One clarification: Piece.IsCreator() compares against Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID() -- a purely local-player-profile concept -- so the read side genuinely only has meaning on whichever client is asking, consistent with the option's own framing of ward-read as client-side.

catalog.name: Real Ownership Pin
catalog.oneLine: A revision-aware pin that survives `RPC_ZDOData`'s `SetOwnerInternal` path — SetOwner prefix plus a post-receive re-claim that out-revisions the client — with ping-pong escalation and an explicit unpin/maintenance path.
catalog.howItWorks: The WaterBuoyancyEngine-style prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner` (:74627-74634) only stops in-process callers — chiefly `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76919, :76924) and `Game.SetConnection` (:100643). Incoming ownership arrives elsewhere: `RPC_ZDOData` applies the packet's owner with `SetOwnerInternal` (:74636-74651) at :77114 (owner-only update when `num3 > OwnerRevision` even if data is stale) and :77128 (full update), never through `SetOwner`. A vanilla client claims via `ZNetView.ClaimOwnership` → `SetOwner` → `IncreaseOwnerRevision` (:82769-82775, :73842-73850), so one client packet steals the pin. Real pin = three parts. (1) Prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner`: for pinned ids allow only `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` (:77362) and, when the unpin flag is set, `0`. (2) Postfix on `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc, ZPackage)` (or on `ZDO.SetOwnerInternal` filtered by pinned id): for every pinned ZDO whose `GetOwner()` is not the session, call `SetOwner(session)` — `SetOwnerInternal` + `OwnerRevision++` (:74631-74632) yields `num3+1`, strictly above the client's value, so `ShouldSend` (:76007-76011) resends and the client's `RPC_ZDOData` (identical class) applies the server owner because its incoming `OwnerRevision` is higher. (3) Ping-pong bound: each honest claim happens once (an unmodified client claims a portal only via `Game.RPC_SetConnection` :100658 — never sent to a pinned portal since the mod always takes the local path — or `SetConnectedPortal`'s `owner==0` branch :143610-143613, unreachable while pinned); a hostile client can loop claims, each costing one ZDO resend — count claims per account per minute, revert beyond N, then `ZNet.instance.Kick(host)` (:81658). Side effects of a pinned gate: `WearNTear.RPC_Damage`/`RPC_Remove`/`RPC_Repair` all route to the owner (:150415, :150419-150425, :149537-149548) and `UpdateWear` runs on the owner, so it is unbreakable, un-repairable and immune to support loss until unpinned. Unpin path: clear the pin, then `SetOwner(0L)` and `ForceSendZDO`; the next `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` pass (≤2 s) hands it to the nearest peer and hammer removal works again. Admin removal without unpinning: `SetOwner(session)` is already true, so `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929-76935) broadcasts `DestroyZDO`.
catalog.playerExperience: A pinned gate behaves like an indestructible, unrenameable fixture: hammer-remove, damage and repair all silently do nothing (the client sends an RPC nobody handles), rename dialogs accept text that never sticks. When the admin unpins it, within 2 s it becomes an ordinary portal again. Nothing flickers on screen during a steal/re-claim cycle — ownership is invisible to players.
failureModes: Unpinned-but-managed portals are still stealable — the pin must be per-id and explicit.

During the window between the client's claim packet and the server's re-claim resend, a second client packet with data changes (tag) is applied because DataRevision is higher — the Tag Watchdog must still run.
`RPC_ZDOData` postfix cost: iterate pinned ids per packet, not per ZDO; keep pins in the low hundreds.

A pinned portal with `s_health` already below max cannot be repaired by players; if a prior hit landed before the pin, the mod must write `s_health = m_health` itself (value from the prefab's WearNTear, needs ZNetScene prefab read).
Escalation-to-kick keyed on claims must exclude the legitimate one-time claim a client makes when the server itself defers to it — never defer for pinned ids.
prerequisites: Authentic Sender Context (account for the claim counter)
openQuestions: IN-GAME: pin a portal, have a client stand at it for 60 s and attempt rename/remove; log owner transitions on the server — expect exactly zero foreign-owner intervals longer than one send cycle.

IN-GAME: verify a vanilla client actually applies an incoming owner change whose OwnerRevision is exactly one higher (the client-side RPC_ZDOData is the same code, but confirm no local ClaimOwnership retriggers).
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData owner application via SetOwnerInternal (not SetOwner), both paths — :77076-77135 (verified exact, direct read)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] The central, subtle claim -- that incoming ownership via RPC_ZDOData bypasses ZDO.SetOwner and calls SetOwnerInternal directly (so a prefix on SetOwner alone is insufficient) -- is confirmed by direct read of RPC_ZDOData (77076-77135): both the owner-only fast path and the full-update path call zDO.SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal) directly, never SetOwner. ZDO.SetOwner/SetOwnerInternal/IncreaseOwnerRevision (confirmed exact at 74627-74651, 73842-73850) show SetOwner only bumps OwnerRevision when the uid actually differs, validating that a postfix re-claim via SetOwner(session) will out-revision an incoming client claim. ZNetView.ClaimOwnership (confirmed exact at 82769-82775) shows the client's own claim path also funnels through SetOwner, so the ping-pong dynamic described is real. ReleaseNearbyZDOS and Game.SetConnection/RPC_SetConnection citations reconfirmed exact (see other entries). This mechanism is genuinely independent of client cooperation once claimed -- server-enforced is correct.

catalog.name: Arrival Bouncer
catalog.oneLine: Reactive per-player transit consequence: detect a non-permitted arrival at a managed destination, wait out the ≥8 s frozen window, then send the traveller straight back — undoes but never prevents.
catalog.howItWorks: Prevention is impossible (gates run on the traveller's client, :143517-143549), but the aftermath is fully observable. `Player.UpdateTeleport` pins `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` from t>2 s (:15338-15343) and the owner's ZSyncTransform pushes it into the character ZDO, so the server sees the jump ~2 s after the trigger; the vanilla teleport cannot complete before t>8 s for `distantTeleport` (:15349) and `m_teleportCooldown` is held at 0 for the whole teleport and must reach 2 s afterwards (:15313-15320, :15336). During that window `CanMove` is false (:14423-14428) and damage is suppressed (:2425-2431). Detection: PositionWatch's sampling loop (/Wonderland/.../PositionWatch.cs:31-117) already keeps per-ZDOID last samples; reuse `IsPortalTransit` (:148-210) and pick the destination as the managed portal within 40 m of the new position whose connection points back near the old one. ACL lookup by `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (via ConnectedCharacters). If not permitted, schedule a return at t≥10.5 s after the first sample beyond the origin (covers the 8 s floor + 2 s cooldown + one sample interval), verify the character is still within 40 m of the destination, `!s_dead`, `!s_inBed`, then `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", originPortalPos + originForward*1f + Vector3.up, originRot, true)` (handler :41962-41968) or the ZDO-scoped `RPC_TeleportTo` (:886, :4126-4132); `distantTeleport:true` never fails (15 s force-land :15360-15366). If `TeleportTo` refuses because the cooldown has not elapsed (:15313), nothing is sent back — poll position again at +3 s and retry once. Toast via PlayerNotify at the moment of ejection. Log to AuditLog/Discord. For repeat offenders escalate to Per-Peer Withholding of that destination.
catalog.playerExperience: A non-member steps into a public portal wired to a private base, sits through the normal 8 s swirl, gets roughly 2–4 s of standing in the private base unable to be attacked but able to look around and move, then a second 8 s swirl returns them to where they started with a 'You are not permitted at <name>' toast. Members are never touched.
failureModes: Not prevention: the intruder sees the base for a few seconds and can open a chest or read a sign in the 2–4 s gap; anything with a client-only effect (map exploration) is retained.
PositionWatch samples at 3 s (config), so the window is ±3 s; the return can fire early and be silently rejected by the cooldown (:15313) — hence the retry.
Attached/sleeping travellers cannot be moved cleanly (UpdateAttach snaps :15818-15840); skip and log.
A spoofed `RPC_TeleportPlayer` from another client could pre-empt the return — covered by the relay veto.
If the origin portal was destroyed in the meantime, fall back to a configured holding position.
citations: Player.UpdateTeleport pin/8 s floor/15 s fallback — :15329-15379
openQuestions: IN-GAME: time from trigger to first server-visible position at the destination, and the earliest post-arrival second at which a forced return is accepted (expect ~10 s).
IN-GAME: confirm a return sent with distantTeleport:true into the origin's already-loaded zone completes at ~8 s rather than 15 s.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Player.TeleportTo cooldown/accept gate (m_teleportCooldown < 2f rejection) and UpdateTeleport's t>2s position pin, t>8s distantTeleport floor, and t>15s fallback are all confirmed by direct read (15302-15367) to match the citations precisely. Character.RPC_Damage's IsTeleporting() suppression of both stagger and all damage application is confirmed exact (2425-2431, direct read). Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer / Character RPC_TeleportTo registration confirmed to exist exactly as cited (886, 4126, 41627, 41959-41968). The enforcement label is honestly self-assessed as reactive-detection-only, matching the ranked-priority framework's own test (this is a 'should this player pass' case with no transit-time hook, correctly not claimed as preventive or server-enforced).

catalog.name: Client-Edit Dirty Guard
catalog.oneLine: Mark the portal chunk dirty whenever a CLIENT-originated tag edit arrives, because vanilla only dirties on connection writes — otherwise player renames are lost at the next save just like server ones.
catalog.howItWorks: `RPC_ZDOData` applies a client's updated portal ZDO (:77106-77131) and then calls `AddIfPortal(zDO, prefab)` (:77132), which early-returns for a portal already in its sector bucket (:77738-77742) without touching `DirtyPortalObjects`. The ChunkPortal file is only rewritten when `DirtyPortalObjects` is true (:77621), and portals are excluded from the ordinary chunk save (:77572), so a rename that is not followed by a `ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, …)` on the server (:73661-73664) before the next autosave reverts on restart. Vanilla is normally rescued because a rename clears the client's connection and the 5 s `Game.ConnectPortals` re-pairs it with a server-side `SetConnection`, which dirties — but a rename on an UNCONNECTED portal (`UpdateConnection` no-op :74962-74975, no re-pair possible) never dirties. Fix: in the Tag Watchdog's snapshot pass, whenever `s_tag`/`s_tagauthor`/`s_creator` on any `GetPortalList()` entry differs from the last snapshot, call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702). Alternatively a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize` filtered by `PortalPrefabHash` that dirties unconditionally — cheaper to reason about, slightly more disk churn. Also dirty after every mod write that is not a Portal-type SetConnection (creator rewrite, LoadFields keys, unique tags).
catalog.playerExperience: None visible until it matters: without the guard, a player names a portal whose partner does not exist yet, the server restarts an hour later, and the name is gone. With it, names survive restarts as players assume they do.
failureModes: Setting the flag rewrites the entire portal chunk at the next save (all portals), which is what vanilla does anyway on any pairing change — negligible.
If the watchdog runs slower than the autosave interval the edit can still be lost; dirtying in the Deserialize postfix is timing-proof.
openQuestions: IN-GAME: rename an unconnected portal on a vanilla client, force `save`, restart, confirm the name is lost without the guard and kept with it.
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData calls AddIfPortal on every applied ZDO — :77132 (verified exact)
ZDOMan.AddIfPortal early return without dirtying — :77732-77752 (verified exact, direct read confirms the bug precisely as claimed)

This exactly matches the option's citation and claim. The fix (calling ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() from a snapshot-diff or a Deserialize postfix) is a plain server-side write with no client dependency -- server-enforced is correct.

catalog.name: Boss Lockdown Correction
catalog.oneLine: NoBossPortals is only world-wide through the `activeBosses` key; the `GetBossEvent()` half is a per-client HUD read — so a server-driven boss lockdown must write `activeBosses` itself and cannot rely on event state.
catalog.howItWorks: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 3 is `NoBossPortals && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0))` (:143528). `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106950) returns `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent` — the boss whose health bar THAT client is currently showing (within `m_maxShowDistanceBoss`), null on any client not near/aggroed. So the first disjunct blocks only travellers who personally have a boss bar on screen; the second is the only genuinely world-wide term. Correction to the globalkeys brief's 'world-wide blackout': it is world-wide only via `activeBosses`, which is client-maintained (`BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27256-27262, decremented in `Character.OnDeath` :3163-3164) and can leak. A server mod that wants a deterministic lockdown sets `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("nobossportals")` and `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 1f)` (:115933-115946, broadcast via `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` :113466-113471) for the duration, and `SetGlobalKey(activeBosses, 0f)` to release; it should also watch for a stuck non-zero `activeBosses` with no boss ZDO alive (scan `Character` prefabs with `m_bossEvent` via `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative`) and zero it. Server-side strictly-enforced alternative: the Managed Network Governor unlinking all portals (SetConnection None) while a boss is engaged — enforced at gate 1 rather than honoured at gate 3. Dungeon doors read the key with a different, positional, EnemyHud-dependent test (:143355, :133631-133645) and are unaffected by `activeBosses`.
catalog.playerExperience: With the correction, a boss lockdown is consistent: every traveller everywhere gets `$msg_blockedbyboss` while the mod holds `activeBosses` ≥ 1, instead of only the players standing near the boss. Portals still look connected and glowing (gate 3 is checked only on entry).
failureModes: Client-honoured: a modified client ignores the key; use connection-nulling for enforcement.
Writing `activeBosses` fights the clients' own increments/decrements — the mod's value can be overwritten by the next boss alert/death; re-assert on a tick while locked.

`SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 1f)` stringifies as `activebosses 1`; the dedupe in RPC_SetGlobalKey is exact-string, so re-asserting the same value is a no-op only if the string matches exactly.
openQuestions: IN-GAME: with `nobossportals` set and no boss alive, set `activebosses 1` from the server and confirm a client 5 km from any boss gets `$msg_blockedbyboss`; then clear it and confirm transit resumes without relog.
evidence: TeleportWorld.Teleport boss gate — :143528 (verified exact, direct read)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] TeleportWorld.Teleport's boss gate at line 143528 was read directly and matches the citation character-for-character: 'GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (GetBossEvent()!=null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses,out v) && v>0))'. RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() (confirmed exact at 106939-106948) depends entirely on EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss() -- a per-client, proximity/aggro-gated UI concept -- validating the correction that this disjunct is NOT world-wide. BaseAI.SetAlerted's activeBosses increment (confirmed exact at ~27256-27259) and Character.OnDeath's decrement (confirmed exact at 3160-3164) confirm activeBosses is genuinely the only world-wide term, and that it is driven by client-executed AI/death logic (client-authoritative for non-server-owned monsters) rather than server logic directly -- correctly supporting the 'client-honoured' label rather than server-enforced, since the mod's own reliable path is to write activeBosses/nobossportals itself via SetGlobalKey/SendGlobalKeys (confirmed exact at 115933-115946, 113466-113471).

catalog.name: Admin Remote Command Channel
catalog.oneLine: A mod-registered `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` console command IS reachable from an admin's vanilla F5 console via `RPC_RemoteCommand` — resolving the ops catalog's self-contradiction — but it needs a server-side `TryRunCommand` prefix because the client only forwards names it already knows.
catalog.howItWorks: Client side, `Terminal.TryRunCommand` looks the first word up in ITS OWN `commands` dictionary (:45737); if found but `IsValid` fails and the command is `RemoteCommand` on a non-server, it sends `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (:45743-45746); an unknown word prints 'not a recognized command' and nothing leaves the client (:45756-45759). Server side, `RPC_RemoteCommand` is admin-gated on the socket host name (:81879-81889) and `InternalCommand` runs `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)` (:81891-81895) — `Console` is instantiated headless by `Game.Awake`. So a NEW command name never reaches the server, but an EXISTING remote-flagged vanilla command does, with its full argument string: `setkey`, `removekey`, `listkeys` are `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` (:43509-43533, :43606). A Harmony prefix on the SERVER's `Terminal.TryRunCommand(string,bool,bool)` (:45734) keyed on a reserved argument shape — e.g. `removekey tpl:<subcommand> <args>` — intercepts before the vanilla handler runs, executes the mod action, and returns false; replies go back with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, text)` (:81635) into the admin's console (the `ZRpc` must be captured from a prefix on `RPC_RemoteCommand` into the Authentic Sender Context). The admin never installs anything and never needs stdin access. Security is vanilla's adminlist check on the platform-verified host name, plus the server's own admin list for the sub-verb. This is the only text-input channel a vanilla client offers the mod; ordinary players still have only emotes/pings.
catalog.playerExperience: An admin presses F5 on an unmodified client, types `removekey tpl:transfer 1234 Bjorn`, and sees the server's reply in the same console. Non-admins get 'You are not admin'. Regular players cannot use it at all.
failureModes: Hijacking `removekey` means a genuine `removekey tpl:...` is impossible — pick a prefix no real key uses and only intercept when it matches.

If `setkey` is chosen instead, `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat` runs on the CLIENT before forwarding? No — `IsValid` fails first on a non-server (onlyServer), so it forwards; but confirm in-game that the client-side cheat check does not swallow it.
`Console.instance` headless is asserted from `Game.Awake` (:100034-100045); if it is null on some build `InternalCommand` NREs and the channel is dead.
Command length is bounded by chat/console input; keep verbs terse.
prerequisites: Authentic Sender Context (capture the ZRpc in RPC_RemoteCommand)
openQuestions: IN-GAME (decisive): from an admin vanilla client's F5 console run `listkeys` and `removekey tpl:ping`; confirm the server log shows 'Remote admin … executed command' and the prefix fires.
evidence: setkey/removekey/listkeys remoteCommand:true — :43509-43546, :43605-43639 (verified exact, direct read of all three)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Terminal.TryRunCommand (public, confirmed exact at 45734-45760, direct read) shows a command name absent from the local `commands` dictionary never leaves the client -- only an EXISTING command flagged RemoteCommand=true that fails IsValid locally gets forwarded via ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text). setkey/removekey/listkeys are all confirmed to carry remoteCommand:true (exact matches at 43509-43533 for setkey, 43535-43546 for removekey, 43605-43639 for listkeys, direct read of all three). ZNet.RemoteCommand/RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand/RemotePrint were read directly and match exactly: RPC_RemoteCommand gates on ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()) before calling InternalCommand, which runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command) on the server's own Console. This fully validates the described admin-only, vanilla-console-native command channel and correctly labels it admin-facing-only.

catalog.name: Event-Driven Localized Overrides
catalog.oneLine: The server can start a PersistentEvent at any position it chooses to apply a localized weather/effect override around a managed portal — a server-driven ambient signal (and a removable server-driven map pin) that vanilla clients honour.
catalog.howItWorks: `PersistentEventSystem.TriggerEvent(name)` resolves the event index and invokes `RequestStartEvent` on itself (:105292-105303 → :105297); the server-side handler (:105341-105379) generates a position via `PersistentEvent.GenerateEventLocation` (Inspector-driven placement rules), records an `ActivePersistentEvent{position, radius}` and broadcasts the JSON list with `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)` (:105407-105410), which every client applies (:105412-105418). Client `EnvMan` consults `GetEnvironmentOverride` for events whose radius contains the player (client :96299-96303), and `Minimap` draws persistent-event pins from the same list (client :57505-57545) — pins that disappear when the server calls `StopEvent` (:105305-105339 → `RPC_RequestStopEvent` :105381-105389 → broadcast). Because the mod runs ON the server, it can bypass `GenerateEventLocation` entirely: construct the `ActivePersistentEvent` with the portal's position and a chosen radius, append it to `m_activePersistentEvents.list` (public field :105073), bump `m_eventIdCounter` (private, reflection), and call the private `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)`. Durations are honoured by the 30 s server sweep (:105209-105235); `duration < 0` is permanent until stopped. The list is saved with the world (:105237-105248). Use: mark a locked hub with the event's weather/effect (which effects exist is Inspector data on `m_possibleEvents`), or use the removable pin as a 'this portal is currently routed here' marker — the one server-driven pin type the server can also take away, correcting the ux brief's 'no way to remove a pushed pin'.
catalog.playerExperience: Approaching a hub that the admin has flagged, the player sees the event's ambient effect (snow, fog — whatever the chosen event carries) begin inside the radius, and a matching event pin on the map that vanishes when the admin clears the flag. It reads as a world event, not as a UI message.
failureModes: Which weather/effects/pins are available depends entirely on `m_possibleEvents` Inspector data; if the list is empty on the server build nothing can be started.
Events also spawn their `objectsToSpawn` server-side via `Object.Instantiate` (:105033) when started through the vanilla handler — bypass the handler to avoid that.
Clients apply the JSON blindly; a malformed struct from reflection breaks every client's event list until the next valid broadcast.
Unrelated to access enforcement — purely a signalling surface.
prerequisites: Extended RPC Veto Table (so clients cannot forge the same list)
openQuestions: IN-GAME: dump `PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_possibleEvents` (internalName, environmentOverride, radius bounds) on the dedicated server; confirm at least one event carries a usable override and that a hand-built ActivePersistentEvent broadcast renders an ambient effect and a map pin on a vanilla client, and that StopEvent removes both.

verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] PersistentEventSystem's TriggerEvent/RPC_RequestStartEvent/StopEvent/RPC_RequestStopEvent/UpdateClientEventsList were all read directly and match exactly (see Extended RPC Veto Table verification, same class). In the CLIENT decompile, EnvMan's environment-override chain calls PersistentEventSystem.instance.GetEnvironmentOverride() (confirmed exact at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:96299), and Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins (confirmed exact at 57505-57541, direct read) draws pins directly from PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_activePersistentEvents.list and REMOVES a pin the moment its eventId disappears from that list -- this directly confirms the option's important correction that this is 'the one server-driven pin type the server can also take away,' unlike RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins. m_activePersistentEvents.list being a public field the server can append to directly (bypassing GenerateEventLocation) is architecturally sound given the confirmed class layout.

catalog.name: Pre-Stream Engine (Server-Initiated Destination Streaming)
catalog.oneLine: A postfix on ZDOMan.CreateSyncList appends the destination zone's ZDOs to the sync list of any peer standing near a managed portal, so the traveller holds the arrival area before stepping in — no client request, no client mod.
catalog.howItWorks: The private ZDOMan.CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer peer, List<ZDO> toSync) (:77212-77261) is the only place the server decides what a peer receives: on the server branch it runs FindSectorObjects around peer.m_peer.GetRefPos() (:77216-77220), filters by peer.ShouldSend (:77223), sorts (:77228), adds the distant ring only if fewer than 10 near objects remain (:77229-77238), then inserts force-sends at the head (:77239, AddForceSendZdos :77263-77286). SendZDOs (:77008-77074) then serializes entries in order until zPackage.Size() exceeds the budget num = 10240 - socket.GetSendQueueSize() (:77015, :77047-77050). TortalPortal's SectorSubscription.ZDOMan_CreateSyncList_Postfix (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/SectorSubscription.cs:106-197) is a shipped, live-tested postfix on exactly this method; it is driven by a client RPC, but nothing in the postfix needs one — the subscription table is plain server state. The Lite engine replaces the RPC with policy: every OnUpdate tick (0.25 s), for each ConnectedCharacter (Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:56) compute the nearest managed portal from ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643); if within PreStreamRadius (default 20 m) and the portal's Portal connection resolves, record Subs[peer.m_uid] = {destPos, expires = now + 5 s}. The postfix, for a subscribed peer, (a) skips when the destination zone lies inside the peer's own near ring (Chebyshev |Δzone| ≤ peer.m_peer.m_simulationDistance.NearSimulationDistance, defaulting to 2 while the handshake value is still (0,0) — SectorSubscription.cs:130-146); (b) calls FindSectorObjects(destZone, new SimulationDistance(near, far, classic:true), tmp, tmpDistant) (:77142); (c) appends every ZDO with peer.ShouldSend(zdo) true — first pass sends the whole area, subsequent passes send only revision bumps, exactly as if the peer were standing there. Because the postfix runs after AddForceSendZdos, appended entries are lowest priority; a peer idling next to a portal has a near-empty own list, so the appended set gets almost the full 10 KB budget each cycle (≈200 KB/s ceiling per peer at one cycle per 0.05 s+N frames, :76843-76861). Per-peer byte budget: the engine caps its own contribution by tracking bytes since last cycle via ZDO.Serialize into a scratch ZPackage (cheap) or, simpler, by capping appended count (default 400 ZDOs/cycle) and letting SendZDOs' size break do the rest. Two knobs the gap asked about, read this pass: ZDO.Type = Prioritized only matters INSIDE ServerSortSendZDOS (:77288-77309, requires HasOwner && owner != receiver) — force-sends and the postfix bypass sorting entirely, so it is irrelevant to pre-streamed data; ZDO.Distant is meaningless for portals (FindDistantObjects reads only m_objectsBySector :77391) and only helps a NON-portal anchor 3-4 zones out when the near list is already drained (:77229). Neither is a lever; the postfix is.
catalog.playerExperience: The player walks toward a managed portal. Nothing visible changes for the first second; in the background their client is receiving the destination base. By the time they reach the 5 m glow ring the destination portal ZDO is already held, so the portal lights up on the first 0.5 s UpdatePortal poll instead of after a RequestZDO round-trip, and the walk-through never dead-fires. On arrival the black screen ends closer to the 8 s floor than the 15 s fallback because IsAreaReady's instance loop (:82074-82079) has all the ZDOs locally and only has to instantiate them at 100/frame (:82096-82098). A player who turns away before entering simply stops receiving after the 5 s expiry; the ZDOs they already got stay in their client for the session (no client eviction path) at a memory cost identical to having walked there once.
failureModes: Budget starvation: appended ZDOs are last in toSync, so a peer whose own area is churning (combat, a raid, building) may never get to them; mitigate by inserting at index (count of force-sends) instead of appending, or by adding ids to peer.m_forceSend (which Insert(0)s at :77275) for the destination portal itself and the ring's first 50 ZDOs.

Wasted bandwidth: a player who loiters at a portal without entering streams the whole destination every time they re-enter the radius; ShouldSend makes re-passes nearly free, but the first pass of a 3000-piece base is ~450 KB — gate on 'approaching' (position delta toward the portal over two samples) not merely 'within radius'.

Ungenerated destination: a zone nobody has visited has no vegetation/location ZDOs at all; the client's own PokeLocalZone runs in SpawnMode.Client and never generates them (:114028), so the traveller arrives on bald terrain — pair with the Destination Zone Ghost Pre-Generation option.

ZDOPeer is a private nested class and CreateSyncList is private: the patch needs the BepInEx publicizer (Wonderland.csproj already sets <Publicize>true</Publicize>); an unpublicized build compiles nothing.

The postfix runs on every send cycle for every peer; keep the subscription lookup a Dictionary<long,Sub> hit and return immediately when Subs.Count == 0 (SectorSubscription.cs:109), or the cost lands on every peer every 0.05 s.

Ownership side-effect: pre-streamed ZDOs are recorded in peer.m_zdos but ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) still only assigns ownership by refPos, so nothing at the destination becomes the traveller's until they physically arrive — correct, but it means a moving anchor's revision bumps must keep flowing through the postfix (they do, via ShouldSend) rather than being assumed synced.
prerequisites: A managed-portal registry (which portal ZDOIDs the mod routes) so the engine knows which portals to arm
BepInEx publicizer for ZDOMan.ZDOPeer / ZDOMan.CreateSyncList / ZoneSystem.SpawnZone
Optionally: Destination Zone Ghost Pre-Generation for never-visited destinations
Optionally: Peer Link Probe for a per-peer lead-time budget

catalog.name: Join-Time Portal Registry Broadcast
catalog.oneLine: At the end of ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo, ForceSendZDO every portal ZDO (and every managed void anchor) to the new peer — one small burst that makes TeleportWorld.TargetFound true for every static destination for the rest of the session.
catalog.howItWorks: Vanilla has no 'send all portals on join' path: ZDOMan.AddPeer (:76767-76773) only registers the ZDOData handler, and the first sync list is whatever FindSectorObjects returns around the refPos the client reported in its PeerInfo packet (:79904, used at :77216). Portals are excluded from the distant ring outright (:77391), so a joining player holds exactly the portals within their near ring and nothing else. Because a vanilla client never discards a received ZDO (only HandleDestroyedZDO removes, and ZNetScene.RemoveObjects only destroys instances :82196-82227), a single push at join is permanent for that session. Mechanism: a Harmony postfix on ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo in the exact shape of Wonderland's PeerJoinLeaveHook.OnPeerInfo (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:26-46, resolves the ZNetPeer via the private ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) and requires m_playerName non-empty so rejected handshakes never fire). At that point m_zdoMan.AddPeer(peer) has already run (:79942), so ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, id) (:77714-77719) is valid immediately. Iterate ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList() (:77648) plus the mod's managed-anchor ZDOIDs and call ForceSendZDO for each. AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77286) then Insert(0)s all of them at the head of the peer's next sync list; because the peer has never seen them, ShouldSend is true (:76013) and every one lands. Cost: N_portals × ~100-160 bytes (uid 12 + revisions 6 + owner 8 + pos 12 + serialized prefab/rotation/connection/two strings); 300 portals ≈ 40 KB ≈ 4 send cycles at the head of the queue, delaying the player's own area by ~0.2-0.3 s during a load screen they are already looking at. Maintenance: portals placed after join are delivered only if in range; add a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589, runs every 5 s) that diffs GetPortalList() against the last snapshot and ForceSendZDO(0-arg broadcast, :77706-77712) any new ZDOID — or hook the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize pair (Wonderland SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70) and push on prefab ∈ Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash. Destroyed portals need no work: SendDestroyed broadcasts DestroyZDO to every peer (:76937-76951). Important limit: this satisfies TargetFound (position + rotation + existence) for STATIC destinations; a far peer's copy is frozen at join-time revision and is only refreshed by another force-send after a real DataRevision bump — see Revision-Bump Redelivery. Persistent per-session memory on the client grows by the portal count, negligible.
catalog.playerExperience: The player logs in and sees the normal loading screen; the burst is invisible. From then on, every portal in the world — including ones the server re-pairs a hub to while they stand next to it — lights up on the first 0.5 s poll and never dead-fires, even if they sprint straight into the trigger. Portals built by other players after they logged in also light up within ≤5 s of being paired. There is no UX cost and nothing to explain.
failureModes: Silent no-op if the postfix fires before ZDOMan.AddPeer: it cannot in 1.0.7 (AddPeer at :79942 precedes the method's return), but a version reorder would make GetPeer(peerID) return null in ForceSendZDO (:77718) and drop every id — assert ZDOMan.instance.GetPeer-equivalent non-null by checking the peer appears in a later SendZDOs, or re-issue the push from the first Heartbeat tick after join.

Respawn/relog do not reset the client's ZDO table, but a client that crashed mid-download and reconnects gets a fresh peer object and a fresh push — fine; the only hole is a client whose download was cut by the 10240-byte cap while its own area was saturated: AddForceSendZdos keeps ids in m_forceSend until sent (removed only at :77051 when actually serialized), so they drain over later cycles — no loss, just delay.

A managed anchor with an unknown non-zero prefab hash logs 'Missing prefab hash' on the client every frame it sits in the near area (:82006); void anchors must use prefab 0 (silent :81999-82002) or a real harmless prefab.
Does nothing for ZDOs whose position later changes (moving anchors) or whose tag the mod rewrites for display — the far peer keeps the join-time copy until a new force-send after a revision bump.
prerequisites: A managed-anchor ZDOID list if the mod fabricates anchors
Revision-Bump Redelivery for anything that changes after the push

Game.ConnectPortals is confirmed public (:100589) as cited, consistent with prior HANDOFF note (the three PRIVATE members are SetConnection/ForceSetConnection/RPC_SetConnection, not ConnectPortals). This is a pure server-side push with no client consent step — 'server-enforced' correctly describes the data-delivery mechanism, and the option correctly distinguishes it from a permission gate (it never claims to control who may pass, only what a client holds).

catalog.name: DestinationPrewarm (Event-Driven Per-Write Push)
catalog.oneLine: Every managed connection write, every approach, every anchor revision bump and every respawn re-pushes the destination ZDO to the peers that are about to need it, so a server-side re-point is never followed by a silent dead walk-through.
catalog.howItWorks: The Join-Time broadcast covers static portals; Prewarm covers change. Define a single function Prewarm(destId, IEnumerable<peerUid>) = for each uid: ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(uid, destId) (:77714-77719), which enqueues into that peer's m_forceSend (:75998-76001) and is Insert(0)'d at the head of its next sync list (:77275) — provided ShouldSend is true (:77273). Trigger set: (T1) on every managed SetConnection(Portal, destId) write, Prewarm(destId, peers whose character ZDO is within PrewarmRadius (default 30 m) of the SOURCE portal) — the player who is standing in the glow ring when the hub rotates is exactly the one the 0.5 s poll (:143507) will not rescue in time if they step in immediately, and a player carrying ore is never polled at all (flag2 false). (T2) on approach: the same 0.25 s watcher the Pre-Stream Engine uses fires Prewarm(destId, {peer}) when a character enters PrewarmRadius of any managed portal; cheaper than full pre-streaming, and enough for the TargetFound gate alone. (T3) on anchor motion: for a destination that is a moving ZDO (ship, player, a server-repositioned void anchor) the far traveller's copy is stale; each mod tick compare ZDOMan.GetZDO(destId).DataRevision against the peer's held revision (ZDOPeer.m_zdos[destId].m_dataRevision, :75965 via the publicized ZDOMan.m_peers :76041) and Prewarm when it differs — because ShouldSend is the same compare, an unconditional ForceSendZDO per tick is also safe and costs nothing when current, but the explicit compare avoids filling m_forceSend with ids that AddForceSendZdos then prunes every cycle. (T4) on respawn: the character ZDO is destroyed on death and recreated (Game._RequestRespawn :100403-100417), but the peer's ZDO table is untouched, so no re-push is needed — include only if the mod ever peer-targets a DestroyZDO revocation. (T5) on managed anchor creation: Prewarm(anchorId, all peers) once, then rely on T3. Budget: each prewarm is one ZDO (~150 B) per peer; even a 20-peer server rotating a hub every 30 s is <1 KB/s. The 10240-byte cap (:77010-77019) only matters for T3 on many moving anchors: cap at one re-push per anchor per 0.5 s. Verification hook: after T1, the mod can confirm delivery by polling ZDOPeer.m_zdos.ContainsKey(destId) (:75981) before it toasts 'portal ready' — see Held-ZDO Ledger Readiness Gate.
catalog.playerExperience: A player standing at a hub watches the server rotate its destination (announce → re-point). The glow flickers off for one poll and back on within ~0.5-1 s instead of staying dark until they walk out and back in; walking in immediately after the announcement always teleports. For moving-anchor routes the player arriving 'behind the ship' lands as close as the 8 s hold allows rather than at where the ship was minutes ago. No visible artefact of the mechanism itself.
failureModes: ForceSendZDO is revision-gated (:77273): a re-push of an unchanged destination sends nothing — correct, but a mod that rewrote the destination's tag WITHOUT a revision bump (ZDO.Set on an unchanged value no-ops, BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue false) will see 'prewarm sent, client still stale'; bump DataRevision explicitly when a resend is required (Revision-Bump Redelivery).

PrewarmRadius too small for a sprinting player: server sees the character position ~50-100 ms + RTT/2 late (client CreateSyncList drains m_clientChangeQueue every 0.05 s :77243-77258) and the push takes RTT/2 + one cycle; at 7 m/s and 150 ms RTT a 10 m radius leaves ~1.2 s — fine; a 5 m radius (the glow ring) leaves ~0.4 s — marginal.

T3 on a fast-moving ship pushes the ship ZDO (large, many fields) to a far peer every 0.5 s ≈ 1-2 KB/s per traveller; acceptable for a handful, not for a whole server watching one ship — rate-limit per anchor, not per peer.
A peer between connect and character spawn has m_characterID None and no position; T2/T3 skip it, T1 must not (they may spawn inside the ring) — use peer.m_refPos as the fallback position for T1.
