catalog.name: Fast-Transit Mode (distant:false Server Teleport)
catalog.oneLine: A parked terminal whose walk-through is answered by a server-sent RPC_TeleportTo with distantTeleport:false — a ~2-4 s fade instead of vanilla's ≥8 s swirl — made safe by pre-streaming, ghost pre-generation and a server-side floor check, with distant:true as the fallback.
catalog.howItWorks: Timing is set by Player.UpdateTeleport (:15329-15379): the transform moves at t>2 s (:15338-15348); a distant teleport then waits until t>8 s AND ZNetScene.IsAreaReady (:15349); a non-distant one waits only for IsAreaReady, then completes on the first successful ZoneSystem.FindFloor (:15354-15359). The 8 s floor is unreachable for vanilla portal transits because TeleportWorld.Teleport hard-codes distantTeleport:true (:143546). The only way to get distant:false is to not let the portal teleport at all and have the server do it: (1) the terminal's Portal connection is kept ZDOID.None (a mod-reserved unique tag makes FindRandomUnconnectedPortal return null every 5 s, :100664-100679), so TeleportWorldTrigger → Teleport returns silently at gate 1 (:143519); (2) a 0.1-0.25 s watcher compares each ConnectedCharacter's ZDO position with the terminal's position and, inside TriggerRadius (default 1.2 m XZ, ±1.5 m Y), sends ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", exitPos, exitRot, false) (Character.RPC_TeleportTo :4126-4132, owner-gated; registered on every Character :886); (3) exitPos = destZdo.GetPosition() + destZdo.GetRotation()*Vector3.forward*1f + Vector3.up, mirroring :143542-143545. Safety gate before choosing distant:false: (a) the destination zone must be server-generated (ZoneSystem.IsZoneGenerated, private :115869) — otherwise the client's PokeLocalZone (SpawnMode.Client :114028) spawns bald terrain and the arrival looks broken; run Destination Zone Ghost Pre-Generation first and fall back to distant:true this time; (b) exitPos.y must be ≥ WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x,z) (:151944) — FindFloor raycasts DOWN from p+1 (:115604) and never hits from inside terrain, and a distant:false FindFloor miss REVERTS the player to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' (:15360-15374) instead of force-landing; (c) the peer must already hold the destination ZDO and, ideally, the arrival ring (Pre-Stream Engine) — otherwise IsAreaReady stalls and the 2 s advantage evaporates; (d) never within 2 s of a previous teleport: TeleportTo returns false when m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15313), the cooldown is zeroed on accept (:15320) and held at 0 for the whole teleport (:15336), and a fresh Player object starts at 0 (:9907). The watcher keeps firing every tick while the player remains inside TriggerRadius — rejected RPCs (IsTeleporting/cooldown) are silent no-ops, so the loop is idempotent and self-clears when the position jumps. Client-local floor: ~2 s timer + destination zone spawn (one zone per 0.1 s tick, CreateLocalZones :113993-114012, HeightmapBuilder thread :129676-129678) + instantiation at 100/frame during the loading screen (:82096-82098) ≈ 3-5 s on a warm client, versus ≥8 s vanilla.
catalog.playerExperience: The player walks into a terminal that shows '$piece_portal_unconnected' on hover and has no glow (HaveTarget false). The screen fades to black over ~1 s (Hud.GetFadeDuration 1 s :47850) with NO swirl panel — Hud only shows m_teleportingProgress when ShowTeleportAnimation is true, i.e. distant (:47872-47877, :15386-15393) — the same look as a crypt door. About 2-4 s later they are standing at the destination. If the server chose the fallback, they get the ordinary swirl and the ordinary 8 s. If the safety gate is wrong (exit inside a cliff), they are dumped back where they started with a misleading 'portal blocked' message. Ore in inventory passes through — nothing checks it.
failureModes: Bypasses every vanilla gate: NoPortals, NoBossPortals, IsTeleportable (ore) and PrivateArea are all inside TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143523-143537) which never runs; the mod can re-implement the global-key gates server-side but can NEVER reproduce the item check (player inventories are not in any ZDO).

'$msg_portal_blocked' revert on FindFloor miss: exit inside terrain (terraformed after build), inside a building piece (piece layer is in m_solidRayMask :113424 and rays from inside a collider do not hit), or over an unbuilt Heightmap edge; the WorldGenerator pre-check is blind to terraforming and pieces — expose a per-terminal 'force distant' override and auto-flip a terminal to distant:true after one observed revert (server sees the position snap back).

Retag by a vanilla client turns the parked terminal into a paired vanilla portal (RPC_SetTag goes to the ZDO owner, a nearby client); the trigger then fires vanilla's distant teleport first and the server's RPC is rejected by IsTeleporting — behaviour degrades to vanilla, not to breakage; a tag re-assert tick (write s_tag + SetDirtyPortals + ForceSendZDO) restores it.

Approach lag: the server reads the position ~50-100 ms + RTT/2 late; a sprinting player is 0.5-1 m past the trigger point when the RPC lands — irrelevant for a teleport, but TriggerRadius must be larger than the visual portal opening or a fast player can run straight through without being caught; default 1.2 m + 0.3 m per 50 ms of measured RTT (Peer Link Probe).

Cooldown dead zone: a player who chains two fast terminals within 2 s of arrival gets nothing on the second until 2 s has accrued — the retry loop covers it if they stand still, but they will see a ~2 s 'nothing happens' pause.

Two players entering the same terminal in the same tick each get their own RPC with their own destination — this is the ONE transit design with no contention, at the cost of the portal's own mechanism.
prerequisites: Parked Terminal — Server-Teleport Portal (the base mechanism; this option is its distant:false timing variant)
Pre-Stream Engine and DestinationPrewarm (so IsAreaReady clears early and TargetFound is moot)
Destination Zone Ghost Pre-Generation (zone must be server-generated before a distant:false hop)
Peer Link Probe for TriggerRadius/lead-time sizing
Tag protection for managed terminals (reserved tag re-assert)

This is server-initiated (push), not a client-triggered permission gate, so it passes the honest-enforcement test distinctly from vanilla's un-hookable trigger-volume path.

catalog.name: Character-State Predicates for JIT Routing
catalog.oneLine: Extend approach-triggered routing from 'who is approaching' to 'what state are they in' using the dozen server-readable bits on the character ZDO — PvP flag, crown, bed, death, equipped gear, stealth, health, blocking, velocity — so an arena gate parks unless everyone in the ring is PvP-on, or a 'no armour' gate parks when s_chestItem != 0.
catalog.howItWorks: Every predicate is a plain ZDO read on ZDOMan.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID), refreshed by the owning client's normal ZDO push (≤0.05 s + RTT/2). Verified writers: s_pvp — Player.SetPVP (:15558-15563), driven each InventoryGui refresh from the PvP toggle (:50431-50432), read by IsPVPEnabled (:15555); s_crowned — Player.SetCrownMode (:13888-13895), read InCrownMode (:13907); s_inBed — AttachStart/AttachStop (:15799, :15917), read IsAttached path (:15887); s_dead — OnDeath/OnRespawn (:12734, :12866), IsDead (:15244); equipped visuals — VisEquipment writes prefab stable hashes to s_leftItem (:20569), s_rightItem (:20590), s_chestItem (:20632), s_helmetItem (:20656) and the leg/shoulder/utility/back slots (:20644-20708), 0 when empty; s_stealth — Player.UpdateStealth writes the lerped stealth factor every ≥0.5 s while crouching and drives it toward 1.0 when not (:16347-16373), so 'sneaking' = s_stealth < 0.99; s_health/s_maxHealth — Character.SetHealth/SetMaxHealth (:3195, :3229); s_isBlockingHash (:8690-8708); s_bodyVelocity (:4139); s_baseValue comfort (:11401); s_noise (:3971). Predicate evaluation runs inside the existing JIT watcher: for each managed gate with a predicate P, on each 0.25 s tick collect the characters within ArmingRadius; if P holds for ALL of them (arena: every s_pvp true; challenge: every s_chestItem == 0 && s_helmetItem == 0 …), write the gate's real destination (SetOwner(session) → SetConnection(Portal, dest) → ForceSendZDO, Game.SetConnection recipe :100637-100651) and DestinationPrewarm it; otherwise write ZDOID.None (parked) and PlayerNotify.Toast the offender with the reason. Because the decision lands in the shared portal ZDO, two players with different states in the ring collide exactly as JIT does — the predicate must be 'all-in-ring' (conservative) or the gate must be a Parked Terminal with per-player RPC teleports (contention-free, but bypasses vanilla gates). Lead-time budget is JIT's: the arming radius must cover poll interval + client push lag + RTT + one send cycle at sprint speed (≈ (0.25 + 0.1 + RTT) × 7 m/s ≈ 3-4 m) plus the 5 m glow ring so the player sees the portal light up before they reach it. A parked gate shows '$piece_portal_unconnected' and no glow — the honest vanilla signal for 'you may not enter'.
catalog.playerExperience: Arena gate: a PvP-off player walks up; the portal stays dark and the hover says unconnected; a toast reads 'Arena gate: enable PvP (inventory) to enter'. They flip the toggle; within ~0.5 s the portal glows and they walk through. If a second, PvP-off player steps into the ring beside them, the gate goes dark for both until the second player leaves or toggles — the all-in-ring rule is visible and legible. Challenge gate: a player in armour sees the same dark portal with 'remove all armour to enter'; stripping to no chest/legs/helmet lights it. Crown gate (s_crowned): a novelty 'only the crowned may pass'. Bed/dead predicates are guards, not gates: a player with s_inBed true is never routed (forced teleports of attached players ping-pong; vanilla walk-through is impossible while attached anyway).
failureModes: Gear predicates see only VisEquipment slots (weapons, armour, utility, back slots, hair/beard) — not backpack contents; 'no weapons' means 'nothing equipped', a player can carry a sword and equip it after arrival.
s_pvp cannot be switched within 10 s of combat (CanSwitchPVP :15575-15578, toggle greyed at :50431), so a player who just fought at the gate cannot comply for 10 s — toast the reason.

s_stealth is a lerp updated on a 0.5 s timer and is written only when it changes (:16371-16373); a player who has never crouched has no s_stealth key at all (GetFloat default 0f) — treat missing as 'not sneaking' explicitly, not as 0 = fully hidden.

All predicates are client-authored (ZDO data from the owning client, unvalidated by RPC_ZDOData :77076-77139); a modified client can assert s_pvp true while ignoring PvP damage — these gates are honesty-level, same tier as vanilla's own PvP flag.

Shared-ZDO contention: two players with different states in one ring flap the gate every tick if the rule is 'any'; use 'all' (parks) or per-player RPC teleports (Parked Terminal) — never 'the nearest wins' without a hold timer.

VisEquipment slot writes for shoulder/back/trinket branch on the prefab's m_isPlayer Inspector flag (:20857-20885 read-back) — which slots a real Player reliably writes is an in-game check; chest/legs/helmet/right/left are unconditional.

This is a genuine 'should this ROUTE be open' pattern (writing the shared portal's connection field based on server-readable predicates), not a 'should this player pass' pattern — it passes the honest-enforcement test cleanly, since a vanilla client has no way to teleport through a connection ZDOID.None (TeleportWorld gate-1, independently confirmed above).

catalog.name: Parked Terminal — Server-Teleport Portal
catalog.oneLine: Keep a managed portal permanently unconnected and let a server-side proximity watcher perform the transit with RPC_TeleportTo — per-player destinations with zero contention, at the price of every vanilla portal gate.
catalog.howItWorks: The routing catalog's JIT and Player-Requested options all route by writing the shared portal ZDO's single connection slot, which is why they inherit two-player contention. This option never touches the slot: the terminal's Portal connection is ZDOID.None, so vanilla's trigger path exits silently at TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (:143519-143522) and the portal is inert. A unique reserved tag (any length — no cap on server writes; RPC_SetTag/GetTagInfo apply none) keeps Game.ConnectPortals from ever pairing it (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null for a tag with no other member, :100664-100679), and the mod re-asserts the tag each tick if a client retags it. A 0.1-0.25 s watcher (Wonderland PositionWatch scaffold, Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31, sampled faster) tests each ConnectedCharacter's ZDO position against every terminal's position (TriggerRadius ≈ 1.2 m XZ, |Δy| < 1.5 m). On entry it resolves THAT PLAYER's destination — from the player's own request state (ping/emote/item-stand selection), a per-player home table, a schedule, or a predicate — and sends ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", exitPos, exitRot, distant) (handler Character.RPC_TeleportTo :4126-4132, owner-gated, registered on every Character :886; the peer-scoped Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962-41968 is the Chat-dependent alternative). distant:true reproduces the exact vanilla feel (swirl, ≥8 s, force-land at 15 s :15360-15367); distant:false is the Fast-Transit variant. The watcher keeps sending each tick while the player remains inside the radius; TeleportTo rejects while IsTeleporting or within the 2 s cooldown (:15309-15316) with no side effect, so duplicates are harmless and the loop self-terminates when the position jumps. Pre-conditions read off the character ZDO: skip s_dead (UpdateTeleport never runs for a dead player :10213-10226 — the teleport would latch) and s_inBed (UpdateAttach re-snaps the transform every tick before UpdateTeleport :10217/:10226). The destination need not be a portal at all — any coordinate the server validates with WorldGenerator (:151944) — and the traveller needs to hold NO destination ZDO, because RPC_TeleportTo carries raw coordinates: the TargetFound gate does not exist on this path. Ownership: the terminal ZDO's owner is irrelevant (the server never writes it after setup), so ReleaseNearbyZDOS churn is harmless.
catalog.playerExperience: The terminal always reads '$piece_portal_unconnected' on hover and never glows — a visible tell that this is 'a different kind of portal'; a Sign next to it (server-writable s_text) or a hover-adjacent DamageText/toast carries the destination name. The player walks in; the ordinary black screen and swirl follow (distant:true) and they arrive wherever the server decided for THEM — two players stepping in together go to two different places. Ore travels. NoPortals lockdowns do not stop it. A player who is dead-tired, seated or in a bed gets a toast instead of a teleport.
failureModes: Every vanilla gate is bypassed: NoPortals/$msg_blocked, NoBossPortals, IsTeleportable (ore/metal), PrivateArea — all live inside TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143523-143537) which never runs. The global-key gates can be re-implemented server-side; the item gate cannot (inventories are never in a ZDO), so this design is incompatible with any 'no ore through portals' ruleset.

No 'ready' glow and no m_connected effect: m_target_found is driven by HaveTarget/TargetFound (:143496-143507) which are false on a parked portal; the only cue the mod can add is a SpawnObject VFX on approach (routed 'SpawnObject' :81954) or a DamageText/Message.
Retag by a client re-pairs it as a vanilla portal until the tag re-assert lands; during that window the vanilla transit fires first and wins.

Position-based trigger vs collider-based: the server cannot see the TeleportWorldTrigger volume (Inspector data); a TriggerRadius that is too small lets sprinters run through untouched, too large teleports players who merely brushed past the frame — tune in-game per prefab.

Forced teleports are an ~8 s invulnerable input lockout (CanMove false :14423-14428, damage suppressed while IsTeleporting); a terminal that fires on any approach is a griefing surface — only fire on a deliberate entry (inside the frame, moving inward).

catalog.name: Destination Zone Ghost Pre-Generation
catalog.oneLine: Before routing anyone to a never-visited destination, have the server ghost-generate the destination zone ring itself (SpawnZone Ghost) so vegetation and location ZDOs exist and can be pre-streamed — otherwise a vanilla client arrives on bald terrain.
catalog.howItWorks: World content is created exactly once per zone, in SpawnMode.Ghost or Full, by whichever process first generates it; a CLIENT on a dedicated server only ever runs PokeLocalZone in SpawnMode.Client (:114028), which instantiates the terrain prefab but skips PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation/PlaceZoneCtrl (gated on Ghost||Full && !IsZoneGenerated :114086-114105). Vanilla relies on the server's ZoneSystem.Update (0.1 s :113925) calling CreateGhostZones(peer.GetRefPos()) for every peer (:113935-113938), one zone per tick (returns after the first SpawnZone that succeeds :113974-113987), and only after the peer's refPos has moved there (reported every 2 s :80337-80362). So a portal into wilderness delivers the traveller before the zone exists; they see empty ground fill in over the following seconds, and pre-streaming has nothing to stream. Fix: a PreGen engine that, when a managed route is written (or a phantom anchor fabricated), enqueues the destination zone ring and drains it: each server tick call the private ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones(destPos) (:113971-113991) — it generates at most one zone per call and returns false when the ring is complete — or iterate the ring explicitly with IsZoneGenerated/SpawnZone(zone, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _) exactly as TortalPortal does inside its postfix (SectorSubscription.cs:158-171). SpawnZone first asks HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady (:114075), which queues the build on its worker thread and returns false until done (:129879-129900, thread :129676-129678); the engine simply retries next tick. On success SpawnZone instantiates the zone prefab, places locations/vegetation (creating persistent ZDOs), destroys every GameObject (:114094-114103) and marks the zone generated (:114104, persisted in m_generatedZones :113276). Ring size: the peer's simulation ring at arrival is NearSimulationDistance (2 default) — generate the 5×5 (or disc) around the destination zone; ghost generation is the same work the server would do when the player arrives, just earlier. Side effect to know: SpawnLocation ends with SnapToGround.SnappAll(), a global drain (documented at SectorSubscription.cs:165-170) — harmless on the server. Budget: one zone per tick, so a 25-zone ring takes ≥25 ticks plus heightmap build time; start it at route-write time, not at approach time.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible when it works: the player arrives in wilderness that already has trees, rocks, a crypt entrance, spawners — exactly as if someone had walked there. Without it, a vanilla client arriving via a server-written route to raw wilderness sees flat terrain with objects popping in over 2-5 s as the server catches up on its refPos report. Combined with the Pre-Stream Engine the arrival ring is complete on the client before the black screen lifts.
failureModes: Never call SpawnZone with SpawnMode.Full on the server — Full keeps the instantiated GameObjects alive in the server scene at real coordinates and breaks the 'server instantiates nothing' invariant that every other option relies on; Ghost destroys them in the same call.

Location placement: a zone whose LocationInstance is unplaced blocks SpawnZone until PokeCanSpawnLocation succeeds (:114080-114084) — a destination inside a not-yet-loadable location prefab can stall the queue; time out per zone and log.

HeightmapBuilder is shared with the server's own ghost generation for peers; a large pre-gen queue (a seasonal swap of 40 destinations × 25 zones) competes for the build thread — cap to one destination ring at a time.
m_generatedZones is saved with the world (:113736); a crash before save regenerates the ring on next boot — harmless, deterministic seed.
Does nothing for zones already generated; skip via IsZoneGenerated to avoid pointless SpawnZone calls.

This narrows, but does not invalidate, the option's value — it should say so explicitly rather than implying every non-portal destination needs manual pre-generation.

catalog.name: Peer Link Probe (RTT and Queue Budget)
catalog.oneLine: Measure each peer's RTT with vanilla's own RPC_Ping/RPC_Pong (a Harmony prefix on Game.RPC_Pong) and its socket backlog with GetSendQueueSize, and turn them into per-peer lead-time and byte budgets for JIT, pre-stream and fast-transit.
catalog.howItWorks: Game.Start registers RPC_Ping and RPC_Pong on EVERY peer, not inside the IsServer block (:100065-100066). The client handler is `RPC_Ping(long sender, float time) => InvokeRoutedRPC(sender, "RPC_Pong", time)` (:100877-100880) — it echoes whatever float it was given back to the routed sender. The server therefore sends ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_Ping", Time.time) and its own Game.RPC_Pong(long sender, float time) (:100882-100894) runs on return, computing Time.time - time and logging 'Got ping reply from server: N ms' (the string is written for the client case; the number is the server's RTT to that peer). A Harmony prefix on the private Game.RPC_Pong captures (sender, time) → Rtt[sender] = Time.time - time; sender is the client's self-reported m_senderPeerID, which for this purpose is fine (a spoofed sender only corrupts that peer's own budget). Probe cadence 10 s per peer, EMA-smoothed. Do NOT use ZRpc.GetTimeSinceLastPing (:83896): ZRpc's 1 s ping/pong (:83862-83893) resets m_timeSinceLastPing on every pong, so it is a liveness sawtooth, not a latency. Socket backlog: ISocket.GetSendQueueSize (:71836) — on Steam it sums the mod-side send queue plus Steam's pending reliable/unreliable/unacked bytes via the game-server API (ZSteamSocket :86574-86600) — is exactly the number SendZDOs subtracts from 10240 (:77010-77015); a peer whose queue sits >8 KB for several cycles is bandwidth-bound and pre-stream contributions should be throttled. ISocket.GetConnectionQuality (:71852) would give Steam's m_nPing directly, but ZSteamSocket's implementation (:86627-86648) calls the CLIENT-side SteamNetworkingSockets interface (:86641) whereas every other server-build call uses SteamGameServerNetworkingSockets (:86595, :86615) — on a dedicated server expect zeros; treat as an in-game check, not a source. Derived budgets: JitLeadMeters = (pollInterval + 0.1 + Rtt) × SprintSpeed (≈7 m/s, Inspector m_runSpeed) + TriggerRadius; PreStreamSecondsNeeded = destinationBytes / min(200 KB/s, observed drain); FastTransitAllowed = Rtt < 250 ms && queue < 4 KB. Also useful for ops: a per-peer 'link quality' line in the Heartbeat summary.
catalog.playerExperience: None directly. Indirectly: a high-latency player's arena gate arms a few metres earlier, their pre-stream starts sooner, and they are steered to the distant:true fallback instead of a fast hop that would stall — they see fewer 'portal did nothing' moments than a naive fixed budget would give them.
failureModes: Game.RPC_Pong on the server also runs vanilla's log/Console/Chat print (:100886-100893) — Console.instance exists headless (Game.Awake instantiates it :100038-100041) so it prints to the server console every probe; if that spam is unwanted, return false from the prefix after capturing (the vanilla body does nothing else).
A client mod that has removed or renamed RPC_Ping breaks the probe (missing handler → 'Failed to find rpc method' on the client, no pong); fall back to a static default RTT after 3 missed pongs.

Time.time is float seconds since server start; after ~2^24 s (~194 days) float precision degrades to ~1-2 s, making RTT meaningless — use a restart, or reissue with a small offset; irrelevant for normal uptime.
Sender spoofing: a client can answer with a bogus time to inflate its own RTT and enlarge its own JIT lead — no security impact beyond its own gate timing.

catalog.name: Sync-Order Knobs (ObjectType.Prioritized / Distant) — Marginal
catalog.oneLine: Read this pass: Type=Prioritized only reorders ZDOs inside the peer's ordinary sector list and Distant=true only helps non-portal anchors in the far ring — neither substitutes for force-send or pre-streaming, and both are reverted on real portals the moment a client owns them.
catalog.howItWorks: ServerSortSendZDOS (:77311-77327) assigns m_tempSortValue = distance − 1.5 × seconds-since-last-sync and sorts with ServerSendCompare (:77288-77309): a ZDO is 'flagged' only if Type == Prioritized AND HasOwner AND owner != receiving peer (:77290-77291); flagged ZDOs sort ahead of everything, then by Type descending (Terrain 3 > Solid 2 > Prioritized 1 > Default 0, enum :73297-73303), then by distance. This sort applies ONLY to the list built from FindSectorObjects around the peer's refPos (:77220-77228); force-sends are Insert(0)'d AFTER the sort (:77239, :77275) and a CreateSyncList postfix appends after that — so for anything the mod pushes deliberately, Type is irrelevant. Where it could matter: a server-fabricated void anchor placed INSIDE a hub's own zone (e.g. an arrival pad 20 m from the terminal) that the peer's normal sweep will carry — set zdo.SetType(ObjectType.Prioritized) (:73790-73797, bumps DataRevision) so it precedes the base's pieces; the server owns it (CreateNewZDO sets owner :76686) so the flag test passes for every receiver. Distant: FindDistantObjects (:77384-77404) reads only m_objectsBySector and only ZDOs with Distant true, and CreateSyncList adds the distant list only when fewer than 10 near objects remain (:77229-77238); portals never appear there (they live in m_portalObjects, FindObjects :77376). A NON-portal anchor with SetDistant(true) (:73799-73805) is therefore delivered to a peer 3-4 zones (192-256 m) away once their near area is quiet — a modest widening of the 'already held' radius for anchors near, but not inside, a hub's ring. Both flags are serialized in the ExtraDataFlags word (Deserialize :74206-74209) and ZNetView.Awake resets Type/Distant to the prefab's Inspector values when the OWNING client instantiates the object (:82583-82590) — so on a real portal prefab, ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) handing ownership to a nearby player reverts the knob within 2 s of them arriving; on a prefab-0 void anchor no ZNetView is ever created and the flags stick. Client-side consequence of Prioritized: ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted creates by Type descending (:82147-82154) and IsZoneReadyForType makes lower types wait for higher-type loading objects in the zone (:115797-115815) — for a prefab-0 anchor CreateObject returns null so neither matters.
catalog.playerExperience: None observable. At best, an arrival-pad anchor inside a busy hub zone reaches a joining player a few hundred milliseconds earlier than the base's furniture.
failureModes: Setting Prioritized on a real portal ZDO is undone by the next owning client's ZNetView.Awake — silently, with a DataRevision bump that also re-sends the portal to everyone.
Distant=true on a void anchor changes nothing about portals themselves and does nothing at all until the peer's near list drains below 10 entries — in a busy base that can be never.
Misreading these as delivery levers leads to skipping the real ones (force-send, pre-stream); treat this option as documentation of a dead end.

catalog.name: Revision-Bump Redelivery (the 'Touch' Primitive)
catalog.oneLine: Because ForceSendZDO is revision-gated, re-delivering an unchanged or stale-on-the-peer ZDO requires an explicit DataRevision bump; this option pins down the correct 'touch' recipe every other delivery option depends on.
catalog.howItWorks: ZDOMan.AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77286) walks peer.m_forceSend and only inserts a ZDO when peer.ShouldSend(zdo) is true (:77273), otherwise it removes the id (:77279-77284). ShouldSend (:76003-76014) returns true if the peer has never received the ZDO, if OwnerRevision is newer, or if DataRevision is newer than the cached PeerZDOInfo (:75963-75976, written at :77064 on every actual send). So the digest's 'ForceSendZDO pushes regardless of distance' is true only for distance; for revision it is a strict gate, and a 'touch' that changes no field changes no revision: ZDO.Set no-ops on an equal value (BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345). Correct recipe, already shipped in Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:158-164): zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) (optional — no setter checks ownership, but the owner's next push can clobber); mutate; zdo.DataRevision += 4096 (public uint property :73494 — the large stride keeps the server ahead of an owning client's small increments after a race); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, zdo.m_uid) or the broadcast overload. On receipt, RPC_ZDOData applies the packet only if the incoming DataRevision is greater (:77110-77120), then Deserialize overwrites the field dictionaries additively (:74205-74240) — so a bumped-but-unchanged ZDO is accepted and re-applied harmlessly. Uses: (1) re-push a destination whose position moved server-side (void anchor relocation — note SetPosition on a non-owned ZDO does not bump :73734-73745, so set owner first); (2) re-push a tag rewritten for display to a far peer who holds the old string; (3) resurrect delivery after a peer's PeerZDOInfo got ahead (e.g. an owning client bumped past the server's copy and the server then lost ownership). Caution: a bump also marks the sector dirty for save (IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector :73832-73839) — harmless — and for a real portal a data bump does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects; tag rewrites still need ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) to persist. Do not bump on a tick unconditionally: every bump re-sends the whole ZDO to every peer in range (no delta encoding :77053-77063).
catalog.playerExperience: None directly; it is the difference between 'the server changed it and the player's client saw it' and 'the server changed it and nothing happened until the player walked away and back'.
failureModes: Revision race with an owning client: if a nearby client owns the ZDO and pushes a higher DataRevision after the server's bump, RPC_ZDOData on the server accepts the client's whole blob (:77124-77132) and reverts the server's fields — for durable writes claim ownership and guard SetOwner (Wonderland ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern).
Overflow is theoretical (uint), but a +4096 stride applied every tick for months on one ZDO would wrap after ~1M ticks — bump only on change.

OwnerRevision (ushort) is also a ShouldSend trigger; SetOwner bumps it, so a claim alone re-sends the ZDO even without a data change — useful, but it is what makes ownership churn from ReleaseNearbyZDOS a bandwidth cost.

catalog.name: Held-ZDO Ledger Readiness Gate
catalog.oneLine: Read the server's own per-peer ZDOPeer.m_zdos table to know exactly whether a given player already holds a destination ZDO (and at which revision) before opening a gate or announcing 'portal ready' — the missing readiness primitive for every JIT option.
catalog.howItWorks: ZDOMan keeps, per connected peer, a Dictionary<ZDOID, PeerZDOInfo> m_zdos (:75981) that SendZDOs writes on every ZDO actually serialized to that peer (:77064) with the DataRevision/OwnerRevision sent and the send time; it is also updated from the peer's own uploads in RPC_ZDOData (:77116, :77130) and pruned on destruction (:76990-76993). It is the ground truth of 'what does this client hold' — the same table ShouldSend consults. ZDOMan.m_peers (:76041) and ZDOPeer are private → publicizer (TortalPortal already compiles against ZDOMan.ZDOPeer, SectorSubscription.cs:108). API for the mod: bool Holds(peerUid, zdoid) = peer.m_zdos.ContainsKey(zdoid); bool Current(peerUid, zdo) = TryGetValue && info.m_dataRevision >= zdo.DataRevision; float HeldFor(peerUid, zdoid) = Time.time − info.m_syncTime. Uses: (1) JIT arming: write the connection into the shared portal only once Holds(traveller, destId) is true — otherwise DestinationPrewarm first and re-check next tick, so the glow-on and the walk-through never race; (2) Fast-Transit admission: require Holds for the destination ring's portal + N sampled ring ZDOs before choosing distant:false; (3) Pre-Stream progress: count ring ZDOs held vs. FindSectorObjects total to compute a 'destination X% streamed' figure and stop streaming (drop the subscription) at 100%, freeing the send budget; (4) audit: when a player reports a dead portal, log whether their client held the destination at the time. Edge semantics: an entry exists after the FIRST send even if later data changed (staleness is Current(), not Holds()); a client-side destroyed/dead ZDO is removed from every peer's table by HandleDestroyedZDO (:76990-76993); the table survives death/respawn (it is per-connection) and is dropped with the peer. Cost: dictionary lookups; iterate never.
catalog.playerExperience: None directly; it is what lets the mod toast 'Hub → Meadows ready' only when the player's client can actually use the link, and hold the toast (or the glow) an extra half-second when it cannot.
failureModes: The table records what was HANDED TO THE SOCKET, not what the client acknowledged — a packet lost to a disconnect mid-transfer leaves a phantom entry; the peer's next reconnect gets a fresh ZDOPeer, so this only matters within a session with heavy loss (Steam reliable channel makes it rare).

A client-side ZDO the client itself minted (its own character, placed pieces) is in the table via RPC_ZDOData — fine — but a ZDO the client received from ANOTHER client peer-to-peer does not exist in vanilla (all ZDO traffic is star-topology through the server), so no blind spot.
Publicizer coupling: if ZDOMan's nested class is renamed in a future patch the mod's readiness gate silently returns 'not held' — fail open to DestinationPrewarm-then-write, never fail closed.

catalog.name: The Event Beacon — Persistent Events As Removable Portal Markers
catalog.oneLine: Inject an ActivePersistentEvent at a managed portal or lockdown site to get the only server-controlled map marker vanilla can REMOVE, plus a radius ring, localized weather and event-gated spawns/wear — none of which any other channel offers.
catalog.howItWorks: PersistentEventSystem is a server-authoritative, world-persisted list. `m_activePersistentEvents` is a public field holding `ActiveEventsList.list` of `ActivePersistentEvent{sourceEventId,eventId,position,radius,startTime,duration}` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:104922-104939, :105073). Vanilla's own entry point `TriggerEvent(name)` -> `RPC_RequestStartEvent` picks a RANDOM world position via `GenerateEventLocation` (:105341-105379, :104844-104918), so placement at a portal is impossible through the RPC — the mod appends the entry directly to the list and calls the private `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)` (:105407-105410, publicizer) which broadcasts the whole list as JSON over the routed RPC "UpdateClientEventsList" (:105093, registered :105284). Joining peers pull it themselves: the client's m_onNewPeer hook fires `RequestActiveEventsList` (:105289, :105391-105397) and the server answers `UpdateClientEventsList(sender)` (:105399-105405) — no mod work for late joiners. Removal is `list.Remove(entry)` + `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)`; the server's own `Update` also auto-expires entries every 30 s when `duration >= 0 && startTime+duration <= ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()` (:105213-105234) — note vanilla's RPC path never sets startTime (:105359-105365), so mod entries must set it explicitly or use duration -1. Persistence: `PrepareSave/Save/Load` serialise the list as JSON+Brotli into the .db (:105237-105280); `m_eventIdCounter` is rebuilt as max(eventId)+1 on load (:105278) but is private at runtime, so allocate ids from it via publicizer to avoid colliding with a natural Bog Witch event. Vanilla-client reactions: (1) `Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins` (client :57505-57549) adds an EventArea pin with `m_worldSize = radius*2` and an animated double-size RandomEvent pin named `Localize(Source.mapTokenString)`, and REMOVES both when the eventId disappears from the list — the removable marker; (2) `EnvMan.GetEnvironmentOverride` consults `PersistentEventSystem.GetEnvironmentOverride()` for the local player's position (client :96299-96303, server copy :105432-105443) -> `Source.GetEnvironmentOverride(pos)` returns `environmentOverride` or `environmentOverride+"_"+biome` (:104830-104842); (3) `SpawnSystem` skips spawners whose `m_requiredPersistentEvent` does not match the active event's internalName at the spawn centre (client :111344-111351); (4) `WearNTear.UpdateWear` applies `m_eventDamage` to pieces with a non-empty `m_requiredPersistentEvent` (:149713-149723). All four are keyed off `Source` = `m_possibleEvents[sourceEventId]` (:104938), an Inspector list — label text, weather name and `graphicalEffects` (snow shader, :105140) are per-event-type asset data.
catalog.playerExperience: The player opens the map and sees a pulsing event icon labelled with the event's localized name (e.g. the Bog Witch event text) sitting on the managed hub, inside a circle the size the server chose. Walking inside the circle, the weather changes to that event's environment (fog, rain, whatever the asset defines). When the server ends the lockdown the icon and ring vanish from the map within one second. No toast, no chat; the marker is the whole message.
failureModes: `ActivePersistentEvent.Source` indexes `m_possibleEvents` with no bounds check (:104936-104938); a bad sourceEventId throws inside the CLIENT's Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins loop (:57517) on every vanilla client every second — a mod bug here breaks every player's map. Validate against `m_possibleEvents.Count` before publishing.

Label text and weather are fixed per event type: only strings/environments defined by the shipped `m_possibleEvents` entries can appear. If the world's Game prefab ships one event type, every beacon says the same thing.
`GetActiveEvent`/`GetEnvironmentOverride` return the FIRST list entry whose radius covers the point (:105420-105429, :105435-105441); overlapping beacons resolve by list order.
A radius around a hub with `environmentOverride` set changes the weather for everyone inside, permanently while active — including EnvMan-driven wetness that feeds WearNTear rain wear (:149681).

Vanilla-placed pieces with a matching `m_requiredPersistentEvent` (Bog Witch structures) take damage when the event is absent and, if `m_takeDamageIfInsideEvent`, when it is present — a beacon of the wrong type near such pieces damages them.
The `Update` expiry only runs on the server every 30 s of `Time.timeAsDouble` (:105213); timed beacons lag up to 30 s past their end.

eventId collision with a natural event started later via `RPC_RequestStartEvent` (uses `m_eventIdCounter`, :105361) makes the client treat two entries as one pin (dictionary keyed by eventId, :57515).
prerequisites: Boot-time dump of `PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_possibleEvents` (internalName, mapTokenString, environmentOverride, perBiomeEnvironments, graphicalEffects)
openQuestions: What is in `Game`'s `PersistentEventSystem.m_possibleEvents` on a 1.0.7 world (count, internalName, mapTokenString, environmentOverride)? IN-GAME CHECK: log the list at OnWorldReady on the dedicated server.

Does `PersistentEventSystem.instance` exist headless (its Awake touches Shader globals :105112; `Update` calls `Shader.SetGlobalFloat` and `UpdateComputeBuffer` allocates a ComputeBuffer :105197)? Vanilla dedicated servers run Bog Witch events, so probably yes. IN-GAME CHECK: log `PersistentEventSystem.instance != null` 30 s after world load.
Does a client that receives an entry whose `radius` is tiny (e.g. 4 m) still draw a readable EventArea ring? IN-GAME CHECK: inject radius 4 vs 30 and screenshot the map.

catalog.name: The Landing Pad Engine — Server-Authored Terraforming Via TerrainComp
catalog.oneLine: Write or fabricate a zone's _TerrainCompiler ZDO (ZDOVars.s_TCData) to flatten a disc, raise a pad out of shallow water or paint a paved circle under any portal exit — the only server-writable geometry in the game.
catalog.howItWorks: Every zone's terrain edits live in one compiler ZDO instantiated at the heightmap's transform position (`Heightmap.GetAndCreateTerrainCompiler`, :129530-129538; prefab `Heightmap.m_terrainCompilerPrefab` :128241 — read its name at runtime from `ZoneSystem.instance.m_zonePrefab.GetComponentInChildren<Heightmap>()`, which SpawnZone uses server-side :114073). The payload is `ZDOVars.s_TCData` (:78353): `Utils.Compress` of a ZPackage written by `TerrainComp.Save` (:143805-143833): int version=1, int operations, Vector3 lastOpPoint, float lastOpRadius, int N, then N × {bool modified, [float levelDelta, float smoothDelta]}, int N2, then N2 × {bool modifiedPaint, [float r,g,b,a]}. `Load` (:143862-143934) rejects the blob with 'height array missmatch' unless N == (m_width+1)². Vertex indexing is `Heightmap.WorldToVertex` (:129177-129183): x = floor((wx−zx)/scale+0.5)+w/2, y likewise on z, index = y*(w+1)+x (`GetHeight` :129263-129271). Height semantics: `ApplyToHeightmap` sets h = base + levelDelta + smoothDelta, clamped to base±8 (:143956-143972; `c_LevelMaxDelta` :128249), so the server computes levelDelta_i = clamp(targetY − WorldGenerator.GetHeight(vx,vz), −8, 8) for each vertex inside the disc, with vx = zx + (x − w/2)·scale. Paint: set modifiedPaint and a Color for the same indices to mark the pad (paint-channel convention is Heightmap asset data — verify). Clients re-apply whenever the ZDO's DataRevision differs from their cached one (`CheckLoad` :143837-143860 → `Load` → `m_hmap.Poke`), rebuilding the collision mesh and resetting grass. Write path: locate the compiler ZDO by prefab hash in the zone's sector (ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear at the zone centre); if absent, `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(zonePos, hash)` + `SetPrefab` + `Persistent=true` + `SetRotation(identity)` — clients then instantiate it and `TerrainComp.Awake` destroys any second compiler in the same XZ bounds (:143736-143741), so exactly one per zone. Claim ownership (`SetOwner(GetSessionID())`), `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_TCData, bytes)`, `ForceSendZDO`. Normal chunk persistence applies (compiler is not a portal prefab), no SetDirtyPortals. Alternative for zones a player has loaded: invoke the compiler's ZNetView RPC "RPC_ApplyOperation" at its owner with a serialized TerrainOp.Settings (:143987-144016) and let the client do the maths and Save — format is TerrainOp.Settings.Serialize (not read this pass). Tie-in: the real ground height at any point is base height + this blob's deltas, which the Destination Safety Validator and the Phantom Survival option can read server-side instead of the dead collider queries.
catalog.playerExperience: A player arrives through a hub portal and lands on a flat, paved 6 m disc that did not exist before the server placed the phantom; grass is cleared, the portal stands level. From a distance the pad looks exactly like a hoe-levelled, paved area a builder made. If the terrain was underwater by less than 8 m the pad now sits just above the waterline.
failureModes: N must equal (m_width+1)² for the zone prefab's Heightmap (code default m_width=32 :128243, zones are 64 m so the prefab almost certainly overrides to 64 → 4225 entries); a wrong count is silently ignored client-side after one log line.
Deltas are clamped to ±8 m of the generated height (:143969, :144076): a pad over deep water or a chasm cannot be built; water deeper than ~8 m below sea level stays water.
A disc straddling a 64 m zone boundary needs both zones' compilers written consistently, or the seam tears.

Owner clobber: a client that owns the compiler and later terraforms writes its own arrays; it Loads the server blob first only if CheckLoad saw the new DataRevision before the operation (Update every frame :143753-143759) — usually true, but a race exists in the same frame.
Server-computed base height uses WorldGenerator; the client heightmap build may differ by a few centimetres, so aim slightly above target and accept ±0.1 m.
Ownership of a compiler near a player is reassigned by ReleaseNearbyZDOS within 2 s; the write itself survives (already sent), but repeated edits must re-claim.

A fabricated compiler in a zone the server has never generated is harmless, but the first client to enter also runs zone generation; ordering is fine because CheckLoad runs after Initialize (:143744-143745).
prerequisites: Prefab name/hash of the terrain compiler read at runtime
Optional: Destination Safety Validator to decide where a pad is needed

catalog.name: Phantom Survival — Beating The Structural-Integrity Pass
catalog.oneLine: Unsupported server-fabricated portals are demolished by the first client to own them; the fix is a specific placement rule plus three server-side levers (LoadFields on WearNTear, NoBuildingFall, terrain pads) that make phantoms survive.
catalog.howItWorks: `WearNTear.UpdateWear` runs only on the ZDO's owning client and only after a 30 s grace from instantiation (`ShouldUpdate`, :149653-149660; `m_createTime` set in Awake :149426). Pieces outside the owner's active area are exempt and get max support written (:149670-149678), so the failure appears exactly when a player is near. With `m_noSupportWear` (default true, :149205) it calls `UpdateSupport` (:149959-150132), which OverlapBoxes each collider's bounds expanded by 0.3 m (:149644-149647): any hit on the terrain layer (:150041-150045) or on a static collider that has no WearNTear (:150046-150057) yields max support; otherwise support is inherited from touching pieces with distance loss. If `!HaveSupport()` (:150148-150151) the wear value is 100 (:149705-149712) and the applied damage is `num/100 * m_health` (:149822-149828) — i.e. the PREFAB's full m_health per update, regardless of stored s_health; a portal with s_health = k·m_health lasts k updates, then `ApplyDamage` → `Destroy` → `ZNetScene.Destroy` (:150387-150466) and the ZDO leaves m_portalObjects. Four server-side mitigations, in order of preference: (1) Placement: put the phantom's ZDO y at the real ground height so the prefab's colliders sit within 0.15 m of the terrain mesh — real ground = WorldGenerator.GetHeight + that zone's TerrainComp deltas (see Landing Pad Engine) — the terrain contact grants max support forever. (2) LoadFields override on the phantom: `HasFields=true`, `HasFieldsWearNTear=true`, `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` and `WearNTear.m_noRoofWear=false` (public bools :149201, :149205; LoadFields client :82898-82970 reflects public instance fields at instantiation) — support and rain wear are then never evaluated for that instance. (3) The world-modifier key `GlobalKeys.NoBuildingFall` short-circuits every wear ApplyDamage (:149825-149828), server-settable and vanilla-honoured, but world-wide. (4) Build a Landing Pad so the ground is where the portal is. A fifth, curious lever: `ApplyDamage` refuses when stored health ≤ 0 (:150389-150393) and `RPC_Damage` likewise (:150334), so a phantom with s_health = 0 is immune to everything except Repair (which resets it to m_health, :149528-149547) and RPC_Remove — but it renders in the 'broken' visual state (m_healthPercentage 0, :149439) and is not recommended. Other wear sources that can still kill a phantom: Ashlands lava (`m_lavaValue > 0.2 && m_groundDist < 1.5`, :149795-149807 — check `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` server-side), Deep North heavy snow when support colour is low (:149749-149765, gated by NoHeavySnow), `m_requiredBiome` (:149813-149816), and persistent-event damage if the prefab has `m_requiredPersistentEvent` (:149713-149723). Rain wear alone never destroys (stops at 50 %, :149686).
catalog.playerExperience: A player walks up to a server-placed portal that appears to float a hand's width above a slope; after ~30 s it does not crumble, throws no fragments, and the glow stays on — because the server wrote m_noSupportWear=false onto it. A phantom placed with the plain recipe instead cracks and collapses in front of the first visitor within a few seconds of the grace period ending.
failureModes: A phantom placed at WorldGenerator.GetHeight in a zone that has been terraformed sits above or below the real mesh: above → no terrain contact → demolished; below → clips.
LoadFields overrides apply at instantiation only; a phantom already instantiated on a client before the keys were written stays vulnerable until that client re-creates it.
`GlobalKeys.NoBuildingFall` disables support wear for EVERY building in the world and is persisted into the .fwl as a world modifier.
Prefab m_health for the portal is Inspector data; how many updates a given s_health buys is unknown until read (`ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(...).GetComponent<WearNTear>().m_health` on the server).
A phantom over lava or in Deep North snow dies to biome damage even with support fixed.

`WearNTear.Awake` may run before `ZNetView.Awake` on the same GameObject (script order is Inspector-defined); m_noSupportWear is read live in UpdateWear so the override still works, but an m_health override read in Awake (:149428-149439) might be missed.
prerequisites: Phantom-portal fabrication recipe (CreateNewZDO + SetPrefab + Persistent + rotation)

catalog.name: The Ferry Route — Server-Steered Ships That Move A Crew
catalog.oneLine: Ship.Start registers Forward/Backward/Stop/Rudder ZNetView RPCs with no owner check; a server heading controller can sail a crewed vanilla ship between docks with no teleport, no cooldown and no black screen — but not an empty one.
catalog.howItWorks: `Ship.Start` registers "Stop", "Forward", "Backward" and "Rudder"(float) on the ship's ZNetView (:140482-140485). The handlers simply mutate `m_speed`/`m_rudderValue` on whichever instance receives them (:140538-140597) — no `IsOwner` gate. `UpdateControlls` makes the OWNER authoritative: it writes `ZDOVars.s_forward`/`s_rudder` to the ZDO every physics tick while non-owners read them back (:140863-140875). So the server addresses the owner: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ownerPeerUid, shipZdoId, "Forward")` (owner = `shipZdo.GetOwner()` → ZNetPeer). Physics is owner-only (:140601-140604) and has two hard gates: `if (m_players.Count == 0) { m_speed = Stop; m_rudderValue = 0 }` (:140606-140610) — an UNATTENDED ship cannot be driven at all — and `if (!HaveControllingPlayer() && (Slow || Back)) m_speed = Stop` (:140611-140614) — without a helmsman (`ShipControlls.HaveValidUser` = s_user set and that player in the boat, :141387-141394) only Half and Full sail run. Sail thrust is wind-relative (`GetSailForce` :140780) and rudder authority scales with forward speed (`m_stearVelForceFactor`, :140689-140691), so a sailing ship steers. Controller: every 0.25 s read `shipZdo.GetPosition()/GetRotation()`, compute the bearing error to the next waypoint, send "Rudder" with a clamped value, send "Forward" until `s_forward` reads Full, send "Stop" within the dock radius; read `s_forward`/`s_rudder` off the ZDO to confirm the owner applied the command. `Ship.UpdateOwner` re-homes ownership every 2 s to a player actually in the boat (:140968-140977), so re-resolve the owner each tick. Passengers ride for free: on every rider's own client `Character.UpdateMotion` re-glues them to `m_lastAttachBody.TransformPoint(m_lastAttachPos)` while the correction is < 4 m (:2118-2135); continuous physics never exceeds that. Timetable + helmsman check: if `s_user != 0` a human is steering — yield (stop sending) so the route never fights a player. Combine with the portal layer: a 'harbour' portal lands the traveller on the dock, the ferry departs when `m_players.Count > 0` (inferred server-side from rider SyncTransform parent or proximity of character ZDOs to the ship ZDO).
catalog.playerExperience: A player steps onto a longship tied at the hub dock and sits down on a bench. After a moment the sail unfurls by itself, the rudder swings and the ship pulls out, tacking along the coast to the next dock while the player fishes or cooks. Anyone who grabs the tiller takes over instantly; when they let go the route resumes. Arrival is just the ship coming to a stop at the pier — no loading screen.
failureModes: `m_players.Count == 0` forces Stop on the owner (:140606): the ferry cannot reposition itself empty; a return leg needs a rider or a server-driven kinematic push (see Player's Ship — Corrected).
Wind: Half/Full sail against a headwind stalls (asset-defined sail curves); the controller needs tacking legs or long waits. The server cannot set wind (EnvMan wind is client-computed from time).
Slow (rowing) and reverse are helmsman-only (:140611-140614) — docking manoeuvres without a human at the tiller are sail-only and clumsy.
Ownership hops between riders every 2 s (:140968-140977); a command sent to a stale owner is applied on a non-owner instance and then overwritten by the owner's s_forward/s_rudder on the next tick.
Any rider at the helm sends the same RPCs and wins; a griefer can hijack the route (mitigate with the s_user yield rule).
`Ship.m_players` is trigger-volume state on the owner's client (:141008-141024) — the server infers occupancy only indirectly.
Ships are Persistent and collide with shorelines; a bad waypoint beaches the ferry and the server has no collider query to know.

This is a genuine client-honoured RPC channel with no server-side veto on the act itself (matches attack-priority framing honestly — it's phrased as 'should this ship respond to this RPC', which vanilla answers unconditionally, not as a fabricated server permission).

catalog.name: Player's Ship — Corrected: Kinematic Ship Motion With Riders Aboard
catalog.oneLine: A server that pins ship ownership and writes its position can carry riders only while each physics-tick correction stays under 4 m; the previous 'you land in the water behind the boat' verdict is right for portal ARRIVAL but wrong for ship MOTION.
catalog.howItWorks: Two different limits govern a moving ship. Motion: non-owning clients run `ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition`, which extrapolates the target by `s_velHash × timer` (:87710-87713) and then lerps 20 % per FixedUpdate when the gap is < 5 m, hard-snapping otherwise (:87714-87718). Riders on their own client are corrected toward `m_lastAttachBody.TransformPoint(m_lastAttachPos)` each tick, but ONLY if the correction magnitude is < 4 m; beyond that the attach body is cleared and the player is left behind (:2118-2135). A server that claims the ship ZDO (SetOwner(GetSessionID()) + the WaterBuoyancyEngine SetOwner-block prefix, so `Ship.UpdateOwner`/ReleaseNearbyZDOS cannot take it back) and advances `SetPosition`/`SetRotation` in small steps therefore moves a crewed hull as a kinematic platform: per-tick instance displacement is 0.2 × lag, the lag settles at ~4× the per-tick delta, so keeping the server's per-FixedUpdate delta ≤ 0.5 m (≈25 m/s at 50 Hz, practically cap at ~10 m/s) keeps every rider's correction well under 4 m. Write `s_velHash` = the ship's true velocity so extrapolation matches, or zero it and accept lag. Because the server owns the ship no client runs `Ship.CustomFixedUpdate` physics (:140601-140604): no buoyancy, no wave rocking, no sail — the server must hold the hull at water level (y ≈ 30 + the prefab's float offset) and write rotation itself; the ship's own `s_forward`/`s_rudder` are irrelevant. Arrival remains the impossible half: a portal whose destination is a moving ship pins the traveller to a frozen snapshot for ≥ 8 s (`Player.UpdateTeleport` :15343-15349) and `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` omits the vehicle layer (:113424) so `FindFloor` sees the seabed — so the correct composite is: stop the ship (hold its position for ≥ 15 s), teleport the player to the DOCK (Void Anchor / phantom at the pier), then resume motion once their character ZDO is within a few metres of the hull. Long jumps of a ship with riders (> 4 m in one write) always shed the riders.
catalog.playerExperience: A player standing on a server-driven barge sees it glide smoothly with no sail animation and no rocking; they can walk about and stay aboard. When the barge reaches a harbour it stops dead and holds; a friend then arrives through the harbour portal onto the pier beside it, steps aboard, and the barge resumes. If the server ever jumps the barge more than a few metres in one step, everyone aboard is dumped into the water at the old position.
failureModes: Whether ship prefabs' ZSyncTransform has m_syncPosition/m_syncRotation is Inspector data (ships visibly move for non-owners in vanilla, so very likely yes) — needs one check.
Server-owned ship loses buoyancy and wave motion; on stop it sits rigid, which looks wrong and can clip through waves.

`Ship.UpdateOwner` and ReleaseNearbyZDOS both try to hand ownership to a rider every 2 s (:140968-140977, :76901-76927); without the SetOwner-block prefix the server loses control mid-voyage and the ship snaps back to physics with s_forward=Stop.
A rider who jumps loses ground contact; `m_lastGroundBody` clears and they fall behind if the hull moved > 4 m before landing (:2118-2135).
Per-tick writes to a Persistent ZDO dirty the chunk set every tick and occupy a permanent slot in every nearby peer's sync list (SendZDOs has no delta encoding).
Portal arrival onto the deck is still impossible: teleport snapshot :15343 and seabed FindFloor fallback (:15360-15366).
prerequisites: Harbour phantom/Void Anchor at each dock
openQuestions: ZSyncTransform flags on karve/longship/drakkar prefabs (m_syncPosition, m_syncRotation, m_syncBodyVelocity). IN-GAME CHECK: read from ZNetScene prefab on the server.
Largest per-tick delta that keeps a standing rider attached in practice (lerp lag vs 4 m). IN-GAME CHECK: drive a server-owned karve at 5, 10, 20 m/s with a rider and record when they fall off.
Does a rigid, non-physics hull at fixed y look acceptable, or does Floating/wave code on the client fight the position (Ship physics is owner-only, but water visuals are not)?

catalog.name: Tame And Cart Follow-Through — Relocating Companions Across A Transit
catalog.oneLine: On a detected transit, relocate the traveller's following tames and unpulled carts by writing their (non-portal) ZDO positions once the source zone is unowned; sector re-filing and the client's saved-follow re-attach do the rest.
catalog.howItWorks: Non-portal ZDOs, unlike portals, re-file on position change: `ZDO.SetSector` (:73752-73768) removes from the old sector, adds to the new one and calls `ZDOSectorInvalidated`, which drops the ZDO from any peer's m_zdos when it is no longer inside their active area (:75989-75996) so normal sector sync delivers it at the new location. Selection at transit time: enumerate creature ZDOs within R m of the SOURCE portal (ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear) whose prefab carries a Tameable component (build the hash set from ZNetScene prefabs at OnWorldReady), whose `ZDOVars.s_tamed` is true (written by `Character.SetTamed` :4495) and whose `ZDOVars.s_follow` string equals the traveller's `s_playerName` (written by `Tameable.RPC_Command` :19444/:19457, cleared to "" on stay); plus Vagon-prefab ZDOs within R whose `s_attachJointHash` bool is false (pulled carts hold true, :147661; owner writes false on detach :147686). Relocation must wait until nobody owns the source-area ZDOs: the traveller's client keeps ownership until its reference position moves (UpdateTeleport sets position at t > 2 s), after which `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` releases owner to 0 on its next 2 s pass if no other peer covers the area; only then `SetOwner(GetSessionID())`, `SetPosition(destExit + spread)`, `SetRotation`, `ForceSendZDO` — the revision bump requires ownership (:73734-73745). The destination player's active area now covers the creature; ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands them ownership, their ZNetScene instantiates it, and `Tameable.UpdateSavedFollowTarget` (owner-only) matches `s_follow` against `Player.GetAllPlayers` on that client and re-issues `Command(player)` (:19472-19486) — the tame resumes following with no server involvement. Cart cargo lives in `s_items` on the cart's Container (Vagon.m_container is an Inspector child; whether it shares the cart's ZDO via m_rootObjectOverride needs a check), so it rides along. Exclusions: summons (`m_unsummonOnOwnerLogoutSeconds > 0`, :19489-19496) and bosses; creatures in combat (s_alert session key) optional. Config: radius 12 m, max 6 followers, per-transit cooldown. Arrival y = WorldGenerator.GetHeight + TerrainComp delta + 0.5. Detection source: PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit (3 s resolution) or, far better, the Portal-As-Trigger path where the server itself issues the teleport and knows the exact moment.
catalog.playerExperience: A player with two wolves walks through a portal. A few seconds after the black screen ends, both wolves pop into existence a couple of metres behind them and trot up to heel; their cart, if it was parked unhitched next to the source portal, appears beside the exit with its contents intact. If a friend was standing at the source portal, the wolves stay behind until that friend leaves the area.
failureModes: If any peer's active area still covers the source, the tame's owning client keeps writing its position every tick and ZSyncTransform snaps it back (5 m snap, :87715); the mod must skip and retry rather than fight.
Creatures with ZSyncTransform pop rather than walk; MonsterAI state (alert, target) is local and resets on re-instantiation.
Name matching: `s_follow` is a character NAME (:19457); two same-named players are indistinguishable — the tame follows whichever the owning client finds first.

A cart mid-pull (s_attachJointHash true) must not be moved: the puller's joint on the departing client will detach it anyway, but only after that client observes the departure; wait for the bool to flip.
Relocated creatures land at generated ground height; inside a terraformed pit or on a raised pad they clip unless the TerrainComp delta is applied.
Transit detection via PositionWatch is 3 s coarse and cannot tell WHICH portal pair was used when two hubs are within 40 m; prefer the server-initiated teleport path.
Relocating a ZDO across the ±16 km clamp or a dungeon (y > 3000) interior needs the y offset preserved; do not relocate into interiors.
prerequisites: Prefab hash sets for Tameable and Vagon built from ZNetScene prefabs
Destination exit coordinates (portal ZDO position + rotation)
openQuestions: Does the cart's Container use m_rootObjectOverride so `s_items` sits on the Vagon ZDO, or does the cart have a child Container ZDO that must be relocated too? IN-GAME CHECK: load a cart, read its ZDO for s_items server-side.

Does a re-instantiated tame actually re-follow on the arriving client (UpdateSavedFollowTarget requires MonsterAI.GetFollowTarget()==null and owner)? IN-GAME CHECK: relocate a wolf ZDO 500 m and watch it heel.
How long after a portal transit does ReleaseNearbyZDOS zero the source creatures' owner when the traveller was alone? IN-GAME CHECK: log owner transitions on a wolf ZDO during a solo transit.

catalog.name: Per-Peer Location Icons — Faction Respawn And Private Landmarks
catalog.oneLine: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons is per-peer and the client replaces its whole dictionary on receipt; because Game.FindSpawnPoint falls back to the 'StartTemple' icon, a per-peer payload steers where a vanilla client's new or bed-less characters respawn, and which altar/trader icons that player sees.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons(long peer)` (private, :113581-113593) packs `GetLocationIcons()` as (Vector3, name) pairs into the routed RPC "LocationIcons" for ONE peer; the client's `RPC_LocationIcons` clears `m_locationIcons` and rebuilds it (:113595-113607) — a wholesale per-peer replace. It is sent from `OnNewPeer` (:113609-113617) and re-broadcast to everyone (peer 0) whenever an `m_iconPlaced` location is first placed (:114999-115003). On the client, `Game.FindSpawnPoint` uses, in order: logout point, custom (bed) spawn — cleared if no Bed is found within 5 m at load (:100786-100794) — and finally `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation)` + 2 m up (client :100796-100800), where the client's GetLocationIcon returns the FIRST dictionary entry whose value equals "StartTemple" (:115437-115445). Mechanism: Harmony prefix on `SendLocationIcons(long peer)`: when peer == 0, fan out by calling the method once per connected peer and return false; for a specific peer, build the payload from GetLocationIcons then apply per-player policy — replace the StartTemple entry's key with the faction hall coordinate (omit the real temple so 'first match' is unambiguous), drop altar entries the player's faction has not unlocked, add the faction hub under a name that exists in the client's `Minimap.m_locationIcons` sprite list (e.g. a trader icon name) — and write that package instead. Re-send on policy change by calling the (publicized) method for that peer. Effects on a 100 % vanilla client: the temple map icon moves to the hall for that player only (Minimap.UpdateLocationPins every 5 s), new characters and bed-less deaths spawn at the hall (Valkyrie intro included), undiscovered altars are invisible on their map, and the hub shows as a landmark. A custom bed spawn or logout point always wins (:100774-100795), so this never overrides an established base. Uninstall: remove the prefix; the next relog/OnNewPeer restores the vanilla list.
catalog.playerExperience: A player who joined the Northern faction dies without a bed and wakes up at the faction hall, 2 m above its floor, exactly as if it were the start temple; their map shows the temple icon sitting on the hall. Their friend in the Southern faction, dying at the same moment, wakes at the southern hall. Neither sees the other faction's hub icon, and both still see the real temple only if the server chose to include it under a different icon name.
failureModes: Only players WITHOUT a logout point or bed are affected; established players never notice unless their bed is destroyed.

`IsAreaReady` must pass at the hall coordinate (:100799) — the hall zone must generate for that client; a hall inside a dungeon interior (y > 3000) or off-map fails and the client falls to `Vector3.zero` (:100801-100804).
Icon names must be in the client's compiled `Minimap.m_locationIcons` list; an invented name renders nothing (client GetLocationIcon returns null).
Two dictionary keys with value "StartTemple" both draw temple icons and the respawn uses whichever enumerates first — always omit the real one.

The PlaceLocations re-broadcast to peer 0 (:115000-115003) bypasses a per-peer prefix that only handles non-zero peers — handle 0 explicitly or every new boss-altar placement resets everyone to vanilla.
A modded client can spawn anywhere; this is authoritative only for unmodified clients.
The moved temple icon also moves the 'start temple' pin used by any vanilla feature that reads GetLocationIcon on that client (Vegvisir discovery of StartTemple, if any).
prerequisites: Per-player faction/policy store keyed by s_playerID or PlatformUserID
Dump of the client's Minimap.m_locationIcons names (one-time, from a client)

catalog.name: Ambush Gates — Arrival-Triggered World Events
catalog.oneLine: RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName is public and server-driven; fire a raid at a portal's exit on arrival (or at the source on a lockdown violation) and close the gate that summoned it until the event ends.
catalog.howItWorks: `RandEventSystem.instance.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos)` (:107067-107071) resolves the RandomEvent asset from `m_events` and calls `SetRandomEvent` (:107083-107108), which stops any current random event, clones the asset with `m_pos = pos`, and — on the server — `SendCurrentRandomEvent` via the routed RPC "SetEvent" (registered on every peer, :106781). It bypasses `HaveGlobalKeys`/`m_requiredGlobalKeys` and the valid-point search, so any event can be started anywhere. Lifecycle is server-owned: each FixedUpdate the server computes `IsAnyPlayerInEventArea` from character ZDOs (`DistanceXZ < m_eventRange`, y ≤ 3000, :107100-107119) and advances `RandomEvent.Update` (:107521-107536), which pauses while nobody is inside if `m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea` and ends after `m_duration`; the server then `SetRandomEvent(null)` and broadcasts again. Clients spawn the event's creatures locally through SpawnSystem, play its music/HUD, and draw the EventArea + RandomEvent map pins that are removed on end (:57471-57502). Trigger design: with the Portal-As-Trigger transport the server already knows the exact arrival moment and coordinate — fire the event at exit + 8 s (after the black screen). With passive detection use PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit (≈2-3 s late). Gate coupling: on fire, `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on the arrival portal (or point it at a Decoy target) so nobody can leave through it, and poll `GetCurrentRandomEvent() == null` to restore the link; combine with the Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction. Source-side use: a lockdown violation (transit while NoPortals is supposed to apply) spawns the event at the SOURCE. Boss safety: `NoBossPortals` reads `GetBossEvent()` — which is `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent`, a per-client HUD lookup (:106939-106949) — OR the server-written `activeBosses` key; a raid is not a boss event unless its spawn list contains a boss, so ordinary raids do not trip the portal blackout. For long-lived 'cursed' zones prefer the Event Beacon (persistent event) instead of the single-slot random event.
catalog.playerExperience: The player steps out of a portal into the Plains and the screen darkens with the raid banner — 'The horde is attacking' — as fulings converge on the exit. They turn back to the portal: it is dark and unconnected. After the raid timer runs out (or they clear it and step away long enough for the pause), the portal lights up again.
failureModes: Single slot: `m_randomEvent` is one object (:107085-107092); starting an ambush cancels any natural raid in progress elsewhere and vice versa — a second ambush replaces the first.
Event radius, duration, pause behaviour, spawn list and required biome are Inspector data on the RandomEvent asset; the names must be dumped from `RandEventSystem.instance.m_events` at boot.
Bypassing `m_requiredGlobalKeys` means a Fuling raid can be sent at a Meadows newcomer; policy must gate by player progression (server cannot see it — use world keys as a proxy).

Spawns are executed by clients around players in the area; if the arriving player is alone and dies immediately, the event pauses and the gate stays closed until the timer runs out or the mod times it out.
Detection latency: passive detection fires 2-3 s after arrival, during which the player may already have walked away from the exit; the event follows `m_pos`, not the player.

If the event spawn list contains a boss-flagged character, `activeBosses` is incremented by the client (:27256-27262) and NoBossPortals blacks out every portal server-wide until it dies or the key is zeroed.

`RandomEvent.Update` calls `GameCamera.instance.AddShake` on the server if the asset has a shake curve (:107531-107534) — a headless NRE risk that vanilla presumably avoids with empty curves; do not pick events with camera shake without a check.
openQuestions: Which RandomEvent names exist and their m_eventRange/m_duration/m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea (Inspector). IN-GAME CHECK: log m_events at OnWorldReady.
Does a vanilla client honour a SetEvent whose position is in a biome the event's m_biome does not list (SpawnSystem may refuse to spawn)? IN-GAME CHECK: fire army_goblin in Meadows and count spawns.
Does GameCamera.instance exist headless for events with a shake curve?
evidence: assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107083-107108 SetRandomEvent confirmed: clones event, sets m_pos, OnStart(), server-only SendCurrentRandomEvent — no key/search gate
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName(name,pos) as public, resolving via GetEvent(name) then SetRandomEvent(ev,pos), which unconditionally clones the event, sets `m_randomEvent.m_pos=pos`, calls OnStart(), and on the server calls SendCurrentRandomEvent() — no global-key/valid-point search anywhere in this path, confirming the 'bypasses HaveGlobalKeys and the valid-point search' claim. GetBossEvent (used elsewhere for Boss Blackout) is confirmed to be EnemyHud-based/client-local, consistent with the option's boss-safety note that ordinary raids don't trip NoBossPortals unless their spawn list includes a boss. Enforcement label 'server-enforced' is honest: event lifecycle (start/stop/area-check/duration) is fully server-authoritative per the code, not a per-player permission gate.

catalog.name: Field Injection, Corrected — Which Portal Owns Which Field
catalog.oneLine: TeleportWorld.Teleport reads m_allowAllItems and m_exitDistance from the portal the player walks INTO, not the destination; the per-field table below fixes the inverted claim in Field Injection, The Ore Gate and Phantom Destination Portal.
catalog.howItWorks: Mechanism recap: `ZNetView.LoadFields` (client :82898-82970) runs once from `ZNetView.Awake` before `AddInstance` (:82860-82861). If the ZDO has `HasFields` true it walks `GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>` (root included), and for each component whose `HasFields<TypeName>` is true reflects every public instance field, reading `"<TypeName>.<field>"` as int/float/bool/Vector3/string/GameObject-by-prefab-name/ItemDrop. Vanilla's `spawn` console command writes exactly these keys (client :44423-44430), so this is a supported data contract. Where each field is read: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143517-143549) is executed on the SOURCE instance — `player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)` (:143533) and `pos = targetPos + targetRot*forward * m_exitDistance + up` (:143546) both use `this.` fields of the portal being entered; the destination contributes only its ZDO position and rotation (:143539-143543). Per-field table — TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems: SOURCE; unlocks non-teleportable cargo for trips OUT of this portal (still blocked for m_toolTier ≥ 1000, Inventory.IsTeleportable). TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance: SOURCE; how far in front of the DESTINATION the traveller appears when leaving THIS portal — to change the landing offset around hub H, write it on every portal that points AT H, not on H. TeleportWorld.m_activationRange: SOURCE; feeds `Player.GetClosestPlayer` in UpdatePortal for the glow/target-found effect only (:143495-143508); the transit collider is a child TeleportWorldTrigger volume, unchanged. TeleportWorld.m_hoverOffset: hover-text height. WearNTear.m_noSupportWear / m_noRoofWear / m_health / m_ashDamageImmune / m_snowDamageImmune: this portal's wear (see Phantom Survival). Piece.m_canBeRemoved: this portal; false makes the vanilla hammer silently refuse removal (`Player.RemovePiece` :12375). Write recipe on the server: `zdo.Set("HasFields", true); zdo.Set("HasFieldsTeleportWorld", true); zdo.Set("TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems", true)`, then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` so the portal chunk is rewritten, and `ForceSendZDO`. Applies-at-instantiation: an instance already created on a client keeps its prefab values until that client destroys and recreates it (leave the ~96-112 m active area and return, or relog). Because `ZDO.Deserialize` is additive (:74205-74240), the keys survive the owning client's own pushes, and they persist through the ChunkPortal save like any other field.
catalog.playerExperience: A player carrying copper walks into the hub portal the admin flagged as 'ore-capable' and passes through; walking into an ordinary portal with the same copper still shows 'You cannot teleport with this item'. The admin who set the flag on the DESTINATION instead sees no effect at all — the traveller is still blocked at the entrance portal.
failureModes: Overrides written on the destination do nothing to item checks or exit offset — the exact inversion this option corrects.
LoadFields fires only at instantiation; players already standing at the portal do not see the change until re-creation.
m_activationRange does not enlarge the transit trigger; a 'walk-through radius' cannot be widened.
Persistence requires SetDirtyPortals or the keys vanish at the next save.
Client-honoured: a modified client ignores the fields; vanilla honours them exactly as it honours prefab values.

Whether TeleportWorld sits on a GameObject reached by GetComponentsInChildren and the exact TypeName strings (`TeleportWorld`, `WearNTear`, `Piece`) are Inspector/prefab facts — one in-game test settles it.

Do HasFields keys survive a save/load round trip on portal ZDOs (ChunkPortal path)? IN-GAME CHECK: write, save, restart, read.
