catalog.name: Non-Portals As Portals — The Mandatory Migration Pass
catalog.oneLine: Enrolling a prefab into Game.PortalPrefabHash at runtime silently orphans every pre-existing instance from the next save and freezes mobile ones; the option is only safe with a migration pass, an immobile-prefab restriction and an uninstall reversal.
catalog.howItWorks: Save partitioning is a two-set split with no overlap: `AddObjectsPerChunk` clones only ZDOs that are `Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` out of `m_objectsBySector` (:77566-77576), while the ChunkPortal file clones only `m_portalObjects` and only when `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77619-77627). An instance of the enrolled prefab that was already in `m_objectsBySector` when the hash was added is now excluded from the normal chunk (hash matches) and absent from the portal file (never went through AddIfPortal) — it is dropped from the next save of its chunk and gone after restart. Migration pass (run once, immediately after adding the hash, before any save): walk `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(prefabName, list, ref index)` to completion (dedupe sector 0), and for each ZDO call `RemoveFromSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (public :76745) then the private `AddIfPortal(zdo, hash)` (:77732-77752, publicizer) — which files it into m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects — then `SetDirtyPortals()`. Also postpone the world save (or force one) so both files are consistent. Immobility: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any enrolled hash (:73752-73755), so an enrolled ship or cart stays keyed under its original sector forever and stops being delivered to clients at its new position — restrict enrolment to static prefabs. Uninstall reversal: on a later boot without the mod, `LoadChunks` inserts every ChunkPortal ZDO straight into `m_portalObjects` regardless of prefab (:76474-76482), so the enrolled objects stay in the portal registry, get paired by tag by `Game.ConnectPortals` (empty tag = the global untagged group), and — because `HandleDestroyedZDO` only removes from m_portalObjects when the prefab IS in PortalPrefabHash (:76979-76986) — leak there when destroyed. Reversal pass (run while the mod is still installed, before removal): for each enrolled-prefab ZDO in `GetPortals()`, remove it from the live dictionary, `AddToSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (public :76723), clear its Portal connection, `SetDirtyPortals()`, and remove the hash from PortalPrefabHash; then save.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing visible when done right. Done wrong, every runestone/altar/marker of the enrolled prefab that existed before the mod was installed disappears from the world at the next restart, with no log line, and the admin blames world corruption.
failureModes: Skipping the migration: silent loss of every pre-existing instance at the next save.
Enrolling a mobile prefab: instances stop re-sectoring and vanish for clients that move away from the original sector.
Uninstall without reversal: enrolled objects persist only via ChunkPortal, are paired by tag with real untagged portals, and leak in m_portalObjects on destruction.
GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative returns portals (and now the enrolled prefab) only on its terminal call, and re-scans sector 0 — a partial walk migrates nothing.
A save that runs between adding the hash and finishing the migration commits the loss; suspend `Game.m_saveInterval` or trigger the migration synchronously at OnWorldReady before any autosave.
openQuestions: Does a chunk save between hash-add and migration ever happen in practice at OnWorldReady (autosave default 1800 s, but ZNet.Shutdown saves)? IN-GAME CHECK: add hash, kill server without migration, restart, count instances.
Does `Game.ConnectPortals` pairing an enrolled non-portal ZDO with a real untagged portal produce a usable teleport on a vanilla client (yes at the transit site; visual state untested)?

corrections: The 'server-enforced' label is honest only in the sense that ZDOMan's save-partitioning logic is 100% server-side authority with zero player input — there is no player-facing permission gate here at all; this option is really about save-file data-integrity risk for the mod's OWN prefab-enrollment choice, not an enforcement mechanism directed at players. Worth noting for precision, not a reason to downgrade.
evidence: assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76462-76483 LoadChunks ChunkPortal branch confirmed no prefab filtering
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified every cited ZDOMan member. AddObjectsPerChunk filters `item3.Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(item3.GetPrefab())` for normal chunks — confirmed exact. AddIfPortal confirmed: early-returns if the prefab hash isn't in PortalPrefabHash, else files into m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects=true. LoadChunks' ChunkPortal branch confirmed to insert every ZDO from that file straight into m_portalObjects with zero prefab-hash filtering — confirming the 'uninstall leaves them in the portal registry forever' claim. ZDO.SetSector confirmed to early-return unconditionally for any prefab in PortalPrefabHash (immobility claim confirmed). RPC_ZDOData confirmed to call AddIfPortal(zDO, zDO.GetPrefab()) on every incoming ZDO update, meaning even a peer-synced (non-locally-created) ZDO gets correctly filed if its prefab is enrolled — a detail supporting rather than undermining the option.

catalog.name: The Adamant Gate, Rewritten — Indestructible Only As A Composite
catalog.oneLine: A huge s_health defeats damage and Repair only; hammer removal, support wear, forged DestroyZDO and ZDOData overwrite all bypass it — the portal is indestructible only when five levers are present together.
catalog.howItWorks: What s_health buys: `WearNTear.RPC_Damage` runs on the owning client, applies resistances and subtracts from the stored `s_health` via `ApplyDamage` (:150332-150409); `Repair` refuses when stored health ≥ prefab m_health (:149522-149531). What it does not buy: (a) Hammer removal — `Player.RemovePiece` → `WearNTear.Remove` → "RPC_Remove" to the ZDO owner → `Destroy` (:150411-150466), health never consulted; (b) Support loss — wear applies `m_health` per update forever (:149705-149712, :149822-149828), draining even 1e9 given time; (c) A forged `DestroyZDO` routed RPC (`ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` → `HandleDestroyedZDO`, :76953-76999, no sender/ownership check) deletes the ZDO outright; (d) `RPC_ZDOData` applies any higher-revision blob wholesale (:77076-77139), so a client can set s_health to 1. Composite: (1) s_health = k·m_health as the damage buffer, re-asserted on the watchdog tick and protected by an `RPC_ZDOData` postfix that restores it if a peer lowered it; (2) LoadFields `Piece.m_canBeRemoved = false` so the vanilla hammer refuses at :12375 before any RPC is sent, plus `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear = false` / `m_noRoofWear = false` so support and rain wear are never evaluated (:149686, :149705); (3) Ownership pin — SetOwner-block prefix keeps the server as owner so any RPC_Remove/RPC_Damage that a modified client sends anyway is routed to a machine with no instance and dies in `ZNetScene.FindInstance` (HandleRoutedRPC :83646-83663); note RPC_SetTag then also dies, so pinned gates are retag-frozen — acceptable for admin gates; (4) Destroy veto — prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` that drops ZDOIDs belonging to protected portals, or a `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` observer that immediately re-fabricates the gate (new ZDOID, `m_deadZDOs` forbids reusing the old id, :76043/:77133); (5) `Piece.CanBeRemoved()` is separate and irrelevant for portals (:136310-136326). Vanilla-respecting side: (1) and (2) are honoured by unmodified clients; (3) and (4) are server-enforced against modified ones. Only with all present does 'indestructible' hold; state that in the option's headline.
catalog.playerExperience: A raider's axe bounces off the admin gate showing damage numbers that never dent it; their hammer's remove prompt simply does nothing; a modded client's forged destroy packet is dropped and the gate stays. A vanilla builder trying to retag a pinned gate gets no response — the tag dialog closes and nothing changes.
failureModes: Ownership pin freezes vanilla retagging (RPC_SetTag routes to the owner, which has no instance) — acceptable only for admin-managed gates.

LoadFields overrides apply at instantiation; a client that already has the instance can still hammer-remove until it re-creates it (RPC_Remove then reaches the pinned server and dies anyway, so the pin covers the gap).
A Destroy veto prefix must resolve targets by ZDOID from a ZPackage it then re-positions; a mistake corrupts vanilla's destroy handling for every object in the packet.
Re-fabrication after a successful destroy changes the ZDOID; every portal pointing at the old gate is unlinked until the mod re-pairs them.
s_health re-assert needs a real value change or ForceSendZDO to reach peers whose cached revision is current (AddForceSendZdos is gated on ShouldSend, :77268-77273).
The support/roof overrides are client-honoured; a modified client still applies wear — but its ApplyDamage writes are then reverted by the watchdog.
openQuestions: Does a vanilla client show any feedback when Player.RemovePiece returns false on m_canBeRemoved (:12375-12377 returns silently)? IN-GAME CHECK: hammer a gate with the override.
How quickly does a k·m_health buffer drain under support loss on a live client (UpdateWear cadence)?

corrections: Top-level enforcement label should be corrected from 'server-enforced' to 'client-honoured' as the primary characterization, since against the project's actual all-vanilla-client population, indestructibility is fully achieved by the two client-honoured LoadFields levers (Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false, WearNTear.m_noSupportWear/m_noRoofWear=false) alone — see also the Phantom Survival correction above, where m_canBeRemoved=false already independently zeroes all non-forced wear damage, further reducing what lever (2) needs to do. Levers (3)/(4) (RPC_DestroyZDO veto, RPC_ZDOData watchdog) are real and correctly described but defend only against a hypothetical modified client, which is explicitly outside this project's stated scope.
evidence: assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77139 RPC_ZDOData revision-gated wholesale apply confirmed exact, no sender/ownership check on the data content itself
Project ground rules state: 'every connected player runs a 100% vanilla client' — levers (3)/(4) address a threat model (modified clients) the project explicitly excludes
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Directly verified WearNTear.ApplyDamage (health<=0 immunity, `@float -= damage` then Destroy on reaching 0), Repair-equivalent health-ceiling behavior, and RPC_ZDOData's revision-gated wholesale-apply (`if (num4<=zDO.DataRevision) continue; ... zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)`) confirming that ANY higher-revision blob — including a forged lower s_health — is applied with no ownership/sender check beyond 'is this peer known' (FindPeer). This matches the option's core 'four levers, none alone sufficient' thesis precisely. However, the project's own stated environment is 100% vanilla clients, not modified/cheating clients — levers (3) RPC_DestroyZDO-veto and (4) RPC_ZDOData-watchdog exist specifically to defend against a MODIFIED client forging packets, which is outside the stated threat model (no player here can run modified code). Against the actual vanilla-only population this audit is scoped to, levers (1) Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false and (2) WearNTear field overrides (both client-honoured, both already verified real via LoadFields) are sufficient on their own for true indestructibility — (3)/(4) are precautionary hardening against a threat that, per the project's own ground rules, doesn't exist in-scope. The headline 'server-enforced' therefore overstates what's actually load-bearing day-to-day; the option's own body is honest about this split, but the top-level label should read 'client-honoured (with optional server-enforced hardening against non-vanilla clients, out of primary scope)'.

catalog.name: Sector Zero, Named — The Headless Zone-Spawn Predicate And Its Reaper
catalog.oneLine: Any ZDO beyond ±16.4 km, and every ZDO in zone (-256,-256), lands in sector 0 — the bucket the server's pinned reference position queries; whether the server instantiates them hinges on one predicate, ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() at zone (15625,15625), and if it is true the server-only reaper destroys any prefab-less ZDO it finds there.
catalog.howItWorks: `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` maps any zone with (x+256) ≥ 512 or (y+256) ≥ 512 to `Sector = 0` (:115760-115773); zone (-256,-256) legitimately maps to 0 as well; `ZDO.SetSector` routes OutsideZones ZDOs to `ZoneSystem.SectorZero` (:73757-73758). The server's `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position at (1e6,0,1e6) → zone (15625,15625); `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` queries `FindSectorObjects` around that zone, and because every neighbouring sector clamps to index 0, `FindObjects` (which dedupes by SectorIndex) visits `m_objectsBySector[0]` + `m_portalObjects[0]` once. `CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105-82143) returns immediately unless `IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:114054-114069) — true only when every zone within NearSimulationDistance of (15625,15625) is in `m_zones`. Those zones are created by `ZoneSystem.Update` → `CreateLocalZones(GetReferencePosition())` (:113930) → `PokeLocalZone` → `SpawnZone(zone, Full)` (:114071-114092), which needs `HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady` at zonePos (1e6, …) — WorldGenerator returns the edge height (−400) there, so the build should succeed, but nothing in the decompile proves the builder completes at that coordinate. If it does, the server instantiates sector-0 ZDOs: `IsZoneReadyForType` does not require m_zones membership (:115797-115810), `CreateObject` runs, and the server-only branch destroys any ZDO whose prefab cannot be instantiated — `item.SetOwner(session); DestroyZDO(item)` with the log line 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' (:82137-82143). Consequences: (a) a Void Anchor (prefab 0) whose coordinate is typo'd beyond ±16.4 km, or placed in zone (-256,-256), is reaped within a frame; (b) a real portal placed there is instantiated on the server — a live TeleportWorld with Awake/UpdatePortal and RPC_SetTag registered, the one place a server-side portal component exists; (c) `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` uses zone distance, not sector index (:76887-76899), so the server never auto-owns those objects — the reaper's explicit SetOwner is what makes DestroyZDO work. Decisive test: log `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` and `m_zones.ContainsKey(new Vector2s(15625,15625))` 60 s after world load, and `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()`.
catalog.playerExperience: None directly. If the predicate is true, an admin who fat-fingers a Void Anchor coordinate to 20000 sees the server log 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' and the connected portal goes dark; if false, the anchor silently works but the ZDO is filed in a bucket nothing but the server ever queries.
failureModes: Predicate unknown: HeightmapBuilder at (1e6,0,1e6) may never report ready, leaving IsActiveAreaLoaded false forever and the server inert on the scene side.
If true, every prefab-0 Void Anchor or unknown-hash ZDO in sector 0 is reaped server-side.
Zone (-256,-256) at world coordinates (−16384, −16384) is beyond the 10.5 km world edge — harmless in practice, but any ZDO there shares the bucket.
Server-instantiated GameObjects in that bucket run full component logic headless (UpdatePortal, WearNTear owner checks) with no Player present — untested code paths.
prerequisites: One logging probe on a live dedicated server
openQuestions: Is IsActiveAreaLoaded() true on a headless 1.0.7 server (does HeightmapBuilder build zones at 1e6)? IN-GAME CHECK as described.

If true, does a real portal ZDO placed in sector 0 get instantiated server-side with a working TeleportWorld (RPC_SetTag then handled by the server)? IN-GAME CHECK: place one at x=20000 and retag from a client.

verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified SectorToIndex: `num=(uint)(sectorX+256); if (num>=512 || num2>=512) Sector=0; else Sector=num2*512+num;` — confirms both the ±16.4km-out-of-range wraparound-to-0 claim AND that zone (-256,-256) legitimately computes Sector=0 via the else branch (num=0,num2=0). Most importantly, CreateObjectsSorted's reaper logic was found at the EXACT cited line (82105 in this copy) and matches the option's description almost verbatim: `if (!IsActiveAreaLoaded()) return;` then for each candidate ZDO, `if (CreateObject(item)!=null) {...} else if (IsServer()) { item.SetOwner(GetSessionID()); ZLog.Log("Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO:"+uid); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(item); }` — this is a precise, high-confidence match. The option's own feasibility label (needs-ingame-check) is appropriately conservative given IsActiveAreaLoaded()'s truth at the pinned reference position still depends on HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady succeeding at (1e6,0,1e6), which this pass did not independently test.

catalog.name: Admin Command Channel — RPC_RemoteCommand Is Alive
catalog.oneLine: A vanilla admin client's console forwards any RemoteCommand-flagged vanilla command it cannot run locally to the server, which runs it through the headless Console after an adminlist check — a prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand keyed on a mod prefix makes this a real text command channel.
catalog.howItWorks: The client's `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (client :45734-45758) looks the first token up in its own `commands` dictionary; if the command exists but `IsValid` fails (e.g. onlyServer commands like `setkey`, `removekey`, `listkeys`, :43509-43533) and the command is `RemoteCommand`, it calls `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (client :45741-45744). On the server `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81888) rejects non-admins via `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — the socket-verified identity — and otherwise `InternalCommand` logs and runs `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)` (:81891-81895); `Console` is instantiated headless in `Game.Awake` (:100038-100041). The mod adds a Harmony prefix on the server's `Terminal.TryRunCommand(string text, bool, bool)`: if `text` starts with `removekey tpl ` (or any RemoteCommand-flagged vanilla verb followed by a mod sentinel), parse the remainder as the mod's command, execute, reply with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, ...)` — the ZRpc is available by prefixing `ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command)` instead, which is the cleaner hook — and return false so vanilla never sees a malformed key. Replies land in the admin's console (`RPC_RemotePrint`). This is an admin-only channel by construction (non-admins get 'You are not admin'); ordinary players still have only emotes/pings. Use for portal admin verbs: list, lock, unlock, retag, pair, place phantom, report.
catalog.playerExperience: An admin presses F5 on an unmodified client and types `removekey tpl lock Hub-North`. The console prints 'tpl: Hub-North locked (3 links cleared)' a moment later. A non-admin typing the same sees 'You are not admin'. Nobody else sees anything.
failureModes: Only vanilla commands flagged RemoteCommand and failing IsValid on the client are forwarded; the sentinel must ride one of them (`removekey`, `setkey`, `listkeys` are the natural carriers).
If the prefix misses, vanilla `removekey tpl` runs on the server and harmlessly tries to remove a non-existent key — but `setkey` as a carrier would ADD a junk world key; prefer `removekey`.
The client's own console echo shows the raw command line; cosmetic.
ListContainsId semantics changed in 1.0.12 to accept either id form (per MIGRATE-1.0.md) — more permissive, not less.
openQuestions: Confirm end-to-end on a live server: admin client `removekey tpl ping` → server log 'Remote admin … executed command' → RemotePrint reply visible in the client console.

RunAction(...); else if (value.RemoteCommand && ZNet.instance && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()) ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text);` confirmed exact. ZNet.RemoteCommand: `if (IsServer()) InternalCommand(null,command); else GetServerRPC()?.Invoke("RPC_RemoteCommand", command);` confirmed. Server's RPC_RemoteCommand confirmed to gate on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — a socket-verified identity check, unspoofable by a plain vanilla client — before calling InternalCommand→`Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`. Confirmed 'setkey'/'removekey' are registered with `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` (both explicitly checked in source), validating the mechanism generically. Confirmed Console (subclass of Terminal, not overriding TryRunCommand) is instantiated server-side in Game.Awake (`if (!Console.instance) Instantiate(m_consolePrefab);`) — necessary for Console.instance.TryRunCommand to have anything to call, and independently corroborated by its use inside the already-verified RPC_RemoteCommand→InternalCommand path. This is a genuinely server-enforced, authenticated admin channel; the Harmony-prefix-on-Terminal.TryRunCommand design is sound because Console doesn't override that method.

catalog.name: Boss Blackout, Corrected — The Half That Is World-Wide And The Half That Is On-Screen
catalog.oneLine: NoBossPortals blocks constructed portals when EITHER the traveller's own HUD shows an active boss (per-client) OR the server-broadcast activeBosses key is > 0 (world-wide); only the second half is a server-observable or server-drivable blackout.
catalog.howItWorks: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 3 (:143528) is `NoBossPortals && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0))`. `GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106949) returns `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent` — the boss health bar currently displayed on THAT client (within EnemyHud's boss show distance and alerted) — so this half is local to each traveller's screen and cannot be read or set by the server. The `activeBosses` half is a float global key the owning client of a boss increments in `BaseAI.SetAlerted` (once per boss via the s_bossCount ZDO bool) and decrements on death (`Character.OnDeath` :3153-3165), broadcast by the server's key store to everyone — world-wide, server-readable, and server-writable (`ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, n)`). Practical consequences for a portal mod: (1) an 'auto-lockdown during boss fights' feature that sets NoBossPortals gets a world-wide blackout only while some client has raised activeBosses; a player fighting a boss whose HUD shows it is additionally blocked locally even when the key is 0 (e.g. the increment was lost). (2) The server can manufacture a blackout by writing `activeBosses 1` and lift it with `activeBosses 0`, independent of any real boss — and should watch for the leak case where a crash leaves the counter stuck. (3) Dungeon doors use a different, positional, EnemyHud-dependent test (`Teleport.Interact` :143355 → `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` :133631-133645) and are unaffected by the key value alone. (4) Any server-side 'blanket drop of remote SetGlobalKey' hardening must whitelist `activeBosses` and `defeated_*`, or client-driven boss progression breaks (:3153-3165).
catalog.playerExperience: With NoBossPortals set, a player 200 m from an aggroed Bonemass (no health bar on screen) is blocked only if some client's increment reached the server; a player inside the fight with the bar on screen is blocked regardless. When the server writes activeBosses 1 for a scheduled 'blackout hour', every portal in the world answers 'blocked by boss' with no boss anywhere.
failureModes: The HUD half is invisible to the server: it cannot log or override a local boss-bar block.
activeBosses is client-maintained; crashes leave it non-zero and portals blocked world-wide until the server zeroes it.
A blanket server-side veto of remote SetGlobalKey (a plausible hardening for NoPortals/TeleportAll) silently breaks `defeated_*` and `activeBosses` updates from clients.
openQuestions: EnemyHud boss show distance and the exact conditions under which a boss bar appears for a non-participant (Inspector m_maxShowDistanceBoss) — decides how often the HUD half fires for bystanders.

verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified TeleportWorld.Teleport's boss gate at the literally cited line: `if (GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent()!=null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out float value) && value>0f)))` — exact match to the option's split-predicate claim. catalog.name: Raid Beacon
catalog.oneLine: Start a vanilla random event at a locked gate from the server: its own centre-screen message, forced music/weather, animated map pin, and client-run spawners become the lockdown's announcement and hazard.
catalog.howItWorks: `RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName(string name, Vector3 pos)` is public (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107067-107071) and calls private `SetRandomEvent(ev, pos)` (:107083-107109), which clones the RandomEvent, sets `m_pos`, and — because `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` — calls `SendCurrentRandomEvent()` (:106952-106962), a `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "SetEvent", name, time, pos)` broadcast. `RandEventSystem.instance` is live headless: `ZNet.SaveWorld` calls `RandEventSystem.instance.PrepareSave()/Save()` (:80534, :80626) and world load calls `Load` (:80765). The server re-broadcasts the current event every 2 s from `UpdateRandomEvent` (:106879-106884), so late joiners get it. Client `RPC_SetEvent` (:106965-106978) sets the same event locally. On each client, `FixedUpdate` (:106812-106821) makes it the *active* event only while `IsInsideRandomEventArea` — `Utils.DistanceXZ(pos, m_pos) < m_eventRange` and `y <= 3000` (:106829-106836). Activation shows `m_startMessage` via `MessageHud.ShowMessage(Center)` (:107539-107550); `EnvMan` takes `GetEnvOverride()` (:107308-107315, client consumer assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:96284) and `MusicMan` takes `GetMusicOverride()` (:107317-107324, client :103759). The client's `Minimap.UpdateEventPin` (client :57464-57503) draws an `EventArea` pin of `m_eventRange*2*0.9` plus an animated `RandomEvent` pin labelled `Localize(m_startMessage)` for **every** client regardless of distance, and removes both when the event clears. Spawners: `SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning` on the zone-owning client calls `RandEventSystem.GetCurrentSpawners()` (:110812) — non-null only when the local player is inside the area and `m_time > m_spawnerDelay` (:107299-107306) — and spawns around players in the zone via `FindBaseSpawnPoint` (:110879), marking each creature `s_eventCreature=true` (:110960-110963). Duration: `RandomEvent.Update` (:107521-107537) only advances `m_time` when `playerInArea` (server computes `IsAnyPlayerInEventArea` from `GetAllCharacterZDOS`, :107111-107121), and ends when `m_time > m_duration` (`m_duration<=0` = never). Mod loop: on lockdown of a managed gate, `SetRandomEventByName(cfgEvent, gatePos + up)`; each tick if `GetCurrentRandomEvent()?.m_name != cfgEvent` re-set it; on lift call `ResetRandomEvent()` (:107073-107076). Event names are Inspector data — enumerate `RandEventSystem.instance.m_events` (public, :106747) at OnWorldReady and expose a config dropdown.
catalog.playerExperience: The instant the beacon starts, every online player sees a pulsing red event marker with the event's own name (e.g. the localized $enemy_army_* text) on their map at the gate. A player who walks within m_eventRange (default 96 m, Inspector per event) gets the vanilla centre-screen raid message, the raid music and forced weather; the zone's spawner then spawns the event's creatures around them (not at the gate), exactly like a vanilla raid. Stepping outside the range ends the music/weather. When the lockdown lifts the pin vanishes, the message clears, and remaining event creatures walk off and despawn (BaseAI :27885-27892).
failureModes: There is ONE random-event slot (`m_randomEvent`); a beacon evicts any organic raid in progress and vanilla's own `UpdateRandomEvent` timer (:106844-106852) or a standalone event (:106858-106878) can evict the beacon — the re-assert tick (or a `StartRandomEvent` prefix, see Event Slot Governor) is mandatory.

Creatures spawn around PLAYERS inside the area, not at the gate; a beacon at an empty gate spawns nothing and its timer does not advance (`m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea`), so it persists until someone visits — intended, but the Discord/heartbeat must not report it as 'active'.
`m_duration` ticks only while someone is inside; a config 'beacon lasts 60 s' is 60 s of player presence, not wall-clock.
Events carrying `m_requiredGlobalKeys` are irrelevant here (SetRandomEventByName bypasses HaveGlobalKeys), but `GetEvent` (:107051-107065) refuses `m_enabled==false` events silently.

`RandomEvent.Update` dereferences `GameCamera.instance.AddShake` when `m_cameraShakeCurve.length > 0` (:107532-107535) — on the server this is headless; vanilla raids survive it in production, implying either empty curves or a live camera object, but a modded event with a shake curve could NRE the server FixedUpdate.
Event pin label and message are the event's own strings; you cannot say 'PORTAL LOCKED' — pair with PlayerNotify/ShowMessage for the actual reason.
Interiors are excluded (y>3000 check) so a beacon on a dungeon-side portal never activates for the player inside.
The event is saved with the world (`Save` :107400-107408); a crash mid-lockdown reloads with the beacon armed — the mod's reconciler must clear stale beacons at OnWorldReady.
prerequisites: Force-Disconnect Lockdown or Per-Network Quarantine-Tag Lockdown (the thing being announced)
Connection Vault and Crash Recovery (to know the beacon is stale after restart)
Event Slot Governor (this list) to keep the slot
citations: RandomEvent fields (m_eventRange=96, m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea, m_startMessage, m_forceMusic, m_forceEnvironment, m_spawn) — :107435-107498
SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning event spawner use — :110795-110816; FindBaseSpawnPoint at :110879; SetEventCreature at :110960-110963
