(:106952-106962), RPC_SetEvent (:106964-106977), IsAnyPlayerInEventArea/IsInsideRandomEventArea, GetBossEvent/GetForcedEvent unrelated to this event (confirmed separately). Enforcement label is honest: the server only owns the shared m_randomEvent broadcast (a route/world-state write), while message/music/spawns are correctly described as client-honoured per-player reactions to that shared state. No route-vs-player conflation found.

catalog.name: Event Slot Governor
catalog.oneLine: Own vanilla's single random-event slot: veto organic raids near managed hubs or during a beacon, and keep a beacon from being evicted, with a prefix on the public StartRandomEvent.
catalog.howItWorks: Organic raids start only server-side in `RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent` (:106838-106852) via `StartRandomEvent()` (public, :107030-107049) and via the standalone-interval branch (:106858-106878) which calls the private `SetRandomEvent(ev, pos)` directly. A Harmony prefix on `StartRandomEvent` returning false suppresses the periodic pick; a prefix on `SetRandomEvent(RandomEvent ev, Vector3 pos)` (AccessTools by name) can (a) return false when `ev != null` and a beacon is armed, or (b) return false when `pos` is within `HubRadius` of any managed hub in `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), which also covers the admin `randomevent`/`event` console commands (:43942-43971) and the admin routed RPC `RPC_ConsoleStartRandomEvent` (:106992-107003). The prefix must let the mod's own calls through (a static re-entrancy flag set around the mod's `SetRandomEventByName`). Because `SendCurrentRandomEvent` already re-broadcasts every 2 s, no extra sync is needed. Persist nothing: the vanilla slot is saved with the world (:107383-107408).
catalog.playerExperience: Players at a managed hub never get an organic raid rolled onto them (the roll still fires elsewhere for other players). During a beacon, the beacon stays up until the mod lifts it; nobody notices the governor exists.
failureModes: Blocking `StartRandomEvent` outright halves the raid rate globally if the prefix is too broad — scope it to positions near hubs or to beacon-active windows only.
The standalone-interval branch bypasses StartRandomEvent; if only StartRandomEvent is patched, standalone events (e.g. bat swarms) still evict a beacon.
`GetPossibleRandomEvents` picks a random player position (:107123-107140) — vetoing by position means the roll is consumed for that interval (no re-roll), a mild rate reduction.

Admin console `event`/`randomevent` are dead on a dedicated console anyway (`Player.m_localPlayer` deref at :43958), but the routed admin RPC is live and the governor must decide whether admins override.
openQuestions: Whether the standalone-interval events are enabled on vanilla worlds (m_standaloneInterval is Inspector data) — IN-GAME: dump m_events.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] StartRandomEvent (:107030-107049, server-gated by IsServer() at top), UpdateRandomEvent's periodic call, private SetRandomEvent (:107083-107109), and RPC_ConsoleStartRandomEvent (:106992-107003, calls StartRandomEvent() directly, admin-checked) all confirmed exact. The gated resource (m_randomEvent/m_forcedEvent) is a pure server-owned field with no per-player semantics -- this is a legitimate 'should this ROUTE (event slot) be occupied' server-enforced veto, not a mislabeled per-player check. Passes the route-vs-player test cleanly.

catalog.name: NoBossPortals Gate Model Correction
catalog.oneLine: Correct the catalog: the boss gate is 'activeBosses key > 0 (world-wide) OR a boss on THIS traveller's HUD (within 100 m and alerted)', not 'RandEventSystem boss event world-wide'.
catalog.howItWorks: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 3 (:143528) is `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0f))`. `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106949) is `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss()?.m_bossEvent` when non-empty — `GetActiveBoss` (:46873-46884) returns the first boss in the LOCAL HUD's `m_huds`, which `TestShow` (:46706-46728) fills only for bosses within `m_maxShowDistanceBoss` (100 f, :46661) of the local player that are alerted or `m_dontHideBossHud`+visible. It has no relation to `m_randomEvent`/`SetEvent`; the server's copy of `RandEventSystem` never sets a boss event (`GetForcedEvent` :106921-106929 is the same HUD lookup). So per traveller: blocked iff (world-wide) the `activeBosses` float key (ordinal 47, written by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27256-27262 and decremented in `Character.OnDeath` :3161-3165, both on the boss-owning client) is > 0, OR (local) a boss is on that player's screen. Consequences for Boss Auto-Lockdown: (1) the server-observable half is only the key — read `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out v)`; (2) the watchdog that zeroes a leaked counter must NOT zero while any boss-prefab ZDO with `s_alert` true exists (`ZDOVars.s_alert` is session-only but live) — scan `ZDOMan` for boss prefabs (`Character.m_boss` on the prefab via `ZNetScene.GetPrefab`) and `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_alert)`; (3) a server can *raise* the world-wide half deliberately with `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 1f)` to blackout every portal for every player without any boss existing — a cheaper Tier-A lockdown than NoPortals with a distinct message ($msg_blockedbyboss), but it collides with vanilla's own accounting (a later boss death decrements to 0 and lifts it early; an alert increments to 2). The blast-radius model for the catalog: key half = whole world, HUD half = ~100 m around each alerted boss, per player.
catalog.playerExperience: With NoBossPortals set: a player 200 m from an alerted boss whose fight has not yet bumped activeBosses passes; a player 50 m from an alerted boss is blocked with $msg_blockedbyboss even if the counter is 0; once the counter is >0 everyone everywhere is blocked. Dungeon doors use a different, narrower test (Teleport.Interact :143355, EnemyHud + same-zone) and are never blocked inbound.
failureModes: Treating `GetBossEvent` as server-visible produces a wrong radius model; the server can never observe the HUD half.

Zeroing activeBosses while a fight is live re-enables portals mid-fight and desyncs vanilla's per-boss `s_bossCount` guard (:27256) — the next death decrements to -1→clamped 0 (:3164), but the next alert of a different boss goes to 1 again; net effect is a fight-long window of open portals.
Forcing activeBosses=1 as a lockdown is undone by any boss death anywhere (Mathf.Max(0, v-1)).
prerequisites: Boss Auto-Lockdown with activeBosses Watchdog (this corrects it)
openQuestions: Which boss prefabs have non-empty m_bossEvent and m_dontHideBossHud — Inspector; IN-GAME: iterate ZNetScene prefabs with Character.m_boss and log m_bossEvent.
evidence: TeleportWorld.Teleport gate :143523-143531 (exact match confirmed by direct read)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified byte-for-byte: TeleportWorld.Teleport gate at line 143528 is exactly `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (GetBossEvent()!=null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses,out v) && v>0f))`; GetBossEvent/GetForcedEvent both resolve via EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss() with no relation to RandEventSystem's m_randomEvent/SetEvent; EnemyHud.TestShow boss branch is exactly `(isVisible && m_dontHideBossHud) || BaseAI.IsAlerted()` gated by m_maxShowDistanceBoss=100f; dungeon Teleport.Interact boss check at :143355 confirmed separate and narrower. This correction is fully accurate and should replace the prior catalog's model.

catalog.name: Teleport-Area Placement Gate Audit
catalog.oneLine: Discover which pieces carry Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea and which prefabs carry an EffectArea with the Teleport bit, because vanilla has a placement gate that mentions teleporting by name and nobody knows what uses it.
catalog.howItWorks: `EffectArea.Type` is a byte flags enum {Heat=1, Fire=2, PlayerBase=4, Burning=8, Teleport=0x10, NoMonsters=0x20, WarmCozyArea=0x40, PrivateProperty=0x80} (:124062-124073). `Player.UpdatePlacementGhost` sets `PlacementStatus.NoTeleportArea` when `component.m_onlyInTeleportArea && !EffectArea.IsPointInsideArea(point, EffectArea.Type.Teleport)` (:13349-13352), and `TryPlacePiece` refuses it with `$msg_noteleportarea` (:12461-12462). `IsPointInsideArea` is a `Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc` on the client's `character_trigger` layer (:124252-124268) — live colliders only, so the server can neither evaluate nor spoof the check; it can only cause a client to instantiate a prefab that carries such an EffectArea. Both `Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea` (:136153) and `EffectArea.m_type` (:124082) are Inspector fields; no prefab name appears in either decompile. The audit is a one-shot server-side pass at OnWorldReady over `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs`/`GetPrefabNames()` (:82345): for each prefab log `GetComponent<Piece>()?.m_onlyInTeleportArea` and every `GetComponentsInChildren<EffectArea>(true)` whose `m_type & Type.Teleport != 0`, plus the PlayerBase/NoMonsters/WarmCozyArea sets, and the same for every `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations[i].m_prefab` (load via `m_prefab.Load()`/`Asset`, release after) since locations are not in ZNetScene. Output feeds the placement-policy engine (a gated piece cannot be placed outside such areas by a vanilla client anyway) and the Fabricated Location Pad option (which location, if any, ships the Teleport area).
catalog.playerExperience: None directly — a log/report. If a portal variant is gated, players see $msg_noteleportarea when trying to place it outside the area; the report tells the operator which variant and where such areas exist.
failureModes: The dedicated server's ZNetScene prefab table is assumed populated with components (Wonderland's ContainerRegistry relies on it) — if a prefab's EffectArea sits on an inactive child, `GetComponentsInChildren(true)` is required.
Location prefabs are SoftReferences; loading all of them at once may spike memory — time-slice and Release.
openQuestions: Which prefab(s) set m_onlyInTeleportArea (candidates: a portal variant added with 1.0) and which location/prefab carries EffectArea.Type.Teleport — IN-GAME dump as described.
Whether the Ashlands portal_stone or any Deep North portal is the gated piece — same dump.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] EffectArea.Type flags enum (Heat=1,Fire=2,PlayerBase=4,Burning=8,Teleport=0x10,NoMonsters=0x20,WarmCozyArea=0x40,PrivateProperty=0x80) confirmed exact at :124062-124073; IsPointInsideArea confirmed as live-collider Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc (client-only, unspoofable server-side, as claimed); Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea (:136153) and its placement-ghost gate (:13349) confirmed exact. Correctly labeled needs-ingame-check since no prefab name carrying these flags appears anywhere in either decompile -- this really is undiscoverable without a runtime log pass.

catalog.name: Fabricated Location Pad
catalog.oneLine: Mint a LocationProxy ZDO server-side so every vanilla client materialises a location's non-networked parts (EffectAreas: NoMonsters, PlayerBase, WarmCozyArea, Teleport) around a hub — a spawn-free, base-flagged, comfort-bearing, and possibly build-unlocking pad with no client mod.
catalog.howItWorks: A vanilla client that receives a ZDO whose prefab is `ZoneSystem.m_locationProxyPrefab` (:113216) instantiates it; `LocationProxy.Awake` (:102631-102635) calls `SpawnLocation()` (:102663-102696), which reads `ZDOVars.s_location` (int hash of the location prefab name) and `ZDOVars.s_seed`, waits on `ShouldDelayProxyLocationSpawning` (:115139-115148, just async asset loading — no key gate), then `ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation(hash, seed, pos, rot)` → `SpawnLocation(..., SpawnMode.Client, ...)` (:115150-115160). In Client mode (:115294-115341) every ZNetView-bearing child is disabled and `Utils.Instantiate(location.m_prefab, pos, rot)` creates ONLY the static parts — meshes, colliders, EnvZones and `EffectArea` components (which register themselves in `EffectArea.Awake`, :124113-124143). Recipe on the server: `int proxyHash = ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationProxyPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode(); var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, proxyHash); z.SetPrefab(proxyHash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetRotation(rot); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_location, locName.GetStableHashCode()); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_seed, seed); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(z.m_uid);` (mirrors `CreateLocationProxy`/`SetLocation`, :115347-115356, :102653-102661). Effects the client then honours: `NoMonsters` makes `BaseAI` flee targets inside and keep out of the +15 m halo (:27924-27940 via :124228-124250); `PlayerBase` counts in `Player.m_baseValue` (20 m radius, :11395) and blocks `SpawnSystem`/`CreatureSpawner` spawns unless `m_insidePlayerBase` (:111010, :5661); `WarmCozyArea` feeds the resting check (:11633); `Teleport` satisfies the `m_onlyInTeleportArea` gate (:13349). Deleting the pad = `SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO`.
catalog.playerExperience: Walking into the hub the player sees whatever static geometry the chosen location has (this is the catch — you get the location's meshes, not an invisible field), monsters refuse to path in and flee, ambient spawns stop, resting comfort applies near it, and if the location carries a Teleport area the otherwise-gated portal variant becomes placeable there.
failureModes: You cannot fabricate a bare EffectArea — only whole vanilla locations; the pad looks like that location (a runestone camp, an altar…). Picking a visually small location with the right areas is the whole design problem and is Inspector data.
The zone's own generated location (if any) still spawns; two locations can overlap.
`PlayerBase` areas raise `baseValue` toward the raid threshold (`CheckBase` ≥3, :107212-107223) — the pad can make hubs raid-eligible; combine with Event Slot Governor.
The proxy ZDO is a normal sector ZDO (not a portal), so it is delivered only to peers whose active area covers it — correct behaviour; ForceSendZDO is only for the first push.
If the location has a DungeonGenerator/interior it is skipped in Client mode (ZNetView children disabled) — safe but confusing.
Persistence: `CreateNewZDO` does not set Persistent or prefab (:76684-76692) — both lines are mandatory or the pad vanishes on restart.
prerequisites: Teleport-Area Placement Gate Audit (to know which location carries which areas)
openQuestions: Name of m_locationProxyPrefab and its ZNetView m_persistent flag — IN-GAME: log `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationProxyPrefab.name` and its ZNetView.
Which vanilla locations carry which EffectArea types — audit option.

Whether a vanilla client cleanly destroys the spawned static location when the proxy ZDO is destroyed (LocationProxy.OnDestroy only unsets loading; the instance is parented to the proxy transform so Unity destroys it with it — expected yes).
evidence: ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int) :76674-76681 confirmed does not set Persistent/prefab
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] LocationProxy.Awake->SpawnLocation() confirmed reading ZDOVars.s_location/s_seed ints and calling ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation->SpawnLocation(...,SpawnMode.Client,...); Client-mode branch confirmed disabling ZNetView children then Utils.Instantiate(location.m_prefab,...) -- static parts only, exactly as claimed. ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int) confirmed public, and confirmed it does NOT auto-set Persistent or call SetPrefab (both are caller responsibilities per the prior review note) -- the option's own recipe already correctly includes z.SetPrefab(proxyHash) and z.Persistent=true, so it has already absorbed that caveat correctly rather than missing it.

catalog.name: Placement Policy Engine
catalog.oneLine: Generalise the per-player cap into a rule chain evaluated at the ZDO-arrival hook: spacing, biome bans, spawn exclusion, ward-permission, interior ban, and ward-proximity — all pure ZDO/geometry reads, rejection by SetOwner+DestroyZDO.
catalog.howItWorks: Hook pair from Wonderland SpawnGovernor (SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58): postfix on private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684-76692) remembering ZDOIDs created with `prefabHashIn == 0` (the `RPC_ZDOData` path at :77123 passes only uid+position), and postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` — the first moment `GetPrefab()` is real. `RPC_ZDOData` calls `AddIfPortal` AFTER Deserialize (:77132), so at evaluation the new portal is NOT yet in `GetPortalList()` — the spacing rule compares against the existing list without self-collision. Filter: `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` (:100021). Rules, all server-side: (1) spacing — min XZ distance to any `GetPortalList()` entry (:77648; use `GetPortals()` :77643 keyed by `ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex` :115748 and its 8 neighbours for O(1)); (2) biome ban — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos)` (:151725); (3) spawn exclusion — `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out spawn)` (:115422) distance; (4) interior ban — `Character.InInterior(pos)` (:4538, y>3000); (5) ward permission — Shadow Ward Index: for each guard-stone ZDO within radius, permitted iff `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)==placerId || pu_id{i}==placerId` (PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers shape :137349-137363) and `s_enabled` (:137423); (6) ward proximity — no portal within N m of a ward the placer is not permitted on; (7) cap — count `s_creator == placer` in the list. Placer identity: `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (written client-side in `Piece.SetCreator` :136415-136424 from `Player.PlacePiece` :12517). Reject: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929 owner-gated) → `SendDestroyed` broadcast → the placing client's `HandleDestroyedZDO` destroys its instance. Toast the reason via `PlayerNotify.Toast` on the peer whose character ZDO has `s_playerID == s_creator`. Rules live in the hot-reloaded .cfg; each rule is independently enabled and logged via AuditLog.
catalog.playerExperience: The player places the portal normally (ghost turns green, materials are consumed by the client), the portal appears for a fraction of a second, then vanishes; a top-left toast says why ('Portals must be 200 m apart', 'No portals in the Ashlands', 'Not permitted on this ward'). With the refund option, the materials drop at their feet.
failureModes: `s_creator` is client-authored and is 0 for pieces the client did not attribute (`Piece.SetCreator` only writes when IsOwner && creator==0) — treat 0 as 'unattributed' and apply only the non-owner rules.
Ward radius is Inspector data (`PrivateArea.m_radius` default 10 f at :137132); the ward rules are wrong until it is read in-game.

`s_creator` can be spoofed by a modified client to another player's id — the cap and ward rules are then attributable to the wrong player; cross-check against the sending peer's character ZDO `s_playerID` (`FindPeer(rpc)` gives the ZDOPeer; map to ZNetPeer by `m_rpc`).

Destroying a WearNTear/Piece-bearing ZDO in the Deserialize postfix is proven for creatures only (SpawnGovernor); the placing client's `Player.PlacePiece` also ran `WearNTear.OnPlaced` and effects — IN-GAME check for orphaned local instance.
Client `ConsumeResources` runs after `TryPlacePiece` returns (:10801-10807) — the materials are gone before the server rejects; refund option required for acceptable UX.
A rejected portal is still in `m_deadZDOs` (:76997) — never reuse its ZDOID.
openQuestions: Client-side cleanliness of destroy-on-arrival for a Piece (orphaned instance? effects?) — IN-GAME with cap=1.
PrivateArea.m_radius on guard_stone — IN-GAME.
Whether s_creator is reliably non-zero for player-placed portals in 1.0.7 — IN-GAME.
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData order :77076-77132 (confirmed exact by direct read)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Confirmed the exact ordering claim that is the option's core premise: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData creates a fresh ZDO via CreateNewZDO(zDOID,vector) with prefabHashIn defaulted to 0 (so the private CreateNewZDO's AddIfPortal(zdo,0) call is a no-op), THEN calls zDO.Deserialize(pkg2), THEN calls AddIfPortal(zdo,zdo.GetPrefab()) at line 77132 with the real hash -- meaning a postfix on ZDO.Deserialize genuinely sees the new portal's real prefab before it is added to GetPortalList(), exactly as claimed. ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (public, :76929), Game.PortalPrefabHash, GetPortalList/GetPortals, ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex, WorldGenerator.GetBiome, ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon, Character.InInterior(Vector3) static overload, Piece.Requirement/SetCreator all confirmed exact. This is a legitimate route-form check (should this ZDO be allowed to exist) fully owned by the server via DestroyZDO -- passes the enforceability test.

catalog.name: Ground-Drop Refund
catalog.oneLine: When the policy engine destroys a freshly placed portal, drop its full build cost on the ground at the site so a server-side rejection never costs materials.
catalog.howItWorks: The server cannot touch the placer's inventory (never networked), but it can create item ZDOs. Read the cost from the prefab, not ObjectDB: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab()).GetComponent<Piece>().m_resources` — `Piece.Requirement[]` of `m_resItem` (ItemDrop) and `m_amount` (:136071-136085; `GetAmount(1)` returns `m_amount`, :136087-136096). Skip the refund when the client paid nothing: piece ZDO `s_cheated` is set true by `Player.PlacePiece` when `NoCostCheat()` or cheated items (:12492, :12561), and `ConsumeResources` is skipped when `GetGlobalKey(piece.FreeBuildKey())` (NoBuildCost, :10805-10807, :136619-136626). For each requirement: `var data = req.m_resItem.m_itemData.Clone(); data.m_dropPrefab = req.m_resItem.gameObject;` (mandatory — ItemDrop.Awake never runs for a prefab, FirstSpawnGrant.cs:218 pattern) then `ItemDrop.DropItem(data, req.m_amount, pos + Vector3.up * 0.5f + jitter, Quaternion.identity)` (:70674-70691), which Instantiates the drop prefab server-side; its `ZNetView.Awake` mints a persistent server-owned ZDO and `component.Save()` writes `s_itemData`; the server's `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects` reaps the GameObject next frame while the ZDO stays and syncs to the placer. Split stacks above `m_shared.m_maxStackSize`. Budget: one refund per rejection, at most N per second globally.
catalog.playerExperience: The portal blinks out, a toast explains why, and a pile of fine wood, greydwarf eyes and surtling cores appears at the placement point for the player to pick up (auto-pickup grabs them if in range).
failureModes: Duplication exploit if the destroy fails or the client never actually consumed (NoBuildCost set, s_cheated): the guards above must be applied, and the refund must be issued only after `DestroyZDO` was accepted (zdo.IsOwner() true).
Position: dropping at the portal origin may be inside its own collider volume on the client — jitter 0.5–1 m and lift; items on water float away (Wonderland WaterBuoyancy already handles).
Items dropped in a non-loaded zone (placer disconnected between placement and evaluation — microseconds, essentially impossible) persist as normal item ZDOs.
`m_extraAmountOnlyOneIngredient`/`m_amountPerLevel` are item-crafting fields; pieces use m_amount only.
A modified client can re-send the same piece ZDO repeatedly to farm refunds — rate-limit refunds per s_creator and per peer.
openQuestions: Whether `ItemDrop.m_onDrop` or `Save()` needs ZNetScene instance state that the headless reaper removes before the first sync — FirstSpawnGrant proves DropItem works live; re-verify for the immediate-destroy-then-drop sequence.
corrections: Enforcement label is accurate but note it describes an unconditional server-side side effect, not a permission decision -- there is nothing here for a hostile client to defeat, which is a different (weaker) sense of 'server-enforced' than options that veto a route or object's existence.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Piece.Requirement (m_resItem, m_amount, GetAmount(int qualityLevel)) confirmed exact at :136071-136096. Player.PlacePiece's cheated-bool computation and its s_cheated ZDO write confirmed at the cited lines. ItemDrop.DropItem confirmed exact -- and confirmed it unconditionally does `Instantiate(item.m_dropPrefab,...)`, so the option's own note that m_dropPrefab must be manually set on the cloned ItemData before calling DropItem is correct and necessary (a real gotcha the option already anticipated rather than missed). Minor label nuance: this module is a compensating action, not a permission gate, so 'server-enforced' should be read as 'server-executed unilaterally' rather than a route/player veto -- it passes trivially since nothing here depends on client cooperation, but the route-vs-player framing doesn't really apply to a pure side-effect action.

catalog.name: Portal Sanctuary
catalog.oneLine: Destroy hostile creature ZDOs the moment they arrive within N m of any portal (or managed hubs only), making arrival points safe without wards, using the same arrival hook as the placement engine.
catalog.howItWorks: Creature spawns are client-side (SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`, :110795-110800) but every new ZDO arrives server-side through `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` → `CreateNewZDO(uid,pos)` → `Deserialize` (:77121-77131). At the Deserialize postfix (SpawnGovernor.cs:58): resolve `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())`, require a `Character` component with `m_faction` not in {Players, PlayerSpawned, TrainingDummy, AnimalsVeg(optional), Dverger(optional)} (`Character.Faction` enum :180-195; `m_faction` :255 is Inspector but readable on the server's prefab table), skip `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_tamed)` (written by `Character.RPC_SetTamed` :4490-4496; present in the first packet because `Character.Awake` reads it from the ZDO on the spawning client), skip bosses (`Character.m_boss`). Distance: `ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex(pos)` (:115748) and its 8 neighbours into `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643, keys are creation-time sectors — portals never move, so exact) then XZ distance ≤ SanctuaryRadius (default 24 m) — or against a managed-hub list only. Reject: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. Event creatures (`s_eventCreature`, :110960-110963) are included by default so a beacon's spawns cannot land inside the sanctuary. Budget: the check is O(9 sectors) per creature arrival; cap destroys per second (e.g. 32) and log via AuditLog. Optional: also sweep pre-existing hostile ZDOs near a hub once at OnWorldReady using `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25).
catalog.playerExperience: A greydwarf that spawns 15 m from the hub portal blinks out the instant it appears (the spawning client sees it for one sync tick, ~50–100 ms). Creatures that WALK into the radius are untouched — this is spawn suppression, not a shield; pair with a Fabricated Location Pad's NoMonsters area for pathing avoidance.
failureModes: Only new ZDOs are caught; creatures wandering in, or already-loaded ones, are not — advertise as 'no spawns', not 'safe zone'.
CreatureSpawner (dungeon/camp spawners) and RandomFlyingBird/Fish also arrive this way — the faction filter must whitelist ambient fauna or fish near a dock hub disappear.
Player-summoned skeletons are Faction.PlayerSpawned (Inspector) — verify per prefab; a wrongly-factioned modded summon would be deleted.
Tames arriving as NEW ZDOs (an offspring born near the portal, `Procreation` spawns with SetTamed) carry s_tamed in the first packet — expected, but IN-GAME verify.
A creature whose spawning client sets fields over two packets (rare) could be evaluated before s_tamed lands — mitigate by re-checking at destroy time.
`ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs` holds destroyed ids for the session; harmless.
prerequisites: Fabricated Location Pad (optional, for pathing avoidance)
openQuestions: Faction values of summoned/allied prefabs and of ambient fauna — IN-GAME dump of Character.m_faction per prefab.
Whether Procreation offspring carry s_tamed in their first ZDO packet — IN-GAME.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Character.Faction enum confirmed exact (Players, AnimalsVeg, ..., PlayerSpawned, TrainingDummy, DeepNorth all present as named). RPC_SetTamed/s_tamed write and Awake-time read confirmed. SpawnSystem.Spawn's SetEventCreature(despawn:true) for eventSpawner creatures, MonsterAI.SetEventCreature/IsEventCreature via ZDOVars.s_eventCreature, and BaseAI's despawn condition `IsEventCreature() && !RandEventSystem.HaveActiveEvent() && no target && !IsAlerted()` all confirmed exact, matching the 'aggro'd troll stays' caveat in playerExperience. Shares the exact same verified ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData/AddIfPortal-ordering hook and DestroyZDO as Placement Policy Engine -- same passing route-form test (object-existence veto, fully server-owned).

catalog.name: Authenticated Global-Key Relay Filter
catalog.oneLine: Replace the blanket 'drop client SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey' with a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC that authenticates by socket and drops only world-modifier keys (ordinal < NonServerOption) and mod-reserved prefixes, passing boss/progression keys through.
catalog.howItWorks: Why the existing option is wrong: (1) vanilla clients legitimately send these RPCs — `Character.OnDeath` calls `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey)` and decrements `activeBosses` (:3153-3165), `BaseAI.SetAlerted` increments it (:27256-27262); `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string)` is `InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946) to `GetServerPeerID()` (:83564-83574). (2) `RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string)` (:116022-116029) receives `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID`, deserialised straight off the wire (:83487-83495) — spoofable to the server's id. The only place the authentic connection is in scope is `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632-83643), which both handles locally (target==m_id) and relays. Prefix: `int pos = pkg.GetPos(); var d = new ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData(); d.Deserialize(pkg); pkg.SetPos(pos);` (`RoutedRPCData` is public, :83463). If `d.m_methodHash` is `"SetGlobalKey".GetStableHashCode()` or `"RemoveGlobalKey"`: `string key = d.m_parameters.ReadString()` (params package is positioned at 0 after Deserialize); classify with `ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue(key, out val, out gk)` (public static, :113560-113581) — DROP (return false) iff `gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (ordinals 0-40, all world modifiers incl. NoPortals=32, NoBossPortals=33, DungeonBuild=34, TeleportAll=35) or the lowercased name starts with a mod-reserved prefix (`tpl_`); PASS everything else (defeated_*, activeBosses=47, killed_*, StoneCircle, AshlandsOcean, custom mod keys). Resolve the real peer by `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (`m_rpc` public, :78780) and allow admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811) if configured; log drops through AuditLog with the socket host name. Returning false from the prefix skips both `HandleRoutedRPC` and `RouteRPC`. The server's own writes never pass through RPC_RoutedRPC (self-dispatch in InvokeRoutedRPC :83588), so no re-entrancy flag is needed.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing visible. Boss kills still set defeated_* and raise/lower activeBosses; a hacked client sending `removekey noportals` gets silently ignored and logged.
failureModes: `setkey`/`removekey` from an admin's F5 console travel as `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889), not as SetGlobalKey, so admin-in-game toggles are unaffected by this filter — but a non-admin cannot use them anyway.

World-modifier keys legitimately arrive from clients only through ServerOptionsGUI on a listen host (never on a dedicated server) — so dropping ordinal<41 is safe on dedicated only; guard with `ZNet.instance.IsDedicated()`.
A vanilla client running Character.OnDeath for a boss whose m_defeatSetGlobalKey is a value-carrying key is still passed (ordinal ≥42).
Peeking the package: the prefix must restore `pkg` position exactly, or the real handler reads garbage; deserialise a copy if in doubt (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())` then SetPos).
openQuestions: Whether any vanilla client path ever sends a world-modifier (ordinal<41) key to a dedicated server legitimately — none found in the decompile; IN-GAME: log all dropped keys for a week before enforcing.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] The strongest-verified option in the batch. Confirmed exact: ZNetPeer.m_rpc is public; ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData is a public class with Serialize/Deserialize exactly as described, params package (m_parameters) is a fresh ZPackage from ReadPackage() positioned at 0; ZPackage.GetPos/SetPos exist; RPC_RoutedRPC's local-handle-vs-relay logic confirmed exact (target==m_id or 0 handles locally, m_server relays); ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue confirmed exact, returning GlobalKeys.NonServerOption on parse failure (so unrecognized/mod-custom keys correctly fall outside the ordinal-based block, matching the design); GlobalKeys enum ordinals hand-counted and confirmed exact -- NonServerOption=41, so 'ordinals 0-40' for the world-modifier block (incl. NoPortals=32, NoBossPortals=33, DungeonBuild=34, TeleportAll=35) is precisely correct, and activeBosses=47 (used elsewhere in the catalog) also checks out. This is a legitimate route-form filter (should this GLOBAL KEY WRITE be applied) with no per-player ambiguity -- passes the enforceability test cleanly and is technically sound as described (Harmony can patch this private method).

catalog.name: Managed-Portal Relay Shield
catalog.oneLine: Rewrite or drop relayed packets that would delete or rewire a managed portal — DestroyZDO batches, Game.RPC_SetConnection, TeleportWorld's RPC_SetConnected — at the same RPC_RoutedRPC choke point, without breaking legitimate destructions in the same batch.
catalog.howItWorks: Three vanilla RPCs can alter a managed portal from any client: (a) `DestroyZDO` — global routed, `RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953-76961) reads a count and N ZDOIDs and `HandleDestroyedZDO`s each with no sender/ownership check, then the server relays the same packet to everyone (RouteRPC :83597-83618, target 0); (b) `RPC_SetConnection(ZDOID portal, ZDOID target)` — global routed, handled server-side (:100653-100662) with no checks, also relayed; (c) `RPC_SetConnected(ZDOID portalID)` — a ZNetView RPC TeleportWorld sends to the partner's owner (:143604-143629) which the server only relays. Prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ref ZPackage pkg)` (Harmony allows `ref` on original args): deserialise a copy; for `DestroyZDO`, read the ZDOID list from `m_parameters`, remove any id in the managed set (position-keyed vault → live ZDOID), and if anything was removed rebuild `m_parameters` (`Write(count)`, remaining ids) and re-serialise the whole RoutedRPCData into a fresh ZPackage assigned to `pkg` so vanilla handles/relays the filtered batch — never drop the whole packet (it batches unrelated deletions). For `RPC_SetConnection` and `RPC_SetConnected` whose target/portal ZDOID is managed: return false unless the real peer (`GetPeers().First(p=>p.m_rpc==rpc)`) is an admin. Vanilla's own server-originated `RPC_SetConnection` (Game.SetConnection :100637-100651) never traverses RPC_RoutedRPC. Also optionally drop `RequestStartEvent`/`RequestStopEvent` (PersistentEventSystem, registered :105284-105287, handled server-side with no sender check :105341-105381) from non-admins. Note the shield covers only the RPC layer; a hostile client can still rewrite the portal via `RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) — that is the Invariant Assertion Harness's job (detect-and-revert from the vault).
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing visible for honest players. A player who legitimately demolishes their own managed portal with a hammer sees it refuse to disappear (the WearNTear destroy path ends in DestroyZDO from the owning client, which is now filtered) — so managed portals must be visibly marked as admin-owned, or the filter must allow the creator.
failureModes: Filtering DestroyZDO blocks LEGITIMATE demolition of managed portals by their creator; decide policy (allow s_creator / allow admins).

`ZNetView.Destroy` on the owning client destroys the local GameObject before sending DestroyZDO; a filtered destroy leaves that client with no instance until the zone reloads — the server should `ForceSendZDO(peer, id)` the surviving portal back.
Re-serialising the package must reproduce RoutedRPCData.Serialize exactly (:83478-83485); a malformed rewrite kills the handler for every peer.
RPC_ZDOData-level rewrites are not covered; the shield is one layer of a two-layer defence.
prerequisites: Connection Vault and Crash Recovery (managed set, ZDOID resolution)
openQuestions: Whether Harmony's `ref ZPackage pkg` substitution in a prefix on this method is honoured under HarmonyX 2.9 (it is per API, but verify with a log).
Client behaviour when its own DestroyZDO for a piece is not echoed back (instance already gone locally) — IN-GAME.
evidence: Game.RPC_SetConnection registration :100067, handler :100653-100662 (confirmed no ownership check, broadcast-exploitable)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] All three exploit paths confirmed exact and, notably, WORSE than the option even states in one respect I independently verified: Game.RPC_SetConnection (registered globally via ZRoutedRpc.Register<ZDOID,ZDOID> at :100067, handler at :100653) performs ZERO ownership/legitimacy check -- any client can broadcast InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,"RPC_SetConnection",anyPortal,anyTarget) and it executes unconditionally both locally at the server (target==0 triggers HandleRoutedRPC on every recipient including the server itself) and relays to everyone else, fully bypassing Game.SetConnection's owner-based routing logic. ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO confirmed to have no sender/ownership check whatsoever. TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected confirmed exact including the IsOwner() guard on the receiving side. The Harmony ref-parameter technique for rewriting pkg in a RPC_RoutedRPC prefix is a legitimate, well-known Harmony capability for reference-type parameters even when the original signature isn't declared ref. The option is appropriately self-limiting ('covers only the RPC layer... RPC_ZDOData is the Invariant Assertion Harness's job'), which is honest scoping, not overclaiming.

catalog.name: Lockdown Legibility Rule
catalog.oneLine: Any key-based (Tier-A) lockdown longer than N seconds must be paired with a per-portal in-world signal — force-disconnect (vanilla UI shows it) or tag suffix + floating text — removed in the same tick the key is lifted.
catalog.howItWorks: With only `NoPortals` set, a vanilla portal is indistinguishable from a working one: `GetHoverText` (:143453-143464) shows `$piece_portal_connected` from `HaveTarget()` (connection != None) and `UpdatePortal` (:143491-143509) lights `m_target_found` from `IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` — neither reads NoPortals/NoBossPortals; the only feedback is `$msg_blocked` after a failed walk-in (:143523-143526). A Tier-B force-disconnect (connection = ZDOID.None) flips the hover to `$piece_portal_unconnected` and kills the glow for free. Rule, as a reconciler invariant: for every lockdown whose planned duration > LegibilityThreshold (default 30 s), the reconciler must observe on every portal in scope either (a) `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)==None`, or (b) `s_tag` ends with the configured marker (≤ 4 chars so a 6-char tag still fits the client's 10-char `TextInput.RequestText(...,10)` box, :143482, :61515-61522) AND a DamageText overlay loop is running for peers within 30 m. On lift, the same tick that removes the key restores connections from the vault / strips the suffix and stops the overlay — the announcement stack then reports 'portals open'. The rule is enforced by the Invariant Assertion Harness: a key-lockdown found without a signal after the threshold is escalated to Tier-B automatically and logged.
catalog.playerExperience: A locked portal either reads [Unconnected] and is dark, or reads its name with a ' [X]' suffix and shows an orange 'Portals locked' floating text when approached — never a glowing, [Connected] gate that rejects you with a one-line message.
failureModes: Tag suffix rewrites change the tag string, and `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100594-100606) tears down any pair whose members differ — the whole tag group must be rewritten inside one tick, or ConnectPortals must be prefixed off during the sweep, or 3+-member groups reshuffle their orphan.

Suffix + player retag during lockdown: the client pre-fills the dialog with the suffixed tag; a player saving it keeps/loses the suffix unpredictably — the watcher must treat 'tag without suffix' as a new base tag and re-suffix.
The overlay is 1.5 s (`m_textDuration`, :46335) and 30 m (`m_maxTextDistance`, :46337) — a re-send loop per nearby peer is required (see Locked-Gate Overlay).
prerequisites: Invariant Assertion Harness and Panic Restore
openQuestions: Whether GuiInputField clamps a pre-filled text longer than characterLimit — IN-GAME.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] TeleportWorld.GetHoverText confirmed exact: text2 = HaveTarget() ? "$piece_portal_connected" : "$piece_portal_unconnected" with no reference to NoPortals/NoBossPortals, confirming the option's central claim that a Tier-A key lockdown gives zero in-world signal. TextInput.instance.RequestText(this,"$piece_portal_tag",10) confirmed exact (the 10-char cap). Game.ConnectPortals tag-mismatch teardown (SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None) when partner tag/connection mismatches) confirmed exact, supporting the same-group-tag-preservation design for the Locked-Gate Overlay mechanism this rule depends on.

catalog.name: Locked-Gate Overlay
catalog.oneLine: The mechanics behind the legibility rule: atomic per-group tag suffixing that survives vanilla's reconciler, plus a budgeted RPC_DamageText loop that floats 'Portals locked' over each locked gate for peers within 30 m.
catalog.howItWorks: Tag suffix: group portals by exact `s_tag` (ordinal, :100597-100601); for each group, in ONE frame, claim ownership (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`), `Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag + marker)`, `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — a tag-only write does not dirty the portal chunk), `ForceSendZDO` — same-group members keep identical strings so `ConnectPortals` phase 1 sees no mismatch and existing links survive; the Mass-Rewrite budget applies per GROUP not per portal (groups are small). Store the original tag in the vault keyed by rounded position. Hover on the client re-reads `GetTagInfo()` every frame (:143455). Overlay: per tick (every 1.2 s) for each locked portal, for each ready peer whose character ZDO (`ConnectedCharacters.All()`) is within 30 m: `ZPackage p; p.Write((int)DamageText.TextType.Bonus); p.Write(portalPos + Vector3.up*2.5f); p.Write("$tpl_locked"/plain text); p.Write(false); ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DamageText", p)` — handler `RPC_DamageText` (:46494-46510) checks distance to the peer's camera ≤ `m_maxTextDistance` (30 f) and `AddInworldText` (:46395+) localises the text and colours Bonus orange (1f,0.63f,0.24f) with 1.5 s duration (:46335). Never TextType.TooHard/Blocked (they mangle the string). Peer-targeted, not broadcast, so cost = (locked portals × nearby peers) per 1.2 s. On lift: strip suffix in the same group-atomic way, stop the loop.
catalog.playerExperience: Approaching a locked gate, an orange 'Portals locked' floats above it every ~1.5 s while within 30 m; the hover reads Tag:"Home [X]" [Connected]. When the lockdown lifts, the text stops and the tag is back to "Home".
failureModes: Untagged groups ("") become " [X]" — a distinct, still-single group; fine, but restore must map " [X]" → "".
Player retags during lockdown reshuffle groups; the watcher re-suffixes on the next tick (one ConnectPortals window of inconsistency, ≤5 s).
Overlay text is not shown when the player's HUD is hidden (`Hud.IsUserHidden`) or outside 30 m; it is decoration, not enforcement.
Marker eats 4 of the 10 client characters if the player edits the tag during lockdown.
prerequisites: Mass-Rewrite Spike Control and Save-Bloat Budget
openQuestions: Whether a vanilla client refreshes the hover string for a portal it currently stands beside after a server-side s_tag write without a zone reload — IN-GAME (GetTagInfo reads the ZDO each frame, expected yes).
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] DamageText.TextType enum confirmed exact (Bonus is a real, last member); RPC_DamageText confirmed exact structure (reads TextType, Vector3, string, bool; computes camera distance; gates on m_maxTextDistance=30f before calling AddInworldText) -- matches the citation precisely including the m_maxTextDistance=30f constant. Game.ConnectPortals tag-equality reconciliation (item.GetString(s_tag) compared ordinally between paired portals) confirmed exact, supporting the claim that same-group members keeping identical suffixed tag strings survive reconciliation. ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals confirmed to exist as a public method (:76702).

catalog.name: Beacon Cleanup Sweep
catalog.oneLine: When a Raid Beacon or organic raid at a managed gate ends, destroy leftover event creatures near the gate server-side instead of waiting for the client-side despawn walk.
catalog.howItWorks: Event creatures carry `ZDOVars.s_eventCreature=true` (SpawnSystem.Spawn :110960-110963 via `MonsterAI.SetEventCreature` :28280-28284). Vanilla despawn is client-side and slow: `BaseAI` only calls `MoveAwayAndDespawn` when `IsEventCreature() && !RandEventSystem.HaveActiveEvent()` and the creature has no target and is not alerted (:27885-27892) — an aggro'd troll stays. On `ResetRandomEvent()` (or when `GetCurrentRandomEvent()` transitions to null), run `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(gatePos, m_eventRange + 32)` (Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25), select ZDOs with `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_eventCreature)` whose prefab has a `Character` and is not `s_tamed`, and `SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO` them, budgeted (≤64 per tick) — same primitives as Portal Sanctuary. Optionally skip creatures currently `s_alert` true within 20 m of a player (let the fight finish).
catalog.playerExperience: The moment the lockdown lifts, the raid horde at the gate vanishes rather than shuffling off into the woods for a minute.
failureModes: Destroying creatures mid-combat drops no loot and can feel like a bug — the alert/proximity skip trades cleanliness for fairness.
Organic raids elsewhere are untouched (sweep is gate-scoped).
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] SpawnSystem.Spawn's s_eventCreature write, MonsterAI.SetEventCreature/IsEventCreature, and BaseAI's slow client-side despawn condition (requires no target and not alerted) all confirmed exact -- correctly motivating the need for a faster server-side sweep. ZDOMan.DestroyZDO confirmed public and usable exactly as the shared primitive from Portal Sanctuary. This is again a route-form (object-existence) decision fully owned by the server -- passes the enforceability test.

catalog.name: Lights Out — server-forced sleep fade (SleepStart/SleepStop)
catalog.oneLine: The server fires vanilla's own 'SleepStart'/'SleepStop' routed RPCs at one peer or at everyone, producing a full-screen sleep fade with input lockout — the only global-blackout primitive that needs no prefab hash and no client mod.
catalog.howItWorks: Game.Start registers two ZDO-less routed RPCs on every peer: ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register('SleepStart', SleepStart) and Register('SleepStop', SleepStop) (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100063-100064). The client handlers are Game.SleepStart -> Player.m_localPlayer.SetSleeping(true) (:100752-100759) and Game.SleepStop -> SetSleeping(false) + AttachStop() + a profile save when m_saveTimer > 60 (:100761-100777). Player.SetSleeping flips the private m_sleeping bool; on the false edge it shows '$msg_goodmorning', grants SEMan.s_statusEffectRested, stamps m_wakeupTime and increments PlayerStatType.Sleep (:15992-16005). While m_sleeping is true, Player.InCutscene() returns true (:15505-15508), which is what disables input, and Hud.UpdateBlackScreen fades the loading canvas to alpha 1 over Game.m_fadeTimeSleep and shows the sleeping-progress panel in preference to the teleport panel (:47853-47871, fade duration :47845-47847). Vanilla only uses this from the server-only Game.UpdateSleeping (:100712-100733), which broadcasts to 0L after EnvMan.SkipToMorning(). A mod invokes the same RPC directly: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'SleepStart') for one player, or 0L for everyone (the server's own local dispatch hits a null m_localPlayer and no-ops). Because the mod never sets Game.m_sleeping, vanilla's UpdateSleeping will NOT send the matching SleepStop; the mod must send 'SleepStop' itself after its work (a Blackout Swap: SleepStart -> rewrite connections/positions -> RPC_TeleportPlayer -> SleepStop). Ordering: Hud gives the sleeping panel precedence over the teleport panel, so a teleport issued under the sleep fade is invisible to the player; Player.TeleportTo has no sleeping check (:15302-15327) and UpdateTeleport still runs from the !IsDead branch of FixedUpdate, so the move completes under the black screen. Time is NOT skipped unless the mod also calls EnvMan.instance.SkipToMorning() server-side (:100729).
catalog.playerExperience: The screen fades to black exactly like going to bed, with the sleeping spinner. The player cannot move or open menus. When the server sends SleepStop the screen fades back in, '$msg_goodmorning' flashes centre-screen, they receive the Rested buff, and — if they were seated or in a bed — they are stood up (AttachStop). If the mod teleported them meanwhile, they wake somewhere else with no portal swirl.
failureModes: SetSleeping(true) blocks Player.AttachStop (:15892) — a player who was in a bed/chair stays attached until SleepStop; a teleport issued to an attached-and-sleeping player ping-pongs (UpdateAttach runs before UpdateTeleport, :10217/:10226).

No matching SleepStop is ever sent by vanilla for a mod-initiated SleepStart (Game.m_sleeping is false on the server, :100718). A crashed mod tick leaves every targeted player black-screened until they relog.
Side effects on wake are not optional: Rested buff, '$msg_goodmorning', Sleep stat increment (:15999-16002) and a player-profile save if m_saveTimer > 60 (:100769-100776).
If a real sleep cycle is in progress (Game.m_sleeping true) the server's own UpdateSleeping will send SleepStop within 2 s and wake the mod's targets early (:100720-100725).
Fade time is Game.m_fadeTimeSleep, an Inspector float — the blackout is not instant; plan the swap for after the fade completes (needs an in-game timing).
prerequisites: Forced teleport option (RPC_TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportTo) if used as a swap cover
openQuestions: Value of Game.m_fadeTimeSleep on the shipped Game prefab (Inspector). In-game: time SleepStart to full black on a vanilla client.
Does a SleepStart delivered while the player is mid-teleport (m_teleporting) break the teleport panel handoff? In-game: send RPC_TeleportPlayer then SleepStart 0.5 s later and observe both overlays.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Every load-bearing citation checks out exactly against the server decompile. Game.Start registers 'SleepStart'/'SleepStop' at :100063-100064 (ZDO-less routed RPCs). Game.SleepStart/SleepStop bodies at :100752-100777 match verbatim (SetSleeping(true)/false+AttachStop+conditional profile save). Player.InCutscene's m_sleeping branch confirmed at :15495-15513 — m_sleeping alone forces InCutscene()=true. Player.SetSleeping body (:15992-16003) confirmed: flips m_sleeping, on false-edge shows $msg_goodmorning, grants s_statusEffectRested, stamps m_wakeupTime, increments Sleep stat — exactly as claimed. Hud.UpdateBlackScreen (:47853-47875) confirmed to give the sleeping panel branch priority over the teleport-progress branch, and GetFadeDuration returns m_fadeTimeSleep (default 3f) only when IsSleeping(). Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15323) has no sleeping check — only IsTeleporting()/m_teleportCooldown<2f gates — confirmed by direct read. AttachStop's 'if(m_sleeping||!m_attached) return' guard does not block SleepStop's flow because SetSleeping(false) is called first, clearing m_sleeping before AttachStop() runs. ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC's local-dispatch-for-targetPeerID==0L branch confirms the server's own HandleRoutedRPC call into SleepStart/SleepStop hits a null Player.m_localPlayer and no-ops safely, exactly as claimed. Enforcement is honestly labeled client-honoured (pure UX, no permission gate implied).

catalog.name: Dream Reel — RPC_SetDreamCinematic queued video
catalog.oneLine: The server queues a named video cinematic that plays on every client's next sleep — an ambient, one-shot narrative channel with no gameplay effect.
catalog.howItWorks: CinematicsManager.Update registers ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<string>('RPC_SetDreamCinematic', RPC_SetDreamCinematic) once ZRoutedRpc and Game exist (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42368-42374). The handler stores the name in the static m_dreamCinematic if Player.m_localPlayer exists (:42616-42623). CinematicsManager.OnSleep plays it when non-empty and the local player IsSleeping(), then clears it (:42607-42614). The vanilla sender is the static CinematicsManager.SetDreamCinematic(name) which broadcasts to 0L (:42601-42605); a mod can call ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_SetDreamCinematic', name) to target one player. Combined with the Lights Out option (SleepStart puts the player into IsSleeping()), the server can force the video immediately rather than waiting for a real bed sleep — OnSleep is what checks IsSleeping(), so the call site of OnSleep decides whether a forced sleep triggers it (it is invoked from the sleep flow on the client; needs confirmation). Video names are the entries of CinematicsManager.m_videos (Inspector data, :42628); only names present in the client's list can play. UX value for portals: a 'network rebuilt' or lore card when a hub is retired; strictly cosmetic.
catalog.playerExperience: Next time the player sleeps (or is put to sleep by the server), a full-screen video plays before the morning fade; Escape/Jump/B skips it (:42379).
failureModes: Requires a real or forced sleep; without Lights Out it is deferred indefinitely.
Video names are Inspector data; an unknown name is a silent no-op or a log line depending on Play()'s handling (unverified).
Registration happens in Update, not Awake; a client that has not yet ticked CinematicsManager.Update drops the RPC with 'Failed to find rpc method'.
Only vanilla-shipped videos exist; no custom content can be injected.
prerequisites: Lights Out (forced sleep) for immediate playback
openQuestions: Which video names exist in CinematicsManager.m_videos on a 1.0.7 client? In-game: dump m_videos[i].name on a client.
Is CinematicsManager.OnSleep invoked from the forced SleepStart path or only from Bed's own sleep sequence? In-game: send SetDreamCinematic then SleepStart and see whether the video plays.
corrections: The uncertain claim 'needs confirmation: whether forced sleep triggers OnSleep' is resolved by the decompile itself: OnSleep is invoked by SleepText.ShowDreamText (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141936-141966), fired from the m_sleepingProgress panel's OnEnable, which activates purely from Player.IsSleeping()==true regardless of how sleep began — so forced SleepStart does trigger the dream video.
Feasibility should move from needs-ingame-check to feasible given this resolved chain (video name must still be present in the client's own m_videos list).
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Core citations all verified: CinematicsManager.Update lazily registers 'RPC_SetDreamCinematic' (:42371-42374), static m_dreamCinematic field (:42314), RPC_SetDreamCinematic handler stores name if Player.m_localPlayer exists (:42616-42622), static SetDreamCinematic broadcasts to 0L (:42601-42605), OnSleep checks IsSleeping() and plays+clears (:42607-42614). The option flagged one open question — 'needs confirmation' whether a server-forced sleep (via the Lights Out SleepStart RPC) actually triggers CinematicsManager.OnSleep() rather than only a real bed-sleep flow. I traced this and it resolves definitively: OnSleep() is called from SleepText.ShowDreamText() (class at :141936, ShowDreamText at :141963-141966), which fires via Invoke('ShowDreamText',4f) in SleepText.OnEnable — and SleepText lives on the m_sleepingProgress GameObject that Hud.UpdateBlackScreen activates purely off player.IsSleeping() (:47868), which is driven solely by the m_sleeping bool that SleepStart's SetSleeping(true) call sets. There is no dependency on how sleep was entered (bed vs forced RPC), so the 'needs confirmation' caveat is resolved to YES — a server-forced SleepStart does trigger the dream video ~4s later. This upgrades feasibility from needs-ingame-check to feasible (still gated by the video name existing in the client's own Inspector-defined m_videos list, an already-acknowledged caveat).

catalog.name: Puppet Strings — server-invoked animator triggers on a player's body
catalog.oneLine: The server invokes the per-character 'SetTrigger' RPC to play any animator trigger (stagger, jump, dodge, gpower, eat, emotes) on a player's body for everyone in view — a non-textual, body-language acknowledgement.
catalog.howItWorks: ZSyncAnimation.Awake registers m_nview.Register<string>('SetTrigger', RPC_SetTrigger) on every ZNetView-bearing animated object including players (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87157). RPC_SetTrigger is a bare m_animator.SetTrigger(name) with no owner check (:87330-87332). Vanilla's own sender broadcasts to ZNetView.Everybody (:87260-87263), so the ZDO-scoped route is: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, characterZdoId, 'SetTrigger', name) — every peer that currently has that Player instantiated (the owner and everyone within its active area) runs the trigger; peers without the instance drop it in ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83656-83663). Targeting a single peer (peer.m_uid instead of 0L) plays it only on that player's own screen. Trigger names that the vanilla Player code itself fires, and that therefore exist on the Player animator: 'stagger' (:2851), 'jump' (:3483), 'interact' (:7659), 'eat' (:7705), 'equip_hip' (:8749), 'dodge' (:15196), 'gpower' (:15717), 'attack_abort' (:23006), 'detach' (:23010), 'attach' (:24045). Emotes are NOT triggers — they go through ZDOVars.s_emote/s_emoteID (:15585-15598) — so an 'emote_*' trigger name is Inspector data. Because this is purely animator state, it changes no ZDO, no position and no gameplay: 'gpower' plays the forsaken-power raise animation without granting anything; 'stagger' plays the stagger without the RPC_Stagger rotation write. UX use: 'request accepted' nod (interact), 'rejected' (stagger), 'hub rotated' (gpower) — visible to bystanders, which makes it a social signal as well.
catalog.playerExperience: The player's character performs the animation on everyone's screen (and their own, third-person). Controls are not locked and nothing else happens.
failureModes: Animator triggers are consumed by transitions; a trigger with no valid transition from the current state is silently swallowed (e.g. 'dodge' mid-air).
A trigger that starts an attack-family clip can desync the owner's Humanoid state machine (m_attack references) until the clip ends; stick to non-attack triggers.
Only peers holding the instance play it; a player standing alone sees only their own body.
Trigger names beyond the ten used by code are Inspector data.
citations: Player.StartEmote (emotes are ZDO fields, not triggers) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598
openQuestions: Full trigger parameter list on the Player animator (Inspector). In-game: on a client, ZSyncAnimation.HasParameter(name, AnimatorControllerParameterType.Trigger) (:87334) for candidate names.
Does 'gpower' fired externally leave any lingering animator bool that blocks the real forsaken-power activation until the clip ends?

catalog.name: Ward Pulse — FlashShield on any guard stone
catalog.oneLine: The server fires the no-arg 'FlashShield' RPC at any ward's ZDO so every nearby client plays the ward's dome flash — a location-anchored, prefab-hash-free VFX for 'this area is portal-locked'.
catalog.howItWorks: PrivateArea.Awake registers m_nview.Register('FlashShield', RPC_FlashShield) (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137202); the handler is m_flashEffect.Create(transform.position, Quaternion.identity) with no owner, sender or enabled check (:137690-137693). Vanilla broadcasts it to ZNetView.Everybody from PrivateArea.FlashShield (:137669-137688). The server needs only the ward's ZDOID: enumerate ward ZDOs once via the prefab hash (ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponent<PrivateArea>() != null, prefab table is populated headless per Wonderland's ContainerRegistry) or by the presence of ZDOVars.s_permitted, then ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, wardZdoId, 'FlashShield'). Every peer with that ward instantiated plays the flash; others drop it in FindInstance. Unlike 'SpawnObject' it needs no effect-prefab name guess and is inherently positioned at the ward. Pair with the ward-as-permission-source option: when a non-permitted player tries a gated portal near a ward, pulse the ward and toast the player.
catalog.playerExperience: The blue dome of the nearest guard stone flashes exactly as if someone had hit a protected piece. No sound beyond the effect's own, no text.
failureModes: Requires the ward to be instantiated on the viewer's client (within ~96-112 m, ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea :82297-82320).
m_flashEffect is Inspector data; a modded ward prefab may have none.
Bystanders read it as 'someone is attacking the base' — misleading if used for benign confirmations.
openQuestions: guard_stone prefab name/hash (Inspector). In-game: enumerate ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs for a PrivateArea component.
catalog.id: gapfill:ux:Ward Pulse — FlashShield on any guard stone
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified precisely. PrivateArea.Awake registers m_nview.Register('FlashShield', RPC_FlashShield) at :137202 (exact). RPC_FlashShield handler is a bare m_flashEffect.Create(transform.position, Quaternion.identity) with no owner/sender check (:137690-137692, exact). Vanilla's own client-side FlashShield(bool) wrapper does have an m_flashAvailable debounce gate before calling InvokeRPC — but that gate lives on the CALLER side (the wrapper method), not on RPC_FlashShield itself, so a server invoking the RPC directly (ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, wardZdoId, 'FlashShield')) bypasses it entirely, exactly as the option assumes. ZDOVars.s_permitted confirmed to exist and be written onto PrivateArea ZDOs (:78529, :137340), supporting the alternative ward-identification strategy the option mentions.

catalog.name: The Free Burst — vanilla's own 'portal connected' effect via a None→X connection flip
catalog.oneLine: Flipping a portal's Portal connection None→X on the server makes every nearby vanilla client play TeleportWorld.m_connected at that portal — the only portal-local VFX that needs no prefab-hash guess.
catalog.howItWorks: TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal runs on the client every 0.5 s (InvokeRepeating in Awake, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143450) and does: flag = HaveTarget(); if (flag && !m_hadTarget) m_connected.Create(transform.position, transform.rotation); m_hadTarget = flag (:143491-143501). HaveTarget() reads GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) != None off the client's copy of the ZDO (:143631-143638), and the connection is network-serialized (ZDO.Serialize :74169-74173). Awake seeds m_hadTarget = HaveTarget() (:143439-143451), so an already-connected portal does not fire on instantiate — the burst fires only on a rising edge observed by the poll. Server recipe: zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid); wait >= 1 s (two client polls) so every viewer has observed None and set m_hadTarget=false; then SetConnection(Portal, target) + ForceSendZDO again. Each 0.5 s poll on each nearby client then sees the edge and spawns m_connected. If the portal is already at its intended target and the burst is wanted as pure feedback, the same None-then-X cycle works; TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads the connection at transit time (:143539) so a player walking in during the ~1 s None window simply gets no transit (gate 1). This is the natural acknowledgement for 'destination changed' in any routing option, and it doubles as an honest signal: the burst means the client's ZDO copy really did change.
catalog.playerExperience: The portal flares with the vanilla 'link established' particle/sound burst. The hover text flips $piece_portal_unconnected → $piece_portal_connected across the same cycle.
failureModes: Game.ConnectPortals may re-pair the portal to a random same-tag partner during the None window (:100607-100622) unless the mod owns pairing for managed portals or the cycle completes inside one 5 s tick and the mod writes last.
A player standing inside the trigger volume during the flip is not re-triggered (OnTriggerEnter fires on enter only, :143672-143681).

ForceSendZDO only sends when ZDOPeer.ShouldSend sees a revision change (:77273); SetConnection with an unchanged value bumps nothing (:74954-74957) — the None step is what guarantees a real revision bump.
Ownership is stolen back within 2 s near a player (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901); the value written survives, the second write must re-claim.
prerequisites: Managed-portal pairing (mod controls ConnectPortals for the portal or writes within one tick)
openQuestions: Minimum None-window for reliable edge detection on a laggy client (poll is 0.5 s, sync sweep is 0.05 s round-robin per peer :76843-76861). In-game: measure with 0.6 s / 1.0 s / 1.5 s windows.
catalog.id: gapfill:ux:The Free Burst — vanilla's own 'portal connected' effect via a None→X connection flip
evidence: TeleportWorld.Teleport() re-checks TargetFound() first, returns early — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143518-143520 (verified, confirms 'gate 1')
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Thoroughly verified, including the two hardest details. TeleportWorld.Awake seeds m_hadTarget=HaveTarget(), registers RPC_SetTag/RPC_SetConnected, and InvokeRepeating('UpdatePortal',0.5f,0.5f) (:143439-143450, exact, matches HANDOFF's independently-confirmed anchors m_activationRange=5f/m_exitDistance=1f). UpdatePortal's rising-edge burst logic confirmed verbatim (:143491-143501). HaveTarget() confirmed to be exactly GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)!=None (:143631-143636). ZDOExtraData.SetConnection confirmed to be a genuine no-op when type+target are unchanged (:74951-74959) — meaning a same-value rewrite would NOT re-fire the burst, correctly forcing the None-then-X two-step recipe the option proposes. Critically, Teleport() itself re-checks TargetFound() first and returns immediately if false (:143518-143520), independently confirming the claimed 'gate 1' safety property. ZDO.SetConnection additionally auto-calls ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() for Portal-type connections (:73656-73665), a bonus not claimed but not contradicting the option.

catalog.name: NEVER USE — RPC_RegisterKill achievement injection
catalog.oneLine: A ZDO-less routed RPC the server can aim at any player that writes enemy/boss kill stats and platform campaign progress into that player's local profile — listed so nobody uses it as a 'feedback' channel.
catalog.howItWorks: Game.Start registers ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<string,int,int,int,bool>('RPC_RegisterKill', RPC_RegisterKill) on every peer (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100069). The handler ignores sender and does GetPlayerProfile().IncrementStatEnemy(enemyName, ...) and IncrementStat(BossKills|EnemyKills); for bossNumber > 0 it additionally increments BossKillSolo/Multiplayer, calls PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform?.ActivityProvider?.CompleteTaskAsync(null, 'Boss'+n, Completed), writes PlatformPrefs 'CampaignProgress', and for bossNumber == 8 completes the 'Campaign' activity (:100837-100866). Vanilla's sender is Game.RegisterKill(playerPeerID, ...) (:100832-100835). There is no gameplay-visible output whatsoever — no message, no effect — so it has zero UX value, and any invocation is silent tampering with a player's statistics and platform achievements. Also note the security face: because m_senderPeerID is unauthenticated and the RPC is peer-addressable, any client can already inject kills into any other client; a server prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632) dropping 'RPC_RegisterKill' packets whose socket peer is not the server is a cheap integrity win.
catalog.playerExperience: Nothing visible. Later, the player's stats page and platform achievements are wrong.
failureModes: Silent corruption of PlayerProfile stats (.fch) and platform campaign state.
cheatsUsed=false marks the increments as legitimate for achievement gating.
openQuestions: Whether ActivityProvider is non-null on the Steam backend (Splatform assembly, outside this decompile) — affects only the blast radius of misuse.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified exactly. Game.Start registers Register<string,int,int,int,bool>('RPC_RegisterKill', RPC_RegisterKill) (:100069, exact match to the 5-parameter shape). Game.RegisterKill/RPC_RegisterKill bodies (:100832-100863) confirmed to ignore the sender parameter entirely and perform IncrementStatEnemy, IncrementStat(BossKills/EnemyKills), and for bossNumber>0 the BossKillSolo/Multiplayer increment, PlatformManager ActivityProvider.CompleteTaskAsync('Boss'+n), PlatformPrefs 'CampaignProgress' write, and bossNumber==8 CompleteActivityAsync('Campaign') — all as claimed, with zero visible feedback of any kind. The 'security face' claim also checks out: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC, the actual network entry point (:83631-83641, verified directly), deserializes RoutedRPCData and forwards purely by m_targetPeerID with no cross-check that the sending rpc/socket actually owns the claimed m_senderPeerID. Correctly and conservatively labeled ruled-out as a UX/feedback mechanism.

catalog.name: Live Portal Markers — removable, labelled map markers via persistent events
catalog.oneLine: The server injects one ActivePersistentEvent per managed hub; every vanilla client draws an EventArea circle plus an animated, LABELLED RandomEvent pin at that position and REMOVES both when the server drops the entry — the removable map surface the catalog said did not exist.
catalog.howItWorks: Client Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins runs every 1 s over PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_activePersistentEvents.list: for each unknown eventId it AddPins an EventArea circle of m_worldSize = radius*2 and a RandomEvent pin (animated, double size) named Localization.Localize(item.Source.mapTokenString); any eventId no longer in the list has both pins RemovePin'd (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57505-57549). The list is server-authoritative: PersistentEventSystem.UpdateClientEventsList(target) sends JsonUtility.ToJson(m_activePersistentEvents) over the routed RPC 'UpdateClientEventsList' and the client RPC_UpdateClientEventsList overwrites its copy (SERVER :105407-105418); new peers request it via m_onNewPeer (:105289, :105391-105404). Both m_activePersistentEvents and m_possibleEvents are public fields (:105070-105073). Server recipe: pick a sourceEventId k whose PersistentEvent has an empty environmentOverride, graphicalEffects == 0 and no objectsToSpawn (enumerate PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_possibleEvents at runtime — the same Inspector list the client has); Add(new ActivePersistentEvent{ eventId = <mod range, e.g. 1_000_000+n>, sourceEventId = k, position = hubPos, radius = 8f, startTime = ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds(), duration = -1.0 }); then ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, 'UpdateClientEventsList', JsonUtility.ToJson(PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_activePersistentEvents)). Bypassing RPC_RequestStartEvent (:105341-105379) avoids GenerateEventLocation, SpawnLocationMidGame and ObjectSpawnSettings.Create — nothing is spawned. duration < 0 is exempt from the 30 s expiry sweep (:105219-105225). PrepareSave/Save/Load persist the JSON in the world file (:105237-105280), so markers survive restarts; after Load, m_eventIdCounter = max+1 (:105278), harmless. Removal: list.Remove(entry) + the same broadcast; clients delete both pins within 1 s. Position and radius are free; the LABEL is fixed to the chosen event type's mapTokenString (:104766) — every hub shows the same word (e.g. the storm's token). radius also sets the circle size (worldSize = radius*2) and bounds every side effect below, so keep it tiny (a few metres).
catalog.playerExperience: A small event circle and a pulsing double-size event icon labelled with the event type's name appear on the map at each hub, for everyone, including players who have never explored there. When a hub is retired the marker vanishes within a second. Walking into the few-metre radius may briefly change the weather if the chosen event type has an environmentOverride.
failureModes: The label is Inspector data per event type (mapTokenString) and cannot be free text; all hubs share it. Which event types exist and their tokens are unknown until enumerated in-game.

Side effects scale with radius: EnvMan uses PersistentEventSystem.GetEnvironmentOverride for the local player inside radius (:105432-105439, EnvMan :95927-95931); UpdateComputeBuffer enables the Snow shader effect if graphicalEffects == Snow (:105124-105150); SpawnSystem spawners with m_requiredPersistentEvent match by internalName inside radius (client :111344-111351); WearNTear pieces with m_requiredPersistentEvent take m_eventDamage depending on being inside/outside a matching event (client :150453-150463) — a piece that REQUIRES a different event and sits inside our marker is damaged. Choose the blandest event type and radius <= 8 m.

RPC_RequestStopEvent (:105381-105389) and RPC_RequestStartEvent (:105341) run on the server with NO sender check — any client can delete the markers (or start real events). Veto 'RequestStopEvent'/'RequestStartEvent' packets from non-server sockets in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix (:83632) or re-assert markers on a tick.

ActivePersistentEvent.Source indexes m_possibleEvents[sourceEventId] on both sides (:104938); an out-of-range index throws in the client's UpdatePersistentEventPins every second. Never use an index the shipped list does not contain.
A client-side PersistentEventIndicator particle (client :105945-105964, nomap-gated) points toward the nearest event when the list is non-empty — cosmetic noise in NoMap worlds.
The pins are not saved and not player-removable; players cannot dismiss them.
citations: PersistentEventSystem fields m_possibleEvents/m_activePersistentEvents — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105070-105073; RPC name strings :105093-105099
openQuestions: Contents of PersistentEventSystem.m_possibleEvents on 1.0.7 (internalName, mapTokenString, environmentOverride, graphicalEffects, objectsToSpawn per entry). In-game: dump on the dedicated server at OnWorldReady.

Does the client render the RandomEvent pin sprite for a persistent event whose type has no dedicated icon (AddPin with PinType.RandomEvent uses the generic event sprite)? In-game: inject one entry and screenshot the map.
Does Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins tolerate 50+ entries without frame cost (O(n^2) key scan each second)?
