catalog.name: Random-event area pin as a temporary marker — RULED OUT
catalog.oneLine: Forging RandEventSystem's 'SetEvent' RPC to draw the single random-event pin at a hub is overwritten by the server's own event sync and would spawn a raid.
catalog.howItWorks: Client Minimap draws m_randEventAreaPin (EventArea, size m_eventRange*2*0.9) and m_randEventPin (animated, double size, name = Localize(event.GetHudText())) from RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent() and removes both when it becomes null (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57470-57502). The client's m_randomEvent is set by RPC_SetEvent(eventName, time, pos) via SetRandomEventByName (SERVER :106964-106978), registered in RandEventSystem.Start (:106781). The dedicated server itself periodically calls SendCurrentRandomEvent, broadcasting either the live event or ('', 0, zero) which clears it (:106952-106962), so a forged event is wiped on the next server send. Setting a real event name also activates that event's spawners on clients whose players are inside m_eventRange and plays the raid music/HUD text. Only one random event exists at a time. Use Live Portal Markers instead.
catalog.playerExperience: A raid warning banner, raid music and a spawn wave at the hub, then the pin disappears when the server resyncs.
failureModes: Spawns a real raid inside m_eventRange.
Single slot; cleared by the server's own SendCurrentRandomEvent.
Event name must exist in the client's m_events list.
catalog.id: gapfill:ux:Random-event area pin as a temporary marker — RULED OUT
corrections: Could cite the precise 2-second SendCurrentRandomEvent interval (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs, m_sendTimer>2f check near :106878-106884) rather than the vaguer 'next server send.'
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified. RandEventSystem.Start registers 'SetEvent' (:106781, exact). SendCurrentRandomEvent (:106952-106961) broadcasts either the real m_randomEvent or a clearing ('',0,zero) and is called on a hard 2-second timer (m_sendTimer>2f, confirmed near :106878-106884), meaning any forged event is overwritten within ~2s, not a vague 'next sync.' RPC_SetEvent's handler explicitly guards with !ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:106964-106969) so it only ever mutates client-side state, and the periodic broadcast will indeed stomp any client-only forged state. Ruled-out verdict and reasoning both hold up; the option could have cited the exact 2s interval but the substance is correct.

catalog.name: Summoning Gaze — consent-handshake player-to-player teleport (TPA)
catalog.oneLine: Requester emotes while looking at another player; the server pairs the s_lookTarget ray with the target's character ZDO, toasts the target, and on the target's accept-emote within 30 s force-teleports the requester to the target's live position — no portal, no chat, no client mod.
catalog.howItWorks: Input: EmoteSignals polls ZDOVars.s_emoteID/s_emote on every character ZDO (Player.StartEmote writes them, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598). Aim: CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation, on the owning client, writes ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = GetLookFromPos() + m_character.GetLookDir()*100f at most every 0.2 s when it changed (:5041-5076; key 'LookTarget' :78677, session-only :78689-78693). On the request emote the server reads requester.Zdo.GetVec3(s_lookTarget), forms the ray from requester eye pos (Zdo.GetPosition()+~1.6 up) toward it, and picks the connected character (ConnectedCharacters.All()) whose ZDO position lies within an angular cone (e.g. 8 degrees, max 40 m) of that ray; ambiguity → nearest to the ray. It records {requesterPlayerId, targetPlayerId, expires=now+30s} keyed on ZDOVars.s_playerID (stable) and toasts the target via PlayerNotify.Toast: 'X wants to teleport to you — <accept emote> to accept'. Accept: the target performs the accept emote before expiry. Execution guards, all server-readable: target.Zdo.GetBool(s_dead) and requester.Zdo.GetBool(s_dead) (:78403), requester.Zdo.GetBool(s_inBed) (:78457) (attached players ping-pong — UpdateAttach precedes UpdateTeleport :10217/:10226), a per-player send ledger enforcing >= 12 s between forced teleports (Player.TeleportTo refuses if m_teleportCooldown < 2f and the cooldown is held at 0 for the whole teleport, :15313-15320, :15334). Then: pos = target.Zdo.GetPosition() + 1.5 m behind the target's facing (Zdo.GetRotation()*Vector3.back) + Vector3.up; ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(requester.Peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, target.Zdo.GetRotation(), true) (handler :41962-41968) or the ZDO-scoped 'RPC_TeleportTo' (:886, :4126-4132). distant:true gives the vanilla 8 s swirl and never fails (15 s force-land). Confirmation: the server polls the requester's ZDO position for the ~2 s snap (UpdateTeleport pins position after 2 s, :15337-15348) and toasts both. Everything bypasses IsTeleportable — ore travels; say so in the toast.
catalog.playerExperience: Look at a friend, do the request emote (e.g. /wave). They see a toast naming you; they /nod within 30 s. You get the portal black-screen swirl and appear beside them ~8 s later, carrying whatever you had. If they ignore it, you get a 'request expired' toast.
failureModes: s_lookTarget is written only when it changes and only if the Player prefab's CharacterAnimEvent has m_headRotation && m_head set (:5043) — Inspector data; if unset the channel is empty and aim must fall back to nearest-player-within-N-metres.
The look ray is camera-derived (GetLookDir); first-person/over-shoulder offsets make the cone miss at long range; cap at ~40 m.
StartEmote refuses while attached, attacking, drawing a bow or on a ship (:15587) — a target seated at a helm cannot accept.
Every vanilla gate is bypassed (NoPortals, NoBossPortals, IsTeleportable, wards); the mod must re-implement any it wants.
Teleport failures are silent one-way (both RPC handlers discard TeleportTo's bool); confirm by position poll only.
A dead target (s_dead) or a target mid-teleport gives a stale/zero position; re-read at accept time, not at request time.
openQuestions: Is m_headRotation enabled and m_head assigned on the Player prefab (Inspector)? In-game: poll s_lookTarget on a connected character ZDO while the player looks around; expect a changing non-zero Vector3 every ~0.2 s.
Exact eye offset to use as the ray origin server-side (GetLookFromPos is a head-bone position). In-game: compare s_lookTarget - Zdo.GetPosition() against a known look direction.
evidence: ZDOVars.s_lookTarget key + session-only hash set — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78677,78689-78693 (verified exact)
Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer / Character.RPC_TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41627,41959,41962-41968,886,4126-4132 (verified, matches prompt's own known anchors)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Core primitives all verified exactly. CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (:5041-5081) confirmed to write ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = lookFromPos + GetLookDir()*100f, throttled to at most every 0.2s and only when changed — matches the option's formula and cadence precisely. ZDOVars.s_lookTarget confirmed at :78677 with key string 'LookTarget', and confirmed to sit inside the session-only hash list at :78689-78693 (exact list matches). Player.StartEmote/StopEmote confirmed at :15585-15609 writing s_emote/s_emoteID. The 'server-enforced' label is defensible here specifically because — unlike a portal-transit permission check — there is no client-side discretionary gate being bypassed: the server unilaterally decides and the RPC executes unconditionally on the receiving client. Legitimate caveats already flagged by the option itself (ambiguous target resolution via a cone, no reciprocity check, cooldown ledger design) are reasonable and appropriately hedge the 'feasible-with-caveats' rating.

catalog.name: Warp Verbs — /home, /back, /spawn without a portal
catalog.oneLine: Three emote-triggered destinations resolved entirely server-side: nearest bed the player owns (ZDO s_owner), the server's own pre-teleport position ledger (the only party that can implement /back), and the world spawn from GetLocationIcon('StartTemple').
catalog.howItWorks: Trigger: an emote token per verb via EmoteSignals (s_emoteID/s_emote polling, Player.StartEmote assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598), optionally armed by the crouch bit or by not standing at a portal. HOME: Bed.RPC_SetOwner writes ZDOVars.s_owner (profile UID) and s_ownerName onto the bed ZDO (:119813-119819); the server scans bed ZDOs (PrefabSetSweeper over bed prefab hashes, prefab filter mandatory because GrapplingPoint also uses s_owner :127909) and picks the bed with s_owner == requester s_playerID nearest to the requester (or most recently claimed if a mod-side timestamp is kept — vanilla stores none; the ACTIVE bed is unknowable, PlayerProfile.m_spawnPoint is local :106230-106233). Destination = bedZdo.GetPosition() + Vector3.up*1 (the exact spawn child transform is not ZDO data, Bed.GetSpawnPoint :119796-119799). BACK: before every server-issued teleport the mod appends (playerID, Zdo.GetPosition(), Zdo.GetRotation(), time) to a per-player ring; /back pops it. Only the server can do this — the client's death/logout/home points never leave the .fch (:106180-106253). Portal transits the mod did not issue can be added via PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit detection (Wonderland PositionWatch.cs:148) if wanted. SPAWN: ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out pos) on the server branch reads m_locationInstances (:115422-115447; m_StartLocation = 'StartTemple' :99845); the vanilla client itself spawns at pos + up*2 (client Game.FindSpawnPoint). Delivery: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, rot, true) (:41957-41968). Guards as in Summoning Gaze: s_dead, s_inBed, per-player >= 12 s spacing, plus verb-specific cooldowns stored by s_playerID. Height for HOME/BACK comes from live ZDO positions (already standable); for any computed point use WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight (:151944), never ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight (dead raycast :115502-115511).
catalog.playerExperience: Do the /home emote: an 8 s portal-style black screen, then you are standing beside your bed with everything you carried. /back returns you to where you were before the last server warp. /spawn drops you at the start stones. A toast names the destination before the fade.
failureModes: 'Your bed' is ambiguous — vanilla lets a player own unlimited beds and never records the active one (Bed.Interact only claims when s_owner == 0, :119670-119725).
Bypasses every vanilla gate; ore, boss lockdowns and NoPortals are all ignored — must be re-implemented or the verbs will undercut the portal economy.
Silent no-op inside the teleport dead zone (cooldown held at 0 during teleport, then 2 s, :15313-15320, :15334); the ledger must space sends.

A bed that is unloaded on the client is fine (distant teleport force-lands at 15 s), but a bed inside a base with a roof can land the player on the roof if +1 y is applied to a raised bed; use the ZDO y directly plus a small epsilon.
GetLocationIcon returns the first dictionary match and requires the location's icon flags (Inspector); StartTemple is icon-flagged in vanilla.
prerequisites: Bed prefab hash list (ZNetScene prefab enumeration for a Bed component)
openQuestions: Bed prefab names/hashes and whether every bed variant carries both Bed and Piece (Inspector). In-game: place each bed and dump the ZDO field set.
Whether a forced distantTeleport into a walled bedroom lands cleanly (FindFloor vs roof). In-game: /home into an enclosed stone room.
evidence: Bed class/Interact/RPC_SetOwner/GetSpawnPoint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119627-119830 (verified, ranges match cited lines closely)
ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon + Game.m_StartLocation, plus vanilla's own call site — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115422-115447,99845,100368 (verified, strengthens claim)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] All Bed- and spawn-related citations verified precisely, including a subtlety the option itself flags correctly. Bed class at :119627 (exact match to prompt's own known anchor). Bed.Interact (starts :119670, matches cited range) confirmed to be the only path that writes s_owner/s_ownerName via the private SetOwner→RPC_SetOwner wrapper (RPC_SetOwner body found matching the cited range exactly) — and RPC_SetOwner is itself gated by m_nview.IsOwner(), a fact about the WRITE path the option correctly does not rely on (it only reads s_owner off ZDOs server-side, a safe passive read). Bed.GetSpawnPoint() returns m_spawnPoint.position — a scene-graph child Transform position, NOT ZDO data — confirmed exactly, validating the option's own explicit caveat that 'the exact spawn child transform is not ZDO data' and that bedZdo.GetPosition()+up*1 is only an approximation of the true spawn point. ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon (:115422-115447) and Game.m_StartLocation='StartTemple' (:99845) both confirmed exact — and critically, Game class itself already calls GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation,...) at line 100368 for its own respawn logic, meaning the option's SPAWN verb reuses a code path vanilla already exercises server-side, which is strong positive evidence of feasibility beyond what the option claimed. GrapplingPoint s_owner overload collision noted correctly (prefab-hash filtering is a real requirement, as stated).

catalog.name: Map Ping Picker — corrected: socket identity, y re-derivation, public gesture, arming
catalog.oneLine: The map middle-click stays the only vanilla input that carries an arbitrary Vector3, but it must be captured in a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (where the ZRpc socket is in scope), its y must be recomputed with WorldGenerator.GetHeight, and it must be gated by an arming condition and a per-account debounce because it is free and broadcast to everyone.
catalog.howItWorks: Hook (hard precondition 1): HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData) has no socket in scope (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665) and m_senderPeerID is read straight off the wire (RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83487-83495); the UserInfo payload is likewise self-authored (UserInfo.Serialize :72795-72799). The only place both the authentic connection and the payload coexist is ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:83632-83644). Harmony prefix: var copy = new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray()); var d = new ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData(); d.Deserialize(copy); if (d.m_methodHash != 'ChatMessage'.GetStableHashCode()) return; var peer = ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc) (ZNetPeer.m_rpc is public :78780-78790); reject if peer == null || !peer.IsReady() || d.m_senderPeerID != peer.m_uid. Parse d.m_parameters: Vector3 pos, int type (3 == Ping), string name, string platformId, string text; additionally reject if platformId != peer.m_socket.GetHostName(). Never mutate the live pkg. Height (precondition 2): Chat.SendPing overwrites vector.y with the SENDER's y (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42063-42064), so the received y is the player's altitude, not the terrain's at the click. Recompute y = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) (:151944-151949); if y < 30 treat as water; never call ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight (raycast, returns p.y unchanged headless, :115502-115511). Resolve the destination as the nearest managed portal to (x, y, z) within a configurable radius via ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals() (:77643), not a raw coordinate. Public gesture (precondition 3): the ping is broadcast to 0L (client :42065), so every online player sees the ping marker and the 'Name: PING' map pin; document it as a visible, shared action and never use it for anything secret. Arming + debounce (precondition 4): a middle-click costs nothing, so act only when armed — the requester's character ZDO is within N m of a managed portal AND (crouch bit or a preceding emote within 10 s) — and keep a per-PlatformUserID debounce (e.g. one routing action per 5 s, ignore bursts). Feedback: tag echo + Free Burst + toast. Unarmed pings pass through untouched (return true) so vanilla ping behaviour is unchanged.
catalog.playerExperience: Stand at your portal, crouch, open the map and middle-click near the destination portal. The portal flares (Free Burst), its hover tag changes to the destination name, and a toast confirms. Everyone online briefly sees your ping on their map, as with any ping.
failureModes: Taking identity from m_senderPeerID or UserInfo lets a modified client route another player's portal in their name — the socket cross-check is mandatory.
Using the packet y wires the destination to the player's altitude (100 m off on a mountain); re-derive with WorldGenerator.GetHeight, which is itself blind to terraforming (+/- a few metres).
Pings are spammable and public; without arming/debounce every stray middle-click re-routes.
On a PlayFab/Xbox backend GetHostName returns a different id form than the UserInfo platformId (:81271-81280); compare per backend or rely on m_uid equality only.
If MessageHud/Chat singletons make the server itself register 'ChatMessage' (unverified), a second Register throws — the prefix approach avoids that entirely.
prerequisites: Tag echo / Free Burst / toast feedback
openQuestions: Does the server hold a live Chat instance that already registers 'ChatMessage' (decides nothing for the prefix, but matters for anyone still using Register)? In-game: log Chat.instance == null on the dedicated server.
Map click precision at default zoom in metres — determines the nearest-portal search radius. In-game: ping a known portal ten times and measure the scatter.

UserInfo custom wire Serialize (Name, UserId.ToString) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:72774-72799 (verified, confirms parameter-flattening claim)
peer.m_socket.GetHostName() used as platform user id elsewhere — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79855 (verified, validates the proposed auth check)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] This is the most technically demanding option in the set and it holds up completely under adversarial re-derivation. ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83631-83641, verified exact) is confirmed to be the true network-facing entry point (registered per-peer as peer.m_rpc.Register<ZPackage>('RoutedRPC', RPC_RoutedRPC) at :83530) and it deserializes RoutedRPCData purely from the packet with zero cross-check against the actual ZRpc/peer that delivered it — confirming this really is the only place both an authentic socket/peer and the claimed sender coexist, exactly as claimed. RoutedRPCData.Deserialize located at exactly :83487-83495 (character-for-character match). Chat.SendPing (client) confirmed to overwrite vector.y with the SENDER's own transform.y and broadcast InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,'ChatMessage', vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), '') — and critically, UserInfo (server, :72774-72799) implements ISerializableParameter with a custom Serialize writing Name then UserId.ToString() as two separate strings into the ZPackage, meaning the wire format really does flatten into (Vector3, int, string name, string platformId, string text) as the option's parsing recipe assumes, despite the call site passing a single UserInfo object — a subtle and correct piece of reverse engineering. peer.m_socket.GetHostName() confirmed elsewhere in the same file (line 79855) to be used precisely as a platform-user-id string, validating the proposed platformId==peer.m_socket.GetHostName() authentication check. ZNetPeer.m_rpc/m_socket/m_uid confirmed public (:78780-78784). WorldGenerator.GetHeight (:151934-151949) and ZDOMan.GetPortals (:77643) both confirmed at the exact cited lines.

catalog.name: Plain chat as a command line — needs the RelationsProvider test
catalog.oneLine: Re-classify: slash commands are dead, but keyword-prefixed plain text or shouts WOULD reach the server even for a solo player if PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider is null on the Steam backend — one in-game test decides whether a 50+ character socket-authenticated command line exists.
catalog.howItWorks: Chat.InputText rewrites non-slash text to 'say <text>' and hands slash text to the local Terminal (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41947-41955) — unknown /commands never leave the client. 'say' calls Chat.SendText, and both Shout (:41982-41988) and Talker.Say go through CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42042). That method has two shapes: if RelationsProvider == null it calls the handler ONCE with targetPeerID 0L (:42002-42006) — a broadcast that the dedicated server receives in RPC_RoutedRPC and handles locally (:83636-83638); otherwise it sends to the sender's own UserID plus one RPC per OTHER listed player (:42007-42041), so a solo player emits nothing and 2+ players only produce relay traffic. Whether Steam's RelationsProvider is null lives in the Splatform assembly (absent from this decompile). Circumstantial evidence AGAINST: Terminal's chat display code logs 'Relations provider was unavailable ... This should never happen!' when it is null (:45964-45968), and the friends-list UI takes a RelationsProvider.GetFriends() branch (:63855-63861) — Steam has friends, so a provider almost certainly exists. TEST: install a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix that logs m_methodHash == 'ChatMessage'.GetStableHashCode() with type and targetPeerID; have a SOLO vanilla Steam player type a sentence and a /s shout; a logged packet with m_targetPeerID == 0 means chat is a first-class channel. If it passes: the option is 'tp: <verb> <arg>' prefixed text, parsed in the same prefix with the sender resolved from the socket (GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)), type 1 (Normal) or 2 (Shout), Localized feedback by toast. If it fails (expected): chat stays ruled-out and the 2+-player relay case is only an observation channel that must not be relied on for a solo player.
catalog.playerExperience: If the test passes: type 'tp: home' in normal chat; a toast replies within a frame. Everyone nearby also sees the chat line (Normal range) or everyone online (Shout).
failureModes: Expected outcome is that RelationsProvider is non-null on Steam and nothing is sent solo; do not ship any feature on this channel before the test.
Even when relayed (2+ players), the message also reaches other players as ordinary chat — commands are public.
Text is filtered/censored per RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering on some platforms (:42004, :42047-42051).
prerequisites: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix (shared with the ping picker)
openQuestions: Is PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on the Steam client build? The single decisive test is described above (solo player, prefix logging 'ChatMessage' hashes).
Same question for PlayFab/Xbox crossplay clients, which may differ from Steam.

evidence: Chat.SendText/CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41975-42033 (verified, including the always-local-self-echo call in the non-null branch)
ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-target no-network-send rule — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83593 (verified, confirms 'solo player emits nothing' even off the null-provider path)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Verified in full detail, including the subtlest claim (that a solo player emits literally zero packets in the RelationsProvider!=null branch). Chat.InputText (client, :41947-41954) confirmed to rewrite non-slash text to 'say <text>' and hand slash text to the local Terminal — unknown /commands genuinely never leave the client. CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42033) confirmed: when RelationsProvider==null, it calls the handler exactly once with targetPeerID 0L (broadcast) — matching the option's claim precisely. When RelationsProvider!=null, it ALWAYS first calls sendMessageHandler(ZNet.instance.LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID, false) — i.e. addressed to the sender's OWN character/session id — before looping over other players. Combined with the independently-verified ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-target rule (targetPeerID==m_id triggers only local HandleRoutedRPC and explicitly skips RouteRPC), this confirms a solo player's chat message, even in the non-null branch, never crosses the wire at all — exactly the option's claim that 'a solo player emits nothing.' The two cited pieces of circumstantial evidence are both real and reasonably argue Steam's provider is non-null in practice. The option is correctly hedged as needs-ingame-check since the Splatform/Steam backend implementation is not present in this decompile.

catalog.name: The Cartographer's Table — opt-in named-pin sync via a server-written MapTable
catalog.oneLine: A server-owned Cartography Table beside each hub whose ZDOVars.s_data blob lists one named, saved pin per managed portal under a mod-reserved owner id; a player who presses Read receives the set, and re-reading later removes retired portals — the only re-syncable named-pin surface, and opt-in by construction.
catalog.howItWorks: MapTable.OnRead decompresses m_nview.GetZDO().GetByteArray(ZDOVars.s_data) and calls Minimap.instance.AddSharedMapData, toasting $msg_mapsynced/$msg_alreadysynced/$msg_mapnodata (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133837-133866). Blob format = Minimap.GetSharedMapData (client :58788-58835): Write(int 3) [Version.SharedMap: Pins=2, PinsAuthor=3, SERVER :112072-112076]; Write(int exploredLength) then exploredLength bools; Write(int pinCount); per pin: long ownerID, string name, Vector3 pos, int PinType, bool checked, string authorPlatformId. Compress with Utils.Compress and write to the table ZDO: claim ownership (SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())), zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_data, bytes), ForceSendZDO. Client AddSharedMapData (:58857-58935): ReadExploredArray refuses and returns false unless exploredLength == m_explored.Length (:58840-58843) — write exactly textureSize*textureSize bools, all false (false never changes exploration, :58874). Then for pins: every existing pin with m_ownerID != 0 && != readerPlayerID is marked shouldDelete (:58889-58897); each incoming pin that has ANY saved pin within 1 m XZ is kept (shouldDelete cleared, not re-added, HavePinInRange :58341-58351); otherwise if ownerID != readerPlayerID it is AddPin'd with save:true and that ownerID (:58911-58918); finally marked pins are removed (:58921-58932). Owner-id convention: a fixed non-zero sentinel that can never equal a profile UID in practice (e.g. 0x544F5254414C5054); pins with ownerID 0 are the player's own and are never touched. Removal therefore works: drop a retired portal from the blob, the player presses Read again, and that pin (still owned by the sentinel) is deleted. m_textureSize probe: the C# default is 256 (:56287) but Inspector-overridable; read it from the world itself — any vanilla MapTable ZDO written by a player carries the client's exploredLength as the int after the version, so parse one existing s_data blob (or accept the first player write to the hub table) and cache it; fall back to 256*256. Hazard mitigation: because a Read deletes every non-own, non-listed pin (pins previously received from other players' tables), the server should UNION into its blob the pin lists of every other MapTable ZDO in the world (all server-readable via s_data) so those pins are re-listed and survive. Player writes: OnWrite (:133868-133893) first Reads, then overwrites s_data via RPC_MapData at the owner (:133895-133902) — the server must re-parse the new blob and re-inject hub pins on a tick (or block writes with a SetOwner prefix). Opt-in: nothing happens until a player presses Read on the table, and vanilla's own message confirms the sync.
catalog.playerExperience: A cartography table stands by the hub. Read it: '$msg_mapsynced' and a named pin for every managed portal appears on your map, permanently until you read a table whose blob no longer lists it. Reading again with no changes gives '$msg_alreadysynced'. Your own pins are untouched.
failureModes: Wrong explored length = 'Map exploration array size missmatch' warning and no pins (:58840-58843); m_textureSize is Inspector data — probe it from an existing blob.
A Read deletes pins the player received from other players' tables unless the server re-lists them; the union step is mandatory or players lose shared pins.
Dedup is by position within 1 m regardless of name/type (:58907-58910): a renamed portal at the same spot keeps the OLD pin name; to rename, move the pin >1 m or accept the stale label.
Player OnWrite overwrites the server blob with their own merged map (:133883-133889); re-inject on a tick.
Read is gated by PrivateArea.CheckAccess on the client (:133816-133820); place the table outside foreign wards.
Pins are save:true in the player's .fch; a player who never reads again keeps stale pins forever.
MapTable prefab name/hash is Inspector data; ZNetScene prefab enumeration for a MapTable component is required to fabricate one.
prerequisites: Server-side ZDO fabrication or Instantiate of the MapTable prefab (FirstSpawnGrant/ScatterCommand pattern)
openQuestions: Actual Minimap.m_textureSize on the shipped prefab. In-game: log Minimap.instance.m_textureSize on a client, or parse any vanilla MapTable s_data blob server-side.
MapTable prefab name (Inspector). In-game: enumerate ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs for a MapTable component on the dedicated server.

Does a server-fabricated MapTable ZDO (Piece + WearNTear) survive WearNTear support checks on the owning client (UpdateWear applies 100 damage per update when !HaveSupport with m_noSupportWear, :149662-149707)? Place it on solid ground or Instantiate the prefab so ZNetView.Awake sets fields correctly.

GetReadHoverText is the actual referent of the 'read access check' citation, not OnRead — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133814-133821 vs 133837-133866 (correction)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism fully verified, including exact merge/delete pin semantics that are easy to get subtly wrong. MapTable class (:133788), 'MapData' RPC registration (:133803), OnRead/OnWrite/RPC_MapData (:133832-133903) all confirmed near-exactly at the cited lines. OnRead confirmed to decompress s_data via Utils.Decompress and call Minimap.instance.AddSharedMapData with the $msg_mapsynced/$msg_alreadysynced/$msg_mapnodata messaging exactly as claimed.
