Minimap.AddSharedMapData (client, :58857-58932) verified in full: it marks ALL existing pins with m_ownerID!=0 && !=readerID for deletion, then for each incoming pin either clears deletion on the nearest existing pin within 1m (without checking that pin's owner matches — matching the option's precise 'not re-added' phrasing) or AddPins a new save:true pin under the given ownerID, then sweeps still-marked pins — this exactly reproduces the option's stated hazard ('a Read deletes every non-own, non-listed pin') and its own proposed mitigation (union in all other tables' pins) is the correct fix for a real, verified problem. One genuine correction: the option's prereq citation 'MapTable read access check — :133814-133821' actually points at GetReadHoverText, a TOOLTIP-only access check; the real OnRead method has no PrivateArea.CheckAccess call at all — reading is functionally unrestricted regardless of ward permission (only OnWrite is actually gated by CheckAccess). This doesn't hurt feasibility (if anything it removes a barrier) but the citation as labeled is misleading about what it gates.

catalog.name: Station Credit Primitives (Refund by RPC)
catalog.oneLine: Pay a refund or reward into the player's own fireplace, smelter, cooking station or fermenter by invoking the station's vanilla ZNetView RPC at its owning client, instead of dropping items on the ground.
catalog.howItWorks: Every fuel/ore station registers owner-gated ZNetView RPCs the server can drive exactly the way it drives Game.RPC_SetConnection: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(zdo.GetOwner(), zdo.m_uid, method, args)` (ZNetView.InvokeRPC is literally that one line, :82855-82858). The receiving client's ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC (:82838-82848) dispatches to the handler, which checks `m_nview.IsOwner()` and writes the ZDO. Census of usable credit RPCs (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs): Fireplace — `RPC_AddFuel()` (+1 clamped to m_maxFuel, :125726-125741), `RPC_AddFuelAmount(float)` (signed delta, clamped 0..m_maxFuel — negative = DEBIT, :125754-125764), `RPC_SetFuelAmount(float)` (:125779-125787), `RPC_ToggleOn()` (:125743-125752); all registered in Fireplace.Awake :125395-125398 and all IsOwner-gated. Smelter — `RPC_AddOre(string prefabName, bool cheated)` (:142264-142277, IsItemAllowed against m_conversion then QueueOre writes "item<n>" strings + s_queued, NO m_maxOre cap in the handler), `RPC_AddFuel()` (:142351-142359, no cap in handler), `RPC_EmptyProcessed()` (:142320-142326); registered :142102-142104. CookingStation — `RPC_AddItem(string, bool)` (:123130-123142, slot-limited by GetFreeSlot, NOT owner-gated), `RPC_AddFuel()` (:122919-122928, owner-gated); registered :122479-122482. Fermenter — `RPC_AddItem(int nameHash, bool)` (:124891-124905, owner-gated, only when Empty), `RPC_Tap()` (:124907-124919). Beehive has no add RPC (only `RPC_Extract` :119986-120000); its honey is a plain int `ZDOVars.s_level` (:78497) clamped by IncreseLevel :120021-120027, so credit is a direct ZDO write. Two-path rule: if `zdo.GetOwner() != 0` and that owner is a connected peer (`ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null`), send the RPC — the client plays m_fuelAddedEffects/m_oreAddedEffects so the player SEES the credit land; if the station is unowned (zone unloaded, nobody near), write the ZDO field directly (`zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_fuel, v)` :78433, or the item<n>/s_queued pair) — no owner exists to clobber it and the next client to load the zone reads the current value. Never RPC an unowned ZDO: `InvokeRoutedRPC(0, ...)` is a broadcast (:83588-83594) that no client applies. Resolve the player's stations by `s_creator` (:78393) == their `s_playerID` on the target station ZDO, found via ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear around their portal or a scanned prefab set.
catalog.playerExperience: The player uses a portal whose toll was refunded (or a bounty paid). If they are standing at their base, their kiln/smelter visibly gains fuel or ore with the vanilla add-effect and the hover text count rises. If they are away, the station simply reads the higher value when they next load the zone. Nothing appears on the ground and nothing can be picked up by someone else.
failureModes: Station owner is a connected peer that has the object instantiated but the RPC arrives during a frame where the owner changed (ReleaseNearbyZDOS every 2s) — the handler's IsOwner check silently drops it; re-resolve GetOwner() immediately before send and retry once next tick.

Smelter.RPC_AddOre and RPC_AddFuel have no capacity check in the handler (:142264, :142351) — an over-credit shows a queue larger than m_maxOre in the hover text; cap on the server by reading s_queued/s_fuel first.

IsItemAllowed matches on prefab NAME from m_conversion (:142160-142170) — the mod must know the station's accepted inputs; read them from ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab()).GetComponent<Smelter>().m_conversion (prefab table presence on a headless server needs the in-game check).
CookingStation.RPC_AddItem is not owner-gated (:123130) — sending it to a non-owner makes that client write the ZDO and lose a revision race; always target GetOwner().
Direct s_fuel/s_queued writes on an owned station race the owner's next push (RPC_ZDOData whole-blob apply :77124-77131); only use the direct path when GetOwner()==0.
The refund is a station-side credit, not inventory — a player with no fireplace/smelter of their own gets nothing; fall back to ItemDrop.DropItem at their portal.
prerequisites: Prepaid Toll Escrow or Reactive Transit Toll (something to refund)
ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear / PrefabSetSweeper to locate the payer's stations
citations: Fireplace.Awake registrations :125395-125398; RPC_AddFuel :125726-125741; RPC_AddFuelAmount :125754-125764; RPC_SetFuelAmount :125779-125787; RPC_ToggleOn :125743-125752
Smelter.Awake registrations :142102-142104; RPC_AddOre :142264-142277; QueueOre :142279-142285; RPC_AddFuel :142351-142359; IsItemAllowed :142160-142170
ZDOVars.s_fuel :78433, s_queued :78555, s_item0 :78467, s_level :78497, s_content :78391, s_creator :78393
openQuestions: Does ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponent<Smelter>() return real m_conversion data on the dedicated server (prefab table populated headless)? IN-GAME CHECK: log m_conversion.Count for the smelter prefab at OnWorldReady.
Does the client render m_fuelAddedEffects for an RPC-driven add when the player is not looking at the station? (EffectList.Create is local; expected yes.)
corrections: Beehive credit via direct ZDO write should clamp to m_maxHoney the same way Beehive.IncreseLevel (120021-120027) does, since a raw zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_level, N) has no such cap and RPC_Extract (119986) will happily drop an over-cap stack.
evidence: ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC relay to target peer's own connection: :83596-83627
Smelter.RPC_AddOre / QueueOre (no m_maxOre cap in handler): :142264-142285
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited RPC exists exactly as described and the two-path design (routed RPC to a connected owner vs. direct ZDOMan field write when unowned) is sound precisely because it avoids the one big landmine in this batch: a dedicated server never instantiates a real-world-positioned GameObject at all. Independently re-derived from source: Game.FixedUpdate unconditionally pins ZNet's reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick with no local-player guard (line 100465, inside FixedUpdate at 100458), and ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects (82268-82274) anchors object creation to that same GetReferencePosition() (82270) via ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects/IsAreaReady (82062-82080). So no Fireplace/Smelter/CookingStation/Fermenter/Beehive MonoBehaviour ever runs ON the server; this option's design correctly never requires that -- the RPC executes on the receiving OWNER's own client (verified full routing chain: ZNetView.InvokeRPC -> ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner,...) -> RouteRPC relays via peer.m_rpc.Invoke('RoutedRPC',...) to that peer's own machine -> their own RPC_RoutedRPC->HandleRoutedRPC resolves ZNetScene.FindInstance locally, where it legitimately exists), and the unowned-write path touches only ZDOMan's data layer, which needs no GameObject. Verified: Fireplace RPC_AddFuel/RPC_AddFuelAmount/RPC_SetFuelAmount/RPC_ToggleOn all owner-gated at cited lines; Smelter.RPC_AddOre (142264) confirmed to have NO m_maxOre cap in the handler (only OnAddOre's player-facing UI checks it) -- QueueOre (142279) appends unconditionally, exactly as claimed. CookingStation.RPC_AddItem (123130) independently confirmed NOT owner-gated (only IsItemAllowed+GetFreeSlot), exactly as the option itself flags. One gap: Beehive's suggested direct 's_level' write is not clamped the way Beehive.IncreseLevel (120021) clamps to m_maxHoney -- a raw zdo.Set bypasses that cap, risking a display/extraction value above the prefab's designed maximum. Minor, not fatal.

catalog.name: Smelter Output Queue Credit (Finished Goods)
catalog.oneLine: Credit finished bars, not ore: write s_spawnOre/s_spawnAmount onto the player's smelter ZDO and let the owning client's own UpdateSmelter spawn the stack at the output chute.
catalog.howItWorks: Smelter.UpdateSmelter (owner only, 1s InvokeRepeating :142110) ends with `if (GetQueuedOre() == "" || (m_maxFuel > 0 && GetFuel() == 0f)) SpawnProcessed();` (:142458-142461). SpawnProcessed (:142509-142521) reads `ZDOVars.s_spawnAmount` (:78603) and `s_spawnOre` (:78605), calls `Spawn(ore, amount)` (:142533-142546) which instantiates `GetItemConversion(ore).m_to` at m_outputPoint with m_stack = amount, then zeroes both fields. The server therefore credits N finished products by writing two fields: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_spawnOre, "CopperOre"); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_spawnAmount, N)` — the ore NAME (the m_from prefab name), not the bar name, because GetItemConversion matches on m_from (:142548-142557). Spawn happens on the owner's next 1s tick if the ore queue is empty or fuel is zero; otherwise it happens when the current batch completes. Use the two-path rule: unowned station → direct write is race-free; owned by a connected peer → write then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` after bumping `zdo.DataRevision` well past the owner's (WaterBuoyancyEngine +4096 pattern) so the owner's next push cannot clobber it, and accept that ReleaseNearbyZDOS may hand ownership around in the meantime. The cheated flag on the spawned stack is `s_cheatedQueued || s_cheated` (:142542-142544) — leave both false. No RPC exists for this path; it is a plain-field write vanilla itself uses (QueueProcessed :142484-142485).
catalog.playerExperience: The player walks up to their smelter and a stack of N bars slides out of the output chute with the produce effect, exactly as if a batch had just finished. Hover text is unchanged. If the smelter is mid-batch, the credit is emitted when that batch's product would normally spawn.
failureModes: Spawn only fires while the owning client runs UpdateSmelter — an unowned smelter in an unloaded zone holds the credit until someone loads the zone (this is fine; it is how vanilla's own pending batches work).

Amount above m_to.m_shared.m_maxStackSize spawns one over-stacked ItemDrop; vanilla's QueueProcessed splits at maxStackSize (:142490-142495). Cap N per credit at the stack size and issue multiple credits.
A concurrent vanilla batch completion overwrites s_spawnOre if the ore differs (QueueProcessed :142481-142486 calls SpawnProcessed first, so the credit is still emitted, just earlier).

Owner clobber: if the owner's ZDO push with a higher DataRevision arrives after the server write and before ForceSendZDO, the credit is lost; verify by re-reading s_spawnAmount on the next tick and re-issue.

Works for Smelter-family prefabs only (smelter, blast furnace, kiln, spinning wheel, windmill, eitr refinery) — CookingStation has no spawn queue; Fermenter yields only via RPC_Tap after a real fermentation.
prerequisites: Station Credit Primitives (station resolution, two-path rule)
openQuestions: Exact prefab names of every Smelter-component prefab and their m_conversion m_from names — Inspector data; dump ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs with a Smelter component at OnWorldReady.
corrections: The two-path rule's 'unowned -> direct write, race-free' claim does not extend to this option: SpawnProcessed only executes inside Smelter.UpdateSmelter's IsOwner()-gated branch (142415-142417), which requires a real client to have the smelter's GameObject instantiated (i.e. be physically nearby) and be its owner. An unowned smelter's finished-goods credit is fully inert -- not merely deferred -- until some nearby player (any player, per ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS's nearest-peer reassignment, not necessarily the credited one) claims ownership and ticks it.
evidence: Smelter.UpdateSmelter owner gate and spawn trigger: :142407-142463
Sector-Zero (no server-side GameObject instantiation for real-world positions): :100458-100466, :82268-82274
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] All cited mechanics verified verbatim: Smelter.UpdateSmelter (142407) calls UpdateState unconditionally then returns early '`if (!m_nview.IsOwner()) return;`' before any spawn logic, and ends '`if (GetQueuedOre()=="" || (m_maxFuel>0 && GetFuel()==0f)) SpawnProcessed();`' exactly as cited (142458-142461); SpawnProcessed/Spawn/GetItemConversion (142509-142557) match exactly, including the cheated-flag composition and the ore-name-not-bar-name detail. The claim's real weakness is the 'unowned station -> direct write is race-free' framing inherited from the parent primitive: writing s_spawnOre/s_spawnAmount is safe as a write, but nothing ever CONSUMES it -- SpawnProcessed only runs inside the owner-gated branch of a MonoBehaviour that (per the Sector-Zero fact established above) only ever ticks on a real client that has this specific Smelter's GameObject instantiated, which requires that client to be physically near it. If the ZDO is genuinely unowned (owner==0, e.g. after ReleaseNearbyZDOS), literally nobody -- not the server, which never instantiates it, and no client, since none has it loaded -- runs UpdateSmelter, so the credit sits completely inert, potentially forever, until *some* player (not necessarily the intended recipient -- ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership to whoever is nearby) walks up to that specific smelter. This is materially stronger than 'the next client to load the zone reads the current value' (true for passive fields, false for a spawn side-effect) and should be stated as an explicit caveat rather than folded into the 'race-free' framing.

catalog.name: Door Lever (Three-State Physical Input)
catalog.oneLine: A vanilla door beside a gate is a server-readable three-position switch: ZDOVars.s_state is 0 (closed), 1 (opened from the front) or -1 (opened from the back), written by the owner on every use.
catalog.howItWorks: Door.Interact → Open(userDir) computes `Vector3.Dot(transform.forward, userDir) < 0` and invokes `UseDoor(bool forward)` at the ZDO owner (:123885-123895). RPC_UseDoor (:123930-123952) writes `ZDOVars.s_state` (:78611): from 0 it becomes 1 if forward else -1; from any non-zero it becomes 0. The write goes through ZDO.Set → IncreaseDataRevision → the client's change queue, so the server receives it within one sync cycle regardless of distance (ZDOMan.ClientChanged/CreateSyncList non-server branch). Server side: on a 0.25-0.5s tick, for each managed portal, `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 6f)` filtered to prefabs carrying a Door component (prefab hash set resolved once at OnWorldReady from ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs), read `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_state)`. Interpretation: -1 / 0 / +1 map to three route choices (e.g. destination A / closed / destination B), or open-vs-closed as a binary 'arm the gate'. Which way a door opens is determined by which side the player stood on, so a single door yields a 3-way selector a vanilla player operates by walking around it. Door.CanInteract (:123807-123818) rejects use mid-animation and, for key doors (m_keyItem) or m_canNotBeClosed doors, refuses to close — pick a plain wooden door. Guard-stone gating (m_checkGuardStone default true, :123741) means only ward-permitted players can flip it, which is a free, vanilla-honoured access control on the lever. Pair with PlayerNotify.Toast on state change for feedback.
catalog.playerExperience: The player walks to the door next to the portal. Opening it from the outside selects destination A (toast: 'Gate set: Outpost'); closing it disarms the gate; opening it from the inside selects destination B. The door animates normally and the portal's connection follows within half a second. Anyone not permitted by the surrounding ward cannot flip the lever.
failureModes: s_state is client-authored: a modified client can set any value; treat it as a selector, never as a payment (same tier as item stands and signs).
Ownership hand-off timing: RPC_UseDoor runs on the owner; if the owner is a laggy remote peer the flip can take a few hundred ms to reach the server.

Vanilla Door.UpdateState animates from s_state on every client (:123773-123785) — a server that also WRITES s_state (see Server Portcullis) must not fight the lever poll; keep input doors and output doors distinct.
Doors count as pieces; a raid or a player can destroy the lever, which reads as state 0 (ZDO gone → treat as 'closed').
prerequisites: The Routing Kernel (to act on the selection)
openQuestions: Which door prefabs have m_canNotBeClosed / m_keyItem set (Inspector) — enumerate Door components on ZNetScene prefabs and log those fields.
evidence: Door.Awake / UpdateState / SetState / CanInteract / Interact / Open / RPC_UseDoor: :123759-123952
ZDO.Set has no ownership check (cross-verified via Fireplace/Smelter/Door/Container handler bodies read directly)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] All citations verified at essentially exact line numbers: Door.Awake InvokeRepeating('UpdateState',0f,0.2f) at :123769; UpdateState's DataRevision-gated poll at :123773-123785; CanInteract at :123807; Interact at :123850, which itself contains the 'if (m_checkGuardStone && !PrivateArea.CheckAccess(...)) return true;' gate right where cited; Open at :123891 computing forward/back via Vector3.Dot and calling InvokeRPC('UseDoor', flag); RPC_UseDoor at :123930 implementing exactly the 0/1/-1 state machine claimed (closed->forward gives 1, closed->back gives -1, anything nonzero->0), with s_state confirmed at ZDOVars :78611. Because ZDO.Set has no ownership check anywhere (independently reconfirmed via multiple RPC-handler bodies read in this pass) and the write reaches the server through the normal, distance-independent ZDO change-queue/RPC_ZDOData path (not through GameObject instantiation), the server-side read of s_state via a spatial ZDO query is sound and does not depend on the server ever instantiating the door's GameObject. The option text itself already correctly labels the guard-stone access control as 'vanilla-honoured' rather than folding it into the server-enforced claim, matching the actual client-side execution point of PrivateArea.CheckAccess inside Door.Interact.

catalog.name: Server Portcullis (Door as Output)
catalog.oneLine: The server opens or shuts a vanilla door by writing s_state; every client within range animates it within 0.2 s — a physical, in-world 'gate is open/closed' signal that needs no HUD channel.
catalog.howItWorks: Door.UpdateState runs by InvokeRepeating every 0.2s on every client that has the door instantiated (:123769) and re-applies `SetState(zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_state))` whenever the ZDO's DataRevision changed (:123773-123785); SetState drives the animator and plays m_openEffects/m_closeEffects (:123787-123805). The server writes `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_state, 1|-1|0)` (ZDO.Set has no ownership check; :73648-73654), bumps DataRevision past the owner's, and ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid) (:77706) so nearby peers get it on the next send cycle (ShouldSend passes because the server's revision now exceeds the peer's cached one, :76003-76014). No RPC needed and no owner cooperation: unlike RPC_UseDoor, a direct field write bypasses CanInteract's animation-state gate. Use: a 'toll gate' door in front of the portal frame that the server swings open only while the route is wired (Park and Release / Prepaid Toll Escrow condition true) and slams shut when the escrow runs dry — the player physically cannot walk into the portal trigger while the door blocks the frame. Combine with Vault Seal to stop the owner re-opening it: the door's own Interact routes UseDoor to the owner (:123894), and if the SERVER owns the door ZDO (claim + ZdoSetOwnerPatch block, WaterBuoyancyEngine pattern) the RPC lands on a peer with no instance and is dropped (HandleRoutedRPC → FindInstance null) — the door becomes server-only.
catalog.playerExperience: The player approaches the portal; the door across the frame is shut. They drop the toll in the chest; a second later the door swings open with the normal creak and they walk through. When the escrow is empty the door closes behind the last traveller and pressing Use on it does nothing.
failureModes: Physical blocking depends on the door actually covering the TeleportWorldTrigger volume — collider geometry is Inspector data; a player can vault, build around, or destroy the door (WearNTear). It is a UX gate, not the enforcement; the connection write remains the enforcement.

If the server does not hold ownership, the owning client can toggle it back (RPC_UseDoor has no server veto); holding ownership makes ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS fight the claim every 2s unless ZDO.SetOwner is prefixed (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313).
A door the server owns cannot be opened by anyone, including admins, until the mod releases it.
Door state write leaves the door ZDO 'dirty' every toggle — negligible.
prerequisites: Park and Release or Prepaid Toll Escrow (something to signal)
WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch (optional, for a server-owned door)
openQuestions: Does any vanilla door prefab's collider actually span a portal frame's trigger volume? Needs an in-game placement test.
evidence: Door.UpdateState unconditional re-apply, no CanInteract gate: :123773-123785
ZRoutedRpc full routing trace confirming server-side FindInstance requirement: :83554-83663
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] Door.UpdateState (123773-123785) unconditionally re-applies SetState from the ZDO's current s_state whenever DataRevision changed, with no CanInteract gate in that path -- confirmed directly, matching the claim that a direct field write bypasses the animation-state gate RPC_UseDoor would otherwise apply. ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC's FindInstance-returns-null-and-drops behavior for a server-owned target (:83646-83663) was independently traced end-to-end: on the sender's client, InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID=serverOwnerId,...) goes to RouteRPC since target != sender's own id, which (client not m_server) forwards to its only peer (the server) via 'RoutedRPC' network call; the server's own RPC_RoutedRPC sees target==its own m_id and calls HandleRoutedRPC locally, which requires ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo) to succeed on the SERVER's own scene -- and per the Sector-Zero fact (server never instantiates real-world GameObjects), this always fails regardless of ownership, so the request silently evaporates exactly as claimed, and for an even more fundamental reason than 'server owns it, so no client answers.'

catalog.name: Vault Seal (Server-Owned Chest Is Unopenable)
catalog.oneLine: While the server holds ownership of a container ZDO, no vanilla client can open it: Container.RPC_RequestOpen only runs on the owner and the server has no instance to answer — a free 'lock this escrow chest during settlement' primitive.
catalog.howItWorks: Container.Interact never opens locally; it invokes `RPC_RequestOpen(playerID)` at the ZDO owner (:122058) and waits for `RPC_OpenResponse(true)` (:122159-122170) before InventoryGui.Show. RPC_RequestOpen (:122134-122157) is gated on `m_nview.IsOwner()` and, when granted, hands ownership to the requester (`SetOwner(uid)`) after ForceSendZDO. If the server owns the chest (`zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, guarded against ReleaseNearbyZDOS by the ZDO.SetOwner prefix in WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313), the routed RPC arrives at the server, ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC → ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null (:83646-83663) and the request evaporates: the client shows nothing (no RPC_OpenResponse ever comes; the '$msg_inuse' message is only shown on an explicit false). Releasing ownership (`SetOwner(0L)`) restores normal opening on the next Interact. Use in the economy: (1) Prepaid Toll Escrow — seal the bound chest for the ~200 ms window while the server debits s_items via ZdoInventoryIO.Save, eliminating the read-modify-write race with a player who has the GUI open (the existing s_inUse guard only avoids the race, it cannot win it); (2) a 'settlement vault' the server fills with tax skim that players can see (hover shows the chest) but never open; (3) freezing a chest whose forged contents are under Inline ZDOData Validator review. The seal is invisible to vanilla except that Use does nothing; add a PlayerNotify.Toast('Vault sealed') from a HandleRoutedRPC prefix that matches m_methodHash == "RPC_RequestOpen".GetStableHashCode() && m_targetZDO == the sealed chest to give feedback.
catalog.playerExperience: The player presses Use on the escrow chest during a settlement tick and nothing happens for a moment (or a toast says 'Settling toll…'); half a second later Use opens it normally and the debited stack is gone. A permanently sealed vault shows its normal hover text but never opens.
failureModes: Holding server ownership near players requires the ZDO.SetOwner Harmony prefix on a global hot path — the predicate must fail fast on the chest's prefab hash / a small ZDOID set.
A client that already OWNS the chest when the seal is requested keeps its open GUI until it closes; the seal only prevents new opens. Check s_inUse (:121994-121996) before sealing and wait.
No vanilla message on a silent drop — players will spam Use; the toast in the HandleRoutedRPC prefix is needed for UX.

Container.CheckForChanges on the owning client reloads on DataRevision (:122305-122313); after the server edits s_items and releases ownership, the next opener gets the server's version via the ForceSendZDO in RPC_RequestOpen? No — the server must ForceSendZDO itself after the edit.
openQuestions: Confirm in-game that a vanilla client shows no message at all when RPC_RequestOpen is dropped (expected: silent) and that InventoryGui does not get stuck in a pending state.
corrections: Attribute the silent-drop to the server's ZNetScene never instantiating real-world-positioned GameObjects at all (Game.FixedUpdate's unconditional reference-position pin + ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects anchoring to it), not merely to 'server ownership meaning no instance' -- the latter is true but is a special case of the former, more fundamental fact.
evidence: Container.RPC_RequestOpen not-owner branch, no response sent: :122134-122157
Wonderland Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs lines 44-53 (independent confirmation from live testing)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Container.RPC_RequestOpen (122134-122157) verified verbatim: the not-owner branch ('if (!m_nview.IsOwner()) { ZLog.Log(...); }') has no attached else and sends NO RPC_OpenResponse at all -- the requester's client never hears back and InventoryGui never opens, exactly as claimed ('the client shows nothing... no RPC_OpenResponse ever comes'). This is real and precisely cited. The correction is about WHY it's true when the server owns the chest: the option frames it as 'the server has no instance to answer,' as if that's a special consequence of server ownership specifically. In fact it is a far more general and even stronger fact, independently confirmed against source in this pass: Game.FixedUpdate pins ZNet's reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) unconditionally every tick (server build, no local-player guard) and ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects instantiates objects only around that same reference position -- so ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance ALWAYS returns null on the dedicated server for anything not literally at that coordinate, independent of who owns it. This is also independently corroborated by the sibling Wonderland mod's own ConnectedCharacters.cs comment, which cites the identical fact from live dedicated-server testing. The practical upshot strengthens rather than weakens the option: the seal doesn't depend on some narrow ownership-specific quirk, it's a structural property of how dedicated servers instantiate objects at all.

catalog.name: Presence-Wired Routes (Owner Online)
catalog.oneLine: A route exists only while its builder — or any member of the route's network — is logged in; a pure server-side predicate over the peer list, enforced at the connection layer.
catalog.howItWorks: Predicate inputs are all server-resident: each portal ZDO carries `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393), the builder's PlayerProfile UID written by Piece.SetCreator on placement (:136415-136424); each connected player's character ZDO carries `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (:78539), the same UID (ConnectedCharacters.PlayerId, Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:30). A route's 'network' = the set of s_creator values across the tag group, optionally unioned with ward permitted lists near either end (pu_id<i>, PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers :137349-137363). Reconcile tick (1 s): `online = ConnectedCharacters.All().Select(c => c.PlayerId).Where(id != 0)`; for each managed route, `open = network ∩ online ≠ ∅`. Open → `Game.SetConnection` semantics both ways (own ZDO if unowned/owner offline, else RPC_SetConnection to the owner, :100637-100651) then ForceSendZDO; closed → SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) on both ends, or point the public end at a Customs House anchor so it still glows. Edge triggers shorten latency: a postfix on ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:26-46) schedules an immediate reconcile — but s_playerID is not yet known at that moment (the character ZDO arrives later, Game.SpawnPlayer ordering), so the join edge only ARMS a fast poll until PlayerId != 0; a PREFIX on ZNet.Disconnect(ZNetPeer) (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:48-58) runs before ClearPlayerData → ZDOMan.RemovePeer (:80009-80013) destroys the character ZDO, so `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(s_playerID)` is still readable and the route closes in the same frame the player leaves. Vanilla's Game.ConnectPortals would re-pair a same-tag closed route within 5 s (:100607-100622), so this requires The Routing Kernel (prefix returning false, or GetPortals() exclusion) — or the Customs House anchor topology, which vanilla's reconciler leaves alone. Hysteresis: hold a route's last state while any network member has PlayerId == 0 (join window) to avoid flapping.
catalog.playerExperience: A guild member's portal network works normally while at least one guild member is online. When the last member logs off, every gate in the network reads Unconnected (or, with the decoy, stays lit but drops travellers into the customs pen). The moment a member logs back in and spawns, the gates reconnect within a second; travellers already inside a trigger must step out and back in.
failureModes: Join latency: s_playerID reads 0 for several frames after the peer is ready; a naive reconcile could briefly treat a returning owner as absent. Hysteresis fixes it.
Same-tag re-pairing by vanilla within 5 s unless the Kernel owns pairing.
s_creator is 0 on portals placed before creator tracking or by admin spawn — treat creator 0 as 'always open' or 'admin-owned' explicitly.
Name-collision-free, but ALT accounts: a member can leave a second account logged in to keep the network wired; presence is a policy, not a proof.
A player who logs out mid-transit (black screen) arrives anyway — the destination was read at entry.
prerequisites: The Routing Kernel (or Customs House anchor topology)
openQuestions: Measured frames between RPC_PeerInfo and s_playerID != 0 on the character ZDO (sets the hysteresis window). IN-GAME CHECK: poll per frame on join.
Whether a player standing inside the trigger volume when the route re-opens needs to step out (OnTriggerEnter only) — expected yes.
corrections: Note explicitly that Game.RPC_SetConnection is a GLOBAL routed RPC (ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register, not per-ZNetView), so its delivery never depends on ZNetScene.FindInstance succeeding anywhere (server or client) -- it is immune to the Sector-Zero instantiation limit that affects GameObject-instance-targeted RPCs like Container's or Fireplace's.
evidence: Wonderland Subsystems/DiscordNotify/PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs (full file read, matches cited behavior)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Re-derived Game.SetConnection, Game.ConnectPortals and Game.RPC_SetConnection directly from source and they match the option (and the prior reviewer's confirmed corrections) exactly: SetConnection (100637-100651) checks 'owner==0 || GetPeer(owner)==null || forceImmediateConnection' before taking the local (server-claims-ownership) path, else delegates via InvokeRoutedRPC(owner,'RPC_SetConnection',...); ConnectPortals' reconcile predicate (100594-100606) is exactly 'target==null || tag mismatch || target.connection==None' with no reciprocity check, matching the confirmed correction. Piece.SetCreator (136415-136424) and ZDOVars.s_creator/s_playerID exist and are gated/populated exactly as claimed. Wonderland's PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs was read in full and matches the cited behavior almost verbatim (RPC_PeerInfo postfix keyed on non-empty m_playerName after all rejection paths, ZNet.Disconnect prefix reading AnnouncedJoins before teardown). One clarifying correction worth adding: RPC_SetConnection is registered as a GLOBAL routed RPC (ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<ZDOID,ZDOID> at :100067), not a per-ZDO ZNetView RPC -- delivery therefore never invokes ZNetScene.FindInstance anywhere (confirmed via the m_targetZDO.IsNone() branch of HandleRoutedRPC at :83646-83650, which dispatches straight through the method-hash table) and so this whole mechanism is structurally immune to the Sector-Zero GameObject-instantiation limits that constrain several other options in this batch -- worth stating explicitly since it preempts an obvious objection.

catalog.name: Offline-Raid Shield (Inverse Presence)
catalog.oneLine: Nobody can portal INTO a base whose owners are all logged out: the inbound leg is unwired while the network is empty, closing the classic 'portal in while they sleep' raid on PvP servers.
catalog.howItWorks: Same predicate machinery as Presence-Wired Routes with the polarity flipped per direction. For a base portal B owned by network N: while `N ∩ online = ∅`, every route whose DESTINATION is B is unwired — the server writes `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on the far ends (or points them at a Customs House anchor), while B itself may keep an outbound link (One-Way Trade Routes are runtime-stable because Game.ConnectPortals never checks reciprocity, :100594-100606). Because a vanilla client resolves the destination at the instant of transit from the SOURCE portal's connection (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143539-143543), cutting the far end's connection is sufficient; B's own state is irrelevant to inbound travel. When any member of N comes online (edge: RPC_PeerInfo postfix arms a fast poll; steady state: 1 s reconcile with PlayerId != 0), the far ends are re-wired. Optional grace: keep inbound open for G minutes after the last member leaves (server-owned timestamp), and re-close on a timer, so a member who crashes can return without racing raiders. Combine with Debtor's Lien semantics: the same 'network' membership set (s_creator ∪ ward pu_id) is the shield's owner list. This is enforcement, not deterrence: the raider's client has no destination ZDOID to teleport to (gate 1 in Teleport returns silently, :143519).
catalog.playerExperience: A raider who found a public gate tagged like the target base walks in while the owners are offline — nothing happens (or, with the decoy, they land in a customs pen). The owners' own outbound gate keeps working for them when they log in, and inbound resumes the moment one of them spawns.
failureModes: Raiders standing physically at the base are unaffected — this only closes the portal vector.
If the base portal shares a tag with public portals, vanilla re-pairs within 5 s unless the Kernel holds pairing; with the decoy anchor topology it is vanilla-stable.
An owner's alt account left online defeats it (policy, not proof).
Grace timers rely on the server's own clock; ZNet.GetTime() is fine but a server restart resets in-memory timers — persist as a world global key if it matters.
prerequisites: The Routing Kernel or Customs House anchor
One-Way Trade Routes (for the outbound-only variant)
citations: TeleportWorld.Teleport destination resolution :143539-143543; gate 1 silent return :143519
openQuestions: Whether server operators want the base's OUTBOUND leg to stay alive while everyone is offline (it is harmless: nobody is there to use it).
evidence: TeleportWorld.Teleport: TargetFound silent-return and connection-based destination resolution: :143517-143543
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] TeleportWorld.Teleport verified directly: it returns silently when '!TargetFound()' (the very first line of the method body, matching 'gate 1... returns silently'), and destination resolution reads 'ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(m_nview.GetZDO().GetConnectionZDOID(Portal))' -- i.e. purely the SOURCE portal's own connection field at the moment of transit, exactly as cited. This confirms the core mechanism: cutting only the far end's (destination's) connection is sufficient to block inbound travel, with no need to touch the base portal's own outbound state. Builds directly and correctly on Presence-Wired Routes' independently-confirmed SetConnection/ConnectPortals mechanics.

catalog.name: Escort Gate (Owner-Nearby Routes)
catalog.oneLine: A route is wired only while its builder stands within N metres of either end — travellers can only pass under escort, and the gate closes within a second when the escort walks away.
catalog.howItWorks: Character ZDO positions are refreshed by the owning client's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync every physics tick and reach the server via the distance-independent client change queue (:77241-77258), so `ConnectedCharacter.Position` is fresh to ~50-100 ms. Reconcile tick at 0.5-1 s: for route (A,B) with owner set O, `open = ∃ c ∈ ConnectedCharacters.All(): c.PlayerId ∈ O && (Dist(c.Position, A.pos) < N || Dist(c.Position, B.pos) < N)`. Write the connection state exactly as in Presence-Wired Routes. Because TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads the connection at OnTriggerEnter (:143517-143543) and TargetFound requires the client to hold the target ZDO (:143640-143655), a route that was closed and re-opened must be ForceSendZDO'd (server → traveller peer) for the destination ZDO or the first walk-through fails silently; do the ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destId) for every peer within ~30 m of A at the moment of opening. Variants: 'escort must be on the SAME side as the traveller' (distance to the traveller's end only); 'convoy' (route stays open for T seconds after the escort transits, using PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit :148 to detect the escort's own hop).
catalog.playerExperience: A visitor at the guild's gate sees it Unconnected until a guild member walks up; the gate lights, the visitor walks through, and behind them the gate goes dark again as the member wanders off. The member themself can always use it because they are, by definition, next to it.
failureModes: Trigger-enter semantics: a visitor already standing inside the portal volume when the escort arrives must step out and back in.

First-transit warm-up: if the traveller's client has never held the destination ZDO the walk-through silently no-ops until RequestZDO completes; mitigated by the proactive ForceSendZDO but not eliminated.
Escort walks off mid-teleport: the traveller still arrives (destination read at entry).
Position freshness for a laggy escort peer can flap the gate at the radius boundary — add 2-3 m hysteresis.
Same-tag re-pairing by vanilla unless the Kernel owns pairing.
openQuestions: Does ForceSendZDO(peer, destId) issued before the traveller's first attempt reliably beat their walk-through? Needs a timing test with a far destination.
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] The specific overload cited, ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id), was independently confirmed to exist with exactly that signature at :77714 (alongside the no-arg ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) at :77706), supporting the claim that a per-peer force-send is available to push the destination ZDO to a specific nearby traveller at the moment a route opens. The rest of the mechanism is a direct, correctly-scoped composition of the independently confirmed ConnectedCharacters/position-freshness and Presence-Wired Routes primitives; no new unverified claims of substance beyond what was already checked for those.

catalog.name: Portal Sickness (Post-Transit Debuff)
catalog.oneLine: Detect a transit after the fact and stamp a vanilla debuff on the traveller — Puke (strips food), Wet, or Frost — as the only server-side way to make 'portal cooldown per player' a felt consequence.
catalog.howItWorks: Detection: PositionWatch.OnUpdate samples every connected character at PositionWatchInterval (default 3 s) and IsPortalTransit (Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:148-215) flags a sample pair whose endpoints both sit within 40 m of portals in ZDOMan.GetPortals() and whose connection links them. The character ZDO position jumps at t>2 s of Player.UpdateTeleport (:15337-15348), so the transit is visible 2-5 s after entry — while the traveller is still inside the ≥8 s distant-teleport black screen (:15349-15352). Grant: `StatusEffectRpc.Grant(who, hash)` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, charZdo.m_uid, "RPC_AddStatusEffect", hash, true, 0, 0f, -1)` → SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect (:28823-28829, owner-gated) → Internal_AddStatusEffect resolves against ObjectDB (:28831-28850) → AddStatusEffect runs CanAdd (base returns true, :31074) and Setup. Which vanilla effects SURVIVE on the client after a remote grant (verified against Player.UpdateEnvStatusEffects :11619-11691, which force-removes effects whose environmental condition is false every tick): Puke ("Puke" — SE_Puke removes one food per m_removeInterval, :29872-29897; harsh), Wet ("Wet" :28698 — only ever ADDED by the env updater, never removed, so it runs to its Inspector TTL; re-ping with resetTime resets m_time :31182), Frost ("Frost" :28712 — movement slow scaled by m_time/m_ttl, :29578-29641), Burning ("Burning" :28710 — with no AddFireDamage the per-tick damage is 0, so it is a cosmetic flame for its TTL), Poison ("Poison" :28716, 0 damage-left → cosmetic). RULED OUT: Cold, Freezing, Resting, Shelter, CampFire (removed each tick at :11652-11689) and Smoked (removed every 2 s at :1121). Duration control: there is no remove RPC anywhere (grep for RPC_RemoveStatusEffect returns nothing in either assembly), so the only lever is re-pinging within the TTL (BuffRosterEngine RepingInterval = clamp(ttl*0.4, 0.2, ttl-0.2), Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:112) for the configured sickness window and then letting it expire. Per-player state: keyed on PlayerId, in memory (sessions are short); the effect itself dies with the character ZDO on disconnect.
catalog.playerExperience: The traveller steps through, sits through the usual swirl, and arrives with the Wet icon (or slowed by Frost, or — on a harsh server — nauseous and losing their food) for the configured minutes. Using another portal before it clears refreshes it. Nothing stops the second transit; the sickness is the price.
failureModes: Detector false positives/negatives: 3 s sampling can miss a short hop between adjacent portals and can misattribute a Ladder/dungeon jump; PositionWatch already suppresses dungeon and respawn jumps (IsLegitimateTransit :119).
The server never learns whether the grant landed (no ack; s_seAttrib :78585 is an attribute bitmask, not an effect list).
Puke strips ALL food within seconds on a vanilla client (one per second) — players will read it as a bug unless announced; prefer Wet/Frost for a 'sickness' that is legible.
Effect assets are Inspector data: TTLs (SE_Wet, SE_Frost) are unknown from the decompile; measure in-game.
Cannot be cancelled early: if the operator disables the feature, active effects run to TTL.
openQuestions: Inspector TTLs of SE_Wet / SE_Frost / SE_Puke on the shipped assets — log ObjectDB.instance.GetStatusEffect(hash).m_ttl on a client.
Whether a grant that arrives during the black screen is applied (Player.FixedUpdate runs during teleport; expected yes) and whether Frost's slow is visible post-arrival.
evidence: Player.UpdateEnvStatusEffects full body (Cold/Freezing/Resting/Shelter/CampFire force-managed, Wet add-only): :11619-11683
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect independently verified to be owner-gated exactly as claimed: both the public AddStatusEffect wrapper ('if (m_nview.IsOwner()) return Internal_AddStatusEffect(...); m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_AddStatusEffect",...)') and the private RPC handler itself ('private void RPC_AddStatusEffect(...) { if (m_nview.IsOwner()) Internal_AddStatusEffect(...); }') check ownership, at :28809-28829. Because a character ZDO's owner is always the player's own connected client, this RPC's delivery is unaffected by the Sector-Zero GameObject-instantiation limit (the target is always instantiated on its own owner's machine). The specific and highly falsifiable claim about which vanilla effects survive a remote grant was checked by reading Player.UpdateEnvStatusEffects (11619-11683) in full: Shelter, CampFire, Resting, Cold and Freezing are ALL unconditionally re-decided (force-added or force-removed) every call, exactly matching the 'RULED OUT' list; Wet is written only via an unconditional AddStatusEffect call with no corresponding RemoveStatusEffect anywhere in that method, exactly matching the claim that it 'runs to its Inspector TTL.' Burning/Frost/Poison are not touched by this method at all (only read, for Burning), consistent with the claim that they run as cosmetic/TTL-bound effects absent an active damage source. This is an unusually precise and independently falsifiable claim that checks out exactly.

catalog.name: Arrival Blessing (Rested on Exit)
catalog.oneLine: The mirror of Portal Sickness: reward a transit into a hub or home gate with the vanilla Rested buff, re-pinged so it outlasts the comfort it would normally give.
catalog.howItWorks: Same detector and RPC as Portal Sickness. Grant `SEMan.s_statusEffectRested` ("Rested", :28692). SE_Rested.Setup (:29958-29963) calls UpdateTTL which computes `m_baseTTL + (comfort-1)*m_TTLPerComfortLevel` from `player.GetComfortLevel()` at the ARRIVAL position and shows '$se_rested_start ($se_rested_comfort:N)' in the centre of the screen — free feedback. Unlike the env effects, Rested is NOT removed by Player.UpdateEnvStatusEffects (it manages 'Resting', a different effect, :11669); it runs to its TTL. SE_Rested.ResetTime (:29975-29978) re-evaluates comfort rather than blindly resetting, so a re-ping only extends when the current remaining time is shorter than the recomputed TTL — meaning re-pings at a low-comfort destination will NOT keep it alive beyond baseTTL; the extension is capped by the arrival comfort. Route-specific: grant only when the destination portal is in a managed 'hub' set, or only when the traveller paid (escrow debit succeeded), making the buff part of the toll's value. Also usable as the 'you were charged' acknowledgement: the toast + buff icon arrive together.
catalog.playerExperience: The traveller arrives at the capital hub and sees 'Rested (Comfort 7)' pop up with the buff icon, exactly as if they had just sat by a hearth, and keeps it for the normal Rested duration.
failureModes: Comfort is evaluated at the arrival point on the client: an arrival in the wild yields baseTTL only and re-pings cannot extend past it.
Same detection latency and lack of ack as Portal Sickness.
Players who already have Rested with a longer remaining time see no change (UpdateTTL only raises).
openQuestions: SE_Rested m_baseTTL / m_TTLPerComfortLevel Inspector values (code defaults 300/60).
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] SE_Rested class location confirmed almost exactly at the cited range (:29944, cited as :29944-29990). Critically, Player.UpdateEnvStatusEffects (read in full for the Portal Sickness check above) manages 'Resting' (SEMan.s_statusEffectResting) as the force-add/remove effect, NOT 'Rested' (s_statusEffectRested) -- these are confirmed to be two distinct hash constants (:28692 Rested vs. the Resting hash used inside UpdateEnvStatusEffects at :11662-11670). This directly supports the option's key claim that a remotely-granted Rested buff is not auto-stripped by the environmental updater and will run to its (re-pingable) TTL.

catalog.name: Per-Player Cooldown Made Visible
catalog.oneLine: Compose route cooldowns with a personal debuff so the cooldown is on the PLAYER not the gate: the gate stays open for others while the recent traveller wears a timer they can see.
catalog.howItWorks: Cooldowns and Throughput Quotas close the ROUTE after a transit, punishing everyone. This option keeps the route open and instead (a) records `lastTransit[PlayerId] = ZNet.instance.GetTime()` from the PositionWatch detector, (b) grants a marker effect with a TTL close to the cooldown (Wet, or Frost for a stronger cue) and re-pings it on the BuffRosterEngine cadence until the cooldown elapses, and (c) when the same player transits again inside the window, escalates: a longer re-ping window, a Portal Sickness Puke pulse, or — the only real enforcement available — Debtor's Lien (unwire every portal that player built for the remainder of the window) and a PlayerNotify.Toast explaining it. The buff icon's remaining-time bar on the vanilla HUD IS the cooldown display; no other channel can show a per-player timer to a vanilla client. Nothing here stops the second transit itself (RULED OUT — Point-of-Transit Enforcement); the consequence is post-hoc and property-based.
catalog.playerExperience: After a hop the player sees a Wet icon draining for the cooldown length. Hopping again early refreshes it and, on strict servers, their own home gate reads Unconnected until the icon clears, with a toast saying why.
failureModes: All the Portal Sickness detector caveats.
Wet as a timer is odd flavour (rain-proof players with a roof still get it) — Frost reads better but slows movement.
A player can hop as much as they like through gates they did not build; only their own gates can be liened.
Re-ping storms: N recent travellers × re-ping interval; trivial at server scale but bound it.
openQuestions: Whether the vanilla HUD shows a remaining-time bar for Wet/Frost (StatusEffect.GetIconText / m_ttl-driven) — Inspector/UI check.
evidence: Shared basis: Portal Sickness verification (SEMan gating, status-effect survival)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] This option is a pure composition of primitives independently verified elsewhere in this pass (SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect owner-gating and delivery to the character's own owning client; the env-status-effect survival facts from Portal Sickness). It introduces no new unverified technical claim beyond citing ZNet.GetTime existing (used elsewhere at Fireplace.GetTimeSinceLastUpdate, a real method) and asserting no server-side gate exists on the second transit itself, which is consistent with the project's central constraint that TeleportWorldTrigger/Teleport never runs server-side.

catalog.name: Trust-Tier Correction: Forgeable Condition Inputs
catalog.oneLine: Re-label every escrow/turnstile/charge-cell/key-item option: the ROUTE decision is server-enforced, but its CONDITION is client-authored ZDO data a modified client can forge — 'server-enforced against unmodified clients' is the honest tier.
catalog.howItWorks: The catalog labels Prepaid Toll Escrow, Token Turnstile, Charge Cells and Key-Item Requirement 'server-enforced' while The Ore Gate is 'client-honoured'. Both classes read fields the owning client wrote: `s_items` on a chest (Container.Save :122294-122301), `s_item` on an item stand, `s_fuel` on a fireplace (Fireplace.RPC_AddFuel writes on the owner :125736), `s_state` on a door. Those fields reach the server through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77140), which authenticates only the SOCKET (FindPeer(rpc) :77078) and then applies the whole blob if `num4 > zDO.DataRevision` (:77110-77131) — no ownership test, no field allowlist, no plausibility check; ZDO.Deserialize (:74206-74241) adds every field present. A modified client therefore writes a full stack of the toll item into s_items, or s_fuel = m_maxFuel, or s_item = the key hash, from anywhere, at any rate, and the server-side gate opens. What distinguishes the two classes is WHERE the decision executes, not who authored the inputs: the escrow family decides on the server and writes the connection (a forger must fabricate STATE); the Ore Gate decides on the client (a forger simply ignores the check). Correct tiering: (1) route/connection writes — server-enforced; (2) conditions read from world ZDOs — 'server-enforced against unmodified clients; inputs forgeable by a modified client without Inline ZDOData Validator'; (3) client-executed checks (Ore Gate, NoPortals, IsTeleportable) — client-honoured. Practical consequence for the economy: never let an escrow balance be a pure count of what is in a chest; keep the SERVER LEDGER (ItemLedger / a mod-side balance file) as the balance of record, treat chest contents as DEPOSIT EVENTS the server drains into its own ledger (ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem), and let the validator gate which deposit events are believed.
catalog.playerExperience: No change for honest players. For operators: the config and docs say plainly that a hacked client can fake a deposit, that the mod flags implausible deposits, and that the route itself cannot be opened by a client — only the evidence for it.
failureModes: Operators who read 'server-enforced' as 'cheat-proof' deploy a toll economy that a single hacked client mints for free.
Even with the validator, provenance cannot be proven — the validator raises the forgery cost from 'one packet' to 'emulate a plausible player session'.
evidence: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData full body: :77076-77140 (FindPeer :77078; revision gate; blind Deserialize apply; AddIfPortal immediately after)
verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData was read in full (:77076-77140) and matches the claim precisely: FindPeer(rpc) (:77078) authenticates only the socket, not any field inside the packet; the per-ZDO apply loop reads a client-declared ownerInternal and, when 'num4 > zDO.DataRevision' (confirmed exact condition, inverted from the 'num4 <= DataRevision' early-continue branch), unconditionally calls zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) with no ownership test, no field allowlist, and no plausibility check of any kind -- exactly as claimed. This directly substantiates the option's central point: the write path for station/chest/door fields is not intrinsically more trustworthy than the Ore Gate's client-side check, only the ROUTE decision (a separate write the server itself performs) is truly server-enforced. Container.Save, Fireplace.RPC_AddFuel and Door.RPC_UseDoor were all independently confirmed to write ZDO fields with no special protection beyond the IsOwner() gate on the RPC handler itself (which a modified client can satisfy by first claiming ownership, itself just another ZDOData entry).

catalog.name: Inline ZDOData Validator (In-Frame Revert)
catalog.oneLine: A postfix on ZDO.Deserialize that, for bound escrow containers and managed portals, compares the just-arrived fields against the last server-approved state and reverts inside the same frame — collapsing the Tag Watchdog's one-tick window to zero and giving the economy its only anti-forgery line.
catalog.howItWorks: Hook point: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData sets OwnerRevision/DataRevision/owner/position (:77126-77129), records the peer's cached revision (:77130), THEN calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` (:77131). A Harmony postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (the same target SpawnGovernor already uses, SpawnGovernor.cs:58) runs with the client's data fully applied and `__instance.m_uid` known. Fast reject: `if (!Watched.Contains(__instance.m_uid)) return;` — a HashSet of ZDOIDs the mod manages (escrow chests, turnstile stands, charge fireplaces, managed portals); everything else costs one hash lookup. Sender identity is not visible in the Deserialize postfix, so ALSO prefix `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` to stash `CurrentSender = ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` in a static for the duration of the call (RPC_ZDOData is synchronous on the main thread). Rules per watched class: PORTAL — `s_tag`/`s_tagauthor`/Portal connection must equal the kernel's approved values (managed portals are server-authored; any client delta is a forgery or a stale echo): revert unconditionally. ESCROW CHEST — accept `s_items` deltas only if (a) the packet's owner field == CurrentSender.m_uid (a vanilla opener always becomes owner via RPC_RequestOpen :122150-122152), (b) `s_inUse == 1` in the same ZDO (Container.UpdateUseVisual writes it on the owner while the GUI is open, :121990-121996; a vanilla s_items write only ever follows OnContainerChanged while a GUI is open), (c) the sender's character ZDO is within ~5 m of the chest, (d) the delta is bounded (no item exceeds m_maxStackSize; total added per second below a config cap; only prefab names ObjectDB knows), and (e) the ZDO's DataRevision advanced by a plausible step. TURNSTILE STAND / CHARGE FIREPLACE — same proximity + owner==sender + bounded-delta rules on `s_item` / `s_fuel`. Revert mechanics: re-write the approved fields (`zdo.Set(...)`, ZDOExtraData.Add is additive so absent fields are untouched), set `zdo.DataRevision = incoming + 4096` (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:158-164 pattern; ZDO.DataRevision has a public setter :73494), then `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706). The peer cache was set to `incoming` at :77130, so ShouldSend (:76003-76014) is true; the forger's client receives the revert (its RPC_ZDOData accepts because 4096+ > its own revision) and any further push it sends with rev ≤ incoming+4096 is discarded by the server at :77110. Escalation: count rejections per PlayerId; on N in M seconds `AuditLog.Flag` + `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` (:81658). Because the revert happens before RPC_ZDOData's loop continues to AddIfPortal (:77132) and before any other subsystem tick, no server-side consumer ever observes the forged value — the Tag Watchdog's one-tick exposure becomes zero.
catalog.playerExperience: Honest players notice nothing: their deposits pass every rule. A cheater who injects a full chest sees the contents snap back to what was really there within one round trip, the toll stays unpaid, and after a few attempts they are kicked with a log line naming them.
failureModes: Provenance is still unprovable: a modified client that emulates a legit session (walk to the chest, set s_inUse, own the ZDO, add one stack per second) passes. The validator raises cost, it does not close the hole.
Rule (a) can false-positive on vanilla edge cases where a client writes a ZDO it does not own (ZDO.Set has no owner check on the client either) — log-only mode first, then enforce.
Rule (b): server-side mod writes (ZdoInventoryIO.Save, VacuumEngine) must be whitelisted by writing through a 'server-approved' snapshot update, or they trip their own validator.
Position rule needs the sender's character ZDO; during the join window (PlayerId 0) or death, skip position and rely on the other rules.
A prefix on RPC_ZDOData that re-parses a COPY of the package (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) is the alternative hook if the static-sender trick is judged too fragile; never advance the live pkg.
Perf: RPC_ZDOData is the hottest inbound path; the HashSet gate must be the first statement of the postfix.
The revert races nothing on the server, but the owner's client can keep re-forging at higher revisions; the kick threshold is the backstop.

verifierReasoning: [gapfill:confirmed] The hook-point claim was directly verified: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData sets OwnerRevision/DataRevision/owner internals and calls zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) immediately before the next loop iteration's implicit continue -- and 'AddIfPortal(zDO, zDO.GetPrefab())' (cited at :77132) does indeed follow right after, confirming a Harmony postfix on ZDO.Deserialize would run with the client's data already applied but before any other subsystem observes it, exactly as claimed. catalog.name: Sender–Owner Binding Rule
catalog.oneLine: The cheapest single validator rule, usable on its own: drop any ZDOData entry for a watched ZDO whose packet-declared owner is not the peer that sent it — vanilla clients always write ZDOs they own or have just claimed.
catalog.howItWorks: Every ZDOData entry carries an `ownerInternal` long that RPC_ZDOData applies with SetOwnerInternal (:77103, :77114, :77128) — a client self-report. But the packet arrives on an authenticated ZRpc whose ZNetPeer is `FindPeer(rpc)` (:77078); `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is the socket-bound session id (:78786; assigned :79905; duplicates rejected by ZNet.IsConnected :79993-80007). Vanilla write paths for economy-relevant fields all run under ownership: Container writes after RPC_RequestOpen made the opener owner (:122150-122152) or when it already was; Sign.SetText calls ClaimOwnership first (:141913-141928); Fireplace.Interact claims when unowned (:125642-125645); CookingStation.CookItem claims (:123105-123108); Door/Smelter/Fermenter/Beehive handlers run on the owner; Piece.SetCreator requires IsOwner (:136417). So for watched ZDOs the rule `packet.owner == sender.m_uid` holds for every vanilla client and fails for a forger who did not first claim ownership (a claim is itself a ZDOData entry with a bumped OwnerRevision, so a careful forger can still comply — this rule alone is a speed bump, not a wall). Implementation: prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData that parses a COPY (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) with the same read sequence as :77087-77105 (int count, N ZDOIDs, then loop: ZDOID, ushort, uint, long, Vector3, ReadPackage), records `(zdoid → ownerInternal)` for watched ids, and lets the real handler run; the ZDO.Deserialize postfix then reads the stashed owner and compares to the stashed sender. Alternative without Deserialize: a transpiler is not needed — the prefix can pre-mark the ZDOID for revert and the existing postfix executes it. Also catches the ownership-steal exploit on managed portals (a client declaring itself owner of a server-owned portal ZDO to re-tag it) because the packet's owner would be the sender but the mod's approved owner is the server: for portals the rule is `owner must be server or the mod-approved peer`.
catalog.playerExperience: Invisible to honest players. A naive forger's chest fill or portal re-tag is discarded before it is applied.
failureModes: A forger that first claims ownership passes; combine with the proximity/in-use/delta rules of the full validator.

Parsing a copy of every inbound ZDOData package costs one allocation and a re-read per packet; gate by watched-set size and by peer count, or only when the package's first ZDOID list intersects the watched set (cheap pre-scan).
Vanilla non-owner writes exist for some fields (e.g. clients set s_creator only when owner, but other mods may not); log-only mode first.

ZNetPeer.m_uid is confirmed to be assigned once during the RPC_PeerInfo handshake (at the IL_04a4 label, :79905) as a socket-bound session identifier, and ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData's FindPeer(rpc) (:77078) resolves the sender purely from the authenticated ZRpc/socket, not from any field inside the packet -- supporting the core claim that 'packet.owner == sender.m_uid' is a meaningful, forgery-resistant signal for vanilla write paths (which all claim ownership before writing) while still correctly conceding, as the option itself does, that a deliberate forger can defeat this specific rule alone by first sending an ownership-claim entry.

domainNotes:
### topologies
THE ONE LOAD-BEARING FACT. Vanilla's runtime reconciler `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626, body read directly and reproduced below) never checks reciprocity. Pass 1's teardown predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604) — it validates that the TARGET exists, shares the tag, and has SOME non-None connection, and nothing else. Pass 2 only touches portals whose own connection IsNone() (:100609). Consequently every non-reciprocal directed topology — fan-in stars, rings, chains with a terminator, in-trees, sinks — is a FIXED POINT of vanilla's own 5-second coroutine, requiring no Harmony patch, no faster tick and no race. That single omission is what makes a zero-client-install portal-topology mod possible at all. Contrast ZDOMan.ConvertPortals (:77812-77848), the pre-NewSaveFormat migration, which DID require `A.tag == B.tag && A.target == B && B.target == A`; the modern runtime pass deliberately relaxed it.

THE THREE INVARIANTS every managed topology must satisfy, at all times, for every member:
(1) the member's target ZDO resolves in ZDOMan;
(2) `target.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` is byte-identical to the member's own s_tag (ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, default "" so all untagged portals are one group);
(3) `target.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`.
Violate any one and the edge is nulled within 5 s, and the freed end is then randomly re-paired inside its tag group by `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` using the shared `UnityEngine.Random` stream (:100664-100679). Invariant (3) is why every chain needs a terminator and why "just set the connection to None to disable a portal" does not work.

THE HARD CEILING. One `ZDOConnection {readonly ConnectionType m_type; readonly ZDOID m_target;}` per ZDO, stored in `ZDOExtraData.s_connections : Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` (:74794-74797, :75524-75534). One destination, ever. Every "many destinations from one place" shape in this catalogue is therefore a Portal Bank (N physical portals), a Switchboard (repointed between transits) or a Carousel (repointed on a timer). Simultaneous fan-out and simultaneous full mesh are structurally impossible, not merely unimplemented. Full mesh over S sites via banks costs S×(S−1) portals; the hub+bank hybrid costs 2S for two-hop any-to-any and is the recommended shape.

PERSISTENCE IS THE OTHER CEILING, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST. The network wire format carries the real ZDOID (`ZDO.Serialize` writes `(byte)m_type` + `m_target`, :74169-74173) but the DISK format collapses each ZDO to one `ZDOConnectionHashData {type, int hash}` slot. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478, read directly) iterates s_connections and for each edge writes `hashData[source] = {type, h}` and then `hashData[target] = {type|Target, h}` — later edges overwrite earlier entries for any shared node. The disk format can only express a pairwise perfect matching. Therefore: rings >2 lose all but one link; one-way links come back BIDIRECTIONAL (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` at :77850-77893 writes both directions when it matches a hash pair); self-loops are erased outright (the source slot is immediately overwritten by the Target slot, :75472-75475); and everything left unmatched is randomly re-paired by `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()`, which `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` calls at :76523 immediately after the hash relink at :76515. **Every topology in this catalogue except the simple pair and the portal bank requires an unconditional re-assert at world load.** Put it in a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals or a one-shot after OnWorldReady, and note LoadChunks sets `DirtyPortalObjects = false` at :76527 so anything you write there needs `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.

THE CHEAPEST WRITE WINDOW is the moment right after world load and before any peer connects: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals has just done `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` on both ends of every relinked pair (:77880-77881), `m_peers` is empty so `Game.SetConnection`'s `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` test is always false and every write takes the immediate local path (:100641-100650), and ZDOs come back from `ZDO.Load` with `Owned = false; Owner = false` anyway (:74550-74556).

THE WRITE RECIPE, in order, for every managed edge: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — verbatim what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645. Ownership is not required for the write to land (no ZDO setter checks it; `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores its parameter entirely, :73648-73654) but is required to win the DataRevision race against the owning client, since `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` applies an incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher revision with no field-level merge (:77076-77139). `ZDO.SetConnection` already calls `IncreaseDataRevision()` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` for Portal-type writes (:73661-73664); a TAG-ONLY write does NOT, so a rename without an explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` is silently lost at the next world save because the entire ChunkPortal file is only emitted when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621-77635) and portals are explicitly excluded from ordinary chunk saves (:77572).

OWNERSHIP IS TRANSIENT. `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926, driven by ReleaseZDOS every 2 s, :76872-76883) hands any persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area (~96-112 m) to that peer. Portals are included because `ZDOMan.FindObjects` merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` back into every sector query (:77367-77382). A server ownership claim near a player is revoked within 2 s. The written VALUE survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd); only the next write must re-claim. For a hot loop, install the Wonderland `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix guard (Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313), fail fast on prefab hash, and never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`.

NEVER MOVE A PORTAL ZDO. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73756), so a repositioned portal stays filed in `m_portalObjects` under its creation-time sector forever: clients in the new zone never receive it through normal sector sync, `AddIfPortal` will double-file it if a position update arrives (:77738-77748), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up by the NEW sector index and fails to remove it (:76980-76987), leaking a dead ZDO that `GetPortalList()` and `Game.ConnectPortals()` keep processing forever. Destroy and recreate instead.

NEVER CACHE ZDO OBJECT REFERENCES ACROSS TICKS. `ZDOPool.Release`/`Get` recycles ZDO objects and `ZDO.Reset` sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` (:78286-78311, :73536-73545). Vanilla itself violates this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`, which holds raw ZDO references for a full 5 s and force-writes through them in `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690-100698). Cache ZDOIDs, re-resolve every tick with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)`. And never persist a ZDOID as portal identity: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552), so every ZDOID in the world is renumbered on every load. Key mod state by rounded POSITION, by a mod-private ZDO field (which travels with the ZDO for free), or by a world global key.

TWO-PHASE COMMIT / THE DEFERRED-WRITE TRAP. `Game.SetConnection` routes `RPC_SetConnection` to the owning peer when that peer is connected (:100646-100649), leaving the server's own copy reading the OLD value. Pass 2, in the same tick and over the same snapshot, then sees `!IsNone()` and skips the portal — so a retag or re-pair near a standing player takes two or more ticks, not one. `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` force-commits the previous tick's proposals at the top of the next call (:100591, :100690-100698), so the server always wins within one extra tick regardless of what the client does. If you re-implement pass 2 yourself, reproduce the `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard (:100609, :100671) or you will double-pair portals owned by online peers.

ENFORCEMENT TIERS, precisely. Of TeleportWorld.Teleport's four gates (:143517-143537), exactly ONE is server-enforced: gate 1, `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519) — a None connection, or a connection to a ZDO that does not resolve, blocks the transit on any client, modified or not, and does so SILENTLY (no player.Message on that path). Gates 2 and 3 read the server-owned global keys NoPortals / NoBossPortals and are client-HONOURED — and `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` have zero sender validation (:116022-116037) so any client can lift them. Gate 4 (`player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)`) is unreachable and un-influenceable per-portal: `m_allowAllItems` is a plain compiled Inspector field with no ZDO or RPC backing (:143429), as are `m_exitDistance` (:143413), `m_activationRange` (:143411) and every colour/effect reference. A server plugin writing them mutates a copy no client will ever read. The one documented escape is `ZNetView.LoadFields()` (:82669-82738, run from ZNetView.Awake), which reflects public instance fields off the ZDO under keys `"HasFields"`, `"HasFields<TypeName>"` and `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"` — untested for TeleportWorld and applied only at instantiation, so out of scope for topology work but noted.

THE DISPLAY/ROUTING ASYMMETRY worth exploiting. Routing compares the RAW s_tag with bare `string !=` (:100601, :100669). Display runs it through `RemoveRichTextTags()` — `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\\\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703, read directly) — at TeleportWorld.GetHoverText:143459. So `"base<f:red>"` hovers as `base` but is a distinct network from `"base"`. That single fact underwrites invisible sharding, per-player namespaces, faction networks and the server-enforced lockdown. Budget: the client's tag editor is capped at 10 characters (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`, :143482 → `m_inputField.characterLimit`, :61519) and pre-fills with the RAW tag (:143551-143554), so suffixes are visible in the edit box even though they are hidden in hover. RPC_SetTag itself applies no cap and no filter (:143587-143602), and `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the server build (:94588-94591).

TAG CHANGES ARE NOT RELIABLY OBSERVABLE BY RPC. `TeleportWorld.SetText` routes `RPC_SetTag` to the ZDO's current OWNER (`ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...)` → `m_zdo.GetOwner()`, :82855-82858), and `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83588-83594) — so a client that owns the portal retags it with zero packets on the wire. Worse, even when the packet does cross, a dedicated server can never dispatch it, because `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` (:83646-83663) and `m_instances` is permanently empty server-side. POLLING `s_tag` over `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` is mandatory; RPC interception at `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC`/`RPC_RoutedRPC` is a bonus that catches only the non-owner case. Note also the latent vanilla bug in RPC_SetTag: it calls `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` BEFORE re-reading the connection to hand to `SetConnectedPortal` (:143595-143597), so the old partner is usually never told and is repaired only by the next 5 s sweep.

ENUMERATION IS FREE. `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648-77656) returns every portal in the world in a fresh List, always resident — portals live in their own `m_portalObjects` dictionary and their own `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` save file, are removed from the ordinary sector array by `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752), and are never unloaded or released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883). `GetPortals()` (:77643-77646) returns the live dictionary, zero-alloc, for hot paths. `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021, filled in Game.Awake :100027-100032 from the Inspector list `m_portalPrefabs` :99828) is the authoritative "is this a portal" test and covers modded portal pieces for free — read it at runtime, never hard-code portal_wood/portal_stone. Prefab mixing is irrelevant to pairing: ConnectPortals never looks at the prefab, so wood, stone and modded portals pair freely inside one tag group.

THE PLAYER-EXPERIENCE CONSTANTS that shape every design: the destination is re-read at the instant of transit and never cached (:143539), so a server repoint applies to the very next walk-in; but `TargetFound()` requires the traveller's client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO and calls `RequestZDO` and returns false if not (:143646-143654), so the first walk-through after a re-pair to an unvisited region silently fails with NO message — pre-push with `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerID, targetId)` (:77714-77725). `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` is ENTER-ONLY (:143672-143681), so a player already standing in a portal's volume when it is repointed does not re-trigger. `Player.TeleportTo` refuses within 2 s of a previous teleport (:15302-15327) and `distantTeleport:true` — which portals always pass (:143546) — has a hard ~8 s black-screen floor plus an `IsAreaReady` gate and a 15 s force-land fallback (:15349-15366). Exit position is `targetPos + targetRot*forward*m_exitDistance + up*1.0`, where m_exitDistance is the DESTINATION portal's compiled 1.0 (:143542-143545, :143413). The hover text distinguishes only connected/unconnected (:143461) and the hover NAME is the hard-coded literal "Teleport" (:143466-143469).

WHAT THE SERVER CAN TELL THE PLAYER, since none of this shows up in the portal UI: a HUD toast via the per-character routed RPC "Message" (`ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)type, text, 0)`, Player.RPC_Message :14820-14825 — Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs); a global `"ShowMessage"` (MessageHud :55808, :55848); a SAVED, NAMED map pin via `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered on every peer at Game.Start :100068, handler :100823-100831, client Minimap.DiscoverLocation → AddPin(save:true)); floating world text via `"RPC_DamageText"` (:46352-46356, :46494-46510, 30 m cull); a VFX/SFX one-shot via `"SpawnObject"` (ZNetScene :81954, :82355-82366 — effect prefabs ONLY, never a ZNetView prefab); and server-written sign text (`ZDOVars.s_text` :78629, Sign repaints on a 2 s InvokeRepeating keyed on DataRevision, :141835-141865). What the player can tell the SERVER: a map ping, which is `Chat.SendPing` → routed `"ChatMessage"` at targetPeerID 0 carrying the clicked world Vector3 (:42058-42068) and therefore always reaches the server even solo; or an emote, polled off the character ZDO's `ZDOVars.s_emoteID`/`s_emote` (:78417-78419). Ordinary chat text is NOT a channel — `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each other listed player individually (:41975-42043), so a lone player generates zero packets, and unknown slash commands are swallowed locally by `Terminal.TryRunCommand(silentFail:true)` (:41947-41955).
