gaps.why: The zdo brief states a fabricated portal 'needs no health/creator/support fields to instantiate correctly' — true for instantiation, wrong for survival; no option models the support pass at all.

gaps.gap: Unlisted server→client output RPCs and their UX value. (1) `SleepStart`/`SleepStop` (Game.Start :100063-100064; handlers :100752-100769) → `Player.SetSleeping(true/false)` (:15992-16005): a server-forced full-screen sleep fade on ALL clients, with a '$msg_goodmorning' message and a Rested buff on wake — a global blackout primitive for the Blackout Swap Protocol (caveat: SetSleeping(true) also blocks AttachStop). (2) `RPC_SetDreamCinematic(string)` (CinematicsManager :42373, :42616-42623) queues a video cinematic to play on every client's next sleep. (3) `ZSyncAnimation` `SetTrigger` invoked BY the server at the character owner plays any animator trigger on that player's body for everyone (the UX brief covers only the client→server direction, :87260). (4) `PrivateArea` `FlashShield` (:137202) is a no-arg ZDO RPC the server can fire at any ward's owner to pulse its dome. (5) `TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal` fires the `m_connected` EffectList on the rising edge of `HaveTarget()` (:143495-143503) — flipping a connection None→X on the server plays vanilla's own 'portal connected' burst on every nearby client for free. (6) `RPC_RegisterKill` (:100069, :100837-100862) writes kill/boss stats and platform achievements into the target player's local profile — an accidental achievement-injection primitive that must be listed as 'never use'. Option spec: fold into the feedback stack with the honest tier (all client-honoured).
gaps.why: The UX brief enumerated eight output channels and missed six vanilla RPCs, two of which (SleepStart, the m_connected effect) are the only global-blackout and portal-local VFX signals that need no prefab-hash guessing.

gaps.gap: `RandEventSystem` writes were never examined — only reads. `RandEventSystem.instance.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos)` (public, :107067-107071) is server-authoritative and broadcast by `SendCurrentRandomEvent` via the `SetEvent` routed RPC (:106952-106978); clients then show `m_startMessage`, force `m_forceMusic`/`m_forceEnvironment` inside `m_eventRange` (RandomEvent fields :107435-107494), draw an EventArea pin of `m_eventRange*2` (client Minimap :57474-57500) and run the event's spawners. The server can therefore START a raid at a portal (a hazard/announcement at a locked gate), and, combined with `NoBossPortals`, MUST correct the catalog's boss-gate model: `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s check at :143528 calls `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()`, which is `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent` (:106939-106949) — a per-CLIENT HUD lookup (boss within EnemyHud range and shown), NOT the world random event; only the `activeBosses` float key is world-wide. Option spec: 'Raid Beacon' (server-started event at a managed gate during lockdown, with the event's own pin/music/message as the announcement) and a corrected Boss Auto-Lockdown that stops describing GetBossEvent as global.
gaps.why: The lockdown and routing options treat raids purely as inputs and the globalkeys brief mis-describes the NoBossPortals gate as 'RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null OR activeBosses>0 → world-wide', which will produce a wrong blackout-radius model.

gaps.gap: Three unauthenticated non-portal RPCs a client can use to attack any portal policy, absent from Ungated RPC Hardening: (1) `PersistentEventSystem.RPC_RequestStartEvent(sender, int)` and `RPC_RequestStopEvent` (:105341-105389) execute on the server with no sender check — any client can make the server spawn event locations (`SpawnLocationMidGame`) and objects (`Object.Instantiate` server-side) anywhere within the event's placement rules, or kill live events; (2) `RPC_UpdateClientEventsList(sender, json)` (:105412-105418) is applied by any NON-server recipient, so a client can broadcast a forged event list to every other client (fake map pins, fake weather) via the server relay; (3) `Ship.RPC_Forward/Backward/Stop/Rudder` (:140482-140485, bodies :140538-140575) set state on whatever machine receives them with no owner or sender check, so any client can steer any ship whose owner is another player. Add all three to the `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix's veto table alongside SetGlobalKey/RPC_SetConnection/DestroyZDO/RequestZDO.
gaps.why: The access domain's hardening list was built from the privatearea brief's routed-RPC census, which never opened the PersistentEventSystem handlers and did not consider ZDO RPCs that lack an IsOwner gate on the receiving side.

gaps.gap: `EffectArea.Type.Teleport` and `Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea` — a vanilla portal-placement gate nobody identified. `EffectArea.Type` is a byte flags enum {Heat, Fire, PlayerBase, Burning, Teleport=0x10, NoMonsters, WarmCozyArea, PrivateProperty} (:124062-124073); `Player.UpdatePlacementGhost` refuses any piece with `m_onlyInTeleportArea` (:136153) unless `EffectArea.IsPointInsideArea(point, Type.Teleport)` (:13349-13352, status NoTeleportArea → '$msg_noteleportarea' :12461-12462). Which piece(s) set `m_onlyInTeleportArea` and which prefab carries an `EffectArea` of type Teleport are Inspector data (candidates: the Ashlands/Deep North portal variants, or a location-only 'portal pad'); if a portal variant is gated this way, then (a) the per-player cap / placement options must account for a vanilla placement restriction they do not know about, and (b) a server-fabricated LocationProxy for the location that carries the Teleport EffectArea (see the structures gap) would let vanilla clients build that portal variant anywhere — a client-honoured 'unlock placement here' lever. Also relevant: fabricated locations carrying `NoMonsters`/`PlayerBase`/`WarmCozyArea` EffectAreas give spawn-free, base-flagged, comfort-bearing pads around a hub. In-game check: dump every prefab in `ZNetScene.m_prefabs` with a Piece whose `m_onlyInTeleportArea` is true and every EffectArea whose `m_type` has the Teleport bit.
gaps.why: The wildcard 'Ashlands Stone Portal' option asserts 'no code difference between portal variants … none of it network-reachable' without having found the one placement-gating mechanism in the assembly that mentions teleporting by name.

gaps.gap: Server-driven vehicles as a transport primitive, and the real limits of moving a ship with riders. `ShipControlls`/`Ship` are steered by ZDO-targeted RPCs the server can send to the ship's OWNER: `Forward`/`Backward`/`Stop`/`Rudder(float)` (:140482-140485) — an autopilot ferry that moves a whole crew without any teleport, cooldown or black screen, and is a genuine 'portal alternative' for the ship-as-destination case every brief declared physically impossible. Separately, a server that pins ownership of a ship (WaterBuoyancyEngine SetOwner-block pattern) and writes its ZDO position makes non-owning clients lerp 20 %/tick or hard-snap when >5 m (ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition :87700-87724), and a rider standing on a ship their client does not own is re-glued to `m_lastAttachBody.TransformPoint(m_lastAttachPos)` ONLY while the correction is <4 m (Character.UpdateMotion :2118-2135; >4 m clears the attach and drops them in the water). So incremental server-driven ship motion (<4 m per physics tick) carries passengers; a long jump does not. Option spec: 'Ferry Route' (server steers an unattended vanilla ship between docks by RPC; timetable + `s_user` helmsman check) and a corrected 'Player's Ship' option that names the 4 m attach limit.
gaps.why: Both ship-related options stop at 'you land in the water behind the boat'; the steering RPC surface and the attach-correction limit that decide whether a server can MOVE a boat with people on it were never read.

gaps.gap: Removable server-controlled map surfaces exist and the catalog says they do not. Beyond `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` (permanent) and `LocationIcons` (unlabelled), a vanilla client renders and later REMOVES: (1) per-persistent-event pins — an EventArea circle sized `radius*2` plus an animated double-size RandomEvent pin labelled with the localized `mapTokenString` (client Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57505-57545, removal :57530-57544); (2) the random-event area pin `m_randEventAreaPin` sized `m_eventRange*2*0.9` (:57474-57500), removed when the event ends. Both are driven by server-authoritative state (PersistentEventSystem JSON broadcast :105407; RandEventSystem `SetEvent` :106952). Labels are per-event-type Inspector tokens, not free text; position and radius are free. Option spec: 'Live Portal Markers' — one persistent-event entry per managed hub (label = the event type's token), removed when the hub is retired; document the fixed-label limitation and the weather side effect.
gaps.why: The UX brief's map-pin option and the wildcard 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces' option both state there is no way to remove a server-pushed marker, which is false and shapes the whole 'pins are one-shot' design stance.

gaps.gap: Economy-side vanilla RPCs the server can send to a station's OWNER to credit or debit world objects were not enumerated: `Fireplace` `AddFuel` (used by the Charge Cells option only as a read), `Smelter` `AddOre`, `CookingStation`/`Fermenter`/`Beehive` add-item RPCs, and `Door` state (`ZDOVars.s_state` 0/1/-1, Door :123781-123949) as a three-state physical switch. Each is a ZNetView RPC with an `IsOwner` gate on the receiving client, so the server can drive it exactly the way it drives `RPC_SetConnection`. Option spec: 'Refund and Credit Primitives' — pay a toll refund by `AddFuel`/`AddOre` at the player's own station rather than by dropping items on the ground (ItemDrop.DropItem is the only credit path the economy brief names), and 'Door Lever' as a fourth cheap input channel next to item stands and signs.
gaps.why: The economy domain's credit path is limited to ground drops and chest blobs; the owner-executed station RPCs are cheaper, tamper-safe (owner gate) and were never listed.

unverifiedClaims: globalkeys brief / Boss Auto-Lockdown option: 'NoBossPortals is a WORLD-WIDE blackout … RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null OR activeBosses > 0'. Verified against assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106939-106949: GetBossEvent() returns EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent — a per-client HUD lookup — so only the activeBosses key is world-wide; the GetBossEvent half is local to each traveller's screen.

privatearea brief routed-RPC census: the four registrations at :105284-105287 are described as 'the RandEventSystem event RPCs'. They are PersistentEventSystem's s_updateClientEventsList / s_requestActiveEventsList / s_requestStartEvent / s_requestStopEvent; RandEventSystem's only routed RPC is 'SetEvent' at :106781. The census also omits that RPC_RequestStartEvent/StopEvent run on the server with no sender check.

ops catalog option 'Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand' is marked ruled-out, but Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45741-45744) forwards any RemoteCommand-flagged command from a vanilla client when IsValid fails, RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879-81889) is admin-gated and runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand, and Console is instantiated headless (Game.Awake :100038-100041). A server-side prefix on TryRunCommand keyed on 'removekey tpl …' makes it a working channel.

zdo-connection brief: 'A server-fabricated portal ZDO needs no health/creator/support fields to instantiate correctly'. Instantiation yes; survival no — WearNTear.UpdateWear (:149662-149707) with m_noSupportWear (default true :149205) applies 100 damage per update when !HaveSupport() on the owning client, so unsupported phantoms are demolished. Needs an in-game check of the portal prefab's WearNTear settings.

codebase brief: 'SectorSubscription's CreateSyncList postfix is useless to a ZERO-CLIENT Lite (vanilla clients never send the request RPC)'. The postfix can be driven purely by server-side policy (append the destination sector for any peer near a managed portal); no client request is required.

zdo-connection / ops briefs: 'a tag-only write is silently lost unless the mod calls SetDirtyPortals' — correct, but the same is true of CLIENT-originated tag edits: RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139) → AddIfPortal early-returns for an existing portal (:77739-77742) without dirtying; vanilla is rescued only when Game.ConnectPortals happens to write a connection afterwards.

targeted brief: LocationInstance.m_position.y 'already carries a procedurally-valid ground height'. True for world-gen-placed instances; ZoneSystem.SpawnLocationMidGame (:115079-115102) sets pos.y = GetGroundHeight(pos), a raycast that is dead on the server, so mid-game-registered instances keep the caller's y until placement re-resolves it in the ghost zone (and in an already-generated zone they are never placed at all: SpawnZone :114084-114091).

routing brief 'World-State Conditional Routing (… Weather)' and the wildcard notes treat weather as a read-only, heavily caveated input. PersistentEventSystem.PersistentEvent.environmentOverride + GetEnvironmentOverride (client EnvMan :96299-96303) gives the server a localized weather override inside any radius it chooses, subject to the event type's Inspector data.

ux brief and wildcard 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces': 'no way ever to remove a pushed map pin'. Persistent-event pins (client Minimap :57505-57545) and the random-event area pin (:57474-57500) are server-driven and removed when the server drops the event.

wildcard 'The Ashlands Stone Portal': 'every behavioural difference is Inspector data … none of it is network-reachable'. Unverified against Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea (:136153) / EffectArea.Type.Teleport (:124068) placement gating at :13349-13352; which prefabs use it is unknown and may be a portal variant.

access brief claim (c) 'ZDO.Deserialize does not wipe fields absent from an incoming packet' — CONFIRMED this pass (ZDO.Deserialize :74205-74240 calls only ZDOExtraData.Add via ZDODataHelper.ReadData :74718-74730; no Release/Reset); corollary that mod keys can never be deleted from a peer stands.

prior-review item 'ZNetView.Awake corrects Type/Distant when owner' — confirmed (:82580-82587); Persistent is never corrected from an existing ZDO (only set on the create path :82615), so a server-set Persistent=true on a fabricated ZDO survives client ownership.

zdo-connection brief: 'Portals sync to nearby clients normally … subject to ReleaseNearbyZDOS' — correct, but the digest's implicit assumption that ZDO.Distant could widen delivery is wrong for portals: FindDistantObjects (:77383-77401) reads only m_objectsBySector, never m_portalObjects.
critics.structuralCritique: The twelve briefs were organised around the portal component, the ZDO connection slot, global keys and the RPC relay — i.e. around the OBJECT a player walks into — and treated the world around it as static, read-only data (WorldGenerator math, m_locationInstances, biome grids). That framing systematically missed the server-authoritative subsystems that CONSTRUCT places: ZoneSystem's ghost generation and `m_generatedZones` (clients never generate anything; the server decides what exists in every zone), the location pipeline (`RegisterLocation`/`SpawnLocationMidGame`/`SpawnLocation(Full)`/`LocationProxy` — one ZDO conjures an entire vanilla structure plus a client-honoured no-build ring), `TerrainComp` (`s_TCData`, the only server-writable geometry in the game), and `PersistentEventSystem` (a persisted, radius-bearing, JSON-broadcast world-state channel with removable labelled map pins, localized weather and event-gated spawns/wear). Because of that blind spot the catalog repeatedly 'rules out' or caveats things vanilla already provides: removable map markers, server-controlled weather, arrival-site preparation, and the admin text channel (the piggyback on remote-flagged console commands). A second systematic error: RPC analysis was done in one direction only. The briefs correctly proved that client→server ZDO-targeted RPCs never dispatch on a dedicated server, then never asked what the SERVER can send to a client that DOES hold the instance — so TeleportWorld's own `RPC_SetTag`/`RPC_SetConnected`, ship steering, `FlashShield`, `SetTrigger`, `SleepStart`, station `AddFuel`-style RPCs and the whole 'owner-executed delegation' pattern that `Game.RPC_SetConnection` already models were left out, and the access domain was built on 'overwrite and fight' instead of 'instruct the owner'. Third, the routed-RPC census was copied between briefs without being opened: four PersistentEventSystem handlers are mislabelled and never read, two of them sender-ungated server-executing spawners. Fourth, persistence was examined only for MOD writes; the interaction of vanilla client edits with `DirtyPortalObjects`, and of phantom objects with WearNTear support and vegetation generation, was never traced, so several 'feasible' options have silent world-state failure modes. Finally, several catalog entries contradict the domain notes written for them (the ops admin-channel entry is ruled-out while its own notes say the RPC works; the boss-gate blackout radius is described as world-wide while the code is per-client HUD), which suggests options were finalised before the notes were reconciled against the decompile.

gaps.gap: Per-peer ZDO withholding (sync-list filtering) as a server-ENFORCED per-player portal gate. Mechanism: the ONLY ways a portal ZDO reaches a client are ZDOMan.CreateSyncList (private, :77212-77241 — FindSectorObjects near peer.m_refPos then peer.ShouldSend) plus the force-send queue drained by AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77287, also gated on peer.ShouldSend) and RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692, GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO). A Harmony postfix on CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer peer, List<ZDO> toSync) that removes portal ZDOs (and their partner/anchor ZDOs) the peer's socket-verified account is not permitted to hold, plus a veto of RequestZDO for those ids in the ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix, means the non-member client never receives the ZDO: no mesh, no TeleportWorldTrigger, and — if the withheld ZDO is the DESTINATION — TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143646-143654) is false forever so gate 1 of Teleport (:143519) refuses silently while the source still hovers '[Connected]'. A modified client cannot obtain the ZDO from any other source (clients never relay ZDOs to each other; RouteRPC on the server forwards RPCs only, :83597-83629). Revocation mid-session: invoke the routed 'DestroyZDO' RPC (registered on every client at :76155) TARGETED at that one peer with a ZPackage of the ids — the client's RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO removes it locally; the m_deadZDOs resurrection block is IsServer()-only (:76994-76998) so re-grant later works, but the server's ZDOPeer.m_zdos cache must be cleared for that id or ShouldSend stays false. Verified caveat: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) assigns ownership to any nearby peer WITHOUT checking peer.m_zdos, so a withheld portal near a non-member becomes 'owned' by a client that has no copy — Game.RPC_SetConnection on that client no-ops on GetZDO==null (:100653-100662) and RPC_SetTag from a member is dropped — so withheld portals must be ownership-pinned to the server (SetOwner prefix + SetOwnerInternal guard). This single mechanism falsifies 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', 'Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing — RULED OUT' (withholding is not divergence: nothing reconverges) and the economy domain's 'should THIS PLAYER pass — impossible for four reasons'. In-game check: withhold one portal from peer B, confirm B sees nothing at the site, confirm B's partner-side portal hovers connected but never teleports, confirm A still transits normally.
gaps.why: The catalog's entire enforcement taxonomy rests on 'one ZDO object, every peer reconverges' — but the server decides what each peer is SENT, and the vanilla client has no other source. Every private-network, faction, admin-only-infrastructure and per-player-lock feature is currently marked reactive or impossible when a genuinely enforced form exists.

gaps.gap: Tame and cart follow-through (moving non-portal persistent ZDOs across a transit). Vanilla tames and carts cannot use portals; this is the most-requested portal feature after ore (TamesPatch in TortalPortal, 'Teleport Wolves', 'CartPortal'). Server-only version: on a detected transit (PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit) enumerate creature ZDOs within N m of the SOURCE whose ZDOVars.s_tamed is true and whose s_follow string (:78429, written by Tameable.RPC_Command :19444/:19457) equals the traveller's s_playerName, plus Vagon ZDOs within reach (Vagon has a Container field, :147342+21, so cargo rides along in s_items). For each: wait until no peer's active area covers it (ReleaseNearbyZDOS will release owner to 0 within 2 s once the traveller has left), then SetOwner(GetSessionID()), SetPosition(destination + offset), ForceSendZDO. Unlike portals, ZDO.SetSector for a non-portal prefab DOES re-file the ZDO (:73752-73768: RemoveFromSector/AddToSector + ZDOSectorInvalidated, which per-peer drops it from m_zdos when outside their area, :75989-75996) so sector sync delivers it at the new location, and the arriving client's Tameable.UpdateSavedFollowTarget (:19478-19497) re-attaches the follow by name via Player.GetAllPlayers on that client. Caveats: only when the source zone is unloaded by everyone (a second player standing at the source keeps ownership and the client's ZSyncTransform overwrites the position — 5 m snap :87715); creatures with ZSyncTransform pop rather than walk; the traveller must be the only same-named player. Must specify: radius, max followers, unsummon/boss exclusions, what happens to a cart mid-pull (s_attachJointHash bool :147661).
gaps.why: Not one of 197 options touches creatures or vehicles as things that travel, despite it being a top-3 request for every portal mod and despite the mechanism (non-portal ZDO relocation) being cleanly distinct from the ruled-out 'move the portal' case.

gaps.gap: Destination pre-generation via ghost-zone spawning at the TARGET. ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones is private (:113971-113992) and only ever runs at peer.GetRefPos() (:113937), which is why the targeted domain concedes 'an unvisited corner has a LocationInstance but no altar/trader ZDO'. The server can call the publicized ZoneSystem.SpawnZone(zone, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _) (:114071) for the destination zone and its neighbours itself, materialising LocationProxy, OfferingBowl-parent, Trader and DungeonGenerator ZDOs (with s_roomData) before any player arrives — turning 'boss altar', 'trader', 'crypt room' targets from 'sometimes' into 'always', and letting the Destination Safety Validator check real placed objects instead of pre-flattening heights. Also fixes m_iconPlaced traders never appearing on LocationIcons. Caveats: SpawnZone instantiates and destroys real GameObjects on the server main thread (:114085-114102) — budget one zone per tick; requires ZoneSystem.IsZoneGenerated check first; interacts with the sector-0 clamp for out-of-range coordinates.
gaps.why: Every 'portal to X location' option is currently gated on a player having wandered near X first; this is the one call that removes the dependency and nobody proposed it.

gaps.gap: Delivery-guarantee engine: join-time portal broadcast + destination pre-streaming. Verified: a joining peer receives only ZDOs near its refPos (CreateSyncList :77212-77241) — there is NO vanilla 'send all portals on join' path (ZDOMan.AddPeer :76767-76773 only registers ZDOData). So every far portal ZDO is absent until RequestZDO, which is exactly the silent first-transit failure the digest names ten times as a gotcha and solves nowhere. Option: (a) on PeerJoinLeaveHook join, ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, id) for every id in GetPortalList() plus every managed anchor — ShouldSend is true for never-seen ZDOs so it always lands, cost is O(portals) small packets once; (b) on every route write, ForceSendZDO(peer, destId) to every peer within activation range of the source; (c) a CreateSyncList postfix that appends the destination zone's ZDOs (FindSectorObjects at the target) for any peer standing within 12 m of a managed portal — the SectorSubscription mechanism from TortalPortal/SectorSubscription.cs:106 but server-initiated, so a vanilla client already holds the arrival area and Player.UpdateTeleport's IsAreaReady gate (:15349) clears at the 8 s floor instead of stalling toward the 15 s fallback. Caveat: AddForceSendZdos is ShouldSend-gated (:77273) — force-send is distance-independent but NOT revision-independent.
gaps.why: The catalog treats the missing-destination-ZDO failure as an unavoidable tax on every dynamic feature; it is a fixable delivery problem with three cheap, verifiable mechanisms.

gaps.gap: Untagged-portal auto-pair suppression. ZDO.GetString(s_tag) defaults to '' (:75079-75082) so every freshly placed, never-named portal in the world is one tag group and Game.ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100607-100622) links it to a RANDOM untagged portal anywhere — a stranger's base, an admin hub — within 5 s of placement. Popular request ('new portals should not connect until named'). Server-enforced fix at the arrival hook (CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfix, SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58): if s_tag == '' write a unique invisible tag ('<' + rounded position hash + '>', stripped from hover by RemoveRichTextTags assembly_utils_SERVER:6700 but distinct for pairing) plus SetDirtyPortals(); the Tag Watchdog reverts to '' → unique on any later clear. Must also handle the load-time case (portals loaded with '' from ChunkPortal, :76474-76482) before the synchronous Game.ConnectPortals at :76523. Caveat: the player's rename box pre-fills with the raw tag (:143551, :61519) so the suffix must be ≤10 chars or the client truncates it on save.
gaps.why: Anti-Grief Tag Integrity covers squatting and near-duplicates but not the '' group, which is the single most common accidental cross-base link on any real server.

gaps.gap: Presence-conditioned routes: routes that are wired only while the builder (s_creator :78393 == s_playerID :78539 of a ready peer) or a member of the route's network is ONLINE, or only while nobody from the network is online (the inverse: offline-raid protection — no one can portal INTO a base whose owners are all logged out). Pure 'should this ROUTE be open' predicate over ZNet.GetPeers()/ConnectedCharacters.All(), so server-enforced at the connection layer; combine with the Customs House decoy so the gate still glows. Variant: owner-nearby (builder within N m of either end) for 'escort-only' gates. Needs the join/leave hooks (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:26/:48) as edge triggers and a reconcile tick as the truth.
gaps.why: Debtor's Lien proved that per-player rules become enforceable when re-expressed over property; presence is the most obvious such predicate for PvP servers and it is absent.

gaps.gap: Placement policy engine at the ZDO arrival hook, with ground-drop refund. The catalog only uses the CreateNewZDO+Deserialize pair (SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58, verified :76684/:76929) for a numeric per-player cap. Popular server rules it can equally enforce, all as pure geometry/ZDO reads at Deserialize time: minimum spacing between portals (GetPortalList distance), biome bans (WorldGenerator.GetBiome :151725 — e.g. no Ashlands portals), no portals within N m of world spawn (GetLocationIcon('StartTemple')), no portals outside a ward the placer is permitted on (Shadow Ward Index), no portals in interiors (y > 3000), no portals within N m of another player's wards. Rejection = SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO. Refund: the server cannot touch the placer's inventory, but ItemDrop.DropItem(itemData, amount, pos, rot) with m_dropPrefab set by hand (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:218 pattern) drops the recipe cost on the ground at the site — reading the recipe from ObjectDB.instance.GetRecipe on the server (retry until ObjectDB resolves). Toast the reason via PlayerNotify.
gaps.why: Placement rules are the second most common admin request after caps and the hook already exists; nobody generalised the cap into a policy engine or addressed the material-loss complaint a destroy-on-arrival produces.

gaps.gap: Consent-handshake player-to-player teleport (TPA/summon) and emote warp verbs with no portal involved. Popular mods: 'TPA', '/home', '/back', '/spawn'. Server-only shape: requester performs emote X while their s_lookTarget (:78677, written every 0.2 s by CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation :5041-5081) points within a cone at another connected character — the server records a pending request keyed on both s_playerIDs and toasts the target; the target performs emote Y within 30 s to accept; the server sends RPC_TeleportPlayer/RPC_TeleportTo (distant:true) to the requester at the target's live ZDO position. Verbs: 'home' = nearest bed with s_owner == playerID; 'back' = the server's own pre-teleport position ledger (the only party that can implement /back, since the client never networks its own history); 'spawn' = GetLocationIcon('StartTemple'). All must respect the 2 s cooldown (:15309-15316), s_dead (:78403), s_inBed (:78457), and bypass every vanilla gate (so ore travels — say so). No 'accept' is possible via chat; emote-only.
gaps.why: The catalog uses RPC_TeleportPlayer only as a portal delivery mechanism; the portal-less warp/summon family that every server-admin mod ships is entirely missing, and the consent handshake is a novel use of s_lookTarget.

gaps.gap: Per-peer LocationIcons payload: per-player respawn override and per-player landmark reveal. ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons(long peer) is per-peer (:113581-113593) and the client's RPC_LocationIcons REPLACES its whole m_locationIcons dictionary (:113595-113607). Client Game.FindSpawnPoint falls through to GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation) whenever there is no logout point and no custom spawn point (verified in the client decompile: logout → bed → StartTemple → zero) — so sending peer B a payload whose 'StartTemple' entry is the faction hall makes B's NEW characters and bed-less deaths respawn there, on a vanilla client, with no other peer affected. Same payload controls which boss-altar/trader icons B's map shows (hide undiscovered altars, reveal a faction's private hub as a 'Vendor' icon). Requirements: prefix SendLocationIcons to substitute the per-peer dictionary (the PlaceLocations re-broadcast at :115000-115003 and OnNewPeer :113609 would otherwise reset it), keep names inside the client's Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list, and note that a custom bed spawn always wins.
gaps.why: 'World Spawn / Start Temple' mentions in passing that the server can relocate the world spawn; nobody noticed the channel is per-peer, which makes it the one place a vanilla client's RESPAWN is per-player server-controlled.

gaps.gap: Fast-transit mode (skip the 8 s hold). Portals always pass distantTeleport:true (:143546) and the traveller is pinned for ≥8 s (:15349). A two-hop relay whose second hop sends RPC_TeleportTo with distantTeleport:false completes at t≈2 s once IsAreaReady (:15337-15352), reproducing the 'Fast Portals / Portal Stations' feel — but only if the destination area is already held by the client (delivery-guarantee engine) and FindFloor succeeds, otherwise UpdateTeleport reverts the player to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' (:15369-15374). Spec must define: pre-stream trigger radius, fallback to distant:true when the destination zone was never generated (SpawnZone ghost first), and the fact that no swirl animation plays (Hud keys the swirl on m_distantTeleport, :47872).
gaps.why: Instant portals are a headline feature of several popular mods; the catalog only warns against distant:false rather than designing the conditions under which it is safe.

gaps.gap: Arrival-triggered world events. RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos) is public and the event system is server-driven (IsServer gates at :105343-105414, :106791-106805). On a detected transit (or on a route being opened) the server can start a raid at the arrival point ('ambush gate'), or at the SOURCE when a lockdown is violated. Combine with the Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction so the gate that summoned the raid also closes. Caveat: reactive (~2 s late), and the event radius/duration are Inspector data on the RandomEvent asset; must not fire inside boss-alerted areas because of the activeBosses leak (:27256-27261).
gaps.why: The catalog reads event state as an input to routing but never treats routing as a trigger for events, which is the mechanism behind every 'cursed portal' / 'dungeon-of-the-day with a welcoming party' design.

gaps.gap: Post-transit status effects (portal sickness / arrival buff). 'Portal Sickness' is a widely-used mod. Server-only: on PositionWatch transit detection, StatusEffectRpc.Grant (Wonderland StatusEffectRpc.cs:27, SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect :28823) a vanilla effect on the traveller's character ZDO — Wet/Cold/Burning as a penalty, Rested as a reward — with a per-player cooldown so re-ping loops (BuffRosterEngine pattern) make it last N minutes. Honest classification: reactive, ~2 s after the move, cannot be removed early (no RemoveStatusEffect RPC exists anywhere), and only vanilla effect assets. Also the only server-side way to express 'portal cooldown per player' visibly, since the route-level cooldown option closes the gate for everyone.
gaps.why: The economy domain has route cooldowns and the ux domain has status effects as feedback, but nobody composed them into the per-player consequence that players actually recognise from existing mods.

gaps.gap: Ownership transfer and orphan adoption by rewriting s_creator/s_creatorIndex. Piece.Awake reads s_creator/s_creatorIndex from the ZDO on every client (:136246-136250) and Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator()==0 (:136417), so a server write of s_creator (no setter checks ownership, :73648) permanently reassigns 'built by' as every vanilla client sees it — the basis for 'transfer this gate to player X', 'adopt admin-spawned portals (creator 0) to a maintenance account', and 'reassign a departed player's portals to a guild'. Cross-check against ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396) so s_creatorIndex stays consistent. Needs SetDirtyPortals(). Caveat: this also flips ward IsCreator semantics on wards themselves if applied to guard stones — scope to portal prefabs.
gaps.why: Every access option treats s_creator as read-only evidence; it is also the writable lever for the ownership-management features (transfer, adopt, reclaim) that admins ask for constantly.

gaps.gap: Portal sanctuary — spawn suppression around portals. SpawnGovernor already destroys creature ZDOs on arrival (SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70); a portal-specific rule 'no hostile creature ZDO may appear within N m of any portal in GetPortalList()' (or of managed hubs only) makes arrival points safe without wards. Server-enforced at the ZDO layer (creature ZDOs are client-spawned and arrive via ZDOData). Must exclude tames (s_tamed) and player-summoned creatures, and budget per tick.
gaps.why: Safe arrival is a standard 'portal hub' feature and the hook is already shipped in the sibling mod; nothing in lockdown/safety addresses creatures at the destination.

gaps.gap: Character-ZDO-bit predicates for approach-triggered routing: s_pvp (:78551), s_crowned (:78399), s_inBed, s_dead, equipped-item hashes, s_stealth. Example: an arena gate whose destination is parked unless every player within the arming radius has s_pvp true — the only way to keep non-PvP players out of a PvP zone on a vanilla client. Example: a 'no armour' challenge gate that parks when the approaching player's s_chestItem != 0. All are JIT variants (write before the trigger, ~2 s lead) and inherit JIT's two-player contention problem; spec them as predicates on the existing JIT option rather than as new gates.
gaps.why: The JIT option only uses position; the character ZDO carries a dozen server-readable bits that turn 'who is approaching' into 'what state are they in', which is what PvP/challenge servers actually want to gate on.

gaps.gap: Auto corpse-run gate. On tombstone creation (TombStone ZDO with s_owner/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint, :19732-19740, :19845-19853) fabricate an ephemeral phantom portal at the player's bed (s_owner match) or the hub, pointed at a Void Anchor 2 m from the tombstone, tagged with an invisible per-player suffix so only that pairing exists, and destroy both when the tombstone despawns (TombStone.UpdateDespawn :19875-19890) or after a TTL. Composes Ephemeral Event Gates + Tombstone target + Anchor, but the lifecycle (death → gate → pickup → cleanup) is not specified anywhere.
gaps.why: Corpse-recovery is one of the most-installed QoL portal features and the pieces exist in three different domains without a composed spec.

gaps.gap: On-join briefing and login-time state push. PeerJoinLeaveHook (Wonderland) fires on RPC_PeerInfo; nothing in the catalog uses the join event as a lifecycle hook for portals. Spec: at join (after the character ZDO appears and s_playerID is non-zero), toast the player's own portal count and orphaned tags, re-push idempotent map pins for their own portals (HaveSimilarPin dedups, client :58363-58374), force-send all managed anchors (gap above), and — for admins by socket host name — a health summary. Also the correct place to seed per-player state (last-seen for lease/GC engines keyed on PlatformUserID, since m_playerHistory carries no timestamp).
gaps.why: Several ops/economy options quietly need a 'last seen' ledger and a per-player state seed, and the catalog never names the event that provides it.

unverifiedClaims: 'Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World' (wildcard): that a ZDO beyond ±16.4 km lands in the same bucket as the server's pinned reference position AND gets instantiated server-side. ZDO.SetSector does route OutsideZones ZDOs to ZoneSystem.SectorZero (:73758), but whether ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted on the server actually passes IsActiveAreaLoaded at (1e6,0,1e6) and instantiates sector-0 ZDOs was not read; treat as needs-ingame-check, not feasible.

'The Void Anchor' claim that prefab hash 0 makes ZNetScene.CreateObject return null silently (:81996-82002) while an unknown non-zero hash logs every frame, and that ZDO's default m_prefab is -1 not 0 — not independently verified this pass; every anchor option depends on it.

ZNetView.LoadFields on vanilla-shipped portal prefabs: whether the client's LoadFields gate is zdo.GetBool('HasFields') alone or also requires prefab-side state, whether the HasFields* keys survive the owning client's own ZDO pushes (Deserialize is additive, so probably yes) and a save/load round-trip, and whether TeleportWorld is reached by GetComponentsInChildren. 'The Ore Gate' and 'Field Injection' are unproven until one in-game test.

Ops 'Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand' is marked ruled-out while the ops domain notes assert Console.instance IS non-null on a dedicated server (Game.Awake :100038-100041) and RPC_RemoteCommand is a working admin-gated channel. The catalog contradicts itself; one of the two is wrong and the in-game check (send a registered onlyServer/remoteCommand command from an admin client's F5 console) has not been run.
Whether an HttpListener (ops HTTP endpoint) works under the dedicated server's Mono runtime and BepInEx sandbox; never checked.

Whether Chat.instance / MessageHud.instance / Minimap.instance exist on the dedicated server. Evidence is contradictory (Game.UpdateSaving guards MessageHud at :100474; ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer dereferences it unguarded under IsDedicated at :80258). This decides whether a server-side ZRoutedRpc.Register('ChatMessage') throws and whether WorldSaveFinished ever fires.
The rich-text regex doubling bypass ('<<color=red>color=red>' survives RemoveRichTextTags) — regex reasoning is plausible but TMP rendering of the survivor on a vanilla client is untested.

That destroying a client-placed portal ZDO inside the ZDO.Deserialize postfix leaves the placing client in a clean state (no orphaned local instance, materials consumed) — SpawnGovernor proves it for creatures only.

ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync on the Player prefab (Inspector) — every 'portal to a player's ship' and 'rider parent' claim rests on it; the confirmed fallback is only ZDOVars.s_user for the helmsman.
PrivateArea.m_radius on the guard_stone prefab — the Shadow Ward Index is wrong at every ward until the Inspector value is read.

The catalog repeatedly states ForceSendZDO 'pushes regardless of distance'; verified this pass that AddForceSendZdos is still gated on peer.ShouldSend (:77273), so a force-send to a peer whose cached DataRevision is current sends nothing. Any 'touch to resync' design needs a real revision bump.

That 3+ same-tag portals strand exactly one member PERMANENTLY across ticks (pairing-algorithm digest). Plausible from the two-tick commit but the interaction with phase-1 teardown of a pair whose partner later gets ownership-deferred was not traced.
EnvMan.instance and GetDayFraction() being live headless — the entire scheduled-routing family assumes it and nothing verifies it.

Whether a vanilla client that has already received a ZDO discards it cleanly on a peer-targeted 'DestroyZDO' routed RPC and accepts re-delivery later (client-side HandleDestroyedZDO path) — required for the revocation half of per-peer withholding.
critics.structuralCritique:
The catalog is wide but built on one unexamined axiom: 'a ZDO is one object and every peer reconverges on it, therefore nothing is per-player'. That axiom is true of DATA and false of DELIVERY. ZDOMan.CreateSyncList, AddForceSendZdos and RPC_RequestZDO are the only three routes a ZDO takes to a client, all three are server-side and patchable, and a client cannot obtain a ZDO any other way. Per-peer withholding turns the 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', 'Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing — RULED OUT' and the economy domain's 'four independent reasons' into a fourth enforcement tier that the taxonomy does not have: server-enforced-by-omission. Every access, economy and lockdown option should be re-scored against it.

Second, the catalog is far more redundant than 197 suggests. Rotating hub appears as Carousel, Rotating Hub, Event Topologies and One-Way Ring Rotation; pairing takeover appears as Displaced Routing, Pairing Authority Takeover, Managed Network Governor and The Routing Kernel; the portal cap appears in wildcard, economy and access; map pins appear in at least four places. A designer choosing between them has no dependency graph and no de-duplicated list of primitives. Collapse to ~25 primitives (connection write, tag write, anchor fabrication, arrival hook, sync-list filter, force-send, global key, routed RPCs to client, ZDO polling of character/stand/sign/chest, ghost-zone spawn, LocationIcons) and express every option as a composition.

Third, the option space is player-centric to the exclusion of everything else that moves through a portal: not one option concerns tames, carts, or creatures at the destination, which is the largest single user-visible hole relative to the mods people actually install.

Fourth, the silent-first-transit failure is named as a gotcha in ten places and solved as a feature in none; the join event is never used as a lifecycle hook; and 'destination exists' is treated as luck (has a player been there) rather than something the server can manufacture with a ghost SpawnZone. These three are the same structural blind spot: the catalog reasons about what the server can WRITE and almost never about what the server can PRE-DELIVER.

Fifth, the ops and wildcard domains carry internal contradictions the catalog never reconciles (Console.instance non-null vs the admin-command option ruled out; ForceSendZDO 'regardless' vs the ShouldSend gate; Sector Zero asserted vs never traced). A verification column per option — 'read in decompile / inferred / needs in-game' — should be mandatory before any of this becomes a spec."

gaps.gap: Field Injection / Ore Gate / Phantom Destination Portal all say per-portal m_exitDistance is overridable 'on the destination phantom'. The decompile says the opposite: TeleportWorld.Teleport computes `pos = targetPos + rot*forward * m_exitDistance + up` with `this.m_exitDistance` — the SOURCE portal's field (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539-143546). A LoadFields override written on the destination ZDO does nothing to the exit throw; it must be written on the portal the player walks INTO. Same for m_allowAllItems (:143533, source). Also m_activationRange only feeds Player.GetClosestPlayer for the glow (:143495) — it does not enlarge the transit collider. Rewrite the three options with a per-field table: field → which portal it lives on (source vs destination) → what it actually changes → applies-at-instantiation caveat. Note in the option's favour that vanilla's own `spawn` console command writes exactly these HasFields keys (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:44423-44430), so the path is a supported vanilla data contract, not an accident.
gaps.why: Three options (wildcard Field Injection, economy Ore Gate, targeted Phantom Destination Portal) and the targeted domain notes propagate a factual inversion from the research digest; a designer following them would write the override onto the wrong ZDO and conclude the mechanism is broken.

gaps.gap: Ownership Pin is described as 'permanently hold managed portals' ownership' via the WaterBuoyancyEngine ZDO.SetOwner prefix. That prefix is insufficient: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies an incoming owner with ZDO.SetOwnerInternal (:77114, :77128), never SetOwner, and the :77112-77117 branch applies an owner change whenever the incoming OwnerRevision is higher even when DataRevision is not. A vanilla client's ZNetView.ClaimOwnership (:82769 → SetOwner → IncreaseOwnerRevision) therefore steals the pin back on the next ZDOData packet. Spec a real pin: (1) SetOwner prefix for ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901); (2) a postfix on ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData or ZDO.Deserialize that re-claims with SetOwner(GetSessionID()) whenever a pinned portal arrives with a foreign owner, bumping OwnerRevision above the client's; (3) an analysis of the ping-pong (each side bumps OwnerRevision by 1; an honest client claims rarely, a hostile one can force a loop — cap and escalate to kick); (4) the unpin path, because a pinned gate cannot be hammer-removed by anyone (WearNTear.Remove :150411 routes RPC_Remove to the owner, the server, which has no instance).
gaps.why: The option is marked client-honoured/feasible-with-caveats but its core mechanism is broken as written; every option that relies on 'the server holds ownership' (Tag-Scramble Lockdown, Managed Network Governor, Adamant Gate, NetworkReassertEngine) inherits the hole.

gaps.gap: Two-Hop Relay (phantom landing pad + RPC_TeleportPlayer) omits the cooldown arithmetic that dominates its UX. Player.TeleportTo sets m_teleportCooldown = 0 on acceptance (:15320) and UpdateTeleport keeps it at 0 for the whole teleport (:15334), only accruing once m_teleporting is false. A distantTeleport does not end before t>8s (:15349). So the server sees the character ZDO land in the lobby at t≈2s, but any second hop sent before ≈t=10s is silently dropped (IsTeleporting :15309, then cooldown<2f :15313), with no signal for when the first hop finished. Spec the relay with: a fixed ≥10 s hold after the lobby position appears, a 'standing in the lobby for ~2 s' UX moment, total black-screen budget (~8+2+8 s), distantTeleport:false for the second hop (completes on IsAreaReady, ~2 s, but rubber-bands with $msg_portal_blocked if FindFloor misses — :15369-15374), and a dead-player / in-bed pre-check (s_dead, s_inBed).
gaps.why: The option is sold as the answer to per-player destinations and rule enforcement, but as written every second hop would silently fail; the honest cost is a ~20 s transit that must be designed around, not discovered in testing.

gaps.gap: Ops rules out the admin command channel entirely ('a vanilla client never forwards a mod command'), and the ops domain notes simultaneously call RPC_RemoteCommand 'a genuine, working channel'. Both are half right. A vanilla Terminal.TryRunCommand only forwards commands present in its own dictionary (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45737-45744), so `tplite.*` never leaves the client — but `setkey`, `removekey`, `listkeys`, `resetworldkeys` are registered isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true (:43509-43533, :43605), so a vanilla ADMIN typing `setkey tplite:dump 3` in F5 sends RPC_RemoteCommand (admin-gated on the socket host name, :81879-81887) and the server runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand (:81893). Spec a piggyback channel: a server-side Harmony prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand (or on the setkey action) that intercepts a reserved `setkey tplite:...` namespace before vanilla's SetKeyAndValueIsCheat check (:43513), executes the mod command, replies via ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, ...) (:81635) into the admin's console, and never lets the fake key reach GlobalKeyAdd. Document that the server-side ZNet.RemoteCommand(cmd) path NREs on rpc==null (:81873→:81893) so the stdin console must not use it.
gaps.why: The catalog and its own domain notes contradict each other, and a real, zero-client admin channel from the vanilla F5 console is currently listed as impossible.

gaps.gap: Global-Key RPC Hardening and Ungated RPC Hardening say 'drop any SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey packet that did not originate from the server'. Two errors. (1) Vanilla clients legitimately originate these RPCs: Character.OnDeath calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey) and decrements activeBosses on the killing client (:3153-3165), BaseAI.SetAlerted increments activeBosses (:27258), and every killed_*/StoneCircle/AshlandsOcean key comes the same way. A blanket drop breaks boss progression and the activeBosses accounting the lockdown's own watchdog depends on. (2) The `long sender` argument of ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022) is RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID, deserialized off the wire (:83489) — a client can set it to the server's id, so a prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey cannot tell local from remote. Spec the hardening as: a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (the only place the authentic ZRpc is in scope, :83632) matching m_methodHash against SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey, parsing the key name, and dropping only keys with GetKeyValue ordinal < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers) plus the mod's reserved prefixes, while passing every ≥41 key through untouched. Add TeleportWorld's client→client 'RPC_SetConnected' (:143622) and 'DestroyZDO' to the relay-drop list for managed portals.
gaps.why: As written, the flagship 'tamper-proof lockdown' either breaks vanilla boss progression or is trivially bypassed by sender spoofing; the fix changes the hook location and adds an allow-list, which is a different option spec.

gaps.gap: Non-Portals As Portals (extending Game.PortalPrefabHash at runtime) omits a data-loss hazard. ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk clones into normal chunk files only ZDOs with `Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` (:77572), while the ChunkPortal file only clones m_portalObjects (:77621-77627). Any ZDO of the enrolled prefab that already existed in m_objectsBySector when the hash was added is in neither set — it is silently absent from the next save of its chunk and gone after restart. Additionally ZDO.SetSector early-returns for the enrolled prefab (:73752), so a mobile enrolled object (ship, cart) stops re-sectoring and its delivery to clients freezes. Spec the option with a mandatory migration pass (walk GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative for the prefab, RemoveFromSector + AddIfPortal each, SetDirtyPortals), a restriction to immobile prefabs, and an uninstall reversal (the vanilla server will load them from ChunkPortal into m_portalObjects regardless of prefab, then pair them by tag).
gaps.why: The option is marked feasible-with-caveats but the caveat that matters — every pre-existing instance of the enrolled prefab is lost on the next save — is absent; shipping it as written destroys world data.

gaps.gap: The catalog rules out per-player transit gating absolutely (access 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', economy 'RULED OUT — Point-of-Transit Enforcement'). Prevention is indeed impossible, but reactive ejection is not: the server sees the traveller's character ZDO land at t≈2 s (:15343), the player is frozen and invulnerable until t>8 s (:15349, damage suppressed :2425), and at ≈t=10 s RPC_TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportTo can send a non-permitted arrival straight back to their origin (or to a holding cell). The player sees the destination for ~2 s and cannot act during the frozen window (Player.CanMove false :14425). Spec a 'Bouncer' option: arrival detection via the PositionWatch straddle heuristic plus the destination portal's connection, an ACL lookup keyed on s_playerID, the ≥10 s hold, distantTeleport:true for the return (never fails), a per-player 'ejected' toast, and the honest tier: reactive-detection-only, undoes but never prevents, defeated only by the same RPC-spoofing a hardened relay already blocks.
gaps.why: A whole class of degraded-but-real per-player enforcement is missing because the ruled-out entries were written as absolutes; the economy and access domains both lose their only per-player consequence that acts on the person rather than their property.

gaps.gap: Every escrow/turnstile/charge-cell option (Prepaid Toll Escrow, Token Turnstile, Charge Cells, Key-Item Requirement) is marked 'feasible/server-enforced' while the Ore Gate is marked client-honoured — but both read client-authored ZDO data. The route gate is server-owned, but the CONDITION (s_items on a chest, s_item on a stand, s_fuel on a fireplace) is written by the owning client and ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies it wholesale with no validation (:77107-77131). A modified client forges a full chest and the toll is free; no ZDOData validator option exists anywhere in the catalog. Spec (a) a tier correction: 'server-enforced against unmodified clients; condition inputs forgeable without (b)'; and (b) an 'Inline ZDOData validator' option: a Harmony postfix on ZDO.Deserialize (or prefix on RPC_ZDOData that re-parses a copy of the package, saving/restoring pkg position) that, for bound escrow containers and managed portals, compares the arriving fields against the last server-approved state and reverts inside the same frame — collapsing the Tag Watchdog's one-tick window to zero and giving the economy its only real anti-forgery line.
gaps.why: The enforcement tier is applied inconsistently across options that share the same trust model, and the one mechanism that would make the economy's inputs trustworthy is not in the catalog.

gaps.gap: Map Ping → Destination and the UX ping picker cite a HandleRoutedRPC prefix as the 'collision-free' hook and take the sender from the packet. HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData) (:83645) has no socket in scope; both m_senderPeerID (:83489) and the UserInfo payload are client self-reports. The hook must be a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632) with the peer resolved via ZNet.instance.GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc). Also missing: Chat.SendPing overwrites vector.y with the PLAYER's y (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42063), so the destination height must be re-derived with WorldGenerator.GetHeight (:151944) — never ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, which is a dead raycast headless; pings are broadcast to every peer (the 'send me here' gesture is public); and a middle-click costs nothing, so the option needs a per-account debounce and an arming gate (crouch bit or proximity) before it re-routes anything. Spec the option with those four requirements as hard preconditions.
gaps.why: The most-recommended input channel in the catalog is specified against the wrong hook for identity and omits the y-override, so a naive implementation attributes pings to spoofed players and wires portals to a height 100 m off the ground.

gaps.gap: 'Chat commands (/portal home)' is marked ruled-out/not-enforceable, but the UX domain's own notes identify the one branch that would make it a first-class channel: Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync collapses to a single targetPeerID 0 broadcast when PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider == null (:42002-42005). That type lives in the Splatform assembly, outside this decompile set. Slash commands remain dead (Chat.InputText :41947-41955), but plain text and shouts would reach the server even solo if RelationsProvider is null on Steam. Re-classify as needs-ingame-check with the exact test (RPC_RoutedRPC prefix logging 'ChatMessage' hashes while a SOLO vanilla player types a sentence and a /s shout), and pre-write the resulting option: keyword-prefixed plain chat as a 50+ character command line with the authentic sender from the socket.
gaps.why: A research-raised open question with the highest payoff of any single test was silently converted into a ruled-out entry; if the test passes, most of the emote/item-stand/crouch schemes become unnecessary.

gaps.gap: No option exists for a boot-time capability probe, yet roughly a dozen options are gated on Unity Inspector data the decompile cannot answer. Spec a first-class 'CapabilityProbe' engine that runs once at OnWorldReady and logs: Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs names + PortalPrefabHash; for each portal prefab, GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names (the LoadFields HasFields<TypeName> keys), ZNetView m_persistent/m_distant/m_type/m_syncInitialScale, presence of ZSyncTransform, TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems/m_exitDistance/m_activationRange; PrivateArea.m_radius on guard_stone; Player prefab ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync and CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation; null-ness of Chat.instance, MessageHud.instance, Minimap.instance, DamageText.instance, Console.instance; the key set of ZRoutedRpc.m_functions (decides Register-vs-Harmony for ChatMessage); ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances(); ZNet.GetReferencePosition(); ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() and m_zones.Count (Sector Zero); EnvMan.instance and GetDayFraction() advancing; and ZNetScene.GetPrefab('portal_wood')?.GetComponent<TeleportWorld>(). Each subsequent engine reads the probe result and self-disables with a logged reason when its precondition is absent.
gaps.why: Every research brief ends with 4-8 'IN-GAME CHECK' items and the catalog carries none of them as a deliverable; without a probe the mod either hard-codes guesses or ships engines that silently no-op, which is exactly the failure mode Wonderland's history records.

gaps.gap: The Adamant Gate overstates 'indestructible'. Writing a huge ZDOVars.s_health only defeats damage: WearNTear.RPC_Damage compares totalDamage against the stored health (:150350) and Repair correctly refuses when health >= m_health (:149528). But hammer removal (Player.RemovePiece → WearNTear.Remove → RPC_Remove to the ZDO owner, :150411-150425) ignores health entirely; support loss applies 100 wear per update forever (:149705-149711) and will eventually drain even 1e9; a forged DestroyZDO (:76953, ungated) deletes it outright; and any client can overwrite s_health via ZDOData. Rewrite the option as a composite: s_health for damage immunity + Ownership Pin (so RPC_Remove routes to a machine with no instance) + Destroy Veto + a support-independent re-assert of s_health on the watchdog tick, and state that it is only 'indestructible' once all four are present.
gaps.why: The option is marked feasible-with-caveats/client-honoured with a headline claim that a single ZDO write makes a portal indestructible; three vanilla paths delete it regardless of health.

gaps.gap: No option turns the LocationIcons channel into what it actually controls: the vanilla client's DEFAULT RESPAWN POINT. Game.FindSpawnPoint (client :100796-100800) falls back to ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(Game.m_StartLocation = 'StartTemple') when the profile has no logout/custom point, and that dictionary is filled only by the server's LocationIcons RPC (:113581-113607, replaced wholesale per receive). A server that sends a StartTemple entry at a different coordinate relocates where new/bedless characters spawn, with zero client mod. Spec it: an OnNewPeer/SendLocationIcons prefix that rewrites the StartTemple position to a mod-chosen hub, the honest scope (only players without a bed/logout point; the real temple still exists), the Minimap side effect (the temple icon moves on every client's map), and the uninstall restore.
gaps.why: The 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces' and 'World Spawn' options treat LocationIcons as a read-only pin overlay and miss that it is the authority for a gameplay-relevant coordinate the server can steer.

gaps.gap: The first-transit warm-up is mentioned in five domain notes but exists as no option or engine. TeleportWorld.TargetFound returns false with NO message when the client does not hold the destination ZDO, firing a one-shot RequestZDO (:143646-143654); ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO answers with a single ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692) consumed on first send (:77048). Every server-side re-point to a far or freshly-fabricated destination therefore produces exactly one silent dead walk-through per player unless the mod pre-pushes. Spec 'DestinationPrewarm': on every managed connection write, ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId) to every peer within N m of the source portal; on every peer join, push the destinations of all managed portals within their active area; a re-push after any destination ZDO DataRevision bump (moving anchors); and the budget interaction with the 10240-byte send-queue cap (:77010-77016).
gaps.why: This is the single most common way a server-only routing mod will be reported as 'broken', and it is currently a footnote rather than a required component with a defined trigger set.

gaps.gap: Sector Zero is listed needs-ingame-check but its option does not state the decisive predicate or its side effects. Verified: SectorToIndex clamps any |x+256|>=512 or |y+256|>=512 to sector 0 (:115760-115773); FindObjects dedupes by SectorIndex so all neighbours of the server's pinned zone collapse to one visit of m_objectsBySector[0] + m_portalObjects[0] (:77366-77380); IsZoneReadyForType does NOT require m_zones membership (:115797-115810); the only real gate is IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:114054), i.e. whether PokeLocalZone(SpawnMode.Full) succeeds at zone (15625,15625). Spec the option around that predicate, list the reaper as a hazard for any Void Anchor with a typo'd coordinate, and note that ReleaseNearbyZDOS uses zone distance not sector index (:76887-76899) so the server will not auto-own those objects.
gaps.why: The option is marked suspicious by the prior reviewer; the sector math checks out but the actual instantiation hinges on one headless zone-spawn predicate nobody has named, and the side effect on Void Anchors is unstated.

gaps.gap: The MapTable shared-map blob is described in the UX domain notes as a server-craftable opt-in 'sync the portal network to my map' button but never became an option. Its two hazards are precise: it deletes every non-own-owner pin not re-listed in the blob (:58824-58875), and the explored array must be exactly Minimap.m_textureSize^2 bools (default 256, Inspector-overridable). Spec it: a server-written MapTable ZDO near each hub, the blob format from Minimap.GetSharedMapData (:58728-58775), a pin owner id convention that keeps player pins safe, the m_textureSize probe, and the reason it is opt-in (the player must press Read).
gaps.why: RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are permanent and unremovable; the MapTable path is the only re-syncable named-pin surface and it was dropped between research and catalog.

gaps.gap: Session-Only Key Writes, Save-Boundary Transparency and Boss Auto-Lockdown never reconcile with each other about what a vanilla client is TOLD. NoPortals produces $msg_blocked only on walk-in; GetHoverText (:143453-143463) and UpdatePortal (:143491-143509) never consult the keys, so a blocked portal reads [Connected] and glows. The catalog's 'Graceful Lockdown and Announcement' covers announcements but no option specifies the per-portal in-world signal that a Tier-B (force-disconnect) lockdown gives for free and a Tier-A (key) lockdown does not: with the connection nulled the hover flips to $piece_portal_unconnected and the glow dies. Spec a 'Lockdown Legibility' rule: any key-based lockdown longer than N seconds must be paired with either a force-disconnect (so vanilla's own UI shows it) or a server-written tag suffix ≤10 chars (e.g. ' [X]') plus a DamageText overlay, and must be removed in the same tick the key is lifted.
gaps.why: Two of the lockdown options rely on the client-honoured key path whose only feedback is a centre-screen message after a failed walk-in; without a legibility rule operators will ship lockdowns that look like bugs.

gaps.gap: Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint asserts HttpListener works under the game's Mono runtime without any evidence; nothing in the decompile can confirm it (it is a System.dll facility, not game code), and Unity's bundled Mono HttpListener has known prefix-binding and HTTPS limitations. gaps.why: Ops was generated without a research brief and this is the one option whose feasibility rests on a runtime the decompile cannot see; it is marked feasible-with-caveats rather than needs-ingame-check.
