critics.structuralCritique: The catalog's biggest honesty problem is not any single option but the enforcement vocabulary. 'server-enforced' is applied to options whose route gate is server-owned but whose triggering condition is client-authored ZDO data (Prepaid Toll Escrow, Token Turnstile, Charge Cells, Key-Item Requirement), while the Ore Gate — which has exactly the same trust model — is labelled client-honoured. The digest's own test ('should this ROUTE be open' vs 'should this PLAYER pass') is necessary but not sufficient; a second axis is missing: 'is the INPUT the decision reads server-authored or client-authored, and is there a validator?'. Every option needs an explicit dependency line ('server-enforced given: Ungated RPC Hardening + Inline ZDOData validator') instead of a bare tier word. Second, the option one-liners carry no citations at all — every `file:line` lives in domain notes and the digest — so an option cannot be audited in isolation, and the prior-session review notes show that when the digest is wrong (m_exitDistance source-vs-destination, RPC_SetTag interception as 'the only hook', nomap 'correctly branching', RPC_RemoteCommand 'working channel') the error propagates into three or four options unnoticed. Each option should restate its two or three load-bearing citations inline. Third, the ruled-out entries are written as absolutes where degraded forms exist (per-player transit → reactive ejection; chat → pending a single RelationsProvider test; admin console channel → setkey piggyback), which is the opposite failure from over-claiming and equally costly. Fourth, the research briefs collectively raise ~40 'IN-GAME CHECK' items and the catalog operationalises none of them: there is no probe engine, and needs-ingame-check options do not name the predicate that decides them (Sector Zero, HTTP endpoint, Scaling). Fifth, cross-cutting engineering requirements that every dynamic option depends on — DestinationPrewarm (ForceSendZDO on re-point), SetDirtyPortals after every non-connection write, ZDOID-vs-position keying, the OwnerRevision race — appear as footnotes repeated in six domain notes rather than as owned components with a defined trigger set; a designer reading one option will miss them. Sixth, the ops block is visibly un-researched relative to the others (its domain notes contradict its own ruled-out entry on RPC_RemoteCommand, and it asserts a runtime facility the decompile cannot see). Finally, 197 options is inflation: at least a third are recombinations of five primitives (SetConnection ownership-claim write, phantom/anchor ZDO, global key write, RPC_TeleportPlayer, ZDO field poll) and would be better expressed as one primitive spec plus a table of compositions, which would also make the tier and dependency labels consistent by construction."

research.topic: Valheim 1.0.7 portal pairing algorithm — exact reverse-engineering of Game.ConnectPortals / ZDOMan portal bookkeeping for a server-only mod
research.summary: There are three distinct "portal connect" routines and only one runs at runtime: `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589), driven by `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` (:100580) which is started once in `Game.Start()` under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` (:100073-100074), fires immediately and then every 5s forever, and is never stopped anywhere in the assembly. The other two — `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (:77850) and `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` (:77812) — are private, load-time-only, and operate on save-file connection *hashes* (`s_connectionsHashData`), not on tags. The runtime tick takes a freshly-allocated, uncached, world-global snapshot from `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648, flattens `m_portalObjects` every call — there is no cache and therefore nothing to invalidate), then runs two passes over that same snapshot: a reconcile pass (:100594-100606) that clears a portal's connection if the partner ZDO doesn't resolve, has a different `tag` string, or itself has no Portal connection (reciprocity is NOT checked, so rings, chains and self-loops are stable), and a pair pass (:100607-100622) that for each still-unconnected portal picks a uniformly random same-tag unconnected partner via `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100664-100679). Tag equality is bare C# `string !=` — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, with `""` as the default, so every untagged portal in the world is one giant tag group. Writes go through `Game.SetConnection` (:100637), which writes locally (stealing ownership) when the ZDO is unowned or owned by a disconnected/absent peer, and otherwise defers to the owning client over `RPC_SetConnection`; the deferred case is force-committed locally on the *next* tick by `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690), so the server always wins ownership within ≤5s.

facts.claim: EXECUTABLE PSEUDOCODE — the full 5s runtime tick. // ---- every 5 s, dedicated server only ---- function Game.ConnectPortals():  (1) PHASE 0 — FORCE-COMMIT PREVIOUS TICK'S PROPOSALS: for each (A,B) in m_currentlyConnectingPortals: if A.connection(Portal) != B.uid: SetConnection(A, B.uid, force=true); if B.connection(Portal) != A.uid: SetConnection(B, A.uid, force=true); m_currentlyConnectingPortals.Clear().  (2) SNAPSHOT: portalList = ZDOMan.GetPortalList()   // new List<ZDO>, all portals in the world, no cache; num = 0.  (3) PHASE 1 — RECONCILE / SELF-HEAL: for each p in portalList (dictionary-bucket order): c = p.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal); t = p.GetString(s_tag)  // default ""; if c.IsNone(): continue; q = ZDOMan.GetZDO(c); if (q == null) OR (q.GetString(s_tag) != t) OR (q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None): SetConnection(p, ZDOID.None, force=false).   // NOTE: no check that q.connection == p.uid.  (4) PHASE 2 — PAIR: for each p in portalList (same snapshot, same order): if IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal(p): continue; if !p.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone(): continue; t = p.GetString(s_tag); cands = [q in portalList where (object)q != (object)p AND q.GetString(s_tag) == t AND q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None AND !IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal(q)]; if cands.Count == 0: continue; q = cands[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, cands.Count)]   // max-exclusive, global Unity RNG; m_currentlyConnectingPortals.Add({A:p, B:q}); SetConnection(p, q.uid, force=false); SetConnection(q, p.uid, force=false); num++; ZLog.Log("Connected portals " + p + " <-> " + q).  (5) if num > 0: ZLog.Log("[ Connected " + num + " portals ]").  // ---- the write primitive ---- function SetConnection(portal, connectionID, force=false): owner = portal.GetOwner()   // 0 if unowned; isOnlinePeer = (ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null); if (owner == 0) OR (!isOnlinePeer) OR force: portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(Portal, connectionID); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.uid)   // applied IMMEDIATELY, locally; else: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner, "RPC_SetConnection", portal.uid, connectionID)   // DEFERRED: server's own copy is unchanged this tick.
facts.implication: This is the complete algorithm a server-only mod must either cooperate with or displace. Every step is reachable from a Harmony patch on the public Game.ConnectPortals, and every primitive it uses (GetPortalList, ZDO.SetConnection, ZDO.SetOwner, ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO) is public.

facts.claim: EDGE-CASE TABLE (N portals sharing one tag T, all initially unconnected, stable state after ≥2 ticks). N=0 or 1: nothing happens; the lone portal's candidate list is empty (only candidate is `skip`) so FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null and it stays ZDOID.None forever. N=2: paired mutually on the first tick. N=3: the first portal in iteration order picks uniformly at random from the other two; the second iterated portal finds both remaining candidates excluded (both are in m_currentlyConnectingPortals and/or already non-None) and is PERMANENTLY orphaned — subsequent ticks re-confirm the surviving pair, so the orphan never rotates in. N=4: two mutual pairs, first-iterated picks randomly from 3, next unpaired picks the only remaining one. N odd: floor(N/2) pairs + exactly 1 permanent orphan. Empty tag "": every portal in the world with no `tag` string written is one single tag group — freshly placed untagged portals auto-pair with a random untagged portal anywhere in the world. Partner destroyed: phase 1 clears (GetZDO==null) within ≤5s, then re-pairs. Partner retagged: both ends cleared by phase 1 (tag mismatch is symmetric), then each re-pairs within its new tag group. Tags differ only by case or trailing space: treated as DIFFERENT groups, no pairing. A→B while B→C (ring/chain): SURVIVES phase 1 indefinitely, because phase 1 never checks reciprocity. Self-loop A→A: SURVIVES (GetZDO(A)=A, tag equals itself, connection non-None). Connection to a non-portal ZDO X: survives if X resolves, X's `tag` string equals the portal's, and X has any non-None Portal connection — and X is never itself iterated because it is not in m_portalObjects.
facts.implication: 3+ portals on one tag permanently strand one member — a free 'broken network' detector for an admin report. Rings, chains, self-loops and non-portal destination anchors are all stable under vanilla's own reconciler, which is the entire foundation for admin-defined fixed networks with zero client install.

facts.claim: There are THREE distinct portal-connect routines and only one runs at runtime. `Game.ConnectPortals()` is public and runs every 5s. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` is private and called exactly twice, both at world load (`ZDOMan.LoadChunks` :76515 and `ZDOMan.Load` :76653 under `version >= Version.World.NewSaveFormat`); it relinks connections from save-file hashes, not tags. `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` is private and called once, from `ZDOMan.Load` :76631 only when `version < Version.World.NewSaveFormat`; it is a legacy migration keyed on `ZDOVars.s_toRemoveTarget`.
facts.implication: A Harmony patch aimed at 'ConnectPortals' MUST specify the declaring type. Patching ZDOMan.ConnectPortals gets you nothing at runtime; patching Game.ConnectPortals gets you the whole live algorithm.

facts.claim: The coroutine is started once, by string name, in `Game.Start()` inside `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`, alongside `InvokeRepeating("UpdateSleeping", 2f, 2f)`. Body: `while(true){ ConnectPortals(); yield return new WaitForSeconds(5f); }` — the first ConnectPortals() call therefore happens synchronously at Start, before the first 5s wait.
facts.implication: Period is exactly 5.0s of scaled game time, phase-locked to server start. Because it was started with the string overload, `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` is the clean way for a mod to take over pairing wholesale (Unity API semantics, not a decompile claim). There is no StopCoroutine for it anywhere in the assembly — it runs for the life of the Game object.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` allocates a brand-new `List<ZDO>` on every call and flattens `m_portalObjects` (a `Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>`) into it. There is no caching layer, no dirty flag consulted, and nothing to invalidate.
facts.implication: Reads are always current — a mod can add/remove portal ZDOs and the very next tick sees them. Cost is one List allocation plus a full copy per 5s tick; acceptable to call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` on a faster timer for instant re-pairing.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE `m_portalObjects` dictionary itself, not a copy.
facts.implication: A mod can mutate the server's portal registry directly (inject or hide portal ZDOs from the pairing algorithm) without any patch at all. Dangerous but powerful — removing a ZDO from this dictionary makes vanilla's pairer blind to it while the ZDO remains live for clients.

facts.claim: `m_portalObjects` is populated exclusively by `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash)`, gated on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefabHash)`. It is called from `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(uid, position, prefabHashIn)` (:76689) and from the ZDO deserialize loop in `RPC_ZDOData` (:77132). AddIfPortal also calls `RemoveFromSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())`, so portals are stored ONLY in m_portalObjects and never in m_objectsBySector.
facts.implication: Any ZDO a mod creates with a portal prefab hash is auto-registered as a portal. Conversely, a destination-anchor ZDO created with a NON-portal prefab hash is invisible to the pairing algorithm (never iterated, never reconciled) while still being a perfectly valid teleport target.

facts.claim: `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is a `List<int>` built once in `Game.Awake()` from `foreach (GameObject portalPrefab in m_portalPrefabs) PortalPrefabHash.Add(portalPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode())`. `m_portalPrefabs` is a serialized `List<GameObject>` Inspector field — no prefab name string appears anywhere in the decompiled C#.
facts.citation: Game.Awake assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100027-100032; field `public List<GameObject> m_portalPrefabs;` :99828; property `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` :99847-ish
facts.implication: The exact set of prefabs treated as portals is Unity asset data. PortalPrefabHash is a public get / private set List<int> — a mod CAN `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add(hash)` at runtime (the list object is mutable even though the setter is private), which is how you would make a custom or additional prefab participate in vanilla pairing.

facts.claim: World-load path: `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` reads the dedicated portal chunk file (`ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)`) and puts those ZDOs straight into `m_portalObjects` + `m_objectsByID`, bypassing `FilterZDO` and `InitialAddToSector` entirely. It then calls `ConnectPortals()` (ZDOMan's, :76515), `ConnectSpawners()`, `ConnectSyncTransforms()`, then `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (:76523), then sets `DirtyPortalObjects = false`.
facts.implication: Portals live in their own save chunk and are all resident in server memory from world load onward. At the moment Game.ConnectPortals runs during load, `m_peers` is empty, so `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner)` is always null and every SetConnection takes the immediate local-write path — a mod hooking load-time pairing never has to deal with the deferred-RPC branch.

facts.claim: Portals are never unloaded or released on the server. `ZDOMan.Update` calls `ReleaseZDOS(dt)` under `IsServer()`, but `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` only reassigns *ownership* — it never removes a ZDO. The only removal path is `HandleDestroyedZDO`. `FlushClientObjects()` is client-only (`if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer())`).
facts.implication: `GetPortalList()` is always a complete, world-global enumeration of every portal in the save — not a loaded-zones subset. A full portal census/report needs no extra bookkeeping and no player nearby.

facts.claim: Portal removal from the registry happens only in `ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO`: it removes the ZDO from its sector's bucket list and deletes the bucket if it becomes empty, then sets `DirtyPortalObjects = true`, then removes from `m_objectsByID` and calls `ZDOPool.Release(zDO)`. The bucket key used is the sector index captured BEFORE removal.
facts.implication: Destroying a portal leaves its partner holding a dangling ZDOID for up to 5s, until phase 1 of the next tick clears it. A mod wanting instant repair calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() from ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed or a fast timer.

facts.claim: `DirtyPortalObjects` (:76139) is a per-save-state flag array consumed ONLY by `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77635) to decide whether to rewrite the portal chunk file. It plays no role in pairing.
facts.implication: `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` is public and is the correct call after a mod mutates portal ZDO data outside of ZDO.SetConnection, to guarantee the change reaches disk. ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...) already calls it internally.

facts.claim: `ZDO.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, zid)` calls `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` (which no-ops and returns false if type AND target are both unchanged), and on a real change calls `IncreaseDataRevision()` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.
facts.implication: Writes are idempotent and self-marking-dirty. A mod re-asserting the same connection every tick costs nothing and generates no network traffic (revision unchanged means no resend), which makes a high-frequency 'integrity re-assert' loop cheap.

facts.claim: `ZDO.UpdateConnection` differs from SetConnection: it returns false and writes NOTHING if there is no existing `s_connections` entry for the ZDO. It never creates a connection, only overwrites one.
facts.implication: `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` uses UpdateConnection, so retagging a portal that had no connection is a pure no-op on the connection field. Do not use UpdateConnection in mod code to establish a link.

facts.claim: The reconcile predicate is exactly `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None`. It does NOT verify that the partner points back at this portal.
facts.implication: Non-reciprocal topologies are fully stable in vanilla: one-way links, rings, hub fan-in, and self-loops all survive indefinitely as long as every participant shares one literal tag string and every participant's connection field is non-None. This is the single most exploitable property for a server-only portal-network mod.

facts.claim: Tag equality uses C# `string !=` on the result of `ZDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with `defaultValue = ""`. That is `string.Equals` ordinal semantics: case-SENSITIVE, culture-invariant, whitespace-significant, no trimming, no normalization. `ZDOVars.s_tag = "tag".GetStableHashCode()`, `s_tagauthor = "tagauthor".GetStableHashCode()`.
facts.citation: Game.ConnectPortals :100597, :100601, :100611; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100669; ZDO.GetString :73967-73970; ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082; ZDOVars.s_tag :78617, s_tagauthor :78619
facts.implication: 'Home' and 'home' are different networks. A tag with a trailing space is a distinct network and an easy invisible griefing/confusion vector — a server-side normalization/validation pass at write time is trivially justified. Because the default is "" (never null), untagged portals compare equal to each other and auto-pair.

facts.claim: `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(portals, skip, tag)` builds a candidate list with `portal != skip` — REFERENCE inequality, because `ZDO` declares no `operator ==`/`operator !=` (it implements only `IEquatable<ZDO>` with `Equals(ZDO other) => m_uid == other.m_uid`). It then returns `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` (int overload, max-exclusive), or null on an empty list.
facts.citation: Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679; ZDO class decl `public class ZDO : IEquatable<ZDO>` :73262; ZDO.Equals(ZDO) :73527-73534; ZDO.GetHashCode :73522
facts.implication: Two distinct ZDO objects with the same m_uid would both be considered valid candidates by `!=` — which is exactly what the sector-duplication bug below produces. Note the asymmetry: `List<ZDO>.Contains`/`Remove` (used by AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO) DO use IEquatable/m_uid equality, while the pairing loop uses reference equality.

facts.claim: Pairing selection uses the shared global `UnityEngine.Random` state, not a dedicated RNG.
facts.implication: Pairing is genuinely non-deterministic and unseeded from the mod's perspective; replacing FindRandomUnconnectedPortal with a deterministic (nearest / oldest / admin-designated) picker is a clean, well-isolated Harmony target with a simple signature.

facts.claim: `Game.SetConnection(ZDO portal, ZDOID connection, bool forceImmediateConnection = false)` writes locally — `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(Portal, connection); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.m_uid)` — when `owner == 0L || ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) == null || forceImmediateConnection`. Otherwise it sends `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner, "RPC_SetConnection", portal.m_uid, connection)`.
facts.implication: CONFIRMS the central claim: the server does NOT need to own a portal ZDO to rewrite its connection — it will forcibly steal ownership whenever the ZDO is unowned or its owner is not a currently connected peer. The only case where it defers is an online player who currently owns that portal's ZDO.

facts.claim: `ZNet.GetUID()` returns `ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`, and `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is assigned from the remote's own GetUID during the PeerInfo handshake. So the test `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` is exactly 'the ZDO's owner is a currently connected remote client'; the server's own session ID is never in ZNet's m_peers list.
facts.citation: ZNet.GetUID :80866-80869; ZNet peer handshake `peer.m_uid = uid;` :79905; ZNet.GetPeer(long) :80492-80502; ZDOMan.GetSessionID :77362-77365
facts.implication: A portal the server itself owns always takes the immediate local-write path (GetPeer(serverSessionID) is null), so mod writes on server-owned portals are always synchronous and visible to the very next line of code.

facts.claim: TWO-PHASE COMMIT: each proposed pair is recorded in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` (a `List<Game.ConnectingPortals>` of raw ZDO object references), and `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals()` — the FIRST statement of the next `ConnectPortals()` call — replays each pair through `ForceSetConnection` (which calls SetConnection with `forceImmediateConnection: true` only if the current value differs), then clears the list.
facts.citation: Game.ConnectPortals :100591; Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698; Game.ForceSetConnection :100629-100635; Game.AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100681-100688; struct Game.ConnectingPortals :99801-99806; field :99903
facts.implication: Even when a connection write is delegated to an owning client, the server force-writes it locally 5s later regardless of ownership. The server therefore ALWAYS wins the pairing decision within one tick — a client that ignores or drops RPC_SetConnection cannot prevent it.

facts.claim: `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` is checked both in phase 2's loop guard (:100609) and inside FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100671). Because the list is cleared at the top of every call, it only guards WITHIN a single tick — it exists precisely because a deferred (RPC) write leaves the server's own copy of the connection reading `None`, which would otherwise let the same portal be paired twice in one pass.
facts.implication: Any mod that re-implements phase 2 must reproduce this guard or it will double-pair portals owned by online players.

facts.claim: ORDERING TRAP: phase 1's `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` is NOT force, so when the portal is owned by an online peer the clear is deferred over RPC and the server's local copy still reads the OLD connection. Phase 2, running in the same tick over the same snapshot, therefore sees `!IsNone()` and skips it. Re-pairing happens only on a later tick, after the client applies the clear and its ZDO update reaches the server.
facts.implication: Retagging a portal a player is standing next to takes 2+ ticks (up to ~10s+ round-trip) to re-pair, not 5s. A mod that wants instant retag→repair should write the tag AND clear/re-establish the connection itself with force semantics (SetOwner(sessionID) then SetConnection) rather than waiting for vanilla.

facts.claim: `Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered unconditionally in `Game.Start()` (outside the `IsServer()` block), so every vanilla client has the handler. The client-side body sets the ZDO's owner to its OWN session ID, writes the connection, and ForceSendZDO's it.
facts.implication: The deferred path works against 100% vanilla clients with no mod — this is vanilla's own cross-machine connection-write protocol. A server mod can invoke the same routed RPC to make an owning client write a connection on the server's behalf.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs on the server every 2s for the server's own reference position and for EVERY connected peer's `m_refPos`, and it reassigns ownership of persistent ZDOs — including portals, because `FindSectorObjects`→`FindObjects` explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` into the result. It releases ownership to 0 when the current owner has left the ZDO's active area, and assigns ownership to a peer when the ZDO is unowned (or its owner is out of area) and the ZDO is in that peer's active area.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS :76872-76883; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924; ZDOMan.FindObjects portal merge :77376-77379; ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects :77142
facts.implication: A server-only mod's ownership claim on a portal near an online player is stolen back within 2s. The connection VALUE it wrote survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd), but any follow-up write must re-claim ownership. Wonderland already solves exactly this with a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix — see /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 (ZdoSetOwnerPatch) and its comment at line 27. That pattern is directly reusable for portals.

facts.claim: DANGLING CONNECTIONS ARE DROPPED AT SAVE TIME, independently of the runtime reconcile. `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData()` (called from `PrepareSave`) only emits hash data for a connection when `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection.Key) != null` AND `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection.Value.m_target) != null` (the target exemption applies only to ConnectionType.Spawned).
facts.implication: A portal pointed at a ZDOID that does not resolve loses its link permanently across a save/load cycle even if something suppressed the runtime reconcile. A mod using a custom destination-anchor ZDO must keep that anchor alive in m_objectsByID or the link will not persist.

facts.claim: Connections are persisted as a generated INT HASH PAIR, not as ZDOIDs. `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` + `connectionData.m_hash`; `ZDO.Load` reads them back into `ZDOExtraData.SetConnectionData`. The source side gets `ConnectionType.Portal` (1) and the target side gets `ConnectionType.Portal | ConnectionType.Target` (0x11) with the SAME hash, generated by `GetUniqueHash` seeded from `ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode() + s_uniqueHashes`.
facts.citation: ZDO.Save :74243-74318 (connection write :74315-74317); ZDO.Load :74596-74598; ZDOExtraData.SetConnectionData :74992-74996; ZDOExtraData.GetUniqueHash :75440-75459; ConnectionType enum :74747-74754
facts.implication: You cannot read a portal's saved destination out of a world file by ZDOID — you must match hash pairs the way ZDOMan.ConnectPortals does. Also: the on-disk connection is inherently directional (source vs target), even though the runtime representation is two independent one-way `s_connections` entries.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (the load-time one) relinks by hash: it takes `GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal)` as sources and `GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal|Target)` as targets, skips any candidate whose runtime `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionType(item2) != ConnectionType.None` (i.e. already relinked this pass), matches on `m_hash` equality, then `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` on both and writes reciprocal `SetConnection(Portal, ...)` on both, `break`ing after the first match. It does not look at tags at all and does not remove the hash data afterwards (unlike ConnectSpawners, which calls RemoveConnectionHashData at :77974).
facts.implication: Load-time relinking is O(sources × targets) and tag-agnostic, and it makes the server the owner of BOTH ends of every portal pair at world load. That is the cheapest possible window for a server mod to rewrite a network: right after load, before any peer connects, every portal ZDO is server-owned.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` (legacy pre-NewSaveFormat migration) is strictly reciprocal: it links A and B only when `A.tag == B.tag` AND `A.s_toRemoveTarget == B.m_uid` AND `B.s_toRemoveTarget == A.m_uid`, and it strips `s_toRemoveTarget` from every portal it touches whether or not the link is made.
facts.implication: Confirms the old save format DID require mutual targeting; the modern runtime reconciler deliberately relaxed that to a one-way check. Irrelevant to a 1.0.7 world but useful for explaining why old-world imports drop asymmetric links.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(zid, type)` returns `ZDOID.None` unless the stored connection's `m_type` matches `type` EXACTLY. `s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` — a ZDO can hold at most ONE connection of any kind, and `ZDOConnection.m_target` is a single readonly ZDOID.
facts.implication: A true simultaneous multi-destination hub is structurally impossible — only one ZDOID fits. Also, writing `Portal|Target` (0x11) onto a portal makes vanilla read it as unconnected (phase 1 skips it, phase 2 re-pairs it), so do not use the Target bit on live portal ZDOs.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is gated on `m_nview.IsValid() && m_nview.IsOwner()` and is registered on the portal's ZNetView in `TeleportWorld.Awake`. A dedicated server never instantiates a portal GameObject, so no ZNetView exists and this method NEVER executes server-side. Its body clears its own connection via `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`, calls `SetConnectedPortal` (which either takes ownership of the partner and clears it, or RPCs `RPC_SetConnected` to the partner's owner), then writes `s_tag` and `s_tagauthor`.
facts.implication: CONFIRMS the central constraint at the tag layer too: a Harmony patch on TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag will never fire on a dedicated server. Server-side tag interception must happen at the ZRoutedRpc relay layer instead.

facts.claim: The server DOES see and relay every `RPC_SetTag` packet: `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` deserializes it, calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (which no-ops for ZDO-targeted RPCs because `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` returns null with no portal GameObject), then calls `RouteRPC` which forwards it to the target peer (or broadcasts if m_targetPeerID == 0).
facts.implication: A prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` or `RouteRPC` keyed on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` is the ONLY server-side interception point for tag changes — this is the same hook shape Wonderland already uses (`RoutedRpcHandlerPatch` on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:315-327). Returning false from a RouteRPC prefix drops the tag change before it reaches the owning client.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` reads only `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` off the connected ZDO and never checks its prefab. `TargetFound()` only requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) != null` on the client, and calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(connectionZDOID)` if it is missing. Its sole caller remains `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter`, gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`.
facts.implication: CONFIRMS the central constraint verbatim, and simultaneously confirms that any ZDO with a position+rotation works as a destination for a 100% vanilla client. The client must actually hold that ZDO, which `ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO` (called by Game.SetConnection) and the RequestZDO round-trip both provide.

facts.claim: BUG/TRAP — sector duplication: `AddIfPortal` looks up `m_portalObjects[zdo.GetSectorIndex()]` and adds the ZDO if not already in THAT bucket, but never removes it from the bucket keyed by its previous sector. `GetSectorIndex()` is derived live from `m_position`.
facts.implication: If a mod moves a portal ZDO across a 64m zone boundary (or a ZDOData update arrives with a new position), that portal appears TWICE in GetPortalList(). Because phase 2's exclusion uses reference inequality (`portal != skip`), the same ZDO object is filtered correctly — but it will be VISITED twice by both loops, and HandleDestroyedZDO will only clean one bucket, leaking the other. Never reposition a portal ZDO; create a new one instead.

facts.claim: BUG/TRAP — pooled ZDO reuse across ticks: `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` holds raw `ZDO` object references for a full 5s. If one of those portals is destroyed in that window, `HandleDestroyedZDO` calls `ZDOPool.Release(zDO)` → `zdo.Reset()` which sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None`, and `ZDOPool.Get()` can hand the same object out for an unrelated new ZDO. The next tick's `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` then force-writes a Portal connection using a stale/recycled reference.
facts.citation: Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO ZDOPool.Release :76990; ZDOPool.Release/Get :78286-78311; ZDO.Reset (`m_uid = ZDOID.None`) :73536-73545
facts.implication: HARD RULE for the mod: never cache `ZDO` object references across ticks. Cache `ZDOID` values and re-resolve with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` every tick. Vanilla itself violates this; the blast radius is small (writes land on ZDOID.None and are filtered out at save by RegenerateConnectionHashData's `Key == ZDOID.None` guard) but it is real.

facts.claim: Iteration order of both passes is the enumeration order of `Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` buckets (hash-bucket order, perturbed by removals), then list order within each bucket. It is not sorted by position, tag, creation time, or ZDOID, and is not stable across server restarts.
facts.implication: Which of 3 same-tag portals gets orphaned is effectively arbitrary and can change across a restart. Any admin-facing feature must not assume stable identity of the orphan; a deterministic replacement picker must sort the list itself.

facts.claim: Per-pair logging: `ZLog.Log("Connected portals " + item2 + " <-> " + zDO2)` (ZDO.ToString() returns `m_uid.ToString()`, i.e. `userID:ID`), plus a per-tick `ZLog.Log("[ Connected " + num + " portals ]")` when num > 0. The load-time routines log `"ConnectPortals => Connected N portals."` and `"ConvertPortals => fixed N portals."` via UnityEngine.Debug.Log.
facts.implication: Vanilla already emits a parseable pairing audit trail to the dedicated server log with zero patching — usable as a cheap Discord notifier before any Harmony work is done.

apis.signature: public void Game.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: THE runtime pairing tick. Public and instance-level, so `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` can be called on demand (e.g. a 0.5s timer for instant re-pairing after a tag change) and is a clean Harmony prefix/postfix/transpiler target. Calling it out-of-band is safe and idempotent: phase 0 force-commits any pending proposals, phase 1 re-validates, phase 2 only touches ZDOID.None portals. A prefix returning false disables vanilla pairing entirely without stopping the coroutine.

apis.signature: private IEnumerator Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine()  // started via StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") in Game.Start, under if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())
apis.notes: Period exactly 5.0f WaitForSeconds, first call synchronous at Start. Because it was started by string name, `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` stops it (Unity API semantics — verify in-game). No StopCoroutine for it exists anywhere in the assembly. Note WaitForSeconds is scaled time; Time.timeScale is 1 on a dedicated server in practice but that is an in-game assumption, not a decompile fact.

apis.signature: public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()
apis.notes: Allocates a fresh List<ZDO> each call and flattens m_portalObjects. Returns EVERY portal in the world regardless of player proximity (the server never unloads ZDOs). No cache, no invalidation. This is the free, zero-bookkeeping world portal census — tag, position (ZDO.GetPosition), rotation, connection (GetConnectionZDOID), and owner (GetOwner) all readable off each element.

apis.signature: public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Returns the LIVE backing dictionary, not a copy. Mutating it changes what vanilla's pairer sees. Keyed by ZoneSystem.SectorIndex (a uint wrapping 64m zone coords, ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex :115762). Use for read-only enumeration by region; mutate only with a clear reason.

apis.signature: private ZDO Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO> portals, ZDO skip, string tag)
apis.notes: Private — reachable via Harmony with `AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")`. A postfix that overwrites __result is the minimal, lowest-risk way to replace random pairing with nearest/oldest/admin-designated selection while leaving every other vanilla behaviour (two-phase commit, ownership handling, logging) intact.

apis.signature: private void Game.SetConnection(ZDO portal, ZDOID connection, bool forceImmediateConnection = false)
apis.notes: Private. Do not reimplement it badly — the exact semantics are: write locally (stealing ownership via `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`) when `owner == 0L`, or the owner is not a connected ZNet peer, or force is true; otherwise send `RPC_SetConnection` to the owner. A mod that wants unconditional immediate writes should call the public primitives directly in the same order: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);`

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: Public. Use ConnectionType.Portal (value 1). No-ops silently if type+target are unchanged. On a real change it bumps DataRevision and calls ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() for you. Do NOT use ZDO.UpdateConnection (:73668) — it refuses to create a connection where none exists.

apis.signature: public ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)
apis.notes: Public. Returns ZDOID.None unless the stored connection's type matches EXACTLY (Portal == 1; Portal|Target == 0x11 does NOT match Portal). Pair with ZDOID.IsNone() (:75950) or `== ZDOID.None` (ZDOID.operator== :75888).

apis.signature: public string ZDO.GetString(int hash, string defaultValue = "")  // hash = ZDOVars.s_tag / ZDOVars.s_tagauthor
apis.notes: Public, and the write side `ZDO.Set(int hash, string value)` is equally public. Writing the tag server-side is a plain ZDO write — no RPC, no 10-char cap (that limit is client UI only), no profanity filter (client display-time only). Default is "" and never null, which is why untagged portals form one tag group.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)  /  public static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()  /  public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: The ownership-claim triad. `ZDO.SetOwner` no-ops if the owner is unchanged; `SetOwnerInternal` sets `Owner = (uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`. ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) pushes to every peer; the `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID)` overload (:77697) targets one peer on the server. WARNING: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901) will reassign ownership away within 2s if a peer is near the portal — guard with a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix (pattern: Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313).

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()
apis.notes: Public. Marks the portal chunk file dirty so the next save rewrites it. ZDO.SetConnection(Portal, ...) calls this automatically; a mod writing the `tag` string alone should call it explicitly to guarantee persistence.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)  /  public ZDO ZDOMan.GetZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: CreateNewZDO makes a real, persistent, server-owned ZDO and auto-registers it as a portal if prefabHash is in Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash. Using a NON-portal prefab hash yields a 'destination anchor' ZDO that TeleportWorld.Teleport will happily read position/rotation from (:143536-143543) but that vanilla's pairer never iterates. GetZDO returns null for ZDOID.None and for unknown ids.

apis.signature: public List<int> Game.PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }
apis.notes: Private setter but the List object itself is mutable: `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add("myprefab".GetStableHashCode())` makes that prefab participate in AddIfPortal / GetPortalList / vanilla pairing. Conversely `.Remove(hash)` at runtime does NOT retroactively un-register already-tracked ZDOs from m_portalObjects.

apis.signature: private void ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC(ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData data)  /  private void ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC(ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData rpcData)
apis.notes: The ONLY server-side hook for TeleportWorld's RPC_SetTag (which never executes server-side). Match on `data.m_methodHash == "RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` and `data.m_targetZDO` (the portal's ZDOID). A prefix on RouteRPC returning false drops the tag change before any client applies it; reading `data.m_parameters` (a ZPackage, SetPos(0) already applied by InvokeRoutedRPC) yields the new tag string and the self-reported authorId. Wonderland already ships this exact hook shape (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:315-327).

apis.signature: public static readonly ZoneSystem.ChunkIndex ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)
apis.notes: Portals are saved to a dedicated chunk file, loaded by ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76474-76482 straight into m_portalObjects. Useful if any offline world-file tooling is ever wanted.

gotchas: Two things are named ConnectPortals. `Game.ConnectPortals()` (:100589) is the public 5s runtime pairer keyed on tags. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` (:77850) is private, runs only during world load, and matches save-file connection HASHES with no tag involvement. Patching the wrong one does nothing at runtime.

Phase 1 never checks reciprocity. `A→B` survives even when `B→C`. This means rings, one-way chains, hub fan-in, and self-loops (`A→A`) are all indefinitely stable in pure vanilla — but ONLY while every participant shares one byte-identical tag string and every participant's Portal connection stays non-None. The moment one member's connection goes None, its neighbours' links get torn down by the `q.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` clause.

Tag comparison is `string !=` — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant. 'Base' / 'base' / 'Base ' are three separate networks. The default value is "" (never null), so every untagged portal in the world is a single tag group and freshly-placed untagged portals auto-connect to a random untagged portal anywhere.

3+ portals on one tag permanently strand exactly one member. The orphan does NOT rotate in on later ticks, because the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself. Which one is stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and is not stable across restarts.

Phase 1's disconnect is NOT forced, so when an online player owns the portal it is deferred over RPC and the server's own ZDO still reads the old connection — phase 2 in the same tick therefore skips it. Re-pairing after a retag near a player takes 2+ ticks, not one.

The server does not need to own a portal ZDO to rewrite it, but ownership is transient in the other direction: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs every 2s and hands portal ownership to any peer in whose active area the portal sits. A mod's SetOwner claim will be stolen back within 2s unless guarded with a `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 does exactly this for floating items).

`m_currentlyConnectingPortals` caches raw ZDO object references for 5 seconds. `ZDOPool.Release`/`Get` recycles ZDO objects on destruction. Vanilla can therefore force-write a connection through a recycled reference. HARD RULE for mod code: cache ZDOIDs, never ZDO objects, across ticks.

`AddIfPortal` adds a portal to the bucket for its CURRENT sector but never removes it from its old bucket. Moving a portal ZDO across a 64m zone boundary duplicates it in `GetPortalList()` and leaks a bucket entry that `HandleDestroyedZDO` will not clean. Never reposition a portal ZDO — destroy and recreate.

`portal != skip` in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is REFERENCE inequality (ZDO has no operator==), while `List<ZDO>.Contains/Remove` used in AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO use `IEquatable<ZDO>.Equals` (m_uid equality). Two ZDO objects with the same uid behave differently in the two places.

A ZDO can hold exactly ONE connection (`Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>`, single readonly target ZDOID). A simultaneous multi-destination hub is structurally impossible, not merely unimplemented. Only time-sliced rotation works.

Writing ConnectionType.Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal makes `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` return None, so vanilla will treat it as unconnected and re-pair it. Only use bare ConnectionType.Portal on runtime portal ZDOs; the Target bit belongs to the save-hash representation only.

Dangling connections are dropped at SAVE time independently of the runtime reconcile: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) only persists a connection when both endpoint ZDOs resolve in `m_objectsByID`. A custom destination-anchor ZDO must stay alive in ZDOMan or the link vanishes across restart even if it looked fine in memory.

`TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is gated on `m_nview.IsOwner()` and the server never instantiates a portal ZNetView, so a Harmony patch on it NEVER fires on a dedicated server. The only server-side interception point for tag changes is the ZRoutedRpc relay (`HandleRoutedRPC` / `RouteRPC`).

`Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered on BOTH server and client (outside the IsServer block, :100070), and the client handler takes ownership for itself. That is vanilla's own cross-machine write protocol — but it also means a hostile client could invoke RPC_SetConnection at any peer to rewrite a portal link; nothing validates the sender. (Same trust gap class the existing spec already flags for RPC_SetTag.)

`Game.ConnectPortals()` runs synchronously during world load from `ZDOMan.LoadChunks` (:76523) and `ZDOMan.Load` (:76658). At that moment `m_peers` is empty so every write takes the immediate local path and the server ends up owning both ends of every pair. That pre-peer window is the cheapest possible time to rewrite a network.

The pairing loop's candidate filter also excludes portals already in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals`. Any reimplementation that drops that guard will double-pair portals owned by online players, because their connection writes are deferred and the server's copy still reads None.
openQuestions: Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (and therefore `PortalPrefabHash`)? The list is a serialized Inspector field on the Game prefab and no prefab-name string for it appears anywhere in either decompiled assembly. Specifically needed to confirm whether the Ashlands `portal_stone` is a separate PortalPrefabHash entry from the wood portal.

Does `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` actually stop it? StartCoroutine was called with the string overload (:100074), which per Unity's API makes the string StopCoroutine valid, but this is a Unity runtime claim, not a decompile claim. IN-GAME CHECK: call it, then watch the server log for the absence of `[ Connected N portals ]` lines after deliberately placing two same-tag portals.

What is `ZNet.GetReferencePosition()` on a dedicated server at runtime? `m_referencePosition` is declared `= Vector3.zero` (:79043) and `SetReferencePosition` (:81016) is the only writer; if it is truly never called server-side, then `ReleaseNearbyZDOS(ZNet.GetReferencePosition(), m_sessionID)` permanently treats the world origin as the server's active area, meaning the server will only auto-retain ownership of portals near (0,0,0). IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition() every 10s on a live dedicated server.

Timing of the ownership tug-of-war: `ReleaseZDOS` runs every 2s and `ConnectPortals` every 5s, both on the main thread but from different drivers (Update vs coroutine). The exact interleaving determines how often a server-written portal connection is followed by an ownership steal before the next write. IN-GAME CHECK: log owner transitions on one portal ZDO with a player standing next to it for 60s.

Does a client cleanly handle a portal whose connected ZDO has a prefab hash it cannot instantiate (a pure 'destination anchor')? `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` only needs `GetZDO != null`, and `Teleport` only reads position/rotation, but `ZNetScene` will still attempt to create an object for that ZDO when the client's active area covers it. IN-GAME CHECK: create an anchor ZDO with an existing harmless prefab hash (e.g. a marker piece) vs. an unregistered hash, stand near each with a vanilla client, and watch the client log for CreateObject failures.

Whether `WaitForSeconds(5f)` is affected by any server-side Time.timeScale manipulation (e.g. the sleep/time-skip path in Game.UpdateSleeping :100712+). IN-GAME CHECK: trigger a sleep skip on a live server and measure the interval between `[ Connected N portals ]` log lines.
correctionsToExistingSpec: Anchor correction: the prompt lists `Game.ConnectPortals()` at :100592. The method declaration is at :100589; :100592 is the `List<ZDO> portalList = ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList();` line inside it. Phase 1 (reconcile) is :100594-100606, phase 2 (pair) is :100607-100622.

Anchor correction: the prompt's range ':77815-77891' for 'ZDOMan-internal portal bookkeeping' actually spans two different methods — `ZDOMan.ConvertPortals()` at :77812 (legacy pre-NewSaveFormat migration keyed on ZDOVars.s_toRemoveTarget) and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals()` at :77850 (load-time hash relinking). The true per-ZDO bookkeeping is elsewhere: `AddIfPortal` :77732, `HandleDestroyedZDO` portal branch :76980-76987, `GetPortalList` :77648, `GetPortals` :77643.

The spec says 'Game.ConnectPortals() ... re-evaluates every same-tagged pair every 5 seconds'. More precisely: it does TWO separate things per tick — a reconcile pass over ALL connected portals (which is where 'wrongly connected' is decided) and a pairing pass over only ZDOID.None portals. Only the second is tag-driven matchmaking; the first is a validity check that also uses tag equality but as a tear-down condition.

The spec's claim 'A ring is self-stable under vanilla's own self-heal check as long as members share a tag and stay non-None; a fan-in hub member can self-loop to stay "connected" without a real return route' is CONFIRMED exactly, and the mechanism is precisely that phase 1's predicate (:100601) checks only `q != null`, `q.tag == p.tag`, and `q.connection != None` — never `q.connection == p.uid`.

The spec's claim 'vanilla's self-heal transitively forces every linked portal to share one literal tag string' is CONFIRMED and should be stated more strongly: the equality is ORDINAL C# string comparison with `""` as default, so case and whitespace differences break a network silently, and ALL untagged portals in the world form one implicit group.

The spec's claim '3+ portals sharing a tag permanently strands one under vanilla's strictly-pairwise algorithm' is CONFIRMED, with the added detail that the orphan never rotates in on later ticks (the surviving pair re-confirms itself every tick) and that which portal is orphaned is dictionary-bucket-order dependent and not stable across restarts.

The spec says the mod can rewrite connections because 'Vanilla itself already takes ownership of an offline portal's ZDO'. Sharpen this: the ownership steal is NOT limited to offline portals. `Game.SetConnection` force-writes whenever `owner == 0L` OR the owner is not a connected peer OR `forceImmediateConnection` is true — and `ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` passes force=true on the very next tick for every pair proposed in the previous one. So the server unconditionally wins any pairing dispute within ≤5s, even against an online owning player.

ADD TO THE SPEC — a mechanism it does not mention: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs on the SERVER every 2s and actively reassigns portal ZDO ownership to nearby peers (portals are included via FindObjects :77376). Any 'proactive server ownership claim on placement' feature (currently listed as [Feasible, medium]) will be undone within 2s near an online player unless it also ships a `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix, exactly as Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 already does for floating items.

ADD TO THE SPEC — a concrete new design primitive it misses: a destination-anchor ZDO created with a NON-portal prefab hash is (a) never iterated by GetPortalList, (b) never reconciled by phase 1, and (c) perfectly valid as a teleport target because TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143536-143543) reads only GetPosition/GetRotation and never checks the target's prefab. A portal P pointed at such an anchor X is permanently stable under vanilla's reconciler provided X resolves, `X.tag == P.tag`, and X has any non-None Portal connection (a self-loop suffices). This makes 'Portal to any computed coordinate' materially simpler and more robust than the spec implies.

ADD TO THE SPEC — persistence caveat for the above: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) refuses to persist a connection whose target ZDO does not resolve in ZDOMan at save time. Any anchor-ZDO scheme must keep the anchor alive in m_objectsByID or the link silently disappears on restart, independent of the runtime reconciler.

REFINE the spec's Group 4 point about RPC identity: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag is unreachable server-side (no ZNetView), so the hardening hook is NOT a patch on TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag — it must be `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` (:83597) or `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83645), matched on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` and `data.m_targetZDO`. The server does relay the packet, so interception and outright dropping are both possible.

REFINE the spec's 'Instant re-pairing after a tag change' item: calling `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` on a fast timer does NOT give instant re-pairing when the portal is owned by an online player, because phase 1's disconnect is deferred over RPC and phase 2 in the same call still sees the stale connection. For genuinely instant behaviour the mod must do the write itself with force semantics (`SetOwner(sessionID)` then `SetConnection`) rather than relying on vanilla's two-pass flow.

REFINE the spec's 'Distinct per-portal display tags within one managed group' [Feasible-with-caveats, medium]: the specific thing that must be bypassed is the `zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != @string` clause at :100601. A postfix on Game.ConnectPortals cannot help (the damage is already done); the options are a prefix returning false for managed portals, a transpiler on that one clause, `StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")`, or hiding managed portals from `m_portalObjects` via the live dictionary returned by `ZDOMan.GetPortals()`.

research.topic: GlobalKeys system end-to-end (server-authoritative levers for a zero-client-install portal mod), Valheim 1.0.7
research.summary: GlobalKeys is a single flat `HashSet<string>` on `ZoneSystem` whose authority is the server: only the server registers `SetGlobalKey`/`RemoveGlobalKey` routed RPCs, and every mutation ends in `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` — a full-snapshot broadcast (`ClearGlobalKeys()` + re-add on each client) that reaches already-connected vanilla clients within one network frame, with no polling interval and no relog required. All four portal-relevant keys (`NoPortals`=32, `NoBossPortals`=33, `DungeonBuild`=34, `TeleportAll`=35) sit below `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption`(41), which means they are "server option"/world-modifier keys: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (the .fwl file, saved on every world autosave) and `ZoneSystem.Save` deliberately strips them from the .db — so they survive relog, reappear at boot via `SetStartingGlobalKeys()`, and change the advertised server-browser "modifiers" badge. World Modifiers / `ServerOptionsGUI` / `WorldModifierOption` are NOT a separate network channel: they are a pure presentation layer that writes the same global keys (`ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys` → `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey`), so global keys are the only vanilla-respecting global lever (the only other genuinely networked global server setting is simulation distance). The claim about the `noportals` console command is CONFIRMED — its whole body is inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` so it is inert on a dedicated server — but the spec's contrast with `nomap` is WRONG: `nomap`'s `IsServer()` branch is itself nested inside the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard, so `nomap` is equally inert. Every key read the client performs (`TeleportWorld.Teleport`, `Inventory.IsTeleportable`, `Player.PlacePiece`) is a live read at the moment of use, never a cached/once-at-join snapshot.

facts.claim: `public enum GlobalKeys` has 53 members; ordinals are PlayerDamage=0 … CarryWeightRate=16, PassiveMobs=30, NoMap=31, NoPortals=32, NoBossPortals=33, DungeonBuild=34, TeleportAll=35, NoPseudoDrops=36, NoBuildingFall=37, NoHeavySnow=38, AllHeavySnow=39, Preset=40, NonServerOption=41, defeated_eikthyr=42, defeated_dragon=43, defeated_goblinking=44, defeated_gdking=45, defeated_bonemass=46, activeBosses=47, StoneCircle=48, KilledTroll=49, killed_surtling=50, KilledBat=51, AshlandsOcean=52, Count=53.
facts.implication: The ordinal split at NonServerOption=41 is load-bearing: indices 0-40 are 'server option' (world-modifier) keys with completely different persistence and lifecycle rules from 42+. All four portal keys are below the line.

facts.claim: Only the SERVER registers the write RPCs; only non-servers register the read RPC: `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer()) { Register<string>("SetGlobalKey", RPC_SetGlobalKey); Register<string>("RemoveGlobalKey", RPC_RemoveGlobalKey); } else { Register<List<string>>("GlobalKeys", RPC_GlobalKeys); ... }`.
facts.implication: The key store is server-authoritative by construction. A server-side mod owns the only writable endpoint; clients can only request writes and receive snapshots.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string name)` is nothing but `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)`; the 1-arg overload targets `GetServerPeerID()`, which on the server returns `m_id` (itself), and `InvokeRoutedRPC` dispatches synchronously via `HandleRoutedRPC` when `targetPeerID == m_id`.
facts.implication: A server-only mod can call the PUBLIC `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(...)` with no publicizer and no Harmony patch; the key is set and broadcast before the call returns. Wonderland's FirstSpawnGrant comment (`SetGlobalKey routes to the server's own handler synchronously`) is decompile-correct.

facts.claim: `RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string name)` performs NO admin, ownership or sender validation — `if (!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)) { GlobalKeyAdd(name); SendGlobalKeys(0L); }`. Same for `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`.
facts.implication: Any vanilla (or hacked) client can set or clear `noportals`/`teleportall` on the server at will. A mod that relies on NoPortals for a lockdown MUST also Harmony-prefix RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey to reject non-server senders, or the lockdown is one client packet away from being lifted.

facts.claim: Every successful mutation broadcasts the whole key set: `SendGlobalKeys(long peer)` does `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, "GlobalKeys", new List<string>(m_globalKeys))`, and callers pass `0L` (broadcast-to-all-peers in `RouteRPC`).
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113466-113471; ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC :83597-83629 (targetPeerID==0 → loop over all ready peers)
facts.implication: A live toggle DOES reach already-connected players. No relog, no reconnect, no zone reload needed.

facts.claim: The client handler is a destructive full replace: `RPC_GlobalKeys(long sender, List<string> keys) { ClearGlobalKeys(); foreach (key) GlobalKeyAdd(key); }`.
facts.implication: Key REMOVAL propagates as reliably as addition (unlike additive-only designs). Corollary trap: any key a client-side mod injected locally is wiped on every server broadcast.

facts.claim: Propagation latency is one routed-RPC hop with no timer or poll: `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` calls `peer.m_rpc.Invoke("RoutedRPC", pkg)` immediately inside the same call stack as the mutation; there is no accumulation buffer or send interval in the GlobalKeys path.
facts.implication: Sub-frame + RTT. A portal lockdown toggled by a mod is honored by connected vanilla clients essentially instantly.

facts.claim: On connect, the server pushes keys explicitly: `ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer(long peerID) { if (ZNet.instance.IsServer()) { SendGlobalKeys(peerID); SendLocationIcons(peerID); } }`, hooked via `ZRoutedRpc.m_onNewPeer` in ZoneSystem.Start.
facts.implication: Joining players get the current key set without any extra work; a mod only needs to ensure its keys are in `m_globalKeys` before the peer connects (or re-broadcast after).

facts.claim: `m_onNewPeer` fires from `ZRoutedRpc.AddPeer(peer)`, which ZNet calls at the very end of `RPC_PeerInfo` AFTER `peer.m_uid = uid` is assigned; `ZNetPeer.IsReady()` is exactly `m_uid != 0`.
facts.implication: No race: the join-time SendGlobalKeys is never dropped by the `peer.IsReady()` filter in RouteRPC.

facts.claim: `GlobalKeyAdd(string keyStr, bool canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true)` mirrors every key whose parsed enum is `< GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (removing any prior entry with the same key-name token first).
facts.implication: Setting `noportals`/`teleportall`/`dungeonbuild`/`nobossportals` at runtime AUTOMATICALLY edits the world's persisted modifier list. The existing spec's suggestion to 'mutate that list alongside any runtime key change' is unnecessary for these keys — vanilla already does it.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.Save(BinaryWriter)` deliberately strips server-option keys from the .db world save: `m_tempGlobalKeysSaveClone.RemoveWhere(x => { GetKeyValue(x, out _, out var gk); return gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption; });`.
facts.implication: NoPortals/TeleportAll/DungeonBuild/NoBossPortals are NOT in the .db. Their only persistence is `World.m_startingGlobalKeys` in the .fwl. Keys ≥ NonServerOption (defeated_*, activeBosses, and every custom mod key like Wonderland's `wonderland_starter_<id>`) go the other way — .db only, never .fwl.

facts.claim: `World.SaveWorldFWLData` writes `m_startingGlobalKeys.Count` then each string into the .fwl package, and `World.LoadWorld` reads them back when `world >= Version.World.GlobalKeys`. The dedicated server's periodic save calls it every cycle.
facts.implication: A runtime portal-key change survives relog and server restart, persisted at the next autosave (`Game.m_saveInterval`, default 1800s, :99914) or on `ZNet.Shutdown(save:true)`. It cannot be made session-only unless the mod removes the key before shutdown or passes canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false.

facts.claim: `ZNet.WorldSetup()` calls `ZoneSystem.instance.SetStartingGlobalKeys()`, which first `GlobalKeyRemove`s enum indices 0..40 (`for (int i = 0; i < 41; i++)`) with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false`, then re-adds every entry of `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys`, then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`.
facts.implication: Boot-time authority is the .fwl list, not the .db. A mod that wants a key guaranteed present must (re)apply it in a postfix on SetStartingGlobalKeys — exactly what Wonderland/WorldRatesPatches.cs does. A mod that wants a key ABSENT must remove it after this runs.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` calls `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.SetPreset(ZNet.World, text)` (unguarded, no `?.`) whenever any starting key parses as `GlobalKeys.Preset`; `SetPreset` re-applies a whole KeyButton/KeySlider key set.
facts.implication: If the world carries a `preset ...` key, the preset's key set is reapplied at every boot and can overwrite a mod's portal keys. Apply mod keys in a POSTfix on SetStartingGlobalKeys, not a prefix.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` reads both portal keys live at the moment of transit: `if (GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)) { player.Message(Center, "$msg_blocked"); return; }` then `if (GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out float value) && value > 0f))) { Message "$msg_blockedbyboss"; return; }` then `if (!player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)) { "$msg_noteleport"; return; }`.
facts.implication: Read live, never cached — a toggle applies to the very next transit attempt. But it is 100% client-executed: vanilla-respecting only, and useless against a modified client.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` has exactly one call site in the whole assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)`, gated on `Player.m_localPlayer != component`.
facts.citation: grep of all `.Teleport(` call sites; TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143674-143682 (call at :143679)
facts.implication: CONFIRMS the central constraint verbatim. There is no server-side hook on the moment of transit at any level — no RPC, no ZDO write, no ownership handshake the server sees before the player has already moved.

facts.claim: `GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals` is checked against a WORLD-GLOBAL condition, not participation: `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null` OR the global key `activeBosses > 0`. `activeBosses` is incremented/decremented by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` for any boss Character, once per boss (guarded by the ZDO bool `s_bossCount`).
facts.implication: NoBossPortals is a server-wide portal blackout for EVERY player the moment any boss anywhere is alerted — not a per-fight lock. The existing spec's 'auto-disable during boss fights' undersells the blast radius.

facts.claim: `activeBosses` (ordinal 47, ≥ NonServerOption) is written via `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, value±1)` from `BaseAI.SetAlerted`, i.e. from whichever process has the boss GameObject instantiated — never the dedicated server, because `Game.FixedUpdate()` pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every fixed step and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` builds objects only around that reference position.
facts.citation: BaseAI.SetAlerted assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:27258-27259; Game.FixedUpdate :100458-100465; ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects :82268-82276; ZNet.GetReferencePosition :81019-81022 (field default Vector3.zero :79043)
facts.implication: The server never instantiates portal GameObjects, boss AI, or any ZNetView — reconfirming that every portal decision must be made at the ZDO layer. It also means `activeBosses` can desync/leak if the owning client crashes mid-fight, leaving NoBossPortals permanently blocking; a server mod can correct it with `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 0f)`.

facts.claim: `Inventory.IsTeleportable(bool allowAllItems)` blocks `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` items BEFORE the TeleportAll check, so `TeleportAll` cannot override that class of item.
facts.implication: `teleportall` is not literally 'allow all cargo'. A hard-coded tier-1000 item (e.g. the Ashlands-tier flametal-class gate) still blocks transit. Document this in the spec's TeleportAll bullet.

facts.claim: `TeleportAll` also drives the inventory UI: `InventoryGui` sets `element.m_noteleport.enabled = !item.m_shared.m_teleportable && !GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.TeleportAll)` and the tooltip appends `$item_noteleport` under the same condition. Both are per-refresh reads.
facts.implication: Toggling `teleportall` live visibly updates every vanilla client's inventory icons and tooltips with no relog — a free, honest UI signal for a server-only mod.

facts.claim: `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` is read in `Player.PlacePiece`-path validation: `if (!component.m_allowedInDungeons && InInterior() && !EnvMan.instance.CheckInteriorBuildingOverride() && !GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild))` → placement refused.
facts.implication: Setting `dungeonbuild` lets vanilla clients place portals (and everything else) inside dungeons. Purely client-honored; the server never validates placement.

facts.claim: The `noportals` console command's ENTIRE body is inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`, and it is registered `isNetwork:false, onlyServer:false, remoteCommand:false, onlyAdmin:true`.
facts.implication: CONFIRMED INERT on a dedicated server console (m_localPlayer is never populated), and `remoteCommand:false` also means an admin cannot fire it remotely. Use `setkey noportals` / `removekey noportals`, or call ZoneSystem directly.

facts.claim: The neighbouring `nomap` command is ALSO fully wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`; its `if ((bool)ZNet.instance && ZNet.instance.IsServer())` branch is NESTED INSIDE that guard, not an alternative to it.
facts.implication: REFUTES the existing spec's framing that nomap 'correctly branches on IsServer()' while noportals does not. Both are equally dead on a dedicated server; the difference is only that nomap additionally has a host-side branch for a listen server.

facts.claim: The server-usable console commands for keys are `setkey`, `removekey`, `resetkeys`, `resetworldkeys`, `setworldpreset`, `setworldmodifier` and `listkeys`, all registered `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` (so they work from the dedicated server's stdin and from an admin client's console).
facts.citation: Terminal console command registrations assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs: setkey :43509-43533, removekey :43534-43546, resetkeys :43547-43552, resetworldkeys :43553-43557, setworldpreset :43558-43568, setworldmodifier :43569-43579, listkeys :43606-43639
facts.implication: Everything the mod needs is reachable from stock commands too — useful as an in-game verification path and as an operator escape hatch.

facts.claim: `setkey` is gated by `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat(fullLine) && !Achievements.IsCheatedAtAll()` — it refuses any key+value combination that the World Modifiers GUI could not itself produce, unless the profile is already cheat-flagged.
facts.implication: A mod calling `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey`/`GlobalKeyAdd` directly bypasses this check entirely — which is both a convenience and an achievement-integrity consideration (`Achievements.MarkAchievementDifficultyDirty()` is called on every add/remove, :113505, :113535).

facts.claim: World Modifiers are NOT a separate network protocol. `ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys(World)` / `KeySlider.SetKeys(World)` / `KeyToggle.SetKeys(World)` / `KeyButton.SetKeys(World)` all funnel into `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(text)` when ZoneSystem exists, and into `world.m_startingGlobalKeys` only when it does not (main-menu, pre-ZoneSystem).
facts.implication: Answers the prompt's last question: global keys ARE the only vanilla-respecting global lever for modifiers. There is nothing extra to set — a mod that writes the keys is doing exactly what the GUI does.

facts.claim: The only genuinely separate server→client networked global setting found is simulation distance: `ZNet.SimulationDistanceServerHandshake` / `RPC_RequestValidSimulationDistance` / `RPC_ValidatedSimulationDistance` → `ApplySimulationDistance` → `ZoneSystem.ApplySettings()`, with the server clamping each peer to `min(client desired, server)`.
facts.implication: Not portal-relevant, but it is the one other lever where the server can cap a client's behavior over the wire. Nothing analogous exists for portals.

facts.claim: The server-browser 'modifiers' badge is a SNAPSHOT of `m_world.m_startingGlobalKeys.ToArray()` taken in `ZNet.OpenServer()` and re-taken only on the Steam registration-retry path; it is encoded into Steam gametags under key `"m"` via `ServerOptionsGUI.TryConvertModifierKeysToCompactKVP` (enum ordinal → value, e.g. `32` for noportals).

facts.implication: `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance` IS non-null on a dedicated server, so `setworldmodifier Portals <opt>` and `ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.*` are callable server-side. `-modifier Portals <option>` on the command line is the zero-code way to set portal modifiers at boot.

facts.claim: `ResetWorldKeys()` removes enum indices 0..40 via the public `RemoveGlobalKey(string)` (i.e. through the RPC, one broadcast each); `ResetGlobalKeys()` does `ClearGlobalKeys(); SetStartingGlobalKeys(send:false); SendGlobalKeys(0L);`.
facts.implication: `resetworldkeys` is the clean 'clear all world modifiers including noportals/teleportall' lever. `resetkeys` is destructive — it also wipes `defeated_*` boss progression from the .db side.

facts.claim: The vanilla client gives NO visual warning that portals are disabled: `TeleportWorld.GetHoverText()` reports only `$piece_portal_connected`/`$piece_portal_unconnected` from `HaveTarget()`, and `UpdatePortal()` (InvokeRepeating every 0.5s) lights `m_target_found` purely from `closestPlayer.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems) && TargetFound()`. Neither consults NoPortals or NoBossPortals.
facts.implication: With `noportals` set, a vanilla portal still looks fully connected and glows; the player only learns it is blocked by walking in and getting a centre-screen `$msg_blocked`. Any UX affordance beyond that requires a different mechanism (e.g. server-side de-pairing, or a tag rewrite).

facts.claim: Non-portal secondary reads of the portal keys: `Teleport.Interact` (dungeon/crypt doors) checks `NoBossPortals && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos)` — a narrower, position-based test, not the global activeBosses test.
facts.implication: Confirms the existing spec's note at its line 100-103: `NoBossPortals` has two different, independently-implemented meanings for world portals vs dungeon doors. Setting the key affects both.

facts.claim: Keys with NO C# read site anywhere in either assembly: `StoneCircle`(48), `KilledTroll`(49), `killed_surtling`(50), `KilledBat`(51), `AshlandsOcean`(52) — they appear only as the enum members. They are consumed exclusively through Inspector string fields (`Character.m_defeatSetGlobalKey` :275, `SpawnSystem.SpawnData.m_requiredGlobalKey`/`m_blockingGlobalKey` :5579-5581, `RandomEvent.m_requiredGlobalKeys`/`m_notRequiredGlobalKeys` :107469/:107481, `CreatureSpawner.m_requiredGlobalKey` :110680, `Thunder.m_requiredGlobalKey` :37230).
facts.citation: grep of all five names, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101320-101324 (enum only); string-field consumers at :275, :5579-5581, :5689-5698, :37284, :107238-107248, :110866, :111242-111246
facts.implication: No portal relevance, but it establishes that the key namespace is open: spawners/events match keys by arbitrary string, so a server mod can gate vanilla spawns with a custom key without touching any enum.

facts.claim: Full set of code-level reads for the remaining server-option keys (all client-executed, all live reads): PassiveMobs (:2499, :26417, :27122, :27213, :27712, :27762, :110930), NoPseudoDrops (:5292), NoWorkbench (:12252, :12333), DeathKeepInventory/DeathKeepEquip/DeathDeleteItems/DeathDeleteUnequipped (:12694-12706), DeathSkillsReset (:12838), AllPiecesUnlocked (:14783), AllRecipesUnlocked (:14984), NoMap (:39163 Achievements.IsCleanNoMap, :101202 Game.UpdateNoMap, :105484), NoCraftCost/NoBuildCost via `Piece.FreeBuildKey()` (:10805, :12261, :48821, :48851, :51528, :136327, definition :136619-136626), Fire (:101214), PlayerEvents (:107145, :107227), WorldLevelLockedTools (:131002), NoHeavySnow/AllHeavySnow (:149749), NoBuildingFall (:149825), and the 17 numeric rate keys in `Game.UpdateWorldRates` (:101131-101147).

facts.implication: Complete map of what a server-only mod can influence through this channel. Note the rate keys are the only ones with a numeric value payload and the only ones that BOTH sides recompute independently (Game.UpdateWorldRates runs on server and client alike).

facts.claim: `Version.World.GlobalKeys = 32` is the .fwl world-version gate for reading `m_startingGlobalKeys` back.
facts.implication: Any world at or above this version round-trips modifier keys; no compatibility concern for 1.0.7 worlds.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.CheckKey(string key, GameKeyType type = Global, bool trueWhenKeySet = true)` is the generic gate used by prefab data; for `GameKeyType.Player` it returns false outright when `Player.m_localPlayer` is null.
facts.implication: On a dedicated server every Player-scoped key check is a hard false. Only Global-type checks are meaningful server-side — another reason the global key set is the mod's only usable key channel.

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string name) / SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key) / SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key, float value)
apis.notes: Public, no publicizer needed. Body is only InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name); on the server the target is itself so RPC_SetGlobalKey runs SYNCHRONOUSLY and the key is readable on return. The float overload formats as "{key} {value}" with InvariantCulture. The GlobalKeys overload stringifies PascalCase, which defeats RPC_SetGlobalKey's case-sensitive dedupe — prefer the lowercase string form ("noportals", "teleportall", "nobossportals", "dungeonbuild").

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.RemoveGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key) / RemoveGlobalKey(string name)
apis.notes: The GlobalKeys overload lowercases; the string overload does not (GetKeyValue lowercases downstream anyway). Routes to RPC_RemoveGlobalKey → GlobalKeyRemove → SendGlobalKeys(0L) only if the key was actually present.

apis.signature: public bool ZoneSystem.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) / (GlobalKeys, out string) / (GlobalKeys, out float) / (string) / (string, out string); public bool GetGlobalKeyExact(string fullLine); public List<string> GetGlobalKeys()
apis.notes: Enum overload hits m_globalKeysEnums; string overloads hit m_globalKeysValues keyed by the lowercase NAME only (value stripped); GetGlobalKeyExact hits the raw m_globalKeys set including the " value" suffix. GetGlobalKeys() allocates a new List each call — do not poll it per frame.

apis.signature: private void ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd(string keyStr, bool canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true)
apis.notes: Requires <Publicize>true</Publicize> (the sibling mod already does this). Direct write with no RPC and no broadcast — you must call SendGlobalKeys(0L) yourself. Pass canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false to set a portal key for THIS SESSION ONLY without writing it into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (i.e. not persisted to the .fwl and not shown in the browser badge). This is the one way to get a non-persistent NoPortals.

apis.signature: private bool ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyRemove(string keyStr, bool canSaveToServerOptionKeys = true)
apis.notes: Publicizer required. Returns false if the key was absent. Same canSaveToServerOptionKeys semantics — pass false to remove from the live set without touching the persisted world modifier list.

apis.signature: private void ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys(long peer)
apis.notes: Publicizer required. peer == 0L broadcasts to every ready peer. Sends the entire m_globalKeys set; the client ClearGlobalKeys()es first, so this is a replace, not a merge. Also calls Player.m_localPlayer?.UpdateEvents() (null-safe on dedicated).

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys(bool send = true)
apis.notes: Public. Wipes enum ordinals 0..40 then re-adds from ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys. The correct Harmony anchor for re-asserting mod-owned world-modifier keys is a POSTFIX on this (see Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-15). Will call ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance.SetPreset unguarded if a `preset` key exists.

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.ResetGlobalKeys(); public void ZoneSystem.ResetWorldKeys()
apis.notes: ResetWorldKeys removes only ordinals 0..40 (the world modifiers, incl. all four portal keys) — safe. ResetGlobalKeys clears EVERYTHING including defeated_* boss progression, then reloads from the .fwl.
