apis.signature: public static string ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue(string key, out string value, out GlobalKeys gk)
apis.notes: Public static. Splits on the first space, lowercases the name, and yields gk == GlobalKeys.NonServerOption for anything unrecognised. Use it to classify a key as persisted-in-.fwl (gk < NonServerOption) vs persisted-in-.db.

apis.signature: public bool ZoneSystem.CheckKey(string key, GameKeyType type = GameKeyType.Global, bool trueWhenKeySet = true)
apis.notes: Public. GameKeyType.Player always returns false on a dedicated server (Player.m_localPlayer null check).

apis.signature: private readonly HashSet<string> ZoneSystem.m_globalKeys; public HashSet<GlobalKeys> ZoneSystem.m_globalKeysEnums; public Dictionary<string,string> ZoneSystem.m_globalKeysValues
apis.notes: m_globalKeys needs the publicizer; the other two are already public. Read-only use is safe; never add/remove directly or the three containers diverge.

apis.signature: public List<string> ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys; public bool World.m_startingKeysChanged; public void World.SaveWorldFWLData(DateTime now)
apis.notes: Reached as ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (static property). GlobalKeyAdd/Remove already keep it in sync for ordinals < 41, so a mod normally never writes it. Calling SaveWorldFWLData directly forces an immediate .fwl flush if you need a key persisted before the next autosave.

apis.signature: public static ServerOptionsGUI ServerOptionsGUI.m_instance; public void ReadKeys(World); public void SetKeys(World); public void SetPreset(World, WorldPresets); public void SetPreset(World, WorldModifiers, WorldModifierOption); public void SetPreset(World, string combinedString)
apis.notes: m_instance IS non-null on a dedicated server — FejdStartup.ParseServerArguments instantiates the prefab if missing (:97483-97486). SetPreset(world, WorldModifiers.Portals, WorldModifierOption.X) is the vanilla-faithful way to set the portal modifier; it internally calls KeySlider.SetKeys → ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey. The exact key strings it writes live in Inspector data, not the decompile.

apis.signature: public static string ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary(IEnumerable<string> keys, bool alwaysShort = false, string divider = ", "); public static bool SetKeyAndValueIsCheat(string setKeyCommand); public static bool WorldContainsCheatedModifiers(World); public static bool TryConvertModifierKeysToCompactKVP<T>(ICollection<string>, out T); public static WorldModifierOption GetActiveCombatDifficulty()
apis.notes: GetWorldModifierSummary returns the literal string "Error!" if m_presets is null (prefab not initialised) — guard before displaying. TryConvertModifierKeysToCompactKVP is what produces the Steam gametag encoding (GlobalKeys ordinal → value).

apis.signature: public static void Game.UpdateWorldRates(HashSet<string> globalKeys, Dictionary<string,string> globalKeysValues)
apis.notes: Public static; also reachable as the public instance wrapper ZoneSystem.UpdateWorldRates() (:113541). Dereferences Minimap.instance and Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() without null checks — fine on a dedicated server in practice, but do not call it before Game/Minimap exist.

apis.signature: public void ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: targetPeerID 0L = broadcast to all ready peers (and dispatch locally). targetPeerID == own id = local synchronous dispatch only. This is the primitive under SendGlobalKeys; use it directly only if you need a custom key-adjacent channel.

apis.signature: Console commands: `setkey <key[ value]>`, `removekey <key>`, `resetkeys`, `resetworldkeys`, `setworldpreset <WorldPresets>`, `setworldmodifier <WorldModifiers> <WorldModifierOption>`, `listkeys [v]`
apis.notes: All registered onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true — they run on a dedicated server's stdin console and can be issued remotely by an admin client. `listkeys` prints both "Current Keys" (m_globalKeys) and "Server Option Keys" (ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys), which is the exact in-game probe for confirming what a modifier slider writes.

apis.signature: Dedicated-server command-line: `-resetmodifiers`, `-preset <WorldPresets>`, `-modifier <WorldModifiers> <WorldModifierOption>`, `-setkey <key>`
apis.notes: `-modifier Portals <option>` and `-setkey noportals` set world modifiers at boot with zero code. `-setkey` writes straight into createWorld.m_startingGlobalKeys (lowercased) with no cheat check.

gotchas: RPC_SetGlobalKey and RPC_RemoveGlobalKey have ZERO sender validation (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116037). Any connected vanilla client can set or clear `noportals` / `teleportall` on the server. Any mod feature built on these keys is trivially defeated unless the mod also Harmony-prefixes both RPCs to drop packets whose `sender` is not the server's own id.

Setting a portal key at runtime PERMANENTLY edits the world: GlobalKeyAdd mirrors every key with ordinal < NonServerOption(41) into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113511), which is written to the .fwl on the next autosave (ZNet.SaveWorldThread :80632). Removing the mod later leaves `noportals` baked into the world. To set a key for the session only, call the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` instead of SetGlobalKey.
ZoneSystem.Save STRIPS every ordinal < 41 from the .db (:113749-113755). Do not expect to find `noportals` in the world database — looking there and finding nothing is not evidence the key is unset.

ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115906-115910) and re-adds only what is in the .fwl. Any mod-owned world-modifier key must be reapplied in a POSTFIX on that method or it silently vanishes at boot.

`ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies to "NoPortals" (PascalCase, :115938-115941) but the store holds only lowercase, so RPC_SetGlobalKey's `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` guard (:116024) never trips — every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the whole key list. In a polling loop this is a broadcast storm; pass the lowercase literal or pre-check with GetGlobalKey.

SendGlobalKeys is a full replace, not a delta: the client does ClearGlobalKeys() then re-adds (:113473-113481). It is cheap (one small string list) but it also means the server cannot push a partial update, and any client-side key state is destroyed on every server-side key change.

NoBossPortals is a WORLD-WIDE blackout, not a per-fight lock: `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528). One player aggroing Eikthyr blocks every portal for every player on the server. Worse, `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded (BaseAI.SetAlerted :27258), so a client crash mid-fight can leave the counter stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked — a server mod should watch for and zero it.

TeleportAll does NOT make everything teleportable: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` returns false for any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` BEFORE the TeleportAll check (:68862-68869). That gate cannot be lifted by any global key.

A vanilla client shows no sign that portals are disabled — GetHoverText still says `$piece_portal_connected` and UpdatePortal still lights the target-found effect (:143453-143508). The player only discovers the block by walking in. Any 'blocked' affordance must come from somewhere else (e.g. rewriting portal tags, or actually breaking the ZDO pairing).

`noportals` AND `nomap` are both dead on a dedicated server console — nomap's IsServer() branch is nested inside the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283). Do not use nomap as the 'correct' counter-example. `remoteCommand:false` on noportals (:45298) also means an admin cannot fire it from a client console.

World Modifiers, presets and WorldModifierOption are not a separate network channel — they are a GUI over the same keys (ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeys → ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey, :59630-59680). There is no second lever to find.

A `preset <string>` key (GlobalKeys.Preset, ordinal 40) in the world's starting keys causes ServerOptionsGUI.SetPreset to reapply an entire slider key set at boot (:115920-115926), which can clobber a mod's portal keys. Check for it with `listkeys` before assuming your key survives a restart.

The Steam/PlayFab browser 'modifiers' badge is snapshotted in ZNet.OpenServer (:79457) and refreshed only on the registration-retry path or a restart — a live toggle leaves the public listing stale. Cosmetic, but it will confuse operators comparing the badge to `listkeys`.

GlobalKeyAdd unconditionally dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` (:113506-113508) and its UpdateWorldRates tail dereferences `Minimap.instance` (:101203). These survive on a dedicated server only because the headless build instantiates the GUI scene. Any change that strips those objects (or calling GlobalKeyAdd too early in startup) turns a key write into an NRE that aborts before SendGlobalKeys.

`setkey` from the console refuses key+value pairs the modifier GUI could not produce unless the profile is already cheat-flagged (ServerOptionsGUI.SetKeyAndValueIsCheat, :43515). A mod calling the API directly bypasses this — and every add/remove calls Achievements.MarkAchievementDifficultyDirty() (:113505), so key churn has achievement-integrity side effects for players.
openQuestions: The exact key strings each WorldModifierOption of `WorldModifiers.Portals` writes live in `KeySlider.m_settings[].m_keys` / `KeyToggle.m_enabledKey`, which are Unity Inspector/prefab data invisible to the decompile (KeySlider.SliderSetting assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:52976-52986; KeyToggle :53266-53276). Ordinals NoPortals=32 and TeleportAll=35 both sit below NonServerOption, which strongly implies both are Portals-slider outputs, but the mapping option→key is unverified. IN-GAME CHECK: on a dedicated server console run `setworldmodifier Portals <each WorldModifierOption in turn>` then `listkeys` and read the 'Server Option Keys' block — it prints ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys verbatim.

Which WorldModifierOption values the Portals slider actually offers (m_modifierSetups is built at runtime from prefab children in ServerOptionsGUI.Initizalize, :59762-59781). IN-GAME CHECK: `setworldmodifier Portals <garbage>` prints 'Invalid input, possible valid values are: ...' (:43571), then try each and see which report 'Missing settings for preset' from SetPreset (:59749).

Whether `Minimap.instance` is genuinely non-null on a 1.0.7 headless dedicated server (Game.UpdateNoMap :101203 dereferences it on every key write). Strong indirect evidence yes — the sibling mod calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server (Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesEngine.cs:55) — but not provable from the decompile. IN-GAME CHECK: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm the log shows no NullReferenceException and that connected clients immediately get `$msg_blocked` on portal entry.

Whether `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary` works headless — it returns the literal string 'Error!' when `m_presets == null` (:59792-59796), and m_presets is populated from prefab children in Awake (:59601). FejdStartup instantiates the prefab on the server path (:97483), so it should be populated. IN-GAME CHECK: `listkeys` on the dedicated console, or inspect the log line 'Saving modifier preset:' after `setworldmodifier`.

Whether the Steam/PlayFab listing ever re-registers after a live key change without a restart (only the failure-retry coroutine re-snapshots, :79436-79462). IN-GAME CHECK: set `noportals` at runtime on a public server, then look at the server-browser modifiers badge from a second machine before and after a restart.

Whether a dedicated server ever instantiates a boss Character (and therefore whether the server itself can ever move the `activeBosses` counter). Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every step (:100464), which should mean never — but ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects still runs and no explicit IsDedicated() guard exists on it (:82268). IN-GAME CHECK: `setkey nobossportals`, aggro a boss with one client, then read `listkeys` on the server console and watch `activeBosses` appear/decrement; also confirm it returns to 0 after the boss dies and after a client force-quits mid-fight.
correctionsToExistingSpec: TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 72 is half wrong. The `noportals` claim is CONFIRMED (body entirely inside `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45286), but the stated contrast — that `nomap` 'correctly branches on ZNet.instance.IsServer()' — is false. nomap's IsServer() branch is NESTED INSIDE the identical `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283, guard at :45263, IsServer at :45270), so nomap is exactly as inert on a dedicated server console. Rewrite as: both commands are local-player-only; neither is usable server-side; noportals additionally has remoteCommand:false so an admin cannot fire it remotely either.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 71 ('mutate that list alongside any runtime key change') describes work vanilla already does. `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd` automatically adds every key with ordinal < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption — which includes all of noportals/nobossportals/dungeonbuild/teleportall — into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113488, :113511), and GlobalKeyRemove removes it (:113524-113527). The real fact is the inverse problem: the mod cannot avoid persisting these keys unless it calls the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false)`. Also, the snapshot is re-taken on the Steam registration-retry path (:79436-79462), not literally 'once'.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 65 should note that `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` is PUBLIC and dispatches synchronously on the server (:115943, ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC :83585-83590), so the GlobalKeyAdd+SendGlobalKeys publicizer pair from WorldRatesEngine.cs is an optimization (avoids the re-broadcast and gives access to canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false), not a requirement.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 65's TeleportAll bullet needs a carve-out: TeleportAll does NOT lift the `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` block, which is tested before the key in Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68862-68869). 'Allow-all cargo' is not literally all.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 67 ('Auto-disable during boss fights — NoBossPortals; vanilla computes "is a boss active" itself') understates the scope. The condition is global — `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528) — so it blocks EVERY portal for EVERY player server-wide whenever any boss anywhere is alerted, not just for fight participants. It also has a second, entirely different implementation for dungeon doors that is position-based (`Teleport.Interact`, :143355), so setting the key changes two unrelated behaviours.

Both line 66 (NoPortals) and line 70 (DungeonBuild) should state the persistence consequence explicitly: these are ordinal-<41 world-modifier keys, so enabling one rewrites the world's .fwl modifier list, changes the advertised server-browser badge, reappears automatically at next boot via SetStartingGlobalKeys, and marks achievement difficulty dirty (:113505). Turning the feature off later requires an explicit RemoveGlobalKey; simply disabling the mod leaves the key in the world.

research.topic: TeleportWorld / TeleportWorldTrigger complete anatomy (Valheim 1.0.7, server vs client assembly)
research.summary: `TeleportWorld` and `TeleportWorldTrigger` are byte-identical between `assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs` (:143402-143682) and `assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs` (:144142-144422) — `diff` of the two regions is empty. The class therefore differs only in *whether it runs*, and on a dedicated server it never does: the SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` (:100458-100466) pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition` to `(1000000,0,1000000)` unconditionally — a line that exists in NO form in the client assembly — so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects`/`CreateObjectsSorted` (:82268, :82105) only ever instantiate ZDOs in a sector 1e6 metres out where no world ZDO lives. No portal GameObject, no `TeleportWorld` component, no trigger collider, no `Player` component (`Player.Awake` :10032 is what fills `s_players`) exists server-side, so `Awake`, `Update`, `UpdatePortal`, `Interact`, `GetHoverText`, `SetText`, `RPC_SetTag` and `Teleport` are all unreachable on a dedicated server. Of the 10 public fields, exactly ZERO are ZDO-backed or RPC'd — `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot`, the colours and the effect refs are plain Inspector-compiled fields, so every per-portal behavioural knob is dead to a server-only mod. What IS server-authoritative is the ZDO layer: `ZDOVars.s_tag` / `s_tagauthor` (two strings, no cap, no filter at write time — `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` in the SERVER build at :94588) and the `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal` connection, which IS network-serialized to clients (`ZDO.Serialize` :74112/:74170-74174) and is re-evaluated by the server-only `Game.ConnectPortals()` coroutine every 5s (:100074, :100589). Two genuine server→vanilla-client teleport RPCs exist and do not touch portals at all: `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` (:41627/:41962) and `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (:886/:4126).

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld` and `TeleportWorldTrigger` are byte-for-byte identical in the server and client decompiles. Extracting server lines 143402-143690 and client lines 144142-144430 and running `diff -u` produces zero output (exit 0). Client line = server line + 740 throughout.
facts.implication: There is no server-specific portal code path to hook. Any behavioural difference is purely about which process instantiates the component, not about differing code.

facts.claim: The SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick. Grepping the literal `SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f` matches ONLY the server assembly — the client's `Game.FixedUpdate` has no such line.
facts.implication: Hard proof (not inference) that the dedicated server's active area is parked 1e6 m outside the world. Confirms the central constraint by mechanism, not just by `Player.m_localPlayer` being null.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` computes its zone from `ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition()`, and `CreateObjectsSorted` returns immediately unless `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` and only instantiates ZDOs returned by `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` for that zone.
facts.implication: No world ZDO is ever turned into a GameObject on a dedicated server, so no `TeleportWorld` MonoBehaviour instance ever exists. `Awake`, `Update`, `UpdatePortal` and the RPC registrations never run server-side.

facts.claim: `Player.Awake` is what adds a player to the static `Player.s_players` list, and `Player.GetClosestPlayer` iterates only that list.
facts.implication: `s_players` is permanently empty on a dedicated server, so `Player.GetClosestPlayer` always returns null there. Any mod idea that reaches players via `GetClosestPlayer`/`GetAllPlayers` is dead; use `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` / ZDO scans instead.

facts.claim: TeleportWorld's full member list is: `Awake`, `GetHoverText`, `GetHoverName`, `Interact`, `UseItem`, `UpdatePortal`, `Update`, `Teleport`, `GetText`, `GetTagInfo`, `GetTagSignature`, `SetText`, `RPC_SetTag`, `SetConnectedPortal`, `RPC_SetConnected`, `HaveTarget`, `TargetFound`, `GetHoverOffset`. There is NO `Start` and NO `OnDestroy`.
facts.implication: No cleanup hook exists to patch. `InvokeRepeating("UpdatePortal", 0.5f, 0.5f)` started in Awake runs for the component's whole lifetime and is cancelled only by GameObject destruction.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Awake` disables the component outright when the ZNetView has no ZDO, then caches `m_hadTarget = HaveTarget()`, registers `RPC_SetTag` (string,string) and `RPC_SetConnected` (ZDOID), and starts `InvokeRepeating("UpdatePortal", 0.5f, 0.5f)`.
facts.citation: TeleportWorld.Awake — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143439-143451 (register RPC_SetTag at :143448, RPC_SetConnected at :143449, InvokeRepeating at :143450)
facts.implication: The `RPC_SetTag` handler only exists on machines that have instantiated the portal GameObject. A dedicated server never registers it and therefore can neither receive nor locally dispatch it via ZNetView.

facts.claim: Every public field of TeleportWorld is a plain Inspector-compiled value with no ZDO read/write and no RPC anywhere in the assembly: `m_activationRange = 5f` (:143411), `m_exitDistance = 1f` (:143413), `m_proximityRoot` Transform (:143415), `m_colorUnconnected` (:143418), `m_colorTargetfound` (:143421), `m_target_found` EffectFade (:143423), `m_model` MeshRenderer (:143425), `m_connected` EffectList (:143427), `m_allowAllItems` bool (:143429), `m_hoverOffset` float (:143431). Private state: `m_nview` (:143433), `m_hadTarget` (:143435), `m_colorAlpha` (:143437).
facts.implication: ZERO per-portal knobs are network-reachable. A Harmony write to `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance` or `m_activationRange` on the server mutates a copy that no player will ever read. Per-portal 'allow all items' and per-portal exit offset are both impossible server-side.

facts.claim: The only ZDOVars keys `TeleportWorld` touches are `ZDOVars.s_tag` ("tag") and `ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` ("tagauthor"), both strings, read in `GetTagInfo`/`GetTagSignature` and written in `RPC_SetTag`. The destination is NOT a ZDOVars key — it is the separate `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal` connection slot.
facts.citation: ZDOVars.s_tag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617; ZDOVars.s_tagauthor — :78619; reads at TeleportWorld.GetTagInfo :143563/:143565 and GetTagSignature :143575-143576; writes at RPC_SetTag :143598-143599
facts.implication: A server mod rewrites a portal's name with two `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, ...)` / `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, ...)` calls and its destination with `zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, targetId)`. There is no third field to worry about.

facts.claim: The 10-character tag cap is enforced ONLY by the client's text-input widget: `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` and `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit`. `RPC_SetTag` performs no length check of any kind.
facts.implication: A server-only mod can write tags of arbitrary length into `s_tag` and vanilla clients will display and match them. Reserved-prefix / long descriptive admin tags are viable. Conversely a server-side cap must be implemented by the mod itself.

facts.claim: Profanity handling is display-only and, in the dedicated-server assembly, entirely absent: `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC(text, ugcType, userId, playerId, handler)` in the SERVER build has the body `return text;`. The client build's version early-returns unless `ugcType == UGCType.ServerName || RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()`.
facts.implication: Calling `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` from a server plugin is a no-op — it would silently do nothing. A server-side profanity filter must use `CensorShittyWords.Filter(input, out output)` (:94295), which IS fully implemented in the server assembly, or the mod's own list.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.GetTagInfo` sets `result.censored = CensorShittyWords.Filter(rawTag, out _)` and `GetHoverText` only surfaces the `$piece_portal_censored_warning` line when `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab`.
facts.implication: On a Steam/dedicated-server backend the censored flag is computed and then discarded. The raw tag string in the ZDO is what every PC player actually sees.

facts.claim: `GetHoverText` strips rich text from the tag via `RemoveRichTextTags()`, which is `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\\\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", "")`.
facts.implication: Colour/size markup written into `s_tag` by a server mod will be stripped from the hover label. Do not plan on coloured portal names via the tag field.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.GetHoverName()` returns the hard-coded literal `"Teleport"`, not the tag and not a localization key.
facts.implication: The portal's hover *name* cannot be changed by any ZDO write. Only the hover *text* (which embeds the tag) is data-driven.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Interact` runs `PrivateArea.CheckAccess(transform.position)` before opening the rename dialog; `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` iterates the static `m_allAreas` list of instantiated `PrivateArea` MonoBehaviours and calls `HaveLocalAccess()`, which consults `m_piece.IsCreator()` / local player id.
facts.implication: Ward protection of the rename action is entirely client-side and unverified by the server. On a server `m_allAreas` is empty and `CheckAccess` would trivially return true. Server-side ward gating of retag needs a mod-maintained shadow ward list.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld` implements `TextReceiver` as `GetText()` → `GetTagInfo().text` (the FilterUGC-passed tag) and `SetText(text)` → `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", text, PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString())`. `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...)` routes to `m_zdo.GetOwner()`.
facts.implication: The rename RPC goes to whichever peer owns the portal ZDO, not to the server. If the server has claimed ownership (the Wonderland `WaterBuoyancyEngine` pattern), the RPC arrives at the server — but the server has no `TeleportWorld` instance to dispatch it to, so it lands in `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC` on nothing. Interception must be done at the `ZRoutedRpc`/`ZDOMan` layer, not on the component.

facts.claim: `RPC_SetTag(long sender, string tag, string authorId)` no-ops unless `m_nview.IsValid() && m_nview.IsOwner()`; if the tag or author actually changed it (a) clears its own Portal connection via `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`, (b) re-reads the (now-None) connection and passes it to `SetConnectedPortal`, (c) writes `s_tag` and `s_tagauthor`. The `sender` argument is never validated against `authorId`.
facts.implication: `authorId` is an unverified client self-report — any client can claim any PlatformUserID as the tag author. Also note the step-(b) bug: by the time `SetConnectedPortal` is called the connection has already been cleared to None, so the old partner is usually never notified and is left to be repaired by `Game.ConnectPortals()`'s 5-second self-heal pass.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly four early-exit decision points before the move, in order: (1) `!TargetFound()` → silent return; (2) `ZoneSystem.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` → `$msg_blocked`; (3) `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0f))` → `$msg_blockedbyboss`; (4) `!player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)` → `$msg_noteleport`.
facts.implication: All four gates are CLIENT-ONLY at the point of execution. Gates 2 and 3 read global keys the SERVER owns and broadcasts, so they are server-influenceable but client-honored. Gate 1 reads the ZDO connection the server can force to None, making it the only server-ENFORCED gate. Gate 4 is unreachable and un-influenceable per-portal.

facts.claim: After the gates, `Teleport()` resolves `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(m_nview.GetZDO().GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal))` fresh, then computes `pos = targetZdo.GetPosition() + (targetZdo.GetRotation() * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` and calls `player.TeleportTo(pos, targetRotation, distantTeleport: true)`, finally `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat(PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed)`.
facts.implication: The destination is read at the instant of transit from live ZDO state, NOT cached. A server-side rotation of a hub's connection takes effect on the very next transit with no client refresh needed. Exit offset uses the DESTINATION portal's own `m_exitDistance` (1.0 by default) — a compiled field, not tunable. `distantTeleport: true` means the player gets the 2-15s loading-screen path in `Player.UpdateTeleport`.

facts.claim: `Player.TeleportTo` refuses if `IsTeleporting()` or if `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, and forwards to the owning client via `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_TeleportTo", ...)` when not owner. `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is registered on EVERY Character's ZNetView in `Character.Awake` and itself re-checks `m_nview.IsOwner()`.
facts.implication: A server mod can force-teleport any vanilla client by invoking the routed RPC `RPC_TeleportTo` against that player's character ZDO and its owner peer. A second forced teleport within 2 seconds of a previous one silently no-ops with no feedback on either side.

facts.claim: `Chat.Awake` registers `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportPlayer", RPC_TeleportPlayer)`; the handler body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. `Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, Vector3, Quaternion, bool)` is a public wrapper over `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", ...)`.
facts.implication: This is a genuine, no-ZDO-needed server→vanilla-client teleport path. Because `Chat.instance` may not exist on a dedicated server, call `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distant)` directly instead of going through `Chat`.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorldTrigger` is a 19-line class: `Awake` does `m_teleportWorld = GetComponentInParent<TeleportWorld>()`, and `OnTriggerEnter(Collider colliderIn)` requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component` before calling `m_teleportWorld.Teleport(component)`. It is the ONLY caller of `TeleportWorld.Teleport` in the entire assembly.
facts.citation: TeleportWorldTrigger — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143664-143682 (only call site of Teleport at :143679); grep for `.Teleport(` on TeleportWorld yields one hit
facts.implication: CONFIRMED: the central constraint holds. Three independent gates make it client-only — no trigger GameObject exists, no Player GameObject exists, and `Player.m_localPlayer` is null. The collider requirement is `GetComponent<Player>()` on the colliding collider itself (the Player's own capsule, not a child collider).

facts.claim: `UpdatePortal` (the 0.5s repeat) only drives visuals: it early-returns unless `m_nview.IsValid() && m_proximityRoot != null`, spawns `m_connected` EffectList when `HaveTarget()` newly flips true, and sets `m_target_found.SetActive(closestPlayer.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems) && TargetFound())`. `Update()` only lerps `m_colorAlpha` into `m_model.material.SetColor("_EmissionColor", ...)`.
facts.implication: The 0.5s poll has NO gameplay effect — it does not gate teleporting. A server-side destination change is honoured instantly at transit time (which re-reads the connection), so the 'destination can change under a standing player within 0.5s' framing is about the glow effect, not the route.

facts.claim: `HaveTarget()` returns `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`. `TargetFound()` additionally requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionId) != null`, and when the target ZDO is not locally present it fires `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(connectionId)` and returns false.
facts.implication: Teleporting requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO, not merely know its id. A newly-server-written connection to a far-away portal means the first walk-through fails silently (returns at gate 1) while `RequestZDO` fetches it; the second attempt succeeds. Plan for a one-transit warm-up after any server-side re-pair.

facts.claim: The Portal connection IS network-serialized: `ZDO.Serialize` sets `ExtraDataFlags.Connections` and writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` + `connectionData.m_target`; `ZDO.Deserialize` reads them back into `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection`. `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` also call `IncreaseDataRevision()` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.
facts.implication: A server-side `SetConnection` genuinely reaches vanilla clients over the wire. This is the load-bearing fact that makes server-only portal re-routing possible at all.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals()` is public and started only server-side: `Game.Start` wraps `StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` in `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`, and the coroutine loops `ConnectPortals(); yield return new WaitForSeconds(5f);`.
facts.implication: Confirmed server-reachable. `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` can be called on demand for instant re-pairing, and its 5s cadence is the window in which any custom pairing must survive.

facts.claim: `ConnectPortals()` pass 1 BREAKS any connection whose partner is null, whose partner's `s_tag` differs from its own, or whose partner's own connection is None — `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)`. Pass 2 pairs each unconnected portal with `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal`, which filters on exact string equality of `s_tag` and picks with `UnityEngine.Random.Range`.
facts.citation: Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100622 (tag-equality teardown at :100601, random pick at :100678); Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — :100664-100679
facts.implication: Cross-tag and one-way links are actively destroyed every 5 seconds by vanilla itself. Any custom topology either keeps every member on one identical literal tag string, or must patch/prefix `Game.ConnectPortals` — a faster re-write timer alone loses the race half the time.

facts.claim: `Game.SetConnection(ZDO, ZDOID, bool)` (private) is the reference recipe: if the portal has no owner, its owner is offline, or `forceImmediateConnection`, it does `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(Portal, connection); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.m_uid);` — otherwise it routes `RPC_SetConnection` to the owning peer. `Game.RPC_SetConnection` is registered on EVERY peer (not server-gated) in `Game.Start`.
facts.implication: A server mod re-pairs portals with exactly those three lines, and for a portal a live client owns it can instead invoke the vanilla routed RPC `RPC_SetConnection(portalZdoId, targetZdoId)` at that peer — a documented, vanilla-honoured server→client instruction.

facts.claim: Portal ZDOs are deliberately excluded from the normal sector map: `ZDO.SetSector` returns immediately if `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(GetPrefab())`, and `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` files them in the separate `m_portalObjects` dictionary AND calls `RemoveFromSector`. `ZDOMan.FindObjects` (used by `FindSectorObjects`) re-merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` back in.
facts.implication: Wonderland's `ZdoSpatialQuery` (which routes through `FindSectorObjects`) DOES see portals — no correction needed there. But because `SetSector` is a no-op for portals, calling `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal never re-files it: it stays keyed under its original sector in `m_portalObjects` forever. Moving a portal server-side silently breaks its delivery to clients in the new zone.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (List<ZDO>) and `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>) are both public. `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is a public `List<int>` populated in `Game.Awake` from `foreach (GameObject p in m_portalPrefabs) PortalPrefabHash.Add(p.name.GetStableHashCode())`, where `m_portalPrefabs` is a public `List<GameObject>` Inspector field.
facts.implication: Free, complete, O(1)-access enumeration of every portal in the world with zero bookkeeping — the basis for admin listings, orphan detection and topology management. And `Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs` is readable at runtime, so the authoritative portal prefab NAME list can be dumped in-game rather than guessed.

facts.claim: No portal prefab name string (`portal_wood`, `portal_stone`, `portal`) appears anywhere in the server or utils decompiles — the only portal-related literals are localization keys (`$piece_portal`, `$piece_portal_tag`, `$piece_portal_connected`, `$piece_portal_unconnected`, `$piece_portal_censored_warning`, `$piece_portal_settag`, `$msg_portal_blocked`). The sibling client mod TortalPortal hard-codes exactly two: `portal_wood` and `portal_stone`.
facts.citation: grep of portal string literals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143461-143482, :15373; TortalPortal/ScatterCommand.cs:158 (`ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood")`); TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:217-219 (`GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative("portal_wood"...)`, `("portal_stone"...)`)
facts.implication: Prefab names and per-prefab `m_allowAllItems` defaults live in AssetBundle data, not code. Never hard-code the list — read `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` / `m_portalPrefabs` at runtime so modded portal pieces are covered for free.

facts.claim: `Inventory.IsTeleportable(bool allowAllItems)` first rejects outright if ANY item has `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000`, and only THEN honours `allowAllItems || ZoneSystem.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.TeleportAll)`; otherwise every item must have `m_shared.m_teleportable`. `Humanoid.IsTeleportable` just forwards to it.
facts.citation: Inventory.IsTeleportable — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880 (toolTier gate at :68864, TeleportAll at :68869); Humanoid.IsTeleportable — :8791-8794
facts.implication: The `TeleportAll` global key does NOT unblock everything — items with `m_toolTier >= 1000` are permanently non-teleportable regardless of the key or of `m_allowAllItems`. Any 'allow all cargo' feature must be advertised with that caveat.

facts.claim: Global keys are server-authoritative and broadcast: `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string)` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)`, which on the server resolves to its own peer id and runs `RPC_SetGlobalKey` locally, then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` broadcasts the whole key list to every peer, and each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and rebuilds its local set.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115943-115946; ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys — :113466-113471; RPC_GlobalKeys — :113473-113481; registration — :113447; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch — :83586-83593
facts.implication: `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, `TeleportAll` and `DungeonBuild` are all cleanly settable from a server-only mod and honoured by unmodified clients exactly as vanilla honours them. This is the 'vanilla-respecting' tier.

facts.claim: The built-in `noportals` console command's entire body is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`, unlike the adjacent `nomap` command which correctly branches on `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` for the global-key half.
facts.implication: CONFIRMED inert from a dedicated server console. A mod must call `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` / `RemoveGlobalKey` directly rather than shelling the vanilla command.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)` is public but does NOT set the ZDO's prefab, persistence, type or rotation — it only pools a ZDO, sets owner to the session id, calls `AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash)` and indexes it. `ZNetView.Awake` shows the required follow-up: `zdo.Persistent = m_persistent; zdo.Type = m_type; zdo.Distant = m_distant; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);`.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692; ZNetView.Awake fabrication block — :82613-82620; ZDO.SetPrefab — :73808-73815; ZDO.Persistent setter — :73323-73340
facts.implication: Fabricating a phantom destination portal server-side works, but `CreateNewZDO` alone produces a non-persistent, prefab-less ZDO that will not survive a save. All five follow-up lines are mandatory. Note `AddIfPortal` fires on the passed hash before `SetPrefab`, so portal registration still works if the hash is supplied to `CreateNewZDO`.

facts.claim: `EffectFade.Awake` grabs `ParticleSystem[]`, `Light` and `AudioSource` from children and its `Update` drives light intensity and audio volume; `TeleportWorld.m_target_found` is a direct reference to one such component.
facts.implication: The 'portal is glowing / ready' feedback is pure local Unity presentation with zero network component. Nothing about a portal's visual state can be driven or read from the server.

facts.claim: `class Teleport` (dungeon doors, distinct from `TeleportWorld`) uses a direct `Teleport m_targetPoint` component reference, not a ZDO connection, and its own narrower boss gate `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos)`; it also increments `PortalDungeonIn`/`PortalDungeonOut` rather than `PortalsUsed`.
facts.citation: Teleport class — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316-143388 (m_targetPoint field :143322, boss gate :143355, stats :143362); Teleport.OnTriggerEnter local-player gate — :143336-143343
facts.implication: Dungeon teleports have NO ZDO layer at all — they are Transform-to-Transform inside a prefab. A server-only mod cannot re-route, audit, or even observe them; the only shared lever is the `NoBossPortals` global key.

apis.signature: List<ZDO> ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()
apis.notes: Flattens m_portalObjects into a fresh List<ZDO>. Allocates on every call — cache it if polling. Returns portals for the ENTIRE world, not a region.

apis.signature: Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Live reference to the internal dictionary — do not mutate. Wonderland's PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit already uses this exact call. Keys are stale if a portal ZDO was ever moved server-side (ZDO.SetSector is a no-op for portals, :73752).

apis.signature: void Game.instance.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: Public. Safe to call on demand for instant re-pairing after a tag write. Also runs itself every 5s from ConnectPortalsCoroutine (:100580), started only when ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:100069-100074). Its pass-1 teardown (:100601) will destroy any connection whose partner's s_tag differs.

apis.signature: List<int> Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash  /  public List<GameObject> Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs
apis.notes: Both public. PortalPrefabHash is filled in Game.Awake (:100027-100032) from prefab .name.GetStableHashCode(). Read m_portalPrefabs at runtime to learn the real prefab names instead of hard-coding portal_wood/portal_stone.

apis.signature: ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)
apis.notes: Use ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal (value 1, :74747-74754). Returns ZDOID.None when unconnected or when the stored connection has a different type.

apis.signature: void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: Writes the connection, bumps DataRevision and flags ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals(). Caller MUST own the ZDO first (zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())) and should follow with ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid) — this is exactly what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645.

apis.signature: void ZDO.UpdateConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: Differs from SetConnection: it only writes if a connection entry ALREADY exists for this ZDO (ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection :74962-74975 returns false when the key is absent). Use SetConnection to create, UpdateConnection to modify.

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id)  /  ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)
apis.notes: The single-arg form pushes to every peer. Required after any server-side portal ZDO edit or the change may wait for the ordinary sync sweep.

apis.signature: static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()
apis.notes: The server's own peer id. Pass to zdo.SetOwner() to claim a ZDO before writing it — the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ownership-claim pattern.

apis.signature: ZDO ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)
apis.notes: Public. Does NOT set prefab/persistence/type/rotation. Follow with zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot); — mirroring ZNetView.Awake :82613-82620. AddIfPortal fires on the hash you pass, so a portal-hash ZDO is registered correctly.

apis.signature: void ZDO.Set(int hash, string value)  — with ZDOVars.s_tag / ZDOVars.s_tagauthor
apis.notes: No length cap, no filtering, no validation at this layer. Claim ownership first. Rich-text markup will be stripped from the hover label by RemoveRichTextTags (:143459).

apis.signature: string ZDO.GetString(int hash, string defaultValue = "")
apis.notes: Reading s_tag needs no ownership.

apis.signature: void ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: Use with "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos (Vector3), rot (Quaternion), distantTeleport (bool) to force a vanilla client's local player to teleport — handler at Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962, registered at :41627. Bypasses Chat.instance entirely on the server side. targetPeerID 0 broadcasts.

apis.signature: void ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: Use with the player's character ZDO owner + ZDOID and "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, distantTeleport — handler Character.RPC_TeleportTo :4126, registered for every Character at Character.Awake :886. More precise than RPC_TeleportPlayer because it addresses a specific character ZDO. Also the channel for Game's "RPC_SetConnection" (portalId, targetId) — registered on every peer at Game.Start :100066, handler :100653.

apis.signature: void ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key)  /  SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key, float value)  /  RemoveGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key)
apis.notes: Routed through ZRoutedRpc; on the server it self-dispatches to RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022) which then broadcasts the whole key list via SendGlobalKeys(0L) (:113466). Relevant keys: NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll, DungeonBuild, activeBosses (GlobalKeys enum :101269-101323).

apis.signature: bool ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key)  /  GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key, out float value)
apis.notes: Plain dictionary lookups against m_globalKeysEnums / m_globalKeysValues (:113309). The float overload lowercases the enum name as the lookup key.

apis.signature: bool CensorShittyWords.Filter(string input, out string output)
apis.notes: Fully implemented in the SERVER assembly (unlike FilterUGC, which is `return text;` at :94588). Returns true if anything was censored and hands back the masked string. Use this if a server-side tag profanity filter is wanted.

apis.signature: bool ZDOMan.instance.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO> zdos, ref int index)
apis.notes: Time-sliced; call in a loop until it returns true. It explicitly walks m_portalObjects (:77457-77470) so it does find portals — but GetPortalList() is strictly better for portals since it needs no prefab-name guess.

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.instance.FindSectorObjects(Vector2s sector, SimulationDistance simulationDistance, List<ZDO> sectorObjects, List<ZDO> distantSectorObjects = null)
apis.notes: Routes through FindObjects (:77366) which merges m_portalObjects back in, so Wonderland's ZdoSpatialQuery DOES return portals. No correction needed to that helper.

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Exists but is the CLIENT's mechanism for pulling a missing destination ZDO. Relevant only as an explanation of why the first transit after a server-side re-pair to a distant portal can silently fail.

gotchas: The server and client copies of TeleportWorld are IDENTICAL source — `diff` of assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143402-143690 against assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144142-144430 is empty. Do not look for a server-specific portal code path; there isn't one. The real server/client divergence is in Game.FixedUpdate (SERVER-only reference-position pin at :100465).

`TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` is `public` and shows up in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable from a server plugin. It is not usefully callable: no TeleportWorld instance ever exists server-side (no GameObject is instantiated), `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs MessageHud.instance, and `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own local profile file.

`TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only. A player already standing inside a portal's trigger volume when the server rewrites its destination will NOT re-trigger — they must step out and back in. This is the real constraint on time-sliced hub rotation, not the 0.5s UpdatePortal poll (which only drives the glow).

Conversely, the destination is NOT cached anywhere: Teleport() re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` and the target ZDO's live position/rotation at the instant of transit (:143539-143543). A server-side re-route applies to the very next walk-through with no client refresh.

`TargetFound()` requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO, not just its id; when absent it calls `RequestZDO` and returns false (:143646-143654). The first transit after a server-side re-pair to a portal in an unvisited region can silently fail with no message at all (gate 1 returns without calling player.Message).

`ZDO.SetSector` returns immediately for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73755). A portal ZDO is filed in `m_portalObjects` under whatever sector it had when `AddIfPortal` last ran. Calling `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal server-side therefore leaves it keyed under its OLD sector forever — clients in the new zone will never receive it through normal sector sync. Moving a portal requires manual re-filing or permanent ForceSendZDO.

`CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the dedicated-server assembly (:94588-94591). A server plugin that calls it as a filter will silently filter nothing. `CensorShittyWords.Filter` (:94295) is the one that actually works server-side.

`RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` parameter is a raw client self-report and is never cross-checked against `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` or the owning ZNetPeer (:143587-143602). Any identity decision keyed off tagauthor is spoofable.

There is a latent vanilla bug in `RPC_SetTag`: it calls `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` BEFORE re-reading the connection to pass to `SetConnectedPortal` (:143595-143597), so the old partner is generally never told. Repair happens only on the next `Game.ConnectPortals()` sweep up to 5s later. Do not model a rename as an atomic two-sided unlink.

`Game.ConnectPortals()` pass 1 tears down any connection whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601). Cross-tag links, one-way links and distinct per-portal display names inside one group are all actively destroyed every 5 seconds by vanilla. A faster mod timer does not reliably win that race — patching or prefixing ConnectPortals is required.

`GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` does NOT allow everything: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` rejects any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` before it ever consults `allowAllItems` or `TeleportAll` (:68862-68870). An 'all cargo allowed' feature must carry that caveat.

`m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot` and all colour/effect refs are plain compiled Inspector fields (:143411-143431) with zero ZDO or RPC involvement. Harmony-writing any of them on the server mutates a copy no client will ever read. There is no per-portal item policy and no per-portal exit offset, full stop.

The vanilla `noportals` console command is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (:45285) and is inert on a dedicated server console — unlike the adjacent `nomap` which correctly branches on `IsServer()` (:45270). Use `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` directly.

`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash)` does not set the prefab, persistence, type or rotation (:76684-76692). A portal ZDO fabricated with it alone is non-persistent and prefab-less and will vanish on world save. Replicate all five lines from ZNetView.Awake (:82616-82620).

`PrivateArea.CheckAccess` iterates the static `m_allAreas` list of instantiated MonoBehaviours and calls `HaveLocalAccess()` (:137547-137594). On a dedicated server that list is empty, so it returns true for everything — it is not usable as a server-side authorization primitive at all.

A server-issued forced teleport (either RPC path) silently no-ops if the target player teleported within the last 2 seconds or is mid-teleport — `Player.TeleportTo` returns false at :15308-15316 with no message on either side.
openQuestions: Which prefabs are actually in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:99828)? The list is Unity Inspector data and no portal prefab name string appears anywhere in the decompiles. IN-GAME CHECK: on a running dedicated server, log `string.Join(",", Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs.Select(p => p.name))` and `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` from a BepInEx plugin at first Heartbeat. This is the only authoritative answer and it also covers modded portal pieces.

What is each portal prefab's baked `m_allowAllItems` value (the Ashlands stone portal is widely believed to be true)? Field at :143429 is Inspector data. IN-GAME CHECK: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(<name>).GetComponent<TeleportWorld>().m_allowAllItems` on a client (the server has no prefab-instantiated components to read from a ZDO, though ZNetScene's prefab table itself may still be populated server-side — verify that too). Purely informational: the field cannot be changed over the network regardless of its value.

What is the actual collider geometry/size on the TeleportWorldTrigger child object, and is it on a child of the TeleportWorld GameObject (Awake uses GetComponentInParent, :143670)? Unity asset data. IN-GAME CHECK: inspect the portal prefab hierarchy in a client-side Unity/ObjectDumper pass. Only matters if a mod ever wants to reason about the transit volume for a position-straddle heuristic — Wonderland's PositionWatch currently uses a flat 40 m radius instead.

Does `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` / `GetPrefab()` return non-null on a dedicated server (i.e. is the prefab table loaded even though nothing is instantiated)? The decompile shows the table exists but proving the server populates it needs a runtime check. IN-GAME CHECK: log `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood") != null` on the server. Determines whether prefab-hash lookups by name are available server-side or whether Game.PortalPrefabHash is the only route.

Does the dedicated server's ZoneSystem actually succeed in creating local zones at (1000000, 0, 1000000) — zone index 15625, within short range — and does that cost anything? `CreateLocalZones(ZNet.instance.GetReferencePosition())` runs at :113930. IN-GAME CHECK: log `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` and `m_zones.Count` on the server. Irrelevant to portal correctness, but relevant if a mod ever wants to move the server's reference position to force server-side instantiation of a region (which would be a very different, much heavier architecture).
correctionsToExistingSpec: REFINES the Central Constraint's reasoning. The spec says '`ZoneSystem`'s local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position'. The stronger and more precise mechanism is: the SERVER assembly's `Game.FixedUpdate` contains a line that does not exist in the client assembly at all — `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465; grep for the literal matches only the server file). Zones ARE created at that position; what makes the server instantiate nothing is that no world ZDO lives there, plus `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105-82112) only walks `FindSectorObjects` for that one sector. Cite :100465 as the primary proof, not the zone system.

CORRECTS 'a player standing at the hub mid-rotation can have their destination change under them (`TargetFound`/`UpdatePortal` poll every 0.5s)'. `UpdatePortal`'s 0.5s InvokeRepeating (:143450) drives ONLY the EffectFade glow and the EffectList spawn — it has zero gameplay effect. The destination is read fresh inside `Teleport()` at :143539-143543. The real constraint is the opposite one: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` (:143673) fires on ENTER only, so a player already standing inside the trigger volume will NOT be teleported by a rotation at all until they step out and back in.

ADDS a hard limit the spec's 'Allow-all cargo through portals' bullet omits. `GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` is checked only AFTER an unconditional rejection loop for `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (Inventory.IsTeleportable, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68862-68870). Some items can never be teleported regardless of `TeleportAll` or `m_allowAllItems`. The feature must be described as 'all cargo except tool-tier-1000+ items'.

CORRECTS the spec's 'vanilla only enforces the 10-char cap in the client UI widget and only profanity-filters at display time' — the second half understates it. On the dedicated server `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is literally `return text;` (:94588-94591), and even on a PC client it early-returns unless `ugcType == ServerName || RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering()` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94907-94910). There is no profanity filtering on PC at display time either. The `censored` warning line is gated on `ZNet.m_onlineBackend == OnlineBackendType.PlayFab` (:143462). Also note that a server-side filter must call `CensorShittyWords.Filter` (:94295, fully implemented server-side), NOT `FilterUGC`.

CORRECTS 'ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash) makes a real, persistent, correctly-owned ZDO with no live GameObject needed'. It does NOT make it persistent and does not even set the prefab on the ZDO — it only pools it, sets owner to the session id, calls AddIfPortal on the hash you passed, and indexes it (:76684-76692). The mod must additionally do `zdo.Persistent = true; zdo.Type = ...; zdo.Distant = false; zdo.SetPrefab(hash); zdo.SetRotation(rot);` exactly as ZNetView.Awake does (:82613-82620), or the fabricated portal disappears on the next world save.

ADDS a gotcha the spec's 'Portal to any computed coordinate' and hub bullets need: `ZDO.SetSector` is a no-op for any prefab in `Game.PortalPrefabHash` (:73752-73755), so portal ZDOs are filed in `m_portalObjects` under the sector they had at registration time and `zdo.SetPosition()` never re-files them. Moving a portal server-side breaks its delivery to clients who enter the new zone. Create-and-destroy, don't move.

REASSURES on a point the spec does not raise: Wonderland's `ZdoSpatialQuery` DOES find portals despite the separate `m_portalObjects` store, because `ZDOMan.FindObjects` (:77366-77381), which `FindSectorObjects` (:77142) calls, explicitly merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` in. No change needed to that helper.

ADDS detail to the Group 3 teleport bullet. Two distinct routed RPCs work, not one: `RPC_TeleportPlayer` (Chat.Awake registration :41627, handler :41962, Vector3/Quaternion/bool, peer-targeted, no ZDO) and `RPC_TeleportTo` (Character.Awake registration :886, handler :4126, same signature, addressed to a specific character ZDO via the 4-arg InvokeRoutedRPC at :83577). The ZDO-addressed `RPC_TeleportTo` is the more precise choice since it names the character rather than trusting the receiving client's `Player.m_localPlayer`.

REFINES 'a fan-in hub member can self-loop to stay connected'. Vanilla's pass-1 teardown at :100601 checks `zDO == null || zDO.GetString(s_tag) != ownTag || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None`. A self-loop (portal connected to itself) passes all three checks trivially — same tag, non-None connection — so it is stable. But `TargetFound()` (:143640) would then succeed and `Teleport()` would move the player to their own portal's position + exitDistance, i.e. a visible 2-second no-op teleport, not an inert portal. That is a worse player experience than the spec implies.

ADDS to the 'Ward-gated portal retag protection' item: the underlying `RPC_SetTag` interception is harder than the spec suggests, because `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, ...)` routes to `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855) and the server has no `TeleportWorld` component to receive it even after claiming ownership — `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC` needs a registered instance (:82836-82848). Interception must happen at the `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`/`ZDOMan` layer, or by simply watching `s_tag` for unexpected changes and reverting them, which is far simpler.

research.topic: rpc-teleport-paths — server→client forced teleport without portals (Valheim 1.0.7, dedicated server)
research.summary: A dedicated server CAN force-move any connected vanilla client, with no client mod, via two independent routed-RPC paths that both funnel into the same method the portal itself uses (`Player.TeleportTo`): the peer-scoped `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (handler registered in `Chat.Awake` on every vanilla client) and the ZDO-scoped `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (handler registered in `Character.Awake`, owner-gated). Neither requires `Chat.instance` on the sender — `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is a one-line wrapper over the public `ZRoutedRpc` API, and the server never needs the method registered locally because `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` forwards by `m_targetPeerID` without a local handler lookup. The only identifier needed is `ZNetPeer.m_uid` (a per-connection long from `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()`); `m_characterID` (ZDOID) is needed only for the ZDO-scoped variant, and the stable cross-session identity (`ZDOVars.s_playerID`) is read off the character ZDO, never used for routing. Every precondition is client-side and silent: `Player.TeleportTo` returns false (no message, no network reply) if the player is already teleporting or if `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, and `Player.UpdateTeleport` only runs inside the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate`, so a dead player's teleport is accepted and then never executed. A `distantTeleport:true` teleport has a hard floor of ~8 seconds of black screen and is visually/audibly identical to a vanilla portal transit, because the "portal VFX" is not portal-specific — `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` keys the teleport animation solely on `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport`. Source dir: /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/libs-Tools/1.0/DECOMPILED/

facts.claim: `Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)` contains exactly one statement: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. It holds no state and touches no Chat field.
facts.implication: A server-only mod never needs Chat.instance. Replicate the one line with ZRoutedRpc.instance directly; calling Chat.instance.TeleportPlayer would NRE if the GUI singleton is absent server-side, for zero benefit.

facts.claim: `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer(long sender, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)` is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender check, no admin check, no distance check, and the bool return of TeleportTo is discarded.
facts.implication: The receiving client gives zero feedback on success or failure. The server gets no ack. A failed teleport is indistinguishable from a delivered one except by watching the character ZDO's position afterwards.

facts.claim: The handler is registered on every vanilla client in `Chat.Awake` via `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportPlayer", RPC_TeleportPlayer)` — confirmed identical in the client assembly (class Chat : Terminal at :41507).
facts.implication: Zero client install required. The RPC name and signature are already live on every unmodified 1.0.7 client.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)` is public and simply forwards to the 4-arg overload with `ZDOID.None` as targetZDO.
facts.implication: This is the exact server-callable entry point. Signature is stable and public — no reflection needed.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)` builds a RoutedRPCData with `m_senderPeerID = m_id`, then: calls `HandleRoutedRPC` locally only if `targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0`, and calls `RouteRPC` only if `targetPeerID != m_id`.
facts.implication: Sending to a specific peer id never runs the method locally, so the server does NOT need the method registered in its own m_functions dictionary. Sending to 0 (Everybody) DOES attempt a local dispatch, which silently misses (see gotchas).

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` on a server with `rpcData.m_targetPeerID != 0` looks up the peer via its private `GetPeer(long uid)` over `m_peers` and invokes `peer.m_rpc.Invoke("RoutedRPC", pkg)` only if `peer != null && peer.IsReady()`. An unknown or not-ready peer id is a silent drop.
facts.implication: Addressing one player is entirely by `long` peer id. A stale id from a disconnected player is a no-op, not an exception — safe to hold ids across ticks, but always re-resolve from ZNet.GetPeers().

facts.claim: `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is a `public long` assigned during the handshake (`peer.m_uid = uid` at ZNet:79905) and `ZNetPeer.IsReady()` is literally `return m_uid != 0`.
facts.implication: m_uid is the ONLY identifier RPC routing accepts. It is a per-connection session id: it changes every time the player reconnects and must never be persisted as identity.

facts.claim: `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` returns the live `List<ZNetPeer> m_peers` (not a copy); `GetConnectedPeers()` returns a copy; `GetPeer(long uid)`, `GetPeerByPlayerName(string)` and `GetPeerByHostName(string)` all linear-scan m_peers and the latter two additionally require `peer.IsReady()`.
facts.implication: Server-side peer enumeration is a public, allocation-free-ish API. GetPeers() returning the live list means do not mutate it; iterate by index or copy if you might disconnect someone mid-loop.

facts.claim: `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` (ZDOID) is set server-side by `ZNet.RPC_CharacterID`, which the client triggers from `ZNet.SetCharacterID` — itself called from `Game.SpawnPlayer` right after the Player prefab is instantiated, and reset to ZDOID.None in `Game._RequestRespawn`.
facts.implication: peer.m_characterID is the server's handle on the player's body, but it is ZDOID.None for a window after connect and again between death and respawn. Always guard with `!peer.m_characterID.IsNone()` before targeting a ZDO-scoped RPC.

facts.claim: `ZNetPeer.m_playerID` (long) is set server-side by `ZNet.RPC_PlayerID`, registered only `if (m_isServer)`; it is the same stable `PlayerProfile.m_playerID` also mirrored into the character ZDO as `ZDOVars.s_playerID`.
facts.implication: Two server-side routes to a persistent player identity: peer.m_playerID directly, or zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID). Use either as the key for a per-player teleport allowance/cooldown table; never m_uid.

facts.claim: The platform identity (SteamID64 for the Steam backend) is `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — `ZSteamSocket.GetHostName()` returns `CSteamID.ToString()`. `ZNet` itself uses this string for the admin/ban lists.
facts.citation: ZSteamSocket.GetHostName, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87018-87021; ZNet admin check ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()) :81670, :81756
facts.implication: Admin-gating a forced-teleport command server-side uses the same string vanilla uses for adminlist.txt — no new identity plumbing needed. `peer.m_playfabId` is the PlayFab-backend equivalent (:78806).

facts.claim: `ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` returns the local character ZDO plus every ready peer's `m_characterID` ZDO, but drops the peer association — it gives ZDOs, not ids.
facts.implication: Useless for RPC targeting on its own. Pair GetPeers() with m_characterID (exactly what Wonderland's ConnectedCharacters.All() does at /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs) to get both halves.

facts.claim: `Character.Awake` registers `m_nview.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportTo", RPC_TeleportTo)` on every Character whose ZDO is non-null, and `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is `if (m_nview.IsOwner()) TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);`.
facts.implication: Second, Chat-independent server→client teleport path: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)`. Owner-gated, so it can only ever move the character to its own owning client — inherently safe.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC through `ZDOMan.GetZDO(targetZDO)` → `ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo)` → `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC`; a missing instance is a silent drop, a missing method logs `"Failed to find rpc method <hash>"`.
facts.implication: RPC_TeleportTo reaches the target only if that client currently has its Player GameObject instantiated. During the respawn/loading screen there is no instance and the packet evaporates, same net effect as RPC_TeleportPlayer's `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard.

facts.claim: `Player.TeleportTo` rejects with `return false` in exactly three cases and no others: `!m_nview.IsOwner()` (it re-forwards via RPC_TeleportTo instead), `IsTeleporting()` already true, or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`. There is no check for dead, attached, sleeping, in a dungeon, on a ship, in combat, or for target distance.
facts.implication: The only two preconditions a server must model are 'not already teleporting' and 'cooldown elapsed'. Neither is observable server-side, so a server mod must track its own send timestamps per player and space forced teleports conservatively.

facts.claim: `m_teleportCooldown` only accumulates in the `!m_teleporting` early-return branch of `Player.UpdateTeleport` and is forced to `0f` on every tick while teleporting AND at the moment `TeleportTo` succeeds.
facts.implication: The dead window is not '2s after the RPC' — it is the entire teleport duration plus 2s after it ends. For a distantTeleport that is ≥10s total. A server retry loop faster than that silently burns every retry.

facts.claim: A freshly constructed Player starts with `m_teleportCooldown` at its default 0, and `UpdateTeleport` runs only from the `else if (!IsDead())` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate`, so the 2s must be accrued after the new Player object exists and is alive.
facts.citation: Player.m_teleportCooldown declaration, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:9907; Player.FixedUpdate :10194-10226 (IsOwner gate :10204, !IsDead gate :10213, UpdateTeleport call :10226)
facts.implication: A 'teleport on join' or 'teleport on respawn' feature MUST wait >2s after the character ZDO appears, or the very first teleport is silently swallowed.

facts.claim: `Player.UpdateTeleport` does nothing at all until `m_teleportTimer > 2f`; only then does it set `transform.position/rotation`, zero `m_body.linearVelocity`, set `m_maxAirAltitude = transform.position.y`, call `EnvMan.ForceInstantEnvironmentSwitch()` and `SetLookDir`.
facts.implication: The character ZDO's position (pushed by ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync) changes ~2s after the RPC, not 8s. That 2s mark is the server's earliest reliable confirmation that a forced teleport landed. Also: m_maxAirAltitude is reset every tick during teleport, so there is never arrival fall damage.

facts.claim: The exit condition is `if ((!(m_teleportTimer > 8f) && m_distantTeleport) || !ZNetScene.instance.IsAreaReady(m_teleportTargetPos)) return;` — a distantTeleport therefore requires BOTH timer > 8s AND the destination zone ready; a non-distant teleport requires only area-ready (so it can finish just after 2s).
facts.implication: distantTeleport:true has a hard ~8s black-screen floor by design — that is the vanilla portal feel, not a loading artifact. distantTeleport:false ends as soon as the zone is ready but has a punishing failure mode (next fact).

facts.claim: After the gate: if `ZoneSystem.FindFloor(target, out height)` succeeds the teleport ends cleanly. If not: when `m_teleportTimer > 15f || !m_distantTeleport`, a distantTeleport is force-landed at `ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(target) + 0.5f`, while a NON-distant teleport is REVERTED to `m_teleportFromPos/m_teleportFromRot` and the player is shown `$msg_portal_blocked`.
facts.implication: Always send distantTeleport:true for a forced teleport. It can never fail — worst case the player is dropped on solid ground at 15s. distantTeleport:false into an unloaded or floorless destination rubber-bands the player back to origin with a misleading 'portal blocked' message.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.FindFloor(p, out height)` raycasts DOWN from `p + Vector3.up * 1f` for 1000m against m_solidRayMask; `GetSolidHeight(p)` raycasts down from `p.y + 1000f` for 2000m and returns `p.y` unchanged on a miss.
facts.implication: A target coordinate below the ground surface will never find a floor (the ray points down). Aim teleport targets at ground height + a small positive Y, exactly as TeleportWorld.Teleport does (`portalPos + forward*m_exitDistance + Vector3.up`, :143540-143545).

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(point)` requires `ZoneSystem.IsZoneLoaded(zone)` AND every ZDO in that sector at near-simulation distance to already have an instance; `ZoneSystem.IsZoneLoaded` additionally requires the zone not be in `m_loadingObjectsInZones`.
facts.implication: The 'is the zone loaded' question is answered entirely on the receiving client against its own scene, using terrain it generates locally. The server never needs the destination loaded and cannot pre-warm it for the client.

facts.claim: `Player.FixedUpdate` calls `UpdateAttach()` (:10217) BEFORE `UpdateTeleport()` (:10226) in the same tick, and `UpdateAttach` unconditionally snaps `transform.position/rotation` to `m_attachPoint` while `m_attached` is true. `AttachStop()` is called from UpdateAttach only when the attach point has become null, and `AttachStop` early-returns if `m_sleeping`.
facts.implication: Teleporting an ATTACHED player (chair, bed, ship seat/helm) makes position ping-pong between attach point and target every physics tick until the original furniture unloads and nulls the attach point. Teleporting a SLEEPING player is worse: AttachStop is blocked by m_sleeping, so nothing frees them. Read ZDOVars.s_inBed server-side and refuse to teleport those players.

facts.claim: `ZDOVars.s_inBed` IS written into the character ZDO (`AttachStart` sets it, `AttachStop` clears it) and the dedicated server already reads it in `Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep`. `Player.m_sleeping` by contrast is a private compiled bool with no ZDO or network backing.
facts.implication: Server can cheaply pre-check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` before a forced teleport — this covers beds AND every chair/ship seat that passes isBed, since s_inBed is written on every AttachStart. It cannot distinguish sleeping from merely sitting.

facts.claim: `Player.IsDead()` reads `m_nview.GetZDO()?.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)`, and `Player.OnDeath` sets that ZDO bool true (cleared in `OnRespawn`).
facts.implication: Death state IS server-readable off the character ZDO. Since UpdateTeleport is skipped for dead players, the server must check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` before sending, otherwise the teleport is accepted (m_teleporting latches true) and never executed.

facts.claim: `Player.IsTeleporting()` returns `m_teleporting`, a private compiled bool; `Player.ShowTeleportAnimation()` returns `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport`. Neither is written to the ZDO.
facts.implication: The server can NEVER see that a player is mid-teleport. Any server-side cooldown must be inferred from when the server itself last sent an RPC and from ZDO position deltas.

facts.claim: `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` picks the loading-screen sub-panel purely from player state: `m_teleportingProgress.SetActive(true)` is chosen when `player.ShowTeleportAnimation()` is true. There is no portal-specific transit effect anywhere in TeleportWorld.Teleport — it only calls `player.TeleportTo(pos, rotation, distantTeleport: true)`.
facts.implication: A forced teleport sent with distantTeleport:true is byte-for-byte the same client experience as a vanilla portal transit — same black screen, same swirl animation, same duration. There is nothing extra to trigger and nothing missing. distantTeleport:false gives no swirl (the dungeon-door feel).

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld`'s own effects — `m_connected` (EffectList, fired when a portal newly gains a target) and `m_target_found` (EffectFade) — live in `TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal`, which is driven by `Player.GetClosestPlayer` and `m_proximityRoot`, and are ambient portal-object effects, not transit effects.
facts.implication: There is no 'portal whoosh at the player' prefab to replay. If extra flourish is wanted, use the generic ZNetScene SpawnObject path (next fact) with some other vanilla vfx/sfx prefab.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene` registers a routed RPC `"SpawnObject"` taking `(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)`; `RPC_SpawnObject` does `Instantiate(GetPrefab(prefabHash), pos, rot)` and logs `"Missing prefab <hash>"` on an unknown hash.
facts.implication: The server can play a one-shot VFX/SFX prefab on one specific client at one position: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "SpawnObject", pos, rot, "vfx_name".GetStableHashCode())`. Wonderland already ships this working with vfx_fermenter_add / sfx_fermenter_add (Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:199-220).

facts.claim: `Game.RequestRespawn(float delay, bool afterDeath)` only sets a flag and schedules `Invoke("_RequestRespawn", delay)`; `_RequestRespawn` then saves and destroys `Player.m_localPlayer` and calls `ZNet.SetCharacterID(ZDOID.None)`. No routed or ZNetView RPC anywhere invokes RequestRespawn.
facts.implication: There is no network path to force a respawn. RequestRespawn is unreachable from the server; the only caller chains are Player.OnDeath (:12847) and TeleportHome.OnTriggerEnter.

facts.claim: `TeleportHome.OnTriggerEnter` is gated on `Player.m_localPlayer != component` and calls `Game.instance.RequestRespawn(0f)`. It is a collider component on a world prefab — no collider or GameObject of it is ever instantiated on a dedicated server.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec: TeleportHome is not a server primitive. Also confirms the second non-portal teleport component: `Teleport.Interact` (dungeon doors) calls `character.TeleportTo(..., distantTeleport: false)` and honours GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals (:143352-143362), also client-only.

facts.claim: A player's respawn location lives entirely in the local character profile: `PlayerProfile.SetCustomSpawnPoint/GetCustomSpawnPoint/HaveCustomSpawnPoint` read and write `GetWorldData(ZNet.GetWorldUID()).m_spawnPoint` inside the .fch profile, written by `Bed.Interact` on the client.
facts.citation: PlayerProfile.SetCustomSpawnPoint, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106224-106238; Bed sets it :119691, :119729; Game.FindSpawnPoint reads it :100346-100372
facts.implication: A server-side 'teleport home' must reconstruct the destination itself (e.g. from Bed ZDO ownership, ZDOVars.s_owner) and then force-teleport to those coordinates. It cannot read or set the player's actual spawn point.
