facts.claim: `RPC_TeleportPlayer` is client-originatable: the vanilla console command `recall` runs entirely on a client, iterating `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` and calling `Chat.instance.TeleportPlayer(peer.m_uid, ...)` for each. `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire and never cross-checked against the ZRpc connection the packet arrived on.
facts.implication: Any modded/cheating client can teleport any other player. But since ALL client→client routed RPCs transit the server's ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC before RouteRPC forwards them, a server-only Harmony patch there can drop packets whose m_methodHash equals "RPC_TeleportPlayer".GetStableHashCode() and whose real connection is not an admin — a genuine, enforceable server-side security win.

facts.claim: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` snaps `transform.position/rotation` to `zDO.GetPosition()/GetRotation()` on the exact frame ownership is GAINED (`flag2 = !m_wasOwner && flag`), then thereafter pushes the transform into the ZDO every tick while owner.
facts.implication: A third, non-RPC move primitive exists: server steals the character ZDO, writes a position, releases ownership; the client snaps on regain. It is far more invasive (Player.FixedUpdate early-returns on !IsOwner, freezing the player) and has none of TeleportTo's loading-screen handling. Prefer the RPCs.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs server-side every 2s and reassigns any *Persistent* ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer when the current owner is absent or out of their own active area; the dedicated server's own reference position is pinned to (1000000, 0, 1000000) by `Game.FixedUpdate` every physics tick.
facts.implication: If the Player ZDO is Persistent, a server ownership-steal self-heals back to the owning client within ~2s, which is what makes the ownership-steal trick recoverable. Whether the Player prefab's ZNetView.m_persistent is true is Inspector data the decompile cannot answer (see open questions).

facts.claim: Other RPCs that move a Character are strictly limited: `Character.RPC_Stagger` only sets `transform.rotation` (and has NO owner check); `Character.RPC_Damage` → `ApplyPushback` applies a horizontal m_pushForce capped by mass and dissipating at 100 units/s; `Character.RPC_FreezeFrame` and `Ragdoll` do not move a live player.
facts.citation: Character.RPC_Stagger, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2841-2852; Character.ApplyPushback :2073-2088, UpdatePushback :2088-2092, call site in RPC_Damage :2518; Character.RPC_FreezeFrame :4571; class Ragdoll :17440
facts.implication: No alternative translation primitive. RPC_Stagger is a free server→client forced *rotation* (no owner gate, so it also works on observers). Note RPC_Damage is fully suppressed while IsTeleporting() — a teleporting player is invulnerable (:2425, :2429, :2582).

facts.claim: `Player.CanMove()` returns false while `m_teleporting`; auto-pickup, stations, building and the inventory GUI are all suppressed by IsTeleporting checks across the client.
facts.implication: A forced teleport is a hard ~8s freeze of all player agency on distantTeleport:true. Do not use it for anything high-frequency; it is a disruptive action that should be rate-limited and announced.

facts.claim: `ZNet.RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` is where `peer.m_refPos` and `peer.m_publicRefPos` are refreshed from the client; `ZNetPeer.GetRefPos()` just returns m_refPos.
facts.implication: peer.GetRefPos() is a coarse, client-reported position updated only on that periodic sync. For an accurate pre-teleport position read use the character ZDO (`ZDOMan.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetPosition()`), which ZSyncTransform refreshes every physics tick.

apis.signature: void ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: THE primary path. `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. Parameter types must serialize exactly as Vector3, Quaternion, bool (ZRpc.Serialize is type-driven — pass a real `bool`, not an int). Never runs locally when targetPeerID != server id, so the server needs no local registration.

apis.signature: void ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: ZDO-scoped variant. `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)` hits Character.RPC_TeleportTo, which is owner-gated and therefore cannot be misdirected. Chat-independent; preferred if you distrust the GUI singleton on any client build.

apis.signature: static ZRoutedRpc ZRoutedRpc.instance { get; }
apis.notes: Null before ZNet initialises. Guard every call site, as Wonderland's PlayerNotify does.

apis.signature: public const long ZRoutedRpc.Everybody = 0L
apis.notes: Broadcast. Also triggers a local HandleRoutedRPC attempt on the server which silently misses (no handler registered). Safe but wasteful; also ZNetView.Everybody = 0L at :82535.

apis.signature: List<ZNetPeer> ZNet.GetPeers()
apis.notes: Returns the LIVE m_peers list, not a copy. Use ZNet.instance.GetConnectedPeers() (:81619) if you may disconnect someone while iterating.

apis.signature: ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeer(long uid)
apis.notes: Note this overload does NOT filter on IsReady(); check peer.IsReady() yourself.

apis.signature: ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeerByPlayerName(string name)
apis.notes: Exact, case-sensitive match on peer.m_playerName; already filters IsReady(). Player names are not unique — prefer resolving by ZDOVars.s_playerID when it matters.

apis.signature: ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeerByHostName(string endpoint)
apis.notes: Matches peer.m_socket.GetHostName() — the SteamID64 string on the Steam backend, the IP on a plain socket. Same key vanilla uses for adminlist/bannedlist.

apis.signature: public long ZNetPeer.m_uid; public ZDOID ZNetPeer.m_characterID; public long ZNetPeer.m_playerID; public string ZNetPeer.m_playerName; public string ZNetPeer.m_playfabId; public bool ZNetPeer.IsReady(); public Vector3 ZNetPeer.GetRefPos()
apis.notes: m_uid = routing address (per-connection, ephemeral). m_characterID = ZDOID of the body (ZDOID.None between connect and spawn, and between death and respawn). m_playerID = stable identity. All public fields, no reflection needed.

apis.signature: List<ZDO> ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()
apis.notes: Loses the peer association — cannot be used for RPC targeting. Use GetPeers() + m_characterID + ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO().

apis.signature: void Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)
apis.notes: DO NOT USE server-side. It is a one-line wrapper over InvokeRoutedRPC and requires the Chat MonoBehaviour singleton. Game.Awake (:100034-100045) only instantiates the Console and ServerOptionsGUI prefabs, and server-run code elsewhere explicitly null-guards MessageHud.instance (:100474) — treat GUI singletons as absent.

apis.signature: void ZNetScene RPC "SpawnObject" (Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)
apis.notes: Server→one-client one-shot VFX/SFX. `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "SpawnObject", pos, rot, name.GetStableHashCode())`. Unknown hash just logs 'Missing prefab'. Proven working in Wonderland's VacuumEngine.

apis.signature: int ZDOVars.s_dead; int ZDOVars.s_inBed; int ZDOVars.s_playerID; int ZDOVars.s_playerName
apis.notes: The full set of server-readable pre-teleport checks: zdo.GetBool(s_dead) to skip dead players, zdo.GetBool(s_inBed) to skip attached/sleeping players, zdo.GetLong(s_playerID) for the cooldown key, zdo.GetPosition() for origin.

apis.signature: bool Player.TeleportTo(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)
apis.notes: Runs ONLY on the ZDO-owning (i.e. local-player) client. Return value is discarded by both RPC handlers — the server can never learn it failed.

apis.signature: void Character.RPC_TeleportTo(long sender, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)
apis.notes: Target of the ZDO-scoped invoke above. Runs on the receiving client, owner-gated. Name and signature are stable in 1.0.7.

apis.signature: private void ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) / private void ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC(RoutedRPCData rpcData)
apis.notes: Harmony-patchable chokepoint on the server for EVERY client-originated routed RPC. A prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC can drop spoofed "RPC_TeleportPlayer" (and "RPC_SetTag") packets by comparing m_methodHash and resolving the true sender via ZNet.instance.GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc).

gotchas: `Chat.instance.TeleportPlayer` is a trap, not a shortcut. It adds nothing over `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC` and introduces a GUI-singleton dependency that Game.Awake (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100034-100045) never satisfies on a dedicated server — it instantiates only the Console and ServerOptionsGUI prefabs, and server-run code elsewhere explicitly null-guards MessageHud.instance (:100474).

Every failure is SILENT and one-directional. `Player.TeleportTo` returns false (:15309, :15313), both RPC handlers discard the return (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent back. The server has exactly one after-the-fact signal: the character ZDO's position changing ~2s after the RPC (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync, :87527). Build confirmation on a position poll, not on the send.

The cooldown is NOT 'the 2 seconds after the RPC'. `m_teleportCooldown` is zeroed on every tick while teleporting and only accrues while idle (Player.UpdateTeleport, :15331-15336), so the rejection window spans the entire teleport plus 2s — ≥10s for a distantTeleport. Anything retrying faster than that burns every retry with no error.

`distantTeleport: false` is dangerous for forced teleports. If `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses at the destination, the client rubber-bands the player back to the origin and shows '$msg_portal_blocked' (:15369-15374) — a lie that will be reported as a mod bug. `distantTeleport: true` can never fail; it force-lands on solid ground at t=15s.

A dead player latches. `UpdateTeleport` runs only inside the `else if (!IsDead())` branch of Player.FixedUpdate (:10213/:10226), so a teleport sent to a dead player sets `m_teleporting = true` and then never advances. Check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` first.

An attached player fights the teleport: `UpdateAttach()` (:10217) runs before `UpdateTeleport()` (:10226) every tick and re-snaps the transform to the attach point. A SLEEPING player is stuck outright, because `AttachStop` early-returns on `m_sleeping` (:15892). Pre-check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)`.

There is no separate 'portal VFX' to attach. Hud picks the teleport swirl purely from `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` (Hud.UpdateBlackScreen :47872, Player.ShowTeleportAnimation :15386) — so distantTeleport:true already IS the portal experience, and nothing you send can add portal-ness to a distantTeleport:false hop.

Targeting `ZRoutedRpc.Everybody` (0) makes the server also try to dispatch locally (:83588). For RPC_TeleportPlayer that misses silently because no handler is registered server-side — harmless, but it means a broadcast teleport moves every connected player, which is almost certainly not what you want.

`peer.m_characterID` is `ZDOID.None` during two normal windows (between connect and Game.SpawnPlayer, and between Game._RequestRespawn and the new spawn — :100270, :100413). A ZDO-scoped RPC_TeleportTo sent in either window is dropped by `ZNetScene.FindInstance` returning null (:83657-83663).

`ZNetPeer.m_uid` is a connection id, regenerated on every reconnect. Persisting it as a player key (for a cooldown table, an allowlist, a home location) will silently misfire after any relog. Persist `ZDOVars.s_playerID` / `peer.m_playerID` instead.

`RPC_TeleportPlayer` is not a server-privileged channel — vanilla's own client-side `recall` console command (:44548-44556) sends it peer-to-peer, and `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is self-reported (:83489). Adding a server force-teleport feature does not create a new attack surface, but shipping one without patching `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` leaves the pre-existing one open.

`Player.CanMove()` returns false for the whole teleport (:14425) and damage/stagger are suppressed by IsTeleporting (:2425, :2429, :2582). A forced distantTeleport is an ~8s invulnerable input lockout — abusable as a stun if the feature is exposed to players.

`ZNetView.InvokeRPC` (:82850) looks like a server-side option but requires a live ZNetView instance, which a dedicated server never has for a Player. Always go through `ZRoutedRpc.instance` with the raw ZDOID.

`Game.RequestRespawn` / `TeleportHome` have NO network entry point at all — not 'gated on m_localPlayer' so much as simply never called from any RPC (:100396, :143393). There is no way to force a respawn server-side.
openQuestions: Is `Chat.instance` actually null on a 1.0.7 dedicated server? The decompile shows Game.Awake instantiating only m_consolePrefab and m_serverOptionPrefab (:100034-100045), which is strong but circumstantial — whether the GUI canvas is part of the loaded 'main' scene is Unity scene data. In-game check: a BepInEx plugin that logs `Chat.instance == null` and `Hud.instance == null` on the first server Update after ZNet connects. (Moot for the recommended design, which never touches Chat.)

Is the Player prefab's `ZNetView.m_persistent` true? `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` only reassigns Persistent ZDOs (:76909), which decides whether a server ownership-steal of a character ZDO self-heals within 2s or strands the player. In-game check: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("Player").GetComponent<ZNetView>().m_persistent`, or read `zdo.Persistent` off a live character ZDO.

Which vfx_/sfx_ prefab names resolve through `ZNetScene.GetPrefab(hash)`? m_namedPrefabs is built from Inspector lists m_prefabs + m_nonNetViewPrefabs (:81941-81952). In-game check: dump `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` once at server start and grep for portal-adjacent effects (vfx_Place_portal_wood, sfx_*) to see what a forced teleport could accompany itself with.

Does a vanilla client actually complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-visited, ungenerated zone within the 15s fallback? The 8s/IsAreaReady gate plus the 15s force-land is clear in code, but real terrain-generation latency on a low-end client is empirical. In-game check: force-teleport a test player 8km into unexplored Ashlands and time the black screen; also confirm no fall damage and no 'portal blocked' message.

How much of the ping-pong actually happens when teleporting a seated/helm-attached player, and how many ticks pass before the origin furniture unloads and nulls m_attachPoint? In-game check: seat a player on a chair and on a ship helm, force-teleport 5km, and observe whether they arrive cleanly, arrive still glued, or desync.

What is the real-world cadence of `RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` (which refreshes peer.m_refPos, :80401)? Determines how stale peer.GetRefPos() is versus the per-tick character-ZDO position. In-game check: log both every second for one player and compare.

Whether the vanilla client's `m_teleportCooldown` is ever reset by anything outside UpdateTeleport (e.g. on scene reload after respawn, given the Player object is destroyed and recreated). In-game check: die, respawn, and time how soon a forced teleport is accepted.
correctionsToExistingSpec: TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:75 — 'A forced teleport issued within vanilla's 2s post-teleport cooldown silently no-ops with no error either side' is directionally right but understates the window. `m_teleportCooldown` is forced to 0 on EVERY tick while teleporting (Player.UpdateTeleport :15336) and is set to 0 when TeleportTo succeeds (:15320), so it only accrues after the teleport fully ends. Combined with the hard `m_teleportTimer > 8f` floor for distantTeleport (:15349), back-to-back forced teleports need ≥10s of spacing, not 2s. Also add the third rejection cause — `IsTeleporting()` already true (:15309) — and the fourth, invisible one: `UpdateTeleport` never runs for a dead player (Player.FixedUpdate `else if (!IsDead())` :10213), so a teleport sent to a corpse latches m_teleporting=true and silently never executes.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:93 — 'TeleportHome/Game.RequestRespawn as a force-respawn primitive — unconditionally gated on Player.m_localPlayer, a confirmed no-op on a dedicated server.' The conclusion is right, the reason is wrong. `Game.RequestRespawn` (:100396) is NOT gated on m_localPlayer — it just sets a flag and schedules Invoke; the m_localPlayer null-checks are inside `_RequestRespawn` (:100403). The real reason it is unreachable is that no routed RPC or ZNetView RPC anywhere calls RequestRespawn; its only callers are Player.OnDeath (:12847) and TeleportHome.OnTriggerEnter (:143398). State it as 'no network entry point exists' rather than 'gated on m_localPlayer'.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:75 — the 'bypassing Chat.instance entirely' recommendation is confirmed correct and can now be made concrete with exact signatures. Two working forms: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (3-arg overload, :83554, targetZDO defaults to ZDOID.None) and `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)` (4-arg overload, :83577, hits the owner-gated Character.RPC_TeleportTo at :4126). The server needs NO local registration of either name, because InvokeRoutedRPC skips local dispatch when targetPeerID != m_id (:83589-83593).

MISSING FROM SPEC (feasible, small) — a forced teleport with `distantTeleport: true` is visually and audibly IDENTICAL to a vanilla portal transit. `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` selects m_teleportingProgress purely from `Player.ShowTeleportAnimation()` = `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` (:47872, :15386-15393), and `TeleportWorld.Teleport` does nothing more than `player.TeleportTo(pos, rotation, distantTeleport: true)` (:143545). There is no portal-specific transit effect anywhere. The spec's Group 3 should say so explicitly — 'portal-feel teleport with no portal' is free.

MISSING FROM SPEC (feasible, small) — server-side pre-flight checks ARE possible even though the teleport itself is unobservable. `ZDOVars.s_dead` (:78403, read by Player.IsDead :15244) and `ZDOVars.s_inBed` (:78457, written by AttachStart :15799, already read server-side by Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep :100744) let the server refuse to teleport dead or bed/chair/ship-attached players — the two states that produce the ugliest failures (latched black screen; position ping-pong with AttachStop blocked by m_sleeping :15892).

REFINES TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:79 — the sender-spoofing hardening item should name `RPC_TeleportPlayer` as a first-class target, not just RPC_SetTag. Vanilla's client-side `recall` console command (:44548-44556) already teleports arbitrary peers from a client, and `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is deserialized off the wire unchecked (:83489). The enforceable chokepoint is `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) on the server, which every client→client routed RPC passes through before `RouteRPC` (:83597) forwards it — a server-only prefix there can drop spoofed teleports by resolving the true sender from the `ZRpc` argument.

REFINES TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:54 (portal-to-bed) — confirmed that `PlayerProfile.SetCustomSpawnPoint` writes only to the local .fch WorldPlayerData (:106224-106238), never networked. But add the useful half: `ZDOVars.s_inBed` IS ZDO-backed and server-readable, so while the server cannot know WHICH bed is a player's spawn, it can know a player is currently in one.

ADD TO TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md:92 — 'Server-enforced max teleport distance/cooldown override — no server execution point exists' is correct for overriding vanilla's values, but a server-only mod CAN impose its OWN distance/cooldown policy on teleports it initiates, keyed on `ZDOVars.s_playerID` / `peer.m_playerID` (:80925) with origin read from `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetPosition()`. It just cannot police portal transits the client initiates.

research.topic: zdo-connection-system (portal pairing, ZDO creation, ownership, persistence) — Valheim 1.0.7
research.summary: A dedicated server can create a fully persistent, vanilla-client-instantiable portal ZDO with no GameObject: `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` + `SetPrefab` + `Persistent = true` + `SetRotation` is the complete recipe (CreateNewZDO does NOT set the prefab hash on the ZDO and does NOT set Persistent — both are caller responsibilities, and getting the prefabHash argument wrong silently makes the ZDO unsaveable). Connections are stored as exactly ONE `ZDOConnection{type,target}` per ZDO in `ZDOExtraData.s_connections`; writing one side never writes the other, so one-way and ring topologies are representable and survive vanilla's 5s self-heal at runtime — but they do NOT survive a world save, because the on-disk format collapses each ZDO to a single `ZDOConnectionHashData{type,int hash}` slot, which can only express a pairwise perfect matching (rings lose a link, one-way links become bidirectional, self-loops are erased). ZDO writes require no ownership at all (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter) and propagate on DataRevision, but the owning client can clobber the whole ZDO blob on its next higher-revision send, and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands portal ownership to any nearby player every 2s — which is why vanilla's `Game.SetConnection` routes through `RPC_SetConnection` to a connected owner instead of writing locally. The single most under-exploited mechanism found: `ZNetView.LoadFields()` is vanilla on both server and client and lets a ZDO override any public instance field of any component on the prefab by reflection — which makes per-portal `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` achievable server-side on a 100% vanilla client, directly refuting the current spec's "Ruled Out" entry. Finally, portal ZDOs live in a separate always-resident `m_portalObjects` dictionary saved to its own `ChunkPortal` file only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set — a tag-only write never sets it, so tag changes are silently lost at the next world save unless the mod calls `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.

facts.claim: A ZDO holds AT MOST ONE connection, ever: `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and `ZDOConnection` is `{readonly ConnectionType m_type; readonly ZDOID m_target;}`. There is no list, no multi-target, no per-type slot.
facts.implication: A true multi-destination hub portal is structurally impossible, and a portal ZDO carrying a Portal connection can never simultaneously carry a SyncTransform connection (e.g. a portal parented to a ship).

facts.claim: `ConnectionType` is a [Flags] byte enum: None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10. Portal/SyncTransform/Spawned are NOT independent bits (1,2,3 overlap), only `Target` is a real flag bit.
facts.implication: `type | Target` is the only legal combination; never try to OR Portal with SyncTransform. Type comparisons must be exact equality, not bit tests.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection(zid, type, target)` writes ONLY `s_connections[zid]`. It does not touch the target's entry. Both vanilla pairing sites call it twice, once per direction.
facts.implication: Writing one side is genuinely one-way at runtime. A mod building a ring or a fan-in must write every edge itself.

facts.claim: `ZDO.SetConnection` (the wrapper) calls `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` only when connectionType == Portal, and only when the underlying value actually changed (SetConnection returns false for an identical type+target).
facts.implication: Re-writing an already-correct connection is a no-op — it neither bumps DataRevision nor dirties the portal save chunk. A resync loop that re-asserts the same value does nothing.

facts.claim: `ZDO.UpdateConnection` differs from `SetConnection`: it returns false and writes nothing if the ZDO has NO existing connection entry at all.
facts.implication: `UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on a never-connected portal is a silent no-op — which is exactly why vanilla `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` can fail to dirty the portal save chunk when retagging a fresh portal.

facts.claim: On disk, a connection is NOT a ZDOID. `RegenerateConnectionHashData()` (called from `ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave`) converts `s_connections` into `s_connectionsHashData`, giving the source ZDO `{type, h}` and the target ZDO `{type|Target, h}` for a fresh unique int h. `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)m_type` + `(int)m_hash`.
facts.implication: Persistence of a pairing is by matched random hash, not by identity. Each ZDO has exactly one hash slot, so the disk format can only express a perfect pairwise matching.

facts.claim: A ring A→B→C→A does not survive a save/reload. Processing C overwrites A's source slot with a Target slot, so after reload only one pair re-links and the third portal is left unconnected and gets randomly re-paired by `Game.ConnectPortals`.
facts.citation: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData overwrite of s_connectionsHashData[key] then [target], assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75471-75475; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals hash matching :77852-77890
facts.implication: Refutes 'rings are feasible' as a persistent topology. Rings are runtime-only and must be re-asserted by the mod after every world load.

facts.claim: A one-way link (A→B, B→None) is silently converted to a two-way link by a save/reload: `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` matches the hashes and writes BOTH `zDO.SetConnection(Portal, item2)` and `zDO2.SetConnection(Portal, item)`.
facts.implication: One-way portals cannot be persisted through vanilla's own restore path; the mod must null the return side again on every world load.

facts.claim: A self-loop (A→A) is erased by a save/reload: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` writes `s_connectionsHashData[A] = {Portal, h}` then immediately overwrites it with `{Portal|Target, h}` because target != None, leaving a Target with no matching source.
facts.implication: The 'self-loop to stay connected' hub trick works at runtime but is wiped at the next restart.

facts.claim: `ZDO.Set(int hash, T value)` performs NO ownership check for any type. The `bool okForNotOwner = false` parameter on the int overload is accepted and then completely ignored.
facts.implication: The server can write tag/health/any field on a portal ZDO owned by a player client without claiming ownership; the write lands locally and bumps DataRevision so it will be sent out.

facts.claim: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition` is the ONE writer that is ownership-gated: it only calls `IncreaseDataRevision()` `if (IsOwner())`. It always updates the local m_position and sector regardless.
facts.implication: Moving a portal the server does not own desynchronizes server and clients — the server must `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` before any position change.

facts.claim: `ZDO.SetSector` explicitly EARLY-RETURNS for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, so portal ZDOs are never re-bucketed into `m_objectsBySector` by a position change.
facts.implication: Moving a portal leaves it filed under its ORIGINAL sector key in `m_portalObjects`. Clients near the new position may not receive it via `FindObjects`; force-send or reinsert manually.

facts.claim: Portal ZDOs are stored in a dedicated `m_portalObjects : Dictionary<SectorIndex, List<ZDO>>` and are REMOVED from the normal sector array by `AddIfPortal`. They are never unloaded and are always resident in server RAM.
facts.implication: 'Target in an unloaded zone' does not exist for portals on the server. `GetPortalList()` is a complete, always-accurate world-wide portal enumeration with zero extra bookkeeping.

facts.claim: Sync to clients still reaches portals: `ZDOMan.FindObjects` adds `m_objectsBySector[idx]` AND `m_portalObjects[idx]` for the same sector index.
facts.implication: Portals sync to nearby clients normally, and are also subject to `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` ownership transfer like any other Persistent ZDO.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs every 2s on the server (via `ReleaseZDOS`) and assigns ownership of any Persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area to that peer, releasing (`SetOwner(0L)`) any it owns outside its own active area.
facts.implication: A portal near a logged-in player is owned by that player's client within 2s. Any server ownership claim on a nearby portal is transient unless a Harmony guard on `ZDO.SetOwner` blocks the reassignment (the pattern Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine already uses).

facts.claim: Vanilla's own portal-write path never assumes server ownership: `Game.SetConnection` writes locally + `ForceSendZDO` only when owner==0 or the owner is not a connected peer; otherwise it routes `RPC_SetConnection` to the owning client, which then does `SetOwner(GetSessionID())` + `SetConnection` on ITS side.
facts.implication: The canonical, race-free way for a server mod to change a portal connection is to reuse `Game.SetConnection` semantics, not to blind-write the ZDO.

facts.claim: Conflict resolution on receive is whole-ZDO, not per-field: `RPC_ZDOData` discards the incoming packet entirely if `incomingDataRevision <= local DataRevision` (applying only an owner-revision bump), otherwise `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` replaces the full data blob.
facts.implication: A server field write on a client-owned ZDO can be silently reverted by the owner's next send. There is no field-level merge.

facts.claim: `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` gates only on revision numbers, never on ownership: it returns true if the peer has never seen the ZDO, or OwnerRevision > cached, or DataRevision > cached.
facts.implication: Server writes to non-owned ZDOs do propagate to clients — ownership is not a transmit gate, only a clobber risk.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(zdo)` is a silent no-op unless `zdo.IsOwner()` — it only appends to `m_destroySendList`.
facts.implication: Deleting a portal server-side REQUIRES `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` first, or nothing happens at all.

facts.claim: Destroying a ZDO releases only ITS own connection entry (`ReleaseConnection(zid)` removes `s_connections[zid]`); the partner's entry keeps pointing at the now-dead ZDOID.
facts.implication: Dangling connections are normal and expected; cleanup is deferred to the 5s `Game.ConnectPortals` sweep.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals` nulls a portal's connection if the target ZDO is missing, the target's tag differs, or the target's own connection is None — but it never checks reciprocity (that the target points back at this portal).
facts.implication: Rings and one-way chains survive vanilla's runtime self-heal indefinitely, as long as every member shares the same literal tag string and no member points at None.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals` runs from `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` started in `Game.Start()` only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`, every 5 seconds, with no `Player.m_localPlayer` dependency. It is `public`.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's central claim about the server-authoritative layer, and confirms a mod can call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` directly for instant re-pairing.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3, int prefabHash)` does NOT write the prefab hash onto the ZDO and does NOT set Persistent. It only uses prefabHash to decide `AddIfPortal`. `ZNetView.Awake` is where vanilla calls `SetPrefab` and sets `Persistent`.
facts.implication: Server-side portal creation must be: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetPrefab(hash); z.SetRotation(rot);` — omitting SetPrefab leaves m_prefab == 0 and the client's `CreateObject` returns null, after which the server itself destroys the ZDO as an 'invalid prefab'.

facts.claim: If `CreateNewZDO` is called with prefabHash 0 (or the private ZDOID overload), `AddIfPortal` never runs; the ZDO stays in `m_objectsBySector`, and `AddObjectsPerChunk` explicitly SKIPS any ZDO whose prefab is in `PortalPrefabHash` — so the portal is written to no chunk file at all and is lost on restart.
facts.implication: Creation order matters. Always pass the real portal prefab hash to `CreateNewZDO`; never SetPrefab a portal hash onto a ZDO created with hash 0.

facts.claim: Portal ZDOs are saved into a single dedicated chunk file `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)`, containing ALL portals in the world, and ONLY when `DirtyPortalObjects` is true. There is no `Persistent` filter on that write.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal block :77621-77635; ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal :113180; ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal branch :76474-76483
facts.implication: Any portal field change must be accompanied by dirtying the portal chunk, or the entire portal file is skipped at save time and every portal reverts to its last-dirtied state.

facts.claim: `DirtyPortalObjects` is set true ONLY by: `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` with type Portal, `AddIfPortal`, and `HandleDestroyedZDO` of a portal-prefab ZDO. A tag write (`zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, ...)`) does NOT set it.
facts.implication: CRITICAL for a tag-rewriting mod: call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` after every server-side portal tag write, or the rename silently vanishes at the next world save.

facts.claim: ZDOIDs are regenerated on every world load: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` and `ZDOID.SetID` forces `UserKey = UnknownFormerUserKey (1)`.
facts.implication: No mod may persist a ZDOID as a portal identity across a restart. Stable identity must be derived from position, a custom ZDO field, or the tag string.

facts.claim: Loaded ZDOs come back with `OwnerRevision = 0; DataRevision = 0; Owned = false; Owner = false` — i.e. every ZDO in the world is unowned immediately after load, until `ConnectPortals` (`SetOwner(GetSessionID())`) or `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` assigns one.
facts.implication: The window right after world load is the cheapest time for a server mod to claim ownership of every portal without contending with clients.

facts.claim: `ZNetView.LoadFields()` — vanilla, on the client, called from `ZNetView.Awake` — reflects over every public instance field of every component on the instantiated prefab and overrides it from the ZDO, keyed `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"`, gated by ZDO bools `"HasFields"` and `"HasFields<TypeName>"`. Supported types: int, float, bool, Vector3, string, GameObject (by prefab name), ItemDrop (by prefab name).
facts.citation: ZNetView.LoadFields assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82970 (identical server copy assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82738); call site ZNetView.Awake :82631
facts.implication: A server-only mod CAN make per-portal `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` real on a 100% vanilla client by writing three ints to the portal ZDO. Also unlocks per-portal `m_activationRange`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_hoverOffset`, and `WearNTear.m_health`. Directly refutes the current spec's 'Ruled Out' entry.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` is a `public bool` instance field on the client's TeleportWorld, exactly the shape `LoadFields` can override.
facts.citation: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144169 (server copy :143429); consumed by TeleportWorld.Teleport -> player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems) :143534 / client Player.IsTeleportable :8793
facts.implication: Client-honored, not server-enforced (same class of guarantee as vanilla's boss gating) — but it is genuinely per-portal and needs zero client install.

facts.claim: `LoadFields` runs only inside `ZNetView.Awake`, i.e. at instantiation. Changing the ZDO afterwards does not re-apply the override to an already-instantiated object.
facts.citation: ZNetView.Awake :82631 (LoadFields call is the last step before AddInstance); ZNetScene.CreateObject assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82225-82248
facts.implication: A per-portal allow-all toggle takes effect for a player only after that portal is (re)created in their scene — i.e. after they leave and return to the area, or on their next login.

facts.claim: A ZDO's extra data is 7 independent int-keyed dictionaries: float, Vector3, Quaternion, int, long, string, byte[]. Keys are arbitrary ints (vanilla uses `"name".GetStableHashCode()`); bools are stored as ints.
facts.implication: Arbitrary portal metadata (owner group, lock state, route id, cooldown timestamp) can be stored on the portal ZDO itself under mod-private hashes and it round-trips through save and network automatically.

facts.claim: Any hash present in `ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly` is stripped from the world save for EVERY ZDO. It is seeded globally from the 16 entries of `ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes` (incl. s_support, s_inUse, s_alert, s_animationSpeed, s_velHash...) plus anything ever passed to `AddSessionHash`.
facts.implication: Never repurpose one of those 16 keys for persistent portal metadata, and never call `AddSessionHash` on a mod key you want saved.

facts.claim: Per-ZDO per-type item count is capped at 32767 by the wire encoding: `ZPackage.WriteNumItems` emits one byte below 128 and otherwise `(byte)((n>>8)|0x80), (byte)n` — n >= 32768 corrupts the stream. `ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk` logs a warning above 100 items of one type on one ZDO.
facts.implication: Practical guidance: a portal should carry a handful of extra fields, and bulk metadata belongs in one byte[] or string, not 200 int keys.

facts.claim: Strings are written with `BinaryWriter.Write(string)` (7-bit length prefix + UTF-8) and byte arrays with an int length prefix — no per-field cap in code. The real ceiling is the 10,485,760-byte socket package limit; an oversized package is logged on send and rejected on receive as 'Invalid pkg size'.
facts.citation: ZPackage.Write(string) :83180-83183, Write(byte[]) :83114-83118; ZSocket size guards :84349-84353 and :84469-84471
facts.implication: Portal tags and mod metadata strings can be arbitrarily long server-side; vanilla's 10-character limit exists only in the client's `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` widget.

facts.claim: `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false when the new value equals the old, which makes `ZDO.Set` skip `IncreaseDataRevision` entirely. Byte arrays compare by reference (`Equals`), so a re-set byte[] always dirties.
facts.implication: Idempotent re-writes generate zero network traffic — safe for a fast reconciliation tick — but also means a 'touch to force resync' trick needs an actual value change or a direct `ForceSendZDO`.

facts.claim: The dedicated server DOES run `ZNetScene.Update -> CreateDestroyObjects` every 1/30s; what prevents portal GameObjects from existing is that `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every tick, and `CreateObjectsSorted` early-returns on `!ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` for that never-generated zone.
facts.implication: Refines the spec's mechanism (the gate is the pinned reference position + unloaded zone, not an absent ZNetScene). Also means a mod that ever moves the server reference position into the real world would start instantiating real portal GameObjects server-side.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps any zone with |x+256| >= 512 or |y+256| >= 512 to Sector 0 — the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position (zone 15625,15625) maps to.
facts.implication: Any ZDO placed beyond ~16320m from origin lands in the server's own 'active' sector bucket. Never create a portal ZDO at such coordinates; in a normal ±10000m world this is unreachable.

facts.claim: `ZDO.Serialize` (network) writes the connection as `(byte)type` + the raw target ZDOID; `ZDO.Save` (disk) writes `(byte)type` + the int hash. Two different encodings for the same field.
facts.citation: ZDO.Serialize :74169-74173 vs ZDO.Save :74314-74318; ZDO.Deserialize :74227-74232 vs ZDO.Load :74592-74596
facts.implication: Clients receive real ZDOIDs and can immediately `GetZDO(target)`/`RequestZDO(target)`; only the disk round-trip goes through the lossy hash-matching path.

facts.claim: A client that lacks the target portal's ZDO calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(connectionZDOID)` from `TeleportWorld.TargetFound`, and the server answers with `GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO(id)` — so an arbitrarily distant destination portal is always deliverable on demand.
facts.implication: Destination portals never need to be in the traveller's loaded zones — `Teleport()` reads position/rotation straight off the target ZDO.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(zid, type)` requires EXACT type equality and returns ZDOID.None otherwise. At runtime `s_connections` never carries the `Target` flag (only `s_connectionsHashData` does), so a `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` query is safe.
facts.implication: Do not write `Portal|Target` into `s_connections` — `TeleportWorld.HaveTarget`/`TargetFound` query plain `Portal` and would see None.

facts.claim: `ZDO.Created`, `Owner`, and `Owned` are `DataFlags` bits that are NOT serialized: `ZDO.Serialize`/`Save` only emit Persistent, Distant, Type, Rotation and SmallPosition from the flag word.
facts.citation: ZDO.DataFlags enum :73284-73295; ZDO.Serialize flag assembly :74146-74162; ZDO.Save :74282-74292
facts.implication: Ownership is carried as a separate `long` in the ZDOData packet (`zPackage.Write(item2.GetOwner())` :77052), not in the serialized blob; `Created` is purely process-local scene bookkeeping.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE mutable `m_portalObjects` dictionary; `GetPortalList()` returns a fresh flattened `List<ZDO>` allocated per call.
facts.implication: `GetPortalList()` is safe to iterate while mutating connections (vanilla does exactly this); `GetPortals()` is not, but is the cheap read for a high-frequency tick.

facts.claim: `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is built in `Game.Awake` from `m_portalPrefabs`, a `List<GameObject>` serialized field — its contents are Unity Inspector data, not visible in the decompile.
facts.citation: Game.m_portalPrefabs :99828; Game.Awake hash population :100027-100032; Game.PortalPrefabHash property :100021
facts.implication: Which prefab names (portal_wood, portal_stone, others) count as portals — and therefore get the special always-resident/ChunkPortal treatment — must be read at runtime from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, never hard-coded.

facts.claim: `WearNTear` and `Piece` tolerate a ZDO with no fields set: WearNTear falls back to the prefab's `m_health`, Piece falls back to creator 0 / creatorIndex -1.
facts.implication: A server-fabricated portal ZDO needs no health/creator/support fields to instantiate correctly on a vanilla client — only prefab, position, rotation and Persistent.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)
apis.notes: Allocates a fresh ZDOID from the server session, sets owner to the server, calls AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash), registers in m_objectsByID. Does NOT set m_prefab and does NOT set Persistent. Must pass the real portal prefab hash here or the ZDO will never reach the portal save chunk.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetPrefab(int prefab)
apis.notes: Mandatory follow-up to CreateNewZDO. Bumps DataRevision. Without it m_prefab stays 0 and the client's ZNetScene.CreateObject returns null.

apis.signature: public bool ZDO.Persistent { get; set; }
apis.notes: Plain DataFlags bit, no revision bump on set. Must be set true or RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS destroys the portal when any peer disconnects (ZDOMan.RemovePeer :76783 -> :77406).

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetRotation(Quaternion rot)
apis.notes: Stored as euler Vector3. Defines the portal exit vector: TeleportWorld.Teleport computes pos + (rot*Vector3.forward)*m_exitDistance + Vector3.up (:143545-143548).

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: One direction only. No-ops if type+target already match. Calls ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() for ConnectionType.Portal. Use ZDOID.None to disconnect.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.UpdateConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: Same as SetConnection but silently does nothing if the ZDO has no existing connection entry. Prefer SetConnection unless you specifically want that guard.

apis.signature: public ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)
apis.notes: Exact type match required; returns ZDOID.None for a type mismatch or no connection.

apis.signature: public ZDOConnection ZDO.GetConnection()
apis.notes: Returns the raw {m_type, m_target} or null. Use when you need to know the type without guessing.

apis.signature: public static List<ZDOID> ZDOExtraData.GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType connectionType)
apis.notes: IMPORTANT: this enumerates s_connectionsHashData (the SAVE-time hash table), not s_connections. It is empty at runtime until a save or a load has populated hash data. For a live connection enumeration use the parameterless GetAllConnectionZDOIDs() :75409 (keys of s_connections) or iterate GetPortalList().

apis.signature: public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()
apis.notes: Fresh flattened list of every portal ZDO in the world, always complete and always resident. Safe to iterate while mutating connections. Allocates per call — cache it on a slow tick.

apis.signature: public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Returns the LIVE internal dictionary. Read-only use recommended; mutating it desynchronizes AddIfPortal/HandleDestroyedZDO bookkeeping.

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()
apis.notes: Public. MUST be called after any portal ZDO write that is not a Portal-type SetConnection (e.g. a tag rewrite, a LoadFields override), or the entire ChunkPortal file is skipped at the next world save.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)  /  public bool ZDO.IsOwner()  /  public bool ZDO.HasOwner()  /  public long ZDO.GetOwner()
apis.notes: SetOwner is a no-op when the owner is unchanged; it bumps OwnerRevision otherwise. Pass ZDOMan.GetSessionID() (== ZNet.GetUID(), :80866) to claim, 0L to release. IsOwner reads a local DataFlags bit — it is 'am I the owner', not 'does it have an owner'.

apis.signature: public static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()
apis.notes: The server's own ZDO session id. ZNet.GetUID() :80866 is a thin alias.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.GetZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Returns null for ZDOID.None and for unknown ids. Portals are always present server-side.

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id)  /  public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Queues the ZDO at the head of each peer's next sync batch regardless of distance. Vanilla pairs every portal connection write with this.

apis.signature: public void Game.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: Public, no local-player dependency. Runs the self-heal sweep then the random same-tag pairing pass. Calling it manually gives instant re-pairing instead of waiting up to 5s.

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects(Vector2s sector, SimulationDistance simulationDistance, List<ZDO> sectorObjects, List<ZDO> distantSectorObjects = null)
apis.notes: Zone-radius spatial query; includes m_portalObjects for each visited sector via FindObjects :77367. Reuses an internal m_visitedSectorIndices HashSet — NOT reentrant, do not call from a nested iteration.

apis.signature: public bool ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO> zdos, ref int index)
apis.notes: Amortized world-wide prefab scan (400 non-empty sectors per call, returns true when finished). The final pass adds m_objectsBySector[0] plus all of m_portalObjects, so portals ARE found — but only on the last call.

apis.signature: public void ZNetView.LoadFields()
apis.notes: Runs on the client inside ZNetView.Awake. Server side you never call it — you write its inputs: zdo.Set("HasFields", true); zdo.Set("HasFieldsTeleportWorld", true); zdo.Set("TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems", true). Keys are "<ComponentTypeName>.<PublicFieldName>".GetStableHashCode(). Supported field types: int, float, bool, Vector3, string, GameObject (prefab name), ItemDrop (prefab name).

apis.signature: public void ZDO.Set(int hash, T value) for float/Vector3/Quaternion/int/long/string/byte[]/bool/ZDOID
apis.notes: No ownership check on any overload. Bumps DataRevision only when the stored value actually changes. ZDOID is stored as two longs under "<name>_u"/"<name>_i" (ZDO.GetHashZDOID :73562) — do not use it for cross-restart identity since ZDOIDs are regenerated on load.

apis.signature: public string ZDO.GetString(int hash, string defaultValue = "") / public void ZDO.Set(int hash, string value)
apis.notes: The portal tag is ZDOVars.s_tag ("tag", :78617) and the author is ZDOVars.s_tagauthor ("tagauthor", :78619). Both plain strings, no length enforcement on write.

apis.signature: private void Game.SetConnection(ZDO portal, ZDOID connection, bool forceImmediateConnection = false)
apis.notes: Private — reachable only via Harmony/reflection, but it is the ownership-correct pattern worth copying: write locally + ForceSendZDO when owner==0 or owner is not a connected peer; otherwise InvokeRoutedRPC(owner, "RPC_SetConnection", portalID, connectionID).

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc "RPC_SetConnection" (ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)
apis.notes: Registered on every peer (not inside an IsServer branch). Sending it to the owning client makes that client take ownership and write the connection itself — the race-free way to relink a portal a player currently owns.

gotchas: A tag-only portal write is silently lost at the next world save. `DirtyPortalObjects` is the only thing that causes the ChunkPortal file to be written (ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621), and `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, ...)` does not set it — `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` :73832 calls `SetDirtySector`, which marks a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). Always call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`.

Non-pairwise topologies are runtime-only. The disk format gives each ZDO exactly one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot, so rings >2 lose a link, one-way links come back bidirectional, and self-loops are erased — all silently, at the next restart (ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData :75460, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850). Any managed topology must be re-asserted by the mod after every world load.

`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does not set the prefab hash on the ZDO (:76684). Calling `SetPrefab` after a `CreateNewZDO(pos, 0)` means `AddIfPortal` never ran, the ZDO stays in the sector array, `AddObjectsPerChunk` skips it for being a portal prefab, and the ChunkPortal writer never sees it — the portal exists in RAM and vanishes on restart with no error anywhere.
`ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` does nothing unless you own the ZDO (:76929). Deleting a mod-created portal requires `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` first.

`ZDOExtraData.GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType)` reads the SAVE hash table `s_connectionsHashData`, not live connections (:75414). At runtime, outside of a save or immediately-post-load window, it returns an empty list. The parameterless overload (:75409) reads live `s_connections`.

Ownership of a portal near a logged-in player is taken by that player's client within 2 seconds (`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` :76901, driven by `ReleaseZDOS` :76872). A server-side ownership claim is transient unless guarded by a Harmony prefix on `ZDO.SetOwner` (Wonderland's `WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch` is exactly this pattern).

Conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field (`ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` :77103-77133). A server write on a client-owned portal can be wholesale reverted by the owner's next higher-DataRevision send. There is no merge.

`ZDO.Set` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321) — so no DataRevision bump and no resync. A 'touch to force clients to re-read' idiom needs `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(uid)` instead.

Position writes on a portal you do not own do not propagate: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition` gates the revision bump on `IsOwner()` (:73734). Worse, `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752), so a moved portal stays filed under its old sector in `m_portalObjects` and may not be delivered to clients near its new location.
`ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` reuses the shared `m_visitedSectorIndices` HashSet (:77144) — it is not reentrant. Do not call it from inside a loop that is itself iterating its results.

`Game.ConnectPortals`'s self-heal compares tags with bare string equality (:100601). Giving two linked portals different display tags breaks the pair within 5 seconds — both sides get nulled and re-paired randomly.

`ZNetView.LoadFields` only runs at instantiation (`ZNetView.Awake` :82631). A per-portal `m_allowAllItems` flip does not reach players already standing next to that portal; it applies on their next scene creation of that object.

`ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly` is a GLOBAL hash set, not per-ZDO (:74776, seeded at :74814). Reusing any of `ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes` (s_support, s_inUse, s_alert, s_velHash, ...) for portal metadata means that key is stripped from the save for every ZDO in the world.

ZDOIDs are regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552, `ZDOID.SetID` :75878). Never persist a ZDOID as a portal identity. Position, tag, or a mod-private ZDO field are the only stable handles.

`WriteNumItems` caps a ZDO's per-type field count at 32767 and corrupts the stream above that (:83237); `WriteToDisk` warns above 100 (:74670). Put bulk metadata in one string or byte[], not dozens of keys.

The dedicated server is not inert on the scene side — `ZNetScene.Update -> CreateDestroyObjects` runs every 1/30s (:82258). What keeps it from instantiating portals is `Game.FixedUpdate` pinning the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465) plus `IsActiveAreaLoaded()` being false there. Any mod that moves the server reference position into the real world would start creating live GameObjects, including portals with colliders.
`ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps out-of-range zones to Sector 0 (:115755) — the same bucket the server's pinned reference position maps to. Never create a portal ZDO beyond roughly ±16320m.
openQuestions: Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828) — the list is Unity Inspector data. In-game check: from a server console/BepInEx hook, log `string.Join(",", Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash)` and cross-reference against `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` names, or log `Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs.Select(p => p.name)` directly at Game.Awake postfix.

Does the portal prefab's ZNetView have `m_persistent = true`, `m_distant = false`, and `m_type = ObjectType.Default`? In-game check: on a client, `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood").GetComponent<ZNetView>()` and read m_persistent/m_distant/m_type; a mod-created ZDO should match those exactly or the owning client will silently rewrite Type/Distant in ZNetView.Awake (:82232-82240) and Persistent will never be corrected at all.

Does the portal prefab actually carry a `WearNTear` and a `Piece` component (assumed from the piece-building system but not provable from the decompile)? In-game check: enumerate `GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>()` on the portal prefab and log type names; this also gives the exact `<TypeName>` strings needed for `HasFields<TypeName>` LoadFields keys.

Does `LoadFields` actually fire for a server-authored `HasFieldsTeleportWorld`+`TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` on a live vanilla client? In-game check: write the three ZDO ints from the server onto one portal, have a player leave and re-enter the area carrying ore, and see whether `IsTeleportable` allows the transit. This is the single highest-value experiment in this report.

Whether `GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>` in LoadFields (:82676) reaches `TeleportWorld` — i.e. whether TeleportWorld sits on the prefab root or a child. It should either way, but the `HasFields<TypeName>` gate key is `TeleportWorld` regardless of depth; confirm by logging in-game.

Whether `ZDOExtraData.GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType)` is genuinely empty at steady state on a running dedicated server (the hash table is only regenerated in PrepareSave and populated by Load). In-game check: log its count 60s after world load and again immediately after a manual `save` command.
correctionsToExistingSpec: WRONG — 'Ruled Out: Per-portal "allow all items" toggle — `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` is a plain compiled field, never ZDO-backed or RPC'd'. It IS reachable per-portal on a 100% vanilla client via `ZNetView.LoadFields()` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898, called from ZNetView.Awake :82631), which reflects public instance fields off the ZDO using keys `"HasFields"`, `"HasFieldsTeleportWorld"`, `"TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems"`. `m_allowAllItems` is `public bool` (:144169) — an exactly supported type. Caveat: the override is applied at instantiation only, so it takes effect for a player on their next scene creation of that portal, and it is client-honored (same guarantee class as vanilla boss gating), not server-enforced.

WRONG/INCOMPLETE — '[Feasible, medium] Admin-defined fixed networks — rings, hub-and-spoke, one-way links ... A ring is self-stable under vanilla's own self-heal check'. Self-stable at RUNTIME only: `Game.ConnectPortals` :100596-100605 never checks reciprocity, so a ring survives the 5s sweep. But the save format cannot express it — each ZDO gets exactly one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75460-75478), so only a pairwise perfect matching round-trips. A 3-ring loses one member on reload; a one-way link comes back BIDIRECTIONAL (`ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` writes both sides, :77879-77885); a self-loop is erased entirely. Any managed topology must be re-asserted by the mod after every world load, and the spec should re-rate this as 'Feasible, medium, requires post-load reconstruction' rather than implying durability.

WRONG — 'a fan-in hub member can self-loop to stay "connected" without a real return route'. True at runtime, false after a save/reload: RegenerateConnectionHashData overwrites the self-referencing ZDO's source slot with its own Target slot (:75472-75475), leaving a Target hash with no matching source, so the loop is dropped and the portal is randomly re-paired.

INACCURATE — '`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` makes a real, persistent, correctly-owned ZDO with no live GameObject needed'. It makes a correctly-OWNED ZDO but neither a persistent nor a prefab-tagged one: `CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` :76684 never calls `SetPrefab` and never sets `Persistent`. The complete recipe is CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) -> `Persistent = true` -> `SetPrefab(hash)` -> `SetRotation(rot)`. Passing prefabHash 0 and setting the prefab afterwards skips `AddIfPortal` and produces a portal that is saved to no chunk file at all.

MISSING — the spec's tag-rewriting items ('Direct tag write/rename bypassing the RPC', 'Reserved/admin tag namespace', 'Server-side tag length cap') all need an explicit `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) after the write. The portal save chunk is written only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is true (:77621-77631), and a tag write does not set it. Without this the rename is lost at the next world save with no log line.

REFINEMENT — 'no portal GameObject/collider is ever instantiated server-side at all — `ZoneSystem`'s local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position'. The conclusion is right, the mechanism is slightly off: `ZNetScene.Update -> CreateDestroyObjects` DOES run on the dedicated server every 1/30s (:82258-82277). The actual gates are (a) `Game.FixedUpdate` pinning `SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1e6,0,1e6))` every physics tick (:100465) and (b) `CreateObjectsSorted` returning early on `!ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:82105-82110, :114054). Worth stating precisely because it means any mod that relocates the server reference position would begin instantiating live server-side portal objects.

MISSING CONSTRAINT — the spec's '[Feasible-with-caveats, small] Portal to a player's live-attached ship via the SyncTransform connection' collides with a hard structural limit: a ZDO holds exactly ONE `ZDOConnection` (:74797, :75524). A portal ZDO cannot simultaneously carry a Portal connection and a SyncTransform parent link. Any ship-attached-portal design must resolve the ship position by reading the SHIP's ZDO, never by parenting the portal.

MISSING — the spec should note that ZDOIDs are regenerated on every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552 + `ZDOID.SetID` :75878 forcing UserKey=1). Several proposed features (admin-designated pairing, managed group registries, favorites) implicitly need stable portal identity across restarts, and a stored ZDOID will silently point at a different object after a reboot. Identity must be keyed on position, tag, or a mod-private persistent ZDO field.

research.topic: privatearea-security — access control and the routed-RPC trust surface around portals on a dedicated server (Valheim 1.0.7)
research.summary: On a dedicated server the only platform-verified identity is `ZNetPeer.m_socket.GetHostName()` (Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth at connect); every other identity token — `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID`, `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId`, `PrivateArea`'s `playerID` payloads, `ZNetPeer.m_playerName/m_playerID/m_characterID/m_refPos`, and `s_playerID` on the character ZDO — is client self-report. `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)`:83632 receives the authentic socket and discards it, so that method is the one and only cross-check hook — and it is also the only veto point, since `RouteRPC`:83597 is called exclusively from there. But the veto is far narrower than it looks: `Game.FixedUpdate()`:100458 pins `SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6)` on the server build only (the client's `Game.FixedUpdate`:100886 has no such call), so `ZNetScene.m_instances` is permanently empty, `ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo)`:82229 always returns null, and **every ZDO-targeted routed RPC — RPC_SetTag, ToggleEnabled, TogglePermitted, WearNTear RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove — is dead code server-side**; worse, `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC`:83577 skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id`, so a client that owns the portal or ward ZDO retags/toggles it with zero packets on the wire. The server's actual exposure is the global (ZDO-less) routed RPCs — `DestroyZDO`, `Game.RPC_SetConnection`, `SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey`, `SpawnObject`, `RequestZDO` — none of which check the sender or ownership, plus `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`:77076, which validates nothing at all and lets any client rewrite any field of any ZDO by bumping DataRevision. A ward's permitted list, creator and enabled flag are trivially server-readable from the ZDO (`permitted` count + `pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>`, `creator`, `creatorName`, `enabled`), but the radius is a compiled Inspector field and `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns true vacuously server-side because `m_allAreas` is always empty.

facts.claim: `Game.FixedUpdate()` in the SERVER build unconditionally calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick. The CLIENT build's `Game.FixedUpdate()` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:100886) contains no SetReferencePosition call at all — it does respawn + ZInput instead.
facts.implication: This is the root cause of everything else. ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects:82268 uses GetReferencePosition:81019 to pick the sector to instantiate, so no world GameObject (portal, ward, piece) is ever created server-side. It is a stronger, more general statement than 'TeleportWorld.Teleport never runs'.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData)` dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC only via `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)`; `FindInstance` looks up `m_instances` (a Dictionary<ZDO,ZNetView> populated solely by object creation).
facts.implication: On a dedicated server m_instances is always empty, so EVERY ZDO-targeted routed RPC handler is unreachable: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag, PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled/RPC_TogglePermitted, WearNTear.RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove all never execute. The server only relays them. A mod cannot Harmony-patch these handlers to gain a server-side decision point — the patch would never be entered.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` deserializes RoutedRPCData from the wire and never touches the `rpc` parameter. `m_senderPeerID` is read straight out of the packet by `RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` and passed verbatim to the handler by both `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` and `ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC`.
facts.implication: `sender` in every routed RPC handler signature is unauthenticated client input. A client can claim any peer id in every packet. This is also the exact hook: the authentic ZRpc is in scope at :83632 and nowhere downstream.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string, params object[])` calls `HandleRoutedRPC` locally when `targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0`, and calls `RouteRPC` (the only thing that puts bytes on the wire) only when `targetPeerID != m_id`.
facts.implication: CRITICAL for Group 4 of the spec. `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, params)`:82855 targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()`. A client that already owns the portal's or ward's ZDO executes RPC_SetTag / TogglePermitted / ToggleEnabled entirely in-process — no packet is ever sent, so the server cannot observe, log, or veto it at the RPC layer. Server-side ward protection must be detect-and-revert on the ZDO, not an RPC veto.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` is private and is invoked from exactly two places: `InvokeRoutedRPC` and `RPC_RoutedRPC`. On the server it forwards to `GetPeer(rpcData.m_targetPeerID)` when targeted, or to every peer except the claimed sender when targetPeerID==0.
facts.implication: A Harmony prefix returning false on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC`:83632 both suppresses local handling and suppresses relaying — a genuine veto for any RPC that does cross the wire. Patching RouteRPC alone only stops forwarding, after the server already handled it locally.

facts.claim: The complete set of global (ZDO-less) routed RPCs a dedicated server actually executes is the `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register` call sites: ChatMessage, RPC_TeleportPlayer, RPC_SetDreamCinematic, RPC_DamageText, ShowMessage, DestroyZDO, RequestZDO, SpawnObject, SleepStart, SleepStop, RPC_Ping, RPC_Pong, RPC_SetConnection, RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse, RPC_RegisterKill, RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation, the RandEventSystem event RPCs, SetEvent, SetGlobalKey, RemoveGlobalKey.
facts.implication: This is the entire server-side routed-RPC attack surface AND the entire set of routed-RPC handlers a server-only mod can meaningfully Harmony-patch. Anything not on this list is dead server-side.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage pkg)` reads a count and that many ZDOIDs and calls `HandleDestroyedZDO(uid)` on each. `HandleDestroyedZDO` performs no sender check, no ownership check and no prefab check — it fires `m_onZDODestroyed`, removes the ZDO from its sector, removes it from `m_portalObjects`, sets `DirtyPortalObjects`, and releases it to the pool.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO — :76953; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO — :76963-76999; registration at ZDOMan ctor :76155
facts.implication: Any vanilla-protocol client can permanently delete ANY portal (or any ZDO) on the server by broadcasting a forged DestroyZDO with targetPeerID 0 — no ward check exists anywhere in this path. Server-only mods CAN observe and veto it (Harmony prefix on RPC_DestroyZDO, or on RPC_RoutedRPC by method hash).

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(ZDO zdo)` — the send side — is gated on `zdo.IsOwner()`; it only queues the ZDOID into `m_destroySendList`, which `SendDestroyed()` broadcasts as the `DestroyZDO` routed RPC to everybody.
facts.implication: For a server-only mod to delete a portal it must first claim ownership (`zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`) — the WaterBuoyancyEngine pattern — then call `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. The asymmetry (owner-gated send, ungated receive) is exactly the exploit.

facts.claim: There is no `ZNetScene.RPC_Destroy` in 1.0.7. Grep for `RPC_Destroy` across the server assembly returns only `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`:76953 and the unrelated `Ship/Vagon RPC_DestroyAttachment` (:119212, :131791). Destruction is `ZNetScene.Destroy(GameObject)`:82024 → `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` → the DestroyZDO broadcast.
facts.citation: grep RPC_Destroy over assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs; ZNetScene.Destroy — :82024-82037; ZNetView.Destroy — :82746
facts.implication: Correct the spec's naming. `ZNetScene.Destroy` requires a live GameObject and is therefore unusable server-side; the ZDO-level entry point is the only one.

facts.claim: `Game.RPC_SetConnection(long sender, ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)` is registered on `ZRoutedRpc.instance` (ZDO-less, so it DOES run on the dedicated server) and performs no sender check, no ownership check, and no prefab check. It takes ownership of the named ZDO, writes the Portal connection to the arbitrary target ZDOID, and ForceSendZDOs it.
facts.implication: Both an unauthenticated portal-hijack primitive for any client AND the cleanest server-side rewire primitive for the mod. Any 'unbypassable lockdown' built on forcing connections to ZDOID.None can be instantly undone by one malicious client. A server mod should veto or authenticate this RPC before relying on connection state.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey` and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` are registered only when `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`, and neither body inspects `sender`.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem registration — :113445-113449; RPC_SetGlobalKey — :116022; RPC_RemoveGlobalKey — :116031; sender-side ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey — :115943
facts.implication: Any client can set or clear NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll and DungeonBuild on the live server. Group 2 of the spec is not tamper-resistant unless the mod vetoes these two RPCs by sender.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` identifies the peer by socket (`FindPeer(rpc)`) but then applies every incoming ZDO wholesale: if the incoming DataRevision exceeds the local one it overwrites OwnerRevision, DataRevision, owner, position and calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)`. There is no ownership test, no prefab allowlist, no field allowlist, no position sanity check.
facts.implication: The real authority hole. Any client can rewrite a portal's tag/tagauthor/connection and a ward's permitted/creator/enabled lists purely as ZDO data, with no RPC involved at all. Any server-side ward or tag protection must be a ZDO watcher that detects and reverts, and must expect to fight a revision race.

facts.claim: `ZDO.Set(int hash, int value, bool okForNotOwner = false)` ignores its `okForNotOwner` parameter entirely; no ZDO setter in either build performs an ownership check. `IncreaseDataRevision()` bumps DataRevision and, only on a non-server, queues `ZDOMan.ClientChanged`.
facts.citation: ZDO.Set — server :73648-73654 / client :73762-73768; ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision — server assembly, method body immediately preceding IncreaseOwnerRevision (see :73605 etc. call sites)
facts.implication: A server-only mod may write any field of any ZDO without owning it, and the write propagates by revision. But the owning client can win a race by bumping first; for durable writes take ownership (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`) then `ForceSendZDO`.

facts.claim: A ward's permitted list lives entirely in the ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_permitted` ("permitted") holds the int count; entries are the raw string keys `"pu_id" + i` (long) and `"pu_name" + i` (string) for i in [0,count); entries with id == 0 are skipped on read.
facts.implication: YES — a dedicated server can fully read (and write) a ward's permitted list from ZDO data alone with no local player and no GameObject. Use `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_permitted)`, then `zdo.GetLong("pu_id"+i, 0L)` / `zdo.GetString("pu_name"+i)`. Note pu_id/pu_name are NOT ZDOVars constants.

facts.claim: A ward's creator, creator name and enabled flag are also plain ZDO fields: `ZDOVars.s_creator` ("creator", long), `ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex` ("creatorIndex", int), `ZDOVars.s_creatorName` ("creatorName", string), `ZDOVars.s_enabled` ("enabled", bool-as-int).
facts.citation: ZDOVars — s_creator :78393, s_creatorIndex :78395, s_creatorName :78397, s_enabled :78423; Piece.Awake read — :136248; Piece.SetCreator write — :136415-136424; PrivateArea.IsEnabled — :137423; PrivateArea.Setup — :137446
facts.implication: A server-only mod can reconstruct IsPermitted/IsEnabled/GetCreator server-side entirely from ZDO reads. `s_creatorIndex` indexes `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396), which the server maintains from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs — the only bridge from a piece's creator to a verified platform identity.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.m_radius` is a public compiled field with class default 10f, set per-prefab in the Unity Inspector. It never appears in the ZDO. `IsInside` compares `Utils.DistanceXZ(transform.position, point) < m_radius + radius`.
facts.implication: A server-side ward-coverage check must hardcode or config the radius; the decompile's 10f is the class default, not necessarily the guard_stone prefab's value. Needs an in-game/asset check.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.CheckAccess(Vector3, float, bool, bool)` iterates the static instance list `m_allAreas`, which is appended to only in `PrivateArea.Awake()` on a live GameObject.
facts.implication: m_allAreas is permanently empty on a dedicated server, so CheckAccess ALWAYS returns true there — vacuously, not as a permission grant. Never call it from server-side mod code as an authorization check; it is a silent allow-all.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.HaveLocalAccess()` calls `m_piece.IsCreator()` and `IsPermitted(Player.m_localPlayer.GetPlayerID())`. `Piece.IsCreator()` compares the ZDO creator against `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID()`.
facts.implication: Both are local-player/local-profile dependent and would NullReference server-side if ever reached. The server-side equivalent must compare the ZDO's `creator` long against a peer-supplied playerID and validate that peer's claim separately.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.GetHoverText()` early-returns "" when `Player.m_localPlayer == null`; `AddUserList`, `GetCreatorName`, `OnObjectDamaged` (static), `InsideFactionArea`, `GetConnectedAreas`, `GetAllConnectedAreas`, `PokeAllAreasInRange`, `StartConnectionEffects` and `FlashShield` all either need the local player or iterate `m_allAreas`.
facts.citation: PrivateArea.GetHoverText — :137234-137285; AddUserList :137287; static OnObjectDamaged :137534; InsideFactionArea :137695; GetConnectedAreas :137608; GetAllConnectedAreas :137618; PokeAllAreasInRange :137451; FlashShield :137669
facts.implication: The only PrivateArea members usable as a server-side model are the pure ZDO reads: IsEnabled:137423, IsPermitted:137311, GetPermittedPlayers:137349 — and they require reimplementing against a raw ZDO, not calling the vanilla method.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled(long uid, long playerID)` and `RPC_TogglePermitted(long uid, long playerID, string name)` both IGNORE the routed-RPC `uid` (sender) argument entirely and act on the payload `playerID`. RPC_ToggleEnabled gates on `m_piece.GetCreator() == playerID`; RPC_TogglePermitted gates only on `m_nview.IsOwner() && !IsEnabled()`. Bodies are byte-identical in the client build.
facts.citation: PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled — server :137414-137421 / client :138154; PrivateArea.RPC_TogglePermitted — server :137399-137412 / client :138139; registrations :137200-137201
facts.implication: Hardening `m_senderPeerID` alone accomplishes NOTHING for these two RPCs — they never read it. Any client can add itself (or anyone) to an un-enabled ward's permitted list, or toggle a ward it did not build, by passing the creator's playerID. Correcting the spec's Group 4 bullet 2.

facts.claim: `PrivateArea.Interact` sends the playerID from `player.GetPlayerID()`, and `Player.GetPlayerID()` reads `ZDOVars.s_playerID` off the player's own character ZDO, written earlier by that same client in `Player.SetPlayerID`.
facts.implication: The playerID in every ward RPC is client-authored end to end. There is no authenticated binding between a playerID and a platform identity anywhere in vanilla.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag(long sender, string tag, string authorId)` ignores `sender`, gates on `m_nview.IsOwner()`, and writes the client-supplied `authorId` verbatim into `ZDOVars.s_tagauthor` and `tag` into `ZDOVars.s_tag`. The caller `SetText` supplies `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString()`.
facts.implication: `authorId` is a forgeable string; it is used only by `GetTagInfo`:143558 to feed CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC on the displaying client. Do not treat s_tagauthor as an audit trail. Note also no length cap and no censoring at write time.

facts.claim: `WearNTear.RPC_Damage(long sender, HitData hit)` ignores `sender`, gates on `m_nview.IsOwner()` and a health>0 check, then calls `PrivateArea.OnObjectDamaged` (only when `m_triggerPrivateArea`, default true) and `ApplyDamage`. `WearNTear.RPC_Remove(long sender, bool blockDrop)` ignores `sender` and gates only on `m_nview.IsOwner()`.
facts.citation: WearNTear.RPC_Damage — :150332-150408; WearNTear.RPC_Remove — :150419-150425; WearNTear.Destroy — :150427-150477; m_triggerPrivateArea default true — :149257; registrations :149410-149411
facts.implication: Ward protection against destroying a portal is entirely inside the ZDO-owning client's RPC_Damage via PrivateArea.OnObjectDamaged, which on that client only flashes the shield — it never blocks damage for Players-faction wards. The server cannot observe or veto RPC_Damage/RPC_Remove at all (no instance), only react to the resulting health write in RPC_ZDOData or to the DestroyZDO broadcast.

facts.claim: The only platform-verified identity in the entire connection handshake is `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`: Steam checks `ZSteamMatchmaking.instance.VerifySessionTicket(ticket, zSteamSocket.GetPeerID())` and PlayFab calls `PlayFabManager.CheckIfUserAuthenticated(...)`, both disconnecting on failure. Everything else in the PeerInfo packet — `uid`, refPos, player name, playfabId — is taken at face value.
facts.citation: ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo — :79782 (uid read), :79823-79828 (refPos/name/playfabId), :79843-79850 (Steam ticket), :79852-79870 (PlayFab auth), :79904-79907 (assignment to peer)
facts.implication: For any server-side authorization decision the trust anchor must be `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`. Everything else is trust-on-first-use over a verified socket.

facts.claim: `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` builds `PlayerInfo.m_userInfo.m_id` from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` per backend, and `UpdatePlayerHistory` folds those verified IDs into `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory`. `ZNet.instance.GetPlayerList()` exposes the result.
facts.implication: This is the server's trustworthy identity table. It is the correct place to anchor a mod's own playerID→PlatformUserID map: observe the (client-claimed) playerID once per session while the socket-verified PlatformUserID is known, and reject later mismatches.
