facts.claim: `ZNetPeer.m_uid` is assigned once from the peer's own PeerInfo packet on that socket, and `ZNet.IsConnected(long uid)` rejects a second peer claiming the same uid. `ZNetPeer.m_playerID`, `m_characterID`, `m_peerRealtimeMultiplaying` and `m_refPos` are set by RPCs that resolve the peer via `GetPeer(ZRpc)` (socket-derived), but the values are client-supplied.
facts.citation: ZNetPeer fields — :78780-78812; uid assignment :79905 and duplicate rejection ZNet.IsConnected :79993-80007; ZNet.RPC_CharacterID :80899; ZNet.RPC_PlayerID :80918; ZNet.RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData :80395-80409; ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) :80504 (private)
facts.implication: m_uid is socket-BOUND (usable as a session handle and cross-checkable against m_senderPeerID) but not verified; m_playerName/m_playerID/m_characterID/m_refPos are socket-bound containers for unverified claims. `GetPeer(ZRpc)` is private — reproduce it with `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`.

facts.claim: `ZNet.RPC_Kick`, `RPC_Ban` and `RPC_Unban` are the only vanilla handlers that authorize against socket identity: `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())`. They are ZRpc-level (peer-direct), not routed RPCs.
facts.implication: This is vanilla's own template for the cross-check a mod must add to routed RPCs. Reaction primitives for a mod: `ZNet.instance.Kick(string)`:81658 and `ZNet.instance.Ban(string)`:81744, both public and server-side.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject(long spawner, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)` is a global routed RPC with no sender check that calls `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(prefab, pos, rot)` on whichever machine receives it — including the dedicated server.
facts.implication: The single exception to 'a dedicated server never instantiates anything'. A client can make the server instantiate an arbitrary prefab (which will then be reaped by RemoveObjects since it is outside the pinned active area). Worth vetoing; not a reliable server-side spawn primitive.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO(long sender, ZDOID id)` calls `GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO(id)` using the spoofable payload sender.
facts.implication: A client can force the server to push any ZDO it names to any other peer — a reconnaissance/amplification primitive, and a direct consequence of the unverified m_senderPeerID.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` is a public `Action<ZDO>` field invoked from `HandleDestroyedZDO`; `ZNetScene.Awake` already combines its own handler onto it.
facts.implication: A non-Harmony, supported server-side observation hook for 'a portal ZDO was destroyed' — fires for both legitimate and spoofed destructions. Pair it with `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` to filter to portals.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan` keeps `m_deadZDOs` (ZDOID→ticks) and, in `RPC_ZDOData`, if the server is creating a ZDO whose id is in m_deadZDOs it immediately takes ownership and destroys it again.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs — :76043; populated in HandleDestroyedZDO :76997; enforced in RPC_ZDOData :77133-77137
facts.implication: A destroyed portal cannot be resurrected by a client replaying old ZDO data — but a mod must also not try to recreate a portal under a previously-destroyed ZDOID. Use `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3, int prefabHash)`:76674 for a fresh id.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals()` and `Game.SetConnection(ZDO, ZDOID, bool)` run server-side from `ConnectPortalsCoroutine` every 5s with no local-player dependency; SetConnection takes ownership itself when the portal's owner is 0 or is not a connected peer, otherwise it routes `RPC_SetConnection` to the owner.
facts.citation: Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine — :100580-100587; Game.ConnectPortals — :100589-100626; Game.SetConnection — :100636-100651; Game.ForceSetConnection — :100628; ZDOMan.GetPortalList — :77648; ZDOMan.GetPortals — :77643
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's Group 1 premise. Also means the server's own rewrites contend with vanilla's 5s reconciliation, and that a server mod calling Game.RPC_SetConnection's logic directly (own the ZDO, SetConnection, ForceSendZDO) avoids the round-trip entirely.

facts.claim: `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer(long sender, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)` is gated on `Player.m_localPlayer != null` and is therefore a no-op server-side, but the SEND side `Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, ...)` is a public wrapper over `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`. Both `RPC_TeleportPlayer` and `ChatMessage` are registered in `Chat.Awake`.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's Group 3 advice: call `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` directly — the server needs no Chat instance to SEND it, only the receiving client needs one to handle it.

facts.claim: The server can send a ZDO-targeted routed RPC to a specific client without owning or instancing anything, using `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, zdoId, method, args)` — the pattern Wonderland's PlayerNotify uses against the player's own character ZDO.
facts.citation: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long, ZDOID, string, params object[]) — :83577; ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long, string, params) — :82850; usage: /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:23
facts.implication: The server→client direction works fine for feedback ('you are not permitted to retag this portal'); it is only the client→server direction for ZDO-targeted RPCs that is dead.

apis.signature: private void ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)
apis.notes: THE cross-check and veto hook. Harmony prefix via AccessTools.Method(typeof(ZRoutedRpc), "RPC_RoutedRPC"). Both the authentic socket (rpc) and the full payload are in scope here and nowhere downstream. Peek the package non-destructively: record pkg.GetPos(), read m_msgID/m_senderPeerID/m_targetPeerID/m_targetZDO/m_methodHash, then pkg.SetPos(saved) before returning true. Returning false suppresses BOTH local handling and relaying (RouteRPC:83597 is only reachable from here and from InvokeRoutedRPC).

apis.signature: public List<ZNetPeer> ZNet.GetPeers()
apis.notes: Returns the live m_peers list (not a copy). Use `GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` to reproduce the private ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc):80504 — the socket→peer mapping needed inside the RPC_RoutedRPC prefix. GetConnectedPeers():80516 returns a copy.

apis.signature: public ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeer(long uid)
apis.notes: Public. Maps a claimed m_senderPeerID to a ZNetPeer — but only proves the id belongs to SOME connected peer, not to the one that sent the packet. Always compare against the socket-derived peer as well.

apis.signature: public string ISocket.GetHostName()  // via ZNetPeer.m_socket or ZRpc.GetSocket()
apis.notes: The ONLY platform-verified identity on a dedicated server (Steam64 / PlayFab id, validated in RPC_PeerInfo:79843-79870). Vanilla's own admin check does exactly this: ZNet.RPC_Kick:81670.

apis.signature: public List<ZNet.PlayerInfo> ZNet.GetPlayerList()
apis.notes: Each PlayerInfo.m_userInfo.m_id is built from peer.m_socket.GetHostName() (:81271-81280) — the server's verified identity table. PlayerInfo struct at :78935 also carries m_name, m_characterID, m_publicPosition, m_position.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.GetZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Resolve a routed RPC's m_targetZDO to a real ZDO inside the RPC_RoutedRPC prefix, so the mod can tell 'this RPC targets a portal/ward' before vetoing. Pair with zdo.GetPrefab():73817.

apis.signature: public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()  /  public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()
apis.notes: Free, complete server-side portal index (vanilla maintains it in AddIfPortal:77733 and HandleDestroyedZDO:76980). GetPortals() is the cheap spatial form used by Wonderland's PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit.

apis.signature: public List<int> Game.PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }
apis.notes: Stable-hash list of every portal prefab name. The correct prefab filter for 'is this ZDO a portal'. Read-only property with a private setter; the list object itself is mutable if you must extend it.

apis.signature: public int ZDO.GetInt(int hash, int defaultValue = 0) / public long ZDO.GetLong(string name, long defaultValue = 0L) / public string ZDO.GetString(string name, string defaultValue = "") / public bool ZDO.GetBool(int hash, bool defaultValue = false)
apis.notes: The server-side ward read. Permitted list: count = zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_permitted); then zdo.GetLong("pu_id"+i, 0L) and zdo.GetString("pu_name"+i) for i in [0,count), skipping id==0 (mirrors GetPermittedPlayers:137349). Also zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_enabled), zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L), zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_creatorName), zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, -1).

apis.signature: public static readonly int ZDOVars.s_permitted / s_enabled / s_creator / s_creatorIndex / s_creatorName / s_tag / s_tagauthor / s_playerID / s_health
apis.notes: Stable hashes of "permitted", "enabled", "creator", "creatorIndex", "creatorName", "tag", "tagauthor", "playerID", "health". Note pu_id<i> / pu_name<i> have NO ZDOVars constant — hash the concatenated string.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid) / public void ZDO.UpdateConnection(...) / public ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)
apis.notes: SetConnection creates-or-replaces; UpdateConnection only replaces an existing entry (ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection:74963 returns false when no entry exists). Both bump DataRevision and set ZDOMan dirty-portals. Use ConnectionType.Portal.

apis.signature: public void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid) / public bool ZDO.IsOwner() / public long ZDO.GetOwner() / public static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()
apis.notes: The ownership-claim pattern: zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) then write then ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid). Required before ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (owner-gated); NOT required for plain field writes (no setter checks ownership) but advisable to win revision races.

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id) / public void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Push a ZDO to every peer, or to one peer. The targeted overload is server-only guarded internally (`if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())`).

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(ZDO zdo)
apis.notes: Owner-gated (`if (zdo.IsOwner())`) — call SetOwner(GetSessionID()) first. Queues into m_destroySendList; SendDestroyed:76937 broadcasts the DestroyZDO routed RPC to all peers.

apis.signature: public Action<ZDO> ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed  (public field)
apis.notes: Delegate.Combine onto it for a Harmony-free 'ZDO destroyed' observer. Fires on both legitimate and spoofed destructions, before the ZDO is removed from m_objectsByID, so the ZDO is still readable inside the callback.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)
apis.notes: Public. Mints a real, server-owned, persistent ZDO with no GameObject. The route to a server-created portal. Fresh ZDOID each call, so it sidesteps the m_deadZDOs:76043 resurrection block.

apis.signature: public void ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: Server→client push. Works for ZDO-targeted RPCs without any local instance (PlayerNotify pattern: InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageType, text, 0)). Also the direct way to force-teleport: InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true) — no Chat.instance needed on the server.

apis.signature: public void ZNet.Kick(string user) / public void ZNet.Ban(string user) / public void ZNet.RemotePrint(ZRpc rpc, string text)
apis.notes: Server-side enforcement primitives. Kick/Ban resolve by PlatformUserID or player name (InternalKick:81689). RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, text) prints into that client's console — a direct, no-client-mod feedback channel.

apis.signature: public void Game.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: Public, runs from ConnectPortalsCoroutine:100580 on the server every 5s. Call directly for instant re-pairing after a tag write.

apis.signature: private void ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage pkg)
apis.notes: Harmony-patchable server-side (it IS a global routed RPC, so it executes on the dedicated server). Prefix to inspect the ZDOID list and drop destructions of protected portals. Note the package is consumed by reading — re-position or re-read as needed.

apis.signature: private void Game.RPC_SetConnection(long sender, ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)
apis.notes: Executes on the dedicated server (global routed RPC). Harmony-patchable for a sender check. Its body is also the exact server-side rewire recipe: SetOwner(GetSessionID()); SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, target); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(id).

apis.signature: private void ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string name) / private void ZoneSystem.RPC_RemoveGlobalKey(long sender, string name)
apis.notes: Server-only registrations (:113447-113448), no sender check. Harmony-patch to restrict NoPortals/TeleportAll/NoBossPortals/DungeonBuild to the mod itself. Public server-side setters: ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string):115943, GetGlobalKey(string):115968, RemoveGlobalKey(string):115993.

gotchas: `PrivateArea.CheckAccess(...)` returns TRUE on a dedicated server for every point, always — not because access was granted but because `m_allAreas`:137173 is empty (nothing is ever instantiated). Calling it from server-side mod code is a silent allow-all that looks like a working permission check. (CheckAccess :137547, m_allAreas.Add only in Awake :137197.)

A client that OWNS the target ZDO never puts the RPC on the wire: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC`:83588 handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID == m_id`, and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,...)`:82855 targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()`. So RPC_SetTag, TogglePermitted and ToggleEnabled issued by the ZDO's owner are invisible to the server. Any 'veto the RPC' design fails for the most common case.

Even when the RPC does cross the wire, the dedicated server NEVER runs the handler: `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83656 requires `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)`:82229 to be non-null, and `m_instances`:81927 is permanently empty. Harmony-patching `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`, `PrivateArea.RPC_TogglePermitted` or `WearNTear.RPC_Damage` on a dedicated server compiles fine and never fires.

Hardening `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` does nothing for the three portal/ward RPCs that matter: `PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled`:137414, `RPC_TogglePermitted`:137399 and `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 all ignore the sender argument entirely and act on a payload `playerID`/`authorId`.

The real hole is not the RPC layer at all — it is `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`:77076, which applies any incoming ZDO wholesale on a higher DataRevision with zero validation. A client can rewrite a portal's tag, a ward's permitted list, a piece's creator and any health value as plain ZDO data, with no RPC involved.

`ZDOMan.DestroyZDO`:76929 is owner-gated on SEND but `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76963 is completely ungated on RECEIVE. Any client can delete any portal on the server by broadcasting a forged `DestroyZDO` (registered globally at :76155). No ward check exists anywhere in that path.

`Game.RPC_SetConnection`:100653 is an unauthenticated global routed RPC that rewires any ZDO's Portal connection to any target. A lockdown implemented by forcing every connection to `ZDOID.None` can be undone instantly by one malicious client — and vanilla's own `ConnectPortals`:100589 will then re-pair by tag 5 seconds later anyway.

There is no `ZNetScene.RPC_Destroy` in 1.0.7. `ZNetScene.Destroy(GameObject)`:82024 needs a live GameObject and is therefore unusable server-side. The only server-reachable destruction entry point is `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO(ZDO)`.

`pu_id0`, `pu_name0`, `pu_id1`, ... are raw runtime-concatenated string keys with NO `ZDOVars` constant (`PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers`:137338). Writing `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (the count) without also writing the matching indexed keys silently produces phantom or truncated entries — `GetPermittedPlayers`:137349 skips id==0 but still honours the count.
`PrivateArea.m_radius`:137132 has a class default of 10f, but the real guard-stone value is a Unity Inspector override invisible to the decompile. Hardcoding 10f will under-cover every ward.

`Piece.SetCreator`:136415 only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0L` — it runs on the placing CLIENT, using that client's local copy of `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` to compute `s_creatorIndex`. So `creator` and `creatorIndex` are client-authored; `creatorIndex` at least points into a server-maintained table (`m_playerHistory`:112396, fed from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs at :81271-81280), so the server can validate it — `creator` (the raw playerID) it cannot.

`ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject`:82355 really does `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate` on the dedicated server — the one client-triggerable exception to 'the server instantiates nothing'. The object is then reaped by RemoveObjects since it sits outside the pinned active area, but it is a free unauthenticated Instantiate.

`ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs`:76043 makes the server destroy any ZDO re-created under a previously-destroyed ZDOID (`RPC_ZDOData`:77133). A mod that deletes and then recreates a portal must use a fresh `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO`:76674 id, not the old one.

`ZDO.Set(int hash, int value, bool okForNotOwner = false)`:73648 — the `okForNotOwner` parameter is dead in both the server and client builds. There is no ownership assertion on any ZDO setter, so a non-owning write succeeds silently and then loses a DataRevision race to the owner. Take ownership for durable writes.

`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc rpc)`:80504 is PRIVATE. Reproduce it with `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (GetPeers:81630 is public and returns the live list) rather than reflecting into it.

`ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` receives a ZPackage whose read position advances as you inspect it. A prefix that peeks at the header must save and restore `pkg.GetPos()` or the real handler will read garbage.

`TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 applies no length cap and no profanity filter at write time — the 10-char cap lives only in the client's `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`:143444 and censoring only at display time in `GetTagInfo`:143558. A hacked client can store an arbitrarily long or hostile tag.

`Chat.Awake`:41624 registers `ChatMessage` and `RPC_TeleportPlayer`, and `MessageHud`:55808 registers `ShowMessage`. If those singletons do not exist on a dedicated server, those global RPC hashes are simply unregistered and `HandleRoutedRPC`:83660 logs 'Failed to find rpc method' — patch targets on them would never fire. Send-side use (`ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(...)`) is unaffected.
openQuestions: What is the actual `PrivateArea.m_radius` on the guard_stone prefab? The class default is 10f (:137132) but it is an Inspector override living in Unity asset data. Exact check: in-game, place a guard stone and binary-search the distance at which another player's build/interact is refused; or dump the guard_stone prefab from the AssetBundle and read the PrivateArea component's m_radius. A server-side ward model is wrong at every ward until this number is known.

Does `Chat.instance` exist on a dedicated server (i.e. does `Chat.Awake`:41624 ever run)? Exact check: connect a client, send a chat message, and grep the server log for `ZLog.LogWarning("Failed to find rpc method " + hash)` from `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83660 with the stable hash of "ChatMessage". Same test with "ShowMessage" for `MessageHud`:55808. Determines whether those two are patchable server-side.

Is `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()`:100564 non-null on a dedicated server? `Piece.IsCreator()`:136436 dereferences it. Only matters if any server mod code path can reach a PrivateArea/Piece instance method, but it settles whether such a call NREs or silently compares against 0. Exact check: a trivial probe patch logging `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()?.GetPlayerID()` on server start.

Does the guard_stone prefab set `m_enabledByDefault` false and `m_ownerFaction == 0` (Faction.Players is a different code path in `OnObjectDamaged`:137642 and short-circuits `GetHoverText`:137240 and `Interact`:137374)? Inspector data. Exact check: dump the prefab, or observe in-game whether a freshly placed guard stone is inactive until the creator interacts.

Which ZDO actually owns a portal in steady state on a live server — the nearest client, or the server after `Game.SetConnection`:100636 claims it? This decides how often a client's RPC_SetTag is purely local (invisible to the server) versus routed. Exact check: on a running server, log `zdo.GetOwner()` versus `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` for every entry of `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` on a 10s timer with players nearby and away.

Does `ZoneSystem`'s local-zone creation on the server ever instantiate anything near (1e6,0,1e6)? The spec asserts it does not; `Game.FixedUpdate`:100465 pins the reference position there but nothing in the decompile proves no zone is generated at that coordinate. Exact check: log `ZNetScene.instance.m_instances.Count` on a running dedicated server over time — it should be 0 or near-0.
correctionsToExistingSpec: Group 4, bullet 1 ('Harden RPC sender identity against spoofing') is correct that `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` and `RPC_SetTag`'s `authorId` are unverified, but incomplete in a way that changes the design: the three portal/ward RPCs in question do not READ `m_senderPeerID` at all. `PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled`:137414, `RPC_TogglePermitted`:137399 and `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag`:143586 ignore their sender parameter and act on a payload `playerID`/`authorId`. Cross-checking m_senderPeerID against the socket buys nothing for them; the mod must instead validate the payload playerID against a socket-anchored identity map.

Group 4, bullet 3 ('reject an RPC_SetTag from a non-permitted player') is not achievable as an RPC veto in the general case. `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC`:83588 short-circuits to local handling and never calls `RouteRPC` when the sender owns the target ZDO, so a client that owns the portal retags it with zero packets. And even when the RPC is routed, `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC`:83656 → `ZNetScene.FindInstance`:82229 is always null on the server, so the handler is never entered there. Ward-gated retag protection must be implemented as a ZDO watcher that detects a change to `ZDOVars.s_tag`/`s_tagauthor` and reverts it (claim ownership, restore, ForceSendZDO), never as an RPC veto.

The spec's central-constraint section attributes the no-instantiation fact to 'ZoneSystem's local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position'. The precise, citable mechanism is `Game.FixedUpdate()`:100458-100465 in the SERVER build calling `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` unconditionally every physics tick — a method body that does not exist in the client build (client `Game.FixedUpdate`:100886 does respawn + ZInput instead). `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects`:82268 reads that position. Also: the consequence is broader than Teleport() — it kills EVERY ZDO-targeted routed RPC server-side via `ZNetScene.FindInstance`:82229.

The spec does not list `Game.RPC_SetConnection`:100653 as an attack surface. It is one: an unauthenticated global routed RPC that takes ownership of any named ZDO and points its Portal connection at any other ZDOID. This directly undermines Group 2's '[Feasible, medium] genuinely unbypassable lockdown — force-disconnect every portal pair server-side': a single malicious client can re-link any pair at will. That bullet should be downgraded to 'unbypassable only if RPC_SetConnection is also vetoed by sender'.

The spec does not list `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`:76953 / `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76963 as an attack surface. Any client can permanently delete any portal (or any ZDO) on the server by broadcasting a forged DestroyZDO with no ward check anywhere in the path. Conversely this IS observable and vetoable server-side, which the spec also omits — `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`:76033 is a public Action<ZDO> giving a Harmony-free 'portal destroyed' hook.

The spec does not mention `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey`:116022/:116031 being sender-unchecked. Every item in Group 2 (NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll, DungeonBuild) can be set OR cleared by any connected client. These keys are not merely 'client-honored' — they are also client-writable.

The task framing names `ZNetScene.Destroy`/`RPC_Destroy`/`ZDOMan.DestroyZDO`. There is no `RPC_Destroy` in 1.0.7 — grep returns only `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO`:76953 and the unrelated `Ship`/`Vagon` `RPC_DestroyAttachment` (:119212, :131791). `ZNetScene.Destroy(GameObject)`:82024 exists but is unusable server-side (needs a live GameObject).

The spec's implicit assumption that portal/ward RPC handlers could be patched server-side to gain a decision point should be stated as explicitly false. The complete set of routed RPC handlers a dedicated server actually executes is the ~20 `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register` sites (:41626, :41627, :42373, :46355, :55808, :76155, :76156, :81954, :100063-100072, :105284-105287, :106781, :113447-113448). Nothing registered on a `ZNetView` is on that list.

Group 4's ward work should note that a ward's permitted list, creator, creatorName and enabled flag ARE fully server-readable from the ZDO with no local player (`permitted` count + `pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>`, per `PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers`:137349) — so the 'Wonderland/Lite-maintained shadow list of wards' the spec calls for is unnecessary for the permission data itself. The only thing genuinely missing from the ZDO is the radius (`PrivateArea.m_radius`:137132, a compiled Inspector field).

research.topic: target-sources-player — everything a dedicated server can locate about a player (1.0.7)
research.summary: All citations are to files in /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/libs-Tools/1.0/DECOMPILED/ (SERVER = assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs, CLIENT = assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs). A dedicated server's complete live view of a player is exactly two objects: the ZNetPeer (uid, PlatformUserID via socket host name, character name, refPos refreshed every 2s, characterID) and the character ZDO behind peer.m_characterID (position/rotation at ~50ms freshness, s_playerID, s_playerName, health/stamina/eitr, s_inBed, s_dead, s_pvp, s_crowned, and every VisEquipment slot as a prefab hash). Everything a player "owns" that survives their logout is a normal persistent world ZDO and is fully server-readable: Bed s_owner/s_ownerName, every placed Piece's s_creator (= that player's profile UID) + s_creatorIndex (→ ZNet.World.m_playerHistory PlatformUserID, persisted in the .fwl), PrivateArea s_creatorName + the pu_id{i}/pu_name{i} permitted list, TeleportWorld s_tag/s_tagauthor, Tameable s_tamed/s_tamedName/s_tamedNameAuthor/s_follow, and TombStone s_owner/s_ownerName/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint plus the Container s_items blob — which is the ONE and only place a player's actual inventory is ever visible to the server. The player's live inventory, skills, recipes, unique keys, map data, custom spawn point, logout point and death point are all PlayerProfile/Player.Save state written only to that client's own .fch file; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. The two non-obvious wins: a player's *active* bed is not stored anywhere server-side, but is inferable live from s_inBed on the character ZDO (position-matched to a bed ZDO) and from peer.m_refPos, which Game.UpdateRespawn pins to the custom spawn point while the player is dead; and ZNetPeer.m_playerID is permanently 0 because no vanilla client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC, so the character ZDO's s_playerID is the only server-side route to a profile UID.

facts.claim: Bed ownership is a pure ZDO write: RPC_SetOwner stores ZDOVars.s_owner (long = PlayerProfile UID) and s_ownerName (string = profile name) on the bed's own ZDO, gated on m_nview.IsOwner().
facts.implication: Every claimed bed in the world is server-readable offline and forever: scan bed ZDOs, read s_owner/s_ownerName. No client involvement, no live player needed.

facts.claim: A player can own an unlimited number of beds. Bed.Interact only writes ownership when GetOwner()==0; claiming a second unclaimed bed does not clear the first, and nothing ever resets s_owner.
facts.implication: "The player's bed" is ambiguous server-side. Any bed-targeting portal feature must either accept the ambiguity, pick by a rule (nearest/most recent), or use the live inference channels below.

facts.claim: Which bed is the ACTIVE spawn point lives only in PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_spawnPoint/m_haveCustomSpawnPoint, keyed by world UID, in the player's local .fch file. Bed.IsCurrent() resolves it by comparing the bed's transform to Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetCustomSpawnPoint().
facts.implication: There is NO server-readable 'active bed' field. Confirms the existing spec's caveat, and rules out ever reading it directly.

facts.claim: Selecting a bed as your spawn point produces zero network traffic: Bed.Interact's non-claim branch calls only Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(GetSpawnPoint()) and a local Message — no RPC, no ZDO write.
facts.implication: Not even an RPC-interception patch can observe a spawn-point change. The only signals are indirect (see the s_inBed and refPos facts).

facts.claim: Bed.GetSpawnPoint() returns m_spawnPoint.position — a Unity child Transform on the bed prefab, never written to the ZDO. The only s_spawnPoint writers relevant to players are TombStone, BaseAI, Fish and RandomFlyingBird.
facts.implication: A server targeting 'the bed' gets the bed ZDO's position+rotation, not the exact lie-down/spawn offset. Close enough for a portal destination; not identical to vanilla respawn placement.

facts.claim: LIVE ACTIVE-BED INFERENCE: the character ZDO carries ZDOVars.s_inBed (bool), and vanilla's own server code already reads it off character ZDOs — Game.UpdateSleeping is gated on ZNet.instance.IsServer() and EverybodyIsTryingToSleep() iterates ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS() reading s_inBed.
facts.citation: Game.UpdateSleeping — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100712-100733; Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep — :100735-100748; Player/Humanoid writes s_inBed at :15799 and :15917
facts.implication: While a player sleeps, the server can read s_inBed==true plus the character ZDO position and match it to the nearest Bed ZDO — a real, vanilla-precedented way to learn which bed a player actually uses.

facts.claim: SECOND ACTIVE-SPAWN INFERENCE: during respawn Game.UpdateRespawn calls ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(customSpawnPoint) (or the logout point), and that reference position is exactly what the client reports to the server every 2s as peer.m_refPos.
facts.citation: Game.UpdateRespawn — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100320 (logout point) and :100349 (custom spawn point); ZNet.RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData — :80395-80408
facts.implication: While a player is dead/respawning, peer.m_refPos leaks their exact custom spawn point (and, at login, their logout point) to the server before any character ZDO exists. A leading indirect route to a player's real home.

facts.claim: peer.m_refPos is updated on the server every 2 seconds regardless of the player's privacy setting; peer.m_publicRefPos only controls whether that position is re-broadcast to other clients inside PlayerInfo.
facts.citation: ZNet.RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80395-80408; ZNet.SendPeriodicData 2f cadence — :80337-80345; ZNet.UpdatePlayerList gating of m_position — :81256-81259 and :81269-81273
facts.implication: Use ZNet.GetPeers()/GetConnectedPeers() and peer.m_refPos, never GetPlayerList()[i].m_position — the latter is empty for any player who turned public position off.

facts.claim: The server's live per-player object is ZNetPeer: m_uid, m_refPos, m_publicRefPos, m_characterID (ZDOID), m_playerID, m_simulationDistance, m_serverSyncedPlayerData, m_playerName, m_playfabId, m_socket.
facts.implication: This plus the character ZDO is the complete live player surface. Everything else must be derived from world ZDOs.

facts.claim: ZNetPeer.m_playerID is ALWAYS 0 on a dedicated server. The server registers rpc.Register<long>("PlayerID", RPC_PlayerID), but nothing anywhere in the vanilla client assembly ever invokes "PlayerID".
facts.citation: ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79916; ZNet.RPC_PlayerID — :80920-80927; CLIENT-side: assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:80108 is the only occurrence of the string "PlayerID" (register only), and m_playerID appears only at :78937 and :81110
facts.implication: Never read peer.m_playerID. The only server-side source of a player's profile UID is ZDOVars.s_playerID on their character ZDO.

facts.claim: Player.SetPlayerID writes ZDOVars.s_playerID (PlayerProfile.m_playerID) and ZDOVars.s_playerName into the character ZDO exactly once, and is called from PlayerProfile.LoadPlayerData during spawn.
facts.implication: Character ZDO → stable per-character identity. This is the value to persist in any server-side per-player registry.

facts.claim: Ordering guarantee: Game.SpawnPlayer instantiates the Player, calls m_playerProfile.LoadPlayerData (which sets s_playerID/s_playerName) and only THEN calls ZNet.instance.SetCharacterID(component.GetZDOID()).
facts.implication: By the time the server knows peer.m_characterID, s_playerID is already set on that ZDO client-side — but the ZDO data still has to arrive over the wire, so tolerate a brief window where s_playerID reads 0.

facts.claim: ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS() returns the live character ZDO of every ready peer (plus the local one, which is None on a dedicated server) by looking each peer.m_characterID up in ZDOMan.
facts.implication: The single cleanest server-side 'all players' enumeration. Wonderland's ConnectedCharacters.All() reimplements this with the peer attached — Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:57-79.

facts.claim: Client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent: any ZDO change on a client calls ZDOMan.ClientChanged, which queues it into m_clientChangeQueue, and the client's CreateSyncList drains that queue wholesale to the server peer.
facts.citation: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision/IncreaseOwnerRevision — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73832-73849; ZDOMan.ClientChanged — :77727-77730; ZDOMan.CreateSyncList non-server branch — :77241-77258; ZDOMan.Update 0.05s per-peer cadence — :76843-76852
facts.implication: The server ALWAYS receives a player's character ZDO updates even though its own reference position is a million metres away. Player positions are fresh to ~50-100ms.

facts.claim: A dedicated server instantiates no GameObjects near any player: Game.FixedUpdate unconditionally pins ZNet's reference position to (1000000,0,1000000) and ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects only ever creates objects in that zone.
facts.implication: Bed, PrivateArea, TeleportWorld, TombStone, Container and Player components never exist server-side. Every fact below must be reached as raw ZDO data. PrivateArea.m_allAreas (:137198) is permanently empty server-side.

facts.claim: Player character ZDOs are non-persistent and are destroyed when the peer disconnects: ZDOMan.RemovePeer calls RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS, which takes ownership of and destroys every non-persistent ZDO whose owner is no longer a connected peer.
facts.implication: Everything reachable only through the character ZDO (live position, equipped gear, health, s_inBed) is available ONLY while the player is connected. Any per-player state a mod wants across sessions must be copied out and stored by the mod, keyed on s_playerID or PlatformUserID.

facts.claim: A player's full inventory is NEVER networked to a dedicated server. Player.Save(ZPackage) serialises inventory, known recipes/stations/materials, uniques, trophies, foods, skills and customData into a package that PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData stores in m_playerData, which is written only to <name>.fch on that client's own disk.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's 'Ruled Out' item. No server-side inventory inspection, no server-side skill/recipe reads, no debiting a living player's own inventory.

facts.claim: ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles() does NOT collect anything: it invokes the "SavePlayerProfile" RPC on each peer, whose handler simply calls Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile on that client, writing that client's own local file. Nothing is returned to the server.
facts.implication: Definitively refutes 'inventory reaches the server at logout/save time'. The logout boundary carries no player data whatsoever.

facts.claim: ZDOVars.s_items is written by exactly one live code path in the whole assembly — Container.Save() — plus a one-time world-version migration in ZDOMan.ConvertContainers. Character ZDOs never carry item data.
facts.implication: Any server-side item read or write must target a Container-family ZDO's s_items byte blob (Wonderland's Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs is the ready-made implementation).

facts.claim: THE EXCEPTION — a dead player's inventory IS server-readable. Player.CreateTombStone moves the whole inventory into a tombstone Container and TombStone.Setup stamps ZDOVars.s_ownerName + s_owner (= that player's profile UID) on the ZDO; TombStone.Awake additionally writes s_timeOfDeath (ZNet time ticks) and s_spawnPoint (the death position).
facts.citation: Player.CreateTombStone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12702-12714; TombStone.Setup — :19845-19853; TombStone.Awake — :19732-19740; TombStone.PositionCheck reading s_spawnPoint — :19921
facts.implication: Server-visible, persistent, offline-readable: who died, exactly where, exactly when, and every item they were carrying. This is the only inventory window and the only death-location record the server ever gets.

facts.claim: The player's own death point / logout point / home point are PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData fields set locally (Player.OnDeath calls Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetDeathPoint) and never leave the client.
facts.implication: Use the tombstone ZDO as the server-side death-location proxy; there is no other.

facts.claim: Equipped/visible gear IS in the character ZDO as prefab stable-hash ints, written by VisEquipment on the owning client: s_rightItem(+quality), s_leftItem(+variant/quality), s_chestItem, s_legItem, s_helmetItem, s_shoulderItem(+variant/quality), s_utilityItem, s_trinketItem, s_leftBackItem/s_rightBackItem, plus s_beardItem/s_hairItem/s_skinColor/s_hairColor/s_modelIndex.
facts.implication: The server can see what a player has EQUIPPED (weapons, armour, utility, back slots) in real time — a partial carry check. It cannot see backpack contents, and vanilla's portal ore check is against the whole inventory, so this does not enable item enforcement.

facts.claim: Every placed building piece records its builder in the ZDO: Piece.SetCreator writes ZDOVars.s_creator (long = the placing player's PlayerProfile UID, identical to that character ZDO's s_playerID) and s_creatorIndex (int = index into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory). Player.PlacePiece calls it for every piece placed.
facts.implication: THERE IS a build-ownership record in every structure ZDO, persistent and offline-readable. This is how a server-only mod knows which portals/beds/wards a given player built, with no client mod and no new bookkeeping.

facts.claim: s_creatorIndex resolves to a PlatformUserID through ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which the server persists in the .fwl world file and pushes to clients via the HistoricalPlayerList RPC (so the client's index is meaningful to the server).
facts.citation: World.SaveWorldFWLData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112587-112591 (load :112709-112713); ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory — :81436-81461; ZNet.SendHistoricalPlayerList — :81317-81341; ZNet.RPC_HistoricalPlayerList — :81419-81434; ZNet.World — :79151; World.m_playerHistory — :112396
facts.implication: Cross-session, account-level ownership of structures without any mod-side registry. Caveat: FindIndex returns -1 if the placer was not yet in the history when they placed, and m_playerHistory holds PlatformUserID + display names only — not character names, not profile UIDs.

facts.claim: Wards: PrivateArea.Setup writes ZDOVars.s_creatorName (the builder's profile name), ownership is the Piece s_creator, activation is ZDOVars.s_enabled, and the permitted-player list is plain ZDO data — s_permitted (count) plus "pu_id{i}" (long playerID) and "pu_name{i}" (string) per entry.
facts.citation: PrivateArea.Setup — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137446-137449 (called Player.PlacePiece:12518); PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers — :137338-137347; GetPermittedPlayers — :137349-137364; IsEnabled/SetEnabled — :137423-137443; ZDOVars.s_permitted — :78529
facts.implication: A server-only mod can fully read a ward's owner and permitted roster from ZDO data alone — the exact prerequisite the spec's Group 4 'shadow list of wards' calls for. No PrivateArea component needed.

facts.claim: Portals carry TWO independent identity fields: Piece s_creator (the placer's profile UID, from PlacePiece) and ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, a PlatformUserID string written by whoever last set the tag (TeleportWorld.SetText sends PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString()).
facts.implication: 'This player's own portals' is answerable server-side two ways: by builder (s_creator == their s_playerID) or by last tagger (s_tagauthor == their PlatformUserID). The two can disagree; s_creator is the stronger ownership claim.

facts.claim: s_tagauthor is a raw, unverified client self-report, but the server CAN cross-check it: peer.m_socket.GetHostName() is the authenticated PlatformUserID the connection was established with (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo verifies a Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth against it).
facts.citation: TeleportWorld.SetText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143579-143585; ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo ticket verification — :79836-79868; ZNet.GetPeerByHostName — :80480-80490; ZNet.UpdatePlayerList deriving m_userInfo.m_id from m_socket.GetHostName() — :81264-81274
facts.implication: Concrete implementation of the spec's Group-4 identity hardening: compare the authorId argument of RPC_SetTag against GetPeerByHostName-derived identity for the sending peer, not against anything the client also chose.

facts.claim: Tamed creatures record an owner only weakly: ZDOVars.s_tamed (bool), s_tamedName (string) and s_tamedNameAuthor (PlatformUserID string, or the literal "host"), plus ZDOVars.s_follow which holds the follow target's CHARACTER NAME string and is cleared to "" on 'stay'.
facts.citation: Character.SetTamed writing s_tamed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4495; Tameable.RPC_SetName — :19272-19279; Tameable.RPC_Command writing s_follow — :19444 and :19457; Tameable.UpdateSavedFollowTarget reading it — :19478-19482; ZDOVars.s_tamed/s_tamedName/s_tamedNameAuthor/s_follow — :78621/:78623/:78625/:78429
facts.implication: 'This player's tames' is reachable server-side only by fuzzy name match (s_follow / s_tamedNameAuthor). There is no tame→playerID field. Names collide; treat as a heuristic.

facts.claim: ZDOVars.s_owner is overloaded across unrelated prefabs — Bed and TombStone store a PlayerProfile UID in it, GrapplingPoint stores a ZDOID.ID of a character.
facts.citation: Bed.RPC_SetOwner — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119813-119819; TombStone.Setup — :19845-19849; GrapplingPoint — write :127909, read :127842; ZDOVars.s_owner — :78517
facts.implication: Never query s_owner globally. Always filter by prefab hash first, or you will attribute grappling hooks to players.

facts.claim: ZNet.PlayerInfo carries m_name (character name), m_characterID, m_userInfo (PlatformUserID / displayName / playfabId / serverAssignedDisplayName), m_publicPosition and m_position — but UpdatePlayerList omits the host's own entry when SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == GraphicsDeviceType.Null, i.e. on a dedicated server.
facts.implication: GetPlayerList() on a dedicated server is exactly the connected peers, no phantom host entry — but with positions blanked for privacy-off players. It is the right source for name↔PlatformUserID mapping, the wrong one for positions.

facts.claim: Name→identity mapping available server-side, in full: peer.m_playerName (the character name, taken from the client's own profile in RPC_PeerInfo) ↔ peer.m_socket.GetHostName() (PlatformUserID) ↔ peer.m_characterID → character ZDO s_playerName + s_playerID (profile UID). ZNet.GetPeerByPlayerName does the reverse lookup.
facts.citation: ZNet.SendPeerInfo writing GetPlayerProfile().GetName() — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79740; ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo assigning peer.m_playerName — :79900-79903; ZNet.GetPeerByPlayerName — :80468-80478; Player.GetPlayerName — :10147-10154
facts.implication: A complete four-way identity join exists live. The two durable keys are s_playerID (per character file) and PlatformUserID (per account); peer.m_uid is a connection and changes every session.

facts.claim: Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() on a dedicated server returns a throwaway `new PlayerProfile()` created in Game.Awake with name "Stranger", a fresh Utils.GenerateUID() m_playerID and no filename (so Load() returns false).
facts.implication: Any vanilla method that compares against GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID() (Bed.IsMine, Piece.IsCreator, TombStone.IsOwner, Container.CheckAccess) is meaningless server-side. Never call them; read the ZDO fields directly.

facts.claim: A player's map data, map pins and build-menu favourites are PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_mapData / the Hud build UI blob inside Player.Save — pure local file content.
facts.implication: TortalPortal's Favorites / PortalMapPins features have no server-side counterpart at all — not even a read.

facts.claim: Player unique keys (Player.m_uniques, AddUniqueKey/TryGetUniqueKeyValue) live in the Player.Save blob and drive only local rate modifiers; they are never sent to the server.
facts.citation: Player.m_uniques — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:9711; Player.Save — :14122-14126; Player.AddUniqueKey — :14528-14540; ZoneSystem.UpdateWorldRates player-key branch — :101148 and :101180
facts.implication: Per-player flags must be stored by the mod (keyed on s_playerID/PlatformUserID) or in world global keys — never expect to read a player key from the server.

facts.claim: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type, hash) enumerates every ZDO that has a given field, but the implementation is a nested foreach over every ZDO and every one of its fields — an unindexed full scan.
facts.citation: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407; the generic extension it delegates to — :75707-75722
facts.implication: Usable for a one-shot startup index (e.g. 'every ZDO with s_owner' or 'every ZDO with s_creator'), never per-tick. For repeated work use ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative (:77442) or FindSectorObjects (:77142), as Wonderland's ZdoSpatialQuery does.

facts.claim: Server→player teleport is a plain routed RPC and does not need Chat.instance: Chat.TeleportPlayer is a one-line wrapper over ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport); the handler is registered by the client's own Chat.Awake.
facts.citation: Chat.TeleportPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41957-41960; Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer — :41962-41968; registration Chat.Awake — :41627; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC overloads — :83554, :83559, :83577
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's Group 3. Target it at peer.m_uid. Wonderland's PlayerNotify (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15-30) shows the same pattern with the (peerID, zdoID, method) overload for ZDO-scoped RPCs like Player's "Message".

apis.signature: List<ZDO> ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()
apis.notes: Every connected peer's live character ZDO. Includes the local character only if one exists (never on a dedicated server). Vanilla itself uses it server-side in Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep.

apis.signature: List<ZNetPeer> ZNet.GetPeers()  /  List<ZNetPeer> ZNet.GetConnectedPeers()
apis.notes: GetPeers returns the live backing list (do not mutate); GetConnectedPeers returns a copy. Filter on peer.IsReady() (m_uid != 0) and !peer.m_characterID.IsNone().

apis.signature: ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeer(long uid)  /  ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeerByPlayerName(string name)  /  ZNetPeer ZNet.GetPeerByHostName(string endpoint)
apis.notes: GetPeerByHostName's argument is the PlatformUserID string (peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) — the authenticated identity. GetPeerByPlayerName matches the character name and requires IsReady().

apis.signature: List<ZNet.PlayerInfo> ZNet.GetPlayerList()  /  int ZNet.GetNrOfPlayers()
apis.notes: Refreshed by SendPeriodicData every 2s. m_position is zero unless that player enabled public position; m_userInfo.m_id is the PlatformUserID; m_characterID is the character ZDOID. No host entry on a dedicated server.

apis.signature: ZDO ZDOMan.GetZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Returns null for ZDOID.None or an unknown id. The lookup for peer.m_characterID → character ZDO.

apis.signature: long ZDO.GetLong(int hash, long default) / string ZDO.GetString(int hash, string default) / int ZDO.GetInt(int hash, int default) / bool ZDO.GetBool(int hash) / Vector3 ZDO.GetVec3(int hash, Vector3 default) / byte[] ZDO.GetByteArray(int hash) / Vector3 ZDO.GetPosition() / Quaternion ZDO.GetRotation() / int ZDO.GetPrefab()
apis.notes: All accessors also have string-name overloads that hash internally — needed for PrivateArea's "pu_id{i}"/"pu_name{i}" keys, which have no ZDOVars constant.

apis.signature: long ZDO.GetOwner() / bool ZDO.HasOwner() / bool ZDO.IsOwner() / void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid)
apis.notes: GetOwner returns a session/peer uid comparable with ZNetPeer.m_uid and ZDOMan.GetSessionID(). SetOwner(ZNet.GetUID()) is the ownership-claim step before writing to an unowned ZDO (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine / ZdoInventoryIO.Save pattern).

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects(Vector2s sector, SimulationDistance simulationDistance, List<ZDO> sectorObjects, List<ZDO> distantSectorObjects = null)
apis.notes: Sector-granular (64m zones); always post-filter by real distance. Wrapped by Wonderland's ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear (Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:24).

apis.signature: bool ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO> zdos, ref int index)
apis.notes: Time-budgeted resumable full-map scan by prefab NAME (hashed internally); returns true when a full cycle completes. The way to enumerate every bed / tombstone / ward / portal in the world.

apis.signature: List<ZDOID> ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(ZDOExtraData.Type type, int hash)
apis.notes: Type is Float|Vec3|Quat|Int|Long|String|ByteArray but only Float/Long/Int/String are implemented (others log an error and return empty). Unindexed O(all ZDOs × all fields) scan — startup/one-shot only.

apis.signature: Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()  /  List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()
apis.notes: Free, already-maintained portal index. Used by Game.ConnectPortals and by Wonderland's PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit.

apis.signature: void ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)  /  (long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)  /  (string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: targetPeerID = ZNetPeer.m_uid; 0L = everybody. The ZDOID overload targets a component RPC registered on that ZDO's ZNetView (e.g. Player's "Message").

apis.signature: Chat.TeleportPlayer(long targetPeerID, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)  — equivalently InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)
apis.notes: Call the ZRoutedRpc form directly; Chat.instance is a GUI singleton and should not be assumed alive on a dedicated server.

apis.signature: ZDOVars constants for player-associated data: s_owner :78517, s_ownerName :78519, s_playerID :78539, s_playerName :78541, s_creator :78393, s_creatorIndex :78395, s_creatorName :78397, s_permitted :78529, s_tag :78617, s_tagauthor :78619, s_inBed :78457, s_dead, s_spawnPoint :78729, s_timeOfDeath :78347, s_items, s_tamed :78621, s_tamedName :78623, s_tamedNameAuthor :78625, s_follow :78429
apis.notes: All are GetStableHashCode() of the quoted literal, so a mod can reconstruct any of them without a hard reference. PrivateArea's per-entry permitted keys "pu_id{i}"/"pu_name{i}" are NOT in ZDOVars — build them as strings.

apis.signature: List<ZNet.CrossNetworkUserInfo> ZNet.World.m_playerHistory  (ZNet.World static property)
apis.notes: Index target of Piece s_creatorIndex. Entries are {PlatformUserID m_id, m_displayName, m_serverAssignedDisplayName, m_playfabId}. Persisted in the .fwl; survives restarts.

gotchas: Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile() is NOT null on a dedicated server — it is a junk profile named "Stranger" with a random UID (Game.Awake:100047). Any vanilla helper that compares against it (Bed.IsMine :119801, Bed.IsCurrent :119787, Piece.IsCreator :136436, TombStone.IsOwner :19865, Container.CheckAccess :122090) silently returns garbage server-side rather than throwing. Never call them.
ZNetPeer.m_playerID is permanently 0: the "PlayerID" RPC is registered by both sides (SERVER:79916, CLIENT:80108) but never invoked by any vanilla client. Reading it looks correct and yields nothing.
ZDOVars.s_owner is shared between Bed/TombStone (PlayerProfile UID) and GrapplingPoint (a ZDOID.ID, :127909). A global s_owner query mixes incompatible value spaces — always filter by prefab hash.

Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator() == 0 and m_nview.IsOwner() (:136417) — pre-existing world-gen structures and anything placed before the check have s_creator == 0, i.e. Piece.IsPlacedByPlayer() == false. Do not treat missing s_creator as 'owned by nobody in particular' without checking that.

s_creatorIndex is FindIndex(...) against ZNet.World.m_playerHistory at placement time and is -1 when the placer is not yet in the history (:136421). It is also a positional index into a list that only ever grows by append — safe across restarts, but useless if it is -1.

ZNet.GetPlayerList()[i].m_position is zero for any player with public position disabled (:81256-81259). peer.m_refPos is populated unconditionally (:80401). Using the former for positions silently produces (0,0,0) targets.

peer.m_refPos is the client's ZNet reference position, NOT the character position — during respawn/loading it is the spawn point, and during normal play it lags the true position by up to 2s. Use the character ZDO position for anything precise.
ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles() sounds like it collects profiles; it does the opposite (tells each client to save its own disk file, :79653). No data comes back.

Character ZDOs are non-persistent and are destroyed on disconnect (ZDOMan.RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS :77406). A per-player cache keyed on the ZDOID or on peer.m_uid dies with the session — key on s_playerID or PlatformUserID and re-resolve every connect.

ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash is a full nested scan (:75707) with no index behind it, and only Float/Long/Int/String are implemented — Vec3/Quat/ByteArray log an error and return empty (:75403-75406). It looks like a cheap query and is not.

The server has no Bed, PrivateArea, TeleportWorld, Container, TombStone or Player GameObject anywhere near a player (Game.FixedUpdate pins refPos to 1e6, :100464). PrivateArea.m_allAreas, Player.GetAllPlayers() and Piece.s_allPieces are all permanently empty; every static-list-based vanilla helper is a silent no-op.
Bed's spawn position is a child Transform (Bed.GetSpawnPoint :119796), not ZDO data. A 'teleport to their bed' feature lands on the bed ZDO's origin, which is not exactly where vanilla respawns them.

A dead player's tombstone Container ZDO is the ONLY server-visible inventory. It is a live Container though — respect ZDOVars.s_inUse before writing (Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy), and it self-destructs once emptied (TombStone.UpdateDespawn :19875-19890).

Tameable's s_follow holds a character NAME string, not an id (:19457), and is cleared to "" when the creature is told to stay (:19444). Name collisions between two characters called the same thing are indistinguishable, and a tame that is not currently following has no owner marker at all.

TeleportWorld.s_tagauthor and Piece.s_creator can disagree about 'whose portal this is' — the first is the last person to set the tag (a PlatformUserID string), the second is the builder (a profile UID long). They are different value types and different semantics; pick one deliberately.
openQuestions: Is the Player prefab's ZNetView m_persistent actually false? RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS (:77406) only destroys non-persistent ZDOs of a departed peer, and the design clearly assumes character ZDOs are among them, but m_persistent is Inspector data (ZNetView.Awake :82616 copies it). IN-GAME CHECK: connect a client, record its character ZDOID, disconnect, then call ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(thatId) from a server-side timer a few seconds later — null means non-persistent as assumed.

What is the vanilla tombstone prefab's exact name/hash? Player.m_tombstone is an Inspector GameObject reference (:9594) and the string never appears in either decompile. IN-GAME CHECK: kill a character, then log the prefab hash of the new ZDO carrying both s_ownerName and s_timeOfDeath, and compare against "Player_tombstone".GetStableHashCode().

Which bed prefabs exist and do they all carry both a Piece and a Bed component (i.e. do all beds have s_creator as well as s_owner)? Prefab composition is asset data. IN-GAME CHECK: place each bed variant, then dump the ZDO's field set and confirm s_creator, s_owner and s_ownerName all appear on the same ZDO.

Does the tombstone's Container write s_items promptly on creation, or only on the first OnContainerChanged after a client instantiates it? Container.Save runs from OnContainerChanged when IsOwner (:122287-122300), and the grave is filled by MoveInventoryToGrave on the dying client (:12709). IN-GAME CHECK: die, then read the fresh tombstone ZDO's s_items from the server within a second — if empty, the blob only lands once the owning client's Container ticks.

How quickly after a peer becomes ready does its character ZDO actually arrive server-side with s_playerID populated? The ordering is guaranteed client-side (Game.SpawnPlayer :100692-100698) but the wire delay is not derivable. IN-GAME CHECK: on RPC_CharacterID, poll GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(s_playerID) each frame and log the number of frames until non-zero.

Do all shoulder/back/trinket VisEquipment slots get written for a Player specifically, or are some gated by m_isPlayer/m_isArmorStand paths that a real Player never takes? The read-back at :20857-20885 branches on m_isPlayer (an Inspector bool). IN-GAME CHECK: equip each slot in turn and dump the character ZDO's int fields.
correctionsToExistingSpec: REFINE — 'Portal to a player's claimed bed … "currently active" bed with multiple beds lives only in that player's local, non-networked save data.' The premise is correct (Bed.IsCurrent :119787 reads PlayerProfile.GetCustomSpawnPoint, and Bed.Interact's spawn-set branch :119719 emits no RPC and no ZDO write), but two live inference channels exist and should be listed: (a) ZDOVars.s_inBed on the character ZDO, which vanilla's own server code already reads via GetAllCharacterZDOS (Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep :100735) — position-match the sleeping character to a bed ZDO; (b) peer.m_refPos while the player is dead, because Game.UpdateRespawn pins the reference position to the custom spawn point (:100349) and it is reported to the server every 2s (:80395). Neither is instantaneous, but both turn 'impossible' into 'observable over time'.

ADD — the spec never mentions that EVERY placed structure carries a builder record in its ZDO: Piece.SetCreator writes ZDOVars.s_creator (the placer's PlayerProfile UID, identical to their character ZDO s_playerID) plus s_creatorIndex (→ ZNet.World.m_playerHistory PlatformUserID, persisted in the .fwl) — Piece.SetCreator :136415, Player.PlacePiece :12514. This makes 'a player's own portals', 'a player's own beds' and 'a player's own wards' server-answerable offline and persistently, which is a stronger basis for per-player portal features than s_tagauthor and should be added to Group 1 and Group 4.

REFINE — 'the server can't inspect a player's inventory anyway (never networked)'. True for a living player's inventory (Player.Save → PlayerProfile.m_playerData → local .fch, :14091/:105706; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles sends nothing back, :79653). Two carve-outs belong in the text: equipped/visible gear IS in the character ZDO as prefab hashes (VisEquipment :20569-20708, incl. back and utility slots), and a DEAD player's entire inventory IS server-readable from the tombstone Container's s_items blob together with s_owner/s_ownerName/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint (TombStone.Setup :19845, TombStone.Awake :19732). Neither enables vanilla's ore check (which is against the full inventory), but both are real server-side data the spec currently denies exists.

REFINE — Group 5's 'portal toll via an adjacent chest … never the traveling player's own inventory'. Correct, and the set of server-writable inventories should be stated as 'any Container-family ZDO', which includes the player's own tombstone — Container.Save is the single s_items writer in the assembly (:122294), with ZdoInventoryIO already implementing the read/claim/write cycle.

ADD to Group 4 — the identity-hardening item says RPC sender identity is unverified but does not say what to check it against. The answer is concrete: peer.m_socket.GetHostName() is the PlatformUserID the connection authenticated with (Steam session ticket / PlayFab check in ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79836-79868), reverse-lookupable via ZNet.GetPeerByHostName (:80480), and RPC_SetTag's authorId is a PlatformUserID string in exactly that format (TeleportWorld.SetText :143579). Cross-checking the two is the whole fix. Also note ZNetPeer.m_playerID is always 0 (no client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC) so it cannot be part of any identity check.

ADD to Group 4 — PrivateArea's permission data needs no 'shadow list' to READ: s_creator (owner), s_creatorName (PrivateArea.Setup :137446), s_enabled, and the permitted roster as s_permitted + "pu_id{i}"/"pu_name{i}" (SetPermittedPlayers :137338, GetPermittedPlayers :137349) are all plain ZDO fields. The shadow list is only needed because no PrivateArea GameObject exists server-side to run the checks — the data itself is fully available, which makes that item smaller than 'large'.

research.topic: Dungeon teleport (class Teleport) vs TeleportWorld, plus a complete inventory of every non-locomotive character position change in Valheim 1.0.7
research.summary: `class Teleport` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316) is architecturally the *opposite* of `TeleportWorld`: it has no `ZNetView`, no `ZDO`, no RPC, no Awake, and no networked state whatsoever — its destination is a plain serialized Unity Inspector reference `public Teleport m_targetPoint` (:143322) resolved through `Transform` math at `GetTeleportPoint()` (:143372). Server and client decompiles are byte-identical for this class. Its NoBossPortals gate (:143355) blocks ONLY the outbound leg (it requires `character.InInterior()`, i.e. the player's current y > 3000f) and its third conjunct `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) dereferences `EnemyHud.instance` — a pure client HUD singleton — so on any headless context it returns false. Dungeon doors deliberately skip *both* `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and `Player.IsTeleportable` (the ore check), which `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143515) applies — so a server-wide `NoPortals` lockdown does NOT close crypt doors and ore always passes through them. The stats (`PortalDungeonIn`=83, `PortalDungeonOut`=84, `PortalsUsed`=15 in `PlayerStatType` :106499) land in `PlayerProfile.m_playerStats` (`IncrementStat` :106287), a local `.fch` save structure that is never networked. Nothing in `Teleport` is server-reachable, readable, or writable — but a dungeon transit IS server-*detectable* after the fact, because the player's character ZDO position y crosses the 3000f interior threshold. Counting every path, there are **five** distinct transform-level relocation mechanisms plus several physics/rescue snaps; only two of them (`Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` and `Character.RPC_TeleportTo`) are reachable from a dedicated server, and both bypass every vanilla portal rule.

facts.claim: `class Teleport` declares exactly four fields — m_hoverText, m_enterText, `public Teleport m_targetPoint`, m_hoverOffset — and has NO ZNetView field, NO Awake(), NO m_nview, NO ZDO access and NO RPC registration anywhere in the class body (lines 143316-143390 inclusive).
facts.implication: There is zero networked state for dungeon doors. A server-only mod cannot read, write, redirect, log, or veto a dungeon door by any ZDO or RPC means, because none exists. Unlike TeleportWorld (which has s_tag/s_tagauthor/ConnectionType.Portal), Teleport is invisible to ZDOMan entirely.

facts.claim: The dungeon exit point is a Unity Inspector object reference (`public Teleport m_targetPoint`) plus Transform math: `GetTeleportPoint() => transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`. No paired ZDO, no ZDOID, no connection type.
facts.implication: Contrast with TeleportWorld, whose destination is `ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal)` and IS server-rewritable. Dungeon destinations are baked into the location prefab asset; rewriting one requires a client-side asset/Harmony patch, which is out of scope for server-only. Also note GetTeleportPoint() is private and is called on *another* instance (`m_targetPoint.GetTeleportPoint()`), which is legal C# but means the exit offset is not overridable via any public surface.

facts.claim: The server and client decompiles of `class Teleport` are textually identical (client copy at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144056-144130). The only difference is line offset.
facts.implication: No server-specific stub or IL stripping to exploit; the code exists on the server binary but is unreachable there for the reasons below. Any Harmony patch on Teleport.Interact WILL compile and apply on a dedicated server and will simply never fire.

facts.claim: `Teleport.OnTriggerEnter` requires `Player.m_localPlayer == component`; `Teleport.Interact` is reached from `Player.Update()` -> `Interact(m_hovering, ...)`, which sits behind `!m_nview.IsOwner() -> return` and raw ZInput button reads.
facts.citation: Teleport.OnTriggerEnter assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143336-143343; Player.Update assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10239, gate at :10257, call at :10291 and :10300
facts.implication: Both entry points into Teleport.Interact are local-player-only, same as TeleportWorldTrigger. Confirms the central constraint extends to the dungeon mechanism: no moment-of-transit server hook exists for either teleport type.

facts.claim: `Teleport.Interact`'s boss gate is a three-way AND: `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(character.transform.position)`. `Character.InInterior(Vector3 position) => position.y > 3000f`.
facts.implication: Because the second conjunct tests the player's CURRENT altitude, the check can only ever be true when the player is already inside an interior. It blocks OUTBOUND (dungeon -> surface) only. The inbound leg (surface, y<3000) is never blocked by NoBossPortals. This refines the existing spec's wording from 'the outbound trip from inside an active boss's own dungeon' to the precise mechanic.

facts.claim: `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` first dereferences `EnemyHud.instance` and returns false if it is null; `EnemyHud.instance` is set only in `EnemyHud.Awake` on the HUD prefab and its `m_huds` dictionary is filled in `EnemyHud.LateUpdate` from `Character.GetAllCharacters()` relative to `Player.m_localPlayer.transform.position`.
facts.implication: The dungeon NoBossPortals check is doubly client-bound: it depends on a UI singleton and on which boss HUD bars that specific client is currently showing. A server-only mod can neither evaluate nor influence it beyond setting the global key. It is 'vanilla-respecting' in the weakest sense — it is honored per-client, based on per-client HUD state.

facts.claim: The boss-proximity test inside `IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` is `ZoneSystem.GetZone(point) == ZoneSystem.GetZone(activeBoss.transform.position)`, and `GetZone` uses only x and z (64m grid, `FloorToInt((point.x+32)/64)`), plus the boss must have `m_bossEvent.Length > 0`.
facts.implication: Y is ignored, which is exactly why the check works at all — the interior is at zoneCenter XZ with y+5000, so it shares the boss's XZ zone. It also means 'in the same 64x64m zone column as the boss', not literally 'in the boss's dungeon'. Practically the boss must also be within EnemyHud's m_maxShowDistanceBoss (100f) and alerted for it to be in m_huds.

facts.claim: `EnemyHud.GetActiveBoss()` returns the FIRST dictionary entry whose character `IsBoss()` is true, and only afterwards does IsInsideActiveBossDungeon test `m_bossEvent.Length > 0` on that one returned character.
facts.implication: If a client's HUD happens to hold a boss-flagged character with an empty m_bossEvent first in Dictionary enumeration order, the whole gate silently fails open even with a real boss event running. Vanilla bug-shaped edge case; irrelevant to server-only work but relevant to anyone claiming this is a reliable lockdown.

facts.claim: `Teleport.Interact` never consults `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and never calls `Player.IsTeleportable(...)`. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` does both (NoPortals at :143523, IsTeleportable at :143533).
facts.implication: MAJOR for TortalPortal Lite: a server-wide `NoPortals` lockdown closes constructed portals but leaves every crypt/dungeon door fully working, including with ore in inventory. Any 'disable all portals' feature must be described as 'disable all constructed portals' or must additionally force-disconnect ZDOs. Ore/metal restriction has never applied to dungeon doors at all.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s boss gate is a different, wider condition than Teleport's: `NoBossPortals && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out float value) && value > 0f))` — global, not positional, and with no EnemyHud dependency.
facts.implication: The two mechanisms share the NoBossPortals key but interpret it completely differently: TeleportWorld = 'any boss anywhere is active -> no portals at all'; Teleport = 'only if you are inside an interior sharing a zone with a HUD-visible boss'. `GlobalKeys.activeBosses` is a server-writable float key (written at Character:3163-3164 and BaseAI:27258-27259), so the server CAN indirectly drive the TeleportWorld gate but not the Teleport one.

facts.claim: `Teleport.Interact` calls `character.TeleportTo(..., distantTeleport: false)`, while `TeleportWorld.Teleport` calls `player.TeleportTo(pos, rotation, distantTeleport: true)`.
facts.implication: distantTeleport=false changes behaviour in Player.UpdateTeleport: no teleport fade animation (ShowTeleportAnimation returns m_distantTeleport, :15382-15389), no wait for ZNetScene.IsAreaReady, and on floor-find failure the player is restored to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' rather than being y-snapped to solid ground. Both still pay the fixed 2s m_teleportTimer and the 2s m_teleportCooldown.

facts.claim: `Player.TeleportTo` (the only override of the virtual; `Character.TeleportTo` base just `return false`) refuses if `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f`, and if not the ZDO owner it forwards via `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_TeleportTo", ...)` and returns false.
facts.implication: Only Players can be teleported at all — `Character.TeleportTo` is a no-op stub and nothing else overrides it (verified in both assemblies: assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:4123 and :15304 are the only two). A server-issued RPC_TeleportTo aimed at a creature ZDO does nothing. A server-issued teleport within 2s of a previous one silently no-ops with no error on either side.

facts.claim: Stats: `PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed` is ordinal 15, `PortalDungeonIn` is 83, `PortalDungeonOut` is 84 (enum has 207 members). `Teleport.Interact` picks between them with `character.InInterior() ? PortalDungeonOut : PortalDungeonIn` — evaluated AFTER TeleportTo returns true but BEFORE UpdateTeleport actually moves the transform 2s later, so it reads the pre-teleport altitude.
facts.implication: The naming is from the player's starting side: if you were in the interior when you pressed Use, it counts as 'Out'. Semantics are correct, but note the increment happens on TeleportTo's *acceptance*, not on completion — a teleport that later fails and restores position ('$msg_portal_blocked') still counted the stat.

facts.claim: `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` delegates straight to `m_playerProfile.IncrementStat`, which writes into `PlayerProfile.m_playerStats[...].m_stats` (an in-memory Dictionary<PlayerStatType,float>) and feeds `Achievements`. Nothing in the path touches ZDO, ZRoutedRpc, ZNet or any packet.
facts.implication: Portal and dungeon-portal usage counts live only in each player's local character .fch and never reach the server. Any server-side 'portals used' leaderboard must be built from the server's own detection, not by reading vanilla stats. The only per-player dictionary the client does ship to the server is `ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData` (:79051, serialized at :80370-80372), which vanilla populates with only 'possibleEvents', 'baseValue' and 'platformDisplayName'.

facts.claim: A dedicated server never instantiates any `Teleport` component at play time. `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick and only `Player.SetLocalPlayer`/`Player.LateUpdate` (owner-gated) ever move it back.
facts.implication: Confirms and extends the spec's central constraint to the dungeon mechanism. ZNetScene/ZoneSystem local-zone creation all key off GetReferencePosition, so nothing is ever created near a player on the server.

facts.claim: The server DOES generate zones around every peer, but only in `SpawnMode.Ghost`: `ZoneSystem.Update` calls `CreateGhostZones(peer.GetRefPos())` for each peer, and `SpawnZone` destroys every spawned GameObject (`UnityEngine.Object.Destroy(tempSpawnedObject)`) immediately after ZDO creation.
facts.implication: Corrects a natural misreading of 'the server instantiates nothing'. It does instantiate, for one frame, during world-gen only. But `ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation` only instantiates children that carry a ZNetView (:115229-115231), and `CreateLocationProxy` passes `spawnNow = (mode == SpawnMode.Full)` so the LocationProxy never expands the visual location prefab on the server (:115318-115332). Teleport colliders therefore never exist server-side even transiently, and even if they did, no Player object exists to enter them.

facts.claim: Dungeon interiors are placed at `base.transform.position.y + 5000f` above the location's zone center by `Location.Awake`, and `Character.InInterior` thresholds at y > 3000f.
facts.implication: THIS is the server-side handle on dungeon teleports. The owning client's ZSyncTransform writes the player's real position into the character ZDO every physics tick, so a server-only mod reading `ConnectedCharacter.Zdo.GetPosition().y` crossing 3000f gets a reliable, no-heuristic 'entered/left a dungeon' signal — strictly better than the portal-transit position-straddle heuristic Wonderland's PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit uses for TeleportWorld.

facts.claim: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every frame from the ZDO owner; `ZSyncTransform.ClientSync` on non-owners only reads.
facts.implication: A server-side write to a player's ZDO position is overwritten within one physics frame by that player's client and is not a teleport primitive. The only server->client relocation channels are RPCs (below).

facts.claim: `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` is a ZRoutedRpc handler registered in `Chat.Awake` on every client, whose entire body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender validation, no admin check, no key check, no IsTeleportable check.
facts.citation: Chat.Awake registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41627 (identical in assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41627); Chat.TeleportPlayer assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41957-41960; Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41962-41968
facts.implication: This is THE server-only teleport primitive against a 100% vanilla client. The server needs no local Chat instance: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, ...)` with targetPeerID != m_id skips HandleRoutedRPC and goes straight to RouteRPC, which as server sends directly to that peer. It also means a server-driven teleport bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, IsTeleportable and PrivateArea entirely — TortalPortal Lite must re-implement any rule it wants.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` as server sends to exactly the named peer when `m_targetPeerID != 0`, and `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches by `methodName.GetStableHashCode()` with no origin check; `RPC_RoutedRPC` on the receiving client likewise accepts any packet whose target matches.
facts.implication: Confirms server->single-client targeted RPC delivery works for any registered method name, which is what makes both RPC_TeleportPlayer and ZDO-targeted RPC_TeleportTo usable from a server-only mod.

facts.claim: `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is registered on every Character with a ZDO (`m_nview.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportTo", RPC_TeleportTo)` inside `if (m_nview.GetZDO() != null)`, NOT inside an IsOwner branch) and its body is `if (m_nview.IsOwner()) TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);`.
facts.implication: Second server-reachable teleport path, addressed by ZDOID instead of peer id: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ownerPeer, playerZdoId, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, distant)`. More precise than RPC_TeleportPlayer (which always hits whatever that peer's local player is) and works even if the target's Chat is somehow absent. Same total bypass of vanilla portal rules.

facts.claim: The server already knows both the peer id and the character ZDOID for every connected player: `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` is set from `ZNet.RPC_CharacterID`, and `ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` resolves them through ZDOMan.
facts.implication: Everything needed to address either teleport RPC is already server-side. Wonderland's Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs already wraps exactly this (peer + ZDO pairs) and should be reused verbatim rather than re-derived.
