facts.claim: Vanilla's only caller of `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is the `recall` console command, which is `isCheat: true, onlyAdmin: true, isNetwork: false` and dereferences `Player.m_localPlayer.transform.position` for the destination.
facts.implication: Confirms the primitive is admin-intended in vanilla, and confirms the vanilla command itself is dead on a dedicated server (needs a local player) — same failure shape as `noportals`. A server-only mod must invoke the routed RPC itself.

facts.claim: The `noportals` console command's entire body is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)`, unlike the adjacent `nomap` command.
facts.implication: Confirms the existing spec's 'Ruled out' entry verbatim. Use ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals) directly. GlobalKeys is an enum (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101304 NoPortals, :101305 NoBossPortals, :101307 TeleportAll, :101319 activeBosses).

facts.claim: THIRD transform-teleport path: `Ladder.Interact` does an instant `character.transform.position = m_targetPos.position; character.transform.rotation = ...; character.SetLookDir(...); Physics.SyncTransforms();` with NO TeleportTo, NO cooldown, NO fade, NO global key check and NO item check — only a `InUseDistance` range test.
facts.implication: A completely undocumented third instant-relocation component, Transform-based like Teleport and equally invisible to the server (Ladder has no ZNetView/ZDO/RPC in the class). Any audit or lockdown feature reasoning about 'all teleports' must list it. It bypasses even the 2s TeleportTo cooldown, so it is also the cleanest vanilla path a cheating client could abuse.

facts.claim: FOURTH path: `TeleportAbility.Setup` (an IProjectile) writes `m_owner.transform.position = position` directly after `ZoneSystem.instance.FindFloor`, picking a random GameObject.FindGameObjectsWithTag(m_targetTag) within m_maxTeleportRange.
facts.implication: Runs on whichever client owns the attacking Character (projectiles are spawned by the attacker's owner). Bypasses Player.TeleportTo entirely, so no cooldown and no fade. Which prefab/attack uses it is Unity asset data and not determinable from the decompile.

facts.claim: FIFTH path: `Valkyrie.SyncPlayer` sets `localPlayer.transform.position` and `localPlayer.GetComponent<Rigidbody>().position` and then forces `ZSyncTransform.SyncNow()`, during the new-character intro drop.
facts.implication: Intro-only, local-player-only; listed for completeness. It is the only vanilla code that force-pushes a player position into the network immediately rather than waiting for the next OwnerSync.

facts.claim: `Trap.TriggerTrap` writes `m_tempTriggeringHumanoid.transform.position = m_tempTriggeredPosition` (the position captured in OnTriggerEnter), which is a freeze-in-place snap, not a teleport; OnTriggerEnter's capture branch already requires `humanoid.IsOwner()`.
facts.implication: Runs on the trap's ZDO owner. Included for completeness of the inventory; it cannot relocate a player anywhere new.

facts.claim: `Attack.UpdateAttach` drags the attacking Character each tick: `m_character.transform.position = position; m_character.transform.rotation = rotation;` plus zeroing its Rigidbody velocity, while latched to m_attachTarget.
facts.implication: A sustained, non-locomotive position override executed by the attacker's owning client (used by latch-on creature attacks). Relevant to any 'impossible movement' anti-cheat: it produces large per-tick position deltas that are not teleports.

facts.claim: Attach/mount/sit relocation: `Player.UpdateAttach` sets `transform.position = m_attachPoint.position` every CustomFixedUpdate while attached, and `Player.AttachStop` sets `transform.position = m_attachPoint.TransformPoint(m_detachOffset)`. Callers are Sadle:18285, Barber:119562, Bed:119721, Chair:120825, ShipControlls:141366 — every one of them gated on Player.m_localPlayer or a local `player` reference.
facts.implication: Attached position is nonetheless SERVER-VISIBLE indirectly: `Player.GetRelativePosition` (:16551-16575) makes ZSyncTransform write `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform` plus s_relPosHash/s_attachJointHash into the character ZDO (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87544-87571). That is the mechanism the existing spec's 'portal to a player's live-attached ship' item relies on.

facts.claim: World-rescue snaps, all owner-gated and all inside `if (num /* zDO.IsOwner() */)` in Character.CustomFixedUpdate: `Character.UnderWorldCheck` snaps y to groundHeight+0.5 when below ground-1 (every tick for players); `Player.EdgeOfWorldKill` MovePosition-pushes inward past 10420m and applies 99999 HitType.EdgeOfWorld damage below y=-10; `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` rescues any ZNetView object below y=-5000 to groundHeight+1.
facts.citation: Character.CustomFixedUpdate assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:982-1017 (owner gate :1000, UnderWorldCheck call :1011); Character.UnderWorldCheck assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:1055-1073; Player.EdgeOfWorldKill assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:11132-11152; ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87505-87526
facts.implication: Complete list of vanilla's out-of-bounds/world-edge/underworld handling. All executed by the owning client; a dedicated server never runs any of them for a player. They produce legitimate large position jumps that a naive server-side teleport detector will flag.

facts.claim: Moving-platform position writes: `Character.UpdateSinkingPlatform` adds `m_lastGroundBody.linearVelocity * dt` to the transform, gated on `this == Player.m_localPlayer` and a `Leviathan` + falling `StaticPhysics` on the ground body; `Character.UpdateMotion` corrects to `m_lastAttachBody.TransformPoint(m_lastAttachPos)` when standing on a ship the client does not own.
facts.implication: Completes the 'character position changes without locomotion' inventory for platform-riding. Neither is server-reachable.

facts.claim: Server-initiable indirect relocation: `Character.Damage` calls `ApplyPushback(hit)` which stores `hit.m_dir * f(hit.m_pushForce)` into m_pushForce, consumed by `AddPushbackForce` in the owner-only UpdateMotion; it arrives over the ZDO-targeted `RPC_Damage`, and `dir.y` is forced to 0.
facts.citation: Character.RPC_Damage assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2405-2420; Character.Damage -> ApplyPushback assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2518; Character.ApplyPushback assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2073-2086; Character.AddPushbackForce assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2051-2066; UpdatePushback decay 100f/s assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:2088-2091
facts.implication: A server can shove a vanilla player horizontally by sending RPC_Damage with zero damage and a nonzero m_pushForce/m_dir. Horizontal-only, short-lived (100 units/s decay), and it is a force not a placement — useful for a nudge/bounce-back mechanic, useless as a teleport.

facts.claim: `Character.RPC_Stagger` only rotates (`transform.rotation = Quaternion.LookRotation(-forceDirection)`) and triggers an animation; it does not move the character.
facts.implication: Rules out stagger as a relocation vector; it is a server-callable rotation vector only.

facts.claim: Respawn does not relocate an existing character — `Game._RequestRespawn` destroys the local Player and `Game.FindSpawnPoint` chooses the new point entirely from the client's own `PlayerProfile` (logout point, custom spawn point, else `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation)`), then `Game.SpawnPlayer` instantiates a fresh Player prefab.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec's 'TeleportHome/Game.RequestRespawn ruled out'. The spawn point lives in the client's .fch (PlayerProfile.HaveLogoutPoint/HaveCustomSpawnPoint), so even the destination is unreadable and unwritable server-side; Bed.Interact writes it via Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint (:119728), locally.

facts.claim: The complete set of routed (non-ZDO) RPCs registered anywhere in the assembly is 19 methods, and exactly one of them relocates a character: RPC_TeleportPlayer. No boss-spawn, event, spawn-system, trader or ragdoll RPC moves a player.
facts.implication: Definitive: RPC_TeleportPlayer (routed) plus RPC_TeleportTo (ZDO-targeted, Character.Awake:886) are the entire server->client relocation surface. OfferingBowl.RPC_SpawnBoss (:135657 / body :135777) spawns the boss and never moves the offering player — there is no boss arena teleport in Valheim.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals` and its 5s coroutine are started only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` in `Game.Start`, and the whole method touches only `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`, `ZDOVars.s_tag` and ConnectionType.Portal — no Player, no Teleport, no dungeon anything.
facts.implication: Confirms the spec. Critically, it also confirms the dungeon mechanism is entirely outside this server-authoritative layer: ConnectPortals can never see, pair, or break a dungeon door.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.m_portalObjects` is keyed off `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, a List<int> built in `Game.Awake` from `m_portalPrefabs` prefab-name hashes, and portal ZDOs are deliberately exempted from normal sector bookkeeping (`ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for them) and saved into their own chunk file (ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal).
facts.citation: Game.Awake assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100026-100032; Game.PortalPrefabHash assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752; ZDO.SetSector assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73757; ZDOMan chunk load assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76482
facts.implication: GetPortalList()/GetPortals() is a global, always-loaded, distance-independent registry — the only ZDO collection in the game with that property. Dungeon doors have no equivalent because they have no ZDO at all. `m_portalPrefabs` membership is Inspector data, so which prefabs count is an in-game check.

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: Server-only teleport primitive #1: InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", (Vector3)pos, (Quaternion)rot, (bool)distantTeleport). Arg types must be exactly Vector3/Quaternion/bool to match Chat's Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool> (:41627) — ZRpc.Serialize is type-driven. No local Chat instance is needed on the server: with targetPeerID != m_id the call skips HandleRoutedRPC and only RouteRPC's server branch runs (:83597-83612). The vanilla client applies it with zero validation (Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962).

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, ZDOID targetZDO, string methodName, params object[] parameters)
apis.notes: Server-only teleport primitive #2: InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, distantTeleport). Dispatched on the client via ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC to Character.RPC_TeleportTo (:4126), which requires m_nview.IsOwner(). Prefer this when you want to be sure you are moving that specific character ZDO rather than 'whatever Player.m_localPlayer is on that peer'. Only Players respond — Character.TeleportTo base is a `return false` stub (:4121).

apis.signature: public ZDOID ZNetPeer.m_characterID  /  public List<ZNetPeer> ZNet.GetPeers()
apis.notes: Peer id (m_uid) for RPC_TeleportPlayer and character ZDOID for RPC_TeleportTo. m_characterID arrives shortly after the peer is ready, so guard for ZDOID.None. Wonderland's Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs already yields (peer, zdo) pairs from exactly this.

apis.signature: public List<ZDO> ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()
apis.notes: Every connected player's character ZDO in one call. Position via ZDO.GetPosition() is refreshed each physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (:87533).

apis.signature: public static bool Character.InInterior(Vector3 position)  //  => position.y > 3000f
apis.notes: Pure static, no Unity/network dependency — safe to call on a dedicated server against a ZDO position. Combined with GetAllCharacterZDOS this is a zero-heuristic server-side dungeon-entry/exit detector: y crossing 3000f. Interiors sit at locationY + 5000f (Location.Awake :133512).

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys key) / RemoveGlobalKey / bool GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys, out float)
apis.notes: Server-writable and broadcast (RPC_GlobalKeys :113452). NoPortals affects TeleportWorld ONLY. NoBossPortals is read by both mechanisms but with different, incompatible conditions (TeleportWorld :143528 global; Teleport :143355 positional + EnemyHud-dependent). activeBosses is a float key the server can write directly to drive the TeleportWorld boss gate without a real boss.

apis.signature: public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList() / public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Global, always-resident registry of TeleportWorld ZDOs only. There is NO equivalent for dungeon doors — class Teleport has no ZDO. Do not expect a dungeon-door enumeration to exist anywhere.

apis.signature: public void Game.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: Public, no local-player dependency, already run every 5s from ZNet.instance.IsServer()-gated coroutine (Game.Start :100074). Touches only TeleportWorld ZDOs.

apis.signature: private void Teleport.Interact(Humanoid character, bool hold, bool alt)  — DO NOT TARGET
apis.notes: Public method on a class with no ZNetView. A Harmony patch compiles and applies on a dedicated server but never executes there, because no Teleport component is ever instantiated (ZoneSystem.CreateLocationProxy passes spawnNow=false in Ghost mode, :115325-115326) and Player.m_localPlayer is never populated.

apis.signature: public bool Ladder.Interact(Humanoid character, bool hold, bool alt)  — DO NOT TARGET
apis.notes: Third instant-relocation component, same server-invisibility as Teleport. Listed so it is not missed in any 'all teleport paths' enumeration.

gotchas: A server-wide `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` lockdown does NOT close dungeon/crypt doors. `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads NoPortals at all. Marketing a 'disable all portals' feature as total is wrong; say 'disable all constructed portals'.

Ore/metal restriction has never applied to dungeon doors. `Teleport.Interact` never calls `Player.IsTeleportable`, unlike `TeleportWorld.Teleport` (:143533). There is nothing to 'enforce server-side' for dungeon doors because vanilla itself does not restrict them.

`Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) returns false whenever `EnemyHud.instance` is null. That makes the dungeon boss gate not merely client-honored but client-HUD-honored: it depends on which boss health bars that specific player currently has on screen (within EnemyHud.m_maxShowDistanceBoss=100f and alerted, EnemyHud.TestShow :46706-46728).

The dungeon boss gate blocks only the OUTBOUND leg. `character.InInterior()` tests the player's current altitude, so a player standing outside (y<3000) is never blocked from entering. Do not describe it as 'blocks the dungeon while a boss is alive'.

`Teleport` has no ZNetView, so there is no ZDO, no s_tag, no connection, no owner, and no ZDOMan registry entry for a dungeon door. There is literally nothing for a server-only mod to read or write. Do not look for a 'dungeon portal list' — none exists at any layer.

A server-issued teleport (either RPC) bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, PrivateArea, and IsTeleportable entirely — the client-side RPC_TeleportPlayer body has no checks at all (:41962-41968). Any rule TortalPortal Lite wants applied to a server-driven warp must be implemented in the mod itself.

`Player.TeleportTo` silently returns false if `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15311-15314). A server sending two teleports inside 2s gets one honored and one dropped with no error, no message, and no way for the server to learn which. Rate-limit on the server side.

`distantTeleport: false` (what dungeon doors use) makes `Player.UpdateTeleport` restore the player to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' if ZoneSystem.FindFloor fails, instead of y-snapping to solid ground (:15359-15376). If a mod reuses distantTeleport:false for a long-range warp into unloaded terrain, the player is silently bounced back.

`Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes only to the local `PlayerProfile`. PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut never leave the client (:100569 -> :106287). Do not plan a server leaderboard on vanilla stats; the only client->server per-player dictionary is ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData, which vanilla fills with three unrelated keys (:79212, :11095, :11400).

The dedicated server DOES instantiate GameObjects — during SpawnMode.Ghost world-gen around each peer's reference position (ZoneSystem.Update :113930-113939). They are destroyed the same frame (SpawnZone :114093-114100), and SpawnLocation only ever instantiates ZNetView-bearing children (:115229), so Teleport/Ladder colliders still never appear. 'The server instantiates nothing' is the right conclusion from the wrong premise.

`Character.TeleportTo` is a `return false` stub; only `Player` overrides it (verified in both assemblies). RPC_TeleportTo aimed at a creature, tame, or ship ZDO does absolutely nothing — it is not a general entity-relocation primitive.

Vanilla's `recall` and `goto` console commands both dereference `Player.m_localPlayer` (:44551, :44562) and are dead from a dedicated server's own console, exactly like `noportals` (:45287). Invoke the routed RPC directly instead of shelling to a command.

`Ladder.Interact` (:132074) relocates a character instantly with no cooldown and no checks whatsoever. It is the cheapest vanilla-legitimate teleport in the game, and it will produce position jumps that any server-side portal-transit detector will misattribute.

Server-side writes to a player's ZDO position are futile: the owning client's `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` rewrites `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every frame (:87533). ZDO position is a read-only view of a player from the server's perspective.
openQuestions: Does the `Teleport` component sit on a GameObject that also carries a ZNetView in the shipped dungeon-entrance prefabs? The decompile cannot say (Unity asset data). It does not change the conclusion (CreateLocationProxy passes spawnNow=false in Ghost mode so the visual prefab never expands server-side), but it would settle whether a Teleport ever exists for a single frame during ghost world-gen. Check: in-editor/AssetRipper inspection of `dungeon_*` entrance prefabs, or a dedicated-server Harmony prefix on `Teleport.Awake`-equivalent (there is none; patch `OnTriggerEnter` and log) and confirm zero hits over a world-gen pass.

Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (the List<GameObject> feeding `Game.PortalPrefabHash` at :100029-100032)? This determines exactly which placed objects ZDOMan tracks as portals. Check in-game: log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Count` and cross-reference against `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` name hashes at server start.

Which creature/attack prefab actually uses `TeleportAbility` (:25523) and what `m_targetTag` does it search for? Inspector data. Check in-game: log from a Harmony postfix on TeleportAbility.Setup on a client and note the owner's prefab name.

Does `Player`'s prefab have `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync` enabled? This gates whether `Player.GetRelativePosition` (:16551) ever writes ConnectionType.SyncTransform + s_relPosHash into the character ZDO, which the existing spec's 'portal to a player's live-attached ship' item depends on. Check in-game: read `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(playerZdoId, ConnectionType.SyncTransform)` server-side while a player is confirmed seated on a moving karve.

Empirically, how large is the position delta and how many physics ticks elapse for a dungeon transit as seen in the character ZDO? Needed to size the y>3000 crossing detector's polling interval. Check in-game: server-side poll of ConnectedCharacters positions at 0.1s and log every sample where |Δy| > 1000.

Does the Ashlands `portal_stone` prefab ship with `m_allowAllItems = true`? Still unresolved (Inspector/AssetBundle data, as the existing spec notes). Check in-game: carry iron through a portal_stone pair on an unmodified client.
correctionsToExistingSpec: The spec's closing section says the dungeon mechanism 'shares the NoBossPortals key'. True, but it must be qualified: `Teleport` ALSO ignores `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` entirely. A 'disable all portals server-wide [Feasible, small]' item under Group 2 is therefore incomplete — it closes constructed portals only, and dungeon/crypt doors keep working. The Group 2 'genuinely unbypassable lockdown' item (force SetConnection to ZDOID.None) is likewise portal-only and has no dungeon-door analogue at any layer.

The spec says the dungeon check 'blocks only the outbound trip from inside an *active* boss's own dungeon'. Refine: (a) 'outbound' is correct and is caused specifically by the `character.InInterior()` conjunct testing the player's CURRENT y > 3000f; (b) it is not 'the boss's own dungeon' but 'the same 64m XZ zone column as the boss' (ZoneSystem.GetZone ignores y); (c) the check additionally requires `EnemyHud.instance != null` and a boss present in that client's own m_huds with m_bossEvent.Length > 0 — so it is client-HUD-state-dependent, a strictly weaker guarantee than the spec's 'vanilla-respecting' framing implies.

The spec says dungeon doors send a character 'to a fixed Transform-based exit point (no paired ZDO)'. Correct, and it should be stated more strongly: `class Teleport` has no ZNetView, no ZDO, no RPC and no Awake at all (:143316-143390). It is not merely unpaired — it is entirely absent from the network layer, so unlike TeleportWorld there is no partial server visibility to exploit.

The spec frames Group 5 portal-use detection as needing the `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` position-straddle heuristic. For the DUNGEON mechanism specifically there is a better, heuristic-free signal: `Character.InInterior(pos) => pos.y > 3000f` (:4538) against the character ZDO position, since interiors are placed at +5000f (Location.Awake :133512). Dungeon in/out logging should be listed as [Feasible, small] with no false-positive class, separate from the portal-transit heuristic.

The spec's 'One More Mechanism To Track Separately' should be 'Three More'. `Ladder.Interact` (:132064-132079) instantly relocates a Humanoid with no TeleportTo, no cooldown, no key check and no item check, and `TeleportAbility.Setup` (:25533-25550) writes `m_owner.transform.position` directly. Both are as server-invisible as `Teleport`, but any audit/lockdown claim of covering 'all teleports' is false without them.

Group 3's 'reuse vanilla's RPC_TeleportPlayer ... bypassing Chat.instance entirely' is confirmed correct and the reasoning can be tightened: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, ...)` with targetPeerID != m_id never calls HandleRoutedRPC locally (:83585-83591), so the server genuinely needs no Chat registration. Add: a second, more precisely addressed path exists via `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (registered unconditionally for any Character with a ZDO, :886) using the ZDO-targeted overload with peer.m_characterID. Also add the hard constraint that neither path applies ANY vanilla portal rule.

Group 5's portal-toll item should note that `Teleport`/dungeon transits cannot be tolled by the same mechanism in any meaningful way, since the dungeon exit is a fixed prefab transform and there is no per-door ZDO to attach a toll chest to.

research.topic: Ships & moving platforms as portal destinations; moving portal ZDOs (Valheim 1.0.7, server-only)
research.summary: A dedicated server can read exactly which ZNetView-bearing Rigidbody a player is riding, because the rider's own client writes it into the rider's ZDO as a `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform` connection plus `relPos`/`relRot`/`attachJoint` fields, and that connection is serialized into the network ZDO blob the server receives (`ZDO.Serialize`:74169 / `ZDO.Deserialize`:74229). Ship and Vagon both carry ZNetView and Rigidbody on the same GameObject (`Ship.Awake`:140444-140445, `Vagon.Awake`:147437/147447), so the connection target is the vehicle's own ZDO — but the whole mechanism is gated on `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync`:87362, an Inspector bool the decompile cannot read; the fully-confirmed fallback is `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship's ZDO, which only identifies the helmsman (`ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl`:141332). A portal's ZDO position CAN be rewritten server-side (`ZDO.SetPosition`:73729) but three things break: the write only bumps DataRevision if the server owns the ZDO (:73740) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 hands portal ownership to any peer within ~96m every 2s; portal ZDOs are permanently exempt from sector re-registration (`ZDO.SetSector`:73754) so `m_portalObjects` stays keyed by the creation-time sector and normal sector-based sync stops reaching the new location; and the new position is never saved (portals are excluded from chunk saves at :77572 and the ChunkPortal file only emits when `DirtyPortalObjects`:77621, which a position write never sets). A vanilla client does NOT rubber-band or re-instantiate on a moved portal ZDO — `ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 applies position only at Instantiate and `ZNetView.Awake` never applies it — so the mesh and the TeleportWorldTrigger collider stay put until the instance is destroyed and recreated, at which point it pops. The one genuinely live-following thing is the *destination*: `TeleportWorld.Teleport`:143539 reads the target ZDO's position at the instant of transit with no prefab validation, so a portal pointed at a Ship ZDO teleports to wherever that ship currently is — except `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343-15349 pins the player at a frozen snapshot for ≥8 seconds, by which time the ship has sailed.

facts.claim: `Character.m_characterParentSync`, `Character.SetCharacterParent` and `RPC_SetCharacterParent` do not exist anywhere in 1.0.7. The only `m_characterParentSync` in the entire codebase is a public serialized bool on `ZSyncTransform`.
facts.citation: ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87362 (grep for SetCharacterParent returns 0 hits in all four decompiles)
facts.implication: Any design doc naming Character.m_characterParentSync or RPC_SetCharacterParent is referencing a pre-1.0 API. The correct handle is the ZSyncTransform component on the Player prefab.

facts.claim: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` — which runs only on the ZDO-owning client — writes the parent as a real ZDO connection: `zDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform, m_tempParent)`, plus `s_attachJointHash` (string), `s_relPosHash` (Vector3), `s_relRotHash` (Quaternion). All of this is inside `if (m_characterParentSync)`.
facts.implication: The rider's own client authors the ship-attachment record. A server-only mod reads it, never writes it.

facts.claim: The connection ZDOID is serialized into the network ZDO packet (`ZDO.Serialize` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` then `connectionData.m_target` as a raw ZDOID) and re-applied on receipt (`ZDO.Deserialize` reads the byte + ZDOID and calls `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection`).
facts.implication: CONFIRMED: the parent-sync link reaches the dedicated server verbatim as a ZDOID. No RPC interception, no live GameObject, no ownership needed to read it.

facts.claim: The disk save path is different from the network path: `ZDO.Save` writes `connectionData.m_hash` (an int from `ZDOConnectionHashData`), not the ZDOID, and `ZDOMan.ConnectSyncTransforms` re-pairs SyncTransform connections by hash on world load.
facts.implication: SyncTransform parentage survives a server restart. A logged-out player's ZDO can still claim a ship parent after a restart — always cross-check the live world positions before trusting it.

facts.claim: `Character.GetRelativePosition` returns the parent only when `IsOnGround() && m_lastGroundBody` and the ground body has a valid ZNetView; `m_lastGroundBody` is `m_lastGroundCollider.attachedRigidbody`, refreshed in `UpdateGroundContact`, which `Character.CustomFixedUpdate` calls only when `zDO.IsOwner()`.
facts.implication: Parent detection is physics-derived on the rider's machine. Anything the rider stands on that has Rigidbody+ZNetView becomes the parent — carts, Leviathans, tamed mounts — so the connection target must be prefab-checked against Ship before it means 'on a ship'.

facts.claim: `Player.GetRelativePosition` overrides the ground path when `m_attached` is set (sitting at a helm, on a chair, in a bed): it uses `m_attachPoint.GetComponentInParent<ZNetView>()`. `ShipControlls` has no ZNetView of its own — `ShipControlls.Awake` does `m_nview = m_ship.GetComponent<ZNetView>()` — so a helmsman's parent ZDOID resolves to the Ship's own ZDO.
facts.implication: Both the standing passenger and the seated helmsman produce the same parent ZDOID (the Ship). One server-side read covers both cases.

facts.claim: When the parent is a Character (a ridden creature), `attachJoint` is set to `m_attachPoint.name` and relPos/relRot are zeroed; for a non-Character parent (a ship), `attachJoint` is `""` and relPos/relRot carry real local-space values.
facts.implication: Server-side, a non-empty `ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash` string on a player ZDO means 'riding a creature'; an empty one with a non-None SyncTransform connection means 'on a vehicle/platform'. Free discriminator.

facts.claim: Ship carries its ZNetView and Rigidbody on the same GameObject (`m_nview = GetComponent<ZNetView>(); m_body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();`), and so does Vagon.
facts.implication: `m_lastGroundBody.GetComponent<ZNetView>()` in Character.GetRelativePosition WILL resolve for both ships and carts. The connection target is guaranteed to be the vehicle's own ZDO, not a child piece's.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType` is `[Flags] { None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 }`, and a ZDO holds exactly ONE connection (`s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>`, one value per ZDO).
facts.implication: Writing a Portal connection onto a player's or ship's ZDO would destroy its SyncTransform connection. Portals hold their own connection, so pointing a portal AT a ship is safe; making a ship hold a reciprocal Portal link would be safe too (ships never have a parent) but a player's would not.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID(zid, type)` returns the target only on an EXACT type match (`valueOrDefaultPiktiv.m_type == type`), and the live in-memory connection on a rider's ZDO is plain `SyncTransform` (2), not `SyncTransform|Target`.
facts.implication: The correct server-side call is `playerZdo.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform)`. Passing the Target flag returns ZDOID.None.

facts.claim: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes the SyncTransform connection ONLY when the parent changes (`if (m_tempParent != m_tempParentCached)`), whereas relPos/relRot are rewritten every time they change.
facts.implication: The connection is a latching signal, not a heartbeat: reading it tells you the last parent the client committed, with no freshness guarantee. Dismount writes ZDOID.None via UpdateConnection (:87568), so it does clear — but only while the client is alive to write it.

facts.claim: Vanilla bug: `OwnerSync` writes the relative velocity into `ZDOVars.s_velHash` ("vel"), but `SyncPosition` reads it from `ZDOVars.s_velRelHash` ("velRel"). The velRel field is never written by anything.
facts.implication: Do not expect `velRel` on a rider's ZDO. `vel` on a parented rider is the ship-local relative velocity, not world velocity — and `vel` is session-only so it never persists.

facts.claim: `s_velHash` and `s_velRelHash` are in `ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes` and are registered into `ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly` at init, so `GetSaveData` filters them out of disk saves. `s_relPosHash`, `s_relRotHash` and `s_attachJointHash` are NOT session-only and DO persist.
facts.implication: relPos/relRot survive a restart on a player ZDO, which can make a stale attachment look live. Velocity does not.

facts.claim: `Ship.m_players` is a plain `List<Player>` maintained by `Ship.OnTriggerEnter/OnTriggerExit` on the live GameObject, and `Character.InNumShipVolumes` is a plain auto-property incremented by the same triggers.
facts.implication: Neither is readable server-side — a dedicated server never instantiates a Ship or Player GameObject. `Ship.IsPlayerInBoat(long)` (:141063), `Ship.HasPlayerOnboard()` (:141075) and `Character.GetStandingOnShip()` (:2999) are all dead ends server-side.

facts.claim: `ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl` runs on the Ship ZDO's owner and writes the steering player's stable PlayerID into the Ship's own ZDO as `ZDOVars.s_user` (hash of "user"); `RPC_ReleaseControl` resets it to 0.
facts.implication: The only 100%-confirmed, Inspector-independent server-readable ship-occupancy signal. It identifies the helmsman only, never passengers. This is what Wonderland/Core/Data/ShipAttachment.cs already ships.

facts.claim: `Vagon` writes only a single bool to its own ZDO (`ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash` used as a bool flag for 'someone is pulling me'); it never writes the puller's identity.
facts.implication: Carts have no server-readable rider identity. The only way to know who is pulling a cart is the puller's own SyncTransform connection pointing at the Vagon ZDO — same Inspector dependency as ships.

facts.claim: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any prefab in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, so a portal ZDO is never added to, removed from, or moved between `m_objectsBySector`, and never triggers `ZDOSectorInvalidated`.
facts.implication: A portal's routing key is frozen. Moving a portal's position changes nothing about which peers the server ships it to.

facts.claim: Portals live in a separate `m_portalObjects` dictionary keyed by the sector index computed at creation/load time (`AddIfPortal` / the ChunkPortal load path), and `FindObjects` merges `m_portalObjects[sectorIndex]` into every sector query.
facts.implication: A portal moved 500m away is still delivered to peers near its ORIGINAL sector and never to peers at its new location. Continuous `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(uid)` is the only way to push a moved portal to everyone.

facts.claim: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition` only calls `IncreaseDataRevision()` if `IsOwner()`. A non-owner's position write mutates the local copy silently and is overwritten by the owner's next ZDOData packet.
facts.implication: A moving-portal mod MUST hold ownership (`zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`) on every tick it writes, or the write is a no-op as far as the network is concerned.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS` runs every 2 seconds and calls `ReleaseNearbyZDOS(peer.m_refPos, peer.m_uid)` for every peer; any persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area whose owner is not itself inside an active area is reassigned to that peer. The dedicated server's own reference position is pinned at (1e6, 0, 1e6) by `Game.FixedUpdate`, so the server always fails the `IsInPeerActiveArea` test for real-world coordinates.
facts.implication: Server ownership of any ZDO near a player is revoked within 2s. Continuous portal movement requires either re-claiming every tick or a Harmony guard on ZDO.SetOwner (the exact pattern Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs ZdoSetOwnerPatch uses).

facts.claim: A portal's position change is never persisted: `AddObjectsPerChunk` explicitly excludes portal prefabs from the normal chunk save, and the dedicated ChunkPortal file is only produced when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set — which only `AddIfPortal`, `ZDO.SetConnection(Portal,...)`, `HandleDestroyedZDO` and `ZDOMan.Load` do. `IncreaseDataRevision`/`SetDirtySector` never set it.
facts.implication: A moved portal snaps back to its saved coordinate on server restart. To persist a relocation you must also force DirtyPortalObjects (e.g. by re-writing the Portal connection) in the same save window.

facts.claim: `HandleDestroyedZDO` removes a portal from `m_portalObjects` using `zDO.GetSectorIndex()` recomputed from the CURRENT position, but the dictionary key was set from the creation-time position.
facts.implication: If a mod moved a portal across a 64m sector boundary and the portal is later destroyed, the dead ZDO leaks in m_portalObjects forever and `GetPortalList()`/`Game.ConnectPortals()` keep processing it. This is a permanent, non-self-healing corruption of the portal registry.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.CreateObject` applies `zdo.GetPosition()` only at `Object.Instantiate`; `ZNetView.Awake` never touches transform.position (it applies scale only, when `m_syncInitialScale` is set).
facts.implication: A vanilla client does NOT re-instantiate and does NOT rubber-band when a portal's ZDO position changes. The mesh and the TeleportWorldTrigger collider stay exactly where they were created. Unless the portal prefab carries a ZSyncTransform, a 'moving portal' is invisible and unusable on the client side.

facts.claim: If a prefab DOES have ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition, a non-owning client lerps 20% per FixedUpdate toward the ZDO position and hard-snaps when the gap exceeds 5m.
facts.implication: This is the branch that would produce visible rubber-banding AND a collider that follows. Whether portal_wood/portal_stone has this component is the single decisive unknown for the whole moving-portal idea.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects` destroys any instance whose ZDO is absent from the current sector query, and `CreateObjects` re-instantiates from the ZDO's current position on the next pass; `CreateDestroyObjects` runs at 1/30s.
facts.implication: A moved portal will teleport (pop) to its new ZDO coordinate the moment a client leaves and re-enters range — and because the sector key is frozen, that boundary is at the OLD location, not the new one.

facts.claim: `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` performs no delta encoding: it writes uid + OwnerRevision + DataRevision + owner + position (38 bytes) followed by a full `ZDO.Serialize` of every field on the ZDO, per peer, per send. `SendZDOToPeers2` gates on a 0.05s timer and services one peer per `ZDOMan.Update`.
facts.implication: A continuously moving portal costs ~80-120 bytes per peer per cycle (position + prefab + connection + tag/tagauthor strings), ~1.6-2.4 KB/s/peer at ~20Hz, times N moving portals. It also permanently satisfies `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` (:76003), so it occupies a sync-list slot forever under the 10240-byte send-queue cap (:77010-77016).

facts.claim: The per-write CPU cost of `ZDO.SetPosition` on a portal is near zero (field assignment; SetSector early-returns), but `IncreaseDataRevision` calls `SetDirtySector` which for a persistent ZDO inserts up to 4 ChunkIndex entries into the dirty-chunk HashSet.
facts.implication: Tick cost is negligible; the real cost is that every move dirties the chunk files at the portal's new location, inflating autosave work even though the portal itself is never written into those chunks.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` resolves the destination at the instant of transit by `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection)` then `zDO.GetPosition()` / `zDO.GetRotation()`, with no prefab-type validation of the target whatsoever.
facts.implication: A portal's Portal connection can legally point at a Ship's ZDO, a player's ZDO, or any other ZDO — the vanilla client will teleport to that ZDO's live position. This is the real 'moving destination' mechanism, and it needs no client mod.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals` (5s coroutine) nulls any portal connection whose target ZDO is missing, has a different `s_tag`, or has no reciprocal Portal connection.
facts.implication: Pointing a portal at a Ship survives only if the ship ZDO also carries the same `s_tag` string AND a reciprocal `SetConnection(Portal, portalUid)` — or if the mod re-writes the link faster than 5s, or patches ConnectPortals. Writing a Portal connection onto a ship is safe (ships never have a SyncTransform parent of their own).

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(connectionZDOID)` when the client lacks the target ZDO; the server answers with `GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO(id)`, and `SendZDOs` removes the id from `m_forceSend` after one send.
facts.implication: A distant moving destination (a ship) is fetched by the client ONCE and then goes stale — TargetFound never re-requests once the ZDO exists locally. Keeping a moving destination fresh on every client requires the server to call `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(shipUid)` every send cycle.

facts.claim: `Player.UpdateTeleport` snapshots the destination once into `m_teleportTargetPos` and then force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate from t>2s; for `distantTeleport` (what portals always pass) completion additionally requires t>8s AND `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady`, with a 15s fallback that drops the player to `ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight + 0.5`.
facts.citation: Player.TeleportTo, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15302-15326; Player.UpdateTeleport, :15329-15376 (2s gate :15337, position pin :15343, 8s/IsAreaReady gate :15349, FindFloor :15354, 15s fallback :15360-15366); TeleportWorld passes distantTeleport:true at :143546
facts.implication: Arriving 'on' a moving ship is physically impossible with vanilla's own teleport: the player is pinned at a frozen world coordinate for at least 8 seconds. Any ship-as-destination feature lands the traveller in open water behind the boat.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` = Default | static_solid | Default_small | piece | terrain — it does NOT include the "vehicle" layer, which `BaseAI` explicitly adds to its own copy of the same mask.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.Awake mask setup, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113424; BaseAI mask setup, :25909; ZoneSystem.FindFloor, :115604; ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight, :115525
facts.implication: `FindFloor`/`GetSolidHeight` cannot see a ship hull if ships are on the vehicle layer, so the teleport-completion check over a boat falls through to the seabed raycast. Strong evidence that vanilla simply cannot land a portal traveller on a deck.

facts.claim: Zones/sectors are 2D in x/z only — `ZoneSystem.GetZone` and `GetSectorIndex` use `point.x` and `point.z` with a 64m grid and ignore y entirely. Dungeon interiors are instantiated at the surface location's zone centre with `y + 5000f`, and `Character.InInterior(pos)` is simply `pos.y > 3000f`.
facts.implication: A portal inside a crypt sits in the SAME sector as the surface above it. No special ZDO handling, no special sync rules — ZDOMan ships it to anyone standing on the ground overhead, and Game.ConnectPortals pairs it identically to a surface portal. Nothing about dungeons needs special server-side code.

facts.claim: Building inside a dungeon is blocked client-side by `!component.m_allowedInDungeons && InInterior() && !EnvMan.CheckInteriorBuildingOverride() && !ZoneSystem.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild)`.
facts.implication: Vanilla-respecting only: a server-side `DungeonBuild` global key write lets any unmodified client place portals in dungeons, exactly the way vanilla's own boss gating is honoured. It is not enforcement.

facts.claim: The dungeon-door class `Teleport` is architecturally unrelated to portals: its destination is a compiled `Teleport m_targetPoint` MonoBehaviour reference with no ZDO and no networking, and its exit point is computed as `transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`.
facts.implication: No server-side mod can retarget, log, or gate a crypt door through the ZDO layer. Its `NoBossPortals` check additionally reads `EnemyHud.instance` via `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631) — a client-only UI singleton.

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` returns false and writes nothing if the ZDO has no existing connection entry, whereas `SetConnection` always writes.
facts.implication: A rider's first-ever dismount is a silent no-op (ZSyncTransform uses UpdateConnection for the detach path at :87568). A player ZDO can therefore have NO connection entry at all rather than an explicit None — treat 'missing' and 'None' as the same 'not attached' state.

facts.claim: `ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea` uses Chebyshev distance <= 1.5 * 64m (=96m) from the zone centre at the default simulation distance, tightened to a 112m disc when NearSimulationDistance==2 and non-classic.
facts.implication: Quantifies the ownership-steal radius in ReleaseNearbyZDOS and the create/destroy boundary that makes a moved portal pop. ~96-112m around each peer.

facts.claim: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3, Quaternion, bool>("RPC_TeleportPlayer", ...)` is a global routed-RPC registration made in `Chat.Awake`, and `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is nothing but `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, distantTeleport)`.
facts.implication: Confirms the existing spec: a server-only mod can invoke the routed RPC by name without touching Chat.instance. This is the only way to actually put a player onto a moving ship — send the RPC repeatedly with the ship's CURRENT position, not once.

facts.claim: On a client, receiving a moved portal ZDO runs `AddIfPortal` again, which looks up `m_portalObjects[zdo.GetSectorIndex()]` using the NEW sector and appends the ZDO under a second key without removing the old entry.
facts.implication: Every sector boundary a moved portal crosses adds a duplicate entry to each receiving client's portal registry, which then appears twice in FindObjects results. Unbounded growth on long-lived client sessions.

apis.signature: ZDOID ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType type)
apis.notes: Pass ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform (value 2) on a player's character ZDO to get the ZDOID of whatever Rigidbody+ZNetView they are riding. Exact type match required — do NOT OR in Target. Returns ZDOID.None when detached or when no entry exists.

apis.signature: ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType ZDO.GetConnectionType()
apis.notes: Cheap pre-check: returns None when the ZDO has no connection entry at all, which is the normal state for a player who has never boarded anything.

apis.signature: void ZDO.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: Always writes and bumps DataRevision; calls ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() when type==Portal. No ownership check, but claim ownership first (zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())) or you race the real owner's revision counter. Overwrites the ZDO's single connection slot.

apis.signature: void ZDO.UpdateConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType connectionType, ZDOID zid)
apis.notes: No-op if the ZDO has no existing connection entry. Use SetConnection unless you specifically want that guard.

apis.signature: void ZDO.SetPosition(Vector3 pos)
apis.notes: Only increments DataRevision when IsOwner(). For portal prefabs the sector re-registration is skipped entirely (SetSector :73754), so the ZDO stays keyed to its creation-time sector.

apis.signature: void ZDO.SetOwner(long uid) / static long ZDOMan.GetSessionID()
apis.notes: Re-claim before every position write. ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901) will steal it back for any peer within ~96-112m within 2s; guard with a Harmony prefix on ZDO.SetOwner the way Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch does.

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID id) / void ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)
apis.notes: One-shot per call — SendZDOs removes the id from m_forceSend after sending (:77048). The ONLY way to push a moved portal, or a live ship position used as a portal destination, to peers outside the ZDO's registered sector. Must be re-issued every send cycle for continuous motion.

apis.signature: List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList() / Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Full enumeration of every portal ZDO in the world, no spatial query needed. Keys are creation-time sectors, so never trust the key as a location — read zdo.GetPosition(). GetPortalList() allocates a new List every call; cache it.

apis.signature: void ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects(Vector2s sector, SimulationDistance simulationDistance, List<ZDO> sectorObjects, List<ZDO> distantSectorObjects = null)
apis.notes: The spatial query Wonderland's ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear wraps. Includes m_portalObjects entries via FindObjects (:77376). Use SimulationDistance(area, 0, classic: true) for a square ring sweep.

apis.signature: ZDO ZDOMan.GetZDO(ZDOID id)
apis.notes: Resolve a SyncTransform connection target to the parent's ZDO, then prefab-check it: ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab()).GetComponent<Ship>() != null.

apis.signature: long ZDO.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_user, 0L)  // on a Ship-prefab ZDO
apis.notes: Stable PlayerID of the current helmsman, 0 when nobody is steering. Fully confirmed, no Inspector dependency. Passengers are invisible to this.

apis.signature: Vector3 ZDO.GetVec3(ZDOVars.s_relPosHash, Vector3.zero) / Quaternion ZDO.GetQuaternion(ZDOVars.s_relRotHash, Quaternion.identity) / string ZDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash)
apis.notes: On a parented rider's ZDO these give the exact deck-local position and rotation, plus the attach-joint name. Empty attachJoint + non-None SyncTransform connection = riding a vehicle; non-empty attachJoint = riding a Character. Cross-check with shipZdo.GetPosition() + shipZdo.GetRotation() * relPos ≈ playerZdo.GetPosition() to reject stale data.

apis.signature: void Game.ConnectPortals()
apis.notes: Public and local-player-free. Also the thing that will null any portal→non-portal link within 5s (self-heal at :100597-100604) unless the target ZDO carries a matching s_tag and a reciprocal Portal connection.

apis.signature: List<int> Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash
apis.notes: Membership decides sector-exemption (ZDO.SetSector :73754), m_portalObjects registration (AddIfPortal :77734) and chunk-save exclusion (:77572). Contents come from the Inspector list m_portalPrefabs (:99828) — enumerate it at runtime, do not assume.

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(long targetPeerID, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport)
apis.notes: Global routed RPC, no Chat.instance needed. The ONLY viable way to put a player onto a ship: issue it repeatedly with the ship's current ZDO position. Note the receiving Player.TeleportTo no-ops if m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15315).

apis.signature: bool Ship.IsPlayerInBoat(long playerID) / bool Ship.HasPlayerOnboard() / long ShipControlls.GetUser()
apis.notes: All require a live Ship MonoBehaviour, which a dedicated server never instantiates (Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position at 1e6,0,1e6 — :100465). Read ZDOVars.s_user off the ship's ZDO instead of calling GetUser().

apis.signature: Ship Character.GetStandingOnShip() / int Character.InNumShipVolumes / bool Character.IsAttachedToShip()
apis.notes: Local instance state only; InNumShipVolumes is a plain auto-property driven by Ship.OnTriggerEnter/Exit (:141023/:141042) with zero networking.

gotchas: The moving-portal idea fails on the client before it fails anywhere else: `ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 sets the transform at Instantiate and `ZNetView.Awake`:82566 never touches position again. Absent a ZSyncTransform on the portal prefab, a vanilla client's portal mesh AND its TeleportWorldTrigger collider stay frozen at the build site no matter what the server writes. It does not rubber-band, it does not re-instantiate — it just ignores you until the instance is destroyed and recreated, at which point it pops.

`ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73754), so `m_portalObjects` stays keyed by the sector the portal was created in. `CreateSyncList`→`FindSectorObjects`→`FindObjects`(:77376) therefore keeps delivering a moved portal to peers near its ORIGINAL location and never to peers at its new one. Every moved portal needs per-tick `ForceSendZDO`.

Moving a portal across a 64m sector boundary permanently corrupts the portal registry: `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76979 removes it using the recomputed current sector index, which no longer matches the dictionary key, so a destroyed portal ZDO leaks into `m_portalObjects` forever and `Game.ConnectPortals()` keeps trying to pair a dead object.

Moved portal positions are not saved. `AddObjectsPerChunk`:77572 excludes portal prefabs from chunk files and the ChunkPortal file is only written when `DirtyPortalObjects`:77621 — which a position write never sets. Every relocation reverts on restart unless you also touch the Portal connection in the same save window.

`ZDO.InternalSetPosition`:73740 only bumps DataRevision when `IsOwner()`. Writing a position you do not own is a completely silent no-op on the wire, and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 revokes server ownership of anything within ~96-112m of a player every 2 seconds. A moving-portal loop that forgets to re-claim ownership appears to work in the logs and does nothing in the world.

On the CLIENT, every sector boundary a moved portal crosses adds a duplicate entry to `m_portalObjects` (`AddIfPortal`:77738 keys on the new sector and never removes the old one). Unbounded registry growth on long client sessions.

The whole parent-sync read depends on `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync`:87362 being ticked on the Player prefab — Inspector data, invisible to the decompile. Wonderland's ShipAttachment.cs header records a live test of the adjacent ground-body approach that was 'granted once, then never again', which is a warning sign even though the mechanism it tested was different.

The SyncTransform connection is a latch, not a heartbeat: `OwnerSync` only rewrites it `if (m_tempParent != m_tempParentCached)`:87546. It persists across restarts via the hash path (`ZDO.Save`:74313 + `ConnectSyncTransforms`:78232), so a disconnected or crashed player's ZDO can keep claiming a ship parent indefinitely. Always cross-check `shipZdo.GetPosition() + shipRot*relPos ≈ playerZdo.GetPosition()`.

A rider's parent is whatever Rigidbody+ZNetView they stand on — carts (Vagon), tamed mounts, Leviathans (Character.CustomFixedUpdate references Leviathan at :1598), moving props. The connection target MUST be prefab-checked for a Ship component before it means 'on a ship'.

Pointing a portal at a Ship's ZDO works at the client transit site (`TeleportWorld.Teleport`:143539 does a bare GetZDO with no prefab validation), but `Game.ConnectPortals`:100597-100604 nulls the connection within 5 seconds because the ship has no matching `s_tag` and no reciprocal Portal connection. You must either fake both on the ship ZDO, out-write the 5s pass, or patch ConnectPortals.

`TeleportWorld.TargetFound`:143653 requests a missing destination ZDO exactly once (`RequestZDO`→`ForceSendZDO`, which `SendZDOs`:77048 consumes). After that the client never re-requests, so a distant moving destination goes stale immediately. Only continuous server-side ForceSendZDO keeps it fresh.

Even with a perfectly fresh destination, arriving 'on' a moving ship is impossible in vanilla: `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343 force-assigns a FROZEN snapshot position every FixedUpdate, and for distantTeleport (which portals always pass, :143546) completion is blocked until t>8s AND IsAreaReady (:15349). The traveller is nailed to an 8-second-old coordinate.

`ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 omits the "vehicle" layer that `BaseAI`:25909 explicitly adds, so `FindFloor`/`GetSolidHeight` do not see a ship hull. Over water they hit the seabed instead, and the 15s fallback (:15363) drops the player to seabed height. Landing someone on a deck is not something vanilla's teleport can do.

Vanilla bug to not build on: `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes relative velocity to `s_velHash` (:87561) while `SyncPosition` reads `s_velRelHash` (:87647). `velRel` is never written by anything. And `vel` is session-only (`s_sessionHashes`:78691), so it is absent from disk.

`ZDO` holds exactly ONE connection (`s_connections`:74794 is one value per ZDO). Writing a Portal connection onto a player's ZDO would wipe their SyncTransform parentage. Ships are safe because they never have a parent.

`ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection`:74962 silently does nothing when no entry exists, so a player who has never boarded anything has NO connection record rather than an explicit None. Treat missing and None identically.

`ZDOMan.SendZDOs`:77053 re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO (every float/vec3/quat/int/long/string/byte[]) on every send — there is no delta encoding — and a permanently-incrementing DataRevision makes `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend`:76003 true forever, so each moving portal permanently occupies a slot in every peer's sync list under the 10240-byte queue cap (:77010).
openQuestions: Is `m_characterParentSync` ticked on the Player prefab's ZSyncTransform? In-game check: have a player board a karve/longship, then from server code read `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetConnectionType()` and `.GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform)`. A type of `SyncTransform` (2) with a non-None target proves it. Corroborate with `GetVec3(ZDOVars.s_relPosHash)` returning a non-zero deck-local offset and `GetString(ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash)` returning "". Repeat while the player walks, stands still, jumps, and sits at the helm, and again after they step onto the dock (should latch to None).

Does the portal prefab (portal_wood, and Ashlands portal_stone) carry a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition? This is the single decisive unknown for 'moving portals'. In-game check: with a player standing next to a portal, run server-side `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetPosition(pos + Vector3.up*3f); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` every tick for 3 seconds. If the mesh glides upward and the walk-through trigger follows, ZSyncTransform is present (expect a 20%/FixedUpdate lerp with a 5m snap, :87715). If nothing visible happens until the player walks ~120m away and back, it is absent and moving portals are dead.

What exactly is in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828)? It decides which ZDOs get sector-exemption, m_portalObjects registration and chunk-save exclusion. Check: at server start, log every hash in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).name`.

Can a portal even be built on a ship's deck, and if so does its ZDO position track the ship? Check: build a portal on a longship, sail 300m, then read that portal ZDO's `GetPosition()` server-side. If it is frozen at the build coordinate, ship-mounted portals are useless as destinations and effectively invisible to the portal registry's location logic.

What Unity layer are Ship hull/deck colliders on? `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 omits "vehicle" while `BaseAI`:25909 includes it. Check: force-teleport a player (via the RPC_TeleportPlayer route) to 1m above a stationary boat's deck and observe whether `UpdateTeleport` completes at deck height (FindFloor hit the hull) or the player falls through into the water (it did not).

Ship top speeds (m_sailForceFactor, m_force, mass) are all Inspector values, so the exact drift distance during the ≥8s teleport hold cannot be computed from the decompile. Check: record a longship's ZDO position server-side at 1Hz under full sail and measure metres travelled in 8 seconds — that number is the minimum miss distance for any ship-as-destination feature.

Does `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` actually let a vanilla client place a portal inside a crypt, or does the portal piece's `m_allowedInDungeons` Inspector bool already permit it? Check: set the global key server-side and try placing a portal inside a burial chamber on an unmodified client.
correctionsToExistingSpec: The spec's phrasing around the ship-attach feature is right in substance but names the wrong member. The flag is `ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync` (:87362), a component-level Inspector bool — there is no `Character.m_characterParentSync`, and `SetCharacterParent`/`RPC_SetCharacterParent` return zero grep hits across all four 1.0.7 decompiles. `Character.m_lastAttachBody` (:600) is a private Rigidbody used only for local anti-slide force on a deck (:2106-2143) and is never networked.

The spec lists 'Portal to a player's live-attached ship' as [Feasible-with-caveats, small] pending only the Inspector check. Two additional blockers were not captured: (a) `Game.ConnectPortals`:100597-100604 will null any portal→ship link within 5 seconds because the ship carries no matching `s_tag` and no reciprocal Portal connection; (b) `TeleportWorld.TargetFound`:143653 fetches a distant target ZDO exactly once via a one-shot ForceSendZDO, so without continuous server-side `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(shipUid)` the client teleports to a stale ship position. This is medium effort with a live tick loop, not small.

The spec does not state that a ship destination is unusable even when technically wired up. `Player.UpdateTeleport`:15343-15349 pins the arriving player at a frozen snapshot coordinate for at least 8 seconds (distantTeleport is always true for portals, :143546), and `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask`:113424 cannot see the vehicle layer, so the traveller lands in open water behind the boat rather than on the deck. 'Portal to a player's live-attached ship' should be re-scoped to 'portal to the water beside where the ship was ~8s ago', or paired with a follow-up `RPC_TeleportPlayer` (:41627) issued after arrival.

The spec's 'Portal to any computed coordinate' via `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` is correct, but should carry the caveat that such a portal can never be MOVED afterwards by the normal sync path: `ZDO.SetSector`:73754 freezes the sector key and `m_portalObjects` is never re-keyed, `AddObjectsPerChunk`:77572 plus the `DirtyPortalObjects` gate at :77621 mean the new position is never saved, and `HandleDestroyedZDO`:76979 leaks the ZDO if it crossed a sector boundary. Created portals should be treated as immutable in position.

The spec correctly notes vanilla takes ownership before writing portal fields, but does not state the mechanical reason: `ZDO.InternalSetPosition`:73740 skips `IncreaseDataRevision()` entirely when the server is not the owner, so a non-owner position write never reaches any client. Combined with `ReleaseNearbyZDOS`:76901 stealing ownership every 2s for any ZDO within ~96-112m of a peer, ownership re-claiming is mandatory per write, not merely 'more reliable' as the Group 1 'Proactive server ownership claim' line implies.

Add to the 'Ruled Out' list: **moving/following portals of any kind**. Not because the ZDO cannot be written, but because (a) vanilla clients never reposition an existing instance (`ZNetScene.CreateObject`:82011 / `ZNetView.Awake`:82566 apply position only at Instantiate), (b) the sector key is frozen so normal sync stops reaching the new location, (c) the move is not persisted, and (d) crossing a sector boundary permanently leaks the ZDO in `m_portalObjects` on destroy. Only the *destination* can meaningfully move, never the gate itself.

The spec's dungeon coverage can be simplified: dungeon interiors need no special server-side handling at all. Zones are 2D x/z only (`ZoneSystem.GetZone`:115741), interiors sit at surface `y + 5000f` (`Location.Awake`:133512) and `InInterior` is just `y > 3000f` (:4538), so a crypt portal occupies the SAME sector as the ground above it and `Game.ConnectPortals` pairs it identically. The only dungeon-specific lever really is the client-honoured `GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild` (:13353), exactly as listed.

`Wonderland/Core/Data/ShipAttachment.cs` deserves promotion in the spec from an implementation detail to the recommended primary mechanism for anything ship-related, because `ZDOVars.s_user` on the Ship ZDO (`ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl`:141332) is fully confirmed from code with no Inspector dependency, whereas the SyncTransform-connection path is not. The trade is coverage: s_user sees only the helmsman, never passengers.

research.topic: target-sources-world — what world-static things a dedicated server can locate and point a portal at (Valheim 1.0.7)
research.summary: The dedicated server has exactly two rich, zero-player, whole-world target registries, and they are world-gen data, not ZDOs: `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` (every location in the world — boss altars, StartTemple, traders, crypts, dungeons, runestone camps — with a ground-height-resolved position, persisted in the world save and fully populated before any player connects) and `World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`: a 2048x2048 / 12m biome+height grid plus flood-filled `BiomeSector`s with world-space `Center`, bbox, height min/max/avg, neighbours, and per-biome `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel`). Everything collider-based in `ZoneSystem` (`GetGroundHeight`, `GetSolidHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `FindFloor`, `GetGroundData`, `IsLava(Vector3)`) is **dead on a dedicated server**, because `Game.FixedUpdate` (server build, :100463) pins `ZNet.m_referencePosition` to `(1e6,0,1e6)` every physics tick, so the only Heightmap colliders that ever exist sit 1,000,000 m from the world. Server-side position validation must therefore be pure procedural math: `WorldGenerator.GetHeight/GetBiome/GetNormal/GetTerrainDelta`, sea level 30, `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` (static, WorldGenerator-only), `WorldGenerator.worldSize/waterEdge`, plus `AltBiomeWorldData.PointHeights` as an O(1) cached 12m height lookup. Object-level targets (a specific altar bowl, a chest, a dungeon room) are ZDOs that only exist after a peer's ghost-zone generation has run for that zone, are found only via the resumable `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (there is no `GetAllZDOsWithPrefab`), and require prefab names that live in Unity asset data. Finally, two vanilla server→client channels already push world coordinates onto a vanilla client's map: the `LocationIcons` routed RPC (also the authority for where a vanilla client respawns, via `Game.m_StartLocation` = "StartTemple") and `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` (arbitrary saved pin, name, type, position).

facts.claim: On a dedicated server `Game.FixedUpdate` unconditionally sets `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick. The client build's `Game.FixedUpdate` has no such line.
facts.implication: Every server subsystem keyed off the reference position operates around (1e6,0,1e6): `ZoneSystem.CreateLocalZones` (:113930), `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82270), `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82112), `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76880). No terrain collider and effectively no GameObject ever exists near real world coordinates.

facts.claim: Every ground/solid/blocked helper on ZoneSystem is a `Physics.Raycast` against layer masks built in `ZoneSystem.Awake` (terrain / Default / static_solid / Default_small / piece).
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.Awake :113419-113425; IsBlocked :115496; GetGroundHeight :115502 and :115513; GetSolidHeight :115525, :115536, :115548, :115574; GetStaticSolidHeight :115590; FindFloor :115604; GetGroundData :115667; IsLava(Vector3) :115647
facts.implication: All of these silently return the fallback (`p.y`, or false) on a dedicated server because no Heightmap/piece collider exists at real world coordinates. They are NOT usable for validating a portal destination. Do not call them and do not trust a `false`/`p.y` result as 'no ground'.

facts.claim: Ghost-mode zone spawning does instantiate a Heightmap (`SpawnZone` instantiates `m_zonePrefab` for every mode) but immediately `Destroy`s the root and all spawned objects at the end of the same call when mode == Ghost.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.SpawnZone :114071, instantiate :114085, ghost teardown :114094-114102; Heightmap.OnEnable→Regenerate :128417-128429; Heightmap.Regenerate→RebuildCollisionMesh :128521-128527
facts.implication: There is a sub-frame window where a peer's ghost zone has a real terrain collider, but it is gone by the next frame. Not a usable query surface; do not design around it.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` is a public `Dictionary<Vector2s, LocationInstance>` holding one entry per zone for EVERY location in the whole world, and it is written to and read from the world save (`Save`/`Load`).
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances :113295; PrepareSave :113734; Save :113742 (locations written :113762-113770); Load :113782 (RegisterLocation replay :113801-113815)
facts.implication: This is the primary server-side world-target registry: complete, whole-map, available at world load with zero players connected, survives restarts, costs one dictionary read. This — not a ZDO scan — is how a server-only mod enumerates boss altars, the start temple, traders, crypts and dungeon sites.

facts.claim: `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` calls `AltBiomeWorldData.VerifyBiomeData(m_world)` and then `ZoneSystem.instance.GenerateLocationsIfNeeded()` immediately after loading the world db, before any peer can connect.
facts.implication: Both the location registry and the biome grid are guaranteed populated by the time a mod's first tick runs on a dedicated server. No 'wait for a player' gating is needed.

facts.claim: `LocationInstance.m_position.y` is set to `WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)` during location generation, and altitude checks in the same loop compare `y - 30.0`.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsTimeSliced :114639, y assignment :114735, altitude test :114736-114742; LocationInstance struct :113001
facts.implication: Every stored location position already carries a procedurally-valid ground height with sea level = 30. A portal target at a location needs no extra height resolution — only a +1..2 m lift. Caveat: it is the PRE-flattening height; a location with `m_clearArea`/terrain modifiers ends up a metre or two off.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(name, out pos)` and `GetLocationIcons(dict)` branch on `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`: the server branch reads `m_locationInstances` directly and emits entries whose `ZoneLocation.m_iconAlways` is true, or `m_iconPlaced` is true AND the instance is already placed. The client branch reads the RPC-received `m_locationIcons` dictionary.
facts.implication: `GetLocationIcons` on the server is the ready-made 'world landmark registry': {world position -> location prefab name} for every icon-flagged location (in vanilla: start temple, boss altars, traders). O(number of location instances), no allocation beyond the dict, no players needed. Cache it; don't call it per frame.

facts.claim: `ZoneLocation` exposes, as public serialized fields readable server-side: `m_prefabName`, `m_biome`, `m_quantity`, `m_unique`, `m_group`, `m_iconAlways`, `m_iconPlaced`, `m_snapToWater`, `m_interiorRadius`, `m_exteriorRadius`, `m_clearArea`, `m_minAltitude`. `m_prefabName` is populated in `SetupLocations`.
facts.implication: From a `LocationInstance` alone the server knows the location's name, biome, exterior/interior radius and whether it is map-iconed — enough to pick a safe stand-off distance from a location's footprint without any collider query.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.FindClosestLocation(string name, Vector3 point, out LocationInstance)` and `FindLocations(string name, ref List<LocationInstance>)` are public and match on `m_location.m_prefab.Name` by linear scan of every location instance.
facts.implication: Direct server-callable 'nearest boss altar / nearest crypt / all traders' lookup. Cost is O(all location instances) per call (thousands of entries on a full map) with a `Vector3.Distance` each — fine on a timer, not per-tick-per-player. Build a name→List index once instead.

facts.claim: Vanilla's own `find` console command resolves world targets with exactly three sources: `FindObjectsOfType<GameObject>()`, `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationList()`, and a blocking `while (!ZDOMan.instance.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(q, list, ref index)) {}` loop. Its autocomplete uses `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` plus `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations`.
facts.implication: Confirms the full server-side target vocabulary: every prefab name is enumerable at runtime (`GetPrefabNames`), and every location definition is enumerable (`ZoneSystem.m_locations` :113248) — so the mod does not need hardcoded vanilla name lists, it can discover them on boot.

facts.claim: There is no `ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab`. The only prefab-wide ZDO scan is `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO> zdos, ref int index)`, which walks the 512x512 = 262144-slot `m_objectsBySector` array and returns after touching ~400 NON-EMPTY sectors.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative :77442-77496 (budget check :77489); ZDOMan ctor `new ZDOMan(512)` :79163; ResetSectorArray :76163
facts.implication: Any 'find every altar/runestone/chest' scan is inherently multi-call and time-sliced. A full pass costs ceil(nonEmptySectors/400)+1 calls and re-hashes the prefab name each call. Wonderland's `PrefabSetSweeper` (Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs) already solves the multi-prefab case in one walk; reuse it.

facts.claim: `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative`'s terminal branch (entered when `index >= m_objectsBySector.Length`) re-scans `m_objectsBySector[0]` — which the loop already scanned at index 0 — and only then adds matches from `m_portalObjects`.
facts.implication: Two traps: (a) ZDOs in sector index 0 (zone (-256,-256) AND the out-of-range fallback bucket, see SectorToIndex :115760-115774) appear TWICE in a complete pass — deduplicate; (b) portal ZDOs are returned ONLY on the final call, so an early-abandoned scan finds zero portals.

facts.claim: Objects inside a location (boss bowls, traders, runestones, chests) get real ZDOs only when `SpawnLocation` runs in Full or Ghost mode; in Ghost mode every child `ZNetView` is instantiated under `ZNetView.StartGhostInit()`, which creates and keeps the ZDO but never registers the GameObject with `ZNetScene`.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115162, ghost ZNetView loop :115234-115267; CreateLocationProxy :115347; ZNetView.Awake ghost path :82612-82628; StartGhostInit :82868; FinishGhostInit :82873
facts.implication: Object-level targets are NOT available for the whole world up front. They materialise per zone the first time a peer's reference position brings that zone within `CreateGhostZones`' simulation distance (:113934-113938). An unvisited corner of the map has location instances but no altar ZDO. Portal targeting must fall back to the LocationInstance position.

facts.claim: `OfferingBowl` is a plain MonoBehaviour with no ZDO of its own — it does `GetComponentInParent<ZNetView>()` in `Start` — and all of its spawn-position logic (`GetSpawnPosition`, `m_spawnPoints`, `m_getSolidHeightMargin`, `m_enableSolidHeightCheck`) is Inspector data used by the interacting client.
facts.implication: Corrects the existing spec: there is no 'OfferingBowl ZDO'. A boss altar is addressable server-side as (a) a LocationInstance of the altar's location, always available, or (b) the altar piece's parent-ZNetView ZDO, available only after ghost generation and only by a prefab name that lives in Unity asset data.

facts.claim: `Vegvisir` (runestone) is a MonoBehaviour whose `Interact` calls `Game.instance.DiscoverClosestLocation(...)`; its `m_locations` list of `VegvisrLocation` (location name, pin name, pin type, discoverAll) is plain Inspector data on the prefab.
facts.implication: A server cannot read which locations a given runestone points at (prefab asset data, never in a ZDO). But it does not need to: `Game.RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation` on the server already resolves names via `ZoneSystem.FindClosestLocation`/`FindLocations`, so the mod can reproduce runestone discovery directly from the location registry.

facts.claim: `Game.DiscoverClosestLocation` invokes the routed RPC `RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation` (registered server-side only), and the server replies with `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse(pinName, pinType, pos, showMap)`, which is registered on BOTH sides in `Game.Start` and whose client handler calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation(pos, type, name, showMap)` → `AddPin(..., save: true, ...)`.
facts.citation: Game.Start registrations :100067-100072; DiscoverClosestLocation :100793-100797; RPC_DiscoverClosestLocation :100799-100821; RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse :100823-100831; client Minimap.DiscoverLocation, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58394-58421; PinType enum :56139
facts.implication: A dedicated server can push an arbitrary SAVED map pin (arbitrary name, any `Minimap.PinType`, any coordinate, plus a HUD message and optional map-open/look-at) to any vanilla client at any time by invoking `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` directly. This is the vanilla-respecting way to show a player where a portal now points. Duplicate suppression is client-side via `HaveSimilarPin`.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons(peer)` packs `GetLocationIcons()` (position + location prefab name) into a ZPackage and sends the `LocationIcons` routed RPC; it fires on every new peer and again whenever an `m_iconPlaced` location is first placed. The client stores it in `m_locationIcons` and `Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` rebuilds pins from it every 5 s, rendering only names it can resolve to a sprite in `Minimap.m_locationIcons`.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons :113581-113593; RPC_LocationIcons :113595-113607; OnNewPeer :113609-113617; PlaceLocations re-send :115000-115003; client Minimap.UpdateLocationPins, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57551-57591; Minimap.GetLocationIcon :57594-57604; Minimap.m_locationIcons :56373
facts.implication: Second server→client map channel, fully server-authoritative: the server controls the entire location-icon pin set on every vanilla client. Pins are `save:false`, double-size, and vanish when removed from the server's list. Limit: only names present in the client's `Minimap.m_locationIcons` asset list render at all; an invented name is silently dropped.

facts.claim: A vanilla client's default respawn point is whatever position the server reported for the key `Game.m_StartLocation` (= "StartTemple") in that LocationIcons package: `Game.FindSpawnPoint` calls `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation, out pos)` and spawns at `pos + Vector3.up * 2f`.
facts.implication: 'Portal to world spawn' is exact and free: read `GetLocationIcon("StartTemple")` server-side. It also means the server can relocate the world spawn for vanilla clients purely by altering the LocationIcons payload — no client mod. Note `GetLocationIcon` returns the FIRST dictionary match, not the closest, and requires the location's icon flags to be set.

facts.claim: `Location.Awake` places a location's interior 5000 m directly above its zone centre (`new Vector3(zoneCenter.x, transform.position.y + 5000f, zoneCenter.z)`), and `Character.InInterior(Vector3 position)` is simply `position.y > 3000f`.
facts.citation: Location :133457; m_hasInterior :133474; interior instantiation :133509-133514; GetZoneCenter :133516-133519; Character.InInterior(Vector3) :4538-4541
facts.implication: Dungeon/crypt interior coordinates are derivable server-side from a location instance: interior lives around (zoneCenterX, ~5030, zoneCenterZ). Any 'is this a surface coordinate' guard should reject y > 3000 exactly the way vanilla does.

facts.claim: `DungeonGenerator.Save()` serialises every placed room (prefab hash, world position, world rotation) into its own ZDO as the byte array `ZDOVars.s_roomData`; `Load()` reads it back. `DungeonDB.GetRoom(hash)` resolves the room prefab.
