facts.citation: DungeonGenerator.Save :152970-153000; Load :153002-153062; ZDOVars.s_roomData :78573; DungeonDB.GetRoom :152489; DungeonDB.GetRooms :152484; Room.Theme :153696
facts.implication: Dungeon interior layout IS server-readable — a mod can enumerate real room positions inside a crypt and pick one as a portal target — but only for dungeons whose zone has already been ghost-generated, and only if it can locate the DungeonGenerator ZDO in the first place (prefab name is Unity asset data; `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` cannot search byte-array fields).

facts.claim: `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type, hash)` supports only Float/Long/Int/String and logs an error for anything else (ByteArray included). It is implemented by walking every ZDO's field dictionary.
facts.citation: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash :75390-75407; backing extension :75707-75722; Type enum (includes ByteArray) :74735
facts.implication: You CAN build a global index of every materialised location by querying the Int field `ZDOVars.s_location` (:78501) — that returns every `LocationProxy` ZDO with its location hash and position (LocationProxy.SetLocation :102653-102659). You CANNOT do the same for `s_roomData`. Cost is O(all int fields in the world); do it once and cache.

facts.claim: `class Teleport` (dungeon/crypt doors) resolves its destination from `public Teleport m_targetPoint`, a plain Inspector reference, via `GetTeleportPoint()` = `transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`. Nothing is stored in any ZDO.
facts.implication: Dungeon entrance→exit pairing is invisible to the server. A 'portal to a crypt entrance' target must be the location instance position or an entrance-piece ZDO, never the Teleport pair.

facts.claim: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` resolves the exit purely from the connected ZDO: `position + (rotation * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up`, reading `GetPosition()`/`GetRotation()` off `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID)`. `TargetFound()` calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO(id)` when the target ZDO isn't loaded locally, and the server force-sends it.
facts.implication: A world target only becomes a portal destination if a ZDO sits at that coordinate with the right rotation. The client will pull a distant target ZDO on demand, so the target does not need to be near anyone. The exit offset is `+1 y` and `m_exitDistance` forward — so the ZDO's y must already be standable, and its rotation controls which way the arriving player is pushed.

facts.claim: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any ZDO whose prefab hash is in `Game.PortalPrefabHash`; portal ZDOs live only in `ZDOMan.m_portalObjects`, keyed by the sector index they had when `AddIfPortal` filed them, and `AddIfPortal` explicitly `RemoveFromSector`s them.
facts.implication: Moving a portal ZDO server-side with `SetPosition` (:73729) leaves it filed under its OLD sector key. `FindObjects` (:77367) for the new sector will not include it, and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) looks it up by the NEW sector index and fails to remove it — a permanent leak in m_portalObjects. Prefer creating a fresh ZDO at the target over relocating one.

facts.claim: Portal ZDOs are saved as a dedicated chunk (`ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal`) with NO `Persistent` check — the whole of `m_portalObjects` is cloned into it whenever `DirtyPortalObjects` is set — whereas all other ZDOs are saved only if `Persistent` is true.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch :77621-77636; non-portal persistence filter :77572; LoadChunks portal branch :76475-76483; SetDirtyPortals :76702; ZDO.Persistent :73323
facts.implication: A mod-created portal-prefab ZDO is persisted across restarts even without setting Persistent, provided `DirtyPortalObjects` got set (which `CreateNewZDO`→`AddIfPortal` does). A mod-created NON-portal ZDO used as a target must set `Persistent = true` explicitly — `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does not (the flag is normally set by `ZNetView.Awake` :82615).

facts.claim: `WorldGenerator` is fully procedural and collider-free: `GetHeight(x,z)`, `GetBiome(x,z)`, `GetBiomeHeight(biome,x,z,out mask)`, `GetNormal`, `GetAverageNormal`, `GetTerrainDelta(center,radius,out delta,out slopeDir)`, `InForest`, `GetForestFactor`, `GetSeed`. `GetHeightMultiplier()` is 200 and sea level is 30.
facts.citation: WorldGenerator :150952; GetHeight :151934/:151939/:151944/:151951; GetBiomeHeight :151964; GetNormal :151920/:151925; GetAverageNormal :151905; GetTerrainDelta :152364-152390; InForest :152353; GetHeightMultiplier :152396; ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel = 30f :113218; c_WaterLevel = 30f :113228
facts.implication: This is the ONLY viable server-side terrain query set. Underwater test = `GetHeight(x,z) < 30`. Slope test = `GetNormal(x,z,r).y` or `GetTerrainDelta`. It is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening, so treat results as +/- a couple of metres and always add clearance.

facts.claim: `WorldGenerator.GetBiomeHeight` returns `-2f * GetHeightMultiplier()` (= -400) for any point with `DUtils.Length(wx, wy) > 10500f`; `GetEdgeHeight` ramps terrain to 0 between 10000 and 10100 m and to -2 between 10490 and 10500 m. Constants: `worldSize = 10000f`, `waterEdge = 10500f`, `waterEdgeSqr = 110250000f`.
facts.implication: World-edge and open-ocean targets are computable exactly. Any candidate with `x*x+z*z > 110250000` is off-map void. `ashlandsMinDistance = 12000f` / `ashlandsYOffset = -4000f` (:151114-151116) and `IsDeepnorth` (:151719) give the Ashlands/Deep North boundaries as closed-form tests.

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(Vector3 position, float lavaValue = 0.6f)` is static and uses only `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome` + `GetBiomeHeight(..., out mask)`, testing `mask.a > lavaValue`. `GetAshlandsHeight` is what writes the lava value into `mask.a`.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap :115637-115646; WorldGenerator.GetAshlandsHeight mask assignment :152161 and :152224; Heightmap.IsLava (collider path, unusable) :129132
facts.implication: This is the one lava check that works on a dedicated server. Use it — never `ZoneSystem.instance.IsLava(...)`, which goes through `GetGroundData`'s raycast and returns `defaultTrue` when no Heightmap is hit. Note `mask.a` means lava only in Ashlands; in Mistlands/Deep North the same channel carries a different mask.

facts.claim: `World.m_biomeData` is an `AltBiomeWorldData`: a 2048x2048 grid at 12 m per cell (`c_pixelSize = 12f`, `c_halfWidth = 1024`) with `PointBiomes[x,y]`, `PointHeights[x,y]` and `PointSectors[x,y]` precomputed from `WorldGenerator.GetBiome`/`GetBiomeHeight` for the whole map, cached to disk as `biomedatacache.bin`.
facts.citation: AltBiomeWorldData :92332; c_textureSize/c_pixelSize/c_halfWidth :92342-92346; GenerateBiomePoints :92429-92457; MapSpaceToWorldSpace :92409-92422; WorldSpaceToMapSpace :92424-92427; SaveCache :92814; TryLoadCache :92830; GetPoint :92882/:92887
facts.implication: O(1) server-side biome + height lookup at 12 m resolution for any coordinate, with no noise evaluation at all: `PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]`. Ideal for a fast first-pass 'is this land' filter before spending a `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` call on the exact point.

facts.claim: `AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors` flood-fills the biome grid into `BiomeSector` regions and converts each sector's `Center`, `Min` and `Max` into WORLD space; `BiomeSector` also carries `HeightMin/HeightMax/HeightAvg`, `Neighbors`, `EdgeCount`, `DistanceFromCenter` and `AltBiomes`. `BiomeTypeInfo` per biome carries `Sectors`, `AllPoints` and `AllPointsAboveSeaLevel`.
facts.citation: AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors :92476-92616 (world-space conversion :92573-92576, DistanceFromCenter :92613); tryFill AllPoints population :92460-92474; BiomeSector :93884-93925; BiomeTypeInfo :94085-94094
facts.implication: 'Biome centroid' targets are a direct read: `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.Biomes[biome].Sectors` gives every contiguous region of that biome with a world-space centre and height range; `Sectors` can be sorted by `EdgeCount` (size) or `DistanceFromCenter`. Caveat: `Center` is the centroid of the region's PERIMETER cells, not its area centroid, so for a crescent-shaped region it can land outside the biome — always re-validate the chosen point's biome.

facts.claim: `BiomeSector.MinZone` and `MaxZone` are both computed from `sector.Min` and with the z component left at 0 (`ZoneSystem.GetZone(new Vector3(sector.Min.x, sector.Min.y))` twice), so MaxZone == MinZone and both are meaningless.
facts.implication: Never use `BiomeSector.MinZone`/`MaxZone`. Derive zone bounds from `Min`/`Max` (which ARE correct world-space Vector2 x/z) yourself. Vanilla's own `IsDiscovered` loop (:92605-92612) is broken by this same bug.

facts.claim: `AltBiomeWorldData` exposes `GetRandomPointByBiomes(Heightmap.Biome)`, `GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(Heightmap.Biome)` (>= 30 m) and `GetRandomSectorByBiomes(Heightmap.Biome)`, all accepting a bitmask of biomes; `ZoneSystem` itself uses these to seed location placement.
facts.citation: AltBiomeWorldData.GetRandomPointByBiomes :92697; GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel :92683; GetRandomSectorByBiomes :92673; RandomBiomeFromBiomes :92707; consumed by ZoneSystem.GenerateLocationsTimeSliced :114681
facts.implication: A 'send me to a random spot in the Plains, on land' target is one vanilla call plus `MapSpaceToWorldSpace`. Uses `UnityEngine.Random` — seed it deterministically if the mod wants reproducible targets.

facts.claim: Leviathans carry a `ZNetView` and a `Rigidbody`, move every FixedUpdate on the owning client, self-destruct on the `submerged` animation tag, and check `ZDOVars.s_dead` on Awake.
facts.implication: Leviathans are NOT a stable world target: transient, mobile, owner-simulated, and destroyed once mined out. Any portal pointed at one will break. Treat them as out of scope.

facts.claim: `Game.ConnectPortals` prunes a portal's connection whenever the target ZDO is missing, carries a different `ZDOVars.s_tag` string, or has `ZDOID.None` as its own connection; it only iterates `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`.
facts.citation: Game.ConnectPortals :100589-100627; FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679; ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648-77657; Game.PortalPrefabHash built in Awake :100021 and :100029-100031
facts.implication: A ZDO used as a portal destination must (a) exist, (b) carry the same tag string, and (c) hold a non-None connection back — otherwise vanilla's 5 s coroutine silently unlinks the player-facing portal. Whether a mod-made target ZDO enters the portal list at all depends on `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (Inspector list, :99828).

facts.claim: `ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations` re-resolves the spawn position with `GetGroundData` (a raycast) at placement time and forces `p.y = 30f` when `m_snapToWater` is set — i.e. the stored `LocationInstance.m_position` is the pre-placement estimate, not the final placed height.
facts.implication: For `m_snapToWater` locations (ocean structures) the real placed height is 30, not `m_position.y`. For everything else, expect a small delta between the stored y and where the location actually sits. Add >= 1 m clearance to any portal target derived from a LocationInstance.

apis.signature: public Dictionary<Vector2s, ZoneSystem.LocationInstance> ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances  // struct LocationInstance { ZoneLocation m_location; Vector3 m_position; bool m_placed; }
apis.notes: Public field, whole-world, persisted in the world save, populated before any peer connects. The primary world-target registry. Keyed by zone; one location max per zone. m_position.y is a WorldGenerator ground height.

apis.signature: public void ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons(Dictionary<Vector3, string> icons)
apis.notes: Server branch reads m_locationInstances and returns {worldPos -> location prefab name} for every location with m_iconAlways, or m_iconPlaced && m_placed. In vanilla that is start temple + boss altars + traders. O(location instances). Cache the result.

apis.signature: public bool ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(string name, out Vector3 pos)
apis.notes: Server branch scans m_locationInstances; returns the FIRST icon-flagged match by dictionary order, not the nearest. `GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation)` ("StartTemple") is the world spawn.

apis.signature: public bool ZoneSystem.FindClosestLocation(string name, Vector3 point, out ZoneSystem.LocationInstance closest)
apis.notes: Linear scan of all location instances comparing m_location.m_prefab.Name. Works with zero players. Build your own name->list index if calling often.

apis.signature: public bool ZoneSystem.FindLocations(string name, ref List<ZoneSystem.LocationInstance> locations)
apis.notes: All instances of one location type. Same O(n) scan. Clears the list first.

apis.signature: public Dictionary<Vector2s, ZoneSystem.LocationInstance>.ValueCollection ZoneSystem.GetLocationList()
apis.notes: Allocation-free enumeration of every location instance; this is what vanilla's own `find` console command uses.

apis.signature: public List<ZoneSystem.ZoneLocation> ZoneSystem.m_locations
apis.notes: Every location DEFINITION (name, biome, quantity, m_iconAlways/m_iconPlaced, m_exteriorRadius/m_interiorRadius, m_unique, m_group). Lets the mod discover the vanilla location vocabulary at boot instead of hardcoding names. Populated by SetupLocations :113619.

apis.signature: public float WorldGenerator.GetHeight(float wx, float wy)  /  GetHeight(Vector3 p)  /  GetHeight(float wx, float wy, out Color mask)
apis.notes: Pure procedural terrain height, no colliders. Sea level = 30. Returns -400 beyond 10500 m. Blind to player terraforming and location flattening.

apis.signature: public Heightmap.Biome WorldGenerator.GetBiome(float wx, float wy, float oceanLevel = 0.02f, bool waterAlwaysOcean = false)
apis.notes: Closed-form biome lookup. Vector3 overload at :151692. Companions: IsAshlands :151697, IsDeepnorth :151719, GetBiomeArea(Vector3) :151682.

apis.signature: public Vector3 WorldGenerator.GetNormal(Vector2 point, float radius = 1f)  /  GetAverageNormal(Vector2 point, float radius, float metersPerSample = 1.5f)
apis.notes: Four GetHeight samples; normal.y near 1 = flat. GetAverageNormal samples concentric rings (max 16) for a smoothed slope. The server-side substitute for a ground-normal raycast.

apis.signature: public void WorldGenerator.GetTerrainDelta(Vector3 center, float radius, out float delta, out Vector3 slopeDirection)
apis.notes: 10 random samples inside the radius; delta = max-min height. This is the exact roughness test vanilla uses to accept a location site (m_maxTerrainDelta defaults to 2f). Uses UnityEngine.Random — non-deterministic between calls.

apis.signature: public static bool ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(Vector3 position, float lavaValue = 0.6f)
apis.notes: Static, WorldGenerator-only, no colliders. The ONLY usable lava check on a dedicated server. ZoneSystem.instance.IsLava (:115647/:115657) goes through a raycast and is useless server-side.

apis.signature: public AltBiomeWorldData ZNet.World.m_biomeData  // PointHeights[x,y], PointBiomes[x,y], PointSectors[x,y], Sectors, Biomes[biome]
apis.notes: 2048x2048 grid at 12 m/cell. Index with AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x) (:92424). IsReady property :92380. O(1) biome+height lookup, disk-cached.

apis.signature: public static Vector3 AltBiomeWorldData.MapSpaceToWorldSpace(Vector2i value)  /  public static int AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float x)
apis.notes: world = (map - 1024) * 12 + 6; map = (world - 6)/12 + 1024. Needed to turn BiomePointCoordinates into world positions.

apis.signature: public BiomePointCoordinate AltBiomeWorldData.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(Heightmap.Biome biome)  /  GetRandomPointByBiomes(Heightmap.Biome)  /  GetRandomSectorByBiomes(Heightmap.Biome)
apis.notes: Accept a biome bitmask. AboveSeaLevel means PointHeights >= 30. Backed by BiomeTypeInfo.AllPoints/AllPointsAboveSeaLevel (:94085). Uses UnityEngine.Random.

apis.signature: public class BiomeSector { Vector2 Center; Vector2 Min; Vector2 Max; float HeightMin, HeightMax, HeightAvg; int EdgeCount; float DistanceFromCenter; List<BiomeSector> Neighbors; List<AltBiome> AltBiomes; Heightmap.Biome Biome; }
apis.notes: Center/Min/Max are WORLD space (x, z as Vector2.x/.y) after GenerateSectors :92573. MinZone/MaxZone are broken — ignore them. Center is a perimeter centroid, so re-validate the biome at the chosen point.

apis.signature: public bool ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string prefab, List<ZDO> zdos, ref int index)
apis.notes: The ONLY prefab-wide ZDO scan (no GetAllZDOsWithPrefab exists). Returns false while more work remains; ~400 non-empty sectors per call across a 262144-slot array. Sector 0 is scanned twice per full pass; portal ZDOs are added only on the final call.

apis.signature: public void ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects(Vector2s sector, SimulationDistance simulationDistance, List<ZDO> sectorObjects, List<ZDO> distantSectorObjects = null)
apis.notes: Anchored radius query. Pass `new SimulationDistance(area, 0, classic: true)` to get the full square ring instead of 1.0's disc filter, then post-filter by real distance — see Wonderland Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs FindNear.

apis.signature: public List<ZDO> ZDOMan.GetPortalList()  /  public Dictionary<ZoneSystem.SectorIndex, List<ZDO>> ZDOMan.GetPortals()
apis.notes: Every portal ZDO in the world, always resident in server memory (portals are stored in a separate ChunkPortal save file and never in m_objectsBySector). GetPortalList allocates a new list each call.

apis.signature: public ZDO ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3 position, int prefabHash)
apis.notes: Creates a server-owned ZDO at any coordinate and runs AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash) — so a portal-prefab hash lands it in m_portalObjects and marks the portal chunk dirty (hence saved). Does NOT set Persistent (default false) and does NOT SetPrefab on the ZDO body; call zdo.SetPrefab(hash) (:73808), zdo.SetRotation(rot) (:73781) and set Persistent (:73323) yourself for a non-portal target.

apis.signature: public static List<ZDOID> ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(ZDOExtraData.Type type, int hash)
apis.notes: Float/Long/Int/String only — errors on ByteArray/Vec3/Quat. `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, ZDOVars.s_location)` (:78501) enumerates every LocationProxy ZDO in the world. Cost is O(all fields of that type across all ZDOs); run once and cache.

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerId, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", string pinName, int pinType, Vector3 pos, bool showMap)
apis.location: registered client-side in Game.Start, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068; handler :100823; client Minimap.DiscoverLocation assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58394
apis.notes: Server->vanilla-client: adds a SAVED map pin with an arbitrary name, any Minimap.PinType (enum :56139), at any coordinate, plus a HUD message and optional map-open/look-at. Fully vanilla-respecting; no client mod. Suppressed client-side if a similar pin already exists.

apis.signature: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerId, "LocationIcons", ZPackage pkg)  // int count, then (Vector3 pos, string locationName)*
apis.location: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons :113581; client handler RPC_LocationIcons :113595; consumed by Minimap.UpdateLocationPins assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57551
apis.notes: Server owns the entire location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, refreshed client-side every 5 s. Also determines where a vanilla client respawns, via the "StartTemple" entry (Game.FindSpawnPoint, client :100796). Only names present in the client's Minimap.m_locationIcons asset list render.

apis.signature: public List<string> ZNetScene.GetPrefabNames()  /  public GameObject ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int hash)  /  GetPrefab(string name)
apis.notes: Runtime enumeration of every registered prefab on the dedicated server, and hash->prefab resolution for classifying a scanned ZDO (e.g. does this prefab carry an OfferingBowl/Trader/Vegvisir component).

apis.signature: public static bool Character.InInterior(Vector3 position)  // position.y > 3000f
apis.notes: Vanilla's own surface-vs-interior test. Location interiors sit at zoneCenter + 5000 y (Location.Awake :133512).

gotchas: The single biggest trap: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGroundHeight/GetSolidHeight/IsBlocked/FindFloor/GetGroundData/IsLava(Vector3)` all COMPILE and all RUN on a dedicated server — they just always return the no-hit fallback, because Game.FixedUpdate (:100463) pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) so no terrain collider exists near real coordinates. They will not throw and will not log. A `GetGroundHeight` that returns `p.y` unchanged looks like a valid answer.

There is no `ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab`. Only `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(string, List<ZDO>, ref int)` (:77442). Existing specs that say 'a plain spatial ZDO scan finds every altar' are describing an API that does not exist in 1.0.7.

`GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` re-scans `m_objectsBySector[0]` on its terminal call (:77445-77455), so any ZDO in sector index 0 — zone (-256,-256) AND the out-of-range fallback bucket that every coordinate beyond +/-16384 m falls into — is returned twice per full pass. Deduplicate.

Portal ZDOs are invisible to `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` until its FINAL call, because they live in `m_portalObjects`, not `m_objectsBySector` (AddIfPortal :77732 removes them from the sector array). An abandoned scan reports zero portals.

`ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752). Moving a portal ZDO with SetPosition leaves the m_portalObjects key stale: the new sector never sees it in FindObjects, and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) can never remove it. Create a fresh target ZDO instead of relocating one.

`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does not set `Persistent` and does not write the prefab into the ZDO body — `ZNetView.Awake` (:82612-82620) normally does both. A hand-made non-portal target ZDO with Persistent=false is never written to the save (GetSaveClonePerChunk filter :77572). Portal-prefab ZDOs escape this because the portal chunk is saved wholesale (:77621).

`BiomeSector.MinZone`/`MaxZone` are garbage: GenerateSectors computes both from `sector.Min`, and passes the y value into `new Vector3(x, y)` so `GetZone` reads z = 0 (:92577-92578). Compute zone bounds from Min/Max yourself.

`BiomeSector.Center` is the centroid of the region's PERIMETER cells (only cells adjacent to a different sector contribute, :92531-92535), not its area centroid. For a crescent or ring-shaped biome region the centre can land in a different biome entirely. Always re-check `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` at the chosen point.

A location's ZDOs (the altar bowl's parent piece, the trader, the runestone, the chests) do NOT exist until that zone has been ghost-generated, which only happens once a peer's reference position brings it inside `CreateGhostZones`' simulation distance (:113934). The LocationInstance exists from world creation; the objects inside it do not. Never assume a boss altar ZDO is findable on a fresh server.

`ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon` returns the FIRST dictionary match, not the nearest, and silently returns false for any location whose `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced` flags are unset — those flags are Unity Inspector data on the ZoneLocation.

`LocationInstance.m_position.y` is the PRE-placement `WorldGenerator.GetHeight`. `PlaceLocations` re-resolves it with a raycast at spawn time and forces y = 30 for `m_snapToWater` locations (:114963-114968). Expect a metre or two of error, and treat ocean locations as sitting at exactly 30.

`mask.a` from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x, z, out Color mask)` means lava only in the Ashlands (GetAshlandsHeight :152224). In Mistlands and Deep North the same channel carries an unrelated mask, and ZoneSystem's own location generator reads it as a 'vegetation' value (:114780-114792). Do not treat mask.a > 0.6 as lava outside the Ashlands — use `IsLavaPreHeightmap`, which biome-gates first.

`class Teleport` (dungeon doors) stores its destination in `public Teleport m_targetPoint` — a compiled Inspector reference with zero networking (:143322). Dungeon entrance/exit pairing is permanently invisible to a server-only mod.

`ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` cannot search ByteArray fields (:75403), so there is no global way to find every `DungeonGenerator` by its `s_roomData` payload. You must reach dungeon generators via prefab name or via their LocationProxy.

`Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` silently drops any LocationIcons entry whose name has no sprite in `Minimap.m_locationIcons` (GetLocationIcon returns null, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57594). Invented location names produce no pin and no error on a vanilla client.
Leviathans have a Rigidbody, are owner-simulated every FixedUpdate, and self-destruct on the `submerged` animation state (:132218-132229). They are not a stable portal target.

The `IsDiscovered` pass in GenerateSectors (:92605-92612) calls `ZoneSystem.instance.IsZoneLoaded` while iterating the broken MinZone/MaxZone range — it is effectively always false on a server. Do not read `BiomeSector.IsDiscovered`.
openQuestions: Which vanilla location prefab names correspond to each boss altar, the traders and the Bog Witch? These live in the LocationList Unity assets, not the C# decompile. In-game check: on a running dedicated server with the mod loaded, dump `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` — for each entry log `m_prefab.Name`, `m_biome`, `m_quantity`, `m_unique`, `m_iconAlways`, `m_iconPlaced`, `m_exteriorRadius` — and separately dump `GetLocationIcons()` on a generated world. The icon-flagged set is the landmark list; cross-reference names against `m_quantity == 1 && m_unique` for boss altars.

Does `SoftReference<GameObject>.Name` (used by FindClosestLocation/FindLocations and GetLocationIcon) resolve without loading the asset, and is it cheap? SoftReference lives in an assembly not present in this decompile set. In-game check: time 10,000 `FindClosestLocation` calls on a dedicated server and watch for asset-load log spam; if it is expensive, key the mod's index off `ZoneLocation.m_prefabName` (a plain string, :112892) instead.

Which prefabs are in `Game.m_portalPrefabs` (:99828, hashed into `PortalPrefabHash` in Game.Awake :100029)? Inspector data. This decides whether a mod-created target ZDO enters `m_portalObjects` (always resident, always saved, force-sendable) or the ordinary sector array. In-game check: log `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` against `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` hashes at server start.

Does a mod-created target ZDO actually have to be a portal-prefab ZDO for `TeleportWorld.Teleport` to use it? The method only reads GetPosition/GetRotation off the connection target (:143536-143541), but `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) prunes based on the target's tag and reciprocal connection, and only iterates GetPortalList. In-game check: create a non-portal-prefab ZDO at a target coordinate, SetConnection both ways, and see whether a vanilla client teleports and whether the link survives the 5 s coroutine.

Does the vanilla zone prefab's Heightmap GameObject carry a MeshCollider on the DEDICATED SERVER build (Heightmap.Awake does `GetComponent<MeshCollider>()` and RebuildCollisionMesh null-checks it, :128368/:128897)? Only matters if someone tries to salvage the sub-frame ghost-zone collider window. In-game check: log `Heightmap.GetAllHeightmaps()` count and each one's transform.position on a dedicated server — expect a handful, all near (1e6, *, 1e6).

How many location instances does a full vanilla 1.0.7 world actually hold, and how long does one `GetLocationIcons`/`FindClosestLocation` pass take on server hardware? This sets whether the mod can query live or must cache. In-game check: log `m_locationInstances.Count` and Stopwatch one full `FindLocations` pass at server boot.

Are `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel` lists retained in memory after `GenerateSectors`, and how large are they (2048*2048 = 4.2M cells distributed across biomes)? Memory cost matters before leaning on `GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel`. In-game check: log `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.Biomes[b].AllPoints.Count` per biome and the process RSS delta at server start.

Which location-icon names does the stock client's `Minimap.m_locationIcons` list actually contain (:56373)? This bounds what a server can render as a location pin without a client mod. In-game check: connect a vanilla client and log the names for which `Minimap.GetLocationIcon` returns non-null, or inspect the Minimap prefab in the shipped assets.
correctionsToExistingSpec: SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to nearest/named boss altar — the real altar is `OfferingBowl`, an always-present world-gen ZDO ... a plain spatial ZDO scan finds every altar with zero new bookkeeping.' — WRONG on three counts. (1) `OfferingBowl` is a plain MonoBehaviour with no ZDO of its own; it does `GetComponentInParent<ZNetView>()` in Start (:135652-135661), so the ZDO belongs to the altar piece. (2) That ZDO is NOT always present — it is created only when the zone is ghost- or full-generated, which needs a peer's reference position nearby (`ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones` :113934, `SpawnLocation` ghost path :115234). On a fresh server, no altar ZDO exists anywhere. (3) There is no 'plain spatial ZDO scan' for a prefab — only the resumable `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77442), and it needs the altar prefab NAME, which is Unity asset data. The correct, always-available, zero-player source is `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` / `FindClosestLocation(altarLocationName, ...)` (:113295, :115707) — world-gen data persisted in the save.

SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to any computed coordinate — `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash)` makes a real, persistent, correctly-owned ZDO.' — REFINE. `CreateNewZDO` (:76674/:76684) sets the owner to the session ID and calls `AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash)`, but it does NOT set `Persistent` (default false, :73323) and does NOT write the prefab into the ZDO body (`SetPrefab` :73808 is a separate call `ZNetView.Awake` makes, :82615-82620). A non-portal-prefab ZDO left at Persistent=false is dropped from the world save (`GetSaveClonePerChunk` persistence filter :77572). A portal-prefab ZDO escapes that because the whole `m_portalObjects` set is saved into the dedicated ChunkPortal file with no Persistent check (:77621-77636) — but only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set, which `AddIfPortal` (:77748) does.

SPEC (Group 1) implicitly: relocating a portal server-side. ADD A HARD WARNING. `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any portal-prefab ZDO (:73752-73757), so `SetPosition` (:73729) does not re-file it: `m_portalObjects` keeps the OLD sector key. Consequences: `FindObjects` for the new sector never includes it (:77376), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` looks it up by the NEW sector index and silently fails to remove it, leaking it in m_portalObjects forever (:76980-76986). Create a fresh ZDO at the destination rather than moving an existing portal.

SPEC (Central Constraint): 'ZoneSystem's local-zone creation is gated on the same permanently-pinned reference position.' — CORRECT, and now precisely citable: the pin is `Game.FixedUpdate` in the SERVER build setting `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` unconditionally every physics tick (:100463-100466); the client build's FixedUpdate has no equivalent line (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:100885). Worth stating the consequence explicitly in the spec: every `Physics.Raycast`-backed ZoneSystem helper (GetGroundHeight, GetSolidHeight, IsBlocked, FindFloor, GetGroundData, IsLava(Vector3)) silently returns the no-hit fallback on a dedicated server rather than failing loudly.

SPEC (Group 1): 'Portal to world spawn / start location, via `ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation)`' — CORRECT, with two caveats worth adding: on the server that method takes the `m_locationInstances` branch and requires the location's `m_iconAlways`/`m_iconPlaced` flag (:115424-115436), and it returns the FIRST dictionary match rather than the nearest. Also worth adding as a feature the spec does not list: the same `LocationIcons` payload is what a vanilla client uses to decide where to respawn (`Game.FindSpawnPoint` client-side :100796), so a server can relocate the world spawn for vanilla clients with no client mod.

SPEC MISSING ENTIRELY — two server→client map channels that are directly relevant to 'show a player where their portal now points', both vanilla-respecting and needing no client install: (a) `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse(pinName, pinType, pos, showMap)`, registered on both sides in Game.Start (:100068) and handled client-side by `Minimap.DiscoverLocation` → `AddPin(..., save: true, ...)` (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58394) — an arbitrary SAVED pin at an arbitrary coordinate with a HUD message and optional map-open; (b) the `LocationIcons` routed RPC (`ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons` :113581), which gives the server full authority over the location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, refreshed every 5 s (Minimap.UpdateLocationPins, assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57551).

SPEC MISSING — the biome-region target source. `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`, :92332, built by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` :79283) is a disk-cached 2048x2048 / 12 m grid of biome + height, plus flood-filled `BiomeSector` regions carrying world-space `Center`, bbox, height min/max/avg, neighbours and size, plus per-biome `AllPoints`/`AllPointsAboveSeaLevel`. It makes 'portal to a random/nearest Plains region, on land' and 'portal to a biome centroid' one-call operations with zero players and O(1) height lookups, and it is the cheapest server-side 'is this coordinate land' filter available.

SPEC MISSING — the server-side position-validation recipe, which the spec never states. On a dedicated server, validate a candidate (x,z) with: (1) `x*x + z*z <= WorldGenerator.waterEdgeSqr` (110250000, :151122) for in-world; (2) `float h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)` (:151944) and require `h > 30f + margin` for dry land (sea level ZoneSystem.c_WaterLevel = 30f, :113228); (3) `!ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(new Vector3(x, h, z))` (:115637) for the Ashlands; (4) `WorldGenerator.instance.GetTerrainDelta(p, r, out delta, out _)` (:152364) with delta <= ~2 for flatness, or `GetAverageNormal` (:151905) for slope; (5) reject `y > 3000f` per `Character.InInterior` (:4538); (6) reject candidates inside any `LocationInstance`'s `m_location.m_exteriorRadius` (:112930) using the location registry; (7) `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (Wonderland Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs, over `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` :77142) to reject spots occupied by pieces or wards. Steps 2-4 are blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening — always add >= 1 m clearance.

research.topic: Existing-codebase assets for TortalPortal Lite: Wonderland server-only engine inventory, full TortalPortal feature classification, PortalLock post-mortem, loader stack
research.summary: Wonderland is a complete, production server-only mod framework that TortalPortal Lite should fork wholesale rather than re-derive: a Heartbeat + SubsystemRegistry tick/lifecycle, a hot-reloading ServerSync'd config with Bind helpers, and ten Core/Data utilities that already solve every server-only primitive a portal mod needs — sector-bounded and time-budgeted ZDO scanning (ZdoSpatialQuery), the per-peer character-ZDO view that replaces the always-empty Player.GetAllPlayers() (ConnectedCharacters), server->vanilla-client toast messages (PlayerNotify), the only reliable vanilla-client->server control channel (EmoteSignals), a routed-RPC status-effect grant (StatusEffectRpc), and a compat shim for the 1.0 sector API (GameShape). Three Wonderland engines are direct portal analogues: WaterBuoyancyEngine's ZDO ownership-claim / SetOwner-block / ForceSendZDO pattern, WorldRatesEngine's GlobalKeyAdd+SendGlobalKeys write path (the mechanism for NoPortals/TeleportAll/NoBossPortals), and SpawnGovernor's ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO+ZDO.Deserialize pair — the ONLY server-side hook that sees a client-placed object appear, which is what a server-enforced portal cap must be built on. Two under-documented capabilities found in Wonderland that the Lite spec does not currently mention: FirstSpawnGrant pushes a real, persistent map pin to a 100%-vanilla client via the routed RPC "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", and VacuumEngine plays vanilla VFX/SFX on vanilla clients via the routed RPC "SpawnObject" — partial server-side replacements for TortalPortal's PortalMapPins and runic-gateway VFX. Of full TortalPortal's ~22 features, 4 are fully replicable server-side, 8 partially (degraded), and 10 are impossible without a client. PortalLock (PAUSED) attempted a server-side portal cap by patching Player.PlacePiece and ZNetScene.Instantiate — both dead on a dedicated server — which is exactly the trap Wonderland's SpawnGovernor documents and avoids.

facts.claim: Wonderland's lifecycle is: BepInEx Awake -> GameShape.Detect() -> ConfigSync built -> WonderlandConfig.Bind -> RegisterSubsystems -> Subsystems.InitializeAll(config, configSync, harmony) -> a Harmony postfix on ZNetScene.Awake drives OnWorldReady; Update() calls PollConfigFile(), Heartbeat.OnUpdate(dt), Subsystems.OnUpdate(). A Lite mod should copy this shape verbatim.
facts.implication: Lite needs no new lifecycle design; copy Plugin.cs, Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs, Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs, Core/Heartbeat.cs and rename. OnWorldReady is the only safe point for ZNetScene/ObjectDB prefab reads.

facts.claim: IWonderlandSubsystem is a 4-method contract (Initialize/OnWorldReady/OnUpdate/Shutdown) plus Name/IsEnabled; SubsystemRegistry wraps every call in try/catch so one failing subsystem cannot take the mod down, and SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch(harmony, patchType) applies a Harmony patch set with a logged warning instead of an exception on failure.
facts.implication: Lite subsystems (PortalNetwork, PortalGovernor, PortalNotify) drop straight into this registry. SafePatch is the required wrapper for every portal-related Harmony patch.

facts.claim: ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(worldPos, radiusMeters, reuseBuffer) returns every ZDO within a real metre radius by calling ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects with SimulationDistance(area, 0, classic:true) and post-filtering by squared distance; it never uses Physics.OverlapSphere because no collider exists server-side away from the pinned reference position.
facts.implication: This is the ready-made 'find portals / altars / beds / ships near point X' primitive for every Lite destination-resolution feature (portal-to-nearest-altar, portal-to-bed, portal-to-ship). Reuse, do not rewrite.

facts.claim: ZdoSpatialQuery has two unanchored whole-map scanners: PrefabSetScanner round-robins ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative across a set of prefab NAMES one chunk per Advance(); PrefabSetSweeper walks ZDOMan.m_objectsBySector directly against a HashSet of prefab HASHES with an explicit sectorBudget, returning true when a full map pass completes. The header records that the name-based scanner re-walks all 512*512=262144 sector slots per prefab and ran to hours for ~800 prefabs, which is why the hash-set sweeper exists.
facts.citation: ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetScanner, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:92; ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper.Advance, same file :135 and :153
facts.implication: For portals specifically NEITHER is needed: ZDOMan.GetPortalList() already returns every portal ZDO in the world for free. Use the sweepers only if Lite needs to scan a non-portal prefab family (OfferingBowl altars, Bed, Ship).

facts.claim: ConnectedCharacters.All() returns (ZNetPeer, character ZDO) pairs for every ready peer via ZDOMan.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID), and the struct exposes PlayerId (ZDOVars.s_playerID - the STABLE identity to persist, not peer.m_uid and not the ZDOID), Name (ZDOVars.s_playerName with peer.m_playerName fallback) and Position. Its header records that Player.GetAllPlayers() is always empty on a dedicated server and that six Wonderland subsystems silently did nothing in their first version because of it.
facts.implication: Every Lite per-player feature (per-player portal cap, portal-use logging, named warps, 'who owns this gate') must go through this, keyed on s_playerID. It is exactly what TortalPortal's own server-side PlayerNames.HarvestPeers re-implements independently.

facts.claim: PlayerNotify.Toast(who, message, center) sends a server->client message to a 100%-vanilla client by invoking the routed RPC "Message" on the player's own character ZDO with (int type, string msg, int amount); the client's Player.RPC_Message hands it to MessageHud.ShowMessage which Localizes it first, so "$piece_portal" arrives translated.
facts.implication: This is Lite's entire player-facing text channel: 'Portal locked', 'Destination rotated to X', 'Portal cap reached (6)'. It replaces TortalPortal's MessageHudPatch/centre messages with zero client install, and it is how a cap refusal or a PIN failure gets communicated.

facts.claim: EmoteSignals is the only reliable vanilla-client->server control channel. It polls every connected character's ZDOVars.s_emoteID counter at 0.25s and dispatches the new ZDOVars.s_emote string to registered handlers. Its header documents why chat is NOT usable: a stock client runs an unknown slash command locally and prints 'not a recognized command', and plain chat is sent as one routed RPC per OTHER listed player, so a player alone on the server produces no chat traffic at all.
facts.implication: Any Lite player-triggered portal action (cycle this gate's destination, lock/unlock, request the portal list as toasts) must be emote-driven, not chat-driven. CacheClaimControl.cs is the worked example of a full emote-command subsystem in ~45 lines.

facts.claim: CacheClaimControl is a complete 47-line worked example of an emote command: Initialize() registers a handler with EmoteSignals, the handler matches the configured emote with EmoteSignals.Is(...fallback), acts on the nearest target within ControlRange, and answers with PlayerNotify.Toast. SupplySwitch is the same pattern plus per-object persisted state.
facts.implication: Copy CacheClaimControl as the skeleton for a Lite 'portal emote command' subsystem. Copy SupplySwitch for the per-portal state file (see next fact).

facts.claim: SupplySwitch stores per-object state in a mod-side file keyed by ZDOID (BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath/Wonderland.SupplyOff.<world>.dat, write-temp-then-move), explicitly NOT on the target's own ZDO, because the owning client rewrites that ZDO every second and a server write there races the owner. Stale entries are pruned on every save via ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id) == null.
facts.implication: Directly reusable for Lite's per-portal metadata (PIN, admin-reserved flag, managed-network membership, rotation index). CAUTION: TortalPortal's own Favorites.cs documents that ZDOMan renumbers every ZDO on world load (ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)), so a ZDOID-keyed file does NOT survive a world reload — key portal state by rounded POSITION instead, exactly as Favorites.cs switched to.

facts.claim: StatusEffectRpc.Grant(who, nameHash) grants any vanilla status effect to a connected player by invoking the routed RPC "RPC_AddStatusEffect" on the character ZDO with (nameHash, resetTime:true, 0, 0f, -1). The receiving client resolves nameHash only against its own already-loaded ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects, so only assets every vanilla client already ships can be granted.
facts.implication: Usable for portal-adjacent flavour (a 'Rested'/'Warm' grant on arrival, a debuff during a portal blackout). Note there is NO RemoveStatusEffect RPC anywhere in the assembly, so a granted effect can only be starved of re-pings, never cancelled.

facts.claim: BuffRosterEngine is the reference per-player, per-slot re-ping loop: it resolves StatusEffect assets by asset name via StatusEffectRegistry, computes RepingInterval as clamp(ttl*0.4, 0.2, ttl-0.2) (or 120s for a permanent effect), and decrements per-slot-per-player cooldowns by the real frame dt from OnUpdate rather than a batched sweep interval.

facts.claim: WaterBuoyancyEngine is the complete ZDO ownership-claim pattern: claim with zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()), mutate, bump zdo.DataRevision += 4096, then ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid); plus a Harmony PREFIX on ZDO.SetOwner that returns false to BLOCK a passive ownership handover away from the server, and a PREFIX on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC that watches for the "RPC_RequestOwn" method hash to grant a 3-second ownership window to a requesting peer.

The RoutedRpcHandlerPatch is also the generic 'intercept any routed RPC by method hash on the server' hook — that is how a Lite mod would see RPC_SetTag traffic.

facts.claim: WorldRatesEngine writes world modifier keys with ZoneSystem.instance.GlobalKeyAdd("key value", true) followed by ZoneSystem.instance.SendGlobalKeys(0L) (peer 0 = broadcast), guarding with a read-back check against both m_globalKeys.Contains(key) and GetGlobalKey(...). WorldRatesPatches re-asserts the keys from postfixes on ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys and ZoneSystem.Start and a prefix on SendGlobalKeys (which also fires per newly-joining peer).
facts.implication: This is the ready-made write path for every Group-2 Lite toggle in TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md: GlobalKeys.NoPortals, NoBossPortals, TeleportAll, DungeonBuild. Copy WorldRatesEngine + WorldRatesPatches and swap the key names; the three-hook re-assert pattern is what makes a runtime toggle survive a restart and reach late joiners.

facts.claim: SpawnGovernor is the ONLY server-side hook in the codebase that sees a client-placed object appear: a postfix on the private ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int) (prefabHash==0 identifies the network-receive path) only REMEMBERS the ZDOID, and a postfix on ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage) — the first moment the prefab hash is actually known — does the check and, if rejected, does zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) then ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo). The header records that a CreateNewZDO-only postfix always sees GetPrefab()==0 and can never act (the first version had exactly that bug).

facts.claim: TortalPortal enforces its portal cap CLIENT-side, in a prefix on Player.TryPlacePiece, counting via CountPlayerPortals(playerID) which unions the ServerSync index against locally-held ZDOs. facts.implication: Fourteen of the mod's ~20 behaviour files are structurally unreachable on a dedicated server. This is the concrete file-level basis for the 'what Lite gives up' table.

facts.claim: PortalLock (PAUSED) attempted a server-side per-player portal cap by reflectively patching every Player method matching *place*piece* with a prefix that early-returns unless ZNet.instance.IsServer(), and by postfixing ZNetScene.Instantiate and ZNetScene.Destroy to register/unregister portals in a YAML index. It identified the player via player.GetPlayerID() called on a Player instance.
facts.implication: Every hook it chose is dead on a dedicated server: Player.PlacePiece/TryPlacePiece require a Player instance the server never has, and ZNetScene.Instantiate/Destroy never run for a client-placed piece (the client instantiates and the ZDO arrives over the wire). Combining an IsServer() guard with a Player-instance hook means the plugin as written could never fire once. Concrete precedent for why Lite must use the SpawnGovernor ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO+ZDO.Deserialize pair.

facts.claim: PortalLock also keyed its index by zdo.m_uid.ToString() persisted to YAML, wrote its own "PL_owner" string key onto the portal ZDO, detected portals by a case-insensitive name substring 'portal' or a GetComponent("Portal") that does not match vanilla's component name (TeleportWorld), and used Player.IsAdmin() by reflection for the admin bypass. Its README concedes it exposes no console commands, only Commands.Reload()/DumpSummary() to be invoked 'from a runtime console that supports calling static methods'.
facts.citation: PortalLock.PlacementPatches.Postfix_Instantiate, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:114-161 (admin check by reflection at :28; component test at :46); /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/README.md
facts.implication: Four further traps Lite must not repeat: (1) a persisted ZDOID key is meaningless across a world reload; (2) the server-side admin check is ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(hostName)/ListContainsId(m_adminList, host), not Player.IsAdmin(); (3) a custom "PL_owner" key is redundant since vanilla writes ZDOVars.s_creator on every player-placed piece; (4) portal detection should use ZDOMan's own portal registry (Game.PortalPrefabHash-backed), not a name substring.

facts.claim: PortalLock's dependency set (libs/) is the 0.x-era CLIENT stack — assembly_valheim.dll, Jotunn.dll, ServerSync.dll, YamlDotNet.dll, 0Harmony.dll, BepInEx.dll and ~25 UnityEngine modules — and it targets net472 with OutputPath pointed directly at ..\..\..\BepInEx\plugins\PortalLock\. It carries a full decompiled_backup/assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs of its own.
facts.implication: Nothing in PortalLock is reusable as code. Its value to Lite is entirely as a negative result: it names the four hooks that do not work and the identity/persistence choices that do not survive. Do not resurrect the project; port the requirement, not the implementation.

facts.claim: Loader stack: BepInEx 5.4.23.5 (libs-Tools/BepInEx.dll), HarmonyX 2.9.0 (libs-Tools/0Harmony.dll), Thunderstore/Hexium dependency string "denikson-BepInExPack_Valheim-5.4.2350" in both manifests. Wonderland targets net472, LangVersion 12.0, Nullable enable, NoWarn CS8600;CS8602;CS8603;CS8604;CS8618;CS8625, AllowUnsafeBlocks, Deterministic; TortalPortal targets net48, LangVersion latest, NoWarn CS8632;CS0618. Wonderland references only 0Harmony, BepInEx, assembly_valheim (publicized), assembly_utils, UnityEngine, UnityEngine.CoreModule, Unity.TextMeshPro, UnityEngine.UI, Splatform and System.Net.Http — the TMP/UI pair only because vendored ServerSync.cs touches them.

facts.claim: Wonderland's csproj points at libs-Tools/1.0/server/* — the Valheim 1.0.7 DEDICATED SERVER assemblies (Steam app 896660, build 25185644, network version 39, Linux install) — and records that client and server assemblies are not interchangeable (different sizes and md5s) and that the libs-Tools ROOT copies are the CLIENT set. TortalPortal references the root (client) copies. Both do a PostBuild MakeDir+Copy of the DLL into HexiumDist/plugins.

facts.claim: TortalPortal's MIGRATE-1.0.md records the mod was re-verified unmodified against Valheim 1.0.12 (build 25253764/25253791, network version 40): 37 types / 55 method bodies changed, the only removed member is PlayerProfile.s_bypassCheatChecks (now a property), no signature/interface/constructor changed, and all 48 Harmony targets still resolve. It also notes 1.0.12 changed ZNet.ListContainsId from flag = list.Contains(filtered) to flag |= ..., so admins listed under either ID form now pass.
facts.implication: The 1.0.7 decompile is a valid authority through 1.0.12 for everything Lite touches. The ListContainsId change makes the ScatterCommand-style adminlist gate more permissive, not less.

facts.claim: Wonderland's -NextSteps.md section 1 explicitly relocated the portal work out of Wonderland to TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md on 2026-09-11, and its RESOLVED v0.6.4 entry records that every portal use used to generate a [SECURITY:PositionWatch] flag because a 3s position sample spans the map during transit, producing ~110 m/s against a 40 m/s ceiling.
facts.implication: Wonderland has already paid for the portal-transit detector in production; Lite inherits a tested, false-positive-tuned heuristic rather than a fresh one, and knows its real-world measured signal (~110 m/s apparent speed over a 3s window).

facts.claim: Wonderland's -NextSteps.md section 3.4 is a complete GlobalKeys round-trip reference: ZoneSystem holds m_globalKeys (HashSet<string>) and m_globalKeysValues, GlobalKeyAdd parses "key value" and synchronously calls Game.UpdateWorldRates, SendGlobalKeys(long peer) broadcasts the full list via ZRoutedRpc "GlobalKeys" (peer=0L = everyone), and the client's RPC_GlobalKeys clears and re-adds every key — a full resync that re-runs Game.UpdateWorldRates independently on the client. RPC registration happens in ZoneSystem.Start(), not Awake().
facts.implication: Because this is a broadcast-and-reparse channel rather than a per-tick ZDO write, none of the Group-2 Lite toggles are subject to the client-ownership/stomp trap. The same section records that GlobalKeys.Preset is cosmetic and never read by Game.UpdateWorldRates.

facts.claim: Neither Wonderland nor TortalPortal registers a slash/console command a dedicated server can usefully receive from a player: TortalPortal's tortal_scatter/tortal_scatterclear are Terminal.ConsoleCommand(isCheat:true, isNetwork:false, onlyServer:false) run on the caller's own machine, with the server half reached only by an explicitly authored routed RPC (TortalPortal_ScatterClear); tortal_pinreload is the same shape.
facts.citation: ScatterCommand.Terminal_InitTerminal_Postfix, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/ScatterCommand.cs:110-118; routed clear RPC registration :53-57; TortalPinLibrary Terminal postfix, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/TortalPinLibrary.cs:727
facts.implication: Confirms EmoteSignals is the only player->server channel for Lite. A console command in Lite is usable ONLY from the dedicated server's own stdin, never from a vanilla player's console.

facts.claim: TortalPortal's SectorSubscription is a genuinely server-side mechanism buried in a client feature: a client routed-RPC ("TortalPortal_AnchorSectors") asks the server to stream the sectors around an arbitrary point, and a POSTFIX on the private ZDOMan.CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer peer, List<ZDO> toSync) appends those sectors to that peer's normal sync packet for a renewal-driven 15s window, with an overlap guard against the peer's own negotiated SimulationDistance and per-tick ghost zone generation for never-generated zones.
facts.implication: The CreateSyncList postfix is the general 'make the server send a client ZDOs it would not otherwise see' lever — the only way Lite could ever get portal data in front of a client that is not standing next to a portal. It is useless to a ZERO-CLIENT Lite (vanilla clients never send the request RPC and would do nothing with the ZDOs), but it is the mechanism to remember if Lite ever gains an optional companion client.

facts.claim: Favorites.cs is client-local by design (a plain text file under BepInEx config, per world, keyed by rounded position) and never crosses the wire; its header states 'which portals somebody likes is nobody else's business'.
facts.implication: Favorites is the clearest 'impossible in Lite' feature: there is no vanilla client-side store the server can write to, and no UI to star from. Any server-side substitute would be a per-player global-key list driving map pins, which is a different feature.

facts.claim: Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep (MaxHealthBroadcastsPerSweep) because the first sweep over a long-running world turned up thousands of damaged pieces at once and each would have become a routed packet to every peer in the same frame; a clipped piece is still fixed in the ZDO and just looks stale until that zone next loads client-side.
facts.implication: Any Lite sweep that touches many portals in one pass (a mass re-tag, a network rebuild, a lockdown that nulls every connection) needs the same per-sweep broadcast budget or it will spike every connected peer.
