apis.notes: For DropItem the template ItemData must have m_dropPrefab assigned by hand (ItemDrop.Awake never runs for a prefab). For Instantiate, the prefab's own ZNetView.Awake sets persistence/object type/prefab hash correctly — a hand-built ZDO that gets any of those wrong vanishes on world reload.

gotchas: RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are added with save:true — they land permanently in the player's own saved pin list and the server has NO removal RPC. A Lite 'portal map pins' feature cannot un-pin a demolished portal, and re-pushing after a rename creates a SECOND pin (HaveSimilarPin matches on name AND type AND position-within-1m). Treat it as a one-shot discovery push, not a live-synced pin set like TortalPortal's PortalMapPins, which adds/removes client-side pins every 2s (PortalMapPins.Rebuild, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalMapPins.cs:89).

ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load — ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) — so any Lite state file keyed by ZDOID silently points at nothing after a restart. TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit exactly this (stars vanished between sessions, Favorites.cs:109-124) and switched to a rounded-position key; Wonderland's SupplySwitch is still ZDOID-keyed and prunes dead ids on save, which masks the same bug as 'the station forgot'. Key Lite portal state by position, or by world global key.

PortalLock's failure mode is the canonical trap: patching Player.PlacePiece / Player.TryPlacePiece / ZNetScene.Instantiate with an `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return true;` guard produces code that can never execute. The server has no Player instance and never instantiates a client-placed piece. Use the ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO + ZDO.Deserialize pair instead.

A Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO ALONE always sees GetPrefab()==0 on the network-receive path — the prefab hash only arrives in the subsequent ZDO.Deserialize. SpawnGovernor's header records this as a shipped bug in its own first version (SpawnGovernor.cs:16-24).

ServerSync's CustomSyncedValue<string> — TortalPortal's entire portal-index delivery mechanism — is invisible to a vanilla client (no ConfigSync RPC is registered there). Anything Lite wants a player to SEE must go through PlayerNotify toasts, RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins, or SpawnObject effects. There is no fourth channel.

A stock client never sends a slash command to the server (Chat.InputText runs it locally and prints 'not a recognized command') and plain chat is routed only to OTHER listed players, so a lone player generates zero chat traffic. Emotes (ZDOVars.s_emoteID / s_emote on the character ZDO) are the only reliable player->server signal. Documented at length in EmoteSignals.cs:8-27, and independently confirmed by CacheClaimControl's header, which records replacing a '/cache claim' chat hook that could never run.

ObjectDB.instance is frequently still null at the ZNetScene.Awake postfix this codebase treats as 'world ready' — live-confirmed 2026-09-11. BuffRosterEngine retries once per tick from OnUpdate until it resolves (BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96); WaterBuoyancyEngine's ObjectDB read at the same hook silently no-ops and is masked only because its ZNetScene prefab loop finds everything anyway. Any Lite OnWorldReady code touching ObjectDB must retry.

On mono, a compile-time binding to a member the loaded assembly lacks throws at JIT of the CALLING method — a try/catch inside that method does not save it. Version-sensitive calls must live in their own method only invoked after a reflection-based detection confirms the shape (GameShape.cs:29-48). Separately, Type.GetMethod's single-result overload throws AmbiguousMatchException when a compatibility patcher injects a same-name/same-parameter overload differing only in return type — enumerate with GetMethods() and filter by hand.

ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID and RPC_SetTag's authorId are raw, unverified client self-reports; nothing cross-checks them against the ZNetPeer that owns the connection the packet arrived on. Any Lite feature trusting a player identity carried in a portal-adjacent RPC needs its own peer cross-check first. TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md Group 4 flags this; the Wonderland codebase contains no hardening for it yet.

Wonderland's ZdoSetOwnerPatch is an unconditional prefix on ZDO.SetOwner — a global hot path touched by ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS on every peer move. If Lite forks it for portals, the predicate must fail fast on prefab hash before anything else, and must never block uid==0 or uid==ZDOMan.GetSessionID().

TortalPortal's cap is CLIENT-enforced (Player.TryPlacePiece prefix) and its own LogRefusal comment records the effective cap 'wandered between values nobody had deliberately set' before a locking config entry existed. Do not port that design into Lite — the SpawnGovernor destroy-on-arrival cap is both server-authoritative and simpler.

StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep because a first pass over a long-running world turned up thousands of dirty ZDOs, each becoming a packet to every peer in one frame. Any Lite sweep touching many portals at once (mass re-tag, network rebuild, a lockdown nulling every connection) needs the same per-sweep broadcast budget.

TortalPortal's SnapGuard and TraderRepair depend on Heightmap.FindHeightmap / a loaded collider, so they are client-only in practice on a dedicated server despite patching types the server also loads. 'The server loads this type' does not mean 'the patch fires'.

Wonderland's SecuritySubsystem.Initialize carries a written post-mortem of a patch that shipped dead: a DamagePlausibility postfix on Character.RPC_Damage could never run server-side, because a damage RPC is routed to the victim's OWNING peer (ZRoutedRpc only handles a routed RPC locally when it is the target or the target is Everybody), and even a locally-handled ZDO RPC needs a live instance via ZNetScene.FindInstance, which the server never has away from its pinned reference position. The same two conditions kill any Lite plan to intercept a per-portal, per-player RPC.

PortalLock detected portals by a case-insensitive 'portal' substring on the GameObject name plus GetComponent("Portal") — vanilla's component is TeleportWorld, so that component test never matched anything. Portal identity should come from ZDOMan's own registry (Game.PortalPrefabHash-backed GetPortalList/GetPortals), which also picks up modded portal pieces for free.
openQuestions: Does RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse actually render on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client identically to Steam? Wonderland ships it behind StarterBoatMapPin (default on) but -NextSteps.md carries no live-test note for it, unlike the Moder/RequireBoat entries which are explicitly dated 2026-09-11. IN-GAME CHECK: connect a vanilla client, have the server invoke the RPC at a known coordinate, confirm the pin appears, log out and back in to confirm save:true really persisted, then re-send the identical payload and confirm HaveSimilarPin suppresses a duplicate.

Does ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject accept an arbitrary effect prefab hash from a routed RPC on a 1.0.7 vanilla client with no server-side instance present? VacuumEngine only exercises vfx_fermenter_add / sfx_fermenter_add. IN-GAME CHECK: server-invoke "SpawnObject" with a portal-flavoured vanilla effect hash at a portal position and confirm a vanilla client plays it; also confirm whether the prefab must exist in ZNetScene.m_prefabs on the SERVER for the hash to be meaningful, or only on the client.

Can the server destroy a client-created portal ZDO inside ZDO.Deserialize's own postfix without a client-side desync? The placing client already has a live GameObject. SpawnGovernor does exactly this for creatures and is shipped, but a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may behave differently. IN-GAME CHECK: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost portal disappears cleanly, leaves an orphaned local instance until the zone reloads, or refunds/consumes the build materials.

Whether a portal ZDO whose connection the server force-writes to ZDOID.None is reliably re-broadcast to a nearby client that currently OWNS that ZDO, or whether the owning client's next push overwrites the server's write. WaterBuoyancyEngine solves the analogous problem with a SetOwner block plus ForceSendZDO; whether portals need the same is untested. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a portal, have the server null its connection, and watch whether the gate reads as disconnected and stays that way for 60s.

Whether a client already standing at a portal picks up a server-side ZDOVars.s_tag change without a zone reload. TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal runs on a 0.5s InvokeRepeating so the connection state probably refreshes, but the hover text goes through a separate GetTagInfo read. IN-GAME CHECK: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and see whether the hover text and the connected/unconnected state both update without walking away.

Whether ZDOVars.s_creator is reliably populated on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7. TortalPortal's PortalExport and PortalRegistry both treat creator==0 as 'admin-spawned or older than the field', which implies usually non-zero but not always — and a server-enforced per-player cap is only as good as this field. IN-GAME CHECK: place a portal on a vanilla client, dump s_creator server-side, and confirm it equals the same value that lands in ZDOVars.s_playerID on that player's character ZDO.

Whether ZNetScene.m_prefabs on the DEDICATED SERVER build contains the portal prefabs with usable components (Wonderland's ContainerRegistry and StructureUpkeep both enumerate ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs server-side and find real components, so this is very likely yes, but Lite depends on it for any GetComponent<TeleportWorld>() prefab test). IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood")?.GetComponent<TeleportWorld>() at OnWorldReady on the dedicated server and confirm non-null, along with m_activationRange / m_exitDistance / m_allowAllItems values.
correctionsToExistingSpec: TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 61 says 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' is 'admin/Discord-facing only, not an in-game player UI'. Too strong. Two in-game, zero-client-install channels exist and are already shipped in Wonderland: (a) PlayerNotify.Toast pushes arbitrary localized text to a vanilla player's MessageHud (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15), so an emote can make the server toast a paged portal list; (b) ZRoutedRpc "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse" pushes a REAL map pin with a chosen name and Minimap.PinType to a vanilla client (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263, registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068, client body assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:101265). Lite can therefore give a vanilla player named portal markers on their own map — a genuine partial replication of PortalMapPins. Unavoidable caveat: the pin is save:true and there is no removal RPC.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md has no entry for server-side portal VFX. Wonderland's VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect (Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162) shows the server can play any vanilla effect prefab on vanilla clients by broadcasting the native "SpawnObject" routed RPC per nearby peer. This does not replicate the procedural runic gateway, but it makes 'a visible/audible cue when a hub rotates, a gate is locked, or a lockdown starts' feasible. Add as [Feasible, small].

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 55 proposes detecting 'a player's live-attached ship' via the ZSyncTransform / ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform link and flags it as needing an in-game Inspector check (whether Player's prefab has m_characterParentSync enabled). Wonderland already ships a BETTER, decompile-confirmed, live-tested signal needing no Inspector data: ShipAttachment.IsSteeringShip reads ZDOVars.s_user (hash of "user") off the Ship's own ZDO, written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl and zeroed by RPC_ReleaseControl (Core/Data/ShipAttachment.cs:12-19, :31). It answers 'is actively steering' rather than 'is standing on', which is the sharper question. Downgrade line 55's caveat and line 56's cruder proximity fallback accordingly.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md has no per-player portal cap entry at all, yet it is the single most valuable server-only portal feature and the one thing Lite would do BETTER than full TortalPortal (whose cap is client-enforced in a Player.TryPlacePiece prefix, PlacementPatch.cs:89, and whose own log comment records the effective cap wandering because any client's config could override it). Mechanism: Wonderland's SpawnGovernor ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO + ZDO.Deserialize pair (SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58), ZDOMan.GetPortalList() counted by ZDOVars.s_creator, destroy-over-limit plus a PlayerNotify.Toast refusal. Add as [Feasible, medium].

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 62 lists 'Proactive server ownership claim on placement' as [Feasible, medium] citing WaterBuoyancyEngine generically. The concrete three-part recipe is worth recording: zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) + zdo.DataRevision += 4096 + ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid) to push; a prefix on ZDO.SetOwner returning false to stop ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS handing the portal back to a nearby client; and a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC keyed on "RPC_RequestOwn".GetStableHashCode() to grant a temporary window when a client legitimately needs ownership (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:158-164, :251, :301, :315).

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md line 76 says self-service named warps should use 'an emote or item-interaction trigger, not a slash command'. Correct, but it understates what exists: EmoteSignals (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs) is a complete shipped emote-command bus with per-character counter tracking, disabled-state reseeding and departed-peer pruning, and CacheClaimControl.cs:16 is a 47-line worked example of a full emote command with nearest-target search, a range config and a toast reply. The effort estimate for any emote-triggered Lite feature should drop accordingly.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md says nothing about where per-portal mod-side state should live, and two shipped precedents conflict. SupplySwitch persists per-object state to a ZDOID-keyed file (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165), while TortalPortal's Favorites.cs documents that ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) on every world load and switched to a rounded-position key for exactly that reason (Favorites.cs:109-124). Lite must key portal state by position or by world global key, never by bare ZDOID. Add this as an explicit design constraint.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md describes Wonderland only as a source of patterns. It is in fact a directly forkable chassis: Plugin.cs (lifecycle + 5s config hot-reload), Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs, Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs (incl. SafePatch), Core/Heartbeat.cs, Core/WonderlandDebug.cs, Core/SafeMath.cs, Core/WonderlandConfig.cs's Bind helper block, Core/Compat/GameShape.cs, Shared/ServerSync.cs, six of the ten Core/Data utilities, AuditLog.cs and the whole DiscordNotify subsystem are portal-agnostic and transfer with a namespace rename — roughly 1,400 lines of already-live infrastructure Lite does not need to write. It should also copy Wonderland.csproj (net472, libs-Tools/1.0/server assemblies), NOT TortalPortal.csproj (net48, client assemblies).

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md's provenance note says it came from a 13-agent audit of the decompiles. It should also record that PortalLock (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/) is a prior, abandoned attempt at exactly the Group-1 portal-cap feature, and that its entire hook set (Player.*PlacePiece*, ZNetScene.Instantiate, ZNetScene.Destroy, Player.IsAdmin, ZDOID-keyed YAML, name-substring portal detection) is dead on a dedicated server. That negative result belongs in the Ruled Out section as the empirical counterpart to the Central Constraint.

TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md's 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' entry does not mention that the whole-world portal enumeration AND its JSON export already exist and already run server-only in the full mod: PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:195) and PortalExport (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32, :75, writing barrkbot_portals.json atomically with per-creator counts, at_cap/over_cap flags and an online set). Effort for that item is near zero — it is a file copy, not a build.

research.topic: player-input-surfaces: what a dedicated Valheim 1.0.7 server can observe a vanilla client doing, and what it can show back, with zero client mod
research.summary: The single decisive finding is that **the vanilla map ping is a free, always-delivered, coordinate-bearing player→server channel**: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick`/`OnMapDblClick` call `Chat.SendPing`, which invokes the routed RPC `"ChatMessage"` at `targetPeerID = 0` (Everybody) with **no permission check and no player-count dependency**, so the dedicated server receives the exact world Vector3 plus the sender's peer id and PlatformUserID every single time. That is a complete destination-selection UI on a stock client: open map → middle-click a spot → server picks the nearest portal. Ordinary chat text is *not* equivalent — `Chat.SendText`/`Talker.Say` target each *other* listed player individually, so with one player online nothing goes on the wire at all, and with 2+ players the packets only pass through the server as **relay traffic** (visible via a Harmony hook on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC`/`RouteRPC`, never via a registered handler). The second-tier input channels are all ZDO-poll based and rock solid: emotes (`s_emote`/`s_emoteID`), equipped items (`VisEquipment` writes `s_rightItem`/`s_leftItem`/`s_helmetItem`… into the character ZDO), item stands (`s_item` = prefab hash), sign text (`s_text`), portal tags (`s_tag`, max 10 chars from the client UI), chest contents (`s_items` blob), position/look-direction (`s_lookTarget`), and every piece built or destroyed (hook `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` + `ZDO.Deserialize`, read `s_creator`). Output back to a vanilla client is richer than expected: `"ShowMessage"` (MessageHud TopLeft/Center), the per-character `"Message"` RPC, `"RPC_DamageText"` (floating world text at any position, any string), `"RPC_TeleportPlayer"` **and** `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` (two independent, completely ungated server→client teleports), `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (a **named, saved map pin** at any position), a fabricated `"ChatMessage"` of type Shout or Ping (chat line + in-world text + a labelled animated map pin), `"LocationIcons"` (icon-only overlay), status effects, `"SpawnObject"` for VFX prefabs, and portal-tag/sign-text rewriting as persistent in-world text. The two hard walls: the server can never see a player's inventory (never networked — so no ore check is reproducible), and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` strips server ZDO ownership near any player every 2s.

facts.claim: The vanilla map ping is a broadcast routed RPC with NO permission gate and NO player-count dependency: Chat.SendPing sends "ChatMessage" to targetPeerID 0 (ZRoutedRpc.Everybody) carrying the clicked world position (x/z from the map click, y forced to the player's own y), type 3 (Talker.Type.Ping), the sender's UserInfo, and empty text.
facts.implication: THE destination-selection surface. A dedicated server receives an arbitrary player-chosen world coordinate from a 100% vanilla client, always, even with a single player online. Middle-click the map = 'send me here'.

facts.claim: A vanilla player triggers SendPing three ways, all in the stock map UI: middle-click on the large map (Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick), double-click on the map while the Ping pin type is selected (Minimap.OnMapDblClick), and gamepad JoyButtonX while the large map is open (Minimap.UpdateMap, pings the view centre).
facts.implication: No keybind config, no client mod, no chat syntax to teach. Mouse and gamepad both covered. Precision is whatever the map zoom allows.

facts.claim: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC only puts a packet on the wire when targetPeerID != m_id; a message addressed to the sender's own id is handled purely locally.
facts.citation: ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83576-83592 (the `if (targetPeerID == m_id || targetPeerID == 0L) HandleRoutedRPC` / `if (targetPeerID != m_id) RouteRPC` pair)
facts.implication: This is the rule that kills chat as a control channel and saves the ping channel. Self-addressed = invisible to the server; 0 = always visible; other-peer = relayed through the server but not locally handled.

facts.claim: Chat.SendText (Shout) and Talker.Say (Normal/Whisper) both route through Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync, which sends ONE RPC to the sender's own UserID plus one to each OTHER listed player's characterID.UserID — never to the server as a distinct target. Only the `PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider == null` branch collapses to a single broadcast at targetPeerID 0.
facts.implication: With exactly one player online, chat text produces ZERO network traffic and the server is blind. With 2+ players it only appears as relay traffic. A registered server-side "ChatMessage" handler will NOT fire for chat text on Steam. Confirms and sharpens Wonderland's EmoteSignals.cs warning.

facts.claim: The dedicated server relays every routed RPC it does not handle locally: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC deserializes the package, calls HandleRoutedRPC only when m_targetPeerID is the server or 0, and then calls RouteRPC for anything not addressed to itself.
facts.implication: A Harmony prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC (or on the private RouteRPC(RoutedRPCData)) sees 100% of peer-to-peer traffic, including whispers, shouts, RPC_SetTag, ward toggles, door use — everything. This is the universal observation hook and needs no RPC-name registration.

facts.claim: ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC receives a fully deserialized RoutedRPCData (m_senderPeerID, m_targetZDO, m_methodHash, m_parameters as a ZPackage positioned at 0) and is called for every RPC addressed to the server or to Everybody, regardless of whether any handler is registered.
facts.implication: Collision-free alternative to ZRoutedRpc.Register for capturing pings: Harmony-prefix HandleRoutedRPC, snapshot data.m_parameters.GetPos(), read, then SetPos back so vanilla's own dispatch still works.

facts.claim: ZDOID.UserID resolves to the ZDOMan session id of the client that minted the ZDO, and ZNet.GetUID() == ZDOMan.GetSessionID() == the value a peer reports as ZNetPeer.m_uid.
facts.implication: A chat/ping RPC's `sender` argument and a character ZDO's m_uid.UserID are the same number as ZNetPeer.m_uid, so a received ping maps directly to a ZNetPeer and therefore to a ConnectedCharacter.

facts.claim: Player emotes are pure ZDO writes on the character ZDO: Player.StartEmote sets s_emote (string), bumps s_emoteID (int), and sets s_emoteOneshot; StopEmote bumps the counter with an empty name. There are 25 vanilla emotes (Emotes enum), all reachable from the emote wheel or by typing /<emote> in chat.
facts.implication: A 25-value discrete selector that always reaches the server regardless of player count, exactly as Wonderland/Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs polls it. Combine with the equipped-item channel below for a 2-axis menu.

facts.claim: VisEquipment mirrors every visible equipped item into the character's own ZDO as a prefab hash: s_rightItem, s_leftItem (+Variant/+Quality), s_chestItem, s_legItem, s_helmetItem, s_shoulderItem (+Variant/+Quality), s_utilityItem, s_beardItem, s_hairItem, plus s_modelIndex/s_skinColor/s_hairColor.
facts.implication: 'Hold item X' is a fully server-readable selector on a vanilla client. Equipping a specific weapon/cape/utility + emoting gives a large, discoverable command space with zero UI work.

facts.claim: An ItemStand stores what is mounted on it as plain ZDO ints: ZDOVars.s_item (prefab stable hash), s_variant, s_quality, s_type (orientation).
facts.citation: ItemStand assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:131475; ZDO writes at :131795 (s_item = stableHashCode), :131570/:131600 region; field reads at :131649-131651
facts.implication: An item stand is a physical radio button the server can read with one ZDO poll. A row of stands next to a portal is a zero-mod destination picker with an in-world, self-documenting UI.

facts.claim: A Sign's text is written straight into its own ZDO by the local client — Sign.SetText calls m_nview.ClaimOwnership() then zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, text) plus s_author/s_authorDisplayName. There is NO Sign RPC; Sign.Awake registers none.
facts.citation: Sign.SetText assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141913-141928; Sign.Awake :141772-141781; Sign.UpdateText :141835-141865 (InvokeRepeating every 2s, redraw gated on ZDO DataRevision)
facts.implication: Corrects the assignment's premise of a `Sign.RPC_SetText`: sign text is observed by polling s_text, not by intercepting an RPC. It is also a bidirectional surface — the server can rewrite s_text and every client repaints within 2s. Default m_characterLimit is 50.

facts.claim: A portal tag is set by TeleportWorld.SetText -> m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId), which targets the ZDO's current OWNER; the handler applies only if m_nview.IsOwner(), and writes s_tag + s_tagauthor after clearing the portal's connection.
facts.implication: The server can observe retags either by polling s_tag on ZDOMan.GetPortalList() or by watching relayed RPC_SetTag traffic. CRITICAL: if the SERVER owns a portal ZDO, the RPC routes to the server, ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null (no GameObject), and the tag change is silently dropped — server ownership of a portal breaks vanilla retagging.

facts.claim: The client's portal-tag text box is hard-capped at 10 characters: TeleportWorld.Interact calls TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10), and TextInput.Show assigns that straight to m_inputField.characterLimit.
facts.implication: A tag-as-command-line gets 10 characters, period. Enough for 'go:mine' or a short destination name, not for structured syntax. Also: the dialog pre-fills with the existing tag, so a long server-written tag risks being clamped and saved back truncated if the player opens the dialog.

facts.claim: Container contents live in the container's own ZDO as a single serialized Inventory blob under ZDOVars.s_items, written by Container.Save() whenever the owning client's inventory changes, with ZDOVars.s_inUse flagging an open UI.
facts.implication: 'Put item X in chest Y' is a fully server-readable input, exactly as Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs already implements (Load/Save/IsBusy). Slower and clunkier than a ping but unambiguous, and it is the only channel that can also charge a toll.

facts.claim: Player character inventories are NEVER in any ZDO. Character/Humanoid/Player write only s_health, s_maxHealth, s_stamina, s_eitr, s_dead, s_pvp, s_stealth, s_inBed, s_playerName, s_playerID, s_noise, s_lookTarget, s_bodyVelocity, s_emote*, s_crowned, s_adrenaline, s_dodgeinv, s_weaponLoaded, s_isBlockingHash, s_wakeup, s_baseValue, s_cheated to their ZDO.
facts.citation: exhaustive scan of `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` inside Character :178-6796, Humanoid :6796-9414 and Player :9414-16500 of assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs; ZdoInventoryIO.cs documents the same conclusion
facts.implication: The server cannot reproduce TeleportWorld's ore/metal check under any circumstances, and cannot charge a player's own inventory. Any server-driven teleport therefore bypasses the item restriction entirely.

facts.claim: CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation writes the player's look target into the character ZDO as ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = eyePos + lookDir * 100f, at most every 0.2s and only when it changed.
facts.implication: The server can tell roughly what a player is LOOKING AT to ~0.2s resolution — e.g. which of several nearby portals/signs/item stands they are facing. Gated on the prefab's m_headRotation/m_head serialized fields (Inspector data).

facts.claim: PrivateArea (ward) state is both RPC-visible and ZDO-visible: it registers ZNetView RPCs "ToggleEnabled"(long playerID), "TogglePermitted"(long playerID, string name) and "FlashShield", and stores ZDOVars.s_enabled / s_permitted / s_creatorName in its ZDO.
facts.implication: 'Toggle your ward twice' is an observable gesture and ward permission lists are server-readable — useful both as an input channel and for the Group-4 ward-gated retag protection already in the spec.

facts.claim: Every piece a player builds becomes a new ZDO the server sees at the moment it arrives: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData calls the private CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int) with prefabHash 0 and only then ZDO.Deserialize(pkg) supplies the real prefab. Piece.Awake reads ZDOVars.s_creator (the builder's PlayerProfile playerID) and s_creatorIndex.
facts.citation: ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692; Piece.Awake :136246-136250; Piece.SetCreator :136416-136424; the two-hook pattern is implemented in Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70
facts.implication: 'Build a specific piece / a specific shape at a specific place' is a real-time, attributable input channel. Same hooks give destruction via ZDOMan's DestroyZDO path.

facts.claim: A dropped item is a fully readable ZDO: ItemDrop.Save writes the whole ItemData as a byte blob under ZDOVars.s_itemData (plus s_quality/s_variant for indexed slots), and the ZDO's own prefab hash identifies the item type.
facts.implication: 'Drop item X on the ground here' is server-observable with position, type and stack. Works with zero player-count dependency.

facts.claim: MessageHud registers the global routed RPC "ShowMessage"(int type, string text) in Start, and RPC_ShowMessage calls ShowMessage unconditionally — the only gate is Hud.IsUserHidden(). MessageType is TopLeft = 1, Center = 2, and the text is run through Localization.Localize.
facts.citation: MessageHud.Start assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:55799-55809; MessageHud.RPC_ShowMessage :55848-55851; MessageHud.ShowMessage :55853-55860; enum MessageType :55705-55709; MessageHud.MessageAll :55843-55846
facts.implication: Primary server->client text output. Server can target one peer with ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "ShowMessage", (int)type, text) or broadcast with 0L. Because Localize runs client-side, sending "$piece_portal" renders in the player's own language.

facts.claim: Player registers a per-character routed RPC "Message"(int type, string msg, int amount) — registered ONLY when m_nview.IsOwner(), and RPC_Message re-checks IsOwner before calling MessageHud.ShowMessage.
facts.implication: Exactly what Wonderland/Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs uses: InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", type, text, 0). Addressed to one player, cannot leak to others, and needs no MessageHud singleton on the server.

facts.claim: Chat registers the global routed RPC "RPC_TeleportPlayer"(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, bool distantTeleport) whose body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` with NO sender check, NO admin check and NO item/boss/NoPortals check.
facts.citation: Chat.Awake registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41627; Chat.TeleportPlayer :41957-41960; Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962-41968; the vanilla `recall` admin command that uses it :44546-44555
facts.implication: Server->client teleport primitive #1. `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` needs only the peer uid — no character ZDOID, no Chat.instance on the server.

facts.claim: Every Character also registers "RPC_TeleportTo"(Vector3, Quaternion, bool) on its own ZNetView, gated only on m_nview.IsOwner(); Player.TeleportTo then runs the standard 2s fade teleport with only IsTeleporting() and a 2s m_teleportCooldown guard.
facts.citation: Character.Awake registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:886; Character.RPC_TeleportTo :4126-4132; Player.TeleportTo override :15302-15327; Player.UpdateTeleport :15329+
facts.implication: Server->client teleport primitive #2, ZDO-scoped: InvokeRoutedRPC(peerUid, characterZdoId, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true). Two independent paths means a working teleport even if one is patched by another mod. Both silently no-op inside the 2s cooldown.

facts.claim: Game registers the global routed RPC "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"(string pinName, int pinType, Vector3 pos, bool showMap) on EVERY client (not server-gated), and its body calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation(pos, (PinType)pinType, pinName, showMap) which does AddPin(..., save: true) and shows a "$msg_pin_added: NAME" toast.
facts.implication: THE server-pushed map pin: arbitrary name, arbitrary position, any PinType (Icon0-4, Bed, Boss, Death...), SAVED into the player's own map profile, optionally centering their map. Duplicate-suppressed by HaveSimilarPin (same name+type within 1m). This is how a player gets a permanent labelled marker for a portal with zero client mod.

facts.claim: A fabricated "ChatMessage" from the server renders on a vanilla client as a chat line + floating in-world text at the supplied position + a large animated, LABELLED map pin lasting m_worldTextTTL = 5s; Shout pins read "<UserInfo.Name>: <TEXT IN CAPS>" and Ping pins read "<UserInfo.Name>: PING".
facts.citation: Chat.RPC_ChatMessage assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41970-41973; Chat.OnNewChatMessage :41775-41816; Chat.AddInworldText :41873-41913 (Ping forces text="PING", Shout uppercases); Minimap.UpdateShoutPins :57624-57650; Minimap.UpdatePingPins :57591-57622; Chat.m_worldTextTTL :41594
facts.implication: Highest-bandwidth single output: one RPC gives text, world text and a labelled map pin. UserInfo.Name is fully server-chosen, so 'Portal Network' can be the speaker. Gate: AddInworldText is skipped only when the map HUD is fully off (m_mode == None) AND the position is > m_nomapPingDistance (50m) away — with the normal minimap visible m_mode is Small, so it always runs.

facts.claim: RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync in 1.0.7 is a one-line stub that always returns Granted synchronously.
facts.implication: Server-fabricated ChatMessages always display — there is no mute/relations filter to defeat and no async delay. It also means the only real branch in CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync is the RelationsProvider null check.

facts.claim: DamageText registers the global routed RPC "RPC_DamageText"(ZPackage) whose payload is {int TextType, Vector3 pos, string text, bool mySelf}; the text is Localize'd and drawn as floating world text, culled only by m_maxTextDistance = 30m and Hud.IsUserHidden().
facts.citation: DamageText.Awake assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46352-46356; DamageText.ShowText(TextType,Vector3,string,bool) :46486-46493; DamageText.RPC_DamageText :46494-46510; AddInworldText :46395-46445; m_maxTextDistance :46338; enum TextType :46309-46319
facts.implication: Arbitrary floating text above any world object within 30m — e.g. hovering a destination name over a portal. TextType.Bonus is the attention-grabber (orange, 1.5x font, 3s). Avoid TooHard (overwrites the text with $msg_toohard) and Blocked (prefixes $msg_blocked:).

facts.claim: ZoneSystem registers "LocationIcons"(ZPackage) on clients only; RPC_LocationIcons CLEARS and replaces the client's whole m_locationIcons dictionary of (Vector3 -> string), and Minimap re-syncs its location pins from it every 5s, rendering an icon only if the name matches an entry in the Minimap prefab's compiled m_locationIcons sprite list. Those pins carry an empty name.
facts.citation: ZoneSystem.Start registration assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113453; ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons :113581-113593; ZoneSystem.RPC_LocationIcons :113595-113607; Minimap location pin refresh :57490-57531; Minimap.GetLocationIcon :58363-58374
facts.implication: An icon-only, unlabelled, server-driven map overlay the server can rewrite at will (InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, "LocationIcons", pkg)). Useful for marking every portal on the map, but no text and the sprite names are Unity asset data.

facts.claim: MapTable stores its shared map payload as Utils.Compress(Minimap.GetSharedMapData(...)) in ZDOVars.s_data, and any player pressing Read feeds it straight into Minimap.AddSharedMapData, which adds PINS (long ownerID, string name, Vector3 pos, int PinType, bool checked, string author) with save:true — and deletes the reader's existing non-own-owner pins that are not re-listed.
facts.implication: A server-craftable blob that hands any reader a whole set of named pins on demand — an opt-in 'sync the portal network to my map' button using an existing vanilla piece. Dangerous: it also wipes other-owner pins not present in the blob, and the explored array length must exactly match Minimap.m_textureSize^2 (code default 256).

facts.claim: ZNetScene registers the global routed RPC "SpawnObject"(Vector3, Quaternion, int prefabHash) which does a bare UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate of any prefab in m_namedPrefabs (which includes the non-ZNetView prefab list).
facts.implication: Server->client VFX/SFX channel: target one peer with a vfx_/sfx_ prefab hash for a visual cue at a portal. NEVER use it with a ZNetView-bearing prefab — every recipient would independently create a duplicate ZDO.

facts.claim: SEMan registers "RPC_AddStatusEffect"(int nameHash, bool resetTime, int itemLevel, float skillLevel, int variant) on the character's own ZNetView (SEMan shares Character.m_nview); the receiving client resolves nameHash purely against its own ObjectDB.
facts.citation: SEMan ctor assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:28724-28729; SEMan.AddStatusEffect non-owner branch :28815-28821; SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect :28823-28829; Internal_AddStatusEffect :28831-28850; implemented in Wonderland/Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs
facts.implication: Server can grant any existing vanilla status effect to a specific player as feedback/reward — e.g. a visible buff icon confirming a selection was accepted. Cannot create novel effects.

facts.claim: ZoneSystem's global-key RPCs are split by role: the server registers "SetGlobalKey"/"RemoveGlobalKey", clients register "GlobalKeys". The server's RPC_SetGlobalKey adds the key then calls SendGlobalKeys(0L), broadcasting the whole key list to everyone; SendGlobalKeys/SendLocationIcons also fire on every new peer.
facts.implication: ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(name) called on the server works end-to-end (routes to itself, then broadcasts). This is the vanilla-respecting lever behind NoPortals/NoBossPortals/TeleportAll — client-honored, not server-enforced.

facts.claim: ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS runs every 2 seconds on the server and calls ReleaseNearbyZDOS for the server's own reference position and for each peer's; any persistent ZDO owned by the server but sitting in a PEER's active area is handed to that peer, because IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, serverSessionId) tests against the server's pinned reference position of (1e6, 0, 1e6).
facts.citation: ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76871-76885; ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927; IsInPeerActiveArea :76887-76899; Game.FixedUpdate pinning SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6) :100465
facts.implication: Server ownership of any ZDO near a player is transient — reclaimed within 2s. Combined with the RPC_SetTag gotcha above, the mod must never hold portal-ZDO ownership persistently; write, then let go, and re-write on a tick.

facts.claim: The server only transmits ZDOs inside a peer's simulation distance around ZNetPeer.m_refPos, plus anything explicitly force-sent; clients conversely send only what they changed (m_clientChangeQueue). ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id) is public and server-side.

gotchas: Chat text is NOT a server input. With exactly one player online, Chat.SendText/Talker.Say produce literally zero packets (targetPeerID == the sender's own id, and ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC only routes when targetPeerID != m_id, :83576-83592). Any design that depends on 'player says a keyword' is broken for a solo player and only works as relay sniffing otherwise.

Slash commands are dead. Chat.InputText strips the '/' and hands the rest to Terminal.TryRunCommand with silentFail:true (:41947-41955, :45734-45758). An unknown command name does nothing and prints nothing; only commands already compiled into the client AND flagged RemoteCommand reach the server, and ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand then rejects non-admins (:81879-81889).

Claiming server ownership of a portal ZDO silently breaks vanilla retagging. TeleportWorld.SetText invokes RPC_SetTag at the ZDO's owner (:143575-143581, ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855-82858); if that owner is the dedicated server, ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC looks up ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo), gets null (no GameObject exists server-side), and drops the RPC with no error (:83650-83668, :82229-82236).

Server ZDO ownership is revoked automatically. ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS runs every 2s; because the server's reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6) (Game.FixedUpdate :100465), any server-owned persistent ZDO inside a player's active area fails IsInPeerActiveArea and is handed to that player (:76901-76927). Write-then-release, and re-apply on a tick; never assume a held claim.

The server can never see a player's inventory. No character ZDO carries s_items; the exhaustive Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO-write scan yields only vitals, identity, emote and pose fields. TeleportWorld's ore/metal restriction is therefore unreproducible server-side, and a server-issued teleport (RPC_TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportTo) bypasses it entirely — you will let players portal with iron and there is no way to detect it.

Portal tags are capped at 10 characters by the client's text widget (TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) :143481 -> m_inputField.characterLimit :61519). Worse, TextInput.Show pre-fills the field with the existing tag — if the server has written a longer tag for display, a player opening the dialog may save back a truncated version.

Portal tags are not rich-text capable in hover: TeleportWorld.GetHoverText runs the tag through .RemoveRichTextTags() (:143458, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700). And vanilla shows portal tags NOWHERE on the map — only on hover.
Chat text has '<' and '>' replaced with spaces in Chat.OnNewChatMessage (:41795-41796), so fabricated chat output cannot use colour or size markup either.

A fabricated Shout/Ping ChatMessage produces its map pin only if Chat.AddInworldText runs, which is skipped when Minimap.m_mode == MapMode.None AND the position is more than m_nomapPingDistance (50f) from the viewer (:41808, :56396). Normal play has the small minimap up (m_mode == Small), so this only bites in nomap worlds or with the HUD hidden.

Registering a routed-RPC name the dedicated server already has throws. ZRoutedRpc.Register uses Dictionary.Add (:83680-83716). Vanilla code at :80258-80281 calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll UNGUARDED under IsDedicated(), and ZNet.InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand ungated (:81894) — both imply GUI singletons may exist headless. Probe ZRoutedRpc.instance's private m_functions before Register, or patch HandleRoutedRPC instead.

MapTable-based pin delivery is destructive: Minimap.AddSharedMapData marks every pin whose m_ownerID is non-zero and not the reader's own for deletion, keeping only those re-listed in the incoming blob (:58824-58875). A crafted blob that omits a player's shared pins wipes them. It also throws/rejects unless the explored bool array length exactly matches the client's Minimap.m_textureSize^2.

Minimap.AddPin forces any type outside [Icon0, m_visibleIconTypes.Length) to Icon3 (:58375-58382), and DiscoverLocation refuses to add a pin if one with the same name+type already sits within 1m (HaveSimilarPin :58363-58374) — repeated server pushes of the same pin are silently no-ops.
Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting() or while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15309-15316), returning false with no message on either side. Rapid server-issued teleports vanish without a trace.
ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' broadcast-instantiates on every recipient: using it with a ZNetView prefab creates one duplicate ZDO per client (:82355-82366). VFX/SFX prefabs only.

Server->client ZDO writes only reach a client whose simulation area covers that ZDO (ZDOMan.CreateSyncList :77212-77241). Rewriting a far portal's tag as a message to a player does nothing until they walk there, unless you call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, zdoid).
ZNet.RemotePrint output lands in the client's Console buffer (:81650-81656), which most players never open — treat it as an admin-only channel, not player feedback.

Map pings are public: Chat.SendPing broadcasts to targetPeerID 0, so every other online player sees the ping marker and its map pin. A ping-driven destination picker is a visible, shared gesture, and is trivially spammable — debounce per player and rate-limit before acting on it.
openQuestions: Does a dedicated server instantiate the GUI hierarchy? Specifically: are Chat.instance, MessageHud.instance, Minimap.instance, DamageText.instance, Console.instance null or non-null? The decompile is contradictory — Game.UpdateSaving guards with `(bool)MessageHud.instance` (:100474) while ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer calls MessageHud.instance.MessageAll unguarded under IsDedicated() (:80258, :80280) and ZNet.InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand unguarded (:81894). IN-GAME CHECK: at BepInEx plugin Awake+30s on the dedicated server, log the null-ness of all five singletons, AND dump the key set of ZRoutedRpc.instance's private m_functions (AccessTools.Field(typeof(ZRoutedRpc),"m_functions")) checking for "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode() and "ShowMessage".GetStableHashCode(). This decides Register-vs-Harmony for the ping hook.

Is PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on a Steam client? It is implemented in the platform assemblies, which are not in this decompile set. If it IS null, Chat.SendText collapses to a single broadcast at targetPeerID 0 (:42002-42005) and ordinary chat text becomes a first-class server input even solo. IN-GAME CHECK: register/patch a server-side "ChatMessage" handler, have a SOLO player type a plain sentence and a /s shout, and see whether the handler fires.

Does the Player prefab have CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation enabled and m_head assigned? Both are serialized Inspector fields gating the ZDOVars.s_lookTarget write (:5043). IN-GAME CHECK: poll s_lookTarget on a connected character ZDO for 10s while the player spins in place; a changing non-zero Vector3 confirms the look-direction channel.

What is Minimap.m_textureSize on the shipped Minimap prefab? The C# default is 256 (:56287) but the Inspector may override it, and Minimap.GetSharedMapData/AddSharedMapData require an exploration bool array of exactly m_textureSize^2 (:58739-58748, :58777-58795). Without this number a server-crafted MapTable blob cannot be built. IN-GAME CHECK: on a client, log Minimap.instance.m_textureSize and Minimap.instance.m_explored.Length.

What location-icon names exist in the Minimap prefab's compiled m_locationIcons sprite list (Minimap.GetLocationIcon :58363-58374)? These are Unity asset entries, invisible to the decompile, and they bound what the "LocationIcons" server-push overlay can render. IN-GAME CHECK: on a client, enumerate Minimap.instance.m_locationIcons and log every m_name.

Is the emote list in the emote wheel the full 25-value Emotes enum on every platform/input device, or is the wheel a subset with the rest reachable only by typing /<emote>? Affects how large a practical emote-based command alphabet is. IN-GAME CHECK: open the emote wheel on a vanilla client and count entries against the enum at :6216-6246.

Does GuiInputField (Valheim's InputField subclass) clamp a programmatically assigned .text to characterLimit? TextInput.Show assigns m_inputField.text = existingTag AFTER setting characterLimit = 10 (:61519-61520). If it clamps, any server-written portal tag longer than 10 chars gets silently truncated the moment a player opens the tag dialog and saves. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, then open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client and re-read s_tag.

Does the dedicated server's ZNetScene ever instantiate a GameObject for a ZDO, or is FindInstance always null? The RPC_SetTag drop-on-server-ownership gotcha depends on this being always-null. IN-GAME CHECK: log ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances() (:82334) on a running dedicated server with players online.
correctionsToExistingSpec: Group 3 says 'Chat-command parsing is unreliable server-side — an emote or item-interaction trigger is the safer entry point, not a slash command.' That is right about slash commands but MISSES the strongest channel in the game: the vanilla MAP PING. Chat.SendPing invokes "ChatMessage" at targetPeerID 0 with no permission check and no player-count dependency (:42058-42068), delivering an arbitrary player-chosen world coordinate to the dedicated server. Middle-click the map (or double-click with the Ping pin selected, or gamepad JoyButtonX) is a complete, precise, zero-mod destination picker. Self-service warps and player-driven portal retargeting are therefore genuinely player-driven, not admin-only.

The spec is silent on WHY chat text fails. The reason is not 'parsing': Chat.SendText and Talker.Say address one RPC per OTHER listed player plus one to the sender (:41996-42043), so a solo player generates no packets at all, and multi-player chat only appears as relay traffic visible through a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC patch — never through a registered handler. Worth stating precisely, because the relay path IS usable when 2+ players are online.

The assignment brief (and by implication the spec's mental model) names `Sign.RPC_SetText` and `ZDOVars.s_text` as an RPC surface. In 1.0.7 there is NO Sign RPC at all — Sign.Awake registers none and Sign.SetText does ClaimOwnership + zdo.Set(s_text, ...) directly (:141772-141781, :141913-141928). Sign text is a POLLED ZDO field in both directions, and it is also a server-writable in-world display that repaints on every client within 2s (Sign.UpdateText InvokeRepeating 2f).

Group 1's 'Direct tag write/rename bypassing the RPC and the 10-character text-entry UI entirely' is correct but incomplete: because RPC_SetTag is delivered to the portal ZDO's OWNER and the dedicated server has no TeleportWorld GameObject, a mod that takes server ownership of a portal ZDO makes vanilla retagging silently fail (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC -> ZNetScene.FindInstance == null, :83660-83667). This directly contradicts Group 1's last bullet, 'Proactive server ownership claim on placement — makes RPC interception more reliable' — it does the opposite for RPC_SetTag. Intercept via ZDO polling or a RPC_RoutedRPC relay patch instead, and never hold portal ownership.

Group 1's ownership-claim bullet also underestimates ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS: any server-owned persistent ZDO inside a player's active area is reassigned to that player every 2 seconds (:76871-76927), because the server's own reference position is pinned at (1e6,0,1e6). A 'proactive claim' cannot be held; it is only ever a momentary write window.

The Ruled Out entry 'no server-pushed map pins' is not stated in the spec, but the spec's 'Every Portal in the Realm, Listed' bullet asserts an in-game player-facing listing is 'unavoidably client work'. That is too strong. Four server-only map surfaces exist on a vanilla client: (a) "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse" -> Minimap.DiscoverLocation adds a NAMED, SAVED pin of any PinType at any position and can center the player's map (:100068, :100822-100829, :58334-58360); (b) a fabricated Shout/Ping "ChatMessage" gives a 5s labelled animated pin at any position (:41775-41816, :57591-57650); (c) "LocationIcons" rewrites the client's whole location-icon overlay (:113595-113607); (d) MapTable's s_data blob delivers a full named pin set to any player who reads a cartography table (:133831-133865, :58797-58875). An in-game, per-player portal map is achievable without a client mod — just not as a live interactive picker window.

Group 5's toll bullet says 'debit a nearby server-visible container, never the traveling player's own inventory (which is never networked to the server at all)'. Correct, and the reason is now pinned exactly: an exhaustive scan of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` in Character/Humanoid/Player shows no s_items on any character ZDO; the only player-carried thing the server CAN see is what is visibly equipped, via VisEquipment's s_rightItem/s_leftItem/s_helmetItem/s_chestItem/s_legItem/s_shoulderItem/s_utilityItem writes into the character ZDO (:20569-20708). That is also a usable player-input alphabet the spec does not mention.

Group 3's 'bypassing Chat.instance entirely' advice is right, and there is a second, independent teleport RPC the spec already names but does not distinguish operationally: "RPC_TeleportPlayer" needs only the peer uid (Chat-registered, global, :41627/:41962) while Character's "RPC_TeleportTo" is per-character-ZDO (:886/:4126). Both are completely ungated on the client — no item check, no boss check, no NoPortals check — and both no-op silently inside the 2s cooldown.
